idea: Combine previous-generation accelerators (HBM2-era parts on non-EUV processes) with attention offload: the new GPU ships query vectors over the network, the retired GPU holds long-context KV in its HBM and returns attention outputs, so only small vectors cross the link.

title: Thermal circuit-breaker integrator tracks row hammer analogically
idea: Borrowed from bimetal thermal breakers: each wordline driver has a tiny leaky capacitor that gets a fixed charge quantum per activation and bleeds with a ~64 ms time constant; when a threshold comparator trips, it requests a neighbor refresh.

title: Video-codec P-frames: delta-encoded memory pages against reference pages
idea: Borrowed from MPEG inter-frame coding: a CXL memory-expander controller keeps 'I-pages' as references and stores near-duplicate pages (VM clones, forked workers, fine-tuned weight variants, beam-search KV copies) as XOR/byte-delta 'P-pages' with offset hints, decoded in a ~20 ns pipeline on read. A MinHash similarity index chooses each page's reference at write-back time.
note: Hardware Difference-Engine; near-duplicate pages via MinHash reference selection is a fair twist.

title: SSD-controller playbook: 28nm CXL controller with page-level LDPC
idea: Adapted from NAND flash, which became cheap by pairing weak cells with smart controllers: a 28 nm CXL memory controller built in existing mature logic fabs applies 4 KB-codeword LDPC, with an on-chip SRAM write-combining buffer for read-modify-write, to unmodified commodity or lower-grade DRAM, exposing a byte-addressable device that tolerates raw BER ~1e-4.

title: Magnify dictionaries: hardware zstd for in-memory logs and JSON
idea: Magnify compression context with trained multi-MB dictionaries per data type (logs, JSON, traces). A CXL-module decompressor at 50 GB/s serves reads, and the in-memory store keeps everything compressed.

title: Eliminate the 64-ms retention spec: ephemeral sub-femtofarad cells for transient tensors
idea: Eliminate the assumption that every bit must survive 64 ms: build a memory class whose storage node is a planar ~0.5 fF capacitor with no pillar and ~100 us retention, used only for AI activations, KV-cache spill and gradients that are overwritten within microseconds; the controller tags allocations by lifetime and never refreshes them.
note: Lifetime-matched no-refresh tier for AI transients; similar to refresh-skipping eDRAM for DNNs.

title: Eliminate writability for frozen weights: via-programmed 3D ROM replaces DRAM
idea: Encode a deployed model's weights as present/absent vias in 4-8 stacked metal layers written by maskless e-beam on mature-node wafers, read by low-swing sensing with no refresh or capacitor, with only activations kept in DRAM.
note: Via-programmed ROM for frozen weights; hardwired-model chips exist; e-beam write throughput for big models is a doubt.

title: Bit-plane progressive fetch stops when precision suffices
idea: Eliminate low-order bits from the bus: store tensors transposed into bit-planes and fetch sign/exponent/MSB planes first; the consumer's datapath signals 'enough' as soon as the result (e.g., top-k ordering or a dot-product bound) can no longer change, and the remaining planes are never sent.
note: Exact early termination on bounds (top-k) is the non-obvious part; bit-plane layout costs write/compute overhead.

title: Memory-side top-k gate returns token indices, not keys
idea: Eliminate shipping full key vectors: each HBM pseudo-channel's base-die slice holds a small dot-product unit and comparator tree that scores the query against stored keys inside the stack and returns only the top-k token indices; only those value rows then cross the interface.

title: Via-ROM weight chiplet: frozen weights need no DRAM
idea: Eliminate DRAM, its writes and its refresh for deployed model weights: encode weights in a single custom via-mask layer of a mature-node ROM die (one via = one bit) hybrid-bonded under the compute die; the data survives power loss by construction.
note: Mature-node via-ROM is ~10x less dense than DRAM; only frozen models; Taalas-like hardwiring exists.

title: Bit-plane-major storage with progressive-precision fetch
idea: Rearrange bit order: weights are stored transposed so that each DRAM burst holds the same bit position of 512 different weights. The accelerator fetches the top 4 bit-planes first and fetches lower planes only for layers or tokens whose error estimate needs them.
note: Close to Any-Precision LLM bit-plane storage and bit-serial accelerators.

title: Transfer-print thin memory membranes, then wire them lithographically
idea: Reverse bond-then-connect: undercut-release memory chiplets into <10 um membranes, pick them with a PDMS stamp onto the logic wafer, planarize with BCB, and pattern vias and copper across both with ordinary lithography, giving a monolithic-like 2-3 um-pitch connection with no bumps.

title: Self-service: read-write-read self-reference removes matched sense amp pairs
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: each read samples the bitline after charge sharing, writes a known '1', shares again and samples a second time, comparing the cell with itself on one capacitor pair; device mismatch, reference bitlines and dummy cells cancel, so sloppy TFT or 180 nm transistors can serve as the sense amp.

title: Token-sweep restore: inference reads replace refresh, shortening capacitors
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: in LLM-inference memory every weight row is activated once per decode step (~10-16 ms) and each activation restores the cell, so the controller disables refresh and guarantees the sweep period; if serving pauses beyond the bound it drops the weights and reloads them from flash, keeping refresh power exactly zero.

title: Base-array mask ROM with one e-beam-written via layer
idea: TRIZ #10 Prior action: pre-build generic NOR-ROM wafers (4F2 transistor arrays, DUV plus SAQP, ~25 masks, no capacitor) in bulk; once a model is frozen, program its weights by e-beam direct-writing a single via layer with two via sizes per bit-pair (2 bits/cell), so inference weights live in silicon with zero refresh and zero standby.
note: No capacitor or refresh for frozen weights; model churn and e-beam throughput limit it.

title: Train models with KV-dropout so memory starvation is harmless
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: inject random KV eviction (drop 30-70% of past tokens' KV, biased toward older ones) as a regularizer during pre- and post-training, turning the harm of missing context into learned robustness so inference can evict aggressively with negligible quality loss.

title: Venus-flytrap analog leaky integrators as row-hammer counters
idea: The Venus flytrap counts touches with a decaying calcium signal (two within ~30 s closes the trap). Each 8-row group gets a DRAM-process capacitor that takes a fixed charge packet per activation and leaks with a designed time constant near the refresh window. Crossing a comparator threshold triggers neighbor refresh, with no SRAM counters or CAM.

title: Buffet-line broadcast: one DRAM read feeds every accelerator
idea: One buffet tray serves every diner. Likewise, a weight-streaming memory node reads each weight block once and puts it on a shared multidrop optical/SerDes broadcast bus. All N data-parallel accelerators in the pod latch it at the same moment, in a synchronized schedule.

title: RISC-V-style royalty-free DRAM patent pool and periphery generator
idea: Like RISC-V plus the MPEG-LA patent pool, a foundation assembles expired 6F2/8F2 cell, sense-amp and DLL patents with donated ones into a royalty-free pool and ships an open-source periphery compiler that generates JEDEC-compliant row/column logic for a given process.
note: Open DRAM periphery compiler (OpenRAM analog) is demoable in software.

title: Drum-era SOAP placement makes shift-register memories act random-access
idea: Revive the IBM 650's Symbolic Optimal Assembly Program, which placed each next instruction where the rotating drum would be when needed: a compiler/controller lays out tensors, KV-cache pages and weights in shift-register arrays (CCD strings, racetracks, delay loops) so the next word reaches the read port just in time, with out-of-order prefetch hiding the rest.

title: Weimer's 1962 TFT reborn: panel-fab memory on Gen-8 glass
idea: Revive RCA's thin-film transistor for memory: build 4-tier oxide-TFT DRAM-like arrays on Gen-8.5 glass in idle LCD and plasma panel fabs at ~1 um features, accept 1% defective cells across huge panels with block codes, and sell them as cheap capacity modules.

title: Core-rope weights: maskless via-programmed BEOL ROM frees HBM
idea: Revive Apollo's core-rope memory, where the wiring itself encoded the program: build generic base wafers with 8 stacked metal crossbar levels and encode a frozen model's weights only in the via layers, written maskless by multibeam e-beam, so each model ships as a ROM chiplet. Weights leave DRAM; HBM keeps only activations and KV cache.

title: Goodyear STARAN revival: multidimensional-access memory serves bit-planes on demand
idea: Revive STARAN's 1972 multi-dimensional-access memory: a flip-network permutation in the HBM base die lets one stored array be read word-wise or bit-plane-wise, so precision-adaptive kernels fetch only the top k bit-planes of weights or activations.

title: Capacitorless 50-microsecond cells sized to transient tensor lifetimes
idea: Invert 'every bit must survive 64 ms' -> design a cell that only lasts ~50 us. A 2-transistor node using only the read-transistor gate capacitance (~0.1 fF, no capacitor) holds activations, gradients and attention scratch whose lifetime is microseconds; the compiler guarantees consumption or rewrite before expiry and hardware timestamps flag expired lines.
note: Same lifetime-matched ephemeral cell, gain-cell variant.

title: Shallow 1 fF pillars rescued by soft-decision sensing and LDPC
idea: Invert 'every cell must read correctly on its own' -> let cells be weak and the code be smart. Etch only 1 fF, AR ~15 pillars; sense amps emit 2-bit soft information (strong/weak 0/1) to an on-die LDPC decoder over 512-bit codewords, tolerating raw BER ~1e-3 that would kill a hard-decision chip.
note: LDPC soft sensing trades capacitor AR for decoder; latency is the doubt.

title: Ephemeral memory: data dies before charge does, so never refresh
idea: Inverts 'stored data must outlive cell retention': a refresh-less DRAM tier holds only AI activations, gradients, KV blocks and packet buffers whose lifetime the compiler/runtime proves is below a guaranteed 10-50 ms retention, with hardware write-timestamps that fault any read past the deadline.
note: Compiler-proved short data lifetimes enable refresh-free tier and shorter capacitors; weak-cell tail must still meet guarantee.

title: OS lossy heap: applications declare error tolerance per allocation
idea: Inverts 'memory must be bit-exact': a new mmap flag (MAP_LOSSY plus an error bound) sends ML activations, image buffers and analytics sketches to a region where the memory controller applies error-bounded floating-point compression (ZFP/SZ-style) on writeback. Exactness stays the default; lossy bytes are opt-in and typed.

title: Rank/select engines enabling succinct trees and graphs in DRAM
idea: Information theory says an n-node tree needs only ~2n bits, yet pointer trees spend ~128n. Add rank/select and balanced-parentheses navigation units next to the memory controller so succinct encodings (LOUDS, BP, Elias-Fano adjacency lists) traverse in O(1) per hop at near-pointer speed.

title: Twenty-millivolt bitline-style die-to-die links bounded by kT/C
idea: The true floor on signal swing is thermal noise sqrt(kT/C), ~0.2 mV rms on a 100 fF bonded link, so 20 mV still gives >10 sigma margin. Replace 0.4 V HBM drivers with charge-dump transmitters and cross-coupled latch receivers clocked like a DRAM sense amp (precharge, share, regenerate), with per-lane offset trim stored at boot.

title: Twin synchronized predictors send only the surprise
idea: Information theory says only unpredicted bits must cross a channel. Run identical stride/context/value predictors on both sides of the memory link; the sender transmits a 1-bit hit flag when the receiver's prediction is right and an XOR residual otherwise, and both update identically so they stay in lockstep.

title: Potluck cookbook: open-source, silicon-proven DRAM periphery IP commons
idea: A potluck works because everyone shares recipes. Fund an open-source library of DRAM periphery blocks (sense amps with offset calibration, row-hammer trackers, pumps, LPDDR/DDR5 PHYs) with silicon-proven layouts on U.S. 28/22 nm processes, so startups and foundries can build memory dies without decades of trade-secret circuit know-how.

title: Venetian blinds: bit-plane layout fetches only requested precision bits
idea: Tilt Venetian blinds to let in only the light you want. Store tensors transposed into bit-planes across column groups, with a precision-select field in the column command so a 4-bit or 8-bit inference read opens only those planes' micro-rows and moves only those bits, not the full 16-bit words.

title: Socketed design-for-disassembly DRAM packages for multi-life reuse
idea: Box [standard die | standard | standard | compression-interposer LGA packages on CAMM/CXL boards | n/a | solderless assembly]: standardize DRAM packages that mount without solder and carry an on-package wear/retention log, so dies move from retired boards to new controller generations.

title: Fixed-rate ZFP codec in the L2 fill path for simulation arrays
idea: Box: lossy random-access compression × L2 fill/evict path × 4×4×4 float block × fixed 8–16 bits per value × HPC fields. Arrays live in DRAM as fixed-rate ZFP blocks; a cache-side codec decompresses on fill and recompresses on eviction, so code sees plain doubles.
note: Fixed-rate ZFP in cache fill path is plausible for HPC; hardware ZFP has prior proposals.

title: Po: shrink the capacitor to amplify — MOS varactor parametric gain
idea: Po: an amplifier with no gain transistor. Sample the bitline differential onto a pair of silicon MOS varactors held in accumulation, then pulse them into depletion so their capacitance falls ~5x while charge is conserved, raising the differential voltage ~5x before the latch.

title: Double-blind inventory clearinghouse to kill DRAM bullwhip hoarding
idea: Po: every warehouse is made of glass. A neutral party collects encrypted inventory and order data from DRAM makers, distributors and top buyers and, via secure multiparty computation, publishes only weekly aggregate true-demand and channel-inventory indices (like JODI for oil).
note: MPC aggregate indices are feasible; participation incentives are the real hurdle.

title: Laser interference gratings plus coarse cuts define the whole array
idea: Worse: insist that every array layer needs a $200M scanner and a custom reticle. Flip: expose the purely periodic wordline/bitline layers with maskless two-beam 193 nm immersion interference lithography (a ~$10-20M tool), pitch-split by SAQP, then trim with one low-resolution DUV cut mask. Arrays need periodicity, not arbitrary shapes.

title: Federated defect-image library compresses new-fab yield ramps
idea: Worse: every new fab learns its defects alone over 2-3 years. Flip: entrants and toolmakers feed inline SEM/optical defect images and parametric fails into a standardized defect taxonomy. Classifiers train federated (data never leaves each fab) and ship root-cause models and recipe corrections to new lines on day one.

title: Banker's insured deposits: refresh-free banks for data with backups
idea: A banker guards insured deposits lightly because losses are covered. Pages with a valid copy elsewhere (model weights, page cache, read-only datasets) go into banks run with refresh off or at 1-4 s, protected by strong per-line detection codes; a detected error triggers a transparent refetch from flash, CXL or a remote replica instead of a crash.
note: At 1-4 s many cells fail; refetch rate and detection overhead decide net gain.

title: Apollo core-rope weaver: frozen weights in via-programmed ROM chiplets
idea: Apollo's flight software was literally woven into core-rope ROM. Production model weights that won't change for a year are mask-programmed into dense, multi-bit, stackable via-ROM chiplets on a mature node and co-packaged beside the accelerator. HBM then holds only KV cache and activations.
note: Mature-node ROM cost/bit not clearly below DRAM; win is refresh-free, no EUV, weights out of HBM.

title: Alien measures memory in entropy: sell 'effective GB' modules
idea: Aliens count entropy, not bytes. Memory makers sell CXL modules whose controller does inline ANS/LZ compression, cache-line dedup and zero-page elision, plus fabric-wide dedup of identical pages (model weights, OS images, KV-cache prefixes) across 1,000 hosts. They price per effective GB.

title: Deep-space LDPC pages: refresh at the 1% retention quantile
idea: CCSDS deep-space links decode reliably near 1e-2 raw BER. Store each 4 KB page as one LDPC codeword (~15% parity, decoder in the HBM base die or CXL controller) and set refresh where 1% of cells have decayed instead of where the last 1e-9 tail cell does; the median retention distribution is far longer than the tail, so the interval grows from 64 ms to ~1-2 s.
note: Extends Hi-ECC ideas to LDPC at 1% BER; page-granular access and decode latency are costs.

title: Lossy NUMA node standard: OS pages tagged by error tolerance
idea: Push a JEDEC/CXL descriptor that publishes each region's raw-BER-vs-refresh curve, plus a Linux 'lossy NUMA node' reached with mmap(MAP_LOSSY). KV caches, media buffers and caches go to 1%-BER regions refreshed rarely; kernel and databases stay on fully protected memory.

title: Genome-assembler succinct structures with rank/select engines in controller
idea: From genome assemblers that squeeze terabyte de Bruijn graphs into succinct bitvectors: add hardware rank/select and Elias-Fano decode units to the memory controller so pointer-heavy structures (graphs, tries, inverted indexes, B-tree internals) are stored near entropy size yet traversed in one or two memory accesses per hop.

title: Progressive-JPEG bit-plane memory: fetch only needed precision
idea: Satellite and web imagery stream progressive bit planes so receivers stop when good enough. Store tensors bit-plane-sliced across columns (sign/exponent plane first, then mantissa planes); each read requests only the top N planes and only those columns are sensed and sent.

title: Token-synchronous memory: decode sweeps restore every row each token
idea: Align the workload clock with the leakage clock: LLM decode reads all dense weights and active KV each token (~20-50 ms) and every DRAM read restores its row, so the refresh engine is removed from the die; a 1-bit-per-row coverage bitmap faults if any row goes unread for one retention window, and sparse MoE experts live in an NV tier.

title: Low-pressure hydrogen backside cooling replaces helium in etch chucks
idea: At molecular scale, H2 conducts heat better than He (0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K), so the 5-20 Torr backside gas under electrostatic chucks can be on-site electrolytic H2. Safety works at tool scale because the gap under a wafer holds only micrograms of H2, far below any flammable inventory, recirculated through a palladium-getter loop.

title: Datacenter fleets as ore: reverse-fab reclaim of retired DRAM dies
idea: Scale shift from fab to fleet: DIMMs retired after 4-6 years are laser/chemically decapped, dies are retested and rebinned, then re-assembled onto new substrates or CXL expander cards as capacity-tier memory with stronger ECC.

title: Bit-significance stack: MSB planes on clean dies, LSB planes on cheap dies
idea: Shift the unit of placement from the word to the bit-plane along the stack's vertical axis: sign, exponent and high-mantissa planes go to 4 protected dies, low-order planes go to 8 dies running at 1% BER with no ECC, and the base die re-interleaves planes into words on the fly.

title: Row-granular decompressor in the sense-amp stripe, after IBM MXT
idea: Failure mined: IBM's MXT compressed main memory died on decompression latency and a costly controller far from the DRAM. Fix: put a wide, row-granular decompressor (zero-run coding plus 4-bit quantization tables for AI weights, KV caches and activations) right after the secondary sense amps. Its work overlaps the activation's tRCD and rows are stored compressed, so effective capacity multiplies with no added latency.

title: Matrix Semiconductor's write-once 3D ROM as a weights tier
idea: Matrix Semiconductor's 8-deck antifuse crosspoint (2001) failed because nobody wanted write-once storage. LLM inference does: burn model weights into a stack of antifuse decks over the accelerator's periphery, read in tens of ns. The weights no longer occupy DRAM, which then holds only KV cache and activations.
note: Hardwired weights offload DRAM; model churn limits value.

title: Sintering: press read-mostly structures into succinct form, remelt on write
idea: Sintering fuses loose powder into a dense part. A runtime detects read-mostly pointer-based structures (hash maps, tries, B-trees, adjacency lists) and 'sinters' them into succinct static encodings: Elias-Fano, rank/select bitvectors, minimal perfect hashes. Writes go to a small mutable 'green' overlay, and the structure is re-sintered when the overlay grows too large.
note: Generalizes succinct packing with auto-detection and overlay; same core mechanism as I-02147.

title: Vacuum pack with crash foam: compress pages, fill freed space with ECC
idea: Packers shrink-wrap a product and fill the leftover box space with foam. Each 4 KB page in the compressed tier is compressed, and the freed bytes hold a long LDPC/BCH code sized to the space left over. At page scale, 1% raw BER needs about 15-23% parity, so any page that compresses 1.3x or better carries its own armor at no capacity cost. Incompressible pages go to a small protected tier.

title: Factory seconds: sell test-reject DRAM dies as AI-grade memory
idea: Outlet stores sell slightly flawed 'seconds'. DRAM makers take dies that fail JEDEC retention or defect screens but run at about 1% raw BER under relaxed refresh, and bin them into an 'AI-grade' SKU: CXL modules with a page-level LDPC controller, sold for error-tolerant data such as KV, activations and low bit-planes.
note: Relaxed-spec AI-grade SKU could widen process windows; needs maker buy-in.

title: Double-cloth weaving: cross-node erasure code replaces replicas and ECC
idea: Double cloth interlaces two layers so either one can carry the load. In-memory stores that replicate 3x across servers instead protect pages with a product code. A light inner LDPC per node (about 6%) cleans most of each node's 1%-BER flips, and an outer (8+3) erasure code across 11 servers corrects whatever the inner decode misses as well as whole-node loss. Per-DIMM ECC goes away.
note: Adds inner LDPC so 1%-BER modules replace per-DIMM ECC.

title: Fettling attention: grind off flip burrs from KV before softmax
idea: Foundry fettling grinds the burrs off sand castings. The KV cache lives in 1%-BER cells as int4, with per-head scales protected. The attention kernel 'fettles' each key and value it loads by clamping it to calibrated per-channel bounds and capping softmax weights (top-k trimmed), so a flip that creates an outlier logit cannot hijack attention.
note: Ranger-style range clamping applied to KV in 1%-BER cells.

title: Zero-helium wafer cooling with low-pressure hydrogen backside gas
idea: Ideal: etch/deposition chucks that need no helium. Closest achievable: run electrostatic-chuck backside cooling on 5-15 Torr H2 (thermal conductivity 0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K for He) from on-site PEM electrolysis, with flow-limiting orifices and an N2-purged plenum so any leak stays below the flammability limit after exhaust dilution.
note: Low-pressure accommodation coefficient and H2 safety/process interaction.

title: Open capacitorless memory macro qualified at every U.S. logic fab
idea: Ideal: every fab already in the country is a memory fab. Closest: a CHIPS-funded open PDK macro (gain-cell array, sense amps, refresh controller) qualified on Intel 18A, TSMC Arizona, GlobalFoundries and SkyWater flows, so any U.S. chip can carry hundreds of MB on-die and GB-class stacked working memory without a DRAM fab.

title: Compiler swaps pointer structures for succinct ones with rank/select instructions
idea: IFR: indexes sized at the information-theoretic minimum. Closest: a profile-guided compiler pass replaces read-mostly maps, sets and trees with succinct equivalents (Elias-Fano, wavelet trees, compressed tries) backed by new rank/select instructions.

title: Traversal descriptors replace command-address pins entirely
idea: Scarcity: zero command/address pins. The host writes a compact traversal program (base, strides, gather-index pointer, tile shape) into a sequencer in the memory base die once; memory then streams data in consumption order with only a 1-bit flow-control backchannel.
note: Memory-side stream sequencer; poor fit for irregular access.

title: H-free sputtered-Si laser grains as in-stack CMOS and floating-body tiers
idea: Sputter amorphous Si at ~100 C (no PECVD hydrogen) over ~0.5-1 um of SiO2 that carries a lattice of small grain-filter holes, then melt it with an excimer-laser pulse: the mu-Czochralski process grows one location-controlled single-crystal grain (3-7.5 um) from each hole, with electron/hole mobilities of 460-510 / 121-250 cm2/Vs reported by the Delft group. The ~100 ns pulse heats only the top ~0.3 um, so oxide tiers below stay cool. Use the grains for (a) complementary sense amps and decoders inside the stack, without Smart Cut's hydrogen implant (B3-09's main risk), and (b) floating-body capacitor-less 1T cells, which need holes and therefore cannot be made in n-type IGZO, for Ge-free 3D silicon DRAM tiers.

title: ECC-paid capacitor: let the code, not the capacitor, carry the last 4 sigma
idea: Today's ~50 mV sense budget exists so that every one of ~1.7e10 cells reads correctly at ~7 sigma of sense-amp (SA) offset and coupling noise, with only on-die SEC as backup. Re-centre the array on a raw BER target of 1e-4 per read. A t=8 BCH code (80 check bits per 512 data bits) in the memory controller or HBM/CXL logic base die absorbs the errors; optionally the SA fires two extra comparator thresholds to hand one soft-information bit per cell to a NAND-style soft decoder. With dV_min of 26 mV instead of 50 mV, the ZrO2/TiN pillar storage node can hold ~2.7 fF instead of 5.4 fF on the same 512-cell bitline: ~640 nm tall instead of 1,300 nm. An SA's offset is static, so codewords run along the row (each bit through a different SA), and outlier SAs are fused out at test like today's column repair. The same rule gives a 0.6 fF cell on a 64-cell local bitline in a 3D tier.

title: Compression-funded ECC: compressible rows earn slow refresh for free
idea: On write, the controller compresses each line: exponent Huffman for float tensors, base-delta-immediate or zero-run for integers and pointers. If the result is <=54 B, it appends 70 parity bits (t=7 BCH over GF(2^10)) in the same 64 B slot and sets a mode bit in the existing ECC/metadata side-band. A per-row counter tracks whether every line in the row is in 'strong' mode; strong rows move to a slow refresh bin (RAIDR-style Bloom filter) and weak rows stay at 64 ms. A line that becomes incompressible demotes its row immediately, the safe direction. Reads run the full decode only when the cheap syndrome is nonzero.

title: Top-k KV from in-memory scoring of MSB-plane sketches
idea: Keys are quantised per channel to INT8 (KIVI-style) and stored as bit planes. The 4 MSB planes live in a PIM-capable tier (HBM-PIM or LPDDR5X-PIM). The low planes and V live in a cheaper capacity tier (LPDDR or CXL DRAM). Each decode step broadcasts the query to bank-level units, which compute approximate q.k scores from the MSB planes with bit-serial adds at the sense-amp stripe or the existing PIM MAC units, and return only scores (2 B per token per KV head). The GPU picks the top-k tokens (k ~ 1-4k) and fetches their full K and V. Nothing is stored twice: the sketch is the high planes of the real data.

title: Thermal arbitrage: keep the bits away from the GPU's heat
idea: HBM sits millimetres from a ~1 kW GPU at 85-95 C (32 ms refresh above 85 C), and server DIMMs run 50-85 C. In a disaggregated design, capacity DRAM (KV pools, cold weights, CXL expanders) moves onto separately liquid-cooled sleds at 30-40 C, linked by optics (B4-14) or CXL. Refresh is set from on-die temperature and canary readings (B4-02), not the 85 C worst case. The cool margin can be spent three ways: (a) 4-30x longer refresh intervals; (b) multi-level rows (B4-05), whose droop budget is a third of single-level; (c) next-generation dies designed to a 'cool spec' with ~30% shorter capacitors.

title: Swap fp16 attention keys for product-quantized codes scored by lookup
idea: Substitute arithmetic on dequantized keys with table lookups. Each cached key becomes 8-16 one-byte product-quantization codes; at decode the query builds a small sub-vector dot-product table, and scores are summed from lookups over the codes, while values use 2-4-bit group quantization. This runs on existing GPUs and unchanged HBM.
note: PQCache-like prior art.

title: Swap full fine-tuned model copies for 1-bit deltas over one base
idea: Substitute per-customer full checkpoints with sign-bit delta matrices plus one scale per row, applied by a fused GEMM kernel over a single resident base model. Full-rank fine-tunes are covered, not just LoRAs, on existing GPUs.

title: Vector-database index fused with the attention KV cache
idea: Combine an approximate-nearest-neighbor index (IVF/HNSW over key vectors) with the KV cache: only centroids and the graph stay in DRAM, full K/V live in flash or a CXL tier, and each decode step retrieves just the top-k tokens with the highest query-key scores.
note: RetrievalAttention, PQCache, MagicPIG already pursue ANN over KV.

title: Drum-era optimum placement lays out weights for flash streaming
idea: Combine 1950s drum 'optimum programming' (placing data where the head will be when needed) with LLM inference from NVMe: the compiler stripes each layer's weights across all NAND channels, dies and planes in exact consumption order and double-buffers into DRAM overlays of a fixed budget so flash reads fully overlap compute.

title: Minify rank width: one-chip sub-rank access controller
idea: Build an FPGA DIMM controller that addresses each x4 DDR5 chip independently through per-chip command buffering, so a random access activates one chip's row instead of 8-16 chips' rows.

title: Eliminate low-order bits until needed: MSB-first bit-plane fetch
idea: Store tensors bit-plane transposed across sub-rows so the controller fetches the top 2-4 bit planes first; attention screening or early-exit logic requests the lower planes only for the ~5-10% of values that matter.

title: Bootstrapped T-switch gain cell zeroes leakage across its write path
idea: TRIZ #12 Equipotentiality + #25 Self-service: write the gain-cell storage node through two series transistors and drive their middle node from the cell's own source-follower output, the guard trick from electrometers and sample-and-hold circuits. The inner transistor then sees ~0 V drain-source, so subthreshold leakage collapses.
note: Known guard/T-switch trick; demoable on MPW, area penalty limits value to eDRAM.

title: Spherical-coordinate quantization of keys and embeddings
idea: TRIZ #14 Spheroidality: convert key and embedding vectors from Cartesian to recursive polar form (one norm plus d-1 angles); after a random rotation the angles are tightly concentrated, so they quantize to 2-3 bits with no per-block scale or zero-point metadata.

title: Frequency-domain storage of activation tensors
idea: TRIZ #17 Another dimension: store saved activations and feature maps after a blockwise DCT/Hadamard transform with truncated high-frequency coefficients, since smooth tensors concentrate energy in few coefficients; the inverse transform is fused into the consuming kernel.
note: DCT/JPEG-style activation compression for training is published art.

title: Typing-indicator-timed KV swap synchronized to user think time
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action: chat traffic has a rhythm of generation followed by 10-120 s of reading and typing; page each session's KV to flash the moment generation ends and start prefetching it back when the client reports the first keystroke, hiding the swap inside human latency.

title: Foveated KV cache: precision decays with attention distance
idea: Like VR foveated rendering, keep full precision only where attention 'gazes' (recent tokens and tokens with high cumulative attention mass) and step other tokens down 16->8->4->2 bits as their attention mass fades, using a background demotion engine that re-encodes in place.

title: Torpor mode: idle containers hibernate to NV, keeping heartbeat pages
idea: Like animals in torpor keeping only vital functions, idle containers and serverless functions are snapshotted to CXL-attached persistent flash in milliseconds, leaving only profiled heartbeat pages (timers, socket state) in DRAM, with userfaultfd lazy restore on wake.

title: Ice-storage KV: precompute corpus attention caches off-peak into NV
idea: Like buildings that freeze ice at night to cool by day, compute KV caches for frequently retrieved RAG documents and system prompts off-peak and store them in persistent flash; at query time they are streamed in and position-corrected rather than prefilled and held in DRAM.
note: Precomputed position-corrected document KV (TurboRAG, CacheBlend); same core as I-00780.

title: Overlay-tree linker streams MoE experts into fixed HBM slots
idea: Revive 1960s overlay trees (IBM 7090/1401 linkers): the model compiler builds a static overlay tree with a resident root (attention, router, shared experts) and N fixed overlay slots, and experts load from LPDDR/NVMe into those slots one layer ahead using a cheap speculative router run on layer L's hidden state. Overlay loads are fixed DMA scripts generated at compile time, not demand paging.
note: Speculative expert prefetch already published (Pre-gated MoE, MoE-Infinity).

title: Router-predicted MoE expert paging from existing SSDs
idea: Inverts 'all experts must be resident': only hot experts stay in DRAM. A small predictor reads router logits from earlier layers and prefetches the likely next-layer experts from NVMe RAID on existing servers, hiding flash latency behind the current layer's compute.

title: Lookahead router streams mixture-of-experts weights from flash
idea: Only ~3-6% of MoE experts fire per token, and later layers' routing can be predicted from the current hidden state. A tiny lookahead router predicts layer l+2 experts and triggers flash fetches two layers early, so only the active expert slice lives in DRAM and the rest sits on NAND.
note: Close to existing expert-prefetch and LLM-in-flash work.

title: Layer-major execution turns all memory traffic into hard-drive streams
idea: Weight bytes per token equal W/B for batch B, and random access disappears if you run one layer over an entire corpus before the next. For offline workloads (embedding, synthetic data, evaluation), stream weights and the corpus's activations layer by layer from striped HDD/NAND arrays, with DRAM only as small staging.

title: Bus timetable: compiled exact page-in schedule for model inference
idea: Inference access order is as fixed as a bus timetable: the compiler emits a cycle-accurate schedule of which weight/KV pages must arrive when, and a DMA engine streams them from flash or CXL into a DRAM ring sized for ~2 layers plus slack, with no demand paging at all.
note: FlexGen/LLM-in-a-flash prior art; works for batch inference.

title: Gang-swapped tenants: time-share whole memory images like CPU cores
idea: Po: only one program exists at a time. Low-duty-cycle VMs, notebooks and agents are gang-scheduled: each entire memory image is snapshotted to CXL-flash and restored in tens of milliseconds at 50+ GB/s when its slot comes, so host DRAM is sized for the active set, not all tenants.

title: Superconducting flux-trap cell taped out on an existing shuttle
idea: Worsen: assume new memory needs a new fab and billions. Flip: store bits as single flux quanta in kinetic-inductance NbN loops, taped out on an existing superconducting-electronics foundry shuttle (~$50-100k per run) and tested in a ~$250k cryocooler, targeting a 1e5-cell array for cryogenic AI datacentres.
note: Shuttle plus cryocooler demo fits $1M.

title: ER triage nurse: three-tier KV precision with a sink summary token
idea: Triage sorts patients by urgency. Every 256 tokens, accumulated attention mass ranks the cached tokens. Critical tokens stay FP8, stable ones are requantized to 2-bit, and the rest are evicted after their values are folded into a running weighted 'sink' token per head, so their aggregate influence survives.

title: Grandmother's leftovers: reuse cached document KV across different prompts
idea: Grandma turns yesterday's roast into today's soup. RAG documents are pre-encoded once into KV chunks stored on NVMe by content hash. At request time the retrieved chunks are spliced into the prompt's KV in any order, and only the ~10-15% of tokens at chunk boundaries or with high deviation are recomputed to repair cross-chunk attention. Software only, two engineers.

title: Construction foreman's just-in-time delivery: router-lookahead MoE expert paging
idea: Foremen have steel delivered the day it is bolted up. A small predictor reads layer L's hidden state and forecasts which experts layers L+1 to L+3 will route to. Those experts are DMA'd from host RAM or NVMe via GPUDirect Storage just in time, and HBM keeps only a hot-expert cache. Software-only, open-source.

title: Console streaming discipline: DRAM as a compiled ring window
idea: From game consoles that stream open worlds from SSD through fixed RAM: an ahead-of-time compiler profiles a workload's deterministic access order (inference layers, ETL stages, simulation sweeps) and emits a streaming schedule so DRAM is only a ring buffer refilled from parallel NVMe at exactly the needed rate.

title: Seed-regenerated tensors replace stored bits with recomputation
idea: Time-shift storage into computation: store a 32-bit PRNG seed plus a few coefficients per weight block, and regenerate weights on the fly in a near-memory generator at read time, so the bit lives as an algorithm.
note: Close to SeedLM-style PRNG weight compression; accuracy loss limits ratio.

title: Tensor-lifetime-matched gain cells on 28 nm logic never refresh
idea: Time-scale matching: AI activations and KV-cache shards live microseconds to tens of milliseconds. A 2T/3T gain-cell eDRAM built on existing 28-40 nm logic lines, with ~100 us-10 ms retention, holds only short-lived data. The scheduler guarantees each read before expiry and lets dead data decay.
note: Refresh-free eDRAM for DNN buffers in literature; easy MPW demo.

title: IBM MXT memory compression revived for KV caches with block-float codecs
idea: IBM's Memory eXpansion Technology (2000) compressed main memory ~2x but died on latency and poorly compressible general data. Put a fixed-ratio 2:1 codec for KV-cache and activation pages (shared-exponent block-float plus entropy coding) in the HBM base die or CXL controller, with fixed page frames so there is no fragmentation and decode is a few-ns pipeline.
note: Fixed-ratio block-float KV compression in controller; FPGA-demoable; overlaps active KV-quantization work.

title: Optane Memory Mode fixed: set-associative DRAM cache with on-controller tags
idea: Optane's Memory Mode used a direct-mapped DRAM near-memory cache, and its conflict misses made performance unpredictable, which killed adoption. Put a 16-way set-associative tag array (SRAM, ~1/512 of capacity) and a way predictor in the CXL memory controller, so a DRAM slice of 1/8 capacity fronts a cheap dense tier (NAND-backed, LPDDR or retired DDR4) with predictable miss rates under 5%.

title: Wire drawing: KV precision drawn down through successive dies with age
idea: Wire is pulled through a series of ever-smaller dies. Each KV token likewise passes through 'dies' as it ages and as its cumulative attention mass falls: FP16 to INT8 to INT4 to INT2, re-quantized in place by a background kernel. Each die's threshold is tuned so the perplexity loss stays below 0.1.
note: Importance/age mixed-precision KV widely pursued (KIVI, ZipCache).

title: Freeze-drying: lyophilize idle tenants, rehydrate in milliseconds
idea: Freeze-drying removes water but keeps structure. An idle container, VM or LLM session is 'freeze-dried' by dropping all regenerable state (page cache, JIT code, allocator slack, KV that can be recomputed from tokens) and compressing the dry residue into a flash tier. An access-order trace is recorded so that rehydration prefetches data in the exact order the process will need it.
note: REAP-style recorded-prefetch snapshots exist; applying broadly to idle tenants and KV.

title: Quench-and-temper training: harden models against the exact flip channel
idea: Steel is hardened by quenching, then tempered to remove brittleness. Models are fine-tuned with 1% bit flips injected into the exact stored bit format (the quantized codes, not the protected scales) using straight-through estimators, then 'tempered' with a short pass on clean data. The hardened model is deployed at 3 bits per weight on 1%-BER memory.

title: Retrofit latent KV into existing models via SVD and brief finetune
idea: IFR: each token's KV is a few dozen numbers. Closest without new silicon: factor each layer's K/V projections by SVD into a shared low-rank latent (MLA-style), cache only the latent, absorb the up-projection into the query and output matrices, then heal with a short distillation finetune.

title: Gist tokens compress long system prompts into cached soft vectors
idea: IFR: shared instructions cost nothing per user. Closest with no materials: a trained compressor distills each long system prompt or document into 16-64 learned gist tokens, so every session caches the gist KV instead of thousands of prompt tokens.

title: Ten people, one kernel module: retire weak pages, run 4x tREFI
idea: 10-person constraint: ship software plus a BIOS setting. A kernel module runs a retention test at 4x the refresh interval and retires the ~0.01-0.1% of 4 KB pages that fail (BadRAM-style memmap exclusion). It stores the compressed failing-page list in the DIMM's user-writable SPD bytes so the list travels with the module, then sets tREFI 4x longer.
note: BadRAM plus longer tREFI; VRT and data-pattern dependence need guardband.

title: Attention computed directly on product-quantized keys
idea: Imposed limit: keys may never be decompressed. Keys are stored as 8-byte product-quantization codes; each query precomputes a small SRAM table of sub-vector dot products and scores every key with table lookups and adds, the way ANN search engines do, and fetches full values only for the top-scoring tokens.

title: Layer-clocked just-in-time weight streaming caps HBM at 4 GB
idea: Scarcity: each accelerator gets only 4 GB of local DRAM. Since transformer layer order is deterministic, the compiler emits an exact transfer schedule so layer L+2's weights and KV blocks land from pooled far memory into a double-buffered ring exactly as layer L finishes.

title: Defect-map matchmaking pairs wafers so tall W2W stacks still yield
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. Keep a pool of thousands of probed DRAM wafers and run an assignment solver that stacks wafers whose bad die sites coincide (bad-on-bad), so defects concentrate in a few stack columns instead of poisoning many.

title: Proof-of-work logic: speculative-decoding drafts run from junk DRAM
idea: Crypto miners shrug off memory errors because every result is cheaply verified. Host LLM speculative-decoding draft models and their caches on retention-reject or relaxed-refresh DIMMs: the full model's verification pass rejects any token a memory error corrupted, so the only cost is a slightly lower acceptance rate.
note: Clever verification-masks-errors insight, but the draft-model memory market is small.

title: Minify tier thickness to 6 nm for 1000-tier atomic stacks
idea: Grow alternating MOCVD 2D-semiconductor channel sheets (MoS2 or WSe2, about 1 nm) and hBN/oxide spacers (about 5 nm) so each tier is 6 nm and 1000 tiers fit in a 6 um stack. Gain-cell storage nodes are gated by shared vertical gate holes etched once per 100-tier deck, as in 3D NAND.
note: 1000 tiers at 6 nm pitch would be far past 10x density; doubt: sequential 2D growth/transfer yield.

title: Composite: silicon sense chiplets mass-transferred onto glass DRAM panels
idea: TRIZ #40 Composite: large glass panels carry stacked oxide-TFT DRAM tiers, while all precision sensing lives in 50x50 um silicon sense chiplets placed every few millimetres by micro-LED-style mass transfer (millions per hour) and wired by panel redistribution layers; glass does storage, silicon does amplification.
note: Multi-tier oxide-TFT DRAM on cheap glass with silicon sense chiplets could hit >10x cost/bit; panel lithography, overlay, us latency doubtful.

title: Vertical charge-coupled memory: no switch per bit, just moving charge
idea: Inverts 'every bit needs its own access transistor': deposit a 200-layer gate/oxide stack (NAND-style, one hole etch), line each hole with a poly-Si or oxide channel, and clock the layer gates in 3 phases so charge packets march along the hole like a vertical CCD. Each hole holds ~60 bits and one sense/regeneration stage at the top restores packets as they circulate, so refresh is continuous and free.
note: CCD clocking in a NAND-style stack removes per-bit transistors and capacitors; poly-channel transfer efficiency and serial latency are the doubts.

title: 3D-NAND toolset builds channel-hole gain cells with no EUV
idea: Ideal: density from tier count with tools already paid for. Closest: in a NAND-style oxide/word-plate stack, each channel hole holds two concentric ALD oxide-semiconductor devices per tier: an outer write channel charging an isolated metal ring, and an inner read channel gated by that ring, so every tier crossing is a capacitorless 2T gain cell built with the 3D NAND etch, ALD and staircase flow.
note: Concentric write/read oxide devices per channel hole gives NAND-like layer economics; doubt: IGZO speed, ring isolation, retention at tier pitch.

title: Band-offset quantum-well bits stacked along a superlattice pillar
idea: Worse: store each bit on a bulky capacitor needing femtofarads. Flip: etch vertical pillars through a Si/Ge-rich superlattice, wrap each Ge-rich well with a tier gate, and store holes in its valence-band well (up to ~0.5 eV offset) as the bit, sensed as a threshold shift of the shared vertical Si channel, which is capacitorless and has no oxide tunneling, so endurance stays unlimited.
note: Capacitorless bit per tier gives ~50x density; doubt: 0.5 eV offset means ~us retention at 85C, not ms.

title: Capacitor-hole racetrack: electroplated domain-wall nanowires in DRAM's high-aspect-ratio mold
idea: Etch the standard honeycomb hole lattice (~20 nm diameter at 35-40 nm pitch) in oxide. Instead of conformal ALD electrodes, electroplate a magnetic nanowire up from a seed at the hole bottom, modulating composition (Co-rich/Ni-rich, or thin Cu spacers) every ~60 nm to make pinning notches. Bits are axial domains separated by Bloch-point domain walls, which cylindrical wires carry without the Walker breakdown that slows flat racetracks. A vertical select transistor under each hole (4F2/6F2 vertical-channel style) drives ~30 uA bipolar shift pulses through the wire. A 20 nm MTJ on the planarised top reads the top bit and writes it (STT, or SOT from a top heavy-metal line). Half of each track is shift buffer, giving 10 data bits per 1.3 um hole and 25 per 3 um hole.
note: 10-25 bits per capacitor hole; doubts: notch electroplating in 20 nm AR-65 holes, shift reliability and heating at ~1e7 A/cm2.

title: Wafer-scale DRAM bonded under a wafer-scale accelerator replaces HBM
idea: Substitute HBM stacks plus interposer with one full DRAM wafer hybrid-bonded face-to-face to a wafer-scale processor: each compute tile gets the DRAM directly beneath it through ~2 um-pitch bonds, and defective DRAM tiles are routed around by the processor's existing redundancy fabric.
note: ~10x lower pJ/bit and TB-class capacity under compute; doubts: accelerator heat on DRAM retention, matching redundancy.

title: Stacked camera-sensor pixel bonding: per-subarray copper ports to logic
idea: Adapted from the pixel-level Cu-Cu hybrid bonding of stacked smartphone image sensors: the DRAM array wafer bonds face-to-face to a logic wafer so each subarray (mat) has its own ~100-wire vertical port. Global I/O routing and shared periphery go away.
note: Per-mat vertical ports remove global I/O; real physics, but needs a DRAM-logic wafer bonding partner.

title: Genotype embeddings regenerated in the memory controller
idea: Recommender embedding tables are TB-scale. Each ID is stored instead as an 8-16 byte genotype code, and a tiny shared decoder MLP in the CXL memory controller expands it into the full 128-512-dim phenotype vector in ~50 ns on read. The full table never exists in DRAM. This is a molecule-to-organism scale jump: store the recipe, not the body.
note: Same generated-embedding mechanism, placed in CXL controller.

title: Eliminate recommender embedding tables with hash-driven embedding generators
idea: Replace TB-scale ID-to-vector tables with deep hash embedding: each ID is hashed by k functions into a dense code, and a small MLP generates its embedding on the fly.
note: Deep Hash Embedding (2021) exists; compute cost and quality loss have limited recsys adoption.

title: Biologist's genome thinking: grow embeddings from hashed IDs, not tables
idea: A genome stores the recipe, not the organism. Recommendation and retrieval embedding tables, often terabytes, are replaced by a generator: several universal hashes of an ID feed a small dense MLP that expresses the embedding on demand. An exact side table remains only for the hottest ~0.1% of IDs.
note: Same as deep hash embedding; hot-ID side table is a minor twist.

title: Image-sensor pinned-photodiode storage node with a transfer gate
idea: Adapted from the CMOS image sensor's pinned photodiode: store the bit as electrons in a fully depleted buried n-well capped by a p+ pinning layer, isolated from every Si/SiO2 interface, and move it to a floating diffusion through a transfer gate. A source follower reads it like a 4T pixel, so ~1-3k electrons suffice instead of ~30k.
note: Pinned wells cut dark current hugely, but 3-4T pixel-like cells are far larger than 6F2; demoable on CIS MPW.

title: Antiferroelectric latent-charge buffer holds stored-1 voltage on a plateau
idea: Reverse the capacitor dielectric's role from passive to defending its charge: use ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric HZO and bias the plate so a stored '1' sits just above the AFE back-switching voltage. As leakage drains the node, AFE domains switch back and release bound polarization charge (~10-20 uC/cm2), pinning the voltage on a plateau the way latent heat holds ice water at 0 C.
note: AFE back-switching plateau multiplies effective hold capacitance; AFE endurance far below 1e15 and nm-scale domain granularity are doubts.

title: Copying: passive optical splitters broadcast one weight read to many chips
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying: in data-parallel inference every accelerator holds an identical copy of the weights. Instead, one memory node reads each weight block once and broadcasts it in lockstep to all accelerators through cheap passive 1:16 PON fiber splitters (mass-produced telecom parts). (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)
note: PON-class optics far below HBM bandwidth; only works for lockstep streaming.

title: Image-sensor pinned photodiode recast as buried, interface-free DRAM storage well
idea: Borrow the CMOS image sensor's pinned photodiode: store the bit as electrons in a fully depleted buried n-well under a p+ pinning layer, read out through a transfer gate onto a floating diffusion exactly like a 4T pixel. The stored charge never touches a Si/SiO2 interface, so interface-trap SRH generation (the source of most of the <=13 fA tail) is shut off; a deep-trench vertical pinned well, as in stacked global-shutter pixels, supplies ~8-15k electrons.

title: Leakage decay as built-in recency weighting for analog KV caches
idea: Invert 'charge decay is a failure that refresh must undo' -> make decay part of the math. KV-cache and state-space values are stored as un-refreshed analog charge whose leakage time constant is programmed per bank by body bias, so stored magnitude decays exponentially with token age, implementing the recency weighting (decay gates, ALiBi-like bias) models already learn.

title: Logic-die decoupling capacitors double as on-demand scratch memory
idea: Invert 'storage elements must be dedicated memory cells' -> reuse the capacitors already on every logic die. An accelerator's deep-trench/MIM decap is split into ~50 fF segments with access switches, so idle decap banks act as eDRAM-like scratch when the supply-noise budget allows and revert to decoupling during load surges.

title: Pinned storage well: the image-sensor trick buries the bit
idea: Inverts 'the bit must sit on a metal-contacted capacitor': store electrons in a buried n-well under a p+ surface pinning layer (the pinned-photodiode structure from CMOS image sensors, built as a deep vertical well), moved in and out by a transfer gate to a floating-diffusion sense node; the pinning layer keeps interface traps filled with holes so they cannot generate leakage.

title: Circulating drum memory: streaming access refreshes ultra-leaky cheap cells
idea: Capacitor size and leakage specs exist only to hold charge for 64 ms; if every row is read-and-restored every 100 us because data circulates through compute like a drum, retention can be 640x worse. That permits planar MIM capacitors on short bitlines and leaky access devices in fully depreciated 28-40 nm fabs, with no high-AR etch and no EUV, behind a controller that streams rows in fixed order.
note: Sequential circulation replaces retention; mature-node planar cells limit density, so 10-100x cost claim is doubtful.

title: Smoke detector: radioisotope micro-battery keeps low-leakage cells alive for decades
idea: Random stimulus 'smoke detector' (a tiny Am-241 source runs for decades) -> a Ni-63 or tritium betavoltaic cell in the module package supplies microwatts forever, refreshing an ultra-low-leakage gain-cell array whose retention is ~1000 s. Data survives loss of external power for ~decades with no new memory material.
note: Package isotope keeps a 1000 s gain-cell array alive; doubts are periphery standby leakage and isotope regulation.

title: Image-sensor 4T pixel gain cell reads 1,000-electron packets
idea: Box: buried-channel storage well (~1-2k e-) x transfer gate + floating-diffusion source follower borrowed from 4T image pixels x correlated-double-sampling column sensing x planar CMOS x Si x CIS fab flow. Full charge transfer onto a tiny floating diffusion gives ~100 uV/e- gain, so a small well replaces the 5 fF capacitor and is written back after read.
note: CIS pinned wells give ~e-/s dark current; doubt is density (~1 um pixels) and transfer speed; CIS MPW demo feasible.

title: 77-kelvin DRAM: crude poly-Si transistors hold charge for hours
idea: Box: MIM charge x solid-phase-crystallized poly-Si TFT (leaky at 300 K) x voltage sense amp x 2D x glass or Si x PECVD a-Si plus furnace crystallization. At 77 K off-current falls by >1e6, so grain-boundary-limited TFTs from a low-mask university flow meet retention for liquid-nitrogen-cooled racks.
note: Grain-boundary trap-assisted leakage may not fall 1e6 at 77 K; easy university test.

title: Astronomy CCD correlated double sampling enables 20 mV memory links
idea: Astronomical CCDs read single electrons by correlated double sampling, subtracting a reset sample from the signal sample. Put clocked CDS receivers on interposer/TSV links so offsets and low-frequency noise cancel, allowing 20-30 mV swings driven from a dedicated switched-capacitor 0.1 V rail.
note: CDS cancels offsets enabling ~30 mV swings; clocking overhead and settling at speed are the doubt.

title: Client-parked compressed KV state between conversation turns
idea: After each turn, the server sends the user's device or the nearest edge PoP a compressed, encrypted latent state of ~0.5-2 MB (MLA-style low-rank KV or a distilled gist-token set). The next request uploads it back. The datacenter then holds no per-session state across gaps of minutes to days.
note: Offloading session state to clients is fresh; long-context KV exceeds 2 MB unless lossy gist compression holds quality.

title: Thermophoretic wafer shielding allows ISO-7 cleanrooms for DRAM fabs
idea: Effect: thermophoresis. Every exposed wafer is held 10-20 K warmer than the gas around it inside sealed carriers and tool mini-environments; the thermophoretic force pushes sub-100 nm particles away from the warm surface, cutting deposition velocity by more than 100x, so the ballroom can be ISO 7 instead of ISO 3-4.

title: Oxygen: porous-silicon oxidation carves many SOI tiers from one epi stack
idea: Grow an epi stack alternating p+ (~1e19) and lightly doped Si, open slits, anodize in HF so only the p+ layers become mesoporous, then oxidize them at ~850 C into buried oxide (FIPOS); the lightly doped layers remain single-crystal device tiers.
note: Porous-Si oxidation (FIPOS) carves many crystalline tiers without SiGe strain limits; boron diffusion and expansion stress are risks.

title: Potassium hydroxide on (110) silicon etches crystal-perfect vertical cell walls
idea: Align lines along <112> on (110) Si and etch in KOH so the slow {111} planes form atomically smooth vertical walls 20-40 nm thick at >100:1 aspect ratio; a deposited oxide/TiN wordline stack crossing the walls turns each wall into a vertical string of DRAM cells.
note: Ultra-high-AR {111} KOH walls are proven in MEMS; novel as DRAM channel sheets, but capacitor placement is unaddressed.

title: Float-glass style liquid-gallium printing of atomically thin Ga2O3 channels
idea: As float glass forms on molten tin, kiss the wafer against a liquid Ga/In alloy. Its self-limiting 1.5-3 nm oxide skin transfers at room temperature as a crystalline wide-gap 2D channel for BEOL access transistors.
note: Room-temperature transfer of Ga2O3 skin from liquid metal as BEOL channel; wafer-scale uniformity and contacts are open.

title: Scrap remelt: near-capacity code, refetch master copy on decode failure
idea: Foundries simply remelt bad castings. Clean data that can be fetched again (page cache, model weights, container images) sits in 1%-BER cells under a near-capacity 4 KB LDPC code with only about 10-12% overhead and a deliberately high failure rate of about 1e-6 per page read. When decoding fails, the page is refetched from SSD or a remote master, which is cheap because it is rare.
note: Accepting rare decode failure for clean data is a nice insight; 4 KB LDPC hurts random-access latency.

title: Taffy-pulled wire-in-glass preform sliced into through-glass-via wafers
idea: Stack copper-cored glass capillaries into a preform, draw it down 500x on a fiber tower, re-bundle and redraw (as multicore fiber is made), then slice the rod like salami into 100 um glass discs. Each disc holds millions of 2 um-pitch through-glass vias formed in one draw.
note: Taylor-wire drawing of Cu-in-glass is real; via registration to pads and Cu/glass CTE are the doubts.

title: Negative-capacitance bitline: electrophysiology's capacitance neutralisation applied to the DRAM sense path
idea: A small amplifier per bitline (or a pre-phase folded into the existing sense amplifier) senses the bitline and drives a feedback capacitor Cf with gain A > 1. That injects a current equal to -Cn*dV/dt, with Cn = (A-1)*Cf. For the 1-2 ns of charge sharing, the bitline's effective capacitance becomes Cbl - Cn; then the neutraliser switches off and the normal latch fires. At Cn/Cbl ~0.7 the cell can shrink 3.3x for the same signal. Amplifier offset is auto-zeroed during precharge.

title: Swap long agent context for sleep-phase consolidation into LoRA weights
idea: Substitute context with weights, the way the hippocampus hands memories to the cortex. A long-running agent periodically 'sleeps', distills its accumulated KV context into a small LoRA delta by test-time training, and then drops the KV.

title: Idle GPU video encoders compress the LLM KV cache
idea: Combine the motion-compensated inter-frame prediction of on-die AV1/HEVC encoders with attention KV tensors: treat each head's K/V across successive token blocks as video frames, encode residuals in the otherwise idle media engine, and decode blocks back into HBM just before attention reads them.

title: Speech-codec linear prediction stores KV cache as residuals
idea: Borrowed from LPC/CELP voice codecs: a tiny per-head linear predictor estimates layer L's keys/values from layer L-1 and the previous token, and only the 1-2 bit quantized prediction residual is stored; predictor coefficients are an offline-fitted codebook. The attention kernel recomputes prediction plus residual on read.
note: Cross-layer KV correlation may be weaker than speech formants.

title: JPEG for KV: DCT along the sequence axis, keep low frequencies
idea: Borrowed from JPEG: blocks of 64 consecutive tokens' keys/values per head are DCT-transformed along the token axis and only significant coefficients are stored with zig-zag run-length coding; attention for old blocks is computed directly in the frequency domain.

title: Holography: superpose thousands of associations in one SRAM hypervector
idea: Borrowed from holograms, where many images share one plate: older KV pairs are bound (permute-multiply or circular convolution) and summed into a fixed set of high-dimensional superposition vectors in SRAM, and attention queries unbind from them, with a small cleanup memory for exact recall of key items.

title: Output-entropy-gated KV precision on existing hardware
idea: TRIZ #23 Feedback: the serving loop watches each request's next-token entropy; while the model is confident, new KV is stored at INT2-INT3, and when entropy spikes it switches to INT8 and re-quantizes recent blocks, a closed loop that spends bits only where uncertainty demands. It runs as software on hardware already deployed.
note: Output entropy is a weak proxy for future attention; dropped bits cannot be restored.

title: Hippocampal sleep replay distills old KV cache into memory tokens
idea: During idle accelerator slots (the analog of slow-wave sleep), a small consolidation network replays each long session's KV cache and distills spans of 64-256 tokens into 4-8 learned 'memory tokens' that reproduce their attention contribution; the originals are freed. Recent tokens stay verbatim (hippocampus) while old context lives as consolidated gist (neocortex).

title: Texture-compression units repurposed to hold activations compressed
idea: Inverts 'GPU texture hardware is only for graphics': activations, KV blocks or embeddings are encoded into fixed-rate block-compressed texture formats (BC/ASTC-style) and read through the GPU's existing texture samplers, which decode them in hardware at full speed.
note: Reuses installed decoders; BC/ASTC artifacts on non-image tensors may hurt accuracy.

title: Near-duplicate KV blocks share a base plus 4-bit residual
idea: Box: approximate dedup × GPU KV pool × 16-token block × LSH on key vectors × shared base + sparse quantized residual. Blocks from different requests (edited system prompts, popular RAG documents, boilerplate code) whose keys fall within a tolerance are stored once with tiny per-request residuals.

title: Token-ID memory: keep the words, regenerate the KV on demand
idea: Po: the program remembers nothing. Long-context sessions keep only token IDs (2 B/token) plus full K/V for a few anchor layers; when attention needs the others, their K/V are recomputed from the anchors in one batched pass on otherwise-idle compute.
note: Must store hidden states, not K/V, at anchor layers (as HCache does).

title: Sleep consolidation: agents distill yesterday's context into small adapters
idea: Po: yesterday's conversation becomes today's neurons. Long-lived agents compress their accumulated context nightly into a low-rank adapter (tens of MB) by self-distillation on U.S.-fabbed accelerators, discarding the GB-scale KV cache and keeping only a short summary window.

title: Navigator's dead reckoning: cross-layer KV stored as deltas from fixes
idea: A navigator takes a full position fix occasionally and dead-reckons between fixes. Full KV is stored only for every 4th layer (the fix). The intermediate layers' KV is stored as low-rank deltas against the nearest fix and reconstructed inside the attention kernel.

title: Demoscene procedural memory: store generators, regenerate tensors in base die
idea: Demoscene 4 KB intros generate whole worlds from tiny programs. Store weights and KV as compact generators (PRNG seeds, low-rank factors, codebook indices) and expand them in a small base-die engine on read, so the array and interface move only the recipe.
note: Seed/low-rank compression known (SeedLM); gain bounded by accuracy loss.

title: Iridium's rainbow: spectral KV keeps only low-frequency sequence components
idea: Iridium is named for the rainbow; along the sequence axis, each head's K and V for closed 256-token blocks are DCT-transformed and only the 32-64 highest-energy coefficients are kept, with attention over old blocks run on the inverse transform or directly in the frequency domain.

title: Mitosis embeddings: tail IDs share rows until gradients disagree
idea: Imposed limit: embedding tables get 1% of their nominal size. New and rare IDs start out sharing one row with their cluster; the trainer tracks how much each ID's gradients disagree with its cluster mates and splits off a private row only when that ID keeps pulling away.

title: Aviation dissimilar redundancy: cross-vendor ECC words
idea: Adapted from fly-by-wire systems that use dissimilar processors from different vendors so one design flaw cannot fail every channel: each ECC codeword in a module or CXL pool is assembled from dies of at least three different vendors or process lots, so a vendor-specific weakness (a hammer-sensitive layout, a lot-wide retention excursion) can hit only one symbol.
note: Dissimilar-lot codeword assembly decorrelates failures; proof needs fleet failure data.

title: Swap discarded bad-row DIMMs for map-carrying discount DIMMs
idea: Substitute 'reject' with 'map and avoid'. Modules with failed rows or banks beyond post-package-repair capacity ship with a bad-address map in the SPD vendor area; firmware hands it to the OS, which never allocates those pages (as badram/memmap already allow). JEDEC signaling is untouched.
note: Practical yield salvage through SPD maps; badram exists, standardizing distribution is the twist.

title: Legacy-node always-on island lets modern DRAM fully power down
idea: Put a 32-64 MB refresh-free die on the package (180 nm thick-oxide or loadless cells) holding page tables, kernel and wake state. Modern DRAM banks then enter deep power-down with no refresh when idle, flushing or discarding their contents.

title: One end-to-end code spanning DRAM array ECC and link FEC
idea: Combine on-die ECC with the interface's link CRC/FEC: compute one strong RS/LDPC code over the line plus metadata at write time, store its parity in the array, and transmit stored parity over the link unchanged so the host corrects array and channel errors in a single decode.

title: EV-battery second life: retention-graded DRAM cascade with refresh tags
idea: Adapted from the second-life market for retired EV batteries: the module SPD gains fields for a measured retention class and required refresh multiplier; retired server modules are re-profiled and resold into edge, PC or cache roles where 2x refresh or lower operating temperature is acceptable.

title: Set-top-box firmware updates: on-die microcoded refresh sequencer
idea: Adapted from over-the-air firmware updates: replace the hard-wired refresh counter with a tiny on-die microcontroller running signed microcode (refresh ordering, multi-rate bins, temperature curves, row-hammer mitigations), updatable by the host through a mode-register channel for the module's whole life.
note: Field-updatable refresh/row-hammer microcode; easy FPGA prototype, incremental gain.

title: Vehicle history report: retention passport and stress odometer per die
idea: Adapted from vehicle history reports and odometers: each die keeps a write-protected record of its factory retention bins and weak-cell map, plus counters for hot hours, activations and refresh-error events, readable by any refurbisher through a standard command.

title: Minify the cost of discovery: an 8-tier DRAM inducement prize
idea: Put up a $400k prize, verified at a neutral university lab, for the first open demonstration of a stack of at least 8 tiers with at least 1 fF per cell and 64 ms retention. The winner grants the sponsor a licensing option.

title: On-die health passport for second-life grading
idea: MAGNIFY what each die knows about its own history: an on-die tamper-proof log of power-on hours, ECC events, row-hammer counts and temperature lets refurbishers grade stacks instantly.

title: Address-free streaming: tensor descriptors replace per-access addresses
idea: Eliminate per-access command/address traffic: the host writes one descriptor (base, strides, tile shape, dtype) into the HBM base die, which generates its own ACT/RD sequences and streams data in consumption order, exploiting bank-interleave knowledge only the memory has.

title: Eliminate overprovisioning: working-set audit with shared-savings DIMM resale
idea: Eliminate padded memory configs: a startup deploys eBPF working-set profilers across a customer's fleet for 60 days, proves which DIMMs are never touched, pulls them, and resells them, splitting proceeds; $1M funds tooling plus five enterprise pilots.

title: Qualify DRAM cold: a liquid-cooled retention grade
idea: Rearrange the spec around the deployment: create a datasheet grade qualified at <=55 C case temperature for direct-liquid-cooled racks, where retention is ~8x longer than at 85 C. Dies that fail 85 C retention screening but pass at 55 C enter this grade instead of downgrade or scrap, and all parts in the grade run 2-4x slower refresh.

title: Deinococcus genome repair: vertical erasure codes span the tiers
idea: Deinococcus radiodurans rebuilds shattered genomes from overlapping copies; stripe each word across 16 tiers of a vertical column plus 4 parity tiers (Reed-Solomon over tiers), so a whole tier lost to 125 C bond voiding, contact drift or a wordline open is corrected on the fly.

title: Grafted controller mezzanine upgrades compression without scrapping DRAM
idea: Gardeners graft new scions onto old rootstock; CXL memory modules put the DRAM on a long-lived rootstock board and the controller and compression ASIC on a pluggable mezzanine, so better compression or a new link standard is adopted by swapping a small card rather than the DRAM.
note: Sensible module modularity; gain depends on compression improving over life.

title: Airbnb for idle cleanroom tools: memory prototyping by the hour
idea: Borrowed from Airbnb monetizing spare rooms: a 10-person team builds a booking, recipe-transfer and wafer-logistics platform over idle tool hours in U.S. university, national-lab and 200 mm commercial cleanrooms, so memory startups route split lots across ALD at one site, etch at another and test at a third.

title: Flight-recorder DIMM interposer capturing command history before each error
idea: An aircraft's black box records the minutes before an incident. An FPGA DIMM interposer (two board spins, about $250k) keeps a rolling 1-second ring buffer of ACT/REF commands and temperature. On any corrected or uncorrected ECC event it freezes and dumps the buffer. Deployed on ~200 partner servers within the $1M, it would build the first large dataset linking real flips to real access patterns.

title: Epidemic contact tracing: ECC events trigger blast-radius refresh
idea: Epidemiologists trace and test the contacts of each case. When row r reports a corrected error, controller firmware treats it as a case. It immediately refreshes and scrubs r+-1..+-4 using the physical adjacency map. If more cases appear, it raises local refresh and asks the OS to quarantine (remap) the hot aggressor pages.

title: 1980s DNQ-novolac i-line strategy for PFAS-free domestic interposers
idea: Standardize HBM interposers and RDL at >=1.5-2 um lines on non-chemically-amplified DNQ-novolac resist and i-line steppers, 1980s tooling that is cheap, available used and buildable in the U.S., and design memory interfaces wide and slow enough to fit those rules.
note: Coarse RDL on i-line is routine; PFAS-free angle is new but costs bandwidth density.

title: Metronome refresh locked to AI all-reduce phases
idea: Random stimulus 'metronome': everything happens on the beat. The accelerator tells HBM the beat of its training step, and the memory controller bunches all refresh into the predictable windows when HBM is idle (network all-reduce, optimizer step on cached data) instead of spreading it uniformly.

title: Rescue rejected DRAM dies behind a strong-ECC buffer controller
idea: Box: existing dies x existing access x existing SA x ECC buffer chip on module x existing substrate x existing fabs. Buy dies that fail JEDEC bins with <=1% bad bits at scrap prices and package them on modules or CXL cards whose buffer chip runs LDPC plus remapping, sold as a new grade.

title: Grade-B DRAM exchange selling dies with certified error maps
idea: Box [medium: any | access: any | sense: standard | integration: DIMM or CXL | substrate: bulk | fab: existing fabs]. A broker buys dies that fail JEDEC retention or hammer limits, tests each to a signed per-die error map, and sells them to hyperscalers whose controllers load the map to retire rows and set per-bank refresh.

title: On-die memory passport logs wear, faults and material content
idea: Worsen: give every chip no history, so recyclers must assume it is junk. Flip: reserve a small OTP/eFuse region where the chip logs total activations, ECC corrections, repairs and a bill-of-materials hash, readable by a standard command, so graders can price and route reuse in seconds.

title: Open DRAM periphery compiler on a shared U.S. pilot PDK
idea: Worse: make every memory startup re-invent sense amps, decoders and PHYs under NDA. Flip: fund an open-source generator, OpenRAM-style but for 1T1C, gain-cell and novel cells, that emits sense amps, row decoders, charge pumps and DDR/CXL PHYs for a shared U.S. pilot-line PDK.

title: Inference model cartridges in via-programmed mask ROM
idea: Worse: hold frozen model weights in refreshing DRAM. Flip: ship weights of stable production models as via-programmed ROM cartridges built on 28-40 nm lines, one custom via mask per model, with 20-50 ns random reads.

title: Open CXL reference controller for static and nonvolatile memories
idea: Worse: make each new memory maker build its own controller and survive hyperscaler qualification alone. Flip: an OCP-style consortium publishes open RTL and firmware for a CXL Type-3 controller with no refresh engine, persistence and wear hooks, and a shared qualification suite.

title: Gleaner's cool tier: sense-marginal dies for liquid-cooled racks
idea: Farmers glean the field after harvest. Dies that fail sense margin only above ~75 C are binned as cool-tier DDR5/HBM, sold at standard JEDEC timings into liquid- and immersion-cooled racks that hold devices under 60 C.

title: Child's rubber stamp: micro-transfer printing memory dielets onto logic
idea: A child stamps hundreds of stickers at once. Release 50x50 um memory dielets from their source wafer on undercut tethers, then pick thousands at a time with a PDMS stamp and print them onto a logic wafer at +/-1.5 um placement.
note: uTP is commercial; tiny dielets limit capacity per placement and I/O density.

title: Smelter manager turns dead aluminum plants into memory fabs
idea: Persona: an aluminum smelter manager who knows where cheap firm power already lands. Site new DRAM fabs on shuttered U.S. smelter sites in the Pacific Northwest, Ohio Valley and Kentucky. These sites already have 300-600 MW grid interconnects, water rights, rail and industrial zoning.

title: Migratory birds follow the sun: shift memory-heavy services across time zones
idea: Birds don't winter where food is scarce. A global scheduler moves memory-hungry, latency-tolerant work (batch inference, embedding refreshes, index builds, prefix-KV warmups) each day to the regions at their nightly trough. Each region's DRAM is then sized for its own interactive peak rather than the sum of all peaks.

title: Insurance actuary prices risk: discounted VMs with memory-pressure insurance
idea: Actuaries price rare events. A cloud or colo sells VMs 25% cheaper whose guests agree that during rare host pressure events up to 30% of their pages may be served from a compressed tier. Credits ('claims') are paid automatically per minute of measured degradation. Billing and telemetry software fits in the budget.

title: Ephemeral-grade DRAM: sell retention rejects to frame-buffer users
idea: Camera, display and network ring buffers overwrite every byte within ~16 ms. Create a product grade for dies that fail the 64 ms retention screen but pass at 16-32 ms, sold to customers whose controllers guarantee a rewrite cadence and issue no refresh at all.

title: Token-ring wordline sequencer for append-only KV-cache mats
idea: KV-caches append and stream tokens in order, so dedicated mats replace the row decoder with a token passed along a chain of shift-register stages (one per 8 wordlines plus a 3-bit local predecoder), allowing random access only at block granularity. Everything is drawn at DUV pitch.

title: Wired-NOR zero-detect lines suppress all-zero bursts at sense stripes
idea: Satellites downlink only non-trivial data: each SA group pulls down a wired-NOR line if any latched bit is 1, so all-zero 64-byte sectors return a 1-bit flag instead of a full burst over global I/O and pins. Sparse AI activations and zero-padded KV pages benefit most.

title: Data-parallel training: model replicas become each other's ECC
idea: In a 10,000-GPU job, every data-parallel rank holds identical weights. Periodically checksum each 2 MB weight shard, compare checksums across replicas over NVLink or InfiniBand, and repair any mismatched shard by copying it from a majority peer. Local HBM errors are then corrected by replication that already exists.

title: Classified-grade DRAM sanitization so secure fleets stop shredding
idea: Classified and financial systems shred all memory. A 10-person lab offers NIST 800-88-style DRAM sanitization (powered-off hold, verified all-zero readback, SPD wipe) with chain-of-custody video and a certificate, so secure fleets resell modules instead of destroying them.
