idea: Toyota-style kanban: a hardware credit counter between the GPU and an NVMe controller releases the next layer's weights or KV pages only when a consumer slot frees, so DRAM/HBM holds exactly pipeline-depth (2-3 layers) of inventory, never the whole model.

title: Pupation: cold pointer structures metamorphose into succinct NV forms
idea: Like a caterpillar reorganizing into a compact pupa, cold pointer-rich structures (tries, graphs, inverted indexes) are rebuilt into succinct rank/select encodings (Elias-Fano, wavelet trees) stored in byte-addressable NV and queried in place without decompression.
note: Succinct encodings placed in NV; same core as I-02147.

title: Progressive-JPEG bit-plane memory with early-stop streaming
idea: Progressive JPEG sends coarse detail first, then fine. Store tensors bit-plane-transposed so a burst returns the MSBs of many values first. The consumer (attention scoring, vector search) ends the stream once it has enough precision, and fetches low bit-planes only for the top-k survivors.

title: EV-battery second-life cascade for retired hyperscaler DIMMs
idea: Borrowing the EV-battery second-life playbook (car pack -> grid storage), retired server DIMMs are run through an automated rig that measures each rank's retention time and row-hammer flip threshold, then re-labelled into tiers (A: production CXL pool, B: cache/scratch, C: read-mostly). An SPD-written 'state of health' field tells the host controller what refresh interval and activation limit to use for that module.

title: T-RAM thyristor latch revived on existing SOI production lines
idea: T-RAM Semiconductor's thin capacitively-coupled thyristor (abandoned around 2010) held bits as the latched state of a gate-coupled pnpn device. Re-target it to existing 22FDX and 45-nm PD-SOI flows, using modern back-bias to cut standby current and ALD gate dielectric to tighten the coupled gate.
note: Same thyristor latch, on FD-SOI.

title: Charge-transfer preamplifier revived with one low-Vt implant
idea: The charge-transfer sense schemes of 1970s DRAMs moved bitline charge through a near-threshold transistor onto a tiny node. One added low-Vt implant mask makes pitch-matched transfer gates that, biased at threshold, pass the cell's signal charge from a ~60 fF bitline onto a ~4 fF node, multiplying voltage swing ~5-10x before the latch.
note: 1970s charge-transfer preamp revived; Vt mismatch of transfer gate limits gain but enables smaller Cs.

title: Ershov hash-consing of tensor blocks across fine-tunes and agent forks
idea: Revive Ershov's 1958 hash-consing in the memory controller: every 4 KB weight or KV block is content-hashed on write and interned in a global table, so identical blocks across fine-tuned variants, unmerged adapters, forked agent contexts and replicas are stored once, and near-identical blocks are stored as base pointer plus XOR-compressed residual. Divergence triggers copy-on-write.
note: Exact plus XOR-residual dedup of blocks overlaps I-01197; full fine-tunes rarely share identical blocks.

title: No.1 ESS program-store/call-store split by page write rate
idea: The 1965 No.1 ESS kept programs in a read-mostly twistor 'program store' and live call data in a small writable ferrite 'call store'. Revive the split: the hypervisor classifies pages by measured write rate, placing read-mostly pages (weights, code, static tables) on denser memories with slow or endurance-limited writes (NOR-like, ReRAM, PCM) and only write-hot pages in DRAM.

title: ETA-10 Revival: Liquid-Nitrogen Pods for Commodity DRAM at 77 K
idea: Revive ETA Systems' 1987 liquid-nitrogen-immersed CMOS supercomputer: immerse standard DRAM in LN2 pods (nitrogen is abundant, unlike helium), where leakage collapses so retention reaches minutes and refresh is switched off, the steeper subthreshold slope lets VARY and wordline drop to ~0.4/1.2 V, and copper resistance falls ~7x.
note: Cryo-DRAM studied widely; cooling overhead at 77 K erodes the claimed ~10x net energy gain.

title: Second life for leaky silicon: refresh-tuned salvage of retention rejects
idea: Inverts 'a die that fails 64 ms retention is scrap': buy fab retention-reject dies and decommissioned server and phone DRAM at scrap prices, profile each chip's retention map on high-throughput testers, and mount them on CXL boards whose controller refreshes at the measured interval (4-8 ms) and remaps the worst rows.

title: TSV-free inductive-coil stack of headless DRAM dies
idea: Inverting 'stacked dies must be wired with TSVs': thinned dies talk through top-metal coil pairs (near-field inductive links, ~1 Gb/s per coil), power arrives by edge wire bonds, and only the bottom master die carries I/O, DLL and regulators while upper dies are headless arrays.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling replaces helium in every chuck
idea: Inverts 'helium is the only safe backside heat-transfer gas': feed electrostatic chucks in etch/CVD/implant with 5-20 Torr hydrogen (thermal conductivity higher than He) from an on-site electrolyzer, recirculated through a palladium-membrane loop with sub-LEL leak sensing; the backside gas never touches plasma.

title: Model-on-ROM: frozen weights etched in 40 nm mask ROM
idea: Inverts 'weights must live in rewritable memory': a frozen foundation model's INT4 weights are etched as mask ROM on existing 40 nm logic lines (~0.01 um2 per bit, so a 7B model needs ~280 mm2 of bitcells across a few dies) next to small accelerators, leaving all DRAM for KV and activations.

title: Kinetic-inductance nanowire loops storing single flux quanta at 4 K
idea: Store each bit as the presence or absence of one flux quantum (Phi0 = 2.07e-15 Wb) in a loop of 20 nm NbN nanowire. Huge kinetic inductance keeps beta_L = 2*pi*L*Ic/Phi0 > 1 in a ~100 nm loop, the persistent current never decays, and a nanocryotron reads it.
note: MIT nanowire flux-loop memory exists; cryo niche.

title: Expiring memory: retention sized to the data's lifetime, never refreshed
idea: AI activations, KV-cache blocks and gradients live 1-500 ms. The allocator tags each buffer with its lifetime and places it in banks whose measured cell retention exceeds that lifetime, and those banks never refresh because the data is dead before it decays.
note: Close to RANA/Flikker retention-aware placement prior art; needs controller-level refresh disable.

title: Built-in-bias antiferroelectric ZrO2 minor-loop dynamic polarization cell
idea: ALD ZrO2 crystallizes antiferroelectric at <=350 C. Asymmetric TiN/RuO2 electrodes (~0.5 eV work-function offset) shift the double loop so zero bias sits inside one lobe, and the field-induced ferroelectric state stores the '1', relaxing over a designed ~1 s with no wake-up or imprint fatigue.
note: NaMLab (Pesic 2016) already showed work-function-biased AFE ZrO2 memory.

title: Spare-die HBM stacks with base-die crossbar remapping
idea: Stack yield compounds as y^N, so 12 dies at 98% bond yield gives ~78%. Build 13-high stacks whose base die holds a channel crossbar that remaps any failed die to the spare, plus spare TSV lanes rerouted at runtime without fuses.

title: Content-addressed memory fabric stores each identical page once
idea: Across a datacenter, KV-cache prefixes, system prompts, libraries and weights repeat thousands of times. A CXL switch hashes 4 KB pages on write, keeps each unique page once in a pooled DRAM/NAND backend, and hands hosts copy-on-write pointers, with a prefix-trie index for KV caches.

title: Address-event storage keeps only coordinates of nonzero values
idea: When activations are >99% zero (ReLU-fied LLMs, spiking nets, event sensors), storing the zeros wastes ~99% of bits. Store tensors as address-event streams (index plus small value) in the interface die, expand them only inside SRAM next to the MAC arrays, and train with sparsity regularizers targeting 99%+.

title: Write-coalescing plus start-gap rotation qualifies 1e11-endurance cells
idea: First-principles budget: a hot line can take ~2e11 writes in 5 years. An on-die 1 MB write-combining SRAM absorbs >95% of hot rewrites, and start-gap row rotation spreads the rest, so per-cell writes fall below 1e10.

title: Fridge magnets: inductive coupling links replace TSVs in stacks
idea: Stick dies together like fridge magnets: replace HBM TSVs with on-die coils that couple data inductively between thinned stacked dies at ~1 Gb/s per coil and ~0.05-0.1 pJ/bit, so no TSV keep-out zones or through-silicon etch are needed.

title: Lotus-leaf droplets: capillary self-assembly bonds memory tiles onto logic
idea: Water beads align on a lotus leaf: put a droplet on each hydrophilic bond site of a logic wafer, release thousands of small (1-2 mm2) known-good DRAM tiles in fluid, and let surface tension pull each tile to <0.5 um alignment before it direct-bonds as the water evaporates. No fine-alignment die-to-wafer bonder is needed.

title: Party balloon: per-pump helium harvest-and-repurify loop
idea: Random stimulus 'party balloon' (helium that silently leaks away) -> treat every dry-pump exhaust as a leaking balloon. A compact hollow-fiber membrane stage plus cold-trap/getter polisher on each etch and implant pump exhaust pulls backside-cooling helium out of the N2 ballast at >90% recovery, repurifies it to 6N and feeds it back to the chucks.
note: Fab helium recovery systems are commercial; per-pump membranes are an incremental twist.

title: Welding torch: bolt-on hydrogen backside-cooling kit for etch chucks
idea: Stimulus 'welding torch' (hydrogen handled safely every day) -> a 10-person team assembles a bolt-on kit (small PEM electrolyzer, palladium purifier, mass-flow controller, H2 sensors and interlocks) that swaps 5-20 Torr helium backside gas for hydrogen (0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K) on existing electrostatic chucks.

title: Magnifying glass: foveated KV precision around attention focus
idea: Like foveated rendering, the KV manager keeps recent tokens and retrieval anchors at FP8, mid-distance tokens at 3-bit and far tokens merged into learned gist tokens, re-sharpening a region from a flash copy when attention mass returns to it.

title: Mosaic tiles: embedding tables assembled from shared tile codebooks
idea: A mosaic renders any image from a few tile colours: store recommendation embedding rows as product-quantized codes into a few shared codebooks, decoded by a memory-side gather engine on a CXL device so the host still sees full-precision rows.

title: MoO2-templated rutile TiO2 capacitor: k of 90 without ruthenium
idea: Box = {medium: charge in rutile-phase TiO2 (k~80-100) | access: Si FET | sense: charge share | integration: 1T1C pillar at AR ~30:1 | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: ALD from TiCl4 made in the U.S. from Florida/Georgia ilmenite, on a rutile-structured MoO2 bottom electrode from Colorado molybdenum}. MoO2 shares the rutile lattice, so it templates rutile TiO2 at low temperature the way RuO2 does, and light Al doping holds leakage down.
note: Rutile templating on RuO2/MoO2 explored; small TiO2 bandgap leakage is the persistent issue.

title: Liquid-nitrogen planar DRAM: helium-free cold shrinks the capacitor tenfold
idea: Box = {medium: charge on a planar 0.5 fF ZrO2 MIM with no pillar | access: Si FET at 77 K | sense: low-noise cryogenic SA | integration: memory sleds immersed in LN2 from U.S. air-separation plants | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: relaxed-pitch patterning with a U.S. multibeam e-beam writer}. At 77 K subthreshold and junction leakage drop by more than 1e6, so retention reaches minutes even with a tiny planar capacitor, and nitrogen cooling avoids the helium chokepoint entirely.
note: Cryo-DRAM studied (Rambus, CryoRAM); LN2 ~10 W/W overhead caps system gain.

title: Shadow router prefetches next-layer MoE experts from CXL flash
idea: Box: tiering × MoE inference runtime × expert × predicted one layer early × CXL-attached low-latency NAND. A tiny predictor maps the current hidden state to the next layer's likely experts, which stream into a small HBM expert cache while the current layer computes.
note: Pre-gated MoE / MoE-Infinity already pursue this.

title: Sense amplifiers double as 100 mV interposer link receivers
idea: Box: DRAM x standard x cross-coupled latch receiver x 100 mV-swing interposer wires treated as long bitlines x Si interposer x standard fab. The interface reuses the DRAM's own sense-amp latch topology as a clocked receiver, so the transmitter only dumps a small charge on the wire, like a cell sharing charge with a bitline.
note: StrongARM latch receivers and ground-referenced low-swing links are established.

title: Flash-resident KV cache with attention-guided prefetch over CXL
idea: Box: dense 3D NAND x standard x standard x CXL/optical link with predictive prefetch engine x SSD x standard. The LLM KV cache lives on flash; a small predictor in the controller uses top-k attention scores to prefetch the token blocks the next step needs into a 10x smaller DRAM buffer.
note: Close to InfiniGen/ShadowKV-style attention-guided KV offload.

title: Second-life CXL memory bricks from retired server DIMM dies
idea: Box[Source=retired DIMMs x Transform=laser debond+KGD retest x Integration=CXL Type-3 x Owner=recycler-OEM JV x Finance=EPR take-back credits x Scale=regional centers]: retired DDR4/DDR5 packages are desoldered, retested at temperature and re-mounted 32-64 per card behind a CXL controller as a far-memory tier, with the recycler paid by extended-producer-responsibility credits.

title: OS compacts live pages into best-retention rows before self-refresh
idea: Po: the best cells do all the work. On entering idle, the OS migrates live pages into rows profiled as the top-decile retention class and powers the rest down with partial-array self-refresh, so the self-refresh interval is set by the best rows, not the worst.
note: Commodity self-refresh interval is internal; needs extended-interval self-refresh support.

title: Fading KV: tokens lose bits as attention ignores them
idea: Po: memory that shrinks when you look away. Each KV entry carries an attention-usage counter and steps down 16 to 8 to 4 to 2 bits, then merges into a pooled summary vector, as its cumulative attention mass decays, mimicking human memory consolidation.
note: MiKV/ZipCache-style mixed-precision KV known.

title: RAID across tiers: one parity tier per sixteen
idea: Worse: let one defective tier among 200 kill or degrade the die. Flip: write each 16-tier group with an XOR parity tier computed in the base die and reconstruct a failed tier's bits on read, so random tier defects become correctable instead of becoming yield loss.

title: Scatter-gather descriptor port returns only the useful bytes
idea: Worsen: open a whole 1-8 KB row to deliver one 4-byte embedding element. Flip: give the HBM base die a descriptor port where the host posts index lists; the base die activates sub-rows, gathers only the requested sectors into dense packets and ships those, so the bus carries only useful bytes.

title: Grade-B DRAM: rebinned decommissioned DIMMs behind CXL expanders
idea: Worse: shred DDR4/DDR5 when servers retire after 4-5 years. Flip: route retired DIMMs through a high-throughput retest line (retention, row-hammer threshold, speed bin) and redeploy them behind CXL Type-3 controllers that translate old DDR generations to any new host, with ECC strength set by each module's measured bin.

title: Plumber's capillary self-alignment: water-droplet HBM die stacking
idea: A plumber knows water finds its level. Drop HBM dies coarsely (+/-20 um) onto hydrophilic bond sites carrying a water microdroplet; surface tension pulls each die into <1 um alignment within milliseconds, then evaporation and one collective hybrid-bond anneal fix every die at once.

title: Alien who sees only entropy: entropy-sized frames in CXL expander
idea: An alien observer sees information content, not 4 KB pages. A CXL Type-3 controller measures each incoming page's compressibility inline and stores it in a 512 B, 1 KB, 2 KB or 4 KB slot. A sub-page indirection table and per-class free lists track the slots, so the host sees full nominal capacity while the media holds only the entropy.

title: Octopus arms think locally: filtering engines inside CXL memory modules
idea: Two-thirds of an octopus's neurons sit in its arms. Each CXL memory module gets a small engine for scan, filter, hash-probe and gather, so analytics and database operators run where the data sits and return only results. That eliminates the host-side staging buffers, decoded copies and hash tables that currently mirror the data in local DRAM.
note: Computational CXL memory widely pursued.

title: Mole lives underground: vector search fully inside SSD controllers
idea: A mole never needs the surface. Billion-scale vector indexes (a graph ANN plus PQ codes, normally hundreds of GB of DRAM) live entirely on SSDs whose controllers walk the graph and compute PQ distances internally. The host keeps only a tiny entry-point table and receives top-k IDs.

title: Hotel concierge: on-module DRAM front desk over flash storage
idea: A concierge keeps tonight's keys at the desk and everything else in storage. An on-module 'memory hotel' pairs 16 GB of DRAM with 256 GB of low-latency SLC flash behind a controller that predicts and prefetches hot 4 KB pages, presenting 272 GB to the host as byte-addressable CXL memory.

title: Work-function-offset antiferroelectric gives two zero-bias states for pacemakers
idea: Pacemakers need memory that idles at zero power for ten years; one added mask patterns a high-work-function RuO2 top electrode (vs TiN) over ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitors, shifting one double-hysteresis loop so two polarization states coexist at 0 V. Antiferroelectric switching avoids HZO wake-up and offers 1e12+ endurance.

title: Automotive tier-RAID: erasure code striped across stacked array tiers
idea: Automotive ASIL-D allows no silent bit loss at 150 C; stripe each 64-byte line across 9 tiers of a 3D array (8 data + 1 parity) read in parallel, so any single tier with weak or hammered cells is rebuilt on the fly. Refresh can then be set by the typical tier rather than the worst cell anywhere in the stack.
note: Chipkill-style parity ported to 3D tiers; parallel 9-tier activation costs power.

title: Dilution-fridge-grade helium recapture ring on every etch chuck
idea: Quantum-computing labs recover >95% of helium boil-off; copy them by adding an edge-scavenging vacuum ring around each electrostatic chuck that captures backside-cooling helium leakage and feeds a tool-side membrane purifier and compressor returning 99.999% He to the chuck line. A fab helium 'bank' meters per-tool recovery the way a cryo lab does.

title: Rocket-test-stand hydrogen as backside wafer coolant instead of helium
idea: Rocket engine test stands handle hydrogen routinely, and H2 conducts heat better than He (0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K). Run chuck backside cooling on 5-20 Torr electrolytic H2 (or H2/Ar) with leak-tight seals, H2 sensors and dilution exhaust, qualifying each etch chemistry for H-radical side effects.

title: Recommender long tail: synthesize rare-ID embeddings from features
idea: From the largest single DRAM user, ad recommenders with TB-scale embedding tables: only IDs seen more than N times get a stored row, and every tail ID's embedding is computed on the fly by a small feature tower from side attributes (category, text, graph neighbors) trained jointly with the model.

title: Digital-hoarder edge case: object-level access sampling exiles untouched objects
idea: From the user who opens everything and touches nothing: the memory controller samples access bits per object rather than per page via allocator-tagged address ranges, and objects untouched for a window are compacted together and exiled to compressed CXL flash with a fault-driven return path.
note: Object-granular far memory (AIFM, Carbink) is known; 80-95% cold claim is optimistic.

title: Fraud-graph pointer chasing executed inside the memory stack
idea: Fraud-detection and social graphs are extreme pointer chasers with one useful word per hop. Put a tiny walker engine in the base die that follows pointer chains and returns only the final result, keeping every intermediate hop inside the stack.
note: IMPICA/Tesseract-class pointer-chasing PIM is known.

title: 77 K immersion pods let storage capacitors shrink tenfold
idea: Jump from cell to datacenter scale: put memory sleds in liquid-nitrogen immersion pods where access-transistor leakage falls by ~6 orders, so retention goes from 64 ms to hours and the capacitor only needs to beat sense-amp offset, not leakage (~0.5 fF instead of 5 fF).
note: Same LN2 cryo-DRAM idea.

title: Tail rows exiled to an on-die SRAM jail
idea: Scale shift: the ppm-scale retention tail is served by a tiny memory with a different timescale; rows or 64 B segments failing a 1 s retention test at sort or in the field are remapped through a CAM into a few hundred KB of on-die SRAM or fast-refresh eDRAM, letting the rest of the array run at 1 s refresh.
note: RAIDR/ArchShield-style prior art; VRT cells escaping profiling are the key risk.

title: Capillary droplet self-alignment for sub-micron chiplet-to-wafer hybrid bonding
idea: Shift alignment from a multi-million-dollar robot to molecular-scale surface tension: hydrophilic pad patterns plus a water droplet pull each DRAM chiplet into register to <200 nm as the droplet evaporates, then Cu/oxide direct bonding locks it. A coarse +/-10 um pick-and-place is enough because the liquid does the last mile.
note: Capillary self-assembly is demonstrated (Tohoku, Leti); cheap tool demo feasible.

title: Function-shipping packets: memory requests carry bytecode run at the hub
idea: Invert the scale of what moves: instead of hauling gigabytes to the CPU, each CXL request carries a ~64-byte verified bytecode (filter, gather, reduce) that a tiny core on the memory hub executes, returning only the result. The fabric moves kernels, not data.

title: Robotic second-life harvest of retired DRAM into CXL memory shelves
idea: DRAM reclaim from retired servers and phones has failed on manual handling, mixed generations and test cost. Decommissioning lines at hyperscalers use robots to pull DIMMs and reflow-desolder LPDDR packages, run a 10-minute BIST sort, and mount mixed DDR3/DDR4/LPDDR parts behind CXL controllers that hide generation differences in pooled second-life shelves.

title: AMD HBCC, fixed: hardware-paged HBM cache with attention-aware prefetch
idea: Vega's High-Bandwidth Cache Controller paged system memory into VRAM in hardware but died because games fit in VRAM anyway. Revive it for LLM serving: HBM becomes a hardware-managed page cache over host LPDDR/CXL, and the prefetcher uses the previous decode step's attention-score sparsity to fetch only KV pages likely to be attended next.
note: InfiniGen-style speculative KV prefetch over unified memory exists.

title: eASIC structured ASIC, fixed: via-programmed ROM holding frozen weights
idea: Mask ROM died because every code change needed a full mask set, and eASIC's single-via customization never found volume. Store a frozen production model's weights in a via-programmable ROM fabric where one cheap non-EUV via mask encodes the bits, so a model update costs one mask and a two-week spin, not a new chip.

title: Optane latency, fixed: look-ahead MoE router hides flash fetch
idea: Optane failed partly because software could not hide its latency on unpredictable accesses. Co-design the model instead: train each MoE router to choose experts for layer L+2 from layer L's hidden state, giving two layers of warning to fetch expert weights from flash into SRAM before they are needed.

title: Barrier-trimmed MTJ trades ten-year retention for tenfold cheaper writes
idea: Effect walk: Neel-Arrhenius thermal activation. Design the MTJ free layer for thermal stability ~25-30 (seconds of retention at 85 C) instead of ~60 (ten years); critical current scales with the barrier, so writes need ~2-2.5x less current and, with shorter pulses, ~5-10x less energy, while a refresh every ~100 ms costs ~1% duty.
note: Known relaxed-retention STT-MRAM concept (Smullen 2011); straightforward to execute.

title: Flux quanta in kinetic-inductance nanowire loops for cryogenic AI memory
idea: Effect walk: flux quantization in superconductors. Each bit is the presence or absence of one flux quantum in a loop of 10-nm-wide NbN or NbTiN nanowire whose large kinetic inductance shrinks the loop to ~0.1 um2; writes and reads use nanocryotron (nTron) switches instead of Josephson junctions, costing ~10^-18 J per access.

title: Conducting ferroelectric domain walls as switchable nanoscale wires
idea: Effect walk: domain-wall conduction. In a thin-film LiNbO3 or ErMnO3 cell, a written charged domain wall bridging two electrodes conducts ~10^4x better than the bulk; short pulses inject or erase the wall to store the bit, and a 0.1-V read through the wall leaves polarization untouched.
note: LiNbO3 domain-wall memory demonstrated (Fudan); Si integration needs bonding.

title: Capillary self-alignment for cheap high-throughput die-to-wafer stacking
idea: Surface tension: hydrophilic bond pads with hydrophobic surroundings, plus a water microdroplet, pull each roughly placed die to <200 nm alignment as the water evaporates, before direct hybrid bonding. Fast, coarse pick-and-place replaces slow precision bonders.

title: Water-droplet capillary self-alignment stacks DRAM dies without thermocompression bonders
idea: Effect: surface-tension energy minimization. Pattern hydrophilic pads inside hydrophobic surrounds on the dies; a coarse, ~$150k used pick-and-place drops each die onto a water film, and capillary force pulls it to <1 um alignment within ~100 ms before direct bonding. A 24-month, $1M program demonstrates 4-high wide-I/O stacks.

title: Cu: electroplated copper coils link stacked dies without TSVs
idea: Replace HBM TSVs with inductive-coupling transceivers: spiral Cu coils, electroless-seeded and electroplated with no argon-sputtered barrier or seed, in each die's top metal pass data magnetically through 20-50 um of thinned silicon.

title: Platinum catalyst banks: analytics filters run at the bank surface
idea: Like a catalytic converter reacting gas on the platinum surface without moving it elsewhere, each DRAM bank group gets a small predicate unit beside its sense amplifiers that decodes dictionary-compressed columns and evaluates WHERE clauses and aggregates in place; only matching row IDs or partial sums cross the I/O.

title: Lanthanide contraction ordering: shrink graph gaps, then stream compressed
idea: Atoms contract steadily across the lanthanides; a reordering pass (community detection plus Gorder) renumbers graph vertices so neighbors get nearby IDs, then adjacency lists are stored as gap-coded Elias-gamma/varint streams decoded by a near-memory unit, turning random neighbor reads into sequential compressed streams.

title: Retread memory: remanufacture retired server DRAM inside ECC shells
idea: Like tyre retreading, harvest DDR4/DDR5 from retired servers, re-test and re-bin at die or package level, and remount it on CXL expanders whose buffer chip adds strong symbol ECC, scrubbing and page retirement to absorb ageing errors.
note: Retired-DRAM reuse behind CXL buffers already done (Azure GreenSKU/Pond); ECC-shell remount adds little new.

title: Erasure-coded decay: refresh only when information is at risk
idea: IFR: refresh happens only when information, not charge, is about to be lost. Store each page with a strong cross-row LDPC/erasure code and let cells decay; a background reader samples syndrome weight per page and re-encodes only pages nearing the correction limit.
note: Strong-ECC refresh relaxation known; parity and latency cost.

title: Two-layer DRAM window streams weights from parallel flash channels
idea: IFR: weights need no DRAM residency. Closest: weights live across 16-64 NVMe/low-latency flash channels and stream layer by layer into a double buffer holding exactly two layers; the batch grows until per-layer compute hides the flash read time.

title: Weight carousel rotates model shards around an accelerator ring
idea: IFR: one copy of the weights serves every chip at once. Closest: N accelerators each hold 1/N of the weights and continuously pass shards around the ring over chip-to-chip links; each chip applies the passing shard to its own batch, so the ring stores weights once instead of N times.

title: KV cache as inverted-file vector index with DRAM-resident centroids
idea: IFR: context length is free. Closest: KV blocks are clustered online into an IVF index stored in flash; DRAM holds only the centroids and a recent window, and each decode query fetches its top-k clusters for sparse attention.
note: RetrievalAttention/ClusterKV-class prior art.

title: Hybrid state-space retrofit replaces most attention layers' KV
idea: IFR: context costs constant memory. Closest with no new hardware: replace 7 of every 8 attention layers in a trained model with linear-recurrent state-space layers (fixed-size state) distilled from the originals, keeping one attention layer in eight for exact recall.
note: Mamba-in-Llama distillation retrofits known.

title: CCD-loop memory: charge packets circulate, no per-bit contact
idea: Scarcity rule: no transistor or contact per bit. Bits ride as charge packets in buried-channel CCD loops of 64 cells clocked by 2-phase gates, and one sense-and-regenerate stage per loop reads and restores each packet as it passes, so a bit costs only ~2F2 of gate pitch.
note: 1970s CCD memory revival; latency penalty.

title: Indium- and gallium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cells
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero indium and gallium (China-dominated). Build a 2T0C gain cell whose write transistor is amorphous Zn-Sn-O made by ALD below 300 C, Si-doped to suppress oxygen-vacancy leakage, with charge stored on the read transistor's gate.

title: Combinatorial abundant-element dielectric library for capacitors
idea: Within $1M/24 months: co-sputter graded Ti-Al-Si-Mg-Ca-O-N thin-film libraries (crustal-abundant elements only) on probe-array wafers, auto-measure k, leakage and breakdown across ~10,000 compositions, and hand the top 10 to ALD recipe development.

title: Droplet self-alignment bonds dies at 10,000 per hour
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: water droplets on hydrophilic pads pull dies into sub-0.5 um alignment by capillary force, then oxide-oxide and Cu-Cu direct bonds form in a ~250 C anneal, with no polymer and no solder to age at 125 C.

title: Ship each binary with its own memory-compression dictionary
idea: Imposed limit: each GB of DRAM must hold 4 GB of apparent data. At build time the toolchain profiles heap snapshots and trains a 64 KB dictionary per object type; the binary carries it, the OS loads it into the memory controller, and each page is compressed against its app's dictionary, tagged with a per-page dictionary ID.

title: NAND-style zig-zag wire-bond stacks put 64 DRAM dies in one package
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. Borrow mobile NAND packaging, where 16-32 dies stack in a zig-zag staircase with wire bonds for cents, and apply it to DRAM as a capacity tier: 64 dies per package on 8 wire-bonded channels at modest bandwidth.

title: Scrub-as-refresh: 1-second refresh, page-level code, lazy scrub
idea: Each 1 KB DRAM page gets ~2% spare columns holding a BCH code (t=12 over GF(2^14)). The refresh engine restores rows about every second with a plain activate-precharge; the array itself is unchanged. A background scrubber decodes and rewrites each row about once a minute, so errors from weak and VRT cells can accumulate for at most one scrub period. Decoding at every refresh would eat most of the savings, so the scrub is lazy. Three add-ons stretch the interval further. (a) Per-subarray canary rows with undersized caps set the interval from measured leakage at the actual temperature, not from the 85 C 6.4-sigma worst case. (b) Retention errors only go one way (charged -> discharged, polarity known per true/anti cell), so an asymmetric (Z-channel) code needs fewer parity bits. (c) A write encoder flips 64-bit words to minimise how many cells sit charged. Fast-path reads use the existing on-die SEC; the page code is consulted only when an error is detected.

title: Minify optimizer state from 16 bytes to ~2.5 bytes/param
idea: Minify training memory: FP8 weights with stochastic rounding (no FP32 master copy), 4-bit block-quantized first moments and factored (row/column) second moments, fused into the optimizer kernel.

title: Eliminate Adam optimizer state with moment-free sign updates
idea: Train with a sign-based optimizer whose only per-parameter state is a 1-bit error-feedback residual, removing the two fp32 moment tensors that Adam keeps for every weight.

title: Eliminate backprop activation storage via forward-only perturbation training
idea: Fine-tune with zeroth-order or forward-gradient estimates: two perturbed forward passes from a shared random seed estimate the gradient, so no activations are stored and memory equals the inference footprint.
note: Matches MeZO.

title: Eliminate full-precision KV for stale tokens with age-tiered quantization
idea: An inference kernel library re-quantizes KV in the background as tokens age: the newest 512 tokens stay at fp16, older ones drop to int4, and the oldest to 2-bit with per-channel outlier rescue.

title: Tensor-train embedding cores with a full-precision hot-ID cache
idea: Box: factorization × recommendation model × embedding row × lookup-time reconstruction × TT cores + hot-row cache. Huge embedding tables become tensor-train cores reconstructed per lookup, with the hottest ~1% of IDs cached at full precision.
note: Matches TT-Rec.

title: Learned indexes replace B-trees and hash directories
idea: Worsen: keep giant B-tree and hash-table indexes in DRAM. Flip: replace them with small learned models (piecewise-linear or recursive model indexes) that predict a key's position with a bounded error window searched on flash.
note: Kraska et al. learned indexes widely studied.

title: Chloride inhibition: predictor blocks silent neurons, only active rows fetched
idea: Chloride channels stop neurons from firing; a tiny SRAM-resident low-rank predictor per FFN layer guesses which 5-10% of neurons will be non-zero for the current token, so only those weight rows are fetched from DRAM, and rarely active neurons live in flash.

title: Dolphin unihemispheric sleep: mirrored hot pages across alternately refreshing subchannels
idea: Dolphins sleep one brain hemisphere at a time. The controller mirrors only the hottest ~1-2% of pages across the two DDR5 subchannels, refreshes them in alternation and steers reads to the awake copy, so refresh never stalls hot reads. Controller RTL plus FPGA evaluation, ~$400k in 18 months.

title: Garbage collector evacuates objects off error-rising rows
idea: Inverts 'errors are hidden from software': the controller exports per-row correctable-error counters to managed runtimes (JVM, Go, Python); their copying garbage collector, which already moves objects, preferentially evacuates live objects from rows with rising syndromes and marks those frames cold-only.

title: Recommender hot rows: replicate embedding rows across banks to dilute activations
idea: Recommendation models with Zipf-skewed embedding lookups hit a few rows millions of times per second. The runtime keeps per-row activation counts in a Misra-Gries sketch and replicates the hottest rows into 4-8 banks, round-robining reads so no physical row crosses the hammer threshold. Bank parallelism also raises bandwidth.

title: Johnson-noise Morris counters shrink telemetry and tiering tables tenfold
idea: Replace exact 32-bit counters in flow tables, feature-frequency tables and page-hotness tables with 4-bit probabilistic Morris counters. Each one increments with probability 2^-c, decided by a comparator on amplified resistor thermal noise. Johnson noise grows with temperature, so the entropy source improves at 125 C rather than degrading.

title: Te: Optane afterlife market redeploys stranded 3D XPoint persistent memory
idea: Buy back stranded and retired Intel Optane PMem inventory, re-certify endurance, and resell it with open-source firmware and driver support to tier-2 clouds as a persistent memory pool.
note: Finite stranded inventory; niche.

title: Magnify tiers 300x: convert idle 3D NAND fabs to gain-cell lines
idea: Reuse 3D NAND tool sets (alternating film stacks, one deep channel-hole etch, staircase contacts) to build 300-500 tier vertical-channel IGZO 2T0C gain cells, with a string-select scheme giving random access per tier and aggressive refresh.
note: NAND-style deposition stacking could give >10x cost/bit; random access per tier and IGZO vertical-channel uniformity at 300+ tiers are big doubts.

title: Crested-barrier capacitor: the capacitor is its own access switch
idea: Inverts 'storage and switch are separate devices': each crossbar node is a floating metal nanolayer between two crested tunnel barriers (e.g., nitride/AlN/nitride trilayers) whose peak collapses at high field, giving ~10^12 current change between the ~3 V write and ~1 V hold; charge on the floating layer is the bit, written in ns by tunneling and read capacitively, from one blanket deposition per deck.
note: Transistor-free, capacitor-tower-free 4F2 decks from blanket depositions would cut cost/bit >10x; doubt: capacitive crossbar readout and 1e12 write/hold contrast.

title: Clam growth-line oscillating bath deposits the whole tier superlattice nonstop
idea: Clam shells lay periodic growth bands from a self-oscillating cycle; engineer the spontaneous potential oscillations known in Cu/Cu2O electrodeposition so a single bath alternates metal wordline layers and oxide-semiconductor layers ~15 nm thick, forming 100 tier pairs in one run with no valve switching, vacuum or tool transfer.
note: Novel use of Cu/Cu2O self-oscillation for tiers; device-grade layers and 300 mm uniformity very doubtful.

title: Optical-disc molding lines make spiral-crossbar memory discs
idea: The optical-disc industry collapsed under streaming, idling injection-molding lines that replicate ~100 nm grooves into a disc every ~3 seconds for cents. Mold one disc with clockwise and one with counter-clockwise sub-one-turn spiral grooves, metallize and polish them, and laminate the discs around a threshold-switching memory film so each pair of spirals crosses exactly once, with both line families reaching a CMOS hub chip bonded at the center.
note: Cheap molded patterning is clever, but cm-long lines and a 200k x 200k passive crossbar defeat speed and selectivity.

title: Kintaro-ame candy draw: shrink a macro array into nanopillars
idea: Kintaro-ame candy hides a face in a log that is stretched and sliced. Build a centimeter-scale preform of glass, metal and semiconductor rods laid out as a DRAM capacitor and bitline cross-section, draw it ~10,000x on a fiber draw tower into a fused multi-core rod, then slice it perpendicular into dies whose pillars already have 100:1+ length, and bond them to a transistor wafer.
note: Drawing a macro preform into aligned nanopillars is a striking idea; draw distortion and registration to transistor arrays need a miracle.

title: Brighton-rock drawn preform sliced into ready-made capacitor wafers
idea: Like seaside rock candy whose lettering is built large and drawn thin, stack a 10 cm glass preform holding thousands of coaxial metal/glass/metal rods, draw and re-stack-draw it (fiber-optic faceplate practice) ~10^5x down to ~40 nm pitch, then saw and polish 10 um slices carrying billions of coaxial capacitors to bond onto transistor wafers.
note: Zero-litho capacitor slices from fiber draw; doubt: metal cores break up at sub-100 nm and registration to transistors is unachievable.

title: Undiced wafer-scale DRAM face-bonded to a wafer-scale accelerator
idea: Jump from die to wafer: keep the 300-mm DRAM wafer whole, use programmable links stitched at each reticle boundary to route around dead mats, and hybrid-bond it face-to-face to a wafer-scale compute wafer so each compute tile gets a multi-GB slab directly above it. No dicing kerf, packages, TSVs or PHYs.
note: TB-scale memory at ~0.1 pJ/bit via W2W bond; doubt: wafer-scale yield, thermal coupling, and fab access.

title: Substitute diced packaged memory with wafer-on-wafer bonding and redundancy routing
idea: Bond a whole DRAM wafer to a whole accelerator wafer without dicing, and route around defective DRAM tiles through a configurable redundancy fabric on the logic side, so no known-good-die test or per-die packaging is needed.
note: ~0.1 pJ/bit at 1-2 um bond pitch is a real 10x+ energy win; widely pursued, and thermal/yield coupling of wafers is the doubt.

title: Minify the data path: each mat bonds straight down to logic
idea: Hybrid-bond every DRAM mat's local I/O directly to the logic die below at 1-2 um pitch, removing global datalines and the PHY, for a 65,536-bit-wide interface at about 250 MHz.
note: Per-mat bonding cuts I/O to ~0.1 pJ/bit (~30x); known direction (SeDRAM-style), so novelty is limited.

title: Pure-play DRAM foundry serving fabless memory designers
idea: Rearrange IDM into foundry: a fab offers a DRAM process (cells, capacitors, buried wordline) as a service with a PDK. Fabless firms and hyperscalers then design their own arrays and periphery, with custom page sizes, banks and interfaces.
note: TSMC-style split could add a supply source; doubt: DRAM design/process coupling is tight and PSMC-style DRAM foundry already exists.

title: Fifteen-minute city: a private DRAM tile bonded over every core
idea: Urbanists keep essentials within a short walk; hybrid-bond at 1 um pitch a 64 MB 3D DRAM tile directly above each compute-core cluster so its data travels under 100 um vertically through ~10k bonds with 0.3 V signalling, with no PHY, SerDes or interposer.
note: Per-core hybrid-bonded DRAM tiles cut transport energy >10x; widely pursued (SoIC/WoW); thermal and yield coupling are doubts.

title: Dumbwaiter: per-mat vertical bond shafts replace global data buses
idea: A dumbwaiter carries food straight up to each floor instead of through the halls. Give every mat its own column of hybrid bonds to a logic die stacked directly above, so data leaves the local sense amps vertically over ~10 um instead of crossing mm-long global I/O lines, serializers and the PHY.
note: Vertical per-mat bonds remove global I/O and PHY energy ~10x; direction already pursued (wafer-on-wafer DRAM, logic-on-DRAM stacking).

title: Wafer-on-wafer DRAM-on-logic accelerators with no package wiring
idea: Worsen: dice wafers, then reconnect chips with long package wires on CTE-mismatched substrates. Flip: hybrid-bond a whole DRAM wafer onto a whole logic wafer (all silicon, CTE-matched) with redundant tiles, so every logic tile has its own memory slab above it and package-level interconnect disappears.
note: ~10x I/O energy cut, but WoW DRAM-on-logic already shipped (UniIC SeDRAM) and pursued by majors.

title: Wafer-on-wafer memory with no PHY, DLL, or pads
idea: Scale jump from die to wafer: bond a whole DRAM wafer face-to-face onto the accelerator wafer so each mat talks to logic through sub-um bonds; there are no DQ drivers, DLLs, ESD diodes, pads or SerDes, and defective mats are bypassed by wafer-level rerouting.
note: ~30x lower I/O energy by bonding DRAM wafer to logic; known path (WOW, SoIC), with yield, thermal and die-size matching as doubts.

title: One hybrid-bond pad per mat: a million vertical channels, no TSVs
idea: Jump from 1024 TSVs per HBM die to ~10^6 hybrid-bond pads at 1-um pitch, giving every DRAM mat its own vertical channel into the compute die directly below. There is no TSV keep-out and no SerDes, and wires are ~10 um long.
note: Mat-granular hybrid-bonded DRAM on compute cuts transport energy >10x; widely pursued, thermal and yield coupling are the doubts.

title: Bank-per-tile memory: DRAM bank footprint equals one compute tile
idea: IFR: 'every operand already sits on top of its ALU.' Backward: lay out a DRAM wafer whose bank grid exactly matches the accelerator's tile grid and face-to-face hybrid-bond it, each bank with a private ~4,000-bond vertical port, so a tile reads only its own bank across ~5 um.
note: 10-30x I/O energy cut is real but already pursued (SeDRAM, SoIC); needs wafer partners.

title: PHY-less bonding: sense amplifiers drive logic registers directly
idea: Ideal: memory bits appear in the processor's registers with no interface at all. Closest achievable: hybrid-bond the DRAM array face-down onto logic at 1-2 um pitch so each sense-amp latch connects through its own bond to a logic-side flip-flop, deleting DQ drivers, SerDes, DLLs and the global data bus.
note: Per-sense-amp bonding deletes PHY/global bus, ~50x link energy cut; widely pursued by majors, needs DRAM wafer access beyond $1M.

title: No global datalines: each subarray bonds straight to logic die
idea: Limit: no bank-level global I/O buses or secondary sense amps. Each subarray's SA stripe has its own local hybrid-bond pads (~0.5 um pitch, ~1e5 per die) that land directly on the logic or accelerator die, so data leaves through the shortest vertical wire.
note: Subarray-direct bonds to logic cut pJ/bit ~6x; already pursued (SeDRAM-style bonded DRAM), needs DRAM wafers.

title: Trim each leaky cell's Vt via access-gate charge trap
idea: Substitute worst-case refresh with per-cell repair. The access gate stack includes a thin nitride trap layer; after retention test, the ppm of tail cells are programmed by hot-carrier injection at their bitline-side edge (bitline biased as drain). That raises their source-barrier Vt by ~150-200 mV without adding storage-side GIDL, and the trapped charge holds for years, as in SONOS.

title: Substitute separate memory die with DRAM built in logic wafer backside
idea: After the backside-power-delivery thinning step that 2 nm-class logic already performs, deposit an oxide-TFT plus MIM-capacitor array in the backside dielectric under the compute tiles, wired through the nano-TSVs the BSPDN flow already etches.
note: Very low energy, but capacity limited to under-die area.

title: Gen-8.5 LCD lines plus panel nanoimprint for oxide gain-cell tiles
idea: Combine written-off display-TFT fabs (oxide sputter and 2.2x2.5 m glass handling) with panel-scale nanoimprint at ~200 nm rules, and build 2T0C oxide gain-cell tiles on glass. The tiles are diced and bonded as a slow capacity tier (~50-100 ns) for cold KV-cache and embeddings.

title: Beamlet-failure-tolerant multi-beam direct write for array layers
idea: Combine massively parallel e-beam writers with cell-level error tolerance: ~1% of beamlets may be dead or drifting with no per-beam correction or redundant rescan. The wafer shifts by a sub-pitch offset each pass so a dead beamlet scatters into isolated bad cells rather than whole lines.

title: Drawn metal-cored glass preform sliced into via-dense interposers
idea: Combine optical-fiber preform drawing with interposer making: stack thousands of metal-cored glass rods into a preform (Taylor-wire process), draw it down until cores reach 5-10 um pitch, fuse into a boule and slice/polish it into wafers, each a through-glass-via interposer with millions of vias; the draw tower cools with N2/forced air rather than helium.
note: Draw-sliced via plates skip drilling; core registration and Cu/glass CTE are doubts.

title: Check-valve cell: two opposing wide-bandgap diodes plus gain read
idea: Adapted from fluid check valves and the Tesla valve: the storage node is filled through one wide-bandgap diode from a 'fill' line and drained through a second, oppositely oriented diode to an 'empty' line. In hold, both lines park so both diodes are reverse-biased, and a read transistor gated by the storage node senses state without disturbing it.

title: Leaky-capacitor analog activation counter per row stops row hammer
idea: MINIFY the row-hammer tracker from multi-KB SRAM count tables to ~2 transistors and one tiny capacitor per wordline driver: each ACT pumps in a fixed charge packet, a calibrated leak drains it with a ~64 ms time constant, and crossing threshold raises a neighbor-refresh request.
note: A leaky capacitor per row counts activations cheaply; leak variation and temperature undermine the threshold.

title: Magnify the cell 20x on display glass: 100 fF planar capacitors
idea: Use LTPO display lines (oxide-TFT cells plus LTPS CMOS periphery) on Gen-8.5 glass at ~1.5 um rules, with planar high-k MIM capacitors of ~100 fF, 20x a silicon DRAM cell. Sense margins become so wide that raw BER is negligible without ECC.

title: Image sensor run backward: pinned-diode memory with floating-diffusion readout
idea: Reverse the pixel: in a U.S. CMOS image-sensor fab, a 4T pixel's fully depleted pinned photodiode stores electrically injected charge instead of photo-charge; reading is complete transfer to a floating diffusion and a source follower onto the column with correlated double sampling, and reverse transfer restores the bit.
note: CIS pinned diodes give long retention without tall caps; density ~10-14F2 limits it to energy tiers.

title: Public golden DRAM array mask set, one private mask
idea: Policy: fund an open, government-owned reference DRAM array mask set and process (the cell, capacitor and bitline layers) that any U.S. fab or startup can license, each differentiating with one private periphery or personalization mask, reversing DRAM from closed IP to shared infrastructure.
note: Open PDK-style shared array process; process know-how, not masks, is the real barrier.

title: Merging: dual-gate access devices decode 1024 rows with 64 drivers
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging moves the last decode stage into the cells: each oxide-TFT access device has a bottom gate tied to a group plate (32 groups) and a top gate tied to an in-group line strapped across groups (32 lines), and conducts only when both are high, so 1024 wordlines need 64 drivers instead of 1024 sub-wordline drivers.
note: Half-select disturb and the dual-gate Vt window are the key risks.

title: Pinned buried-well cells borrowed from image-sensor photodiodes
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying (from CMOS image sensors): store each bit as electrons in a fully depleted buried n-well capped by a p+ pinning layer, the trick that brings photodiode dark current to a few e-/s. A transfer gate dumps the packet onto a floating diffusion and source follower shared by 8 vertically stacked wells, read with correlated double sampling.
note: Image-sensor pinning cuts generation leakage; doubt: full-well charge at DRAM pitch.

title: Mitochondrial cristae ribs fold lateral capacitors into short 3D cells
idea: Cristae multiply membrane area by inward folds; build each lateral capacitor tier from a mini-superlattice of three SiGe sub-layers with different Ge content, so the single lateral wet recess carves a rib-and-groove cavity and the electrode/dielectric deposited into it gains ~3x area per unit length.

title: Chromatophore retroreflector I/O: memory modulates a broadcast light sheet
idea: One off-package laser floods the top of the memory stack with light. An array of electro-absorption or MEMS 'pigment cell' shutters over cat's-eye retroreflectors modulates that light and sends it back to a photodetector array on the host. The DRAM drives only a ~fF capacitive shutter, the way a chromatophore expands a pigment sac, and has no laser or heat of its own.
note: Needs GHz EAM on DRAM die; MEMS shutters far too slow.

title: Video P-frames: delta bitlines swing only when data changes
idea: Video codecs send only what changed between frames; skip bitline equalization between successive activations in a subarray and sense each new row against the bitline's previous value with a dummy-cell reference, so a bitline toggles only where the new row differs, while the controller orders correlated rows back to back.

title: Fiber-drawn copper-in-glass microwire umbilical for off-package memory
idea: Draw a glass preform holding thousands of copper rods (the Taylor-wire version of optical fiber drawing) into a flexible 'umbilical' with ~10,000 isolated conductors per mm². Polished end faces hybrid-bond to pads, so memory stacks can sit 1-3 cm away instead of on the interposer.
note: Taylor-wire bundle as hybrid-bondable cable; pad registration of drawn cores is the doubt.

title: Bell Labs electret back-gate holds access devices deeply off
idea: Revive Sessler and West's 1962 Bell Labs foil electret: implant a permanent negative trapped-charge layer, charged by corona or electron beam, into the Al2O3/SiO2 buried oxide under thin-body access transistors. This gives a built-in ~1 V reverse back bias with no charge pump, on U.S. FD-SOI lines; a boosted front-gate pulse restores on-current.
note: Trapped-charge stability at temperature and required density are doubts.

title: Bucket-brigade analog strings storing multilevel weights in tiers
idea: Revive the 1969 Philips bucket-brigade delay line from echo pedals: vertical strings of discrete capacitor-plus-transistor stages pass analog charge packets holding 4-bit levels, read by a string-foot ADC, with ~1% level errors from charge loss tolerated by inference weights.

title: Drum-style lockstep weight broadcast replaces replicated HBM weight copies
idea: Revive the magnetic-drum principle, where data circulates past many fixed heads: keep ONE copy of model weights in a pod-level pool and stream it every token step over a DWDM optical broadcast (passive 1:64 splitters). All inference replicas consume the same rotating stream in lockstep and hold only a small sliding window locally. A 100 GB model at 50 steps/s needs ~40 Tb/s, about four 100-channel fibers.
note: Optical lockstep broadcast of one weight copy to many replicas; 40 Tb/s ingest per pod and lockstep scheduling are the doubts.

title: Goto parametron revival: phase-encoded links pumped by shared resonant clock
idea: Each link endpoint is a varactor parametric oscillator pumped at 2f by a package-wide resonant LC clock grid; a bit is the 0 or pi phase of the subharmonic oscillation, seeded by a tiny injection and amplified by pump energy, so there is no rail-to-rail driver.
note: High-Q resonators limit per-lane rate to ~f/Q; on-chip LC Q caps energy recovery.

title: CCD memory revival: bucket-brigade charge conveyors replace HBM global datalines
idea: Build buried-channel CCD lanes in the HBM core and base dies that shift whole rows of charge packets from banks to the PHY with three-phase resonant clocks, sensing only at the lane end, instead of precharging and swinging long global I/O lines.
note: Charge-transfer efficiency over long lanes and DRAM-process compatibility unproven.

title: Trim each leaky access transistor once, like programming flash
idea: Inverts 'the leakage tail is frozen at fab-out': add a thin nitride trap layer in the access-transistor gate stack; at wafer test retention-profile every cell and apply a one-time hot-carrier program pulse only to the ~0.1% tail cells, raising their Vt by 150-300 mV so their OFF current falls 10-100x. A BIST mode re-trims in the field as cells age.
note: Flash-like one-time Vt trim of tail cells; trap layer may add VRT and disturb.

title: Lopsided access transistor: wide-gap storage-side contact kills GIDL
idea: Inverts 'the access transistor is symmetric': replace only the storage-node-side source/drain extension with a thin wide-gap oxide semiconductor contact, so the gate-to-storage overlap, where GIDL band-to-band tunneling dominates, sits in a >3 eV material while the bitline side stays silicon for drive current.
note: Si/oxide-semiconductor interface traps may add TAT leakage; contact resistance unclear.

title: Virtual cells: unpatterned film where fields, not etches, isolate bits
idea: Inverts 'each access transistor is a patterned island': deposit a blanket, unetched oxide-semiconductor film over crossing gate grids, and bias a 'fence' grid negative so it depletes the film around every crossing, electrostatically forming isolated storage pockets and access channels; each tier needs only metal-line masks, no active-area or channel etch.

title: Leaky charge-packet activation counter cell in every row
idea: Inverting 'row-hammer tracking needs digital counters': each row gets one extra cell in a counter column that receives a fixed charge packet on every activation instead of being restored; the same sense amp compares it to a threshold during activate, refreshing neighbors and resetting it when crossed, while natural leakage forgets old activations like a sliding window.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembly patterns capacitors, defects absorbed by codes
idea: Inverts 'every pillar must print perfectly': pattern the honeycomb storage-node array with directed self-assembly on a 193i guide pattern; DSA's notorious ~0.1-1% missing or merged pillars, long a blocker, now fall within the cell error budget.
note: Pairs DSA's known defectivity with array-level coding budget; placement error and 1% defects stress ECC overhead.

title: Image-sensor floating-diffusion readout replaces bitline charge sharing
idea: First principles: a 5 fF cell at 0.5 V holds ~15,600 e-, yet CMOS image sensors resolve ~1 e- because they fully TRANSFER charge onto a ~0.5 fF floating diffusion instead of sharing it with a ~40 fF bitline. Build the DRAM cell as a pinned storage node + transfer gate into a floating diffusion shared by 4-8 cells, read by a local source follower (~300 uV/e-), so a ~500 e- (0.1 fF) cell gives a ~150 mV signal.
note: Full charge transfer cuts Cs needs; junction dark current at ~500 e- and shared readout area are the doubts.

title: Bitline segments become the successive-approximation capacitor DAC
idea: For multi-level read, split each bitline into binary-weighted segments (1:2:4 units of cells) with segment switches and perform charge-redistribution SAR using the bitline's own parasitic capacitance as the DAC; the parasitic that normally kills signal becomes the converter's reference.
note: Bitline parasitic used as the SAR DAC; MLC DRAM margins and retention remain the risk.

title: Area-cheap foil cells: planar 8 fF capacitors without high aspect
idea: Fabricate 1T1C arrays roll-to-roll on polyimide by UV nanoimprint at ~1 um features, using a flat 1 um^2 metal/AlOx(10 nm, spatial ALD)/metal capacitor per cell and a printed oxide TFT access device.
note: Physics checks out (8 fF flat, ns charging); multilayer R2R registration, yield and periphery integration are the doubts.

title: Bit-plane split: MSBs in silicon, LSBs on glass
idea: The bits of a weight or activation differ in importance by powers of two, so they need not share a medium. Keep sign, exponent and top mantissa bits in silicon DRAM and the low mantissa planes in a glass-TFT tier with relaxed retention and no ECC; both are read in parallel and recombined on the fly, and LSB errors cost little accuracy.
note: Fresh split of bit significance across media; glass-tier latency matching is the doubt.

title: Stained glass: ferroelectric memory panels from Gen-8.5 display fabs
idea: Random stimulus 'stained glass' (large panes, assembled) -> 1T1C ferroelectric memory with IGZO thin-film transistors and HZO capacitors is made on 2.2 x 2.5 m glass panels in display fabs, then the panels are diced into CXL memory tiles for a capacity tier.

title: Freestanding single-crystal SrTiO3 membranes bonded as planar DRAM capacitors
idea: [Box: paraelectric perovskite charge | Si 4F2 VCT | charge-share SA | low-temperature membrane bonding | SrTiO3 donor wafer | epitaxy + water-soluble Sr3Al2O6 release] Grow epitaxial SrRuO3/SrTiO3 at ~700 C on a donor, free it by dissolving a Sr3Al2O6 sacrificial layer, and bond the membrane onto the finished transistor array below 300 C, then pattern planar or <=10:1 capacitors with k~150-300. The crystal's thermal budget never touches the access transistor or lower tiers.
note: Wafer-scale membrane bonding and thin-film k dead layer are doubts.

title: Mux-in-array, sense-out-of-array: oxide-mux array die bonded at micron pitch
idea: Box: Si capacitor charge x BCAT x sense amps moved to a separate logic die x wafer-to-wafer hybrid bond at 1 um pitch x Si x array die fabbed with array plus BEOL IGZO 1:32 bitline multiplexers only. Because bonding cannot reach 30 nm bitline pitch, each bond pad serves 32 bitlines through an oxide-transistor mux, while sense amps, decoders and I/O come from a cheap mature-node logic wafer.

title: Po: array runs on 0.4 V — Marx-stacked bitline sampling
idea: Po: an array that runs on 0.4 V. Drop VARY to ~0.4 V; after charge sharing, the bitline differential is sampled onto four small capacitors in parallel, which are then switched into series like a Marx generator, presenting ~4x the voltage to a latch that restores to 0.4 V.
note: Marx-style series stacking of sampled differential; sampling caps steal charge or add kT/C noise.

title: Po: the periphery is the product — open bonded interface
idea: Po: a DRAM company that makes no memory cells. Define an open JEDEC-style hybrid-bonding contract between array wafers and periphery wafers (pad map, analog bitline/wordline electrical specs, timing), so any foundry or new U.S. entrant can build periphery dies that pair with any vendor's array wafers.

title: Harvest HBM stacks from retired accelerators onto new boards
idea: Po: dead GPUs are memory mines. Run a laser-assisted debond and reball line that lifts HBM stacks off retired or failed accelerator interposers, re-tests them, and mounts them on a low-cost organic carrier as CXL or inference memory modules.
note: Debonding microbumped HBM from interposers and re-carrying 1024-bit buses on organic is hard; supply gain could be real.

title: Display-fab TFT-on-glass capacitor memory panels
idea: Worsen: insist all working memory comes from 12 nm EUV wafers. Flip: build 1T1C cells with oxide TFTs on Gen-10.5 display glass at micron design rules and stack panels as a slow, multi-level bulk tier behind a small DRAM cache.
note: Micron-rule 1T1C cells are ~25 um2 not 1 um2, so $/GB falls far short; slow tier competes with NAND.

title: Charge-trap trimming raises threshold of only the leakiest transistors
idea: Worse: let the one-in-a-million leaky access transistor set refresh for the whole chip. Flip: include a thin Si3N4 trap layer in the access-gate stack; at test, cells flagged as leaky get a Fowler-Nordheim program pulse via their wordline and bitline that traps electrons and raises their Vt ~0.3 V, permanently pulling them out of the tail.
note: Programming leaky cells' Vt at test removes the tail; trap stability in the access gate is the doubt.

title: Fresco artist: Taylor-drawn metal-in-glass via plates
idea: Fresco pigment bonds into lime and lasts centuries: draw a bundle of glass tubes filled with copper or silver, as in the Taylor-wire process, into a rod with millions of 5 um metal cores, then slice it into via wafers so the conductors are sealed inside glass with no polymer.

title: Contactless charge-shift KV-cache memory printed with gratings only
idea: Extreme user: AI KV-cache, written sequentially and read in streams. Store it in a CCD-like charge-transfer register (parallel gate lines over a buried channel clocked to shift packets to an edge sense amp) with no per-cell contacts, capacitors or vias, so every dense layer is a 1D grating printable by immersion SAQP or nanoimprint.

title: Porous-silicon sacrificial tiers replace SiGe in 3D DRAM stacks
idea: Scale shift from bulk electrochemistry (porous Si for MEMS and solar) to 3D-DRAM tier formation: grow alternating heavily boron-doped and lightly doped Si epilayers, anodize only the heavy layers into porous Si through slit trenches, then oxidize or etch them away to release lateral access-transistor layers, avoiding scarce Ge and SiGe misfit defects.

title: Rank-order sensing of constant-weight codes needs no threshold
idea: Time jump: let charge decay for minutes, because only ordering matters; data is stored in 8-cell groups as a 4-of-8 constant-weight code (70 words, ~6 bits) and a winner-take-all sense circuit picks the four highest-charge cells. Decay shifts absolute levels but not the order until the weakest '1' meets the strongest '0', so optimizer state rewritten each training step never needs refresh.
note: Rank modulation (flash) applied to DRAM decay; tail cells still bound the window.

title: Sell DRAM by the perishable byte-second
idea: Datacenter-scale business model: memory is priced per byte-second of guaranteed retention; 'perishable' refresh-free SKUs ship with no refresh engine and a certified 10 s window at a 30-40% discount, and tenants pay a premium only for data that must outlive it, served from NV tiers.

title: Bond-pad interleaving makes 1% dead hybrid bonds correctable
idea: Shift the error budget from the cell scale to the bond scale: each codeword's bits are spread across many hybrid-bond pads, so a pad lost to a particle or void looks like scattered bit errors that the 1%-tolerant code already fixes. Bonding then runs with relaxed cleanliness and planarity and no spare-pad repair.

title: Contactless capacitive stacking through 1 um dies, link errors folded in
idea: Replace data TSVs with capacitive couplers across dies thinned to ~1 um: the coupled signal is marginal (raw link BER ~1e-3), but it is simply added to the 1% cell error budget and corrected by the same code. Dies join by oxide-oxide fusion bonding, with only a few large vias for power.
note: Folding link BER into the cell ECC budget is the twist; 1 um dies are extreme.

title: MeRAM timing fixed with NMR-style composite write pulses
idea: Inston's voltage-controlled MeRAM stalled because precessional VCMA switching needs pulse widths exact to ~50 ps, and the anisotropy spread from cell to cell caused write errors. Borrow NMR composite pulses: a three-segment voltage sequence (90-180-90 equivalent precession angles) whose errors cancel to first order in both pulse width and anisotropy.
note: NMR composite pulses to cancel width/anisotropy errors is a non-obvious transfer; precession nonlinearity may limit first-order cancellation.

title: PLEDM resurrected with one epitaxial CaF2 tunnel barrier
idea: Hitachi's PLEDM vertical gain cell used a stack of Si3N4/poly-Si tunnel barriers, which made writes slow and the process complex. Replace the stack with one ~1.5 nm CaF2 barrier, grown epitaxially and lattice-matched on Si under the storage node. A surrounding gate bends the Si bands to open tunneling for writes. Because the barrier is a trap-free crystal, the off-state has no trap-assisted tunneling tail.
note: Epitaxial CaF2 on Si is real; gate-modulated tunneling with fast writes unproven.

title: SONOS charge traps repurposed to trim leaky-tail access transistors
idea: SONOS and nanocrystal flash lost on retention and slow programming, neither of which matters if a cell is programmed about once a year. Add a nitride charge-trap layer to the gate stack of the buried-wordline access transistor. After retention test, use hot-carrier pulses to inject electrons into only the ~0.01% of tail transistors, raising their Vt by ~150 mV and pulling them out of the leakage tail.
note: Once-a-year charge-trap Vt trim of only tail transistors clips the refresh-setting tail; doubt: nitride in gate stack adding traps.

title: Time-to-latch sensing rescues Z-RAM floating-body margin
idea: Failure mined: Innovative Silicon's Z-RAM read the parasitic bipolar current of a floating body, and the 0/1 current difference shrank below sense-amp offset at 32 nm. Fix: read the delay until the parasitic BJT latches under a fixed bias ramp. That delay depends exponentially on stored body charge, and a time-to-digital converter shared by 16 bitlines digitizes it.
note: Exponential latch delay turns small body-charge differences into timing, but Z-RAM also failed on retention and variability.

title: CCD memory resurrected for AI weight streaming, where serial access wins
idea: Fairchild and Intel CCD memories (1970s, up to 256 kb) died because serial access gave long latency versus random-access DRAM. AI inference streams weights and KV pages sequentially, so build loops of 1k-4k charge-transfer stages per bitline that burst at GHz rates into one sense amp; cells are contactless overlapping-gate wells with no capacitor stack and no per-cell tungsten contact.
note: Serial-access fit for weight streaming; CTE over thousands of transfers.

title: Quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3 makes planar storage capacitors at 77 K
idea: Effect walk: quantum paraelectricity. Below ~100 K, SrTiO3 (or KTaO3) permittivity climbs into the thousands because quantum fluctuations suppress the ferroelectric transition, so a 10-nm epitaxial film on a planar cell stores 5 fF in a small fraction of today's area; at 77 K the access-transistor leakage tail also drops by >10^6.
note: Quantum-paraelectric STO plus 77 K; thin-film k collapse is the risk.

title: Idle LCD panel fabs print multi-tier oxide memory on glass
idea: Effect: wide-bandgap suppression of intrinsic carrier generation (n_i ~ exp(-Eg/2kT)) gives oxide transistors minutes-long retention even at 1 um rules. Retool idle Gen-8.5 LCD lines, which already run <=350 C oxide TFT processes with i-line litho, to stack 8 tiers of 2T0C gain cells on 5.5 m2 glass, about 0.7 TB per panel.
note: Idle LCD capacity as memory fab; density at i-line rules likely 5x optimistic.

title: Hydrogen-anneal surface migration forms stacked silicon-on-nothing tiers for 3D DRAM
idea: Effect: surface-energy-driven Si migration in H2. Etch a lattice of deep holes with periodic diameter modulation (scallops), then anneal in H2 at ~1100 C: surface diffusion closes each scallop into a flat buried void, giving several single-crystal Si sheets separated by empty plates (multi-layer silicon-on-nothing). Filling the voids with oxide yields 3D DRAM tiers without a 100+ layer Si/SiGe epitaxial superlattice.

title: NbO2 Mott tripwire integrates row activations, fires neighbor refresh
idea: Effect: Mott insulator-metal transition. Each wordline strap gets a tiny RC node that receives a fixed charge packet per activation and leaks with a ~64 ms time constant; an NbO2 threshold switch (Mott transition ~800 C, so stable at 95 C, unlike VO2) across the node snaps metallic once the node crosses ~0.6 V (about N activations within the window) and pulses a refresh-request line for the two neighboring rows. The result is an analog, self-decaying per-row counter of ~100 nm^2 with no SRAM tracker tables.
note: Self-decaying Mott/RC counter per row replaces tracker tables; per-row device variability is the doubt.

title: Latch resolution time becomes LDPC soft information for weak cells
idea: Effect: regenerative metastability, where a latch's resolution time grows as log(1/input). A time-to-digital tap shared across 8 sense amps records how fast each SA resolved, giving a per-bit confidence (LLR) to a soft-decision LDPC decoder over a 2 KB page, so raw BER ~1e-3 becomes acceptable versus ~1e-6 for SECDED.
note: Resolution time gives soft info in one destructive sense; 10x density claim far-fetched.

title: Oxygen-vacancy back gate trims every leaky row after test
idea: Effect: field-driven oxygen-vacancy drift in HfOx. Each stacked thin-film tier has a back-gate dielectric of oxygen-deficient HfOx; after retention test, a forming-like pulse drifts vacancies toward or away from the channel, permanently shifting a tail row's Vt by ~+100 mV: a non-volatile per-row analog leakage fuse.
note: Per-row nonvolatile Vt trim could rescue broad-spread thin-film tiers; vacancy retention at temperature is doubtful.

title: Ti: NiTi shape-memory micro-clamps make HBM stacks test-then-commit
idea: Pattern sputtered NiTi micro-spring fingers on interposer pads that stay open at room temperature and clamp onto HBM microbump arrays when warmed past Af (~70 C); the whole package is run at speed while clamped, bad stacks are released by cooling and swapped, and only then is permanent underfill/reflow committed.
note: SMA micro-springs at microbump pitch unproven; test-before-commit is the real value.

title: Overflow fusion-draw glass panels host U.S.-made panel DRAM
idea: Display glass is made by overflow fusion draw in Kentucky; on those 3 m panels, use U.S.-built i-line steppers and PECVD to stack 8-16 tiers of indium-free oxide gain-cell DRAM at ~1 um features, getting density from stacking and panel area instead of shrinking.
note: Display-fab stacked gain cells at ~1 um; ~$5-8/GB slow CXL tier, but beats only contract price, not $1.48 cost.

title: MLCC laminate: interdigitated plates replace the tall pillar capacitor
idea: Copy multilayer-ceramic-capacitor stacking: deposit ~30 alternating TiN and Ru electrode layers separated by 5 nm high-k into a 300 nm stack, cut per-cell blocks, then selectively recess Ru on one sidewall and TiN on the other with different wet chemistries so each wall contacts only odd or only even plates.

title: Memory inside the glass-core package substrate beneath the processor
idea: IFR: 'memory takes zero extra package area and sits millimeters from compute.' Backward: deposit several oxide-semiconductor gain-cell tiers directly on the glass core of the package substrate (flat, 400 C tolerant), then build the redistribution layers on top, so the GPU's own substrate becomes a multi-GB memory plane reached through micro-bumps.
note: Gain-cell tiers on glass core at panel litho give low density per layer; yield over large panels is a doubt.

title: Contamination-tolerant oxide memory built in warehouse-grade cleanrooms
idea: Ideal: memory that can be built in a garage. Closest: pick cell materials (wide-gap oxide channels, Al2O3, Mo) whose leakage is insensitive to Fe/Cu/Na at 10-100x semiconductor limits, and run them in ISO-6 sealed-minienvironment 'warehouse fabs' with display/solar-grade chemicals and gases costing ~5-10x less than ppt-grade.
note: Treats impurity tolerance as a materials design axis to cut cleanroom/UPW/chemical cost; particles still kill dies.

title: Millisecond DRAM: tiny capacitors legal because data dies young
idea: Ideal: a capacitor that stores just enough charge for exactly as long as needed. Closest achievable: specify a die class with ~1 fF cells (aspect ratio ~15:1 instead of 60-75:1) guaranteed for only ~2 ms retention, sold exclusively behind a TTL/streaming interface that refuses allocations longer than 1 ms, so it is never refreshed.
note: Retention tail and sense margin at 1 fF are the doubt; TTL interface makes refresh-free legal.

title: Freestanding epitaxial SrTiO3 membranes transferred as k-300 capacitor dielectric
idea: Scarcity rule: no dielectric with k below 100. Grow single-crystal SrTiO3/BaSrTiO3 on a water-soluble Sr3Al2O6 sacrificial layer, release wafer-scale membranes, and bond them onto the DRAM transistor array below 400 C; the dead-layer-free crystal keeps k ~300 at 10 nm so planar or 3:1 caps reach 5 fF.
note: Freestanding STO membranes avoid dead layer; per-cell electrode contact and planar area still limit Cs.

title: Thresholds must move only twice per idle: ferroelectric Vt-parking access transistor
idea: Limit: leakage may be killed only by a stored state, not by continuous bias. Embed a thin HZO layer in the access gate stack. Before a long idle, one global pulse polarizes it so every access transistor's Vt rises ~0.5 V ('parked', ~1e8 lower subthreshold leakage); an un-park pulse restores the low Vt before access. Ferroelectric endurance is spent only on rare idle transitions.
note: Global park pulse may disturb stored charge; FE in gate stack adds traps and Vt spread.

title: Borrow the image sensor's darkness: pinned storage diode with transfer gate
idea: Limit: the storage node may never touch an oxide interface. Store the bit as electrons in a buried n-well under a p+ pinning layer, as in a 4T CMOS image-sensor pixel, and write and read it through a transfer gate to a floating-diffusion sense node with a gain transistor. Pinning eliminates interface-state generation, which is how image sensors reach dark currents of ~1e-18 A per pixel.

title: Doping-superlattice 3D DRAM: porosify p+ layers instead of SiGe
idea: Constraint: no SiGe epitaxy, because strain caps the tier count. Grow fast all-silicon epi with alternating p+/p- doping, then electrochemically porosify only the p+ layers from the vertical-bitline slit to open lateral cavities for capacitors and gates, allowing 100+ tiers without strain relaxation.
note: Dopant-selective porosification avoids SiGe strain; dopant interdiffusion over 100 tiers is the doubt.

title: No Spruce Pine quartz: dirtier wafers paid for with ECC
idea: Imposed limit: no high-purity Spruce Pine crucibles. Grow CZ ingots in synthetic-silica or multiply reused crucibles and accept higher oxygen and metal content, which fattens the retention tail. Compensate with per-die retention fingerprinting, two-rate refresh and a stronger on-die RS code (16-bit symbols per 256 B), turning a purity spec into an ECC budget.
note: Turning crucible purity into an ECC budget relieves Spruce Pine dependence; metal contamination effects uncertain.

title: IGZO gated-diode strip: a capacitor-module-free 3D DRAM tier ('two-gate NAND-like DRAM')
idea: Each tier holds a horizontal GAA IGZO (or IGO) strip with two gates: an access wordline and a plate gate. Write '1': with the wordline on and the bitline at 0 V, electrons accumulate under the positively biased plate. Write '0': with the bitline high, the well stays empty. Read: precharge the bitline, open the wordline, pull the plate low, and the stored electrons transfer completely to the bitline. A '0' moves almost nothing because a fully depleted 10 nm IGZO film has near-zero depletion capacitance. The plate is a row-shared line driven at 2.5 V, so the signal is set by the plate swing, not VARY, and the bitline can run at ~0.45 V. Built like Kioxia's SiN-replacement horizontal IGZO tiers: both gates are word-plane metal, and no lateral recess-and-fill capacitor module is needed.

title: BEOL bonus tiers: oxide gain-cell tiers stacked on a finished Si DRAM die
idea: Take a conventional 1-beta-class DRAM die, give ~15% of its area to extra sense and write-verify circuits, and after its last metal and hydrogen alloy anneal, seal it with an Al2O3/SiN hydrogen barrier and deposit 8 tiers of oxide gain cells (coax 4F2 B3-04, or vertical 2T0C) over the whole die, periphery included. The fast Si 1T1C array remains the hot tier (~15 ns), and the oxide tiers above form a dense, low-refresh warm tier (~30-50 ns) in the same package and interface. The add-on is a BEOL module that a separate, cheaper fab could run on finished DRAM wafers.

title: Broadcast weight bus: one copy of the model feeds N lock-stepped replicas
idea: A weight server (HBF or DRAM, as in B4-12/16) streams each layer's weights on a fixed schedule onto WDM optical waveguides, split 1:N by passive splitters (with semiconductor optical amplifiers if needed) to N accelerators. The replicas run decode in lock-step by layer, on a global layer clock. Each accelerator feeds the weight stream straight into its tensor cores through an SRAM skew buffer of a few MB, while its own HBM holds only KV and activations. One 4-16 TB/s stream serves all N receivers, because optical fan-out needs one modulation for any N.

title: Jot-RAM: image-sensor pinned wells and correlated double sampling for few-electron multi-level memory
