title: Swap 64-bit pointers for region-relative 32-bit pointer instructions
idea: Substitute absolute 64-bit pointers with hardware base-plus-offset addressing. New load and store instructions take a 32-bit offset from a per-region base register with a hardware bounds check, so C/C++ compilers can emit 32-bit pointers in heaps above 4 GB without software decode overhead.

title: Swap ECC-chip overhead for end-to-end checksums on reloadable data
idea: Substitute hardware ECC with software integrity for data that can be reloaded. Model weights, container images and page-cache copies of files sit on non-ECC DIMMs, guarded by per-block hashes that a background scrubber checks; a mismatched block is simply re-read from SSD. ECC DIMMs keep only mutable state.

title: Flyover twinax cables replace motherboard memory traces
idea: Substitute long PCB memory traces with ultra-low-loss twinax cables terminated right beside the CPU socket, so memory modules sit in a separate sled and each channel supports more DIMMs or longer reach without retimers.
note: Flyover cables already ship.

title: Graded-speed DRAM bins packaged into wide slow modules
idea: Substitute prime-only DRAM sourcing with fab speed-reject and down-bin dies, graded on an open-source FPGA DRAM tester and packaged into wide, slow modules where 2x more chips at lower clock deliver the same bandwidth.

title: Substitute blind refresh with compiler-proven refresh-by-use schedules
idea: A compiler/runtime for AI training proves that every row of a tensor region is read or written within its retention time each iteration, and marks those regions refresh-exempt in a controller table.
note: Refresh-by-access (Smart Refresh) known; compiler proof is the twist.

title: Substitute landfill for CXL afterlife pools of retired DDR4 DIMMs
idea: Swap scrapping old DIMMs for CXL memory appliances whose controllers host 16-32 harvested DDR4 DIMMs each as a far-memory tier, with the controller absorbing timing and retention quirks.
note: Hyperscalers already reuse DDR4 behind CXL.

title: Substitute lone mid-size buyers with a memory purchasing cooperative
idea: Swap thousands of small spot-market buyers for a member-owned cooperative (like rural electric co-ops) that pools demand from universities, SMB clouds and OEMs to sign multi-year allocations and run a shared buffer inventory.
note: Purchasing co-ops are established practice.

title: Share the accelerator cold-plate loop with HBM and DIMMs
idea: Extend the GPU liquid-cooling cold plates over HBM stacks and DIMMs to hold the arrays at 30-40 C instead of 85-95 C. Thermal sensors then step the refresh multiplier down from 2x to 0.25x.
note: Liquid-cooled DIMMs/HBM already deployed; refresh gain bounded by refresh share.

title: Retention-certified DRAM grades sold at a premium
idea: Use legacy test flows to bin dies by measured retention (256 ms, 1 s at 45 C) and program the refresh setting into SPD. Long-retention bins go to battery devices; leaky bins go to cooled data centers.

title: Legacy DDR4 dies aggregated by a 28nm CXL base
idea: Co-package 8-16 dies from mature DDR4 lines on a 28 nm logic base that runs the DDR4 cores slowly but wide in parallel and exposes a CXL memory interface, taking over refresh management, ECC and hammer mitigation in the base.

title: Cross-die shared redundancy pool for stacked memory
idea: Combine stack interconnect with repair: rather than each die carrying its own spare rows and columns, pool spares on one die (or spread across the stack) and remap failing rows of any die through the base die's TSV/bond network with a content-addressable remap table.

title: Segment-base hardware makes 32-bit compressed pointers universal
idea: Combine x86-style segment base registers with pointer compression: the load/store unit adds a per-region base plus a 3-bit shift to 32-bit references in a single cycle, so C/C++/Rust allocators and runtimes can use compressed pointers in any heap, not only JVM/V8-style ones.

title: Retired DDR4 DIMMs pooled behind a compressing CXL controller
idea: Combine decommissioned DDR4 modules (built on pre-EUV nodes) with a 28 nm CXL pooling controller that adds inline compression and per-DIMM health remapping, deployed as the far-memory tier of new servers instead of being shredded.

title: SmartNIC fuses page compression with far-memory transport
idea: Combine a 28 nm FPGA SmartNIC's packet pipeline with a page compressor: pages evicted to remote memory are compressed, encrypted and RDMA-sent in one pass, and on fault the NIC decompresses directly into the host page, so far memory costs no CPU and stores 2-3x more per remote GB.
note: Combination of known far-memory and NIC offload.

title: Pharma cold chain: a refrigerated memory tier near minus 30 C
idea: Adapted from the pharmaceutical cold chain: capacity DIMMs sit in sealed, dry-nitrogen-purged sleds on a separate glycol loop chilled to about -30 C by a shared rack chiller, and the controller scales the refresh interval with measured die temperature.

title: SSD pSLC trick: aging regions downgrade to twin-cell differential mode
idea: Adapted from SSDs that run worn TLC blocks in pseudo-SLC mode: when telemetry shows a region's retention degrading, the controller reformats it so each bit uses two adjacent cells storing complementary charge, sensed differentially. The region loses half its capacity but gains ~4x retention and stays in service.
note: Twin-cell and CLR-DRAM prior art.

title: Particle-detector zero suppression for sparse data bursts
idea: Borrowed from LHC detector readout zero suppression: each column group computes a wired-OR nonzero flag during sensing, and bytes that are all zero are sent as a 1-bit tag instead of toggling global data lines and I/O drivers.
note: Zero-value compression and DBI are known.

title: Caterpillar-style remanufacturing harvests DRAM from retired servers
idea: Adapted from Caterpillar Reman's core-deposit model. Hyperscalers return DIMMs from 4-6-year-old servers for a credit; a reman line desolders DRAM packages, burns them in, screens them at derated timings and rebuilds them into modules for edge, PC and CXL-pooled capacity tiers.

title: Ugly-produce partial-good DRAM dies with fused-out banks
idea: Adapted from grocers selling cosmetically imperfect produce. Bin DRAM dies that have dead banks or subarrays, which are normally scrapped, as partial-good parts: on-die fuses remap the address space, an SPD field reports usable capacity, and OS/CXL memory managers consume the odd-sized capacities.

title: Egg-grading economics: retention-graded dies sold with refresh maps
idea: Food grading sells every egg by grade; test each DRAM die's retention tail and sell weaker dies as a managed-refresh grade with a per-die weak-row map stored on the module, so the controller refreshes only those rows faster instead of the die being repaired or scrapped.

title: Satellite downlink budgets: storage-side filtering before data reaches DRAM
idea: Borrowed from Earth-observation satellites that process onboard because downlink is scarce: each query gets a 'downlink budget' in host DRAM bytes, and the planner pushes filters, projections and pre-aggregation into computational SSDs until the result fits, so raw scans never land in DRAM.

title: Toyota kanban: WIP tokens keep fused-operator intermediates on-chip
idea: Borrowed from kanban cards that cap work-in-progress between stations: a dataflow accelerator passes hardware kanban tokens between fused operator stages, and a producer may emit a tile only when its consumer returns a token, bounding every intermediate tensor to a fixed SRAM budget so activations never touch DRAM.

title: 1990s VCSEL ribbon optics disaggregate memory onto rack shelves
idea: Adapted from 1990s 12-channel 850 nm VCSEL parallel-optics datacom modules on multimode ribbon: memory moves to dedicated shelves linked to compute by many slow parallel VCSEL lanes, with driver and receiver chips at 180 nm or larger.

title: Prestressed-concrete trick: stress films flatten ultra-thin memory stacks
idea: Adapted from prestressed concrete: calibrated PECVD nitride/oxide films are deposited on the back of each thinned DRAM die so their built-in stress cancels the warpage that appears at bonding temperature. 30 um dies then stack flat with simple thermocompression.
note: Backside stress films for warpage are routine practice.

title: Automotive remanufacturing: reclaimed server DRAM recertified with defect maps
idea: Adapted from remanufactured auto parts that are torn down, tested and resold with a warranty: retired DDR4/DDR5 RDIMMs from hyperscaler decommissions run through a retention-and-hammer characterization rack built from off-the-shelf FPGA testers, weak rows are written into an SPD-extension defect map, and modules ship with firmware that makes the OS retire those pages at boot.
note: Already done (Azure CXL DDR4 reuse, refurb resellers).

title: Airline fare classes: reliability-tiered cloud memory pricing
idea: Adapted from airline fare classes that sell the same seat at different prices with different guarantees: cloud providers offer VM memory in three tiers (full Chipkill ECC, single-error correction on relaxed refresh, detect-only on salvaged DRAM) at stepped prices, backed by separate physical pools and SLA terms stating error rates.
note: Heterogeneous-reliability memory proposed (Luo et al. 2014); pricing tiers incremental.

title: Magnify the retention tail into a product: long-retention premium bin
idea: Measure each die's retention distribution at wafer sort and sell the top-quartile dies as 'LR' parts with a guaranteed 256 ms-1 s refresh spec at a premium to hyperscalers; controllers read the bin and lengthen tREFI accordingly.

title: Minify refresh by die position: per-die refresh in HBM stacks
idea: On an FPGA-with-HBM board, measure how retention varies with each die's position in the stack, then have a custom controller issue per-channel refresh at rates matched to each die's measured temperature and retention rather than the hottest die.
note: Temperature/retention-aware refresh well known; modest overall energy gain.

title: XOR-delta writes: send only the changed bytes
idea: MINIFY write traffic: the base die keeps the old cache line, the host sends only the nonzero bytes of new XOR old plus a bitmask, and the base die patches the row with a masked write.

title: Self-healing links with spare lanes and field remap
idea: MAGNIFY lane redundancy to ~10% spares with a base-die crossbar that keeps checking bump and TSV margins in service and retires links degraded by electromigration on the fly.

title: Memory leasing with guaranteed take-back and refurbishment
idea: MINIFY ownership: vendors lease HBM and CXL modules, take them back at end of term, refurbish and redeploy them, which gives them a financial reason to design for disassembly.

title: Magnify tolerated defects: Swiss-cheese DIMMs ship bad-page maps
idea: Sell DIMMs certified to contain up to 2% bad 4 KB pages, with the bad-page list in SPD. Firmware and the OS/hypervisor exclude those pages at boot, like NAND bad-block tables.

title: Eliminate refresh for ephemeral data: lifetime-tagged no-refresh DRAM regions
idea: Software tags allocations with a maximum lifetime (activations, gradients, KV-cache blocks consumed within milliseconds); the controller maps them to banks with refresh disabled, and a per-region epoch timer faults if data outlives the guaranteed retention bin. Data that dies before it decays is never refreshed.
note: Similar to RANA and partial-array refresh; low-risk, modest gain.

title: Eliminate charged cells: inversion encoding plus refresh skip for discharged rows
idea: Each row stores a 1-bit inversion flag chosen at write time so most cells sit in the discharged, non-leaking state; rows whose cells are all discharged (zero pages, sparse activations, quantized weights' high bits) are flagged and skipped by refresh.

title: Eliminate row decoders: token-passing wordlines for streaming memory tiers
idea: For sequential tiers (AI weights, KV-cache streams, checkpoints), remove the row decoder tree. Each wordline driver holds a one-bit token in a 2-transistor dynamic stage and passes it to the next row on every activate clock, so rows open in a fixed order. A 'jump' tap every 512 rows allows coarse seeks.

title: Eliminate the guest OS inside every VM with unikernel images
idea: Compile cloud services as unikernels or library OSes that link only the kernel functions they use, removing the 200 MB-1 GB guest kernel, init system and page cache that each VM duplicates.

title: Eliminate host DRAM staging: GPU servers spec'd with quarter memory
idea: Use GPUDirect Storage loaders so weights and datasets go NVMe-to-HBM directly, and publish an open reference server spec with 256 GB host DRAM instead of 1-2 TB; it is a software plus integration business.

title: Die passport: on-die non-volatile test history ends retesting
idea: Eliminate repeated testing at every packaging step: each memory die carries a small OTP/ReRAM log written at wafer sort, burn-in and post-bond test (bin, repair map, timing margins, weak rows), read by the stacker and later by the system.

title: Eliminate refresh for compiler-proven short-lived tensor pages
idea: Stop treating refresh as a service every page gets. The ML compiler/runtime proves that each activation or KV buffer is rewritten or freed within T_live (typically under 5 ms) and tags its pages with a page-table 'lifetime' bit. The controller's refresh engine then skips any row whose last write is younger than the measured worst-case retention minus a margin.
note: Smart Refresh/RANA-style skipping is known.

title: Eliminate retention-fail scrap: sell weak dies as fast-refresh grade
idea: Eliminate the 64 ms retention gate: dies that fail 64 ms but pass 16-32 ms are bought, binned and sold with an SPD flag that forces the controller's existing 2x/4x refresh mode; ~$400k for binning and qualification.

title: Fuse-less DRAM: host controller holds the repair map
idea: Reverse who repairs: the die ships without fuse/antifuse banks or address-compare redundancy logic; failing rows and columns are recorded in a signed on-module SPD map at test, and the memory controller or OS remaps them to spare rows at boot.

title: Reverse logistics: remanufacture retired server DRAM
idea: Reverse the supply flow: build industrial lines that harvest DRAM packages from decommissioned servers, re-ball them, run a burn-in and binning test, and re-module them into certified 'second-life' DIMMs for less demanding tiers.
note: Refurb DIMM market already exists; supply adds at low capex.

title: Excessive action: multi-row activation sums redundant copies in weak mats
idea: TRIZ #16 Partial or excessive action: in mats with weak cells or high temperature the controller writes each bit into 2-4 rows sharing the same bitlines and later opens them together so their charges sum on the bitline, trading capacity for 2-4x signal instead of scrapping the die or raising refresh.

title: Retired server DIMMs reharvested into pooled CXL memory
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round, memory flowing back up the supply chain: hyperscalers return DDR4/DDR5 from decommissioned servers to a qualification line. The line desolders the DRAM, retests it at speed and temperature, bins it by retention class, and rebuilds it onto CXL Type-3 expander cards for capacity tiers.

title: Per-recipe scarcity ledger that feeds back into process engineering
idea: TRIZ #23 Feedback: meter each tool's use per wafer of He, ALD precursors, fluorinated gases, UPW and kWh. Price each at a shadow scarcity cost (e.g., helium at its outage price) inside the fab's cost-per-bit model, so recipe changes are scored and rewarded on scarce-resource reduction.
note: Shadow-priced sub-metering is sound management practice; incremental.

title: Follow-the-moon placement of memory-hungry jobs across regions
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action: route memory-heavy batch work (long-context KV-heavy jobs, analytics, fine-tuning) to whichever regions are in their nightly interactive trough, so each region's DRAM is sized for the global average instead of its own daytime peak plus batch.

title: Via-programmed mask ROM freezes model weights into old-node silicon
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: freeze 'liquid' read-only weights into 'solid' via-programmed NOR/NAND mask ROM on 180 nm lines, where only one via mask changes per model, so frozen weights and vocabulary tables leave DRAM for cheap, refresh-free, one-transistor-per-bit storage.

title: Lizard basking: per-tier refresh follows the stack's thermal gradient
idea: Lizards shuttle between sun and shade; in a 3D stack over logic, top tiers near the spreader run ~10-15 C cooler than bottom tiers, so embed a thermistor per tier group, refresh each tier at its own temperature-derived rate, and place refresh-sensitive or rarely touched data in the coolest tiers.

title: Pit-viper pit organs: canary cells time refresh per mat at 125 C
idea: Pit vipers sense heat with dedicated ultra-sensitive organs; put deliberately weakened canary cells (smaller capacitor, wider access device) in every 3D mat, check them each refresh tick, and refresh a mat only when its canaries start to fail, measuring real leakage at the actual local temperature and age.

title: Hermit-crab re-shelling: retired DDR4 rehoused in CXL expanders
idea: Hermit crabs move into shells that others discard. Buy DDR4 DIMMs from server decommissioning, screen them with a 24-hour retention and row-hammer test, and resell them inside CXL Type-3 expander cards with DDR4 controllers as a warm memory tier.

title: Immune self-tolerance binning keeps dies with weak cells
idea: The immune system learns to tolerate self after thymic screening instead of destroying every odd cell. At wafer sort, write each die's weak-retention rows into an on-die fuse self-map and ship the die with per-row adaptive refresh and remapping, instead of scrapping dies that fail a uniform 64 ms test.

title: Apoptotic eat-me telemetry retires memory packages before they fail
idea: Like cells displaying phosphatidylserine before apoptosis, each DRAM package exports correctable-error rate, retention drift and hammer-count signals; crossing a threshold triggers live migration of its pages and schedules a tool-less swap of just that unit, so failures never crash jobs or force whole-board scrap.

title: Datacenter spleen grades and recirculates aging memory modules
idea: The spleen filters old red blood cells and recycles their iron; a campus test station receives every pulled module, characterizes retention, hammer threshold and speed, and re-dispatches it to the tier it can still serve (hot, warm, approximate, scrap), feeding results back to procurement.
note: Grading and redeploying pulled modules; same reuse core as I-04900.

title: Hermit-crab reuse: re-home DRAM from retired modules into CXL expanders
idea: Hermit crabs move into shells others have left. A U.S. reverse-logistics business does the same for retired server DIMMs and boards: robots desolder the DRAM packages, which are retested, speed-binned and graded for warranty, then re-mounted in high-capacity CXL memory expanders that hide their slower speed behind tiering.
note: Same retired-DRAM-to-CXL reuse mechanism.

title: Apoptotic cascade: retire a failing page's predicted spatial accomplices
idea: Apoptotic cells signal their neighbours; when the OS retires a page for a hard error, a learned fault-cluster model of the die (shared wordline, bitline, sub-wordline driver, TSV column) pre-emptively migrates and retires the physically co-located pages most likely to fail next, before they produce uncorrectable errors.

title: Mycorrhizal memory commons: cross-tenant DRAM lending over CXL fabric
idea: Like fungal networks shuttling carbon from sun-rich trees to shaded ones, rack-scale CXL 3.x switches let servers with idle DRAM lend pages to memory-starved neighbours. A broker reads per-host free-memory telemetry, rebalances continuously, and pays lenders per GB-hour from a 'carbon credit' ledger.

title: Pando clonal SRAM chiplets from oversupplied 28 nm logic
idea: Pando is one aspen organism expressed as thousands of identical stems on shared roots. A standard UCIe SRAM chiplet, identical across foundries and traded as a commodity like DDR, is made in oversupplied 28-40 nm fabs and stacked under accelerators as last-level memory.

title: Airline departure board: compiler-published buffer lifetimes elide refresh entirely
idea: Airlines know every departure in advance and staff gates accordingly. AI accelerator compilers know statically when each activation or gradient buffer is next rewritten; they publish per-region lifetimes to the memory controller, which skips refresh for any row guaranteed to be rewritten or freed within tREFW.

title: Camel-nose countercurrent cascade rinses for periphery wet benches
idea: A camel's nasal turbinates recover exhaled water by countercurrent exchange. Plumb periphery wet benches as 4-stage countercurrent cascades: fresh UPW enters only the final rinse and its overflow feeds the stage before, with inline resistivity/TOC sensors advancing wafers instead of timed overflow; periphery's relaxed contamination spec permits it.

title: Radio broadcast reads: one activation multicast to many consumers
idea: One transmitter serves a whole city; in a 3D DRAM-on-logic stack, activate a row of shared weights once and multicast it over a base-die broadcast bus to all 16-64 compute tiles subscribed to that row address in the same step (batched or tensor-parallel inference).
note: Batched inference already amortizes weight reads via on-chip buffers.

title: MRI zero-boil-off logic: per-tool helium recapture and reliquefaction
idea: Borrowing from MRI magnets that went 'zero boil-off' with cold-head recondensers: fit every etch/deposition cluster with a helium recapture manifold on electrostatic-chuck backside-gas leak paths, load-lock purges and leak-check exhaust, feeding a small cryocooler purifier that recompresses or reliquefies He for reuse. Fab helium becomes a closed inventory topped up a few percent per month instead of a consumable.
note: Same per-tool He recapture as I-11246.

title: MRI zero-boil-off approach: helium recapture skids for fab tools
idea: Borrowed from modern MRI magnets, which lose almost no helium because a cryocooler recondenses boil-off: a small team builds bolt-on skids that collect helium from chuck backside, leak-check and purge exhausts, run it through a membrane separator, pressure-swing adsorber and cryo-purifier, and return 6N helium to the tool manifold.

title: Actuarial adaptive test: warranty-priced risk replaces blanket burn-in
idea: Borrowed from insurers, who price risk statistically instead of inspecting every customer: a small team builds a model using each die's inline and probe parametrics to predict field-failure probability, skips long burn-in and retention screens for the low-risk ~80%, and backs the shipped population with a priced warranty reserve.

title: Airline overbooking for RAM: overcommit by measured no-show rate
idea: Hypervisors record, per application class, the fraction of allocated memory never touched ('no-shows') and overbook physical DRAM by that rate, with a pre-agreed bump protocol (compress, then demote to CXL flash) for rare oversubscription and a yield-managed premium for guaranteed seats.

title: Second-life DRAM: retired DDR4 reborn in CXL cold tiers
idea: Like EV batteries repurposed for grid storage, harvest DDR4 DIMMs from decommissioned servers, bin them with a test robot, and mount them in CXL expansion boxes acting as a compressed cold tier behind new DDR5.

title: Shared parking for memory: co-locate day and night workloads
idea: Like office parking reused by residents at night, pair anti-correlated workloads (daytime inference, night batch training/ETL) on one DRAM pool and swap working sets via fast NVMe snapshots at shift change, sizing DRAM to the peak of the sum rather than the sum of peaks.
note: Diurnal colocation and harvest VMs are known practice.

title: Fractional-reserve memory banking with a CXL reserve pool
idea: A bank keeps only part of its deposits as cash. Servers likewise promise more DRAM than they hold, and a rack CXL pool acts as the reserve. A telemetry-driven 'reserve ratio' sets how much local DRAM backs promised capacity. When a run starts, a 'lender of last resort' compresses cold pages to a swap tier.
note: Close to Microsoft Pond pooling and overcommit.

title: Five-star tube grading reborn: retention-graded DRAM for relaxed refresh
idea: Revive the military practice of hand-selecting premium 'five-star' vacuum tubes: test every U.S.-made DRAM die for retention on U.S. testers, bin the tail-free fraction as long-retention parts certified for a 4-8x refresh interval, and sell them at a premium to U.S. hyperscalers whose controllers apply the certified interval.
note: Vendors already bin; retention-graded parts studied in RAIDR/AVATAR; VRT undermines static grading.

title: Audio-RAM revival: sell partially defective DRAM for tolerant AI workloads
idea: Revive 1980s ARAM, defective DRAM sold for answering machines: bin HBM/DDR dies that fail full spec, burn their bad-row maps into on-die fuses/SPD, and sell them for error-tolerant KV cache and low-precision activation storage, with the OS/runtime retiring the mapped rows.

title: Wartime salvage drive for DRAM: harvest chips from retired servers
idea: Revive WWII scrap-salvage logistics for memory: collect DDR4/DDR5 modules from decommissioned servers, robotically desolder and re-ball the packages, burn-in and retest them, and rebuild them onto CXL memory-expander cards pooled as a slower tier.

title: Erlang-B trunk dimensioning for rack-pooled CXL memory
idea: Treat servers' memory peaks like telephone call traffic: the rack shares a CXL memory 'trunk' sized with Erlang-B for a 0.1% blocking target, and blocked requests overflow to compressed swap the way blocked calls overflowed to alternate routes. Each server keeps only its base load locally.

title: Cray-2 Fluorinert revival: boiling-pinned memory retunes refresh without water
idea: The Cray-2 (1985) ran its stacked boards submerged in circulating Fluorinert. Immerse DIMMs and HBM in a low-GWP two-phase fluid boiling at ~50 C, which pins every die at that temperature, then calibrate refresh interval, sense trims and ECC strength once for 50 C instead of the 85-95 C worst case; vapour is condensed by dry coolers.

title: Staktek-Style Package Stacking to Bypass the TSV Bottleneck
idea: Revive the 1990s Staktek/Dense-Pac technique of stacking finished, fully tested packages with flex-frame rails: towers of 4-8 conventional wire-bonded DDR5 packages per site build 256-512 GB capacity RDIMMs on ordinary OSAT lines instead of TSV lines.

title: Data that dies young: refresh-free banks for transient tensors
idea: Inverts 'every byte must be retained until overwritten': the compiler tags each AI tensor with its lifetime (activations and KV segments often live <10 ms), and the memory controller places them in banks whose refresh is masked off, guaranteeing reuse or overwrite within the profiled retention window; only weights and long-lived state sit in refreshed banks.

title: No fuses, no spare rows: ship DRAM with a signed defect map
idea: Inverting 'every die must look perfect': delete redundant rows/columns, fuse banks and repair logic; at test, write each die's failing 4 KB pages into a signed SPD defect map and have the memory controller or OS allocator skip them like NAND bad blocks.

title: Follow-the-moon: shift memory-heavy batch to regions with idle DRAM
idea: Inverts 'memory demand is local in time': a global scheduler moves memory-bound batch work (index builds, embedding generation, training-data prep) to datacenters in their night trough, where DRAM sits idle after interactive demand falls.

title: Read-mostly asymmetric links: fat downstream lanes, thin upstream lane
idea: Invert 'memory links are symmetric and bidirectional': inference reads 20-100x more than it writes, so build PHYs with unidirectional memory-to-host lanes (no turnaround, simpler drivers and termination) plus a narrow write lane.

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal at 400 C erasing the leakage tail
idea: The <=13 fA retention-tail cells come from trap-assisted tunneling through a few interface and junction dangling bonds. A 20 atm D2 anneal at 400 C passivates them, and the Si-D bond resists hot-carrier and field depassivation several times better than Si-H, cutting the tail at its physical source.
note: High-pressure D2 anneal already used commercially.

title: Controller-held repair map deletes on-die fuses and compare logic
idea: Repair information is only (#faulty rows x log2 N) bits, a few kbit, yet fuse banks and address comparators cost percent-level die area. Ship dies with no redundancy steering; the bad-row/column map measured at test is stored in the module SPD and the host controller remaps physical addresses.

title: Harvest DRAM dies from retired servers into CXL memory pools
idea: Charge storage causes no atomic change, so DRAM has no wear-out and a retired DIMM's dies still embody every scarce input. Desolder and retest dies at scale, rebin by speed and retention, and repackage them into CXL Type-3 expanders with stronger ECC and patrol scrub as tier-2 memory.
note: Same retired-die harvest into CXL as I-01583.

title: Exponent-dictionary storage for BF16 and FP8 tensors
idea: Measured from the data, the 8-bit exponent field of trained BF16 weights and activations holds only ~2.5-3 bits of entropy because values cluster within a few octaves. Logic on the HBM/CXL base die stores each 128-value block as 3-bit codes into a per-block 8-entry exponent palette plus raw sign and mantissa, with a raw fallback for outlier blocks.
note: DFloat11/ZipNN known; ~1.4x.

title: Stack-distance profiler sizing each VM's DRAM to its miss-curve knee
idea: The minimum DRAM a workload needs is set by its reuse-distance distribution, not its allocation. A hardware Mattson stack-distance sampler in the memory controller (hashed address sampling with a small SHARDS-style tree) builds each VM's miss-ratio curve in real time; the hypervisor grants local DRAM up to the knee and backs the tail with compressed or CXL memory.
note: SHARDS/MRC-based memory sizing is known; hardware sampler is incremental.

title: Phase-shifting jobs to anticorrelate memory peaks in a pool
idea: Provisioning for the sum of peaks instead of the peak of the sum wastes capacity. A scheduler fingerprints each job's memory-over-time curve (batch ETL, training checkpoints, nightly builds) and offsets start times so that peaks interleave, then sizes the shared pool to the measured peak of the sum plus a margin.

title: Sub-ambient coolant loop priced against Arrhenius refresh savings
idea: Tail leakage has Ea ~0.6-0.9 eV, so retention doubles every ~8-10 C, and dropping junctions from 85 C to 25 C buys ~60-100x retention. Route 10 C facility water to the memory cold plates first, and let on-die sensors stretch refresh to 1-4 s.

title: Lifetime-tagged refresh-free banks for short-lived tensors
idea: A bit needs refresh only if it must outlive its charge. Compiler/runtime tags allocations with predicted lifetime, and activations, gradient buffers and per-step scratch (<20 ms) go to banks with refresh disabled. A per-region birth-time register faults any read past the retention deadline.

title: Compress-then-protect: compression slack carries strong ECC
idea: Real 64 B lines have entropy well below 512 bits (zeros, pointers, small integers; 1.5-2x compressible with BDI/FPC). The controller compresses each line and fills the freed bits with BCH parity up to t=8. Incompressible lines fall back to normal SEC.
note: Compress-and-protect already published (COP).

title: DRAM refinery re-bins decommissioned server DIMMs into CXL capacity
idea: First principle: DRAM has no intrinsic wear-out (no tunnel-oxide damage as in flash), so a 5-year-old server DIMM's cells are physically almost as good as new. Regional refineries pull retired DDR4/DDR5 at hyperscaler decommission, run 48-hour retention and pattern screens, re-bin at relaxed timing, and remount modules or dies onto CXL Type-3 expander cards for capacity-tier memory.
note: Already pursued (e.g., hyperscaler DDR4 reuse behind CXL).

title: Wine-cellar retention bins sell short-retention dies to rewrite-heavy buyers
idea: Random stimulus 'wine cellar': each vintage goes to the buyer it suits. Bin dies by measured retention: long-retention bins (>=1 s) sell at a premium to edge/mobile, while dies failing the 64 ms spec, now scrapped or repaired, ship to AI training racks with a 16 ms controller-managed refresh, where data is rewritten every few ms anyway.

title: Empty mailbox flag: zero-word detect skips internal data toggling
idea: Don't open the mailbox if it is empty: a wired-NOR at each local sense-amp group flags all-zero 64-bit words, and the chip sends a 1-bit flag on a side line instead of toggling the global data lines, I/O drivers and PHY; ReLU activations, sparse weights and fresh pages are 50-90% zeros.

title: Seesaw: vertical twin cell holds each bit across two tiers
idea: A seesaw rises on one side as it falls on the other: in a 3D die each bit is complementary charge on two cells stacked directly above one another on a vertical bitline pair, sensed differentially. The signal doubles and leakage is common-mode, so cheap tiers buy far longer retention behind a standard DDR5/LPDDR5 interface.

title: Dating app: wafer-map matchmaking before wafer-to-wafer HBM stacking
idea: A dating app pairs compatible profiles: probe-test each DRAM wafer, store its defect map, and use an assignment solver to choose which wafers and which rotation (0/90/180/270) to bond wafer-to-wafer so bad sites land on bad sites. Dice the pre-bonded stacks into HBM core blocks with the standard HBM interface.

title: Thermostat: per-tier refresh skipping follows the HBM stack's thermal gradient
idea: A thermostat acts on local temperature: each HBM core die reads its own sensors and tier position (top dies run 5-15 C cooler than dies near the base) and quietly executes only a fraction of the controller's REF commands, for example 1 in 2 below 70 C. Commands and timing stay JEDEC; only internal energy drops.
note: Temperature-compensated refresh is established; per-die skipping is incremental.

title: Airline overbooking: sell 140% of rack DRAM, keep CXL standby seats
idea: Treat DRAM like airline seats: provision each server at ~70% of its tenants' summed peak, size a rack-level CXL pool from no-show statistics, and 'bump' the lowest-value pages (compress first, then pool) when a peak lands; the hypervisor publishes a per-VM bump-probability SLA.

title: Morse code: Huffman exponents decoded at line rate in controller
idea: Morse gives E a single dot: entropy-code only the exponent field of BF16/FP8 tensors per 4 KB block (about 2.5-3 bits of information in 8) and decode in a 16-lane table-driven unit in the memory controller, keeping sign and mantissa raw for fixed-latency random access.
note: Exponent entropy coding (DFloat11, ZipNN) is active art; controller placement is the twist; ~25-30% gain.

title: Card catalog: base-die Bloom filters answer misses before crossing link
idea: Like a library card catalog: the HBM/CXL memory base die keeps Bloom-filter catalogs of key-value and embedding tables, so a lookup that would miss is answered 'absent' without moving data across the link or opening a row.

title: Lego: double-sided commodity LPDDR around FPGA as poor man's HBM
idea: Like Lego bricks: stock LPDDR5X packages are placed on both sides of a thin, short-trace substrate directly around an FPGA or accelerator die, with 16 or more channels in parallel, using a standard OSAT build. A demo module fits within $1M.

title: Hourglass: lifetime-tagged tensors stored in refresh-free rows
idea: The compiler/runtime tags tensors whose lifetime is shorter than the profiled retention floor (activations, gradients alive <20 ms); the controller places them in banks with refresh suspended, and timed-out data is treated as expired rather than corrupted - the sand runs out only after the data is dead.
note: Refresh skipping for short-lived data is known art (Flikker/RAPID-style).

title: Thrift store: refurbished hyperscaler DIMMs rehomed behind CXL ECC expanders
idea: Retired DDR4/DDR5 DIMMs are field-tested, binned and mounted on CXL expander cards whose controllers add symbol-level ECC, sparing and patrol scrub, giving them a second 3-5 year life as memory-tier capacity.

title: OS free-page list drives row-granular partial refresh
idea: Box: standard DRAM x standard access x standard sense x per-row refresh-enable bitmap inside the DRAM written by the OS allocator via mode-register commands x system x Si x zero masks. Freed or never-allocated pages stop being refreshed; the OS zeroes them on allocation anyway.
note: ESKIMO-style semantic refresh and PASR are prior art.

title: Tool-level helium recapture loops with polymer membranes
idea: Box [helium lever: recapture | location: each etch chamber exhaust | purifier: PIM-1/polyimide membrane + small compressor | return: chuck supply line]: collect He from electrostatic-chuck backside leaks and leak-test exhaust, purify it to 5N at the tool and recycle it, buying cylinders only for makeup.

title: Price LLM APIs per KV-gigabyte-second to shape context demand
idea: Box: demand shaping × API pricing × request × billing × KV-GB-second meter with shared-prefix discounts. Customers pay for the memory-time their context occupies, with discounts for shared prefixes and short sessions, nudging agents to summarize and reuse.

title: Harvest stranded VM memory into spot memory capacity
idea: Box[Source=allocated-but-idle VM memory x Transform=hypervisor balloon and telemetry reclaim x Integration=standard DIMMs x Channel=evictable memory-harvest instances]: the hypervisor reclaims memory that VMs reserve but never touch (often ~25%) and resells it as evictable capacity.

title: Sanitize-not-shred policy saves decommissioned DIMMs
idea: Box[Policy=NIST 800-88 style guidance that certifies power-off plus pattern overwrite for volatile DRAM x Owner=standards body + insurers x Channel=reuse market]: since DRAM is volatile, verified pattern-write and power-off clears it, so certify that and stop the security-driven shredding of retired server memory.

title: Route chilled-water inlet to DRAM first for retention-tiered cooling
idea: Po: DRAM lives in a refrigerator. Re-plumb liquid-cooled AI racks so the coldest inlet water (~15 C) crosses DRAM cold plates before the GPUs, holding arrays near 25 C instead of 85 C, and have the controller apply temperature-compensated refresh tables that stretch tREFI as leakage halves every ~10 C.
note: Needs non-JEDEC refresh stretching beyond 64 ms; cooling-refresh link well known.

title: Free-page hints stop refresh of unallocated rows
idea: Po: memory only remembers what someone cares about. The OS streams its free-page bitmap to the DRAM controller via a new mode-register/CXL command; rows whose pages are all free are dropped from the refresh rotation and are zero-initialized on next allocation.

title: Po broken chips are the product: bank-salvage CXL memory
idea: Po: 'sell only the broken chips.' Extracted: dies that fail final test because of one or two dead banks or a slow mat, scrapped or downgraded today, are packaged with a small CXL controller that keeps a per-die bank map and presents a contiguous address space, priced per good GB.

title: Partially-good dies become full modules through controller remap
idea: Po: the bad dies are good. Stop scrapping DRAM dies with dead banks or exhausted redundancy; bin them by usable fraction, pair 75%-good dies per slot and let a CXL or module controller remap addresses around dead regions.

title: Helium-free fab: closed-loop chuck gas recapture and substitutes
idea: Po: the fab breathes no helium. Retrofit existing etch/CVD electrostatic chucks with closed-loop backside-gas recirculation and membrane purification, substitute H2/Ar or N2 where heat-transfer margin allows, and recover He from leak-check and stage purges.

title: Rumor memory: erasure-coded replicas instead of triple copies
idea: Po: data exists only as rumors spread among neighbors. In-memory databases and caches replace 3x replication with Reed-Solomon (e.g., 8+3) striping across nodes' DRAM and rebuild lost shards over RDMA on failure.
note: Hydra/EC-Cache/Carbink prior art.

title: Fractional-reserve memory: oversell DRAM with a lender of last resort
idea: Po: memory banks lend memory like money. Hypervisors sell 1.5x physical DRAM based on a model of peak co-occurrence across VMs, backed by a compressed-memory plus CXL-flash central-bank tier that absorbs runs, with priced insurance for tenants wanting guaranteed residency.

title: Split objects: hot fields stay, cold fields shrink and move out
idea: Po: every object is cut in half. A profile-guided compiler peels each struct into a hot part (fields touched on fast paths) and a cold part that is batch-compressed in a separate region and reached through a 4-byte handle only when rare paths need it.
note: Chilimbi-style structure splitting plus cold-part compression.

title: Data never comes home: query predicates applied in the network path
idea: Po: the data never enters memory. Intel Agilex FPGAs (Intel 7, fabbed in Oregon/Arizona) sit in the NIC path and apply predicates, projections and decompression to incoming storage and network streams, so host DRAM buffers hold only matching rows and needed columns.

title: Tattletale chip: domestic per-page access counters for exact tiering
idea: Po: memory that tattles on itself. A small GlobalFoundries Malta-fabbed companion chip on each CXL memory module counts activations per page (and per line in hot pages) from the command stream and publishes heatmaps, replacing the CPU's imprecise page-table scanning.

title: Bit-plane slicing puts NN weight LSBs in rarely refreshed rows
idea: Worse: protect every bit of a neural network equally. Flip: store weights transposed into bit planes; MSB planes go to normally refreshed rows and the low 4 bit planes to rows refreshed 16x slower, where rare flips cost under 0.1% accuracy.
note: EDEN/Flikker-style approximate refresh for DNNs is known.

title: Allocator-driven REFSKIP command cancels refresh of dead data
idea: Worse: keep refreshing memory nobody will read again. Flip: add a DDR/CXL REFSKIP range command that the allocator, garbage collector and KV-cache evictor issue on free; the DRAM clears a per-row live bit and its refresh engine skips dead rows until the next write.
note: ESKIMO and PASR-style prior art.

title: Leakage-controlled oscillator sets Arrhenius-tracking refresh rate
idea: Worse at 125 C: refresh at a fixed rate chosen for the hottest day of a 10-year life. Flip: drive the refresh timer from an oscillator whose capacitor is charged by the off-current of a replica access transistor, so the refresh rate follows real leakage from -40 to 125 C and with aging.
note: Leakage-tracking refresh timers and TCSR are established art.

title: Thermal-map data placement keeps long-lived data in coolest banks
idea: Worse at 125 C: place long-lived data next to the hot spot and refresh the whole die for the hottest bank. Flip: per-bank on-die thermal sensors feed the controller, which migrates rarely written pages to edge banks 10-15 C cooler and refreshes each bank at its own temperature-indexed rate.

title: Background in-field retention test remaps newly weak rows to spares
idea: Worse at 125 C: trust a factory retention map that ages and drifts over 10 years. Flip: the refresh engine rotates one row per period through an extended-interval check-after-wait test, logs cells that weakened through aging or VRT, and remaps them to spare rows while keeping the rest at relaxed refresh.

title: Helium-as-a-service loop with per-tool recovery skids
idea: Worsen: vent every liter of helium after one pass through a chuck or leak test. Flip: fit each tool with a membrane plus PSA recovery skid and have a third-party operator own the helium inventory, billing fabs per liter lost, so >90% recovery becomes the operator's profit motive.

title: Ship imperfect dies with burned-in defect maps for OS remapping
idea: Worse: scrap every die that still fails after the repair fuses run out. Flip: sell dies with residual bad rows. An on-die eFuse defect map is read at boot, and the kernel or CXL controller excludes those pages (badblocks for RAM), creating a priced-per-good-GB 'capacity-certified' grade.

title: ISA-level compressed references for every language
idea: Worsen: make every pointer 64 bits even when a heap is under 32 GB. Flip: add region-base registers and load/store forms that widen 32-bit compressed references on the fly in the address-generation unit, so C++, Rust, Go and Python runtimes all get Java-style compressed pointers without software decode.

title: One end-to-end ECC codeword from cell to core
idea: Worsen: re-encode data at every hop, with on-die ECC, link CRC, controller ECC and cache ECC each adding bits and latency. Flip: generate one strong codeword when data enters the array, ship its raw parity bits over the link and decode only once in the processor, deleting link and on-die ECC logic.

title: Elastic ECC migrates aging pages to stronger codes
idea: Worse: fix one ECC strength at manufacture, so the part over-protects when young and dies when old. Flip: the controller tracks corrected errors per page and promotes degrading pages to stronger codes (SEC-DED, then chipkill-class, then 2x replication) by borrowing capacity, so a module loses ~1% capacity per year instead of failing.
note: Close to Morphable ECC / FREE-p.

title: Sushi chef's freshness window: refresh-free ephemeral memory with expiry
idea: A sushi chef never stores fish past its window; it is served fresh. A new 'ephemeral' allocation class for activations, KV scratch and network buffers stamps each row with its write time; those rows are never refreshed, and the controller traps any read after the guaranteed retention window (e.g., 32 ms at the measured temperature) so software recomputes.

title: Hermit crab's borrowed shell: re-screen retired DIMMs at faster refresh
idea: A hermit crab moves into a used shell. Hyperscaler-retired DDR4/DDR5 modules are bulk-tested hot for retention, re-binned, and redeployed behind CXL memory expanders that run them at 2-4x refresh rate with stronger ECC as pooled cold-tier memory.
note: CXL reuse of retired DIMMs already practiced by hyperscalers.

title: Hermit-crab DIMM: depreciated-node dies behind a translating buffer
idea: A hermit crab moves into an old shell. A module buffer chip presents standard DDR5 to the host but drives two interleaved ranks of older-node DDR4-class dies from fully depreciated fab lines, translating commands and refresh and matching DDR5 bandwidth with a few ns of added latency.
note: Similar to CXL DDR4 reuse and MRDIMM buffering.

title: Cartographer's contour map: exponent-dedupe compression in base die
idea: A map keeps contours, not every pebble: the HBM base die stores and sends AI tensors as per-block shared exponents plus mantissa deltas (BF16/FP8 exponent dedupe), and decompresses at the controller, so fewer bits cross the TSVs and PHY.
note: Shared-exponent formats (MX) already capture much of this.

title: Coal miner's canary: sacrificial early-failure sensors for each memory link
idea: The canary dies first and warns the miners: each package includes intentionally weakened replica bonds, TSVs and lines (narrower, at higher current) that fail first under the same 125 C stress and trigger proactive remapping or service.

title: Mayfly biologist: short-lived buffers tagged so they're never refreshed
idea: A mayfly lives a day and needs no long-term maintenance: the compiler or runtime tags buffers whose lifetime is shorter than the refresh window (ML activations, staging buffers, packet rings), and the controller sets a per-row no-refresh bit for them until they are freed.

title: Knitter's lifeline thread: epoch undo-log turns DUEs into rollbacks
idea: A knitter threads a lifeline so mistakes can be ripped back: the memory controller journals the old contents of overwritten lines for the last ~10 ms epoch into a protected region, so after an uncorrectable error the affected process or VM rolls back to the epoch boundary instead of crashing.

title: Single-implant gated-diode amplifying cell for $1 IoT microcontrollers
idea: A $1 IoT MCU in 40 nm logic needs megabytes of RAM without a capacitor module; one added implant mask forms a gated diode whose gate capacitance is large when '1' is stored (inverted) and tiny when '0', so boosting the gate during read amplifies the '1' several-fold (2T1D cell). Everything else uses existing logic layers.
note: IBM 2T1D gated-diode cell is prior art.

title: Overclocker-style margin binning routes weak dies into tolerant tiers
idea: Overclockers prove dies vary widely: an on-die SA margin sweeper characterizes every die at test, and dies that miss JEDEC margins are sold into KV-cache and approximate-memory tiers with relaxed refresh and ECC instead of being scrapped. DUV-only dies with wider variation stay economical.

title: Xenon-anesthesia recapture logic for every rare gas in fab exhaust
idea: Hospitals recapture exhaled xenon anesthetic with cryogenic adsorbers because Xe is so scarce, yet fabs dump Ne, Kr and Xe from lasers, implanters and etchers. Fit point-of-use pressure-swing/cryo-adsorption cartridges that capture rare gases before dilution and regenerate them centrally to 99.99%.
note: Neon recycling for excimer lasers already sold by laser vendors.

title: Hyperscale DIMM harvest: retired DDR4 dies reborn as CXL memory
idea: Industrial users with 30-year lines already buy reclaimed chips, and hyperscalers retire millions of DDR4 DIMMs every 4-5 years. An automated U.S. harvesting line tests retired DIMMs, bins them by retention and refresh margin, and mounts them behind CXL memory-expander controllers as a cheap far-memory tier.

title: Fuse defective DRAM dies into half-capacity IoT memory grades
idea: Extreme user: $1 IoT boards that need 64-512 Mb, not 16 Gb. At wafer sort, map failing banks and laser-fuse dies with dead banks into 1/2 or 1/4-capacity SKUs with a standard remapped address space instead of scrapping them (HBM core dies included).

title: Thousand-tab browser freezing: pixels now, DOM later
idea: From the power user with 1,000 open tabs: background tabs and apps are frozen into a compressed render snapshot plus serialized semantic state (scroll, form fields, JS heap roots); DOM, layout trees and JIT heaps are freed and rebuilt lazily only when the user returns, while the snapshot displays instantly.

title: Overclocker binning in reverse: weak-retention dies sold as refresh-class parts
idea: Overclockers profile each module's true margins and tune timings to match. Do the reverse for retention: dies that fail 64 ms but pass 32 ms get a 'refresh class' written into vendor bytes of the standard SPD, and the BIOS sets the controller's existing programmable tREFI or 2x-refresh mode to suit.

title: Answering-machine grade: partial-good dies with a standard bad-region descriptor
idea: 1980s answering machines used 'audio RAM': dies with known bad cells. Define a JEDEC-style descriptor, fused on die and mirrored in SPD, that lists failed subarrays so OS allocators (badram-style) and CXL controllers skip them. Fabs then sell 90-99%-good dies as a priced grade instead of scrapping them.

title: Refresh-interval SKUs: sell DRAM priced by retention bin
idea: Scale jump from wafer sort to market structure: test every die at four refresh intervals (64 ms, 256 ms, 1 s, 4 s at 85 C) and sell long-retention grades at a premium to phones, IoT and cold CXL tiers running relaxed refresh, while short-retention dies go to always-busy AI servers whose traffic refreshes rows anyway.

title: Per-bank TTL timers replace the refresh scheduler
idea: Swap the 64 ms refresh clock for allocation lifetimes: host allocations carry a time-to-live, each bank's periphery holds a countdown timer instead of refresh counters, and on expiry the bank's data is declared dead and the bank power-gated; TTLs are capped below the bank's certified retention.

title: Inductive-coil links replace TSVs between stacked dies
idea: Scale the transformer down: draw ~20-um on-chip coils in thick 180-nm-era metal on each thinned die and pass data magnetically through the stack at Gb/s per coil, so stacked DRAM needs no TSV etch, fill or keep-out zones.
note: ThruChip-style inductive links are demonstrated; coil area and power delivery still need TSVs.

title: Wire-bonded staircase stacks multiply trailing DRAM per package
idea: Borrow NAND's 16-high staircase stack at existing OSATs: thin trailing-node DRAM dies to 40 um, offset them in a staircase and wire-bond them to a shared substrate. That reaches 16-32 GB per package for capacity-tier modules without TSVs.

title: Procure DRAM in touched-byte-hours, not installed gigabytes
idea: Hyperscalers and OEMs size memory contracts and server SKUs from fleet telemetry of touched GB-hours, meaning pages accessed in each 2-minute window. They buy installed DRAM at the 95th percentile of the touched set plus a compressed far tier. Part of what vendors are paid covers effective capacity delivered through compression.

title: Algebraic views evaluated at the memory port
idea: Many resident tensors are cheap functions of others: GQA repeat_kv expansions, broadcasts, padding, transposes, rotary-embedded keys. Store only the base tensor plus a view descriptor, and have the load unit or a near-memory engine evaluate the view on each read. Work moves from write time to read time.
note: GQA kernels already avoid repeat_kv copies.

title: Year-two DIMM remanufacturing: re-profile, re-fuse, resell
idea: No EUV: take back modules at year two, re-test them with fleet telemetry, re-fuse repairs and retire weak ranks, then resell them with a refreshed warranty. Time shift: product life runs past 5 years and needs no new wafers.

title: Harvested DDR4 into heavily coded CXL memory pools
idea: No EUV: put DDR4 from decommissioned servers behind CXL controllers that add chipkill-plus-erasure coding and per-row retirement, tolerating aged parts with higher error rates. Existing silicon becomes a second-life memory tier.

title: LPDDR partial-array self-refresh made real by OS compaction
idea: LPDDR has offered Partial Array Self-Refresh for years, but it went unused because OS allocators scatter live pages across every bank. Add a kernel 'refresh-aware compaction' pass that migrates live pages into the fewest banks before idle and marks the empty banks to the controller, which then stops refreshing them.

title: AMD HSA, fixed: kill shadow copies with shared virtual memory
idea: AMD's HSA/hUMA promised CPU-GPU shared pointers but died from a weak software ecosystem. Inference stacks today keep a host pinned copy, a framework copy and a GPU copy of weights; enforce single-copy with HSA-style shared page tables where the GPU maps host LPDDR directly and loaders mmap checkpoints instead of reading them into buffers.

title: Error-correcting pointers rescued from PCM to absorb DRAM hard faults
idea: Error-Correcting Pointers (ECP) were invented for PCM wear-out and died with it. Fix by moving them to DRAM: each 64B line gets 2-3 pointer-plus-replacement-bit entries in on-die spare cells, populated in the field when scrubbing finds a permanently failing bit, so SECDED stays reserved for soft errors.
note: ECP-style pointers in DRAM proposed before; modest yield gain.

title: eDRAM's refresh burden replaced by decay-as-miss caches
idea: Intel's Crystal Well and IBM POWER eDRAM caches were dropped partly over refresh power and hot retention. Fix: never refresh; each line carries a coarse write-epoch tag, any line older than its retention budget or failing ECC is treated as a cache miss and refetched, and dirty lines are evicted before their epoch expires.
note: Close to known refresh-free/decay eDRAM cache work (Refrint, Hi-ECC).

title: Lifetime-matched no-refresh regions hold short-lived AI tensors
idea: Effect: exponential RC charge decay used as a free timer. A new mode register and allocator hint expose per-bank refresh-off regions; the runtime places activations, KV-cache scratch and gradient buffers that live <32 ms there (each write restores charge), so those rows are never refreshed.

title: Silicon-oxygen HSQ resist becomes the patterned inter-tier dielectric directly
idea: Spin hydrogen silsesquioxane, write cell-isolation and inter-tier oxide patterns by e-beam, develop, and cure it into a SiO2-like dielectric that stays in the device, so each tier's isolation is written rather than deposited, masked and etched; repeat per tier on alignment marks.

title: Phosphorus monolayer doping uniformly dopes vertical pillar sidewalls without implant
idea: Graft a self-limiting monolayer of a phosphorus-bearing molecule (e.g., diethyl vinylphosphonate) onto HF-cleaned vertical Si pillars, cap with evaporated SiO2 and spike-anneal to drive a conformal ~1e20 cm^-3, few-nm-deep n+ layer into every sidewall and pillar top.

title: Point-of-use helium recapture loops on every tool
idea: Periodic-table walk, He (2): the element is irreplaceable in a few steps, so fit each remaining He user (cryopumps, leak checks, CZ purge blends) with polymer-membrane plus PSA recapture and local recompression, returning >90% to a fab ring main instead of venting.

title: Al: self-passivating pages escalate ECC in place like alumina
idea: Like aluminum growing oxide only where exposed, controller RTL escalates a page to a stronger mode (extra symbols borrowed from a metadata carve-out, or duplicate plus checksum) the moment it logs a correctable error, leaving the rest of memory at lean ECC.

title: S: vulcanized cross-channel parity rebuilds rows lost to hammer
idea: Like sulfur cross-linking rubber chains, a CXL/FPGA controller keeps the XOR of row N across four channels in a fifth channel, updated on writeback, so a row that on-die ECC reports uncorrectable is rebuilt from the cross-link.
note: Like IBM RAIM; 25% overhead.

title: Retreaded memory: remanufacture DRAM dies from retired servers
idea: Like truck-tire retreading and auto-part remanufacturing, hyperscalers return 3-5 year old DIMMs to a line that desolders packages by IR reflow, retests at speed, re-bins by retention and speed, and rebuilds them onto new modules with spare dies and sparing-aware firmware for CXL memory-expansion tiers.

title: Auto-parts remanufacturing line rebins harvested server DRAM into CXL pools
idea: Run a reman line: robots strip DIMMs from retired servers, packages are desoldered, X-ray screened, burned in and retention-binned, then reballed onto CXL Type-3 expander boards whose controller sets refresh and ECC per bin.

title: Retreading: remanufacture retired DIMMs into graded CXL expanders
idea: Tire retreaders reuse old carcasses. A remanufacturing line pulls DDR4/DDR5 from decommissioned servers, retests the chips, bins them by retention and speed, and remounts them on CXL expander cards whose controller maps around weak rows. The cards are sold as a warm memory tier.
note: Remanufacturing business variant of I-04900 with retention binning.

title: Factory-seconds HBM: sell partly failed stacks as shorter SKUs
idea: Like outlet garments, stacks with one or two dead dies get fused-off remap in the base die and ship as 8- or 10-high parts instead of being scrapped. Pricing tiers make the seconds a market.
note: Partial-good harvesting is standard practice in chips.

title: Ripstop quarantine bay: hot rows migrate into victimless sparse rows
idea: Ripstop fabric uses a reinforced grid where tears stop; reserve ~1% of each bank as a 'ripstop bay' in which only every third row holds data, and when the activation tracker flags an aggressor, migrate its data into the bay where it has no data-bearing physical neighbours to disturb.
note: Very close to AQUA (MICRO 2022).

title: OS-driven TRIM for DRAM: never refresh dead rows
idea: IFR: only living data is maintained. A new JEDEC command, like SSD TRIM, lets the OS and hypervisor declare row ranges free (freed pages, ballooned guest memory); the device refresh counter skips them until the next write.

title: OS-visible elastic capacity retires failed mats instead of modules
idea: Ideal result: memory that degrades by grams, not kilograms. Periphery reports failed or weak mats through a standard interface, and the OS offlines just those address ranges, shrinking capacity by a fraction of a percent per fault.

title: Retired DDR4 reborn in CXL expanders as compressed far tier
idea: IFR: memory already mined is used forever. Constraint: no new extraction of W, Hf or Ta, so harvest DDR4 DIMMs from decommissioned servers, test and bin them, and mount them in CXL type-3 expanders behind an inline compressor as a far tier for cold pages.

title: Rack spot market for stranded memory, priced per GB-second
idea: Ideal: no gigabyte sits idle anywhere. Closest achievable: CXL-attached rack memory pools publish idle capacity to a scheduler that leases it per GB-second to neighbouring servers, migrating cold pages at ~10 ms granularity and reclaiming on demand.

title: Bad-cell-map grade: ship scattered-defect dies with fused bitmaps
idea: Ideal: no die is ever scrapped. Closest: dies failing JEDEC only because of scattered bad cells are sold as a new grade carrying a fused, compressed bad-cell map that the host reads at boot, retiring the affected 4 KB pages or placing error-tolerant tensors there.

title: Refresh hides in compute bubbles: pull-in synchronized to AI kernel phases
idea: 10-person constraint: only the scheduler is ours. A runtime hook signals the memory controller when a compute-bound phase starts (e.g. a high-arithmetic-intensity GEMM tile). The controller pulls in up to the JEDEC-allowed 8 pending refreshes during that bubble and postpones refresh during bandwidth-bound phases.

title: Second-life DRAM harvested from retired AI servers
idea: Rule: no retired DRAM goes to shredding. An industrial line desolders DRAM packages from 4-5-year-old hyperscaler boards, grades them with BIST, reballs them and assembles new modules with chipkill and stronger ECC for tier-2 CXL expansion memory, priced at 30-50% of new.

title: U.S. memory remanufacturing depots instead of new fabs
idea: Rule: failed memory must be repaired, not replaced. Regional U.S. depots equipped with testers, PPR programmers, die-rework and reball lines receive failed modules from hyperscalers. Most failures are a single die or row, so modules are repaired and returned within days.

title: Fleet-learned repair: OTA refresh and PPR updates by lot signature
idea: Rule: repair must reach modules already in the field. The vendor aggregates anonymized ECC logs from millions of modules, learns failure signatures per wafer lot, and pushes firmware updates that adjust refresh rates and run pre-emptive soft PPR on modules carrying the same lot ID before they fail.

title: Tensor-aware codec in the memory controller (hardware DFloat11 + optional lossy KV)
idea: A codec in each GPU memory partition, with a matching engine in the HBM4 logic base die for capacity management, Huffman-codes the 8-bit exponents of tagged BF16 tensors. About 40 symbols are used, ~2.6 b entropy. Sign and mantissa are packed raw, 32 values per 64 B sector -> ~44 B. Fixed-rate block coding (32 exponents in a 96-112 b budget with an escape code) keeps random access at sector granularity. An optional lossy mode, under software control, applies KIVI-style per-channel K / per-token V 2-bit quantisation with a full-precision residual window. Unlike LZ-class CXL compressors (Marvell Structera, ZeroPoint: 2-3x on general data), this codec targets floating-point tensors, which LZ compresses poorly.

title: Swap new DIMMs for retired DDR4 behind CXL expanders
idea: Substitute new wafers with recycled bits. DDR4 harvested from decommissioned servers is tested, binned and mounted on CXL expanders as a second memory tier in new DDR5 servers, and OS tiering places cold pages on it.
note: Hyperscalers already deploy reused DDR4 behind CXL.

title: Swap live background-tab heaps for pixel-and-state snapshots
idea: Substitute a background tab's DOM and JS heap (often 100-500 MB) with a compressed screenshot plus URL, scroll position and form state. The browser rehydrates the tab by reload and state replay on focus, and service-worker caches make the reload fast. No hardware change.

title: Swap random request placement for document-affinity routing of long contexts
idea: Substitute random load balancing with context-aware routing. The balancer fingerprints each request's large shared context (a codebase, a contract, a transcript) and sends every request on that context to one GPU group, replicating hot documents only when queue depth demands.
note: Prefix-aware routing deployed in SGLang/llm-d.

title: Rack daemon lends idle server RAM over RDMA
idea: Substitute buying more local DRAM with a kernel swap backend that pages cold memory into idle RAM on neighbouring servers via RDMA verbs, with replicated pages and fast failover.
note: Infiniswap/Fastswap-style disaggregated memory is well known.

title: Erasure coding replaces triple replication in in-memory stores
idea: Combine storage-style Reed-Solomon coding with in-memory data grids (Redis, parameter servers, session stores): keep k data shards plus m parity shards across nodes and update parity with RDMA-shipped XOR deltas on writes instead of holding three full DRAM replicas.

title: Gated lateral thyristor latch in thin SOI foundry
idea: MINIFY the bistable to one gated PNPN body: in a 45/22 nm SOI MPW, a lateral thyristor with a capacitively coupled gate holds '1' by regenerative latching and '0' by blocking, with ~nA holding current and ~1-2 ns gate-pulse writes; no capacitor, no refresh.
note: T-RAM (TCCT) was commercialized and licensed around 2009; standby current and variability limited it.

title: Magnify effective capacity: compression engine in the base die
idea: Prototype a stack whose logic base die compresses cache lines inline, with 64B lines packed into variable slots by a metadata table, using an FPGA in front of commodity DRAM. Then tape out the engine as a $200k chiplet.

title: Minify exact state to sketches: sketch-first analytics engine
idea: Minify exact hash aggregations, distinct counts, quantiles and join estimates to HyperLogLog, Count-Min and KLL sketches carrying explicit error bars. Exact recomputation from flash happens only when the query demands it.

title: Minify indexes 100x with piecewise-linear learned indexes
idea: Minify B-tree internal nodes and hash directories into PGM-style piecewise-linear models with guaranteed error windows. Each lookup does one model step and one bounded scan.

title: Minify training-data buffers: decode media at last moment
idea: Minify data-loader DRAM by keeping images, video and audio in their compressed codec form in host memory. They are decoded only inside the accelerator, tile by tile, right before the first layer (on-GPU JPEG/AV1 decoders).

title: Eliminate the full gradient buffer by fusing backward with update
idea: Apply each layer's optimizer update the moment its gradient is computed in the backward pass, then free that gradient immediately, so the full-model gradient tensor never exists (LOMO-style fused update).

title: Eliminate 3x replication in memory caches using erasure coding
idea: A drop-in memcached/Redis cluster proxy stripes values with Reed-Solomon RS(10,4) across nodes and decodes on the client, replacing triple replication for durable caches.

title: Eliminate per-worker model copies via shared read-only weight mappings
idea: A serving framework loads weights once as a read-only mmap of safetensors files shared by all CPU workers, and shares a single GPU copy across worker processes using CUDA IPC handles, instead of each worker loading its own.

title: Eliminate parsed object trees: query JSON directly from raw bytes
idea: Services replace DOM-materializing JSON/protobuf parsers with SIMD on-demand cursors over the raw buffer (a structural-index tape), so no object tree is built in memory.
note: simdjson On-Demand already does this.

title: Eliminate serverless warm pools with lazy snapshot-restored microVMs
idea: Idle function microVMs are snapshotted to NVMe; on invocation a userfaultfd handler restores pages lazily, prefetching a recorded working-set trace, to reach under 10 ms cold starts without keeping instances in RAM.

title: Counter-current rinse cascade: last rinse feeds the first
idea: Reverse water flow direction: the cleanest final-rinse water flows backward to feed earlier, dirtier rinse stages and then pre-wash, as in counter-current extraction, before reclaim.

title: Fuse the optimizer into backward so gradients never fully exist
idea: Rearrange the training step from backward-then-update to update-during-backward: the optimizer applies each parameter tensor's gradient the moment it is produced and frees it at once, with gradient clipping taken from a running norm of the previous step.

title: Guests drop their page cache so one host cache serves all
idea: Reverse double caching in virtualization: guest kernels mount files through DAX over virtio-pmem/virtiofs, so file pages come straight from the host's single page cache, and guests report free pages back at once.

title: Old memory serves new CPUs: DDR4-to-CXL transplant bridges
idea: Reverse the retirement order: when servers retire, their DDR4 DIMMs move onto CXL expander cards with DDR4-to-CXL controllers in new-generation servers. The memory gets a second 4-5 year life instead of being shredded.
note: Already deployed (Azure Pond-style DDR4 behind CXL controllers).

title: RAMDAC-style palettized tensors decoded by near-memory lookup tables
idea: TRIZ #32 Color changes: as 1990s VGA stored 8-bit palette indices instead of 24-bit color, store weights and embeddings as 3-4-bit indices into per-tensor 8-16-entry palettes learned by k-means; a 180 nm RAMDAC-like LUT chip on the memory path expands indices to FP16 on read.
note: k-means palettization is already standard (Deep Compression, Core ML).

title: Segment:offset 32-bit relative pointers for in-memory data structures
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter change: like 8086 segment:offset addressing, data structures store 32-bit (or 16-bit) offsets relative to a segment base held in FS/GS or a register, inside 4 GB arenas, halving pointer width; compilers emit base-plus-offset loads at ~1 cycle of cost.

title: Pharma plate screening: composition-spread capacitor libraries on one wafer
idea: Borrowed from drug discovery, which screens thousands of compounds in parallel plates: co-sputter from three targets to make continuous composition gradients (Ti-Zr-Al-O, Sr-Ti-Nb-O) across one wafer, shadow-mask 10,000 MIM capacitor dots, and auto-probe k, leakage and breakdown overnight with one sputter tool and a probe station.
note: Composition-spread high-k screening is 1990s art (van Dover).

title: Contact sheets: statistical sketches in DRAM, full records in NV
idea: Like photographers picking from thumbnails before pulling negatives, keep probabilistic sketches (count-min, HyperLogLog, quantile digests) in DRAM and full records in persistent memory; queries that tolerate bounded error are answered from sketches and only exact queries touch NV.

title: Entropy-coded weights decoded inside registers, never materialized
idea: Inverts 'data must be decompressed before compute': weights stay Huffman/ANS-coded in DRAM and HBM and are decoded per tile into shared memory or registers inside the matmul kernel. The main target is BF16/FP8 exponent fields, which carry only ~2-3 bits of entropy.
note: Essentially DFloat11/ZipNN; ~30% lossless.

title: Learned indexes replace in-memory hash tables and B-trees
idea: Inverts 'an index stores keys and pointers': piecewise-linear models predict a key's position in a sorted array to within a small error window, replacing in-memory B-trees and hash indexes. Software only, on any existing CPU.
note: Kraska 2018; widely pursued.

title: Idle containers hibernate to NVMe and restore pages lazily
idea: Box: evict whole process × orchestrator × container × idle >N s × checkpoint image + userfaultfd lazy page-in. Idle services are checkpointed to local flash and their memory freed; a request wakes them in milliseconds with pages faulted in on demand.

title: Count-min and HyperLogLog sketches replace exact per-key stream state
idea: Box: probabilistic sketch × stream processor × per-key state × continuous × bounded-error counters. Counting, distinct and top-k operators keep fixed-size sketches with ~1% error bounds instead of exact per-key hash maps.

title: Online miss-ratio curves right-size every in-memory cache
idea: Box: right-size × every application cache × cache instance × continuous × spatially sampled miss-ratio curve. Each cache samples ~0.1% of keys to build its miss-ratio curve online, and an operator shrinks caches to the knee where the marginal MB stops buying hits.

title: Pointerless graphs: succinct structures for national-scale analytics
idea: Po: data structures without pointers. Graph, trie and index workloads (knowledge graphs, genomics, search) are rebuilt on succinct encodings (rank/select bitvectors, wavelet trees, Elias-Fano adjacency) and queried in compressed form on domestic CPUs.

title: Scarcity chargeback: bill teams the real price of gigabyte-hours
idea: Po: every line of code shows its memory price tag. Enterprises and agencies charge internal teams the current spot price of U.S.-made DRAM per GB-hour, and CI gates block merges that push a service past its byte budget without sign-off.
note: Standard FinOps practice.

title: Rewrite random-access algorithms as streaming passes over disk
idea: Worsen: write pointer-chasing code that demands everything in DRAM. Flip: recast graph, join and sort workloads as external-memory streaming algorithms (sort-merge, bucketed scatter-gather, semi-streaming graph sketches) so data lives on HDD or QLC and DRAM holds only sort buffers.
note: Classic external-memory algorithms.

title: Desert camel's stored fat: lossless entropy-coded weights decoded in shared memory
idea: A camel carries dense fat and converts it to water only when needed. BF16 weights live in HBM with the low-entropy exponent field Huffman-coded and the mantissa left raw. Each kernel decodes its tile into SM shared memory just before the matmul, so expanded weights never exist in DRAM.

title: Embargoed Soviet tinkerer: CXL tier built from scrapped DDR4 DIMMs
idea: With no new chips available, the tinkerer reuses old ones. Off-the-shelf FPGA CXL boards (~$5-10k each) each host 8-16 decommissioned DDR4 RDIMMs, burned in and binned by error rate, and expose them as a CXL Type-3 warm tier; firmware adds patrol scrubbing and thermal throttling. Budget: ~$400k for boards and lab, ~$600k for two FPGA/firmware engineers over 24 months.

title: Tetris player clears lines: mesh fragmented pages without moving objects
idea: A Tetris player clears half-empty rows. A meshing allocator finds two virtual pages whose live objects don't overlap in offset, copies one into the other, and remaps both virtual pages to the same physical frame, freeing a frame without changing any pointer. A fleet fragmentation profiler proves the payoff, and the work fits well under $1M.

title: Ant colony's pheromone trails: route requests to replicas holding their prefix
idea: Ants follow pheromone to where the food already is. An inference router keeps a decaying radix-tree sketch (the 'pheromone') of which prompt prefixes each replica holds and sends each request to the longest match, balanced against load. Each shared prefix is then cached once per fleet instead of once per replica. A few engineer-months.

title: Race-car telemetry decay: multi-resolution rings that downsample in place
idea: From F1 and flight telemetry with fixed memory: metric and trace stores keep a fixed-size ring per series in which a background engine merges older samples into progressively coarser buckets (mean, min, max, quantile sketch), so memory per series is constant regardless of retention.
note: RRDtool-style rings, long established.

title: Desolder, retest, rebin: die-level DRAM harvesting from e-waste
idea: Scale jump from discarded device to die: reflow DRAM packages off retired phones, laptops, GPU boards and DIMMs, then screen them on existing ATE testers at trailing test houses for speed and retention. Re-ball the good parts onto new modules for edge, IoT and capacity tiers.

title: Compression-funded ECC spends freed bytes on stronger parity
idea: No EUV: when a 64B line compresses to 48B, the controller stores 16B of extra parity in the freed space, raising correction from 1 to ~8 symbols for that line. Weak DUV arrays get strong protection without fixed overhead.

title: Endpoint-sensed rinses replace fixed-time water rinses
idea: Within $1M/24 months: retrofit wet benches with inline resistivity and TOC sensors in the rinse drain and software that ends each rinse when effluent purity recovers, instead of fixed worst-case recipes; pilot on 10 benches.

title: 2050 watchmaker places phosphorus atoms as multi-electron bits
idea: A 2050 watchmaker places atoms instead of gears. Hydrogen-resist STM lithography places 4-atom phosphorus donor clusters in silicon at 3 nm pitch; each cluster holds 0-3 extra electrons (2 bits), sensed by an adjacent single-electron transistor. A national atomic-precision consortium runs MEMS arrays of 10^5 STM tips to write each wafer.
note: 100x density if it worked, but extra-electron binding needs cryo and 1e5-tip STM writing is a miracle.

title: Minify writes to one: model weights in stamped ROM cartridges
idea: Inference weights, the bulk of AI memory, are written once per model; store them in 100+ layer 3D via-programmed ROM nanoimprint-stamped from a master, with DRAM-class random read, shipped as swappable per-model cartridges so DRAM holds only KV cache and activations.
note: Write-once weights in stamped 3D ROM could undercut DRAM $/GB; doubts are per-model masters and DRAM-class read from deep stacks. Taalas/HBF adjacent.

title: Array-only DRAM sensed directly by the processor's sense amplifiers
idea: Eliminate the memory die's periphery and PHY: the DRAM die carries only cells, local bitlines and wordline stubs; every 32-bitline group feeds a local charge-transfer pre-amp to one ~1 um hybrid-bond pad, and the sense amps, decoders and row buffers live in the logic die beneath on fast low-voltage transistors. The 'interface' is a bitline.
note: Array-on-logic bonding is pursued (CBA); putting sense amps on processor die across bitline-pitch bonds is bold, unproven SNR.

title: Micro-HBM carpet: dozens of tiny stacks over the die
idea: Eliminate the beachfront limit and interposer distance: instead of 8 large edge stacks, hybrid-bond ~64 small 4-high 1-2 GB stacks directly over the compute die's area with thermal pillars between them, each feeding the tile beneath it.
note: Short vertical wires cut I/O energy ~15x; DRAM over hot logic raises refresh and thermal limits.
