title: Make the interposer the memory: DRAM-filled active interposer
idea: Swap substrate and memory roles: build the large silicon interposer under an accelerator (2,500+ mm2, relaxed 40-65 nm pitch, mostly empty silicon) as an 8-tier relaxed-pitch DRAM array with routing on top, so the accelerator sits directly on ~100 GB of memory with micron-scale vertical access.
note: Turns interposer silicon into ~100 GB under the accelerator; doubt: huge-area DRAM yield and 3D relaxed-pitch process.

title: Flip the interposer: wafer-scale DRAM becomes the substrate
idea: Reverse the substrate role: instead of a passive silicon interposer carrying GPU and HBM side by side, a full 300 mm DRAM wafer (cell arrays plus a top hybrid-bond layer) is the substrate, and compute chiplets are hybrid-bonded face-down onto it at ~9 um pitch so each chiplet sits directly over its own memory tiles. Global chiplet-to-chiplet wiring runs in the DRAM wafer's upper metals.
note: Micrometre vertical paths cut pJ/bit 30x vs HBM; doubt is wafer-scale DRAM yield, thermal coupling and needing a DRAM fab partner.

title: Compute on top, memory underneath, power through the stack
idea: Reverse HBM's placement: the accelerator die sits on top of a DRAM stack next to the heat sink, dense power-TSV columns through every DRAM die feed it, and the memory interface becomes a direct face-to-back hybrid bond into the top DRAM die.
note: Big vertical bandwidth and energy gain; feeding hundreds of watts through DRAM dies costs area and noise.

title: Endosymbiotic transfer: array dies keep no brains; logic die holds all
idea: Mitochondria moved most of their genes to the nucleus; strip memory dies to bare arrays with minimal drivers (no ECC, refresh logic, repair fuses or BIST) and hybrid-bond many of them to one logic-node 'nucleus' die that does sensing, strong LDPC decoding, refresh scheduling and fault mapping for all, so arrays use the cheapest array-only process.
note: Arrays-only dies plus shared decoder die; 100x claim overstated, CBA/Xtacking-like.

title: Sense-amp-direct bonding: logic reads subarray stripes without global I/O
idea: Invert 'data must leave through global I/O, serializers and pads': hybrid-bond a logic die so every subarray's local sense-amp stripe has ~1 um-pitch bond pads directly above it and logic consumes row buffers in place.
note: Exposing full row buffers to logic kills overfetch and global I/O energy; needs DRAM-fab cooperation and dense bonds over SA stripes.

title: Undiced wafer-scale DRAM with defect-routing mesh bonded to accelerators
idea: Leave a 300 mm DRAM wafer undiced, link its ~2,000 mats through a redundant on-wafer mesh that test maps around bad mats, and wafer-to-wafer bond it face-to-face to an accelerator wafer so every compute tile has DRAM within millimetres.
note: Wafer-scale bonding removes packaging and cuts pJ/bit ~10x; doubts: compound wafer yield matching and thermal coupling.

title: Metal-free vertical-bitline 3D gain-cell stack with doped-polysilicon wordline tiers
idea: Bits rise linearly with tiers while wafer cost rises ~1% per tier because lithography is shared. Stack 120 tiers of in-situ-doped poly-Si wordlines (no W replacement gate) with 2T0C Zn-Sn-O gain cells around vertical bitline holes in a relaxed ~100x100 nm per-tier footprint; gain cells tolerate poly resistance because their gate load is ~0.1 fF.
note: Gain cells tolerate poly WL resistance, enabling 120 cheap tiers; doubt is 2T cell integration per tier around vertical BL.

title: Run vertical gain-cell DRAM through idle 3D NAND fab lines
idea: First principle: most of the capital in a 3D NAND fab is alternating-stack deposition, high-AR channel-hole etch and staircase formation, which is exactly the tool set needed for a vertical-channel 2T0C gain cell: a stack of horizontal wordline layers pierced by oxide-semiconductor channels. Port the NAND flow (ONON stack, channel hole, replacement gate) to a gain-cell DRAM so NAND overcapacity in down-cycles produces DRAM with no new tools.
note: Reuses installed 3D NAND tooling for vertical oxide 2T0C DRAM; doubt is gain-cell density and retention vs 1T1C.

title: Bond sense amplifiers straight to compute and delete the PHY
idea: A bit only has to travel ~10 um vertically, so PHY, SerDes, global datapath and pads are overhead, not physics. Hybrid-bond each subarray's local sense-amp column outputs at 1 um pitch directly to registers in the logic die beneath, running millions of unserialized connections at ~200 MHz so the bitline restore charge is essentially the only signaling energy.
note: Same subarray-direct bonding; millions of 1 um bonds and register area on logic are the doubt.

title: Logic on top, memory beneath through dedicated power columns
idea: Box: DRAM stack x standard x standard x power columns through reserved DRAM zones plus face-to-face signal bonds x DRAM as base x hybrid bonding. The accelerator die sits on top of the DRAM stack, next to the cold plate, and the DRAM below carries dedicated power-via columns, putting every compute tile ~50 um from its memory.
note: Area-scaled bandwidth near 0.1 pJ/bit; DRAM under hot logic and limited capacity are the doubts.

title: Word-sized micro-mats, each with its own bond to logic
idea: Po: the page is the size of a word. Cut the array into 64x64-cell micro-mats, each with its own small sense amps and one sub-um hybrid bond straight down to the controller/compute die, so an activation opens only 64 bits and delivers all of them; millions of independent mats replace a few hundred 8 KB pages.
note: Word-sized activation per bonded micro-mat kills overfetch, ~10x random-access energy; doubt: SA and bond area per 4k cells.

title: Octopus's arm brains: 3D latch sense amps on 8-cell bitlines
idea: An octopus puts neurons in every arm. A back-end oxide-semiconductor latch sense amp is stacked above every 8-cell vertical bitline segment, so a cell shares charge with ~0.2 fF instead of a ~60 fF, 512-cell bitline, and only a gated global line carries the result out.
note: 8-cell bitline segments cut bitline load ~100x, easing charge wall and array energy; doubt: n-only oxide latch offset and speed.

title: Polar explorer's 77 K cold-memory pods run by gas suppliers
idea: A polar explorer knows cold preserves things. At 77 K access-transistor leakage falls by more than 10^6, so a cell needs ~0.3 fF instead of 5 fF: the 70:1 pillar gives way to a planar MIM cap over a vertical-channel 4F^2 transistor, and 7 such tiers are bonded. The pods are LN2-immersion memory, sold as a service by industrial-gas firms.
note: Leakage collapse at 77K enables tiny planar caps and tiers; doubt: 0.3 fF sensing margin and cooling energy overhead.

title: Wafer-scale DRAM carpet bonded beneath a wafer-scale accelerator
idea: Jump from die stacks to whole wafers: hybrid-bond an entire 300 mm DRAM wafer face-to-face under a wafer-scale logic wafer at 2 um pitch, so every compute tile owns the ~50 mm2 of DRAM directly beneath it through millions of vertical links. Dead DRAM tiles are fused out by a wafer-level map and the tile above borrows its neighbor's memory over the on-wafer mesh.
note: TB-scale DRAM under every tile at ~0.05 pJ/bit; doubts: logic heat raises DRAM refresh, wafer yield.

title: 77 K memory pods: cold sensing permits flat capacitors and tiers
idea: Failure mined: the Microsoft-Rambus cryo-DRAM program was shelved because cooling general servers cost more than it saved. Fix: target AI clusters that already run liquid-nitrogen loops. At 77 K leakage falls by >1e6 (refresh nearly vanishes), kT/C noise and SA offset fall ~2-4x and bitline resistance falls ~6x, so a 0.4 fF planar MIM cell is enough and can be stacked in deposited tiers.
note: 77 K kills leakage so 0.4 fF flat cells stack in tiers; doubt is cooling economics and tier transistors.

title: IBM eDRAM micro-sense-amps built inside each 3D DRAM tier
idea: Failure mined: IBM's deep-trench eDRAM, with 3-transistor micro sense amps on 32-cell local bitlines, died only because GlobalFoundries quit 7 nm. Fix: carry the micro-SA into 3D, with a 3-transistor thin-film micro-SA beside each 16-cell lateral bitline in every tier. Each tier becomes a self-sensing short-bitline array, where a 1 fF planar capacitor still yields ~100 mV.
note: Short 16-cell local bitlines let ~1 fF lateral caps work in 3D tiers; doubt: thin-film micro-SA mismatch and tier transistor quality.

title: Trilogy's wafer-scale dream fixed: an unsawn DRAM wafer as memory backplane
idea: Gene Amdahl's Trilogy failed on wafer-scale yield and on CTE-driven delamination between the wafer and its packaging. Keep a whole 300 mm DRAM wafer unsawn (~3-4 TB raw at ~0.4 Gb/mm2), map out bad reticles at test, and hybrid-bond logic chiplets face-to-face only onto good reticle sites; because everything is silicon on silicon there is no CTE mismatch, and dicing, packaging, TSVs and interposers disappear.
note: TB-class memory at face-to-face bandwidth, no package/TSV; doubts: power delivery, heat, I/O off wafer, reticle-map yield.

title: Photoconductive receivers let one optical broadcast replace replicated weight copies
idea: Today every GPU's HBM holds an identical weight copy for data-parallel inference. Instead, a single master copy is broadcast over waveguide or free-space optics to dozens of compute dies. Each die captures the bits just in time with photoconductive Ge sampling receivers and keeps only a small staging buffer.
note: Broadcast variant with Ge photoconductive samplers; receiver bandwidth and synchronization are the doubts.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory pool lets capacitorless gain cells hold for hours
idea: Effect: carrier freeze-out and suppressed thermal generation at 77 K. A CXL-attached rack memory pool runs at 77 K, where generation current falls >1e10x and kT noise drops 4x, so 2-transistor gain cells with only ~0.05-0.1 fF parasitic node capacitance hold data seconds to hours and their tiny signals read cleanly. There is no capacitor module and almost no refresh.
note: 77 K makes capacitorless stacked gain cells viable; cryocooler overhead and system cost doubtful.

title: Copper bond per bitline gives every bitline its own sense amp
idea: Hybrid-bond the cell-array wafer face-to-face to a logic wafer at ~0.4 um Cu pitch so every short local bitline (64 cells) lands on its own sense amplifier built in an advanced logic node, abolishing open/folded bitline sharing.
note: Per-local-bitline SA via sub-um bonding attacks overfetch, Cs and periphery; bond pitch vs bitline pitch geometry is the doubt.

title: Dopant-free Schottky source/drain unlocks 64-tier lateral 3D DRAM
idea: IFR: the lateral transistor in each tier needs no implant. Through the vertical slit, recess each deposited Si or oxide tier and convert the exposed ends into dopant-segregated metal/silicide Schottky contacts, so all 64 tiers get source and drain in one conformal step instead of impossible deep implants.
note: Solves lateral S/D doping in deep tiers; Schottky contacts trade write current against off-leakage.

title: Convert idle 3D NAND fabs into DRAM-class tier lines
idea: IFR: the factory already exists and is paid for. Retool underused, depreciated 3D NAND fabs, whose channel-hole etch, ALD and staircase tools are the same ones needed, to make deposition-defined DRAM-class cells (short-retention charge-trap or oxide gain-cell tiers), with joint ventures that give NAND makers a DRAM-priced product.
note: Tool overlap is real; missing piece is a proven stackable DRAM-class cell with unlimited endurance.

title: Vertical crosspoint TFT: 1T1C cell with two masks per layer
idea: IFR: the cell is just the place where two lines cross. At each bitline/wordline crossing, a vertical oxide-semiconductor channel grows in a self-aligned via through the wordline, which wraps it as the gate, and a small pad on top is the storage node facing a common plate film; each layer needs only two non-EUV masks.
note: Self-aligned two-mask layers; doubt: tiny pad capacitance for sensing and real per-layer cost.

title: Processor-hosted sense amps make memory dies pure cell fabric
idea: Ideal result: the memory die holds nothing but bits. Hybrid-bond a cell-only die face-to-face onto the accelerator die, which carries all sense amps, decoders and row buffers in advanced logic at ~1 um bond pitch, so data never crosses a PHY.
note: Cell-only die on processor removes periphery and PHY; 1 um bond pitch cannot reach ~40 nm bitlines without on-die muxing.

title: Zero-capacitance bitline: one bonded sense amp per vertical pillar
idea: IFR: 'the bitline has no capacitance, so any stored charge reads.' Backward: in a vertical-bitline 3D array, Cu-Cu hybrid-bond each pillar foot (or each group of 4 pillars via a local mux) at ~300-400 nm pitch to its own sense amplifier on a logic wafer, so the bitline is only the 2-3 um stack height (~0.1 fF) instead of a 1,000-cell planar line.
note: Tiny bitline lets 0.3-0.5 fF lateral caps sense; doubt: 300-400 nm hybrid-bond pitch and SA area per pillar.

title: Inside-out cell: concentric shells built around one etched hole
idea: IFR: 'one hole builds every tier with no lateral patterning.' Backward: etch one hole through a 100-layer wordline-plane/sacrificial stack, recess each sacrificial layer by a self-limiting digital etch, and fill each annular cavity as nested shells (outer plate, high-k, storage node, oxide-semiconductor channel) so each tier forms a ring cell around the central vertical bitline, gated by its own wordline plane and sized only by film thickness.
note: One critical mask per ~100 tiers; doubt: annular capacitor gives ~1 fF, nested-shell fill in recesses.

title: Open-licensed DRAM array IP lets any foundry make commodity memory
idea: Ideal: every fab can make DRAM. Closest: a consortium develops a proven 6F2 array plus process-module recipes validated on 2-3 foundries' tool sets and licenses them per wafer (an ARM model for memory), so logic foundries add DRAM lines without a decade of process R&D.
note: ARM-style licensing could break the oligopoly; doubt: recipes are tool-coupled and incumbents hold patents.

title: Leaky 3D NAND string with direct-tunneling nanodots for seconds retention
idea: Adapt 3D NAND but make it leak on purpose: replace the 5 nm tunnel oxide with 1.8 nm SiO2 plus Si nanodots so writes use direct tunneling in ~20 ns with no hot-carrier wear, retention is ~seconds, and the NOR-connected vertical array is refreshed like DRAM.
note: Sunrise Memory's quasi-volatile 3D NOR pursued this; doubt: ~1e11 endurance versus DRAM-class unlimited.

title: LCD panel fabs make DRAM by the square meter on glass
idea: Adapted from TFT-LCD backplanes (an LCD pixel is literally a 1T1C DRAM cell): run 1T1C oxide-TFT arrays on 3 m x 3 m Gen-10.5 glass in idle display fabs, reach ~375 nm features with self-aligned quadruple spacers, and stack 8 TFT tiers; accept 200-500 ns access and a heavy refresh budget.
note: Panel-area bits could be several-x cheaper; $1-2k per 8-tier SAQP panel is optimistic and 200-500 ns is not DRAM-class.

title: Magnify signal ratio with a local gain transistor every 16 cells
idea: Hierarchical bitline: a 16-cell local bitline (~2-3 fF) drives the gate of one local amplifier transistor that conditionally discharges the long global bitline, MAGNIFYING the effective Cs/Cbl ratio from ~1:10 to ~1:1.
note: If ~1 fF cells sense via local gain, short caps enable 3D tiers; doubt is local-amp variation and area.

title: Eliminate sputtered magnetic stacks: electroplated vertical racetracks in alumina pores
idea: Eliminate per-bit cells and argon-sputtered MTJ stacks: electroplate Co/Ni nanowires with composition modulated every 20 nm (built-in pinning notches) into 2-5 um anodic alumina pores, and shift magnetic domain walls past one read/write head at each pore base with current pulses; each pore holds ~100 bits.
note: Parkin-style 3D racetrack; reliable DW shifting in plated wires and per-pore read heads remain unsolved.

title: Endosymbiotic DRAM layer grown directly on accelerator logic
idea: Mitochondria live inside the host cell instead of in a separate organ; because <=400 C oxide access devices retain charge for seconds even at 85-105 C, fabricate a 1T1C memory layer in the BEOL directly above accelerator compute tiles, wired by vias instead of HBM PHYs and TSVs.
note: Monolithic oxide DRAM over compute cuts pJ/bit ~8x; doubt: capacity per layer vs HBM stacks.

title: Hole quantum-well floating body in SiGe for long retention
idea: Po: the stored charge lives in a room with no exit. Build a capacitorless floating-body cell with a buried compressively strained SiGe layer under the channel whose valence-band offset traps holes in a quantum well, so stored holes cannot recombine through the source/drain junctions as fast as in plain silicon.
note: Capacitorless 4F2 would bypass the charge wall; SiGe-well 1T-DRAM is known and FBC disturb/margin killed Z-RAM.

title: Hearing-aid analog: weights compute inside 3D-NAND strings
idea: From hearing aids running keyword spotters with analog in-memory compute: large-model weights live in 3D-NAND arrays operated as analog vector-matrix multipliers (string currents sum the products), so weights never occupy DRAM and only activations move.
note: Weights never in DRAM if it works; analog precision, read disturb and NAND speed are the doubts; widely researched.

title: Z-RAM reborn: floating-body cells in natively insulated stacked nanosheet tiers
idea: Z-RAM died because floating-body storage needed costly SOI wafers and its hole-storage margin collapsed at scale. Build it in a Si/SiGe superlattice 3D stack where removing the SiGe leaves every Si tier naturally insulated (SOI for free), and bias the wordline plane of the tier below negative as a back-gate that deepens the hole well, so each tier is a capacitorless 1T cell.
note: Capacitorless floating-body in released Si tiers resembles NEO X-DRAM; FBC retention scaling is the core doubt; back-gate is the twist.

title: Si: 100-tier deposited polysilicon floating-body cells, grain leakage tolerated
idea: Deposit alternating poly-Si/oxide layers as in 3D NAND and form capacitorless floating-body cells whose stored holes set the threshold; grain-boundary leakage makes ~1% of cells retain too briefly, which the code covers, so no single-crystal Si/SiGe epitaxy or wafer bonding is needed.
note: 3D NAND-style FB DRAM pursued (e.g., NEO X-DRAM); 1% weak cells exceeds practical ECC budgets.

title: Volatile 3D NAND: direct-tunnel charge-trap strings run as DRAM
idea: Ideal: DRAM at flash prices. Closest: build a 200+-layer 3D-NAND-style string with a 1.5-2.0 nm tunnel oxide (vs 5-7 nm) so programming is direct tunneling at ~4-6 V in ~100 ns without Fowler-Nordheim damage, giving ~1e12+ endurance; retention falls to ~1-10 s, so the array is refreshed like DRAM behind a DRAM-cache controller.
note: Close to SunRise-style quasi-volatile 3D NOR; endurance of thin tunnel oxide at 1e12+ is the key doubt.

title: Thermally drawn fiber preforms yield coaxial capacitor bundles
idea: Adapt optical-fiber drawing: build a macroscopic preform of metal/glass/metal coaxial rods, draw it ~1000x down to 30 nm features over km lengths, slice it into thin wafers of parallel coaxial capacitors, and hybrid-bond them onto access-transistor wafers.
note: Capacitor length becomes slice thickness, decoupling AR from etch; registration and 30 nm draw breakup are doubts.

title: Turbine-blade eutectic solidification grows built-in vertical nanorod plates
idea: Borrowed from directionally solidified eutectic alloys used in turbine blades: solidify a Si-TaSi2 eutectic ingot so billions of aligned metallic TaSi2 nanorods run through monocrystalline Si, then slice wafers in which each rod is a ready-made vertical capacitor plate or buried bitline, with cells formed around them by one mask.
note: Self-organized eutectic rods as pre-built vertical plates is unseen; rod pitch is microns at practical growth rates.

title: Eliminate storage-node lithography: transistors electroplate their own capacitor towers
idea: Eliminate the storage-node mask and etch: after building the access transistors, immerse the wafer in a plating bath and turn on every wordline so each working transistor's drain contact sources current and plates its own Ni/Ru nanotower; then add ALD dielectric (N2 purge) and top plate. No argon-sputtered seed is needed because the drains are the seeds.
note: Transistors plate their own nodes: self-aligned, mask-free, built-in yield screen; free-standing AR-100 towers will lean and collapse.

title: Vertical plated-wire memory: NiFe-lined holes through word-plane stack
idea: Revive 1960s plated-wire memory (NiFe electroplated on beryllium-copper wire, non-destructive readout, flown in Apollo-era and Skylab systems): etch vertical holes through an epitaxial stack of heavily doped silicon word planes by metal-assisted chemical etching, electroplate a circumferentially magnetized NiFe film on each hole wall around a copper core, and store a bit where each word plane crosses a hole. A word current tilts the magnetization slightly and the core senses the induced voltage without destroying it.
note: 3D NDRO magnetic memory from one hole mask is new; inductive read signal collapses at sub-100 nm.

title: Light-pumped self-restoring cell: photodiode gated by its own charge
idea: Box: cap x Si access nMOS x SA x backside-illuminated die under a uniform LED/laser sheet x thinned Si x BSI image-sensor process. Each cell adds a photodiode in series with a tiny transistor gated by the storage node, so a global light flash tops up only nodes that are already high, refreshing the whole array in parallel without any row activation.
note: Light-driven, self-gated top-up refreshes the whole array with zero activations; doubts: photodiode area per cell, stray photocurrent into 0-nodes.

title: Millefiori glass-cane draw sliced into litho-free vertical access arrays
idea: Assemble a cm-scale preform holding ~10^4 coaxial access-transistor cross-sections (chalcogenide-glass semiconductor core, glass gate dielectric, low-melting metal gate). Thermally draw it 10^4x as Venetian millefiori cane or optical fiber is drawn, then slice 100 nm discs: each slice is a ready-made array of vertical gate-all-around access switches.
note: Multimaterial fiber draw (Fink lab) sliced into GAA access arrays; doubts: 10 nm uniformity, chalcogenide channel quality, contacting slices.

title: Substitute sense amplifiers with complementary n-IGZO/p-SnO oxide gain cells
idea: Pair n-type IGZO and p-type SnO (or Cu2O) thin-film transistors in a 3T cell whose storage node gates a CMOS-like inverter, so a read drives a rail-to-rail level onto a short local line with no sense amplifier and no restore. Sputtered below 350 C, patterned with ArF only, stackable in BEOL.
note: Sense-amp-free rail-to-rail read removes overfetch; p-type oxide mobility and leakage are the doubt.

title: Laser-induced periodic ripples: light self-organizes the grating
idea: Reverse projection imaging into self-organization: scan femtosecond laser pulses over a thin film to create laser-induced periodic surface structures with periods of lambda/5 to lambda/10, then transfer them as the array line grating.

title: LCD chemistry: ferroelectric nematic liquid as a self-healing high-k dielectric
idea: Borrow display liquid crystals: fill a shallow cup capacitor with a ferroelectric nematic LC (RM734/DIO class, Ps ~6 uC/cm2, low-frequency permittivity ~1e3-1e4) confined in a 5-nm gap between alignment layers; as a liquid it cannot fatigue or crack, and breakdown spots self-heal by flow.
note: Giant static k likely collapses at ns and in 5 nm gaps; easy to test.

title: Po: the bit is when, not how much — wordline ramp
idea: Po: memory read by timing. Ramp the wordline slowly: an access transistor holding '0' turns on near Vwl=Vt while one holding '1' turns on only near Vt+VDD/2, so a per-bitline edge detector timestamps the first bitline movement against the ramp and decodes data from turn-on time and direction, largely independent of Cs.
note: Ramp-timed turn-on decoding is clever, but first-movement detection is still charge-limited by Cs/Cbl and noise.

title: All-zinc ferroelectric FETs on glass: wurtzite ZnMgO gate on ZnO
idea: 1T FeFETs die on the ferroelectric/semiconductor interface: traps, depolarization and a parasitic interlayer that eat retention and endurance. Wurtzite Zn(1-x)Mg(x)O has been reported ferroelectric and is lattice-matched to ZnO, so sputter a coherent ZnMgO gate on a ZnO channel on glass with no interfacial oxide, and run it as a nondestructive-read cell needing only seconds-to-days retention.

title: Layer-by-layer perovskite nanosheets give k-200 dielectric for shallow capacitors
idea: Effect: giant 2D dielectric polarizability plus electrostatic self-assembly. Alternate dips in polycation and exfoliated Ca2Nb3O10 or Sr2Nb3O10 nanosheets (k ~200 at ~10 nm) coat low-AR holes at room temperature. With k about 5x that of ZrO2 stacks, 5 fF fits in a ~12-15:1 hole.

title: Ca: lattice-matched CaF2/Si epitaxial superlattice for strain-free 3D tiers
idea: Grow alternating single-crystal Si and CaF2 layers (~0.6% mismatch) in one pump-down; CaF2 serves as tier isolation and as a sacrificial layer that etches with high selectivity to Si, avoiding the strain accumulation that caps SiGe/Si stacks.

title: Car e-coat for capacitors: self-limiting electrophoretic high-k fill
idea: Automotive e-coating paints car bodies conformally because the deposited film insulates and halts further deposition; apply electrophoretic deposition of 3-5 nm SrTiO3/BaTiO3 nanocrystals into high-AR capacitor holes, field-driven and self-limiting, followed by a low-temperature densification anneal.

title: Turbine-blade EB-PVD columns: seeded columnar growth forms capacitor electrodes
idea: Borrow the electron-beam PVD that grows columnar thermal-barrier coatings on jet blades: place TiN seed dots with the single added mask, then evaporate TiN at grazing incidence with wafer rotation so self-shadowing grows isolated straight 1-2 um columns only on seeds, later coated with high-k and top plate.

title: Directionally solidified eutectic films freeze into aligned nanoscale wordline lamellae
idea: Ideal: wires that freeze into place. Closest: laser zone-melt a thin film of an abundant eutectic (Al-Al2Cu or NiAl-Mo) on an insulating substrate so directional solidification grows aligned conducting lamellae at 30-80 nm spacing set by scan speed (lambda^2 v = const); selectively etch one phase to leave parallel metal lines.

title: Spacer cascade turns solar-grade screen printing into nanoscale lines
idea: Ideal: nanolines from the cheapest printing tool on Earth. Closest: screen- or gravure-print 10-20 um mandrel lines on panels or wafers, then run eight successive conformal-deposition/etch-back spacer cycles (each doubling line count, 2^8 = 256x) to reach ~50-80 nm-pitch gratings using only blanket depositions and etches.
note: Eight spacer doublings from printed mandrels accumulate thickness and edge errors far beyond the final 50-80 nm pitch.

title: Holographer's superposition: bind thousands of key-value pairs into shared vectors
idea: A hologram spreads the whole scene across every fragment. Distant-past key-value pairs are bound by circular convolution (holographic reduced representations) and summed into a fixed bank of 64 superposition vectors per head. A query unbinds them by correlation to retrieve an approximate value, while recent tokens stay exact.
note: 64 superposition vectors per head cannot hold thousands of pairs at usable recall; resembles compressive/linear attention.

title: Superposed tensor storage with random-sign binding keys
idea: IFR: one buffer holds many tensors at once. Closest: k low-precision tensors (e.g., gradient accumulators of k micro-batches or k LoRA deltas) are each multiplied by a random +/-1 key vector and summed into one buffer; unbinding with the same key recovers each one with noise that error-tolerant training absorbs.
note: Cross-talk noise scales with k; k=4-8 dense tensors give SNR near 1, too noisy without sparsity.

title: U.S. stacking hubs: import arrays, add value through hybrid bonding
idea: Ideal: the U.S. gains DRAM capacity without first building a $15B fab. Closest achievable: fund domestic advanced-packaging hubs that buy known-good DRAM wafers from several allied fabs and do thinning, hybrid bonding, base-die attach and test in the U.S., later becoming the integration point for U.S.-made arrays.

title: Import known-good wafers, stack in America on open base die
idea: Scarcity: the U.S. has 1-2% of DRAM wafer capacity. Buy commodity DRAM wafers from any vendor under a wafer-level KGD spec, then do the high-value steps (thinning, hybrid bonding, a vendor-neutral base die from a U.S. logic foundry, final test) in U.S. OSATs.

title: SRAM-only inference fleets bought on logic-foundry capacity
idea: Worse: tie every AI accelerator to HBM supply. Flip: buy inference fleets of SRAM-only chips that shard whole models across hundreds of chips' on-die SRAM, procuring logic-foundry wafers instead of DRAM wafers.

title: Masks with printable defects accepted as fixed erasure addresses
idea: Combine reticle defect maps with on-die bad-cell tables. A printable mask defect repeats at the same array address in every die, so masks with tens of array-region defects can skip repair and actinic re-inspection, and those addresses are preloaded as known erasures in every die's code layer.

title: Memory-footprint budgets written into federal software procurement
idea: Combine the software bill of materials (SBOM) requirement with a measured memory-footprint disclosure: federally procured software must report peak and steady-state RSS on standardized workloads, and contracts score bids on GB per transaction.
note: Novel policy lever; impact depends on enforcement and spillover to industry.

title: Kiva-style robots shuttle memory sleds between racks on demand
idea: Borrowed from warehouse robots that bring shelves to pickers: 1-4 TB CXL memory sleds are hot-pluggable at the top of each rack, and aisle robots physically relocate sleds overnight or within minutes to racks whose forecast demand exceeds supply, steered by a cluster-wide memory demand forecaster.
note: Physically moving sleds is novel, but CXL switching and cabling get most of the benefit without robots.

title: Day-old bakery pricing: discounted refresh-free 'ephemeral RAM' cloud tier
idea: Borrowed from bakeries selling day-old bread at a discount: a cloud instance class offers memory guaranteed only ~1 s without access (hardware refresh off), surfaced through a 'spoiled page' signal like SIGBUS; stream processors, inference servers and caches opt in at ~40% lower price per GB.

title: Consume-on-read: destructive DRAM read becomes free reclaim
idea: Add an RD-CONSUME memory command that reverses DRAM's read-then-restore order: the sense amp delivers the line, skips the restore, and the controller flips the line to 'free' in a bitmap. Queues, NN activations and NIC ring buffers that are read exactly once get their capacity back at read time, with no software free or zeroing.

title: ECC check bits double as free dedup fingerprints
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: the controller already computes SECDED/Chipkill check bytes for every 64 B line it writes; concatenating a page's check words yields a 512-byte signature that serves as a near-free dedup/similarity fingerprint, kept incrementally in a small on-chip table and byte-verified on a hit, so no CPU hashing or KSM-style scanning is needed.
note: Clever reuse of existing check bits; needs controller access; dedup gains modest.

title: Hermit-crab strategy: memory tiers built in idle display-TFT fabs
idea: Hermit crabs move into shells others built; repurpose idle Gen-6/8.5 oxide-TFT display lines (all <=400 C, already depreciated) to make low-leakage 1T1C oxide-TFT DRAM at ~0.8-1.5 um rules, diced into tiles for a CXL capacity tier, with conversion grants for US and allied display/solar fabs.
note: Micron-scale rules give ~$5-30/GB, not below DRAM cost; niche capacity tier.

title: Disk-drive head wafer fabs pattern fine-pitch memory interposers
idea: Invert 'interposers must come from semiconductor foundries': repurpose recording-head wafer fabs in Minnesota, which already pattern sub-100 nm thin-film features, to make redistribution layers and fine-pitch interposers for memory stacks.

title: Memory Star: federal memory-efficiency label for cloud procurement
idea: Memory demand is working set x replication x headroom, and procurement measures none of the three. A GSA/DoD procurement standard would require vendors to report GB-hours per unit of work on standard benchmarks and give price preference to the top quartile, as ENERGY STAR did for watts.
note: Energy-Star-style GB-hours-per-work label for federal procurement; adoption and benchmark gaming are the doubts.

title: Po: a chip sold on its periodic table — abundance preference
idea: Po: a memory chip graded by its periodic table. Federal procurement and CHIPS rules give DRAM whose periphery and interconnect use only Earth-abundant elements (certified BOM: no W, Co, Ru, Ta, Hf, In, Ga) a 10% purchase preference and accelerated depreciation on the tooling.

title: Reuse row-hammer activation counters as free tiering telemetry
idea: Worsen: add yet more counters and page-table scans to find cold memory. Flip: export the per-row activation counts that PRAC/RFM row-hammer defenses already keep inside new DRAM to the OS, which uses them as a zero-overhead hotness map to demote cold rows to a compressed or CXL tier.

title: Solyndra-proof loan guarantees for non-silicon memory fabs, indexed to DRAM prices
idea: Solyndra died in 2011 when the incumbent's input (polysilicon) price collapsed, not because its glass-tube technology failed. Structure CHIPS/DOE loans for glass-, foil- or SiC-substrate memory fabs with repayments indexed to a DRAM contract-price index (pausing below a floor) and tranches tied to tools re-taskable to displays or power devices.
note: DRAM-price-indexed repayment for non-silicon memory fabs is a novel financing twist.

title: Ramtron's PZT exile solved: FeRAM in inkjet piezo-MEMS fabs
idea: Ramtron's PZT ferroelectric RAM stayed niche partly because PZT and Pt/Ir electrodes contaminate CMOS lines, which forced a segregated module. Piezo-MEMS fabs that make inkjet heads and sensors already run PZT/Pt/Ir on 200 mm with 1990s-class tools: put the ferroelectric capacitor module there, on top of 0.35-0.18 um CMOS wafers.
note: Non-obvious reuse of inkjet piezo-MEMS PZT lines for FeRAM capacitor modules; niche markets.

title: Latch resolution-time monitor flags weakening cells before they fail
idea: Effect: exponential regeneration in a bistable latch (metastability). Standard-cell time-to-digital counters on a few sense amps per mat measure how long each latch takes to resolve; since resolution time grows as tau*ln(Vswing/dV), a slow decision reveals a cell whose charge is nearing the trip point, and the controller raises refresh only for that row.

title: Hammer-triggered twin-cell mode doubles signal only where needed
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): the controller only issues ACT/REF/RFM as today. When the die's internal activation counter flags a row as an aggressor or victim, it silently remaps that row into twin-cell mode, storing each bit as a charge and its complement in two adjacent cells sensed differentially, which doubles signal and makes single-cell disturb flips harmless.
note: Requires array support for twin-cell remap; simulation-provable.

title: Quantum-dot charge RAM at 4 K: spin-qubit process lines repurposed for dense cryogenic memory
idea: On a 300 mm Si/SiGe or Si-MOS spin-qubit process, each cell is a gate-defined dot (plunger gate) with a barrier gate to a shared reservoir lead. A bit is 'full' (~10-30 electrons) or 'empty'; Coulomb blockade is not needed, only the barrier. Write: open the barrier (ns tunnelling) with the plunger set. Hold: the barrier is pinched off, so tunnel rates are far below 1e-6/s and thermal activation over ~50 meV (~140 kT) is impossible at 4 K. Read: a single-electron-transistor charge sensor shared by 4-8 dots, or gate reflectometry, with crossbar-shared gate lines. Cryo-CMOS drives the lines.

title: Open university interposer testbed decouples arrays from sensing logic
idea: Substitute captive DRAM-fab periphery development with an open platform: a university-built passive Si interposer with 2 um microbumps joins test cell arrays (MIM caps plus IGZO access devices) to FPGA or shuttle-ASIC sense logic, so any lab can iterate on sensing schemes in weeks.

title: Hexagonal 60-degree lattice replaces square grid for vertical-channel cells
idea: Substitute the orthogonal wordline/bitline grid with a triangular lattice: vertical-channel transistors at hexagonal close-packed sites defined by block-copolymer self-assembly, wordlines along one lattice direction and bitlines along a second at 60 degrees, so each cell occupies sqrt(3)/2*(2F)² = 3.46F² instead of 4F².
note: ~13% density only.

title: Molecular monolayer doping replaces BF3/PF3 implants on 3D sidewalls
idea: Substitute beamline BF3/PF3/GeF4 implants (which cannot reach 100-tier hole sidewalls anyway) with monolayer doping: self-assembled allylboronic-acid-pinacol-ester or diethyl-vinylphosphonate monolayers coat every exposed Si sidewall, are capped with ALD oxide, and spike-annealed into ~5 nm conformal junctions on all tiers at once.
note: Monolayer doping (Javey) is proven; conformal doping of 100-tier sidewalls is a sensible application.

title: Substitute hydrogen for helium as backside wafer-cooling gas
idea: Etch and implant electrostatic chucks flow helium at 5-20 Torr behind each wafer; swap it for H2 (thermal conductivity ~0.18 vs ~0.15 W/m-K) at the same pressure, recirculated through an on-tool palladium purifier and diluted far below LEL with N2 ballast in the foreline; use an H2/Ne blend where hydrogen reactivity matters.

title: Swap per-host duplicate pages for one fleet-shared CXL read-only copy
idea: Substitute per-host duplicates with one rack copy. Read-only pages (kernel text, shared libraries, container layers, model weights, JIT code caches) are hashed across the rack, one canonical copy is stored in a CXL-switched memory appliance and mapped read-only into every host, and writes copy-on-write into local DRAM.

title: Swap server-side user state for client-carried signed state blobs
idea: Substitute server memory with the client's memory. Recommendation and session services stop keeping per-user embeddings, histories and sessions in DRAM: each client holds its own encrypted, signed state vector of a few KB and attaches it to every request, and servers keep only shared item tables.

title: Open-source memory base die on 130 nm shuttle runs
idea: Substitute proprietary HBM base dies with an open-source base die (PHY, BIST, repair logic) taped out on low-cost 130/180 nm multi-project-wafer shuttles, so small teams can stack or attach commodity DRAM dies under their own controller.

title: Substitute unknown error positions with known erasures from weak-cell maps
idea: Store a compressed weak-cell location map (from wafer test plus online profiling) in a small fuse/NV block; the controller tells the decoder those bits are erasures, and an RS/BCH code corrects erasures at half the parity cost of unknown errors, so a die with 10x more weak cells ships with the same ECC overhead.
note: Map-based erasures double correction; ArchShield-like.

title: Substitute digital ECC decoders with charge-sharing triple-cell majority voting
idea: Store each critical bit in three cells on one bitline and open all three wordlines at once; charge sharing gives the analog majority directly at the sense amp, so TMR correction costs one activation and no decoder logic.

title: Substitute symmetric ECC with Z-channel codes plus charge-minimizing inversion
idea: Since leakage only drains charged cells (one-way errors), use asymmetric-error-correcting codes that cost fewer parity bits, and store each word with a polarity flag that minimizes the number of charged cells.
note: Z-channel codes exploit unidirectional leak; true/anti-cell mix complicates.

title: Substitute chipkill inside a DIMM with erasure coding across CXL devices
idea: Stripe memory across a pool of CXL memory devices with an RS(10,2)-style code so any whole device can fail; this allows cheap, lower-grade modules with no per-module ECC chips.
note: Cross-device RS adds write amplification and latency; enables downbinned modules.

title: Substitute static ferroelectric storage with rolling polarity rotation against imprint
idea: Store data XOR a per-region epoch mask and rewrite regions in background with the mask flipped on a slow schedule, tracked by an epoch bit, so no ferroelectric capacitor sits in one polarization long enough to imprint.

title: Substitute absolute FeFET levels with rank-modulation coding
idea: Encode multi-bit data in the relative order of threshold voltages among a group of FeFET cells, not absolute levels, so uniform relaxation or depolarization after power loss does not change the stored value.

title: Substitute discard with retention-graded bins for high-refresh customers
idea: Swap scrapping dies that fail 64 ms retention for retention-graded bins (16/32 ms) sold to AI-training and streaming buyers whose data is rewritten faster than it decays, with the controller refresh rate set from the bin ID in SPD.
note: Sell leakage-tail rejects with faster refresh; small yield gain.

title: Refresh activations double as in-DRAM copy and zeroing
idea: Fuse refresh with RowClone/Ambit-style bulk operations. The controller queues pending page-zeroing, page-copy and scrub-repair work against rows that are due for refresh, and runs each in the same ACT-ACT-PRE that restores the row.

title: Erasure decoding serves reads that collide with refresh
idea: Stagger refresh so only one chip in a rank refreshes at a time. A read that hits the refreshing chip is reconstructed from the other chips plus the ECC/parity chip, the way a RAID degraded read works.

title: Abatement waste heat drives membrane distillation back to ultrapure water
idea: Combine the fab's 50-80 C waste heat (thermal abatement, compressors, heat-pumped chiller return) with membrane distillation: rinse and scrubber effluent passes against a PFAS-free polypropylene/ceramic hydrophobic membrane so only vapor crosses, yielding near-UPW feed that needs only final ion-exchange polishing.

title: Erasure-coded HBM stacks built from barely tested dies
idea: Combine storage-array Reed-Solomon erasure coding with HBM stacking: 12+2 dies are stacked with only a gross-short screen, and each line is striped across dies with RS(14,12). Up to two dead dies plus 1% cell errors per die are tolerated.

title: Sketch-grade DRAM standard turns yield fallout into supply
idea: Combine yield-fallout bins with workloads that natively tolerate 1% bit errors (Bloom filters, count-min sketches, embedding tables, quantized KV-cache). A JEDEC-style approximate grade with an SPD flag and OS allocator lets these dies ship rather than be scrapped, with public research clusters as anchor buyers.

title: Bit-plane tensor layout enables precision-on-demand memory
idea: Combine image bit-plane slicing with memory placement: store each BF16/FP8 tensor as separate pages per bit plane (sign+exponent, high mantissa, low mantissa). Low-significance planes are placed in compressed or slower tiers or dropped under pressure, and kernels fetch only the planes their current precision needs.

title: Address-event memory bus transmits only nonzero values as spikes
idea: Combine neuromorphic address-event representation with the DRAM interface: the base die encodes each burst as (index, value) events for nonzero bytes and drives an asynchronous clockless bus that toggles only when an event fires; zero runs cost no transitions and the host rebuilds dense lines.

title: Write-hot pages on leaky rows: application writes become free refresh
idea: Combine the OS page allocator with per-row retention profiling: pages whose write interval is shorter than a row's measured retention are placed on weak rows, since every write restores full charge; those rows become refresh-exempt while a write-interval monitor guarantees the deadline, and only cold-data rows get nominal refresh.

title: Checkpoint-replay memory: training runs on lightly refreshed DRAM
idea: Combine HPC checkpoint/restart with relaxed refresh: activations and optimizer state live in DRAM refreshed at 4-8x the nominal interval, and any ECC-detected failure triggers recomputation of the affected micro-batch from the last checkpoint, which training stacks already do for node failures.

title: Leak-direction-aware inversion: store each row mostly in safe state
idea: Combine data-bus inversion with the physics that true cells only leak 1->0: the controller inverts any row segment holding more charged than discharged cells and stores a flag bit, so at most half the cells sit in the vulnerable charged state; anti-cell regions use the opposite polarity.
note: At most half the cells charged; refresh gain is limited because weak cells can still hold 1s.

title: SPD-embedded factory retention maps standardized through JEDEC
idea: Combine wafer-level test data with the module SPD: a policy push for a JEDEC field carrying per-bank/per-row retention bins measured at test, so every controller can apply multi-rate refresh and weak-row placement from day one without slow in-field profiling.
note: Standard weak-row map enables multi-rate refresh; adoption is the hurdle.

title: Kelvin-probe imaging maps thousands of cell retention curves in parallel
idea: Combine Kelvin probe force microscopy with retention testing: fabricate arrays with exposed storage-node pads, write them, then time-lapse map surface potential across thousands of nodes to extract full leakage distributions and the spatial correlation of tail cells without per-cell probing. Buildable in a university nanofab: standard AFM/KPFM tool.

title: Hydrogen-getter cap layer stabilizes oxide-channel access transistor tails
idea: Combine Ti/Pd hydrogen-getter films from vacuum packaging with oxide-semiconductor access transistors: a patterned getter layer above the passivation absorbs mobile hydrogen that would otherwise drift into the channel and shift threshold voltage, narrowing the leakage and drift tail. Buildable in a university nanofab: sputtered metal and one lithography step.

title: Hydrocarbon immersion cold racks rescue retention-marginal recycled DIMMs
idea: Fuse fluorine-free synthetic hydrocarbon (PAO) immersion cooling with second-life memory. Recycled modules that fail 85 °C retention run at about 30 °C, where leakage drops roughly 10× and refresh intervals stretch, which re-qualifies rejected parts.

title: Airline heavy-check rotation: drain, heal and return pooled memory live
idea: Adapted from airlines rotating aircraft through heavy checks while the fleet keeps flying: in a CXL memory pool, the fabric manager live-migrates data off a module flagged by retention telemetry, runs a service cycle on it (full retention re-profile, bias recovery, row repair), then returns it, with ~5% spare capacity covering modules in service.

title: LCD gate-on-array shift registers replace row decoders
idea: Borrowed from LCD gate-on-array scanning: rows in streaming banks are selected by a token passed down a compact shift register (one 4-6 transistor stage per wordline), exactly as panels scan gate lines. Random access stays in a smaller decoded side bank.

title: Pooled PCR group testing finds weak-retention cells in field
idea: Borrowed from Dorfman pooled testing: after an extended retention pause, the periphery merges many rows' compare results onto a wired-OR fail bus, flags pools with any failure, and bisects only failing pools; the results fill a per-row refresh-bin table.

title: LCD overdrive pre-emphasis speeds slow thin-film bitlines
idea: Borrowed from LCD response-time overdrive: column drivers apply a brief over-voltage pulse sized by a lookup table of previous and target state, so slow 20-40 cm2/Vs oxide-TFT bitlines and wordlines settle in about a third of the time.

title: Cellular frequency reuse: four-color tier activation shares drivers
idea: Adapted from cellular frequency-reuse coloring: tiers and subarrays are assigned four 'colors' and neighboring same-color regions never activate together, so one wordline-driver bank serves four tiers in rotation and aggressor rows are never adjacent to active victims.

title: Turbo-generator hydrogen cooling replaces helium on wafer chucks
idea: Adapted from large power-plant turbo-generators, which are cooled with pressurized hydrogen because its thermal conductivity beats helium's. Feed electrolyzer-made H2 at ~5-15 Torr into the sealed e-chuck backside gap of deposition, implant and non-H-sensitive etch tools, with generator-style purity monitors, dilution exhaust below LEL and purge interlocks.

title: Nuclear-reject unseparated zirconium-hafnium feeds capacitor dielectrics
idea: Nuclear-grade zirconium is expensive mainly because neutron-absorbing hafnium must be stripped out, but DRAM ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 dielectrics tolerate and can even benefit from Hf. Make Zr ALD precursors directly from unseparated zircon (natural ~2% Hf) and use the Hf as a tetragonal-phase stabilizer.

title: Glass-cullet recycling turns spent fab quartzware into crucible feedstock
idea: Adapted from glassmakers' cullet remelting. Collect retired diffusion tubes, wafer boats, etch rings and bell jars (all made from HPQ fused silica), plasma-melt them, strip surface metals with chlorine-gas refining, and refuse the result into crucible inner-layer sand.

title: Hard-disk patterned-media trick: copolymer density multiplication for templates
idea: Copy the HDD bit-patterned-media playbook: e-beam writes only a sparse guide lattice at 2-3x the final pitch, a PS-b-PMMA or high-chi block copolymer fills in the hexagonal lattice by directed self-assembly, and the rectified pattern is etched into the NIL or mask master.

title: Razor-blade coatings: tetrahedral amorphous carbon deep-etch hardmasks
idea: Razor blades and engine parts are coated with ta-C (>70% sp3 diamond-like carbon) by filtered cathodic arc; use 100-200 nm boron-optional ta-C as the hardmask for capacitor and contact deep etch in place of thick amorphous-carbon and tungsten-doped carbon hardmasks.

title: Airline fare classes and overbooking for server DRAM
idea: Borrowed from airline revenue management: the hypervisor sells each host's DRAM in fare classes (guaranteed, flexible, standby) and overbooks by a learned 'no-show' rate of allocated-but-untouched pages; bumped tenants are migrated to a compressed/CXL tier and credited automatically. An EMSR-style booking-limit algorithm resets per-class caps hourly.

title: Scalable-video bit-planes: shed least-significant planes under memory pressure
idea: Borrowed from scalable video coding, where enhancement layers are dropped on congestion: tensors are stored bit-plane-major (MSB plane first), so the memory manager frees LSB planes in place when pressure rises, degrading precision gracefully without re-encoding; reads fetch only the planes that remain.
note: Bit-plane-major storage with in-place LSB shedding under pressure; any-precision work exists.

title: Grocery spoil-and-restock: refresh-free DRAM as clean-only cache
idea: Borrowed from produce departments that discard spoiled stock and restock from the warehouse: DRAM runs with refresh off and holds only clean copies whose master lives in CXL or flash; each row has weak 'canary' cells plus a CRC, a read that finds a tripped canary simply re-fetches, and dirty data stays in a small SRAM write buffer that writes through.

title: Elevator destination dispatch: early row hints let DRAM pre-open
idea: Adapted from destination-dispatch elevators, where riders key in their floor in the lobby: cores send a cheap bank/row hint on a side channel tens of nanoseconds before the real request. The DRAM groups riders and opens each row once for many requests.

title: Aerospace time-triggered networks: compiler-scheduled DRAM with no command bus
idea: Adapted from time-triggered Ethernet and fly-by-wire scheduling: for static AI dataflow, the compiler emits a full timetable of activations and bursts and loads it into the DRAM base die. The die then streams on schedule, with no per-access commands, arbitration or handshakes.

title: Film-editing proxies: fetch most-significant bit-planes first, refine on demand
idea: Adapted from VFX proxy editing and progressive JPEG: tensors are stored as bit-planes in separate DRAM rows. The accelerator fetches the top 4-8 bits first and requests lower planes only for values whose contribution matters (e.g., large attention scores).

title: Compact-disc scratch codes make TSV defects harmless
idea: Adapted from CD CIRC interleaving: each data word is spread across many TSVs with a Reed-Solomon erasure code, so a few open or leaky TSVs become erasures corrected on the fly instead of needing spare-TSV repair or scrapping the stack.
note: TSV opens are a small share of stack yield loss; RS over TSVs simple.

title: Congestion-charge pricing for DRAM row openings
idea: Adapted from London's congestion charge: the OS/hypervisor meters each process's row activations through memory-controller counters and charges them against a quota. Runtimes and allocators respond by restructuring data layouts for locality.
note: ACT metering resembles hammer throttling; developer behavior change is uncertain.

title: Hybrid-ARQ incremental-redundancy ECC with far-stored heavy parity
idea: Adapted from LTE/5G hybrid ARQ, where the first transmission carries a light code and extra parity is sent only if decoding fails: each 64 B line carries only a small inline detect-and-correct-one code, while a strong Reed-Solomon parity per 4 KB region lives in a separate low-traffic row group and is fetched only on the rare detected failure.

title: Railway sidings: on-die hot-row SRAM cache absorbs hammering
idea: Adapted from rail yards that pull a heavily used train onto a siding to keep the main line clear: each bank has a 16-entry row-wide SRAM siding; when a row's approximate activation count (Misra-Gries tracker) crosses ~200, the row is copied into the siding and served from SRAM until it cools, so the physical row stops toggling.

title: Election risk-limiting audits replace exhaustive retention testing
idea: Adapted from risk-limiting election audits that certify a result by sampling ballots until statistical confidence is reached: wafer retention test samples random rows per mat with a sequential probability ratio test, stops early on clearly good mats, and escalates to a full retention sweep only for mats whose samples look risky; residual uncertainty is covered by in-field ECC.

title: Air-traffic separation zones filled with checkable parity
idea: Adapted from air-traffic control, which keeps separation buffers between aircraft but watches them with radar: the OS page allocator places guard rows between security domains (ZebRAM-style), but instead of leaving them empty fills each with XOR parity of its neighboring data rows; guard rows are verified and rewritten at each scrub, so a hammer flip in a guard is detected and any flip in a data row is correctable.

title: Chaos engineering certifies software so memory specs can relax
idea: Adapted from Netflix-style chaos engineering, which injects failures in production until systems tolerate them: a hypervisor-level injector flips random bits in tagged memory regions at controlled rates, and applications that pass sustained injection at BER ~1e-7 are certified to run on relaxed memory pools with weaker ECC, longer refresh and lower-bin dies.

title: Blood-bank cross-matching of DRAM dies to workload retention needs
idea: Adapted from blood typing and cross-matching: each die's retention tail, row-hammer threshold and timing margin are encoded as a 'blood type' in SPD. The memory scheduler cross-matches dies that fail the 64 ms JEDEC retention spec to workloads that rewrite data constantly (KV caches, activations, stream buffers), where natural rewrites stand in for refresh.

title: Five-minute electricity-style spot market for pooled CXL memory
idea: Adapted from grid operators' 5-minute real-time dispatch: rack-level CXL memory pools post free GB every 5 minutes into an internal auction. Tenants bid by latency tier, and the hypervisor migrates pages to the winners, with locational prices for near and far pools.

title: Minify charged cells: discharge-biased coding skips empty-row refresh
idea: The controller encodes each line (XOR with a learned base plus bus-invert, polarity flipped for true/anti-cell subarrays) so >90% of cells sit in the discharged, non-leaking state, and a per-row flag marks rows with no charged cells, which are never refreshed.

title: Shift-register row sequencer replaces decoders in streaming banks
idea: MINIFY the row decoder in designated stream banks to a circular shift register that advances one wordline per ACT plus a coarse 1-of-16 jump decoder, since AI weight and KV streams open rows in order; random traffic is steered to normal banks.

title: Skip restore for read-once data like KV-cache streams
idea: MINIFY restore work: a read-and-forget command lets the SA latch the row without driving restore current back into the cells, and the controller marks the row invalid, for data consumed once (streamed activations, KV pages being evicted).

title: Back-gate-pulsed dual-gate IGZO sense amplifiers
idea: Dual-gate IGZO SA transistors (<=350 C) get their back gate pulsed to +2 V only during the ~2-3 ns sense window, MAGNIFYING drive current ~3x, and parked at -1 V otherwise, MINIFYING leakage.

title: Magnify yield: stitch rejected DRAM dies into good ones
idea: Buy partially failing or downbinned DRAM dies at scrap prices, then pair three partial dies under a small remap and sparing logic die (FPGA first, then a $100k MPW ASIC) that presents one fully good logical die in a stacked package.
note: Vendors already sell off-spec dies; bare-die supply access and assembly cost are the risks.

title: Minify TSV count 4x with PAM-4 and time-multiplexed vias
idea: Design TSV transceivers that send PAM-4 at 2x the symbol rate, with 2:1 time-multiplexing, so a quarter of the TSVs carry the same bandwidth. Validate on a TSV interposer MPW and license to stack makers.

title: Minify precision on demand with bit-plane sliced storage
idea: Minify what stays resident by storing tensors, images and sensor arrays transposed into bit planes. The top planes live in DRAM and the low-order planes in CXL flash, which are fetched only when a consumer asks for full precision.

title: Clockless delay-insensitive memory interface
idea: MINIFY clocking to zero: replace the DDR clock, DLLs and training with 1-of-4 delay-insensitive handshake coding between DRAM and host, so the I/O idles at zero dynamic power.

title: Pluggable memory modules in an optical transceiver form factor
idea: MINIFY the replacement unit to a faceplate-pluggable module in an OSFP-like case holding DRAM plus a photonic link, hot-swapped like a network transceiver.
note: Optical CXL memory pooling exists; OSFP form factor is a packaging twist.

title: Minify hammer-counter updates with 4-bit probabilistic Morris counters
idea: Keep a 4-bit Morris-style approximate counter per row in spare cells. On each activation an on-die LFSR increments it only with probability base^-c, so 4 bits span ~1k-30k activations and the counter is rewritten on only a few percent of activations. Victim refresh fires at a threshold set with a safety margin.

title: Minify protection for regenerable data: CRC-detect, then recompute
idea: Classify data as regenerable (activations, KV cache, decompressed copies, file cache) and store it with only an 8-bit CRC per 512 bits. On a mismatch the runtime recomputes or re-fetches it from the source instead of correcting it.

title: Eliminate the one-size retention spec: per-die retention descriptor standard
idea: Propose a JEDEC extension in which each die stores its measured retention distribution (per bank, per temperature) in an on-die fuse table and the host sets tREFI per bank from it; validated dies advertise 128-512 ms classes. The single worst-case 64 ms contract disappears.

title: Eliminate refresh of read-only copies: re-fetch from durable backing store
idea: Read-only data (weights, embeddings) is mapped to never-refreshed banks with strong per-line ECC; when ECC flags drift the line is re-fetched from a NAND or CXL pool that holds the master copy, and a scrubber rewrites lines nearing their measured retention age. Refresh becomes on-demand repair.
note: Refetch from backing store instead of recompute; same skip-refresh-and-regenerate core.

title: Eliminate the restore phase: consume-on-read memory for single-use data
idea: Add a destructive-read command and 'read-once' regions whose sense amps never write back. Activations, gradient buffers, evicted KV entries and packets are read once, then the row is marked free, so the SA fires at low swing and the row closes right after the burst.
note: Destructive-read regions for read-once traffic; related to restore truncation and IBM destructive-read eDRAM.

title: Eliminate fluorinated test fluids: self-heating hammer-pattern thermal screening
idea: Hot test and burn-in normally rely on PFPE (Galden/Fluorinert) chillers and baths. Instead each die heats itself to 95-125 C with an all-bank activate pattern (~1-2 W), closed-loop on an on-die ring-oscillator thermometer, so handlers need only air-cooled chucks and retention screens run at true temperature.
note: Self-heating test removes PFAS fluids; temperature uniformity is the question.

title: Eliminate helium from the fab: hydrogen backside cooling and tracer leak checks
idea: Replace helium backside gas on etch and CVD electrostatic chucks with low-pressure hydrogen or forming gas (higher thermal conductivity, sealed with flow monitoring), and replace helium mass-spec leak checks with 5% hydrogen tracer detection.

title: Eliminate sideband ECC bits for AI tensors using algorithmic checksums
idea: Put recomputable AI data on non-ECC channels and protect it with algorithm-based fault tolerance: row and column checksums on each matmul, with recompute on mismatch, so no memory ECC is needed for those regions.

title: Eliminate unneeded mantissa bits with bit-plane tensor storage
idea: Tensors are laid out as separate bit planes; a profiler sets per-tensor error budgets and the planes below them are never written, while the memory controller fetches only the planes a kernel asks for.

title: Orthogonal-access memory reads rows or columns, killing transposes
idea: Eliminate transpose and relayout copies: each cell in a dedicated tile gets two access devices on orthogonal wordline/bitline pairs (dual-port 2T gain cell), so a weight tile is read row-major in the forward pass and column-major in the backward pass without being moved.

title: Controller-less DRAM: compiler emits cycle-exact raw memory commands
idea: Eliminate the memory controller's queues, reorder logic and refresh scheduler: for static AI graphs the compiler schedules every ACT/RD/WR/REF at cycle level with temperature-guarded margins, and the PHY simply replays the command stream.

title: One shared non-volatile weight copy mapped by sixteen hosts
idea: Eliminate per-server weight copies: a CXL 3.x multi-headed NV memory device holds a model once and 16 hosts map it read-only; hosts keep only KV caches and activations in local DRAM.
note: Per-token weight bandwidth through one shared device is the bottleneck.

title: Eliminate in-DRAM parity: keep strong parity on flash, CRC in DRAM
idea: For read-mostly pages (weights, code, embeddings), DRAM stores only a 16-bit CRC per 512 B, and a strong Reed-Solomon parity block lives on CXL-attached flash or the SSD. A CRC miss triggers a parity fetch and reconstruction.

title: Eliminate weak-cell errors by storing safe states: data inversion masks
idea: True cells fail only from charged to discharged, and anti-cells only the reverse. The controller keeps a weak-cell map and, for each 64-bit word, picks one of 4 XOR masks so every known weak cell stores its non-decaying state. The 2-bit mask index replaces some ECC bits.

title: Eliminate discard-on-error policy: re-harvest retired fleet DIMMs die-by-die
idea: An e-waste and procurement rule requires that DIMMs hyperscalers retire at correctable-error thresholds be offered to a re-test line before shredding. The line re-characterizes each die, maps its faults and repackages the healthy dies (the majority) into remapped modules for tolerant workloads.

title: Eliminate perfect-bit requirement: Grade-C DRAM for error-tolerant workloads
idea: Eliminate the near-zero-error spec where it does not matter: modules with measured raw BER ~1e-12 to 1e-9 are sold for CDN video caches and checkpoint staging protected by software CRC and re-fetch; ~$500k pilot with one CDN.
note: Approximate-DRAM idea with a concrete CDN pilot; yield gain is small.

title: Lay the capacitor down: MLCC-style 30-electrode stacks inside each cell
idea: Rearrange from tall-and-thin to flat-and-many: deposit 30 alternating TiN/Nb2O5 layers, pattern 180 nm cells with two offset staircase edge contacts so odd and even electrodes interleave like a ceramic MLCC; capacitance comes from layer count, not etch depth or litho.

title: Run the image-sensor pixel backward: pinned-photodiode memory lines
idea: Convert depreciated 180-110 nm CMOS image-sensor lines into memory by reversing the pixel: inject charge into each pinned photodiode from the floating diffusion (fill-and-spill), hold it in the pinned well (dark current ~1-10 e-/s), then transfer forward and read by correlated double sampling with column ADCs; 3000 e- full well and 2 e- noise allow ~6 bits per cell.
note: Pinned well gives seconds retention but ~0.2 um2/bit and slow CDS read limit to warm tier.

title: Steer data into the discharged state on unmodified DRAM
idea: Flip data polarity from outside the chip: commodity DRAM mixes true-cell and anti-cell subarrays. Map them once per part number with retention tests, then have the controller XOR-invert data per address so zeros, the most common value, land as discharged charge in both cell types, replacing today's random scrambling with a polarity-aware mask.

title: Tail bounty: pay for decades of worst-cell leakage cut
idea: Reverse the research metric from median to tail: a CHIPS-funded open prize pays per decade of 1-ppm-tail off-current reduction, measured on standard 1 Mb access-transistor test arrays built on shared 130/65 nm multi-project-wafer shuttles at existing U.S. foundries. Winning device recipes are licensed to DRAM makers.

title: Token-passing row sequencer replaces the random-access row decoder
idea: Reverse random access into order: for AI-weight and KV-cache streaming parts, rows open as a token shifts one wordline per step through a shift-register chain with a small jump table, deleting the NAND-tree row decoder and its pitch-limited predecode buses.

title: Periphery first, indium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cells last
idea: Reverse front-end order: finish CMOS periphery, then build a 2T gain-cell array in BEOL from sputtered zinc-tin-oxide (no indium, no gallium) at <400 C on top of the logic.

title: Test in the field, not on the tester: self-learned error maps
idea: Reverse when testing happens: ship dies after minimal wafer sort, and let on-die BIST plus ECC syndrome logging build and update the bad-cell map during normal use, within the 1% BER budget.

title: Speculative pre-free with lineage recompute on surprise reuse
idea: Invert keep-until-proven-dead: the runtime predicts each large object's last use, frees it at once, and keeps only its lineage (the operator and inputs that made it); a mispredicted later read triggers recomputation instead of a fault.

title: Tenants rent idle DRAM back to the provider every second
idea: Reverse ownership inside each server: VMs and containers hold memory as one-second leases priced by an auction in the hypervisor; tenants earn credits for memory they release, and the host hands it to memory-hungry neighbors through free-page reporting.

title: Reject-bin DRAM becomes the approximate-data memory tier
idea: Reverse the quality order: dies and DIMMs that fail retention or weak-cell binning (already made, normally scrapped) are packaged into an 'approximate' CXL tier with masked-error semantics, holding error-tolerant data such as video frames, NN activations and low-attention KV.
note: Approximate tier from reject-bin dies; same salvage core as I-05808; approximate DRAM (Flikker) is known.

title: Certify crypto-erase so retired DIMMs are resold, not shredded
idea: Reverse the security default: a NIST/ISO-certified power-off and pattern-overwrite attestation for volatile DRAM, with signed logs from the server BMC, replaces mandatory physical shredding of memory modules in government and enterprise disposal rules.

title: Harvest laptop and console DRAM from e-waste into CXL sleds
idea: Reverse the supply chain: automated desolder, reball and burn-in lines pull DDR4/DDR5 BGA packages from recycled laptops, consoles and SO-DIMMs, bin them by speed and retention, and remount them on CXL far-memory cards behind a compression controller.
note: Reballed reclaimed DRAM reliability and volume limited.

title: Lane-direction-reconfigurable PHY for read-heavy phases
idea: Reverse fixed DQ symmetry: each lane has a transmitter and a receiver at both ends and can be reassigned in microseconds, so during LLM decode ~90% of lanes point memory-to-host and they flip back for checkpoint writes; per-burst bus turnaround disappears.

title: Memory as master: the stack pushes tensors to compute
idea: Reverse who initiates: the host writes a descriptor program (tensor shapes, strides, schedule) once, and a DMA engine in the DRAM base die pushes data on its own schedule into the accelerator's SRAM over a write-only link; the host never issues per-line reads.
note: Descriptor-driven push resembles decoupled access and DMA streaming.

title: Weak cells hold only clean pages, re-fetched on error
idea: Rearrange placement by dirtiness: pages with an intact copy in flash or CXL far memory (weights, code, read-mostly caches) go to cheap weak-retention DRAM protected only by a 16-bit CRC, and a CRC failure triggers a re-fetch instead of correction; a line is migrated to strong ECC banks on its first write.

title: Memory that trades capacity for parity as it ages
idea: Rearrange the parity/data split over the product lifetime: modules start with ~2% parity, and as the error log shows a region degrading, the controller re-encodes it with a stronger code and hot-unplugs the freed pages from the OS, degrading gracefully instead of failing.

title: Memory leasing with depot rejuvenation and retention re-binning
idea: TRIZ #20 Continuity of useful action: makers lease socketed DDR/CXL modules to hyperscalers and take them back every ~3 years; depots map retention, bulk-anneal to heal dielectric traps, re-bin by retention class and re-lease to less demanding tiers.
note: Leasing executable; anneal-based rejuvenation of retention traps is unproven.

title: Bootstrapped guard node gives the inner switch zero voltage to leak
idea: TRIZ #12 Equipotentiality (the electrometer guard trick): put two access transistors in series and drive their middle node from a source follower whose gate is the storage node. In retention the inner transistor sees ~0 V across it and leaks almost nothing, while all leakage from the bitline is absorbed by the actively driven guard node.
note: Density trade confines it to cache/eDRAM tiers.

title: Compiler-tagged ephemeral memory that is never refreshed
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: let data that will die anyway go unrefreshed. Compilers and AI runtimes place allocations whose lifetime is shorter than guaranteed retention (activations, KV-cache blocks overwritten each step, staging buffers) in an 'ephemeral' region whose rows the controller never refreshes, with a hardware write-timestamp that faults reads of expired data.

title: Curvature: ring-gate annular transistors make edge-free matched sense amp pairs
idea: TRIZ #14 Spheroidality: the cross-coupled sense-amp transistors are drawn as annular (ring-gate) devices with the drain in the centre, so there is no STI channel edge; edge-related threshold mismatch and narrow-width effects, a major part of sense-amp offset, disappear, and curvilinear masks from multi-beam writers make the rings printable.

title: Continuity: rolling-scan drum memory needs only a shift-register row scanner
idea: TRIZ #20 Continuity of useful action: like a display gate driver, a shift register sweeps every row in order, sensing and restoring each (so refresh is the scan itself) and presenting each row to a page buffer as it passes; requests wait for their row to come around, removing row address decoders, refresh logic and most control.

title: Plateless bridge capacitor stores one bit between twin nodes
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging: merge the two capacitors of a twin cell into one capacitor whose two electrodes are both storage nodes, each reached by its own access transistor on complementary bitlines, with no common plate. Writing puts +V/-V across the single capacitor and the sense amp sees the full differential charge.

title: Read-restore 3T gain cell: every read is a refresh
idea: TRIZ #23 Feedback: add a p-type third transistor whose gate is the precharged read bitline and whose channel links the storage gate to a restore rail. When a stored 1 pulls the read bitline low, the feedback device turns on and tops the storage node back up; a stored 0 leaves the bitline high and the device off.

title: Thermal-expansion valves cut idle purge-gas flows automatically
idea: TRIZ #37 Thermal expansion: fit tool gas lines with passive bimetal or shape-memory valves keyed to chamber-wall or heater temperature. When a chamber idles and cools, the valve throttles He, N2 and H2 purge to a trickle, and it reopens as the heaters ramp, with no software change or recipe requalification.

title: Photopatternable hafnium-oxo resist that becomes the functional film
idea: TRIZ #32 Color changes (change a substance's properties): use a Hf/Zr oxo-cluster resist that, after exposure and development, is annealed straight into dense HfO2/ZrO2 that stays as a hardmask, spacer or isolation layer, so the patterned film is never etched.

title: Ephemeral-grade dies: retention-failing DRAM sold for TTL-bounded data
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap short-living objects: dies that fail the 64 ms retention screen but hold data for 4-8 ms are sold as E-grade parts with refresh logic fused off, and the runtime places only data with a hard time-to-live below the rated window (collective-communication buffers, prefetch staging, pipeline handoffs), invalidating pages at expiry.
note: Data-lifetime-aware refresh skipping is known (e.g., accelerator eDRAM); new as a binning SKU.

title: Silicon-carbide refresh-free memory in idle EV power-device fabs
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: the same 150/200 mm 4H-SiC lines that make EV MOSFETs (overbuilt in the U.S. as EV demand slowed) produce 1T1C memory, since SiC's 3.26 eV gap suppresses thermal generation so strongly that SiC MOS storage cells have shown retention extrapolating to years at room temperature.
note: SiC DRAM retention was shown in the 1990s; density 50-100x below DRAM limits it to niche tiers.

title: Floating-body 1T cells revived for millisecond-lived pipeline buffers
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: rather than fight floating-body retention (why 1T-DRAM failed), embrace it - build SOI or stacked-Si floating-body cells with ~10-100 ms retention and use them only for data overwritten every few ms (pipeline-parallel handoff buffers, double-buffered GEMM tiles, network rings), with refresh logic removed.

title: Controller-side pointer high-bit extraction into per-page region tags
idea: TRIZ #2 Taking out: the memory controller detects 64-bit words whose upper 24 bits equal a per-page 'region tag' (pointers into the same heap region), strips those bits and packs eight 40-bit pointers into a 40-byte slot, restoring them on read with one mux stage. It is hardware compressed-oops for every language, not just the JVM.

title: Encode-heavy, decode-cheap memory codec trained by idle cores
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: reads outnumber writes ~3-10x, so use an asymmetric codec: pages are written raw, then idle cores or a background engine re-encode warm pages with expensive search (optimal parsing plus per-page tANS tables), while the read path is a fixed two-stage table-lookup decoder with deterministic ~10 ns latency.

title: Live-morphing data structures between dense and succinct forms
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: runtime libraries let every hash map, vector and index switch representation online, morphing cold instances into succinct forms (Elias-Fano, rank/select bitvectors, minimal perfect hashes) and expanding hot ones back to pointer-rich forms, driven by sampled access counts.
note: Online dense/succinct morphing; switching cost and pointer stability are issues.

title: Precision-transcoding DIMM buffer for tagged ML address ranges
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: a 180 nm buffer chip on the module holds a small range table; writes to tagged ranges are converted FP32 to BF16 or FP16 to FP8 with stochastic rounding and stored packed into a half- or quarter-size physical region, and reads are expanded back, so precision varies by region with no software changes.

title: The other way round: DRAM pushes a precompiled tensor schedule
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: instead of the GPU requesting every line, the compiler loads a tensor-streaming schedule into the HBM base die. The base die opens rows in a fixed order and pushes data to the accelerator, so the command/address bus becomes a rarely used control channel.

title: Spheroidality: ring of compute chiplets with memory inside and outside
idea: TRIZ #14 Spheroidality (curves instead of lines): place compute chiplets in a ring on a large panel substrate, giving the ring both an inner and an outer shoreline. Memory stacks sit inside the hole and around the outside.

title: Spheroidality: radial server board with memory cards as equal spokes
idea: TRIZ #14 Spheroidality: lay out a round motherboard with the CPU or accelerator at the center and memory cards plugged in radially like spokes. Every channel gets the same short trace length, so more DIMMs fit per channel at full speed. Built with existing PCB and connector lines. (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)

title: Z-channel asymmetric code with minority-charge data inversion
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: retention failures are almost only charged-to-discharged, so each word stores an inversion flag that minimizes charged cells (using the known true/anti-cell polarity of each row) and is protected by a Z-channel asymmetric code that corrects only charge-loss flips.

title: Continuous stressed-read margin probing predicts failing cells
