title: Substitute bulk silicon with back-gated FD-SOI for dynamic-threshold cells
idea: Build the array on ultra-thin-body SOI with a buried back-gate plane held at deep negative bias during retention (high Vt, low leakage) and pulsed toward zero only under the activated mat, so the front wordline needs only a ~0.8 V swing; the recessed-channel BCAT etch module and VPP pumps go away.

title: Substitute dissipative line charging with adiabatic resonant charge recovery
idea: Drive bitline precharge and wordlines from LC resonant rails using high-Q spiral inductors in a thick-copper redistribution layer borrowed from RF BEOL, ramping lines over ~5 ns so most of their CV2 energy returns to the tank instead of heating drivers.

title: Substitute random-access cells with short-loop charge-coupled shift-register memory
idea: Store bits as charge packets in 64-stage CCD loops built only from parallel gate lines (no per-cell contacts, capacitors or access transistors), ideal for SAQP or self-assembled line/space patterning; a read clocks the loop past its single sense node using ~0.3 V three-phase clocks.

title: Substitute copper die-to-die wires with microLED free-space optical links
idea: Each DRAM die face carries arrays of mass-transferred GaN micro-LEDs and silicon photodiodes (1-2 Gb/s per lane, thousands of lanes) that talk across the stack or to the processor through short imaging optics, replacing TSV/microbump buses and SerDes.

title: Femtosecond-laser-written waveguides inside glass interposers
idea: Substitute copper interposer RDL with optical waveguides written in 3D inside a fused-silica interposer by femtosecond-laser index modification, evanescently coupled to grating ports on the GPU and HBM base die; waveguides cross in 3D without crosstalk, collapsing many routing layers into one glass volume.

title: Origami flex interposer folds memory stacks around the processor
idea: Substitute the flat interposer with a 2 um-line polyimide flex bonded at the GPU edges and folded up and over, so HBM stacks mount on vertical walls and above the GPU, tripling the number of stacks within 5 mm of the die edge.

title: Substitute DRAM fabs with idle display panel fabs making oxide memory
idea: Swap new DRAM fabs for under-used Gen-8.5 LCD/OLED lines, whose IGZO backplane processes already stay below ~350-400 C, upgraded with sub-um panel steppers to make 2T0C oxide gain-cell memory dies on glass.

title: Charge-active, polarization-parked hybrid capacitor rows
idea: Combine a DRAM capacitor and a FeRAM capacitor in one ZrO2/HZO bilayer: rows in active use run as fast volatile charge cells, and when a row sits idle past ~10 ms the controller issues one plate pulse that copies its charge state into the ferroelectric polarization and powers the row down. Idle rows cost zero refresh, and the first access restores them to charge mode.
note: Parking idle rows into polarization cuts idle refresh; NVDRAM-like hybrids exist.

title: Silicon carbide cell array hybrid-bonded to silicon periphery
idea: Build the access transistors and storage junctions in 4H-SiC (Eg 3.26 eV) and hybrid-bond the array to a Si CMOS periphery wafer.
note: Hour-scale retention from SiC ni is real (Purdue); doubt is SiC MOS interface quality at DRAM pitch.

title: Antiferroelectric capacitor that switches to nonvolatile mode for sleep
idea: Use a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor: high-k and non-remanent in DRAM mode. On sleep, a plate-line offset bias (as in work-function-engineered AFE memory) parks the loop so two polarization states hold with no power, and wake reads them back.

title: Image-sensor floating-diffusion readout with correlated double sampling
idea: Adopt CMOS image-sensor pixel readout: a transfer gate moves cell charge onto a ~0.5 fF floating diffusion read by a source follower, sampled before and after transfer (correlated double sampling) to cancel kTC noise and offset at ~2 electrons rms. A cell then needs only ~1,000 electrons (~0.15 fF at 1 V).

title: Open array-periphery bond standard plus CHIPS grants
idea: Publish an open die-to-die standard that fixes the bitline-group, wordline and power pinout between DRAM array wafers and periphery wafers, and use CHIPS-style grants to have U.S. trailing logic fabs (90-22 nm) build the periphery tier for any array maker.

title: Subarray sense amps fused with micro-ring optical modulators
idea: Bond a photonic wafer over the DRAM array so every subarray's local sense-amp row drives silicon micro-ring modulators directly; the latched bit biases the ring's PN junction, and global bitlines, I/O muxes and SERDES become one WDM waveguide bus running over the mats.

title: Vertical bitline pillar with built-in preamp transistor at its base
idea: Merge the local sense preamp into each vertical bitline of a 3D DRAM: a gain transistor whose gate is the short vertical bitline converts the charge-share signal to current before it reaches the long global bitline.

title: Nanoimprint template also prints the self-assembly guide pattern
idea: Combine nanoimprint and directed self-assembly: one imprint stamps sparse 40-80 nm guide posts plus a chemically patterned brush, then a high-chi block copolymer fills in 4-8x denser features and heals imprint defects for capacitor-hole and active arrays.

title: Excimer-laser crystallized silicon tiers for monolithic 3D DRAM
idea: Combine LTPS-display line-beam laser crystallization with 3D DRAM: amorphous Si tiers are deposited one at a time over the finished lower tiers, and each is melted and crystallized by a nanosecond laser that heats only the top ~50 nm. This replaces Si/SiGe epitaxial superlattices.

title: DRAM dies embedded in glass-core substrate cavities under processor
idea: Combine the glass-core package substrates now arriving for AI packages with embedded-die technology: laser-form cavities in the glass core, embed thinned commodity DRAM/LPDDR dies face-up, and connect them with through-glass vias straight up into the GPU bump field so memory sits ~300 um below compute instead of beside it.

title: Double-sided interposer with HBM mounted directly beneath the GPU
idea: Combine double-sided module assembly with 2.5D packaging: mount HBM stacks on the underside of a thin interposer directly under the GPU, connected by ~100 um through-interposer vias instead of 5-10 mm lateral wires, with the package substrate cavity-milled to receive them.
note: Heat and GPU power delivery must pass through the memory region.

title: Leaky-bucket hammer counter: IGZO TFT integrator on each wordline
idea: Combine the networking leaky-bucket with the wordline driver: each activation pumps a fixed charge quantum through an IGZO TFT onto a small MIM capacitor, while a subthreshold TFT drains it with a ~32-64 ms time constant; crossing a threshold triggers neighbor refresh. Buildable in a university nanofab: sputtered IGZO, ALD gate oxide and MIM at <=350 C.

title: Solar-cell recombination layer between cells absorbs hammer electrons
idea: Combine the defect-rich recombination junctions of tandem solar cells with DRAM isolation: line the gap between adjacent storage nodes with a thin, deliberately defective a-Si or heavily doped poly film that recombines electrons injected from the hammered row before they reach the victim node. Buildable in a university nanofab: PECVD/LPCVD film on paired-node test structures.

title: Dual-mode HZO/ZrO2 capacitor: volatile bit with ferroelectric safety copy
idea: Combine a DRAM capacitor with a ferroelectric backup in one ALD stack: a paraelectric ZrO2 layer holds the normal volatile charge, while a thin Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 layer is polarized only by an occasional higher-voltage backup pulse; if charge decays or ECC flags the row, the FE polarization is read to restore it. Buildable in a university nanofab: ALD plus <=400 C anneal.

title: MLCC-style interdigitated plate stack inside each storage node
idea: Copy multilayer ceramic capacitor construction at nanoscale: fill a wide shallow trench with 12 alternating metal/high-k layers, then use selective lateral recess on opposite sidewalls (as MLCC end terminations alternate) so odd plates tie to the storage node and even plates to the plate line.

title: Snap-through nanodome bit copied from thermostat snap disks
idea: Fabricate a prestressed 20 nm SiN/TiN dome over each cell that, like a bimetal snap disc or keyboard tactile dome, has two stable buckled states; an electrode pulse snaps it up or down in ns and the gap change is read capacitively.
note: Snap-through dome per cell; nm-scale thermal stability and ns actuation are open.

title: DVD replication: molded substrates carry all cell topography
idea: Adapted from DVD/Blu-ray replication (a nanostructured disc molded every ~3 s from one nickel stamper): mold glass-ceramic or high-Tg substrates that already contain capacitor wells, gate trenches and contact steps, then conformally coat electrode, high-k, IGZO and metal and planarize, so array geometry needs no lithography.

title: Engine remanufacturing: harvest and restack DRAM dies from e-waste
idea: Like remanufactured engines and toner cartridges: buy scrapped server DIMMs by the ton, debond and retest the dies, then edge-stack or hybrid-bond 8-16 known-good dies onto a new logic base die with fresh interface and strong ECC, sold as certified 'reman' capacity memory.
note: Debonding packaged dies for hybrid restack is impractical; DIMM/CXL reuse is the realistic path.

title: Telephone line concentrators: one sense amp serves 1024 bitlines
idea: Adapted from telephone line concentrators where many subscribers share few trunks: a tree of oxide-TFT pass switches inside the array tiers lets 1,024 bitlines share one CMOS sense amp, and each cell is an active gain cell so it can drive the long shared path instead of sharing tiny charge.

title: Cultured quartz from oscillator industry crushed into crucible sand
idea: The quartz-oscillator industry grows ultra-pure cultured quartz in hydrothermal autoclaves, using low-grade quartz as nutrient. Run large autoclaves purely for crucible feedstock, then crush and acid-leach the cultured bars into <10 ppm-impurity HPQ sand.

title: Coca-Cola bottler franchise for a portable capacitorless memory module
idea: Coca-Cola ships concentrate and lets local bottlers add abundant local water. Adapt this by licensing a capacitor-free BEOL memory concentrate (PDK, recipes, precursor specs, test IP) that any CMOS fab, including US 28-65 nm and MEMS fabs, bottles onto its own wafers with local, non-chokepoint materials.

title: Holographic-grating interference lithography for the periodic cell lattice
idea: Adapt diffraction-grating and security-hologram production: print the strictly periodic array layers with three-beam 193 nm interference or displacement Talbot lithography (one periodic phase mask scanned in z), which writes hexagonal hole lattices across a full field with near-unlimited depth of focus and no projection lens; a cheap KrF trim exposure clears the array edges.

title: MicroLED mass transfer: printing known-good DRAM array tiles
idea: Borrow microLED micro-transfer printing: build ~200 um DRAM array tiles on a donor wafer, test them, then elastomer-stamp only known-good tiles onto periphery wafers at the sense-amp interface; failed sites are re-printed as microLED repair does.

title: Accumulative roll bonding: 3D DRAM tiers from repeated layer transfer
idea: Metallurgy builds nanolaminates by repeatedly rolling and folding; build 3D DRAM tiers by hydrogen-implant smart-cut transfer of 30-50 nm single-crystal Si sheets onto an oxide-bonded stack, then bond stack to stack to double tiers each round (8 to 16 to 32 to 64), instead of growing a 100+ layer Si/SiGe superlattice.
note: Doubling cuts serial rounds but not total bonds (63 for 64 tiers).

title: Fiber-to-the-home splitter broadcasts model weights to many accelerators
idea: Adapted from passive optical networks (PON): a shared weight-memory pool transmits each layer's weights once on an optical channel, and a passive 1:32 splitter delivers the same stream to 32 accelerators at the same moment. Each accelerator keeps only KV-cache and activations in local HBM, not its own copy of the weights.
note: 1:32 split loss and lockstep layer sync across GPUs are key doubts.

title: Deep-space soft-decision decoding inside the DRAM sense amp
idea: Adapted from deep-space telemetry (Voyager/Mars links decode near the noise floor with soft-decision LDPC): each sense amp reports the bit plus a 2-bit confidence derived from its latch time-to-decision (measured by a shared counter), and an on-die LDPC decoder over 512-bit codewords uses those soft values. Ambiguous bits from half-charge cells are flagged and corrected rather than guessed.

title: Nanometre proton-intercalation channel bit with nanosecond writes
idea: MINIFY the ion path to ~2 nm: a gain-cell read channel of MoO3 or Nb2O5 sits on a sub-5-nm solid proton reservoir; a 1-2 V, 5 ns gate pulse moves protons in or out, shifting channel conductance ~10x for non-destructive reads, with retention set by reservoir barrier thickness.
note: Protonic ns switching shown; endurance to 1e12+ and retention are unknowns.

title: Magnify the dielectric's job: linear high-k by day, ferroelectric at shutdown
idea: Make the DRAM capacitor dielectric a ZrO2/HfZrO2 morphotropic blend that acts as a k~50 linear dielectric under normal +/-0.5 V operation, and only when a power-loss detector fires a 2.5 V plate pulse is stored charge converted into remanent polarization; a power-up pulse converts it back.
note: Dual-mode DRAM/FeRAM HZO capacitors are being researched (cf. NVDRAM); field-induced conversion reliability uncertain.

title: Minify the switch to two terminals: OTS selector plus FE capacitor
idea: Pair each ferroelectric capacitor with an ovonic threshold switch selector in a 1S1C stack: half-select voltages stay below the OTS threshold so unselected cells see no disturb, while the selected cell gets the full switching pulse; 4-8 layers stack above CMOS periphery.
note: FE endurance below DRAM-class; OTS threshold variability vs destructive read.

title: Magnify sense time: integrating time-to-digital sensing for 1.5 fF cells
idea: MAGNIFY the sensing window from ~2 ns to 20-40 ns: after charge sharing, a constant-current integrator per bitline pair races both lines to a threshold and a shared counter (TDC) records which crosses first and by how much, resolving 5-10 mV differences a latch cannot.

title: Sense-amp resolution time becomes soft information for row LDPC
idea: MINIFY sense margin almost to zero and MAGNIFY the code: each SA's latch-resolution time (slow = low confidence) is captured as a soft bit, and an 8 Kb row-level LDPC codeword (~3% parity) is decoded in the periphery, tolerating raw BER up to 1e-4.

title: SiGe HBT preamps exploit bipolar matching for tiny signals
idea: MAGNIFY matching precision by switching device physics: one SiGe heterojunction-bipolar differential preamp per 16 bitlines (Vbe mismatch ~1 mV versus 10-20 mV for minimum MOS) amplifies the signal before a CMOS latch.

title: Switched-capacitor bitline doubler magnifies signal before latching
idea: After charge sharing, switches reconnect the two halves of each bitline pair in series (a switched-capacitor voltage doubler), MAGNIFYING the differential signal ~1.8x before the latch fires, which lets VARY MINIFY to ~0.5-0.6 V.

title: Minify DRAM die to 0.5 mm2 confetti, self-assembled onto logic
idea: Make DRAM as tiny 0.5 mm2 micro-dies, whose small area gives near-100% yield, and deposit thousands at once onto logic wafers by fluidic self-assembly into shaped receptor wells, followed by hybrid bonding.
note: FSA placement accuracy vs hybrid bonding pitch.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching digs 150:1 capacitor holes without plasma
idea: Magnify aspect ratio while shrinking gas use to zero: a perforated Ag or Pt catalyst film immersed in HF/H2O2 sinks vertically into silicon, carving 150:1 holes with no fluorocarbon plasma, RF power or helium-cooled chuck. The silicon walls are then oxidized into the capacitor scaffold.
note: Catalyst registration and wall roughness at 20-30 nm holes unproven.

title: Minify the page: 64-byte cache-line-granular paging
idea: Minify the paging unit from 4 KB to 64 B: the memory controller keeps per-line access bits and a line-level remap table, evicting never-touched lines inside 'hot' pages to a compressed CXL/flash tier while the page stays mapped. A miss to an evicted line is refilled by hardware in ~1 us without an OS fault.
note: Per-line remap metadata and microsecond stalls on misses are the doubts.

title: Memory dust: fluidic self-assembled micro-DRAM chiplets
idea: MINIFY chiplets to ~0.5 mm^2 (128 Mb each) and place thousands of them into etched receptor sites on the compute wafer by shape-matched fluidic self-assembly, borrowing microLED mass-transfer methods.

title: Eliminate destructive read: erasable conductive ferroelectric domain walls as bits
idea: Eliminate charge-sharing readout: in single-crystal LiNbO3 thin-film nanocells, a field pulse writes or erases a charged, conducting domain wall bridging two side electrodes in ns; reading is a small current through the wall (on/off ~1e3) that leaves the polarization undisturbed.
note: Same conductive-wall mechanism.

title: Eliminate the storage-node conductor: retention-designed charge traps in nanolaminate dielectrics
idea: Eliminate the conductive storage node and its capacitor: store charge in a band of engineered traps (e.g., Ti dopants in Al2O3 tuned to ~1.0 eV depth) behind a 1.5-nm direct-tunneling oxide, so writes take ~10 ns at under 2 V and thermal emission gives seconds-to-minutes retention, a deliberately leaky flash sized for DRAM duty.
note: Direct-tunnel memory known; engineered trap depth for minutes retention; endurance is key doubt.

title: Eliminate capacitor-hole etching: self-ordered anodic alumina pores become storage nodes
idea: Eliminate the HAR plasma etch, which needs helium backside cooling and argon-diluted plasmas: CVD aluminum from dimethylaluminum hydride (not argon sputtering), then anodize it in oxalic acid, guided by nanoimprinted dimples aligned to the transistor grid, to grow straight 20-30 nm pores at AR 100+. ALD with N2 purge and electroless Ru turn each pore into one capacitor.
note: AAO pores give cheap AR>100, but registering self-ordered pores to a 30 nm transistor grid is unproven.

title: Eliminate the leakage tail in place: on-die electrothermal annealing of weak cells
idea: Eliminate retention-weak tail cells without furnaces or forming-gas and argon anneals: drive a short high current through selected wordline segments so Joule heating takes the local access transistors to ~300-400 C for microseconds, annealing the interface and junction traps behind variable-retention-time and GIDL tail cells; the controller targets the cells its retention profiler flags.

title: Eliminate sensing during refresh: node-gated broadcast recharge pulse
idea: Add a small second transistor whose gate is the storage node, linking the node to a shared restore line; a bank-wide pulse on that line tops up every node holding '1' (transistor on) and leaves '0' nodes untouched (transistor off). Refresh becomes one global pulse with no row activation, sense amplifiers or bitline swing.

title: Eliminate silicon periphery footprint: n-only oxide-TFT dynamic logic above array
idea: Drop PMOS entirely and build decoders, wordline drivers and column logic from n-type oxide-semiconductor TFTs in the BEOL directly over the cell array, using bootstrapped domino-style NMOS-only logic with capacitive self-boost loads. Sense amps stay in silicon.

title: Eliminate the page: AND-gated two-transistor pillar cells
idea: In a vertical-bitline 3D array, each cell has two series access gates, a tier wordline and a pillar-select gate, so a cell connects only when both are high; one activation opens a single 64-tier pillar instead of an 8 Kb row.
note: Fine-grained activation known (half-DRAM, SALP); 3D stack absorbs the second gate's area.

title: Interposer that remembers: BEOL non-volatile memory inside it
idea: Eliminate the interposer's passivity: the ~2500 mm2 silicon interposer (65 nm-class, cheap, U.S.-fabbable) becomes an active interposer with BEOL MRAM or HZO FeRAM arrays and simple peripheral CMOS under and between chiplets, stacking 3-4 BEOL array layers.

title: Ferroelectric content-addressable KV store returns matches, not data
idea: Eliminate scanning KV caches over the bus: store quantized key signatures in 2-FeFET ternary CAM cells so a query is broadcast into the array and only matching token addresses come out; the index survives power cycles.

title: Grid-flexible datacenters: non-volatile memory lets racks drop at peaks
idea: Eliminate the 'stay powered to keep state' requirement: with NV working memory, racks cut to zero power within milliseconds on utility demand-response signals and resume exactly where they were; policy lets utilities fast-track interconnection for certified interruptible NV-equipped load.
note: Depends on DRAM-class NV memory that does not yet exist; policy half is executable.

title: Eliminate the silicon wafer: panel-fab memory sold by good-gigabyte
idea: Build oxide-TFT DRAM on Gen-8 glass panels with existing display tools, all at <=400 C. Tile it into ~1 cm2 tiles, each with its own tile router, and map dead tiles at test. Modules are sold by the panel's verified good capacity, and software only ever sees good tiles.

title: Phase not charge: parametric-oscillator bits sustained by their own pump
idea: Turn refresh from a tax into the storage itself: each bit is a high-Q nanomechanical or LC resonator pumped at 2f by a shared row line, oscillating in one of two phases (0 or pi) that the pump keeps alive; read by phase comparison, write with a brief seed pulse (a modern Goto parametron).
note: Nanomechanical parametron memory demonstrated; resonator area and pump distribution limit density.

title: Make refresh opt-in in the JEDEC standard
idea: Reverse the default in the DRAM standard: define a 'host-guaranteed retention' mode in which the die's internal refresh counter is disabled and the host certifies every row is touched or refreshed within the window, backed by an on-die watchdog bitmap that raises an alert if any row ages out. This standardizes what coverage-based, multi-rate and placement-based controllers need from existing dies.

title: Stand DRAM dies on edge: TSV-free sideways HBM
idea: Rotate the HBM stack 90 degrees: bond thin core dies into a block, saw and polish one face so every die's edge exposes its top-metal lines, then hybrid-bond that polished edge face directly onto the logic die. Each die talks through thousands of edge wires along its 10 mm edge instead of TSVs.

title: Lay the capacitor flat and laminate it: MLCC-in-cell
idea: Replace the tall cylinder with a nanoscale multilayer ceramic capacitor: 6-10 alternating TiN/ZrO2 layers ALD-deposited laterally into a recess, with even electrodes tied to the storage node at one sidewall and odd ones to the plate at the other via selective alternating recess. Capacitance scales with layer count, not aspect ratio.

title: Sense amps built from tier transistors inside each 3D tier
idea: Swap periphery and array roles in an oxide-semiconductor 3D DRAM: build n-only clocked, capacitively bootstrapped sense amplifiers from the same IGZO transistors beside every mat in every tier, so each tier senses locally and only digital data drops to the CMOS base.
note: n-only bootstrapped IGZO sense amps beside each mat; slow and variable but feasible in university TFT runs.

title: Maskless interference lithography for the array, one trim mask
idea: Reverse which part needs a mask: pattern the periodic capacitor lattice with three-beam 193 nm interference (no reticle) at ~70 nm pitch, multiply hole density with block-copolymer DSA, and add one cheap DUV trim mask that blocks the lattice outside the arrays.
note: Interference plus DSA for periodic capacitor lattice; defectivity and trim alignment are the unknowns.

title: Laser in the host, mirror in the memory: optical backscatter
idea: Reverse who emits light: the accelerator package holds the only laser and sends continuous-wave light to each DRAM stack, where reflective electro-absorption modulators on the base die encode read data onto the returning beam, like RFID backscatter. The DRAM side has no laser, no transmitter thermal tuning and no high-power driver.
note: Remote laser and reflective modulators known from CPO and PON.

title: Stack untested dies, route around failures with a base-die crossbar
idea: Reverse test-then-stack: stack 14 lightly tested dies for a 12-die product and put a channel crossbar in the base die that maps logical channels onto whichever dies and channels pass final package test, set by fuses. Yield comes from routing around defects rather than from known-good-die screening.

title: Bookshelf stack: dies stand on edge in an etched rack
idea: Rotate the stack 90 degrees: thin dies are diced, given sidewall pads by angled shadow-mask evaporation over the edge, and inserted vertically into a DRIE-etched silicon rack whose trench floors carry solder pads, so every die connects straight to the base with no TSVs and no die-to-die relay.

title: In-array analog activation integrator replaces digital hammer counters
idea: Move hammer tracking from periphery into the array: each row gets one extra tiny cell that receives a fixed charge packet through a diode-connected path on every activation and slowly leaks; when its voltage crosses a threshold during the row's own sensing, a flag triggers refresh of both neighbors, with the leak rate setting the time window.
note: Per-row leaky charge counter; variation of tiny leak/charge packets sets threshold accuracy.

title: Age-adaptive cells step down from multi-level to binary storage
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: store 2 bits per capacitor (4 charge levels sensed against a ramped reference) while the array is young; as retention tails widen, the controller re-formats aging pages to 1 bit/cell with large margin, and later to a refresh-heavy cold tier, rather than failing the module.
note: Flash-style mode downgrade applied to DRAM; MLC DRAM margins are the doubt.

title: Segmentation: above-array oxide switches slice each bitline into eight
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation resolves 'long bitline for few sense amps' versus 'short bitline for big signal': row-address-controlled IGZO isolation switches, built in BEOL above the array at zero silicon area, cut each bitline every 64 cells so only the segment holding the active row is connected to the sense amp.

title: Merging: wordline driver doubles as analog row-hammer activation counter
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging: each sub-wordline driver gets a tiny pumped capacitor that gains a fixed charge packet on every activation and leaks with a ~32 ms time constant; when it crosses a Schmitt threshold the driver flags its two neighbours for targeted refresh. Counting is merged into the device that already sees every activation.

title: Excessive action: 256-tier vertical bitline read by chopper auto-zero amplifier
idea: TRIZ #16 Excessive action: one vertical bitline is deliberately overloaded with 256 tiers of planar ~1 fF thin-film capacitor cells (bitline ~300 fF, signal ~1.5 mV) and read by a chopper-stabilized, auto-zeroed, correlated-double-sampling amplifier under the array that integrates for ~1 us, so one amplifier serves 256 stacked cells.

title: Asymmetry: per-bitline read inverters, one slow shared write scanner
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: for read-mostly AI weights and KV-cache, a 2T oxide gain cell is read non-destructively by a single minimum-size inverter per bitline (no latch, no reference, no restore), while writes go through one high-voltage scanning write driver per 64k cells at ~10 us per row.

title: Grounded shield planes interleaved between tiers to stop row hammer
idea: TRIZ #11 Beforehand cushioning: deposit a ~3 nm grounded TiN or doped-Si plane in the dielectric between every pair of 3D tiers (and a buried shield line between adjacent wordlines in 2D). The shields absorb wordline coupling and collect migrating electrons from an aggressor row before they reach victim storage nodes.

title: Glass-panel memory sheets on idle display fab lines
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap short-living objects: replace precious 300 mm wafers with cheap Gen-8.5 glass (~5.5 m2) and run 4-8 stacked layers of IGZO 2T0C gain cells at ~1.5 um rules on existing LCD/OLED backplane lines. Panels (~15-20 GB per layer) are diced into memory tiles for a CXL-attached 100-200 ns capacity tier.
note: Panel cost at 1.5 um rules suggests ~$10-20/GB, not $2-5; real lever is idle display capacity.

title: Inside-out gain cell: storage core gates its surrounding channel tube
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: form each 4F2 pillar as an insulated metal core (the storage node) wrapped by gate oxide and a thin IGZO channel tube that is the read transistor. A small vertical write transistor stacked on top charges the core, so the core gates the whole tube circumference with no separate capacitor.
note: Core-gated IGZO tube is a neat 4F2 2T0C variant; vertical CAA IGZO gain cells already reported.

title: Monolayer MoS2 gain-cell tiers stacked by wafer-scale film transfer
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells and thin films: grow wafer-scale monolayer MoS2 on reusable sapphire templates and transfer the films one by one onto the stack below 300 C, each film becoming a tier of 2T0C cells. The 1.8 eV bandgap and 0.7 nm body give off-currents below ~1e-19 A/um, and with no capacitor the tier pitch can shrink to ~30 nm.

title: Leakage-ratioed loadless pair holds state across two tiers
idea: TRIZ #9 Preliminary anti-action: build a true/complement storage-node pair across two tiers with cross-coupled access devices whose off-state leakage is pre-engineered (Vt, length) to be ~10x stronger toward the rail each node already sits at. Leakage then holds the state like a loadless 4T SRAM instead of erasing it.
note: 10x leakage ratio must survive the very variability tail that drives refresh.

title: Pre-formed porous cleave layer makes CZ wafers reusable donors
idea: TRIZ #10 Prior action: before any device processing, anodize a double-porosity silicon layer into a prime CZ wafer and grow 3-5 um of device-grade epitaxial silicon on top (ELTRAN-style). After the array front-end, the wafer is bonded to a carrier or periphery wafer and cleaved at the porous layer, and the donor is re-polished and reused 10-20 times.
note: Porous layer must survive the DRAM front-end thermal budget before cleave.

title: 77 K memory tier lets fabs drop recessed-gate access transistors
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter changes: run memory racks in liquid-nitrogen immersion, where thermally activated junction and subthreshold leakage fall by >20 orders of magnitude and only tunneling remains, so low-field planar cells hold charge effectively indefinitely while cold and refresh is switched off; the fab then builds simple planar or shallow-fin access transistors instead of the 3-4 mask buried-channel module.

title: Planar AlScN ferroelectric capacitor replaces the 70:1 pillar
idea: TRIZ #40 Composite materials: alloying ~25-30% Sc into AlN makes a wurtzite ferroelectric with remanent polarization ~80-110 uC/cm2 (4-5x HZO), so a flat 30x30 nm, ~10 nm-thick AlScN capacitor sputtered on the storage contact switches ~1.5-2 fC, matching a 5 fF pillar's signal, using PVD tools U.S. BAW-filter fabs already run at volume.

title: Local quality: LCD-line glass interposers with zoned fine-line RDL
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: run idle Gen-4/5 LCD TFT lines (1.5-3 um lithography on 730x920 mm glass) to make multilayer Cu RDL glass interposers. Fine lines go only in the memory-to-compute shoreline zones and coarse power planes everywhere else, and a-Si/IGZO TFT switches are built in as lane-repair multiplexers. (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)
note: Reusing idle LCD lines plus TFT lane-repair muxes is the twist.

title: Homogeneity: deep-trench eDRAM built into passive silicon interposers
idea: TRIZ #33 Homogeneity: silicon interposers already made at 65 nm on plentiful lines get one added deep-trench capacitor mask (plus existing transistor flow where available) to carry GB-scale eDRAM in otherwise passive silicon under the accelerator.
note: Needs active (transistor) interposer, not passive; GB-scale at 65 nm trench density is plausible.

title: Mitochondrial cristae lamellar capacitor for lateral 3D DRAM cells
idea: Mitochondria pack membrane area into folded cristae joined to the body by narrow junctions. In a horizontal 3D DRAM tier, build the lateral capacitor from a thin Si/SiGe sub-superlattice inside the tier. Selectively etch out the SiGe to leave 4-6 thin shelves branching off a narrow neck, then coat them conformally as cristae-like folded electrodes.

title: Neuron first-spike latency: time-coded multilevel cell readout
idea: Neurons encode stimulus strength in their first-spike latency. Store four charge levels per cell and read by dumping the node onto a precharged line with a threshold inverter. A time-to-digital converter shared across 64 columns measures the trip time to ~10 ps, and that time sorts the levels instead of voltage-margin-limited multi-threshold sensing.
note: Time-coded sensing known in NVM; DRAM 4-level charge margins are thin.

title: Bone-marrow niche domain wall: conductive wall parked in pinning notch
idea: Long-lived plasma cells survive only in particular bone-marrow niches. Store the bit as whether a conductive ferroelectric domain wall sits in an engineered pinning 'niche', a notch in a thin-film LiNbO3 mesa between two read electrodes. A field pulse moves the wall in or out, and the wall's metallic conduction (10^3-10^6 on/off) is read non-destructively at low voltage.
note: Same conductive-wall mechanism with pinning notch.

title: Coral biomineral templating grows one crystal grain per access transistor
idea: Corals deposit amorphous calcium carbonate that crystallizes into oriented single crystals on an organic template; deposit amorphous In2O3/InGaO, place one ~10 nm crystalline seed per transistor site, and crystallize laterally at 300-350 C so every channel is a single grain with no boundary.

title: Nicotinic coincidence-gated access FET opens only with row AND column
idea: The nicotinic receptor opens only when two acetylcholine molecules bind; give each BEOL access FET two independent gates (top on the wordline, bottom on a column-segment select line) with Vt set so neither alone inverts the channel.
note: Dual-gate AND selection ends overfetch; Vt variability makes 'neither gate alone inverts' margin tight.

title: Dendritic bitline trees with spine amplifiers at every branch
idea: Replace long flat bitlines with a neuron-like dendritic tree in the 3D stack: each 8-cell twig joins its branch through a one-transistor oxide-TFT charge-transfer preamp at the branch point (an active dendritic conductance), so a cell only ever charges ~5-10 fF of twig instead of ~60 fF of bitline.
note: TFT preamp offset and variability limit gain.

title: Magnetosome-chain bond pads self-align dies to 50 nm
idea: Mimic magnetotactic bacteria's magnetite chains: embed CoPt nanomagnet chains under each die's alignment pads and their mirror image on the target wafer, so during die-to-wafer hybrid bonding on a thin water film, magnetic attraction plus capillarity pulls every die into sub-100 nm registration in parallel without a precision bonder.

title: Snake-molt cleaving stacks forty single-crystal tiers from one donor
idea: A snake sheds a perfect thin copy of its skin each cycle; hydrogen-implant and cleave 30 nm single-crystal Si films from one reusable, repolished donor onto the growing stack with 20 nm oxide bonding interlayers, building 40 monocrystalline tiers, then pattern all tiers at once with one hole/slit etch and lateral recess.
note: Monocrystalline tiers are plausible, but a bond/cleave/CMP per tier is not near-flat cost.

title: Exoskeleton-molt imprint tiers: nanoimprint each monolithic memory tier cheaply
idea: Arthropods form each new cuticle against the old one; build 10 monolithic oxide-semiconductor 2T0C tiers above CMOS and pattern each tier's critical layers by jet-and-flash nanoimprint from one shared master set replicated into daughters, at ~1/8 the per-layer cost of an EUV exposure and with no scanner.

title: Murmuration checks: each cell group verifies seven neighbours in-array
idea: Starlings stay coherent by each tracking ~7 neighbours; place tiny check nodes in the CMOS under the array so each 8-cell group carries local parity shared with 7 overlapping neighbour groups (a spatially coupled LDPC evaluated locally), and the array iteratively corrects itself during refresh without shipping data to the controller.

title: Neon-lamp bistability via broken-gap 2D Esaki diode latch
idea: Early computers latched bits in neon lamps' negative resistance; build a cell where two series broken-gap tunnel diodes (e.g., black phosphorus/SnSe2 or WSe2/SnSe2) form a Goto-pair bistable node with pA valley current, plus one access transistor, so the node self-restores like SRAM in ~3F2 with no refresh.
note: Tunneling SRAM revisited with 2D broken-gap junctions; RT peak-to-valley ratio and uniformity are the bet.

title: Thin-film solar liquid-phase crystallization: monocrystal-grade silicon for stacked access tiers
idea: Thin-film solar groups melt silicon on glass with a scanning line-focus diode laser so it recrystallizes into centimeter-scale grains. Apply line-laser liquid-phase crystallization to each deposited amorphous-silicon tier of a 3D DRAM, seeded through windows opened in an alumina inter-tier dielectric with hot phosphoric acid, to get near-single-crystal lateral access channels without fluorinated etch or wafer bonding.

title: Photomultiplier dynode cascade pre-amplifier for femtofarad cells
idea: Borrow the photomultiplier's dynode chain: the bitline feeds a stack of three gated-diode charge amplifiers, each transferring and multiplying the packet (~3x per stage by collapsing a gate-boosted capacitance) before the latch fires. A 1.5 fF cell then looks like a ~20 fF cell to the latch.
note: Builds on IBM gated-diode amplifier work.

title: Fiber-optic EDFA-style in-line repeaters along long bitlines
idea: Like optical amplifiers spaced along long-haul fiber, insert a tiny IGZO TFT preamp/isolation switch in the BEOL every 128 cells, buffering each local segment's signal onto a global bitline, so one silicon SA serves an 8x longer bitline.

title: Deep Space Network weak-signal sensing frees capacitors from wet mold-strip
idea: NASA hears Voyager's 20 W transmitter by building great receivers, not louder transmitters. Correlated double sampling (sample the bitline after equalize and after charge share, subtract on a capacitor pair) plus a low-noise preamp resolves ~15 mV, so cells can use a ~1.5 fF, ~15:1 dry-etched capacitor instead of a 70:1 cylinder that needs a wet HF mold-oxide strip and many high-AR rinse/dry cycles.

title: Croissant lamination: tier doubling by repeated wafer fold-and-bond
idea: Like laminated dough that doubles its layers with every fold, grow an 8-tier Si/SiGe superlattice once, then bond the wafer face-to-face onto a copy of itself, Smart-Cut the donor and repeat, so four bond cycles give 128 tiers. No single epitaxy run ever exceeds the SiGe strain-relaxation limit, and each tier keeps single-crystal quality for the lateral transistor.

title: Hotel-keycard micro-rows: coincident gating opens only 64 bits
idea: Like a keycard that opens one room instead of the whole floor, give each 3D DRAM cell a series pair of access gates, the tier wordline plus a vertical column-group select, so an activation opens only the 64 cells at the intersection rather than an 8 Kb page, and only those bitlines swing and restore.

title: RV 12-volt rule: short pillars let the array run at 0.35 V
idea: Low-voltage DC works in RVs because the runs are short; build vertical-bitline mats with 32-cell bitlines (Cb ~1.5 fF), giving a charge-transfer ratio near 0.6 that supports sensing at VARY 0.35 V with a ~100 mV signal, with sense amps in a bonded low-voltage logic wafer.

title: Pottery bisque-then-glaze: capacitor-first flow, transistors on transferred silicon
idea: Borrowed from pottery, where the clay body is fired hot first and the glaze cooler later: build the capacitor array first with a 700-800 C crystallized SrTiO3 or rutile TiO2 dielectric (k~100), planarize, Smart-Cut-transfer a thin single-crystal Si film on top, then form access transistors at <=450 C with laser dopant activation.

title: MicroLED mass transfer: stamp-printed DRAM dielets onto logic wafers
idea: Borrowed from microLED displays, which move millions of 10 um LEDs at once with elastomer stamps: make 100x100 um DRAM array dielets on cheap mature-node wafers, undercut-release them, and transfer-print hundreds per die directly onto accelerator wafers beside the compute, wired with one redistribution layer.

title: 1950s diode-capacitor store reborn as stacked selector-capacitor crosspoint decks
idea: Early machines held bits on capacitors gated by diodes rather than transistors. Revive it as 1S1C: planar MIM capacitors stacked with a two-terminal ovonic or punch-through selector (~1e-15 A off) in BEOL decks, accessed by V/2-biased crosspoint lines with short 64-cell bitline segments so ~0.5 fF suffices.
note: 1S1C crosspoint decks avoid transistor; selector leakage and half-select disturb are the risk.

title: Sperry MNOS shadow trap: access transistor stores a sleep copy
idea: Revive Sperry's 1967 metal-nitride-oxide-semiconductor memory: give the access transistor a thin nitride charge-trap layer. On entering deep sleep, a row-by-row pulse injects trap charge according to each cell's bit (1e5-1e6 cycles is ample for sleep events) and the array powers off with zero refresh; on wake, the trap-shifted Vt is sensed and rewritten to the capacitor.
note: Trap layer in access gate may itself create VRT; nvSRAM-style precedent.

title: Moll-Tarui ferroelectric transistor as a sleep-only Vt shifter
idea: Revive the 1963 Moll-Tarui ferroelectric-gate transistor, but switch it only when entering and leaving long idle: a thin HZO layer, using hafnium refined in Albany, Oregon, sits in the access-transistor gate stack. It is poled to raise Vt ~0.4-0.5 V during self-refresh and re-poled to low Vt on wake, so endurance needs are only ~1e6-1e8 events.
note: Ferroelectric Vt shift toggled only per sleep; junction/GIDL leakage then limits gain.

title: Selectron-style binary-coded tier selection replaces staircase contacts
idea: Revive RCA's Selectron, whose grid bars picked one eyelet by binary coincidence: at each mat edge every tier's wordline passes through log2(N) series select transistors whose thresholds are binary-coded per tier with log2(N) chop masks (the mask-halving trick already used for staircases), so 7 complementary vertical select-gate pairs choose one of 128 tiers. Fourteen contacts replace 128 staircase landings.
note: Log2(N) contacts; per-tier Vt coding in deep stacks is hard.

title: STARAN associative processor as near-memory KV pre-filter
idea: Revive the Goodyear STARAN associative array: a TCAM beside the HBM stack holds a 64-bit SimHash of each cached key, the query hash is broadcast, and match lines fire for keys within a Hamming threshold. Only those ~1-3% candidates are fetched at full precision while the rest of the KV sits compressed in a slower tier.
note: SimHash TCAM recall for attention top-k uncertain.

title: Bell Model V two-out-of-five revival: reference-free top-k sensing
idea: Bell Labs relay computers stored digits in 2-out-of-5 constant-weight codes so every word checked itself. Store each 64-bit word as a 68-cell constant-weight codeword with exactly 34 charged cells (C(68,34) is about 2^64.6); instead of comparing each cell to a fixed Vref, a winner-take-all network marks the 34 highest-voltage cells as charged, so uniform decay, temperature drift and plate noise cancel out.

title: Swiss Watch-Chip Subthreshold Design for DRAM Periphery at 0.4 V
idea: Revive Eric Vittoz's 1970s CEH/CSEM watch-chip methodology (subthreshold CMOS for microwatt budgets) for DRAM periphery: decoders, sense-amp control and I/O run at 0.35-0.45 V with body-biased logic and wide, slow, parallel paths replacing fast narrow ones.
note: Wide-slow subthreshold periphery cuts CV2 but adds latency; array energy unaffected.

title: Buried germanium quantum well confines holes without any p-n junction
idea: Invert 'retention is set by junction leakage' -> set it by a band offset. Holes are stored in a compressively strained Ge quantum well 5 nm below a Si channel; the ~0.5 eV valence-band offset confines them with no p-n junction, so the defect-driven GIDL/junction tail becomes designed thermionic escape with retention ~exp(dEv/kT).
note: Twist on quantum-well floating-body 1T-DRAM work.

title: Gen-10.5 display glass memory trades density for cheap area
idea: Invert 'cost per bit comes from shrinking the cell' -> buy area instead. A Gen-10.5 glass sheet is ~9.6 m^2 (~140 300-mm wafers); build 1T1C cells at ~1 um^2 with planar 20 fF MIM capacitors and IGZO access (retention minutes, refresh nearly gone), giving ~1 TB of cells per sheet in under-utilized display fabs.
note: Buys cheap area on Gen-10.5 glass; n-only IGZO periphery and micron rules limit speed and energy.

title: Water-released single-crystal BST membranes stacked as capacitor tiers
idea: Invert 'high-k must be deposited polycrystalline in place' -> grow perfect crystal elsewhere and transfer it. Epitaxial (Ba,Sr)TiO3 on a water-soluble Sr3Al2O6 sacrificial layer is released as a freestanding membrane (k ~300-1000 vs ~40 for ALD ZrO2), laminated onto glass or foil carriers under oxide-TFT access, and the growth substrate is reused.
note: Freestanding BST membranes known; transfer yield and thin-film dead layer cut real k.

title: Ferroelectric trim transistor nulls each sense amp's offset
idea: Inverting 'sense-amp offset is frozen at fabrication': one HZO ferroelectric trim FET in each sense amp's tail is programmed once at wafer test to cancel its measured offset, so the latch can use minimum-size transistors and resolve ~40 mV instead of ~100 mV.

title: Micro-bitlines with a gain transistor every sixteen cells
idea: Inverting 'cell charge must swing a long bitline by itself': bitlines are cut into 16-cell micro-bitlines (~3 fF) that each gate a single local gain transistor driving the global bitline, so a 1-2 fF capacitor gives a readable signal.
note: Local gain per segment relaxes Cs; gain-transistor Vt variation and area per 16 cells are doubts.

title: Vertical-bitline triple-tier activation computes majority inside stack
idea: Inverts 'tiers are independent storage whose data must leave the stack.' Open three tiers on a shared vertical bitline at once so charge sharing yields bitwise majority, and copy between tiers by one vertical charge share, so whole-pillar AND/OR/copy/zero never crosses the I/O.

title: Per-tier 2T preamp at pillar junction cuts needed charge 5x
idea: Inverts 'bitlines are passive wires to an edge sense amp.' Place a two-transistor gain stage where each tier's short local bitline meets the vertical global bitline, so the storage node drives a gate instead of a long line, letting Cs fall from ~5 fF to ~1 fF.

title: Open standard periphery-free array tier any mature fab can build
idea: Inverts 'one company makes the whole DRAM stack.' Publish an open spec for an array-only tier (bond-pad map, electrical rules, materials limited to Si, Al, Ti, N, O and Cu-Mn) so many small fabs supply interchangeable tiers to independent stacking houses.
note: Spec is cheap to publish; mature fabs lack DRAM capacitor capability, so adoption is the doubt.

title: Print the array once; later layers grow onto it
idea: Inverts 'each layer is lithographically re-registered'. One EUV exposure defines the honeycomb of active pillars; wordline recess, storage-node contact, landing pad and capacitor are then built on it by area-selective ALD, selective epitaxy and spacer self-alignment, so the pattern is inherited rather than re-printed.

title: Optical broadcast of one weight copy to 64 accelerators
idea: Invert 'each accelerator owns a private copy of the model': one memory pool streams weights once into a passive optical star coupler that splits the same light to 64 GPUs in lockstep; each GPU consumes the broadcast layer by layer and keeps only activations and KV in local HBM.
note: Needs TB/s per GPU in lockstep after 64-way split loss; resembles Cerebras weight streaming.

title: Stack-first, test-later: base die remaps around untested dies
idea: Invert 'only known-good dies are stacked': stack lightly tested dies with ~20% spare capacity and let the base die run full BIST after bonding, building a per-subarray remap table that routes around bad rows, banks or whole dies.

title: Wurtzite AlScN ferroelectric delivers planar 11,000-electron bits
idea: Sputter Al0.7Sc0.3N at <=400 C, thinned to ~5 nm to keep coercive voltage near 2 V. Its 2Pr ~ 200 uC/cm2 delivers ~1.8 fC (~11,000 e) from a flat 30x30 nm capacitor, versus ~0.1 fC from a dielectric, in a 1T1C destructive-read cell with no high-AR pillar.
note: AlScN FeRAM is actively researched; endurance far below DRAM's unlimited requirement.

title: ALD oxide quantum-well charge bucket gated by band bending
idea: Grow a 3 nm In2O3 well between Ga2O3 barriers (dEc ~ 0.9 eV) by ALD at <=300 C, under a gate and over a read channel. A gate pulse bends the bands to inject electrons thermionically, retention tau = tau0*exp(dEc/kT) gives ~0.5 s at 85 C, and stored electrons shift the read channel's threshold.

title: Freestanding SrTiO3 membrane transfer gives k~300 capacitors cold
idea: Grow single-crystal SrTiO3 on a donor wafer over a water-soluble Sr3Al2O6 sacrificial layer, release it in water, and transfer and bond the ~5 nm membrane onto the memory wafer at <=300 C. Crystallization happens off-wafer, so the product never exceeds 400 C yet gets a k~300 dielectric.
note: Off-wafer crystallization is smart; wafer-scale 5 nm transfer and dead layer are risks.

title: Junction-free Ga2O3 back-end access transistor at 4.8 eV bandgap
idea: Intrinsic generation scales as n_i ~ exp(-Eg/2kT), so go past IGZO (~3.2 eV) to ALD amorphous or nanocrystalline Ga2O3 (~4.8 eV). Build n-channel thin-film access transistors below 400 C above the periphery, with no p-n junction at the storage node, and suppress oxygen-vacancy traps with an N2O plasma plus an Al2O3 cap. The only leak paths left are gate-dielectric tunneling and deep-trap emission, and film thickness controls both.

title: Junctionless nanosheet access device removes the storage-node p-n junction
idea: Make the access transistor a uniformly n+ (~1e19 cm^-3) 5 nm nanosheet that the wordline workfunction fully depletes when off. Source, channel and storage node are then one doping type, so no reverse-biased metallurgical junction touches the storage node. A buried dielectric, not a p-well, isolates it from the substrate.

title: Quantum-confined 3 nm silicon body widens the bandgap without new materials
idea: Confining silicon to a ~3 nm body raises its subband edges, so the effective gap grows ~0.2-0.3 eV. Because n_i ~ exp(-Eg/2kT), generation drops by about exp(-0.25/0.052), roughly 100x. Build the vertical access channel as an ultrathin crystalline silicon shell on a dielectric core (macaroni-style as in 3D NAND, crystallized by laser or lateral solid-phase epitaxy), so the whole depletion region around the storage node is confined.
note: Confinement widens gap ~0.25 eV; thickness variation and SPE-film traps threaten the 100x.

title: Tier-wide buried back-gate plane pulsed negative during retention
idea: Deposit a continuous conductive back-gate plane under each tier's lateral access-transistor layer; during idle a charge pump holds it near -1 V, raising every access transistor's Vt through body coupling, and returns only the tier being accessed to 0 V.

title: Cubic mats with sense amplifiers at the array centroid tier
idea: Build each mat as a 64x64x64 cube instead of a 512x512 square and place its sense amps and local I/O in the middle tier, so every cell is at most 32 lateral pitches plus 32 tier pitches from its amplifier.
note: CMOS sense tier mid-stack is hard; could be done with bonded half-stacks.

title: Binary-coded vertical tier select replaces staircase contacts
idea: Give each tier a tiny thin-film decoder hard-wired to its own tier number and run only log2(N) true/complement address rods vertically through the stack, so selecting one of 128 tiers needs 14 rods instead of a 128-step staircase with 128 contacts.

title: Z-critical cell puts every sub-20 nm dimension in film thickness
idea: Build stacked source/sacrificial/drain layers and later replace the sacrificial layer through a slit with channel, gate dielectric and wrap gate, so channel length, oxide, capacitor gap and wordline spacing are all set by ALD or epitaxy thickness and lithography prints only features of 40 nm or more.

title: Spalled 20-micron device films reuse each Czochralski donor fifteen times
idea: First principles: a DRAM die's devices live in the top <1 um of a 775 um wafer, so >99.8% of the high-purity silicon (and the quartz-crucible life that grew it) is mechanical ballast. Grow a 20 um epi layer, peel it off with a Ni-stressor controlled spall, bond it to a low-grade recycled handle wafer, then CMP and re-epi the donor for ~15 reuse cycles.

title: Thirty-two-cell local bitlines shrink the storage capacitor tenfold
idea: Signal is dV = Vcell*Cs/(Cs+CBL): a ~50 fF bitline forces ~5 fF cells, but a local two-transistor sense stage every 32 cells (CBL ~3 fF) yields the same ~100 mV from ~0.5 fF, so the capacitor becomes a shallow AR~7 cup.
note: Removes HAR capacitor but local-sense mismatch and area may cancel density.

title: Atmospheric spatial ALD deposits 150 oxide tiers without vacuum or helium
idea: Vacuum pumps, load locks and chambers dominate deposition cost, not atoms (a 10 nm tier is ~0.2 mg per wafer). Move wafers under gas-bearing spatial-ALD heads at 1 atm in N2, depositing ZnO channel, Al2O3 dielectric and Al:ZnO electrode tiers in-line at ~$3 per tier per wafer.

title: Mask-free interference lithography for every periodic array layer
idea: First principle: a DRAM array is a lattice whose whole information content is one unit cell plus two lattice vectors (~100 bits), yet each array layer goes through a $300k+ EUV mask and a ~$200M projection scanner. Print the active, wordline, bitline and storage-node-contact layers with a reticle-free 4-beam 193i (or EUV) interference stepper that has no projection optics, and trim the array edges with one coarse DUV block mask, so masks are needed only for the periphery.

title: Area-selective deposition pattern propagation: zero-overlay layer stacking
idea: First principle: overlay error exists only because each layer is aligned optically; if each new layer nucleates only on a material exposed by the layer below (inhibitor SAMs that bind oxide but not metal, and the reverse), the pattern propagates chemically with zero misalignment. Design the cell so landing pads, contacts and the capacitor bottom electrode are each grown selectively on the previous layer, leaving one litho master for the array.

title: MLCC-style laminated capacitor: deposit plates, don't etch towers
idea: First principle: capacitance needs electrode area, which can come from many thin horizontal plates, as in a multilayer ceramic capacitor, instead of one tall vertical tower. Deposit 30 alternating TiN/high-k layers as blankets, punch one shallow hole per cell, and use selective lateral recess plus side contacts to tie odd plates to the storage node and even plates to the plate line.

title: Photon-counting avalanche receivers near the 20-photon quantum limit
idea: A shot-noise-limited receiver needs only ~20 photons per bit for 1e-12 BER, while PIN+TIA links burn ~10^4 because of amplifier noise. Use Ge-on-Si avalanche/SPAD arrays with pulse-position modulation, where each photon pulse carries log2(M) bits, so the laser budget falls by orders of magnitude.
note: SPAD dead time and jitter limit lane rate; laser is only part of link energy.

title: Soft-decision sensing lets 1.5 fF capacitors meet target BER
idea: First-principles budget: bitline kT/C noise is only ~0.3 mV against ~100 mV of signal, so most of today's 5 fF of charge is spent on worst-case sense-amp offset and not on thermal noise. Sense each bitline with three staggered trip points (2-bit soft output) and feed log-likelihoods to a rate-0.94 LDPC over 1 KB, letting Cs drop to ~1.5 fF.

title: Mask-free interference lithography for the periodic DRAM array layers
idea: A DRAM array is a periodic lattice whose information content is a few numbers (pitch, angle, phase); encoding it in a $1M mask and EUV photons is overkill. Expose the dense array layers with multi-beam 193 nm immersion interference or achromatic Talbot lithography, using a conventional scanner only for the cut, trim and array-edge layers.
note: 193i interference pitch ~70 nm needs pitch splitting; cut-layer overlay is the risk.

title: Janus coin: ferroelectric semiconductor channel that stores and senses itself
idea: Stimulus 'two-faced coin' -> use 2D alpha-In2Se3, a semiconductor whose own lattice polarization can flip, as the transistor channel; the polarization direction sets the threshold, so one device both stores and reads the bit with no capacitor and no separate ferroelectric gate layer.
note: alpha-In2Se3 FeS-FETs demonstrated in labs; endurance and 2D integration unproven at DRAM cycles.

title: Rust: hematite antiferromagnet switched by orbital torque, no heavy metals
idea: Stimulus 'rust' -> use alpha-Fe2O3 (hematite), an insulating antiferromagnet, as the bit: its Neel vector is rotated by orbital-Hall torque from a light Ti or Cr layer instead of Pt or W spin-Hall metals, and read by spin-Hall magnetoresistance. Stacks are sputtered and Ar-ion-milled, so no fluorine etch.
note: Read signal (SMR ~0.1%) far too small for fast sensing.

title: Thimble capacitor: ultra-low leakage lets Cs shrink tenfold
idea: Random stimulus 'thimble': a tiny cup is enough if nothing spills. Pair a sub-0.01 fA access device with local short-bitline sense amps so a 0.5 fF stubby capacitor (AR ~8:1) holds the bit, deleting the 60-75:1 pillar etch, the support-mesh wet removal and the many high-AR cleans and IPA/scCO2 dries of today's capacitor module.
note: Low-AR cap needs aA-class access plus short bitlines; signal margin at 0.5 fF is the doubt.

title: Magnifying glass: one-transistor local preamp every sixteen cells
idea: A magnifying glass enlarges the signal before the eye sees it: split each bitline into 16-cell local segments of ~1 fF; the cell shares charge with this tiny segment (about +/-300 mV), which drives the gate of one segment transistor that discharges the long global bitline, while a separate write-back transistor restores.

title: Canal locks with side basins: stepwise adiabatic bitline charging
idea: Water-saving canal locks fill and drain in steps from side basins and reuse most of the water. Raise the sense-amp rails (and so 8k bitlines) in 6-8 steps from on-die tank capacitors at intermediate voltages, and on precharge return each step's charge to its basin, so the supply only tops up resistive losses.
note: Known stepwise-charging art; 6-10x optimistic given switch losses and SA regeneration needs.

title: Rusting aluminum: anodic alumina self-orders capacitor holes without EUV
idea: Stimulus 'rust' (corrosion that builds structure) -> anodize an aluminum film in oxalic/phosphoric acid so it self-organizes into a hexagonal array of straight nanopores (~25-60 nm pitch, AR >100), registered by a light DUV pre-pattern; use the pores as the capacitor mold, ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN, then dissolve the alumina.

title: Lighthouse: solid-state 213 nm interference lithography for cell arrays
idea: Stimulus 'lighthouse' (one coherent beam marks a whole coastline) -> pattern the perfectly periodic DRAM capacitor and active arrays by three-beam immersion interference from a 5th-harmonic Nd:YAG 213 nm laser (no neon excimer gas, no mask, no EUV), then pitch-split with self-aligned spacers.
note: Periodic arrays suit maskless interference; honeycomb fidelity, stitching and edge trim are the doubts.

title: Woodworm: metal-assisted chemical etching bores capacitor holes plasma-free
idea: Stimulus 'woodworm' (a tiny creature bores straight tunnels) -> pattern an Ag or Pt catalyst mesh, then etch in HF/H2O2 at room temperature; the catalyst sinks vertically and bores AR >100 holes in sacrificial silicon that become the capacitor mold.

title: Velcro: detachable memory chiplets outlive their accelerators
idea: Velcro lets parts be reused: attach LPDDR/HBM-class memory to accelerators with low-temperature anisotropic conductive film or fine-pitch sockets (<200 C) instead of permanent solder and underfill, so memory is harvested and redeployed when the compute die is replaced every 2-3 years.
note: HBM generations change interfaces; SI at fine pitch through ACF/sockets doubtful.

title: Rubber stamp: micro-transfer-print DRAM confetti into logic BEOL
idea: An elastomer 'rubber stamp' picks thousands of 200 um DRAM tiles from a released source wafer at once and prints them into cavities in the processor's upper metal layers, within 50 um of the cores, where they are connected by one RDL layer.
note: Cavities in logic BEOL displace routing; tile-to-core proximity gain uncertain.

title: Chandelier: DRAM blades hung edge-on perpendicular to processor
idea: Forced 'chandelier': DRAM dies are mounted vertically, edge-on, like hanging crystals, with sidewall pads soldered to the processor substrate. Coolant flows between the blades, and 32 or more blades fit per package with no TSVs.
note: Edge-on die stacking known (Irvine Sensors cubes); edge pad density limits.

title: Bicycle chain: spatially coupled LDPC links codewords along a row
idea: Each 64 B line's parity also covers slices of its neighbors like chain links, forming a spatially coupled LDPC across a 1 KB page that a sliding-window decoder in the base/buffer die resolves while the page is open.
note: Whole-page decode conflicts with 64 B access latency.

title: Desert cactus: Ga2O3 access transistors keep cells hydrated at 125 C
idea: The cactus's thick skin hoards water: a 4.8 eV bandgap Ga2O3 channel deposited by mist-CVD/ALD in BEOL forms the vertical access transistor over silicon-formed capacitors, where intrinsic generation at 125 C is negligible and off-current can stay <1e-20 A for 10 years.
note: Wider gap than IGZO but BEOL Ga2O3 TFT quality and mobility are poor.

title: Reef: idle LCD panel fabs pattern IGZO gain-cell memory glass
idea: Random stimulus 'artificial reef' -> retired hulls host new life. Oversupplied Gen 8.5/10.5 LCD fabs, which already make IGZO TFTs, pattern ~1.5 um 2T0C gain-cell arrays with local sense amps on glass; one 5.5 m2 substrate at ~5 um2/cell holds ~1.1 Tb (~137 GB).
note: IGZO 2T0C retention is excellent; ~$2-8/GB slow tier plausible but below DRAM density by orders.

title: Temporary tattoo: micro-transfer-print DRAM chiplets directly onto accelerator BEOL
idea: Random stimulus 'temporary tattoo' -> press, peel, transfer. Elastomer stamps pick up ~10,000 thinned 100 um DRAM chiplets per stroke from source wafers made in many small fabs and print them onto accelerator BEOL or panels, with printed RDL.

title: Catalyst-etched 200:1 silicon capacitor holes using DSA mesh and Florida HF
idea: Box = {medium: charge on ALD dielectric in metal-assisted-chemically-etched Si holes | access: buried vertical FET | sense: charge share | integration: 1T1C in bulk Si | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: U.S.-made block-copolymer DSA defines a Au/Ag catalyst mesh, then HF/H2O2 etches straight 200:1 holes}. The HF comes from fluorosilicic acid recovered at Florida phosphate plants instead of imported fluorspar, and the etch needs only wet benches, not imported high-AR plasma etchers.
note: MACE reaches high AR; uniformity at sub-30 nm holes is the doubt.

title: Scanner-free cell arrays: laser interference lithography plus e-beam periphery
idea: Box = {medium: charge on pillar capacitors | access: vertical FET | sense: standard SA | integration: periodic array patterned separately from the periphery | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: 4-beam 193 nm interference exposure from U.S. lasers gives a defect-free ~68 nm pitch dot lattice, pitch-split 2-4x by ALD spacers, while a U.S. multibeam writer exposes only the irregular periphery}. Cell arrays are perfectly periodic, so they need interference, not imaging, which removes imported scanners and masks.
note: Mask-free periodic arrays; overlay between lattice and periphery is the doubt.

title: Multi-threshold soft-sensing sense amps feed LDPC decoder in base die
idea: Box: shrunk 2.5 fF cap x Si access x 3-reference soft sensing x HBM base-die decoder x bulk Si x standard. Each SA compares against three references and ships a 2-bit log-likelihood value; a rate-0.89 LDPC decoder in the logic base die corrects a 1% raw cell BER to <1e-15 (BSC capacity at p=0.01 is ~0.92).

title: Standardize a raw-tolerant DRAM grade with soft-bit interface
idea: Box: any cell x any access x soft-output SA x host-side decoding x any substrate x any fab. Push a JEDEC-style spec, backed by CHIPS-funded qualification, for 'RT-DRAM' rated at 1% raw BER that exposes soft bits and moves ECC into the host or CXL controller, so suppliers can sell relaxed dies interchangeably.
note: 1% raw BER needs heavy soft-decision ECC and adds latency; JEDEC adoption is slow.

title: Per-tier thin-film decoders replace 3D DRAM wordline staircases
idea: [Box: lateral 1T1C | IGZO lateral FET | conventional SA | monolithic 3D tiers | Si | same ALD IGZO forms a decoder in each tier] Build a tiny IGZO decoder at the array edge of every tier that listens to a shared vertical bundle of log2(N) tier-address lines plus one wordline-drive line, so N tiers need ~log2(N)+k vertical contacts instead of an N-step staircase.

title: N-type-only IGZO sense latches built inside every 3D tier
idea: [Box: lateral 1T1C | IGZO access | nMOS-only bootstrapped dynamic latch | monolithic BEOL tiers | Si | ALD IGZO] Rather than hauling every tier's bitline down to CMOS under the array, build a compact n-only cross-coupled latch (precharge-evaluate with bootstrap capacitors) from the same IGZO in each tier, sensing short local bitlines and driving amplified full-swing data onto a global line.

title: Array tiers on reclaimed or glass carriers, bonded to foundry periphery
idea: [Box: IGZO 1T1C/2T0C tiers | IGZO | standard SA | CMOS-bonded-array hybrid bond | reclaimed Si or glass carrier | DUV-only; periphery from U.S. 22-28 nm foundries] BEOL IGZO array tiers do not need single-crystal Si, so build them on cheap reclaimed or glass carrier wafers and hybrid-bond them to periphery wafers bought from existing U.S. 22-28 nm DUV foundries.
note: Supply-chain strategy: no prime wafers or EUV for array tiers; IGZO DRAM retention/speed still TRL 3-4.

title: Silicon-carbide access transistors make DRAM cells nearly non-leaking
idea: Box [MIM cap | 4H-SiC trench MOSFET (3.26 eV gap) | Si voltage SA | array-on-periphery hybrid bond | 200 mm SiC wafers from the EV supply chain | DUV litho]: build the cell array on SiC, where intrinsic carrier density is ~1e-8 cm-3 versus 1e10 for Si, so junction and GIDL leakage collapse, then bond it onto a Si periphery wafer.
note: SiC DRAM retention shown in the 1990s; dense SiC cells and interface traps are the doubt.

title: Maskless four-beam interference lithography for periodic DRAM cell arrays
idea: Box [honeycomb cap array | buried WL | voltage SA | standard | Si | immersion four-beam interference from a 266 nm solid-state laser + spacer doubling]: because the cell array is perfectly periodic, expose its holes and gratings with interfering beams (~46 nm half-pitch, no mask, no projection lens), halve the pitch with spacers, and trim array edges with a coarse LED block exposure.
note: Same maskless interference patterning of periodic arrays as I-05715.

title: Fluidic self-assembly of known-good DRAM micro-tiles onto wafer carriers
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x standard sensing x micro-tile assembly x 300 mm passive-RDL carrier x shape-keyed fluidic self-assembly. Tested 1-4 mm2 DRAM tiles (yield ~99% because tiny) are suspended in liquid and settle into keyed recesses on a carrier with fine-pitch RDL, building large memories with near-100% assembled yield and no pick-and-place.
note: Inter-tile interconnect density and bonding yield are the doubts.

title: Short segmented bitlines with local sense let 1.5 fF capacitors suffice
idea: Box: shallow capacitor charge (~1.5 fF) x standard access x hierarchical local sense amp every 32 cells placed under the array x 2D x Si x capacitor AR ~20. Cutting bitline length from 512-1024 cells to 32 lowers bitline capacitance ~20x, preserving the transfer ratio with a capacitor one third the size, so the capacitor module becomes a shallow single-etch step.
note: Hierarchical bitlines known; CMOS-under-array area for 32-cell SAs is the doubt.

title: Capacitive proximity coupling makes memory tiles reworkable, not bonded
idea: Box: 1T1C DRAM tile x standard access x charge-domain receiver x capacitive pads at 15 um pitch across a 1 um gap x spring-clamped Si carrier x no bump, no bond. Memory tiles are clamped face-down over the logic chip's pad field and talk through capacitive coupling, so a failing tile is unclipped and swapped instead of scrapping a $30k package.
note: Sun proximity communication heritage; power delivery and 1 um gap clamping are open.

title: Z-channel coding lets a one be stored at eighth charge
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: asymmetric reference near the empty level | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Because DRAM charge only leaks away (1->0), the sense reference sits just above empty with a small guard band and '1' is written at ~0.35 V; the rare 1->0 losses are fixed by a unidirectional Bose-Lin code needing ~half the check bits of symmetric BCH.

title: Redundant-residue in-DRAM arithmetic self-corrects low-voltage compute errors
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: bit-serial compute sense amps | integration: processing-in-memory subarrays | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Values are stored as residues modulo small coprime moduli plus two redundant moduli; sense-amp adders do multiply-accumulate in each residue channel independently at 0.4 V, and the redundant residues locate and correct a faulty channel.
note: RNS-based in-memory compute with redundant moduli; bit-serial SA arithmetic is slow.

title: Energy-grade DRAM bins sold against a contracted raw BER
idea: Box [medium: any | access: standard | sense: standard | integration: hyperscaler-owned host decoder | substrate: bulk | fab: existing fabs]. Fabs test each die for the lowest VARY/VPP that meets a contracted raw BER (e.g., 1e-5) instead of zero errors and sell it as an 'E-grade' part priced per pJ/access to buyers who run strong host codes.

title: JEDEC soft-information pins export per-read confidence to hosts
idea: Box [medium: any | access: standard | sense: sense amp with margin comparator | integration: standard DIMM | substrate: bulk | fab: existing]. A JEDEC standard adds one confidence bit per 8 data bits, set when the sense differential fell below a guard threshold, so host decoders treat low-confidence bits as erasures and arrays can run at much lower voltage.

title: Gen-8.5 display fabs print oxide gain-cell memory panels
idea: Box[Source=idle LCD fab x Medium=IGZO 2T0C gain cell x Substrate=2.2x2.5 m glass x Fab=TFT photolithography x Integration=diced tiles on CXL cold tier x Owner=panel-maker JV x Finance=hyperscaler prepay]: under-used display lines pattern ~1 um oxide gain cells across m2-scale glass, dice it into tiles and stack them as low-density but extremely cheap byte-addressable cold-tier memory.

title: Po: one capacitor, two opinions — coaxial nested-electrode two-bit pillar
idea: Po: a capacitor that holds two opinions. Extracted: build the pillar as a coaxial MIMIM (inner core, dielectric, middle tube, dielectric, outer shell); inner and outer capacitors are independent storage nodes reached by one transistor at the top and one buried at the pillar base.
note: Coaxial two-node pillar doubles bits; coupling and buried transistor are hard.

title: Po: one cell holds a byte — big analog cells on glass
idea: Po: a single cell holds a whole byte. Extracted: invert scaling: make cells ~400x larger at 250 nm nanoimprint rules on glass panels (area cost ~1/5,000 of silicon) so each ~10 fF node has kT/C noise ~0.6 mV and 256 charge levels (8 bits) fit in 1 V, read with time-to-digital ramp sensing and re-quantised on every refresh.
note: Glass area memory plus 8-bit analog cells; slow sensing and drift.

title: Sense-amp latch-time telemetry skips refresh for healthy rows
idea: Po: every read is a medical exam. A tiny time-to-digital converter on the local sense amps measures how fast each activated row resolves (faster = more charge left); rows with ample margin set a skip counter so their next one or two scheduled refreshes are dropped, and VRT cells are caught in the act.
note: Per-SA TDC area and resolution vs charge margin is the doubt; retention-aware refresh known (RAIDR), in-array sensing is the twist.

title: AlGaN/GaN polarization well storing floating 2DEG charge for days
idea: Po: the electron is locked in a polarization cage. Use a floating AlGaN/GaN island as the gate of a read transistor; the polarization-induced 2DEG well in 3.4 eV GaN holds electrons with negligible thermal generation for days, written through a thin AlN tunnel barrier.
note: Tunnel-barrier writes raise endurance and speed doubts versus DRAM-class needs.

title: Multi-fab tier sourcing: thin tier wafers from mature U.S. fabs
idea: Po: every tier comes from a different factory. Define an open 10 um-thin 'tier wafer' standard (array plus local sense, standard bond grid, redundancy lanes) that any 28-40 nm U.S. fab can make; a stacking house hybrid-bonds 8-32 known-good tiers from different suppliers onto a base logic die with per-tier remap.
note: Stacking 28-40 nm tiers lowers capital but cost/bit stays above leading-edge DRAM.

title: Sixteen-cell micro-bitlines with per-tier oxide-TFT sense latches
idea: Po: every cell has a sense amp next door. In each oxide-semiconductor tier place a 4-TFT latch every 16 cells along the bitline so local bitline capacitance falls from ~60 fF to ~2 fF; latches drive a global bitline down to the base die.

title: Factory-programmed charge-trap back-gates permanently stiffen every tier
idea: Po: the transistor is told once, forever, to stay off. Give each tier's lateral access transistors a buried ONO charge-trap back-gate programmed once at final test to shift Vt by about +0.8 V, cutting subthreshold leakage ~1e8x while a boosted front gate restores on-current; no negative wordline generator is needed.

title: Witness cells per row enable decay-aware differential sensing
idea: Po: the bit knows how old it is. Store each row as differential 2T2C pairs inside the same vertical pillar so both halves leak almost equally (common mode), plus two witness cells written with known 1 and 0 at the same moment; at read the sense threshold is set from the witnesses, so data stays readable after 90% of the charge has leaked.
note: Tail leakage is random per cell, so pairs rarely leak equally; gain likely below claimed 10-30x.

title: Laser-seeded single-grain channels erase the leakage tail
idea: Po: every transistor is carved from a perfect crystal. In each 3D tier, crystallize the access channel from amorphous Si by location-controlled excimer-laser growth from a seed hole (micro-Czochralski) so every channel is one grain; grain-boundary trap-assisted tunnelling, the main source of the fA tail in polycrystalline tiers, disappears.

title: Po crucible made of ice: cold-copper skull-melt Czochralski silicon
idea: Po: 'the crucible is made of ice.' Extracted: pull 300 mm CZ ingots from a melt held in a water-cooled segmented copper crucible, where induction heating levitates and stirs the melt and a frozen silicon skull is the only wall contact, so no high-purity quartz crucible is consumed and no oxygen dissolves from silica walls; a cusp magnetic field damps convection for radial dopant uniformity.
note: 300 mm skull-melt growth stability is unproven; melt power ~2-3x.

title: Po memory sold by the square meter: DRAM tiles on display glass
idea: Po: 'memory is sold by the square meter like carpet.' Extracted: run oxide-TFT gain-cell arrays on Gen-8.5 (2.2 x 2.5 m) display glass in under-used LCD fabs, then cut the panel into memory tiles mounted beside processors. One panel has ~80x the area of a 300 mm wafer and uses no single-crystal silicon, no quartz crucible and no EUV.
note: Oxide-TFT gain cells on Gen-8.5 glass; micron-scale pitch gives low density and slow long lines.

title: Random cell placement mapped after fabrication by on-die address table
idea: Po: lithography happens after the chip is finished. Form cells by mask-free stochastic self-assembly (e.g., nanowire forests at random positions under a coarse word/bit grid), then at wafer sort electrically discover which crossings form working cells and burn a per-die logical-to-physical map into an on-die translation table, an FTL for geometry.

title: Single grayscale exposure carves the entire 3D DRAM staircase
idea: Po: one exposure makes every layer. A multi-tone grayscale mask and a linear-contrast resist print a ramp of resist heights in one shot, and a proportional-selectivity etch transfers it into all 26-100 tier landing steps at once instead of dozens of trim-etch cycles.
note: Resist-height control below 1% needed to land on each of 100 tiers.

title: Voltage-stacked HBM recycling one current through every die
idea: Po: every die stands on a different ground. Wire the 8-16 dies' supplies in series (die k between kV and (k+1)V), feed the stack at ~12 V, and use small on-die switched-capacitor balancers plus level-shifted signalling so the same current flows through all dies.
note: Series-stacked die supplies; DRAM bursty current mismatch stresses balancers.

title: Silicon interband tunnel-diode latch cell needing no refresh
idea: Worsen: make the cell need constant topping-up at 1 V or more. Flip: tie the storage node to a pair of series Si/SiGe resonant interband tunnel diodes whose negative differential resistance creates two stable node voltages, so the cell self-latches at ~0.3 V with pA standby current (tunneling SRAM revived with CMOS-compatible diodes).
note: Tunneling SRAM shown in III-V and Si RITD; diode uniformity at density is hard.

title: Shadow-latch cell that hands its bit to a nonvolatile twin
idea: Worsen: keep refreshing billions of idle bits all night. Flip: pair each DRAM cell group with a tiny ferroelectric tunnel-junction shadow element; when a bank goes idle its bits are copied into the shadows in one burst, refresh stops, and the bits are restored on wake.
