note: Same copy-to-ferroelectric idle parking.

title: Esaki-diode bistable cells restored by one global plate pulse
idea: Worse: refresh by activating 8 KB rows one at a time through sense amps. Flip: add a vertical tunnel-diode pair on each storage node to create an NDR latch with two stable voltages, then periodically pulse the shared cell plate so every cell in a mat snaps back to its own stable point at once, with no sensing or row activation.
note: Si Esaki valley current sets standby power; TSRAM precedent.

title: 4H-SiC access-transistor arrays built in U.S. SiC power fabs
idea: Worse at 125 C: use silicon, whose intrinsic carrier density explodes with temperature. Flip: build the access transistor and a trench capacitor in 4H-SiC (n_i ~1e-5 cm^-3 at 125 C versus ~1e12 for Si) using under-used U.S. SiC power-device fab tooling, bonded to a Si periphery wafer.

title: Ga2O3 write transistor stacked over silicon read transistor
idea: Worse at 125 C: rely on IGZO, whose oxygen vacancies and hydrogen drift Vt when hot. Flip: a 2T gain cell with a laser-crystallized beta-Ga2O3 write device (4.8 eV gap, stable lattice) above a Si read FET, so the storage node sees a wide-gap off state while reads stay fast and non-destructive.

title: Two-transistor analog charge integrators count activations per wordline
idea: Worse: let rows be hammered with zero memory of past activations. Flip: every local wordline driver deposits a fixed charge packet on a per-row leaky MOS integrator at each activation; a shared comparator in the driver strip samples it on activation and fires neighbor refresh when it crosses threshold, while the leak resets it naturally each window.

title: Talbot interference lithography for perfectly periodic array layers
idea: Worse: run a $200M single-source EUV scanner to print what is just a periodic grating. Flip: print the array's hole and line layers with achromatic Talbot or multi-beam immersion interference exposure, whose 'mask' is a cheap grating, and keep DUV only for aperiodic cut and periphery layers.

title: Grounded shield tiers between wordline tiers stop row hammer
idea: Worse: place aggressor wordlines nanometers from victim storage nodes with nothing in between. Flip: insert a thin grounded conductive shield plane between adjacent wordline tiers (one extra deposition per tier pair) that terminates the aggressor field and blocks trap-assisted charge migration between tiers.

title: In-stack gain tiers segment vertical bitlines every 32 tiers
idea: Worse: hang 300 tiers of cells on one vertical bitline so its capacitance buries the signal and forces a sense amp per short column. Flip: insert a 'gain tier' every 32 tiers containing a local charge-to-current amplifier and a segment switch on each vertical bitline, so a 1-2 fF cell sees only its 32-tier segment and one base sense amp serves the whole column.
note: Local gain stages per bitline segment, same family as dendritic preamps.

title: Hot-wall batch epitaxy grows a hundred superlattice wafers per run
idea: Worse: grow 200-period Si/SiGe stacks one wafer at a time for hours in single-wafer RPCVD. Flip: grow the superlattice in a hot-wall UHV-CVD/LPCVD batch furnace holding ~100 wafers, using fast gas-pulse switching for abrupt interfaces and in-situ X-ray reflectometry on a witness wafer.

title: Open-hardware process chambers built by U.S. machine shops
idea: Worse: depend on a handful of tool vendors with 18-month lead times. Flip: fund open-source reference designs for ALD, etch and furnace modules with standard SEMI interfaces and open controllers. A national lab qualifies each once; regional machine shops then build and service them, like certified aircraft parts.
note: Open ALD tool demo feasible; matching vendor performance is the doubt.

title: Idle Gen-8.5 display fabs make glass-panel memory
idea: Worse: limit DRAM to round 300 mm wafers while LCD fabs sit idle. Flip: convert surplus Gen-8.5 display lines (2.2x2.5 m glass, ~70x a wafer's area) to make oxide-TFT gain-cell memory panels with their existing steppers and sputter/PECVD tools, then dice them into tiles for capacity-tier modules.

title: Optical-multicast KV prefix CDN inside the rack
idea: Worsen: let every GPU hold its own KV copy of the same system prompt and RAG documents. Flip: a rack memory node stores each shared prefix's KV once and streams it to subscribing GPUs over an optical broadcast star, so GPUs keep only per-request suffix KV.

title: Socketed HBM-class modules that outlive three GPU generations
idea: Worsen: solder memory to the GPU so it is scrapped whenever compute retires after 3-4 years. Flip: mount HBM stacks on a compression-mount, fine-pitch land-grid module beside the processor on a glass substrate, so memory is reused across accelerator generations and later redeployed into CXL expanders.
note: Needs fan-out to socketable pitch; HBM wear-out after years hot.

title: Maskless e-beam via-ROM dies hold frozen model weights
idea: Worsen: keep read-only inference weights in refresh-hungry DRAM. Flip: make generic ROM wafers on a mature node where one via layer encodes the bits (multi-size vias for 2 bits/cell), and write that layer per model with multi-beam e-beam direct-write, so a weight die needs no capacitor, no refresh and no custom mask.

title: Soft-decision sense amps feed LDPC, accepting 40% smaller capacitors
idea: Worse: force every sense amp to make a hard 0/1 call and throw away how close the call was. Flip: add a second offset-biased latch per sense-amp group that outputs a 1-bit confidence flag with each bit, and run a soft-decision LDPC code in the controller (as NAND does), which corrects far more raw errors per parity bit than hard BCH.
note: Soft info relaxes Cs; LDPC latency on the DRAM read path is the doubt.

title: Analog charge accumulator per row counts activations without SRAM
idea: Worse: track hammering with large SRAM counter tables in the periphery. Flip: give each row one extra MOS capacitor (pure Si) that receives a fixed charge packet on every activation and leaks slowly; when its voltage crosses a threshold the neighbors are refreshed and the accumulator resets.

title: Electric eel's stacked cells: voltage-stacked subarrays reuse one charge
idea: An electric eel stacks thousands of low-voltage cells in series. Four subarrays sit in a series voltage stack across a 2.2 V rail, each in its own 0.55 V domain, so charge one subarray draws while sensing flows on as the next one's supply; a small push-pull regulator balances mismatched activity.

title: Ski patrol's avalanche trigger: feedback-FET access switch
idea: Ski patrol releases a whole avalanche with one small charge. The access device is a gated p-i-n-i-n feedback FET whose intrinsic regions are electrostatically doped by the gate; past threshold, injected carriers collapse the internal barriers by positive feedback, giving <1 mV/dec switching at ~0.5 V and a hard barrier when off.
note: Feedback FETs are themselves latching 1T-DRAM cells; clean release as access switch is the doubt.

title: Postal carrier rings one doorbell: BEOL TFT micro-wordline drivers
idea: A postal carrier rings one doorbell, not the whole building. Oxide-TFT micro-wordline drivers are stacked in the back end over the array, one per 16-cell wordline segment, AND-ing a global row line with a column-group line, so an access charges only 16 cells' gates and swings only 16 bitlines.
note: Oxide-TFT drive speed for ns wordlines is a doubt.

title: Embargoed Soviet engineer prints arrays with mask-free laser interference
idea: With no EUV and no mask shop, the Soviet engineer treats the array as a crystal lattice. A 4-beam 193 nm immersion interference exposure prints the whole field's periodic hole and line grid without a mask, spacer doubling takes it to ~20 nm pitch, and one coarse KrF trim mask cuts mats and edges.
note: Overlay/registration of maskless interference to prior layers is the key doubt.

title: Glassblower makes crucibles from polysilicon plants' waste chloride
idea: Persona: a fiber-optic glassblower. Flame-hydrolyze silicon tetrachloride, the unavoidable byproduct of U.S. Siemens polysilicon plants, onto a rotating graphite mandrel (the outside-vapor-deposition method used for fiber). Sinter the 99.9999% synthetic silica soot into crucibles with an Al-doped outer layer for creep stiffness.

title: 2050 engineer: rutile titania on tin-oxide electrodes, no hafnium
idea: Persona: a 2050 engineer who sees Hf, Zr and Ru as a passing habit. Grow rutile-phase TiO2 (k ~90-110) below 400 C on an antimony-doped SnO2 bottom electrode, whose rutile structure templates the high-k phase. Add 2 nm Al-doped interlayers to suppress leakage.
note: Rutile templating works, but TiO2's ~3 eV gap gives high leakage, the reason industry chose ZrO2.

title: Monk's discipline: three-mask memory tier with spacer-defined vertical TFTs
idea: A monk keeps only what is necessary. Build each tier with three coarse masks: vertical oxide TFTs whose channel length equals a deposited film thickness (~20 nm) on the sidewall of a stepped dielectric, with gate and storage node formed by conformal ALD around the step, so 1 um-class lithography yields 20 nm-class devices at <=350 C.

title: Write-once-per-session charge-trap cells for append-only AI KV caches
idea: KV caches are appended once per token, read thousands of times and discarded at session end, so each location sees ~1e4-1e6 writes per lifetime, not 1e15. Bits are electrons in a thin SiN/Al2O3 trap layer programmed by 50-100 ns channel-hot-electron pulses, bulk-erased per page at session end and read non-destructively by threshold sensing.
note: CHE programming energy and threshold-sense latency may miss DRAM-class speed.

title: Self-gated keeper turns charge cell static for polar-night weather stations
idea: Arctic stations sleep for months on stored energy; one implant mask forms a tiny vertical keeper transistor along each storage-node sidewall, gated by the node itself and fed from a VDD-biased diffusion shared by neighbors, so a '1' weakly turns on its keeper and tops itself up while a '0' stays off. Leakage-ratio bistability, as in loadless 4T SRAM, replaces refresh.
note: Loadless-4T style leakage-ratio bistability; keeper current window vs leakage tail is the doubt.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain walls repurpose U.S. lithium niobate photonics fabs
idea: Telecom photonics users already run thin-film lithium niobate lines; one mask adds electrode pairs on LNOI so writing a domain creates a charged, conductive domain wall between them, read non-destructively by its 1e3-1e5 current contrast without switching polarization.
note: Reuses LNOI lines; sub-50 nm wall reliability unknown.

title: CubeSat COTS mindset: half-charge capacitors in short 30:1 pillars
idea: CubeSats fly cheap commercial parts and absorb upsets in software. Size the cell capacitor for a 1% raw-BER sense margin (~2-2.5 fF) instead of ~5 fF, so pillar aspect ratio drops from ~65:1 to ~30:1 with standard high-k.
note: 1% raw BER needs heavy ECC; noise margin doubt.

title: Image-sensor column ADCs with CDS read two bits per cell
idea: Copy 50-megapixel phone sensors that digitize 1-electron-noise columns in parallel: every bitline pair gets a single-slope ADC sharing one global ramp, with correlated double sampling (sample at precharge, again after charge share) to cancel kTC noise and SA offset. Cells store four charge levels for 2 bits/cell.
note: CDS removes offset, but cell Cs and leakage spread still squeeze the four levels.

title: Charge-domain popcount on sense stripes prefilters KV-cache tokens
idea: Store 64-bit locality-sensitive-hash signatures of keys; after sensing, each SA XNORs its bit with a broadcast query bit and dumps a unit charge onto a mat-level summing capacitor, whose voltage (Hamming similarity) one ADC per mat reads. Only top-scoring tokens' full keys leave the chip.

title: Grating-maker method: solid-state deep-UV interference lithography for arrays
idea: Makers of astronomical diffraction gratings print meter-scale periodic lines by interfering laser beams, with no mask; use a frequency-quintupled Nd:YAG (213 nm) or solid-state 193 nm laser, built on nonlinear crystals with no argon-fluoride or neon gas, in two-beam and four-beam interference to print the array's line and hole lattices at ~40 nm pitch. Spacer pitch-splitting then reaches ~20 nm.
note: 40 nm pitch is below the 213/193 nm two-beam interference limit; needs pitch-splitting from ~70-100 nm; throughput doubtful.

title: RFID fluidic self-assembly: shaped DRAM tiles settle into logic sockets
idea: Five-cent RFID tags place millions of chips by letting shaped dies settle into matching wells in a liquid flow; dice DRAM arrays into 0.5 mm trapezoidal tiles, flow them over a logic wafer with matching recesses and hydrophilic capillary pads, then hybrid-bond in nitrogen. Logic wafers get stacked memory at wafer throughput with no pick-and-place and no argon plasma activation.

title: Training activation-stash memory: 100 ms retention, no high-k capacitor
idea: AI training stashes activations for only ~10-500 ms between forward and backward passes, an extreme user that never needs 64 ms-class retention. Build a dedicated stash DRAM with planar or shallow-trench SiO2/SiN capacitors (~0.5 fF) sized so data turnover beats worst-case retention, plus a deadline-tracking controller that refreshes only pages older than their budget.
note: 0.5 fF sensing margin is the doubt; data-lifetime refresh ideas known.

title: Astronomy CCD shift-register memory for streaming KV-cache reads
idea: Astronomers' CCDs move charge packets with >99.9999% transfer efficiency using only polysilicon gates over oxide, with no per-cell contacts or metal capacitors. KV-cache reads are long sequential streams, so build CCD loop memories with sense amps every few thousand stages, ~4F2 cells, and refresh by circulation.
note: 1970s CCD memories lost to DRAM; transfer speed and charge at nm scale are the doubt.

title: Aircraft anodizing tank grows billions of capacitor molds without lithography
idea: Aerospace anodizing self-organizes aluminum into hexagonal nanopore arrays with AR >1000:1 using only Al, acid and volts. Sputter Al on the wafer, nanoimprint a pre-texture that registers pores to the access-transistor grid, two-step anodize to 40-60 nm pitch, then ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN inside the pores.
note: AAO nanocapacitors known; registration of pores to the access grid at 40 nm pitch and defect density are the doubts.

title: Gen-8.6 display-glass oxide-TFT DRAM for capacity-hungry AI tiers
idea: Extreme user: AI clusters that need petabytes of warm memory and tolerate relaxed density. Build IGZO-TFT 1T1C arrays on 2.2x2.5 m display glass in idle Gen-8.6 LCD/OLED fabs (each panel ~70x a 300 mm wafer area) with the sense amps on attached silicon chiplets.

title: Micro-transfer-printed DRAM tiles onto logic replace TSV stacking
idea: Extreme user: flexible wearables built by elastomer-stamp transfer printing. Release thin DRAM tiles by undercutting a sacrificial layer, pick thousands at once with a PDMS stamp and print them face-up onto logic wafers, then connect them with a thin-film redistribution layer.

title: Mars-rover microspring sockets make HBM stacks field-replaceable
idea: Planetary hardware survives -120/+20 C cycling with compliant interconnect. Attach each HBM stack to the interposer through lithographic MEMS microsprings at 20-40 um pitch, clamped by a frame lid instead of soldered microbumps, so a stack that fails final test or dies in the field is swapped rather than scrapping the GPU module.
note: Microsprings exist; signal integrity at HBM rates and 20 um pitch unproven.

title: Stadium-broadcast optical star coupler shares weights across 64 accelerators
idea: Broadcast TV sends one stream to millions of receivers. Keep one copy of model weights in a shared memory appliance whose optical output is split by a passive star coupler to 64 accelerators at once; each GPU's HBM holds only KV cache and activations while layers stream in lockstep.
note: Resembles weight streaming; 64-way passive split loss and lockstep scheduling are the doubts.

title: Phone-PMIC embedded die: DRAM inside the substrate under GPU
idea: Phones embed PMICs and passives inside the PCB core to save height. Embed thinned DRAM dies in cavities of the accelerator's organic substrate directly beneath the GPU, connected by laser-drilled microvias to the GPU's bottom bumps.
note: GPU underside is mostly power delivery; thermal and PDN conflict.

title: GaN-on-diamond radar trick: diamond interlayers enable 32-high stacks
idea: Military radars bond GaN to CVD diamond to dump extreme heat flux. Insert 20-50 um CVD-diamond spreader layers every four DRAM dies, with laser-cut windows for TSVs, carrying heat sideways to a side-wall cold plate.

title: Quantum erasure conversion: sense amps flag low-margin bits as erasures
idea: Neutral-atom quantum computers convert errors into erasures at known locations. Borrow that by adding a second, offset-threshold comparator to each sense amp, so any bit whose bitline differential falls below ~40 mV is flagged 'uncertain' and sent to the controller as a per-burst erasure mask on an extra pin. The controller runs erasure-aware Reed-Solomon decoding, which corrects about twice as many erasures as unknown errors for the same parity.

title: Let cells decay: soft-decision LDPC reads stretched-refresh charge
idea: Time shift: deliberately run refresh at 1-2 s and treat retention loss as a noisy channel; sense amplifiers add a second offset reference so each read also returns a 'weak' flag, and an on-die LDPC decoder uses those soft bits to correct 1e-4-class decay errors, scrubbing rows whose weak-flag count rises.
note: Soft-decision sensing adds NAND playbook; decoder latency and second-reference read cost are doubts.

title: Dual-timescale back-gate: deep negative bias only during idle seconds
idea: Time shift between access bursts (ns) and idle stretches (s): build the array on thin-BOX SOI with a per-bank back-gate plane held near 0 V during bursts for strong on-current, then pumped to about -2 V after ~10 us idle, raising access-transistor Vt ~200-300 mV and cutting subthreshold leakage ~100x.
note: Deep back-bias cuts subthreshold but raises GIDL, which dominates the tail.

title: ZnON back-end access tier stacked over the periphery
idea: Scale shift from front-end silicon to the back end of line: build access transistors in zinc oxynitride (Zn, O, N; no In or Ga) at <=400 C directly above the CMOS sense amplifiers and stack 4-8 tiers; the wide bandgap and absence of hole conduction give ~1e-18 A/um off-current while ~50-100 cm^2/Vs mobility keeps ns access.

title: Image-sensor pinned-photodiode storage: hold the bit like a dark pixel
idea: Scale and time shift from CMOS image sensors, whose pinned photodiodes hold charge 10-100 ms at ~1 e-/s dark current: store each bit as a charge packet in a fully depleted buried n-well capped by a p+ pinning layer, moved by a transfer gate onto a floating-diffusion gain node for sensing, so the pinned surface removes the interface generation that dominates DRAM leakage.
note: Same pinned-storage concept; minutes retention claim ignores transfer-gate leakage.

title: JEDEC refresh-free mode with certified retention window
idea: Scale jump to the industry: a JEDEC mode-register bit disables refresh entirely and advertises a vendor-certified retention window (for example 2 s at 85 C) proven at qualification, and OSes and AI runtimes get a standard malloc_ttl API to place only data whose idle time fits.
note: Si DRAM retention tail cannot certify 2 s at 85 C without profiling/ECC; fits IGZO cells.

title: Tier-wide back-gate plane flips cells between sprint and hibernate modes
idea: Time-multiplex the transistor threshold: each thin-film tier sits on its own buried back-gate plate, biased toward low Vt during active windows (ns to us) and swung negative during idle (seconds) to raise Vt by ~0.4 V, which cuts subthreshold leakage by ~10^4 and stretches refresh from 64 ms to seconds. It needs one plate per tier and no wiring per cell.

title: Maskless wafer-flash interference lattice with a coarse cut mask
idea: Expose the entire wafer's capacitor-hole lattice in one flash with three-beam 193 nm laser interference (hexagonal pattern, no mask, no projection lens), reach final pitch by self-aligned pitch splitting, and erase the lattice outside the arrays with a cheap KrF keep/cut mask.

title: Second-life HBM: laser-debond retired stacks into CXL memory cards
idea: Stretch the stack's timescale from a 3-year accelerator life to 10 years: retired accelerators have their HBM laser-debonded, re-bumped and mounted on a cheap organic carrier beside a small CXL controller ASIC that speaks the HBM PHY. Each card becomes a 100+ GB pooled memory device.

title: Passive silicon interposer becomes a trench-capacitor memory layer
idea: Exploit the scale of an otherwise idle ~2500 mm2 65 nm silicon interposer: etch deep-trench capacitors and simple access transistors into its unused area to form ~0.5-1 GB of eDRAM microns from the logic. It acts as a giant page buffer between HBM and compute.

title: Row-scale LDPC: decode the whole 8 KB activated row at once
idea: Shift the ECC codeword from 64 bits to the 64 Kb row that activation already drags out: a rate-0.85 LDPC code spans each row and a pipeline in the base die decodes it as the row lands in the buffer. A 1% raw cell BER drops below 1e-15 with ~15% parity (BSC capacity at 1% is 0.92).
note: Rate-0.85 near capacity at 1% BER needs long iterative decode; partial writes force row parity updates.

title: Z-RAM revived: SiGe quantum-well hole trap on bulk silicon
idea: Z-RAM died because holes stored in an SOI floating body leaked out through the junctions within milliseconds, and SOI wafers cost too much. Bury a 5-8 nm Si0.6Ge0.4 layer under a bulk vertical channel: its ~0.3-0.4 eV valence-band offset forms a hole well that keeps stored holes away from junction fields, and a p+ counter-doped floor isolates the body with no SOI.
note: Same SiGe hole-well capacitorless cell, bulk planar variant.

title: NRAM with exactly one nanotube junction per cell via DNA origami
idea: Nantero NRAM stalled on random CNT fabrics: a variable number of tube junctions per cell spread the switching distribution, and the feedstock needed costly purification. Use DNA-origami templates anchored in lithographic binding sites to place exactly two crossed CNTs per cell (chirality purity is irrelevant because switching is electromechanical), then strip the DNA with an O2 plasma.
note: DNA origami CNT crossing shown (2010); placement yield and plasma damage at wafer scale are risks.

title: Racetrack without current: VCMA peristaltic domain-wall pumping
idea: IBM's racetrack stalled because moving domain walls needed ~1e7-1e8 A/cm2 and walls pinned randomly. Lay three-phase gate electrodes along a short 16-bit CoFeB/MgO track: sequential voltage-controlled anisotropy waves, a local electrostatic version of bubble memory's rotating field, push every wall one notch per clock with no current through the track.
note: Voltage-driven DW pumping cuts shift energy; VCMA coefficients may be too weak to depin walls reliably.

title: STT-MRAM write current cut by orbital torque from light metals
idea: STT-MRAM's bid to replace DRAM (Hynix/Toshiba, Spin Memory) died because the write current needed a big access transistor and broke down the MgO. Drive the free layer with orbital-Hall torque from a Cr or oxidized-Cu underlayer, converted to spin at a thin Ni interface; orbital Hall conductivity can exceed Pt's without Pt or tungsten.
note: Orbital Hall is hot research; SOT three-terminal cell undermines claimed 10-15F2.

title: NRAM's van der Waals idea, crystallized: sliding-ferroelectric bilayer bit
idea: NRAM's insight, a nanoscale state latched by van der Waals energy far above kT, was undone by random CNT fabrics. Keep the vdW latch but make it crystalline: a rhombohedral-stacked bilayer h-BN or 3R-MoS2 whose out-of-plane polarization flips when the layers slide by one bond length under a gate field, a lattice-locked stacking state that holds above 125 C.
note: Same rhombohedral bilayer sliding bit.

title: Z-RAM revival: SiGe hole well keeps floating-body charge
idea: Innovative Silicon's Z-RAM died because holes stored in the floating body recombined at the source/drain junctions, and GIDL ate the sense margin as bodies shrank. Grow a 5 nm strained Si0.7Ge0.3 quantum well inside the fully depleted body under a Si cap. Holes then sit in a valence-band pocket ~0.25 eV deep, away from the high-field junction corners where they used to recombine.

title: SESO memory reborn on 2 nm single-crystal silicon nanosheets
idea: Hitachi's SESO used ~3 nm polysilicon channels: quantum confinement widened the bandgap and cut leakage to ~1e-19 A, but grain boundaries made devices variable and slow. Thin single-crystal SOI nanosheets to 2 nm with self-limiting low-temperature plasma oxidation, which raises the effective gap to ~1.6-1.8 eV. Raised epitaxial source/drain recovers the on-current.

title: CCD memory's junctionless charge wells as refresh-light storage
idea: CCD memories (Fairchild, Intel 2416) lost to DRAM on random access, but their charge sat in potential wells under gates, with no source/drain junction. Store each bit in a buried-channel well under a gate and clock it through a short 4-8 cell chain to a shared sense node. The storage node then has no p-n junction and no GIDL edge, and its only leakage is thermal generation in a fully depleted buried channel.

title: ThruChip inductive links tucked under the sense-amp stripe
idea: Failure mined: Keio's ThruChip inductive coupling and Samsung's Wide I/O both died, coils on area cost and TSVs on yield cost. Fix: lay the coupling coils in spare top metal directly over sense-amp stripes and arrays, beat crosstalk with code-division multiplexing among neighboring coils, and receive with sense-amp-style clocked latches. Data then crosses 8-12 thinned dies with no signal TSVs, only power vias.
note: Coils over sensitive bitlines risk coupling noise into the array.

title: Temperature-proofed T-RAM: vertical thyristor pillars with PTAT-tracked gate
idea: T-RAM (thyristor RAM) was dropped because its latch hold current and blocking voltage drifted strongly with temperature, causing standby leakage and fails at 85C. Build a 4F2 vertical p-n-p-n pillar with a gated base, driving the gate from an on-die PTAT (proportional-to-absolute-temperature) reference in each bank so latch current stays constant from -40 to 125C. Latched cells need no refresh and no capacitor.

title: Toshiba chain-FeRAM revived as vertical chains of antiferroelectric cells
idea: Toshiba's chain-FeRAM (each cell a transistor in parallel with a ferroelectric capacitor, cells in series like NAND) died with PZT's hydrogen damage and a 2D footprint. Build it vertically: a pillar of gate-all-around tiers, each shunting a thin antiferroelectric ZrO2 capacitor ring, with one contact per chain. To read a tier, its shunt turns off while the others stay on.
note: AFE ZrO2 chains cut contacts; endurance below DRAM-class unlimited is a doubt.

title: Core-memory coincident selection for 3D tier addressing without staircases
idea: Ferrite core memory died on hand-threading labor, but its coincident-current X-Y selection was elegant. Make each 3D DRAM access transistor dual-gated, one gate on a horizontal tier plane and one on a vertical pillar gate, so a cell turns on only when both are driven. N planes by M pillars then select any cell with N+M drivers instead of a staircase and decoder per tier.

title: Alien Technology's fluidic self-assembly for replaceable DRAM mat chiplets
idea: Alien Technology's fluidic self-assembly (FSA) of tiny dies into shaped wells failed commercially for RFID. Make DRAM as 0.5 mm 'mat chiplets' that self-assemble into receptor wells on a periphery wafer and attach with low-melt solder. Bad chiplets are melted out and replaced, and at end of life all chiplets are released in a hot bath for retest and reuse.

title: Self-assembly's defect killer made irrelevant by cell-level defect maps
idea: Directed self-assembly never met logic defect specs (<0.01/cm2). Accept raw lamellar block-copolymer line arrays with ~1% bad crossings; after fab a controller sweep writes a compressed per-array defect bitmap, and the memory controller skips bad sites through Bloom-filter lookups so the media never needs to be perfect.
note: Defect-tolerant crossbars (Teramac/HP) known; the cell itself is unspecified.

title: HP memristor's forming and selector killers fixed in a depreciated fab
idea: HP Labs' TiO2 memristor (The Machine) died on per-cell electroforming, variability and a separate selector, with no fab partner after the SK hynix deal lapsed. Use a self-rectifying Ta2O5/TaOx bilayer with a built-in series-resistor film so each deck is formed by one global flood pulse, and build 32 decks at 40 nm with dry 193 nm litho, 2 bits/cell, in a fully depreciated 300 mm fab.

title: Z-RAM, fixed: floating-body cells for microsecond-lived activations only
idea: Z-RAM (Innovative Silicon) died because floating-body charge retention was too short and variable for 64 ms DRAM duty. Use capacitorless floating-body cells only for data whose lifetime is microseconds, such as pipelined activations between layers, so the retention spec drops ~1000x and no refresh logic is needed in a ~4F^2 SOI cell.

title: Optane App Direct, fixed: read-only weights served from NAND
idea: Optane persistent memory died partly on crash-consistency programming complexity and write wear. Sidestep both by exposing only immutable data: a CXL controller maps SLC NAND as read-only load/store memory, caches 256 B sectors in the NAND dies' own page-buffer latches, and serves model weights and embedding tables with no DRAM buffer.
note: Like XL-Flash/CMM-H; microsecond NAND latency makes load/store stalls painful.

title: Sun Proximity Communication fixed by capillary self-alignment and electronic pad steering
idea: Sun's capacitive face-to-face proximity communication died because overlapping chips needed micron-level alignment and gap control that packaging could not hold. Place DRAM tiles over logic tiles by water-droplet capillary self-assembly (hydrophilic landing sites give <1 um placement), set the gap with oxide standoffs, and oversample each signal with a 3x3 cluster of transmit micro-pads from which the receiver picks the best-aligned one at boot: no solder, no TSVs, reworkable tiles.

title: KryoTech fixed: hermetic Peltier-cooled DRAM tile trades refresh for density
idea: KryoTech's sub-ambient PC cooling (1990s) died on condensation and compressor cost. Cool only the low-power DRAM stack (a few W) to ~20 C with a thin-film thermoelectric inside a hermetically sealed dry-nitrogen package cavity while the logic stays at 85-100 C. Retention roughly doubles every ~10 C, so the tens-of-times longer retention can be spent on less refresh or a 30-40% smaller storage capacitor.
note: Peltier COP next to 85-100 C logic is poor; capacitor-relaxation spin is interesting.

title: X-Celeprint transfer printing failed in displays; print DRAM dielets onto logic
idea: Micro-transfer printing (X-Celeprint/X Display) stalled because displays needed millions of microLEDs placed at six-sigma yield. Memory needs only tens to hundreds of large dielets per wafer: undercut-release 5-10 um thick DRAM dielets, pick them in parallel with PDMS stamps onto a logic wafer, and connect them with one lithographic Cu/Al redistribution layer over the planarized surface, with no bumps, solder or TSVs.

title: RAIDR's VRT killer exposed by accelerated trap-toggle burn-in screening
idea: Multi-rate refresh (RAIDR) died because Variable Retention Time cells jump between strong and weak bins after profiling. Fix exactly that at test: a burn-in recipe alternating high temperature, negative-wordline and GIDL-stress phases forces trap occupancy to toggle hundreds of times in minutes, so VRT-prone cells reveal themselves and are fused to spare rows before binning.

title: Nantero NRAM's random-fabric variability replaced by crossed aligned nanotube bilayers
idea: Nantero's NRAM spent two decades unshipped at scale partly because spin-coated random CNT fabric gave cell-to-cell differences in junction count and switching. Fix: deposit two layers of pre-aligned, sorted nanotubes crossed at 90 degrees (Langmuir-Schaefer or floating evaporative assembly) so every cell contains the same number of tube-tube junctions.

title: LNG regasification cold runs a 77 K refresh-free memory tier
idea: Effect: thermally activated junction and GIDL leakage collapse at 77 K, stretching DRAM retention from 64 ms to hours. Build cryo-memory pods at LNG import terminals, where regasification throws away ~830 kJ of cold per kg, and cool commodity DRAM with liquid-nitrogen loops (never helium) at re-centered voltages.

title: Repeated smart-cut transfers stack single-crystal transistor tiers with donor reuse
idea: Effect: hydrogen-platelet exfoliation. Implanted H forms a cleave plane, so 100-200 nm single-crystal Si layers are bonded and split one at a time onto a cold DRAM wafer; each tier's lateral access transistors are patterned before the next bond. Donor wafers are re-polished and reused 10+ times.

title: Moire magnification: printed interference marks enable nanometer roll-to-roll overlay
idea: Print paired gratings of slightly different pitch on each layer of an R2R interposer; their Moire fringes magnify misalignment 100-1000x and cameras feed real-time web registration actuators, enabling 1-2 um lines with ~100 nm overlay.

title: Negative wordline undershoot sweeps hammer-injected electrons back
idea: Effect: minority-carrier drift and recombination. Part of row hammer is electrons injected from the aggressor's inverted channel diffusing to the victim storage node; right after precharge, the aggressor wordline gets a ~2 ns negative undershoot that accumulates holes under the gate and recombines or drifts the injected electron cloud back before it reaches the victim. Only the wordline driver waveform changes.
note: Negative wordline bias already standard; undershoot pulse twist, gain likely below 5x.

title: N: boron-alloyed AlN ferroelectric replaces the 70:1 capacitor pillar
idea: Use sputtered Al(1-x)B(x)N (no scandium), whose remanent polarization ~100-130 uC/cm2 is ~15-20x the charge density a linear DRAM dielectric holds at 1 V; a planar 40x40 nm capacitor switches ~3-4 fC, close to a 70:1 pillar's 5 fC, sensed as in 1T1C FeRAM.
note: High coercive field and fatigue are the barriers.

title: Zn: indium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cell stores three bits per node
idea: Use a ZnSnO (no In, no Ga) two-transistor gain cell whose ultralow off-current holds 8 charge levels on the read-transistor gate; level spacing is squeezed until ~1% of symbols land one level off, which a Gray-coded soft-decision LDPC per row corrects.
note: Indium-free 8-level gain cell with LDPC; ZTO off-current and level drift are key unknowns.

title: Si: JEDEC AI-grade memory class admitting 1% raw cell errors
idea: Define a JEDEC grade for AI weights and KV cache in which devices may ship with up to 1% raw cell BER, the controller carries a standardized LDPC/erasure layer, and buyers get a guaranteed post-correction error rate; DRAM dies now scrapped or down-binned for weak cells, and every leaky or low-margin new cell, become sellable.

title: Gallium-oxide access transistor exploits self-trapped holes to kill GIDL
idea: Ga: use a beta-Ga2O3 (4.8 eV) channel for the access FET; holes generated by band-to-band tunnelling at the drain edge self-trap as immobile polarons, so they cannot carry GIDL current or charge a floating body, and the n-only material has no hole conduction path.

title: Anodic alumina self-ordered pores template vertical gate-all-around access pillars
idea: Al: anodize a deposited aluminum film so it self-organizes into hexagonal nanopores (pitch 25-100 nm, set by anodizing voltage), guided by a coarse DUV pre-pattern, and use the pores as a mold or hard mask for vertical channel pillars wrapped by a gate.

title: Indium-free zinc-tin-oxide access transistors stacked as relaxed-pitch tiers
idea: Zn: use amorphous ZnSnO, made of abundant zinc and tin, as the access-transistor channel in BEOL tiers patterned by ArF immersion at F~20-30 nm; ZTO off-current ~1e-19 A/um gives seconds-to-minutes retention, so each tier uses a small planar capacitor and density comes from 8-16 tiers instead of EUV shrink.

title: Dual-mode Hf-Zr-O capacitor parks idle data as polarization, stopping refresh
idea: Hf: make the storage dielectric an HfZrO stack that behaves as a linear dielectric at DRAM bias but switches ferroelectrically under a higher 'park' voltage; when a page goes idle, the controller writes its data as remanent polarization (no refresh), and on wake restores it to charge mode, using the larger capacitor area a DUV-only cell affords for ample switched charge.

title: Silicon carbide vertical 4F2 cells for near-refresh-free retention
idea: Build vertical-channel 4F2 cells in 4H-SiC (3.3 eV gap) on the 200 mm SiC wafer base scaled for EV power devices: implanted buried n+ bitlines, trench gate-all-around channels and a stacked capacitor on top, where intrinsic carrier density ~1e-9 cm^-3 suppresses junction and GIDL leakage by >1e8 vs Si.
note: Purdue showed long-retention SiC DRAM in 1990s; SiC MOS interface and wafer defects hurt dense 4F2.

title: Germanium-free 3D DRAM tiers by doping-selective electrochemical etch
idea: Periodic-table walk, P (15): grow a 30-100-tier all-silicon superlattice of n+ (P) and p (B) layers instead of Si/SiGe, then remove the p layers laterally in TMAH under electrochemical bias, where the n layers passivate at the p-n junction.
note: Same all-Si dopant-contrast superlattice with selective removal as I-08470; electrochemical p-n etch stop is established.

title: Fe: magnetically steered parallel self-assembly of DRAM chiplets
idea: Deposit a patterned soft-magnetic Fe/Ni film on the back of each thinned DRAM chiplet and place an addressable electromagnet array beneath the target logic wafer in a fluid bath; thousands of chiplets settle and orient simultaneously into hybrid-bond sites with sub-um magnetic capture instead of serial pick-and-place.
note: Magnetic capture to sub-um alignment for hybrid bonding is unproven.

title: Er: erbium-amplified optical broadcast shares one weight copy
idea: Stream model weights from a single DRAM pool through an Er-doped waveguide-amplified 1-to-64 optical splitter tree, so every accelerator receives the same weight stream each step instead of each holding its own HBM copy; the amplifiers cancel the ~18 dB split loss.

title: Zn: Indium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cells built in idle LCD fabs
idea: Retool depreciated Gen-6/8 display lines to make ZTO (Zn, Sn, O only; no In or Ga) 2T0C gain-cell DRAM on glass at ~1 um rules, stacking a few layers; one Gen-8 panel yields ~100 GB per layer, diced into CXL capacity-tier tiles.

title: Prestressed magnetoelectric bit: tempered-glass stress makes strain-switched magnets bistable
idea: Copy tempered and prestressed glass: build a permanent biaxial stress into a Terfenol-D (TbDyFe) nanomagnet on a PMN-PT piezo pillar. The prestress creates two stable easy axes at +/-45 degrees, and a voltage pulse strains the magnet from one to the other. A tunnel junction reads it.
note: Straintronics prior art; Terfenol uses Tb/Dy and PMN-PT scaling is hard.

title: Hot-foil stamping bit: single heat pulse toggles a GdFeCo magnet
idea: A hot-foil stamp transfers its image with one heat pulse. In the same way, a ~10 ps current pulse heats a GdFeCo ferrimagnet nanodot, and ultrafast Gd/Fe sublattice exchange toggles its magnetization with no field, no spin torque and no polarity. An MTJ on top reads it.

title: LCD-line excimer laser crystallizes poly-Si periphery above the array
idea: Borrow the 1990s LTPS LCD backplane process: deposit a-Si over the finished array, then crystallize it with excimer-laser pulses that melt only the top ~50 nm while the array stays below ~400 C. Build 180 nm-rule periphery (pumps, predecoders, control) in that layer and wire it down to the array.

title: Newspaper-press memory: IGZO DRAM arrays in idle LCD panel fabs
idea: Like a newspaper press trading resolution for acreage, run 2T0C/1T1C IGZO arrays at ~1 um rules on Gen-6/8.5 glass in under-used LCD and LTPS fabs, dice them into memory tiles and pair them with small CMOS controller chiplets as a CXL capacity tier.
note: Idle display fabs as CXL capacity tier at $3-6/GB; yield at GB scale and ~100 ns access are doubts.

title: Coin-sorter assembly: fluidic self-assembly of DRAM micro-chiplets onto logic
idea: Like coin sorters dropping coins into shaped slots, agitate 300 um shape-keyed mature-node DRAM micro-chiplets in fluid over a logic wafer with matching receptor wells so they fall in and lock, then planarize and connect them with one RDL, placing thousands per minute.

title: Electrolytic-capacitor foil anodizing makes self-ordered capacitor holes
idea: Aluminum electrolytic-capacitor makers grow porous alumina by anodizing foil; deposit a thick Al film over the access-transistor layer, pre-texture it with a shallow imprint at the landing-pad pitch, and anodize in sulfuric acid at low voltage to grow ordered 40-60 nm pitch pores registered to the texture, then line them with TiN/ZrO2/TiN.
note: Pore registration to cell grid at 40 nm pitch is the key doubt.

title: Welding-bead crystallization builds germanium-free 3D DRAM tiers
idea: A seam weld's moving melt bead resolidifies as one grain; deposit each 3D-DRAM tier as amorphous silicon on oxide and scan a solid-state green laser line across it so the melt zone recrystallizes laterally from a seed via into the tier below, building single-crystal channels tier by tier.
note: Seeded laser recrystallization is known for monolithic 3D; lower-tier thermal budget and grain defects are the doubt.

title: Batik dopant-resist stacks make germanium-free 3D DRAM tiers
idea: In batik, wax marks what the dye must not touch; grow an all-silicon stack in which sacrificial tiers are heavily boron-doped and channel tiers lightly doped, then remove the sacrificial tiers laterally with a dopant-selective electrochemical or HNA-type etch, replacing SiGe sacrificial layers.
note: Same dopant-selective sacrificial-tier removal as I-08470.

title: Crystal casting in hollow molds: lateral selective epitaxy per tier
idea: Build the tier stack from cheap deposited oxide/nitride, carve hollow lateral oxide tubes in each tier off a vertical seed shaft, and grow single-crystal Si laterally inside them from one substrate seed by template-assisted selective epitaxy, casting all tiers' access-transistor channels in one growth run.

title: Tumbling bricks: fluidic self-assembly of DRAM micro-tiles onto logic
idea: Fabricate 200 um trapezoidal DRAM array tiles at one high-yield site, then tumble them in a carrier liquid over logic wafers with matching etched recesses (RFID fluidic assembly style) so shape keys and capillary/solder forces seat each tile, followed by batch bonding and one redistribution layer.

title: Nano-Velcro stacking: reworkable HBM dies swapped after test
idea: Replace permanent hybrid bonds with interlocking Cu nanowire hook-and-loop arrays grown in alumina templates that cold-weld under modest pressure yet allow controlled debond; test the stack, pull and replace failing dies, then anneal to make joints permanent.

title: Candle-dipped sidewall channels: ALD thickness sets transistor width
idea: Like dipping candles to build layers on a wick, pattern one mandrel mask, ALD a 3 nm IGZO film on the mandrel sidewalls and etch back so each sidewall becomes a vertical channel whose width is the film thickness; gate dielectric and wordline deposit and recess self-aligned, giving two cells per mandrel.

title: Brewery-to-sanitizer conversion: 3D NAND lines build vertical gain cells
idea: Like distilleries switching to hand sanitizer, convert a 3D NAND line during gluts: keep its stack deposition, channel-hole and slit masks and tools, swap the charge-trap fill for an IGZO channel, and add exactly one mask that splits each hole's gate ring into separate write and read gates, forming a 2T0C vertical gain-cell string.

title: Newspaper web press: roll-to-roll nanoimprinted flex interposer film
idea: Run polyimide film through a roll-to-roll line like a newspaper press: a nickel roller stamp nanoimprints 2 um wiring trenches, slot-die coats seed, and electroplating fills them at metres per minute. The film is then laminated under HBM stacks and the GPU instead of a silicon interposer.
note: 2 um overlay on dimensionally unstable polyimide web is the key doubt.

title: Composite-autoclave batch curing of hundreds of HBM stacks at once
idea: Pre-tack dies into stacks, vacuum-bag whole carriers like aerospace composite layups, and apply isostatic gas pressure and heat in an autoclave so hundreds of stacks bond in one cycle. Uniform pressure replaces serial thermocompression heads.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain wall bit read by current
idea: IFR: read the bit without disturbing it. Closest achievable: in a thin LiNbO3 or BiFeO3 mesa a write pulse creates or erases a charged domain wall between two side electrodes; reading passes a small current only when the conductive wall exists, leaving polarization untouched.
note: Nondestructive DW read in LiNbO3 is published; scaling below 50 nm and endurance unknown.

title: Printed charge-coupled shift-register memory with no per-bit transistor
idea: IFR: memory with zero transistors per bit. Closest achievable: print clocked electrode rows on a continuous oxide-semiconductor film so charge packets shift CCD-style along short lanes to a single sense node per lane; many short lanes keep latency near 100 ns.
note: 1970s CCD memory revived on oxide film; charge transfer efficiency and printed pitch are limits.

title: Open sense-interface standard makes periphery dies universal and reusable
idea: Ideal result: any cell array plugs into any periphery. Define a bond-level standard (bitline pitch, timing, trim protocol) between cell dies and periphery dies, so U.S.-made periphery dies work with multiple cell fabs and can be re-bonded to the next array generation.

title: Plate-tier capacitor: storage node overlaps an interleaved plate layer
idea: IFR: 'the capacitor takes no extra area or height.' Backward: alternate every channel tier with a thin plate-electrode tier separated by 4-6 nm high-k, so each lateral cell's storage node is a parallel-plate capacitor over its own top and bottom footprint (~0.25 fF at k=40), with no lateral capacitor arm; pair with short local bitlines that need only that much charge.

title: Square-meter memory from idle Gen-10.5 LCD panel fabs
idea: IFR: 'the fab already exists and costs nothing new.' Backward: run 8 stacked tiers of 2T0C oxide-semiconductor gain cells at ~1 um rules on 2.9 x 3.4 m LCD glass panels in under-used display fabs, accepting ~100x lower areal density because processed panel area costs hundreds of dollars per m2 versus tens of thousands for DRAM wafers.
note: Same display-fab oxide memory panel mechanism.

title: Refresh-free silicon-carbide DRAM in existing U.S. SiC power fabs
idea: Ideal: memory that never refreshes, made of silicon and carbon. Closest: 4H-SiC 1T1C cells (3.26 eV gap, generation leakage ~1e-19 of Si; 1990s demos showed multi-year room-temperature retention) built on 200 mm SiC lines in North Carolina/New York idled by the power-SiC glut.
note: Purdue showed SiC DRAM retention in 1990s; large F, poor SiC MOS interface and wafer cost limit it to niche tiers.

title: Square-meter laser interference lithography for perfectly periodic memory arrays
idea: Ideal: one flash of light patterns a whole panel. Closest: two- or three-beam interference of a 266/213 nm solid-state laser writes periodic lines or hexagonal dots (pitch >=0.12 um) over Gen-8 panels or R2R webs in seconds with no reticle or projection optics; only periphery and staircases use cheap panel steppers.

title: Kerfless epitaxial lift-off wafers end high-purity quartz crucible dependence
idea: Ideal: wafers without crucibles. Closest: grow 50-100 um epitaxial Si on a porous-Si release layer of a reusable parent wafer, peel and bond it to a cheap carrier, and reuse the parent 30-50 times, so one Czochralski crucible supports ~50x more wafers.

title: One logic die multiplexes periphery for four bonded array dies
idea: Ideal: periphery costs nothing. Closest: leave only bitline sense amps and local drivers on array dies, and move decoders, I/O, DLL, refresh and ECC logic to one 28 nm logic die that time-multiplexes four stacked array dies through fine-pitch hybrid bonds.

title: Single-mask vertical thyristor pillars cut from blanket p-n-p-n epitaxy
idea: Ideal: a cell patterned by one exposure. Closest: grow a blanket p-n-p-n Si/SiGe epitaxial stack, cut it into 4F2 pillars with one DSA-assisted hole pattern, and form a self-aligned spacer gate on the p-base; the regenerative thyristor latch stores the bit with no capacitor.
note: T-RAM physics known; standby current and temperature sensitivity sank it before.

title: Film-thickness-defined vertical gain cells need only immersion lithography
idea: Ideal: every critical dimension set by deposition, none by light. Closest: vertical write-over-read transistors in one pillar whose channel lengths equal deposited spacer thicknesses and gate lengths equal ALD metal thicknesses; only pillar placement uses 193i at ~40 nm half pitch, giving a ~4F2 capacitorless 2T gain cell.
note: Deposition-defined CDs remove EUV; vertical 2T gain cells under research.

title: Charge-coupled shift-register memory revived with spacer-patterned gates
idea: Ideal: a memory with no per-cell transistor and no capacitor. Closest: rebuild 1970s CCD memory as many short (32-64-bit) recirculating loops of overlapping gate electrodes formed by self-aligned double patterning on DUV; charge packets in surface potential wells are clocked past one shared sense/restore amplifier per loop.

title: Resonant interposer bus that recycles line charge every cycle
idea: Ideal: moving a bit costs zero energy. Closest achievable: integrate spiral inductors in the interposer so each memory data line resonates with its own capacitance; bits are encoded as the phase of a resonant swing and 60-80% of the CV2 energy sloshes back each cycle instead of being dumped to ground.

title: Field-programmed antifuse stacks: burn weights through the memory interface
idea: Ideal: a memory you write once at deployment and never maintain. Closest achievable: multi-layer antifuse crosspoint dies (gate-oxide breakdown with diode select, 4F2 per layer) are programmed in place through the accelerator's own memory channels when a model is deployed, then served read-only with no refresh and no standby power.
note: 3D OTP crosspoint existed; models change often and HV programming through memory channels is hard.

title: Per-row trimmed negative wordline for tail rows only
idea: Ideal: zero off-state leakage. Closest: each row gets a 2-bit trim register set at test that picks its standby wordline voltage from -0.2/-0.4/-0.6 V, so rows holding tail cells get deep negative bias (~10x lower subthreshold leakage) while healthy rows stay shallow and avoid the GIDL penalty of deep bias.

title: III-nitride resonant-tunneling floating well: ns write, hour retention
idea: Scarcity rule: refresh is banned. Store electrons in a GaN quantum well clad by AlN barriers (~2 eV offset) so thermionic leakage is negligible, and write through an AlN/GaN/AlN double-barrier resonant-tunneling stack that conducts only when the gate aligns its resonant level near 1 V. Read through the HEMT channel that the stored charge depletes.
note: GaN port of ULTRARAM; nitride polarization and trapping complicate RTDs.

title: Contactless snap-through nanomembrane: bistable mechanical bit, vacuum-insulated
idea: Scarcity rule: vacuum is the only insulator allowed. A pre-buckled SiN or few-layer-graphene membrane over a sealed 20 nm cavity has two stable shapes; an electrostatic pulse from a bottom electrode snaps it up or down, and one access transistor senses the capacitance difference. It never touches anything, so there is no stiction or contact wear.

title: Gallium-oxide access transistor plus refresh-rate register cuts refresh 4x
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): keep the pins and protocol, and change only what the die reports. Replace the Si access transistor with a 4.8 eV beta-Ga2O3 vertical channel whose off current is ~1e-6 of Si so 5 fF holds for minutes, and have the die permanently report the slowest refresh-rate code already defined in the MR4 temperature/refresh register, so unmodified controllers issue 4x fewer REFs.
note: Clever MR4 refresh-code reuse; BEOL-compatible Ga2O3 channel quality is the doubt.

title: Racetrack rows: ACT shifts a domain-wall track, tRCD hides it
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): keep DDR's ACT-then-READ page model. Map each row address to a shift position of perpendicular domain-wall racetracks under a line of read/write heads; ACT drives a current pulse that moves the tracks to that position within tRCD (~14 ns at ~500 m/s covers ~64 bits at 100 nm spacing), the heads latch the row into sense amps, and PRE writes it back.
note: At 100 nm bit spacing horizontal tracks are not denser than DRAM cells; pinning variability remains.

title: Crested-barrier floating node written by DRAM's existing 3 V wordline rail
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): no new supply pins, so reuse the ~3 V VPP rail DRAM already has. Store charge on a floating node behind a crested SiO2/Si3N4/SiO2 barrier whose peaked profile collapses under high field for ns writes but stays thick at hold fields for hours of retention; reads sense the storage transistor's threshold shift.
note: Crested barriers known (Likharev); reuse of VPP rail is a practical twist; tunneling endurance unknown.

title: Wordline-swing ceiling of 1 V: band-to-band tunnel FET access device
idea: Limit: the access device may swing only 1 V yet must still cut off by 10 decades. Use a vertical p-i-n tunnel FET (SiGe source pocket, Si channel, n+ storage-side drain). It turns on by band-to-band tunneling at sub-60 mV/dec and has no thermionic subthreshold tail, so off-current is set by the reverse-biased p-i-n diode (aA range). Asymmetric doping blocks ambipolar leakage from the storage side.

title: Refresh fixed at one second: sense amps flag low-confidence bits
idea: Limit: the refresh interval is forced to 1 s and the cell cannot improve. Add a dual-reference margin check to the sense amp (a second sense against a shifted reference) so cells whose signal sits near the decision point are flagged as erasures. The ECC decoder can then correct about twice as many errors, because an erasure costs half a correction.

title: Bitline capped at 10 fF: segment amplifiers inside the array tier
idea: Limit: no bitline may exceed 10 fF. Every 32 cells, a 2-transistor local amplifier (gate on the local bitline, drain on a global bitline) is built in the same vertical-channel tier as the access transistors, turning charge sharing into current gain on a global line.
note: Local amplifiers in vertical-channel tier; their Vt variation is the key doubt.

title: Dual-mode HZO: linear dielectric daily, ferroelectric only at shutdown
idea: Constraint: non-volatile, without ferroelectric fatigue. The capacitor runs as a sub-coercive high-k DRAM cell during operation; at power-fail, bipolar plate-line drivers pulse +/-Vc row by row so each cell's stored charge sets its polarization, and at power-up a destructive ferroelectric read with a dual-reference SA reloads the charge state.

title: BEOL oxide-TFT sense amps above NV crossbar: die equals array
idea: Constraint: NV crossbar cells (BEOL-compatible MRAM/ReRAM/FTJ). Build the sense amps, column muxes and local drivers from complementary oxide TFTs (n-IGZO plus p-SnO or Te) in the BEOL directly above or between crossbar tiers, so the front-end silicon under the array holds only global logic.

title: Coarse-litho tall stack: 48 ArF-dry tiers beat EUV density
idea: Because nothing exceeds 400 C, oxide 4F2 cross-point tiers can be stacked sequentially without disturbing lower tiers. Each tier uses only two ArF-dry masks at 65 nm, and density comes from tier count instead of litho.

title: Spatial-ALD nanolaminate replaces Si/SiGe epitaxy for 128 tiers
idea: Under 400 C, deposit 128 alternating 8 nm IGZO (or indium-free ZTO) channel layers and 20 nm AlOx sacrificial layers in one spatial-ALD run, then build lateral 3D DRAM cells by hole/slit recess as in Si/SiGe flows.
note: Removes strain limit; IGZO vs AlOx etch selectivity and low mobility are open.

title: Known-good-tier lamination: binned two-tier oxide modules
idea: Under 400 C, fabricate two-tier oxide DRAM modules on cheap glass carriers, test and bin each one, then laminate only good modules by 250 C Cu-Cu hybrid bonding into 16-tier stacks. Modules are made in parallel, not in series.

title: Packaging houses become DRAM fabs using 400 C tool sets
idea: Under 400 C, advanced-packaging and OSAT plants already run PVD, plating, ALD, steppers and hybrid bonders. They add oxide DRAM tier modules on purchased CMOS periphery wafers, with no furnaces or EUV.

title: Self-ordering anodic alumina pores as lithography-free capacitor molds
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero EUV and zero plasma for the capacitor layer. Deposit thick aluminum over the storage-node contacts, nanoimprint shallow pits on the contact grid, and anodize in sulfuric or oxalic acid so pores self-organize at the pits and grow straight to AR >100; open the barrier oxide at the bottom and fill with electrode and dielectric.

title: Display-fab memory: stacked oxide-TFT DRAM on Gen-8.5 glass
idea: Constraint: no silicon wafers at all. Repurpose idle Gen-8.5 LCD/OLED backplane lines to build 1T1C capacity memory at ~1 um rules on 5.5 m2 glass, about 100 GB per TFT tier and 8 stacked tiers per panel, sliced into CXL capacity modules with ~200 ns access.

title: Open tall-stack die standard turns memory dies into auctioned commodity
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. A JEDEC-style open spec fixes die size, thickness, pad maps and test interface for stackable DRAM dies so any vendor's dies drop into 32-64-high stacks; buyers reverse-auction dies and independent stackers compete separately.

title: Half the voltage: 0.5 V array rescued by on-die BCH
idea: Imposed limit: half the array voltage. Run VARY at ~0.5 V with offset-cancelling sense amplifiers and accept raw BER ~1e-5 from the reduced sense margin. A low-latency on-die BCH(t=2) code per 128 bits, decoded in parallel with column select, cleans up the result.
note: Halving VARY cuts bitline energy but SA margin at 0.5 V may give far worse than 1e-5 BER.

title: Charge-transfer pre-sense on a long bitline: sub-fF cells without shortening the bitline
idea: Conventional sensing divides the cell charge by Cs + Cbl (35 fF), so only ~7 mV survives from a 0.5 fF cell. In charge-transfer pre-sensing (Arimoto/Mitsubishi lineage) the bitline is precharged through its own transfer gate, which therefore self-biases at its own threshold and cancels Vt mismatch. When the cell dumps charge, the bitline moves a few mV, the transfer gate conducts in subthreshold, and the charge flows onto a small sense node. Gain = Cbl/C_sn. The twist is pairing this with an IGZO access device (1 aA), so a 0.3-0.5 fF cell still retains 45-75 s, and using offset-cancelled latches. The capacitor becomes a ~120 nm stub (AR ~6) or even the gate-plus-junction capacitance of a vertical channel.

title: 2-bit/cell 1T1C on an oxide access device
idea: Write one of four levels (0, 1/3, 2/3, 1 x VARY) through a vertical IGZO access transistor (OCTRAM/Samsung VCT style). Read by successive approximation: charge-share onto a short bitline, decide the MSB against a mid reference, then the LSB against a reference chosen by the MSB (or a time-domain ramp), then restore all four levels. A silicon cell cannot do this, because its 13 fA tail leaks a full level in milliseconds. At 1 aA the droop is 0.18 mV/s, so a 15 mV level budget lasts ~80 s. Combine with 128-cell bitlines (bonded periphery) or charge-transfer pre-sense (B1-04) for margin.

title: Vertical oxide semi-floating-gate 1T1D gain cell (4F2, capacitor-less, stackable)
idea: A vertical ALD In2O3/IGZO channel pillar is wrapped by a metal floating gate (FG), which is wrapped in turn by a control-gate wordline. A Schottky or MIS diode (Pt/IGZO, p-NiO/IGZO heterojunction, or a thin Al2O3 tunnel diode) links the FG to the drain/bitline at the pillar top. Write: the wordline couples the FG below the bitline, the diode forward-biases and the FG charges to the bitline level. Hold: raise the wordline so the diode is reverse-biased. Read: the FG charge sets the channel current, non-destructively. The reverse current of the diode sets retention, and the cell fits in the footprint of one vertical transistor. Fudan's Si SFG (Science 2013) showed ns writes at <2 V, but its embedded TFET/diode made it large; oxide BEOL lets the diode sit vertically on top.

title: Capacitive-NDRO ferroelectric gain cell for a read-mostly DRAM tier
idea: An HZO (or Zr-rich) capacitor with asymmetric electrodes has a zero-bias capacitance that differs between its two polarization states (imec reports a capacitive window ~8.7 at 0 V). The capacitor is the coupling element of a read transistor gate (1T-1C_FE or 2T-nC with n<=4). A small read pulse (below coercive) on its plate couples more or less charge onto the gate, and the read transistor converts that to current. Reads are non-destructive and never switch polarization; writes are full switching pulses. The memory is non-volatile, so there is no refresh and no restore, and pages need not be activated wholesale. Small n is essential: capacitive coupling dilutes as 1/n.

title: VCMA crosspoint MRAM with deliberately relaxed (refreshed) retention
idea: Each crosspoint is an OTS selector plus a perpendicular CoFeB/MgO MTJ with a high VCMA coefficient. A ~0.5-1 ns voltage pulse lowers the anisotropy so the free layer precesses half a turn, with no write current through a transistor, so there is no access transistor and the cell is 4F2. Thermal stability Delta is chosen for refreshed operation (Delta ~44-48 for 1 s to 1 min, vs ~64 for 10-year non-volatility), allowing a smaller or thinner free layer and lower write voltage. A 'refresh' is a TMR read plus conditional rewrite, done rarely. Four BEOL decks stack over CMOS.

title: Protonic gain cell (H+ in WO3 behind a PSG electrolyte)
idea: Three terminals: a WO3 channel between source and drain; a nanoporous PSG electrolyte (2-5 nm) above it; a Pd (or PdHx) gate that serves as the proton reservoir. A gate pulse at ~1 V/nm drives H+ into or out of WO3 in ns; each inserted proton is charge-compensated by an electron, which raises channel conductance. At read voltages the field is too low to move protons, so the state is non-volatile and the read is non-destructive. Multi-level storage is natural (analog conductance). The 'protonic nano-supercapacitor stub' variant, which uses the same chemistry as a 2-terminal capacitor holding ~18x today's charge per area, is rejected: its charge cannot be extracted at low field in ns (see notes).

title: 2D-barrier quasi-volatile 1T cell (seconds-to-minutes retention traded for endurance)
idea: A graphene or MoS2 channel sits over an hBN tunnel barrier (2-4 layers) and a floating gate or charge-storage layer (HfO2/Al2O3 or graphene). Fudan's PoX showed 2D-enhanced hot-carrier injection programming in 400 ps at 5 V, with 5.5e6 cycles. Fudan's 2D semi-floating gate showed 10 s retention with ~15 ns writes. The twist is to tune barrier thickness and injection mechanism (direct tunnelling vs hot-carrier) for a DRAM point: retention 10-100 s at 85 C, writes <=10 ns at ~2-3 V, and endurance as the optimisation target rather than retention. The read is non-destructive (gain cell). The cell is 1T, 4F2, BEOL-stackable if 2D films grow on wafers.

title: Capacitor-first inverted flow with perovskite super-k
idea: On a bare carrier or Si wafer, deposit a conductive-oxide bottom electrode (LaNiO3, Nb:SrTiO3 or doped SnO2), sputter/ALD 10-12 nm (Ba,Sr)TiO3 or SrTiO3 into short pillars or cups, and RTA at 650-750 C to crystallize (k 100-250); add the top electrode and planarize. Then build vertical IGZO/ZTO access transistors directly on the capacitor top contacts at <=400 C (the OCTRAM-style transistor-over-capacitor arrangement), and finally hybrid-bond the logic periphery wafer on top. Because the capacitor comes first, no transistor, metal or gate stack ever sees the perovskite anneal. The bit is a normal 1T1C charge sensed through a short bitline.

title: In-tier complementary-oxide sense amplifiers (no-bond short bitlines)
idea: Build complementary oxide TFT latch sense amplifiers (n-IGZO/ZTO + p-TeSeOx, mobility ~15 cm2/Vs, on/off 1e6-1e7) in a dedicated BEOL tier above or below the memory tier(s), connected by short vias to 64-cell local bitline segments. Short bitlines (Cbl ~8 fF instead of ~35 fF) cut the needed storage capacitance to ~1.2 fF and allow VARY ~0.4 V; the local SA restores the cell and drives a global bitline to the Si periphery. In 3D stacks one SA tier serves N memory tiers, so bitline capacitance no longer grows with tier count. Offset-cancelled (auto-zero) SA topology absorbs oxide Vt mismatch.

title: Maskless interference lithography for an all-periodic cell wafer
idea: Two (or four) coherent 193 nm beams interfere in water immersion to write a fringe pattern at half-pitch ~34.5-36 nm; two crossed exposures give post or hole lattices at ~70 nm pitch, and one SADP halves that to ~35 nm. Scanning-beam interference lithography (Doppler writing) phase-locks the fringe to wafer marks for overlay and covers 300 mm continuously. Array edges and the few non-periodic features are cut by a coarse KrF/i-line trim exposure whose overlay is not critical. Possible only because bonded periphery has removed all random logic from the cell wafer.

title: BEOL-only cell mini-line on reusable glass carriers, bonded to trailing-node periphery
idea: Oxide gain-cell or oxide 1T1C stacks (8-32 tiers) are deposited and patterned on a 300 mm CTE-matched glass carrier with a laser-release layer, using only PVD/ALD/PECVD, dry etch, ArF/NIL, CMP, cleans and a hybrid bonder: no >450 C furnaces, implanters, epitaxy or EUV. The finished stack is hybrid-bonded face-down to a periphery wafer (sense amps, decoders, I/O) from a trailing-node foundry at 1-2 um pitch, which A3's model says is enough for litho-light oxide pitches. The glass is laser-debonded through its transparent back and reused.

title: Trailing-node fab reuse: CMOS-under-array deep-tier MLC oxide memory at F=65 nm
idea: Run the fab's 65 nm CMOS flow to build sense amps, decoders and write-verify DACs, then stack 16-24 tiers of vertical IGZO/ZTO 2T0C cells over them (CMOS-under-array, as in 3D NAND CuA), with one hole etch per tier group at F=65 nm, ALD channels and recessed gates. Each cell stores 3-4 bits by write-verify; long oxide retention gives the level stability that MLC needs. No bonding, no immersion, no EUV.

title: Coaxial 4F2 2T0C: the storage node is the core gate of a read-channel shell
idea: Each cell is one pillar on a 2F x 2F grid. The core is a metal storage node (~20 nm diameter, ~150 nm tall) wrapped by a gate dielectric and an ALD IGZO/IGO shell; the shell is the read transistor's channel and the core is its gate (an inverted channel-all-around device), contacted by a source plane at the bottom and a read-bitline ring at the top. Above the core sits the write transistor: a short vertical oxide channel gated by a write-wordline ring, linking the write bitline at the pillar top to the core. Four line levels (source rows, read-bitline columns, write-wordline rows, write-bitline columns) each run at 2F pitch at different heights, so the 2T0C occupies 4F2 per tier. Tiers stack monolithically at <=400 C over CMOS-under-array.

title: Ge-free dopant-contrast superlattice (Si / Si:B) for 3D silicon DRAM
idea: 3D silicon DRAM (Samsung VS-DRAM, SK hynix, imec) starts from an epitaxial Si/Si0.8Ge0.2 superlattice whose SiGe layers are later etched out to free horizontal Si channels; imec's 120-bilayer stacks still show dislocations because the 0.84% mismatch accumulates strain, and A2 puts fleet-scale Ge demand at 6-38% of refined supply. Instead grow intrinsic Si alternating with heavily boron-doped Si (1-3e20 cm-3, optionally carbon co-doped, or with ~1-4% Ge to null the small lattice contraction) by the same low-temperature RPCVD. Remove the sacrificial layers through the slit with dopant-selective chemistry: an HF/HNO3/CH3COOH etch that attacks heavily doped Si far faster than intrinsic Si, or selective electrochemical porosification of the p+ layers followed by a fast porous-Si strip. The intrinsic layers become channels; boron tails matter only until the sacrificial layers are gone.
note: HNA/porous-Si selectivity known; boron outdiffusion and lateral etch uniformity through 100+ tiers are the doubts.

title: Approximate 4-level DRAM for low-order planes and 2-bit KV
idea: A 2-bit DAC-driven write driver writes one of four levels (0, 0.35, 0.70, 1.05 V). Reads use charge sharing followed by a 3-threshold successive sense, with extra reference levels from split reference bitlines as in the 1997 4-level 4 Gb DRAM. Gray coding makes an adjacent-level error a +/-1 LSB error of the 2-bit field. MLC rows hold only data classes that tolerate ~1e-3 level error: KIVI-style 2-bit KV (one element per cell), the low mantissa planes of BF16 (with B4-04), and MX/FP4 element codes whose shared scales stay protected. Exact data stay single-level. On short bitlines (128 cells, e.g., with sense amps under the array) the same scheme becomes exact.

title: BitNet-native charge-sharing popcount PIM in commodity 1T1C
idea: Ternary weights {-1, 0, +1} are stored as two bit-masks (positive and negative) in 1T1C rows, and activations are bit-sliced (INT8 into 8 binary planes). For each activation plane, the controller first RowClones the selected weight rows, ANDed with the activation mask (Ambit-style), into dedicated compute rows. It then activates 8 compute rows at once on the same bitlines. Charge sharing gives a bitline voltage proportional to the number of charged cells (0-8), which a 3-bit flash ADC shared by 8-16 bitlines in the SA stripe digitises. A small near-bank adder shifts and accumulates the partial sums. Weights never leave the bank.

title: Seconds-ULTRARAM: a resonant-tunnelling floating gate retuned from 1,000-year retention to DRAM-class speed
idea: A floating gate above a III-V (or 2D) channel is isolated by a triple-barrier resonant-tunnelling stack. Two quantum wells of different thickness sit between three barriers and line up only at the programming bias (~2.5 V today), so electrons pass resonantly with no hot-carrier damage; off resonance the stack blocks. The read is a non-destructive channel-conductance measurement, making this a gain cell with no capacitor. The DRAM retune thins the barriers and wells, which lowers the retention target from 1,000 years to seconds or days, pulls the resonance voltage toward ~1-1.5 V and raises current density for ns writes. A 2D van der Waals version (graphene/hBN/MoS2 resonant barriers) could be transferred onto Si BEOL.

title: Myelinated bitline: vacuum-sheathed bitline segments with non-latching 2T 'nodes of Ranvier'
idea: Bitlines are enclosed laterally in a sealed vacuum or air cavity, extending today's air spacers to the full bitline sidewall and the bitline-to-landing-pad gap. Every 32-64 cells the bitline breaks at a 'node': a BEOL IGZO 2T amplifier (source follower plus reset, non-latching) stacked above the array. The node turns the local segment's charge-sharing voltage into a current on a global bitline, and the main sense amp sits at the end as it does today. Unlike a local sense amplifier, the node neither latches nor restores, so it fits in BEOL above the array; restore runs through the global path.

title: Swap linear dielectric for antiferroelectric charge-burst capacitor dielectric
idea: Replace the ZrO2/Al2O3 linear cap dielectric with a field-induced antiferroelectric (ZrO2-rich HfZrO or Pb-free NaNbO3-based) whose AFE-to-FE transition sits just below the write voltage, so writing a '1' adds the released polarization (~15-25 uC/cm2) to the linear charge. At zero field the film relaxes back to the non-polar phase, so there is no remanent imprint and the cell stays a volatile DRAM cell.

title: Swap stored charge for conducting ferroelectric domain wall presence
idea: In thin-film LiNbO3 or BiFeO3 mesa cells, the bit is whether a charged, conducting domain wall bridges two side electrodes. Writing creates or erases the wall in ns, and reading senses wall conduction (on/off >10^4) without switching polarization.
note: Widely pursued (Fudan, Belfast); LNOI wafers make device demos cheap.

title: Substitute plasma-etched capacitor holes with self-ordered anodic alumina pores
idea: Deposit 1-2 um of aluminum over the cell transistors, pre-dimple it with a coarse DUV pattern registered to the landing pads, then anodize in oxalic acid: pores self-order into a hexagonal lattice at a pitch set by voltage (~2.5 nm/V) with AR >100:1 in minutes. Open the pore bottoms, ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN inside, and keep the alumina as the mechanical support.

title: Substitute plasma etch with metal-assisted chemical etching for vertical silicon pillars
idea: Pattern a Pt or Au catalyst mesh (lift-off or block-copolymer), then immerse the wafer in HF/H2O2: silicon under the catalyst dissolves and the mesh sinks straight down, carving vertical-channel-transistor pillars or buried-wordline trenches at >100:1 with no ion damage and no bowing; the catalyst is stripped and reclaimed.

title: Substitute zirconia capacitor dielectric with templated rutile titania near k=100
idea: Grow rutile-phase TiO2 (k ~80-120) by ALD at <=400 C on a RuO2 bottom electrode whose lattice templates the rutile phase, with Al doping to block leakage, so the same ~5 fF fits in a hole of AR ~25:1 instead of 70:1.
note: Long-studied (RuO2-templated rutile); leakage at low EOT is the blocker.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain walls in thin-film lithium niobate
idea: Combine the thin-film lithium niobate photonics platform with domain-wall nanoelectronics: a voltage writes or erases a charged domain wall between two electrodes, and the wall conducts 1e3-1e6x more than the bulk crystal. Read is a small non-destructive current through the wall, and the polarization holds the bit with no refresh.

title: Ferroelectric semiconductor channel: alpha-In2Se3 holds bit in itself
idea: Fuse channel and storage element: alpha-In2Se3 is a 2D semiconductor whose own lattice is ferroelectric, so switching its polarization changes the channel conductance directly. A one-transistor cell with no gate ferroelectric and no capacitor stores the bit in the channel and reads it non-destructively.

title: Molybdenum-dioxide electrodes template rutile TiO2 for short lateral capacitors
idea: Combine a rutile-structured MoO2 storage electrode (from Colorado molybdenum) with ALD TiO2 so the dielectric grows in its rutile phase (k ~80-100) below 400 C, with light Al doping to curb leakage, replacing imported Ru/RuO2 templates and k~40 ZrO2.
note: Rutile templating on MoO2 is published; rutile TiO2 leakage remains the doubt.

title: Anodic aluminum oxide pores serve as the capacitor mold
idea: Combine electrochemical anodization (self-ordered AAO reaches aspect ratios above 200 in wet baths) with the DRAM capacitor. Al is deposited over the landing pads and imprint-textured so pores nucleate over each pad, anodized at room temperature into 15-20 nm pores 2-3 um deep, and the electrodes and dielectric are then ALD-coated inside.

title: Store context as entropy-coded tokens, regenerate KV on demand
idea: Combine the model's own next-token probabilities with arithmetic coding: cold context is evicted from the KV cache and kept only as token IDs coded at ~1-2 bits per token, and when attention needs a span a burst prefill kernel recomputes its K/V. A tiny per-span key summary decides when recompute is worth it.
note: Recomputing a mid-context span needs causal prefix states; entropy coding IDs is irrelevant.

title: Anodized aluminum pores self-assemble the capacitor forest without etch
idea: Borrowed from architectural aluminum anodizing: sputter 3 um of Al over the access-transistor array, imprint shallow dimples at cell sites, and anodize so hexagonal pores self-align to them at ~100:1 aspect ratio; line the pores with TiN/high-k/TiN to form every capacitor without plasma etch or EUV.

title: Optical-disc error correction lets arrays ship with 1% dead cells
idea: Borrowed from CDs and Blu-ray, which ship with defects and rely on interleaved Reed-Solomon/LDPC: design arrays with soft-decision sensing and ~25% parity so up to 1% dead or weak-retention cells are absorbed, eliminating laser repair and per-cell screening.

title: Aerospace anodizing: aluminum-oxide nanopore templates for capacitors
idea: Instead of EUV plus deep plasma etch of 60-75:1 holes, deposit thick aluminum, nanoimprint shallow seed pits, and anodize it in oxalic or sulfuric acid (aircraft anodizing chemistry) so ordered vertical pores grow 1-3 um deep, then line them with TiN/ZrO2-Al2O3/TiN. Elements: Al, O, S, C, Ti, Zr, N only.

title: Sleep consolidation: idle-time compression of agent memory into gist tokens
idea: Borrowed from hippocampal sleep replay and spaced repetition: when an agent session idles, a background pass replays older context through the model to distill each chunk into a few learned gist tokens, keeping full-fidelity KV only for items retrieved repeatedly (high recall strength) and dropping the rest.

title: Court-stenographer chords: bigger tokens shrink KV until it fits SRAM
idea: Borrowed from stenotype machines that write whole words in one chord: the model uses latent multi-byte patch tokens (dynamic 8-16-byte patches) so each KV entry covers ~4x more text, and with latent low-rank KV projection a 32k-character context fits in on-die SRAM.

title: Anodized-alumina 1000:1 pore capacitor forest on foundry CMOS
idea: MAGNIFY aspect ratio to ~1000:1 with a beaker: sputter Al onto finished foundry CMOS wafers, anodize it into self-ordered 20-40 nm pores, then ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN inside; each 250-nm landing pad catches ~30 pores so no pore-to-cell alignment is needed. Tools: an anodization bath, one ALD tool and one contact litho.

title: Sputtered complementary-oxide SRAM layer stacked over any chip
idea: MINIFY the fab to a sputter tool: room-temperature sputtered p-type SnO and n-type ZnSnO thin-film transistors form cross-coupled 6T latches above finished foundry CMOS; repeat the 4-mask module to stack several memory layers.
note: p-SnO stability and 6T TFT area limit density; oxide CMOS SRAM previously shown.

title: Magnify endurance with antiferroelectric ZrO2 given a built-in bias
