idea: Antiferroelectric ZrO2 survives 1e12+ cycles but has no remanence; asymmetric electrodes (TiN vs RuO2 work-function offset) plus a fixed-charge dipole interlayer shift the double loop so one AFE loop straddles zero field, creating two stable remanent states.

title: Tin-oxide seed grows hafnium-free rutile titania with k near 100
idea: Magnify k ~2.5x: a 2 nm SnO2 seed (rutile lattice) on the bottom electrode makes ALD TiO2 crystallize as high-k rutile below 450 C, with Al doping to tame leakage. It replaces ZrO2/HfO2 and the Ru-oxide templates used before.

title: Indium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cell keeps data minutes at 125 C
idea: Magnify bandgap, minify chokepoints: build 2T0C gain cells from amorphous Zn-Sn-O (Eg ~3.3 eV), whose off-current stays below 1e-19 A/um at 125 C, with no indium, no gallium and no high-AR capacitor.
note: In-free twist on widely pursued IGZO 2T0C.

title: Self-ordering anodic alumina templates for capacitor holes
idea: Minify capacitor-hole lithography to zero: anodize a deposited aluminum film so it self-organizes into a hexagonal nanopore lattice (aspect ratio >100), then line pores with electrode and high-k by ALD.

title: Minify KV vectors to 16-byte global product-quantized codes
idea: Minify each 128-dim FP16 key/value head vector (256 B) to a 16-byte product-quantization code against fleet-trained codebooks kept in on-chip SRAM. Attention scores are computed directly from lookup tables (asymmetric distance), never dequantizing.
note: PQ/VQ KV compression already published (PQCache etc.); 1 bit/dim accuracy doubtful.

title: Minify weights to seeds: on-chip PRNG regenerates weight blocks
idea: Minify stored weights to an LFSR seed plus a few coefficients per block. On-chip PRNG units regenerate a pseudo-random basis and combine it into the weights at matmul time, after a seed search at compression time.
note: SeedLM-style; 1.5 effective bits likely loses accuracy.

title: Magnify the cache ratio 128:1: flash-backed DRAM-class memory
idea: Present SLC 3D NAND as byte-addressable memory through a controller with a DRAM cache 1/128 of capacity, write coalescing, hot-page prediction and terabyte-wide wear leveling; NAND is written only on eviction, so endurance holds by architecture.
note: Known (CMM-H, IMDT); microsecond misses and write amplification break DRAM-class claims.

title: Eliminate the separate capacitor: ferroelectric-semiconductor channel stores the bit itself
idea: Eliminate both the capacitor and the gate stack: make the channel from a ~3-nm ferroelectric semiconductor (alpha-In2Se3) whose locked in-plane/out-of-plane polarization modulates its own conductance by 1e3-1e5, so one device is both storage and access, with a non-destructive read.

title: Eliminate plasma etch and PFAS gases: catalyst-drilled capacitor holes
idea: Define a silver nanodot catalyst array by block-copolymer self-assembly on a thick sacrificial silicon mold, then immerse in HF/H2O2 so each dot sinks vertically (metal-assisted chemical etching), drilling 15-20 nm holes beyond 100:1; build electrodes in the holes, strip the mold, and recover the silver from the bath.

title: Eliminate the high-aspect-ratio capacitor etch with anodized alumina pores
idea: Deposit 2-3 um of aluminium over the landing pads, pre-dimple it with a shallow DUV-defined seed lattice, and anodize it so self-ordered hexagonal nanopores grow straight down onto each pad; ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN then lines the pores. No resist, no hard mask and no HAR plasma etch are used for the storage node.
note: Barrier layer at pore bottom must be opened.

title: The wall is the bit: conducting domain walls in insulating ferroelectric
idea: Rearrange which part stores the data: in LiNbO3 or BiFeO3 films a domain wall conducts while domains insulate; a write creates or erases a wall across a 20 nm electrode gap, and a sub-coercive read senses the wall current without disturbing it.

title: Metal digs the hole: catalyst-assisted chemical etching
idea: Reverse plasma-from-above into catalyst-from-below: put Au/Ag catalyst dots (patterned by DUV or dewetting) on silicon and let metal-assisted chemical etching sink them downward, carving 200:1 vertical trench capacitors at room temperature in a wet bench.

title: Per-block local losses discard activations before next block runs
idea: Reverse the training order from forward-all-then-backward-all to forward-and-learn per block: each block gets an auxiliary head or a forward-gradient estimate, updates at once, and frees its activations before the next block executes.

title: Ferroelectric/paraelectric superlattice in stabilized negative capacitance, effective k ~80
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter change: stack ~1-nm HZO ferroelectric layers between Al2O3/ZrO2 paraelectric layers sized so the ferroelectric sits on its stabilized negative-capacitance branch, making the series stack capacitance larger than either layer alone, with no hysteresis. Contradiction resolved: thick (low-leakage) dielectric vs. high capacitance.
note: HZO/ZrO2 superlattice capacitance boost actively pursued; stabilization without hysteresis is the gap.

title: Equipotentiality: clamped motionless bitlines with charge-transfer sensing
idea: TRIZ #12 Equipotentiality: each bitline is held at a constant potential by a cascode clamp; the cell's charge flows through the clamp onto a ~0.5 fF sense node, amplified by the capacitance ratio, and restore injects charge back through the same clamp, so the large bitline never swings.
note: Restore through clamp still swings cell; 10x energy claim overstated.

title: Antiferroelectric-boundary dielectric biased for a giant effective permittivity
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: tune a ZrO2-rich HfZrO film to sit at its field-induced tetragonal-to-polar transition, and offset the plate voltage so the storage window rides the steep part of the P-E curve. The local dQ/dV gives k_eff ~80-120 without full ferroelectric switching.

title: Hafnium-free antiferroelectric zirconia boosts charge near switching field
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transitions: tune pure tetragonal ZrO2 so its field-induced transition to the polar orthorhombic phase sits just above the array voltage. The plate is biased at the edge of that transition, where steep dP/dE gives ~1.5-2x charge per area over linear ZAZ.
note: MPB/AFE ZrO2 for DRAM Cs widely pursued.

title: Hemoglobin cooperativity: antiferroelectric window multiplies effective capacitance
idea: Hemoglobin releases most of its oxygen inside a narrow pressure window by cooperative switching. Bias the cell plate of an antiferroelectric ZrO2-rich capacitor so the 0 and 1 node voltages straddle its field-induced AFE-to-FE transition. The transition releases extra polarization charge, giving k_eff ~80-150 within the 1 V swing.

title: GC-rich bonds: ultra-wide-bandgap Ga2O3 channels let capacitors shrink below 1 fF
idea: Thermophile genomes are GC-rich (three hydrogen bonds per pair) for a higher melting point; likewise use ALD Ga2O3 (Eg ~4.8 eV) as the vertical channel in each tier, whose thermally generated off-current stays ~1e-21 A even at 125 C, so a sub-1 fF planar MIM capacitor per tier holds data for seconds.
note: ALD Ga2O3 off-current is defect-limited, not thermal; overlaps IGZO 2T0C work.

title: Honeycomb anodic alumina self-orders capacitor holes at extreme aspect
idea: Bees build hexagonal comb from local wall rules; sputter aluminum over the landing pads and anodize it, so pores self-organize into a hexagonal lattice whose pitch is set by voltage (25-60 nm) and whose sites are pinned by shallow DUV-printed dimples on the pads; pores grow 5-10 um deep in a wet bench, then get ALD electrode and dielectric.

title: Deck of cards: sliding-ferroelectric bilayer stacking flips store bits
idea: Shuffle cards by one atom: in parallel-stacked bilayer hBN or 3R-MoS2, AB versus BA stacking gives opposite out-of-plane polarization, switched by ~1 V across ~1 nm as one layer slides a third of a lattice spacing; build cells from exfoliated or CVD bilayers with e-beam-defined gates and read the polarization as a threshold shift in a stacked MoS2 channel.

title: Diatom biomineralization: DNA-origami templates place 10-nm storage nodes
idea: Diatoms grow silica shells on protein templates; adsorb DNA-origami tiles carrying metal seeds on a 10-nm grid onto shape-matched landing sites defined by relaxed e-beam litho, then grow storage nodes or floating islands from the seeds by ALD or electroless plating, burning off the origami afterward.
note: Kershner 2009 placement on landing sites is prior art; yield is far from needed.

title: Black-silicon MacEtch: catalytic wet etching of 100:1 capacitor holes
idea: Borrowed from solar black-silicon texturing, where Ag/Au catalyst sinks into silicon in HF/H2O2 and drills vertical pores: deposit an amorphous-Si capacitor mold, pattern a thin gold mesh on the hole lattice, immerse so the catalyst etches straight down to AR >100 at room temperature, strip the gold and line with electrode and dielectric; a small team runs it on a wet bench.

title: Foldable-phone Z-fold flex memory stack
idea: Foldable phones bend circuits on polyimide. Mount thinned DRAM dies along one long polyimide flex (cured ≤350 C) carrying fine Cu traces, test every die flat, then Z-fold the strip accordion-style into a stack. Tier-to-tier signals travel over the folds instead of TSVs.

title: Telegraph codebook KV: position-free phrase blocks shared rack-wide
idea: Like 1880s commercial telegraph codes that replaced common phrases with five-letter codewords, frequently reused segments (system prompts, tool schemas, popular documents) get codewords whose KV is computed once in a position-independent form and kept in rack-pooled memory. Sessions store only codeword references, and RoPE re-rotation plus a small boundary-correction pass place the phrase at any offset at read time.
note: Overlaps CacheBlend/EPIC-style position-independent caching.

title: Briggs log-table interpolation for cross-layer KV cache
idea: Henry Briggs printed logarithms only at anchor points plus difference columns for interpolation. Store full KV only for anchor layers (every 4th) and, for in-between layers, a per-head low-rank correction to the linear interpolation of the neighbouring anchors' KV, reconstructed on the fly in the read path.

title: Swiss-cheese tiers: stack defective layers, remap holes in base die
idea: Inverts 'every cell in a die must work.' Accept 3D tiers with up to ~5-10% dead cells, map defects at wafer probe into a per-stack CAM/remap table held in the logic base die, and drop per-tier redundancy rows/columns, so tier yields no longer multiply into stack yield.

title: Copper-catalyzed MacEtch drills 100:1 holes without plasma tools
idea: Inverts 'high-aspect-ratio holes need plasma etch with W or carbon hard masks.' Use metal-assisted chemical etching with a patterned Cu catalyst in HF/H2O2 so silicon dissolves only beneath the catalyst, driving vertical holes and pillars past 100:1 at room temperature.

title: Grow the holes: anodized alumina pores as capacitor molds
idea: Inverts 'deep capacitor holes must be plasma-etched': deposit thick aluminum over the array and anodize it; self-ordered hexagonal pores with aspect ratios above 100:1 (pitch set by anodization voltage, registration seeded by a shallow imprint) become the capacitor mold, lined with electrode and dielectric by ALD.

title: Nitrogen-cooled racks freeze leakage, switching refresh off
idea: Inverts 'memory runs at room temperature': immerse DRAM modules in liquid nitrogen from air-separation units (no helium), where junction and subthreshold leakage fall by >1e6 and retention stretches from 64 ms to hours or days; firmware disables refresh for working sets whose lifetime is below the cryogenic retention.
note: Same LN2 cryo-DRAM mechanism as I-02504; adds refresh-off firmware.

title: Anodized-alumina pores as a ready-made capacitor forest
idea: Inverts 'storage nodes must be individually patterned'. Anodize sputtered aluminium in oxalic acid so it self-orders into hexagonal pores (~25-60 nm pitch, AR >100:1); a 180 nm stepper only fences cell groups, and atomic-layer-epitaxy reactors of the 1990s TFEL-display type line the pores with electrode/dielectric/electrode, several pores in parallel per cell.
note: AAO MIM nanocapacitor arrays are well published; registration to cells is the issue.

title: Catalytic gold-mesh wet etching drills 200:1 nanoholes
idea: Inverts 'deep holes require plasma'. Metal-assisted chemical etching: a perforated Au film (stepper-defined then spacer-shrunk) sinks into Si in HF/H2O2, drilling straight pores or freeing pillars at AR 100-200:1 at room temperature, then the Au is stripped in iodide before any thermal step.

title: Lensless interference lithography with 1990s excimer lasers
idea: Inverts 'lithography needs a lens and a mask'. Interfere two or three line-narrowed 248/193 nm excimer beams (Lloyd's-mirror geometry) at the wafer to expose ~110-130 nm-pitch gratings or hexagonal arrays over a whole 200 mm wafer in one flash, then halve with one spacer step.

title: Canonicalized document KV shared across all tenants
idea: Inverts 'each request owns its KV cache': RAG chunks, tool schemas and system prompts are normalized into canonical position-independent KV blocks (re-rotated to the needed position at use) and stored once per cluster under a content hash, so any tenant that retrieves the same document reuses the same KV blocks.
note: CacheBlend/EPIC-like; cross-chunk attention loss needs blending.

title: Local-loss training lets each block free activations immediately
idea: Inverts 'backprop must store every activation': blocks train on local objectives (per-block predictive or contrastive heads, plus a periodic short global sync), so each block's activations are freed as soon as its local update finishes.

title: Charge-recycling bus: stacked voltage domains reuse every transition
idea: Invert 'each bit transition dumps its charge to ground': split the bus into N series-stacked voltage domains so charge discharging a line in domain k charges a line in domain k-1, with a small balancing regulator closing the loop.
note: Stacked-domain charge recycling is decades-old art; balancing regulator and data-dependent imbalance limit gains.

title: Ferroelectric-semiconductor channel that stores and reads its own bit
idea: Use alpha-In2Se3, whose locked in-plane/out-of-plane polarization sets its own band bending and conductance, as the transistor channel. A gate pulse writes the polarization, and the read is a non-destructive channel conductance with no separate capacitor or ferroelectric gate stack.
note: In2Se3 FeS-FET demonstrated (2019); retention suffers from in-channel depolarization.

title: Liquid-nitrogen DRAM: freeze out leakage, then shrink the capacitor
idea: Run the array at 77 K, where thermally activated leakage (junction generation, subthreshold, trap-assisted) falls by >1e6 because it scales as exp(-Ea/kT). Design out the weakly temperature-dependent GIDL with a lower wordline-off bias, so a 0.3 fF planar MIM holds data for hours and refresh is dropped. Racks are LN2-cooled at ~10x wall-power overhead on the much smaller memory heat.

title: Erasable conducting domain walls as non-destructive ferroelectric bits
idea: In thin-film z-cut LiNbO3-on-insulator, a field pulse injects a charged head-to-head domain wall between two electrodes that conducts ~uA, and a reverse pulse erases it. The read senses the wall current and never switches the polarization.
note: LiNbO3 domain-wall memory actively researched; wall pinning, speed and density at scale open.

title: Antiferroelectric back-switching plateau acts as a constant-voltage charge reservoir
idea: Add a thin antiferroelectric ZrO2 film in parallel with the storage dielectric. Size it so the written '1' voltage is above its field-induced polar switching and its back-switching edge sits just above the sense threshold. As leakage drains the node, the AFE back-switches and releases ~10-20 uC/cm^2 of polarization charge at a nearly constant voltage, pinning the node like a clamped reservoir.

title: Johnsen-Rahbek solid-contact chuck conducts heat with zero backside gas
idea: Contact conductance h ~ 1.25 k_s (m/sigma)(P/H)^0.95 grows with true contact area; a Johnsen-Rahbek chuck gives ~10x the clamp pressure of a Coulomb chuck, and a compliant 50 um pyrolytic-graphite skin raises true contact from ~0.1% to a few percent, reaching gas-gap-class 500-1000 W/m2K with no gas.

title: Tin-oxide rutile template grows k~90 TiO2 capacitors without Ru
idea: Rutile TiO2 has k~90-170 but only forms rutile at DRAM temperatures on a rutile-structured template, today RuO2 (Ru ~90% South Africa). Use conductive Sb:SnO2 or metallic MoO2 (rutile family, ~2-3% mismatch) as bottom-electrode template and 2-5% Al-doped TiO2 to raise the leakage barrier.

title: Catalyst-assisted wet etching digs 100:1 capacitor holes without fluorocarbon plasma
idea: Silicon dissolves only beneath a noble-metal catalyst in HF/H2O2 (metal-assisted chemical etching), so holes sink straight down at room temperature with no ion angular spread limiting depth. Pattern a catalyst mesh at storage-node pitch, sink 100:1 holes into silicon to revive trench-capacitor DRAM, then strip the catalyst in iodide etch.

title: Regenerate weights from PRNG seeds in the HBM base die
idea: A trained weight block can be approximated as a few coefficients times pseudo-random basis vectors. Store, per 8x8 block, a 16-bit LFSR seed and 4 low-bit coefficients; an LFSR array in the HBM logic die regenerates the basis and the weights at read bandwidth, replacing stored bits with deterministic computation.

title: Position-free KV storage for cross-user chunk dedup
idea: The same RAG documents and system prompts recur across users at different offsets, which defeats prefix caching. Store each chunk's keys before RoPE, under a content hash; apply the rotary rotation for the real position at read time, and run a small learned correction pass over the first few tokens of each chunk to restore cross-chunk attention.

title: Garden hose: conductive ferroelectric domain wall opened or kinked off
idea: Stimulus 'garden hose' (flow on, or kinked off) -> in a thin LiNbO3 or BiFeO3 mesa, a write pulse creates or erases a charged head-to-head domain wall bridging two electrodes; the wall conducts ~1000x more than the bulk, so read is a small nondestructive current and the wall stays put without power.
note: LiNbO3 domain-wall memory demonstrated by several groups; CMOS integration and scaling remain.

title: Honeycomb: anodized alumina pores template 500:1 capacitors, no plasma
idea: Stimulus 'honeycomb' -> anodize an aluminum film in oxalic acid so it self-organizes into hexagonal pores (40-60 nm pitch, AR up to 500:1), guided by a nanoimprinted pre-dent, then ALD TiN (from TiCl4/NH3) and ZrO2/Al2O3 into the pores. The electrolyte digs the holes: no fluorocarbon etch, no NF3 chamber clean.
note: Same AAO pore capacitor; registration to the access device.

title: Honeycomb: anodic alumina pores self-register on landing pads as capacitor molds
idea: Random stimulus 'honeycomb' -> an aluminum film deposited over the landing-pad array is anodized at ~10-12 V, so pores nucleate at the pad-induced topographic dimples and grow straight down as a self-ordered hexagonal array with aspect ratio >100. The pores serve as the storage-capacitor mold, which needs no lithography and no high-AR plasma etch.

title: Dynamic copper-filament crosspoint memory refreshed like DRAM
idea: Box = {medium: volatile nanoscale Cu filament in SiO2 that dissolves over ~1 s | access: none (self-rectifying stack) | sense: filament on/off current ~1e3 | integration: 4F2 crosspoint stacked 8 layers | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: sputtered Arizona copper + PECVD SiO2}. Filaments are kept deliberately thin so they relax on their own, which allows low compliance current and longer endurance, and a 1 s refresh rewrites the ones.

title: Refresh interval set by 1% failure point, scrubbed by ECC
idea: Box: standard cap x Si access x SA plus decode-on-refresh x controller scrub x bulk Si x standard. Retention is specified where 1% of cells fail instead of at the 1e-9 tail, which stretches refresh ~16-30x; each refresh pass reads through the decoder and writes back corrected data so errors never pile up.
note: 1% raw BER needs heavy codes; decode-on-refresh energy is the doubt.

title: Calcium titanate perovskite capacitors from earth-abundant elements
idea: Box [CaTiO3 (k~150) cap | Si access | voltage SA | pillar | Si | thermal ALD from a Ca cyclopentadienyl + Ti amide + O3 with N2 purges]: grow perovskite CaTiO3 on a conductive Nb:TiO2 bottom electrode that seeds crystallization near 450 C, with no Sr, Ru or Hf.

title: Low-aspect-ratio capacitor from ALD rutile-TiO2/SrTiO3 on Ru, k~100
idea: Box: k 100-150 dielectric charge x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x ALD on Ru/RuO2 electrodes that template rutile or perovskite growth below 450 C. With k~100 vs ~40 today, the same ~5 fF fits in an AR ~25 pillar, so the module drops the cryo-etch, the support mesh and two hardmask layers; leakage is held by Al doping and a thin wide-gap interface layer.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as 100:1 capacitor molds on chip
idea: Box: MIM charge x sputtered IGZO TFT x voltage sense amp x BEOL test chip x Si/SiO2 x two-step Al anodization in oxalic acid. A sputtered Al film is anodized into hexagonally ordered pores (~60-100 nm pitch, AR >100) with positions seeded by a light EBL pre-pattern, then ALD TiN/HfO2/TiN coats the pores, so the capacitor mold forms in a beaker, not a cryo-etcher.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching carves 100:1 capacitor trenches without plasma
idea: Box: Si trench charge x planar Si MOSFET access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x MacEtch with an EBL-patterned noble-metal mesh in HF/H2O2. The catalytic film sinks vertically into Si at room temperature, carving smooth high-AR holes in a wet bench; the catalyst is stripped and holes are lined by ALD.

title: Lloyd's-mirror crossed interference exposures print maskless pillar lattices
idea: Box: Si charge x vertical pillar transistor x standard sensing x 2D x Si x 266/325 nm laser Lloyd's-mirror interference lithography, two exposures at 90 degrees. Interference fringes print a perfectly periodic dot lattice over the wafer in seconds with no mask, and array-edge cuts plus periphery are added with a contact-aligner exposure.

title: Po: the bit is a border — conductive ferroelectric domain-wall memory
idea: Po: the bit is not the country but its border. Extracted: in thin LiNbO3 or BiFeO3, write or erase a charged domain wall across a nano-gap; the wall conducts 1e3-1e6x more than the bulk, so the bit is wall present/absent, read non-destructively by a small current.
note: Same conductive domain-wall bit.

title: Anodized aluminum pores as self-drawn capacitor molds
idea: Po: the metal draws its own circuit. Deposit thick Al, pre-dent it with a coarse DUV hexagonal guide grid, and anodize: self-ordered alumina pores form at 25-40 nm pitch with aspect ratios >150:1 in minutes; ALD TiN/high-k/TiN into the pores makes the capacitors with no high-AR plasma etch and no capacitor-hole EUV.

title: Forward-only training: learn without storing the forward pass
idea: Po: training forgets the forward pass. Gradients come from forward-mode derivatives (JVPs with random tangents, variance-reduced by local layer-wise losses), so no activations are kept for backprop and memory stays O(one layer) regardless of depth.

title: Born-compressed tensors: math on codebook indices, never decompressed
idea: Po: data is born compressed and dies compressed. Weights and KV are stored as vector-quantized codebook indices, and the accelerator computes dot products from precomputed lookup tables of codeword-by-query partial products, never expanding values to FP16 in memory.

title: Erasable conducting domain wall in thin-film lithium niobate
idea: Worsen: read bits by dumping their charge onto a bitline, destroying them. Flip: store the bit as the presence or absence of a charged conducting domain wall in a thin-film LiNbO3 mesa between two electrodes; a field pulse injects or erases the wall, and a small read voltage senses its >1000x conductance without moving it.
note: Same LNOI conducting-wall bit.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina scaffold for litho-free capacitor arrays
idea: Worsen: pattern every capacitor hole with EUV and plasma etch. Flip: anodize an aluminium layer so it self-organizes into hexagonal 20-40 nm pores at >100:1 aspect ratio, ALD electrode/high-k/electrode inside the pores, and register access transistors to the natural lattice.
note: AAO nanocapacitors known; registering transistors to self-ordered lattice is hard.

title: Fatigue-free sliding ferroelectric bilayers built by tear-and-stack
idea: Worsen: assume a new storage material needs a fab to evaluate. Flip: with a ~$300k glovebox and transfer stage, tear-and-stack parallel bilayer hBN or 3R-MoS2 whose polarization flips by interlayer sliding (no ion motion), and spend 24 months proving 1e12+ cycles and 10 ns switching on 100-device arrays.

title: Alpha-In2Se3 ferroelectric-semiconductor channel storing bits in-channel
idea: Worsen: need a separate capacitor plus a transistor for every bit. Flip: CVD-grow alpha-In2Se3, a 2D semiconductor that is itself ferroelectric, so the channel's own polarization sets its conductance (one device gives storage plus read gain); a $600k university program demonstrates 100-device arrays and 10 ns writes within 24 months.
note: FeS-FET with alpha-In2Se3 already published; retention and endurance open.

title: Anodized aluminum self-ordered pores form capacitor molds
idea: Worsen: lithographically print and plasma-etch billions of capacitor holes per die. Flip: deposit thick aluminum, pre-texture it with a coarse imprint and anodize it. The Al2O3 self-organizes into hexagonal pores with AR >500 at a pitch set by voltage (~2.5 nm/V), and those pores become the capacitor mold, so no capacitor etch tool is needed.

title: Keep 2-byte token IDs, re-encode middle-context KV on demand
idea: Worsen: hold about 100 KB of KV per token for the whole context. Flip: evict KV for middle context, keep only the token IDs, and when a light attention predictor flags a region as relevant, recompute that region's KV in a batched prefill burst.
note: Without stored KV, predictor needs some summary to flag relevance.

title: 100:1 memory overcommit backed by compressed flash
idea: Worsen: give each tenant dedicated DRAM sized for its peak. Flip: overcommit physical DRAM 100:1 across bursty tenants (functions, dev environments, idle VMs) with zstd-compressed NVMe swap and working-set snapshots that restore in about 5 ms.

title: Append-only log memory on SLC flash with DRAM write buffer
idea: Worsen: send random small writes to flash and kill it in weeks. Flip: make memory log-structured, with writes coalesced in a small DRAM buffer and appended sequentially to SLC flash, random reads served directly from flash, and garbage collection run in idle time.

title: Charge-recycling stacked-voltage memory bus at 50 mV swing
idea: Worsen: swing every link wire rail-to-rail at 1.1 V and dump the charge to ground. Flip: stack link lanes in series voltage domains so the charge one lane releases on a transition becomes the next lane's supply, and run interposer lines at ~50-100 mV differential swing into sense-amp receivers.
note: Adds 50-100 mV swing to stacked-domain recycling; 5-10x claim optimistic.

title: Musician hears four pitches: self-referenced 4-level DRAM cell
idea: A musician hears four notes where an engineer hears 'high or low'. Store four charge levels in a standard capacitor, and pair every 64 cells with a reference cell written in the same burst. The sense amp compares against a twin that has leaked by the same amount (relative pitch) instead of a fixed threshold.

title: Shaker minimalist: two-mask thyristor crosspoint on purchased epi wafers
idea: The Shaker craftsman removes every unnecessary step. Buy wafers with an in-situ-doped p+/n/p/n+ epi stack from a vendor, etch line mask 1, fill, then etch perpendicular line mask 2, leaving self-aligned 4F2 thyristor pillars. Each pillar is a bistable latch with ns read and write.

title: Lost-wax sculptor casts capacitors in self-organised alumina pores
idea: Persona: a bronze sculptor who casts into a mould instead of carving. Anodize an aluminum film into porous anodic alumina, whose pores self-organize at 30-60 nm pitch with aspect ratios >100:1, seeded by shallow DUV-imprinted dimples aligned to the contacts. Deposit ALD TiN/dielectric/TiN inside the pores.

title: Aerospace anodizing grows 200:1 nanopore capacitor templates without etch
idea: Extreme user: aerospace aluminum finishing lines. Anodize a deposited aluminum film in oxalic/sulfuric acid so self-ordered nanopores (AR >200:1) grow, guided into register by a shallow imprinted pre-pattern; thin the pore-bottom barrier by voltage ramp-down, then ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN inside.

title: Relaxor polar-nanoregion dielectric for k near 70
idea: Scale down to 2-5 nm polar nanoregions: dope ZrO2/HfO2 laminates with La/Nb to make a relaxor-like dielectric whose nanoregions rotate freely under field (slim loop, no remanence), giving high effective permittivity without ferroelectric hysteresis loss.
note: MPB/relaxor hafnia-zirconia for high k is actively pursued; leakage at 5 nm is the doubt.

title: Antiferroelectric ZrO2 phase switch pumps extra charge
idea: Scale down to the lattice: operate the capacitor dielectric as an antiferroelectric whose field-induced tetragonal-to-orthorhombic transition releases a burst of polarization charge above a threshold voltage, then fully returns at zero field (no remanence, no wake-up fatigue).

title: Lithium niobate domain-wall conduction gives nondestructive reads
idea: Scale down to 1 nm domain walls: in wafer-bonded single-crystal LiNbO3 films a written ferroelectric domain creates a conducting wall between electrodes, so the bit is read by current without switching.

title: Retention-class mats exposed as address bits
idea: Use test time as a time machine: at wafer test, hours-long 85 C dwells measure each mat's worst cell, tail cells are remapped to spare rows, and mats are binned into retention classes (0.1, 1, 10, 100 s) that the decoder exposes as high address bits; the allocator places each object only in a class longer than its maximum idle time, and refresh is never issued.

title: Anodized aluminum pores template capacitors from a U.S. wet bench
idea: Swap plasma etch for slow electrochemistry: a film of U.S.-smelted aluminum is anodized for hours in acid and self-organizes into hexagonal pores with >100:1 aspect ratio, guided by a shallow imprinted dimple pattern; the alumina becomes the mold for TiN/high-k/TiN capacitor shells.

title: Ramtron's capacitor repurposed: antiferroelectric charge-dump DRAM storage node
idea: Ferroelectric capacitors failed in FeRAM because reads were destructive and fatigue accumulated, but DRAM reads are destructive anyway. Use a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric whose field-induced polar phase stores ~15-25 uC/cm2 of extra charge above its switching field and back-switches on read, dumping that charge onto the bitline.

title: Optane Memory Mode, fixed: associative tag-in-ECC cache over CXL flash
idea: Optane's Memory Mode died on direct-mapped DRAM-cache conflict misses that exposed 300+ ns media. Replace it with a 4-way set-associative near-memory DRAM cache whose tags and way-predictor live in DDR5 ECC spare bits, fronting a cheap CXL SLC-NAND tier, with promotion only on second touch to stop cache pollution.
note: Tags-in-ECC DRAM caches and CXL flash memory (CMM-H) exist; NAND miss latency threatens <10% slowdown.

title: Cell SPE local stores, fixed: compiler-scheduled flash-to-SRAM layer streaming
idea: Cell's SPEs died because programmers hand-wrote double-buffered DMA into 256 KB local stores. Transformer inference is a fully static dataflow, so the compiler generates the DMA schedule: stream layer N+1 weights from NVMe flash into SRAM while layer N computes, picking batch size so compute time covers flash read time.
note: FlexGen-like; KV and activations still need DRAM, so not truly DRAM-free.

title: FeRAM's fab-poisoning PZT replaced by built-in-biased antiferroelectric ZrO2 capacitors
idea: Ramtron FeRAM never entered DRAM fabs because lead-based PZT contaminated lines and did not scale. Fix: use the ZrO2 that DRAM capacitors already deposit, an antiferroelectric, between asymmetric work-function electrodes (e.g., TiN bottom, high-work-function RuO2 top) whose built-in field shifts one double-hysteresis loop to zero bias, making the capacitor bistable and nonvolatile.
note: Work-function-shifted AFE ZrO2 NVM already shown (Pesic 2016).

title: Ferroelectric-semiconductor channel: the transistor itself is the bit
idea: Effect walk: locked in-plane/out-of-plane ferroelectricity in a semiconductor. A 3-nm alpha-In2Se3 channel's own polarization sets its band bending and conductance; a ~0.5 V gate pulse switches the channel dipoles, and reading at 0.1 V drain bias senses a ~10^3 current ratio without disturbing polarization.

title: Nonlinear-permittivity probe reads ferroelectric bits below coercive field
idea: Effect walk: nonlinear dielectric response. The second-order permittivity of a ferroelectric is odd in polarization, so a 50-mV sinusoid far below the coercive voltage produces a second-harmonic charge whose phase flips with the bit; a local lock-in style sense stage reads it while leaving the domain untouched.

title: Antiferroelectric capacitor pins stored-one voltage as charge reservoir
idea: Effect: antiferroelectric double-hysteresis switching. The cell capacitor uses AFE ZrO2 with plate bias set so a stored '1' sits just above the backward switching field; as leakage drains charge, polarization release (~2Pr x area, ~10x the linear charge) holds the node near that voltage, which stays above the sense threshold, and reads look like normal charge sharing. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.

title: Negative-capacitance HZO stack gives planar tier capacitors k~70
idea: Ferroelectric negative capacitance: an HZO/ZrO2/Al2O3 superlattice is tuned so the ferroelectric layer sits in a stabilized negative-capacitance regime, raising the series stack's effective permittivity toward k~70. Each tier can then use short lateral planar capacitors instead of AR 60-75 pillars.
note: MPB/NC HZO high-k for DRAM caps actively pursued; NC stability debated.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain-wall crossbars in thin-film lithium niobate
idea: Domain-wall conduction: in LNOI wafers, which photonics fabs already make, voltage pulses create or erase conductive domain walls across each nanocell. Reading senses wall current without switching, so the read is non-destructive and the walls persist with no power.
note: Domain-wall memory in LiNbO3 already published (Fudan); LNOI availability helps demos.

title: Template-stabilized rutile titania reaches k near 100 without hafnium
idea: Effect: rutile TiO2 has k ~80-170 but normally forms low-k anatase. ALD it onto a lattice-matched rutile-structure conductor (Sb:SnO2 or MoO2 instead of scarce Ru) so epitaxial templating locks in rutile, and use Al doping at grain boundaries to plug leakage.

title: Monolayer doping reaches buried lateral transistors in 3D DRAM tiers
idea: Effect: self-limiting chemisorption plus solid-source diffusion. Implanters cannot reach sidewalls 20 tiers down, so flood the slit with a phosphonic- or boronic-acid monolayer that bonds to every exposed Si surface, cap it, and spike-anneal to drive 3-5 nm abrupt junctions. One wet step dopes all tiers at once.

title: Beaker-anodized alumina provides lithography-free capacitor molds on test wafers
idea: Effect: field-assisted oxide dissolution that self-organizes pores. Sputter 3 um of Al on a transistor test wafer and anodize twice in oxalic or sulfuric acid to grow hexagonal pores at 40-60 nm pitch and AR >60:1 with zero litho; a shallow imprinted pre-texture registers pores to cells, then ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN. Budget: ~$60k electrochemical stations, ~$500k ALD and university fab time, plus the team.

title: B: sliding-ferroelectric bilayer hBN stores bits in stacking order
idea: Use parallel-stacked bilayer hexagonal BN, whose interlayer polarization flips when one layer slides by a third of a bond length (AB to BA), as a gate dielectric; the stacking state shifts the channel threshold and is read non-destructively.
note: Sliding-ferroelectric memory actively pursued (ns, 1e11 cycles shown); aligned wafer-scale bilayers are the gap.

title: Zr: hafnium-free ZrO2 antiferroelectric with built-in bias as bit
idea: Sandwich pure antiferroelectric ZrO2 between electrodes of different work function (e.g., TiN and a Ti-Al alloy) so the double hysteresis loop shifts and one loop straddles zero, giving two stable zero-bias states with a large field-induced switching charge as the signal.

title: Ba: BaTiO3 negative-capacitance layer boosts series storage capacitance
idea: Stack a thin BaTiO3 ferroelectric in series with the cell's linear ZrO2 and tune thicknesses so the ferroelectric runs on its stabilized negative-capacitance branch; the series stack then exceeds the linear capacitor alone, giving more charge per area at the same voltage.
note: NC-boosted DRAM capacitors widely studied; quasi-static stability and hysteresis contested.

title: N: volatile SONOS with 1.5 nm tunnel oxide, direct-tunnel writes
idea: Thin the SONOS bottom oxide to ~1.5 nm so electrons enter the Si3N4 trap layer by direct tunneling in ~10 ns at ~2 V (no Fowler-Nordheim damage, so endurance can approach 1e12+), accept ~seconds retention with ~1% early-decay cells, and refresh at that interval.

title: H: proton-intercalated MoO3 cell holds 16 analog levels for AI
idea: Gate a MoO3 channel through a thin phosphosilicate-glass proton electrolyte so each 5 ns pulse inserts a fixed dose of H+, giving 16 conductance levels; AI weights and KV-cache values are stored natively analog, and ~1% level errors are absorbed by the network's own noise tolerance.

title: Sulfur-vapor conversion of patterned molybdenum gives per-tier MoS2 channels
idea: In each BEOL tier, sputter 1-2 nm Mo pre-patterned into channel islands and convert it to MoS2 in sulfur vapor at ~450 C (no H2S); the 0.65 nm channel keeps electrostatics ideal in a 20 nm lateral transistor and its 1.8 eV gap limits off-current.

title: Titanium dioxide rutile on fluorine-tin-oxide electrodes for compact lateral capacitors
idea: Use conductive F-doped SnO2 (rutile structure, ALD at ~250 C) as the storage-node electrode so ALD TiO2 nucleates directly as rutile (k ~80-100) instead of anatase (k ~30), replacing Ru-templated stacks; 1% Al doping plus a thin Al2O3 interlayer hold leakage.

title: Zirconia antiferroelectric capacitors double stored charge per lateral cavity
idea: Tune ~7 nm ALD ZrO2 (thickness plus Si/Al doping) into an antiferroelectric pinched-loop state whose field-induced polar transition sits just under the 1 V storage voltage, so the capacitor releases ~2x the charge of a linear dielectric of equal area; with no remanent polarization it avoids ferroelectric fatigue.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as a plasma-free capacitor mold
idea: Periodic-table walk, Al+O (13,8): deposit 2-3 um Al over the array, nano-imprint pore seeds aligned to storage-node contacts, and anodize in oxalic/sulfuric acid so vertical pores self-grow at AR >100; open the barrier in H3PO4 and ALD the electrode/dielectric stack inside.

title: Phosphorus ATP trade: spend FLOPs, store KV for every fourth layer
idea: ATP is the cell's currency for spending energy instead of storing work; the model stores KV only for layers 0, 4, 8 and so on, and a small adapter MLP co-trained with the model predicts the skipped layers' K and V from the nearest stored layer at attention time for ~3% extra FLOPs.

title: Zone-refining domain walls: LiNbO3 conducting walls as nondestructive bits
idea: A zone-refining heater sweeps a molten zone through a bar. Here a short pulse sweeps a ferroelectric domain wall across a tiny single-crystal LiNbO3 mesa made by thin-film ion slicing. The bit is whether a conductive wall bridges the electrodes, read as a uA wall current without switching polarization.

title: Asymmetric ferroelectric capacitor read by small-signal capacitance
idea: IFR: read polarization without ever flipping it. Closest achievable: build a ferroelectric capacitor with dissimilar electrodes (e.g. TiN vs WOx) so up and down polarization produce different depletion and thus different small-signal capacitance; a tiny AC probe below the coercive field reads the bit.

title: Germanium-free 3D DRAM stacks using boron-doped silicon sacrificial layers
idea: Ideal: 3D tiers grown from silicon alone. Closest: grow the multi-tier epitaxial stack as alternating undoped Si and heavily boron-doped Si (or Si:C) instead of Si/SiGe, and remove sacrificial layers laterally by dopant-selective electrochemical porosification + oxidation or doping-selective wet etch.

title: Commodity-plastic block copolymer DSA with infiltration-grown alumina hard masks
idea: Ideal: patterns written by molecules for free. Closest: spin high-chi PS-b-P2VP that self-assembles into 16-24 nm-pitch hexagonal cylinders, use sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O) to grow AlOx inside one block as an etch-robust inorganic mask, and guide it with cheap ArF-dry or imprint patterns at 4-6x pitch.
note: DSA defectivity remains the decade-old blocker; 100x claim overstated.

title: Self-ordering anodized-alumina pores as litho-free capacitor molds
idea: Ideal: capacitor holes that pattern themselves. Closest: anodize a thick Al film over the cell array, seeded by shallow DUV-imprinted dimples on the storage-contact grid, so it self-orders into the same honeycomb lattice DRAM already uses (25-35 nm pitch, >100:1 pores); ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN lines the pores, replacing the capacitor-mold lithography and high-aspect-ratio dry etch.

title: Liquid-nitrogen operation turns logic gain cells into seconds-retention memory
idea: Ideal: a transistor that never leaks, so no capacitor is needed. Closest: run capacitorless 2T/3T Si gain cells made in standard logic fabs at 77 K in LN2-cooled memory sleds, where subthreshold and junction leakage fall by >10^6 and retention rises from ~50 us to seconds.
note: Same cryo-leakage mechanism as I-08049, applied to gain cells.

title: 28 nm inline compression buffer that doubles bits per DIMM
idea: Ideal: every bit holds two. Closest achievable at trailing nodes: a 28 nm buffer chip that replaces the RCD/data buffer runs line-rate base-delta and LZ compression with a metadata cache, presenting 1.5-2x logical capacity; KV-cache, zero pages and sparse tensors compress well.

title: Antiferroelectric transition boosts stored charge in standard 1T1C
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): same 1T1C array, sense amps and timings. Replace the ZrO2 dielectric with a tuned antiferroelectric ZrO2/HfZrO film and bias the plate so the 0-to-VARY swing crosses the field-induced AFE-to-FE transition, whose extra polarization charge gives an effective k above 100; the film relaxes back on discharge with no remanence or wake-up.

title: Molecular monolayer doping replaces arsine and phosphine implants
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero toxic hydride gases and no implanter for cell junctions. Graft a self-assembled monolayer of phosphorus- or boron-bearing molecules onto silicon, cap it with oxide and spike-anneal to drive a sub-5 nm conformal junction, which also works on the sidewalls of lateral 3D-DRAM channels that beamline implants cannot reach.

title: Inductive coil links stack DRAM dies without any TSVs
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: stacked dies thinned to <20 um talk through on-chip spiral coils and receive power through heavily doped silicon columns, so there are no TSV etch/fill/reveal steps, no microbumps and no metallurgical joints to grow intermetallics over a decade at 125 C.

title: Compiler-inferred regions shrink garbage-collector headroom to 1.1x
idea: Imposed limit: a managed heap gets 10% headroom instead of 100-200%. Escape analysis assigns allocations to lexical regions that are freed in bulk, and hardware-assisted read barriers allow concurrent compaction with no semispace copy reserve.
note: 10% headroom risks GC thrash; region inference and concurrent compaction are known.

title: Seed-regenerated weights: memory interface synthesizes matrices from tiny seeds
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. Store each weight block as a PRNG seed plus a few combination coefficients; an LFSR basis generator in the memory base die regenerates the block on the fly at read time, trading cheap logic gates for stored bits.
note: Same seed-regeneration mechanism, placed in base die.

title: Substitute hydrogen forming gas with deuterium-in-nitrogen anneal
idea: Substitute the H2/N2 (or argon-diluted) forming-gas anneal with high-pressure D2 in N2 after BEOL. Si-D bonds at access-transistor interfaces resist field- and hot-carrier-driven depassivation ~10x better (kinetic isotope effect), so fewer traps form over the part's life. No rare gas is used at any step.
note: Deuterium anneals known since the 1990s.

title: Substitute die scrap with elastic-capacity SKUs that shrink gracefully
idea: Swap the pass/fail bin for a 'degraded-capacity' product: dies failing retention or defect bins are sold at reduced capacity (e.g., 24 Gb from a 32 Gb die) with an exposed bad-region map that the OS/hypervisor offlines, sold to hyperscalers at a discount.

title: Carbide-scrap tungsten urban mine feeding domestic WF6
idea: Combine U.S. cemented-carbide tool scrap recycling (zinc process plus oxidation to APT) with a domestic tungsten metal and WF6 plant dedicated to fab wordline, contact and DRAM buried-gate metallization.
note: Carbide zinc-process recycling is mature; WF6 plant is the add.

title: HBM speed-bin rejects repurposed into edge inference cards
idea: Combine HBM stacks that fail top speed or thermal bins with lower-clock edge and enterprise inference accelerators designed around derated HBM, sold as a 'B-grade HBM' SKU class.

title: Wine second-label program for partial-good DRAM dies
idea: Adapted from chateaux selling declassified barrels under a second label: dies with one or two dead bank groups are fused off and sold as lower-density SKUs (e.g., 24 Gb from 32 Gb) under a separate brand. Controllers and firmware are told the remapped topology.

title: Zonal car memory pool shares one hot-rated DRAM bank
idea: Minify DRAM per vehicle: a zonal architecture puts one ECC-protected, 125 C-qualified DRAM pool in the central computer and serves zone controllers over PCIe or automotive Ethernet, instead of each ECU carrying its own.

title: Eliminate scrap from partial dies: sell them as JEDEC 24Gb parts
idea: Design 32 Gb DDR5 dies so any one quarter of the array can be fused off; dies with a dead quadrant are configured as the non-binary 24 Gb density already in the DDR5 spec and built into standard 24/48/96 GB modules that hosts already support.

title: Eliminate wide scribes: in-die test structures, plasma dicing, 10 um streets
idea: Move process-control monitors and alignment marks into dummy areas inside the die, shrink scribe streets from ~60-80 um to ~10 um, and singulate by plasma dicing; dies are unchanged JEDEC DDR5/HBM parts.

title: One wordline-cut mask halves every page
idea: Add one cut mask that splits each wordline at mat center, and re-wire the existing interleaved sub-wordline drivers (even rows driven from the left, odd from the right) so each half-wordline is driven from its own side, letting the controller open half-pages independently.
note: Half-page activation is known art (Half-DRAM, sub-wordline segmentation).

title: Closed-loop helium: reverse from venting to recapturing
idea: Rearrange the gas flow: put helium recapture, purification and recompression skids on every etch, implant and backside-cooling tool, and switch backside cooling to H2/N2 mixes where the thermal budget allows.

title: University nanofab packaging commons with an open bonding PDK
idea: Reverse the innovation order: fund a network of ~10 university nanofabs with a shared open PDK for RDL, glass interposers and die-to-die bonding on purchased commodity DRAM dies, so startups prototype memory packaging in months before any commercial line exists.
note: Overlaps CHIPS NAPMP-style prototyping programs.

title: Spare hybrid-bond pads with bit-steering for plasma-activated bonding
idea: Rearrange the bond interface into a repairable bus: HF-free surface prep (N2/O2 plasma activation, water rinse) leaves more bond voids, so each 32-pad group carries 2 spare pads and a bit-steering mux, configured at stack test, that routes around open pads.
note: Spare TSV/pad steering is well-studied.

title: Sampling working-set monitor chip that shrink-wraps container limits
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells: a 180 nm chip on the module samples 1-in-1024 accesses into a count-min sketch per 2 MB region and reports true working sets, letting the OS shrink each container's memory 'shell' to fit and reclaim the remainder to compressed or far tiers.
note: DAMON/TMO do this in software; chip adds accuracy.

title: Probe-free wafer-level retention soaks via on-die BIST
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution: tester-bound retention testing is replaced by on-die BIST that runs multi-hour, multi-temperature retention and hammer profiling while whole wafers sit in U.S.-built burn-in ovens on a power-only contact; results are read out later in one quick touchdown.

title: Unihemispheric-sleep twin subarrays hide refresh behind mirror reads
idea: Dolphins sleep one brain hemisphere at a time; mirror the hottest ~3-5% of rows into twin subarrays of the same bank so reads hit the awake copy while the other copy refreshes, with writes posted to both or tracked by a dirty bit.
note: Subarray-parallel refresh hiding (SALP-style) known; mirroring adds capacity cost.

title: Squirrel scatter-hoarding: distributed national reserves of fab chokepoint materials
idea: Grey squirrels scatter-hoard across hundreds of small caches so no single loss is fatal. Policy: tie CHIPS incentives to every US memory fab holding 90-day rotating caches of helium (ISO dewars), HPQ crucibles, WF6 and Hf precursors, with a pooled inter-fab lending rule during outages, instead of one central stockpile.

title: Palo Verde model: periphery chiplet fab running on reclaimed sewage
idea: Arizona's Palo Verde nuclear plant cools with treated municipal wastewater instead of freshwater. Site a U.S. periphery/logic-chiplet fab beside a city wastewater plant, take tertiary effluent as UPW feedstock, run zero-liquid-discharge with air-cooled chillers, and contract long-term effluent rights.

title: CDO tranching: retention-binned die pools before stacking
idea: Treat dies like loan pools: measure each array die's retention tail and speed at wafer sort, sort into tranches and build stacks only from matching tranches (senior tranche to HBM with relaxed refresh, junior to consumer DRAM), instead of stacking randomly and binning the stack by its worst die.
note: Die binning before stacking is near existing practice; modest yield gain.

title: Interstate-highway policy: national open memory-chiplet interposer shuttle
idea: The federal interstate program set lane standards and paid for the backbone. Do the same here: fund a U.S. open interposer shuttle with a standard memory-chiplet PHY and footprint, so any startup's memory die can be co-packaged with commodity compute on a fixed quarterly schedule.

title: Fiber-Bragg distributed thermometry setting per-mat refresh rates
idea: Fiber Bragg gratings measure temperature every metre along a fiber. Tiny diode or ring-oscillator thermometers are placed in every mat, and each mat's refresh multiplier follows its own temperature: hot spots under an HBM base die or next to a GPU get 2x, cool mats get 1x. Today the whole die refreshes at its worst-case temperature.

title: Ramtron EDRAM/Mitsubishi CDRAM: SRAM Row Cache on Every DRAM Bank
idea: Revive the 1990s Enhanced DRAM and Cached DRAM, which put SRAM row caches beside each bank: a 2-4 row SRAM cache per subarray serves repeated hits (hot KV heads, embedding rows) with no activation and lets the DRAM row close at once, reducing activations that also drive row hammer.
note: EDRAM/CDRAM/Virtual Channel DRAM already did this; AI hit rates uncertain.

title: 28 nm CXL controller with inline zero-line and base-delta compression
idea: Inverts 'compression costs host CPU cycles': a CXL expander ASIC built on existing 28 nm lines removes zero lines and applies base-delta-immediate compression per 64 B line, with a small metadata cache, and exposes about 2x the physical DRAM as logical capacity.
note: CXL compression ASICs already commercial.

title: Deep-trench eDRAM chiplet mosaic from U.S. logic fabs
idea: Invert 'bandwidth must come from dense commodity DRAM': tile 16-32 small deep-trench eDRAM chiplets (IBM-heritage process at GlobalFoundries New York) around the accelerator as a hot tier for activations and KV, packaged in the U.S.

title: Salvage-binned DRAM: fuse off dead banks, sell lower capacity
idea: Inverts 'a die with a dead bank is scrap': map failing banks or channels, fuse them off, and sell 24 Gb parts from 32 Gb die or reduced-channel HBM stacks, the way GPUs are salvage-binned.

title: Rental car: standalone MRAM modules from existing U.S. eMRAM foundry lines
idea: Random stimulus 'rental car' (use someone else's fleet now) -> STT-MRAM modules (CXL/DIMM) are taped out on embedded-MRAM processes already qualified at U.S. 22 nm foundry lines, using spare BEOL capacity with no new fab.

title: Seed library: open-source memory PHY and controller for U.S. startups
idea: Like a seed library lending seeds: fund an open-source LPDDR/UCIe-memory PHY and controller, silicon-proven on an open U.S. MPW, so U.S. chiplet and memory startups skip $5-10M IP licenses.

title: Sticky note: domestic R2R bonding films for HBM stacking
idea: Random stimulus 'sticky note' -> stick, peel, restick. US roll-to-roll coating lines produce temporary bond/debond tapes and non-conductive bonding films (NCF) for thin-wafer HBM stacking, now sourced from a few Japanese suppliers.

title: HBM base die Huffman-codes BF16 exponent planes on write
idea: Box: lossless entropy coding × HBM logic base die × 4 KB tensor tile × on write × static Huffman on the exponent plane. The base die splits BF16 words into raw sign/mantissa planes and an exponent plane coded at ~2.6 bits instead of 8, re-expanding on read, so the stack transparently holds and moves fewer bits.

title: Discounted soft-RAM VMs back 30% of memory with compressed tiers
idea: Box: oversubscribe × cloud pricing × VM × customer opt-in × compressed and remote backing. A VM class sells nominal memory at a discount where the coldest 30% is backed by compressed or remote memory under a published p99 fault-latency SLO.

title: Accelerator SKUs designed to absorb partially failing HBM stacks
idea: Box[Source=HBM stacks with one weak core die x Transform=GPU firmware masks affected pseudo-channels x Integration=unchanged HBM PHY x Owner=GPU vendor x Channel=lower-capacity SKU]: plan reduced-capacity accelerator SKUs that mask defective pseudo-channels, so stacks that fail full test still ship.

title: Po hafnium falls out of reactors: naval-zirconium hafnium chain
idea: Po: 'hafnium is nuclear waste.' Extracted: hafnium is separated only when nuclear-grade zirconium is made, so contract U.S. nuclear zirconium producers to convert their hafnium byproduct directly into HfCl4 and amide precursors at home, and qualify capacitor stacks that accept mixed Hf/Zr feed (HZO-like) so unseparated, cheaper feedstock works.

title: Po the fab has no drain: zero-liquid-discharge with fluoride mining
idea: Po: 'the fab has no drain pipe.' Extracted: segregate wastewater by chemistry, reclaim >90% to UPW feed with RO and electrodeionization, crystallize the brine, and precipitate fluoride as acid-grade CaF2 (a fluorspar substitute) and ammonia as fertilizer for sale.

title: ANS entropy decoder in the HBM base die
idea: Worsen: store bf16 weights raw even though their exponents carry under 3 bits of entropy. Flip: store weights entropy-coded with rANS in HBM and decode them at line rate in logic on the HBM base die, so the GPU sees plain bf16 while the stack holds about 70% of the bytes.

title: Refresh-free cells let memory sit directly on hot logic
idea: Worsen: never stack memory on logic because heat wrecks DRAM retention. Flip: since SRAM and ROM hold state at 105 C+ without refresh, bond them directly on the hottest compute tiles with a copper thermal-pillar grid through the memory, and push any DRAM to the cooler package edge.

title: Wine merchant's vintages: retention-binned DRAM dies sold by grade
idea: Wine is sold by vintage, not poured away for missing Grand Cru. Test every die at 32/64/128/256 ms retention and sell grades: long-retention dies at a premium for phones and laptops, and dies that fail 64 ms (scrapped or heavily repaired today) as 'short-retention' parts run at 16 ms refresh in cache-like or CXL-pool roles.

title: Kidney physiologist cascades rinse water through graded reuse loops
idea: Persona: a kidney physiologist, since nephrons reuse water through counter-current cascades. Meter every rinse stream's conductivity and TOC in real time and route it down a ladder: final rinse, then first rinse, then scrubbers, then cooling tower, then irrigation. Polish the top rung with on-tool EDI, so each litre serves 4-6 duties before discharge.

title: Grain-silo farmer stockpiles helium, quartz and tungsten in strategic reserve
idea: Persona: a farmer who stores grain against drought. Create a U.S. critical-fab-input reserve holding 18-24 months of helium (stored in depleted gas fields), synthetic quartz crucibles, W powder and WF6, neon and fluorochemicals. Finance it with a small fee per wafer start and release stock only above a price trigger.
note: Helium reserves exist (Cliffside); a multi-input fab reserve financed per wafer start is executable policy.

title: Child's 'mom keeps the flashlight': remote lasers outside the hot zone
idea: Lasers wear out fast at 125 C, so keep them where it is cool: a remote laser bank in a 50 C zone sends CW light over glass fibre, and the 125 C memory package holds only athermal SiN-assisted Mach-Zehnder modulators and Ge detectors, with no light source inside.

title: MiG-25 engineer: coarse-pitch mature-node 150 C memory interface
idea: The MiG-25 beat titanium jets with robust steel and tubes: define a 150 C-rated memory chiplet interface using 40 um copper pillars and a 28-65 nm base die built in existing U.S. mature fabs, accepting a bit more energy per bit in return for huge margins.

title: Brain-implant heat rule: DRAM-logic tile mosaic stitched by bonded bridges
idea: A brain implant may not warm tissue 1 C, so heat must never pool under memory; instead of stacking DRAM on hot logic, tile 1 mm DRAM and logic chiplets in a checkerboard mosaic and stitch adjacent edges with a hybrid-bonded bridge die carrying thousands of sub-100 um links. Every logic tile touches four DRAM tiles while no DRAM sits above a hotspot.
note: Thermal win is modest; bridges similar to EMIB.

title: Racing the beam: framebuffer-free composition at scanout
idea: From the Atari 2600, which had 128 bytes of RAM and drew each scanline just in time: display controllers composite UI layers, video planes and overlays line by line from tile lists at scanout, keeping a few line buffers in SRAM instead of triple-buffered 4K/8K framebuffers and intermediate surfaces in DRAM.
note: Display overlay planes already do much of this.

title: Aquifer storage banks winter water for summer fab demand
idea: Time shift from daily to seasonal: inject treated surplus municipal and stormwater into a local aquifer in wet months, then recover it as UPW feed in drought months. This decouples desert fab sites (Arizona, Idaho, Texas) from peak-season shortages.

title: Short-loop micro-line compresses yield learning from years to months
idea: Time-shift the learning loop: a dedicated micro-line runs 30-50-step short-loop wafers containing only the module under study with 5-day cycle times, feeding fixes to the main line instead of waiting for 90-day full-flow wafers.

title: Abandoned molybdenum gates revived as recoverable, US-sourced wordline metal
idea: Molybdenum gates were tried in early MOS and dropped for polysilicon because of oxidation and processing problems. Replace tungsten in buried and 3D wordlines with ALD Mo under a nitride cap that blocks oxidation, and design the stack so the Mo can be selectively leached and recovered at end of life.
note: ALD Mo replacing W is already being adopted industry-wide; end-of-life leaching is the only twist.

title: Fab helium recapture loops, fixing why 1990s recovery was abandoned
idea: Earlier fab helium-recovery efforts were abandoned once helium got cheap. With Qatar offline, add membrane/cryogenic recapture skids on every etch and CVD tool's backside-cooling and purge lines with a site liquefier, switch non-critical purges to argon, and use contracts that reward recaptured volume.

title: DDR5 on-die ECC miscorrection fixed by exposing syndromes to host
idea: DDR5's on-die SEC hides raw errors and can miscorrect a double error into a triple error that host Chipkill then misses. Fix: return the on-die syndrome bits in spare burst slots or a metadata sideband so the host decodes a true concatenated product code that knows which symbols the die already touched.
note: Known problem space (BEER/HARP); the 10x raw-BER claim is overstated.

title: Short mean-free-path molybdenum wordlines from U.S. mines replace tungsten
idea: Below ~15 nm width, line resistivity is dominated by electron mean-free-path scattering, where barrier-less Mo (~11 nm MFP) beats W plus TiN liner. Convert buried wordlines and contacts to Mo CVD, tied to offtake contracts with U.S. molybdenum producers (primary and copper by-product).

title: Al: wire-bonded stacks behind DDR5 buffers free TSV capacity
idea: Build 128-256 GB RDIMMs/MRDIMMs from 4-8-die staggered stacks connected with Al/Cu wire bonds (NAND-style) behind the module's data buffers instead of TSV-based 3DS; the buffers hide the stub loads so the host still sees a standard DDR5 module.
note: LRDIMM-style buffered wire-bond stacks are proven; frees TSV capacity for HBM.

title: Baker's dozen tier: build N+1 legacy dies, cull the weakest
idea: Bakers add a thirteenth roll against shortfalls; stack 9 mature DRAM dies for an 8-high product and route them through a small switch matrix in the base die so the worst tier, by retention or row-hammer threshold, is disabled after assembly test.
note: N+1 die stack with worst tier disabled; same spare-layer remap idea as I-00148.

title: Oil-well drilling: revive U.S. deep-trench eDRAM modules as DRAM bricks
idea: Deep-trench capacitors are drilled into the substrate like oil wells; restart deep-trench eDRAM process modules in U.S. SOI trailing fabs to make stand-alone eDRAM brick chiplets with trench Cs above 10 fF for L4 and near-memory caches.
note: Proven process but ~10x lower density than DRAM; niche cache bricks.

title: Moonshine stills for helium: modular skids on stranded U.S. wells
idea: Like a moonshiner's portable still, skid-mounted membrane and pressure-swing helium purifiers sit on low-volume Kansas, Montana and Arizona gas and nitrogen wells that big plants ignore, filling ISO cryo-containers run on a milk route to U.S. fabs under long-term offtake contracts.
note: Small-well helium purification skids are already commercial.

title: DRAM-free inference pipeline across hundreds of mature-node SRAM chips
idea: IFR: no DRAM at all. Closest using only Si, Al, Cu, Ti, N and O: partition a model layer by layer across many 40-65 nm SRAM-heavy chips (TiSi2 contacts, Ti-barrier Cu, SiON/poly gates, no high-k metal gate) so every weight sits in SRAM beside its MAC, and pipeline large batches through the chain.
note: Groq/Cerebras-style SRAM pipelines; removes DRAM but raises cost per bit.

title: Substitute anhydrous HF-alcohol vapor for dilute HF baths
idea: Etch sacrificial and native oxides with anhydrous HF plus methanol vapor at 30-50 Torr in single-wafer chambers, where adsorbed alcohol catalyzes the etch and byproducts leave as gases, replacing DHF dips and their overflow rinses.
note: Commercial since 1990s.

title: Substitute tungsten wordlines and contacts with chlorine-ALD molybdenum
idea: Replace WF6-based tungsten in buried wordlines, bitline contacts and periphery plugs with molybdenum deposited by ALD from MoO2Cl2, eliminating the TiN barrier and nucleation layers that fluorine chemistry demands. Mo's shorter electron mean free path gives lower resistivity than W below ~15 nm line width.
note: Mo ALD already adopted by industry.

title: Printed photonic wire bonds link memory chiplets to fibers
idea: Substitute sub-micron active alignment of optical engines with two-photon-polymerized freeform waveguides printed in place between laser, modulator chiplet and fiber, so one 3D nanoprinter lets a small team assemble optical memory links.

title: Loadless four-transistor cell held by access-leakage balance
idea: Cross-coupled NMOS drivers with PMOS access devices: in standby, the PMOS off-leakage feeds the high node and outweighs the driver leakage, so the cell latches statically with no refresh (as NEC demonstrated at 180 nm).

title: Deuterium-annealed access transistors slow hot-carrier aging at 125 C
idea: Magnify the isotope mass: passivate Si/SiO2 interface traps with deuterium instead of hydrogen in the final anneal, using D2 from domestic heavy-water electrolysis; the heavier bond resists hot-carrier and BTI desorption 10-50x better.

title: Minify replicas: erasure-coded in-memory stores across the rack
idea: Minify 3x in-memory replication (Redis, caches, Spark persist) to ~1.4x using Reed-Solomon (10,4) striping across rack hosts over RDMA/CXL. Parity is computed in SmartNICs, and a lost shard is reconstructed in microseconds.

title: Eliminate on-die charge pumps: VPP delivered from package PMIC
idea: Remove VPP, VBB and VBLH charge pumps and regulators from every DRAM die; supply them from one high-efficiency package-level PMIC through dedicated backside power vias shared across the stack.
note: DDR4 already takes VPP externally.

title: Eliminate SSD mapping DRAM fleet-wide with zoned flash placement
idea: Mandate zoned namespaces or flexible data placement across storage fleets, so the host writes log-structured and the SSD drops its page-level FTL map, which costs about 1 GB of DRAM per TB of flash.

title: Eliminate new DRAM purchases: CXL boards that re-home retired DDR4
idea: A small hardware team designs a CXL Type-3 card around an off-the-shelf CXL memory controller with 8 DDR4 slots and builds a test-and-bin line, turning DIMMs from decommissioned servers into a far-memory tier.

title: Persistent current instead of leaky charge: niobium flux-loop memory
idea: Reverse decay into perpetuity: each bit is a single flux quantum circulating in a superconducting niobium loop built with the 1990s Nb/AlOx/Nb trilayer process (1-2 um junctions) at 4 K, where current flows forever without refresh; a Josephson junction switches on read depending on loop current.
note: 1980s Josephson memory; density is poor.

title: I/O lands in SRAM, bypassing DRAM bounce buffers entirely
idea: Reverse the I/O path: NICs and SSDs DMA straight into reserved LLC or accelerator SRAM slices under credit-based flow control, and consumers process the data there, so read-once network and storage payloads never stage in DRAM buffers or the page cache.
note: Intel DDIO/DCA already lands I/O in LLC.

title: Self-calibrating sense amplifiers let periphery use relaxed transistors
idea: TRIZ #23 Feedback: each sense amp stores its own offset on its bitline capacitance during a pre-sense calibration phase, and a per-mat trim register is updated at power-up, raising tolerable Vt mismatch from ~10 mV to ~40 mV.
note: Offset-cancellation SAs already in production.

title: Time-multiplex accelerator HBM between inference peaks and training troughs
idea: TRIZ #20 Continuity of useful action: the same HBM pool hosts serving KV caches at diurnal peaks and fine-tuning/eval activations at night, with sub-minute handoff via sharded checkpoints to CXL/flash, so no byte sits idle 12 hours a day.

title: Pacinian-corpuscle auto-zero sense amp responding only to change
idea: Pacinian corpuscles ignore steady pressure and respond only to change. Before the wordline fires, each sense amp stores its own input offset on small capacitors while the bitlines are equalized (auto-zero). It then senses only the change, cancelling latch Vt mismatch.
note: Offset-cancelled SAs already ship in DDR4/DDR5.

title: Brood-to-honey comb reuse time-multiplexes training buffers
idea: Bee comb cells switch from rearing brood to storing honey; the compiler likewise assigns each physical DRAM region a planned succession of roles (forward activation, then gradient, then optimizer scratch) from a global lifetime graph with in-place kernels, so no region idles between roles.
note: XLA/TVM memory planning does this.

title: Artificial-reef carriers house retired DDR4 DIMMs as CXL memory
idea: Coral reefs grow on sunken wrecks; a CXL Type-3 carrier card with standard DIMM slots and an inline compression engine lets operators move retired DDR4 RDIMMs into new servers as a compressed second tier, with tool-less DIMM swaps and the carrier itself reused across server generations.
note: DIMM-slot CXL carriers for retired DDR4; same as I-04900.

title: Liquid-CO2 dry cleaning: supercritical drying stops capacitor pillar collapse
idea: Dry cleaners replaced perchloroethylene with liquid CO2, and textile dyers now dye in supercritical CO2 with no water. After the capacitor-mold wet etch, swap the water/IPA rinse-dry for a supercritical-CO2 exchange-and-vent step so no liquid meniscus ever pulls 60-75:1 pillars together; a process-only change behind an unchanged DDR/HBM interface.

title: Sous-vide nanotwinned copper hybrid bonding at 150 C
idea: Sous vide reaches doneness at low temperature over a long time. Electroplate (111)-oriented nanotwinned Cu pads, whose fast surface diffusion lets Cu-Cu hybrid bonds form at 150 C over several hours in batch ovens.
note: Nanotwinned Cu low-temperature bonding is established prior art (NYCU).

title: Dry cleaning revival: vapor HF and UV-ozone replace wet benches
idea: Revive 1990s anhydrous HF/alcohol vapor oxide etching and UV-ozone organic removal for a large share of the 100+ wet clean steps in a DRAM flow, keeping RCA wet cleans only where particles demand them.

title: Core-plane inhibit wire: bit-level write suppression for low-endurance tiers
idea: Core planes used an inhibit line to stop a bit from flipping; build the same into a university-fabbed ReRAM/PCM array, where each bit driver compares new and stored data and inhibits unchanged bits so a write pulses only the bits that change.

title: Push queries into computational SSDs so buffer pools shrink
idea: Inverts 'a database must cache pages in DRAM to be fast': filters, projections and aggregations run inside SSD controllers next to the flash, so only qualifying rows reach host memory and the buffer pool is sized for results instead of the working set.

title: DIMM reincarnation: retired DDR4 behind 28 nm CXL bridges
idea: Inverts 'retired DIMMs are e-waste': hyperscalers pull DDR4 from decommissioned servers, retest it and mount it on CXL Type-3 cards whose controller is made on existing 28 nm logic lines. The result is a slow but large tier for cold pages and KV spill.
note: Already pursued by Azure/Meta (Pond-style DDR4 on CXL).

title: Pool chlorine tablet: MoCl5-grown molybdenum electrodes replace WF6 tungsten
idea: Stimulus 'pool chlorine tablet' -> deposit storage-node contacts, landing pads and plate electrodes as molybdenum by ALD/CVD from MoCl5 or MoO2Cl2 plus H2 instead of tungsten from WF6; Mo has lower resistivity in narrow features and needs no TiN barrier. Molybdenum is mined in Colorado and Arizona.
note: Industry already adopting Mo ALD for contacts and wordlines.

title: Immune memory: VRT suspects remembered forever via controller Bloom filter
idea: Variable-retention-time cells toggle good/bad and evade one-shot profiling; any address that ever yields a correctable error enters a counting Bloom filter (the 'memory T-cells'), and rows holding suspects get permanent 2x refresh or a stronger code.

title: Display-scrap indium and gallium loop feeding oxide-semiconductor memory
idea: Box [feedstock: spent IGZO sputter targets + end-of-life panels | refining: acid leach + solvent extraction | product: targets and ALD precursors | buyer: BEOL oxide-memory fabs]: contract recyclers to recover In/Ga from spent targets (only ~30% of a target is consumed) and scrapped panels, and recast them as dedicated memory-grade feedstock.
note: Spent ITO/IGZO target recycling is already standard practice.

title: Retrain tokenizers for fewer tokens per document, shrinking KV
idea: Box: fewer tokens × tokenizer × token × next model refresh × larger multilingual/code-aware vocabulary with frequent multi-word merges. New model generations adopt tokenizers that encode the same text in 20–30% fewer tokens, and KV size scales with token count.

title: Organ-donor program: retired DIMMs reborn as a CXL cold tier
idea: Po: dead memory comes back to life. Hyperscalers route decommissioned DDR4/DDR5 through a retest line that builds per-die weak-row maps, then mount the modules behind CXL controllers with strong ECC and map-based row retirement as a cold memory tier for VMs and caches.
note: Azure already reuses DDR4 behind CXL.

title: Heavy-water reactor engineer: deuterium-cured access transistor interfaces
idea: A CANDU operator has tonnes of heavy water on hand. Replace the final forming-gas anneal with a 10-20 atm deuterium anneal so Si/SiO2 and junction dangling bonds are capped with Si-D bonds, which resist hot-carrier and thermal depassivation ~10x better than Si-H and so stop traps from growing into variable-retention cells over life.
note: High-pressure D2 anneal already in production use.

title: Ham radio operator's near-field link: coil-coupled stack without TSVs
idea: Ham operators talk without wires. Put 30-60 um inductive coils in the top metal of every die, glue thinned dies into a stack, and send data die-to-die by near-field magnetic coupling at ~1-8 Gb/s per coil and ~0.1-1 pJ/bit. Power comes in on edge wire bonds, and the design can be taped out on an MPW.
note: ThruChip inductive coupling already demonstrated with DRAM stacks.

title: Deep-sea pressure: high-pressure deuterium anneal heals stacked-tier traps
idea: Deep-ocean hardware shows how pressure drives gas into solids; anneal finished 3D DRAM tier stacks in 20-50 atm deuterium/nitrogen at <=400 C so deuterium penetrates many tiers and passivates the channel and interface traps behind the leakage tail, staying within the stack's thermal budget. Deuterium bonds resist hot-carrier and activation-stress depassivation.

title: N: cryogenic nitrogen aerosol lifts particles with zero liquid
idea: Sweep an expanding jet of N2/Ar cryogenic aerosol (frozen micro-particles) across the wafer so momentum transfer lifts nanoparticles, after which the aerosol sublimes with no residue; use it wherever megasonic DI scrubs are used today.

title: Aluminum remelt: retired DDR4 recast as a CXL far tier
idea: Aluminum is infinitely recyclable; likewise decommissioned servers' DDR4 DIMMs are tested, binned and mounted on CXL Type-3 expander cards whose controller adds stronger ECC and page compression, then deployed as the cold tier under new DDR5 hosts.
note: Same retired-DDR4-on-CXL mechanism as I-04900.

title: Neon closed shells: zero and constant lines never touch DRAM
idea: Neon's full electron shell makes it inert; the controller keeps a 2-bit tag per 64 B line (zero, repeated byte, repeated word, real) in a 0.4%-overhead table cached in controller SRAM, so writes of trivial lines only update the tag, reads are synthesized on chip, and the unused backing lines join a free pool.

title: Pinned-photodiode storage well from 180 nm image-sensor fabs
idea: Fuse the CIS 4T pixel with a DRAM cell. Charge sits in a fully depleted buried n-well whose surface is pinned by p+, away from the Si/SiO2 interface, and is read by a transfer gate onto a floating diffusion and source follower. This is built on existing 180 nm CIS lines.
note: Pixel-scale 4T cells are ~1000x larger than DRAM cells; retention is real but density kills it.

title: LCD active-matrix backplane repurposed as bulk dynamic memory
idea: An LCD pixel is already a 1T1C DRAM cell refreshed at 60 Hz. Depreciated Gen-2/3 a-Si or LTPS lines (2-4 um rules) could pattern huge TFT-capacitor arrays with on-glass sense amps, and very wide rows offset the microsecond row time.
note: Reuse depreciated LCD lines as 1T1C arrays; cost/area falls 100x but density falls far more, so cost/bit worsens.

title: Curie-point magnetic taggants encode material recipe for automated recycling
idea: Mold compound and substrates carry a few mg of ferrite microparticles with chosen Curie temperatures (e.g. 60/90/120/150 C). A recycler sweeps magnetization against temperature to decode the bill of materials and die grade, then routes each part to reuse or the right refinery.
note: Clever Curie-point barcode, but sorting is a niche lever on supply.

title: Wire-in-resin printed packages stack commodity memory BGAs
idea: Substitute substrate layers and TSVs with a printer-robot that embeds insulated fine copper wire inside 3D-printed resin frames as it prints, routing 3D connections between stacked commodity LPDDR packages and the host board.

title: Murray's-law tapered power-tree generator for DRAM periphery
idea: Blood vessels and leaf veins follow Murray's law (parent radius^3 = sum of children's), minimizing transport cost per volume. An open-source EDA plugin synthesizes periphery VDD/VPP/VSS distribution as Murray-tapered trees instead of uniform meshes, with IR-drop sign-off on a test layout. Two engineers plus licenses, ~$600k in 24 months, then licensed to DRAM/eDRAM teams.

title: Physarum flux-reinforcement floorplanner for global data and command buses
idea: The slime mould Physarum thickens tubes that carry flow and prunes the rest, finding near-optimal networks. Its flux-reinforcement model drives the routing of a DRAM die's global data, command and test buses, weighted by real access traces. Software only, ~$400k over 18 months, released and licensed.

title: Lateral-line sensor tape maps helium leaks along every gas line
idea: Fish sense flow along the body with a lateral line of tiny neuromasts. Print a tape of thermal-conductivity microheater sensors every 5 cm (helium conducts heat ~6x better than air) with printed NFC readout, and wrap it along gas sticks, VCR fittings and chuck feeds to locate helium leaks in real time.
