note: Fallout bare dies are more bondable than scrap; LDPC latency suits CXL capacity only.

title: Catt-spiral wafer-scale stacks bonded without known-good-die sorting
idea: Revive Trilogy/Anamartic wafer-scale integration and Ivor Catt's self-configuring spiral: wafer-to-wafer bond 8 whole DRAM wafers; at power-up tiles self-test and chain into a spiral that bypasses dead tiles, while live tiles tolerate up to 1% failing cells through local codes.

title: ELTRAN porous-silicon layer transfer reuses seed wafers twentyfold
idea: Revive Canon's 1990s ELTRAN: anodize a CZ seed wafer into a double porous-silicon layer, grow 1-5 um device-grade epitaxial silicon on it in hydrogen with SiHCl3, bond it to a recycled handle with a thin conductive bond, split at the porous layer by water jet, then re-polish and reuse the seed 10-20 times. DRAM front-end steps run in the low-oxygen epi layer.
note: Wafer is a small cost share; resource angle and low-O epi are the gain.

title: Bell Labs ADPCM codec compresses KV cache along token axis
idea: Put a G.726-style adaptive differential PCM codec in the HBM base die: each key/value channel is predicted from the previous two tokens by a 2-tap adaptive predictor and only a 3-bit residual with adaptive step size is stored, decoded by a tiny MAC in the read path. Full-precision 'key frames' every 64 tokens bound drift.
note: Similar to CacheGen-style token-delta coding; base-die placement is the twist.

title: Denning working-set billing for cloud memory
idea: Price cloud memory by each VM/container's measured working set (Denning 1968, sampled by WSClock in the hypervisor) instead of reserved GiB, auto-demoting untouched pages to compressed or far tiers and exposing the meter to developers.

title: Floppy soft-sectoring revival: per-region code strength formats dry-cleaned dies
idea: Soft-sectored floppies were formatted after manufacture around their actual media defects. After wafer test, firmware formats each subarray with an ECC strength chosen from its measured defect density (none, SECDED, BCH-4 or retire) and records it in a die format table, so the clustered, edge-heavy particle defects of an all-dry clean flow (cryogenic aerosol, radical plasma, vapour HF) cost a few percent of capacity instead of whole dies.

title: Voyager concatenated coding across HBM dies forgives dry-bonded voids
idea: Voyager paired a convolutional inner code with a Reed-Solomon outer code so bursts the inner code missed were cleaned up. In HBM, each die keeps a light inner code while an outer Reed-Solomon code spans corresponding banks of all 12-16 dies (one symbol per die), so a die region lost to a bonding void or open TSV is just an erasure the outer code fills.

title: Hyperscalers consign their own tools inside memory fabs
idea: Inverts 'the fab owns its capital'. A cloud buyer purchases a block of scanners and etchers, consigns them into a memory maker's line, and receives that block's output at cash cost plus a tolling fee, as in chemical tolling.

title: Wide-slow capacity DRAM bins from trailing DRAM lines
idea: Inverts 'DRAM must hit speed bins': existing 2x/1x-nm DDR4 lines run to relaxed timing specs (longer tRCD, lower clock) and allow more repaired rows, tuned for CXL capacity tiers whose latency is already ~200 ns. Looser bins raise yield and the share of each wafer that can be sold.

title: Reclaim ECC lanes for data and guard tensors with checksums
idea: Inverts 'every word needs hardware ECC': a 28 nm CXL controller uses the ECC chips' lanes as extra data capacity for regions holding ML weights and KV. Those regions are protected instead by per-tensor checksums, with a re-fetch from a golden copy on mismatch.
note: Reclaims ~25% capacity for reloadable/tolerant regions; needs controller support.

title: Firmware-defined PHY: one memory stack sold into any standard
idea: Invert 'a DRAM's interface is frozen at tapeout': give the base die a reconfigurable PHY that firmware sets to DDR5, LPDDR5X, wide HBM-like or UCIe/CXL modes, so one stack ships into whichever market is shortest.
note: Pin counts and packages differ across DDR5 and HBM.

title: Buy untested die by the kilogram, grade them in-system
idea: Inverts 'the vendor tests and bins every die': hyperscalers buy dies with only gross-function test, skipping hours of retention and speed test, at a discount; servers run a self-test boot phase, build each die's weak-cell map and place data by quality tier.

title: Hammer-proof zone of shield-row-separated pages for page tables
idea: Inverts 'every wordline must hold data': one cut mask converts every other wordline in 1/32 of each bank into a grounded shield row; the OS places page tables, kernel code and keys only in this zone, where no row has an active neighbor.
note: Hardware version of ZebRAM/CTA page-table isolation.

title: Retrofit mature U.S. DUV fabs with one reliability mask
idea: Inverts 'competitive DRAM needs the newest EUV node': a policy-backed program funds mature 2x-nm DUV lines in the U.S. to add one RDL mask exposing every die's internal ECC syndromes and repair ports to a companion controller chiplet, which applies map-based tolerance so cheap, weaker legacy cells serve AI tiers.
note: Mature-line supply policy with map-based tolerance.

title: Refundable deposit on every memory module, redeemed at certified reuse
idea: Inverts 'memory flows one way to landfill': a bottle-bill-style ~5% deposit on each DIMM/LPDDR module is refunded when it is returned to a certified retest-and-reuse center, guaranteeing a return stream.
note: Bottle-bill model; secondary supply modest share.

title: Harvest wafer-edge die normally lost to nonuniformity
idea: Inverts 'edge die are scrap': shrink edge exclusion and keep the outer ring of die, whose CD and film-thickness drift raises cell faults up to the 1% budget, and sell them in the error-tolerant grade.

title: 200 K cool-not-cryo DRAM retargets Vt to cut wordline voltage
idea: At 200 K the Boltzmann limit falls from 60 to 40 mV/dec, and junction generation (Ea ~0.6 eV) is ~5e6 lower than at 85 C. Run memory sleds at 200 K with single-stage vapor-compression cooling. Spend the leakage windfall by lowering access-transistor Vt by about a third, so at equal Ioff wordline VPP drops from ~3 V to ~2 V and the array from ~1.1 V to ~0.8 V.

title: Negative-charge Al2O3 liner accumulates STI sidewalls against surface generation
idea: Borrow the passivation physics of PERC solar cells and backside-illuminated image sensors. Line the STI trenches next to storage nodes with 3-5 nm ALD Al2O3 carrying ~-3e12 cm^-2 fixed charge. This accumulates holes on the p-type sidewall and pushes the depletion region away from STI interface traps. Surface generation, which scales with Dit x n_i in depletion, falls by orders of magnitude once the surface is accumulated.

title: Voltage-stacked tiers reuse one supply current through four arrays
idea: Power four tier groups in series (0-1 V, 1-2 V, 2-3 V, 3-4 V) so the same current flows through each array once, with interleaved address mapping to balance activity, small push-pull regulators to absorb mismatch and level shifters at tier boundaries.
note: Voltage stacking known in logic; activity balancing across DRAM tiers and level shifting are the risks.

title: Rolling probe-wheel test and laser-fuse repair inline on the web
idea: Run each printed array web under a roller probe that contacts test pads at line speed, measure every mat's retention and margin, and immediately laser-cut printed fuses to remap failing mats to ~3% spares before lamination.

title: Lease bit-hours with guaranteed take-back of every module
idea: First principle: memory's value is the service (bit-hours), not ownership, and ownership strands bits in idle or retired machines. Sell DRAM as a lease priced per GB-month with contractual take-back, embedded serial and health logs, and redeployment of returned modules into lower-tier fleets.

title: Re-patternable EUV mask blanks: strip absorber, keep the multilayer
idea: First principle: an EUV mask's value is its defect-free Mo/Si multilayer blank, and the pattern is just information in the absorber. Add an etch-stop capping layer so the absorber can be stripped without damaging the blank, and rewrite the same blank with a new pattern when a design is revised.

title: Open repair-port mandate lets anyone rebin and repair DRAM
idea: First principle: every DRAM already holds spare rows and post-package-repair fuses; only the access is closed. Create a JEDEC standard and a procurement rule requiring a documented, authenticated repair interface (PPR, fuse map, test modes) on all DRAM, so third parties can repair and rebin used and marginal parts.

title: Entropy-sized pointers: hardware 32-bit region-relative pointer storage
idea: A 64-bit pointer inside a heap carries only log2(reachable objects), about 28-34 bits of information. The allocator sets a per-page pointer-map bit; the memory controller stores tagged words as 32-bit offsets from a per-1 GB region base held in page metadata and re-expands them on load.

title: Single-copy capability fabric across kernel, driver and framework
idea: In an AI or analytics pipeline, data often sits in 3-5 copies (page cache, user buffer, framework tensor, pinned staging, device memory). Make physical frames capability-owned: storage DMA lands once in a CXL-shared frame, and ownership moves by updating a page-table capability enforced by the IOMMU instead of by memcpy.

title: Memory-in-pixel panels absorb the framebuffer out of DRAM
idea: A display backplane already is a memory: every pixel has a TFT and a storage capacitor on glass. Put a 1-3 bit latch or oxide-TFT gain cell in each subpixel (memory-in-pixel) and composite static layers directly in the panel, so phones, laptops and VR headsets stop keeping triple-buffered framebuffers and static layers in DRAM.
note: Sharp MIP exists; 1-3 bits per subpixel is too few for HDR color.

title: Active interposer sums partial results while data travels
idea: Bits that will be added together should never travel separately. Make the interposer an active 28 nm die with reduction trees at routing junctions between HBM stacks and compute tiles, so all-reduce, gradient accumulation and partial-sum merging happen inside the wire and only reduced results reach the GPU.

title: Erasure-coded subarrays give on-die chipkill at 3x defect density
idea: Die yield follows exp(-A*D0). Spare rows fix point defects, but one dead subarray or sense-amp stripe kills the die. Stripe each access across 18 subarrays as RS(18,16) symbols, so any two dead subarrays are erased by fuse map.

title: JEDEC raw-BER memory class with mandatory host code
idea: Propose a JEDEC/OCP device class specified by raw bit-error rate (e.g., <=1e-6 per bit per second) instead of all-cell 64 ms retention. In exchange, the host must implement a defined end-to-end code and scrub rate.

title: Read-verify-only refresh for non-destructive gain cells
idea: With no capacitor, a 2T/3T gain cell stores the bit on the read transistor's gate and reads it non-destructively as current. Refresh becomes a cheap read scan against a 'decay-warning' threshold set above the decision level, and only the ~0.1-1% of cells crossing it are rewritten.
note: Read-scan refresh of non-destructive cells; refresh energy only.

title: National open physics-of-failure testbed for capacitorless cells
idea: CHIPS/NIST funds a shared lab that runs standardized retention, disturb, endurance and VRT stresses on any capacitorless cell (gain, floating-body, volatile MRAM, domain-wall). It publishes raw distributions and activation-energy-based acceleration models.

title: Open patent pool for abundant-element process substitutions
idea: Qualification cost scales with test-hours, not with the number of fabs, yet every fab re-qualifies substitutes alone and patents are scattered. A government-seeded pool licenses all abundant-element substitutions (TiN for W, ZrO2 for HfO2, Zn-Si-O for IGZO) FRAND at a flat per-wafer fee and publishes shared HTOL and retention data.

title: Gear-shift bitline restore through stepped reservoir rails
idea: Random stimulus 'bicycle gears': climb the hill in small steps instead of one strain. During refresh the sense amp swings bitlines to VARY in four steps via switched on-die reservoir capacitors (0.25/0.5/0.75 VARY) that are recharged by the previous row's discharge, instead of one hard swing from the rail; refresh has timing slack, so the slower adiabatic swing costs no bandwidth.

title: Castle moat liner with negative fixed charge around storage junction
idea: Random stimulus 'castle moat': a ring that repels attackers before they reach the wall. Line the isolation trench beside each storage-node junction with ALD Al2O3 carrying ~-5e12 cm^-2 fixed charge (borrowed from solar-cell field passivation), accumulating holes at the junction periphery and pinching the depletion region where trap-assisted and GIDL leakage live.

title: Junkyard-magnet gettering band under every array mat
idea: Random stimulus 'junkyard crane magnet': pull the scrap out before it does damage. Form a carbon-implanted, oxygen-precipitate gettering band 1-2 um below each mat that captures Fe, Cu and Ni atoms which would otherwise sit in junctions as single deep-level traps, the usual root of fA-scale retention-tail outliers.
note: Modern DRAM tails are dominated by GIDL/TAT at intrinsic defects, not metals; 10x tail shrink unlikely.

title: Tea-bag vapor monolayer doping grades the storage junction
idea: Random stimulus 'tea bag': steep it gently and the dose is set by contact. Dose the storage-node side of the vertical channel with a self-limiting vapor-phase phosphorus-precursor monolayer, cap it in situ and flash-anneal; one dry cycle gives a conformal, deliberately graded, low-peak junction on every pillar face.
note: Monolayer doping known (Javey); applied to graded storage junction.

title: Thermostat-dial controller trades refresh rate for cooling water hourly
idea: Random stimulus 'thermostat dial': one knob, two costs. The memory controller publishes a live curve of refresh overhead versus HBM temperature; the facility's cooling optimizer runs memory hotter (refresh doubles per ~10 C) during hot afternoons instead of switching cooling towers to evaporative mode, and lets memory cool down on cool nights.
note: Memory is a small share of facility heat; water claim overstated.

title: Ration-book liters-per-gigabit ceiling for subsidized DRAM fabs
idea: Random stimulus 'ration book': a fixed allotment forces clever cooking. Tie U.S. memory subsidies to a published liters-per-Gb ceiling for the access-device FEOL that steps down 10x over eight years, with bonus credits for adopting dry clean, dry resist, area-selective deposition and product-level refresh-energy cuts.

title: Swiss cheese: two partial-good dies packaged as one standard DDR5 die
idea: Cheese with holes still sells by the block: bin dies with dead banks or mats, then package two complementary partial dies with a tiny bridge die that steers each bank address to whichever die has it working. The package is one standard 16/24/32 Gb DDR5 device, and dies scrapped today become product.
note: Bridge-die bank steering adds latency; supply gain ~5-10%.

title: Postage stamp: half-inch minimal fab for oxide gain-cell tiles
idea: Stimulus 'postage stamp' -> a 10-person team runs a minimal-fab line (half-inch wafers, sealed local shuttles, no cleanroom) making zinc-tin-oxide gain-cell memory tiles below 400 C, bonded onto logic chiplets as near-memory.
note: Half-inch wafers give tiny bit output; cost per bit poor despite low capex.

title: Vending machine: bill memory per compressed resident byte-second
idea: Pay for what drops out of the machine: cloud providers meter memory by actual resident bytes after compression and dedup, sampled each second, instead of allocated GB, plus a discounted 'evictable' class; every developer gains a direct reward for compressing, freeing and sharing.

title: Customs declaration: pages declare tolerated error for lossy compression
idea: Goods declare their contents at the border: add 2 tolerance bits to page-table entries (exact, 1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1 relative error) that runtimes set for activations, gradients and embeddings, letting the memory controller apply lossy codecs (mantissa truncation, block floating point) to tagged pages. OS and firmware only.
note: Approximate memory tagging studied (Flikker etc.).

title: Lighthouse rotation: a vacated rotating subarray enables continuous online stress testing
idea: One subarray per bank is always empty and the vacancy sweeps around the bank like a lighthouse beam (data moved by in-DRAM row copy); while empty, it is stress-tested at full speed for retention, hammer and VRT and the weak map is updated with no downtime.

title: Bonsai pruning: planned capacity shrink retires weakest rows yearly
idea: Instead of every cell meeting 10 years at 125 C at fab, the module ships with a declared pruning curve and asks the OS (CXL/ACPI hot-remove) to offline its weakest ~0.5% of rows per year based on in-field aging data, under a contractual capacity schedule.

title: Quilt: inkjet adaptive interconnect stitches mismatched salvaged die into modules
idea: Random stimulus 'patchwork quilt' -> odd scraps make a blanket. Salvaged die of mixed vendors and sizes are placed roughly on a panel; a camera maps actual positions and inkjet/aerosol-jet prints a custom redistribution layer for every module.

title: Element passport: incentives only for cells built from domestic elements
idea: Box constraint as policy: CHIPS and DPA Title III funds and a federal purchasing preference go only to storage-element stacks whose every element (e.g., Si, Al, B, N, O, Hf, Zr, Mo, Cu, Zn, Fe, Ti, Pt/Pd, V, Te) has U.S. primary production, with matched loans for domestic high-purity Hf/Zr/Mo ALD-precursor plants. Each cell design files a bill of elements traced to a U.S. mine or refinery.

title: Floating-gate offset trim written into each sense amp at test
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x trimmed latch x planar x bulk Si x one added embedded-floating-gate mask. Each SA includes a small floating-gate transistor programmed at wafer sort to null its measured Vt mismatch, cutting input-referred offset from ~20 mV to ~2-3 mV.
note: Nonvolatile FG trim of SA Vt; known analog trick, embedded FG mask adds cost to DRAM flow.

title: Dead-zone sense amps flag uncertain bits as erasures, not errors
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x dual-offset comparator with dead zone x per-column flag bit x bulk Si x standard. Each SA has two skewed comparators; when they disagree the bit is marked erased, and since Reed-Solomon corrects twice as many erasures as unknown errors, a 1% raw BER that is mostly flagged costs only ~4-6% parity.

title: CHIPS tranche paying per kilogram of rare gas designed out
idea: Box [lever: federal memory incentive | metric: kg He/Ne/Ar/Kr/Xe avoided per wafer | verification: tool-level mass-flow logging | kicker: guaranteed DoD offtake for certified rare-gas-free memory]: pay fabs per audited kilogram of rare gas eliminated and give certified flows priority procurement.

title: Sub-page hardware meshing merges fragmented heap pages without moving objects
idea: Box: defragment × page-table extension × 1 KB chunk × background scan × chunk-mask PTE. A 4-bit chunk map in each PTE lets two virtual pages whose live 1 KB chunks do not overlap share one physical frame, so the allocator reclaims fragmentation while every pointer stays valid.
note: Hardware version of Mesh allocator.

title: Hot remote memory sleds rejecting heat through dry air coolers
idea: Box: DRAM or gain cell with retention tuned for 105 C x standard x standard x optical CXL link x air-cooled sled x standard. Memory moves out of liquid-cooled accelerator packages into separate sleds running at 45 C inlet, cooled by dry coolers with no evaporative towers.

title: ReRAM CAM repairs individual failing bits in the field
idea: Box [medium: capacitor + side ReRAM CAM | access: standard | sense: standard + CAM match | integration: monolithic BEOL | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. A 64k-entry ReRAM content-addressable table in the periphery stores failing-cell addresses found by boot-time BIST and supplies the replacement bit on a match, dropping repair granularity from whole rows or columns to single bits.

title: Regulatory idle-watts-per-terabyte metric forcing refresh-aware servers
idea: Po: refresh is illegal. Add a measured idle-memory-watts-per-TB line to server efficiency rules and large procurement specs (ENERGY STAR, EU ecodesign, federal data-center buys), tested in self-refresh, so vendors must ship temperature-compensated refresh, partial-array self-refresh and OS free-page hints enabled by default.

title: Constant-bias field plate over storage junction suppresses GIDL
idea: Po: the drain sees no electric field. Split the buried wordline into an active gate over the channel and a separate field-plate segment over the storage-node overlap held at a fixed mild positive bias, so the gate-to-drain field that drives band-to-band GIDL never forms even while the active gate sits at negative hold.

title: Refresh-free device class written into standards and procurement
idea: Po: refresh is outlawed. Propose a JEDEC device class 'RF0' plus a CHIPS procurement preference: devices advertise per-region guaranteed retention, controllers carry data-expiry semantics (reads after expiry return poison), and refresh commands are optional, creating a market for long-retention 3D cells and lifetime-aware software.
note: Standards pull is executable; market impact depends on long-retention cells existing.

title: Po fab tools are open-source: cloned 1990s equipment designs
idea: Po: 'semiconductor tools are open-source like Linux.' Extracted: fund a public library of reverse-engineered, patent-expired 1990s tool designs (i-line/KrF steppers, LPCVD furnaces, RIE, implanters) and certify U.S. machine shops to build them, so new 200 mm memory lines need not wait on a shrinking used-tool market.
note: Legacy 200 mm lines cannot make cost-competitive DRAM.

title: Strategic memory reserve buys gluts, contracts legacy U.S. lines
idea: Po: the government buys RAM like oil. A U.S. strategic DRAM reserve buys bits in price troughs and releases them in shortages, paired with long-term offtake contracts at existing domestic legacy DRAM lines (auto/industrial parts), smoothing the cycle that deters investment.

title: Wavelength-addressed rack memory pool with passive grating routers
idea: Po: an address is a colour. Each pooled DRAM module owns a laser wavelength, and a passive arrayed-waveguide grating router connects any accelerator to any module just by tuning its transmitter, so no electronic switch sits in the memory path.

title: Universal pre-built interposer customised by a single via mask
idea: Po: every package uses the same package. Pre-fabricate a standard interposer with a dense crossbar of horizontal and vertical lines in volume, and personalise each product with only one via mask that connects chosen crossings.

title: Wafer-sibling weak-cell maps predict faults across a fleet
idea: Po: a die inherits its siblings' diseases. Every DIMM uploads in-field error and weak-row logs keyed by wafer lot and die (x,y); a fleet database learns spatial signatures such as edge-ring capacitor bowing and pushes predicted weak rows to sibling dies' controllers, which boost refresh on those rows or retire them before the first error.

title: Move retention screening out of the fab and into boot
idea: Po: the factory never tests retention. Vendors skip the long multi-temperature retention test on ATE and ship with mandatory on-die BIST that profiles retention during first boots and idle periods, burning a weak-row map into antifuses and retiring or refresh-boosting rows in the field.
note: Shifts test cost to BIST; VRT risk.

title: Small-die variants that harvest partial reticle fields at wafer edge
idea: Po: the wafer edge is the most valuable land. The reticle carries the main 24-32 Gb die plus a 4-8 Gb small die built from the same array mats; partial fields at the wafer edge, normally lost, are diced into small dies for IoT, auto and embedded markets.
note: Small die in every field costs interior area unless edge uses separate reticle.

title: Negabyte rebates that pay software to shrink memory footprint
idea: Po: memory is negative. Like utility negawatt programs, cloud providers and governments pay software vendors a rebate per GB-hour of verified footprint reduction (fleet telemetry against a baseline), funded by avoided DRAM purchases.

title: Deliberately imperfect bits: shorter capacitors for AI tensor mantissas
idea: Worsen: insist every bit of every byte meet 1e-15 error at worst-case retention. Flip: build a tolerant cell class with ~40% less capacitor height for neural-network weights and activations; sign and exponent bits live in full cells while low-order mantissa bits live in short cells refreshed rarely.
note: Similar to Flikker-style approximate DRAM; two capacitor heights add process cost.

title: JEDEC retention-negotiated refresh replaces fixed 32/64 ms
idea: Worse: standardize the worst-case refresh interval for every die ever made. Flip: a JEDEC spec in which each device advertises its measured, temperature-indexed refresh need and the controller negotiates the interval, with a mandatory on-die guard canary.

title: Ship lightly repaired dies with exported bad-row maps, NAND-style
idea: Worse: scrap any die whose defects exceed on-die fuse and spare-row capacity, and keep growing redundancy area. Flip: ship dies with minimal spares plus an exported defect and weak-row map that the memory controller uses to remap rows, the way NAND controllers handle bad blocks.
note: NAND-style bad-row maps need ecosystem/JEDEC buy-in.

title: Helically twisted vertical bitline pairs cancel coupling noise
idea: Worse: run neighboring vertical bitlines in parallel through 100 tiers so their mutual coupling swamps a 5 fF cell signal. Flip: swap the positions of each bitline pair every N tiers through staggered intra-stack crossover vias, so aggressor coupling cancels like a twisted-pair cable.
note: Twisted bitlines are known in planar DRAM; vertical crossover vias are the new part.

title: U.S. fluorine from phosphate-fertilizer fluorosilicic acid waste
idea: Worsen: buy the fluorine behind HF, NF3 and WF6 from Chinese and Mexican fluorspar. Flip: capture the fluorosilicic acid (H2SiF6) already scrubbed at Florida and Louisiana phosphate plants, convert it to anhydrous HF plus high-purity silica, and feed domestic electronic-grade NF3/HF plants.

title: N+1 spare core die with TSV bypass crossbar in HBM
idea: Worsen: make every die in a stack a single point of failure. Flip: add one spare core die and a programmable TSV crossbar in the base die. A die that fails at test or in the field is fused out and its channels remapped to the spare, repairing the stack in place.

title: Recovered Memory Credit counts reused bits toward CHIPS targets
idea: Worsen: give subsidies only for new fab wafers, so a reused bit earns nothing. Flip: create a U.S. Recovered Memory Credit in CHIPS and federal procurement, where certified reused or repaired GB count toward supply targets, backed by extended producer responsibility take-back for servers.

title: Substrate-agnostic memory qualification standard unlocks non-silicon suppliers
idea: Worse: write qualification specs that implicitly assume bulk-Si dies and block every alternative. Flip: create a JEDEC/OCP 'memory tile' standard defined only by electrical, thermal and reliability behavior plus a tile form factor, with funded shared qualification labs, so glass, SiC or ceramic memory is qualified once and bought widely.

title: Compress before encrypt with type-tagged controller codecs
idea: Worsen: encrypt memory first so every byte looks random and nothing compresses. Flip: put a compression stage ahead of the memory-encryption engine, choosing a codec per page type tag (float-exponent, pointer-delta, small-int, text) and storing ciphertext of the compressed line.
note: Size side-channel leakage is the key doubt for confidential VMs.

title: Yield-elastic stacks binned by good-bank count, not die count
idea: Worsen: scrap a 12-high stack because one die has a bad bank, compounding loss with height. Flip: design the base die to remap at bank granularity across dies and sell stacks by working-bank count (e.g., 12 dies sold as 10.5-die capacity), so partially bad dies go into product instead of scrap.

title: Nondestructive-read multicast: one row read serves many requesters
idea: Worsen: use destructive reads so every read is written back and each requester triggers its own activation. Flip: with capacitorless nondestructive cells (gain cells, SRAM), let the interface broadcast one row read to all subscribed chiplets via a multicast tag, with no restore phase.

title: Sense reference that slides with time since last refresh
idea: Worse: sense a cell that has decayed for 60 ms against the same fixed VDD/2 reference used for a freshly written one. Flip: each bank keeps a timestamp of its last refresh, and a DAC lowers the '1'-side reference along the measured decay curve, so sensing stays centered on the shrinking signal and the retention window stretches.
note: Helps median decay, not fast-decaying tail cells.

title: Right-to-raw-errors mandate opens on-die ECC telemetry to hosts
idea: Worse: keep on-die ECC corrections hidden so hosts cannot see weakening rows until they fail. Flip: make CHIPS-funded purchases and JEDEC standards require DRAM to expose per-row corrected-error counters, retention bins and hammer counts through a standard health interface, so host software can do adaptive refresh, retirement and tiering.

title: Titanium-magnesium hydrogen getter shields zinc-oxide channels from drift
idea: Worse: let hydrogen from passivation films and packaging diffuse into ZnO-family channels, where it acts as a donor and shifts threshold. Flip: deposit a thin Ti/Mg getter layer (abundant, hydride-forming) above the oxide-semiconductor tier and inside the package seal so stray hydrogen is chemically captured before it reaches the channel.
note: Hydrogen control in oxide TFTs is a known concern; getter approach plausible.

title: Memory-footprint labels and app-store fees on bloated software
idea: Worse: let apps ship duplicate runtimes and 2-3x bloat because RAM is treated as free. Flip: app stores, browsers and cloud marketplaces publish a measured resident-memory score per app and apply ranking penalties or listing fees above a category baseline, feeding a memory-efficiency bounty pool.

title: Guide-star dummy bitline cancels mat-wide noise in real time
idea: Astronomers measure atmospheric blur on a guide star and subtract it. Each mat keeps a dummy bitline pair whose cell holds a known value; its deviation at sense time measures the instantaneous common disturbance, which is fed forward to every SA reference node in that mat within the same strobe.
note: Reference/dummy arrays already cancel much common-mode noise.

title: Immune patrol: margin sweep on a test row during REF
idea: An immune system samples for threats constantly. During each REF command the die spends a few ns reading a reserved per-bank test row at a slightly shifted precharge level and keeps a running estimate of the best VBLP, re-centering the sense eye as cells and SAs age.

title: Monk's quiet hour: sense strobes dodge output-driver noise
idea: A monk prays when the monastery is quiet. An on-die scheduler knows when other banks' read bursts switch the DQ drivers and shifts each sense-amp strobe by up to ~500 ps inside tRCD slack so latching never coincides with output supply noise.

title: Shopkeeper's open recipe: public pitch-matched periphery compiler
idea: A shopkeeper sells flour, not only finished bread. Fund an open generator for pitch-matched sense amps, sub-wordline drivers, fuse boxes and DDR5/HBM PHYs, qualified to JEDEC specs, so new U.S. DRAM entrants spend effort on the array, not on decades of hidden periphery know-how.

title: Ballroom mirror twins: one self-mating die forms a two-high stack
idea: Two identical dancers form a pair by mirroring. Design one die whose bond-face pad map is 180-degree symmetric, then wafer-to-wafer bond two identical wafers, one rotated. A mode fuse makes one die's periphery serve both arrays and power-gates the twin's.

title: Soviet vacuum-tube engineer's all-inorganic hermetic memory package
idea: Soviet tubes lasted because they held no organics: build the memory-logic package with zero polymers, using a glass core, Cu-Cu hybrid bonds, CVD SiCN/SiO2 gap-fill instead of underfill and mould, and an anodically bonded glass lid filled with dry nitrogen.
note: Polymer-free package for 125 C qualification; reliability niche.

title: Utility lineman's high-voltage lines: 12 V delivery into the stack
idea: Linemen send power at high voltage to cut current: deliver 12 V up a few power TSVs and convert to ~1 V with switched-capacitor converters in the memory base die, cutting the current per power via about 10x.

title: Monk's vow of simplicity: RAM-Star label for lean software
idea: Take a monk's austerity: federal procurement adopts a 'RAM Star' certification, modeled on Energy Star, that requires software to meet memory-footprint benchmarks per workload (browsers, Java services, containers), backed by runtime guidance (compressed pointers, arena allocators, page sharing).

title: Bottle-deposit grandmother: refundable deposit on every memory module
idea: Like a bottle deposit, add a refundable $2-5/GB deposit when DIMMs and LPDDR boards are sold, paid back when the module is returned to a certified refurbisher. This guarantees a steady reverse-logistics flow for harvesting and reuse.

title: Charge-coupled serial memory tier for streaming camera frame buffers
idea: Edge cameras write and read frames sequentially, so bits are stored as charge packets in a CCD-style buried channel and clocked along gates with no per-bit access transistor or contact; random access happens at block granularity through a small SRAM head. Each bit occupies ~2-3F2 with no capacitor pillar.
note: Sequential-only niche; CCD transfer efficiency and latency limit to frame-buffer tiers.

title: Mask-selected ferroelectric phase makes hybrid volatile and persistent mats
idea: Industrial controllers want working memory that snapshots on power loss; a thin Si- or La-oxide dopant sublayer is deposited blanket before the ZrO2 dielectric and the single added mask strips it from ordinary mats, so on anneal the doped mats crystallize orthorhombic (ferroelectric) and the rest tetragonal (linear high-k). One die carries DRAM mats and persistent ferroelectric mats from one flow.
note: Twist on NVDRAM HZO work; dopant control in pillars.

title: Single cut-mask splits each pillar into differential twin half-capacitors
idea: Avionics users fear neutron upsets; one added cut mask slices each cylindrical bottom electrode into two half-shells, each on its own access path, storing complementary charges. Reading the pair differentially doubles signal per stored charge, removes reference cells and half-VDD bitline noise, and a strike on one half cannot flip the comparison alone.

title: Segmented plate-line bootstraps stored charge for 0.4 V harvesters
idea: Thermoelectric-harvesting IoT runs at ~0.4 V; one cut mask splits the common capacitor plate into per-row plate lines so the selected row's plate is pulsed during read, bootstrapping the stored node ~2x before charge sharing. The bit is written at low array voltage yet read with a full-size signal.
note: Plate-line drivers add area; plate pulsing is known.

title: Hyperscaler fleet learning: refresh set from wafer-map telemetry
idea: A hyperscaler runs millions of DIMMs. Log correctable-error and retention telemetry against each die's fab ID (lot, wafer, X-Y) to build a fleet model of retention by wafer position and process lot; new DIMMs get per-bank refresh rates from that model at install, with no slow per-row profiling.

title: AR-glasses budget: drop the negative-wordline pump and cut VPP
idea: AR glasses have milliwatt memory budgets. Lower the wordline high from ~3 V to ~2.2 V and remove the negative-wordline charge pump, lowering access Vt to keep write speed; the higher off-current and occasional incomplete writes push raw BER toward 1%, which the code tolerates.

title: Twin decaying reference cells written alongside every row
idea: Downhole tools at 200 C see retention collapse to milliseconds; each row carries two reference cells written '1' and '0' at the same instant as its data, and at read they are charge-shared into a mid-level reference that sags exactly as the row's own '1' cells leak. Sensing becomes relative instead of absolute.

title: Completion-detecting self-timed sense amps remove worst-case guard bands
idea: Asynchronous circuits built for deep-space radiation and 30-year aging corners signal when they are done; dual-rail SA outputs feed a completion tree per mat that fires column access as soon as every latch has resolved, instead of waiting a fixed tRCD set by the slowest cell at end of life.

title: Dual-threshold margin sensing sets each row's own refresh interval
idea: Like event cameras that report only changes: during refresh, a second coarse comparator in each SA stripe flags whether any cell in the row came in below a 'healthy' margin window. Healthy rows skip the next 1-3 refresh rounds; only flagged rows keep the base rate, driven by measured margin instead of a static profile.

title: Bit-significance-tiered sense amps: big for MSBs, tiny for LSBs
idea: KV-cache and weight tensors tolerate errors in low mantissa bits: columns mapped to sign and exponent bits get large offset-compensated SAs, while LSB columns get minimum-size latches running at ~1e-4 BER with relaxed refresh. The controller fixes the bit-to-column layout.

title: Bitcoin-miner siting: DRAM fabs at stranded hydro and flare gas
idea: Crypto miners chase stranded megawatts in Pacific Northwest hydro, Texas flare gas and curtailed wind. Site new U.S. DRAM capacity at those nodes with interruptible-load contracts covering deferrable loads (abatement, UPW heating, test and burn-in) and cold-climate free cooling for chillers.
note: Fabs need firm power; interruptible share limited to deferrable loads.

title: Wartime materials board: per-gigabyte chokepoint-intensity procurement standard
idea: WWII production boards rationed tin and rubber by making designers report and cap use per unit. Require a certified 'chokepoint ledger' per gigabyte (mg W, liters He, g HPQ, g PFAS, liters UPW) for CHIPS-funded and DoD purchases, with price preferences for parts under a declining cap, like CAFE standards for memory.

title: Venus-lander silicon carbide gain cell: retention measured in years
idea: NASA's SiC JFET ICs have run for a year at 460 C in Venus conditions, and at room temperature the same 3.3 eV bandgap makes storage-node leakage ~1e-21 A. Build a 2T SiC gain cell that stores charge on a JFET gate junction, so memory needs no refresh, no capacitor dielectric and no tungsten.

title: Constellation-satellite short-life qualification trims barrier and liner metals
idea: Satellite constellations fly parts qualified for 5 years, not 25, and AI-accelerator DRAM is scrapped after ~4 years. Define an 'AI-life' DRAM grade with 4-year electromigration and TDDB targets that allows thinner TaN/TiN barriers and liners, Al instead of W in periphery local interconnect, and reduced reliability guardbands.

title: Depreciation-zero heritage-node DRAM consortium for 30-year industrial users
idea: Extreme user: industrial and rail customers who want a part frozen for 30 years. A consortium buys written-off 20-25 nm DRAM fabs, freezes an open process design kit, and runs it at near-zero depreciation for industrial/auto/IoT bits, moving those volumes off leading-edge lines.

title: Swappable cartridge chamber liners replace NF3 plasma cleaning
idea: Extreme user: a submarine or habitat fab where no fluorine gas may be stored. Deposition tools get quick-change ceramic/quartz liners that a robot swaps every N wafers; spent liners are cleaned offline by bead blasting or hot KOH, and metal deposits are cleaned in situ with Cl2.

title: Nanoimprint arrays with non-fluorinated hydrocarbon release layers
idea: Extreme user: medical-sensor makers who already require PFAS-free supply chains. Print DRAM array layers by jet-and-flash nanoimprint whose quartz templates use octadecyl-silane or DLC anti-stick coatings instead of fluorosilanes, with a shrink-releasing resin.

title: Climate-model error contracts: malloc with a declared tolerance
idea: From climate and CFD codes that already accept lossy float compression: add malloc_lossy(size, abs_err) so the OS maps the region through a controller-side fixed-rate block-transform codec that guarantees the bound, with the bound recorded in the page table entry and checked by the codec on every write-back.

title: Subsea-repeater cold spare: an unpowered extra die per stack
idea: Undersea cable repeaters carry unpowered cold spares through a 25-year unserviceable life. Add one unpowered DRAM die to each HBM/3DS stack, with a base-die crossbar that moves a degrading die's contents to the spare and remaps its channels once its corrected-error rate crosses a threshold. Powered-off silicon accumulates no BTI, hot-carrier or hammer stress.

title: Exascale checkpoint inside DRAM: RowClone shadow rows for rollback
idea: Exascale machines survive frequent faults through checkpoints. Add an in-DRAM SNAPSHOT command that copies a row to a shadow row in a reserved subarray by bitline copy (~90 ns, no bus traffic). When an uncorrectable error hits, the runtime rolls back to the shadow copy instead of killing the job.

title: Coal-mine canaries: deliberately weak sentinel rows in every subarray
idea: Fabricate 2-4 canary rows per subarray with ~30% less capacitance, so they fail first as temperature, aging or hammer stress rises. The DRAM's internal logic samples them during standard REF slots. When canaries flip, it quietly spends extra internal refreshes on that subarray, the same way TRR already does, all within the unchanged DDR5/HBM REF protocol.
note: Weak-Cs canaries may not mirror rare trap-driven VRT tail cells.

title: Dead-die HBM stacks: GPU remaps around dead channels, stacks still ship
idea: Treat HBM stacking yield as the extreme case. A stack with one defective die is normally scrapped after the costly stacking step. Instead, sell it as a 7/8-capacity part: its SPD-style descriptor lists the dead die's pseudo-channels, and the GPU memory controller compacts its address map around them over the unchanged HBM interface.

title: JEDEC refresh-hint command lets software own retention time
idea: Scale shift from silicon to standards: define a REFHINT/RETAIN command for DDR6, LPDDR6 and CXL.mem carrying per-range 'live until' and 'tolerates N errors' fields that DRAM self-refresh logic honours, plus a vendor-published per-bank retention-curve register.

title: Atomic aluminate dipole sets threshold, channel left undoped
idea: Scale shift from statistical dopant atoms (~10-20 randomly placed per channel at F=12 nm) to one deterministic atomic sheet: a ~0.3 nm AlOx layer at the gate-dielectric/SiO2 interface forms a dipole shifting nFET Vt by +0.2-0.4 V, so the access channel can be left undoped; lower doping lowers the storage-junction field and collapses the trap-assisted tunnelling and GIDL that form the tail.

title: Ring-counter time-slot addressing for streaming weight mats
idea: Replace the address with time: mats dedicated to streamed AI weights use a shift-register token that walks the wordlines in fixed order, one per clock, so a row's address is simply its time slot; random access remains only at mat level and row decoders shrink to one token flop per row.

title: Open-source CHIPS-funded DRAM periphery IP commons
idea: Scale up from company to nation: a federally funded, silicon-proven, royalty-free library of DRAM periphery blocks (sense amps, sub-wordline drivers, pumps, PHYs) on U.S. 28 nm processes, so a new U.S. entrant only has to develop arrays.

title: Strategic DRAM reserve banks wafers during gluts for shortages
idea: Time shift across the 3-4 year memory cycle: in glut years such as 2023, a government or consortium buys finished DRAM wafers and known-good dies from existing fabs near cost. They sit in nitrogen-purged dry cabinets (dies are stable for a decade) and are released to existing packaging lines in shortages like 2026.

title: Gen-8.5 display fabs print gain-cell memory on meter-scale glass
idea: Scale jump from the 300 mm wafer to 2.2 x 2.5 m glass: idle LCD/OLED backplane lines build 2T oxide-TFT gain cells (indium-free ZnSnO or IGZO) at 1.5 um rules. That gives ~3 GB per m2, or ~15 GB per sheet, diced into modules behind an SRAM/DRAM cache.
note: Gen-8.5 oxide-TFT memory is a real capacity pool but ~$20-40/GB does not beat DRAM.

title: Existing U.S. solar ingot pullers make carrier wafers for bonded DRAM
idea: Scale shift across industries: bonded and stacked DRAM uses full prime CZ wafers as mechanical carriers and handles. Existing solar M12 ingot lines already pull ~300 mm-diameter ingots with lower-purity crucibles, so they can be sliced and polished into handle and monitor wafers.
note: Solar-grade ingots for handle/dummy wafers is plausible; carrier share of demand overstated.

title: 5 mm2 DRAM dielets tolerate dirtier fabs via exponential yield
idea: Shrink the die from ~70 mm2 to ~5 mm2 dielets: under Poisson yield a 3x higher defect density still yields >90%, so the line can run looser particle control and fewer inline inspections; dielets are assembled by die-to-wafer hybrid bonding onto a logic base.

title: Regulated-utility fab shells depreciated over thirty years
idea: Split the fab's timescales: buildings, utilities and UPW plants (~40% of capex) become a regulated-utility asset with 30-year recovery and a capped return, leasing space to U.S. DRAM makers whose tools stay on short cycles.

title: Follow-the-night DRAM provisioning across continents
idea: The global fleet is treated as one memory pool over 24 hours. Deferrable memory-heavy jobs (embedding rebuilds, batch inference, index builds, ETL) are routed to whichever region is in its diurnal trough. Each region's DRAM is then sized for the flattened global curve, not for its local evening peak.

title: Memory-efficiency label: GB-hours per transaction disclosure standard
idea: This adds zero masks. A federal cloud procurement rule, plus an Energy-Star-like label, requires software vendors and cloud services to report resident GB-hours per standard transaction or per inference token, with bid credits for each halving.
note: Energy-Star-like disclosure for GB-hours; slow, modest effect.

title: Cloud instances discounted by measured page compressibility
idea: This adds zero masks. The provider measures each tenant's compressibility and dedup ratio over a month, places compressible tenants on compressed-memory hosts, and passes back a discount. That creates a market incentive for compressible data layouts.

title: DRAM in the socket cavity on the CPU package underside
idea: Use the package's other face: LPDDR packages mount on the land side of the CPU substrate inside a cavity in the socket and motherboard, putting memory ~2 mm under the die instead of 5 cm away on DIMMs. The top side stays free for cooling.
note: Socket cavity costs CPU land pins; channel shortening is real.

title: Two-threshold sensing exports erasure flags over a side channel
idea: Shift from binary to graded certainty at the cell-to-wire boundary: sense amps resolve twice with offset references, marking gray-zone cells as erasures, and a sparse erasure bitmap travels beside the data. Erasure decoding corrects ~2x more than blind errors, so a 1% raw BER needs only ~8% parity.

title: B-grade die recapture: weak-cell DRAM fallout into heavy-ECC stacks
idea: Move the pass/fail line from zero unrepairable bits to <=1% weak cells: dies that fab test would scrap or down-bin are stacked on a heavy-LDPC base die and sold as full-capacity memory, with a buyer contracting for fab fallout at scrap-plus prices.
note: Post-repair DRAM yield loss is smaller than claimed; heavy LDPC adds latency.

title: Sell capacity-years: DIMMs that shrink gracefully as rows retire
idea: Time shift (time-zero spec -> lifetime contract): ship modules with weaker cells that the OS retires row by row as they degrade, and price them per guaranteed GB-year with a declining capacity curve (e.g. 100% -> 92% over 5 years). Today those weaker cells are screened out at the factory.

title: Federal reliability-graded memory standard creates demand for DUV parts
idea: No EUV: a U.S. procurement standard defines 'graded memory' (module-level ECC plus row retirement plus telemetry) so federal and hyperscale buyers can buy DUV-made, weaker-cell DRAM at full qualification. Policy shifts demand toward non-EUV domestic supply.

title: 1 Gb UCIe DRAM tiles so many small fabs feed one package
idea: Scale jump from die to package: define a tiny standard DRAM chiplet (1 Gb, UCIe-like edge interface, fixed footprint). Small or legacy fabs anywhere make tiles, and packaging houses tile dozens of them, possibly from different makers, onto a base die.

title: Consortium defect-map commons that pools years of yield learning
idea: Time compression by pooling: member fabs upload anonymized, federated defect and wafer-map data, and shared models flag excursions that one fab alone would need years of wafers to recognize.

title: Hot-zone beachhead: launch where silicon DRAM hurts most
idea: Nantero, Optane and early MRAM died without a market where they beat DRAM on day one. Launch a 125 C-native storage element first in Grade-1 automotive and industrial LPDDR sockets, where silicon DRAM must refresh ~8x faster and derate, and pre-sell to Tier-1s with 10-year supply contracts that fund the fab ramp.

title: IBM's cryogenic dream made cheap with LNG terminal cold
idea: IBM's cryogenic Josephson computer died on refrigeration cost. At 77 K, DRAM access-transistor leakage drops by ~1e5-1e6 and refresh effectively vanishes. Site memory-heavy racks at LNG regasification terminals, which normally dump ~0.8 MJ of cold per kg into seawater, and use a nitrogen loop to hold DRAM pools at 77-100 K.
note: Cryo DRAM known; LNG waste cold siting is the twist but geographically niche.

title: Canon ELTRAN porous-silicon donor wafers reused for 3D DRAM tiers
idea: Canon's ELTRAN layer transfer (epitaxy on porous Si, split at the porous layer) lost to Smart Cut. It suits bonded 3D DRAM tiers well: grow each tier epitaxially on porous Si, bond, split, re-porosify the donor and repeat about 20 times.

title: Optane write-off lesson: universal second-life interface on every DRAM die
idea: Intel's Optane exit ended in a large inventory write-down, partly because the dies worked only with one CPU interface. Put a small standardized test-and-reuse port (JTAG-like self-test plus a slow generic protocol) and a wear log on every DRAM die. Dies harvested from retired HBM and DDR modules can then be retested and repackaged into CXL capacity modules.
note: Retired DRAM reuse already happens in CXL; standard port needs vendor/JEDEC adoption.

title: Undo the helium reserve sell-off: a chip-grade helium strategic stock
idea: The U.S. sold its Federal Helium Reserve (completed 2024), so Qatar's 2026 outage hit fabs with no buffer. Re-create a fab-dedicated stock: require 80-90% recapture of chuck-backside and leak-check helium (membrane plus cryogenic recovery) and bank recovered surplus and U.S. field helium in the Cliffside storage under a strategic-stock lease.

title: Buy bankrupt DRAM makers' patent portfolios to arm a U.S. entrant
idea: Qimonda's buried-wordline and 4F2 vertical-channel work, plus Elpida, Z-RAM, T-RAM and Kilopass portfolios, ended up with patent-assertion entities or in drawers after failure. A U.S. entrant (or a DOE-backed pool) buys or exclusively licenses them to gain freedom to operate for buried-wordline, vertical-channel and capacitorless designs on a low-EUV older node.
note: Many Qimonda/Elpida-era patents expire around now, eroding value.

title: Pay memory subsidies per gigabyte shipped, not per fab dollar
idea: Capex-first support such as Solyndra's loan guarantee failed by funding plants that never reached competitive cost. Restructure U.S. memory support as a production tax credit per Gb of DRAM-class memory shipped from U.S. fabs, decaying over 10 years, with a bonus per Gb made without EUV layers.

title: MCM known-good-die curse fixed: contactless near-field wafer test
idea: 1990s multichip modules died of the known-good-die problem, and HBM repeats it because hybrid-bond pads cannot be touched by probe needles (scratches ruin bonding), so dies are bonded half-tested. Add a field of tiny capacitive/inductive near-field couplers in top metal and test each DRAM wafer at full speed, including burn-in and retention, through a matching contactless probe card before any bonding.

title: Cu-Mn self-forming barrier, failed in fine lines, revived for TSVs
idea: Cu-Mn alloy seeds that self-form a MnSiO barrier on anneal were dropped from advanced BEOL because residual Mn raised resistivity in 20 nm lines, a penalty that vanishes in 2-10 um TSVs, hybrid-bond pads and contact plugs. Use Cu-0.5%Mn seed in HBM TSVs, hybrid-bond pads and base-die contact plugs to eliminate Ta/TaN barriers and W plugs; the 2-3 nm self-formed barrier also frees TSV diameter.

title: Silicon-on-AlN failed on bonding; AlN as hybrid-bond dielectric spreads heat
idea: Silicon-on-aluminum-nitride SOI, meant to cure self-heating, died because rough AlN bonded poorly. Hybrid-bond interfaces need only a few hundred nm of dielectric: deposit smooth amorphous AlN (~10-30 W/m-K vs ~1.4 for SiO2) capped with 10 nm of SiCN for bonding chemistry, so every HBM tier gets a lateral heat-spreading plane at each bond line.

title: Carbon-cluster proximity gettering borrowed from image-sensor dark current
idea: Effect: impurity gettering. C3H5 molecular-ion clusters implanted ~1 um below the array (the CMOS image-sensor technique that cut dark current) form a dense sink that traps Fe, Cu and Ni during thermal steps, pulling midgap metal generation centres away from storage junctions. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
note: Proven CIS technique; DRAM tail is largely GIDL/TAT, so metal gettering gain may be limited.

title: Antifuse weight ROM banks rotate through over-the-air model updates
idea: Freeze automotive perception weights into oxide-breakdown antifuse arrays with in-array MAC. Ship 8 banks and burn one per model release, so each OTA update takes a fresh bank. A broken-down oxide filament is permanent at 125 C.
note: Antifuse density low; 8 banks of model weights costly area; automotive niche.

title: Random-telegraph-noise dither enables unbiased 2-bit KV caches
idea: Quantize KV values to 2 bits with stochastic rounding, which keeps the expectation unbiased. The random bits come from single-trap random telegraph noise in minimum-size transistors. Trap switching speeds up at 125 C, so the entropy source gets better with heat over the 10-year life.
note: RTN entropy source unnecessary; 2-bit KV known.

title: Capillary wicking: roll-embossed two-phase cooling film laminated onto memory stacks
idea: Hot-emboss micro-pillar wicks and vapor channels into copper-clad polymer film on R2R lines, then seal and laminate it as an ultra-thin vapor chamber over HBM; capillary pumping returns condensate with no pump.
note: R2R embossed wick laminate; cheaper HBM heat spreading, incremental thermal gain.

title: Thin-oxide tunneling canary cells set each row's refresh interval
idea: Effect: direct/Fowler-Nordheim tunneling plus subthreshold leakage, made deliberately stronger. Each row carries 2-4 canary cells whose access device has a thinner gate oxide and shorter channel, so they fail ~4x earlier than the weakest real cell with the same temperature and voltage dependence. Rows refresh at a long default interval (256 ms+) and drop to a shorter interval only when a periodic check finds a flipped canary.

title: Per-tier Seebeck thermopiles let 100-tier stacks refresh by tier
idea: Effect: Seebeck thermoelectric voltage. In a ~100-tier 3D DRAM whose inner tiers run 10-20 K hotter than outer ones, thermocouple pairs formed in the staircase contacts read each tier's temperature with zero bias power; the controller assigns per-tier refresh intervals (cool tiers ~4x longer) and steers hot data to cool tiers.

title: Na: big-capacitor LTPS DRAM on soda-lime glass in idle LCD fabs
idea: Build 1T1C DRAM with low-temperature poly-Si transistors and large planar capacitors on soda-lime glass (SiN barrier against Na+) in depreciated Gen-6/8 LCD lines at 1-2 um rules; a 2.8 m2 Gen-6 panel holds ~1e11 cells (~10 GB after periphery), and panel defect densities that would kill logic are fine because <=1% bad cells are mapped and coded out.
note: ~10 GB per Gen-6 panel implies far above DDR5 $1.48/GB cost; LTPS speed limits it to slow tier.

title: Helium nanocavity gettering layer beneath every storage-node junction
idea: He: implant a low-dose helium layer ~200 nm below the buried-channel access transistors and anneal it into nanocavities whose inner surfaces chemisorb Fe, Cu, Ni and Au, so a gettering sink sits within diffusion range of every storage junction instead of at the wafer backside; the helium used is grams per fab-year, immune to the Qatar outage.

title: Silicon-on-nothing pocket removes the storage-node junction's bottom area
idea: Si: use an empty-space-in-silicon process (etch a hole array, hydrogen-anneal so silicon migrates and seals a void) to place a vacuum pocket beneath each storage-node diffusion, leaving the junction floating with only its sidewall touching the body.

title: Chlorination plus ligand-exchange thermal ALE for 3D DRAM lateral recess
idea: Periodic-table walk, Cl (17): recess TiN, ZrO2 and Al2O3 laterally inside 3D DRAM tiers by cyclic thermal atomic-layer etching, chlorinating with SOCl2 or BCl3 then removing the surface with TiCl4 or trimethylaluminum ligand exchange, avoiding the HF step of standard thermal ALE.

title: Sn: tin-oxo resist doubles as hardmask, leaves as stannane
idea: Vapor-deposit a Sn-oxo-carbon resist, dry-develop it, keep the remaining SnOx as the etch hardmask, then remove it with an H2 plasma that converts tin into volatile SnH4 (the trick used to clean EUV collectors).

title: Cesium clock TTL memory: allocations that expire in hardware
idea: Using a cesium-clock-style global timestamp, allocations made with a TTL (session state, request buffers, cache entries) carry an expiry field in line/page metadata, and the controller sweeps expired lines into a free list with no GC or free() call, faulting cleanly if a stale pointer touches them.

title: Xenon strobe multicast: one weight read lights up all chiplets
idea: A xenon flash lights a whole room at once; the HBM base die gets a multicast fabric so one row read of a weight tile is delivered simultaneously to every compute chiplet in the package, and to all batched tenants of the same model, replacing per-chiplet weight copies with one shared copy.

title: S: Sb2S3 phase-change photonic crossbar pools memory across accelerators
idea: Use low-loss antimony-sulfide (Sb2S3) phase-change cells on silicon-nitride waveguides as non-volatile 2x2 switches in a 64x64 optical crossbar between accelerators and memory sleds; a route is set by one heater/laser pulse and then holds with zero static power, reassigning memory capacity per job.

title: Si: die-agnostic DDR5 buffer builds RDIMMs from any surplus die
idea: Put a silicon bridge buffer (extended RCD plus data buffers) on a standard DDR5 RDIMM that speaks JEDEC DDR5 to the host but drives LPDDR4X/LPDDR5, DDR4 or downbinned dies behind it, translating timing and bank structure, so modules can be assembled from whatever DRAM die is in surplus.

title: Au: right-to-reuse rule stops shredding retired server DIMMs
idea: Policy: require hyperscalers and IT-asset recyclers to route retired DDR4/DDR5 server DIMMs through certified re-test and resale before any gold-recovery shredding, with a per-GB reuse tax credit; reused modules drop into existing DDR slots unchanged.

title: C: carbon co-implant getters point defects at storage-node junctions
idea: Add a shallow substitutional-carbon co-implant (~1e20 cm^-3) at the storage-node contact junction; carbon traps Si interstitials and binds Fe/Cu, preventing the deep-level clusters that create trap-assisted-tunneling hotspots in the depletion region.

title: Cu: copper conductive-bridge antifuses give unlimited in-field row remapping
idea: Replace one-time fuses in the repair block with Cu-ion conductive-bridge cells programmable at ~1.5 V in the field, so the controller can remap hundreds of failing rows and columns over life (and undo them), instead of DDR5's handful of post-package-repair slots.
note: Soft PPR plus controller remaps already give field repair; CBRAM integration adds cost.

title: Au: Gold-finger DIMM deposit-refund law drives memory take-back
idea: Levy a $3-10 refundable deposit per DIMM/SODIMM, like bottle bills, redeemable at certified harvesters whose gold-finger and DRAM resale value fund the program and feed reballing lines.
note: Same bottle-bill deposit as I-05037.

title: Zr: Open-source zirconia trench-capacitor DRAM PDK for U.S. foundries
idea: Publish an open PDK and macro compiler for a ZrO2/TiN deep-trench 1T1C DRAM cell on 130-90 nm U.S. foundries, so defense, auto and industrial buyers source companion DRAM domestically.

title: Ga: Abundance-screened bill-of-materials procurement rule for memory
idea: Learning from China's 2023 gallium and germanium export controls, a federal procurement rule scores memory by mass-weighted element supply concentration and gives price preference to non-volatile memories built only from abundant elements.

title: Solar-cell fixed-charge passivation spacer on the storage junction
idea: Borrow PERC/TOPCon solar-cell field-effect passivation: put a SiNx/AlOx spacer with engineered fixed charge (positive next to the n+ storage node) over the storage-junction surface. The surface stays accumulated, so surface SRH generation and the GIDL fringe field are suppressed.
note: Surface generation is only part of the tail; CIS uses similar passivation.

title: Bearing-style selective assembly pairs leaky arrays with tight sense amps
idea: In a CMOS-bonded-array flow, map each array wafer's retention and each periphery wafer's sense-amp offset before hybrid bonding. Then pair dies by measurement, as bearing makers match graded balls to races, so the leakiest arrays get the lowest-offset sense amps.

title: Cleanroom-airlock double gate splits voltage across two stacked channels
idea: Put two independent gates on the same vertical pillar with a floating middle node, like a cleanroom airlock with two doors. In hold, the middle node settles mid-rail, so each channel sees half the Vds.

title: Pre-printed forms: sea-of-gates periphery personalized by two i-line metal masks
idea: Like printers who stock pre-printed letterhead and add only the name, fab one universal 180 nm periphery master with gate-array sites for pumps, decoders and control. Interface width, protocol (DDR/LPDDR/CXL-lite) and redundancy are personalized with just two metal masks, the 1990s ASIC gate-array method.

title: Tailor's marker nesting: shape dies to harvest wafer-edge silicon
idea: Garment cutters nest pattern pieces to minimize scrap; design mature-node memory as small self-contained hexagonal banks that plasma dicing can cut in any outline, so partial wafer-edge regions yield sellable small dies.

title: Inventory carrying cost: bill cold resident memory like warehouse stock
idea: Manufacturers price inventory by its carrying cost. Clouds and internal chargeback bill memory by touched versus untouched GB-hours (taken from page access bits): untouched pages cost 3-5x more, and pages released to a compressed tier earn a credit. Teams finally get a price signal to shed cold memory.

title: Kintsugi spares: repair rows built from a stronger cell technology
idea: Kintsugi mends pottery with gold so the repair is the strongest part; instead of spare rows from the same weak array, put repair capacity as SRAM or oxide gain-cell rows on the hybrid-bonded base die, so failed or weak rows remap to cells with no retention tail and no hammer sensitivity.

title: Power-by-the-hour: lease memory bits, take modules back, redeploy
idea: Rolls-Royce sells engine thrust-hours, not engines. Memory makers keep ownership of modules and bill per GB-hour, with telemetry from the SPD/CXL controller. Modules are reclaimed, re-screened and redeployed across customers as one fleet over 2-3 service lives.

title: Two-threshold sensing turns every read into a retention health check
idea: Ideal result: refresh only the bits that are truly about to fail. Every Nth activation, the SA stripe fires against a second, offset reference that flags cells whose signal is within 30% of failing; the controller logs those rows for faster refresh and stretches refresh for the healthy majority.

title: Short local wordlines so abundant TiN replaces tungsten fill
idea: Ideal: a wordline with zero resistance. Work backward: make resistance irrelevant by splitting each buried wordline into 64-cell segments driven by local sub-wordline drivers placed under the array (CMOS-under-array), so all-TiN or doped-poly gates suffice and WF6 tungsten fill disappears.

title: Ashable carbon capacitor mold removed dry, ending pillar collapse
idea: Ideal: the capacitor mold vanishes without touching the pillars. Closest: build the pillar mold from amorphous carbon instead of oxide, so after electrode ALD it is removed by an O2/N2 plasma ash rather than an HF dip-out, eliminating capillary pillar collapse, supercritical-CO2 drying and the nitride support-mesh lithography.

title: Ephemeral-memory cloud SKU: cheap RAM that forgets after 50 ms
idea: Ideal: users pay only for memory during the instant they use it. Closest achievable: a cloud instance class exposes a large never-refreshed 'ephemeral memory' region whose contents are guaranteed only 50 ms after the last write, priced ~40% lower, with SDKs for streaming ETL, video, AI activations and network buffers that fit the contract.
note: 50 ms guarantee is below the 64 ms refresh window, so little salvage of weak dies; refresh savings modest.

title: ML-grade memory class with declared raw BER
idea: Ideal: fabs build cells exactly as weak as the workload can tolerate. Closest: JEDEC/OCP define an ML-grade memory class that declares raw BER and retention distribution and mandates host-side strong ECC, so fabs can relax the capacitor target from ~5 fF to ~3 fF and ship parts that today fail retention screens.

title: 180 nm RAS hub chip lets leading-edge dies ship raw
idea: Ideal: the DRAM die is pure array and all reliability logic is free. Closest: a buffer chip built in a fully depreciated 180 nm US fab sits on each DIMM and performs page-level BCH, a bad-row remap CAM and hammer tracking for 8-16 dies, so memory makers can drop on-die ECC and ship dies through relaxed retention screens.

title: Hammer-proof legacy tier for page tables and keys
idea: Ideal: hammering cannot hurt what matters. Closest: page tables, kernel structures and crypto keys live in a small 180 nm DRAM or SRAM tier whose wide cell spacing makes it physically immune to row hammer, so the dense main memory can drop costly TRR to cheap probabilistic neighbor refresh backed by ordinary ECC.
note: Protects privilege structures but not user-data integrity attacks.

title: RAM-mileage standard: GB-per-request ratings in public procurement
idea: Ideal: software that needs no memory at all. Closest achievable: an Energy-Star-style rating of memory footprint (GB-seconds per transaction or per token) required in government and hyperscaler procurement, with annual CAFE-like improvement targets.

title: Digital-twin DRAM fab flight school for process engineers
idea: Ideal: experienced fab engineers available instantly. Closest achievable: a national academy runs a full-fab simulator that replays real, anonymized excursion data from partners and certifies yield engineers in 6 months, the way pilots train on simulators.

title: Freedom-to-operate DRAM built only from expired patents
idea: Ideal: technology with no owner. Closest achievable: design a DDR4/LPDDR4-compatible part using only expired-patent cell, stacked-capacitor and sense-amp techniques, backed by a formal freedom-to-operate audit, so an entrant faces no royalty stack or injunctions.
note: Design-around using only expired art; JEDEC-essential patents and performance gap remain.

title: Significance-aware HBM lanes: compact cells for bf16 mantissa bits
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): DQ lanes and bursts stay identical. Because inference stacks lay out bf16/fp8 tensors with fixed bit positions per DQ lane, build core dies whose arrays behind sign/exponent lanes keep full-size capacitors while arrays behind low-mantissa lanes use half-height capacitors with relaxed retention (raw BER ~1e-4), enabled by an existing mode-register write and defaulting to full reliability.
note: Approximate DRAM for DNNs known; cutting capacitor height yields well under 30% cost per bit.

title: Idle power budget of 1 mW per GB: in-DRAM compaction before self-refresh
idea: Limit: in self-refresh the die may refresh only the rows it truly needs. On self-refresh entry, an on-die engine applies zero, pattern and base-delta compression to each subarray, packs the data into fewer subarrays with in-DRAM row copy, and stops refreshing the vacated subarrays. It decompresses on exit.

title: No column decoder: CCD-style shift-out of the latched row
idea: Limit: no column decoder and no global column-select lines. After sensing, the sense amps are linked by two pass transistors each into a dynamic shift register that clocks the row out serially toward taps placed every 256 bits at the bank edge, like a CCD image sensor; random column access becomes 'shift N from the nearest tap'.
note: Random column access pays shift latency.

title: Ferroelectric-imbalanced sense latches keep open rows across power loss
idea: Constraint: open pages must survive an instant power cut with zero dump time. Two small HZO capacitors on each SA's internal nodes are polarized by the latched value in a ~10 ns pulse on power-fail detect (not on every activation, to spare endurance); when power returns, their remanent imbalance biases the latch so it re-resolves to the same value, recovering ~256 kB of open-row state.

title: Microwatt refresh island: coin cell keeps IGZO memory alive for years
idea: Constraint: data survives mains loss, with no NV material. Pair hour-retention IGZO DRAM with a tiny always-on periphery island (a ~2 uW clock, counter and row walker) that refreshes one row every ~1 ms from a 20 mAh lithium cell or harvested trickle, while all other periphery is cut off.

title: Brownfield DRAM fabs on retired coal plants
idea: Imposed scarcity: no new water rights, no new transmission and no greenfield permit time. Site fabs on retiring coal plants that already hold industrial water allocations, cooling reservoirs, high-voltage interconnects and rail, and convert boiler halls into utility buildings.

title: Helium-free fab: hydrogen-neon chuck cooling and hydrogen-tracer leak checks
idea: Constraint: zero helium deliveries. Switch electrostatic-chuck backside cooling in high-AR etch and deposition from He to H2/Ne blends with redesigned micro-groove chucks that restore gas conductance, replace He leak testing with 5% H2/N2 tracer sniffers, and membrane-recapture any legacy He.
note: Supply-risk removal, small cost gain.

title: Revive IBM-heritage deep-trench eDRAM as hot-rated standalone memory
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: license the existing SOI deep-trench eDRAM process (~25-40 fF cells) held by a U.S. foundry and productize it as standalone 125 C DRAM in its New York fabs, with no new tool or process development.

title: Line-level page meshing in the memory controller
idea: Imposed limit: no physical page may be less than 90% occupied. The controller keeps a 64 B-line indirection table, so two half-empty pages whose live lines do not overlap merge into one physical page without any change to virtual addresses; this brings Mesh-style compaction to unmanaged C/C++ heaps.
note: Hardware Mesh: 64B indirection table costs metadata/TLB-like lookups; known Mesh allocator art moved into controller.

title: Memory insurance: fleets sized for median, peaks covered by pooled policy
idea: Imposed limit: servers are bought with P50 memory, not P99. Tenants buy 'memory insurance' units; on a peak, a rack-level compressed far-memory reserve plus eviction of preemptible jobs pays out, priced actuarially from fleet telemetry so the operator carries the statistical risk.

title: Contactless inductive probing qualifies every die before stacking
idea: Scarcity: nothing may touch the die before bonding, since probe marks ruin hybrid-bond surfaces. Each die carries an on-die coil array and test controller; a coil probe card powers it inductively and runs full-speed tests wirelessly, so only pristine known-good dies enter the stack.

title: Partial-good HBM: channel-isolated stacks sold and run degraded
idea: Rule: a dead channel must not kill a stack. Each HBM pseudo-channel gets independent power gating and fuse-isolatable TSV groups, so stacks with failed channels ship as 75% or 50% capacity SKUs, and channels that fail in the field are fenced off instead of retiring the stack.

title: Every GB sold must come back: DRAM module deposit-refund
idea: Self-imposed limit: no DRAM leaves the loop. A per-GB deposit at sale is refunded when modules are returned to certified reclaimers, which guarantees feedstock for die harvesting and cascade reuse.
note: Same bottle-bill deposit as I-05037.

title: No silicon wafer: substrate-neutral CHIPS grants paid per verified bit-capacity
idea: Forced limit: subsidies cannot favour Si. A grant tranche pays per verified Gb of monthly capacity added per dollar of capex, open to glass, foil, SiC and disk lines, with milestones audited by third-party benchmark.

title: No silicon wafer: multi-project panel shuttles for memory startups
idea: Forced limit: startups cannot afford a wafer lot. A panel foundry runs shared Gen 6 glass shuttles where 100 or more startups each get a tile of oxide-memory process, at about 1/100 of a mask set and lot.

title: Etch-compensated graded tier stack: uniform lateral recess by composition grading
idea: 3D DRAM sets each cell's channel and capacitor length by a lateral recess from a vertical hole or slit, and Lam notes that recess sizes vary along the stack because the etchant depletes with depth. Instead of fighting that with chemistry, pre-compensate at deposition: ramp each tier's sacrificial composition with depth (Ge fraction in SiGe, Si/N ratio and hydrogen content in SiN, or boron level in B3-06 layers) so the intrinsic etch rate rises where etchant supply falls. Calibrate the profile once per stack recipe from per-tier TEM; the only tool knob is a gas-flow ramp. Finish with a few tens of lateral atomic-layer-etch cycles to trim the last nanometres uniformly.

title: Hydrogen-lean batch-furnace mold for oxide 3D DRAM
idea: NAND-style oxide 3D DRAM needs a 32-128-pair SiO2/SiN mold; single-wafer PECVD films carry ~3-25 at.% hydrogen, and hydrogen drives IGZO Vt drift (H-doping under PBTI, which imec cut ~30x with an H+O anneal). With the periphery on a separate bonded wafer, the cell wafer's mold can be made hot: deposit the alternating stack in a batch LPCVD furnace (100-150 wafers per load, ~4% H in LPCVD SiN, <1% in high-temperature oxide), then out-gas it at 800-900 C before any oxide channel is deposited (for example by Kioxia-style SiN->IGZO replacement). Add per-tier ALD Al2O3 hydrogen barriers around the replacement channels and finish with an O-rich anneal instead of forming gas.

title: Adiabatic refresh: recycle bitline and wordline charge with stepwise tanks or piezo-MEMS resonators
idea: During refresh (and optionally background activates), the VARY and VPP rails feeding a bank are ramped rather than fixed. The ramp comes from either (a) N-step tank-capacitor banks (stepwise charging) or (b) a resonant LC whose inductor is a compact AlN piezoelectric MEMS resonator or a package inductor, as in adiabatic or reversible logic. The sense amplifier makes its regenerative decision with a small non-adiabatic kick, then the bitline swing to VARY or 0 follows the ramped rails, and precharge returns charge to the tanks instead of shorting it. Wordlines (3 V, pumped at ~45% efficiency) are ramped the same way. No cell change is needed.

title: 77 K oxide MLC gain-cell stage for cryogenic and superconducting computers
idea: IGZO/IWO 2T0C gain cells (no capacitor) sit in BEOL tiers on a 77 K cryo-CMOS periphery wafer. At 77 K, oxide-cell leakage collapses (8,000 s reported for IGZO 2T0C) and threshold drift (PBTI, hydrogen motion) is thermally frozen. Si subthreshold swing falls to ~15-20 mV/decade, so periphery and wordlines run at ~0.4 / 1.0 V, and Cu resistance drops several-fold. Together these make 3-4 bits/cell with write-verify realistic. The stage links to 4 K superconducting logic through the thermal-break link in imec's architecture.

title: Superconducting kinetic-inductance memory with frequency-multiplexed readout (4 K)
idea: Each cell is a NbN (or similar) nanowire loop whose kinetic inductance (~70 pH per square) holds a persistent current; one flux quantum is one bit. Heater cryotrons (hTrons) or nanocryotrons drive a branch normal to write and to read. Row-column arrays exist (MIT and NIST). The twist: each column's sense element is a superconducting resonator at its own frequency on a shared feedline (MKID-style), so thousands of columns read out through one coax and 4 K wiring heat drops sharply.

title: Swap capacitor electrons for flux quantum in kinetic-inductance nanowire loop
idea: At 4 K, a NbN or NbTiN nanowire loop whose kinetic inductance is ~100x its geometric inductance stores one flux quantum in under 1 um2. It is written and read by nanocryotron (nTron) gates instead of large Josephson junctions.
note: Same KI nanowire loop memory.

title: Substitute raw data storage with leakage-minimizing per-row polarity coding
idea: Substitute raw data with a per-row inversion flag chosen at write time so most cells sit in their discharged, non-leaking state (true-cell/anti-cell layout included). The row's charged-cell count is stored, and rows with few charged cells are refreshed at a relaxed rate.

title: Substitute beamline implant with self-assembled monolayer doping on 3D channels
idea: Substitute ion implantation (whose plasma flood guns run on argon or xenon) with monolayer doping.
