Phosphorus- or boron-bearing molecules self-assemble on exposed Si sidewalls from solution, are capped with oxide, and are driven in by semiconductor diode-laser spike heating, forming a conformal, damage-free, sub-5 nm junction even on the lateral channels of 3D DRAM tiers.

title: Substitute hydrogen-passivated oxide channels with HF-vapor fluorine passivation
idea: Substitute hydrogen, a shallow donor and instability source in oxide semiconductors, with fluorine: oxide-channel access transistors are annealed in anhydrous HF vapor diluted in N2 instead of CF4/Ar plasma. The fluorine fills oxygen vacancies and replaces mobile hydrogen.

title: Controller-side remap tables replace on-die fuse redundancy
idea: Substitute on-die laser/e-fuse banks and redundancy address comparators with a per-device bad-row/bad-column table held by the memory controller (like an SSD FTL), filled at test and refreshed during field scrubbing.
note: ArchShield-style controller fault maps are prior art.

title: Keyed Feistel scrambler in decoder randomizes physical row adjacency
idea: Substitute the fixed logical-to-physical row map with a tiny keyed Feistel permutation in the row predecoder, re-keyed each refresh epoch with background migration, so attackers cannot know which physical rows neighbor their aggressors.

title: Sputtered IGZO thin-film decoders stacked above the cell array
idea: Substitute crystalline-silicon row decoders with sputtered IGZO TFT decoders built at <=350 C on top of the array (ALD HfO2 gate, Mo source/drain). A university nanofab can demonstrate a 64-row decoder over a MIM-cap test array with i-line lithography.
note: Oxide-TFT periphery above array is actively researched.

title: Infiltrated block-copolymer dots replace EUV pillar-hole patterning
idea: Substitute EUV contact/pillar patterning with self-assembly: PS-b-P2VP cylinders form a hexagonal lattice at 20-28 nm pitch inside coarse ArF-dry guide trenches, 3 cycles of sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O) turn P2VP domains into AlOx hard-mask dots, PS is O2-ashed and the pattern transferred with Cl2/HBr.
note: BCP DSA with SIS hardmasks is demonstrated research; defectivity has blocked adoption.

title: Water-droplet self-alignment with alkylsilane rings replaces precision die placement
idea: Substitute high-precision pick-and-place for die-to-wafer DRAM stacking with capillary self-alignment: a water droplet on each hydrophilic bond site pulls the coarsely dropped die into ~0.2 um registration, the surrounding hydrophobic ring made from octadecyltrichlorosilane or plasma-polymerized HMDSO instead of the usual fluorinated FDTS.

title: Substitute robotic pick-and-place with capillary fluidic self-alignment for die bonding
idea: Dispense a water droplet on a hydrophilic bond site ringed by hydrophobic SAM; a roughly placed DRAM die (+/-50 um) is pulled into <0.5 um alignment by surface tension in milliseconds, the water evaporates, and oxide/Cu hybrid bonding follows. Precision comes from physics, so a coarse gantry can drop >10,000 dies per hour.
note: Water-droplet die self-alignment already demonstrated (Tohoku, CEA).

title: Substitute ion implanters with molecular monolayer doping and in-situ epitaxy
idea: Replace most of DRAM's ~20-30 implant steps with self-assembled dopant-bearing molecular monolayers (boron or phosphorus esters) that are capped and spike-annealed, plus selective in-situ-doped epitaxy for source/drain. Dose is set by the molecular footprint and coats 3D pillars that line-of-sight implants cannot reach.

title: Substitute litho-etch pairs with area-selective bottom-up deposition
idea: Use small-molecule or SAM inhibitors that adsorb only on dielectric so ALD grows metal (or dielectric) only where wanted, forming landing pads and capacitor bottom contacts self-aligned to underlying features without a lithography and etch pair. Selectivity loss is reset with periodic deposition-etch supercycles.

title: Swap replicated cluster datasets for threads that migrate to data
idea: Substitute moving data with moving computation. On a remote access, a thread's ~200-byte context hops to the node that owns the data instead of the data being fetched or cached locally, so graph and sparse datasets are stored exactly once across the cluster.

title: Swap small tokenizers for vocabulary transplants that shrink KV per text
idea: Substitute a 32k-token vocabulary with a 200k+ one tuned to code and multilingual text: new embeddings are initialized from compositions of old-token embeddings, then a short fine-tune follows. The same document becomes fewer tokens, so fewer KV entries.

title: Charge-recycling bus: adjacent lines trade charge instead of dumping it
idea: Substitute rail-to-rail drivers with series-stacked voltage domains across a wide HBM bus: charge dumped by a falling line in one domain recharges a rising line in the next, and resonant LC tanks recycle clock-line energy.

title: Silicon-core vias: trench-isolated die silicon replaces copper TSV fill
idea: Substitute copper-filled TSVs with pillars of the die's own heavily doped silicon, isolated by an oxide-filled annular deep trench, so there is no copper CTE mismatch and the stress keep-out around each via largely disappears.
note: Known (Silex Sil-Via); high resistance limits to slow lanes.

title: Substitute laser fuse repair with in-field cuckoo remap in HBM base die
idea: Replace one-shot fuse row repair with a 64-byte-granular cuckoo-hash remap table in the HBM logic base die, backed by spare rows, that is rewritten in the field whenever ECC sees a recurring error, so dies with 10x more defects than today's repair budget still ship.

title: Substitute hours of factory retention testing with in-field learning
idea: Ship dies with only basic test and fast-refresh guard bands; the controller profiles retention per row over the first weeks of service at real temperature and then relaxes refresh row by row.

title: Substitute fixed-rate ECC with time-since-write graded ECC for NV
idea: NV data is first stored with a light code; as a line stays unwritten (cold), a background engine re-encodes it with stronger codes because retention loss grows with time and unpowered periods; an orderly shutdown re-encodes all lines to the strongest tier.
note: Retention-aware ECC known from NAND/PCM.

title: Substitute blocking ECC decode with speculative use of raw NV data
idea: Let the CPU consume raw NV read data immediately while a strong ECC decoder (needed for weak NV cells) checks in parallel; on a detected error the pipeline rolls back like a branch mispredict.

title: Substitute new dies with remanufactured dies from retired server DIMMs
idea: Swap virgin DRAM for remanufactured DRAM: robotic de-soldering lines pull dies off decommissioned hyperscaler DIMMs, re-ball them, run retention/row-hammer/BIST screens and re-mount them on new PCBs sold in warranty tiers.

title: Logic-fab BEOL finger capacitors as DRAM storage nodes
idea: Combine the metal-oxide-metal finger capacitors that every logic back-end already offers with BEOL oxide-semiconductor access transistors, so a standard logic interconnect stack (interdigitated M3-M8 lines) becomes the storage capacitor field. No special capacitor module, high-AR etch or memory fab is needed: any U.S. logic fab can print DRAM-class memory above its own logic.
note: MOM capacitors give only fF per um2, so density is ~100x below DRAM, not one third.

title: Work-function-imprinted antiferroelectric ZrO2 nonvolatile cell
idea: Combine antiferroelectric ZrO2's double hysteresis (fatigue-resistant, 1e11+ cycles) with asymmetric electrodes, a TiN bottom and a high-work-function MoO3-capped top, whose built-in field shifts one AFE loop to straddle 0 V. The film then holds two remanent states at zero bias like a ferroelectric but switches through the gentler field-induced AFE transition.
note: Work-function-shifted AFE loops for nonvolatility already published (NaMLab); still destructive read.

title: Liquid-nitrogen immersed DRAM racks where retention outlasts data
idea: Combine LN2 immersion cooling (already used for HTS cables and extreme overclocking) with commodity DRAM pools: at 77 K access-transistor leakage falls by many orders of magnitude, stretching retention from 64 ms to hours, so refresh is simply switched off. Cryo also speeds transistors ~20% and cuts wire resistance several-fold.

title: Compressed packing fills freed rows with leak-aligned padding
idea: The controller compresses pages, packs them into fewer rows, and writes the freed rows entirely with each cell type's leak-direction value (0 for true cells, 1 for anti-cells). A per-row flag marks those rows refresh-exempt until reallocated.

title: Compiler tensor liveness wired into per-row refresh skip
idea: The ML compiler already knows every tensor's lifetime. It tags buffers whose last read comes within the guaranteed retention window (activations in the decode loop, gradient staging, temp scratch), and the controller sets per-row no-refresh bits until they are freed.
note: Close to RANA-style lifetime-aware refresh for accelerators.

title: Retention-binned page allocator matches data lifetime to row strength
idea: Profile each row's retention class at test and store the map in SPD. The OS places frequently rewritten data in weak rows and long-lived data in strong rows, each class refreshed at its own rate.

title: Oscillator timed by real DRAM cells clocks refresh
idea: Build a relaxation oscillator whose timing element is a group of real array cells (same capacitor and access transistor) discharging to a threshold; its period tracks actual retention across temperature, voltage and process and directly sets each bank's refresh interval.
note: Replicas track the mean, not the VRT tail.

title: Charge-transfer presensing doubles cells per bitline
idea: Revive 1990s charge-transfer presensing: a Vt-compensated transfer transistor between a long bitline and a small sense node amplifies the signal by the capacitance ratio, so 1,024 cells per bitline work and the number of SA stripes halves.
note: 1990s charge-transfer presensing revival.

title: Nanotwinned copper pads enable 150 C bonding of heat-sensitive memory tiers
idea: Fuse (111)-oriented nanotwinned copper, electroplated from US-mined copper on US-built plating tools, into hybrid-bond pads; its fast surface diffusion forms Cu-Cu bonds at ~150 C, so finished AFE-capacitor or thin-film-transistor memory tiers can be stacked repeatedly without retention-damaging 300-400 C anneals.

title: Skip hafnium-zirconium separation: qualify natural-ratio zirconium precursors
idea: Combine the two elements nature already combines: electronics needs no nuclear-grade Hf/Zr separation, so qualify ALD precursors made directly from unseparated zircon (~2% Hf) for ZrO2 capacitors and specify periphery dielectrics as natural (Zr,Hf)O2.

title: Polymer-copper hybrid bond whose bonding polymer becomes the underfill
idea: Combine HBM die bonding and underfill: the one added mask patterns a photo-definable BCB/polyimide around Cu pads; at bonding, Cu-Cu interdiffuses while the polymer flows and cures into a void-free underfill, eliminating SnAg microbumps and capillary underfill.
note: Known hybrid-bonding variant.

title: Tidal memory: scheduler pairs anti-correlated job footprints
idea: Combine the cluster scheduler with per-job memory-phase profiles: co-locate jobs whose peak footprints alternate in time (nightly ETL vs daytime serving, train vs eval phases) and shuttle the idle job's pages to a CXL/compressed tier at each phase boundary.

title: RAID-5 parity across DIMMs replaces per-rank chipkill
idea: Combine RAID-5 striping with main memory: one parity DIMM covers a group of 4-8 data DIMMs, a per-line CRC carried in burst metadata detects errors, and reconstruction from parity runs only when a CRC fails, replacing per-rank ECC devices.

title: Succinct filters plus on-flash learned index shrink key-value indexes
idea: Combine ribbon/cuckoo filters with a learned on-flash index: a DRAM-resident filter (~1 byte per key) answers whether a key exists and in which segment, and a learned model stored on the SSD locates the record in one read, replacing full in-DRAM hash indexes.

title: Real-time memory exchange fused with VM balloon drivers
idea: Combine spot-market pricing with hypervisor ballooning: tenants post idle guest memory as sell orders, the balloon driver reclaims it within seconds when bought, and the buyer receives it through a CXL pool or same-host remapping.

title: Base-die line compressor storing size tags in spare ECC bits
idea: Combine the HBM base die with a hardware cache-line compressor (base-delta plus shared FP8/BF16 exponents) whose per-line size tag lives in spare ECC/metadata bits, so two compressed lines pack into one slot transparently and the host sees normal addresses.
note: Compresso/Attache-style metadata compression known.

title: Single LED-cured nanoimprint defines via and trench for interposers
idea: Combine nanoimprint lithography with dual damascene: a two-tier stamp imprints via and trench together into a UV-curable dielectric cured by 365 nm LED arrays, followed by electroless seed and Cu plating. No scanner, no excimer laser, no argon PVD.
note: Dual-damascene NIL studied since 2000s; defectivity is the issue.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory vault: 77 K DRAM pool with near-zero refresh
idea: Combine rack-scale CXL memory pooling with liquid-nitrogen immersion (N2 is 78% of air, unlike helium cryogenics): at 77 K access-transistor leakage collapses so retention stretches to hours, refresh nearly stops, wires are ~6-7x less resistive and commodity DRAM runs at reduced VDD.
note: Cryo DRAM studied; 10 W/W lift eats refresh savings.

title: Chip-first printed fan-out: interconnect printed directly onto placed dies
idea: Combine pick-and-place die embedding with aerosol-jet printing: DRAM and controller dies sit face-up in a molded panel and Ag/Cu nanoparticle inks plus polyimide dielectric are printed across die edges at 10-20 um lines, then sintered with near-IR diode lasers instead of xenon flash lamps.
note: 10-20 um printed lines limit to LPDDR-class densities.

title: Retired-server DRAM harvesting line feeding CXL expander cards
idea: Combine e-waste DIMM recovery with CXL memory expansion: an automated line desolders DDR4/DDR5 packages from retired DIMMs, reballs and characterizes each chip for retention and speed, bins them, and remounts them on CXL Type-3 cards whose controller maps weak rows and applies per-chip adaptive refresh. No new wafers, so no new rare gas.
note: Adds package-level harvest and reball; extra cost versus whole-DIMM reuse.

title: Bit-plane-transposed tensors: exponent planes refreshed, mantissa planes left drifting
idea: Combine approximate computing with bit-plane storage: the controller transposes BF16/FP8 tensors so each DRAM row holds one bit-plane; sign/exponent planes go to normally refreshed rows and low-mantissa planes to rows refreshed 8-16x less often, so any flip lands at a known, low significance.
note: Flikker-style critical/non-critical refresh; transposition costs bandwidth.

title: Refresh-as-migration: Feistel row remapping advanced by refresh copies
idea: Combine refresh with RowClone-style in-subarray copy: each refresh step copies one row into a spare slot and advances a keyed Feistel permutation of logical-to-physical rows, so physical neighbors of any logical row change every few milliseconds and hammering cannot stay on fixed victims; the copy replaces the plain refresh.
note: Similar to RRS/SRS/SHADOW row shuffling.

title: Speculative early data return with late strong ECC verdict
idea: Combine CPU branch speculation with ECC: the controller forwards raw data immediately while a strong multi-symbol decoder runs in parallel; on an error the core squashes dependent instructions like a mispredicted branch and replays with corrected data.
note: Same speculative forward plus replay.

title: Self-referencing rows: decaying reference cells set the read threshold
idea: Combine reference cells with the data row: each row carries a '1' and a '0' reference cell written with the data, so they decay alongside it; the sense threshold is set at the midpoint of their residual levels, letting partially leaked data resolve correctly. Buildable in a university nanofab: TFT/MIM test arrays with an off-chip comparator.

title: Canary patch with thinned dielectric acts as self-timed refresh clock
idea: Combine canary cells with an oscillator: each subarray holds a few cells with a deliberately leakier, thinner dielectric patch, and their decay crossing triggers that subarray's refresh, automatically tracking temperature, aging and process instead of a fixed worst-case timer. Buildable in a university nanofab: one extra lithography step and a thinner ALD deposition.

title: Effective-GB compressed CXL modules sold with capacity warranty
idea: Combine inline hardware LZ4/zstd compression and a deduplication engine with a commercial guarantee: the vendor sells 'effective GB' and warrants 2× capacity on qualified workloads, with telemetry and true-up credits.

title: Kinetic-inductance nanowire loops from astronomy photon detectors
idea: Borrow MKID detectors and MRI persistent switches: store the bit as a persistent current in a 100 nm NbN nanowire loop whose large kinetic inductance lets the loop be tiny, switched by a nanowire heater-cryotron, for cryogenic AI racks.
note: Same KI nanowire loop memory.

title: Image-sensor correlated double sampling for bitline sensing
idea: Borrowed from CMOS image sensors: a switched-capacitor column comparator samples the bitline onto one small cap right after precharge (capturing kTC reset noise, random-telegraph noise and its own offset) and onto a second cap after the wordline opens, then decides on the difference. Everything common to both samples subtracts out.
note: Offset-cancellation SAs already ship; sampling adds kT/C noise.

title: Flash translation layer remaps bad rows outside the die
idea: Borrowed from NAND SSD bad-block management: DRAM dies ship with no redundant rows, fuse banks or address comparators; the memory controller loads a per-die bad-row map from SPD and remaps addresses into a pooled spare region.

title: Rebreather-style closed helium loop for etch and ALD chucks
idea: Adapted from closed-circuit diving rebreathers, which scrub and recirculate expensive heliox instead of venting it. Each tool gets a foreline tap that captures backside-cooling helium leaking past the e-chuck (plus leak-check station exhaust), strips it through a getter cartridge and cold trap, and recompresses it into the chuck supply loop.

title: Dry-cleaner supercritical CO2 replaces water rinses after etch
idea: Adapted from dry cleaning's switch from perchloroethylene to supercritical CO2. Strip post-etch polymer residue and dry high-aspect structures in scCO2 with small co-solvent doses, with the CO2 recycled through a separator and compressor; with no surface tension, tall pillars cannot collapse.

title: Architectural low-E glass zinc-tin-oxide for an indium-free gain cell
idea: Low-emissivity window coaters sputter zinc stannate (ZTO) over huge areas of glass every year. Adapt their target chemistry and rotary-sputter tooling to a two-transistor, zero-capacitor gain cell whose wide-bandgap ZTO write transistor leaks sub-fA, so the read transistor's gate holds the bit for seconds.

title: Hydrogen-cooled power generators: helium-free wafer chuck cooling
idea: Large power-plant generators are cooled with hydrogen because its thermal conductivity beats helium's; replace helium backside gas in etch, deposition and implant electrostatic chucks with low-pressure H2 or forming gas from on-site electrolysis, using the generator industry's purity monitoring and leak detection.

title: Game procedural generation: regenerate pseudorandom tensors from seeds
idea: Borrowed from seed-generated game worlds: any tensor that is pseudorandom by construction (random-feature projections, frozen random bases, sketch hash tables, dropout masks) is stored as a 64-bit seed and regenerated on demand by a counter-based Philox unit beside the tensor core. Models are trained with seeded frozen bases so only small learned coefficients are stored.
note: SeedLM/PRANC-like; few production models store large random tensors.

title: Ride-hail surge pricing for an intra-cluster DRAM spot market
idea: Borrowed from surge pricing: the cluster scheduler publishes a real-time internal price per GB-second of DRAM per rack; frameworks (Spark, LLM servers, JVMs) subscribe and automatically switch to compressed formats, smaller caches or quantized KV when the price spikes, with costs charged to team budgets.

title: VoIP silence suppression: never store zero or constant lines
idea: Borrowed from VoIP, which sends a tiny comfort-noise descriptor instead of silence: the memory controller keeps a per-page bitmap of zero or single-value 64-B lines, allocates no DRAM for them and synthesizes them on read, compacting the remaining lines into a smaller frame.

title: Seismic stacking: memory-side reduce-on-write for accumulation buffers
idea: Borrowed from seismic and astronomical co-adding, where traces are summed on arrival instead of stored: memory expanders implement vector add-on-write (FP32/BF16), so N producers (gradient buckets, histograms, embedding-gradient scatters) accumulate into one shared buffer instead of each holding a private copy for a later reduction.

title: Electricity spot market for rack-scale memory capacity and bandwidth
idea: Adapted from wholesale power markets with 5-minute nodal pricing: CXL-pooled memory in a cluster is auctioned in short intervals. Jobs bid for capacity and bandwidth, and lightly loaded servers sell their stranded DRAM back into the pool.
note: CXL pooling with market allocation; pooling itself is widely pursued.

title: Cellphone LTCC radio modules become 30-layer ceramic memory substrates
idea: Adapted from the low-temperature co-fired ceramic tape lines of 1990s handset RF front-ends: silver wiring is screen-printed on 30+ green tape layers with punched vias and co-fired, then DRAM dies are flip-chipped around a processor. Dense routing comes with no silicon interposer and no lithography below 50 um.

title: Shingled solar-cell stacking: staircase DRAM dies with adhesive edge joints
idea: Adapted from shingled PV modules: DRAM dies are stacked offset like roof shingles so each die's pad row stays exposed, and each step is joined with dispensed electrically conductive adhesive instead of wire bonds or TSVs.
note: Essentially Vertical Circuits/Invensas conductive-polymer stair-step stacking.

title: Telephone hybrid echo cancellation doubles bandwidth per memory pin
idea: Adapted from the 2-wire telephone hybrid and V.34/1000BASE-T echo cancellers: reads and writes travel on the same wire at the same moment, and each end subtracts its own transmitted signal using 180 nm analog circuits.

title: Canal-lock stepwise charging lowers memory bus switching energy
idea: Adapted from canal locks that lift boats in stages: bus lines charge in sequence from a ladder of N tank capacitors at intermediate voltages instead of straight from VDD, so each transition dissipates ~1/N of the conventional CV^2.

title: Railroad hump yard sorts memory requests on 180 nm buffer
idea: Adapted from gravity hump-yard classification: a 180 nm buffer chip between processor and DRAM bins incoming requests by bank and row onto 'classification tracks' with a deep sorting network. It then releases each 'train' as one activation followed by many column reads.

title: Display-driver tape-automated bonding puts memory dies on reel-to-reel film
idea: Adapted from the chip-on-film/TAB lines that bonded 1990s LCD driver chips: DRAM dies are bonded with anisotropic conductive film onto polyimide tape patterned at 20-30 um pitch, reel-to-reel and solder-free at 150-200 C. The memory tapes then attach around the processor.
note: COF/ACF bonding of DRAM dies; pitch too coarse for HBM-class buses.

title: Psychoacoustic masking applied to bit-plane refresh of AI tensors
idea: Adapted from MP3/AAC perceptual coding, which spends bits only where the ear notices: the controller stores bf16/fp8 weights bit-plane transposed so sign, exponent and high-mantissa planes sit in normally refreshed rows while low-mantissa planes sit in rows refreshed 8-16x less often; a per-layer sensitivity score (Hessian trace computed at load) sets how many planes each tensor sends to the slow-refresh zone.

title: Camera hot-pixel map: cell-level defect substitution table on die
idea: Adapted from CMOS image sensors, which ship with hundreds of dead pixels mapped out and patched in the ISP instead of scrapping the sensor: retention-weak and stuck cells found at test or in the field are recorded as compressed (row, column) entries in a small table on the logic base die, and a substitution engine overwrites those exact bit positions on every read with bits held in the table's own SRAM.

title: TCP congestion control for refresh: AIMD on correctable-error signals
idea: Adapted from TCP's additive-increase/multiplicative-decrease loop, which probes for capacity until packets drop: each bank's refresh interval is lengthened in small steps while on-die ECC reports zero corrections and halved immediately when the correction rate crosses a threshold, so refresh tracks the bank's real retention at its current temperature and age.

title: Food use-by dates: refresh-free perishable memory for short-lived data
idea: Adapted from perishable-food logistics, which ships milk faster than its shelf life instead of preserving it: a 28 nm logic-compatible 2T/3T gain-cell memory built in existing mature fabs never refreshes; allocations carry an expiry timestamp shorter than the measured retention, and the runtime places only short-lived data (activations, gradient buckets, network buffers) there, reallocating before expiry.

title: Kinetic-inductance nanowire loop storing a single flux quantum
idea: MINIFY the superconducting memory loop from ~10 um2 to ~0.1 um2 by replacing geometric inductance with NbN nanowire kinetic inductance; a bit is one circulating fluxon, written and read by nanocryotron (nTron) gates at 4 K.
note: Same KI nanowire loop memory.

title: Photonic-crystal nanocavity bistable bits in a silicon photonics foundry
idea: MINIFY optical bistable memory from fiber loops to ~1 um3 photonic-crystal nanocavities whose carrier-plasma bistability holds a bit at tens of nW bias; designed by a small team on a photonics MPW and written/read by wavelength-multiplexed light on the same bus used for chip-to-chip optical I/O.

title: Silicon-carbide CMOS foundry DRAM for 200 C environments
idea: MAGNIFY bandgap from 1.1 to 3.3 eV using a commercial 4H-SiC CMOS MPW: 1T1C or gain cells whose intrinsic carrier density is ~1e-8 cm^-3 (vs 1e10 in Si) retain data at 200 C longer than silicon DRAM does at 25 C; a small team sells into down-hole, aerospace and EV-inverter markets.
note: SiC DRAM cells demonstrated (Purdue 1990s); valuable niche, not mainstream.

title: Harvest and re-bin DRAM dies from retired server DIMMs
idea: MAGNIFY the life of existing storage elements: a small reverse-logistics shop buys decommissioned DDR4 DIMMs, retention-tests every die at elevated temperature, re-bins by refresh class and rebuilds CXL memory expanders whose controller applies per-die refresh rates.
note: DDR4 reuse behind CXL already pursued by hyperscalers; supply impact modest.

title: Barrier-free spin-orbit bit read by anomalous Hall cross
idea: MINIFY the magnetic stack to three sputtered layers with no tunnel barrier: a perpendicular Co dot on a Pt Hall cross is switched by spin-orbit torque from in-plane current and read by its anomalous Hall voltage with a differential sense amp, needing one litho step and one sputter run.
note: mV-level AHE read limits it to small cache arrays.

title: Minify the refreshed footprint: compress-then-park unrefreshed rows
idea: The memory controller compresses cold pages (base-delta/LZ, ~2-3x) into packed regions and disables refresh on the vacated rows using subarray-granular partial-array self-refresh, so the refreshed footprint shrinks with the data.

title: Magnify the log, minify the NV tier: per-store persistent journal
idea: Mirror every store into a 64 MB MRAM ring-buffer journal on the module (64 B appends via write combining) with periodic incremental snapshots to NAND; after power loss full DRAM state is rebuilt by snapshot plus journal replay.

title: Minify idle power to zero: park non-volatile memory ranks fully off
idea: Because NV working memory keeps data unpowered, the hypervisor consolidates hot pages and cuts power entirely (not just refresh) to idle ranks within microseconds, so a power-capped rack can install ~2x more memory at the same watts.

title: Thirty-two-cell averaged reference minifies reference error
idea: MAGNIFY the reference: each mat's sense reference is generated by charge-averaging 32 dummy cells written half 0 and half 1 at every refresh, so it tracks process, temperature and leakage with sqrt(32) less random error than a single dummy.

title: Per-driver BEOL bootstrap capacitor self-boosts every wordline
idea: Each wordline driver gets a local high-k MIM bootstrap capacitor (<=300 C) that capacitively lifts the selected wordline above VDD at the moment of selection, MINIFYING the global VPP network and its pump to a small reserve.

title: Minify the 3D demo: 4-tier Si/SiGe cells on 100 mm coupons
idea: Buy commercial Si/SiGe superlattice epitaxy wafers (about $5-10k each), then in a rented university cleanroom selectively remove SiGe, ALD gate and capacitor stacks, and demonstrate a 4-tier lateral-channel 1T1C cell with retention data in 18 months.
note: Credible low-cost data point; not a step change itself.

title: Magnify coil count, minify TSVs: inductive-coupled die stack
idea: Tape out a $100k 40 nm MPW chip with thousands of top-metal micro-coils as through-chip wireless links, then thin and glue-stack 8 dies with no TSVs to prove the bandwidth, energy per bit and yield gain.

title: Minify bitline noise: helical twisted bitlines across tiers
idea: In a 3D vertical-bitline array, route bitline pairs so they swap tier positions every 16 cells, forming a helix that cancels BL-BL coupling noise. Prove it with SPICE and extracted parasitics plus a small 130 nm MPW test array.
note: Twisted bitlines are classic DRAM; 3D extension is incremental.

title: Minify transferred tier to 30 nm: ion-cut two-tier 1T1C
idea: Use vendor Smart Cut SOI services to bond and transfer a 30 nm single-crystal Si film onto a first finished cell tier, then build the second tier below 450 C with laser anneal in a university fab, proving 2-tier monolithic 1T1C for about $500k.

title: Supercritical CO2 cleans and dries tall capacitors without ultrapure water
idea: Minify water and surface tension together: replace post-etch wet cleans and the UPW/IPA rinse-dry with supercritical CO2 plus a small co-solvent dose, so 70:1 pillars never feel capillary forces.

title: Hydrogen-free back end with titanium getters stabilizes oxide cells
idea: Minify the hydrogen inventory: deposit every dielectric above oxide-semiconductor transistors by ozone-ALD or PVD (no silane or NH3 PECVD), and wrap each array in a Ti/TiN getter cage so mobile hydrogen cannot reach channels during 10 years at 125 C.

title: Inductive chip-to-chip links stack memory dies without TSVs
idea: Minify vertical metal to zero: stack thinned memory dies and pass data through on-chip coil pairs (near-field inductive coupling), with power through edge wire bonds, eliminating TSVs, their copper fill and microbumps.

title: Liquid-silane ink laser-annealed into roll-to-roll polysilicon
idea: Magnify printed transistor mobility about 10x by coating cyclopentasilane ink and laser-crystallizing it into polysilicon on the web, giving ~100 cm2/Vs access and sense transistors.
note: Liquid-silane laser-crystallized Si is known (Shimoda 2006).

title: Minify every pointer to 32 bits with hardware expansion
idea: Minify 64-bit pointers to 32-bit region-relative offsets in a new C/C++ ABI mode. The load/store unit adds a per-region base register on the fly (like Java compressed oops, but for native code), and a trap widens a region if it overflows 4 GB x alignment.

title: Magnify similarity: LSH near-dedup with XOR deltas
idea: Magnify dedup from exact matches to near matches: locality-sensitive sketches find pages that are >=90% similar, and each is stored as a pointer to a base page plus a compressed XOR delta. Reconstruction runs inline in the CXL expander.

title: Minify integer widths with compiler value-range struct shrinking
idea: Minify data layouts at compile time: whole-program value-range analysis narrows fields (64 to 16 bits where provable), reorders fields to remove padding and packs booleans into bitfields. A guarded overflow trap re-widens a type at runtime if a profile was wrong.

title: Magnify the time axis: diurnal DRAM time-sharing
idea: Magnify memory scheduling from space to time: serving fleets lend 30-50% of their DRAM through CXL pooling to batch, ETL and training-data jobs off-peak. Pages come back within seconds via compressed swap when traffic rises.

title: Minify hash-table slack with near-memory probe engines
idea: Minify hash-table empty space: a near-memory probe engine runs cuckoo/Robin-Hood lookups at 95-97% load in a single round trip, instead of the 50-70% load software keeps for speed.

title: Minify backing for zeros: 64-byte sparse-backed virtual tensors
idea: Minify physical backing so only non-zero 64 B blocks of a tensor occupy DRAM: the MMU keeps a per-block occupancy bitmap, like a sparse file, and post-ReLU activations and 90%-structured-sparse weights get no frames for their zeros.

title: Sense amplifiers reused as 50 mV link receivers
idea: MINIFY signal swing to ~50 mV by using the DRAM's own latch-type bitline sense-amplifier design (already built to resolve ~100 mV) as the receiver for low-swing differential links between DRAM and base die.
note: StrongARM-style latch receivers for low-swing links are standard; 100x claim ignores driver and clock overhead.

title: Descriptor-driven memory with no command bus
idea: MINIFY command traffic: the host writes access descriptors (stride, gather list, tile shape) once, and the base die generates every address itself, so the bus carries only data.
note: Same descriptor-driven no-command-bus mechanism.

title: Minify hammer aim: re-keyed row permutation every refresh window
idea: Each subarray maps logical to physical rows through a 16-bit keyed Feistel permutation. During refresh the controller re-keys one subarray per window and migrates its rows with in-DRAM RowClone, so a hammering pattern loses its physical neighbors within ~64 ms.

title: Minify temperature: sealed -30C DIMM enclosures stretch retention 1000x
idea: Run DRAM in sealed, dry-nitrogen DIMM enclosures held near -30C by thermoelectric or two-phase cold plates, so condensation cannot form. Junction and GIDL leakage roughly halve per 10C, so retention rises ~1000x versus 85C operation.
note: Cooling cost vs modest refresh savings.

title: Magnify ECC scope to the rack: erasure-coded CXL memory pools
idea: Stripe CXL-pooled memory with a 10+2 Reed-Solomon code across separate memory modules, so a dead chip or module is rebuilt rather than lost. Individual DRAM dies drop on-die ECC and ship with relaxed specs.

title: Minify ECC latency by speculating data and replaying on error
idea: Forward read data to the core before ECC finishes. The decoder runs in parallel, and on a rare error it raises a poison/replay signal that flushes dependent instructions, as after a branch mispredict.
note: Speculative ECC forwarding known in literature.

title: Magnify burn-in to days: catch variable-retention cells on panel racks
idea: Run every finished glass panel through a multi-day 125C burn-in in racks while repeatedly profiling retention. Variable-retention-time cells, whose telegraph states can take hours to appear, are caught and remapped before shipping.
note: Long burn-in catches more VRT, but new VRT cells appear in field.

title: Magnify scrub rate with one tiny patrol engine per panel tile
idea: Put a tiny patrol-scrub engine in each of thousands of panel tiles. It reads, corrects and rewrites its tile every ~100 ms, far faster than DRAM's one scrubber per die, so a single-bit error is fixed before a second lands in the same codeword.

title: Magnify technician output 10x with a fab digital-twin academy
idea: Build a physics-accurate VR digital twin of a DRAM fab (tool faults, contamination events, yield excursions) so community colleges certify technicians in 3 months instead of 2 years of on-the-job training.
note: VR fab training already offered by vendors.

title: Eliminate resistance: superconducting persistent-current loop cryogenic memory tier
idea: Store each bit as a clockwise or counter-clockwise persistent current in a superconducting NbN loop, accessed through a kinetic-inductance nanowire switch briefly driven normal by a write pulse. A persistent current never decays, so there is no leakage and no refresh; deploy as a 4 K tier beside superconducting or quantum compute.
note: Nanocryotron loop memories already demonstrated; cryo niche.

title: Eliminate refresh of unallocated memory: OS free-page refresh mask
idea: The OS page allocator exports a free/zeroed-page bitmap to the memory controller over a CXL or DDR mode-register channel; rows holding only free pages are excluded from refresh and zero-filled on reallocation. Servers commonly leave 20-50% of DRAM unallocated or as droppable clean cache.
note: Close to PASR/ESKIMO prior art.

title: Eliminate per-cell access transistors: CCD recirculating memory from university nanofab
idea: Build a three-phase surface-channel CCD (two poly levels, 2 um contact lithography, standard university processing) in which data circulate as charge packets past a regenerating sense stage each lap; no cell has its own access transistor or junction leak path, and each lap is the refresh. Target streaming weight memory where access is sequential anyway.
note: 1970s CCD memories existed; sequential access is not DRAM-class random access.

title: Eliminate thermal generation: 4H-SiC MOS dynamic memory cell
idea: Build 1T1C cells on purchased 4H-SiC epi wafers with NO-annealed thermal oxide and an npn or MOS access device; with a 3.26 eV gap the thermal generation rate is ~1e-17 of silicon's, so stored charge lasts hours or longer at room temperature, as early academic SiC test cells showed. University fabs already process SiC power devices.
note: Purdue demonstrated SiC DRAM cells in the 1990s; density and wafer cost limit it.

title: Eliminate the substrate body: XeF2-released suspended nanowire gate-all-around access device
idea: Pattern Si nanowires by e-beam lithography, undercut them with XeF2 vapor so they hang free, then wrap them with ALD HfO2/TiN to form a gate-all-around access device with no body contact and no junction to substrate. The storage node connects only to the suspended wire.

title: Eliminate dummy mats: auto-zeroed self-referenced open-bitline sensing
idea: Remove the reference bitline and the half-populated dummy arrays that 6F2 open-bitline mats need at their edges. Each SA samples its own bitline onto a 2 fF capacitor just before the wordline rises and again after charge sharing, and a switched-capacitor comparator decides on the difference, cancelling SA offset and precharge error in the same step.

title: Eliminate temperature sensors and refresh timers: canary-row retention sentinels
idea: Delete the on-die thermal sensors, refresh-rate tables and fixed 64 ms timer. Each bank instead holds 4 canary rows built with ~60% of normal Cs, checked periodically, and the bank refreshes only when a canary loses its pattern. Refresh then tracks actual leakage, including the 13 fA tail, at the current temperature and voltage.

title: Eliminate redundancy fuses: spare-free dies with controller-side row retirement
idea: Strip spare rows and columns, eFuse/antifuse banks and repair CAMs from the die. Each die ships a bad-row bitmap measured at wafer test and stored in SPD flash, and the controller remaps failing rows into a reserved 0.5% of normal rows through a 4-way hashed remap table.

title: Eliminate photoresist: area-selective deposition self-aligned to lower tiers
idea: Use vapour-delivered inhibitor molecules that adsorb only on dielectric (or only on metal) so the next film grows only where the underlying tier's pattern allows, eliminating resist coat, aqueous TMAH develop and wet strip for self-aligned layers.
note: Resist-free self-aligned layers via ASD; widely pursued, water framing is the only new angle.

title: Eliminate TSVs: shingled stacks with laser-written edge interconnect
idea: Stack dies offset like roof shingles so each die's pad row is exposed, then write vertical interconnect down the stepped edge with laser direct-write or aerosol-jet silver, with no TSV etch, liner, copper plating or reveal.

title: Eliminate wafer slicing and polishing: dry spalled kerfless donor films
idea: Peel 20-50 um silicon films from an ingot face by controlled spalling with a sputtered stressor layer instead of wire-sawing, lapping and polishing wafers, and use the films as thin tier donors for stacked arrays.

title: Eliminate retention-test hours: profile weak cells silently inside refresh
idea: Skip the long hot pause and retention tests on ATE; the die uses part of each JEDEC tRFC window to read-compare sample rows at stretched intervals, learns which rows sit in the leakage tail and refreshes them more often internally. The host still issues standard REF commands.
note: Similar to published online profiling (REAPER/AVATAR); FPGA-demoable.

title: Eliminate storage for all-zero cache lines in the memory controller
idea: A per-page 64-bit presence bitmap in the controller marks zero 64B lines, which occupy no DRAM; nonzero lines are packed contiguously and the bitmap is cached on-chip, so a zero-line read costs no DRAM access at all.

title: Eliminate redundant buffer copies with OS move-semantics page ownership
idea: The OS gains a linear-ownership primitive: a buffer moves from NIC to kernel to app to serializer by page remapping with the old mapping revoked, so a request path holds one copy of data instead of 3-4.
note: fbufs/IO-Lite style remapping is old art.

title: Eliminate unused high bits with profile-guided field narrowing
idea: An LLVM plugin records observed value ranges of struct fields in production profiles, then shrinks int64 fields to 8/16/32 bits, bit-packs booleans and reorders fields to remove padding, with trap-on-overflow guards.
note: Profile-guided struct narrowing; guards add complexity.

title: Eliminate VFIO memory pinning with IOMMU page-fault passthrough
idea: A hypervisor patch set uses ATS/PRI page-request faults so GPU/NIC passthrough VMs stop pinning all guest memory, letting those VMs be overcommitted and ballooned like ordinary ones.

title: Eliminate Python object boxing with tagged-pointer CPython build
idea: A drop-in CPython fork encodes small ints and floats as tagged pointers and stores homogeneous lists as unboxed typed arrays, keeping C-API compatibility through lazy boxing.

title: Eliminate peak provisioning with an internal revocable DRAM spot market
idea: A cluster agent sells revocable memory leases to batch jobs at a price set by node pressure, and reclaims leased pages within 100 ms by compressing them to zswap when the owner needs them back.

title: Eliminate DRAM from inference: model pipelined across FPGA SRAM boards
idea: A small team builds a chassis of off-the-shelf FPGAs linked by serial transceivers; each FPGA holds a slice of a quantized model entirely in its on-chip URAM/BRAM, and tokens stream through the pipeline with no external DRAM.

title: Non-volatile PHY state enables nanosecond link sleep and wake
idea: Eliminate link retraining: store each lane's DFE taps, CTLE settings, phase offsets and VREF in ferroelectric latches inside the PHY, so the entire memory PHY can be power-gated between bursts and resume in <100 ns with no retraining.
note: Retention registers already hold taps; CDR/PLL relock is the real wake cost.

title: ADC-free time-domain readout of ferroelectric weight crossbars
idea: Eliminate the ADCs that dominate compute-in-memory: stationary NV weights in a FeFET crossbar discharge a precharged column at a rate proportional to the dot product, and a pulse-width output feeds the next layer or a time-to-digital counter.

title: Epoch-tagged dual-slot lines make crash consistency fence-free
idea: Eliminate persist barriers and write-ahead logging: each NV line has two slots; writes go to the uncommitted slot tagged with a hardware epoch, and a single per-epoch commit record flips which slot is valid, so recovery discards incomplete epochs automatically.
note: Shadow paging/epoch persistency well studied.

title: Switch-side erasure coding replaces triple-replicated persistent memory
idea: Eliminate 3x replication traffic for durable in-memory state: the CXL switch stripes NV memory writes across 10+4 Reed-Solomon shards on different modules and computes parity in the switch, so state survives power loss and module failure.

title: Eliminate ECC from the critical path: speculative data use with rollback
idea: Forward raw data to the core immediately and run a much stronger, slower code (2-symbol RS or LDPC over 256 B) in parallel. A detected error squashes dependent instructions, as a branch mispredict does, and replays them with corrected data.

title: Eliminate unknown error locations: treat mapped weak cells as erasures
idea: Store the boot-profiled weak-cell positions for each codeword and pass them to the decoder as erasures. An RS code with 2r parity symbols corrects 2r erasures but only r unknown errors, so correction strength doubles at the same overhead.
note: Same erasure-map decoding.

title: Eliminate price opacity: public DRAM contract index and cash-settled swaps
idea: Eliminate opaque bilateral pricing: a ~$700k startup gathers anonymized contract and spot trades from buyers, publishes a daily DRAM bit index, and partners with a commodity broker to offer cash-settled swaps.

title: Eliminate laptop-memory dead end: SO-DIMM-to-CXL carrier card
idea: Eliminate the form-factor dead end of laptop memory: an FPGA-based CXL Type-3 card hosts eight mixed DDR4 SO-DIMMs harvested from e-waste laptops and presents them to modern servers as a slow capacity tier; $1M covers board design, controller IP and a 200-card pilot.

title: Store the absence: deep-depletion SiC capacitors hold bits for years
idea: Reverse what the bit is: a 4H-SiC MOS capacitor pulsed into deep depletion stores '1' as a missing inversion layer; with a 3.26 eV gap, thermal generation is ~1e18 slower than silicon, so the empty state lasts years at room temperature. Built on 150 mm SiC power lines with 0.5-1 um steppers.

title: Core memory reborn: electroplated permalloy nano-toroid stacks
idea: Swap charge for flux: plate 1 um permalloy rings around through-mask copper posts (1990s thin-film-head plating) in 20 tiers, select by coincident X/Y half-currents and sense on a shared winding, a destructive read like DRAM but with zero leakage and unlimited endurance.

title: Cold old node: 77 K planar-capacitor DRAM at 180 nm
idea: Reverse the scaling logic: run a 180 nm 1T1C array whose storage element is only a planar MOS capacitor (no trench, no stack) at liquid-nitrogen temperature, where junction and subthreshold leakage fall >1e6, so a 2 fF planar cap holds data for hours while the transistors gain mobility and steeper slope.
note: Same cryo-leakage trade; old node keeps capital low but density poor.

title: Capacitor that shrinks on read: gated-diode voltage amplification
idea: Reverse the capacitor's role mid-operation: a 180 nm gated diode stores charge in its inversion layer; on read the gate is raised so capacitance collapses from Cox to Cdep, pushing the charge out as a 3-5x larger bitline voltage swing, built-in gain without a sense transistor.
note: IBM gated-diode amplifier cell already published.

title: One contact for eight bits: NAND-chained capacitor strings
idea: Rearrange cells from parallel to series: chain eight 180 nm 1T1C cells with one bitline contact (as in early-1990s NAND-structured DRAM proposals), read them destructively in fixed order from the contact end and write back in reverse order, so contacts no longer set cell area.
note: Toshiba's 1990s NAND-structured DRAM.

title: Bit-plane layout: MSB planes refresh fast, LSB planes rarely
idea: Rearrange tensor layout: transpose AI weights and activations into bit-planes so each DRAM row holds one significance level, then give sign/MSB rows normal refresh and the lowest 3-4 bit-plane rows 8-16x slower refresh. Rare decay flips in LSB planes perturb values by less than quantization noise, which models already tolerate.
note: Bit-significance refresh tiers (Flikker, Sparkk) already proposed; FPGA demo easy.

title: DIMM buffer chip takes over refresh with per-row retention map
idea: Rearrange who owns refresh: at OSAT test, profile each die's per-row retention under hot, pattern-stressed conditions and store a compressed weak-row list in a 28 nm buffer/register chip on the DIMM. The buffer intercepts host REF commands, keeps the DRAM out of auto-refresh, and issues RAS-only (ACT/PRE) refreshes at 64 ms only to the ~1% weak rows and at 256 ms+ to the rest.

title: Back-gate dynamic threshold on existing 22/28 nm FD-SOI lines
idea: Rearrange threshold control from fixed doping to a live back gate: build 1T1C eDRAM cells with MIM capacitors on existing 22FDX/28FDS FD-SOI processes, holding the array's back-gate well at strong reverse bias in hold (Vt +250-300 mV) and switching it to forward bias only for the subarray being accessed. The thin BOX also isolates the storage node from the substrate, so there is no storage-node junction leakage.
note: Dynamic reverse back-bias in hold on FD-SOI eDRAM; known knob, niche eDRAM segment.

title: Weak rows get the hottest-written data
idea: Reverse page placement: the OS uses a per-row retention map to put frequently rewritten pages (stacks, network buffers, KV-cache heads) onto the weakest rows, since every write restores them, and cold read-mostly pages onto the strongest rows. The refresh interval then follows the strong rows.
note: Retention-aware placement (RAPID) is prior art.

title: Sense-amp latches become CPU-addressable cache, array the backing store
idea: Reverse the roles of periphery and array: SA latches become low-leakage retention latches that hold a row for milliseconds, tags live in the controller, and the open rows of all banks (tens of MB) serve as a directly addressed last-level cache; the array is touched only on misses.
note: Cached DRAM / virtual-channel memory prior art.

title: Back-plane under each tier becomes a retention lock
idea: Reverse the gate side: each IGZO tier sits on a blanket conductive back-plane, held at 0 V during access and pulsed to about -1 V when the subarray idles, pushing the channel deep into depletion. The only added mask is the back-plane contact.

title: Talk through the stack, not drill it: inductive die coupling
idea: Rearrange vertical connection from metal to field: stack thinned DRAM dies that exchange data by on-chip inductive coils (wireless near-field links) instead of copper TSVs.

title: Zero scrap: every die sold with its error map
idea: Reverse yield accounting: instead of discarding dies that fail repair, grade all dies by measured raw BER up to 1% and sell them as error-mapped memory for ECC-heavy AI inference tiers.

title: Ship it unrepaired: the host controller does the repair
idea: Reverse who repairs: remove laser fuses, redundancy rows and much of the repair test from the die; ship with an on-die defect map read at boot and let the memory controller remap bad rows like an SSD flash translation layer.
note: Close to ArchShield and controller sparing art.

title: Crystal-plane etch: the silicon lattice draws the trenches
idea: Reverse plasma-defined walls to crystal-defined walls: on (110) silicon wafers, a coarse KrF mask opens slots and anisotropic wet etch (TMAH-like) stops on vertical {111} planes, giving atomically smooth, ultra-high-AR buried-wordline or capacitor trenches.

title: Threads migrate to data so each cluster byte exists once
idea: Reverse data-to-compute: for read-mostly shared sets (embedding tables, graphs) each node holds a disjoint shard, and lightweight threads or continuations hop to the node that owns the next address (Emu-style migration) instead of every node caching replicas.

title: PGO reorders struct fields fleet-wide to delete padding
idea: Rearrange fields literally: a link-time pass uses profiles to reorder struct members by size and co-access, move cold fields into side tables and rewrite every access, applied automatically across a fleet's C, C++ and Rust builds.

title: Follow-the-sun memory: batch work chases idle DRAM across continents
idea: Rearrange workloads in time and space: batch inference, embedding generation and analytics move every few hours to regions whose interactive demand is in its nightly trough, so each region's DRAM is sized for a flattened global load instead of its local peak.
note: Geo-shifting batch work for diurnal troughs; same core as I-03975.

title: Transpose in the base die: return columns, not rows
idea: Rearrange data order at the stack boundary: a small SRAM corner-turn buffer in the HBM base die gathers strided elements (e.g. one head's slice across many tokens of a KV cache) from open rows in many banks and packs them into dense column-major bursts, so the link carries only the bytes requested.

title: Bumpless capacitive face-to-face: the passivation is the link
idea: Reverse 'remove the dielectric to connect': leave the 0.5-1 um passivation intact, use 5 um pads on each die as coupling capacitors, and align the dies face-to-face with an adhesive; pulse-mode receivers detect the coupled edges, so no UBM, solder or CMP-grade hybrid-bond surface is needed.
note: Sun's proximity communication demonstrated this.

title: Photonic wire bonds written after chips are placed
idea: Reverse align-then-place: place memory-side and host-side photonic dies coarsely (+-10 um), image their couplers, and write freeform polymer waveguides between them by two-photon lithography, so the link adapts to placement error rather than demanding sub-micron alignment.
note: Already demonstrated (KIT, Vanguard).

title: Alignment-free z-axis film from anodized-alumina nanowires
idea: Reverse 'align pad to pad': anodize a porous alumina film (~100 nm pores at 200 nm pitch), electroplate copper nanowires through it, and laminate it between memory and logic dies; any pad overlap connects through many parallel nanowires while the alumina insulates laterally, so pitch is set by pad size, not alignment accuracy.

title: Asymmetric Z-channel codes for one-way charge-loss errors
idea: Flip the symmetric-error assumption: retention and hammer errors in true-cells are almost all 1->0, so the array is built with true-cells only (no anti-cells) so every cell leaks toward the same logical value, and SECDED is replaced by unidirectional-error codes (Bose-Lin / Z-channel LDPC) that need fewer check bits per corrected error.

title: Idle-time self-hammering maps each row's true flip threshold
idea: Reverse attacker and defender: in idle windows the controller copies a row aside, hammers it with known patterns, records the activation count at first flip, and programs per-row thresholds into mitigation logic, re-running as the chip ages.
note: Svard-like; read-disturb thresholds vary over time.

title: Hydrocarbon-refrigerant chilled memory tier that barely refreshes
idea: Flip from refreshing hot memory to chilling it: a capacity-tier DRAM shelf is held near -20 C by propane (R290) or CO2 (R744) vapor-compression loops instead of HFC refrigerants or fluorinated immersion fluids, stretching retention ~1000x so refresh drops to seconds.
note: Cold DRAM known; chiller energy offsets refresh savings.

title: Proximity meniscus rinse: water touches only a moving strip
idea: Rearrange rinsing from flooding the wafer to scanning a proximity head that holds a thin meniscus against it, like an immersion-litho water hood. The head supplies and vacuums water at the same time and dries the wafer by the Marangoni effect.

title: Deliberately weakened canary capacitors trigger targeted per-mat rejuvenation
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying: place a few 'canary' copies of the storage element in every mat, built with ~20% thinner dielectric or smaller Cs so they age first; their retention, checked during refresh, triggers the heal action (anneal, detox pulse or spare swap) for that mat only.
note: Canary cells known; modest guard-band recovery.

title: Deliberately weak canary cells trigger refresh per mat only when needed
idea: TRIZ #11 Beforehand cushioning: plant a sacrificial early warning. Each mat includes a few canary cells with ~50% of normal capacitance and a slightly leakier junction; a tiny always-on comparator polls them, and the mat is refreshed only when a canary flips, automatically tracking local temperature, voltage, aging and process corner (ECC backs up the rare cell weaker than its canary).
note: Monitor/replica-cell refresh tuning is patented prior art; temperature-compensated refresh already captures much of the gain.

title: Leak-safe polarity coding; rows with no charged cells skip refresh
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: instead of fighting the direction leakage pushes, store data in the state leakage drives toward. A per-64-bit inversion flag chosen at write time minimises the number of charged cells; rows whose charged-cell count is zero (zeroed pages, sparse or quantised tensors) are flagged and never refreshed, and refresh priority follows charged-cell count.
note: Zero-value refresh skipping with inversion is published art.

title: Asymmetry: leak-aware reference skew plus non-leaking-state data encoding
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: cells leak only from '1' toward '0', so the sense reference is shifted toward the '0' side, letting decaying '1's stay readable much longer, while the controller applies a per-64 B invert flag so that at least half the stored bits sit in the non-leaking discharged state that tolerates the reduced margin.
note: True/anti-cell layout complicates which state is non-leaking.

title: Hydrogen replaces helium as wafer backside coolant and carrier gas
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter change, resolving 'need a high-conductivity heat-transfer gas' vs 'helium is scarce': switch electrostatic-chuck backside cooling and CVD/ALD carrier flows from He to H2 (D2 where isotope passivation helps) at 5-20 Torr, where H2 conducts heat as well as or better than He (0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K). Leak rates stay below the flammability limit by design, supply comes from on-site electrolysis, and exhaust goes to the existing burn abatement.

title: Supercritical-CO2 release deletes capacitor support-lattice masks
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics/hydraulics: replace liquid mold-strip and drying, whose capillary forces topple tall pillars, with anhydrous mold removal and supercritical-CO2 drying; with zero surface tension, freestanding 80-100:1 pillars survive without SiN support meshes.

title: Matryoshka weight residency: MSB nest in DRAM, residual off-board
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: quantize weights with nested codebooks so the 4-bit code is literally the top nibble of the 8-bit code; DRAM/HBM holds only the 4-bit nest while the residual nibble sits in CXL memory or flash and is streamed per layer only when a cheap per-token confidence probe says that layer needs full precision.
note: Matryoshka quantization (2025) exists.

title: Provision DRAM at median compression ratio with emergency spill tier
idea: TRIZ #11 Beforehand cushioning: size each server's physical DRAM for the median, not worst-case, compression ratio and pre-install a cushion (a small battery-backed NAND-on-CXL tier plus a pinned 3% reserve) that absorbs a ratio collapse instantly while the scheduler migrates the offending workload away.
note: Operational strategy for compressed memory overcommit; ratio-collapse risk handled by spill tier.

title: Anti-correlated memory-peak co-scheduling across a cluster
idea: TRIZ #12 Equipotentiality: profile each job's memory-over-time curve and bin-pack jobs whose peaks are anti-correlated (phase-shifted GC cycles, batch vs interactive, prefill vs decode) onto the same host, so hosts are sized for the peak of the sum instead of the sum of peaks; memory stays 'level' instead of every host being lifted to peak.

title: Cache-resident streaming rings that skip DRAM entirely
idea: TRIZ #21 Skipping: NICs and SSDs inject data into an LLC-pinned ring (DDIO-style) whose credit-based flow control is matched to the consumer's processing rate, so streaming data is consumed and dropped before it is ever written back to DRAM.
note: DDIO-style; known direction.

title: Seed-regenerated tensors replace stored random matrices
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying: replace stored pseudo-random data (random projections, sketch matrices, hash tables, dropout masks, random-feature kernels) by a seed plus a counter-based PRNG (Philox-style) unit near memory that regenerates any element on access, a perfect copy that costs no bits.

title: 640K-style memory budgets enforced in CI and procurement
idea: TRIZ #9 Preliminary anti-action: stop bloat before it ships; every service declares bytes-per-request and bytes-per-session budgets that CI heap profilers check (a regression fails the build), and public procurement scores bids on measured DRAM per transaction, much as 1990s developers lived within 640 KB.

title: Deterministic lockstep replay replaces resident state for idle actors
idea: TRIZ #17 Another dimension: store idle entities (game objects, agents, session actors, simulation cells) in the time dimension, keeping only their input event log since the last checkpoint, and regenerate state by deterministic replay when touched, the way 1997-era RTS games synchronized by inputs only.

title: Retired-DIMM far-memory sleds behind 180 nm bridge controllers
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap short-living objects: harvest DDR3/DDR4 modules from decommissioned servers into sleds run at derated speed (DDR3-800 class) by 180 nm bridge controllers with ~3 Gb/s SerDes, exposing them as a compressed far-memory tier for cold pages.

title: Equipotentiality: constant-voltage current-mode TSV signaling
idea: TRIZ #12 Equipotentiality (avoid raising and lowering): a low-impedance common-gate receiver holds each TSV at a fixed mid-rail voltage, and data is sent as the direction of a ~50 uA current. The TSV and microbump capacitance never charges or discharges.

title: Periodic action: follow-the-sun scheduling of memory-heavy jobs
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action: memory sits idle on a daily cycle. A global scheduler moves memory-hungry batch jobs (fine-tuning, embedding builds, KV-heavy batch inference) to regions during their off-peak hours and leases out idle DRAM pools through CXL-attached capacity APIs. (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)

title: Parameter change: chilled DRAM zones cut refresh bandwidth theft
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter changes: give DRAM its own 10-20 C coolant loop on a cold plate separate from the 60 C compute loop, built from existing chiller hardware. Retention roughly doubles for every ~10 C drop, so the refresh interval can stretch 4-8x through standard temperature-controlled refresh modes. (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)
note: Known retention-temperature physics; chiller energy and nonstandard refresh modes erode gain.

title: Phase transition: transient-liquid-phase bonding stacks DRAM in standard reflow
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transitions: replace scarce hybrid bonders with Cu-Sn transient-liquid-phase bonding in existing OSAT reflow and thermocompression tools. A thin Sn layer melts and converts to high-melting Cu3Sn, so later tiers bond at ~20 um pitch without remelting earlier ones. (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)

title: Bit-significance placement: exponent in strong rows, mantissa in leaky
idea: TRIZ #16 Partial action: the controller splits BF16/FP8 tensors so sign/exponent bits go to fully refreshed, ECC-protected rows while low mantissa bits go to rows refreshed 16x less often or to weak-binned dies, sold as an AI-grade memory SKU.
note: Close to EDEN/Flikker approximate DRAM; weak-die SKU angle adds supply value.

title: Unrepaired weak cells kept as live refresh-rate governors
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: instead of repairing every weak cell, ~1,000 known-weak cells per bank stay in place holding a known pattern; checking them each window measures real leakage (temperature, aging, radiation) and sets refresh just above their failure point.

title: U.S. reliability-broker buffer remediates sub-spec domestic DRAM dies
idea: TRIZ #24 Intermediary: a CXL/DIMM buffer chip fabbed on a U.S. mature logic line (12-22 nm class in New York) runs a strong LDPC code plus row remap over dies from U.S. DRAM fabs that fail JEDEC retention or hammer bins, and the module ships as spec-compliant.

title: Errors as cache misses: detect-only DRAM refetches peer replica
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: for read-only AI weights replicated across a cluster, U.S.-made inference memory carries only a cheap CRC per 4 KB page; a detected error discards the page and refetches it from a peer node's copy over the fabric, so cells may run at raw BER ~1e-5.

title: Strong oxidants: ozone leaching recovers tungsten from fab waste streams
idea: TRIZ #38 Strong oxidants: ozone/peroxide oxidative leaching recovers tungsten from CVD-W chamber cleans, CMP slurry and scrap wafers as tungstate, refined back to WF6 on-site; no lithography mask is added at all.

title: Pheromone-evaporation allocator expires short-lived data without refresh
idea: Ant trails evaporate on purpose; an allocator API (malloc_ttl) places data with lifetime shorter than retention (activations, scratch KV, network buffers living 1-20 ms) in rows whose refresh is disabled by an 'evaporating' bit, and the row traps on read after its TTL.

title: Sparse neural coding keeps most cells in the non-leaking state
idea: Cortex fires sparsely to save energy; encode each word with an inversion flag (or a low-weight 8b/9b code, aware of true- and anti-cell polarity) so 60-70% of cells sit in the discharged state that cannot lose data, and skip refresh on rows whose code flags them all-discharged (zero pages).
note: Zero-row skipping and polarity-aware encoding known.

title: Cell-membrane-mimetic molecular seal on oxide-FET back channels
idea: Lipid bilayers are only 5 nm thick yet nearly impermeable to ions; seal the exposed back channel of BEOL oxide access FETs with a densely packed fluoroalkyl phosphonic-acid monolayer (vapor-deposited at 120 C) capped by ALD Al2O3, blocking the O2/H2O adsorption that creates surface donor states and random-telegraph Vt jumps.
note: SAM back-channel passivation of IGZO TFTs is known.

title: Electrocyte-stacked access pair exploits series-stack leakage suppression
idea: Electric eels stack electrocytes in series; build each BEOL access device as two vertically stacked oxide FETs on one wordline, so in the off-state the floating midpoint self-biases, giving the upper FET negative Vgs and reduced Vds, at zero extra footprint because the stack is vertical.

title: Olfactory combinatorial 3-of-24 constant-weight wordline decoder
idea: About 400 olfactory receptor types encode trillions of odors combinatorially. Replace one-hot predecode with a constant-weight code: each local wordline driver connects to a unique triplet of 24 shared select lines (2,024 triplets) through a vertical 3-gate stacked transistor. Only the triplet with all three lines high fires, and every other triplet has at most two high.
note: m-of-n decoding is known art; 3-gate stack is the twist.

title: Cuckoo strategy: host raises the on-die ECC and hammer logic
idea: Cuckoos let other birds raise their chicks. Write a JEDEC-style proposal plus open reference RTL in which the host controller does what each die's periphery does today (on-die ECC, refresh-management counters, thermal refresh) using metadata in ordinary rows, so 'lean' dies can omit those circuits. Three engineers, FPGA demo and standards work, ~$900k in 24 months.

title: Retinal light adaptation: sense references track hot cells' decay
idea: The retina adapts by referencing each photoreceptor to its neighbourhood average; in each 3D mat keep a few reference cells per row written with 1 and 0 alongside the data, and derive the sense reference from their live average so the threshold drifts down with the same temperature-driven leakage as the data cells.

title: Hydra stem-cell renewal: retire rows as they age at temperature
idea: Hydra avoids ageing by continuously replacing worn cells from stem cells; profile every row's retention in the background at 125 C and progressively retire rows whose retention or variable-retention-time behaviour degrades into a 2-3% spare-row pool, updating a per-bank remap table over the decade.
note: Online retention profiling and row retirement echo RAIDR/AVATAR; niche at 125 C.

title: Aquaporin-studded roll-to-roll membranes for ultrapure water reclaim
idea: Aquaporin channels pass about a billion water molecules per second while rejecting ions. Embed aquaporins or synthetic pillar[5]arene water channels in roll-to-roll-cast polyamide reverse-osmosis films for the UPW reclaim loop, running at about half the pressure of standard RO.

title: Kidney countercurrent membrane cascade recovers helium from tool exhaust
idea: The loop of Henle multiplies concentration with countercurrent flow across selective membranes. Put roll-to-roll-cast polymer membrane sheets (polyimide or PIM films) in a countercurrent cascade on etch and CVD exhaust, concentrating dilute helium stage by stage to >99.999% for reinjection.

title: Bone-remodeling deposit-and-resorb supercycles self-align contacts without masks
idea: Bone is laid down and resorbed continuously, with net growth only where signals favor it; run ALD supercycles that deposit a dielectric everywhere and then a short etch that removes the thinner nuclei on metal but not the faster-grown film on oxide, repeated ~30x, so an isolation mask grows only on dielectric and contacts self-align.

title: Epigenetic methylation bits trigger heterochromatin-style in-place page compaction
idea: Each 4 KB page carries 2 'methylation' bits set by the OS or ML runtime; methylated pages are packed by the controller into dense heterochromatin form (entropy-coded, 3-4x) inside the same DIMM while acetylated pages stay open and uncompressed. Marks are inherited by forked or copied pages, like epigenetic inheritance through cell division.

title: Ebbinghaus forgetting curve erodes low-order bits of aging data
idea: Tagged tensors (cached activations, retrieval embeddings, KV) lose least-significant bits on a forgetting schedule unless re-accessed, with each access acting as rehearsal that resets the clock; the controller periodically repacks eroded lines into denser formats.

title: Quorum sensing decides when shared pages get local replicas
idea: Bacteria act only when autoinducer concentration crosses a threshold; each host counts remote accesses to a pooled page from its cores, makes a local replica only when demand crosses a quorum, and dissolves it when the signal decays, otherwise serving the page from the shared CXL pool.

title: Fly mushroom-body hashing finds near-duplicate pages for delta storage
idea: Fruit flies tag odors via random sparse expansion then winner-take-all; the controller applies the same FlyHash to sampled page contents to bucket near-duplicates, storing each as a delta against a bucket representative (checkpoints, VM snapshots, model replicas with slight drift).
note: Difference Engine did similarity-based page patching.

title: Salmon-run return: retired GPUs serve their HBM as KV pools
idea: Salmon die upstream and fertilize the forest; aging training GPUs are redeployed as dedicated KV-cache and expert-weight memory nodes over NVLink or RDMA, running only memory-serving firmware, so their HBM keeps supplying fast capacity to new accelerators instead of being shredded.

title: Genome-like health ledger travels with every memory module
idea: Each module stores a tamper-evident lifetime record (hours, temperature, ECC events, hammer counts, repairs) in extended SPD, like DNA carrying heritable history, readable by any buyer or recycler to price and place the module in its next life; mandated in procurement standards.

title: Myelinated interposer links with nodes-of-Ranvier regenerators
idea: Long GPU-to-memory interposer wires are cut into insulated segments wrapped in a thick low-k 'myelin' sheath, with tiny sense-and-restore 'nodes' every ~1 mm that regenerate a ~100 mV low-swing signal, as in saltatory conduction. Energy is spent only charging short low-capacitance segments, so memory stacks can sit 10-20 mm from the logic instead of 1-2 mm.

title: Penguin-huddle rotation: migrate hot data so no stack overheats
idea: Emperor penguins take turns between the cold edge and the warm centre of the huddle. Likewise the memory controller tracks per-stack temperature and periodically moves the hottest pages from stacks next to the GPU hotspot to cooler edge stacks, keeping every stack below the 85 C point where refresh doubles.
note: Thermal-aware memory management is prior art.

title: Lesion-wiring: fine-tune each model on its own DIMM's fault map
idea: Like a developing brain rewiring around a lesion, an accelerator profiles its own HBM's weak-cell map at a relaxed 1 s refresh, then runs a short fine-tune in which exactly those weight bits are clamped to their decayed values, so the deployed model stops depending on them and weight regions run permanently at the relaxed refresh.
note: Similar to EDEN and Matic error-aware retraining.

title: Deinococcus polyploidy: scattered multi-copy for the critical 1% only
idea: Deinococcus radiodurans survives shattered chromosomes by keeping 4-10 genome copies and reassembling; replicate only page tables, kernel and allocator metadata 3-4x across banks with different physical neighbours and TSV columns, repairing by consensus on read, so the other 99% of memory runs with much lighter ECC.
note: Selective protection of critical data is known; modest ECC savings.

title: Wolff's-law remodeling: hot rows migrate into guard-flanked bunkers
idea: Bone reinforces where it is loaded; keep a small pool of 'bunker' rows in each bank that are physically flanked by unused guard rows, and when a row's activation rate crosses a threshold the controller swaps it into a bunker, where hammering has no victims.

title: Muller's-ratchet recombination: two error-riddled copies make one clean page
idea: Sexual recombination breaks Muller's ratchet by mixing genomes with different mutations; store each page twice in very cheap cells with only an 8-bit CRC per 8-byte chunk (detect, not correct), assemble reads chunk by chunk from whichever copy passes, rewrite the failing chunk, and fall back to a rare third copy on double hits.
note: Mirroring plus checksums is ZFS-style known art; 2.25x overhead eats most of the cheap-media gain.

title: Hermit-crab vacancy chains for synchronized DIMM cascade resale
idea: Hermit crabs queue by size and swap shells all at once, so every crab upgrades in one event. A marketplace pre-matches hyperscaler refresh dates with tiers of second-life buyers (enterprise, edge, education, embedded), so tested DIMMs move down a pre-arranged chain within days instead of being shredded.

title: Ant-trail data-in-motion: activations stream, never parked in DRAM
idea: Ant trails hold information in moving traffic and evaporating pheromone, not in a warehouse. Accelerators are scheduled so intermediate activations circulate through chip-to-chip pipeline links and are consumed before they ever need to be parked in DRAM.
note: Activations are a small share of inference memory versus weights and KV.

title: Plywood veneer slicing: film-thickness-defined 5-nm electrode combs
idea: Veneer exposes the edges of thin layers: grow 40 alternating 5-nm ALD TiN/Al2O3 layers on a sidewall (or MBE GaAs/AlGaAs, then cleave) and use the exposed edge as a stamp or mask (SNAP-style) to transfer a 10-nm-pitch line array; cross two such arrays with ultrathin ZrO2 so each intersection is a storage capacitor for gain-cell or diode-isolated arrays.
note: SNAP prior art; fan-out contacts and crossbar access devices remain unsolved.

title: Cold-chain time-temperature indicator cells trigger refresh by accumulated thermal dose
idea: Vaccine shipments carry time-temperature indicators that integrate Arrhenius dose rather than trusting a schedule. In each subarray keep a few canary cells deliberately built leakier than the 6-sigma tail (wider junction implant); rewrite them at each refresh, poll them cheaply, and refresh the subarray only when a canary flips.

title: Foveated rendering for memory: refresh low-order mantissa bit-planes far less
idea: VR headsets render full detail only where the eye looks. Store AI weights and KV caches bit-plane-wise so sign, exponent and top mantissa bits live in normally refreshed rows, while the lowest 3-5 mantissa bits of BF16/FP8 sit in rows refreshed 8-16x less often and are allowed rare flips.

title: Let out-of-the-money options expire: recomputable data receives no refresh
idea: Traders let options expire when exercising costs more than they are worth. Tag regions holding recomputable data (KV-cache blocks rebuildable from tokens, cached embeddings, prefetch buffers) as 'expire-allowed': they get long or no refresh, ECC flags any decayed line, and the runtime recomputes it on demand.
note: Same skip-refresh-and-regenerate mechanism.

title: Roundabout traffic: self-timed completion detection per mat
idea: Like a roundabout letting cars go as soon as the way is clear instead of waiting for a fixed signal cycle, each SA latch drives a dual-rail done signal, and a per-mat completion tree releases column access when that mat's slowest SA resolves, not after the chip's worst-case tRCD.

title: Turbogenerator hydrogen cooling replaces helium as electrostatic-chuck backside gas
idea: Large power-plant generators are cooled with hydrogen because its thermal conductivity (~0.18 W/m-K) beats helium (~0.15). Use onsite PEM-electrolysis H2, or a sub-flammable H2/N2 blend at the ~10 Torr backside pressure, as the wafer-to-chuck heat-transfer gas in etch and CVD chucks, treating the small leak into the plasma as a known minor process species.

title: Phosphate-fertilizer fluorine recovery turns fab waste into synthetic fluorspar
idea: Phosphate plants recover fluorosilicic acid and convert it to AlF3 and HF instead of mining fluorspar. Precipitate fab HF, chamber-clean and abatement fluoride as acid-grade synthetic CaF2, or route it into fluorosilicic-acid-to-HF conversion, closing the fluorine loop behind the HF, NF3 and WF6 a DRAM fab buys; the DDR/HBM product is identical.
