note: Echoes DeHon-era stochastic decoders; litho-free 4F2 at 5 nm would be 10x, but gain cells at crossings and access speed unproven.

title: Photographic latent-image bit: few silver atoms hold a few electrons
idea: Silver-halide film keeps a stable 4-atom Ag cluster as the latent image, which development later amplifies. Here sub-3 nm Ag clusters self-assembled in an oxide each hold 1-5 electrons behind a Coulomb-blockade barrier. An integrated single-electron transistor 'develops' the latent charge on read.
note: ~1000x less charge per bit; RT Coulomb blockade needs sub-3 nm uniformity, and offset charges plague SETs.

title: Plywood veneer: Smart-Cut array laminates share one periphery base
idea: Like plywood glued from thin veneers, transfer thin 180 nm array layers (cells and bitline selects only, no periphery) one at a time onto a periphery base wafer using 1995 Smart-Cut hydrogen splitting and oxide bonding. Each veneer's bitlines drop through vertical vias to the shared SA/decoder base.
note: Shared periphery under 8-16 transferred array layers; doubt is per-layer thermal budget for access devices and capacitors, and compounding bond yield.

title: Vertical CCD loops in channel holes with built-in refresh
idea: IFR: no cell needs a switch because the bit travels to the switch. 3D-NAND-style channel holes with 64-128 tier gates are clocked as a charge-coupled device; packets circulate around ~32-position loops and pass one regeneration/sense amplifier at the top every lap, so refresh is inherent and there is one transistor per loop.
note: Short vertical loops claim DRAM-class lap time; same transfer-efficiency risk as I-04670.

title: 2D heterojunction thyristor crossbar: bistable bits without capacitors
idea: IFR: the bit holds itself and needs only two wires. Each crosspoint is a vertical p-n-p-n van der Waals stack (WSe2/MoS2) acting as a thin-film thyristor that latches on or off; a sub-100 pA holding bias keeps '1', '0' draws nothing, and a reverse pulse resets it, so there is no capacitor and no refresh.
note: Stacked two-terminal latching cells could exceed 10x density; doubt: pA holding current and multilayer 2D transfer yield.

title: SiGe quantum-well hole pocket replaces capacitor in each tier
idea: IFR: the transistor body is itself a leak-proof bucket. In epitaxial Si/SiGe/Si superlattice tiers, holes are stored in a buried compressively strained Ge-rich quantum well under each lateral channel; the ~0.3-0.5 eV valence-band offset confines them and their charge shifts channel Vt for non-destructive reads.
note: 0.3-0.5 eV valence offset implies microsecond-scale thermal hole emission at room temperature; retention doubtful.

title: Quadrant-gated pillars: four lateral storage pockets per tier
idea: IFR: one bitline pillar serves every direction. Around each vertical bitline pillar, split the tier wordline into four independently driven quadrant gates, each gating a short lateral oxide channel to its own storage pocket, so each pillar holds four cells per tier.
note: Four pockets per pillar per tier multiplies 3D density; tiny per-pocket storage and quadrant gate control are doubts.

title: Two-mask array: hole-and-slit concentric annular 3D DRAM cells
idea: Limit: the whole array may use only two critical masks. One hole mask through 96 Si/SiGe tiers defines vertical bitlines, and a timed lateral recess from each hole carves a concentric ring per tier (BL core, then an annular channel gated by the tier plates above and below, then an outer ring capacitor). One slit mask cuts the plates into wordline regions, so a cell is the crossing of one hole and one tier-region.
note: 8x density with zero EUV; doubt: tiny ring Cs and multi-ring timed lateral recess uniformity.

title: Vertical charge-coupled shift columns with zero transistors per bit
idea: Limit: no access transistor per bit. Each 4F2 column is a stack of 3-phase clocked gate tiers forming CCD potential wells. Charge packets shift down the column at about 2 GHz to one sense node at its base, giving page access in about 10-30 ns.
note: Dup of vertical CCD string; 2 GHz shifting in deposited channels is implausible.

title: Porous-silicon release layers recycle donor wafers across forty tiers
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. Build DRAM on a porous-silicon cleave layer (ELTRAN-style), transfer only the 2 um device film into the stack, then re-epi and reuse the donor substrate 10-20 times; 40+ films fit in the height of three normal dies.
note: Donor reuse makes 40-tier film stacks affordable; capacitor height, thermal budget and multiplicative bond yield are the doubts.

title: Minify tunnel oxide to 1.5 nm: leaky 3D NAND as DRAM
idea: Take a 200+ layer charge-trap 3D NAND flow and thin the tunnel oxide to about 1.5 nm, so cells write by direct tunneling in about 10-50 ns and leak in about 1-10 s. The controller refreshes them like DRAM, and direct tunneling may avoid hot-carrier wear.
note: NAND density for working memory; doubt: string-read latency, byte access, and 1e15+ cycle endurance.

title: Minify the litho tool to a spin coater: block-copolymer arrays
idea: Spin-coat high-chi block copolymers that phase-separate into 12-16 nm pitch hexagonal dot arrays, use them as etch masks for vertical pillar cells, align domains to wordlines with coarse i-line trenches (graphoepitaxy), and absorb assembly defects with redundancy.
note: DSA removes EUV; doubts: decades-old defectivity problem and capacitor at 12-16 nm pitch hits charge wall.

title: Eliminate the three-terminal transistor: threshold-switch selector 1S1C crosspoint DRAM
idea: Isolate each capacitor with a two-terminal volatile threshold switch (OTS or NbO2 Mott selector) stacked directly on it in a crosspoint, addressed by V/2 biasing; no wordline transistor and no lateral device, so tiers stack like 3D crosspoint.
note: Would remove the lateral-transistor blocker for 3D, but OTS/Mott selector off-leakage is orders above the needed sub-fA.

title: Reverse the charge wall: 50-electron bits read by single-electron transistors
idea: Instead of fighting for ~30,000 electrons in a 5 fF pillar, store ~50 electrons on a 0.01 fF planar node and move all the gain into the reader: a 3-5 nm room-temperature silicon Coulomb island coupled to the node swings its current by decades per few electrons.
note: Few-electron node with SET gain removes the capacitor; doubt: room-temperature SET variability, Yano-style prior art.

title: Optane's abandoned threshold-switch stack reused for capacitor crosspoint DRAM
idea: Revive the shelved 3D XPoint selector process: pair an Ovonic threshold switch with a tiny MIM capacitor (1S1C) in stacked crosspoint decks so the selector replaces the access transistor; OTS threshold scatter and leakage cause ~1% cell errors that tile-level codes correct.
note: Same OTS+MIM crosspoint; codes cannot fix pA-scale selector leakage limiting retention.

title: Transistorless 1S1C crosspoint: threshold switch guards each capacitor
idea: Inverts 'a DRAM cell needs an access transistor.' Put a volatile ovonic threshold switch in series with a small MIM capacitor at every crosspoint of stackable 4F² line layers; full-select pulses exceed threshold to read/write, half-selected cells stay off, and decks stack like 3D XPoint.
note: Same OTS+MIM crosspoint; pA off-leakage forces sub-ms refresh.

title: Vertical CCD charge-packet strings replace per-bit transistors and capacitors
idea: Box = {medium: charge packets in buried-channel potential wells | access: three-phase clocked ring gates, no per-bit FET | sense: floating-diffusion source follower at the string end | integration: vertical 32-bit CCD strings in deep holes | substrate: Si | fab: 3D-NAND-style hole etch + conformal gate stack}. Each vertical hole is a 32-stage CCD; a random access shifts the string past one amplifier in <30 ns, and every access recirculates and re-amplifies the packets, so refresh happens as a side effect of normal shifting.
note: Duplicate vertical CCD; charge-transfer efficiency over 32 stages in hole channels is the doubt.

title: 3D NAND strings retuned for DRAM retention and endurance
idea: Time-shift flash from 10-year retention to ~1 s: thin the tunnel oxide to 1.5-2 nm direct tunneling so charge traps in a 200-tier vertical string write in ns with 1e15 cycles, refreshed like DRAM, using existing 3D NAND fabs.
note: Claims ns writes and 1e15 cycles from charge traps; overstated.

title: Ten-electron quantum-dot storage node read by a single-electron transistor
idea: Jump down to the electron count: store a bit as ~10 electrons on a 3-nm silicon quantum dot behind an engineered double tunnel barrier, whose Coulomb blockade gives ms-to-s retention. An adjacent single-electron transistor reads it, its current swinging fully per electron, so cell capacitance is ~1 aF instead of 5 fF.
note: Yano-style SET memory known; doubt: room-temperature variability and background charge.

title: Optane's selector, not its PCM: OTS-gated capacitor crosspoint DRAM
idea: 3D XPoint's real breakthrough was the ovonic threshold switch (OTS) selector; what killed it as a DRAM substitute was slow, wearing phase-change material (PCM). Pair the OTS with a MIM capacitor (one selector, one capacitor) in stacked crosspoint decks. The OTS snaps on above threshold to charge or discharge the cap in nanoseconds and blocks under half-select, giving transistor-free DRAM cells of 4F2 per deck.
note: Same OTS+MIM crosspoint; retention set by selector leakage is the blocker.

title: Band-offset Ge quantum wells store holes behind a heterobarrier
idea: Effect: heterojunction band offset. Charge is stored as holes in a buried SiGe/Ge quantum well under each access channel; the ~0.5 eV valence-band offset confines them so thermionic loss falls ~exp(-0.5 eV/kT), giving seconds of retention with no capacitor, and reads sense the threshold shift of the overlying channel (built-in gain-cell amplification).
note: Capacitorless stackable 1T would be big; doubt retention vs GIDL/tunnelling, QW 1T-DRAM known.

title: Ni: Ni(OH)2 pseudocapacitive storage node stores tens of times more charge
idea: Coat the storage electrode with 2-3 nm of Ni(OH)2 and a thin solid proton conductor so a write drives faradaic Ni2+/Ni3+ redox, whose pseudocapacitance (hundreds of uF/cm2) is tens of times a high-k dielectric (~7 uF/cm2); the charge dumps onto the bit line like a normal DRAM read.
note: Redox charge would break charge wall; doubt: 10 ns faradaic kinetics, self-discharge, 1e15-cycle endurance.

title: Transistorless crosspoint DRAM with wide-bandgap Schottky selector and capacitor
idea: IFR: 'no access transistor, so cells stack like crosspoint.' Backward: replace the transistor with a two-terminal back-to-back Schottky selector in a wide-bandgap oxide (e.g., Ga2O3 with Pt contacts) targeting ~1e-19 A half-select leakage, in series with a small MIM capacitor, stacked as 1S1C crosspoint decks of only word and bit lines.
note: Schottky selector needing 1e12 on/off and 1e-19 A leakage is the miracle required.

title: Embrace random wiring: self-assembled crossbars mapped after fabrication
idea: Ideal: wiring that costs nothing because nobody designs it. Closest: grow dense random or partly ordered nanoline crossbars (dewetting, DSA) with a cell wherever lines cross; reach lines through a coarse-litho stochastic decoder (randomly doped address wires, Lieber/DeHon style) and run a one-time BIST discovery pass that writes a per-chip address-translation table.
note: Revives DeHon/Lieber stochastic decoding; doubt is a fast per-crosspoint cell with selector, and usable yield.

title: Backside-power flow repurposed to build capacitors behind the transistors
idea: Combine backside-power-delivery/BSI wafer thinning with the 1T1C cell: access transistors and bitlines are built on the front, the wafer is bonded to a carrier and thinned to the channel bottoms, and the storage capacitors are formed on the exposed backside drains, so bitline and capacitor no longer compete for one plane.

title: Steel mini-mill disruption: EUV-free DUV mini-fabs for mature DRAM
idea: Nucor beat integrated mills by entering at rebar with cheap electric-arc mini-mills; build 10-20k wafer-starts/month fabs using refurbished 193i scanners and SAQP to make 1y/1z-class DDR4, LPDDR4 and CXL-expander dies, sell into the commodity tier the HBM-focused majors are abandoning, then climb node by node.

title: Memory-only 450 mm wafers with a stripped-down tool set
idea: The G450C 450 mm program died around 2016 because toolmakers would not fund ~$20B of development against uncertain orders from three logic giants. DRAM uses far fewer distinct tool types than logic, so a memory-only 450 mm consortium with government cost share qualifies only ~40 tool types and pre-commits volume.

title: Merchant-foundry periphery wafers bonded to array-only DRAM wafers
idea: Substitute DRAM-process periphery with periphery made on depreciated 28/22 nm merchant-foundry logic lines and wafer-bonded to array-only wafers. DRAM fabs then spend all their EUV and DRAM-specific tool time on cell arrays, and periphery is bought by the wafer.

title: Substitute EUV with nanoimprint for periodic DRAM array layers
idea: Replace EUV exposure of the repetitive storage-node-contact, landing-pad and bitline layers with jet-and-flash nanoimprint (UV-cured resist pressed by a 1x quartz template replicated from an e-beam master); keep EUV/ArF only for irregular periphery. Imprint defects are absorbed by row/column redundancy mapped to each template's defect map, and templates rotate through a replica line.

title: Substitute monolithic DRAM die with array wafer bonded to logic periphery
idea: Fabricate the cell array on an array-only wafer (no periphery transistors and no dual/triple gate-oxide modules, roughly half the masks) and the sense amps, decoders and I/O on a 28-16 nm logic wafer, then hybrid bond the two wafer-to-wafer at ~1 um pitch.

title: Substitute ballroom cleanrooms with sealed tool-to-tool mini-environments
idea: Build the fab as a sealed transport network where pods dock tool-to-tool under nitrogen, with ISO-1 cleanliness only inside tools and AMHS tubes, so the building itself is an ordinary ISO-8 warehouse.

title: Photonic base die turns HBM into a fiber-attached appliance
idea: Substitute the HBM base die's electrical PHY with a silicon-photonics base die (microring modulators, Ge detectors, fiber V-grooves), so a stack talks over fiber at ~1 pJ/bit and can sit anywhere on a board or rack.
note: Celestial AI and Ayar Labs pursue optical memory attach.

title: Substitute integrated memory makers with a pure-play DRAM foundry
idea: Swap the three vertically integrated DRAM makers for a TSMC-style pure-play DRAM foundry offering a cell-array process plus design kits, so fabless memory companies and hyperscalers tape out custom DRAM.

title: Passing-gate trenches become shield lines that back-bias neighbors
idea: Combine row-hammer shielding and leakage control in one buried trench: every passing-gate buried wordline is replaced by a line held at about -0.5 V that both screens active rows from aggressor coupling and back-gates the adjacent access channels into deeper off-state.

title: Mature U.S. foundry periphery wafers hybrid-bonded under array-only wafers
idea: Combine Xtacking-style wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding with idle U.S. 28-40 nm logic foundry capacity. The DRAM wafer carries only cells, bitline sense amps and wordline drivers; decoders, I/O, DLL, charge pumps and test logic are made on mature logic wafers and bonded face-to-face at ~1 um pitch.

title: Active interposer merging HBM base dies with GPU memory controllers
idea: Combine the HBM logic base die and the GPU-side memory controller/PHY into one active interposer in a 12-16 nm logic node: DRAM core stacks bond directly onto it with controllers right underneath, so both ends of the PHY pair vanish and the GPU reaches memory over on-chip-style wires.
note: Converges with HBM4 custom base dies.

title: Buyer-owned memory cooperative fab, Ocean-Spray style
idea: Combine agricultural co-op ownership with a DRAM fab. Tier-2 clouds, automakers, PC OEMs and defense primes buy member shares in proportion to their volume and receive output at cost plus a reserve, with patronage dividends when prices spike.

title: Pure-play foundry model with an open DRAM cell PDK
idea: Borrow TSMC's split of design from manufacturing: a DRAM foundry runs one qualified cell process with an open process design kit (cell, sense amp and redundancy libraries), and many fabless memory designers tape out custom DRAMs (AI-tuned page sizes, CXL, in-memory compute) on shared capacity.

title: Automotive microcontroller fabs: hafnium-free poly-SiON periphery wafers
idea: Carmakers' MCUs run on 40/28 nm poly-gate SiON processes in underused U.S. fabs; move row decoders, wordline drivers, I/O and control onto such a Hf-free wafer (contacts in TiN-lined Al, not W) and hybrid-bond it to the array wafer, which keeps only pitch-matched sense amps.

title: Magnify die to the full wafer: wafer-scale DRAM
idea: Make a 300 mm wafer one memory, with no dicing: tiles are linked by an on-wafer mesh with spare-tile rerouting. Bond it face-to-face to a wafer-scale compute wafer, so there are no packages, PHYs or scribe lines.
note: Cerebras-style wafer-scale with WoW memory; well-trodden direction.

title: Periphery on legacy 200 mm US fabs, bonded to array
idea: Minify what needs a leading-edge fab to only the dense cell array; make the 49% periphery (sense amps, decoders, I/O) on underused 200/300 mm mature-node US fabs, then wafer-to-wafer hybrid bond the two.

title: Eliminate periphery from the memory wafer: subarray-granular hybrid bonding
idea: The memory wafer carries only cell arrays with 16:1 bitline muxes at each subarray edge; sense amps, decoders and I/O sit on a separately made logic wafer joined by ~400 nm pitch hybrid bonds at subarray granularity.
note: CBA/periphery-on-separate-wafer is widely pursued for 3D DRAM and NAND; 400 nm subarray bonding is aggressive.

title: Eliminate die-by-die thermocompression bonders: wafer-on-wafer HBM core stacking
idea: Hybrid-bond whole core-die wafers on top of each other and dice finished stacks, replacing hundreds of slow pick-and-place TCB bonds per wafer with one bond per layer; the base die still speaks standard HBM3E/HBM4.

title: Periphery wafer on top in leading-edge logic, array beneath
idea: Rearrange the stack: an array-only wafer is hybrid-bonded face-to-face at ~0.5 um pitch to a periphery wafer made in a 3 nm-class GAA logic process, so SAs and sub-wordline drivers are ~5x denser than DRAM-process periphery.

title: Merchant periphery wafers: U.S. array startups build only arrays
idea: Reverse vertical integration: one U.S. fab sells known-good periphery wafers with a standard hybrid-bond map, while startups and national labs fabricate only array wafers (~20 fewer masks) in small U.S. fabs and bond them domestically.
note: CMOS-bonded arrays already pursued (Xtacking, VCT DRAM); bond pitch vs bitline density is key.

title: Rotate the page vertical: one cell per tier, 64-bit activation
idea: In 3D DRAM, reverse the activation axis: a short vertical word-pillar gates exactly one cell in each of 64 tiers, and each tier senses on its own horizontal bitline, so one activation opens a 64-bit vertical column instead of an 8 kb row.

title: Ship periphery to logic fabs: array-only DRAM wafers bonded to CMOS
idea: Rearrange array and periphery: the DRAM fab builds only cell arrays, and a mature-node logic foundry builds the sense amps, decoders and I/O on a separate wafer. The two are hybrid-bonded wafer to wafer, as Xtacking does for NAND.

title: Taking out: periphery made in U.S. mature fabs, bonded to arrays
idea: TRIZ #2 Taking out pulls the ~49% periphery off the EUV array wafer: sense amps, decoders, pumps and I/O are made on 28-40 nm logic wafers in existing U.S. fabs and hybrid-bonded face-to-face at ~1 um pitch onto array-only wafers. A national 'periphery foundry' program qualifies one bonding interface that several array suppliers can use.

title: Array-only wafers bonded to U.S. mature-node periphery wafers
idea: TRIZ #2 Taking out: pull all periphery (sense amps, decoders, charge pumps, I/O) off the DRAM wafer onto a 28-40 nm logic wafer from a U.S. foundry, then wafer-to-wafer hybrid bond at ~1 um pitch. The DRAM fab runs only the array flow, so its EUV and high-AR tools spend all their time on bits.
note: CBA/Xtacking for DRAM widely pursued.

title: Segmented fab: array-only line plus mature-node periphery wafer
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation resolves 'leading-edge cells vs cheap periphery': run only the ~25 array-critical layers in a slim array fab, build sense amps, drivers and I/O on a 28-40 nm logic wafer bought from idle U.S. foundry capacity, and join them by wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding under the mats. The array fab no longer needs high-voltage, multi-Vt or logic-metal modules.

title: Disposable nanoimprint daughter templates for periodic array layers
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying plus #27 Cheap short-living objects: write one master template by e-beam, replicate hundreds of daughter templates by imprint, and run each daughter for ~1-5k wafers on jet-and-flash imprint tools for capacitor-hole and landing-pad layers, discarding it when defects accumulate while array redundancy absorbs the rest.

title: Segmentation: per-tile 2-high DRAM micro-stacks bonded over compute
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation, resolving 'more bandwidth vs. limited die-edge shoreline': replace 6-8 edge-mounted 12-high HBM stacks with ~64 two-high DRAM micro-stacks hybrid-bonded on top of each compute tile at ~9 um pitch. Each micro-stack feeds only the tile beneath it, and the logic NoC handles sharing.
note: DRAM-over-compute widely pursued; thermal coupling to hot logic is the main doubt.

title: Taking out: move DRAM periphery to foundry wafers, hybrid-bond back
idea: TRIZ #2 Extraction: strip sense amps, decoders and I/O off the DRAM wafer so the scarce DRAM fab prints only cell arrays, while plentiful logic foundries build the periphery wafer; the two are joined by wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding at 1-2 um pitch.
note: Cell-on-periphery bonding is already widely pursued for 4F2/3D DRAM.

title: Cell-to-pack memory: unsingulated DRAM wafers bonded onto compute wafers
idea: Like EV cell-to-pack removing the module layer, skip die singulation, packages and DIMMs: wafer-bond whole yield-mapped DRAM wafers (with spare-tile rerouting) onto whole compute wafers so memory meets compute through millions of bonds at full wafer scale.
note: Widely pursued (SoIC, wafer-scale); compound yield issue.

title: Prefab-housing utility cores: periphery wafers from mature U.S. logic fabs
idea: Modular housing builds the plumbing and electrical core in a factory and drops it on site. Split DRAM into an array wafer (DRAM fab) and a periphery CMOS wafer built on 28-40 nm logic lines at U.S. foundries with spare capacity, then hybrid-bond them face-to-face; the bonded die presents the same DDR5/HBM pins and timing.

title: Core-stack business model: periphery wafers from mature U.S. fabs
idea: Core memory was sold as a woven stack from one vendor and a driver/sense chassis from another. Split DRAM the same way: array-only wafers (cells and bitlines, no periphery) from existing DRAM fabs are hybrid-bonded to periphery wafers built on depreciated 28-40 nm U.S. logic lines, creating a merchant market for memory periphery.

title: Array-only DRAM wafer with periphery bonded from US 28nm logic
idea: Inverting 'cells and periphery share one wafer process': the DRAM fab builds wafers with only access devices, bitlines and capacitors (no periphery transistors, fewer implants and masks), while sense amps, decoders and I/O are made on a 28nm logic wafer in a US foundry and hybrid-bonded face-to-face at ~1 um pitch along every subarray edge.

title: Buried back-gate plane per tier: negative hold bias, low-swing wordlines
idea: Inverts 'the access transistor threshold is fixed.' Give every tier a doped-Si back-gate plane under its channels, biased strongly negative during hold to raise Vt and crush leakage, then relaxed per bank on access, so wordlines swing ~1.5 V instead of ~3 V.

title: Hyperscaler joint venture owns a cost-plus DRAM fab, Airbus-style
idea: Inverts 'buyers and makers of DRAM are adversaries over margin': 4-6 large buyers form a joint-venture entity that owns a U.S. fab running a licensed process from a second-tier vendor, sells at cost, and splits output pro rata to equity.

title: Array-only fabs bond to US logic-foundry periphery wafers
idea: Split the business: a new entrant builds an array-only fab (capacitors and access devices, no periphery CMOS), and buys periphery wafers from US 22-28 nm logic foundries, joined by wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding with periphery under the array.

title: One sense amplifier per vertical stack, multiplexed across 32 tiers
idea: Because only one tier of a bank is activated at a time, give each vertical column of 32 tiers a single sense amplifier reached through a per-tier select transistor at the column foot, instead of one sense amp per bitline per tier.
note: Vertical-bitline 3D DRAM already puts one SA per column; known architecture.

title: Periphery from depreciated U.S. logic fabs, hybrid-bonded to array
idea: First principle: the array needs the finest pitch, but the periphery (~49% of the die) only needs ~28 nm-class CMOS. Make array-only wafers in the DRAM fab and the periphery on fully depreciated 28-65 nm U.S. logic fabs, then join them by wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding.
note: CBA/Xtacking known; mature-fab sourcing twist.

title: Relocatable fab pods: containerized modules with high resale value
idea: First principle: fab capital is expensive partly because it is stranded: a fab building cannot be moved or resold. Factory-build fab segments as sealed clean pods with minienvironment tools inside, bolt them together in months, and move, refurbish or resell them later, which lowers the risk premium on capital.

title: Bank-level attention PIM moves KV from HBM to LPDDR
idea: An HBM bit costs ~3x the wafer area of a DDR5 bit (TSVs and yield loss), yet the KV cache only needs bandwidth for one dot product. Put q.k and softmax-weighted v accumulation units at each LPDDR bank, so the KV cache lives in commodity DRAM and only scores and results cross the bus.

title: Seed bank: national shuttle wafers for wild storage-element candidates
idea: Stimulus 'seed bank' -> a CHIPS-funded 300 mm back-end shuttle where any lab drops a candidate storage stack into a standard 1T1X 1 Mb test array four times a year, with shared ns-pulse testers, 10^15-cycle endurance rigs and open retention-tail data. One-off device papers become array statistics in 6 months.

title: Ice-cream sandwich: U.S. mature-node periphery wafers bonded to arrays
idea: Split every die into an array-only wafer (cells, bitlines, capacitors) and a periphery wafer (SAs, decoders, pumps, I/O) built on existing U.S. 28-40 nm logic lines, joined by wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding with one bond per bitline staggered along its length (a ~50 um bitline has ~1.5 um2 of footprint, room for a 1 um-pitch pad).

title: Ship in a bottle: cell wafer bonded onto 28nm periphery wafer
idea: Build the ship outside, then slide it in: make a cell-only wafer (arrays, bitline sense amps and local column mux in the cell process) and a separate periphery wafer in a mature 28 nm logic fab carrying decoders, data paths and the standard DDR5 PHY, then wafer-to-wafer hybrid bond at ~0.5 um pitch with one bond per 16 bitlines. The bonded die is a normal DDR5 x8 part with the same pinout, commands and timing.

title: Food truck: periphery-as-a-service from U.S. mature-node logic fabs
idea: Random stimulus 'food truck' (cook elsewhere, serve on site) -> the array wafer, which carries the EUV and capacitor steps, is made in a lean array-only fab. The CMOS periphery wafer (sense amps, decoders, I/O) is bought from existing U.S. 28-40 nm logic foundries and hybrid-bonded wafer-to-wafer.

title: Mosaic: wafer-scale DRAM-on-logic with defective tiles mapped out
idea: Forced 'mosaic': a whole undiced DRAM wafer is bonded face-to-face to a logic wafer, and tiles found bad at test are fused out of a mosaic address map. The result is one wafer-scale memory with no packaging, no PHYs and no dicing between memory and compute.
note: Wafer-on-wafer bonding plus tile map-out; Cerebras-style redundancy is known, matched wafer yields and thermals are the doubt.

title: Orchestra: US logic fabs build periphery wafers bonded to imported arrays
idea: Random stimulus 'orchestra' -> sections rehearse separately and play together. The cell array wafer (capacitors, WL/BL) comes from existing Asian DRAM fabs; the periphery (~49% of die) is built as a separate CMOS wafer in US logic fabs and joined by wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding, Xtacking-style.
note: CMOS-bonded-array is already on every DRAM maker's roadmap; US-periphery angle is the twist.

title: Sequential smart-cut stacking of single-crystal planar 1T1C tiers
idea: Box = {medium: charge on a planar trench-free MIM | access: lateral single-crystal Si FET in each transferred film | sense: SA on the base die | integration: 16-32 tiers by repeated hydrogen-implant layer transfer below 400 C | substrate: reusable donor wafers | fab: low-temperature bonding + splitting}. Each tier is a thin crystalline Si film with near-bulk access transistors, avoiding the poor poly or oxide channels that hurt monolithic 3D.
note: Sequential smart-cut 3D known (CoolCube-like); cost per transferred tier high.

title: Hafnium-free periphery: array bonded onto mature SiON-poly CMOS wafer
idea: Box [standard 1T1C array | Si access | sense amps on bottom wafer | Cu-Cu hybrid-bonded CMOS-bonded-array | array wafer + 28-40 nm SiON/poly periphery wafer | split fab]: build sense amps and decoders on a mature node with no HfO2/La high-k metal gate and no EUV, then bond the array wafer on top.

title: Pure-play DRAM array foundry for fabless memory designers
idea: Box[Owner=foundry x Medium=standard 1T1C array PDK x Integration=customer periphery/logic x Business=wafer-per-month service]: a DRAM fab sells array wafers with a PDK and IP library, the way TSMC sells logic, so fabless firms design custom DRAMs (AI, automotive, CXL) without owning a fab.

title: Buyers' cooperative co-owns a U.S. DRAM fab via take-or-pay
idea: Box[Owner=cooperative of hyperscalers, automakers and OEMs x Finance=prepaid take-or-pay offtake x Operator=contract manager x Scale=megafab]: members prepay 10-year offtake pro rata to equity and receive bits at cost-plus, with an operator running the fab.
note: Same buyer co-op plus take-or-pay offtake as I-01806.

title: Po: an array die that cannot decode
idea: Po: an array die that knows no addresses. Row/column predecoding, redundancy CAMs, refresh counters and command logic move to a hybrid-bonded logic-node base die, which drives pre-decoded one-hot group selects through ~1 um-pitch bonds; the array die keeps only sub-wordline drivers, SAs and final pass gates.

title: Periphery outsourced to idle 28 nm logic wafers, bonded under array
idea: Po: half the chip is missing. Existing DRAM fabs make array-only wafers (cells, bitlines, minimal local sense) while idle 28-40 nm logic fabs make periphery wafers (decoders, sense amps, I/O); the two are hybrid-bonded wafer-to-wafer with periphery under the array.

title: Hyperscaler take-or-pay SPVs that own DRAM fab lines
idea: Po: the customer owns the fab. Like LNG trains financed by 20-year take-or-pay contracts, 3-5 hyperscalers fund a special-purpose vehicle that owns a DRAM line run by an incumbent or new entrant, receiving output at cost-plus in proportion to equity.

title: Array wafer plus foundry periphery wafer joined by hybrid bonding
idea: Po: one chip is two chips from two countries. A DUV-only DRAM fab makes array-only wafers, while a U.S. 28/22 nm logic foundry makes the periphery wafer; the two are wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonded so the ~49% periphery sits under the array.

title: Hybrid-bonded area pads above each bank replace the global datapath
idea: Worse: haul every bit across the die through global I/O lines and serializers to edge pads. Flip: place hybrid-bonded area-array pads directly above each bank's column logic so a logic die below reads each bank locally, deleting global I/O buses and most serializers.

title: U.S. mature logic fabs build control dies; DRAM fabs only arrays
idea: Worse: build control periphery on scarce, EUV-laden DRAM wafer starts. Flip: contract control, I/O, pump and test dies to U.S. 28-40 nm logic foundries and hybrid-bond them to array-dense dies from DRAM fabs that keep only bitline sense amps and spend the rest of the wafer on bits.

title: Unsawn wafer-scale memory slab bonded to a logic wafer
idea: Worse: dice, package and TSV-stack small dies, losing kerf, pads and 20-30% stack yield. Flip: hybrid-bond an entire array wafer face-to-face onto a logic wafer, keep it whole, and route around failed tiles with a programmable on-wafer mesh, so no dicing, packaging or HBM TSVs are needed.

title: Vacuum-continuous fab where wafers never meet cleanroom air
idea: Worsen: build ever-bigger ballroom cleanrooms where huge air handlers filter air around wafers 24/7. Flip: link tools with sealed vacuum or N2 tunnels and maglev carriers so the wafer's environment is always a tool interior, letting building air drop to industrial grade.
note: Mini-environments and Minimal Fab already exist.

title: Mature-node SiON periphery wafers bonded under the array
idea: Worsen: build the 49% of the die that is periphery in the same leading-edge flow, with Hf/La high-k metal gates and EUV. Flip: make the periphery logic on 28-40 nm SiON-gate wafers in existing U.S. mature fabs and hybrid-bond it beneath an array-only wafer, so hafnium, lanthanum and EUV appear only where the cell needs them.
note: CMOS-bonded-array widely pursued; mature-node periphery must still meet SA pitch and I/O speed.

title: Periphery from U.S. mature foundries bonded to array-only wafers
idea: Worse: build sense amps and logic in the same costly DRAM process that compromises both. Flip: make array-only wafers in the DRAM fab, buy the periphery wafer (sense amps, decoders, I/O) from a 28/22 nm U.S. foundry, and hybrid-bond the two wafer-to-wafer at sub-micron pitch.
note: Bonded-periphery DRAM is already on industry roadmaps.

title: Pure-play DRAM foundry with open PDK for fabless designers
idea: Worse: keep the DRAM process locked inside three IDMs. Flip: a DRAM foundry offers an array PDK (cell, capacitor, sense-amp macros) and multi-project wafers, so fabless startups and hyperscalers can tape out custom PIM, wide-I/O or CXL-native DRAM.

title: Bank-under-tile: each compute tile owns the DRAM bank beneath it
idea: Worsen: route every bit across a shared bus to a DIMM 10 cm away. Flip: hybrid-bond DRAM face-to-face onto logic at ~1 um pitch so each compute tile talks only to the bank directly below it through thousands of vertical wires, with no PHY, no shared bus and no SerDes.

title: Farmer's co-op grain elevator: shared toll-EUV hub for new fabs
idea: Farmers don't each own a grain elevator. A neutral co-op owns a cluster of 4-6 EUV scanners sited among several new U.S. memory fabs (start-ups, IDMs, national labs); sealed FOUP shuttles carry wafers to the hub for their EUV layers only, members pay per exposure, and capacity shares are owned like co-op stock.

title: Downhole-grade FD-SOI periphery wafer bonded under array via bitline mux
idea: Without EUV, put SAs and decoders on a 22-65 nm DUV FD-SOI wafer (the substrate downhole and space chips use for heat and radiation) and hybrid-bond it to an array wafer that holds only cells plus an 8:1 bitline select mux, matching ~0.5 um bond pitch to 30-40 nm bitlines. FD-SOI back-bias trims SA offset per mat.

title: Trusted-packaging-first US strategy: stack imported wafers domestically
idea: DoD trusted-foundry users secure supply through trusted assembly. Fund US memory OSATs that buy commodity DRAM wafers from several countries and do base-die integration, stacking, test and HBM/CXL module assembly onshore, with tariff exemptions on wafers and offtake from federal AI programs.

title: Move the 49% DRAM periphery onto idle 28 nm logic wafers
idea: Scale split by function: sense amps, decoders and I/O are built on existing 28-40 nm logic wafers and hybrid-bonded under array-only wafers from existing DRAM fabs. Each EUV-rich DRAM wafer then carries ~90% array instead of ~51%.
note: Periphery-under/over-array bonding pursued by major DRAM makers.

title: Bond cheap-logic periphery under a minimal-mask array wafer
idea: Split the die across two wafers: the 49% periphery is built on a mature 28 nm logic wafer, the array on a stripped-down ~15-mask array-only wafer, and the two are joined by wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding at sub-1 um pitch.
note: Cell-on-periphery bonding (Xtacking-style) widely pursued for 4F2 DRAM.

title: 600 mm glass panel interposers with embedded silicon memory bridges
idea: Jump the interposer from a 300 mm wafer to a 600x600 mm glass panel: through-glass vias and multilevel RDL are made on LCD-fab tools, and small silicon bridges are embedded only under the HBM-to-logic edges. One panel yields ~5x the interposer area of a wafer at LCD-class cost per m2.

title: Undiced wafer-scale DRAM routes around defects via on-wafer mesh
idea: Scale jump (die -> wafer): keep the 300 mm wafer whole, stitch reticles with a fault-tolerant mesh NoC, and at bring-up disable defective reticle tiles in software. Dicing, packaging and per-die yield loss disappear, so a die-killing defect costs one tile.

title: Bubble-memory precedent: federal rugged-memory purchase guarantee for domestic production
idea: Magnetic bubble memory survived years longer because U.S. military and aerospace buyers needed rugged storage. Replicate that with a DoD/DOE/automotive consortium that guarantees purchase of at least 10M units per year of a 125 C/10 y-qualified, U.S.-fabbed DRAM-class element for five years, paid only after qualification.
note: Advance market commitment; executable policy, but not provable with $1M.

title: Anamartic wafer-scale memory revived with hybrid-bonded Catt spiral routing
idea: Anamartic's Wafer Stack (Ivor Catt's spiral that threads good dies past bad ones) died on the cost of 1980s wafer-level interconnect. Hybrid-bond an undiced DRAM wafer face-to-face onto a logic wafer that carries the spiral self-test router. At power-up each subarray tests itself and the router chains every good one into one address space, giving a 300 mm memory slab with no dicing, packaging or TSVs.

title: Fill Optane's empty fab: a toll memory foundry for fabless DRAM
idea: Optane died partly because Intel alone could not fill the Lehi fab, so fixed costs crushed unit cost. Create a memory toll foundry with an open DRAM PDK (cell, sense-amp and redundancy libraries) so AI-chip firms and hyperscalers tape out custom DRAM dies and share one fab's utilization.

title: Hybrid Memory Cube revived: packetized cube over UCIe, no SerDes, no interposer
idea: Micron's HMC died from long-reach SerDes power (~10 pJ/bit total) and latency plus a closed consortium. Keep its smart logic base die and packet protocol, but replace the SerDes with clock-forwarded UCIe-Standard links (~0.5 pJ/bit) over a plain organic substrate at 2-10 mm reach, and publish the packet layer as an open spec so the cube becomes a drop-in memory chiplet that any accelerator can place without CoWoS.
note: Overlaps JEDEC SPHBM4 and UCIe memory efforts on organic substrate.

title: IRAM fixed: leading-edge logic hybrid-bonded under every DRAM subarray
idea: Berkeley IRAM, Venray TOMI and UPMEM stalled because logic built in a DRAM process is 3-10x slower and wire-starved (about 3 metal layers). Wafer-to-wafer hybrid-bond (<1 um pitch) a 5 nm logic wafer face-to-face to a DRAM array wafer stripped of most periphery, so each 512-row subarray gets its own decoders, sense-adjacent SIMD lane and controller in fast CMOS directly beneath it.
note: Wafer-bonded periphery under array is widely pursued for 4F2/3D DRAM.

title: 77 K cryogenic stacks let 3D tiers use sub-femtofarad capacitors
idea: Carrier freeze-out of thermal leakage: liquid-nitrogen-cooled 3D DRAM stacks at 77 K cut access-transistor leakage by about 1e6. Lateral tier capacitors of 0.3-0.5 fF then retain data for seconds or more, so planar thin tiers replace high-AR pillars.
note: Same 77 K leakage-collapse idea applied to 3D tiers.

title: Hydrogen-split layer transfer stacks single-crystal silicon tiers for 3D DRAM
idea: H: for each tier, bond a hydrogen-implanted donor wafer onto the finished lower tier below 400 C and cleave at the implant plane (Smart-Cut), leaving a ~30 nm single-crystal Si film in which DUV-patterned lateral access transistors are built; donors are reused ~10x, so density comes from tiers, not EUV shrink.

title: Cu: hybrid-bond periphery wafers from idle U.S. mature-node fabs
idea: Split each DRAM into an array-only wafer from the DRAM fab and a periphery wafer (decoders, I/O, control, SA back-ends) made on 28-65 nm logic lines in U.S. fabs, joined by Cu-Cu hybrid bonding at ~1 um pitch.
note: CBA is already on all three incumbents' roadmaps; the US mature-fab angle is the twist.

title: Chassis-body marriage: trailing U.S. logic fabs supply DRAM periphery wafers
idea: Automakers build chassis and bodies on separate lines and marry them; DRAM makers would fabricate array-only wafers and buy periphery wafers (sense amps, decoders, I/O) from U.S. 28-65 nm foundries under contract, then hybrid-bond the two.

title: Printing-plate family tree: replicated nanoimprint templates replace array EUV
idea: Like a record plant electroforming many stampers from one master, write a single e-beam master for the honeycomb storage-node and landing-pad layers, replicate it into ~1,000 daughter templates, and print those layers by jet-and-flash nanoimprint; each daughter is retired after a fixed wafer count before defects accumulate.

title: Shipyard block construction: arrays at memory fabs, periphery at logic foundries
idea: Shipyards build hull blocks in parallel at different yards and join them. Make array-only DRAM wafers at memory fabs, and periphery/IO/control wafers at underused U.S. logic foundries on 28-16 nm. Join them by wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding, as CMOS-bonded-array NAND does.

title: Periphery outsourced to US mature-node wafers bonded under array
idea: IFR: 'the DRAM fab only makes array.' Backward: split each die into a pure-array wafer (cells and bitlines only) and a periphery wafer (charge pumps, wordline drivers, I/O) made at a U.S. 28-90 nm foundry, then hybrid-bond them, so the array fab drops all high-voltage and logic steps.

title: Stack depreciated-node DRAM wafers instead of buying an EUV node
idea: Ideal: more density with no new tools. Closest: keep fully depreciated DUV-only 1x-nm-class DRAM lines running, thin complete wafers to ~3 um and hybrid-bond 4-8 of them into a monolithic stack with a fine-pitch vertical bus, so bits per footprint come from tier count while every tier runs on paid-off equipment.

title: Sealed vacuum wafer backbone replaces the ISO-3 cleanroom ballroom
idea: Ideal: no cleanroom at all. Closest: wafers travel only through a linear vacuum/N2 tunnel that docks every tool (an extended cluster-tool backbone with mag-lev carriers), so the building needs ISO 8 air, not ISO 3-4 fan-filter ceilings, and queue-time oxidation disappears.

title: Factory-built cleanroom pods shrink DRAM fab build to 18 months
idea: Ideal: a fab appears overnight. Closest: standardize a 10k-wafer-per-month DRAM module as transportable prefabricated cleanroom and subfab skids, with tools installed and qualified at the module factory, then shipped and craned onto a slab; capacity grows pod by pod.

title: Charge-trap NOR weight towers hybrid-bonded under the GPU
idea: Ideal: weights that persist with no power and arrive at DRAM speed. Closest achievable: stack 3D charge-trap NOR (vertical channels, ~100 ns random read, wide parallel pages) in an HBM-shaped tower, hybrid-bond it to the base die, and use it only as a read-mostly weight store updated at deployment.

title: Hyperscaler take-or-pay prepayments bankroll an independent DRAM entrant
idea: Ideal: a fab that costs its builder nothing. Closest achievable: 4-6 hyperscalers prepay 30-40% of a $15B fab as 10-year take-or-pay wafer-start contracts with step-in rights, which makes the rest project-financeable like an LNG terminal.

title: Array wafer carries only cells: periphery from U.S. legacy fabs
idea: Limit: the EUV array wafer may hold only cells and sense amps. Global decoders, pumps, I/O, DLL, test logic and fuses go on a 28/40 nm wafer from under-used U.S. legacy fabs and are joined by wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding at ~1 um pitch.

title: Hafnium-free periphery on mature SiON wafers bonded under array
idea: Imposed scarcity: no hafnium and no EUV in the periphery. Build sense amps, decoders and I/O on a separate 40 nm poly/SiON CMOS wafer in any mature U.S. fab and hybrid-bond it face-to-face under the array wafer.

title: Thin wafer-on-wafer DRAM with spare layers (64-high in today's package height)
idea: Stack whole DRAM wafers thinned to ~4-10 um wafer-on-wafer with bumpless via-last TSVs of ~1-2 um diameter, the Tokyo Tech / WOW Alliance (BBCube) approach. Because wafer stacking cannot select known-good dies, add spare layers (18 for 16, or 72 for 64) and let the base die map out failed die sites layer by layer after in-die repair. Thin silicon makes each TSV ~20x smaller in area including keep-out and cuts stack thermal resistance ~3x versus bump stacks, and 10 um layers allow 64-high stacks inside today's package height.

title: Swap SiO2 tunnel barrier for InAs/AlSb resonant triple barrier
idea: Store charge on an InAs floating gate isolated by an InAs/AlSb triple-barrier resonant-tunnelling structure (ULTRARAM-style). At about 2.5 V the resonance aligns and electrons tunnel quickly at low energy; at 0 V the 2.1 eV AlSb conduction-band offset blocks them, so retention exceeds years.
note: This is Lancaster's ULTRARAM.

title: Swap capacitor for vertical gated thyristor bistable latch
idea: A vertical p-n-p-n silicon thyristor with a gated base holds the bit regeneratively: latched on or blocked off, with gate pulses giving ns switching (the T-RAM/VLT lineage). It is built at 4F2 with F = 28-40 nm using DUV double patterning.
note: T-RAM/Kilopass VLT prior art; standby current and variability stalled it.

title: Wireless charging coils: TSV-free inductively stacked HBM
idea: Borrow Qi chargers and RFID near-field links: stack thinned DRAM dies without TSVs, pass data through on-chip aluminum spiral coils across ~10 um adhesive layers at Gb/s per coil, and bring power through a few wide edge or through-mold vias.

title: Endoscope imaging bundles carry microLED arrays for off-package HBM bandwidth
idea: Adapted from medical coherent fiber bundles with 10,000+ cores: a microLED array on the DRAM base die images straight into a bundle that lands on a photodiode array on the accelerator. The result is thousands of slow parallel lanes (~2 Gb/s each) with no lasers and no WDM.

title: Wide-slow microLED imaging-fiber links to a disaggregated memory bay
idea: Worsen: tie memory to within 5 cm of the processor so it can't be shared or cooled separately. Flip: drive hundreds of parallel microLED channels at ~2-4 Gb/s each through a coherent imaging-fiber bundle at ~0.5 pJ/bit with no DSP, so commodity DDR sits meters away in a dedicated memory bay.

title: Nanoimprint stamps print the cell layer; 180-nm steppers align everything else
idea: Scale the coin mint down to nanometers with Chou's 1995 nanoimprint: an e-beam-written master stamp, made once and cheaply replicated, presses ~15-nm hole patterns into resist for the cell layer. 180-nm KrF steppers handle the coarse periphery and straps.

title: N: GaN micro-LED arrays form a wide-slow optical memory bus
idea: Bond 1,000-element GaN micro-LED emitter arrays and Si photodiode arrays to the memory controller and to a remote DRAM sled, each LED running 2-4 Gb/s NRZ into one core of an imaging fiber bundle, so the bus stays massively parallel and protocol-light like HBM instead of serializing.
note: Essentially the approach already commercialized by microLED-bundle startups.

title: MicroLED imaging-fiber links: each pixel a memory bit lane
idea: Ideal: thousands of wires with no wires. Closest achievable: put ~10,000 GaN microLEDs and silicon photodiodes on the DRAM base die, couple them into a coherent imaging fiber bundle and land it on a matching array on the GPU, each pixel carrying 2-4 Gb/s NRZ with no SerDes, lasers or modulators.

title: Tier address encoded in epitaxial doping replaces 3D staircase contacts
idea: Substitute the staircase (one contact landing per tier) with a vertical decoder: each tier's select transistors are grown with an in-situ doping (thus Vt) set by its binary tier address, and ten vertical gate pillars (true/complement for 5 address bits) pass through all 32 tiers, so an address code turns on the series select chain of exactly one tier, like a NAND decoder.

title: Fluorine-free DRAM flow certification as a U.S. permitting fast lane
idea: Create a U.S. 'fluorine-free memory' track: CHIPS/DoD funding and EPA permitting priority for DRAM lines that use no F-gases or PFAS (built from epi stacks + Cl/Br etch + Mo-chloride + AAO/drawn-glass capacitors), with defense/hyperscaler offtake; the fab skips F-GHG point-of-use abatement and PFAS wastewater treatment.
note: Policy is executable but presupposes a fluorine-free DRAM flow that does not yet exist.

title: Light-powered contactless self-test of bare memory dies
idea: Substitute probe-card test with optical test: each die carries a tiny photovoltaic cell and LED; a light flash powers on-die BIST and the die blinks its pass/fail and repair map to a camera, testing thousands of dies in parallel without contact.
note: Flash-powered PV gives mW; full-speed DRAM BIST needs far more power.

title: Oxide retention gate in series with a fast silicon access transistor
idea: Put an oxide-semiconductor transistor in series with each Si access device, driven by a per-bank retention line. That line stays on while the bank is active, so it adds no switching delay, and turns off when the bank idles; the Si device does all the fast switching.
note: Series IGZO retention gate on a Si access device is a non-obvious hybrid; cell area and integration are the doubt.

title: Display backplane fab fused with DRAM: panel-scale memory sheets
idea: Combine an oxide-TFT display backplane line (3 m Gen-10.5 glass, ~1.5 um rules, a storage capacitor already in every pixel) with DRAM: print 4 stacked tiers of 1T1C cells with small local subarrays, then dice the panel into capacity-tier CXL memory sheets.
note: ~1000x lower bit density vs 100x cheaper area: cost/bit likely worse than DRAM; capital per bit not better.

title: Harvested server DRAM dies restacked with sidewall-metallized interconnect
idea: Combine e-waste recovery with 3D stacking: dies desoldered from retired US hyperscaler DIMMs are retested, thinned, given an RDL that routes pads to one edge, glued into 8-16-high cubes, and wired together by laser-patterned metal on the lapped cube sidewall (Irvine Sensors-style), assembled at US OSATs.
note: Decapsulating packaged retired dies and sidewall-wiring cubes is doable but low-yield; old low-density dies limit value.

title: Bit-significance-aware arrays: dense sloppy LSB mats, robust MSB mats
idea: Combine the numeric structure of AI tensors with DRAM layout. One mask set prints two mat types: LSB mats at a near-failure tight pitch running ~1% BER, and sign/exponent/MSB mats at relaxed pitch. The controller swizzles each word so low-significance mantissa bits land in the dense mats.

title: Fat landing pads printed by immersion, bridged pairs tolerated
idea: Combine enlarged storage-node landing pads with bridge-aware interleaving: overlay can drift +/-4 nm instead of +/-2 nm, and the ~1% of pads that short to a neighbor create paired errors that the code interleave is built to absorb. A 193i scanner can then replace EUV on that layer.

title: Interleaved product codes let array layers run in ISO-5 bays
idea: Combine particle-defect statistics with 2D-interleaved product codes in which each codeword spans cells at least 1 um apart in both axes, and with segmented wordlines and bitlines, so a killer particle costs one symbol per codeword. Less critical array back-end layers then run in ISO-5 bays rather than ISO-3 minienvironments.

title: Confidential-computing integrity MACs reused as dedup fingerprints
idea: Combine the per-line MACs and integrity tree that memory-encryption engines (TDX/SEV-SNP style) already compute with a deduplication index: read-only pages encrypted under a shared convergent 'dedup key domain' produce identical MAC roots, so the controller detects and merges them without decrypting.
note: Convergent keys for dedup under TDX/SEV weaken confidentiality and need address-independent MACs.

title: One modulated laser beam powers and clocks the stack's top die
idea: Combine power-over-fiber photovoltaics with optical clock distribution: a modulated 1550 nm laser lands on InGaAs photovoltaic cells bonded to the top HBM die; the DC part powers the top die's I/O and refresh logic and the envelope yields a low-jitter clock redistributed downward, deleting clock TSVs and per-die DLLs.
note: Power-over-fiber efficiency is low; saves only clock TSVs and DLLs.

title: Noise-cancelling wordlines: opposite pulses neutralize neighbor disturbance
idea: Combine active noise cancellation with wordline drive: when a wordline rises, drivers inject a small, timed opposite-polarity pulse on its two neighbors, cancelling the capacitively coupled disturbance on victim access gates; amplitude is calibrated per array. Buildable in a university nanofab: TFT arrays driven by external pulse generators.

title: Pinned buried-well storage node copied from CMOS image sensors
idea: Store the bit as electrons in a fully depleted buried n-well pinned by a p+ surface layer, exactly like a pinned photodiode, and move it in and out through a transfer gate to a floating-diffusion read node; the stored charge never touches the Si/SiO2 interface or a contacted junction.
note: Image-sensor pinned wells as DRAM node is fresh, but full-well charge collapses at DRAM pitch.

title: Self-clearing capacitor electrodes from metallized film capacitors
idea: Copy metallized-film capacitors that self-heal: use a 2 nm oxidizable top electrode (TiN/Al) so a one-time wafer-level clearing pulse makes each weak spot in the high-k burn its local electrode into insulator, deleting that leakage path.
note: Clearing in nm-thin high-AR electrodes may open circuits or damage neighbors.

title: Four-shared readout cluster copied from smartphone camera pixels
idea: Adapt the 4-shared pixel: four tiny storage wells (~0.5 fF, no tall capacitor) share one floating diffusion and one source-follower gain transistor via four transfer gates, read one at a time with correlated double sampling.
note: Pixel-sharing analog; transfer to floating diffusion is destructive.

title: District-metered well taps measure each subarray's real leakage
idea: Adapted from water districts that find leaks by metering minimum night flow per zone: give each subarray its own isolated p-well with a metered tap. During idle, an on-die current integrator reads the well current (where junction and GIDL leakage ends up), sets that subarray's refresh rate from the measurement, and flags sudden jumps caused by VRT or aging.
note: Aggregate well current reflects mean leakage, not the tail cells that set retention.

title: Solar advanced hydrogenation: light-assisted trap passivation of storage junctions
idea: Adapted from the PV industry's advanced hydrogenation, which uses intense illumination during a 200-400 C anneal to shift hydrogen into its mobile, reactive charge state: run it after the access-transistor module so hydrogen reaches and passivates the deep-level defects at the storage-node junction that create the leakage tail.
note: PV hydrogen charge-state control applied to junction deep traps; unclear it reaches metal-related tail defects.

title: Farm-equipment right-to-repair: open retention and repair command standard
idea: Adapted from the right-to-repair rules won for farm equipment: a JEDEC requirement backed by federal procurement rules that vendors publish the commands to read retention maps, trigger post-package repair and set refresh multipliers, so independent shops can repair and re-grade modules.

title: Bottle-deposit systems: refundable deposit funds module retention re-profiling
idea: Adapted from container-deposit schemes: add a refundable deposit (~$2-5) to each memory module, redeemable at certified refurbishers that re-profile retention, remap weak rows and re-grade modules into refresh classes; unredeemed deposits fund the re-test equipment.

title: Corrugated cardboard flutes: tiers deposited over sinusoidal templates
idea: Borrowed from corrugated board, where a fluted middle sheet multiplies stiffness and surface: etch a shallow sinusoidal corrugation into the base, then deposit the 3D tier stack so every horizontal tier and its lateral capacitor follow the wave, multiplying electrode area without deep etches.

title: Magnify test parallelism with display voltage-imaging retention maps
idea: Repurpose the non-contact voltage-imaging testers used on LCD backplanes, where an electro-optic modulator reads millions of pixel voltages at once, to image every memory cell's stored-voltage decay through a test-mode electrode layer. The result is a cell-exact retention map per panel in minutes.

title: Eliminate row-hammer counter SRAM: leaky-capacitor analog activation integrators
idea: Replace the digital per-row activation counters (TRR/PRAC tables) with one analog integrator per 8-row group. Each ACT dumps a fixed charge packet, tapped from the wordline driver's own swing, onto a deliberately leaky MOS capacitor with a ~64 ms decay. When its voltage crosses a threshold inverter, the group's neighbors are refreshed.
note: Leakage-based decay drifts strongly with temperature; threshold calibration is the doubt.

title: Eliminate PFAS permitting drag: fluorine-free periphery fast-lane policy
idea: Create a federal/state permitting fast lane and cost share for DRAM periphery lines certified fluorine-free (Cl/Br/O etches, MoO2Cl2 metal, PAG-free resists, Cl2/O2 chamber cleans, PFPE-free test). Publish it as an open reference flow with shared yield data, so new U.S. periphery fabs avoid PFAS-driven permit delays and EU restriction risk.

title: Driverless memory die read by host-powered backscatter
idea: Eliminate the DRAM's output drivers: the processor launches a carrier on each DQ line and the memory die only toggles a tiny switch that changes the line's termination impedance (like an RFID tag), so the reflected wave carries the data; all transmit energy and big driver transistors sit on the logic die.

title: Eliminate the hard sense decision: latch resolve time as confidence
idea: Measure how long each sense amplifier takes to resolve, using a per-column time-to-digital stamp; metastability time scales as log(1/dV). Slow-resolving bits are marked low-confidence and fed as soft information to a soft-decision LDPC/BCH decoder.

title: Floating segment node: cells leak into neighbors, not the bitline
idea: Rearrange the isolation hierarchy: group 4-8 cells on a short local node that connects to the bitline through one segment transistor. In hold the segment device is off, so the local node floats and settles between the cells' stored voltages; each access transistor sees a small Vds, and any path to the bitline must cross two off devices in series (stack effect).

title: Trim the tail: charge-trap access transistors programmed at test
idea: Reverse a flash technique into a DRAM fix: build access transistors with an ONO (SONOS) charge-trap gate stack in an existing 40-65 nm embedded-SONOS fab. At wafer test, measure each cell's retention and give the tail cells (~0.01-1%) a one-time program pulse that raises their Vt ~200 mV and cuts their leakage 10-100x, folding the tail into the bulk distribution.
note: Per-cell test-time Vt trim of tail access devices; wordline disturb of trap layer is the doubt.

title: Reverse the plate's role: drop the plate to park idle cells
idea: Segment the capacitor plate per subarray and, when a subarray goes idle, ramp its plate down ~0.3-0.4 V so all floating storage nodes couple down with it; stored '1's then sit at lower field versus the gate/junction (less GIDL and trap-assisted leakage) while '0's sit slightly below ground held off by the negative back-bias. The plate ramps back up before the next activation, restoring the levels.
note: Lowering plate drives '0' nodes negative, raising access-transistor Vgs and subthreshold leakage; net gain uncertain.

title: LCD backplanes are already 1T1C DRAM: repurpose glass-panel fabs
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying: every LCD/OLED pixel is a thin-film transistor plus storage capacitor refreshed at 1-120 Hz, and LTPO oxide TFTs already hold charge at 1 Hz. Redesign Gen-6/8.5 glass backplanes at ~1 um rules into mm-scale memory tiles with LTPS periphery, stacked in several TFT tiers, refreshed at ~1 Hz instead of every 64 ms.
note: Gen-8.5 cost per area at ~1 um density gives roughly $3-10/GB, not cheaper than DRAM.

title: Refresh-piggybacked in-situ recompression by the memory logic die
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: DRAM must open every row each refresh window anyway; the HBM/CXL logic die issues column reads into rows already opened for refresh to scan, dedup-fingerprint and recompress cold pages, so compaction rides on maintenance activations instead of adding its own.
note: Using refresh-opened rows for compaction is novel; refresh internals do not expose data to the logic die.

title: Chromatophore test pixels: optical wafer-wide readout of BIST results
idea: Cephalopod chromatophores show internal state on the skin. Each mat gets a tiny electrochromic (WO3/PEDOT) pad driven by its built-in self-test pass/fail latch. With power supplied through a few probe needles, a camera images the whole wafer during the BIST run and reads millions of mat results in parallel.

title: Nanocellulose build-up film replaces single-source ABF substrate dielectric
idea: Plant cell walls are cellulose microfibrils in a matrix, stiff and low-expansion. Cast roll-to-roll cellulose-nanofibril/bio-epoxy film (CTE ~5-10 ppm/K, close to silicon) with a silane moisture barrier as the build-up dielectric for DRAM and HBM package substrates.

title: Hermit-crab strategy: retrofit idle LCD panel fabs for oxide-TFT memory
idea: Hermit crabs move into empty shells; buy idle Gen-8.5 LCD/OLED backplane fabs (2.2 x 2.5 m glass, IGZO TFT lines installed) and run 2T0C gain-cell arrays at 1-2 um rules on glass (~30 GB per panel) for capacity-tier CXL memory, bonded to small CMOS controllers.
note: ~20 GB per 5.5 m2 panel; cost per GB likely above DRAM contract.

title: Pollinator robots move memory sleds to where demand blooms
idea: Bees ferry pollen between flowers; rack robots carry blind-mate, hot-plug CXL memory sleds rated for thousands of insertions from underused racks to those whose KV and batch demand will peak, guided by tomorrow's forecast.

title: HDD PRML joint detection replaces bitline shielding and twisting
idea: Treat bitline-to-bitline coupling as intersymbol interference, as an HDD read channel does: sample 8 adjacent bitlines with two-level comparators, run a 4-state Viterbi detector in the column path that decides all 8 jointly, then restore. Shield lines, twist regions and folded layouts are dropped for minimum-pitch open bitlines.

title: Cross-laminated timber: rotate tier orientation to cancel wafer bow
idea: Borrowed from cross-laminated timber, which rotates the grain 90 degrees per layer so warping cancels: in stacked 3D DRAM, rotate wordline/bitline direction 90 degrees every N tiers and alternate tensile and compressive film stacks so anisotropic stress cancels, keeping bow under ~50 um at 64+ tiers.

title: Jigsaw-puzzle chiplet edges triple die-to-die shoreline
idea: Use room-temperature plasma dicing to cut memory and compute chiplets with interlocking jigsaw or crenellated edges. Mating pieces meet along a meandering seam that is bridged by short fine-pitch RDL or edge-coupled links.

title: RFID backscatter: memory die reflects and never transmits
idea: Like passive RFID tags, the memory die modulates the impedance of an RDL-patterned antenna (≤250 C) to backscatter a carrier sent by the processor. The memory side needs no transmitter or PLL.

title: PRML read channel undoes bitline crosstalk instead of shielding
idea: Port the partial-response maximum-likelihood detection IBM introduced for magnetic disks in 1990. Groups of 8 adjacent bitlines are sampled by 3-bit flash comparators after charge sharing, and a small Viterbi detector decides the bits jointly using the die's measured coupling matrix. Inter-bitline crosstalk becomes a modeled channel instead of noise that has to be shielded or twisted away.

title: Thyristor latch wordline drivers from one implant
idea: Revive the thyratron, in its SCR form, as a wordline driver. One added implant mask forms a PNPN stack at each sub-wordline end. A tiny decoder pulse triggers it, it latches the wordline high from a pulsed 3 V rail, and it resets when the rail drops at precharge, so no level shifter or large thick-oxide PMOS is needed.
note: An SCR latch driver removes level shifters; latch-up and reset timing are the risks.

title: Capacitance-collapse bitline boost from one varactor implant
idea: Echoing 1950s varactor parametric amplifiers, each bitline gets a strip of MOS varactor, formed by one added accumulation-well implant mask, held in its high-capacitance state during charge sharing. Just before latching it is switched to depletion, roughly halving total bitline capacitance, so with charge conserved the differential voltage about doubles with no transistor noise.
note: Collapsing bitline capacitance after charge sharing gives noiseless signal gain; common-mode shift needs handling.

title: Sonic-film memory: strain pulses address bits instead of transistors
idea: Revive Sperry's 1960s sonic-film memory: an AlN transducer launches a GHz strain pulse along a magnetostrictive Fe-Co strip, and a global current pulse writes only where the strain pulse is at that instant (magnetoelastic coincidence). The inverse effect reads the bit back, so a bit's location is set by time of flight.
note: Time-of-flight addressing makes access serial, not random-access DRAM class.

title: Core memory reborn as plated toroids around through-glass vias
idea: Revive 1950s coincident-current ferrite core memory on 515x510 mm glass panels: laser-modified, wet-etched through-glass vias at ~3 um pitch get an electroplated square-loop NiFeMo toroid, and the X, Y and sense wires become ordinary panel redistribution layers instead of hand-threaded wire. The panel is a passive array; drivers and sense amps sit on a small CMOS chiplet at its edge.

title: Goto parametrons built in BAW-filter fabs store phase bits
idea: Revive Eiichi Goto's 1954 parametron, which held a bit as the 0 or pi phase of a parametrically pumped resonator, using arrays of ScAlN micro-resonators pumped at 2f by a shared on-chip line; a bit is read by mixing with a reference phase and written by briefly injecting a seed tone. The pump sustains the state, so there is no leaking capacitor and no access-transistor tail.

title: IBM 360 card-capacitor ROM stacked as thin-film back-end layers
idea: Revive CCROS, the System/360 card-capacitor read-only store: each layer is a word-line metal, a thin dielectric and a bit-line metal, with a '1' wherever an e-beam-defined coupling pad exists, and pulsing a word line couples charge onto the bit lines with no transistor or diode in the array. Dozens of layers stack using only deposition and patterning.
note: Transistorless capacitive ROM stacked in BEOL; signal shrinks with bitline load, e-beam throughput limits.

title: Dekatron-style ferroelectric counting capacitor tracks page hotness
idea: Like dekatron tubes that stepped one state per pulse, a sub-coercive ferroelectric capacitor switches a fixed fraction of its domains on each access pulse, accumulating a nonvolatile count. One capacitor per 64 KB region sits in a small university-built HZO array beside the memory controller and is read and reset each epoch to drive tier migration.
note: Accumulative sub-coercive HZO switching used as an analog hotness counter is a new application; variability is the doubt.

title: Plated-wire looms weave copper interposer fabric instead of silicon CoWoS
idea: Revive the 1960s plated-wire memory weaving looms to weave 15-25 um insulated copper wires at ~40 um pitch into a fabric that is laminated into an organic panel and laser-opened at die sites, forming long memory-to-logic links.

title: Intel 1103 gain cells hold parity: physics diversity decorrelates failures
idea: Intel's 1970 1103 used a 3T cell read non-destructively through a gain transistor. Keep data in 1T1C cells but store the ECC check bits in a separate stripe of 3T gain cells, which have no capacitor, leak by a different mechanism and are not disturbed by wordline hammering, so one row event or leaky subarray cannot corrupt data and parity together.
note: Physics-diverse parity storage; gain-cell retention may be worse than 1T1C.

title: Babbage's locking detents: time-to-latch flags ambiguous bits as erasures
idea: Babbage designed the Difference Engine to jam rather than pass a figure wheel resting between two digits. Each sense-amp group gets a tiny timer measuring latch resolution time (which grows as ln(1/dV)); slow-resolving bits are flagged as erasures and the ECC decodes with their positions known, which doubles what the same parity repairs (a SECDED code corrects 2-3 erasures).
note: Sense-amp resolution time as soft info; per-group timers locate group not bit.

title: Uncorrectable-error insurance underwrites relaxed-refresh deployments
idea: Operators won't run DRAM outside spec because a rare uncorrectable error is an unpriced tail risk. Form a small underwriting venture that prices that risk from controlled retention-stress data and fleet telemetry. It sells per-server policies that pay out on detected uncorrectable errors for customers running certified extended-refresh settings. The actuarial model, test lab and a reinsurer partnership fit within $1M and 24 months.
note: Financial hedge for relaxed refresh is unusual; actuarial data and reinsurer appetite within $1M doubtful.

title: Sliced laminate edge face exposes every bitline for side contact
idea: Laminate printed array foils, saw the block perpendicular to the bitlines and polish the cut face so every bitline of every foil appears as a dot at ~25 x 10 um pitch, then print redistribution or bond an edge-mounted silicon sense die directly onto that face.

title: Self-passivated chamber walls eliminate NF3 cleans for ALD and CVD
idea: ALD/CVD films grow only where precursors find reactive sites; keep chamber walls and liners capped with a renewable small-molecule inhibitor re-dosed each lot and held above the precursor desorption temperature, so walls never accumulate film and periodic NF3 remote-plasma cleans disappear.
note: Inhibitor surviving all precursors at wall temperature is the doubt.

title: Rework-orthogonal layer stack: strip and redo any failed step
idea: First principle: wafers are scrapped because removing a bad layer damages the layers beneath. Give each pair of adjacent layers an etchant with >1000:1 selectivity (for example, thin Ge-rich sacrificial interlayers under metals that dissolve in H2O2), so any misprocessed module can be stripped and redeposited, extending rework loops from litho to every module.

title: Multimode-fiber speckle hashing finds duplicate pages for free
idea: A multimode glass fiber is a fixed random matrix, so the speckle pattern at its output is a random projection of its input, which is a locality-sensitive hash. Modulate candidate pages or KV chunks onto a laser, send them through the fiber and read a 1-kpixel camera; matching speckle signatures flag exact and near-duplicate content for merging.
note: Optical random projection as LSH is real; modulating pages onto light costs more than software KSM hashing.

title: Abacus bead: electron packet shuttled between twin floating islands
idea: Stimulus 'abacus' (a bead slides, nothing is added or removed) -> each cell has two oxide-isolated floating nano-islands joined by a gated tunnel barrier; writing moves a fixed packet of ~5,000 electrons left or right, and a differential sense amp compares the two islands. Total charge is conserved, so substrate/junction leakage disappears and common-mode drift cancels while the signal doubles.
note: Charge-conserving differential pair cancels common-mode leakage; tunneling write endurance is the doubt.

title: Organic food label: certified fluorine-free memory gets procurement and permit advantage
idea: Stimulus 'organic food label' -> create a U.S. 'PFAS-free memory' certification (no PFAS resists or surfactants, no fluorinated etch or clean, no WF6) tied to federal procurement preference and fast-track water permits, because fluorine-free fabs skip PFAS wastewater treatment and clear the coming EU PFAS restriction. It pulls the fluorine-free storage elements in this cell into early demand.

title: Knitting: loop-end wordline layout deletes the SAQP cut mask
idea: Random stimulus 'knitting' (one yarn, closed loops, nothing cut) -> instead of cutting the closed ends of self-aligned quadruple-patterned spacer loops, which takes an extra critical mask, each loop is used as ONE electrical wordline that crosses two transistor rows. The active-area pattern is staggered so that each bitline contact sees only one gate in the loop, and the loop ends land on a sacrificial 'selvedge' strip that a blanket CMP trims away.

title: Bucket brigade: oxide-TFT charge-transfer FIFO for pipelined activations
idea: Firefighters pass buckets down a line: build a back-end IGZO charge-transfer shift-register (CCD-like) memory that supports only FIFO access, eliminating row decoders and most sense amps, and use it for pipeline-parallel activation queues and streamed weights, which are naturally sequential.
note: Decoder-less sequential memory in BEOL IGZO; transfer efficiency and speed are doubts.

title: Echo: DRAM die backscatters host carrier, never drives line
idea: Forced 'echo': the host sends a continuous carrier, and the DRAM die only switches its termination impedance to reflect a modulated echo (RFID-style backscatter). The slow-transistor DRAM process never has to build high-speed drivers.
note: DRAM still switches impedance at GHz; host must cancel its own carrier echo at speed.

title: Latch resolution time as free confidence signal for decoding
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x metastability-timed latch x per-SA time comparator x bulk Si x standard. A tiny counter measures how long each latch takes to resolve; slow resolution (small input) marks the bit low-confidence, giving the decoder soft information without extra reference reads.

title: Refresh-time 2D parity scrubbing computed inside sense amplifiers
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: standard | sense: sense amps with XOR accumulator latch | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. During each refresh sweep the sense amps XOR every refreshed row into a column-parity latch and compare it with a stored parity row (updated by write deltas), while per-row parity bits flag the row, so the row-column intersection locates and fixes single flips at zero extra activations.
note: XOR accumulation in sense amps during refresh makes scrubbing free; write-delta parity upkeep costly.

title: Bond-interface dielectric turns facing pads into storage capacitors
idea: Po: the glue is the memory. Bond two wafers through a 4 nm ZrO2/Al2O3 laminate deposited on the facing Cu pads, so each pad pair becomes a MIM capacitor (~5-7 fF at 400 nm pitch); the top wafer holds access transistors and the bottom a common plate plus periphery.

title: Hard-drive head fabs make magnetic working memory
idea: Po: the disk-drive factory makes RAM. HDD read-head fabs already deposit and ion-mill sub-20 nm MTJ stacks at volume; as head demand flattens, use their deposition and milling lines to add SOT-MRAM layers onto 28 nm CMOS wafers shipped in from mature foundries, as a refresh-free DRAM-class tier.
note: Clever capacity reuse, but SOT-MRAM density is far below DRAM.

title: Negabytes: pay to free memory like utilities pay for negawatts
idea: Po: we pay people to un-buy memory. A federal program modeled on utility demand-side programs pays a verified $/GB-year for DRAM freed through software or architecture changes, measured by fleet telemetry; freed U.S.-made modules are bought back and redeployed to defense, research and domestic manufacturers.
note: A negawatt-style buyback for freed DRAM is new; verifying freed GB is the doubt.

title: Free-space optical memory links through immersion coolant
idea: Po: the liquid is the wire. In immersion-cooled racks, memory sleds and accelerator boards face each other through the dielectric fluid and exchange data over arrays of collimated micro-LED and photodiode pixels (imaging links), replacing copper backplanes and cables.

title: Self-healing interposer with GeTe switches rerouting dead bumps
idea: Po: the package rewires itself after it is built. Embed phase-change GeTe RF switches in the interposer routing layer so that, after assembly test, channels are re-routed around open microbumps or bad TSV lanes by pulsing the switches once.

title: Light elevator: optical broadcast through windows in stacked dies
idea: Po: the chip is a window. One mask both opens a metal-free optical shaft through each die's wiring and defines a silicon ion implant forming a defect-mediated 1550 nm detector that absorbs a few percent, so one beam from the base die broadcasts clock and commands to all 16 dies in turn.

title: Cochlea-style dithered repeated comparisons beat sense-amp offset
idea: The ear's hair cells detect sub-noise sounds with help from noise. A tiny clocked comparator, isolated from the bitline, fires 7 times before and 7 times after the wordline rises while a known triangular dither is coupled in; the difference of the two vote counts cancels the comparator offset and resolves a signal below it, then the main latch restores.
note: Vote-count averaging below offset; 14-comparison latency and dither noise.

title: Embargoed Soviet engineer's shingled staircase stack with overlap coupling
idea: Under embargo with no TSV etcher or interposer: shingle 8-16 thinned DRAM dies like roof tiles, each overlapping the one below by ~200 um, and pass signals through the overlap by capacitive proximity pads under 1 um of oxide, while power comes in by ordinary wire bonds on the exposed step.
note: Proximity coupling relayed through shingled overlaps; ~1 Tb/s per stack is well below HBM.
