title: Farmer's crop rotation: supply TSVs swap VDD and VSS roles
idea: A farmer rotates crops so soil recovers: on-die power switches periodically swap which TSV groups carry VDD and which carry VSS, reversing the DC current direction in each via every few hours so electromigration damage partly heals.

title: Alien's indifference to testing: fountain-coded tiles across untested printed foil
idea: An alien never inspects parts one at a time: data is spread with a rateless (Raptor-style) code over many small printed memory tiles, and the controller reads tiles in parallel and stops as soon as any k good symbols decode, so dead or flaky tiles that were never tested or mapped simply don't contribute.

title: Record-solar-cell passivated contact at the storage-node junction
idea: Record silicon solar cells reach junction saturation currents of ~1-5 fA/cm2 with a ~1.5 nm tunnel oxide capped by doped polysilicon (TOPCon). Form the capacitor-to-access-device contact the same way, so the heavily doped, defective region sits in the poly rather than in the silicon and contact-region generation current collapses.

title: DirectFlash for DRAM: hyperscalers buy raw, retention-unscreened dies
idea: Some all-flash array vendors buy raw NAND and manage it themselves. Hyperscalers likewise buy DRAM dies that skip hot retention test, laser repair and retention binning, at a discount, and run them behind their own LDPC/CXL controller sized for 1% cell BER.
note: DRAM latency budget makes 1%-BER LDPC hard outside far-memory tiers.

title: Latch resolution time as free soft information for decoding
idea: Time-domain readout: because a latch resolves in ~tau*ln(V/dV), a strobe flip-flop samples each SA output a few hundred ps before the normal strobe, flags any SA not yet resolved as weak, and feeds the flags as erasures to the decoder on the base die.

title: Coaxial-cable cell: shell transistor wrapped around a core capacitor
idea: Scale a coaxial cable down to 40 nm: in one vertical hole, ALD an outer gate, gate oxide and oxide-semiconductor shell channel, then fill the core with a MIM capacitor, so the access transistor surrounds its own storage node. The bitline contacts the top of the shell and the bottom of the core is the plate, giving a 4F2 cell from one etch.

title: Every LCD pixel is a DRAM cell: display-fab memory sheets
idea: Scale from wafer up to Gen 8.5 display glass: an active-matrix pixel is a transistor plus a storage capacitor, so idle display fabs with 1-2 um litho can make giant oxide-TFT 1T1C sheets. Dice and laminate 32 sheets into a bulk tier for capacity-hungry, latency-tolerant work such as KV-cache spill.
note: Oxide-TFT 1T1C at 1-2 um gives ~$2-3/GB per layer before periphery; long lines hurt latency.

title: Micro-spring phonon chucks conduct wafer heat with no backside gas
idea: Scale jump from gas molecules to MEMS: the chuck face carries millions of ~10 um compliant SiC micro-springs that electrostatic clamping presses into solid contact. They carry ~500-1000 W/m2-K of heat by phonons, comparable to helium backside gas.

title: Williams tube read-around fix: analog row-hammer integrators
idea: Williams tubes failed partly because reading one spot disturbed its neighbors (the 'read-around ratio'), so refresh had to be set by worst-case counts. Give each DRAM row driver a tiny leaky capacitor that receives a charge packet on every neighboring activation and decays over time. When its voltage crosses a comparator threshold, the driver requests a targeted refresh of that row.

title: HP SAIL single-stamp imprint patterns roll-to-roll oxide access arrays
idea: HP's self-aligned imprint lithography (spun out as Phicot) died chasing large display backplanes, where web stretch ruined overlay. Pattern every layer of an oxide-TFT access array on a web with one multi-height imprint stamp, etched back level by level, so the layers stay self-aligned whatever the foil distortion. Target small memory tiles that can absorb defects through redundancy.
note: Single-stamp self-aligned imprint solves web overlay; micron pitch keeps density too low for cost/bit win.

title: Thyristor-pair sense amplifier: T-RAM's latch reborn as periphery
idea: Failure mined: T-RAM died because a thyristor used as the storage cell had temperature-dependent holding current and standby leakage. Fix: use a cross-coupled gated-lateral thyristor pair as the bitline sense amplifier instead of the 6-8 transistor latch. It is biased only for the ~5 ns of sensing, so holding-current drift and standby leakage never matter, and its regenerative pnpn gain resolves ~20 mV in one step.

title: Silicon LEDs failed on efficiency; SPAD receivers make them enough
idea: Silicon light emitters were abandoned for links because indirect-gap emission is 1e-5 efficient or worse. Across bonded dies (<20 um of oxide), a receiver built from silicon single-photon avalanche diodes needs only ~20-50 photons per bit, so a reverse-biased avalanche-mode Si junction, emitting fast 600-900 nm hot-carrier light, can signal die-to-die with no III-V, Ge or In.
note: SPAD photon budget makes Si emitters viable; dead time limits per-channel rate.

title: MEMS relay computers died of contact wear; relays pool memory instead
idea: Berkeley-style MEMS relay logic failed because contacts wore out within ~1e9 cycles and switched too slowly for logic. Memory pooling switches only when allocations change (minutes), so build an in-package crossbar of electrostatic poly-Si relays with TiN/carbon contacts (no Ru, Pt or W) that physically re-wires memory chiplets between compute dies, with zero standby power and no SerDes.
note: Rare switching sidesteps relay wear; signal integrity of thousands of GHz lanes through contacts is the doubt.

title: Recirculating GHz phonon loops revive mercury delay-line memory on chip
idea: Effect walk: piezoelectric transduction of acoustic waves. Bits are 100-ps acoustic pulses circulating in a thin-film LiNbO3-on-Si phononic waveguide loop, regenerated once per lap by a piezo transducer and amplifier; slow-wave phononic-crystal sections (group velocity <200 m/s) pack more bits per micron.
note: Sequential access and low density restrict to a streaming niche.

title: Polarity-encoded piezo resonators read by RF echo, never switched
idea: Effect walk: sign of the piezoelectric coefficient. Nanoscale ferroelectric AlScN contour-mode resonators store the bit as the sign of d33; a tiny RF ping on a shared line excites 64 resonators at distinct frequencies, and each response phase (0 vs 180 degrees) reveals its polarization while most stored mechanical energy returns to the line.
note: Frequency-multiplexed resonant read is clever but resonator area kills density.

title: Bank-wide ferroelectric back gate flips array Vt for sleep
idea: Effect: remanent ferroelectric polarization. A shared HZO back gate under each subarray's vertical-channel transistors is pulsed once on self-refresh entry to polarization 'down', adding ~0.4 V of nonvolatile back-bias that shuts the leakage tail with no continuous negative pump; on exit a pulse restores 'up' for full drive.

title: Electrochromic BIST pads let cameras read wafer test without probe cards
idea: Effect: electrochromism. Each die's built-in self-test drives a small WO3 electrochromic pad (H+ or Li+ intercalation) that turns dark blue when a mat or bank fails. A full-wafer membrane supplies only power and a few control pins, and a camera reads the pass/fail map of every die on the wafer in seconds, so no dense signal probe cards or tester channels are needed.
note: Camera-read electrochromic pass/fail pads avoid tester channels; full-wafer power contact is still needed.

title: Stochastic-resonance multi-reads recover bits from undersized gain cells
idea: For error-tolerant data (images, embeddings, low-order weight bits), shrink storage nodes to ~1 fF in a gain-cell array with non-destructive reads. Add calibrated noise to the sense reference and average 4-8 fast reads; the dither lifts the sub-threshold signal across the decision line (stochastic resonance), giving acceptable bit-error rates.
note: Stored-charge noise is frozen at write, so repeated dithered reads may not average it out.

title: Phase-change drift doubles as a built-in page age clock
idea: Give each page a Ge-rich GST cell that is reset on access. Structural relaxation makes its resistance drift upward as log(t), so reading the cell tells the controller the time since last use. A co-located reference cell drifts at the same 125 C temperature and normalizes the reading. Eviction to compressed or NVM tiers picks the oldest pages without timestamp SRAM.
note: Novel use of drift, but page age is cheap in software; temperature normalization hard.

title: Johnsen-Rahbek electroadhesion: programmable roller stamps transfer only known-good DRAM dies
idea: A roller stamp with an addressable electrode array energizes Johnsen-Rahbek electroadhesion only under dies that passed wafer test, lifting thousands of known-good DRAM chiplets per revolution and printing them onto a moving interposer web.

title: Si: deep-trench DRAM built into the passive interposer itself
idea: Interposers are thousands of mm2 of idle silicon: fabricate 1T1C eDRAM in them using the deep-trench capacitors (~30-60 fF, far above the ~5 fF pillar wall) that interposer lines already offer for decoupling, at 65-90 nm DUV rules, as a memory tier beside the HBM stacks.
note: Turns passive interposer into active DRAM wafer; only ~1-2 GB per interposer and big-area yield risk.

title: Mg: MgO stochastic tunnel junctions as coin-flip hammer counters
idea: A BEOL MgO magnetic tunnel junction beside each row driver gets a sub-critical pulse on every activation, switching with probability ~1/500 from thermal noise; a switched junction triggers neighbor refresh and is reset, giving a hardware probabilistic counter with no tables and no attacker-predictable state.

title: Al: U.S. BAW-filter fabs make aluminum-boron-nitride ferroelectric memory
idea: RF BAW filter fabs already sputter piezoelectric AlN at volume; adding boron co-sputtering yields wurtzite Al(1-x)B(x)N ferroelectric (Pr >100 uC/cm2) capacitors and FeFETs as a BEOL non-volatile memory.
note: BAW fab reuse for AlBN is non-obvious; huge coercive field and low endurance limit it to NVM.

title: Automotive e-coat bath self-plugs capacitor dielectric pinholes
idea: Before the top electrode goes on, immerse the array in an electrophoretic polymer/oxide paint bath and bias the bottom electrodes. Only pinholes and thin spots conduct, so insulating deposit grows exactly there and stops itself, just as car-body e-coat seals only the exposed metal.
note: Polymer plugs must survive later thermal steps in 3D capacitors.

title: Hydraulic-accumulator antiferroelectric reservoirs replace oversized wordline charge pumps
idea: Like a hydraulic accumulator that banks pressure for peak demand, put antiferroelectric ZrO2 capacitors under the sub-wordline driver strips. A small pump charges them slowly, and during activate bursts they release a large charge at a near-constant voltage plateau set by the field-induced phase switch-back.

title: Andon-cord sense amps flag slow-resolving cells for targeted refresh
idea: Like Toyota's andon cord, which any worker pulls to flag a problem, each SA strip gets a tiny resolution-time detector (XOR of the latch nodes sampled at a fixed delay after enable). Any SA still metastable at the strobe pulls a shared andon line, so the controller logs that row as weak and refreshes it more often while others refresh less.
note: SA resolution time as in-situ retention monitor; data-pattern and VRT dependence may hide weak cells.

title: Flemish-bond stacking: staggered tiers share each sense-amp strip vertically
idea: Like bricks laid in Flemish bond so joints never line up, offset alternate 3D-DRAM tiers by half a mat. Every SA strip then sits between the bitline ends of the tier above and the tier below and serves both through short vertical vias.

title: Fluidic self-assembly drops 180 nm periphery blocks into array wafers
idea: Borrow 1990s fluidic self-assembly (Alien Technology, 1994): make charge pumps, I/O, fuse/test and command logic as trapezoidal ~50 um blocks on depreciated 180 nm lines. Pour them as a slurry over the array wafer, whose etched recesses accept only the matching shape, then wire them with one coarse i-line metal layer.

title: Brewed photoresists: fermentation-made fluorine-free photoacid generators
idea: Use engineered yeast and E. coli the way breweries and pharma ferment: make bio-based aromatic sulfonium cations, camphor- or lignin-derived sulfonic acid anions and chain-scission polymer backbones, giving ArF and KrF resists with no perfluoroalkyl sulfonate PAGs and no fluorinated surfactants.

title: Lattice-defect-aware codes for self-assembled cell arrays
idea: Block-copolymer self-assembly makes near-perfect hexagonal arrays whose defects are known topological types (dislocations, disclinations, grain boundaries) that displace lines or wedges of cells; design hexagonal-lattice codes whose syndromes recognise exactly those fault shapes, so DSA-patterned arrays with ~1e-4 defect density stay usable.

title: Supercritical-CO2 decaffeination-style healing of capacitor dielectric vacancies
idea: Coffee is decaffeinated by supercritical CO2 that penetrates whole beans; use scCO2 carrying trace H2O2 or ozone, with no argon plasma or anneal ambient, to reach the bottom of 70:1 capacitor trenches at under 150C and refill oxygen vacancies in ZrO2/HfO2 that create the leakage tail.
note: Novel low-T vacancy refill; doubt ozone/H2O2 transport and reaction in 70:1 trenches.

title: Vernier-select contacts absorb misregistration from solid-state interference lithography
idea: A machinist's vernier reads alignment from offset scales; pattern the periodic array with solid-state-laser interference lithography (quadrupled Nd:YAG, no excimer neon), print periphery contacts as a vernier set of offset candidates, and after test electrically select whichever candidate landed on each line.

title: Panel-scale DRAM made on display oxide-TFT glass lines
idea: IFR: memory as cheap per square meter as a television. Use Gen 8.5+ display fabs' oxide-TFT lines (1-1.5 um features, ultralow-leak IGZO-class TFTs already in mass production) to build huge-area 1T1C tiles, with CMOS sense and I/O chiplets bonded along tile edges so each panel holds hundreds of GB.
note: At 1-1.5 um features ~10 GB/m2, so $100-300/m2 is ~$10-30/GB, worse than wafer DRAM cost.

title: Passive RF resonators let every wafer report its own metrology
idea: Ideal: zero metrology tools. Closest: scribe lines carry passive LC resonators built from the layers made so far, whose resonance shifts with CD, film thickness and overlay; a contactless RF reader in each load port interrogates every wafer in seconds after each module, replacing sampled CD-SEM/OCD for go/no-go.

title: Hadamard-coded multi-row reads give tiny MRAM signals root-N SNR
idea: Constraint: non-volatile resistive cells with weak signal. Because MRAM reads are non-destructive, activate N rows at once with +/-1 Hadamard-coded read biases over N sense cycles and invert the code in a small digital block; the Fellgett multiplex advantage gives a sqrt(N) SNR gain per cell (4x at N=16).

title: Bitlines as last-gasp battery for finishing in-flight NV writes
idea: Constraint: no write may be torn when power dies. At power-fail detect, switches tie every precharged bitline and VPP-node capacitance on the die (~3 uF total at 0.5-3 V) to a shared rail that powers completion of in-flight NV writes and a write-buffer flush.

title: Swap electron storage for proton position in hydrated-oxide gate
idea: A 3-terminal cell shuttles H+ between a Pd-H reservoir and a WO3 channel through a 5 nm phosphosilicate-glass proton conductor. Pulses of ~5 ns at ~1 V (as in MIT's protonic resistors) set the channel conductance, which is read non-destructively.
note: Endurance of protonic devices under DRAM duty is unknown.

title: Substitute mask lithography with solid-state DUV interference patterning
idea: Substitute neon-buffered excimer scanners with a frequency-quintupled solid-state laser (213 nm) in a two- or four-beam interference tool that prints the periodic wordline and active gratings without a mask; cut layers are done by imprint.

title: Image-sensor ramp comparators replace per-bitline DRAM latch sense amps
idea: Substitute per-bitline cross-coupled latches with the column-parallel single-slope ramp comparator borrowed from CMOS image sensors. The bitlines act as analog sample-and-hold nodes, one comparator plus counter serially digitizes 16 bitlines against a global ramp, and a burst write driver then restores the row.

title: Soft-decision dual-time latch sampling feeds on-die LDPC
idea: Substitute the hard binary sense decision with soft information: each latch output is sampled at an early and a late strobe, and disagreement flags a low-confidence bit. An on-die soft-decision LDPC over 512-bit column words then corrects them.
note: Dual-strobe soft info plus LDPC; decode latency is costly at DRAM access times.

title: CCD charge shifting replaces bitlines for column readout
idea: Substitute the bitline with a polysilicon charge-coupled column: stored charge packets are clocked down the column like a CCD imager to a single floating-diffusion sense node at the column end. This revives 1970s CCD memory for sequential AI streams with two-level poly in a university fab.

title: Substitute helium backside cooling with electrolyzer hydrogen and closed-loop capture
idea: Run electrostatic-chuck backside cooling in etch, CVD and implant tools with 5-20 Torr hydrogen (higher thermal conductivity than helium) from an on-site electrolyzer, and fit remaining helium uses (leak check, purge, litho) with cryogenic capture-and-reuse loops. Chuck seals get diffusion barriers so exhaust stays well under the H2 lower explosive limit.

title: Liquid-metal-loaded underfill doubles as shield and heat path
idea: Substitute epoxy-silica underfill between stacked dies with an elastomer carrying oxide-skinned gallium-alloy droplets that stay insulating but raise thermal conductivity ~5x; laser-sintering selected regions of the same film turns them into a conductive ground mesh.

title: Contactless memory slot: PCB coil pairs replace DIMM connector pins
idea: Substitute metal edge-finger contacts with arrays of near-field coupled coil pairs etched in ordinary PCB copper on module and motherboard, driven by a small transceiver FPGA/ASIC; modules slide in without contact, are hot-swappable and the slot pitch can shrink.

title: 3D-printed micro-spring sockets for test-then-stack dies
idea: Substitute tungsten-rhenium probe needles and permanent bonds with two-photon-printed polymer micro-springs metallized by electroless plating, forming sockets that contact bare-die pads for at-speed known-good-die test and temporary mounting.
note: Two-photon printed probes for KGD test; MEMS probe cards already address this.

title: Electrohydrodynamic-printed copper pillars replace bumping lines
idea: Substitute photolithographic bumping and plating with electrohydrodynamic direct printing of 5-10 um copper micro-pillars voxel by voxel onto die pads, so one desktop printer turns bare purchased dies into fine-pitch flip-chip parts.

title: Substitute helium-cooled thermal anneals with sub-400 C microwave anneals
idea: Swap RTP/furnace steps and their helium cooling for selective microwave and forming-gas anneals at <=400 C that heal oxide-channel defects, designing a memory flow that consumes no helium at all.
note: Microwave anneal is known; helium use in anneals is a modest share.

title: MOS varactor storage node with self-amplifying C-V nonlinearity
idea: Combine an RF varactor with the storage capacitor: build the node as an accumulation-mode MOS capacitor whose capacitance is high when charged to '1' and drops ~3x near '0', so the stored charge difference exceeds that of a linear capacitor of the same average size. The C-V nonlinearity acts as built-in gain at charge-share time.

title: BEOL complementary oxide latch: n-IGZO plus p-SnO cross-coupled
idea: Combine n-type IGZO with p-type SnO or Cu2O thin-film transistors into a cross-coupled CMOS latch built in the back-end and stacked 4-8 tiers over logic. Like SRAM it holds state statically with no refresh, but oxide off-currents (~1e-19 A) make standby power ~1000x lower than silicon SRAM.
note: p-type oxide TFTs weak; latch density per tier low.

title: Bank-to-bank recycling of bitline restore charge
idea: When a bank precharges, its bitlines (half at VARY, half at ground) are not simply equalized to VBLP; a switch matrix first dumps the high-side charge into the reservoir feeding the next bank's restore, recycling about half the bitline charge.

title: Boron-doped etch-stop superlattice replaces SiGe for lateral 3D DRAM
idea: Build the 3D DRAM tier stack as single-crystal Si epitaxy with alternating heavily boron-doped layers (US borate supply) instead of Si/SiGe, then remove the p++ layers with a dopant-selective HNA-type wet etch to open lateral capacitor and channel cavities, using no germanium.
note: Boron diffusion smears thin p++ layers across 100+ tiers.

title: Topcoat-free immersion resist via self-segregating siloxane additive
idea: Combine resist and immersion topcoat (zero masks): a hydrocarbon-siloxane block additive floats to the resist surface during spin coat and forms the hydrophobic water barrier normally made by fluorinated topcoats and fluorinated surface additives.

title: Metal SADP spacers become the finished bitlines
idea: Combine self-aligned double patterning with metallization: the spacer is deposited conformally as Ru or Mo rather than oxide, etched back, and the mandrel removed, so the spacers are the bitlines. Hard-mask transfer, metal deposition, metal etch and two cleans are skipped.

title: Liquid-metal membrane chuck replaces helium backside cooling
idea: Combine the electrostatic chuck with a sealed, compliant membrane filled with gallium-indium liquid metal or a phase-change medium that conducts heat from the wafer backside. This removes the helium backside gas used in every etch and deposition chamber.
note: Ga contamination risk in fab chambers.

title: MacEtch TSVs whose catalyst becomes the plating seed
idea: Combine metal-assisted chemical etching with via metallization: a perforated Au/Ag catalyst film sinks into silicon in HF/H2O2 at room temperature, carving 50-100 um vertical holes, and the same catalyst left at the via bottom serves as the seed for bottom-up Cu electroplating after an electrografted polymer liner. No Bosch DRIE (helium backside cooling) and no argon-sputtered seed.
note: Au catalyst left in silicon is a deep-level contaminant that may hurt DRAM retention.

title: Diode-laser photoreduction writes copper redistribution lines directly
idea: Combine laser direct imaging with metal deposition: coat a copper-formate/amine complex film, scan a 405 nm GaN diode-laser array to photothermally reduce it into 2-5 um Cu lines, rinse unexposed film and electroless-thicken. No photoresist, no excimer scanner (ArF/KrF need neon) and no argon-sputtered seed.

title: Thermomigrated aluminum trails form TSVs with no etching
idea: Combine solar-cell thermal-gradient zone melting with through-silicon vias: print Al dots on an n-type wafer and apply a vertical temperature gradient (IR heating below, chilled plate above) so molten Al-Si droplets migrate through the wafer, leaving Al-saturated p+ columns (~1-2 ohm each) junction-isolated from the bulk.
note: Resistive p+ columns suit only power or slow signals; junction leakage and Al doping concerns.

title: Inkjet-printed oxide memory made usable by heavy LDPC coding
idea: Combine solution-processed, inkjet-printed In-Zn-O TFT plus capacitor arrays (maskless, <300 C) with strong LDPC and spare-block mapping, so arrays with 1e-3 defect/BER rates still deliver error-free storage. Buildable in a university nanofab: a printer, hotplate and probe station.

title: Rice-husk silica crucibles to break Spruce Pine dependence
idea: Combine U.S. rice-milling waste (Arkansas/California husk ash, about 90%+ amorphous SiO2) with acid-leach and plasma purification to make 6N synthetic silica, then fuse it into the inner liner of CZ crucibles over a lower-grade outer shell.
note: Purifying husk ash (K, Ca, P) to 6N crucible grade is the doubt.

title: Carbon-mandrel inverse damascene for fluorine-free contact holes
idea: Combine amorphous-carbon pillars (patterned with O2 plasma) with conformal low-temperature oxide fill and CMP. The carbon mandrels are then ashed out in O2, leaving contact or storage-node holes in oxide without ever etching oxide.

title: Fab air-separation LN2 feeding cryo-pods for retention-reject dies
idea: Combine the liquid nitrogen produced by a fab's on-site air-separation unit with sealed 77 K memory pods. Dies binned out for retention tails (leakage collapses at cryo, so retention reaches seconds or more) are packaged into cryo-cooled far-memory appliances.
note: DRAM retention soars at 77 K; cryo overhead and niche recovered volume limit impact.

title: Anodized-aluminum nanopore templates as litho-free capacitor holes
idea: Borrow the electrolytic-capacitor industry's anodization: deposit Al over the access-transistor array, anodize it into self-ordered hexagonal nanopores (AR >200, pitch set by anodizing voltage), and line each pore with ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN as the storage capacitor. A shallow dimple pre-pattern on the landing pads registers each pore to its transistor.
note: AAO MIM capacitors known; pore-to-transistor registration and ordering defects are the real issue.

title: Polarization-division multiplexing: charge plus polarization in one node
idea: Like fiber links sending two polarizations on one fiber, store two orthogonal variables per node: a low-field charge level and the polarization direction of a thin ferroelectric layer in the same stack, read first by low-field charge sensing, then by high-field switching-current sensing.
note: At most 2x bits; polarization read is destructive and interferes with the charge level.

title: Deep-space soft-decision LDPC reading of decayed DRAM charge
idea: Adapted from the soft-decision LDPC decoding used by deep-space probes and 5G: a dual-threshold sense amplifier produces a 2-bit confidence value per cell before latching, and an on-die LDPC decoder over 512-bit codewords uses that soft information. Cells that have decayed near threshold are corrected rather than refreshed pre-emptively.

title: SerDes decision-feedback equalizer cancels bitline crosstalk
idea: Borrowed from high-speed SerDes DFE: sense amps fire in two staggered phases, and the decided values of phase-1 neighbors feed back through small programmed coupling capacitors to subtract their known crosstalk from phase-2 bitlines. Open-bitline arrays can then run at minimum pitch without dummy reference mats or twisting.
note: DFE-like feedback in staggered sensing; two-phase sensing already known.

title: EV battery-balancing capacitor ladder for stepwise bitline restore
idea: Borrowed from switched-capacitor active balancing in EV battery packs: bitlines are restored in three steps from a ladder of tank capacitors held at intermediate voltages, and on precharge they return charge down the same ladder instead of drawing everything from VDD.
note: Tank capacitor area must be comparable to the total bitline capacitance.

title: Open-pit mine benches: one cone etch exposes every tier
idea: Borrowed from open-pit mining benches: instead of 3D-NAND-style resist-trim staircases (dozens of litho/trim cycles), one tapered isotropic etch cuts a conical pit through the whole 3D DRAM tier stack so every wordline tier surfaces as a concentric ring on the pit wall. Contacts land on the rings at radii set by cone angle and tier thickness, using a single contact mask.

title: Self-stratifying paint: one-coat multilayer litho stacks
idea: Industrial coatings use self-stratifying paints that separate into primer and topcoat in one application; formulate a single spin-on film that, during bake, segregates by surface energy into a silicon-rich hardmask bottom layer, an organic underlayer and a fluorinated-segment resist top layer.

title: Display-industry sputtered zinc oxynitride channels for back-end gain-cell tiers
idea: The display industry sputters large-area oxide TFT channels; with In and Ga banned, use reactive-sputtered zinc oxynitride (ZnON, mobility ~50-100 cm2/Vs) with Al2O3/SiO2 gates to stack 2T0C gain-cell tiers above CMOS, each tier made by room-temperature sputtering and DUV litho, no epitaxy.

title: Freeze-dried heap: dehydrate cold objects, rehydrate on touch
idea: Borrowed from freeze-drying food: the garbage collector moves objects untouched for N cycles into a 'dehydrated' arena where pointers become 24-bit arena-relative varints, headers are dropped and fields are entropy-coded; a load barrier rehydrates an object into the live heap on first access.

title: Air-freight belly cargo: harvest stranded memory inside peripherals
idea: Borrowed from airlines selling spare cargo space under passenger cabins: idle DRAM in SmartNICs, DPUs, SSD controllers, BMCs and HBM on under-used inference cards is exported as a unified low-priority tier over PCIe/CXL, with a broker that preempts it when the device needs it back.
note: Peripheral DRAM share is usually small except idle GPU HBM.

title: Audio mastering dither: retention decay as free training noise
idea: Borrowed from audio mastering, where deliberate dither noise improves perceived quality: activations saved for backprop live in refresh-free DRAM, with sign/exponent bits stored in the non-leaking state so only mantissa LSBs can decay, and the sparse bit flips that accrue before the backward pass act as stochastic-rounding/dropout-like noise.
note: Close to EDEN/Flikker; refresh is a small share of DRAM power.

title: Video-codec P-frames for tensors: ship only deltas between tiles
idea: Adapted from MPEG motion-compensated inter-frame coding: the controller and a logic layer in the DRAM base die keep a reference tile and send only quantized residuals for activation, KV or optimizer tiles that change little step to step. Periodic 'I-frames' bound drift.

title: Deep-space LDPC coding lets memory links run at 50 mV swing
idea: Adapted from deep-space probes that trade coding gain for transmit power: the DRAM bus carries a short high-rate LDPC/polar code so swing drops from ~250-400 mV to ~50 mV. The PHY decoder cleans a raw BER of 1e-4 down to 1e-18.
note: LDPC decode latency and energy hurt memory links.

title: Gate-leakage load latch: engineered leakage holds static bits
idea: MAGNIFY a parasitic into the mechanism: in a 2-transistor cell on thin-oxide foundry devices, gate-tunneling current of one transistor acts as a pA pull-up and subthreshold current of the other as pull-down; sized so their I-V curves cross three times, the node has two stable voltages and holds statically.
note: Variation-sensitive; area is well above a DRAM cell.

title: Minify sense-amp count: one amplifier serially resolves eight held bitlines
idea: MINIFY the SA population 8x: bitlines are left floating after charge sharing (they hold the signal for ~100 ns as their own capacitors), and an 8:1 analog mux steps one larger, low-offset SA across them, each resolve-and-restore taking ~3 ns.

title: Minify the fab: iterate 3D tiers on half-inch-wafer tools
idea: Rent time on half-inch-wafer minimal-fab tool sets, about 1/1000 the capex of a 300 mm line with cycle times of days, to run hundreds of 3D DRAM tier process splits (deposition, selective recess, ALD) in 24 months.
note: Minimal Fab exists; tool set may lack needed epi/ALD capability.

title: Aluminum boron nitride capacitor: linear daily, ferroelectric at shutdown
idea: Minify hafnium and zirconium to zero: use wurtzite AlBN (abundant Al, B, N) as the capacitor dielectric. In normal use it runs below its coercive field as an ordinary linear DRAM capacitor, and it is switched as a ferroelectric only at power-down to save the memory image.

title: On-die microheaters anneal away trap damage: heat to heal
idea: Magnify temperature briefly to minify aging: polysilicon heaters under each bank pulse to ~250 C for seconds during maintenance windows, annealing BTI traps and trap-assisted leakage paths so lower-margin, cheaper materials survive 10 years at 125 C.

title: Magnify the substrate: DRAM on Gen-8.5 display glass panels
idea: Magnify the substrate from a 300 mm wafer (0.07 m2) to a 2.2x2.5 m display-glass mother panel (~80x the area) and build oxide-TFT 2T gain-cell arrays on idle LCD/LTPO backplane lines, dicing panels into memory tiles bonded to silicon periphery.
note: Relaxed rules make bits per panel too few for 10x cost gain.

title: Magnify compression effort with neural codecs on spare tensor cores
idea: Magnify compression effort for cold pages: learned autoencoder and context-model codecs, trained per page class (heap, tensors, text), run on the accelerator's idle tensor cores to compress and decompress the cold tier instead of LZ4.
note: Neural codec latency and energy on page faults; 3-5x over LZ4 on heap data unproven.

title: Magnify the controller: transparent columnar transposition of records
idea: Magnify the memory controller into a layout engine: arrays of structs marked by the allocator are stored column-wise with frame-of-reference, delta and dictionary encoding, and a gather unit presents ordinary rows to the CPU.

title: Diels-Alder reversible underfill that unzips at 120 C
idea: MINIFY rework damage: the underfill is a thermally reversible Diels-Alder polymer network that depolymerizes near 120 C, so microbumped memory dies lift off cleanly and re-underfill afterward.

title: Eliminate dielectric deposition: anodically grow the capacitor dielectric from its electrode
idea: Eliminate the deposited dielectric: form a Nb or Ta bottom electrode by CVD or electroless plating, then anodize it so a dense Nb2O5 (k~40) or Ta2O5 (k~25) film grows inward at ~2 nm/V, perfectly conformal at any aspect ratio, with thickness set by voltage to ~0.1 nm. No plasma, no sputter targets and no rare-gas ALD purges are used.

title: Eliminate deposition-plus-etch: patternable metal-oxo resist becomes the capacitor dielectric
idea: Eliminate separate dielectric deposition and etch: coat a Hf- or Zr-oxo-cluster photoresist, expose it with 365-nm UV LEDs or e-beam (no excimer laser), develop it, and anneal the remaining pattern into dense HfO2/ZrO2 that stays in place as storage dielectric and node isolation, so the resist is the device.
note: Resist-derived oxide density and leakage likely worse than ALD.

title: Eliminate the gate oxide: exfoliated beta-Ga2O3 Schottky-gate MESFET access
idea: Exfoliate or pattern beta-Ga2O3 nanomembranes and gate them directly with a Ni/Au Schottky gate, so there is no gate dielectric and no oxide or interface traps to cause random-telegraph leakage or variable retention time. The 4.8 eV gap gives aA-class off current.

title: Eliminate plasma-etch damage: KOH crystallographic (111) sidewall vertical channel
idea: Define vertical access-transistor channels by anisotropic KOH/TMAH etching of (110) silicon so channel sidewalls are atomically flat (111) planes instead of plasma-roughened surfaces, then grow thermal gate oxide. Lower interface-state density and no etch damage remove generation and VRT centers.
note: Thermal oxide on (111) Si has higher Dit than (100); smoothness may not net out.

title: Eliminate scanners for periphery: imprint with hydrocarbon-release molds
idea: Pattern the 40-100 nm periphery layers by jet-and-flash nanoimprint using an acrylate resist with no fluorinated surfactant and a mold anti-stick layer of octadecylsilane instead of the usual fluorosilane. Transfer the pattern with Cl2/HBr/O2 etches only.

title: Eliminate on-die redundancy: system-level page retirement replaces spares
idea: Drop spare rows, columns and laser-fuse boxes; ship each die with a signed bad-region map that the memory controller and OS use to retire 4 KB pages, accepting a few tenths of a percent of lost capacity.
note: Column faults span many pages; page retirement handles them poorly. Easy to simulate from fault maps.

title: Eliminate cell-level lithography: vapour-deposited, plasma-developed block copolymer holes
idea: Deposit a block copolymer film from vapour (iCVD) that self-assembles into a hexagonal hole array at the 4F2 pitch, guided by the transistor topography, and develop it by dry plasma removal of one block, with no spin coat, aqueous develop or wet strip.

title: Eliminate storing what can be recomputed: controller rematerialization engine
idea: The memory controller keeps a small recipe table for pages derivable from other data (activations from layer inputs, decompressed tensors, positional tables) and regenerates them in a near-memory MAC array on access instead of fetching them.

title: Eliminate CVD electrodes: electroless ruthenium plating inside capacitor holes
idea: Seed the capacitor mold holes with a palladium-activated monolayer and electrolessly plate conformal Ru bottom and top electrodes from a wet bath, replacing CVD/ALD TiN.

title: Eliminate the raw object: cache media as neural latent codes
idea: Image, video-thumbnail and document caches keep learned latent codes from a neural codec instead of raw or JPEG bytes; an inline accelerator decodes them on access, with perceptual error bounds per tenant.

title: Clockless delay-insensitive memory channel without DLLs or training
idea: Eliminate the clock: replace DDR strobes, DLLs, PLLs and link training on short on-package links with a 1-of-4 delay-insensitive code (2 bits on 4 wires, one transition per symbol, receiver detects completion and acknowledges). Timing adapts automatically to voltage, temperature and process.
note: Async DI codes known; wire overhead and completion detection eat gains.

title: Eliminate stored parity: decode weights against their known statistical prior
idea: Drop the 12.5% ECC parity for frozen model weights. The controller instead runs maximum-a-posteriori correction using the known per-tensor distribution of bf16/fp8 values (exponents cluster in a ~6-value window; signs and mantissas follow measured histograms), and repairs implausible words. A tiny CRC per 4 KB only confirms the fix.

title: Eliminate the package: decap scrap modules, rebond known-good DRAM die
idea: Eliminate the package as a one-way trip: laser plus fuming-acid decapsulation strips mold compound from scrapped DRAM packages, freed dies are re-probed on wafer-sort-style chucks, re-bumped, and re-assembled into new multi-die packages or chiplet substrates.

title: Read by emptying with a spoon: charge-metering multilevel readout
idea: Reverse sensing from measuring a level to counting scoops: a ~100 fF 180 nm cell stores one of 16 charge levels; readout clocks the charge through a CCD-style metering gate that skims fixed ~6 fC packets onto the bitline while a counter tallies packets until empty, a 4-bit value without an analog ADC.
note: Charge-packet counting avoids ADC; metering accuracy and 16-clock latency on 180 nm.

title: Let the electrode become the dielectric: anodized metal-sponge capacitors
idea: Reverse deposition: oblique-sputter a porous aluminum or niobium sponge into each 180 nm cell, then anodize it so the metal converts itself into conformal Al2O3 or Nb2O5 (k ~41) that self-limits at ~2 nm per volt even inside hidden pores; fill with CVD TiN as the counter electrode, like an electrolytic capacitor.
note: Anodic oxide leakage far above DRAM fA budget.

title: Polarization-built well: GaN 2DEG pocket holds charge for hours
idea: Reverse doping-defined wells for polarization-defined ones: in AlGaN/GaN the built-in polarization makes an electron well with no dopants; a gated, isolated 2DEG pocket stores electrons behind a 3.4 eV-gap barrier and an adjacent HEMT channel senses it, using 0.25-0.5 um GaN RF fab tools.
note: Trap-driven drift; GaN density is poor.

title: Self-referenced double sampling cancels sense-amp offset and bitline mismatch
idea: Reverse where the reference comes from: sample the bitline after charge sharing onto capacitor A, write a known '1' through the same cell and sample again onto B, then compare A against B in the same comparator so its offset and the bitline mismatch cancel; restore the true value afterwards (MRAM self-reference transplanted to DRAM).
note: MRAM destructive self-reference ported to DRAM; extra write and latency per read.

title: Delete the spare rows and fuses; the code is the repair
idea: Reverse post-fab repair: remove redundant rows/columns, laser/e-fuse banks and repair test flow from the die, and rely on page ECC sized for 1% BER to absorb defective cells.

title: Client-held KV cookies make chat servers stateless between turns
idea: Reverse who stores the conversation: after each turn the server compresses the session KV into a learned latent (~100-500 KB), encrypts and authenticates it, and returns it to the client like an HTTP cookie; the next request uploads it and the server expands it again.
note: 100x learned KV compression doubtful; token-ID parking or SSD offload cheaper.

title: Pulse-position signalling: four bits per single edge
idea: Reverse amplitude-based encoding: each lane sends exactly one edge per symbol window, and that edge's position among 16 time slots carries 4 bits, read by a shared time-to-digital converter, so the wire toggles once per 4 bits instead of about twice.
note: TDC slot resolution at multi-Gb/s is the limit.

title: Coaxial microbumps: two signals per bump, self-shielded
idea: Rearrange the bump: plate a core pillar, coat it with conformal ALD or parylene dielectric, then plate a ring shell, giving a coaxial bump whose core carries one signal and whose shell carries ground or a second signal.

title: Skewed cross-bank row mapping scatters hammer victims across codewords
idea: Rearrange the address map so a logical row is built from physical rows at different indices in each of 8 banks (index = L XOR bank-hash); a hammered logical row disturbs a different logical victim in each bank, so any victim word gets errors in at most one 1/8 slice, which a per-slice symbol code corrects.
note: Attacker aware of hash can aim multiple aggressors at one victim word; needs secret keying.

title: Scheduled reverse-polarity detox pulses push oxygen vacancies back
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action + #9 Prior anti-action: during idle windows the controller swaps plate bias so every capacitor in a mat sees a brief inverted field (~-1.2 V, ~1 us), driving field-drifted oxygen vacancies and trapped charge back toward their as-built distribution before they form leakage percolation paths.
note: Retention tail is mostly junction/GIDL, not dielectric vacancies; recovery pulses need data moves.

title: Oscillation: bitline voltage tunes ring oscillators, counters compare frequency
idea: TRIZ #18 Mechanical vibration: after charge sharing, each sense node starves the supply of a tiny ring oscillator; a counter shared by 16 bitlines tallies cycles over 2-5 ns against a reference oscillator, turning a sub-10 mV difference into a digital count with built-in noise averaging, followed by a digital write-back.
note: Averaging over time cancels noise, not static Vt mismatch.

title: Cold-trap recovery of unreacted ALD metal precursors
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: put fore-line cryotraps and a valve synchronized to the precursor pulses on ALD chambers. The ~90-95% of metal-organic precursor (TEMAZr, TEMAHf, TDMAT, Ru/Co organometallics) that normally burns in abatement is condensed into returnable canisters for the supplier to redistill.

title: Acid-leached rice-husk silica as high-purity crucible feedstock
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap short-living objects: the crucible is single-use anyway, so source its silica from a cheap renewable stream. Leach rice husks with HCl/oxalic acid to strip K, Ca and Fe, burn them under controlled oxidation to amorphous SiO2, chlorine-purify the ash at ~1000 C, and arc-fuse it into crucible inner layers.
note: Reaching 5N, especially low Al and alkali, from husk ash is the doubt.

title: Defect-absorbing soft-remap arrays that tolerate cheaper patterning
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: make the address map flexible instead of the process perfect - each 1 Mb mat carries ~3% spare rows/columns and an on-die CAM that remaps failing 64-cell groups at test and in the field, so the fab can run older ArF immersion scanners with ~1.5x worse overlay and accept cell-defect rates near 1e-4.
note: Overlay error is systematic, not random, so remap can't absorb 1.5x worse overlay.

title: Millisecond flash anneal crystallizes high-k after periphery is built
idea: TRIZ #21 Rushing through: a 1-3 ms xenon flash or laser anneal heats only the surface ZrO2/TiO2 dielectric above 900 C, forming high-k tetragonal/rutile phases (k ~45-80) while underlying periphery and metals stay below ~500 C.

title: Hydraulics: liquid-metal micro-well sockets for reworkable memory chiplets
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics and hydraulics: replace solder microbumps with micro-wells filled with Ga-In liquid metal at ~40 um pitch on the substrate. Memory chiplets press in and are tested in place, and a failed one can be pulled out and replaced. (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)

title: Lung-surfactant monolayer prevents high-AR pillar collapse during drying
idea: Lung surfactant lowers its surface tension as an alveolus shrinks, so small alveoli do not collapse. Before the final rinse-dry, coat storage-node pillars with a fluorinated phospholipid-like monolayer whose surface tension falls on compression. The capillary forces that pull AR >100 pillars together (stiction) then self-cancel as the gap narrows.
note: Bio-inspired twist on SAM and low-tension drying; gain limited to a modest AR increase.

title: Lowdin tautomer bit: proton-transfer hydrogen-bond ferroelectric layer
idea: DNA base pairs can flip protons across their hydrogen bonds (Lowdin tautomers). Use a proton-transfer organic ferroelectric, such as croconic acid or a designed base-pair-analog crystal, whose polarization flips when protons hop ~0.6 A along the H-bonds with no heavy-ion motion. It serves as a ferroelectric capacitor or FeFET gate layer.
note: Croconic acid films: thermal and moisture stability at BEOL is a doubt.

title: Bird-lung one-way flow: every restore goes to a fresh row
idea: Birds ventilate unidirectionally instead of tidally; likewise, after a destructive read the sense amps write the page into a different spare row in the same subarray (tracked by a small per-subarray remap table), so data flows through rows rather than being restored in place and the vacated row becomes the next spare.
note: Related to randomized row swap mitigations; extra row operation per activation costs energy and latency.

title: Clotting-capsule self-healing printed interconnect raises foil-memory yield
idea: Blood clots seal wounds automatically. Embed 5 um microcapsules of copper-formate ink in the printed dielectric over the lines; a crack ruptures them and the released ink, reduced to copper by local Joule heating from a test current, bridges the open line.

title: Silk fibroin water-developed resist for non-critical DRAM layers
idea: Silkworms spin fibroin from water and fix it by beta-sheet crystallization. Coat aqueous silk fibroin as a resist that UV or e-beam exposure crosslinks or breaks, developed in pure water, for implant masks and thick non-critical layers.
note: Metal-ion contamination of protein resists in FEOL.

title: Phototropic resistless patterning: exposed surface sites switch on growth
idea: Shoots grow toward light; coat the wafer with a monolayer of photolabile-capped amines (nitroveratryl-type groups) that 193/248 nm light uncaps, and only uncapped sites nucleate ALD of the hardmask or metal. The pattern is grown directly, with no resist coat, bake, develop, strip or descum.

title: Elephant-ear vein chucks end helium backside cooling in fab tools
idea: Elephants shed heat through dense vein networks in thin ears; build electrostatic chucks with an embedded two-phase microchannel 'vein' network under a 0.5 mm ceramic face and a compliant nanostructured graphite contact layer, replacing helium backside gas in etch and deposition chambers.
note: Solid contact conductance in vacuum without gas is the doubt.

title: Cochlear ramp etch exposes every tier's contact in one step
idea: The cochlea maps frequency to position along a tapered duct; print a grayscale, thickness-tapered hardmask wedge once and ion-mill it together with the stack so the slope transfers into the tiers, opening each tier's wordline as a stripe at its own lateral position. One exposure and one etch replace the 30-100 resist-trim cycles of a staircase.

title: Integrate-and-fire checkpoints store only threshold-crossing activations
idea: Saved activations for backprop are recorded like spikes: each neuron accumulates its value against a membrane threshold and only crossings are written as (index, quantized value) events; dense tensors are never materialized and are reconstructed from events plus a leak model during the backward pass.

title: Alternative splicing assembles many fine-tuned models from shared exons
idea: A library of weight blocks (exons) is stored once; each task variant is a splice map selecting and ordering blocks plus tiny per-variant tweaks, the way one gene yields many proteins, so serving 100 fine-tunes needs one exon library rather than 100 copies.

title: DNA-hybridization fluidic self-assembly of memory chiplets
idea: Chiplet bond pads and interposer landing sites carry different complementary DNA strands, so chiplets tumbled in a fluid bath bind only to their matching sites; a reflow then melts the solder and burns off the DNA. Thousands of known-good dies assemble in parallel instead of by serial pick-and-place.
note: DNA residue and fine-pitch alignment accuracy are doubts; FSA is prior art.

title: Spike-timing code: one edge carries several bits by position
idea: Instead of NRZ or PAM4 levels, each symbol window carries a single transition placed in one of 8-16 time slots (pulse-position coding, like neurons encoding information in spike timing), so each transition carries 3-4 bits. Transition count, the main CV^2 cost of a wire, falls.
note: Timing jitter caps slot count at high rates.

title: Coral accretion: mask-free additively grown ceramic memory interposer
idea: Corals build a skeleton by accreting mineral layer by layer. A ceramic interposer is grown the same way, alternating aerosol-jet-printed alumina-glass dielectric with nano-silver traces densified by cold sintering below 200 C, so each package's routing prints straight from CAD with no masks and no wafer fab.

title: Sunflower phyllotaxis layout: golden-angle memory placement on glass panels
idea: On a large glass-panel substrate, memory chiplets are placed around the accelerator at golden-angle (137.5 degree) spiral positions like sunflower seeds. That gives the densest uniform packing at growing radius, spreads heat evenly, and makes wire length to the nth chiplet grow only as sqrt(n).
note: sqrt(n) wire length holds for any 2D packing; golden angle adds little.

title: League-table standings: rank-modulated bits immune to uniform charge loss
idea: A league table cares who is ahead, not absolute points: group six cells and encode data in the permutation order of their charges (rank modulation), written by charging each cell just above the previous one and read by a winner-take-all comparator tree; uniform leakage shrinks all charges together without changing the order.
note: Rank modulation known for flash; comparator-tree sensing of tiny charges is costly.

title: Electrolytic capacitor trick: anodized porous niobium with self-healing oxide
idea: Electrolytic capacitors win with porous foil plus an anodic oxide that regrows over any defect; sputter Nb through a self-ordered porous-alumina template to form nanorod electrodes, grow the Nb2O5 dielectric (k~40) by room-temperature anodization (~2.5 nm/V, self-limiting), and periodically 're-form' arrays with a slight over-bias that heals leakage sites.
note: Anodic Nb2O5 leaks more than ALD ZrO2; AAO-templated nanorods are not denser than pillars.

title: Solar-cell black silicon: litho-free nanograss electrodes multiply capacitor area
idea: Solar cells use maskless cryogenic SF6/O2 RIE to grow self-masked 'black silicon' needles 1-2 um tall at ~100-nm spacing; apply the same etch to texture each capacitor's bottom electrode for a 10-20x area gain, then line it conformally by ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN so each cell pad needs only coarse contact lithography.

title: Pyrolytic self-cleaning oven: wordline heaters anneal VRT traps in the field
idea: Self-cleaning ovens periodically run very hot to burn off residue. In a maintenance window, migrate a bank's data, then drive current through its buried metal wordlines as resistive heaters to hold the array near 250 C for seconds, re-annealing VRT and hydrogen-related traps (as shown for NAND self-healing) before the data returns; no chemistry at all.

title: Tantalum-capacitor anodic forming grows high-k dielectric in a beaker
idea: Borrowed from tantalum and niobium electrolytic capacitors, which 'form' their dielectric by anodizing porous metal at a set voltage, giving perfectly conformal oxide at ~1.5-2 nm/V: line storage holes with Nb or Ti, anodize at 2-4 V in a wafer-scale electrolyte cell a 10-person team can build, self-limiting Nb2O5/TiO2 (k 40-80) to exact thickness, then fill the top electrode.

title: PCB electroless plating replaces tungsten CVD contact plugs
idea: Borrowed from PCB through-hole metallization, which plates millions of holes with no vacuum: seed DRAM bitline-contact and landing-plug holes with a Pd-activated monolayer, then electroless-plate cobalt or nickel-boron bottom-up on a wet bench, replacing WF6 CVD tungsten.

title: Motion-compensated memory pages: shifted reference plus residual
idea: Borrowing H.264 P-frame motion compensation: a CXL memory controller finds, for each cold 4 KB page, a reference page and a byte-offset 'motion vector' (pages that match after a shift, e.g. realigned structs or shifted buffers) and stores only the vector plus an entropy-coded residual; reads reconstruct in a short pipeline from a hot reference-page cache.

title: Sleep consolidation: idle gaps distil sessions into persistent memory tokens
idea: Like the hippocampus replaying the day into cortex during sleep, while a chat or agent session is idle the server compresses its KV cache into ~64 learned memory tokens written to persistent flash and frees the DRAM; the session resumes by loading those tokens.
note: Lossless flash offload already frees idle KV; summary loses fidelity.

title: Vehicle-to-grid sessions: clients store their own encrypted state
idea: Like EVs lending their batteries to the grid, user devices persist their own compressed, encrypted, MAC-tagged session state (quantized gist/KV tokens, app session) in local flash and upload it with the next request, so servers hold no DRAM for idle users.

title: Gecko-foot probes test hybrid-bond pads without damage
idea: Gecko feet grip with millions of soft setae. A contactor of metal-coated polymer micro-pillars, molded at room temperature, touches fragile hybrid-bonding pads gently for at-speed known-good-die test. It then lets go, leaving no scratch or particle.

title: Safety-stock ECC: spare parity chips loaned as capacity while healthy
idea: Inventory systems size safety stock to demand variance. On 10-chip DDR5 ECC DIMMs, the FPGA/CXL controller packs data into the two ECC chips for regions with a measured-low error rate, protecting them with a small CRC carved from the data. When telemetry shows errors rising, the region converts back to full ECC and the OS gives the capacity back.

title: Pilot-tone automatic gain control lowers array voltage
idea: Like the AGC in 1930s tube radios: each activation also reads two pilot cells (a known 1 and a known 0) on dedicated bitlines, and their sensed amplitude sets the main sense amps' latch-enable delay and reference trim in real time. Margin tracks temperature and aging directly, so VARY can drop from ~1.0 V toward 0.7 V without worst-case guardbands.

title: Tape-style run-length coding lets bitlines pack tighter
idea: Magnetic tape used run-length-limited codes to avoid worst-case flux patterns. Add a 64b/68b write encoder that forbids the worst bitline coupling patterns, such as a lone 1 between 0s on adjacent bitlines of one row, so sense amps never see the worst aggressor sums. No mask is added at all.

title: Core-plane diagonal sense wire becomes a noise-reference bitline
idea: Core-memory sense wires ran diagonally so half-select noise from every drive line canceled. Route one dummy bitline per mat diagonally across all bitlines in existing metal, with at most one via-mask change. It picks up the same wordline kick and coupling noise as the real bitlines and serves as a live reference subtracted at each sense-amp group.
note: Diagonal dummy bitline as noise reference; diagonal routing in a dense array is awkward.

title: Holographic Hadamard spreading of words across 64 tiers
idea: Revive holographic memory's trick of spreading each bit over the whole hologram: apply a Walsh-Hadamard transform across 64 tiers before writing, so 1% scattered cell errors, or one whole failed tier, become sparse errors recovered by sparse-error (compressed-sensing) decoding after the inverse transform.

title: Seven-track tape parity rebuilt as a physical 3D product code
idea: Revive 1950s tape drives' lateral-plus-longitudinal parity: one parity tier per 16 tiers plus parity pillars per row put every bit in row, column and tier codewords, decoded iteratively to correct 1% scattered cell errors along all three axes.

title: Electroless bottom-up fill for wordlines and contacts, no sputtering
idea: Revive Brenner and Riddell's 1946 electroless plating: grow buried wordlines and bitline contacts bottom-up from a Pd-colloid-seeded floor with autocatalytic Co-B or Ni-B and a self-assembled monolayer diffusion barrier, so neither an Ar-sputtered TiN liner nor tungsten CVD is needed. The bath fills high-AR trenches without voids.

title: Nano hemispherical-grain roughening boosts capacitor area without litho
idea: Revive the 1990s hemispherical-grain (HSG) polysilicon trick that roughly doubled 64 Mb capacitor area by seeding amorphous silicon until it beaded into grains: apply it to the walls of 3D-DRAM lateral capacitors, where there is more room, using LPCVD SiH4 seeding in H2/N2 to form 3-5 nm grains, then convert them to TiN or silicide electrodes.

title: Brody-style stencil metallization replaces litho for DRAM top metals
idea: Revive T. Peter Brody's 1973 first active-matrix display, built without photolithography by evaporating each layer through aligned metal shadow masks: deposit DRAM's coarse upper metals, pads and redistribution (>=1-3 um) by thermal or e-beam evaporation through reusable silicon-nitride stencils. Each stencil serves thousands of wafers, with no resist, develop, etch or argon sputter.

title: Bell Labs beam-lead revival: cantilevered gold beams tile dies interposer-free
idea: Revive Lepselter's 1960s beam-lead process: gold beams plated on the die are released by a KOH/TMAH back-etch through a laser-ablated hard mask (no HF, no fluorine plasma) to cantilever 50-100 um past the edge, then thermocompression-bonded to neighboring memory and logic dies.

title: Pioneer-probe convolutional coding lets HBM run hot on dry coolers
idea: Pioneer 9 (1968) used convolutional codes with sequential decoding to pull data out of very noisy channels. HBM pages are encoded along each burst with a rate-15/16 tail-biting convolutional code decoded by a pipelined Viterbi in the logic base die, tolerating raw BER ~1e-3 at 6% overhead, enough to run the stack at ~115 C at the standard refresh rate.

title: One sense amp resolves four bitlines in sequence
idea: Inverting 'one sense amp per bitline pair': four bitline pairs charge-share simultaneously, are isolated, and hold their analog signals while a single sense amp resolves and restores them one after another in ~2 ns slots.
note: Held bitline signals resolved sequentially by one SA; coupling during hold is the risk.

title: Constant-weight coding with winner-take-half rank sensing
idea: Inverting 'a reference must come from a dummy cell or twin bitline': rows store data in a constant-weight code (exactly 8 ones per 16-cell group), and a winner-take-half circuit declares the 8 highest bitlines of each group to be ones, so no reference voltage exists at all.
note: Constant-weight codes with rank sensing remove references; WTA circuit area and 15% overhead.

title: In/Ga-free ZnMgO:Al BEOL access transistors for stacked arrays
idea: Inverts 'oxide-TFT DRAM needs indium and gallium.' Use Mg-alloyed ZnO (band gap up to ~4 eV, Al-doped contacts) as the BEOL access channel and stack capacitor-cell tiers above the logic at <400 C.
note: Polycrystalline ZnO grain boundaries likely worsen the tail versus amorphous IGZO.

title: Dirty bulk, clean skin: metallurgical silicon substrate under thick epi
idea: Inverts 'the whole wafer must be 11N electronic grade': use upgraded-metallurgical-grade (5-6N) seed-cast mono silicon as the substrate, add a buried phosphorus/aluminum gettering layer and a carbon-doped epitaxial diffusion barrier, then grow a 10 um high-purity epitaxial skin from silane where all devices live.

title: Fab that breathes with the grid: buffer WIP to follow cheap power
idea: Inverts 'a fab runs flat out 24/7': size work-in-progress buffers in front of the most energy-hungry steps (epitaxy, furnaces, CVD, abatement burners, chillers) so they run hard during curtailed solar/wind hours and idle at peaks, add chilled-water thermal storage, and schedule with a cycle-time vs $/MWh co-optimizer.

title: Back-end oxide CMOS latches: static memory stacked over logic
idea: Inverts 'static memory must live in the silicon substrate': build cross-coupled latches from n-type amorphous ZnO and p-type SnO/Cu2O thin-film transistors in the metal stack at <350 C, several tiers high, with wide-gap leakage below 1e-18 A per device.
note: p-type SnO/Cu2O are leaky; the 1e-18 A standby claim holds only for n-type oxides.

title: Sixteen-fold spacer multiplication on a 1990s KrF stepper
idea: Inverts 'resolution belongs to the scanner'. Print 360 nm-pitch lines on a KrF stepper and run four rounds of sidewall-spacer transfer (LPCVD nitride/oxide spacers plus RIE), each halving pitch, to reach ~22 nm-pitch array lines with no overlay-critical steps.

title: Dewetted metal nano-islands roughen electrodes into area
idea: Inverts 'the capacitor needs an ordered geometry'. Anneal a 5 nm sacrificial Sn film so it dewets into ~15-25 nm random islands, use them as an RIE mask to texture the poly-Si storage node into nanopillars (the 1990s hemispherical-grain trick taken ~10x further), strip, then coat with dielectric.

title: Time-coded analog tensor links instead of binary symbols
idea: Invert 'link symbols are digital bits': for weights and activations each wire carries a pulse whose width/edge timing encodes a 6-8-bit value, generated by a delay line and decoded by a time-to-digital converter, accepting ~1 LSB noise that AI numerics tolerate.
note: 6-8-bit timing resolution at speed is jitter-limited.

title: Anodized-aluminum substrates with copper-filled pores replace ABF film
idea: Invert 'package dielectric must be polymer build-up film': anodize thick U.S. aluminum sheet into porous alumina whose self-ordered vertical pores are electroplated with copper to form dense vias, then pattern RDL on top.
note: AAO interposers researched; thick AAO brittleness is the doubt.

title: Interference-lithography buses: the memory bus is a grating
idea: Invert 'interconnect needs mask-based photolithography': memory buses are thousands of identical parallel lines, so pattern them with maskless two-beam laser interference lithography (U.S.-buildable tool), then cut and connect line ends with coarse lithography.

title: Laser decap and rebump LPDDR die mined from e-waste phones
idea: Inverts 'e-waste recycling means shredding for gold': robotic lines laser-decapsulate package-on-package stacks from recycled phones, extract the LPDDR die, re-bump and retest them, and package them for IoT, automotive and edge boards.

title: Balanced-code words generate their own mid-level sense reference
idea: Encode each 64-bit word as a 68-bit constant-weight code (exactly 34 ones), so the average of the word's own bitlines is exactly halfway between its decayed '1' and '0' levels. A charge-sharing copy of the word's bitlines becomes the SA reference, tracking leakage at 125 C automatically.
note: Average reference does not rescue tail cells that decay fastest.

title: Inductor ping-pong moves charge from closing to opening wordline
idea: Connect the wordline being closed to the next wordline being opened through a shared on-die or interposer inductor for one LC half-cycle, so the 3 V charge transfers almost entirely instead of being dumped to ground, then top off the remainder from the pump.

title: EHD jet-printed pillar capacitors grown upward, never etched
idea: Use multi-nozzle electrohydrodynamic jet printing to stack silver nanoparticle droplets into 0.5 um-wide, 5 um-tall pillars on each cell's storage pad, then coat them with spatial-ALD AlOx and a conformal printed counter-electrode.
note: Additive printed pillars give large Cs but only at micron pitch; foil-scale niche.

title: Sol-gel gallium oxide printed channels give day-scale retention
idea: Inkjet or slot-die print Ga2O3 sol-gel channels (Eg ~4.8 eV), densify them by deep-UV photo-annealing below 250 C, and use them as access transistors in foil arrays with 4k-cell bitlines, since refresh traffic disappears.
note: Printed Ga2O3 gives long retention but very low density; foil niche.

title: Inverse-opal printed electrodes multiply capacitor area twentyfold
idea: Convectively assemble 200 nm polystyrene spheres into embossed cell wells, infill electroless nickel, burn out the spheres, then coat spatial-ALD AlOx and infill a conductive-polymer counter-electrode, forming a sponge capacitor per cell.

title: Nickel-aluminide intermetallic buried wordlines replace tungsten below 15 nanometers
idea: At sub-15 nm widths line resistivity scales with rho0*lambda (bulk resistivity x electron mean free path), not rho0, and ordered B2 NiAl has a few-nm mean free path so its size penalty is small. Fill buried-wordline trenches with Ni/Al ALD nanolaminates and anneal to NiAl, which self-passivates with Al2O3 and needs no TiN barrier.

title: Gallium-free zinc-tin-silicon oxide channels for low-leak gain cells
idea: Oxide gain cells leak little because Eg>3 eV makes intrinsic carriers ~1e-25 cm-3 and holes immobile; mobility comes from overlapping metal ns orbitals, which Sn4+ 5s supplies as well as In3+, while Si (strong Si-O bond) takes Ga's carrier-suppressing role. Deposit amorphous Zn-Sn-Si-O by ALD as read and write channels.

title: One ALD chemistry family builds every layer of the cell
idea: First principle: tool count scales with the number of distinct materials in the flow. Make the channel (IGZO), electrodes (degenerate In2O3:H/ITO), dielectric (Ga2O3/HfO2 laminate) and passivation from one In/Ga/Zn/Hf precursor set in one multi-station ALD cluster, changing only cycle ratios and oxidant.

title: Thermoplastic, solvent-release packages make DRAM dies recoverable
idea: First principle: epoxy molding compound is a thermoset that cannot be undone, so it traps the die forever. Package DRAM in a high-Tg thermoplastic (e.g., liquid-crystal polymer) with a solvent-releasable underfill, so a low-temperature solvent bath frees bare, intact dies for retest and redeployment.

title: Seashell nacre: titania nanosheets self-stack into a k~125 dielectric
idea: Stimulus 'nacre' (layered bricks of mineral) -> exfoliate Ti0.87O2 nanosheets in water with tetrabutylammonium hydroxide and deposit them layer by layer by Langmuir-Blodgett at room temperature, giving a ~5 nm dielectric with k~125 and low leakage; no plasma, no fluorinated surfactants.

title: Seashell roar: chopped, dithered comparator voting senses sub-offset signals
idea: A seashell turns random noise into a perceptible 'ocean': use stochastic resonance. After charge sharing, sample the bitline onto a small isolated cap, then fire a minimum-size comparator 8 times against a reference dithered by an on-die junction-noise source, swapping inputs on alternate firings (chopping) to cancel offset, and majority-vote in a 3-bit counter before restore.
note: Chopping plus majority voting resolves sub-offset signals; latency and sampling-cap charge loss.

title: Spider web: MOF cartridges catch and recycle fluorocarbon etch gases
idea: Stimulus 'spider web' (a net tuned to its prey) -> put metal-organic-framework adsorbent beds, pore-tuned to C4F8, C4F6, NF3 and SF6, on etch exhausts instead of burn-box abatement; temperature-swing regenerate, purify and return captured gas to cylinders.

title: Pearl: one seeded ferroelectric grain per cell kills variability
idea: Random stimulus 'pearl' (one crystal grows around one seed) -> a self-aligned nucleation seed (a ZrO2 or TiN facet) is planted at the bottom of each ferroelectric capacitor, so the HZO crystallizes as a single orthorhombic grain per cell instead of random multigrain.

title: Tetris: memory-controller line compaction collapses fragmented heaps
idea: Like Tetris rows clearing once full, a controller-side engine migrates live 64 B lines out of sparsely occupied pages into dense pages during idle cycles, tracked by an SRAM-cached line-remap table so software pointers never change; fully emptied pages are handed back to the OS.

title: Zipper merge: approximate cross-request KV block deduplication
idea: Two lanes zip into one: hash every 16-token KV block with locality-sensitive hashing; when a new block lies within epsilon of a canonical block from any request (same RAG passage at a different offset, near-identical prompts), store a pointer plus a sparse int4 residual, applying a RoPE offset correction at read.

title: Fridge magnet: magnetic self-alignment for low-cost chiplet assembly
idea: Like a fridge magnet snapping into place: dies get patterned Ni/Co pads and are dropped onto a substrate over a patterned magnet fixture that pulls each die to sub-micron alignment, then bonded in a batch oven, with no $5M placement tool.

title: Gold assay: karat-graded salvage DRAM with per-row refresh maps
idea: Random stimulus 'gold assay' -> grade by purity, price by karat. Decommissioned server DIMMs are assayed with a per-row retention histogram, graded (e.g. 18k/14k/10k), and the grade's row map is loaded into a CXL expander that refreshes weak rows often and strong rows rarely.
note: RAIDR-style per-row refresh on salvage; VRT makes profiles drift.

title: Parametric varactor amplification boosts bitline voltage after charge sharing
idea: Box: stacked cap x Si access x parametric amplification x MOS-varactor bitline segments x bulk Si x standard. After the cell shares charge onto the bitline, a pump pulse drives MOS varactors on the bitline pair into depletion, shrinking capacitance so V = Q/C and the differential rise 3-5x before the latch fires: low-noise gain from capacitance modulation.
note: MOS varactor capacitance pumping raises signal, but added varactor capacitance erodes net gain.

title: Multi-row OR-sensing reads sparse zero blocks in one activation
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x threshold-OR sensing x 8-wordline simultaneous activation x bulk Si x standard. For sparse activations and pruned weights, eight rows open at once and the SA only asks whether any charge is present (group testing); all-zero groups are confirmed with one sense instead of eight, and the extra multi-row disturb (<1%) is tolerated.
note: OR-sensing of 8 rows to confirm zero blocks; true/anti-cell encoding and disturb complicate it.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching carves single-crystal VCT pillar forests
idea: [Box: MIM charge | single-crystal Si VCT | charge-share SA | monolithic | Si | DSA-patterned Pt/Au catalyst mesh + HF/H2O2 MacEtch] A perforated noble-metal mesh sinks into Si in HF/H2O2 and leaves straight, plasma-damage-free 20 nm pillars at AR >50, which become the vertical channels.

title: Germanium-free 3D DRAM using porosified p+ silicon sacrificial tiers
idea: Box [lateral cap | lateral Si access per tier | voltage SA | 3D stacked tiers | CZ Si | all-Si epi + electrochemical porosification]: grow alternating p++ (B 1e20) and lightly doped Si epi tiers instead of Si/SiGe, then after slit etch anodize only the p++ layers into porous Si and remove them laterally, leaving suspended single-crystal channels.
note: Boron diffusion from 1e20 tiers and lateral anodization contact through slits are the doubts.

title: ALD alumina nano-topcoat replaces fluorinated immersion-litho topcoats
idea: Box [any | any | any | any | Si | ArF immersion]: after resist coat, grow 2-3 nm of 60 C ALD Al2O3 from TMA/H2O as the leach barrier, cap it with a fluorine-free hydrocarbon monolayer for water receding angle, and let the TMAH developer dissolve it.

title: Beaker-grown anodic Nb/Ta/Hf oxide as the capacitor dielectric
idea: Box: barrier-type anodic oxide charge x EBL-patterned IGZO access x standard sensing x 2D test array x Si x room-temperature electrochemical anodization of a sputtered valve metal. The bottom electrode's surface is anodized at ~1.5-2 nm/V into a dense dielectric (Nb2O5 k~40, Ta2O5 k~25) whose thickness is set by a voltage and whose pinholes self-heal during growth.

title: Spin-coated, UV-cured indium-zinc oxide access transistors in BEOL
idea: Box: MIM charge x solution-processed InZnO TFT x voltage sense amp x BEOL x Si or glass x sol-gel spin coating plus deep-UV photo-annealing below 250 C. A nitrate precursor coats the topography and 185/254 nm UV generates ozone and radicals that condense the oxide network, reaching 5-20 cm2/Vs with no vacuum deposition.

title: Glancing-angle-deposited nanohelix electrodes multiply capacitor area, maskless
idea: Box: MIM charge on a 3D nanocolumn electrode x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x glancing-angle e-beam evaporation at ~85 degrees with substrate rotation. Self-shadowing grows isolated TiN or Ru columns or helices of set height on EBL-seeded storage pads, then ALD dielectric and top electrode coat them for 5-20x area with no high-AR etch.

title: Direct nanoimprint of sol-gel high-k: pattern the dielectric itself
idea: Box: imprinted metal-oxide charge x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x thermal imprint of a ZrO2/HfO2 sol-gel with a PDMS replica of an EBL master. The functional film acts as the resist: imprinting forms corrugated 3D capacitor shapes and a cure converts it to oxide, deleting the resist-etch-strip sequence.

title: Bosch scallop-engineered corrugated capacitor walls double area
idea: Box: Si trench charge x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x time-multiplexed DRIE with deliberately deep, tuned scallops. Etch/passivation cycle times are set to cut 30-50 nm periodic corrugations, then conformal ALD TiN/high-k/TiN coats them, giving a fixed-depth trench ~1.5-2.5x sidewall area from a recipe timing parameter.
note: Works for large-pitch Si trench caps; 30-50 nm scallops can't fit sub-50 nm holes.

title: Pulse-position DRAM I/O encodes three bits per edge
idea: Box: DRAM x standard x time-to-digital receiver x pulse-position-modulated TSV and interposer lanes x Si x standard. Each lane sends one edge per unit interval whose position among eight timing slots encodes 3 bits, so wires toggle 3x less often for the same data.

title: Laser-forward-transferred copper redistribution on glass, no plating bath
idea: Box: LPDDR dies x standard x standard x fan-out RDL x glass panel x laser-induced forward transfer (LIFT) of Cu nanoparticle ink plus laser sintering. 8-15 um RDL lines are written digitally from a donor ribbon and sintered in place, replacing resist coat/develop, seed sputter, electroplating, strip and etch and the rinse after each.

title: Copper wires ultrasonically embedded in thermoplastic form the interposer
idea: Box: LPDDR or HBM-lite x standard x standard x wire-scribed routing x hot-embossed thermoplastic carrier x ultrasonic embedding of 15 um insulated Cu wire. A CNC head lays and embeds insulated wires into the polymer like a multiwire board, with laser-ablated ends forming pads: no etch, no plating, no rinse.

title: Po: memory made of molasses — thermally selected glassy-electrolyte crossbar
idea: Po: memory made of molasses. Extracted: print a crossbar of polymer electrolyte that is glassy (ions frozen) at operating temperature but softens above Tg; a coincident current pulse heats only the selected crossing above Tg so ions drift to set its conductance, then it re-freezes, making heat the selector.
note: Heat as selector; us thermal writes and low endurance keep it out of DRAM class.

title: Lazy refresh with LDPC resurrection across row groups
idea: Po: let bits die, then resurrect them. Refresh 8x less often and protect each group of 8 rows with a soft-decision LDPC code whose parity sits in a spare row; sense amps report a soft confidence level, and the decoder rewrites corrected data on read, treating decay as a noisy channel.

title: Po: memory trims its own readers via dummy cells
idea: Po: memory that calibrates the circuits that read it. At power-up each SA's offset is measured by repeatedly sensing balanced bitlines, and a correction charge is written into a dedicated dummy cell on that bitline pair; before every sense the dummy wordline fires and pre-biases the bitline by exactly that offset, refreshed alongside normal refresh.
note: Offset storage as dummy-cell charge; trim precision limited by dummy-cell Cs variation and leakage.

title: Let bits decay and recover them with cross-tier erasure codes
idea: Po: memory that is allowed to rot. Disable refresh and stripe each 64 B line across 12 tiers with an 8+4 Reed-Solomon erasure code plus weak-cell location maps from test, so the retention tail is corrected at read while the median cell holds data for minutes, longer than most working sets live.
note: Cross-tier erasure codes for retention errors; 50% parity offsets refresh savings.

title: Po the chuck is a hairbrush: gas-free nanofiber thermal contact
idea: Po: 'the wafer is cooled by a hairbrush, not a gas.' Extracted: replace helium backside gas in electrostatic chucks with a dense, vertically aligned boron-nitride-nanotube or carbon-nanotube forest capped with a thin alumina skin, whose millions of compliant tips conduct heat under electrostatic clamping as well as ~10 Torr of helium.

title: Po the crystal draws the pattern: facet-defined sub-litho fins
idea: Po: 'the crystal is the lithographer.' Extracted: on (110) silicon, TMAH wet etch stops on vertical {111} planes, so a coarse 40 nm DUV pattern yields atomically flat vertical walls; self-limiting oxidation then thins fins to 8-10 nm, giving access-transistor fins and buried-wordline trenches without EUV.
