idea: Time shift in thermal processing: deposit amorphous Si for each 3D-DRAM tier, then sweep a microsecond-pulse laser so melt fronts grow laterally from a seed opening, giving one grain per access transistor while the short melt keeps lower tiers below 450 C.
note: Grain-filter laser crystallization known; repeated tiers stress lower-tier thermal budget.

title: Thin-film gated thyristor cells stacked in tiers
idea: Shrink the regenerative gain of kiloamp power thyristors to a cell: build gated thin-film p-n-p-n thyristors vertically in each poly-Si tier at 180-nm rules, each acting as both storage element and amplifier. Cells need no capacitor and drive uA read currents into long shared bitlines.
note: T-RAM tried and failed; poly-Si thyristor standby current and variability are the doubts.

title: Rutile TiO2 high-k grown on niobium-doped tin-oxide template electrodes
idea: Jump to the atomic lattice: rutile SnO2 matches rutile TiO2 within ~3%. A conductive Nb- or Ta-doped SnO2 bottom electrode therefore templates ALD TiO2 into its rutile phase (k ~80-100) at low temperature without Ru/RuO2, and Al doping of the TiO2 suppresses leakage.
note: Same rutile-templated TiO2 as I-07553 with Nb-SnO2 electrode.

title: Nanosecond laser crystallization builds silicon tiers atop finished arrays
idea: Time-shift the thermal budget from furnace hours to nanoseconds: deposit amorphous Si on each finished tier and melt-recrystallize it with a ~30 ns excimer pulse seeded through small vias, so it becomes near-single-crystal while layers below stay under 400 C; repeat per tier for monolithic 3D DRAM.

title: Talbot self-imaging prints the cell lattice with U.S. lasers
idea: Displacement Talbot lithography: a 1:1 periodic phase mask from a U.S. mask shop and a U.S.-built 213/266 nm solid-state laser self-image the lattice across the whole wafer with near-unlimited depth of focus; no projection optics, so no imported scanner.

title: Micro-LED imaging-fiber links move HBM a meter from the accelerator
idea: Scale HBM's parallelism into optics: a 2D array of hundreds of micro-LEDs and photodiodes couples into a coherent imaging fiber bundle, each pixel a 2-4 Gb/s lane, so a stack can sit a meter away at HBM-class width with no lasers or SerDes.

title: Memristor without filaments: conducting ferroelectric domain walls in LiNbO3
idea: HPE's TiO2 memristor died from random oxygen-vacancy filaments that caused variability, sneak paths and ~1e6-1e9 endurance. Replace the filament with a charged, conducting domain wall in a thin-film LiNbO3 mesa: writing nucleates or erases the wall deterministically at a lithographic edge, and a sub-coercive read senses wall conduction between side electrodes without moving it.
note: Same LiNbO3 charged-wall NDRO cell.

title: Dense MRAM's heat-and-crosstalk wall broken by antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions
idea: Early dense-MRAM efforts lost thermal stability at small sizes and high temperature, and stray fields coupled neighbouring bits. Store the bit in the magnetic-octupole order of noncollinear antiferromagnetic Mn3Pt (TN ~475 K), read through an all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junction: exchange-enhanced anisotropy and zero net moment give Delta > 60 at 125 C in a 20 nm cell with no stray-field crosstalk.
note: Mn3Pt AFM tunnel junctions are an active research front; TMR still small.

title: BeSang monolithic 3D fixed with seeded rapid-melt-growth tiers
idea: BeSang and other monolithic-3D ventures failed because low-temperature upper tiers had poor polysilicon transistors. Open seed windows to the single-crystal tier below and deposit amorphous Si over the oxide. Melt it with nanosecond laser pulses so it regrows laterally as single crystal from each seed (rapid-melt growth), while lower tiers stay under 450C.
note: Seeded rapid-melt growth variant; lateral growth length from seeds is limited.

title: Canon ELTRAN porous splitting stops grinding away 96% of HBM wafers
idea: HBM core dies are ground from 775 um to ~30 um, wasting ~96% of each Cz wafer; Canon's ELTRAN (double porous-Si layer, water-jet split) died because SOI demand was small and Smart Cut won. Grow the DRAM device epi on sealed porous silicon, process and bond it into the stack, water-jet split, and re-polish the donor for 10-20 reuses.

title: Graphene lacked a bandgap; MoS2 capacitorless gain cells grown on glass
idea: Graphene logic programs stalled because a zero bandgap gives no off-state. Monolayer MoS2 (1.8 eV, 0.7 nm) shows off-currents below 1e-18 A/um: grow it by MOCVD at <=450 C directly on display glass and build 2T gain cells where the read transistor's gate is the storage node.
note: 2D-channel gain cells actively researched; low-temp MOCVD uniformity on glass is the doubt.

title: Cavendish Kinetics' stiction problem inverted into a refresh-free NEMS bit
idea: Cavendish Kinetics' MEMS memory fought stiction and pivoted away. Make stiction the storage: back-end nano-cantilevers latch by van der Waals force onto a contact (1) or rest open (0) and are released by a pull-off electrode, and the electromechanical hysteresis window rejects half-selected cells so a passive crossbar needs no transistor.
note: Essentially Nantero's original CNT vdW-latched crossbar concept.

title: 3D XPoint rebuilt vertically: one hole mask for 200 layers
idea: 3D XPoint died on cost: every deck needed its own critical patterning and tall double etch, so two decks never undercut DRAM enough. Use the 3D NAND recipe instead: stack 200 metal/oxide word planes, drill one hole array, line holes with a self-selecting chalcogenide film and fill with a metal bitline pillar, so every plane-pillar crossing is a cell made with the same single critical mask.
note: Vertical RRAM/PCM proposed widely; endurance makes it storage-class, not DRAM-class.

title: Mask ROM's per-design killer fixed: imprinted ROM for frozen AI weights
idea: Mask ROM died because every code change needed new masks and weeks of lead time. Frozen AI model weights are read every token but almost never rewritten, so store them in 16-deck 3D diode-ROM where every layer is a common template except one via layer per model, imprinted from a template e-beam-cut in a day, with 2 bits/cell coded by via size.
note: 3D diode ROM echoes Matrix Semiconductor OTP.

title: Racetrack shift errors fixed with disk-style servo markers and self-clocking codes
idea: IBM's racetrack memory stalled because domain walls pin or overshoot, so one bad shift offsets every following bit. Fix: borrow hard-disk servo practice by interleaving fixed marker domains and writing data in a run-length-limited self-clocking code, so the read head detects any over- or under-shift and re-shifts before decoding.
note: Position-error codes for racetrack already studied.

title: Cavendish NEMS memory's stiction killer turned into the latching mechanism
idea: Cavendish Kinetics' NEMS memory pivoted away because cantilevers stuck unpredictably (stiction). Fix: design for controlled stiction, using a self-assembled monolayer that sets adhesion energy inside a narrow window so a beam latched to the 'on' contact stays put unpowered, while a counter-electrode pulse plus the beam's spring force releases it reliably.

title: IBM Josephson memory density fixed with NbN kinetic-inductance persistent loops
idea: IBM's 1980s Josephson computer was cancelled largely because superconducting loop memory cells were microns wide and Pb-alloy junctions failed on thermal cycling. Fix: store bits as persistent supercurrent in ~100 nm NbN nanowire loops whose kinetic inductance replaces bulky geometric inductance, with cycling-robust Nb/AlOx junctions and moats that trap stray flux away from cells.
note: Kinetic-inductance nanowire memory cells already researched; niche cryogenic market.

title: Flash-as-DRAM endurance killer fixed by triple-barrier resonant-tunneling storage
idea: Attempts to use floating-gate flash as working memory died on tunnel-oxide wear (~1e5 cycles) and high write voltage. Fix: replace the oxide with an InAs/AlSb triple-barrier resonant-tunneling structure that is opaque at rest but passes electrons at a ~2.5 V resonance, so charge enters the floating gate without hot-carrier damage (UltraRAM-style).

title: Noncollinear antiferromagnet bits pack tight with zero stray field
idea: Effect walk: spin Hall switching + anomalous Hall effect in a Weyl antiferromagnet. 10-nm Mn3Sn islands store the bit as the chirality of their triangular spin order, switched by spin-orbit torque from an adjacent line and read by the sign of the large anomalous Hall voltage they emit despite near-zero net moment.

title: Layer-counted h-BN tunnel barrier dials retention like a knob
idea: Effect walk: direct quantum tunneling through atomically defined barriers. A 2D semi-floating-gate cell (graphene or MoS2 storage layer) sits behind exactly N layers of h-BN; because direct-tunneling current drops ~10x per added 0.33-nm layer, N=4-6 sets retention near 1 s while 10-ns writes use direct (not Fowler-Nordheim) tunneling at 2-3 V that creates no oxide traps.
note: Close to published hBN semi-floating-gate quasi-nonvolatile cells; write/hold ratio 1e8 via direct tunneling is the doubt.

title: Buried Ge quantum well holds holes behind a band-offset wall
idea: Effect walk: heterojunction band-offset confinement. A capacitorless cell stores holes in a 5-nm compressively strained Ge quantum well beneath a Si channel; the ~0.5 eV valence-band offset, not a leaky p-n junction, is the retention barrier, and stored holes shift channel threshold for a gain read.
note: SiGe/Ge quantum-well capacitorless DRAM studied since ~2010; retention gain modest.

title: Bulk photovoltaic read: polarization reports its sign as photocurrent
idea: Effect walk: bulk photovoltaic (shift-current) effect. Ferroelectric nano-capacitors (BaTiO3 or CuInP2S6) under a shared transparent electrode are flood-illuminated by a backside waveguide flash; each cell's photocurrent sign equals its polarization direction, integrated by a per-column gain stage without switching the domain.
note: Ferroelectric-photovoltaic NDRO already shown (2013); tiny shift currents.

title: Sliding ferroelectric bilayer flips by interlayer slip at 0.2 V
idea: Effect walk: sliding (stacking) ferroelectricity. In a parallel-stacked h-BN or 3R-MoS2 bilayer, the out-of-plane dipole reverses when one layer slides one bond length (AB to BA) under ~0.1-0.3 V, and a graphene-contacted tunnel junction reads the ~10x tunneling-resistance change non-destructively.

title: Van der Waals stiction latch: nanoflap stays stuck until kicked
idea: Effect walk: van der Waals/Casimir adhesion. A 50-nm graphene or SiC nanoflap is pulled into contact by a ~0.5 V electrostatic pulse and held at zero power by vdW adhesion; a second electrode releases it, and a 10-mV contact-resistance check reads the state.
note: Essentially the Nantero NRAM vdW-held contact mechanism.

title: Monolayer MoS2 channel tiers stacked at 20 nm pitch
idea: Quantum confinement: atomically thin MoS2 channels, MOCVD-grown at <450 C, have a ~2 eV confined bandgap that suppresses off-state tunneling and thermionic leakage about 1000x versus silicon. Because each channel is only 0.7 nm thick, tiers can stack at ~20 nm pitch, which makes 50+ tiers practical.
note: 2D-channel DRAM widely pursued; BEOL MOCVD quality.

title: Layer-transferred InAs/AlSb resonant-tunneling floating-gate tiers
idea: Resonant tunneling: a triple-barrier InAs/AlSb stack passes charge into a floating gate only when ~2.5 V aligns the resonance, and blocks it otherwise, giving very long retention. The III-V layers are grown on cheap substrates, then oxide-bonded as 4 stacked tiers onto CMOS logic.
note: Essentially ULTRARAM; endurance far below DRAM needs.

title: Unipolar VCMA-MTJ with thin-film diode enables stacked cross-point MRAM
idea: Voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy: precessional writes with timed unipolar voltage pulses flip perpendicular MTJs at fJ energy, so each cell needs only a one-way thin-film diode instead of a transistor. Unipolar operation lets 4F2 MRAM cross-point tiers be repeated in BEOL.
note: UCLA MeRAM diode cross-point already proposed; precessional write error rates and timing precision.

title: Built-in-bias antiferroelectric ZrO2 capacitors stacked in 1T-nC strings
idea: Field-induced antiferroelectric-ferroelectric transition: ZrO2 capacitors with asymmetric-workfunction electrodes shift the double hysteresis loop so one lobe straddles zero bias, giving two non-volatile states. Antiferroelectric switching fatigues less than true ferroelectrics. Several such capacitors are stacked vertically on one access transistor.

title: Mn3Sn antiferromagnet bits switched by Neel-order spin-orbit torque
idea: Effect: the noncollinear antiferromagnet Mn3Sn has a large anomalous Hall effect and tunnel magnetoresistance despite near-zero net moment. Switch its octupole order with current pulses and read it through Mn3Sn/MgO/Mn3Sn junctions, which removes IrMn pinning, Ru spacers and Pt torque layers.

title: Band-to-band tunneling access transistors flatten the retention leakage tail
idea: Effect: quantum band-to-band tunneling. Replace the thermionic access FET with an all-silicon tunnel FET whose off-state leakage is set by tunneling, giving aA/um levels that barely depend on temperature. The weak-cell tail vanishes, and the low on-current is fine because charging 5 fF at 1 uA takes only ~5 ns.
note: TFET access devices studied; ambipolar/GIDL and storage-junction leakage still set the tail.

title: Displacement-Talbot self-imaging prints periodic cell arrays without projection optics
idea: Effect: Talbot self-imaging. A periodic phase mask lit at 193 nm re-images itself at Talbot planes; sweeping the mask-wafer gap (displacement Talbot) averages out depth sensitivity and prints 36-40 nm-pitch honeycomb landing-pad and storage-node arrays across a full field in one flash. Only the aperiodic periphery goes to a scanner, and dummy rows at the array edge absorb the Talbot edge defects.

title: Photochromic absorbance-modulation layer lets i-line steppers print 30 nm features
idea: Effect: reversible photochromism. A diarylethene layer over the resist is held opaque by a ring-shaped 325 nm standing wave, while 365 nm light bleaches and passes only a sub-diffraction central aperture (absorbance modulation). Recycled i-line steppers with a dual-wavelength illuminator then print dense contact arrays at 30-40 nm.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory pool exploits frozen leakage for refresh-free density
idea: At 77 K, thermally activated junction leakage and GIDL fall by more than 10^6, stretching retention from 64 ms to hours. A shared DRAM pool in an LN2 bath can then use 2-3x smaller capacitors and no refresh, and it serves a whole rack over optical links.

title: Pockels effect: thin-film lithium niobate modulators bonded on HBM base die
idea: Heterogeneously bond thin-film LiNbO3 microring modulators onto the HBM base die so the stack speaks optics directly at ~0.5-1 V drive and ~50 fJ/bit modulator energy; memory sits meters from the GPU over fiber with no electrical SerDes.
note: Optical memory links pursued by Celestial, Ayar, Lightmatter; ring thermal tuning on hot base die.

title: Fe: hematite Néel-vector bit flipped by titanium orbital torque
idea: Store the bit in the Néel vector of a ~5 nm alpha-Fe2O3 island, switch it with orbital-Hall current from an adjacent Ti strip (light-metal orbital torque instead of Pt/W spin-Hall), and read it by spin-Hall magnetoresistance or a stacked tunnel junction; antiferromagnetic order has no stray field and switches in picoseconds.

title: Mn: Mn4N ferrimagnetic racetrack shifts domain-wall bits at km/s
idea: Build racetracks from Mn4N (only Mn and N, perpendicular anisotropy, near-compensated so walls move ~1-3 km/s) and shift domain-wall-encoded bits past one read/write port with current pulses, so tens of bits share a single access transistor.
note: Racetrack long pursued; shift reliability, and horizontal-track density gain is modest.

title: Cr: Cr2O3 magnetoelectric antiferromagnet written by voltage, not current
idea: Use a thin boron-doped Cr2O3 layer whose antiferromagnetic domain is selected by a voltage pulse under a small fixed bias field (magnetoelectric E-times-H switching), read via its boundary magnetization by anomalous Hall in an adjacent film or a stacked tunnel junction.

title: Ruthenium redox-molecule storage node holds charge for minutes
idea: Ru: graft a monolayer of Ru-polypyridyl redox molecules on the storage electrode so stored charge lives in discrete molecular oxidation states behind an electron-transfer barrier; the access transistor writes and reads by oxidizing or reducing them, and charge loss needs thermally activated back-transfer (seconds-minutes) rather than ms-scale junction drain.
note: ZettaCore pursued porphyrin redox molecular memory; integration and endurance stalled it.

title: Silicon seed-window lateral overgrowth grows each crystalline tier in place
idea: Over each finished tier, deposit oxide, open a sparse grid of seed windows to the crystalline tier below and grow Si by selective epitaxial lateral overgrowth until fronts merge, then CMP to 30 nm; merge seams are laid out under wordline-cut and dummy regions.

title: Mn3Sn antiferromagnetic bit: written by torque, read by tunneling
idea: Periodic-table walk, Mn (25): store bits in the chiral spin order of the Weyl antiferromagnet Mn3Sn, switched by spin-orbit torque and read by tunneling magnetoresistance in Mn3Sn/MgO/Mn3Sn; no stray field, so cells pack without magnetic crosstalk, and THz dynamics allow sub-ns writes with magnetic-class endurance.

title: Ti: TiOx ReRAM weight vault evicts static AI weights from DRAM
idea: Store frozen model weights in dense non-volatile TiOx ReRAM on an accelerator side-die with on-die dequantization; weights are written only at deployment, so DRAM/HBM holds only KV cache and activations.

title: Offset-printed alpha-In2Se3 sheets: ferroelectric semiconductor channel holds the bit
idea: Like offset printing transfers ink from a blanket roller, a wafer-scale stamp transfers MBE-grown alpha-In2Se3 layers onto the logic wafer. The bit is polarization inside the semiconductor channel itself, so no separate ferroelectric gate is needed, and channel conductance reads it non-destructively.

title: Anodized-aluminum capacitor forest: self-ordered 1000:1 pores without etching
idea: Copy architectural aluminum anodizing. Sputter 1 um of Al over the transistor array, imprint dimples aligned to the storage contacts, and anodize at ~10 V in sulfuric acid so pores self-order at ~25 nm pitch, one per dimple. ALD then lines each pore with TiN/TiO2-Al2O3/TiN.

title: Knitted MgB2 persistent-current loops for a cryogenic memory tier
idea: Interlock superconducting MgB2 loops like knitting (Tc 39 K, Mg and B only). Each loop holds a bit as a circulating persistent current, a flux quantum in or out, switched and sensed by an MgB2 nano-bridge, forming a 20 K cryocooled memory tier beside cryogenic AI accelerators.

title: Gun-bluing rust bit: oxidized-iron antiferromagnet switched by orbital torque
idea: Borrow gun bluing, the controlled oxidation of steel: thermally oxidize Fe films into epitaxial alpha-Fe2O3 (hematite) nanodots whose Neel vector is the bit. A Cr/CuOx line underneath switches it by orbital Hall torque, and spin-Hall magnetoresistance reads it.

title: Veneer-stacked hBN: sliding ferroelectric bit from boron and nitrogen
idea: Like plywood veneers laid at controlled grain angles, stack two hBN monolayers in parallel (AB/BA) alignment so out-of-plane polarization flips with a one-third-lattice interlayer slide. A graphene channel underneath reads it non-destructively as a resistance shift.
note: Duplicate sliding-ferroelectric hBN bit.

title: Watch-detent Goto pair of tunnel diodes holds each node
idea: Like a watch escapement detent, each storage node is the midpoint of two series tunnel diodes (Goto pair) whose N-shaped I-V curves give two stable voltages. The node self-restores to 0 or 1 at only the diodes' valley current.

title: Spinning-jenny sensing: one amplifier spins across sixteen gain-cell bitlines
idea: As one spinning-jenny wheel drove many spindles, pair non-destructive-read gain cells with one shared, high-quality sense amp per 16 read bitlines through a 1:16 mux. Reads do not destroy data, so only requested columns are sensed and no row restore is needed.

title: Seeded cast-mono tiers: single-crystal upper layers by rapid melt growth
idea: Solar cast-mono ingots grow single-crystal silicon from seed plates; do the same per tier by depositing amorphous Si/SiGe in oxide crucibles with a seed via to crystalline silicon below, flash-melting for microseconds and letting it recrystallize laterally into single-crystal islands for lateral access transistors.
note: Seeded lateral melt regrowth for monolithic 3D is established research (micro-Czochralski, SLS).

title: Cross-grain veneer slicing: epitaxial superlattice edges define sub-10 nm lines
idea: Plywood shows its plies when cut across the grain; grow a 400-layer Si/SiGe superlattice in a trailing-fab epi reactor, cleave and polish its edge, recess the SiGe, and use the edge as a stamp (superlattice nanowire pattern transfer) to print 8-10 nm half-pitch metal line arrays onto array wafers.

title: Perfect-binding spine: print stack interconnect on the die edges
idea: Stack thinned DRAM dies like book signatures with all inter-die wiring routed to one polished edge, then pattern vertical interconnect along that spine by laser-direct-write seeding and electroplating, the way a binder glues a spine, eliminating TSVs and their keep-out zones.

title: Micro-Czochralski laser seeds: one window mask grows tier crystals
idea: Open seed holes with the one added mask in the inter-tier oxide, deposit amorphous Si above, and melt it with an excimer laser so each hole bottom acts as a tiny Czochralski seed and grain filter, recrystallizing one location-controlled single-crystal grain per array tile for the next tier's access transistors.

title: Log-raft capillary self-assembly of DRAM dies onto logic wafers
idea: Drop DRAM dies onto water droplets confined by hydrophilic pad islands on a logic wafer; surface tension pulls each die into alignment within 0.5 um in under a second, like logs self-aligning in a river raft. The water then evaporates and a hybrid bond forms.

title: Wide-bandgap charge well that never needs refresh
idea: IFR: a bit that holds itself forever with zero leakage. Closest achievable: store the bit as a deep-depletion charge well in a 4H-SiC (3.3 eV) MOS capacitor with a SiC access FET, where thermal generation scales as exp(-Eg/2kT) and falls by roughly 10^16x vs silicon, so retention moves from ms to hours.
note: SiC DRAM with long retention shown in 1990s; density and SiC MOS quality limit.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric bilayer stacking registry as the bit
idea: IFR: switch the bit by nudging atoms, not by pushing charge across barriers. Closest achievable: in rhombohedral bilayer hBN or MoS2 the AB vs BA stacking registry carries opposite out-of-plane polarization; a ~0.3 V pulse slides one layer by one bond length and the polarization is read as a threshold shift in an adjacent 2D channel.
note: Same sliding-ferroelectric registry bit.

title: Antiferromagnetic Mn3Sn bit flipped by spin-orbit torque
idea: IFR: a bit with no stray field, no wear and picosecond speed. Closest achievable: a noncollinear antiferromagnet (Mn3Sn) whose magnetic octupole order is switched by spin-orbit torque from a heavy-metal line and read via its large anomalous Hall or tunnelling signal; zero stray field lets cells pack at minimum pitch.
note: Restatement of the Mn3Sn SOT bit.

title: Proton-position gate: bit stored as hydrogen location in gate
idea: IFR: store a bit by moving the lightest ion a few nanometres. Closest achievable: a gain cell whose read-transistor gate holds a ~5 nm proton conductor (phosphosilicate glass or hydrated HfO2) capped by an H-blocking layer; ns pulses shuttle protons toward or away from the channel, shifting threshold, and read is nondestructive.

title: Roll-to-roll transferred monolayer MoS2 gain cell
idea: IFR: an access channel too thin to leak. Closest achievable: R2R-transfer CVD monolayer MoS2 (1.8-2 eV gap, 0.7 nm thick, ideal electrostatics) onto foil to build 2T0C gain cells where the read-transistor gate is the storage node, with off-currents below 1e-18 A.

title: Gated Esaki-diode latch makes each cell self-holding
idea: IFR: the bit stays put with no refresh and no extra transistors. Engineer the storage-node junction as a degenerate band-to-band tunnel diode in series with a gated load so the node has two stable points on an N-shaped I-V (Goto-pair style), held by a picoamp-scale standby current.

title: Ferroelectric deadbolt raises access threshold only during sleep
idea: IFR: lock the door when you leave. A thin ferroelectric in the access-transistor gate stack is flipped once at sleep entry to raise Vt by ~0.5-1 V (deep off, retention of hours) and flipped back at wake, so it cycles once per sleep event (~1e6 lifetime) rather than per access.

title: BEOL oxide-transistor preamps chop bitlines into tiny segments
idea: Ideal result: every cell has its own amplifier. Closest: one IGZO thin-film preamp in the BEOL above each 16-cell bitline segment converts the local charge into a current on a global bitline, so the silicon SA sees a large current signal instead of a millivolt swing.

title: Heterostructure hole-well pillar: capacitorless 4F2 vertical cell
idea: IFR: 'the transistor is its own capacitor.' Backward: grow the vertical channel pillar with a 5 nm Ge-rich SiGe quantum well mid-pillar; holes trapped behind the valence-band offset shift the threshold and are read non-destructively as drain current, written by band-to-band tunneling.
note: SiGe quantum-well 1T-DRAM is studied art.

title: Carbon-nanotube CMOS periphery on glass beneath oxide arrays
idea: IFR: 'periphery is fast, complementary and made at 200 C.' Backward: deposit aligned >99.99% semiconducting carbon-nanotube films on glass, build n- and p-type CNFET sense amps and decoders at <=250 C, then stack oxide-semiconductor cell tiers directly above with no thermal damage.
note: CNFET monolithic 3D (N3XT, SkyWater) is established; complementary CNT yield and speed are the doubts.

title: Atmospheric spatial ALD on moving webs: no vacuum, no helium
idea: Ideal: atomic-precision films made in open air. Closest: spatial-ALD heads with gas-bearing-separated precursor zones (TMA/H2O, DEZ/H2O, TiCl4/H2O) coat 1-2 m webs or panels at 1-5 m/min at atmospheric pressure, laying down gate oxide, capacitor dielectric and ZnO channel with no vacuum chambers, He backside cooling or PFAS chamber cleans.
note: Atmospheric spatial ALD on webs exists; film quality and leakage for memory unproven.

title: Self-replicating nanoimprint stamps make each memory layer cost cents
idea: Ideal: a mask that copies itself forever. Closest: write one e-beam quartz master per layer, replicate it into thousands of UV-cured polymer daughter stamps (and granddaughters from those), and use each daughter for ~100 roll-to-plate imprints on panels or wafers before recycling.
note: Replica NIL stamps exist; 10-20 nm overlay and defect accumulation rule out DRAM critical layers.

title: Selector-only chalcogenide crosspoint decks at two masks per layer
idea: Ideal: a cell that is just a wire crossing. Closest: one amorphous chalcogenide threshold-switch layer at each crosspoint whose threshold voltage is set by write polarity (selector-only memory); each deck needs two DUV line masks, decks stack 4-8 high over CMOS, with no capacitor and no transistor per cell.
note: SOM actively pursued by Micron/Intel; DRAM endurance unlikely.

title: Grayscale exposure etches every 3D tier contact in one step
idea: Ideal: a 3D array whose tier contacts cost one step. Closest: for a capacitorless 3D floating-body or gain-cell stack, replace the multi-mask trim-and-etch wordline staircase with one grayscale (variable-dose) exposure that makes a resist ramp of N heights; a proportional etch transfers it, opening every tier's landing at once.

title: Transformer prefetcher in CXL controller makes flash act like DRAM
idea: IFR: infinite capacity at DRAM speed via a perfect oracle. Closest: a CXL expander fronting SLC NAND with a 5% DRAM cache runs an on-controller sequence model trained on each tenant's miss stream (page deltas plus PC hints sent over CXL), issuing prefetches 50-100 us ahead.

title: Interposer decoupling trenches repurposed as gigabyte-class eDRAM
idea: Ideal: the package's dead silicon stores data for free. Closest achievable: passive silicon interposers already carry deep-trench decoupling capacitors; add a 65-90 nm access transistor per trench plus simple sense periphery so the ~2,500 mm2 interposer becomes a ~0.5-1 GB eDRAM L4 directly under the HBM and GPU.

title: Tail exile: weak cells banished to an SRAM patch
idea: Ideal: a DRAM that never refreshes. Closest: a power-on BIST at elevated wordline-off stress finds the ~0.1% of cells with retention <2 s and stores their addresses in an on-die CAM plus a small SRAM patch that shadows those bits; the other 99.9% of the array is refreshed every 2-4 s instead of every 32-64 ms.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric van der Waals bilayer as fatigue-free gain gate
idea: Scarcity rule: no domain-wall pinning defects allowed. Use a sliding ferroelectric (rhombohedral bilayer MoS2 or parallel-stacked hBN), whose polarization flips by a one-third-lattice interlayer slip rather than ion displacement, as the gate of a 2D-channel read transistor; the dangling-bond-free vdW interface removes the charge trapping that limits HfO2 FeFETs.

title: SiGe quantum-well hole pocket extends floating-body retention
idea: Scarcity rule: silicon-family materials only, no capacitor. Grow a buried Si0.6Ge0.4 well in the body of a vertical gate-all-around channel; its ~200 meV valence-band offset traps holes written by impact ionization or GIDL and shifts threshold for read, while the offset blocks hole recombination into source and drain.
note: Same SiGe quantum-well hole-pocket cell.

title: Conducting domain-wall bit in thin lithium niobate mesas
idea: Scarcity rule: the sense path may use no stored charge at all. A 10 nm LiNbO3 mesa either contains or lacks a charged conducting domain wall bridging two side electrodes; an in-plane voltage pulse injects or erases the wall, and read is its nA-level current, a nondestructive resistive read.
note: Same LiNbO3 charged-wall NDRO cell.

title: Tri-level cells pack 24 Gb into a 16 Gb array
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): only densities JEDEC already defines may ship. Store three charge levels per cell and encode 3 bits in every 2 cells (9 states >= 8) with a two-step sense against half-level reference cells inside tRCD, so a 16 Gb-sized array ships as a standard, already-legal 24 Gb DDR5 die.

title: VCMA precessional MTJ write with retry loop hidden inside tWR
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): every write must finish inside DDR5's ~30 ns tWR. A voltage-controlled-magnetic-anisotropy MTJ switches by a 0.5 ns precessional pulse at ~0.5 V with near-zero current, and because its single-shot error rate is ~1e-3, the die runs write-verify-retry up to 10 times within tWR, turning a probabilistic element into a deterministic DDR write.

title: Bank-wide floating-body refresh fired in a single REF slot
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): REF commands keep arriving on the spec schedule. Use bistable floating-body cells whose parasitic bipolar transistor latches, so one REF fires a bank-wide source pulse that pumps '1' cells back to full hole charge by impact ionization while '0' cells stay empty, restoring every row at once; the remaining REFs become no-ops.
note: Bipolar-latch FB holding/refresh known from Z-RAM work; temperature latch margin unresolved.

title: Hybrid gain cell: silicon read transistor, WSe2 write transistor
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): ACT/RD/WR/PRE behavior unchanged. A 2T gain cell stores the bit on the gate of a Si FinFET read device, written through a BEOL monolayer WSe2 p-FET whose 1.6 eV gap and atomically thin body give off current below 1e-19 A; reads are nondestructive, so the die skips restore inside tRAS and uses the slack to precharge early.
note: Si/oxide hybrid gain cells widely pursued; WSe2 p-FET swap adds 2D transfer yield risk.

title: Stepwise adiabatic charging of wordlines from on-die tank capacitors
idea: Limit: 4x less activation energy without lowering any voltage. Wordlines and bitline restore are charged in N steps from a bank of deep-trench tank capacitors held at intermediate voltages, then discharged back step by step into the same tanks, so dissipation scales ~1/N.

title: In-sense-amp capacitor taps shield finite-endurance NV cells from writes
idea: Constraint: NV cells (FeRAM/MRAM, ~1e10-1e12 cycles) must still behave with DRAM-class endurance. Each sense amp gets four capacitor taps that act as an in-SA DRAM row cache; writes coalesce there, and a row is written to the NV array only on eviction or at power-fail, flushed with an on-die energy reserve.

title: Open tier-PDK and known-good-tier marketplace
idea: Limit: no single company may own the whole stack. Publish an open interface spec for bondable array tiers (pad pitch, test pads, select-switch protocol) so fabs of many sizes sell tested array tiers to independent stackers that assemble them on logic.

title: Room-temperature surface-activated bonding of 5 um memory dies
idea: Under 400 C, Ar-beam surface activation bonds Cu/SiO2 die faces at room temperature, so thermal-expansion warpage never builds up. This allows 5 um dies and 32-48-high stacks.
note: SAB is known; room-temperature Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonds are weak without anneal.

title: Synthetic crucibles from polysilicon-plant tetrachloride waste
idea: Imposed scarcity: no natural high-purity quartz. Take the SiCl4 byproduct that Siemens polysilicon plants make (~3-4 kg per kg of poly), flame-hydrolyze it into silica soot as optical-fiber preform makers do, and press and sinter the soot into whole crucibles (not just inner liners) next to U.S. poly plants.

title: Rutile titania on MoO2 electrodes: hafnium- and zirconium-free capacitors
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero Zr and Hf. Use conductive MoO2 (a distorted-rutile oxide) as the storage-node electrode so ALD TiO2 grows directly as rutile (k ~80-100) at low temperature, with Al doping to hold down leakage in the thin film.
note: Same rutile TiO2 on MoO2 template as I-10317 (ALD instead of bath); leakage is the doubt.

title: Fluidic self-assembly drops DRAM dies into hybrid-bond sites
idea: Scarcity: die bonders are the bottleneck tool. Dies with a keyed outline and hydrophobic backside are tumbled in a carrier liquid over a logic wafer with matching hydrophilic recesses; capillary forces self-align them to <0.5 um and the wafer is batch-annealed into Cu-Cu hybrid bonds.
note: Capillary self-assembly for hybrid bonding researched at Tohoku/imec.

title: Voltage-stacked DRAM tiers slash power bumps by four
idea: Scarcity: only 15% of bumps may carry power. Put 4 DRAM dies in series voltage domains (each floating 1.1 V above the one below on a 4.4 V rail) so one current flows through all tiers; small switched-capacitor balancers absorb mismatch and signals cross domains through capacitive level shifters.
note: Same series-stacked tier supply idea.

title: Bookshelf packaging stands DRAM dies on edge at 60 um pitch
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. Route all die I/O to one edge, wafer-level plate that edge into contact fingers, and slot dies vertically like books into a glass rack whose floor carries the bus; no TSVs or stacking bonders, and coolant flows between the books.
note: Same bookshelf die mounting.

title: Passive optical splitter broadcasts one weight copy to sixteen accelerators
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. Instead of every accelerator holding the full model, one memory node streams weights through a passive 1:16 optical star coupler while all 16 accelerators run the same layer in lockstep; each consumes the broadcast and keeps only activations and KV locally.

title: Inductively coupled tall stack wired only by two power bars
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. Every tier talks to its neighbors through on-die coil pairs (no signal TSVs), and power enters through two thick copper bars plated into a single slot cut down the stack's side, so the only vertical metal in a 64-tier stack is power.
note: Coil-coupled tiers plus sidewall power bars; close to Kuroda's known proposals.

title: No silicon wafer: idle Gen 8.5 LCD fabs make oxide-TFT memory panels
idea: Forced limit: no Si wafers. Convert overbuilt Gen 8.5 LCD backplane fabs (2.2x2.5 m glass, about 70x the area of a 300 mm wafer) to make IGZO 2T gain-cell arrays at about 1 um rules, sold as a slow-DRAM capacity tier.

title: Ge-free, NAND-line 3D oxide gain cell (oxide/nitride mold + channel replacement)
idea: Deposit 16-64 SiO2/SiN pairs by PECVD (standard NAND tools). One HAR hole/slit etch exposes all tiers; SiN is removed with hot phosphoric acid and replaced in every tier by ALD IGZO/ZTO horizontal channels (Kioxia's 3D OCTRAM SiN->InGaZnO replacement) plus recessed W/Mo gate and storage-node fills. Vertical wordline pillars gate the write transistors through all tiers (IMECAS dual-gate vertical-WL 2T0C); each storage node is a metal island that gates the tier's read transistor, so no lateral capacitor is needed. 2-3 bits/cell with write-verify multiplies the tier count.

title: NIL-only periodic cell wafer (bonded periphery makes every layer imprintable)
idea: A master template (e-beam- or DSA-written) is replicated into working templates; jet-and-flash imprint defines each field's hole or line lattice with no projection optics. Because the cell wafer of a bonded 4F2 VCT or vertical gain-cell array needs only 2-3 overlay-critical layers (channel holes, wordline, contact) and later layers self-align, NIL's overlay and pattern-variety weaknesses matter less. 3D templates can define line + contact in a single imprint (dual-damascene style). Defects are absorbed by redundancy and ECC (B2-15).

title: Porphyrin redox monolayers soaked into existing capacitor trenches
idea: Worsen: develop a deposition tool for a new dielectric. Flip: use wet chemistry to self-assemble redox-active porphyrin monolayers inside existing MIM or trench test capacitors so each molecule stores discrete electrons at fixed redox potentials; the budget is chemistry, a probe station and 24 months of cycling tests.
note: Essentially ZettaCore's porphyrin molecular memory; cheap to re-test, but precedent did not scale.

title: Load-sharing magnetic matrix switch moves row decoding into package
idea: Revive the 1950s load-sharing matrix switch, the core-era decoder in which a few binary drive lines threaded through a pattern of transformers excite exactly one output: build it as coupled planar transformers in the organic package substrate so 10 binary-weighted primaries select one of 1,024 wordline-group drivers. The DRAM die keeps only local wordline drivers; global row predecode transistor trees leave the litho die.
note: Core-era load-sharing switch revived in package; 1,024 outputs still need die bumps, and GHz transformer fidelity is doubtful.

title: Glass-coated microwire twistors woven into memory fabric on looms
idea: Revive Bell Labs' 1957 twistor (helically magnetized tape wound on a wire) using Taylor-Ulitovsky glass-coated CoFeSiB microwires, already drawn by the kilometre at 5-20 um diameter, given helical anisotropy by torsion annealing; an industrial loom weaves them with copper word straps into a fabric whose crossings are bits, read by giant magneto-impedance. No wafer, litho or vacuum tool touches the array.
note: Novel loom-woven GMI microwire array; doubt: 1-10 Mb/cm2 density and serial magnetic sensing are far from DRAM-class access.

title: Indium-free zinc-tin-silicon oxide gain cell with graded self-insulator
idea: Combine channel and gate insulator in one co-sputtered Zn-Sn-Si-O film whose Si fraction ramps from ~5% (semiconducting channel) to ~50% (amorphous insulator) in a single chamber pass, forming a 2T gain-cell storage transistor with no indium, no gallium and no separate gate-oxide ALD.
note: Single-pass graded channel-to-insulator film; interface trap density is the doubt.

title: Self-clearing capacitor electrodes borrowed from metallized-film power capacitors
idea: Combine the self-healing of metallized-film capacitors with DRAM MIM capacitors: an ALD ZrO2/Al2O3 dielectric under a 5-10 nm sputtered Al (or TiN/Al) top electrode thin enough that a breakdown spot's discharge vaporizes or oxidizes the electrode locally, isolating the defect while the cell keeps working at slightly lower C. Buildable in a university nanofab: ALD, sputter and lift-off only.
note: fJ stored energy too small to clear electrodes itself; an external clearing pulse in a nanofab test is cheap to try.

title: Active glass interposer with oxide-TFT repeaters
idea: Move the PHY into the substrate: build low-temperature IGZO thin-film-transistor repeaters, multiplexers and charge-recycling drivers directly on a glass interposer (sputter plus contact litho, <350 C), so memory and compute dies use tiny low-swing pads and the interposer regenerates signals over centimetres.
note: IGZO TFT speed far too low for Gb/s repeaters.

title: Blessing in disguise: random sense amp offsets form a reference ladder
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: a bank of 8 tiny unequalized latches per 64 bitlines samples each held bitline voltage in turn; their natural random offsets (sigma ~15 mV), measured once at test, act as a free reference ladder, so the pattern of which latches flip gives 2-3 bits of soft information or multilevel reads with no reference generators.
note: Random latch offsets as free reference ladder; drift with BTI and temperature undermines calibration.

title: Xylem transpiration draws metal nanoink void-free into deep capacitor holes
idea: Trees lift sap by evaporation through nanoporous leaf surfaces; cap the wafer with a nanoporous evaporation membrane so solvent leaves only through the top, pulling a Ru or Mo nanoparticle ink into 60:1 storage-node holes without trapped voids, then sinter at ~350 C.

title: Diatom biosilica: room-temperature porous low-k dielectric for panel RDL
idea: Diatoms grow hierarchically porous silica from silicic acid at room temperature using polyamines and silaffin-like peptides. The same chemistry deposits porous silica (k ~2.0-2.3) on organic or glass panels as the RDL dielectric, with no CVD tools and no high-temperature cure.
note: Bio-templated porous silica film quality, leakage and moisture uptake unproven for RDL.

title: Parametron phase-locked sense amps immune to transistor offset
idea: Revive Goto's 1954 parametron. Each sense node is a tiny resonator (MOS varactor plus active inductor) pumped at 2f, which can only oscillate in one of two phases, and the bitline's charge-sharing signal seeds which phase wins. The decision depends on the seed's sign relative to a common pump rather than on matched transistor pairs, and phase outputs can be majority-voted (parametron logic) for free in-periphery error voting.
note: Resonator and pump asymmetry acts like an offset; an active inductor at bitline pitch is costly.

title: Cochlear hair cell: Hopf-bifurcation oscillator as sense amplifier
idea: Outer hair cells reach huge gain for faint sounds by sitting just below an oscillation onset (a Hopf bifurcation). Bias a 3-4 transistor local oscillator per bitline pair right at onset; the small charge-sharing signal pushes it into oscillation at phase 0 or phase pi, and a phase detector latches the bit before a restore driver writes back.
note: Critical slowing down near the bifurcation slows the decision; the oscillator's own asymmetry acts like an offset.

title: Charged microring junction: bits read by wavelength, not bitlines
idea: Worsen: read every bit through a long, power-hungry copper bitline. Flip: on a ~$60k silicon-photonics shuttle, store each bit as charge on the depletion capacitance of a microring's PN junction, which shifts its resonance, so one waveguide reads 32-64 bits in parallel by wavelength; demonstrated within 24 months.
note: Ring size and junction leakage make density and retention poor; demo on shuttle is easy.

title: Blu-ray replication lines injection-mold nanostructured capacitor templates
idea: Worse: let idle optical-disc factories rot while capacitor etch bottlenecks fabs. Flip: injection-mold high-temperature PEI/PEEK substrates from a nickel stamper carrying ~100 nm pit arrays at ~3 s per part. ALD low-temperature electrodes and high-k into the pits, then laminate an oxide-TFT layer on top.

title: Nanosolar's aluminum foil anodized into capacitor pores with diode floors
idea: Nanosolar's roll-to-roll CIGS on aluminium foil died on efficiency, but its cheap Al-foil web still works. Anodize the foil roll into self-ordered alumina pores at 100 nm pitch and 60:1 aspect ratio, and line them by ALD as MIM capacitors. Stepping down the anodization voltage at the end thins each pore floor's barrier layer to ~2 nm (about 1.2 nm per volt), forming a self-aligned MIIM tunnel diode as each cell's access element.
note: Etch-free anodized pores; 2 nm MIIM diode access leaks too much and lacks gate selection.

title: Piezo-stack package clamp tunes die stress to shrink leakage tail
idea: Effect: piezo-junction effect (stress-modified bandgap and trap emission rates). A small mechanical team builds a module heat spreader with a PZT stack that applies controlled compressive stress (tens of MPa) to DRAM packages; a closed loop driven by measured retention finds the stress setpoint that minimizes trap-assisted junction leakage.
note: Tens of MPa shifts the bandgap by only meV; cheap to test with a clamp on DIMMs.

title: Oblique ion-sputter ripples self-organize sub-pitch word-line gratings
idea: Effect: Bradley-Harper sputter instability. 500 eV Ar+ ions hitting a hardmask 60-70 degrees off normal grow ripples with a 20-30 nm period on their own, and a coarse ArF pre-pattern at 4x that period pins the ripple phase and direction (guided self-organization). The ripples are transferred as the word-line grating, replacing SAQP's spacer deposition and etch loops with one broad-beam step.

title: Kirkendall voiding hollows solid pillars into double-sided cylinder capacitors
idea: Effect: nanoscale Kirkendall effect. Fill capacitor molds with solid Co or Ni pillars and sulfidize them: metal diffuses outward faster than sulfur diffuses inward, leaving a hollow tube. An H2 reduction and a thin TiN overcoat then make both inner and outer walls electrode area. This drops the double-sided cylinder flow's support-mesh litho, mold strip and extra liner deposition.
note: Sulfidize-reduce volume changes likely collapse 30 nm AR60 tubes.

title: Rayleigh-Plateau breakup converts one line pattern into dot arrays
idea: Effect: Rayleigh-Plateau capillary instability. Print a single 1D grating of thin amorphous-Si or Cu lines, then anneal: each line breaks into droplets at a fixed wavelength (~4.5x the line diameter), and shallow notches printed by the same mask pin the droplet positions. One litho step yields a 2D landing-pad or node array instead of two crossed patterning passes.

title: Electrochromic gel images leaky storage nodes across a whole wafer
idea: Effect: electrochromic ion insertion. Before the capacitor is built, cover the exposed storage-node contacts of a test wafer with a WO3 electrochromic gel film and bias the substrate: nodes with leaky junctions pass current that darkens the film above them, so a $20k camera maps the leakage tail of millions of cells in one integrated exposure. $1M builds the test structures, gel and optics over 24 months.

title: Notch-guided crack propagation cuts sub-10 nm isolation gaps without cut masks
idea: Effect: controlled brittle fracture. Deposit a brittle, tensile SiNx film and use cheap i-line litho to place micro-notches; cracks start at the notches and run straight along designed stress channels, leaving 5-10 nm gaps that become word-line or active-area cuts. $1M on 150 mm wafers over 24 months measures straightness and placement accuracy.

title: Stochastic resonance: noise-assisted bistable receivers detect 30 mV memory signals
idea: Drive an array of bistable comparators with deliberately injected uncorrelated noise so a sub-threshold 30 mV signal biases their switching statistics; majority-summing 16 comparators recovers each bit at low BER on a fraction of today's swing.
note: Calibrated comparators already sense 30 mV; injected noise and 16x comparators likely eat the savings.

title: Mott transition: printed VO2 off-die ESD clamps strip I/O pad capacitance
idea: Print VO2 nanoparticle-ink clamps on the package substrate at each memory I/O; an ESD surge drives them metallic so they shunt the current, letting on-die ESD diodes (100-300 fF per pad) shrink to minimum size.
note: VO2 goes metallic near 68 C, below DRAM operating temperature; die handling still needs on-die ESD.

title: Coulomb blockade: printed gold-nanoparticle films as threshold bus terminations
idea: Print ligand-capped 2-4 nm Au nanoparticle arrays whose collective Coulomb-blockade threshold keeps them insulating for small signals but conducting beyond a size-tuned voltage; as terminations they absorb reflections only during overshoot instead of burning static ODT current.
note: Nanoparticle films are too resistive to match ~40 ohm.

title: Sodium-ion electret back-gates set each tier's threshold without wiring
idea: Implant a controlled Na+ dose into the buried oxide beneath each tier of p-channel lateral access transistors, drift it to the BOX top in a one-time field anneal, then seal it with SiN; the frozen charge acts as a permanent back-gate bias raising |Vt| by ~0.3 V.
note: Na+ remains mobile at operating temperature; fab contamination.

title: Zn: self-evaporating ZnO scaffold opens 3D-DRAM tier gaps
idea: Stack Si/ZnO tiers, cut the vertical slits, then anneal in hydrogen so ZnO is reduced and the high-vapor-pressure Zn evaporates out through the slits, leaving clean cavities for gate and capacitor fill with no selective wet or radical etch.
note: Si tiers on ZnO are not single-crystal; Zn is a deep-level trap hurting retention.

title: Bi: capillary-infiltrated molten Bi-Sn fills high-AR cavities
idea: Coat the array with a thin wetting liner, flood with molten Bi-Sn eutectic (~140 C) under gas pressure so it wicks into capacitor top-plate cavities and plugs, then wipe the excess with a heated blade before it freezes; Bi's solidification expansion offsets shrink voids.
note: 140 C melt incompatible with later ~400 C BEOL; Sn/Bi contamination.

title: Se: xerographic charge-image patterning with dry nanoparticle toner
idea: Coat the wafer with a thin amorphous-selenium photoconductor, corona-charge it, expose with patterned light so charge leaks where lit, then cascade charged hardmask nanoparticles that stick only to the charge image; fuse, etch and sublime away the Se.

title: Na: sodium-silicate geopolymer encapsulant replaces epoxy around HBM stacks
idea: Fill and encapsulate HBM stacks with a low-temperature (~80 C cure) sodium-silicate aluminosilicate geopolymer loaded with AlN, giving an inorganic mold with CTE ~6-8 ppm/K, ~3-5 W/m-K and no outgassing; package outline and ballout stay unchanged.
note: Mobile Na+ ions are a classic semiconductor contaminant; moisture and ionic migration doubt.

title: Brewed S-layer protein crystals as sub-EUV lithography templates
idea: Ferment bacteria whose surface-layer proteins self-assemble into 2D crystals with hexagonal ~10-15 nm lattices, recrystallize them on wafers over a coarse DUV guide pattern, and use the pores as metal-deposition or etch templates for landing pads and capacitor seeds.

title: Mass-balance reconciliation: repair flips by enforcing data's built-in invariants
idea: Chemical plants reconcile noisy flow meters against mass-balance constraints. Data that already carries invariants (monotone CSR row offsets, sorted index arrays, distributions that sum to 1, histograms with known totals, rotation matrices) is stored raw in 1%-BER cells. On load, a reconciliation unit finds entries that violate the invariant and resets them to the least-squares value consistent with their neighbors, so the data's own structure replaces ECC. Delta-compressing the monotone arrays saves 2-4x on top.
note: Invariants detect but rarely correct exact index values; undetectable in-range flips.

title: Printed ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal bit that heals itself
idea: IFR: a ferroelectric that cannot fatigue because it is liquid. Closest achievable: inkjet ferroelectric nematic mesogens (RM734/DIO class, P ~6 uC/cm^2) into printed microwells between printed electrodes; polarization is read capacitively and the fluid order regrows after every switch (us today, targeting ~100 ns in nanowells).
note: Retention without anchoring-induced bistability doubtful; microsecond switching.

title: Vicinal-wafer atomic steps template sub-15 nm wordline lines
idea: Ideal: the crystal itself is the mask. Closest: anneal a miscut Si surface so atomic steps bunch into a periodic ridge array with a 10-20 nm period set by the miscut angle; area-selective deposition decorates the step edges into a hardmask for wordline lines across the whole wafer, with one DUV cut mask for line ends.
note: Step meandering and bunching nonuniformity over 300 mm won't meet wordline CD control.

title: Graceful-forgetting KV memory: leakage as the eviction policy [SPECULATIVE]
idea: KV elements are stored sign-separated: the sign sits in exact rows, the magnitude as a 4- or 8-level charge in true-cell polarity, so leakage only ever reduces magnitude. Rows holding the recent window, attention-sink tokens and controller-flagged heavy hitters are refreshed under a lease (B4-03). All other KV rows are never refreshed. Over seconds to minutes their magnitudes droop level by level. A fully discharged row reads as all zeros, and the allocator reclaims it on zero-detect. The model sees a continuous 'forgetting curve' resembling H2O/StreamingLLM-style eviction, at zero refresh energy. Training or fine-tuning with the decay model (as RANA did for CNNs) teaches the network to expect it.
note: Retention tail spans orders of magnitude cell-to-cell, so decay is noisy rather than graceful.

title: Aircraft-leasing model for scanners and etchers
idea: Copy AerCap/GECAS: a lessor buys scanners, etchers and deposition tools in bulk, leases them to fabs on 5-8 year operating leases with standard return conditions and maintenance reserves, and re-markets returned tools to the next fab, including startups and mini-fabs.

title: Continuous-recharge Czochralski from PV: many ingots per crucible
idea: PV pullers grow 5-10 ingots per crucible by recharging granular polysilicon through a feed tube; adapt multi-recharge Cz, with devitrification-promoting crucible coatings for longer life, to 300 mm DRAM-grade wafers with in-line oxygen control.

title: Kalundborg industrial symbiosis around a U.S. memory fab
idea: Adapted from Denmark's Kalundborg park, where plants trade waste streams: co-locate a U.S. fab with an onsite air-separation unit (nitrogen, argon, neon), a sulfuric-acid regenerator, a greenhouse and a data center that buys both fab output and its low-grade heat.

title: One via mask personalizes page, bank and 2T2C mode
idea: Business model reversal: fabricate a single universal DRAM wafer and make products with one via mask that rewires mats into 1 kB or 2 kB pages, HBM pseudo-channels, or a 2T2C mode (two cells per bit for double signal and ~10x retention, half density) for automotive and low-refresh customers.
note: Metal/bond options for organization already standard; 2T2C SKU is a modest extension.

title: Pioneer-species beachhead: enter at 125 C niche, scale downward
idea: Like lichens colonizing fresh lava where nothing else grows, a U.S. startup memory maker launches only in 125-150 C automotive, defense and downhole markets that incumbents underserve, where premiums are 3-5x per bit, and uses that learning curve to scale into commodity later.

title: Dumb-die DRAM moves DLL, training and refresh logic to controller
idea: Periphery logic on a DRAM process costs 3-4 logic generations more per transistor. Strip the DRAM die to array, sense and simple I/O; the controller on a leading logic node owns clock deskew (forwarded clock), PHY training, ECC, refresh scheduling and row-hammer tracking.

title: Barrier-free molybdenum buried wordline recessed deeper, tungsten-free
idea: Box: standard cap x buried-channel access with barrier-less Mo wordline x SA x in-array x Si x CVD/ALD Mo using the existing recess pattern (zero added masks). Mo's low narrow-line resistivity without a TiN liner lets the conductor sit further below the storage junction at equal wordline resistance, shrinking gate-storage overlap.

title: Po memory that never shrinks: perpetual-node legacy DRAM franchise
idea: Po: 'memory that never shrinks.' Extracted: freeze a copy-exact 180-150 nm DRAM process for 20+ years and sell long-life legacy parts (SDR to DDR3, small densities, industrial, auto and defense) under take-or-pay supply contracts, so those markets stop consuming leading-edge wafers and end-of-life buys.
note: Legacy DRAM vendors already serve this; needs a fab line beyond $1M.

title: Depreciation arbitrage: keep paid-off 1y/1z DRAM lines running
idea: Po: the oldest fab makes the cheapest bit. Instead of converting fully depreciated 1y/1z-class DRAM lines to HBM, sign 5-year take-or-pay contracts for DDR4/LPDDR4/DDR5 at cash cost, steering auto, PC and edge demand there and freeing leading lines for AI.
note: Already common incumbent practice.

title: Refurbished tools fill empty shells of existing fab sites
idea: Po: factories build factories. Buy decommissioned 193i scanners, etchers and ALD tools from closing 200/300 mm lines, refurbish them and install them into unused cleanroom shell space already built at existing DRAM and logic sites.

title: U.S. 125 C 'hot DRAM' line on mature 40 nm tooling
idea: Worse: leave automotive and defense 125 C memory to a few legacy offshore lines. Flip: stand up a U.S. line on used 40 nm DUV tools making large-Cs (~25 fF) trench cells with thick-oxide, long-channel access devices whose physics already meets 125 C for 10 years, funded by automotive and DoD offtake.

title: Universal wafer: one mask set, late personalization for every SKU
idea: Run a single DRAM wafer design in U.S. fabs for every product and personalize at the end (I/O width, speed bin, ECC mode, density) through e-fuses, top-metal options and packaging, so the line never changes over.

title: Refinery side-draws: U.S. steel-plant air separators harvest neon
idea: Oil refineries pull extra fractions from column side-draws; add crude rare-gas columns to the big air separation units at U.S. steel mills and chemical plants, purify neon, krypton and xenon centrally, and recycle the fab's ArF/KrF laser exhaust through the same plant.

title: Moly roaster to wordline: Colorado molybdenite becomes a tungsten-free metal
idea: Integrate like a steel mill from ore to coil: roast Climax/Henderson molybdenite concentrate to MoO3, chlorinate it on site to MoO2Cl2 CVD precursor, and deposit fluorine-free molybdenum fill for buried wordlines, bit-line contacts and periphery plugs.

title: Sacrificial-polymer air-gap bitlines raise sense transfer ratio
idea: Substitute oxide bitline spacers with vacuum: a sacrificial polymer between bitlines is thermally decomposed through a porous cap, lowering bitline capacitance. Spin-coat, cap and bake steps fit a university fab.

title: Molybdenum from oxychloride replaces WF6 tungsten in 3D wordlines
idea: Substitute WF6-CVD tungsten in replacement-gate wordlines, staircase contacts and buried wordlines with molybdenum deposited from MoO2Cl2 (or MoCl5) + H2, which nucleates barrier-free on Al2O3/SiO2 so the TiN glue layer is dropped and more of each 15-20 nm tier cavity is conductor.

title: Substitute molybdenum for tungsten in buried wordlines and contacts
idea: Deposit buried wordlines and storage/bitline contacts by ALD/CVD molybdenum from MoO2Cl2 instead of tungsten from WF6; Mo needs no thick TiN barrier or nucleation layer, so more of the narrow trench is conductor. Source Mo from US primary mines (Climax, Henderson) and copper-mine byproduct.

title: Substitute domestic glass-core substrates for single-source ABF build-up film
idea: Build DRAM and HBM package substrates on borosilicate glass cores with laser-drilled through-glass vias and US-made photo-imageable polyimide redistribution layers instead of Ajinomoto ABF laminates.

title: Substitute water rinse-dry with supercritical CO2 for high-AR capacitor arrays
idea: Replace DI-water rinse and dry after capacitor mold strip with supercritical CO2 plus co-solvents, which has zero surface tension, so ultra-high-AR electrode cylinders cannot lean or stick together. This deletes the mid- and top-level nitride support meshes (two patterning steps) and allows AR >100.

title: Swap separate host and device copies for one unified package memory
idea: Substitute the host-DRAM plus device-HBM pair with one coherent physical pool on a CPU+accelerator package. Data loader buffers, pinned staging areas and checkpoints then exist once instead of twice.
note: Grace Hopper, MI300A and Apple unified memory already exist.

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal hardens interfaces against the leakage tail
idea: Replace the final forming-gas anneal with a high-pressure deuterium furnace anneal, a 1990s hot-carrier fix. Si-D bonds resist breaking far better than Si-H, so fewer interface traps form to drive trap-assisted GIDL and VRT.
note: High-pressure H2/D2 anneal tools already sold to DRAM makers.

title: Copper-mine by-product molybdenum replaces tungsten in buried wordlines
idea: Adapted from copper miners' practice of recovering molybdenite as a by-product (Utah and Arizona porphyries). Contract US mine molybdenum into MoCl5/MoO2Cl2 ALD precursors and switch buried-wordline and bitline-contact fill from TiN/W to barrier-thin Mo.
note: Mo wordline/contact fill already being adopted.

title: Colorado molybdenum replaces Chinese tungsten in wordlines and contacts
idea: Minify tungsten to zero: convert buried wordlines, bitline contacts and landing pads to Mo from domestic Climax/Henderson ore, with a US-built MoO2Cl2 precursor plant. Mo's shorter electron mean free path gives lower line resistance than W below ~15 nm.

title: Glass-core interposers replace ABF build-up in memory packages
idea: Minify the organic substrate: use borosilicate glass cores with laser-drilled through-glass vias as the package and interposer for memory stacks, CTE-matched to silicon (~3 ppm/K).

title: Eliminate tungsten: molybdenum buried wordlines and contacts from U.S. ore
idea: Replace W buried wordlines, bitline contacts and periphery plugs with fluorine-free ALD/CVD molybdenum (MoO2Cl2 precursor) sourced from Colorado/Arizona primary and by-product Mo. Mo's shorter electron mean free path gives lower line resistance than W below ~15 nm, so the buried wordline can be recessed shallower, which also reduces GIDL.
note: Molybdenum replacement for W is widely pursued by toolmakers and memory makers.

title: Move the wafer, not the gas: atmospheric spatial ALD
idea: Reverse which element moves: wafers travel under fixed precursor/purge gas heads at atmospheric pressure, instead of pulsing gases into a vacuum chamber around a static wafer.

title: Barrierless molybdenum buried wordline from a fluorine-free precursor
idea: TRIZ #2 Taking out: deposit Mo by ALD/CVD from MoO2Cl2 (no WF6) directly in the buried-wordline trench. Without fluorine there is nothing to attack the gate oxide, so the 2-3 nm TiN barrier that W needs can be removed, and at 10-15 nm widths Mo's shorter electron mean free path gives lower resistance than TiN/W.

title: Deuterated-drug kinetic isotope effect hardens access-transistor interfaces
idea: Deuterated drugs slow metabolism because C-D bonds break more slowly than C-H. Replace the forming-gas H2 anneal with high-pressure D2 from Canadian heavy-water stocks so Si-D bonds passivate the access-transistor and STI-edge interfaces and resist hot-carrier and GIDL-stress depassivation; DDR/HBM refresh commands are unchanged, on-die refresh management simply tracks fewer weak rows.
note: Deuterium anneal is known and already used.

title: Scuba rebreather loop recycles excimer-laser neon in DUV scanners
idea: Closed-circuit rebreathers scrub contaminants and recirculate the diluent gas. Put a getter and cryo-purification loop on every ArF/KrF excimer laser to strip fluorine-reaction contaminants (HF, CF4, O2) from the ~96% neon buffer and re-inject it, topping up F2 from onsite electrolysis; only litho tools change, DDR/HBM products do not.
note: Excimer neon recycling is already offered by laser vendors.

title: 1970s molybdenum-gate MOS revived to replace tungsten wordlines
idea: Revive molybdenum-gate MOS, and the WWII practice of substituting molybdenum for tungsten: fill buried wordlines and bitline contacts with barrier-thin Mo deposited from MoCl5/MoO2Cl2 instead of WF6, sourced from US mines.

title: Adaptive patterning wires each module to measured die positions
idea: Invert 'wiring masks are fixed before chips are placed': place DRAM and logic dies loosely, measure each die's true position and write custom redistribution per package with maskless lithography (Arizona adaptive-patterning lines).
note: Deca adaptive patterning already commercial.

title: Tungsten-free DRAM: ALD molybdenum wordlines plus Cu-Mn bitlines
idea: Box [ZrO2 cap | buried-channel Si RCAT | voltage SA | planar 1T1C | CZ Si | thermal ALD + electroplating]: fill buried wordlines with liner-free ALD Mo from MoO2Cl2/H2 and replace W bitlines, contacts and periphery plugs with electroplated Cu wrapped in a self-forming MnSiOx barrier.

title: Tungsten-free retrofit: molybdenum precursors in existing CVD chambers
idea: Po: memory needs no tungsten. Swap WF6 for MoO2Cl2/MoCl5 precursors in existing W CVD/ALD chambers (minor heater and delivery changes) for buried wordlines, contacts and plugs, gaining lower resistance in narrow lines.

title: Colorado molybdenum replaces Chinese tungsten in buried wordlines
idea: Worse: keep 80%-China tungsten in every buried wordline, contact and plug. Flip: switch to fluorine-free, barrierless Mo CVD sourced from U.S. Climax/Henderson mines; Mo has lower resistivity than W at thin dimensions.
note: Mo replacing W is already being adopted.

title: Trusted-foundry molybdenum wordlines from Colorado ore replace Chinese tungsten
idea: Defense trusted-foundry users must avoid adversary-sourced metals. Molybdenum is mined in the U.S. (Climax, Henderson) and has a shorter electron mean free path than W, so it beats W resistivity in <20 nm trenches. Deposit Mo by ALD/CVD from MoO2Cl2 into buried wordlines and bit-line contacts with thin or no TiN liner.

title: Defense-trusted DRAM uses chloride-precursor molybdenum wordlines, no WF6
idea: Extreme user: defense buyers who must avoid Chinese tungsten and fluorinated gases. Replace WF6-CVD tungsten buried wordlines and contacts with molybdenum from MoO2Cl2/H2, barrier-less, and run a chlorine-only metal stack.

title: Deuterium isotope passivation trims the access-transistor leakage tail
idea: Scale down to the isotope: anneal in D2 instead of H2 so interface traps are capped with Si-D bonds, which resist desorption and trap-assisted tunneling more strongly over years of operation, shrinking the GIDL tail.
note: High-pressure D2 anneal is known and already commercial.

title: Drop-in molybdenum precursor swap in existing tungsten CVD chambers
idea: Molecule-level substitution: replace WF6/H2 with fluorine-free MoO2Cl2 in the same CVD chamber hardware on existing trailing lines. Contacts and periphery lines fill with Mo, whose ~11 nm mean free path needs no TiN barrier at small widths.

title: Idle 65 nm back-end lines make interposers replacing glass-cloth substrates
idea: Scale shift from PCB laminate to wafer BEOL: existing 65-130 nm copper back-end lines pattern 2-4 metal-layer passive silicon interposers and bridges for DRAM packages and HBM-lite stacks. These replace BT/ABF laminates built on T-glass cloth.

title: 1970s molybdenum-gate MOSFETs revived as fluorine-free buried wordlines
idea: Mo-gate MOS of the 1970s was abandoned because molybdenum oxidized and etched badly next to polysilicon. A buried wordline entombs the metal: deposit Mo by ALD from MoO2Cl2 (chlorine, not fluorine) directly on a thin barrier, recess it, and seal it with SiN so oxidation never occurs.

title: Mo: molybdenum-chloride CVD replaces tungsten in periphery contacts
idea: Fill periphery contacts and wordline straps with Mo from MoO2Cl2 and H2 CVD (H2 carrier, N2 purge, no argon) instead of WF6 tungsten; Mo's short electron mean free path lowers resistance in narrow lines.

title: Gallium harvested from alumina-refinery Bayer liquor
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ga (31): install amidoxime ion-exchange columns on Bayer liquor (~100-200 ppm Ga) at U.S. and allied alumina refineries, turning a waste stream into tens of tonnes per year for oxide channels and GaN periphery power.
note: Bayer-liquor recovery is how nearly all primary gallium is already made.

title: Fluorine-free molybdenum buried wordlines from oxychloride ALD
idea: Periodic-table walk, Mo (42): deposit buried-channel wordlines by ALD Mo from MoO2Cl2 + H2 (chloride, no WF6); Mo's ~11 nm electron mean free path beats W's ~15.5 nm in 10 nm trenches, and without fluorine attacking the gate oxide the TiN barrier can be thinned or dropped.

title: Deuterium passivation of junction traps to shrink leakage tail
idea: IFR: no trap ever helps an electron hop. Replace the final forming-gas anneal with a high-pressure deuterium anneal so access-device interface and junction dangling bonds are capped by Si-D bonds, which resist thermal and hot-carrier dissociation far better than Si-H (kinetic isotope effect).
note: High-pressure deuterium anneal already used/studied for DRAM retention.

title: Gold-free, glass-cloth-free DRAM packaging via fan-out redistribution
idea: Ideal: a package that is just the chip. Closest: replace board-on-chip gold-wire FBGA packages on BT laminate (near-monopoly T-glass cloth) with wafer-level fan-out: copper RDL plated directly over a reconstituted mold wafer, solder balls on the RDL.

title: Getter-coated chamber walls replace helium-loop cryopumps
idea: Combine the chamber liner with the vacuum pump: sputter a TiZrV non-evaporable getter film on PVD chamber liners that pumps H2, CO and H2O at room temperature and reactivates during normal bake/seasoning, with small turbo pumps handling argon.
note: Cryopump helium is closed-loop; real helium saving small.

title: Aluminum-doped zinc oxide top plate replaces germanium SiGe fill
idea: Combine the plate electrode and pillar-forest gap fill (zero added masks, same plate mask): replace the boron-doped poly-SiGe plate fill over the TiN top electrode with ALD/CVD ZnO:Al, which fills conformally at ~200 C and conducts ~1e-3 ohm-cm.

title: On-die moisture sensor replaces helium leak testing of cavity packages
idea: Combine package sealing with an on-die interdigitated capacitive moisture sensor and micro-heater read out through DRAM test-mode registers: after sealing optical/mm-wave cavity memory packages, a short heat-soak and capacitance trend gives each unit's leak rate, and the sensor keeps monitoring in the field.

title: Rare-gas content ledger in packaging PDKs and CHIPS grants
idea: Combine the packaging process-design kit with a per-step bill of gases: each OSAT/fab step declares its He/Ne/Ar/Kr/Xe consumption, EDA flows total it per product, and CHIPS-style packaging grants pay a per-stack bonus for products built on rare-gas-free flows.

title: LCD polarity inversion cancels oxide-TFT bias stress
idea: Borrowed from LCD dot inversion, which keeps liquid crystal from DC drift: the periphery stores each row inverted on alternate refresh epochs, tracked by a per-row polarity bit, so IGZO access and sense transistors see near-zero average bias stress.

title: Organic-food certification model for PFAS-free capacitor-free memory
idea: Copy USDA Organic's audited-label model. Certify memory made in flows free of perfluorinated etch gases, PFAS photoacid generators and fluoropolymer wetted parts, which becomes achievable because a capacitor-free cell drops the 60:1 fluorocarbon etch, and sell it at a premium to EU buyers facing PFAS restrictions.

title: Eliminate open-bitline dummy edge mats: self-referenced double sampling
idea: Replace reference-from-neighbour-mat sensing with a sense amp that samples its own bitline before and after charge sharing on a small on-SA capacitor, so the half-used dummy mats at array edges disappear.
note: ~3-5% area only.

title: Crucible-free memory: laser-crystallized silicon gain cells on glass
idea: Reverse the substrate dependency: deposit amorphous silicon on glass or metal-foil panels and excimer-laser-crystallize it (1990s LTPS display process, >=1 um rules) into 2T gain cells, so the storage tier needs no Czochralski ingot, no high-purity quartz crucible and no 300 mm wafer.

title: Cache becomes main memory: DRAM-less servers for small-state services
idea: Reverse the hierarchy: services whose working set fits in large stacked caches (DNS, firewalls, routing, rate limiters, lookup services under ~256 MB across sockets) are rewritten to run entirely from 3D-stacked L3/SRAM with flash as backing, and their servers ship with one minimal DIMM or none.

title: Fluorescent tracers encode storage-stack chemistry for automated recycling sorting
idea: TRIZ #32 Color changes: dope each die's passivation with distinct carbon-dot or Mn:ZnS emission signatures that encode its storage-stack chemistry (Ru vs TiN electrodes, Hf vs Zr dielectric); shredder lines sort fragments optically into chemistry-matched streams for metal recovery.
note: Recycling niche with small memory impact.

title: Precursor cryo-trap recovery returns hafnium and ruthenium to suppliers
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: ALD uses only ~1-10% of its metal-organic precursor, so fit each ALD/CVD exhaust with a cold trap or adsorbent cartridge that captures unreacted Hf, Zr, Ru and Mo compounds, shipped back to the supplier for re-purification in a closed loop.

title: Camel-nose countercurrent water recovery from fab exhaust
idea: Camels recover water from exhaled breath with cooled, hygroscopic nasal turbinates. Put cyclically cooled, desiccant-coated turbinate heat exchangers in wet-scrubber and cooling-tower exhausts that capture vapour on the way out and release it as condensate during reverse-flow regeneration, feeding the UPW reclaim plant.

title: Nacre-stacked titania nanosheets printed as hafnium-free capacitor dielectric
idea: Copy nacre's brick-and-mortar layering: exfoliate layered titanate into 1 nm Ti0.87O2 nanosheets (k~125) and lay them down roll-to-roll by Langmuir-Blodgett transfer, interleaved with sub-nm polymer mortar that blocks leakage paths at sheet edges. Use the film as the storage capacitor of printed oxide-TFT memory cells or as decoupling sheets on DRAM modules.

title: Stencil spray-paint: shadow-mask deposition of periphery pads and power
idea: Like a graffiti stencil, deposit the periphery's wide top-level features (pads, power straps, redistribution at >=2 um) through a reusable silicon-nitride MEMS stencil held in proximity during sputtering or evaporation. No resist, develop, strip or post-etch clean.

title: OLED fine-metal-mask evaporation: resistless shadow patterning of thick metals
idea: Borrowed from OLED fabs, which pattern pixels by evaporating through fine metal masks with no photoresist: pattern DRAM's coarse top-metal, power grid and redistribution layers (>3 um lines) by depositing through reusable Invar shadow masks on a small-team-built aligner, deleting coat, expose, develop, etch and strip for those levels.

title: LCD polarity inversion: per-row epoch flip of stored data
idea: LCDs invert pixel polarity every frame so that DC stress does not cause image sticking. Each row stores its data XORed with a per-row epoch bit that toggles on every scrub pass, so no cell or access transistor holds the same charge polarity for months. The controller decodes with the flag bit.

title: Reinsurance pool: rack-level CXL spare memory absorbing failing pages
idea: Reinsurers pool rare risks across many insurers. Each rack keeps a shared CXL-attached spare pool of about 2% of rack capacity. The hypervisor live-migrates pages from any DIMM whose correctable-error rate rises into the pool, so individual DIMMs ship with thinner margins and fewer on-die spare rows.

title: Zipper pairing: interlock weak and strong columns across chips per codeword
idea: Zipper teeth alternate: at module test each chip's retention-weak column groups are profiled and a per-DIMM permutation table in the RCD/buffer reroutes column bits so every ECC codeword pairs one chip's weak column only with other chips' strong columns, guaranteeing at most one weak bit per codeword.
note: ~5% sellable-bit gain via buffer-chip remap.

title: Hibernating bear: hot-triggered compaction parks cold pages in strong rows
idea: Above ~105 C the controller or OS compresses cold pages 2-3x, packs them into the strongest-retention subarrays, and turns refresh off for the emptied subarrays (partial-array self-refresh).

title: Tea-kettle whistle: ECC error rate, not temperature, drives thermal throttling
idea: Per-bank on-die ECC correction counters feed the SoC power manager; when corrected-error rate crosses a budget, adjacent compute is throttled or cooling boosted, replacing fixed 85/95 C thresholds that assume worst-case cells.

title: Luggage tag: printed NFC history label for second-life DIMMs
idea: Random stimulus 'luggage tag' -> the bag carries its own itinerary. A roll-to-roll printed passive NFC tag with printed nonvolatile memory, laminated on each DIMM, logs power-on hours, peak temperature, row-hammer counters and retest results, signed by the operator.

title: Interposers made from reclaimed monitor and reject wafers
idea: Po: fab garbage is the interposer. Collect test, monitor and scratched prime wafers, re-polish them, laser-drill vias with no mask, and add one thick copper redistribution layer with a single mask for simple HBM-to-logic routing.

title: Bulk acoustic delay-line loop memory from RF filter fabs
idea: Worsen: build bits only in scarce DRAM fabs. Flip: store bits as acoustic pulses circulating in short AlN/ScAlN bulk-acoustic delay lines made by RF-filter foundries, with a CMOS regenerator per loop; a $1M, 24-month prototype targets 100 ns loops as a refresh-free buffer.
note: Delay-line density is tiny (~mm per kbit).

title: Magnetite-core ceria abrasives recaptured and reused tenfold
