idea: Eliminate any deep etch: deposit a strained SiNx bilayer by SiH4/NH3/N2 PECVD (no helium or argon dilution) topped with electrode and dielectric layers, then dissolve a sacrificial layer so the stack curls into a multi-turn nano-roll; a 30x30 nm footprint could host a coil with 5-10x the area of a planar capacitor.
note: Multi-layer stack rolls to hundreds of nm diameter; sub-30 nm multi-turn rolls unlikely.

title: Eliminate dopants: polarization-induced 2DEG GaN access transistor
idea: Replace the doped Si access device with an AlGaN/GaN heterostructure whose channel electrons come from spontaneous and piezoelectric polarization rather than dopants, turned off with a recessed p-GaN gate. No implant, no random dopant fluctuation and a 3.4 eV gap remove the junction and thermal-generation leakage tail.

title: Eliminate the Boltzmann limit: feedback-FET access device
idea: Use a gated p-i-n feedback FET whose intrinsic region holds charge barriers that collapse abruptly under positive feedback, giving <1 mV/dec switching. The device is hard off at 0 V gate and fully on near 1 V, so the 3 V wordline and the negative-wordline pump are removed.
note: A p-i-n feedback FET conducts one way and is hysteretic; an access switch must write both states.

title: Eliminate the semiconductor: ALD MIIM tunnel-diode 1D1C cell
idea: Isolate each capacitor with a metal-insulator-insulator-metal diode (ALD Al2O3/Ta2O5 between dissimilar work-function metals) whose step-tunneling barrier gives ~1e6 nonlinearity; cells are crosspoint-addressed by V/2 biasing, and at hold bias tunneling is exponentially suppressed. Every layer is a university ALD or sputter step.
note: Hold leakage at full storage voltage conflicts with write current.

title: Eliminate the channel: volatile Ag/Ag2S gap-type atomic switch access
idea: Use a gap-type atomic switch: a 1-2 nm vacuum gap between an Ag2S electrode and a Pt counter electrode, where a gate pulse grows a single-atom Ag bridge for access and the bridge dissolves spontaneously when bias is removed. The off state is a true vacuum gap with tunnel leakage below 1e-20 A.

title: Eliminate the consumable wafer: foil arrays stacked like paper
idea: Build thin-film DRAM arrays on a reusable sapphire carrier, release each 2-5 um array foil by laser lift-off, and laminate dozens of foils into a stack with printed vertical vias; the carrier returns to the line hundreds of times.
note: Printed vias cannot meet array pitch; thin-film cells on sapphire are leaky.

title: Eliminate pitch-defining lithography: rotated superlattice slices
idea: Grow a 1000-period Si/SiGe or Si/oxide multilayer whose film thicknesses set the 10-12 nm line pitch, slice it perpendicular to the layers, and bond the slab flat so the layers become parallel bitlines/channels; litho is needed only for coarse cuts.
note: Like SNAP superlattice transfer; tiling 12 um slabs across a wafer with alignment is the hurdle.

title: Eliminate regulator losses: series-stacked bank domains recycle bitline charge
idea: Stack four bank groups in series across 4x0.5 V rails so charge dumped from one bank's bitlines flows down to power the next domain instead of to ground, with a small switched-capacitor balancer absorbing load mismatch.
note: Charge recycling via stacked domains is known; 10x claim ignores load imbalance and balancer losses.

title: Eliminate the 1 V array: 0.25 V storage with auto-zeroed sense amps
idea: Store and sense at 0.25 V from an efficient buck rail and run all long data wires at 50-100 mV, using offset-cancelling sense amps that sample their own offset onto a capacitor before each activate.
note: 0.25 V storage gives tiny signal vs noise/leakage; offset cancellation helps but retention margin is thin.

title: Retention-dial memory: one die is both DRAM and storage
idea: Eliminate the DRAM-to-SSD copy and the two-chip BOM: use a spin-torque or ferroelectric cell whose write pulse width/amplitude sets retention (short pulse: hours, ~1e15 endurance, ns writes; long pulse: 10 years), with the base die re-writing pages in long-retention mode as they cool.
note: STT retention is set by thermal stability, not write pulse; mechanism questionable.

title: Access transistor turns avalanche amplifier during the read window
idea: Reverse the access device's job on read: for a 1 ns window its drain junction is biased just above breakdown, so the few hundred electrons released from a tiny 0.1 fF node trigger quenched impact-ionization gain of ~100 (SPAD-like) and produce a full-swing bitline signal; at idle it is a normal off transistor.

title: Grow, don't etch: VLS nanowire electrodes at 150:1 aspect ratio
idea: Reverse subtractive to additive: Al or Sn catalyst dots on each storage node grow vertical silicon nanowire electrodes by vapor-liquid-solid growth (150:1 is easy to grow and impossible to etch), then ALD high-k and a conformal top electrode wrap them.
note: Catalyst contamination, placement at DRAM pitch, and conformal ALD fill in a dense 150:1 forest remain hard.

title: Cell refreshes itself: storage-gated keeper on a pulsed restore rail
idea: Reverse who refreshes: instead of the periphery sensing and rewriting row by row, add a tiny second transistor to each cell whose gate is the storage node and whose channel links the node to a shared restore rail. Pulsing the rail to a boosted level (about VARY+Vt) tops up only cells still holding a '1' (their keeper is on) while '0' cells stay off, so one array-wide pulse refreshes millions of cells with no sense amps, no bitline swing and no bank lockout.
note: As described the keeper's gate equals its source when the rail is high (Vgs=0), so it cannot top up; topology needs rework.

title: Split the cell across wafers: capacitors bonded onto transistors
idea: Fabricate storage capacitors on a separate wafer where perovskite (Ba,Sr)TiO3 can be crystallized at 650-750 C (k~100-300), then bond it face-to-face onto the transistor wafer through a self-aligning nano-pad lattice and strip the capacitor carrier. Transistor and capacitor never share a thermal budget.

title: Pillars first, tiers grown around them
idea: Invert stack-then-etch: start with short vertical Mo bitline pillar stubs on the base, then build each tier bottom-up around them (deposit and planarize dielectric and channel), extending each pillar by area-selective deposition per tier, so no 60+ tier high-aspect-ratio hole etch is ever needed.
note: Area-selective deposition mushrooms laterally each tier; selectivity loss compounds over 60 tiers.

title: Let the pores place the cells: anodic alumina template
idea: Reverse 'cells define holes': anodize aluminum into a self-ordered hexagonal pore array (~40-60 nm pitch, AR >500), use the pores as capacitor molds, then self-align the access transistors to the pore lattice instead of drawing them by litho.
note: Pore lattice defects make transistor self-alignment hard.

title: Pattern once, select forever: permanent scaffold lattice
idea: Reverse 'one mask per layer': define one master dielectric grid by double spacer patterning at the very start and keep it as a permanent scaffold; every later layer only fills or opens grid cells, chosen with coarse i-line block masks.

title: Electron recapture pulse after aggressor activation bursts
idea: Reverse the hammer charge flow: after N activations of a row, the drivers apply a brief opposite-polarity pulse to the neighboring passing wordlines and local well contact to drift injected electrons back toward the aggressor's drain before they reach victim storage nodes.

title: Bistable buckled 2D-membrane nanodrum stores the bit as curvature
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution + #14 Spheroidality: a pre-compressed few-layer hBN or graphene membrane over a ~30-nm cavity buckles either up or down; an electrostatic pulse from the top or bottom electrode snaps it over, and its capacitance to the bottom electrode reads the state without disturbing it. No charge is stored, so nothing leaks.
note: Buckled-membrane bits studied; density and ns snap at 30 nm uncertain.

title: Self-rolled-up nanomembrane Swiss-roll capacitor in every cell
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells + #7 Nesting: deposit a strained TiN/ZrO2/TiN/SiN multilayer flat with no deep etch, then release a sacrificial layer so built-in strain rolls it into a 5-10-turn tube; each turn adds electrode area, and lateral rolls suit horizontal 3D DRAM tiers.

title: Self-ordered anodic-alumina pores host lithography-free coaxial access transistors
idea: TRIZ #31 Porous materials: anodise an aluminium foil or Al-coated glass panel so it self-organises into hexagonal nanopores at 30-60 nm pitch (~1e10-1e11 per cm2). ALD lines each pore coaxially with bottom electrode, wide-gap oxide channel, gate dielectric and a wrap gate at the top, with the lower pore volume forming the storage capacitor: gate-all-around access at near-4F2 density without EUV.

title: Hermetic NEMS relay access switch: an air gap is the perfect off-state
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution, inverted: replace the field-effect switch with an electrostatically actuated nano-cantilever relay built on glass and sealed in a vacuum/inert micro-cavity. Open, the gap gives zero channel leakage so retention is set only by capacitor dielectric leakage (minutes to hours); closed, a metal contact gives near-ideal write/read with abrupt switching at low actuation voltage.

title: Vacuum-nanogap field-emission access transistor on sapphire
idea: TRIZ #39 Inert atmosphere (vacuum): a <50 nm vacuum channel, operable near atmospheric pressure because it is shorter than the mean free path of air, separates a sharp emitter from the storage electrode on a sapphire substrate, with a surrounding gate modulating field emission. With no semiconductor in the channel there is no thermal generation or band-to-band leakage in the off state.
note: Writing a 0 needs emission from a blunt storage electrode; bidirectional low-voltage FN access is the doubt.

title: Thermal expansion: latching bimorph nano-relays as zero-leakage wordline decoders
idea: TRIZ #37 Thermal expansion: wordline decoders are built from bistable electrothermal bimorph nano-relays patterned in BEOL metal and oxide layers above the array, with no transistors; a heat pulse flexes a relay into contact where it latches mechanically, routing ~3 V wordline drive with zero off-state leakage.
note: Decoder relays switch on every activation; 1e9-1e12 cycles falls far short.

title: Feedback: shared sigma-delta loops read three bits per cell
idea: TRIZ #23 Feedback: after charge sharing each bitline holds its voltage on its own capacitance while one 1-bit sigma-delta modulator per 128 bitlines visits them in turn, feeding back charge packets until balanced, resolving 8 charge levels (3 bits) per planar cell in ~2 us instead of a binary latch per bitline.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as litho-free capacitor molds
idea: TRIZ #31 Porous materials, resolving 'taller capacitor vs. costlier etch': sputter ~3 um Al over the storage-node landing pads and let the pad topography seed pore nucleation. Anodizing then grows self-ordered 20-25 nm pores straight down at AR >150:1 in minutes; thin the barrier at the pore bottoms and ALD TiN / high-k / TiN into the pores, keeping the alumina as the mechanical support lattice.

title: Antiferroelectric gate held between its double loops as volatile bistable
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: use a ZrO2 antiferroelectric layer in each cell transistor's gate and park the wordline plane at a hold bias between the two hysteresis loops, where both the nonpolar and the field-induced polar phase are stable. A short over- or under-pulse toggles the phase and the channel Vt reads it.
note: AFE minor-loop endurance at ns speeds and hold-bias disturb are unproven.

title: Negative-capacitance gate stack amplifies tiny gain-cell storage charge
idea: TRIZ #8 Anti-weight: counter the 'weight' of a tiny stored charge with an internal uplift: add a thin ferroelectric layer to the read transistor's gate, matched to operate in its negative-capacitance regime, so the storage node's voltage is amplified at the channel surface. The storage node can then be just the bare gate (~0.1 fF) with an unchanged read margin.
note: Static negative capacitance remains contested; hysteresis-free gain at storage node unproven.

title: Anodized mesoporous silicon electrodes multiply capacitor area
idea: TRIZ #31 Porous materials: anodize heavily doped silicon electrode arms in HF to form 3-5 nm mesopores, line the pores with ALD Al2O3/TiO2 nanolaminate, and fill them with TiN, so each electrode becomes a sponge with ~3-10x the surface area.
note: 3-5 nm pores cannot hold a ~5 nm dielectric plus TiN fill at DRAM electrode widths.

title: Undercritical ferroelectric zinc-magnesium oxide adds negative-capacitance boost
idea: TRIZ #16 Partial action: place a thin wurtzite Zn1-xMgxO ferroelectric (a 2021 discovery made only of abundant elements) in series with Al2O3 and deliberately keep it just short of switching. It then operates in its negative-capacitance region and raises total stack capacitance above that of the Al2O3 alone.

title: Matryoshka multi-shell capacitor contacted by etch-selective recesses
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting resolves 'more charge but no taller hole': ALD alternating TiN and Ru electrode shells separated by ZrO2 inside one hole, then a TiN-selective top recess and a Ru-selective bottom recess tie odd shells to the storage node and even shells to the plate, giving 3-4 parallel capacitor walls per hole.
note: Multiple electrode/dielectric shells do not fit in a ~30-40 nm hole.

title: Stiction-latched nanopillar relay built with the capacitor-hole etch
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: use the existing 70:1 mold etch to free-stand a ~20 nm TiN pillar between two side electrodes; a pull-in pulse snaps its tip onto one electrode where van der Waals adhesion (stiction, normally a yield killer) holds it at zero power, and the read senses which side conducts.

title: Twin tunnel-diode latch grown where the capacitor used to be
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging joins storage and restoring in one element: epitaxially stack two Si/SiGe interband tunnel diodes in a short ~5:1 hole above the access transistor; their negative-differential-resistance curves cross at two stable node voltages, and with sub-pA peak current the node self-latches (TSRAM-style).
note: Sub-pA peak current with tight ITD variation at cell scale is the doubt.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric 3R-MoS2 channel as a refresh-free 1T cell
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: store the bit as the stacking order (AB vs BA) of a wafer-scale CVD-grown bilayer 3R-MoS2 channel; a gate pulse slides the layers by one bond length, flipping out-of-plane polarization and shifting threshold voltage, which persists without power and without mobile ionic defects to fatigue.

title: Elapsed-time-aware sensing reads decayed charge without refresh
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: instead of holding charge constant, make the read reference follow it - each row stores a few-bit write-epoch tag, and the sense reference is stepped down along the measured decay of matched reference cells written at the same time, keeping cells readable ~10x longer; paired with a page time-to-live, refresh is never issued.
note: Reference cells track median decay; tail/VRT cells still fail.

title: Nacre brick-and-mortar perovskite nanosheet capacitor dielectric
idea: Copy nacre, where staggered aragonite bricks sit in a thin organic mortar. Tile exfoliated Ca2Nb3O10-type perovskite nanosheets (k ~200 at 2-3 nm) in staggered, overlapping layers bonded by a 0.3 nm Al2O3 mortar, deposited by flow-coating into the capacitor. The staggered seams force leakage paths to wander, the way shell deflects cracks.

title: Photosynthetic cascade trap: stepped wells carry electrons out of reach
idea: Reaction centres prevent charge recombination by hopping the electron down a chain of acceptors, each step further away. Build the storage node as a graded staircase of 3-4 oxide-semiconductor quantum wells (e.g. IGZO/Ga2O3/ZnMgO with stepped conduction-band offsets) beside a transistor channel. A write pulse cascades electrons into the far well, where back-tunneling is exponentially suppressed by distance, shifting Vt non-volatilely; an opposite low-field pulse reverses the cascade.
note: Stepped barriers echo crested/VARIOT tunnel stacks; retention-vs-write-speed tradeoff persists.

title: Calcium-transient diffusive selector as a volatile two-terminal access switch
idea: Synaptic Ca2+ floods in and is cleared within ms; use an Ag-nanocluster diffusive threshold switch in sputtered SiO2 (room temperature) as the access device: a bitline-wordline pulse forms a filament that spontaneously dissolves within ~1 us, leaving a high-resistance off-state with ~1e10 on/off.
note: fA off-current and 1e15 endurance both orders beyond diffusive selectors today.

title: Magnetotactic self-alignment of single-crystal silicon nanowire access transistors
idea: Magnetotactic bacteria align along field lines via magnetosome chains; grow defect-free Si nanowires with gate-all-around shells at >900 C on a donor wafer, tip each with a Ni 'magnetosome' segment, release them into a fluid and pull them upright into pre-etched BEOL vias over the capacitor array with a magnetic field at room temperature, then contact them at low temperature.

title: Neuron-membrane ionic double-layer storage capacitor
idea: A neuron stores charge across a 4 nm membrane using ions, not a thick high-k oxide. Replace the 60-75:1 pillar with a planar cell that stores charge in the electric double layer at a TiN/solid proton-conductor interface (phosphosilicate glass or a CsH2PO4-type solid acid), reaching 10-30 uF/cm2 versus ~3 uF/cm2 for ZAZ, sealed by an ion-blocking ALD cap so ions never leave the cell.

title: DNA-brick crystal hardmasks replace EUV for array layers
idea: Grow 3D DNA-brick crystals with a honeycomb lattice at 24-36 nm pitch on a sparse DUV-printed guide, then mineralize them into a silica or alumina hardmask by sol-gel growth inside the DNA, the way biosilica forms on organic templates. Use it only for the storage-node and bitline-contact array layers, which are purely periodic.
note: Wafer-scale DNA crystal defectivity.

title: Pinecone hinges self-fold a planar array into ten stacked panels
idea: Pinecone scales fold by bilayer differential swelling; build a planar thin-film memory array on a released 1 um membrane with stress-engineered SiN/metal hinge strips between panels, then release it so the panels accordion-fold (Miura pattern) into a 10-high stack, with hinge lines carrying the bus wires to a base contact row.

title: Cortical folding: polyimide memory sheet folded into TSV-free stacks
idea: The cortex folds a thin sheet to fit a large area into a small skull. Oxide-TFT memory tiles are deposited directly on one continuous polyimide sheet with copper traces, tested flat, then folded accordion-style into a stack, so tier-to-tier wiring runs around the folds instead of through TSVs.

title: Magnetosome chains: exchange-couple low-stability bits for collective retention
idea: Magnetotactic bacteria align magnetite crystals too small to be stable alone into a stable chain dipole; build fast spin cells with thermal stability ~20 kT arranged in short exchange-coupled chains whose collective stability is ~60 kT, writing by flipping one end and letting a domain wall propagate along the chain.
note: Chain stability vs single-cell write conflicts; domain-wall propagation reliability.

title: Ion-channel memory made on battery gigafactory thin-film lines
idea: Neurons store state as ion distributions gated by channels. Electrochemical RAM cells push protons or Li ions into an oxide channel to set its conductance; electrolyte stacks (LiPON, ALD solid electrolytes) from U.S. battery thin-film lines are deposited over CMOS read circuits.
note: Li/proton ECRAM endurance and speed fall short of DRAM-class; battery-line reuse is the twist.

title: Heme-inspired spin-crossover molecular memory printed onto CMOS
idea: Hemoglobin's iron flips between high-spin and low-spin states when oxygen binds. Fe(II) spin-crossover complexes designed for room-temperature bistability and electric-field switching are printed or vapor-deposited over CMOS sense transistors, which read the spin state as a change in channel conductance.

title: Supercapacitor pseudocapacitance gives planar cells pillar-level charge
idea: Borrowed from supercapacitors: replace the 70:1 MIM pillar with a shallow cup lined by a 5-nm hydrous RuO2 or Ti3C2 MXene electrode against a 2-nm proton-conducting solid electrolyte (e.g., hydrated Zr-phosphate). Faradaic surface-redox capacitance of ~50-100 uF/cm2 versus ~3-5 uF/cm2 for ZrO2 MIM means a 30-nm cup only ~60 nm deep (AR~2) stores ~5 fF.
note: Faradaic redox completing in <10 ns with sub-fA self-discharge is the core doubt.

title: Quipu knots: topological polar textures as unknottable bits
idea: Inca quipu stored data in knots that cannot untie by accident; store a bit as the topological charge of a polar skyrmion or vortex in a 20-nm oxide-superlattice nanodisk (PbTiO3/SrTiO3, or lead-free BaTiO3/SrTiO3), which cannot relax continuously to the trivial state, switched by a field pulse from a top tip electrode and read by its distinct capacitance or tunneling conductance.
note: Polar skyrmions need epitaxial oxide superlattices; switching and read at 10 nm unproven.

title: Electrolytic-capacitor anodizing: alumina pore templates grow vertical access channels
idea: Aluminum electrolytic-capacitor makers anodize foil in oxalic or phosphoric acid, self-organizing billions of straight nanopores. Anodize a deposited aluminum film over the array (pitch 25-40 nm set by anodizing voltage), thin the pore-bottom barrier in phosphoric acid, then fill pores bottom-up with selective epitaxial silicon to form gate-all-around vertical access channels, with no fluorocarbon high-aspect-ratio etch anywhere.

title: Rubber vulcanization: sulfur-healed MoS2 vertical access channels at back-end temperature
idea: Vulcanization uses sulfur to cure rubber's weak links. Grow bilayer MoS2 by MOCVD from Mo(CO)6 and H2S at <=450 C on the capacitor top as a vertical access channel, 'vulcanize' its sulfur vacancies (the dominant trap and leakage path) with an in-situ H2S anneal, and encapsulate with ALD alumina from TMA/water instead of fluoropolymer passivation.

title: Image-sensor single-slope ramp ADC reads two bits per cell
idea: Copy the CMOS image sensor's column ADC: one global ramp generator per bank plus a 6-transistor comparator and 2-bit counter latch per bitline turn the developed bitline voltage into one of 4 levels; restore writes back one of 4 voltages from shared DAC rails.
note: Four levels in ~100 mV signal with leakage drift leaves ~20-30 mV steps.

title: Jellyroll-wound memory ribbon: battery winding replaces tier deposition
idea: Borrowing the lithium-ion jellyroll, fabricate a long released ribbon (thin polyimide on a sacrificial carrier) carrying one tier of low-temperature thin-film transistors and planar MIM capacitors, then wind it on a mandrel so every turn becomes a tier. Tier-to-tier and tier-to-logic contacts run through edge tabs exactly like battery current collectors, landing on a radial bus bonded to the CMOS base.
note: Registering edge tabs over 100 turns; low per-tier density.

title: Self-ordering anodic pore lattice sets the cell pitch litho-free
idea: Borrow anodized-aluminium battery and supercapacitor electrodes: anodize a deposited Al film over a coarse seed pattern (every 4th site) so it self-organizes into a hexagonal pore lattice at ~30 nm pitch and AR >100, then use the same pores as templates for both vertical-channel access transistors and capacitors in one self-aligned lattice.

title: Gearbox gate: negative-capacitance access transistor runs 0.8 V wordlines
idea: Like a gearbox multiplying torque, add a thin ferroelectric negative-capacitance layer matched to the access-transistor gate so the channel potential swings ~3x the wordline swing; drive wordlines 0-0.8 V while keeping the 13 fA off-state and drop the VPP charge pump.

title: Tesla-valve diode cells: crosspoint 1D1C array without wordline gates
idea: A Tesla valve rectifies flow with no moving parts; build a crosspoint 3D array where each capacitor is reached through a wide-bandgap Ga2O3/NiO heterojunction thin-film diode, selected by coincidence of a 1.2 V row-plate pulse and a bitline offset, removing the 3 V gated wordline and the access transistor.
note: A diode cannot both write 0 and 1 cleanly; sub-fA reverse leakage per cell needed.

title: LTPS excimer-laser crystallization builds polysilicon tiers at low temperature
idea: Borrowed from AMOLED backplanes, which turn amorphous Si into polysilicon with line-beam excimer lasers without heating the glass: deposit a-Si for each 3D DRAM tier and laser-crystallize it in nanoseconds, so tiers stack on finished CMOS and earlier tiers within BEOL thermal budgets.

title: Window-glass trick: vertical infrared optical bus through silicon stack
idea: Silicon is as clear at 1310 nm as window glass is to sunlight. A laser array on the base die shines straight up through the thinned die stack. Every tier has resonant-cavity detectors tuned to its own wavelength, so each takes only its channel and lets the rest pass. Return traffic uses modulated retroreflectors.
note: BEOL metal in every tier blocks light; needs windows and per-tier detectors.

title: DSL-on-old-copper: multi-tone HBM over plain organic substrate
idea: DSL got broadband out of old phone wire. Use DMT/OFDM multi-tone signaling, with bits loaded per tone, on cm-long traces in organic substrate. Wide memory stacks then connect with no silicon interposer or bridge.
note: DMT DSP power far exceeds 1-2 pJ/bit at HBM widths.

title: Electrolytic-capacitor memory: pseudocapacitive planar cell beats the pillar wall
idea: Early electrolytic storage used electrochemical double layers for enormous capacitance. Deposit ALD hydrous RuO2 or MnO2 with a solid proton-conducting electrolyte as a planar storage capacitor on an existing 65/90-nm logic flow, reaching ~5 fF in ~0.05 um2 with no high-aspect-ratio etch.
note: ns ion response and self-discharge.

title: Plasma-panel sustain refresh: threshold-gated global top-up pulses
idea: Revive the AC plasma display's inherent memory, in which a global sustain waveform re-fires only the cells that already hold wall charge: place a sharp threshold element (for example a punch-through diode) between each storage node and a shared sustain plane, then pulse the plane. Only nodes still above threshold (stored 1s) conduct and are topped up to full, while 0s stay below threshold and are left alone.

title: Crested-barrier MIM tunnel diode as a two-terminal access device
idea: Revive Mead's 1960 metal-insulator-metal tunnel-emitter work and Likharev's crested-barrier proposal: a nitride/alumina/nitride trilayer with a peaked barrier gives Fowler-Nordheim nonlinearity steep enough that current at half bias is ~1e-9 of full-bias current. It serves as a two-terminal access device between capacitor and bitline, selected by plate-line pulsing, so access devices can stack in BEOL above logic.

title: Plasma-panel sustain waveform refreshes cells without sensing
idea: AC plasma displays (1964) held every pixel with nothing but a global sustain pulse and wall-charge bistability. Give each cell a series threshold-switching selector (e.g., NbOx) to a global pulsed sustain rail: cells still above threshold (decaying 1s) conduct and are topped up, and cells near zero stay off. The whole array refreshes in one global pulse, with no row activation and no sense amp.

title: Geiger-tube avalanche junction amplifies bitline charge
idea: Like a Geiger-Müller tube or a modern SPAD: one added implant mask forms a high-field p+/n junction at each sense node, biased just below breakdown, with the bitline voltage setting its reverse bias. The signal's sign decides whether impact-ionization multiplication (~10-50x) happens before the latch fires, and the junction is then quenched.
note: Geiger-mode charge gain at sense node; dark counts and breakdown spread across millions of SAs are the doubt.

title: Zuse Z1 mechanical memory shrunk to buckled silicon-carbide nanobeams
idea: Revive Konrad Zuse's 1938 sheet-metal mechanical memory as NEMS: a SiC nanobeam pre-buckled by residual stress snaps between up and down states under electrostatic pull and is read capacitively without switching. Because the state is mechanical geometry, no charge can leak away.
note: Buckled-beam NEMS memories exist in research; 1e15+ endurance and density at DRAM pitch are the doubts.

title: 1990s BST capacitor revived with US-molybdenum SrMoO3 electrodes
idea: Revive the abandoned gigabit-era barium-strontium-titanate capacitor (k~200-300) using conductive perovskite SrMoO3 electrodes, with molybdenum mined in Colorado, instead of Pt/Ru. The dielectric grows lattice-matched without a low-k dead layer.
note: BST thin-film dead layer and leakage killed it; SrMoO3 oxidizes in BST growth ambient.

title: Williams tube reborn: microcolumn e-beams write charge on blank plates
idea: Revive the 1947 Williams-Kilburn tube: an i-line-patterned array of field-emission microcolumns at 2 um pitch, in a sealed MEMS vacuum, each steers a ~10 nm spot over a 200x200-bit patch of an UNPATTERNED SiO2/Si3N4 storage plate. The beams write charge and read it back by secondary-emission current, so bit density comes from the beam spot, not from lithography.

title: Anodized-alumina pores as self-ordered capacitor holes, no plasma etch
idea: Revive 1960s anodized thin-film capacitor chemistry: anodize an aluminum layer over the transistor array so self-ordered hexagonal pores (40 nm pitch, aspect ratio 100+:1) grow without lithography or plasma etch. The pores are lined with ALD TiN/Al2O3-TiO2/TiN, and each DUV-defined landing pad collects several pores in parallel.

title: Tunnel-diode SRAM revived with SiGe interband diodes in contacts
idea: Revive the 1960s Esaki tunnel-diode store and TI's 1990s tunneling SRAM (one transistor plus two series negative-resistance diodes) using CVD-grown Si/SiGe resonant interband tunnel diodes stacked inside the cell contact plug, so the bistable latch sits under the bitline contact. The cell is static at near-1T area, so the capacitor module is deleted.

title: Vacuum-channel nano-triode as a leakage-free DRAM access switch
idea: Revive the vacuum tube at 50 nm: replace the access transistor with a vacuum-channel triode whose emitter tip and collector are separated by a ~30 nm sealed vacuum gap made by an undercut etch and gated by a surrounding electrode. A vacuum gap has no junction or GIDL path, so the capacitor leaks only through its dielectric.

title: Hydrogen-ion projection exposes straight capacitor holes, no plasma etch
idea: Revive the 1990s-2000s European ion projection lithography, which pushed helium ions through stencil masks, using protons from a hydrogen source instead: 100-200 keV protons cross ~2 um of resist with almost no lateral scatter, so stencil projection exposes capacitor holes at AR >100 directly in a thick resist mold that ALD then fills.

title: Bubble-memory chevron ratchets driven by one global rotating field
idea: Revive 1970s bubble memory's key trick, a global rotating in-plane field that moves every domain one step per cycle along permalloy chevrons: nanoimprint asymmetric pinning chevrons into e-beam-evaporated Co/Pt or ferrimagnetic multilayers (no argon sputtering) and drive all tracks with a GHz rotating field from two crossed package striplines. No per-track transistor or current is needed; only read and write heads sit at the loop ends.
note: GHz rotating field strength and sub-50 nm domain stability doubtful.

title: Plasmonic contact printing with UV LEDs and disposable masks
idea: Revive 1970s contact printing, abandoned because masks wore out, with two 2026 fixes: each wafer gets a disposable conformal mask nanoimprinted from a master, and a 365 nm UV-LED source excites surface plasmons in the mask's silver layer so near-field exposure resolves ~22 nm half-pitch. No laser gas and no mercury-lamp argon or xenon fill is involved.

title: Solid-state Williams tube: charge puddles in an unpatterned film
idea: Invert 'each bit needs a discrete patterned capacitor' -> store charge puddles in a continuous film. A semi-insulating high-k layer (rho ~1e15 ohm-cm) lies between orthogonal row/column electrode grids with a thin rectifying MIM-diode interlayer; charge injected at a crossing stays local because lateral RC spreading takes longer than seconds, like the 1947 Williams CRT memory in solid form.

title: Resonant-tunneling-diode pinning lets all cells self-restore simultaneously
idea: Invert 'refresh means reading each row and writing it back' -> let every cell restore itself at once. Each storage node connects to a shared pulsed rail through a series pair of BEOL resonant-tunneling diodes whose N-shaped I-V gives two stable node voltages; a ~1 ns global rail pulse every few ms snaps all cells to the nearer level without sensing or row activation.

title: Self-assembled random nanodot capacitors with post-fab address remapping
idea: Invert 'every cell must be lithographically placed, identical and good' -> accept random cells and map them. Block-copolymer self-assembly drops ~15 nm metal nanodot capacitors at random over a relaxed 40 nm crossbar; built-in self-test classifies each crossing (empty, one dot, several, retention class) and writes a remap table so the controller uses only good sites.

title: Ferroelectric nematic liquid-crystal capacitors filled like LCD panels
idea: Invert 'the capacitor dielectric must be a deposited solid' -> use a liquid. Ferroelectric nematic LCs (RM734/DIO class) show apparent permittivity of 1e3-1e4; display fabs capillary-fill them into nano-trench capacitors on glass with oxide-TFT access and seal them exactly as LCD lines do.
note: Same ferroelectric nematic LC capacitor dielectric.

title: Charge-density-wave phase bits in 1T-TaS2 films on sapphire
idea: Invert 'storage needs atoms or spins to move' -> store the bit in collective electron order. 1T-TaS2 switches between insulating and metallic charge-density-wave states with ps-ns electrical pulses and holds each with hysteresis; wafer-scale CVD TaS2 on sapphire gives cells read by a ~10-100x resistance contrast.

title: Nanoimprinted sol-gel high-k cup capacitors on roll-to-roll polymer web
idea: Invert 'capacitor geometry is defined by lithography plus etch' -> stamp it. A reusable master with 30 nm x 600 nm pillars imprints cup cavities into spin-on TiO2/BaTiO3 sol-gel on polyimide web, then ALD electrodes coat them, replacing EUV and HAR plasma etch with mechanical replication at metres per minute.
note: TFT speed and overlay on polymer web are far from DRAM needs.

title: Nanomechanical relay access: an air gap is the off-state
idea: Inverts 'the switch must be a semiconductor': each storage capacitor is isolated by an electrostatically actuated NEMS cantilever relay (Ru- or carbon-coated beam over a ~5 nm air gap) that physically breaks contact, so the OFF state is an open circuit and leakage is only through the capacitor dielectric. Bitlines are equalized before contact closes (cold switching) so contacts survive >10^15 cycles.

title: Vacuum-nanogap field-emission access: electrons cross nothing when off
idea: Inverts 'carriers flow through a solid channel': the storage node ends in a sharp nanotip facing the bitline across a sealed ~10 nm vacuum gap; a wordline gate raises the local field above emission threshold for read/write, while below it the exponential Fowler-Nordheim law gives >10^12 on/off with no channel to leak. Gaps are made by sacrificial-layer release plus a wafer-level hermetic ALD seal.

title: Leakage-keeper latch: make the leaks hold the bit, stacked vertically
idea: Inverts 'leakage destroys stored data': build a loadless 4-device latch where the access devices' OFF leakage is engineered ~10x larger than the cross-coupled drivers' leakage, so leakage itself replenishes the high node and the cell is static with no refresh. Stack the four devices in two BEOL tiers (n-type and p-type oxide channels) over CMOS so the footprint approaches a 1T1C cell.
note: Loadless 4T SRAM known (NEC); p-type oxide channels are poor, stability margins tight.

title: Battery bit: store data as redox state, not loose charge
idea: Inverts 'a bit is free charge on a capacitor': each cell is a nanoscale solid-state redox couple (e.g., proton-intercalated WO3 against a reservoir) whose open-circuit potential encodes the bit; leakage only slowly shifts state of charge, and a gain transistor whose gate sits on the redox electrode reads it nondestructively.
note: ECRAM-like; 10-100 ns ion kinetics and endurance doubtful.

title: Predictable decay: compensate unrefreshed analog weights instead of refreshing
idea: Inverts 'decay is an error to prevent': store neural-net weights as 4-6-bit analog charge in simple unrefreshed capacitor cells whose decay is a known exponential, and have the accelerator scale each tile's outputs by exp(+t/tau) using a per-tile timestamp and reference cell, reloading tiles from a NAND copy every few seconds.
note: Per-cell tau spread is lognormal over decades; a per-tile exp correction cannot fix it.

title: Wafer-on-edge stack: deposition thickness sets the cell pitch
idea: Inverts 'the array is patterned face-up by lithography.' Deposit ~300 alternating Si/SiO2 (or n+/p) layer pairs, saw the wafer into slabs, rotate each slab 90 degrees and bond its cut edge to a logic wafer, so film thickness rather than EUV sets one cell pitch; only the orthogonal pitch is patterned, by coarse litho on the exposed edge.

title: All-silicon tier superlattice isolated by doping-selective porosification
idea: Inverts '3D tiers need Si/SiGe epitaxial superlattices.' Grow alternating p+ and lightly doped Si epi layers, electrochemically convert only the p+ layers to porous Si through slits, then oxidize them into buried oxide, giving stacked single-crystal SOI tiers from Si and B alone.

title: Cu2O/ZnO all-oxide CMOS periphery tier above the array
idea: Inverts 'sense amps and decoders must be silicon CMOS under the array.' Build complementary oxide transistors (p-type Cu2O, n-type ZnO:Al) in a BEOL tier over the cell field to hold local sense amps and decoders, freeing the silicon below for more array.
note: p-type Cu2O mobility and matching too poor for sense amps; moving periphery over array is the right target.

title: DNA origami places capacitor sites without EUV
idea: Inverts 'arrays must be patterned by light': DNA origami tiles made by bacterial fermentation self-assemble onto coarse pre-patterned landing pads and carry metal-oxide nanoparticle hardmask dots at 10-15 nm pitch that define capacitor and contact positions; the DNA is burned off after pattern transfer.
note: DNA-templated lithography is known; placement defectivity and registration at 10-15 nm are unproven at wafer scale.

title: Nano-relay switch with vacuum capacitor: zero off-current cells
idea: Inverts 'the access device is a leaky transistor and the capacitor needs high-k': replace the access transistor with a ~50 nm electrostatic nano-relay whose open contact is a true vacuum gap (no subthreshold current) and store charge on a plain SiO2 or vacuum-gap capacitor in the same sealed cavity, so retention is set only by surface leakage (years).
note: Relay contact endurance (~1e9-1e12) far below DRAM access counts; cell area large.

title: Sliding ferroelectric boron nitride bilayers: switch by gliding, not ions
idea: Inverts 'polarization switching means displacing ions, which fatigues': store the bit in the stacking order (AB vs BA) of a bilayer hexagonal boron nitride, flipped by a vertical field that slides the layers one bond length; sliding creates no vacancies, so endurance may be effectively unlimited.
note: Sliding ferroelectricity demonstrated in lab flakes; wafer-scale controlled bilayer stacking and readout unresolved.

title: Silicon double-barrier quantum-well memory: UltraRAM without indium or antimony
idea: Inverts 'nonvolatile memory must be slow and high-voltage': gate a floating node through a Si/SiO2/Si/SiO2 double barrier (two 1-2 nm oxides around a ~2 nm silicon well) that only conducts when a ~2.5 V write aligns the well level (resonant tunneling) and is opaque otherwise, giving ns writes and years of retention.

title: Self-rolling strained films make Swiss-roll capacitors
idea: Inverts 'capacitors are etched into the substrate'. Pattern a strained bilayer (SiNx stressor plus metal/dielectric/metal) at 1 um rules on a sacrificial layer; on release it rolls into a 10-20-turn tube that multiplies plate area per footprint ~20x, then the rolls are anchored and planarized as a capacitor tier.

title: Rank-modulation sensing via winner-take-all on charge order
idea: Store data as the ORDER of charge levels among a group of cells, read by a winner-take-all network that finds which cells hold the most charge. Uniform leakage at 125 C lowers all charges together but preserves order, so no absolute reference is needed.

title: All-perovskite SrTiO3 capacitors on SrMoO3 electrodes shrink lateral 3D cells
idea: In 3D DRAM the lateral capacitor sets cell length and capacitance per area scales with k, so SrTiO3 (k~150-300) shortens it ~5x versus ZrO2. Use lattice-matched SrMoO3 (~1.8% mismatch, ~5 uOhm-cm, the most conductive oxide) for both electrodes, with an oxygen-getter interlayer to stop insulating SrMoO4 forming.

title: Dopant-free Schottky tiers skip implant in buried 3D layers
idea: Implanters cannot reach buried tiers anyway, so remove dopants: use 6 nm undoped Si channels with nickel-silicide Schottky source/drain formed by lateral silicidation from the bitline hole, and set threshold by gate work function.

title: Ninety-degree hydrothermal zinc-oxide nanowires form vertical gain-cell forests
idea: Crystal growth needs supersaturation, not vacuum: ZnO nanowires grow from zinc nitrate/HMTA solution at 90 C on seed dots placed at 20 nm pitch by DUV plus pitch division. Each wire is a 4F2 vertical gain-cell channel; repeat seeding to build 5 decks.
note: Single nanowire per 20 nm seed and hydrogen donor background doping make off-state control doubtful.

title: Complementary SnO/ZnO sense amplifiers live inside the memory tiers
idea: Periphery is ~49% of the die because sense amps need CMOS on the substrate; p-type SnO (Sn2+ 5s hole band) plus n-type ZnO gives an oxide CMOS that deposits in the same tiers, so each tier carries its own sense/latch beside its cells.
note: SnO hole mobility and oxide-TFT Vt variation undermine sense-amp matching.

title: Vicinal-wafer atomic step bunches as litho-free wordline templates
idea: First principle: a Si wafer miscut by angle theta has atomic steps every a/tan(theta), and controlled step bunching during anneal forms periodic facets at a 10-30 nm pitch set only by theta and temperature. Decorate the bunched step edges by step-flow selective deposition (e.g., CaF2 or a silicide) to make parallel hard-mask lines across the whole wafer in one anneal, with zero lithography, for the wordline and bitline layers.
note: Step bunching pitch uniformity and line cuts/registration unproven.

title: Smart-window electrochromic glass as analog weight-stationary crossbars
idea: Ion intercalation in WO3/NiO films, the chemistry of US-made smart windows, holds a non-volatile analog conductance that changes only when ions are driven. Pattern crossbars of these cells on window-glass coating lines, so frozen inference weights sit in place as conductances and matrix-vector products happen through Ohm's and Kirchhoff's laws, with no weight bits in DRAM.
note: ECRAM known; window coating lines cannot meet device geometry; drift.

title: Pottery glaze: nanoscale barrier-layer giant-k capacitor dielectric
idea: Stimulus 'glazed pottery' (conductive body, insulating skin) -> build the dielectric from 3-5 nm oxygen-deficient TiO2-x grains each wrapped in a ~1 nm Al2O3 skin by alternating chloride/organometallic ALD; charge piles up at the many thin internal barriers (the CaCu3Ti4O12 trick) for an effective k of several hundred.
note: Maxwell-Wagner giant k relaxes at high frequency and leaks; 8 nm films hold only 1-2 grains.

title: Kitchen sponge: electrodeposited MnO2 pseudocapacitive storage node
idea: Stimulus 'kitchen sponge' (soaks up far more than its surface suggests) -> coat the storage node with ~3 nm MnO2 grown by aqueous electrodeposition from a manganese sulfate bath, with a thin hydrated ZrO2 proton conductor as solid electrolyte; surface Mn3+/Mn4+ redox stores ~10-50x the charge of a dielectric of equal area.
note: Faradaic MnO2 kinetics are ms-scale; ns charge/discharge and retention unproven.

title: Mood ring: fluorine-free ferroelectric nematic fluid in nanowells
idea: Stimulus 'mood ring' (liquid crystal that changes state) -> fill 20 nm wells with an RM734-class ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (a polar fluid with ~6 uC/cm^2 and no fluorine, unlike most display LCs); a field pulse flips the polar director up or down and boundary anchoring holds it, read as a polarization current or capacitance. A fluid self-heals, so there are no fatigue-causing defects.

title: Weathervane: surface-anchored dipolar molecular rotors with nitrile dipoles
idea: Stimulus 'weathervane' (points one way until pushed) -> a monolayer of tripod-anchored molecular rotors whose paddle carries a strong nitrile/nitro dipole (not the usual fluorinated dipole groups), designed with two detents 180 degrees apart; a gate field flips the paddles and the collective dipole shifts a FET threshold by ~0.3 V.
note: Same rotor-dipole FET bit; flip field for a retention-grade barrier is impractically high.

title: Mousetrap NbO2 threshold switch in series with storage contact
idea: Random stimulus 'mousetrap': nothing happens until the trigger passes a threshold, then it snaps. Insert a thin NbO2 threshold-switching layer in the storage-node contact; in retention the tiny voltage across it keeps it insulating as a second, non-MOS leakage barrier, while the ~VARY/2 seen during access snaps it conductive in nanoseconds.
note: NbO2 selectors leak far above fA; series threshold switch idea known for crosspoints.

title: Library whisper: virtual-ground charge-transfer sensing keeps bitlines frozen
idea: In a library nobody raises their voice: hold every bitline at a fixed potential with a cascode charge-transfer amplifier so it never swings; the cell's charge flows through into a ~0.5 fF integrating node at the SA, giving a large local voltage, and restore pushes the same charge back through the cascode.
note: Restoring a 1 needs the cell node, and so the bitline, at VDD; a bitline that never swings cannot restore.

title: Sourdough starter: bacterial S-layer protein crystals as nanohole templates
idea: Random stimulus 'sourdough starter' (living culture self-propagates) -> recrystallized bacterial surface-layer proteins form 2D lattices with 10-30 nm spacing and hexagonal or square symmetry on wafers. They are used, after mineralization, as hardmask templates for storage-node hole arrays, and their crystallization is guided by a coarse prepattern.
note: S-layer patterning known; domain size and registration limit.

title: Compass needle: voltage-controlled anisotropy lets one transistor serve many MTJs
idea: Random stimulus 'compass needle' (flipped by a field, no current) -> MTJs written by voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy, with precessional switching at near-zero current. The access transistor no longer needs to be wide, so 8-16 MTJs share one transistor in a 1T-nMTJ string at relaxed 28-40 nm litho.

title: Thermos flask: NEM relay access device with vacuum-isolated storage node
idea: Random stimulus 'thermos' (a vacuum gap stops heat leaking) -> the access transistor of a DRAM-like cell is replaced by a nano-electromechanical relay whose open contact is a vacuum gap, and the storage node sits in a sealed air-gap cavity. Off-state leakage is essentially zero, so charge persists for years.

title: Hologram sticker: photopolymer slab stores weights read by light
idea: Credit-card holograms are cheap: record model weights as page holograms in a room-temperature-cured photopolymer slab and read millions of bits per laser flash onto a CMOS image sensor beside the accelerator, streaming weights optically instead of holding them in DRAM.

title: Complementary oxide-TFT sense amplifiers built in the metal stack
idea: Box: 1T1C x IGZO access x CMOS-TFT latch (n-IGZO + p-SnO) x monolithic over array x Si x 400 C sputter BEOL. Cross-coupled latches and column muxes are made as stacked oxide thin-film transistors directly over the cell array, so periphery stops competing for silicon area.
note: p-type oxide mobility and Ioff are the blockers.

title: Solid-electrolyte double-layer nanocapacitors as DRAM storage nodes
idea: [Box: electric-double-layer ionic charge | Si VCT | charge-share SA | BEOL over array | Si | ALD solid proton/Li-ion conductor between blocking electrodes] Replace the dielectric with an ultrathin solid electrolyte so charge sits in Helmholtz double layers (~20 uF/cm2, roughly 3x a 0.5 nm-EOT high-k), giving ~5 fF with only ~10:1 aspect ratio.
note: Same as I-04769 with proton/Li conductors; ionic response time is the blocker.

title: Anodic alumina pore lattice as mask-free 4F2 VCT array template
idea: [Box: MIM charge | coaxial IGZO VCT grown inside pores | charge-share SA | BEOL over CMOS | Si | Al anodization, no lithography for the cell lattice] Deposit Al over the bitlines, pre-texture it with a coarse ArF seed grid, and anodize to grow self-ordered hexagonal pores at ~25-40 nm pitch; ALD gate oxide, IGZO channel and storage contact coaxially inside each pore, with pore walls as the gate spacer.

title: Self-rolling strained nanomembrane capacitors coil into cell-size towers
idea: [Box: rolled multilayer MIM charge | VCT | charge-share SA | BEOL | Si | strained bilayer deposition + sacrificial release, coarse ArF patches only] Deposit a strained TiN/high-k/TiN stack on a sacrificial film; releasing each patch makes it roll into a multi-turn Swiss-roll tube anchored on its pad, with capacitance set by film area and number of windings.

title: Spacer-split pillars give two cells per 4F2 footprint
idea: [Box: two half-capacitors | split VCT with two independent channel faces | charge-share SA | monolithic | Si | ArF pillars + self-aligned spacer slot] Pattern pillars at relaxed ArF pitch, then cut each in half with a self-aligned spacer-defined slot so its two faces become separate channels gated by left and right wordlines, each tied to its own half-capacitor.
note: Two half-capacitors at 2F2 each worsen the charge wall; slot-split channel control is hard.

title: Wurtzite ZnMgO ferroelectric capacitors replace hafnia and scandium
idea: Box [Zn0.6Mg0.4O ferroelectric polarization | Si access | charge sense with write-back | near-planar stacked cap | CZ Si | ALD/MOCVD]: use wurtzite zinc-magnesium oxide, whose ~80 uC/cm2 switchable polarization gives roughly 10x the signal charge of a 5 fF linear cap in a near-planar footprint.

title: DNA-origami masks pattern sub-10 nm capacitor arrays without EUV
idea: Box [ZrO2 cap | Si access | voltage SA | standard | Si | DNA-origami self-assembly on coarse docking sites + silica mineralization]: dock origami tiles carrying a programmed honeycomb of 8 nm openings onto DUV-defined sites, mineralize them with DNA-templated sol-gel silica into a hard mask, and transfer the hole array into the capacitor mold.

title: Bottom-up VLS-grown vertical nanowire access transistors on landing pads
idea: Box: Si capacitor charge x vertical gate-all-around Si nanowire grown, not etched x voltage sense amp x capacitor-over-transistor x Si x vapor-liquid-solid growth from Al or Sn catalyst dots placed by electroless self-aligned deposition on bitline contacts. ALD then wraps the gate and a spacer etch forms wordlines, giving a 4F2 vertical cell without an EUV pillar exposure.

title: Area-selective deposition grows capacitor electrodes up from landing pads
idea: Box: TiN/ZrO2 capacitor charge x standard BCAT x voltage sense amp x 2D x Si x area-selective CVD with inhibitor monolayers. Instead of depositing a 1.5 um mold, etching 70:1 holes and stripping the mold, Ru or TiN pillars grow upward only on the landing pads while the dielectric is inhibitor-passivated, then high-k and top electrode fill around them.

title: Nanoelectromechanical relay access device with true zero off-leakage
idea: Box: MIM charge x vertical NEMS contact relay (TiN beam over an ALD sacrificial gap) x voltage sense amp x BEOL x Si x three-mask surface micromachining plus vapor-HF release. An open relay passes no current, so the leakage tail (fact 3) and refresh vanish, and the device needs only sputter, ALD and release tools.

title: Strain-driven self-rolling nanomembranes form Swiss-roll capacitors per cell
idea: Box: multi-turn rolled MIM charge x planar oxide TFT x standard sensing x vertical tube x Si x stress-engineered PECVD SiNx bilayer on a sacrificial Ge layer. A flat stack (strained bilayer, metal, ALD oxide, metal) is patterned with contact litho and released, and built-in strain rolls it into a 3-5 turn tube that multiplies capacitor area 10-50x per footprint with no high-AR etch.

title: CVD-grown carbon-nanotube forests as high-area storage-node electrodes
idea: Box: MIM-on-CNT charge x planar access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x catalytic CVD of vertically aligned CNT bundles from lift-off-patterned Fe/Al2O3 dots on each storage pad. ALD Al2O3/HfO2 and TiN then wrap the forest, whose ~100x surface area per footprint gives fF-scale capacitance from small pads without etching holes.
note: Forest density on sub-100 nm pads and ALD nucleation on CNT are unproven.

title: Capacitively bootstrapped neighbor wordlines dip negative during activation
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: low-Vt planar | sense: standard | integration: monolithic with MIM coupling caps between adjacent wordline drivers | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. A small coupling capacitor between each wordline driver and its neighbours' hold nodes pulls neighbours ~0.5 V negative exactly while the aggressor is high, passively closing victim access devices; this lets a low-Vt access transistor run with a ~1.5 V wordline.
note: Low-Vt access still leaks in standby; coupling only helps during activation.

title: Double-sampling sense amps catch late-resolving bits at low voltage
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: Razor-style dual-sample sense with shadow latch | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Each sense amp latches at a nominal time and again ~1.5 ns later; a disagreement marks a slowly resolving low-signal bit, which is corrected from the shadow sample and its row queued for restore at higher voltage.

title: Po: a door opening to a secret knock — resonant-tunnelling floating node
idea: Po: a door that only opens for the right knock. Extracted: wrap the storage node in a Si/SiGe/SiO2 double-barrier stack whose resonant level aligns only at the write bias; at hold bias it is off-resonance and opaque (hours of retention), at write bias electrons pass resonantly in ns at low field without damaging the oxide.
note: Si/SiO2 resonant tunneling weak at room temperature; UltraRAM-like concept.

title: Po: the capacitor is a sponge — dealloyed nanoporous storage electrode
idea: Po: the capacitor is a sponge. Extracted: deposit a TiN-Al alloy into a shallow cup, selectively dealloy the Al to leave a nanoporous TiN electrode with 5-10x surface area, then ALD-coat dielectric and top electrode through the pores (a nanoscale successor to hemispherical-grain silicon).
note: ALD dielectric plus top electrode would clog nanopores inside 30-40 nm cups.

title: Po: nobody knows where the bits are — random nanoparticle self-mapped crossbar
idea: Po: nobody knows where the bits are. Extracted: spin-coat charge-storing nanoparticles at random between two imprinted line grids; after fabrication the chip probes every crossing, keeps those with a working node, and stores the map in a small on-die table, replacing costly placement with a one-time self-test.
note: Defect-tolerant self-mapping (Teramac-like); reading single-nanoparticle charge without a transistor is the doubt.

title: Vacuum-channel field-emission nanotriode as DRAM access device
idea: Po: the transistor channel is empty. Build the access device as a sealed ~10 nm vacuum gap between a sharp emitter tip on the bitline side and the storage node, gated by a wordline ring; electrons cross only when the gate field thins the emission barrier, so the off state has no semiconductor, no junction and no GIDL.

title: Po: a photon-counter sense amp — Geiger-mode silicon junction
idea: Po: a sense amp as sensitive as a photon counter. Gate a pair of small Si p+/n junctions just above breakdown (Geiger mode, as in a SPAD) during sensing; the bitline differential biases which side avalanches first, the avalanche current latches that side, and a doped-poly quench resistor resets it.

title: Block-copolymer gyroid sponge as a giant-area storage capacitor
idea: Po: the capacitor is a sponge. Self-assemble a block copolymer into a gyroid network over each access transistor, convert it to a porous metal scaffold with ~10 nm struts, island it per cell with a shallow trench, then ALD electrode/ZrO2/electrode inside for 20-40x projected area.
note: Gyroid unit cell ~30-50 nm exceeds cell pitch and pores cannot host a full MIM stack.

title: Breathing varactor capacitor stores at low voltage, reads boosted
idea: Po: the capacitor breathes. Replace the MIM capacitor with a MOS varactor whose plate line holds it in accumulation (high C) during idle so stored charge sits at ~0.2 V, then switches to depletion (C drops ~5x) at read to boost the node to ~1 V; at 0.2 V GIDL and junction leakage fall by orders of magnitude.
note: Storing at 0.2 V cuts stored charge; boost does not add signal charge.

title: Po the fab never etches: bottom-up area-selective capacitor growth
idea: Po: 'the fab is forbidden to etch.' Extracted: grow capacitor pillars bottom-up by area-selective deposition, with inhibitor monolayers blocking growth on the oxide field while TiN or Mo grows only on exposed storage-node plugs, re-dosing the inhibitor every few nanometers to reach AR 60+. This removes the high-aspect-ratio fluorocarbon mold etch.
note: Selectivity loss and lateral mushrooming at AR 60 are unsolved.

title: Periphery micro-tiles fall into place by fluidic self-assembly
idea: Po: the transistors find their own seats. Make sense-amp/decoder micro-tiles on a cheap logic process, dice them into shape-keyed blocks, and flow them over array wafers with matching etched recesses where shape and capillary forces seat them; one RDL then wires them in.
note: FSA placement accuracy (um) far from bitline-pitch sense-amp matching.

title: Grow capacitor pillars upward by area-selective deposition
idea: Po: no etching, only growing. Pattern only tiny seed pads, then use area-selective deposition (inhibitor-blocked dielectric, nucleating metal) to grow TiN or Ru pillars straight up ~1 um, followed by conformal high-k and top plate: the capacitor is built additively, not dug.
note: ASD selectivity over 1 um of growth will mushroom and bridge.

title: Three-mask crosspoint capacitor arrays stacked in 28 nm BEOL
idea: Po: memory with only three masks. Build stacked tiers of 1-selector-1-capacitor crosspoint cells (threshold-switch selector plus thin-film capacitor at each line crossing) in a mature foundry's BEOL with two line masks and one via mask per tier.

title: Optical backscatter pixels: DRAM reflects instead of emitting light
idea: Po: memory that reflects rather than shines. One mask etches micro-cavities in the top dielectric over an existing metal layer used as a mirror; a blanket electro-optic polymer fills them, and the top electrode modulates how much of the lid laser's light each pixel reflects to a detector array.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as capacitor hole templates
idea: Po: aluminum drills the holes. A deposited aluminum film is two-step anodized so self-ordering yields hexagonal nanopores at 40-60 nm pitch with aspect ratios over 100:1; pore registry is seeded by a DUV-patterned pre-texture, and the alumina template is lined TiN/high-k/TiN to form storage capacitors.

title: Roll-to-roll anodized alumina templates for ultra-high-aspect capacitors
idea: Worse: keep the cell signal tiny so sense amps must stay large and bitlines short. Flip: grow nanoporous anodic alumina continuously on a roll-to-roll aluminum line, transfer the AR>200 pore film onto the array, and ALD-coat the pores into capacitors, with storage-node pads wider than the pore pitch so each node captures several pores.

title: Multi-tier porous-oxide isolation: one bath makes 150 SOI tiers
idea: Worse: get single-crystal channels in every tier by bonding 150 wafers or by fragile SiGe replacement. Flip: grow a p+/p- doping superlattice of single-crystal Si, then electrochemically anodize from the slits so only the p+ layers turn porous, and thermally oxidize the porous layers into insulator, leaving 150 single-crystal Si-on-insulator tiers from one wet step.

title: Metal-induced lateral crystallization from bitline holes seeds all tiers
idea: Worse: accept leaky poly channels in deposited tiers or pay for 200 epitaxial or bonded layers. Flip: deposit cheap a-Si tiers, drop a Ni or Al nucleant into the vertical bitline holes, and anneal at ~500 C so crystallization fronts grow laterally from each hole along every tier at once, giving near-single-grain channels exactly where the access transistors sit, then strip the nucleant.
note: Ni contamination worsens the very leakage tail it targets.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching drills capacitor holes without plasma
idea: Worsen: etch every capacitor hole with fluorocarbon plasma (C4F6/C4F8) in $10M+ tools that struggle past AR 70. Flip: pattern a porous Ag or Au catalyst mesh and use metal-assisted chemical etching (HF/H2O2) to sink vertical holes into a silicon mold at AR >100 in a wet bath, then convert the mold to oxide or replace it.

title: Bacterial S-layer protein crystals as honeycomb capacitor masks
idea: Worsen: require EUV scanners from one supplier, tin plasma and hydrogen to print every capacitor array. Flip: self-assemble bacterial surface-layer proteins, which naturally form 2D hexagonal crystals with 10-30 nm periods, on the wafer, mineralize them into an oxide hard mask, and use that lattice to set the capacitor honeycomb with one coarse DUV alignment layer.

title: Probe-less wafer test: on-die BIST powered and read optically
idea: Worse: test every die on multimillion-dollar ATE with slow probe-card touchdowns. Flip: put a tiny photovoltaic cell and an LED/photodiode link on every die. Flood-illuminate the wafer so all dies self-test with on-die BIST at once and report pass/fail and repair maps optically in parallel.
note: Flood light generates carriers that wreck DRAM retention test; PV power too low.

title: Roll-to-roll memory tape on stainless steel foil
idea: Worse: process memory one rigid wafer at a time through vacuum load locks. Flip: run 30 um stainless-steel foil, planarized with spin-on glass, through roll-to-roll UV nanoimprint, atmospheric deposition and sputter zones to make cell layers continuously, then cut and stack the tape into blocks.

title: Anodic alumina pores on glass grow vertical access transistors
idea: Worse: pattern every vertical transistor with EUV contact holes. Flip: sputter aluminum on glass and anodize it into self-ordered 20-40 nm hexagonal pores. Fill the pores with ALD oxide-semiconductor channels wrapped by an ALD gate, giving vertical gate-all-around 4F2 access transistors with no transistor-level lithography.
note: AAO pores do not register to wordline/bitline grid.

title: Plywood DRAM: laser-lifted polyimide tiers laminated into stacks
idea: Worse: grow 26+ tiers sequentially on one substrate, so one bad tier scraps them all. Flip: fabricate each tier in parallel on polyimide over a reusable glass carrier, test it, laser-lift-off the good ones with OLED LLO tools, and laminate 32 known-good tiers with self-aligned through-tier vias.

title: Remote epitaxy through graphene lets one template seed hundreds of tiers
idea: Worse: consume a fresh single-crystal substrate for every device layer. Flip: grow single-crystal oxide or III-N films through a graphene interlayer on a reusable sapphire/GaN template, peel each membrane off with a Ni stressor, and stack the membranes as 3D memory tiers. The template is reused for every peel.
note: Remote epitaxy reproducibility and stacking hundreds of aligned membranes.

title: Neural generative codec memory with residual correction
idea: Worsen: store every structured dataset verbatim in DRAM. Flip: train a per-dataset generative model and store only its weights plus a small entropy-coded residual; an accelerator in the memory path reconstructs requested records exactly by running the model and adding the residual.
note: 30-300x overclaimed; learned codecs beat zstd modestly and decode latency is huge in memory path.

title: VO2 Mott hysteresis gives a one-element volatile latch
idea: Worsen: require a capacitor to remember a bit. Flip: bias a nanoscale VO2 element inside its insulator-metal hysteresis window, where it stays either metallic or insulating; a short pulse flips it and a small read current senses resistance, giving a one-resistor-one-selector latch stacked in the link die BEOL.
note: Needs thermal/bias hold near 68 C transition; holding power and variability.

title: Archimedes' lever: negative-capacitance ferroelectric boosts storage capacitor
idea: An ancient Greek engineer would add a lever rather than a longer arm. Put a thin ferroelectric, stabilized in its negative-capacitance branch, in series with the ZrO2/Al2O3 storage dielectric so the stack's effective capacitance exceeds that of the dielectric alone, reaching an effective k>100 in today's pillar.
note: Stable NC boost in leaky thin stacks remains contested; antiferroelectric ZrO2 boosting is known.

title: Origami artist: self-rolled Swiss-roll nanomembrane capacitor, plasma-ashed release
idea: An origami artist creates depth by folding a flat sheet. Deposit a flat, strained MIM stack on a polymer sacrificial layer; O2 plasma ashes the polymer away, and the released stack rolls itself into a ~10-turn Swiss-roll capacitor with 10-20x the capacitor area per footprint and no deep etch.
note: Rolled-up nanomembrane caps exist at micron scale; rolling at ~20 nm cell pitch with registration is implausible.

title: Firefighters' bucket brigade: CCD charge transfer replaces long bitlines
idea: A bucket brigade passes water hand to hand instead of filling a long pipe. Cells line a buried-channel CCD column; on access, the selected cell dumps its packet into the CCD, low-swing three-phase clocks walk it ~32 stages to a floating-diffusion sense node at the mat edge, and it is walked back to rewrite, so no long bitline is ever charged.
note: 32-stage CCD transfer likely too slow for DRAM latency; revives 1970s CCD memory.

title: Child's whisper: +/-100 mV storage with auto-zeroed sense amps
idea: A child asks why memory shouts when a whisper carries. Store bits as +/-100 mV around the mid level instead of 0/1.1 V with bitlines parked at mid; chopper/auto-zero sense amplifiers cancel their own offsets to <3 mV each cycle, and a low-Vt access device suffices because the storage node always sits near the bitline potential.

title: Wine taster's sip: non-destructive subthreshold current read without restore
idea: A taster sips; she never drains the bottle. The wordline rises only to a subthreshold 'sip' level for ~2 ns; the storage-node voltage modulates the access device's subthreshold current exponentially, and a current-mode sense amp on a bitline held at mid reads it while drawing <1% of stored charge; a per-row read counter triggers a full restore only after ~50 sips.
note: Sensing ~0.1 fC of subthreshold charge on a large bitline in 2 ns is near the noise floor.

title: Glassblower's drawn fiber: coaxial capacitors pulled from a preform
idea: The glassblower does not etch holes; they draw them. Assemble a macroscopic preform of low-melting metal cores in glass-dielectric cladding with outer metal, draw it 1000x, bundle and redraw it to ~100 nm coax pitch, then slice 5 um discs and bond them to an access-transistor wafer. Coax pitch finer than pad pitch means each pad statistically lands on at least one coax.
note: Same as I-03373; statistical pad landing removes alignment.

title: Potter's coil: self-rolling strained membrane turns planar array into tiers
idea: The potter builds tall vessels by coiling. Fabricate a planar gain-cell array on a pre-strained SiN/Si bilayer nanomembrane and release it with a sacrificial undercut so it self-rolls into a ~20-turn scroll. Wordlines run continuously along the spiral and contacts sit only at the outer edge.
note: Dup of self-rolling membrane array.

title: Crystal-growing alien: epitaxial SrTiO3 capacitors on silicon tier sidewalls
idea: A species that grows its tools as single crystals would make the dielectric epitaxial. Sr-passivate the (001) sidewalls of single-crystal Si tiers and grow epitaxial SrTiO3 by MBE or ALD with no SiO2 interlayer, against a degenerately doped Si electrode.

title: Soviet reverse-engineer rebuilds UltraRAM from silicon and oxide
idea: Persona: the classic Soviet copy of a Western design built from domestic materials. Replace UltraRAM's InAs/AlSb triple-barrier resonant-tunnelling stack with Si/SiO2 double barriers around a silicon quantum well. Electrons tunnel resonantly into a floating gate at ~2-3 V, and off resonance the barrier blocks leakage for years.
note: Si wells on amorphous SiO2 are not epitaxial; roughness smears resonance.

title: Metallurgist's layer exchange: aluminum-induced crystalline germanium periphery at 350 C
idea: Old metallurgists knew metals dissolve and reprecipitate semiconductors. Stack amorphous Ge over thin Al with a native-oxide barrier; at 300-350 C the Ge diffuses through the Al and recrystallizes beneath it as large-grain (>10 um), (111)-oriented film, giving high-mobility sense-amp and decoder transistors in tiers above the array.

title: Bookbinder's peel: room-temperature spalled single-crystal silicon tiers
idea: A bookbinder peels sheets rather than sawing them. A stressed nickel film peels a ~5-10 um single-crystal silicon sheet off a donor at room temperature (controlled spalling); plasma-activated oxide bonding (<=300 C) places it, CMP thins it to ~100 nm, and a tier of Schottky NiSi source/drain transistors (<=400 C) is built; this repeats per tier, with the donor reused.

title: Sticker-book kid: micro-transfer-print periphery chiplets onto low-T arrays
idea: A kid peels finished stickers onto a page. Make sense-amp and decoder chiplets (~100x100 um) in a cheap mature CMOS fab, release them by undercut, pick thousands at once with an elastomer stamp using kinetic adhesion, and print them onto the <=400 C memory-array wafer or panel, wired by one BEOL redistribution layer; the memory fab itself never exceeds 400 C.
note: ~1 um placement cannot meet bitline-pitch sense-amp connections.

title: Temporary-tattoo decal: freestanding perovskite membranes as capacitor dielectric
idea: A child applies a temporary tattoo. A materials supplier grows single-crystal SrTiO3 or BaTiO3 on a water-soluble Sr3Al2O6 sacrificial layer; dissolving that layer frees the membrane, which the memory fab laminates like a decal onto planar stacked-tier capacitors and bonds at <=300 C.

title: Quantum-paraelectric strontium titanate capacitor with k near ten thousand
idea: Cryogenic quantum-computer controllers can use SrTiO3, whose permittivity climbs to ~1e4 near 4 K because quantum fluctuations suppress ferroelectric order, giving tens of fF in a planar 0.01 um2 cell. The generalizable version strain-tunes SrTiO3/KTaO3 superlattices on scandate-like buffers so the incipient-ferroelectric permittivity peak sits at 300-350 K, targeting k~300-1000.
note: Room-temperature k peak via strain is plausible, but thin-film dead layers and leakage cut k sharply.

title: FD-SOI back-plane island stores bit beneath buried oxide
idea: Space-grade FD-SOI already sits on a thin buried oxide; one implant mask forms isolated doped islands in the handle wafer under each transistor, and charge injected into an island shifts the front channel threshold through the 20 nm BOX like a back gate. The BOX shields the island from front-side transient strikes and front junction leakage.

title: Venus-lander vacuum nanogap field-emission access switch
idea: Vacuum electronics are the switches that survive Venus' 460 C surface; build each access device as a vertical ~10 nm sealed vacuum gap with a sharp emitter on the storage-node side and a gate ring, so electrons cross by field emission only when the wordline raises the tip field. Off, there is no channel, junction or trap to leak through.

title: RFID-cheap transistorless crosspoint capacitors with MIIM tunnel selectors
idea: Penny RFID tags use two-terminal tunnel structures. Replace the access transistor with a back-to-back metal-insulator-insulator-metal tunnel selector (~1e6-1e8 I-V nonlinearity) in a 4F^2 crosspoint of stacked capacitors; half-selected cells leak and disturb, giving ~1% raw BER that page coding absorbs.

title: SPAD-style avalanche first stage turns electrons into digital pulses
idea: LIDAR single-photon detectors get enormous gain from impact ionization; the SA first stage is an impact-ionization MOSFET biased just below breakdown, so a stored '1' (~1000 electrons) triggers a self-sustaining avalanche that is quenched and reset like a SPAD, while a '0' does not.

title: Downhole-200C Ga2O3 vertical gain-cell tiers become refresh-free at room temperature
idea: Design the cell for a 200 C oil-well logging tool: a capacitor-less 2T gain cell whose write and read transistors are vertical beta-Ga2O3 (4.8 eV bandgap) pillars at 4F2, stacked 8-16 tiers over CMOS by low-temperature ALD. A cell qualified to hold charge 10 ms at 200 C holds it for many minutes at 85 C, so the same array ships to datacenters with refresh essentially gone.
note: Low-temp ALD Ga2O3 is amorphous, poor mobility; IGZO already gives long retention.

title: Two-mask-per-tier self-aligned crosspoint gain cell for $1 IoT
idea: A $1 IoT chip cannot afford 30 masks, so define every memory tier with exactly two orthogonal line masks, as in crosspoint memory: line set A forms the write wordline plus storage gate, line set B forms the bitline plus vertical channel, and a 2T gain cell self-aligns at every crossing. All tiers reuse the same two masks.
note: Self-aligning write, read and storage of a 2T cell with only two line masks is very constrained.

title: MLCC-style nanolaminate storage capacitor with interdigitated ALD electrodes
idea: Multilayer ceramic capacitors get high capacitance cheaply from hundreds of interleaved electrodes; build each DRAM storage node as an ALD nanolaminate of 6-10 alternating TiN/ZrO2 layers (nitrogen purge, no sputtering) in a lateral cavity, contacting odd electrodes on one side and even electrodes on the other by selective wet recess. Capacitance scales with layer count instead of aspect ratio.

title: Radiation-detector diamond: carbon access transistors with near-zero leakage
idea: Particle-physics and implant users rely on CVD diamond because its 5.5 eV bandgap gives essentially no leakage. Build hydrogen-terminated diamond surface-channel FETs with ALD Al2O3 passivation as DRAM access devices, on polycrystalline diamond grown in a university microwave-plasma CVD reactor.
note: H-terminated diamond stability and Si integration are miracles.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous ruthenium electrode inside every storage pillar
idea: Scale shift from battery-electrode science to the cell: deposit a Ru-Al alloy liner in the hole, selectively etch the Al to leave a 3-5 nm ligament nanosponge, then coat with ALD high-k and top electrode so one pillar has 3-5x internal surface area.
note: No room to coat 3-5 nm ligaments with dielectric plus electrode inside a ~20 nm hole.

title: 2D tunnel-diode bistable latch stacked in BEOL
idea: Shift the Goto-pair latch from III-V wafers to atomic layers: two WSe2/SnSe2 band-to-band tunnel diodes in series form a bistable node with negative differential resistance, plus one oxide access transistor, all in BEOL tiers.

title: Global pulse self-restore: whole-die refresh in one nanosecond broadcast
idea: Time shift from serial row-by-row refresh (8k REF commands per 64 ms) to one die-wide pulse: each cell adds a tiny gain transistor gated by its own storage node, with its drain on a shared 'restore' mesh; pulsing the mesh to VARY for ~2 ns tops up every node still reading '1' (gain device on) and leaves '0' nodes untouched, with no wordline, bitline or sense-amp activity.
note: As described, a node-gated device sourcing into its own node cannot restore above Vnode-Vt; needs a boosted gate.

title: Silicon NEMS relay as access switch: an air gap never leaks
idea: Scale jump from the telephone relay to a 60 nm silicon beam: each cell's access device is a doubly clamped Si beam pulled onto a TiN contact by the wordline's electrostatic force; when released, a ~5 nm gap gives effectively zero off-current, so retention is limited only by the capacitor dielectric.
note: Needs ~1e15 contact cycles; relays demonstrated far below that.

title: NEMS contact-switch access device with true zero off-current
idea: Scale jump from MEMS relays to ~20 nm: the access transistor is replaced by a nano-electromechanical contact switch with a vacuum gap when off, so the storage node leaks only through the capacitor dielectric and surfaces, giving hours of retention; refresh is omitted and data idle longer moves to NV.

title: Anodic alumina nanopores template 40-nm-pitch vertical transistors
idea: Let self-ordering electrochemistry pattern below the litho scale: anodize an aluminum film so hexagonally ordered pores form at ~40-60 nm pitch, set by the anodizing voltage. Coat the pores by atomic-layer epitaxy with gate dielectric and a semiconductor channel to make vertical surrounding-gate transistors; 180-nm litho only defines mat boundaries and straps.
note: Gate electrode placement inside alumina and addressing an unregistered hex lattice are unsolved.

title: Germanium-free 3D DRAM tiers from dopant-contrast silicon superlattices
idea: Instead of Si/SiGe stacks (germanium is ~60%+ China-controlled), grow alternating p++ boron-doped and intrinsic Si tiers in one low-temperature epi run. Anodization porosifies only the p++ layers, which are then oxidized into tier isolation. Scale shift: atom-level dopant contrast replaces alloy contrast to define 26+ tiers.
note: Dopant-contrast superlattice avoids Ge; dopant diffusion over 26+ tiers and porous-Si control are doubts.

title: Atom-precise probe master cloned through a template family tree
