idea: Ideal: stacking never wastes a good die. Closest achievable: build 13-high stacks sold as 12-high, with a crossbar of redundant TSV lanes in the base die so any one failing core die or TSV column is mapped out at final test.

title: Leakage must be a product, not a sum: stacked double-gate pillar
idea: Limit: no single gate may hold off the full voltage. In a vertical-channel 4F2 pillar, split the gate into two stacked electrodes that are driven together to turn on. When off, the mid-channel node floats to an intermediate potential, so each segment sees about half the Vds, and DIBL and GIDL drop superlinearly (the stack effect) at zero added footprint.

title: Backside bitlines buried under a 4F2 vertical-channel array
idea: Limit: the front side may carry only capacitors and wordlines. After the 4F2 pillars are formed, flip-bond the wafer, thin it, and pattern bitlines on the exposed pillar bottoms from the backside. This removes bitline contacts and buried-bitline doping steps from the front.

title: Buyer carries the inventory: DRAM wafer tolling contracts
idea: Self-imposed limit: the fab owns no product risk. A hyperscaler buys raw wafers, chemicals and masks, owns the work-in-process, and pays the fab a fixed conversion fee per wafer, the way oil refineries are paid under tolling contracts.
note: Close to existing foundry/consignment models.

title: Weight-streaming DRAM die: few banks, wide rows, no refresh
idea: HBM4 dies carry 256 banks and wide internal datapaths to serve random access from many pseudo-channels. A weight stream instead reads the same addresses in the same order every decode step. A streaming die uses ~16 large banks whose full rows are latched into a row-wide output FIFO and shifted onto TSVs, and a programmable sequencer replaces command decoding and per-bank state machines. It has no REF logic or refresh timers, because use refreshes every row (B4-03), with only a minimal self-refresh for idle. Mats and bitlines can be longer wherever the stream hides latency. It keeps the HBM base-die and TSV interface, so it stacks or sits beside HBM4 and HBF.

title: Substitute oxygen-precipitate gettering with implanted nanocavity gettering layer
idea: Substitute intrinsic oxygen-precipitate gettering with a buried band of nanocavities 1-2 um under the cell array, made by light-ion implant and anneal. Cavity walls bind Fe, Cu and Ni far more strongly than precipitates do, pulling the deep-level metal centers that create tail cells away from the storage junctions.
note: Implanted-cavity proximity gettering is 1990s art.

title: Substitute helium backside cooling with hydrogen for cryogenic implants
idea: Substitute the helium backside gas in the implanter chuck with low-pressure H2, which conducts heat even better than helium, to hold wafers at -100 C during storage-node junction implants. The cold implant fully amorphizes the region, which then regrows by solid-phase epitaxy without end-of-range dislocation loops.

title: Substitute plasma channel thinning with thermal atomic-layer etching
idea: Substitute argon-ion or plasma recess of ultrathin channels with thermal atomic-layer etching (oxidation/fluorination plus ligand-exchange cycles, N2 purged). It removes ~0.1 nm per cycle with no ion damage and sets channel body thickness to within one monolayer.

title: Dopant-free undoped nanowire channels shrink sense-amp mismatch
idea: Substitute doped-channel sense transistors with undoped SOI nanowire gate-all-around devices whose Vt is set by gate work function (TiN/TaN), removing random dopant fluctuation. Oxidation thinning and e-beam patterning are university-standard.

title: Sawtooth multilayer mold replaces smooth capacitor cylinder walls
idea: Substitute the uniform oxide capacitor mold with a 10 nm-period SiO2/SiN nanolaminate; after the hole etch, recess SiN laterally ~5 nm in hot phosphoric acid so the ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN conforms to a sawtooth sidewall with ~1.7x surface area, a deterministic successor to 1990s hemispherical-grain poly.

title: All-epitaxial Si/SiGe stack etched only with HBr/Cl2 chemistry
idea: Substitute the oxide/nitride stack of 3D DRAM (etched with C4F6/C4F8/CH2F2) with an all-semiconductor Si/SiGe epitaxial stack whose slits and holes are etched only with HBr/Cl2/O2 at cryogenic chuck temperature (SiOxBry sidewall passivation), deferring every dielectric to non-fluorinated fills (aminosilane ALD SiO2, TMA Al2O3) planarized by CMP instead of etch-back.

title: Argon fast-atom activated Si-Si bonding replaces HF-last tier bonding
idea: Substitute HF-dip hydrophobic bonding and oxide-interface bonding with room-temperature surface-activated bonding: an Ar fast-atom beam in UHV strips the native oxide and two single-crystal Si tiers are pressed into a conductive, oxide-free junction, so vertical bitline/channel pillars run continuously through layer-transferred tiers.
note: Ar-FAB surface-activated bonding is established (Suga).

title: One CZ donor wafer supplies twenty tiers via repeated layer splitting
idea: Substitute 'one CZ wafer per device layer' with 'one CZ donor per ~20 layers': H/He co-implant a donor, bond to the growing stack, split at ~400 C, restore the donor with touch CMP and H2 anneal (no HF), re-implant; each transferred 50-200 nm single-crystal Si layer becomes a partially pre-processed array tier.

title: Substitute US wellhead membrane helium for Qatari LNG helium
idea: Deploy skid-mounted multistage membrane plus PSA units at US gas wells holding only 0.3-1% helium (too lean for cryogenic plants) and ship 99.999% helium in tube trailers on long-term contracts to fabs.

title: Substitute laser cold-splitting for wire-saw wafering and lapping
idea: Focus a pulsed laser to write a subsurface damage plane inside the ingot, cleave a 300 mm wafer off with a polymer stressor or thermal shock, then use dry plasma stress relief instead of slurry lapping, wet etch and multi-step wet polish.

title: Substitute fab-heat membrane distillation for fresh-water intake
idea: Route RO reject and rinse effluent through membrane-distillation modules heated by 40-70 C process-cooling return water, polish the distillate back to UPW, and crystallize the brine for zero liquid discharge.

title: Substitute photoresist patterning with block-copolymer self-assembly for capacitor honeycomb
idea: Cylinder-forming PS-b-PMMA (or high-chi PS-b-PDMS) packs naturally into the same hexagonal lattice as DRAM storage nodes; a sparse ArF guide pattern (one post per 3-4 sites) registers the film and the polymer fills in the rest, then PMMA cores are removed and transferred into the hard mask. One DUV exposure plus spin-coat and 250 C bake replaces a double-EUV or SAQP hole sequence.
note: DSA for DRAM holes widely pursued; defectivity limits.

title: Substitute sawn bulk wafers with reusable porous-silicon donor layer transfer
idea: Anodize a parent wafer to form a double porous-silicon release layer, grow 30-50 um of device-grade epitaxial silicon, bond it to a low-cost polysilicon carrier and split at the porous layer; the parent is re-polished and reused 20-50 times. DRAM front-end only needs the top few microns of single crystal.

title: Swap fixed DIMM ownership for optically re-patched memory blades
idea: Substitute static wiring with a reconfigurable optical patch panel. Memory blades connect to servers through optical circuit switches, which reassign blades to servers every few minutes or hours following scheduler forecasts, so capacity physically follows demand.

title: Swap raw bf16 in HBM for ANS-coded tensors decoded at load
idea: Substitute raw storage with entropy-coded storage. An asymmetric-numeral-system decoder in the GPU's L2-to-SM path, driven by a per-tile offset table, lets weights and KV live entropy-coded in HBM and expand transparently on load. bf16 exponents carry only ~2.6 bits of entropy, and activation tiles are often sparse.
note: Software analogs (DFloat11, ZipNN) exist; hardware decoder is the twist.

title: Swap uncompressed line storage for controller compression with ECC-hidden metadata
idea: Substitute raw line storage with compressed lines whose compression tag hides in unused ECC code-space encodings. The SoC controller compresses each 64 B line (zero, base-delta, frequent-pattern) and packs compressible pages 2:1, with no separate metadata lookups. Standard DDR5 RDIMMs, JEDEC commands and timings stay unchanged, and the OS sees elastic capacity with a balloon for overflow.
note: Attache/CRAM hide compression metadata already.

title: Air-gap suspended interposer wires: vacuum dielectric instead of oxide
idea: Substitute the oxide/polyimide around long interposer lines with air: a sacrificial polynorbornene layer is thermally decomposed after RDL build, leaving copper lines suspended on periodic posts and cutting line capacitance ~3x.

title: Sidewall-written stack wiring replaces TSVs in DRAM cubes
idea: Substitute TSVs with wiring on the stack's faces: dies route pads to their edges, the stacked cube's sides are planarized, then copper traces are laser-direct-written down each sidewall; four faces give ~4,000 lines per cube at 10 um pitch.
note: Sidewall interconnect done by Irvine Sensors/Vertical Circuits.

title: Memory lives in the top-of-rack switch, not in servers
idea: Substitute per-server DIMMs with DRAM co-packaged inside the rack switch ASIC module and exposed over existing Ethernet/CXL ports as a shared pool with line-rate atomics; servers keep only small local DRAM.

title: Substitute static twin-cell mode with on-the-fly pairing of weak rows
idea: Rows flagged weak by profiling switch into differential twin-cell mode (two adjacent cells per bit on complementary bitlines) under a mode bit, while healthy rows stay single-cell, so capacity loss is only local.
note: Close to CLR-DRAM reconfigurable twin-cell.

title: Substitute verified strong MRAM writes with sloppy writes plus BCH
idea: Write STT-MRAM at ~0.6x critical current with no write-verify, accepting ~1e-4 write error rate, and correct with BCH-6 per 512 bits; the smaller write current allows a ~40% smaller access transistor.

title: Substitute vented helium with closed-loop recapture and hydrogen backside cooling
idea: Swap once-through helium in etch-chuck backside cooling and furnace purges for on-tool cryogenic recapture loops plus H2/Ar backside gas on chucks that tolerate it, so a fab's helium draw drops to make-up losses.
note: On-tool He recapture plus H2/Ar backside; recovery loops already common in labs/MRI, resilience gain not memory step change.

title: Substitute Spruce Pine quartz crucibles with synthetic sol-gel silica crucibles
idea: Swap natural high-purity quartz sand for crucibles cast from synthetic silica made by hydrolysing SiCl4 (a polysilicon by-product), with a Si3N4 inner coat to extend pulls per crucible.
note: Synthetic inner-layer crucibles already exist.

title: Substitute factory burn-in ovens with in-host self-burn-in
idea: Swap long ATE/oven burn-in for shipping modules after short screens and running a 72-hour on-board BIST burn-in inside the customer's server at first boot, reporting telemetry and remapping weak rows before production use.

title: Substitute vacuum ALD clusters with atmospheric spatial ALD lines
idea: Swap vacuum ALD tools for atmospheric-pressure spatial ALD heads (oxide channels and dielectrics at 150-250 C) that move the wafer under gas curtains, built by U.S. tool makers.

title: Substitute furnace polysilicon with excimer-laser LTPS periphery tiers
idea: Swap furnace-crystallized silicon for display-industry excimer-laser annealing that melts a-Si into high-mobility polysilicon in nanoseconds while the substrate stays below 400 C, giving fast periphery transistors in upper tiers.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembly patterning hexagonal capacitor arrays
idea: Combine directed self-assembly of PS-b-PMMA cylinders, which form hexagonal close-packed arrays at 20-28 nm pitch, with the DRAM capacitor array, which is already hexagonal: a coarse DUV prepattern guides the cylinders, which are transferred into a hard mask to define capacitor holes. Spin-on chemistry replaces one or two EUV or quad-patterning layers.
note: DSA for DRAM holes widely pursued; defectivity is the barrier.

title: Thin-film flux-closure nanorings: magnetic core memory reborn
idea: Combine 1960s ferrite core memory with thin-film lithography: each bit is a 50-100 nm CoFeB ring whose vortex magnetization circulates clockwise or counterclockwise, switched by a current pulse through a central via and read by a TMR sensor at the ring edge. Closed flux means no stray field between neighbours and no refresh.
note: Vortex MRAM rings proposed around 2000 (Zhu, Prinz).

title: Floating-gate shadow block behind each DRAM subarray
idea: A double-poly EEPROM block behind each subarray acts as a nonvolatile shadow (nvSRAM fused with DRAM). Before power-down, rows stream through the sense amps into the shadow and refresh stops; on wake the shadow restores them, and shadowing can be limited to an OS-state slice.

title: Canary rows with undersized capacitors gate refresh timing
idea: A mask change gives a few rows per subarray ~70% of normal capacitance, and they are written with a known pattern. A background sampler issues refresh only when canaries start to flip, so the rate tracks real temperature, voltage and aging.
note: Canary cells track temperature but not the random VRT tail.

title: SIMOX buried oxide under the storage diffusion
idea: Build cells on 1990s SIMOX SOI so the storage n+ sits directly on buried oxide, shrinking its pn junction to a thin sidewall. A body tie suppresses floating-body bipolar leakage.

title: Thin p-epi on p+ substrate with buried sink drains leakage
idea: Fuse the CCD vertical-overflow-drain design with DRAM. Storage nodes sit in thin, lightly doped epi over a heavily doped, short-lifetime substrate, plus an n-buried layer biased as a carrier sink that removes thermally generated charge before it reaches storage nodes.

title: Liquid-nitrogen racks with cryo-CMOS periphery and no refresh
idea: Combine datacenter immersion-cooling infrastructure with 77 K operation: access-transistor leakage drops by orders of magnitude so retention reaches hours, and periphery gains ~2x mobility with lower wire resistance; redesign the periphery for 77 K with higher Vt and VDD near 0.6 V.
note: Cryo DRAM studied; cooling overhead erodes energy gains.

title: Array cell capacitors as flying caps for on-die converters
idea: Wire blocks of spare and edge DRAM cell capacitors (very high density at ~5 fF each) into a multi-phase switched-capacitor converter that generates VPP, VBB and VARY at ~80-85% efficiency instead of ~30-40% for Dickson charge pumps.
note: Cell-type reservoir caps already used in DRAM periphery; SC converter twist.

title: DIMM PMIC takes over VPP and VBB generation
idea: Extend the existing 180/130 nm BCD power-management chip on DDR5 modules with two more rails (VPP ~3 V and a negative VBB) delivered through dedicated balls, so DRAM dies delete their charge pumps and pump decap; inductor-based BCD converters run at ~90% versus ~30-40% for on-die pumps.

title: Inductive coil links replace TSVs in trailing-node stacks
idea: Stack 8 trailing-node DRAM dies with no TSVs: data and commands move vertically through on-chip coils drawn in existing top-metal layers (ThruChip-style inductive coupling), while power arrives through staircase wire bonds at OSATs.

title: Boot-calibrated dummy cells cancel each sense amp's offset
idea: At power-up, measure each SA's offset by sweeping a reference on a dummy bitline cell, then write a compensating charge into a per-bitline dummy cell that is charge-shared with the real cell on every read and refreshed with the row.

title: Display-fab panel interposers for wide-IO memory modules
idea: Use idle Gen-6 LCD lines (1.5-2 um lithography on large glass panels) to pattern multilayer redistribution interposers for wide, slow DRAM-to-processor links, replacing scarce silicon interposers.

title: Bit-significance placement with per-subarray voltage and refresh
idea: Give each subarray its own VARY tap and refresh rate set by mode register; the memory controller places AI tensors' sign and exponent bits in strong, often-refreshed subarrays and low-order mantissa bits in low-voltage, rarely refreshed ones.

title: Bootstrapped wordline drivers revive 1980s self-boost, shrinking pumps
idea: Use per-driver-group MOS bootstrap capacitors to self-boost the wordline above VDD at activation, as early NMOS DRAMs did, so only a tiny VPP pump remains to hold leakage.

title: Shingled die staircase with vertical bond-via wires replacing TSVs
idea: Fuse NAND-style offset die stacking with free-standing vertical copper wire arrays (US-developed bond-via-array): each DRAM die is shifted to expose an edge pad row and molded ~50 um-pitch vertical Cu wires rise from the substrate to every die, built on Arizona OSAT lines.

title: Barrierless molybdenum contacts silicide themselves during the fill anneal
idea: Combine contact barrier, fill and silicide into one ALD Mo step from a fluorine-free chloride precursor (MoO2Cl2): Mo deposits directly on Si and a ~600 C anneal forms a MoSi2 interface, deleting the Ti/TiN liner and WF6 tungsten fill.

title: Top dummy die etched into a water microchannel cold plate
idea: Combine HBM's topmost dummy spacer die with a cold plate: deep-etch 100 um microchannels into it and pump water/glycol through, replacing two-phase immersion in fluorinated (Novec-type, being phased out) fluids for hot AI racks.

title: Puller heater coils also generate the melt-damping magnetic field
idea: Combine the CZ heater and the melt-stabilizing magnet (zero masks): drive segmented heater coils with phase-shifted AC so they produce a traveling magnetic field that damps melt convection, replacing superconducting cusp magnets and their helium cryostats.
note: Resembles existing heater-magnet module research for traveling-field CZ.

title: Supercritical CO2 dries capacitor pillars without collapse or water
idea: Combine final rinse/dry with mechanical protection (zero masks): after the mold strip, displace water with a co-solvent and then closed-loop supercritical CO2 (zero surface tension) so tall pillars never see capillary force.

title: Arsenic-free n-type junctions via phosphorus epi and laser activation
idea: Combine source/drain formation with doping (zero masks): selective in-situ phosphorus-doped Si:P epi grows only on exposed Si, and nanosecond laser melt activates it, replacing arsenic implants and furnace spikes.

title: 28 nm SRAM-chain pipeline with codebook weights replaces DRAM
idea: Combine weight-stationary pipeline parallelism across many 28 nm SRAM-rich chips (~300 MB each) with 2-3-bit vector-quantized codebook weights decoded at the MAC array, so a whole model lives in mature-node SRAM spread along a board-level chain.
note: Groq/Cerebras-like; SRAM bits far costlier than DRAM bits.

title: Contactless inductive wafer probing at full speed for known-good dies
idea: Combine inductive-coupling transceivers with wafer sort: every DRAM core die carries a small coil-array test port so the prober couples wirelessly at full 6-10 Gb/s and runs retention, row-hammer and speed screens before thinning and stacking, with no probe damage or large test pads.
note: Non-contact inductive probing published (Keio).

title: Printed polymer optical waveguides replace helium-drawn glass fiber links
idea: Combine package build-up layers with optics: photo-pattern siloxane polymer waveguides (LED-cured) into the substrate and board to link co-packaged optical engines on GPUs and memory modules over 10-50 cm. Glass fiber needs helium for preform consolidation and draw cooling; polymer waveguides need none.

title: Plastic dielectric waveguide carries sub-THz memory links between boards
idea: Combine CMOS 140-300 GHz transceivers with low-loss PTFE/HDPE dielectric ribbon waveguides plugged at the package edge, so memory boards reach compute over 0.5-2 m at 50-100 Gb/s per lane with no lasers, no glass fiber (helium-drawn) and no fine-pitch copper.

title: ReRAM soft-fuse table in BEOL enables lifelong self-repair
idea: Combine filamentary ReRAM (sputtered TaOx/HfOx between TiN electrodes) with the redundancy fuse bank: repair addresses live in a reprogrammable BEOL ReRAM array above the periphery, so the chip remaps newly failing rows in the field and can undo mistakes, replacing one-time laser/e-fuses. Buildable in a university nanofab: sputter plus two lithography layers.

title: DIMM deposit-refund system modeled on bottle bills
idea: Fuse beverage-container deposit laws with memory. A $2-5 per-module deposit is added at sale and refunded when the module comes back through certified collectors, who feed the reuse and re-binning chain instead of shredders.

title: Coal-mine canary cells that call for refresh only when needed
idea: Adapted from mining canaries and aviation condition-based maintenance: each subarray carries a few sentinel cells built with ~30% less storage capacitance and a longer gate-drain overlap, so they decay faster than the worst real cell. A tiny comparator polls them, and the bank is refreshed only when a sentinel crosses its threshold, not on a worst-case 32/64 ms timer.

title: Image-sensor black-reference rows let the sense threshold track decay
idea: Adapted from the optical-black reference pixels image sensors use to subtract dark current: every row stores a few reference cells written to 1 and 0 at the same moment as the data. On read, a charge-sharing averager builds the sense reference from those cells' decayed levels instead of a fixed VDD/2.

title: Water-utility night pressure reduction: idle-mode rebias of array wells
idea: Adapted from utilities that lower mains pressure at night because leakage scales with pressure: when the DRAM enters self-refresh, it raises the array p-well bias toward 0 V (cutting the storage-junction field that drives trap-assisted leakage) and deepens the wordline-off voltage to hold subthreshold leakage, then restores active-mode biases on exit.

title: Regenerative-braking refresh: recycle bitline and wordline charge
idea: Adapted from regenerative braking: when one subarray finishes restoring a refreshed row, its high bitlines are connected through charge-sharing switches to the next subarray's bitlines before discharging, and wordlines are driven by an LC resonant (adiabatic) driver that returns wordline charge to a tank instead of ground.

title: Smartphone pixel binning for leaky rows
idea: Borrowed from phone-camera pixel binning: when a retention monitor flags a weak row pair, the controller switches it to binned mode, where both cells hold the same bit and both wordlines open together to sum charge on the bitline; healthy rows stay at 1 bit per cell.
note: Twin-cell/CLR-DRAM modes are known art.

title: Qi-style inductive coupling stacks glass memory sheets without vias
idea: Borrowed from wireless charging and NFC coils: thin glass memory sheets are laminated with planar coils at each I/O site, passing data and clock inductively through glass, which unlike silicon has no eddy-current loss.
note: ThruChip inductive coupling is established art.

title: Mini-LVDS timing-controller links for on-panel data lines
idea: Borrowed from the reduced-swing differential links between TV timing controllers and source drivers: global data lines on a memory panel become current-mode differential pairs with ~200 mV swing, terminated at each mat cluster.

title: Space-station water recovery chain for 95% ultrapure-water reclaim
idea: Adapted from the ISS water recovery system: vapor-compression distillation, multifiltration beds, catalytic aqueous-phase oxidation and conductivity-gated reject loops. Segregate rinse streams by contamination class at every wet bench and run each class through a modular distillation and catalytic-oxidation skid that returns water to UPW polishing.

title: Pulp-mill chlorine-free bleaching chemistry replaces sulfuric-peroxide wafer cleans
idea: Paper mills replaced chlorine bleaching with totally chlorine-free ozone/peroxide sequences. Adapt that sequence: replace SPM (piranha) resist strips and SC-1 cleans with ozonated DI water carrying dissolved CO2, followed by UV-activated peroxide, all generated on site from oxygen, water and electricity.
note: Ozonated-water resist strip is known; not a full SPM replacement for heavy implant resist.

title: Decaffeination supercritical CO2: collapse-free drying for taller capacitors
idea: Adapt coffee decaffeination and supercritical extraction plants: after the wet etch that frees capacitor pillars, replace IPA drying with supercritical CO2 exchange (zero surface tension) so capillary forces never bend or stick pillars, letting aspect ratio climb toward 100-115:1 with fewer support layers.

title: Food-packaging spatial ALD: conveyor-speed liners and spacers
idea: Roll-to-roll barrier-film lines for food packaging coat by moving the substrate under fixed precursor and purge zones; use atmospheric spatial ALD heads for DRAM's low-aspect-ratio ALD films (spacers, liners, periphery gate stacks) and reserve slow temporal ALD only for the deep capacitor stack.

title: Single-use bioreactor logic: disposable etch-chamber liner cartridges
idea: Biopharma moved from cleaned stainless tanks to single-use bags; give high-AR etch and CVD chambers robot-swappable disposable liner cartridges (yttria-coated alumina shells) replacing 12-24 h wet-clean maintenance.
note: Replaceable process kits exist; incremental uptime gain.

title: Float-glass online APCVD: vacuum-free mold and interlayer oxides
idea: Float-glass lines coat moving ribbons at atmospheric pressure with SiO2 and SiOxCy; adapt gas-curtain-isolated atmospheric CVD heads (TEOS/ozone, silane/N2O) for DRAM's thick capacitor mold oxides, interlayer dielectrics and gap fills, with no vacuum chamber, load lock or turbo pump.

title: Warehouse cross-docking: I/O buffers skip DRAM, land in cache
idea: Borrowed from cross-dock logistics where pallets go straight from inbound to outbound trucks: NIC and NVMe DMA writes are steered into reserved LLC/accelerator-SRAM 'dock doors' with a scheduled consumer appointment, and the consumer's completion frees the door; only overflow spills to DRAM. A hardware yard scheduler enforces the appointment windows.

title: Backup-appliance dedup at cache-line granularity inside CXL expanders
idea: Borrowed from backup-appliance deduplication: the CXL expander hashes each 64-B line on write, keeps the hash in spare ECC/metadata bits, and maps identical lines to one physical copy through a reference-counted translation table; writes to shared lines trigger copy-on-write inside the controller.
note: HICAMP-style line dedup known.

title: Radar phased-array beams link compute boards to remote memory sleds
idea: Adapted from military AESA radar tiles: 60-140 GHz beam-steered phased arrays on memory sleds and compute boards form reconfigurable wireless links across a rack. Any accelerator can steer a beam to any memory sled without cables or connectors.

title: Telecom MEMS optical cross-connects time-share memory pools among accelerators
idea: Adapted from MEMS-mirror optical circuit switches in telecom cores: fiber links between memory shelves and accelerators are re-pointed in milliseconds, moving terabytes of DRAM to whichever job is in its memory-heavy phase (e.g., decode versus prefill).

title: Infrared focal-plane cubes turned sideways: memory cube edge-bonds to processor
idea: Adapted from 1990s defense IR focal-plane cube stacking: thinned DRAM dies are laminated into a cube, one side face is lapped flat, and bond pads are patterned on that face with a contact aligner. The cube stands on edge so every die's edge talks straight down to the processor.

title: Nokia-era embedded-die circuit boards hide DRAM inside processor substrate
idea: Adapted from 1990s HDI cellphone boards with laser microvias and embedded components: thinned DRAM dies are laminated inside the processor's organic substrate directly under the SoC and connected by stacked laser microvias.
note: Embedded-die substrates (AT&S, TDK) known; thermal and yield under SoC risky.

title: Bridge strain-gauge sentinels: deliberately weak canary cells gate refresh
idea: Adapted from structural health monitoring, where cheap gauges alarm before the bridge fails: each subarray includes a column of sentinel cells built with ~70% of nominal capacitor height (one extra trim step) so they leak first; a subarray is refreshed only when its sentinels begin to flip, checked for free during normal activations.

title: SYN-cookie style epoch-keyed row scrambling against hammering
idea: Adapted from network security's stateless key rotation (SYN cookies, ASLR re-randomization): the DRAM die applies a keyed bijective permutation (a 4-round Feistel on row-address bits) between logical and physical rows inside each subarray and re-keys every epoch by migrating rows during refresh slots, so no attacker holds a fixed set of physical neighbors for more than one epoch.

title: MRI zero-boil-off helium recapture loops for fab tools
idea: Adapted from closed-loop liquefiers in MRI suites and physics labs: capture helium exhaust from wafer backside cooling, leak checks and etch/implant chambers, purify it with cryogenic adsorbers and pressure-swing beds, and reinject it into the fab supply.

title: Optical-fiber flame hydrolysis for synthetic quartz crucible liners
idea: Adapted from flame-hydrolysis/OVD deposition used to make ultra-pure fiber preforms in New York: lay a synthetic fused-silica liner on crucibles made from ordinary U.S. quartz, so only the layer that touches the melt needs ultra-high purity.

title: Nanoimprint master replicates capacitor hole arrays without EUV
idea: MINIFY litho cost per layer: e-beam write one 20-nm-hole master, then UV-nanoimprint the storage-node hole layer wafer after wafer with a ~$2M tool; periodic hole arrays are the ideal imprint case because overlay tolerance is loose.

title: Magnify the gate-drain underlap to defuse GIDL
idea: Stretch a 15-25 nm ungated, lightly doped drain extension along the vertical pillar between wordline and storage node so peak drain field drops from ~1.5 to <0.6 MV/cm, exponentially suppressing band-to-band (GIDL) and trap-assisted tunneling. A thin fringing field plate tied to the bitline restores on-current.

title: Magnify cells per bit on demand: OS-elastic twin-cell mode
idea: Let the OS/hypervisor flip under-used DRAM regions into 2-cells-per-bit differential mode (complementary cells on paired bitlines) that tolerates ~10x more charge loss and is refreshed at 1 s; regions revert to 1 cell/bit when demand rises, controlled by a per-subarray mode register.

title: Thousand-point on-die thermal map sets per-mat refresh
idea: MAGNIFY temperature sensing from 1-2 sensors per die to one ~50 um2 ring-oscillator thermometer per mat (~1,000 per die), and scale each mat's refresh interval to its local temperature, since leakage doubles roughly every 10 C.
note: Per-region temperature-aware refresh proposed in literature.

title: Evict charge pumps: package PMIC supplies VPP to sixteen dies
idea: MINIFY on-die high-voltage generation to zero: one ~85%-efficient switched-inductor PMIC on the HBM base die or DIMM generates VPP/VBB for all dies and delivers them on dedicated TSVs or balls, replacing on-die capacitive pumps.

title: Magnify mat size with mid-bitline charge-transfer preamplifiers
idea: MAGNIFY bitlines from 512 to 2,048 cells by inserting a charge-transfer (Heller-type PMOS) preamplifier at the midpoint that moves far-segment charge onto a small node with gain, halving the number of SA stripes and decoder columns per bit.

title: Quarter-size sense amps with one-time digital offset trim
idea: MINIFY SA transistors 4x and accept ~40 mV offset; at wafer test, measure each SA's offset and store a 4-bit code in a dense trim array that drives a small capacitive DAC on the latch node during every sense.

title: One shared SerDes chiplet replaces eight dies' wide PHYs
idea: MINIFY each DRAM die's PHY, DLL and I/O ring (~8-10% of area) to a narrow on-package bridge port, and MAGNIFY a single 224G SerDes chiplet that serializes traffic for eight dies.

title: Magnify redundancy to 30% spare tiers with boot-time self-repair
idea: Design 3D DRAM with about 30% spare tiers and rows, plus a built-in self-test that remaps failing rows at every power-on, so a stack can tolerate a defect density about 10x higher than 2D DRAM.
note: Built-in self-repair with heavy redundancy, NAND-style; known approach.

title: Hot-rated memory enables waterless dry-cooled datacenters
idea: Magnify the allowed memory temperature from 85 C to 125 C: qualify server DRAM to Grade 1 (temperature-tracking refresh, thicker capacitor dielectric) so racks can run 60 C warm-water loops with dry coolers and no evaporative cooling.

title: Reusable parent wafer: porous-silicon layer transfer
idea: Minify Czochralski crystal use: grow a thin epitaxial silicon device layer on a porous-silicon release layer, transfer it to a cheap carrier, and reuse the parent wafer 50+ times.

title: Minify copies: single-copy OS across NIC, kernel, app
idea: Minify the 2-4 duplicate copies of file and network data (NIC ring, page cache, user buffer, DB buffer pool) with an OS where one capability-guarded buffer is shared read-only by every layer. Double caching between the OS page cache and the database is banned.
note: Zero-copy and O_DIRECT already reduce duplication.

title: Sub-THz plastic waveguides for meter-scale memory links
idea: MAGNIFY carrier frequency to ~300 GHz and carry memory traffic over cheap polymer dielectric waveguides (~100 Gb/s per lane) from shared memory boxes up to 1-2 m away, with no lasers.

title: Few fast TSVs: 16 Gb/s per TSV
idea: MAGNIFY the rate per TSV to ~16 Gb/s with tiny on-die serializers, so ~90% of HBM data TSVs disappear (about 100 per stack instead of ~1,000+).

title: Inductive-coil stacks held by removable adhesive
idea: MINIFY the metallurgical bond to zero: dies talk through on-chip inductor coils, are stacked with a reworkable adhesive, and a failed die is peeled out and replaced with no bumps to reflow.
note: ThruChip inductive stacking exists; power delivery still needs vias.

title: Four-high replaceable memory bricks in a 2D array
idea: MINIFY the repair unit: instead of 12- to 16-high stacks, use many 4-high bricks tiled flat on the substrate, each individually removable, so a failure costs one small brick.

title: Minify repair granularity to single 64-bit words via on-die CAM
idea: Replace part of the row/column fuse redundancy with a ~2k-entry content-addressable remap table per bank that redirects single failing 64-bit words to a spare word array. It is programmed at test and updated in the field.
note: Word-level CAM remapping proposed before; moderate yield gain.

title: Minify sentinels: deliberately weak canary cells pace adaptive refresh
idea: Build a few canary cells per subarray with ~30% smaller capacitors or leakier access devices. A background engine checks them every few ms, and the refresh rate follows the first canary failures, tracking temperature and aging in real time instead of worst-case guardbands.
note: Canary cells pacing refresh, same as replica tracking.

title: Minify hydrogen with getter-laced glass to freeze oxide-TFT drift
idea: Embed hydrogen-getter layers (Ti- or Pd-alloy films or getter-doped glass) in or on the substrate to absorb hydrogen that diffuses into IGZO channels and drives threshold drift and leakage growth.

title: Magnify codeword spread across millimeters to defeat particle-defect clusters
idea: Display-fab particles kill clusters of cells tens of um across. Physically scatter each codeword's symbols across tiles millimeters apart, which is cheap on panels, so any cluster hits at most one symbol per codeword.
note: Standard interleaving practice.

title: Minify soft-error charge collection with thin films on insulating substrate
idea: Thin-film transistors on glass or sapphire have ~50 nm active layers over an insulator, so an alpha or neutron strike collects ~100x less charge than in bulk silicon junctions. Use low-alpha borosilicate glass so the substrate adds no emitters.
note: Thin-film-on-insulator SER benefit is well known.

title: Minify speed, magnify bins: JEDEC DDR-Slow capacity grade
idea: Standardize a JEDEC grade with ~2x relaxed timings and refresh (e.g. 256 ms window at low temperature) that accepts speed- and retention-failed bins from any node and lets old lines qualify, targeted at CXL capacity tiers.

title: Eliminate plasma in 3D cells: vapor-HCl lateral etch carves horizontal capacitors
idea: Eliminate plasma steps in a 3D DRAM stack: grow 30-60 Si/SiGe bilayers by hydrogen-carrier CVD, cut slits, then use highly selective vapor HCl at 600-700 C to remove SiGe sideways and open the horizontal capacitor cavities and channel spaces in one gas-only, plasma-free step before ALD dielectric and electrode.

title: Eliminate the worst-case guard band: deliberately leaky canary cells
idea: Embed a few sentinel cells per subarray built with intentionally shortened access transistors so they leak 4-8x faster than any real cell; a tiny comparator watches them and refreshes that subarray only when a canary crosses threshold. Refresh then tracks real temperature, voltage and aging instead of the 64 ms worst-case spec.

title: Eliminate implant damage: molecular monolayer doping for access junctions
idea: Form storage-node and bitline junctions by grafting a phosphorus- or arsenic-bearing molecular monolayer onto silicon, capping it and driving in by rapid thermal anneal, giving ultra-shallow junctions with no ion-implant end-of-range defects. Implant-induced deep traps are a key source of the trap-assisted junction leakage tail.

title: Eliminate lithography: block-copolymer self-assembled pillars for vertical access transistors
idea: Spin a PS-b-PMMA block copolymer, anneal it into a hexagonal 20-30 nm pitch pattern, transfer it into silicon as vertical pillars, and build surrounding-gate access transistors whose channel length is set by etch depth (long, low-leakage), not lithography. Only contact lithography is used for coarse alignment.
note: DSA for DRAM honeycomb patterns heavily pursued; defectivity the gate.

title: Eliminate the DLL and clock tree with delay-insensitive handshake I/O
idea: Replace the DRAM's DLL, clock distribution and read-preamble training with a 4-phase bundled-data handshake per byte lane. The die returns data with a completion strobe generated by a replica bitline that tracks the real array, so it needs no clock at all.

title: Eliminate half the sense-amp stripes with decomposable-polymer air-gap bitlines
idea: Pattern bitlines with Cl-based etch, fill between them with polynorbornene (a fluorine-free sacrificial polymer, patterned in O2), cap with TEOS oxide, and decompose the polymer at ~400 C. The air gaps cut bitline capacitance ~35%, so bitlines can be ~1.6x longer per SA and roughly every other SA stripe is deleted.

title: Eliminate column decoders and CSL wiring: sense latches as shift registers
idea: After sensing, chain the SA latches into a two-phase shift register (2 transfer gates per SA), so the row buffer clocks out serially to 64 edge taps. The column decoder, the column-select lines and one metal/via level disappear, and the remaining wiring is Cl-etched Al/Mo.
note: Recalls VRAM serial access memory.

title: Eliminate identical tiers: hot short-bitline tiers over dense tiers
idea: Build the top 4 tiers of a 3D stack with short bitlines and fast, frequently refreshed cells and the lower tiers with long bitlines and dense cells; an on-die migration engine moves hot rows upward over vertical bitline bridges.

title: Eliminate the sacrificial bulk wafer: porous-silicon lift-off with donor reuse
idea: Grow a 10 um device-grade epi layer on a double-porous-Si release layer, bond it to a carrier wafer cast from low-grade solar silicon, split at the porous layer with a water jet, run the DRAM flow on the transferred layer, and re-polish the CZ donor for 30-50 reuses.

title: Eliminate DRAM-only fabs: BEOL MIM 1T1C memory in U.S. logic foundries
idea: Build standalone 1T1C memory chiplets using stacked MIM capacitors in the back-end of existing 22-28 nm U.S. logic processes, as Intel's eDRAM did, at lower density but zero new tooling.
note: MIM eDRAM density ~10x below DRAM; PB/yr supply claim optimistic.

title: Eliminate one-crystal-per-wafer: kerfless epitaxial lift-off from reusable parent wafers
idea: Grow a 50-100 um device-grade epitaxial silicon layer on a double-porous-silicon release layer atop a Czochralski parent wafer, bond it to a reclaimed-silicon carrier and cleave; the parent is re-porosified and reused 20-50 times.

title: Eliminate tungsten and its liner: barrierless molybdenum buried wordlines
idea: Fill buried-wordline trenches with molybdenum deposited by ALD/CVD directly on the gate dielectric with no TiN barrier, and spend the freed liner volume on conductor.

title: Eliminate CMP: subtractive metal patterning plus flowable self-planarizing dielectric
idea: Pattern bitlines and landing pads by direct etch of blanket Ru or Mo instead of damascene, then gap-fill with flowable SiOC that self-levels and is etched back to an optical endpoint, removing chemical-mechanical polish steps.

title: Eliminate leading-edge logic for HBM base dies: depreciated 28 nm US fabs
idea: Make HBM3E/HBM4-compatible base dies in fully depreciated 28-40 nm US logic fabs, using wider, slower internal channels to the core dies and a 28 nm PHY tuned to the JEDEC data rate. The GPU sees a standard HBM stack.

title: Eliminate CD-variation rework: per-bank voltage trims absorb multipatterning spread
idea: Instead of tightening process windows with more metrology, rework and scrap, trim each bank's VPP, VBLH and sense timing at sort so slow or leaky banks from DUV multipatterned arrays still meet JEDEC tRCD/tRAS and refresh specs. Host-visible timing is unchanged.

title: Eliminate time-zone idle DRAM with follow-the-sun memory scheduling
idea: A global scheduler moves memory-heavy batch, training and offline-inference jobs across continents so each region's DRAM serves its local daytime peak and other regions' night-time batch load.

title: Simultaneous bidirectional DQ: reads and writes share each wire
idea: Eliminate bus turnaround and half the data pins: both ends drive each on-package lane at once and subtract their own known transmitted signal with a hybrid echo canceller (as gigabit Ethernet does), so reads and writes flow concurrently on the same wire.

title: Air-gap interposer wiring cuts per-bit wire capacitance
idea: Eliminate the dielectric between HBM-to-GPU interposer lines: after patterning, selectively etch a sacrificial polymer to leave lines suspended in air (k~1 vs ~3.5) on periodic support posts, then seal with a cap layer.

title: Non-volatile write FIFO in the PHY makes pins persistent
idea: Eliminate cache-flush and fence round trips: put a small ferroelectric-capacitor-backed write queue in the controller PHY and memory base die so a write is durable the moment it crosses the pins; the queue drains to the NV array at leisure and replays after power loss.

title: Latching phase-change optical switches pool memory at zero hold power
idea: Eliminate the always-on electrical switch in memory pooling: build the rack's memory fabric from GST-clad silicon-photonic switches whose routing state latches non-volatilely, so host-to-memory assignments persist through power loss and cost no energy to hold.

title: Eliminate factory final test: in-field BIST screening and soft repair
idea: Eliminate long DRAM final test and burn-in: dies ship after short wafer sort, carrying on-die BIST and soft post-package repair, and finish retention and pattern screening inside the customer's system during the first weeks of operation.

title: Eliminate the patent thicket: public commons from distressed DRAM portfolios
idea: Eliminate royalty barriers: a public-private fund buys DRAM patent portfolios from exited or bankrupt players and licenses them royalty-free to any US-made memory entrant, with pooled defensive countersuit rights.

title: Eliminate dummy monitor wafers with in-situ virtual metrology
idea: Eliminate the monitor, dummy and seasoning wafers that eat wafer starts: in-chamber optical emission and RF sensors plus virtual metrology qualify tools on product wafers, keeping reclaimed monitors only for audits.

title: Refresh scan turns uniform rows into a single metadata bit
idea: Reverse refresh from a pure cost into a survey: as the refresh engine senses each row, a small comparator in the sense-amp stripe detects rows that are all-0 or all-1 and sets a bit in a per-subarray bitmap. Those rows drop out of the refresh schedule and their contents are regenerated from the bitmap when next opened.

title: Swap hydrogen for deuterium in the final DRAM anneal
idea: Reverse the isotope: in existing mature DRAM lines, replace the forming-gas hydrogen anneal that passivates interface and STI traps with a high-pressure (~20 atm) deuterium anneal in existing high-pressure anneal tools. Si-D bonds resist hot-carrier and thermal depassivation far better than Si-H, so fewer traps reactivate into the GIDL and variable-retention-time tail.

title: Elastic twin-cell rows: trade capacity for retention on demand
idea: Reverse one-cell-per-bit into two-cells-per-bit at run time: a decoder change in DRAM built on existing mature lines lets the controller pair a row with its twin across the open-bitline sense amps and store complementary charge, so the amplifier sees a full differential instead of a half signal. Regions switched to twin mode (phone standby, long-lived cold data) lose half their capacity but retain ~4-10x longer.
note: CLR-DRAM and MCR-DRAM are prior art.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory: cool the DRAM, shrink the sense amps
idea: Reverse the thermal assumption: memory sleds run at 77 K in liquid nitrogen produced on site by U.S. air-separation plants (no helium); junction and GIDL leakage collapse, mobility roughly doubles and Vt mismatch tightens, allowing half-size SAs and VARY ~0.6 V.

title: Silicon switched-capacitor PMIC replaces on-die charge pumps
idea: Reverse where high rails are made: VPP, VBB and VARY come from a U.S.-fabbed silicon switched-capacitor converter on the module, fed through bumps; silicon is chosen over GaN because gallium is ~98% Chinese.

title: Self-timed sense amps signal completion, absorbing mature-node variation
idea: Reverse the timing source: each SA group raises a dual-rail done flag when its latch has regenerated and the bank proceeds when all flags are up, so periphery built at U.S. 28-40 nm fabs runs at typical rather than worst-case speed.

title: One line mask, rotated 90 degrees, makes 4F2 crosspoints
idea: Use a single SAQP mandrel mask twice: expose it, then rotate the wafer 90 degrees and expose it again on a second hardmask, so its lines define both the wordline and bitline grids and their intersections self-align the vertical-channel pillars of a 4F2 cell.

title: Pillar-first, dielectric-last molybdenum wiring
idea: Reverse the damascene order: blanket-deposit molybdenum, subtractively etch pillars and lines, then gap-fill oxide around them instead of filling metal into dielectric holes with WF6 CVD.

title: Reuse one donor wafer ten times for 3D tiers
idea: Reverse the substrate from consumed to recycled: grow crystalline Si on a porous-Si release layer on a donor wafer, transfer a thin layer to the DRAM stack, then re-polish and re-grow so each Czochralski wafer gives 10+ tiers.

title: Compression pays for ECC: eight-chip DIMMs keep full protection
idea: Reverse 'ECC needs spare chips': the controller compresses each 64 B line by at least 8 bytes (most lines allow it) and writes the ECC into the freed space; the rare incompressible line goes to a small overflow region marked by a pointer flag.
note: COP/Frugal ECC prior art.

title: Rack-wide deduplicated page cache in one pooled memory box
idea: Move the OS file page cache, which often fills 30-50% of server DRAM with the same container layers, binaries and datasets, out of every host into one rack-level CXL memory pool indexed by file-content hash; hosts map those pages read-only.

title: Accumulate-on-write: the host sends sums, never reads back
idea: Reverse read-modify-write ownership: the interface gains an 'add' write command, and the HBM base die does the read, the BF16/FP32 add and the write-back next to the array, so gradient accumulation, optimizer moments and KV updates never cross the link twice.
note: Memory-side atomics/PIM reductions are known art.

title: Air-gap transmission lines by sacrificial polymer release
idea: Reverse 'more dielectric': pattern interposer signal lines on a sacrificial polymer (e.g. polynorbornene) and thermally decompose it through a porous cap, leaving copper lines suspended in air (k~1) instead of polyimide (k~3.3).
note: Sacrificial polynorbornene air gaps are known art (Georgia Tech); interposer wire C is a modest share of total access energy.

title: Cryogenic copper interposer at 77 K for memory packages
idea: Reverse room-temperature design: run the memory package in liquid nitrogen, where copper resistivity falls ~7x and DRAM retention rises by orders of magnitude, and draw interposer lines 7x narrower or longer so more memory dies connect at the same pJ/bit.

title: Test-reject DRAM dies sold as graded AI cache memory
idea: Reverse the reject bin into a product line: dies failing retention or hammer specs are packaged into 'Grade-R' modules with published per-row maps, sold for KV caches and recomputable buffers with host software ECC and short-TTL use at ~40% of prime price.

title: Passivate last: high-pressure deuterium anneal after every plasma step
idea: Reverse the order and swap the passivant: instead of fluorine incorporation in gate and junction oxides, the finished wafer gets a final ~20 atm D2 anneal after all plasma and BEOL steps so no later damage undoes it, and Si-D bonds resist hot-carrier breakage far better than Si-H.

title: Stamp instead of shine: nanoimprint as an EUV second source
idea: Reverse patterning from projection to contact: qualify nanoimprint lithography, already proven for NAND, for DRAM's periodic array layers (wordlines, bitlines, storage-node contacts). EUV/ArF is kept only for the irregular periphery.
note: Canon NIL already evaluated by SK hynix/Kioxia; overlay and defectivity are the gates.

title: Deuterium passivation targeted only at the storage-node junction
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: the leakage tail lives at the storage-node junction and its interface traps, so give that one spot a different material property. A self-aligned opening at the storage-node contact admits a deuterium implant plus anneal; Si-D bonds resist hot-carrier and thermal depassivation far better than Si-H (giant isotope effect), so tail traps stay passivated over life and VRT is suppressed.
note: Deuterium anneal well known; localized implant at storage contact is a minor twist.

title: Curvature-rounded, ultra-graded storage junction to flatten peak field
idea: TRIZ #14 Spheroidality: replace sharp corners with curves. A hydrogen-anneal silicon-migration step rounds the recess-channel corners at the storage-node edge, and a laser-spike-diffused wide graded junction replaces the abrupt one, cutting the peak lateral field from ~1 MV/cm toward ~0.6 MV/cm, where trap-assisted tunnelling depends exponentially on field.

title: Two-threshold margin sensing during refresh learns each row's retention online
idea: TRIZ #20 Continuity of useful action: refresh is pure overhead, so make every refresh also a measurement. Sense amps perform a second, offset sensing pass during refresh; rows whose '1' signal has decayed past a warning threshold are promoted to a faster refresh bin and rows with large margin are demoted to slower bins, building a live per-row retention map that tracks VRT and aging.

title: Millisecond flash-lamp anneal gives crystalline, low-trap stacks on cheap glass
idea: TRIZ #21 Skipping (rushing through): heat only the top micrometres to ~900-1000 C for ~1 ms with xenon flash lamps, so the gate dielectric densifies and the oxide channel crystallises while the soda-lime glass or polymer substrate stays below its softening point.
note: FLA on glass/polymer TFTs is established; trap reduction modest.

title: Reusable donor wafers via porous-silicon release of device layers
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: only the top ~1 um needs device-grade crystal, so grow a double-porous Si release layer on a premium CZ donor, epi the device layer, bond it to a cheap reclaimed or multicrystalline handle, split at the porous layer and re-polish the donor for 10-20 reuses.

title: Multi-port read-only shared pool for rack-wide weights and images
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: split memory into an asymmetric write-rarely class (model weights, OS images, libraries, reference data) held once per rack in a multi-ported 180 nm memory controller with 16 slow, wide ports, like 1990s dual-port VRAM or mainframe shared storage, while each server keeps only small private read-write DRAM.

title: 180 nm silicon-photonic links for rack-scale memory pooling
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution: replace copper memory links with optical ones built on 200 mm, 180 nm photonics lines (ring modulators and Ge photodiodes need no fine lithography), giving accelerators reach to a shared memory pool with only tens of ns of flight time, so each carries less local HBM.

title: Porous page mapping backs only written 256-byte chunks
idea: TRIZ #31 Porous materials: a 180 nm memory-side translation chip makes each 4 KB (or 2 MB huge) page 'porous'; only the 256 B chunks actually written get physical backing, tracked by a per-page 16-bit occupancy mask, and unwritten holes read as zero and cost nothing.
note: Zero-line elimination in memory-side compression (MXT, Compresso) covers this.

title: Prior counteraction: counter-bowed dies for 24-high stacks
idea: TRIZ #9 Preliminary anti-action: measure each tier's bonding warpage, then deposit a tuned SiN backside stress film so each thinned die is pre-bowed the opposite way and goes flat at bonding temperature. This removes edge voids in hybrid-bonded 16-24-high stacks.

title: Segmentation: legacy LPDDR4 dies tiled into an HBM-emulator package
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation: instead of one tall TSV stack, tile 24-32 known-good LPDDR4/DDR4 dies from mature 1x/2x-nm DRAM lines flat on a fan-out RDL substrate from existing OSAT lines. Each die gets its own x16 channel, and a 28 nm hub die aggregates them into a 1024-bit HBM-like port. (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)

title: Prior counteraction: pre-emphasis lets HBM-class links run on organic substrate
idea: TRIZ #9 Preliminary anti-action: put feed-forward equalization and per-lane deskew in a 28 nm base/hub die that pre-distorts signals against the known channel loss. This allows 1024-bit memory links on ordinary 2/2 um organic fan-out substrates instead of silicon interposers. (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)
note: Organic RDL interposers with HBM already shipping.

title: Dynamics: optical circuit-switched rack memory pool from 90 nm photonics
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: build memory-pooling links with silicon photonics from existing 90/45 nm photonics foundry lines, plus a MEMS optical circuit switch that reconnects DRAM sleds to whichever servers need them every few seconds. (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)

title: Mechanics substitution: polymer optical waveguides replace copper memory traces
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution (replace the copper field with light): laminate siloxane polymer waveguides into ordinary PCBs on existing PCB lines, and put 28 nm VCSEL driver chips at the memory controller and on the modules, so memory channels run optically across the board. (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)

title: Color change: wavelength-addressed memory modules on passive AWG routers
idea: TRIZ #32 Color changes: give each memory module its own wavelength. The controller picks a module by tuning its laser color, and a passive arrayed-waveguide grating routes the light, so there is no electrical or optical switch in the path. All parts come from trailing-node photonics and InP laser lines. (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)

title: Homogeneity: maskless direct-write silicon interposers in 200 mm fabs
idea: TRIZ #33 Homogeneity: make interposers from silicon, which matches the dies' CTE, in idle 200 mm fabs, and pattern 2 um Cu RDL with maskless laser direct-imaging tools borrowed from the PCB industry. Interposers can then exceed the reticle limit without stitching and need no masks. (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)
note: Maskless 2 um RDL tools exist (e.g. digital litho); 200 mm wafers limit interposer count.

title: Bit-granular weak-cell extraction into an on-die patch SRAM
idea: TRIZ #2 Taking out: at wafer sort the 0.01-0.1% of cells with retention under 1 s are pulled out individually; a small per-bank address CAM plus SRAM data bits shadows them, so array refresh is set by the median cell (seconds) instead of the 13 fA tail.

title: Mat-location-tuned ECC strength map from fail-bit statistics
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: mats at array edges, next to sense-amp stripes or on known litho hotspots borrow spare columns to run a t=2-3 BCH code while interior mats keep SEC; the strength map is fused at sort from fail-bit-map statistics.

title: Per-boot keyed Feistel scramble of physical row adjacency
idea: TRIZ #9 Prior counteraction: an on-die 4-round Feistel network keyed by a per-boot random seed permutes logical-to-physical rows within each subarray and is re-keyed incrementally each refresh window, so an attacker cannot know which logical rows sandwich a victim.
note: Similar to RRS/SRS randomized row swap; re-keying requires costly row migration.

title: Rewritable on-die remap CAM for lifetime self-retirement
idea: TRIZ #11 Beforehand cushioning: replace one-shot antifuse post-package repair with an SRAM remap CAM loaded from a small rewritable on-die store and backed by a 1-2% hidden row reserve, so the scrubber retires rows as they begin failing, SSD bad-block style, an unlimited number of times.

title: Molybdenum-filled TSVs match silicon expansion, shrinking stress zones
idea: TRIZ #37 Thermal expansion: through-silicon vias are filled with domestic molybdenum (CTE ~5 ppm/K, near silicon's ~3) instead of copper (~17), removing the thermomechanical stress that degrades retention of nearby cells and forces keep-out zones.

title: Merging: regional memory utility selling pooled DRAM as GB-hours
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging: a utility operator owns rack-scale CXL-switched DRAM pools in colocation hubs and leases capacity per GB-hour to many tenants, merging the stranded headroom each server is provisioned with into one shared pool.

title: Beforehand cushioning: mandated closed-loop helium recovery in every memory fab
idea: TRIZ #11 Cushion in advance: retrofit wafer-backside cooling, leak-check and litho purge lines with capture, membrane purification and recompression loops reclaiming ~90-95% of helium on-site, with a 6-month buffer cylinder bank.

title: Inversion: mask-frozen DRAM nodes depreciated over 15 years
idea: TRIZ #13 Inversion: stop node migration; freeze a DRAM node's mask set for 15 years and allow just one added mask per generation for incremental gains (e.g., a second capacitor tier), so tools fully depreciate before replacement.

title: Myelin sheath bitline: air-gap wrap raises cell-to-bitline transfer ratio
idea: Myelin wraps axons to cut their capacitance. Wrap each buried bitline in a sealed vacuum or air-gap sheath (k~1), segmented by short SiN 'nodes of Ranvier' for mechanical support, cutting bitline capacitance by ~40-50%.
note: Air spacers on bitlines already in DRAM production; incremental.

title: Quorum-sensing sentinel cells pace refresh per subarray
idea: Bacteria act only when autoinducer concentration passes a threshold; embed in each subarray five deliberately weakened sentinel cells (smaller capacitor, implanted to leak ~3 sigma worse than the real tail) with a local comparator, and refresh that subarray only when a quorum of 3 of 5 drops below threshold.

title: Cardiac-pacemaker coupled oscillators sweep refresh as traveling waves
idea: Sinoatrial cells are weakly coupled oscillators with built-in backups; give each subarray a local ring-oscillator refresh timer coupled to its neighbors so the phases lock into a traveling wave, letting refresh march subarray by subarray while the others keep serving.

title: Antioxidant hydrogen-scavenger layer guards oxide-channel access transistors
idea: Cells use catalase and glutathione to sacrificially mop up reactive species before they damage DNA; pattern a hydrogen-gettering film (Ti-rich TiNx or an oxygen-rich ZrOx sink) next to but isolated from the In2O3/InGaZnO channel so it irreversibly traps hydrogen diffusing from later PECVD SiN and BEOL dielectrics at <=400 C.

title: Rod-and-cone dual-mode back gate for BEOL double-gate access FETs
idea: Retinas switch between fast cones and sensitive rods; make BEOL access FETs double-gate oxide channels whose bottom gate is a shared per-mat plane at 0 V in active mode (low Vt, high Ion) and driven to about -2 V in retention mode, raising Vt ~0.5 V.

title: Electric-eel stacked charge pump built from spare array capacitors
idea: Electric eels stack thousands of electrocytes in series to reach 600 V. Build the VPP/VBB pumps from blocks of ordinary high-AR cell capacitors (dummy rows at mat edges, thousands in parallel), switched by array transistors into a series-parallel ladder stack, instead of planar MOS capacitors in the periphery.

title: Leaf-vein looped wordline mesh survives broken staircase contacts
idea: Copy reticulate leaf venation, where loops reroute flow around damage: tie each tier's wordline plate to its driver through a looped mesh of 3-4 staircase contacts with distributed straps, so an open contact or cracked stair reroutes current through neighbouring loops instead of killing the tier.

title: Double-helix twin cells: complementary bit pairs in adjacent tiers
idea: DNA pairs every base with its complement so damage is detectable; store each bit as true and complement charge in two cells in vertically adjacent tiers of the same column, which share temperature, process and leakage environment, and sense them differentially against each other so 125 C leakage becomes common-mode.

title: Haversian canals: copper heat channels keep a hot stack isothermal
idea: Bone threads Haversian canals through dense tissue to serve deep cells; run Cu-filled canal pillars through dummy columns of the 3D array every ~20 um, linking each tier to the heat spreader, so a 100-tier stack over logic adds <3 C above a 125 C ambient instead of ~15 C.
note: Thermal TSVs/pillars are known 3D IC practice.

title: Nautilus septa: each tier group sealed in its own hermetic chamber
idea: The nautilus seals each shell chamber with a septum pierced only by the siphuncle; deposit hermetic ALD Al2O3/SiN septa above and below every few tiers of an oxide-semiconductor 3D array, pierced only by metal-plugged vertical bitlines, so moisture and hydrogen from upper layers cannot migrate down during 10 yrs at 125 C.

title: Biomineralization-style area-selective growth replaces subtractive etch steps
idea: Shells and bones place mineral only where an organic matrix tells them to. Pattern a sacrificial molecular matrix (phosphonic-acid self-assembled monolayer) once, then grow capacitor supports, hardmasks and spacers additively by area-selective ALD only on matrix-free regions, skipping blanket-deposit/litho/etch cycles.

title: Stem-cell wafers: one front-end mask set, differentiated in last metals
idea: Stem cells differentiate on signal; run one universal array-plus-periphery front end for DDR5, LPDDR, HBM base and CXL parts, then personalize I/O, bank grouping and density bin in the last two metal layers by maskless e-beam or laser direct write.

title: Tardigrade dormant-wafer banks absorb DRAM demand and price swings
idea: Tardigrades suspend metabolism and revive on demand; run wafers through the capital-heavy front end (array and capacitor) during demand troughs, park them in dry-nitrogen 'cryptobiosis' stockers, and finish BEOL and test in 3-4 weeks when prices spike.

title: Octopus-arm memory modules reduce data before it reaches the host
idea: Two-thirds of an octopus's neurons live in its arms; likewise CXL memory expanders carry local filter, aggregate, top-k and embedding-pooling engines so the host receives answers rather than raw rows, eliminating host-side staging buffers and duplicate working copies.

title: Hydra stem-cell spare pool differentiates into failed modules
idea: Hydra renews itself from stem cells; each rack keeps 3-5% of memory as undifferentiated hot spares that silently mirror compressed copies of the most failure-prone ranges and instantly take over an address range, with dead units swapped in monthly batch maintenance.

title: Octopus nerve ring: stack-to-stack shortcut bypassing the processor
idea: Octopus arms exchange signals through a nerve ring without involving the brain. In the same way, the HBM base dies around an accelerator get a ring of short interposer links to their neighbours, so KV-cache moves, page migration and memory-side reductions go stack-to-stack without crossing the GPU's PHYs and on-chip network.
note: Memory-network chaining (HMC) known.

title: Ant-bridge glass chiplets: embedded glass bridges link memory and GPU
idea: Army ants build bridges only where the column must cross a gap. Likewise small glass bridge chiplets with 1-2 um lines are embedded in an organic substrate only under the GPU-to-memory edges, replacing both full silicon interposers and silicon EMIB-style bridges; the bridges are cut from large panels patterned with display-class lithography.
note: EMIB-like bridges and glass substrates both pursued by industry.

title: Synaptic pruning: over-wired glass RDL, then prune defects after test
idea: Brains overgrow synapses and then prune the unused ones. Glass interposers are built with ~2x redundant fine-pitch routes between GPU and memory sites; after assembly, built-in test finds open or shorted routes, and laser or electrical fuses prune the bad links and the unused spares.

title: Hermit-crab reuse mandate: thymus-screened retired DIMMs into CXL pools
idea: Hermit crabs live in shells others discard; a federal right-to-reuse rule plus procurement credit routes hyperscalers' decommissioned DDR4/DDR5 into CXL memory pools instead of shredders, after an automated 'thymic' stage that stress-tests each DIMM and maps out weak rows before reissue.

title: Aquaporin membranes turn brackish groundwater into fab ultrapure water
idea: Aquaporin channels pass water near the diffusion limit while rejecting ions. Membranes with embedded biomimetic aquaporins treat brackish aquifers in the U.S. Southwest into UPW feed at lower pressure, and close the loop on fab wastewater.

title: Endosymbiont memory-as-organelle: royalty IP inside every accelerator die
idea: Mitochondria live inside cells but keep their own genome. A memory company licenses a capacitorless on-die memory macro, with its own test and repair firmware, to AI accelerators and SoCs for per-bit royalties, so the bits are made on logic wafers instead of in memory fabs.

title: Solar-wafer gettering sinks buried under arrays to vacuum up tail metals
idea: Multicrystalline solar silicon became usable through phosphorus-diffusion and cavity gettering that pull Fe, Cu and Ni out of the active volume. Build a sacrificial gettering band 2-3 um under each DRAM array (carbon co-implant plus a hydrogen-implanted cavity layer, no scarce helium) and add a late low-temperature 'gettering soak' so transition-metal deep-level traps migrate away from storage junctions.
note: Gettering already standard in DRAM wafers; incremental tail gain.

title: Regenerative braking for bitlines: recycle refresh charge into the next subarray
idea: Electric vehicles recover braking energy instead of burning it in friction brakes. After a subarray's refresh, before equalization, connect its high-side bitlines through a charge-sharing switch matrix to the next subarray's bitlines so the next refresh starts part-charged, recovering a further ~25-40% of bitline CV^2 beyond normal equalization.

title: Pressure-cooker deuterium anneal replaces fluorine interface passivation of access gates
idea: Pressure cookers cook through at lower temperature by raising pressure. Instead of fluorine implants or F-containing gate stacks, run a 20-25 atm pure-D2 anneal at ~350 C after capacitor and BEOL so deuterium penetrates deep buried-wordline and vertical-channel interfaces that forming gas cannot reach; Si-D bonds resist hot-carrier and thermal depassivation better than Si-H.

title: District-heating supply of wordline high voltage from base die
idea: Like a district heating plant replacing a boiler in every house, generate VPP (~3 V) and negative back-bias in one efficient inductive or switched-capacitor converter on the HBM base die or DIMM PMIC, and deliver them to every core die through dedicated TSVs/pads instead of many small on-die charge pumps.

title: Grid capacitor banks: dummy cell capacitors become pumps and decap
idea: Like a utility's capacitor bank, gang the edge/dummy rows of the cell array, whose high-AR capacitors are already built (~50 fF/um2), in parallel as charge-pump flying capacitors and on-die decoupling, replacing large planar MOS capacitors in the periphery.

title: Insurance pool: hashed global spare columns replace per-mat redundancy
idea: Like insurers pooling risk instead of every household holding reserves, remove the redundant columns from each subarray and give each bank a shared pool of spare column segments addressed by a small CAM keyed on (subarray, column), mapped in at the column path.

title: Radio aperture synthesis: twin mini-cells summed on one bitline
idea: Like an interferometer combining small dishes into one big aperture, store each bit in two half-size capacitors on different tiers/wordlines that fire together onto one bitline; their charges add, so each capacitor needs only ~2.5 fF.

title: Liquid-CO2 garment dry-cleaning for periphery post-etch residue
idea: Dry cleaners replaced perchloroethylene with liquid CO2. Clean every periphery post-etch and post-ash step with supercritical CO2 plus 1-3% alcohol/amine cosolvent in a pressure chamber that recaptures >95% of the CO2, keeping one short single-wafer UPW rinse only before the gate.

title: Canal-lock water-saving basins for bitline precharge
idea: German canal locks store emptied water in side basins at intermediate heights and reuse it to refill; give each mat 8 on-pitch reservoir capacitors at VDD/8 steps so bitlines discharging after a row closes dump charge stepwise into the basins and the next subarray's bitlines refill from them, taking only the final step from the supply.
note: Stepwise/adiabatic charge recycling is known; on-pitch reservoir area and timing eat most of the claimed 6-8x.

title: Lithium-from-brine playbook: membrane skids harvest helium from U.S. gas streams
idea: Like Salton Sea direct-lithium-extraction plants that pull a minor element out of brine already being pumped, DRAM makers fund containerized hollow-fiber membrane plus pressure-swing-adsorption skids at U.S. nitrogen-rejection units, CO2 wells and small gas fields carrying 0.3-1% He, under fab offtake contracts that pay per liter delivered.

title: Optical-fiber preform chemistry builds synthetic crucible inner walls
idea: Optical-fiber preforms are made by flame-hydrolyzing SiCl4 (VAD/OVD) into ultra-pure soot that is sintered into glass. Deposit a 3-5 mm VAD-soot synthetic-silica inner layer onto a crucible shell made of ordinary non-Spruce-Pine quartz sand, then vacuum-sinter it bubble-free so the melt only ever touches synthetic silica.

title: MP3 bit reservoir: fixed compressed slots with borrowed bits
idea: MP3 frames borrow unused bits from a shared reservoir to hold a constant bitrate; likewise every compressed page gets a fixed 2 KB slot (address = index x 2 KB, no translation table) and pages that overflow borrow 256 B chunks from a per-region reservoir located via a tiny overflow bitmap.
note: Close to Linearly Compressed Pages with exception region.

title: Bullwhip damping: cache each block in exactly one stack layer
idea: Like supply chains where every tier hoards safety stock, the app cache, runtime, OS page cache, hypervisor and storage controller each cache the same block; a cross-layer exclusive-caching protocol passes block ownership tokens on eviction so each block lives in exactly one layer.
note: Exclusive caching protocols (Wong-Wilkes) known.

title: Sushi conveyor: weights circulate a ring, each chip grabs its plate
idea: Model layers circulate continuously on an optical/SerDes ring of accelerators like plates on a kaiten-sushi belt; each chip computes on the layer passing it and holds only a 2-3 layer window locally instead of a full or gathered copy.
note: Weight streaming and FSDP-style rings are known; needs large batches.

title: Flight recorder: MRAM intent journal makes DRAM a crash-safe cache
idea: Like an aircraft black box logging only essential parameters, a small MRAM ring records memory-tier metadata (page-map updates, dirty-line intents, epoch markers) so a flash-backed memory can treat DRAM purely as a volatile cache and rebuild consistent state after power loss.
note: Small NV journal for tier metadata is known practice.

title: Tidal-flow reversible lanes matched to read/write mix
idea: Reversible highway lanes follow the commute. HBM data lanes are split into groups, and the controller sets each group's direction per epoch (for example 15 read : 1 write during decode). This replaces symmetric bidirectional bursts and the turnaround bubbles they cause.

title: Vinyl-pressing nanoimprint stamped RDL trenches and vias
idea: Records are pressed from a master. Likewise, UV-nanoimprint a reusable master into polymer dielectric at room temperature to form 0.5-1 um RDL trenches and via cups in one stroke. Electroplate Cu, then CMP, with a final cure ≤250 C.

title: Post-tensioned-concrete stress films enabling 15 um dies
idea: Post-tensioned concrete is pre-loaded to resist sagging. Deposit tuned compressive and tensile PECVD SiN/SiO2 films at ≤350 C on die backsides to cancel warpage, so 15 um core dies bond flat.
note: Backside stress-compensation films are standard practice.

title: Apoptotic rows: autonomous self-test and soft repair during self-refresh
idea: Cells that detect their own damage trigger programmed death (apoptosis). During self-refresh, an on-die BIST samples rows at extended retention. Rows that fail retire themselves and swap in spare rows through soft-PPR registers, which persist in a small OTP block. The die reports the swaps to the host through mode registers.

title: Power-by-the-hour DRAM leasing with manufacturer take-back
idea: Like Rolls-Royce leasing jet-engine thrust-hours, memory makers keep ownership of modules, bill per GB-hour from on-module telemetry, and take modules back at end of term for retest and redeployment in lower tiers.

title: Svalbard-style shared die vault replacing last-time-buy hoarding
idea: Like a seed vault, an industry cooperative stores Grade-1 qualified DRAM wafers sealed in dry nitrogen at low temperature, then packages and 125 C-screens die on demand for members, so OEMs stop each holding 5-10x over-buys for 10-year programs.

title: Contiguous-disk bubble tracks driven by one global rotating field
idea: Late-1980s bubble chips used ion-implanted contiguous-disk tracks that moved sub-lithographic bubbles under a global rotating in-plane field. On existing 200-mm lines, deposit perpendicular CoTb films, define tracks by ion implantation through a 0.5-um mask (no magnetic etch), drive every track at once with a package-level rotating-field coil, and detect with same-fab magnetoresistive bridges.
note: us latency; a capacity tier, not DRAM-class.

title: Bell Labs CCD memory revived: charge rings with one regenerator
idea: Revive the 1970s CCD serial memories (invented at Bell Labs in 1969, later sold as CCD RAMs): store bits as charge packets in gated MOS potential wells with no per-bit contact or junction, arranged in short rings that pass one regeneration amplifier. Build them at relaxed nodes on U.S. CCD and imager fab processes.
note: Serial latency limits it to a capacity tier; dark current still forces regeneration.

title: Molybdenum-gate MOS revived: graded-work-function wordlines that cut GIDL
idea: Revive the refractory molybdenum-gate MOSFETs of the 1970s: replace tungsten buried wordlines with Colorado-mined molybdenum whose nitrogen content is graded with depth, so the gate work function is high over the channel (good Vt) and low where the gate overlaps the drain (less band bending), suppressing GIDL.
note: Dual-work-function buried wordlines already ship; Mo replacing W widely pursued.

title: Stepwise wordline charging from cell-capacitor tank banks
idea: Revive 1990s adiabatic stepwise charging. Each wordline rises to 3 V in 6 steps through switches to tank capacitors held at intermediate voltages and falls back through them, recovering most of its CV² energy. The tanks are dummy DRAM cell-capacitor arrays reused in the periphery, so the only added mask is a block mask that opens the storage-node module there.

title: ThruChip inductive coupling revived to strip signal TSVs from HBM
idea: Revive Kuroda's abandoned ThruChip Interface: replace the thousands of signal TSVs in an HBM stack with on-die spiral coils that couple data inductively between thinned dies, keeping only a few coarse, wide-pitch power TSVs.

title: Wartime tungsten scrap reclamation feeds domestic fab tungsten chemistry
idea: Revive 1940s cemented-carbide scrap reclamation (the zinc process) and capture tungsten from WF6 exhaust and chamber cleans, converting both into fab-grade WF6 and W targets inside the US for DUV-only memory lines.

title: IBM-style memory leasing: makers own bits, reclaim and redeploy
idea: Revive IBM's 1950s practice of leasing core memory instead of selling it: DRAM makers lease modules by the GB-month, keep ownership, and are paid to reclaim, retest and redeploy them into second-life tiers.

title: Tape-automated-bonding revival: folded polyimide tapes stack DRAM without TSVs
idea: Revive 1970s reel-to-reel TAB: DRAM dies are inner-lead-bonded to non-fluorinated PMDA-ODA polyimide tape with 20 um-pitch copper leads, and the tape is accordion-folded so 8-16 dies stack with their leads converging on a base die.

title: IBM TCM revival: glass-ceramic cofired substrates replace silicon interposers
idea: Revive IBM's 1980s thermal conduction module substrate: 30-60-layer cofired glass-ceramic/copper panels, screen-printed with Cu paste and mechanically punched 50 um vias, carrying many HBM-class stacks plus logic over 100-150 mm.
note: 15-20 um lines give low bandwidth density versus 2 um interposers.
