idea: Time-shift the reliability screen: skip factory burn-in ovens and long retention tests, ship dies with on-die BIST that runs adaptive stress patterns during the first weeks of server idle time, and retire weak rows through the host before data is trusted.

title: Colorado molybdenum replaces Chinese tungsten from mine to monolayer
idea: Vertical integration across scales: Colorado molybdenite is refined domestically into MoO2Cl2/MoCl5 ALD precursors, and molybdenum replaces tungsten in buried wordlines and contacts, where its shorter electron mean free path gives lower resistance below 20 nm width.

title: Kerfless epitaxial wafers: one seed crystal reused fifty times
idea: DRAM uses only the top few microns of a 775 um wafer: grow a 20-50 um epitaxial Si film on a porous-Si release layer atop a reusable seed wafer, lift it off onto a low-cost domestic carrier, and re-polish the seed for ~50 reuses.

title: Thin sol-gel synthetic liner so crucibles need 10x less HPQ
idea: Scale jump from bulk to skin: build the crucible body from lower-grade quartz and line only the 1-2 mm surface that touches the melt with synthetic sol-gel silica made from chemical precursors.

title: Monolayer molecular doping instead of ion implanters
idea: Scale jump from beamline accelerator to molecule: self-assembled monolayers of phosphorus- or boron-bearing molecules coat the silicon, and a spike anneal drives the dopant in, replacing implanters and their Ar/Xe flood guns for shallow source/drain and periphery junctions.

title: Delay-line regeneration reborn as a self-timed refresh wave
idea: Mercury delay-line memories died on serial latency, but they refreshed themselves by recirculating every bit through a regenerator. Make refresh a travelling wave in the same way: each subarray refreshes one row locally, then hands a token to its neighbor, so refresh ripples continuously across the die. There are no global REF commands or all-bank stalls; the controller only sees a known 1-of-N subarray busy.

title: Automata Processor salvaged as a sense-amp key-match GET engine
idea: Failure mined: Micron's Automata Processor put state machines next to DRAM arrays and died on an alien programming model. Fix: add one XOR plus wired-NOR comparator per 64 sense amps and expose a single command, GET(key). A broadcast key is matched against every key in the open row (one hash bucket), and only the matching value leaves the chip.
note: Close to Sieve-style in-DRAM matching.

title: TSV-free HBM: ThruChip inductive links plus power-only vias
idea: HMC's power-hungry SerDes and Keio's ThruChip inductive-coupling interface both stalled, and HBM won while paying a large TSV tax. Stack DRAM dies with on-die spiral coils carrying data over near-field links (~0.1 pJ/bit). Keep only a sparse ring of large power TSVs at the die edge, so about 90% of TSVs and their keep-out zones disappear.
note: ThruChip known; power vias remain.

title: Bubble-memory bootloop map applied to 3D DRAM strings
idea: Magnetic bubble chips shipped with defective minor loops masked by an on-chip loop map, then died on speed. Give every 3D DRAM die a rewritable defect map at the vertical-string level. Firmware retires defective or worn strings in the field, and the map's health record grades the die for second-life reuse.
note: Redundancy and post-package repair are standard DRAM practice; extension to strings is incremental.

title: Supercritical CO2 cleaning, abandoned in 2000s, revived for capacitor rinse-dry
idea: Supercritical CO2 wafer cleaning was abandoned on particle redeposition and slow high-pressure single-wafer chambers. Aim it at the one place it wins: replace the repeated wet clean and IPA dry of 60-75:1 pillars with SC-CO2 plus amine/alcohol cosolvent residue removal and stiction-free drying, recirculating >95% of CO2 captured from ammonia or ethanol plants.

title: Purdue's 1990s silicon-carbide DRAM rebuilt on EV-glut SiC wafers
idea: Purdue built 4H-SiC DRAM cells in the 1990s with retention of hours or longer at room temperature, killed by expensive, micropipe-riddled SiC wafers. EV power electronics has since driven 200 mm SiC to low defect density and falling prices; build a planar or trench 1T1C cell on 4H-SiC whose 3.3 eV bandgap makes junction and GIDL leakage negligible.

title: ThruChip inductive coupling replaces HBM's through-silicon via tax
idea: Keio's ThruChip Interface (inductive coils in standard metal layers) never displaced TSVs because coil area and link power looked worse at 2010 bandwidths. Put 30-50 um coils in the DRAM top metal under each channel, thin dies to ~20 um, stack with adhesive only and bring power through edge wirebonds, so no via etch, fill, reveal or keep-out zones remain.

title: HP The Machine, minus memristor: rack single-copy read-only data
idea: HP's The Machine died because its memristor never shipped, orphaning a sound idea: fabric-attached memory shared by many nodes. Use CXL 3 shared memory with commodity DRAM to hold exactly one rack-wide copy of read-only data (model weights, reference genomes, dictionaries, container layers) mapped read-only into every host.
note: CXL 3 shared memory widely discussed; GPU HBM copies remain.

title: Global Memory Service, fixed: a spot market for idle fleet DRAM
idea: UW's 1990s Global Memory Service paged to idle workstations' RAM but died on 10 Mb/s networks and owners' lack of incentive. With 400G RDMA, run an internal spot market where hosts post unused DRAM at a price, borrowers bid for 1 GB revocable leases, and the scheduler packs elastic jobs onto borrowed memory.

title: Transparent huge pages, fixed: per-4KB valid bitmap stops bloat
idea: Databases disable THP because 2 MB pages physically back untouched memory and bloat RSS. Give each 2 MB TLB entry a 512-bit valid bitmap read by the page-table walker so only touched 4 KB frames are physically backed, keeping TLB reach without the bloat.
note: Partial-subblock TLBs (Talluri-Hill) and Ingens/HawkEye cover this; needs CPU changes.

title: Everspin MRAM, fixed: MRAM write-combining journal makes NAND workable memory
idea: Everspin MRAM never reached Gb density, so it never replaced DRAM. Use a small MRAM as a nonvolatile write-combining journal in front of NAND: random 64 B stores land in MRAM at ns latency, are coalesced into full NAND pages in the background, and reads check the MRAM index first.
note: MRAM write caches in SSDs already shipped.

title: Connection Machine, fixed: bit-serial compute inside cache SRAM arrays
idea: Thinking Machines' CM-1 used 65,536 bit-serial processors with private memory and died on cost and programmability. Do bit-serial compute inside existing SRAM subarrays by activating two wordlines and sensing bitline AND/NOR on transposed data, so each bitline is a processor and activations are processed where they sit.
note: Neural Cache / Compute Caches prior art.

title: RDRAM's royalty trap fixed: royalty-free open memory-PHY commons for newcomers
idea: Rambus RDRAM lost partly because per-chip royalties, litigation and costly at-speed test made it pricier than SDRAM. Create a RISC-V-style foundation that funds, silicon-proves and licenses royalty-free DRAM-side PHYs, TSV/hybrid-bond I/O cells and controller IP, backed by a defensive patent pool of CHIPS-Act buyers, so a U.S. memory or packaging startup can tape out a base die without a $10-30M IP bill.

title: Sub-THz plastic waveguides lost to optics; In/Ga bans flip that
idea: Polymer dielectric waveguides carrying 100-300 GHz carriers lost to optical cables because lasers were cheaper at volume. With In/Ga-based lasers ruled out, use solid polyethylene or PTFE ribbons fed by CMOS sub-THz transceivers to connect compute sleds to memory sleds at 1-3 m, carrying 100+ Gb/s per ribbon at ~1-2 pJ/bit with no lasers.

title: nCHIP silicon MCMs revived as 180 nm HBM interposers
idea: Early-1990s silicon-substrate multichip modules (nCHIP and others) died for lack of a product valuable enough to pay for them. HBM is that product: run thin-film silicon interposer and bridge lines (0.4-2 um wiring, Bosch-etched through-silicon vias, a 1994 process) in idle 200 mm, 180 nm-0.5 um fabs to add capacity beside the CoWoS-class packaging bottleneck.

title: Irvine Sensors cubes: edge-wired DRAM stacks without TSVs
idea: Irvine Sensors stacked bare memory dies into edge-wired cubes for military use in the 1990s, and the method never went mainstream. Fix: laminate 8-16 thinned standard DDR dies, route their pads to the cube's side face, and pattern the side wiring with 1990s thick-film lithography, giving high-capacity stacks for CXL and server modules without TSVs.

title: Orbital Hall torque from chromium writes magnets without tungsten or platinum
idea: Effect walk: orbital Hall effect. Replace W/Pt/Ta spin-Hall write lines in SOT magnetic cells with light 3d metals (Cr, Ti, V) whose orbital Hall conductivity is predicted ~10x Pt's spin Hall conductivity, converting the orbital current to torque through a 1-nm Ni or Gd conversion layer under the free layer.
note: Orbital Hall torque is an active research field.

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal hardens traps behind the leakage tail
idea: Effect: kinetic isotope effect. Replace the final forming-gas anneal with 10-20 atm D2 so Si-D bonds passivate interface and GIDL-region traps; Si-D resists field- and hot-carrier-driven depassivation ~10-50x better than Si-H, so fewer traps reactivate into weak or VRT cells over life. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.

title: Arrhenius canary rows set the die's internal refresh skipping
idea: Effect: thermally activated leakage with known activation energy (~0.6 eV). Each mat holds canary rows with deliberately smaller capacitors that fail at a known fraction of real-cell retention; counters time their decay at actual temperature, and the die skips REF work on real rows whenever canaries prove margin. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.

title: Majority-state inversion plus bitline parking silences idle leakage
idea: Effect: asymmetric leakage (a node at substrate and bitline potential cannot decay). On write, each row gets an internal inversion flag in on-die ECC spare bits chosen so most cells hold the low state; in self-refresh/power-down the bitlines park at 0 V, so those cells see zero drain bias and zero junction bias, and bitlines re-equalize within tXS. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.

title: Stressor-driven controlled spalling reuses one CZ wafer twenty times
idea: Effect: fracture mechanics. A tensile Ni stressor film plated at room temperature drives a crack parallel to the surface at a depth set by film stress (Suo-Hutchinson mode mixity), peeling 10-20 um single-crystal Si layers without kerf. Bond them to carriers at <=300 C for junctionless accumulation-mode cell transistors, re-polish the donor and repeat; sold as a wafer-leasing model.

title: Remote-plasma atomic-oxygen oxidation retires quartz furnaces at 400 C
idea: Effect: radical-driven oxidation kinetics. Atomic oxygen from a microwave or ICP remote plasma oxidizes and nitrides silicon at 300-400 C with near-thermal interface quality (Dit ~1e10/cm2eV). Gate, liner and isolation oxides come from single-wafer chambers instead of 900 C batch furnaces.
note: Radical/plasma oxidation tools are commercial.

title: Surface-activated room-temperature bonding stacks memory layers without solder
idea: Effect: dangling-bond covalent adhesion. An argon fast-atom beam strips native oxides so Cu-Cu and SiO2-SiO2 surfaces fuse at room temperature in vacuum, stacking thinned DRAM or oxide-memory layers at <1 um pitch with no Sn-Ag microbumps, underfill or 400 C bonding anneal.
note: Surface-activated bonding is established; particle sensitivity and alignment at <1 um pitch are the issues.

title: Kerr soliton microcomb: one shared laser powers all memory chiplet optics
idea: A single SiN Kerr microcomb per rack generates 64-128 phase-locked wavelengths distributed over fiber as an optical power utility; memory chiplets carry only modulators and detectors, no lasers, removing per-chiplet laser cost, heat and failure.

title: Total internal reflection: roll-to-roll nanoimprinted polymer waveguide flex for memory optics
idea: UV-nanoimprint single-mode fluorinated-acrylate waveguides on a moving polyimide web, with tapered adiabatic couplers that mate evanescently to SiN chips; the flex carries 64+ optical lanes from memory modules to the processor package.

title: Dielectric waveguiding: extruded polymer mm-wave tubes carry memory traffic one meter
idea: Continuously extrude low-loss PTFE/PE dielectric waveguide ribbons and launch 140-220 GHz carriers from CMOS transceivers into them, giving 100+ Gb/s per tube over 1 m with no lasers for board-to-board memory-pool links.

title: Chlorine atomic-layer etching thins channels one monolayer at a time
idea: Cl: thin DUV-defined vertical or lateral silicon channels with cyclic Cl2 adsorption plus low-energy ion removal, ~0.5 A per self-limiting cycle, so body-thickness variation across the array falls below ~0.3 nm regardless of the litho that defined the starting shape.

title: KrF excimer melt-anneal recrystallizes storage-node junctions defect-free
idea: Kr: after the storage-node implant, flash the surface with a tens-of-ns 248 nm KrF excimer pulse that melts only the top ~30-50 nm, so the junction regrows by liquid-phase epitaxy, annihilating end-of-range implant loops and forming a box-shaped junction without deep diffusion.

title: Si: porous-silicon layer transfer reuses one seed wafer
idea: Grow periphery substrates as thin epitaxial Si (SiH2Cl2/H2) on an electrochemically porosified seed wafer (ELTRAN-style), split them off with a water jet and reuse the seed 10-20x, avoiding argon-purged Czochralski pulling and Spruce Pine quartz crucibles for most periphery wafers.
note: ELTRAN-style reuse known; epi wafers usually cost more than CZ.

title: Nitrogen: aluminum-nitride inter-tier heat spreaders hold retention in hot stacks
idea: Use sputtered/ALD polycrystalline AlN (30-100 W/mK vs 1.4 for SiO2) as every third inter-tier dielectric and as the bonding dielectric of memory-on-logic stacks, with AlN-filled dummy holes acting as vertical thermal pillars to the lid.

title: Porous-silicon reusable seed: one CZ crystal, fifty DRAM wafers
idea: Periodic-table walk, Si (14): anodize a seed wafer into a double-layer porous Si, grow a 5-8 um epitaxial device layer, build or bond, then cleave at the weak porous layer and re-polish the seed for 20-50 reuses; the carrier can be reclaimed or upgraded-metallurgical Si because DRAM devices use only the top ~1 um.
note: ELTRAN-type reuse; epi cost offsets wafer savings.

title: Fab-side closed tungsten loop from exhaust and spent targets
idea: Periodic-table walk, W (74): cryo-trap unreacted WF6 from W-CVD exhaust and redistill it, and send spent targets, shields and chamber scrap to zinc-process reclamation under a fab take-back contract.
note: Exhaust WF6 recapture and target reclamation are known; modest W relief.

title: Tin-oxide spacers etched by hydrogen for fluorine-free multiple patterning
idea: Periodic-table walk, Sn (50): use ALD SnO2 as the SADP/SAQP spacer and hardmask, etched in H2/CH4 plasma (volatile SnH4) with high selectivity to Si, SiO2 and carbon, while Si and carbon are etched in Cl2/HBr/O2, a full pitch-quartering flow without CF chemistry; Sn is reclaimed from exhaust.

title: He: helium-free fab using hydrogen backside cooling and recapture
idea: Replace He as electrostatic-chuck backside gas with H2 (similar thermal conductivity) or Ne, switch leak checks to H2/N2 forming-gas sniffers, and recover residual He from tool exhaust with membranes, decoupling uptime from Qatari supply.

title: K: ion-exchanged glass panels replace silicon HBM interposers
idea: Build HBM interposers on 510x515 mm thin glass panels toughened by K+/Na+ ion exchange, laser-drill through-glass vias, and pattern redistribution layers with panel-class tools instead of a 300 mm silicon interposer line.

title: F: anhydrous HF vapor dip-out frees capacitor pillars without rinse
idea: Remove the oxide capacitor mold with anhydrous HF plus alcohol vapor at reduced pressure instead of a wet buffered-HF dip, DI rinse and spin-dry; no liquid touches the pillars, so there is no capillary collapse either.

title: H: remote atomic-hydrogen pre-clean replaces RCA wet benches
idea: Remove native oxide, carbon and metal-organic residue before epi and gate steps with remote atomic hydrogen at 300-500 C plus NF3/NH3 radical oxide removal in the same vacuum cluster, so wafers go from etch to deposition without a wet bench.

title: Cl: ClF3 vapor carves 3D-DRAM lateral recesses dry
idea: Use low-temperature ClF3 gas-phase etching, which removes SiGe with very high selectivity to Si, oxide and nitride, to cut lateral recesses across 26-100 tiers in one batch vacuum step instead of wet selective etch and long rinses.

title: Mo: subtractive dry-etched molybdenum metal layers with no CMP
idea: Deposit blanket Mo, pattern it with dry Cl2/O2 etch, then gap-fill with flowable dielectric cured by UV, the reverse of Cu/W damascene, so the metal layer needs no CMP and no post-CMP clean.
note: Subtractive Mo/Ru widely pursued for logic BEOL.

title: Gold standard: spot-priced GB-seconds that make apps shed memory
idea: Clouds price memory per GB-second at a spot rate tied to fleet DRAM utilization, unbundled from vCPU, and expose an API so applications bid for cache size; elastic caches (Redis, JVM heaps, KV caches) shrink automatically when the price rises, and providers sell memory futures to large tenants.

title: Fluoropolymer nonstick tensors: activations flow chiplet-to-chiplet, never landing in DRAM
idea: PTFE is the fluorine-carbon coating nothing sticks to; the compiler maps inference layers as a spatial pipeline across chiplets so activations stream SRAM-to-SRAM over 0.1-0.3 pJ/bit die-to-die links with credit flow control, and DRAM never stores activations or partial sums.
note: Dataflow chiplet pipelines are established (Cerebras, Tenstorrent).

title: C: polyethylene dielectric waveguides carry sub-THz memory traffic
idea: Drive 140-300 GHz carriers from plain CMOS transceivers into solid polyethylene/PTFE ribbon waveguides (cheap carbon-chain plastic, no lasers, no fiber alignment) between accelerator trays and memory sleds, each ribbon carrying 8-16 lanes at ~50-100 Gb/s.

title: Na: ion-exchanged graded-index waveguides written into soda-lime interposers
idea: Exchange Na+ ions in soda-lime or aluminosilicate glass for K+/Ag+ through a patterned mask in a molten-salt bath, writing buried graded-index optical waveguides into the glass interposer itself to route light between co-packaged optics and memory chiplets.

title: Hf: HfO2 antifuse farms enable massive post-stack HBM repair
idea: Add a dense HfO2-breakdown antifuse array (1T1AF, ~0.1 um2 each) to the HBM base die that remaps failing core-die rows, columns and whole sub-banks found after stacking and at-speed test, far beyond today's limited post-package repair fuses.

title: Si: retention-graded silicon sells dies failing 64 ms as R-grade
idea: Create a JEDEC-style relaxed-retention grade (e.g., 16 ms refresh window) with a per-die weak-row map written into SPD; host controllers refresh faster only where flagged, and AI-inference fleets buy these dies at a discount.

title: He: Helium-recapture-as-a-service skids leased per fab bay
idea: A third party installs membrane plus cryo-adsorption helium recovery skids on chuck backside-cooling, leak-check and purge exhausts, owns the gas, re-purifies it to 6N on site and sells the fab guaranteed helium availability at a fixed price per wafer start.

title: Laser-trimmed wordline-low voltage per subarray at its leakage minimum
idea: Like laser-trimming thin-film resistors to spec, measure each subarray's leakage vs negative-wordline voltage at wafer test. Fuse-trim each subarray's VNWL and body bias to the bottom of its own V-shaped curve, the balance of subthreshold against GIDL.
note: Per-subarray trimmed VNWL; same mechanism.

title: Splat-quenched metallic-glass gates kill grain-driven sense-amp mismatch
idea: Borrow rapid-quench casting of metallic glass: deposit the SA gate metal as an amorphous alloy (e.g., Ta-Si-N or Zr-Cu-Al sputtered on a cold substrate) with no grains. With no random TiN grain orientations there is no grain work-function variation between the two latch transistors.

title: Flying-shuttle sense enable rides the wordline's RC wave
idea: Like Kay's flying shuttle carrying the weft across every warp in one throw, route sense-enable on a delay-matched line parallel to the wordline. Each SA then fires just after its own cell's wordline actually rises, instead of every SA waiting for the slowest far-end cell.

title: Diffusion-furnace bipolar sense amps: BiCMOS revival for millivolt signals
idea: Like a batch furnace that dopes thousands of wafers identically, bipolar transistors match by diffusion depth and emitter area rather than gate litho. Use 1990s BiCMOS to put bipolar differential pre-amps (Vbe mismatch ~0.5 mV) ahead of CMOS latches, shared across column groups.
note: BiCMOS bipolar preamps for low offset, same core idea.

title: Sourdough mother-culture: reference cells that age exactly like data
idea: Like a baker feeding a starter alongside every batch, each mat keeps two reference columns that are rewritten to '1' and '0' at every refresh. On activate they charge-share into a reference that has leaked exactly as much as the data cells since their last refresh.

title: Putting-out system: 180 nm module hub does ECC, repair and refresh
idea: Like the pre-industrial putting-out system that sent specialized steps out to cottages, strip on-die ECC, repair maps, refresh scheduling and row-hammer tracking off every DRAM die. Put them in one 180 nm hub chip per module that runs wide and slow (e.g., 512 bits at 400 MHz).

title: Balanced-layup tiers: alternating stress plies cancel 3D wafer bow
idea: Composite laminates avoid warp with symmetric, balanced layups; design each 3D DRAM tier pair with opposite-sign film stress (tensile channel ply, compressive wordline ply) and orthogonal line directions, so stress and anisotropy cancel every two tiers instead of accumulating.

title: Vinyl-record pressing: nanoimprint stampers for capacitor and channel layers
idea: Records are pressed from nickel stampers replicated from one master; write one e-beam master of the capacitor-hole layer, electroform daughter stampers, and imprint every wafer in mature fabs, aligning to coarse periphery marks.
note: NIL for memory is pursued by Canon/Kioxia; defectivity and overlay are known issues.

title: Electroforming bath: superconformal cobalt fill replaces CVD tungsten wordlines
idea: Jewelry electroforming fills molds bottom-up; use suppressor/accelerator plating chemistry for bottom-up cobalt or copper fill of buried wordlines and 3D lateral wordline recesses on existing plating tools, dropping CVD tungsten.
note: Superconformal Co ECD is used in logic contacts; incremental tungsten substitute.

title: Net-shape deposition: area-selective ALD as 3D-printing for films
idea: Additive manufacturing puts material only where the part needs it; use intrinsically chemoselective ALD (dielectric growing on TiN but blocked on SiO2 by an inhibitor vapor pulse, Ru or Mo growing only on metal) to build capacitor dielectrics, liners and caps in place, skipping blanket-deposit, litho and etch-back cycles.

title: Gutenberg movable-type interposer from standard bridge pieces
idea: Keep a catalog of pre-made standard silicon bridge tiles (memory-PHY, power, crossbar), the way a printer keeps metal type, and compose each product's interposer from them in a molded frame. No new interposer masks are needed per product.
note: Close to CoWoS-L/EMIB bridge reuse already practiced.

title: Standard-gauge memory chiplet footprint like ISO shipping containers
idea: Publish a CHIPS-funded open standard bump map, PHY and stack height for memory chiplets so any domestic DRAM, MRAM or gain-cell die slots onto any base die, the way ISO containers made intermodal shipping work.
note: Overlaps UCIe/JEDEC efforts.

title: Shipping-container reliability shell for alt-fab memory dies
idea: Containerisation let any cargo ride any ship; define a standard CXL buffer-chip 'container' (strong symbol ECC, scrubbing, page retirement, refresh management) so dies from new rare-gas-free alt-fabs (NIL, DSA, interference litho, UV-LED lines) plug into servers interchangeably despite raw BER ~100x worse than DDR5.

title: Carbide-tool zinc reclaim feeds domestic tungsten targets and WF6
idea: Machine shops recycle cemented-carbide tools by the zinc process. Build a U.S. stream that turns scrap carbide and spent tungsten targets into 6N WF6 precursor and sputter targets: zinc-melt breakdown, oxidation, APT conversion, then fluorination or pressing.

title: Bank-paired bitline charge recycling during refresh
idea: IFR: charge that falls in one bank is the charge that rises in another. Refresh banks in pairs offset by half a cycle, linking their bitline restore rails through a 2-4 step switched-capacitor ladder so bank A's discharge toward precharge directly supplies bank B's restore swing.

title: Leak-aligned data encoding with standby bitline biasing
idea: IFR: every cell leaks toward the value it already holds. Each row gets an inversion flag chosen so most cells sit in the state their dominant leakage path (true-cell vs anti-cell) cannot corrupt, standby bitlines are held at the matching rail, and rows are refreshed by count of vulnerable cells only.

title: Shift-token wordlines replace decoders for streaming AI weights
idea: Ideal result: no address decoding because the next row is always known. For weight-streaming tiers, chain sub-wordline drivers into a shift register so a single token ripples row to row; only stream entry points use a coarse decoder.

title: Completion-detecting sense amps make access time average, not worst case
idea: Ideal result: a read that takes exactly as long as that bit needs. Each SA stripe adds a done-detector on replica latches that signals when regeneration completes; the controller uses an asynchronous handshake instead of a fixed worst-case tRCD.

title: Weak rows convert to twin-cell mode on the fly
idea: Ideal result: aging cells heal by teaming up. The row decoder can tie two physical rows into one logical row storing true and complement, so the SA sees a 2x differential signal; rows failing retention are downgraded to twin mode instead of being fused out.
note: Close to CLR-DRAM's coupled-cell mode.

title: Interference-printed array: zero EUV inside the cell field
idea: IFR: 'the array needs no masks at all.' Backward: because the cell field is perfectly periodic, print it with two-beam 193 nm immersion interference (~76 nm pitch) plus spacer quadruple/octuple patterning to ~19/10 nm, with crossed exposures for pillars, and reserve projection or EUV litho for mat edges and periphery only.
note: Pre-EUV DRAM already used SAQP from 193i; interference mandrel saves little.

title: Turn polysilicon-plant waste SiCl4 into synthetic-silica crucibles
idea: Ideal: crucibles made from something we throw away. Closest: route silicon tetrachloride byproduct from U.S. Siemens-process polysilicon plants through flame hydrolysis into synthetic fused-silica soot, then sinter into full-body or inner-wall crucibles with ~10x lower metal impurities than natural HPQ.

title: Supercritical-CO2 cleaning replaces most ultrapure-water wet cleans
idea: Ideal: a fab with no water. Closest: replace post-etch residue removal, post-CMP clean and capacitor-hole cleans with supercritical CO2 plus small co-solvent/chelator doses, which penetrates 100:1 holes with zero surface tension and is >95% recycled by depressurize-recompress loops.

title: Closed-loop recovery of tungsten, hafnium, zirconium from fab waste
idea: Ideal: scarce metals that never leave the fab. Closest: cold-trap and scrub unreacted WF6 and Zr/Hf amide precursors from ALD/CVD exhaust (ALD utilization is often <5%), chemically strip PVD shields and chamber kits, and ship recovered oxides to a domestic refiner for re-precursor synthesis.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling with palladium recovery replaces scarce helium
idea: Ideal: etch and deposition need no helium. Closest: switch electrostatic-chuck backside gas to H2 (thermal conductivity close to He) at sub-flammable volumes, with a Pd-membrane capture-and-reuse loop on each tool; keep He only where H2 chemistry is incompatible.

title: Rack-wide content-addressed page pool for weights and libraries
idea: IFR: each distinct byte exists once per rack. Closest: a CXL memory pool indexes immutable 2 MB pages (model weights, container layers, shared libraries, JIT code) by 128-bit hash; every host maps them read-only through a small local cache, with copy-on-write on modification.

title: Lossless rANS-coded weights decoded inside the HBM base die
idea: IFR: weights are stored at their true information content. Closest: BF16/FP8 exponents (about 2.6 bits of entropy in 8) and top mantissa bits are rANS-coded per tensor, and line-rate decoders in the HBM/LPDDR logic die expand them so the host sees ordinary BF16.

title: Sub-page MMU mapping merges sparse pages into one frame
idea: IFR: zero fragmentation. Closest: the MMU gains a 256 B mesh granularity inside 4 KB pages so two half-empty pages whose live slots do not overlap share one physical frame; a hardware bitmap scanner finds mergeable pairs.

title: Laser-free rack memory pool over a passive copper backplane
idea: IFR: memory follows demand anywhere. Constraint: optical links need GaAs/InP lasers and InGaAs detectors (Ga, In), so stay electrical: a 1.5 m passive Cu twinax backplane and mature-node CXL switches with Al-Cu/Ti wiring pool DRAM across 16-32 hosts, sized to the P99 of the aggregate rather than each host's peak.

title: TSV-free cube stacking with sidewall-printed interconnect
idea: Ideal: a memory stack with no holes in it. Closest achievable: route each DRAM die's bus to one edge, stack dies like playing cards, polish the stack face and pattern a 2 um redistribution layer across the exposed edges so all vertical wiring lives on the sidewall outside the silicon.

title: Plastic sub-terahertz waveguide ribbons replace copper memory channels
idea: Ideal: a memory channel with no copper loss. Closest achievable: run D-band (110-170 GHz) carriers through polymer dielectric waveguide ribbons between the GPU package and memory modules up to ~1 m, launched by CMOS on-die couplers, so memory can sit off-package without optics.

title: Single optical clock broadcast removes clock-recovery from memory links
idea: Ideal: every chip already knows when each bit will arrive. Closest achievable: distribute one low-jitter mode-locked optical clock to all memory and compute chiplets through a passive splitter tree, making every link source-synchronous to a common reference with no CDR, DLL or link training.
note: HBM is already source-synchronous with forwarded clocks; benefit mainly for SerDes.

title: Retention-bounded FIFO DRAM die with no row decoders
idea: Ideal: a memory that is a pipe, holding data only while it flows. Closest achievable: a streaming DRAM die organized as a circular buffer of rows driven by a sequential row counter, sized so wrap-around time is below retention; it has no random row decoder, no refresh counter and only a head/tail pointer interface, serving as the staging buffer between flash or remote memory and the GPU.

title: Crossbar parity mats: a 2D product code built into geometry
idea: Ideal: error correction as part of the array geometry, with no decoder. Closest: each 180 nm mat reserves one parity row and one parity column maintained by XOR trees in the sense-amp and column stripes, so any single bad cell sits at the intersection of a failing row parity and a failing column parity and is flipped back.

title: Active probe-card BIST tiles to break the DRAM test bottleneck
idea: Ideal: testing that is instant and free. Closest achievable at trailing nodes: a 65 nm active probe wafer with one BIST engine per die site tests and burns in every die on the wafer in parallel at speed, cutting reliance on scarce memory ATE.

title: Low-barrier volatile MTJ refreshed by the REF commands DDR already sends
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): DDR insists on refresh, so make refresh useful. Use a 12-15 nm STT-MTJ designed with low thermal stability (Delta ~25-30, retention of seconds), which cuts write current ~4x so a tiny access transistor suffices, and let standard REF commands trigger internal read-and-rewrite of aging rows; holding costs zero leakage.
note: Low-Delta refreshed MRAM is known for caches; MTJ cell is not denser than DRAM.

title: Metal impurities rationed to zero: carbon-cluster proximity gettering under storage junctions
idea: Limit: no transition-metal atom may survive within 1 um of a storage junction. Implant carbon-cluster (C3H5) ions to form a gettering layer a few hundred nm beneath the array, the trick CMOS image sensors use against hot pixels. The layer captures Fe, Ni and Cu that would otherwise sit in junction depletion regions as deep-level generation centers.

title: Normally-off banks: domain-wall latches keep decoder and row state
idea: Constraint: nothing may be lost at power-off, periphery included. Mode registers, open-row addresses and decoder latches use magnetic domain-wall or FeFET latches, so a bank with an NV array power-gates completely between bursts and wakes in ~ns with no re-init or retraining.

title: Delete plate-line drivers: bitline-only bipolar FeRAM drive
idea: Constraint: non-volatile 1T1C ferroelectric, without FeRAM's large, slow plate-line drivers. Tie all plates to a fixed mid-rail and switch polarization by driving the bitline to +V or -V around it (bipolar bitline drivers built into the SA), so the plate needs no driver and no decoding.

title: Mirror-tier pairs share one horizontal bitline sheet
idea: Limit: half a metal layer per tier. Build tiers as mirrored pairs around a single horizontal bitline plane, with cells above and below contacting the same bitline. This halves bitline layers and cuts tier pitch about 25%.

title: Stack-only U.S. fab: domestic 3D integration of imported array wafers
idea: Limit: no new DRAM front-end fab for three years. Fund U.S. hybrid-bonding and tier-stacking lines that buy array and periphery wafers from several allied sources and do all 3D integration, test and redundancy remap domestically.

title: Supercritical CO2 replaces ultrapure water in cleaning
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero ultrapure water for post-etch clean and dry. Run residue removal and drying in supercritical CO2 with small co-solvent and chelator doses inside sealed cluster modules, recompressing and recycling >95% of the CO2.

title: Carbide-scrap tungsten turned into domestic WF6
idea: Within $1M/24 months: bench pilot that takes U.S. cemented-carbide scrap (drill bits, inserts) through the zinc reclaim process, oxidizes and hydrogen-reduces it to tungsten powder, fluorinates it with on-site F2, and distills 6N WF6 for wordline CVD.

title: Crucible-free wafers: epitaxial lift-off from reusable seed wafers
idea: Constraint: no new high-purity quartz crucibles. Grow 20 um device-grade epi on a double-porous-silicon release layer, bond it to a polysilicon or SiC-ceramic handle, split it off, re-polish the seed and reuse it 20-50 times.

title: Hot wafer-sort at 150 C replaces package burn-in ovens
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: test retention on 150 C hot chucks at wafer sort to map each die's leakage tail, fuse weak rows into redundancy and burn a per-bank temperature-refresh table into eFuses, so no packaged burn-in is needed and every shipped die is pre-screened 25 C beyond its rating.
note: Burn-in screens infant mortality beyond retention; packaging defects not caught at sort.

title: Glass-lid wafer-level package: hermetic, polymer-free, sealed before dicing
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years with zero polymers: direct-bond a borosilicate lid wafer carrying through-glass vias onto the finished DRAM wafer at low temperature, forming a hermetic chip-scale package before dicing with solder-free Cu pillar outputs.

title: Subtractively etched ruthenium wiring: no copper damascene, no barriers
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: deposit blanket Ru, plasma-etch it into lines and gap-fill with dielectric, skipping trench etch, barrier/seed, plating and Cu CMP; ruthenium's high melting point gives ~10x electromigration headroom at 125 C and nothing can diffuse into the cells.

title: ABF-free ceramic package substrates sidestep the build-up film chokepoint
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: replace organic ABF build-up substrates (one dominant film supplier) with low-temperature co-fired glass-ceramic substrates and silver-sinter die attach, whose expansion matches silicon and which do not absorb moisture or creep at 125 C.

title: Sacrificial-polymer air gaps between bitlines, no extra mask
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: fill bitline gaps with a thermally decomposable polymer, cap it with porous SiCN and bake at ~400 C so it evaporates through the cap, leaving rigid air gaps that stay stable at 125 C.

title: Rack-wide one-physical-copy rule via content-hashed CXL pages
idea: Imposed limit: no 4 KB page may exist twice in a rack. Each host's memory controller hashes read-only pages (kernel text, libraries, container layers, model weights) and swaps duplicates for pointers into a shared CXL-attached content-addressed pool, with copy-on-write on the first store.

title: Zero dies scrapped: AI-tolerant DRAM grade for out-of-spec dies
idea: Imposed limit: no die may be scrapped for retention or margin. Create a new JEDEC-like grade specified at 16 ms retention and BER 1e-8 that requires system-level ECC, recompute or ABFT. It is sold at a ~40% discount into inference clusters whose software stacks tolerate it.

title: Memory leasing with telemetry-driven swap and refurbishment
idea: Rule: the maker keeps ownership, so repairability is its own profit motive. Memory is leased by GB-month, and the vendor monitors error telemetry, swaps degrading modules proactively, then refurbishes and redeploys them, which rewards designs that last.

title: Spruce Pine cut off: synthetic-silica crucible liners from polysilicon byproduct
idea: Self-imposed limit: no natural high-purity quartz. Crucible inner layers are made from sol-gel synthetic silica derived from SiCl4, a waste stream of polysilicon plants, and CZ pullers run multi-recharge pulls so each crucible yields 3-5 ingots.

title: Shared-rail SOT tier on hot logic (4 MTJs per write rail)
idea: A W/Ta (or field-free FM/Ta) spin-orbit rail carries the write current; four MTJs sit on it, selected by per-MTJ voltage biasing (VCMA-assisted) or by staggered critical currents along the track. One write transistor and per-MTJ read selects are shared. Thermal stability is designed for 125 C junction temperatures, so data persist where Si DRAM would need ~4 ms refresh. Reads use TMR; writes take <10 ns at <100 fJ. This is not a commodity-density play; it attacks the memory-on-logic bottleneck.

title: ASD self-aligned landing pads and top contacts
idea: After the contact plugs are exposed in dielectric, Mo (or W) is deposited by area-selective ALD/CVD that nucleates only on metal or semiconductor surfaces, with small-molecule or SAM inhibitors on the dielectric and periodic atomic-layer-etch 'defect clean' cycles to remove stray nuclei. The pad grows a controlled height and mushroom width, self-aligned to its plug, so the landing-pad litho/etch step (patterned with EUV or multipatterning at leading nodes [UNVERIFIED-PK]) is not needed. The same approach caps vertical oxide channels in 4F2 VCT and gain-cell arrays.

title: Coil-stacked HBM: inductive links instead of TSVs, NAND-style wire-bonded power
idea: Replace HBM's through-silicon vias and micro-bumps with inductive-coupling links: each thinned DRAM die carries ~2,000 small coils in its top metal over the array, and data hop vertically between dies by magnetic coupling (Keio's ThruChip Interface). Power enters the way NAND stacks do it: staggered dies with wire bonds, or a few coarse power vias at the die edge. The DRAM die loses its TSV keep-out field and the stack loses TSV/bump yield loss; coils also tolerate several um of misalignment, so stacking needs no fine-pitch alignment.

title: TSV-free inductive stacking for short memory-on-logic stacks
idea: Dies thinned to ~10 um are glued rather than bump-bonded. Data crosses between stacked dies through pairs of ~30 um on-chip spiral coils at ~8 Gb/s each. Power and ground use a few highly doped silicon vias or edge connections. There is no TSV etch or fill, no microbump yield loss and no hybrid-bond overlay.

title: Swap fixed capacitor for gated-diode varactor that amplifies on read
idea: Store charge in the inversion layer of a gated diode (IBM 2T1D cell). At read the gate is pulsed: a stored '1' keeps its inversion capacitance and boosts the node voltage several-fold, while a '0' collapses to depletion capacitance, which gives built-in voltage gain.
note: Literally IBM 2T1D prior art.

title: Swap stored weight matrices for an on-chip PRNG weight synthesizer
idea: Substitute stored bits with regenerated bits. Each weight block is post-fit as a few coefficients times matrices from a seeded LFSR basis, and a hardware synthesizer next to the tensor cores regenerates the block in SRAM from (seed, coefficients) at use time. DRAM holds only seeds and coefficients.
note: SeedLM (2024) is essentially this; ~int4-equivalent savings.

title: Gated-diode storage amplifies its own charge on read
idea: Replace the capacitor with a planar MOS gated diode. A stored 1 keeps it inverted, so a gate pulse boosts its voltage 3-5x; a stored 0 leaves it depleted with little boost. This fits a 180 nm logic flow.

title: Fab waste heat drives membrane distillation for zero liquid discharge
idea: Magnify water reuse to ~98%: route 40-60 C process-cooling return water through membrane-distillation stacks that purify spent rinse and scrubber water back to UPW feed, and crystallize the brine on site.

title: Self-aligned imprint: all layer masks in one stamp
idea: Minify alignment steps to zero by encoding all layer geometries as stepped heights in one 3D roll-to-roll imprint stamp; successive etch-backs reveal each level, so layers are perfectly registered even on a stretching web.
note: This is HP's SAIL process.

title: Magnify the pool to a regional spot market for stranded DRAM
idea: Magnify the memory pool from the host to the region: clouds sell stranded DRAM (on hosts whose cores are sold out) as a spot-priced remote cache/swap tier over RDMA, with preemption notice and automatic fallback to flash.
note: Memtrade and Infiniswap already trade stranded memory over RDMA.

title: Eliminate ultrapure-water rinses: supercritical CO2 cleans that stop pillar collapse
idea: Replace wet clean, rinse and IPA dry after capacitor-mold strip and post-etch steps with supercritical CO2 plus small co-solvent doses, recompressing and reusing >95% of the CO2.

title: Inductive coupling coils replace HBM signal TSVs
idea: Swap the wire for a field: core dies talk vertically through on-chip coil pairs drawn in existing top metal (zero masks), and power rides highly doped silicon vias made with the one added implant mask, so the HBM stack needs no metal TSVs.
note: Kuroda's ThruChip inductive coupling plus highly doped Si power vias is established art.

title: Execute directly on compressed data, never decompress into DRAM
idea: Reverse decompress-then-compute: near-memory ALUs run filters, joins and aggregates directly on dictionary-, run-length- and bit-packed column encodings, and LLM kernels consume codebook-quantized weights as indices, so no decompressed copy is ever materialized in DRAM.
note: Columnar DBs and LUT-GEMM already do this.

title: Mesh merging: two half-empty heap pages share one frame
idea: Break the one-virtual-page-per-frame rule: a malloc runtime randomizes object placement so sparse pages rarely collide, finds page pairs whose live objects don't overlap, and remaps both virtual pages onto one physical frame.
note: Mesh (Powers et al.) already published.

title: Mantis-shrimp Bouligand stacking breaks dielectric leakage percolation paths
idea: Mantis shrimp clubs resist cracks with helicoidal (Bouligand) layers, each rotated a few degrees from the last. Build the capacitor dielectric from 4-6 sub-1 nm crystalline sublayers separated by one-monolayer nucleation-reset films. Each sublayer then re-nucleates with randomised grain orientation, so grain boundaries never line up into straight through-paths.

title: Archaeal tetraether-style Cu grains spanning the hybrid bond interface
idea: Hyperthermophilic archaea survive >100 C with tetraether lipids that span the whole membrane instead of two stacked leaflets; analogously, use (111) nanotwinned Cu bond pads and a ~200 C anneal that drives grain growth across the interface so single grains span both dies, erasing the bond line where voids nucleate under 125 C electro- and thermomigration.

title: Space-station water recovery loop for zero-discharge DRAM fabs
idea: The ISS recovers ~98% of its water with vapor-compression distillation plus catalytic oxidation. Build fab ultrapure-water systems as zero-liquid-discharge loops: segregate rinse streams by contaminant, drive membrane distillation with 30-40 C fab waste heat, recover dilute HF and NH4OH, and return >90% of water to UPW.

title: Wastewater to ultrapure water with fab waste heat
idea: Inverts 'UPW starts from fresh water': feed the UPW plant from municipal treated wastewater, use the fab's 30-40 C chiller reject heat to drive membrane distillation ahead of RO/EDI polishing, and send reject brine to industrial users.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembly carving sub-10 nm storage islands without EUV
idea: Anneal a high-chi block copolymer (e.g., PS-b-PDMS) at <=250 C so it self-assembles into hexagonal 8-10 nm-pitch dots registered to a coarse DUV guide pattern. Transfer the dots as hard masks that define magnetic, ferroic or charge-storage islands; pitch comes from chi*N thermodynamics, not photon wavelength.
note: DSA and bit-patterned media widely pursued; defectivity and registration remain the known blockers.

title: Inductive coupling links replace TSVs in hot memory stacks
idea: At 125 C, Cu TSVs suffer protrusion and voiding under thermal cycling and add keep-out zones; inductive coil links (contactless, ~1 Gb/s per coil) carry data between stacked dies with no metal through silicon. Power still uses a few large TSVs.

title: Zero-liquid-discharge water loop using fab waste-heat membrane distillation
idea: Box [water source: RO reject + CMP/wet-bench rinse | heat source: 30-60 C process-cooling return | unit: membrane distillation + crystallizer | output: UPW feed]: recover >95% of reject water using heat the fab already throws away and crystallize the salts.

title: Lifetime-predicted arenas: allocate objects by when they will die
idea: Po: garbage never exists. A learned model predicts each allocation's lifetime from its call-stack signature and places objects with similar death times in the same huge-page arena, which is released whole, so fragmentation holes never form.

title: Unikernel diet: specialized library-OS images for every service
idea: Po: the operating system is part of the app. Services built with a domestic hardened toolchain are linked into single-address-space unikernels holding only the OS components they call, dropping per-VM kernel, init, daemon and page-table overhead from ~150-300 MB to ~10-20 MB.
note: Unikernels are long-known; adoption barrier, not invention.

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal to harden storage-node junctions
idea: Worsen: leave hydrogen-passivated interface traps that de-passivate and feed the leakage tail. Flip: replace the final forming-gas anneal with high-pressure deuterium, whose heavier isotope bonds resist hot-carrier and thermal de-passivation (the giant isotope effect), and test tail retention on purchased DRAM test wafers within 24 months.
note: High-pressure D2/H2 anneal already used in DRAM fabs (HPSP tools).

title: Deuterium-annealed access transistors shrink the leakage tail
idea: Worsen: let hydrogen-passivated interface traps depassivate under stress, so retention tails grow and refresh rates climb. Flip: do the final forming-gas anneal with deuterium. The heavier Si-D bond resists hot-carrier and GIDL-driven breaking, which tightens the access-transistor leakage tail that sets refresh.

title: Near-duplicate pages stored as deltas to a canonical library
idea: Worsen: store thousands of pages that differ in only a few bytes as full copies. Flip: the controller fingerprints pages with similarity hashes, keeps a library of canonical base pages, and stores each similar page as a compressed XOR delta against its base.
note: Difference Engine (2008) did this.

title: Switch-SRAM hot tier ends per-server hot-key replication
idea: Worsen: replicate the hottest keys on every cache server to survive load skew. Flip: serve the top 0.1% of keys from the SRAM of programmable top-of-rack switches, which absorbs skew in-network, so servers stop keeping replicas and run at higher fill.
note: NetCache (2017).

title: Titanium-submarine engineer: Hf-free rutile TiO2 templated on RuO2
idea: A Soviet engineer who built titanium-hulled submarines uses the metal his country has in plenty. Grow rutile-phase TiO2 (k~90-110) templated on RuO2 bottom electrodes below 400 C, with Al doping to tame leakage, in place of HfO2/ZrO2 stacks.
note: Rutile TiO2 on Ru/RuO2 with Al doping extensively studied (Hwang group).

title: Half-full bucket: restore depth set by refresh pointer position
idea: A child carries a half-full bucket when the next stop is close. The die knows where its internal refresh pointer is, so after an access it restores a row only to ~85% charge when that row's refresh is imminent and fully when it is far away.
note: Restore truncation (HPCA 2016) is prior art.

title: Child's time-out corner: quarantine hammering rows in a spaced subarray
idea: A child who keeps poking siblings is sent to the time-out corner: once a row's activation count spikes, the controller moves that aggressor's data into a quarantine subarray where every other row is an empty guard row, so the row can be hammered without disturbing anyone.

title: Firmware-style unikernels erase per-VM operating system footprint
idea: From single-purpose embedded firmware: cloud services are linked with only the library-OS components they use into unikernels on a thin hypervisor, removing the general-purpose kernel, init system and page cache from every VM.
note: MirageOS-era idea; containers already share kernels.

title: Unity CMOx fixed: swap slow oxygen ions for nanosecond protons
idea: Unity Semiconductor's CMOx, which exchanged oxygen ions between oxide layers, died from slow, high-voltage switching. Shuttle protons instead, through a phosphosilicate-glass electrolyte into a WO3 channel: high-field proton insertion has shown ns programming, and conductance is read without disturbance.
note: Nanosecond PSG/WO3 protonic resistors already demonstrated (MIT 2022).

title: Carbon-chain block copolymers self-assemble the 4F2 cell grid without EUV
idea: Spin cylinder-forming PS-b-PMMA (or high-chi PS-b-PDMS) on a coarse e-beam/i-line guide pattern so it self-assembles a hexagonal hole array at 20-24 nm pitch, remove the minority cores, and transfer the holes into an Al2O3 hard mask for vertical-channel 4F2 pillars.

title: Distillery heat-recovery stills turn fab waste heat into UPW
idea: Whisky distilleries and desalination plants cascade heat through multi-effect stills; route the fab's 30-45 C process-cooling heat into membrane distillation modules that turn reject brine and rinse wastewater back into ultrapure-water feed, approaching zero liquid discharge.

title: Roof-shingle die stacks with aerosol-jet printed ramp interconnects
idea: Offset each die by 100 um like roof shingles so edge pads stay exposed, then aerosol-jet 3D-print conductive ramps down the staircase to make the vertical bus. No TSVs are drilled into the DRAM.

title: Persistent-current superconducting loop memory for cryogenic racks
idea: IFR: the bit circulates forever with zero loss. For cryogenic AI racks, store bits as clockwise or counter-clockwise persistent currents in NbN kinetic-inductance nanowire loops switched by nanocryotron gates, with no leakage, no refresh and no static power.

title: Rutile TiO2 grown on the ruthenium bitline template
idea: Under 400 C, the Ru electrode lines of each tier are surface-oxidized to RuO2, which templates rutile Al-doped TiO2 by ALD at 280 C with k of about 80-100. These are planar or shallow-trench capacitors integrated straight onto the electrode tier.
note: Extensively studied for DRAM; leakage at thin EOT is why it has not been adopted.

title: Backlight-powered loadless latch on glass holds bits with photocurrent
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: oxide TFTs are normally shielded from light because it raises leakage; instead deliberately bathe a transparent glass memory panel in steady dim backlight. Each cell is a cross-coupled n-type TFT pair whose high node is held up by a photodiode's photocurrent (replacing the pull-up of a loadless SRAM), tunable by light intensity to out-supply leakage at any temperature.

title: Wiegand-wire revival: exchange-spring strips that self-generate read pulses
idea: The Wiegand effect (1970s access cards) uses a hard shell and soft core that snaps abruptly, producing a voltage pulse independent of drive speed. Make planar CoPt-hard/NiFe-soft bilayer strips on an existing 180-nm line; the bit is the hard layer's direction, and a read field ramp triggers a soft-layer snap only when antiparallel, inducing a pulse in a pickup line.
note: Unusual self-generated read pulse; density niche.

title: Injection-locked ring-oscillator phase stores bits inside link retimers
idea: Worsen: use leaky charge to store a bit. Flip: store each bit as the 0-or-pi phase of a sub-harmonically injection-locked CMOS ring oscillator, reviving Goto's parametron inside link retimers where clocks already run, and read it by phase comparison.

title: S: sublimable sulfur scaffolds support tall structures, then vanish
idea: Fill cavities and slits with molten elemental sulfur (melts ~115 C) as a temporary mechanical support and planarizer during subsequent steps, then sublime it away in vacuum at ~150-200 C, leaving clean cavities.

title: Minify the charge to a few electrons on Coulomb-blockaded nanodots
idea: Store bits as 5-10 electrons on sub-3 nm Si nanodots whose charging energy (>10 kT) blocks thermally activated escape, sensed non-destructively by a gate-coupled single-electron transistor; writes use direct tunneling through ~2 nm oxide at low voltage, avoiding high-field wear.
note: Few-electron dots promise extreme density; doubts: retention through ~2 nm oxide, room-temperature variability and background charge. Known art.

title: Tree rings: magnetic racetrack on vertical hole walls, one litho layer
idea: Random stimulus 'tree rings' (records stored along depth) -> a perpendicular magnetic multilayer is deposited conformally on the sidewall of each NAND-like vertical hole, and bits are stored as domains along the depth, shifted by current pulses to a read/write MTJ at the top. One hole lithography defines 32-128 bits.
note: If domain shifting works, ~50x bits per litho step; but this is Parkin's original 3D racetrack, unproven for decades.

title: Po: chips grown not made — anodic-alumina vertical racetrack forests
idea: Po: chips are grown, not made. Extracted: anodize aluminium so it self-organises into ~1e11 hexagonal pores/cm2 with no lithography, electroplate Co/Ni multilayer nanowires into them, and use each wire as a vertical racetrack where 20-50 domain walls are shifted by current pulses past a read/write junction at the pore base.
note: Parkin vertical racetrack in AAO nanowires; 20 years unproven, serial shift latency breaks DRAM-class access, pore-base contacting unsolved.

title: Soviet engineer converts the tractor plant: NAND lines making DRAM
idea: Like a tractor factory retooled for tanks, a 10-person design team writes 1-2 mask deltas and recipe changes so an existing 3D NAND line (staircase, channel holes, tier stack) builds a vertical 2T0C gain cell. An ALD oxide-semiconductor liner replaces the poly-Si channel in the hole. The fab runs it as foundry lots.
note: DRAM on depreciated NAND tools; doubt: gain cell in a series-string hole needs far more than 1-2 mask deltas.

title: Turn lithography sideways: film thickness sets every critical dimension
idea: Move the critical dimension from lateral litho to vertical film thickness: gate length, channel thickness and capacitor dielectric are all LPCVD or sputter thicknesses with nm control, and the only litho is a 180-nm-pitch slot and hole pattern. That pattern is punched through eight 32-tier poly-Si decks (AR ~9 each), so a 0.065-um2 column over 256 tiers is ~0.00025 um2 per bit.
note: Thickness-defined CDs is the 3D NAND recipe; poly-Si channels leak far too much for DRAM retention.

title: HP/UCLA molecular crossbar's yield killer solved by defect-mapped stochastic decoders
idea: The 2007 160-kbit rotaxane molecular memory worked, but only ~25% of bits were usable and its decoders could not be lithographed at that pitch. Fix: adopt Teramac-style defect tolerance with nanowire decoders formed stochastically (random doping codes) and mapped at power-up, writing data only to verified bistable junctions through a logical-to-physical map with rateless coding across junctions.
note: DeHon/Teramac defect tolerance is old art; molecular switch speed and endurance unproven.

title: Monolayer 2D channels shrink the lateral access device to 5 nm
idea: IFR: the lateral transistor takes up no length. Use a 0.7 nm MoS2 or WSe2 monolayer channel in each 3D tier (low-temperature MOCVD or transfer); its atomic thinness suppresses short-channel leakage so gate length drops to ~5 nm and the tier cell footprint shrinks ~3x.
note: Shorter lateral transistor cuts tier break-even toward 10x density; doubt: 2D contacts and growth across ~30 tiers.

title: Coulomb-blockade nanodot bit: ten electrons, held by charging energy
idea: Scarcity rule: the bit gets 1000x less charge. Self-assembled 2 nm Si dots in the gate oxide store 5-10 electrons each, and their Coulomb charging energy (>10 kT) blocks back-tunneling so retention comes from electrostatics rather than oxide thickness; a sensitive gain transistor reads the threshold shift.
note: Few-electron bit; Yano/Tiwari single-electron memories stalled on offset charge and dot variability.

title: Move the bits, not the sensor: one read head per track
idea: Inverting 'every bit sits still and sensing comes to it': 64 bits are stored as magnetic domains along a vertical nanowire and shifted by current pulses past a single MTJ read head at the track base, so one sense amp and one access device serve 64 bits.
note: Vertical racetrack would give ~64 bits per access device; reliable domain shifting in 3D tracks has stalled for 15+ years.

title: Origami-folded membrane array stands planar capacitors on edge
idea: Po: memory is folded like a paper fan. Fabricate a 2D array with large, low-AR planar capacitors on a 50 nm membrane with stressed SiN/Cr bilayer hinges between cell rows; on release the membrane self-folds into a vertical accordion so each 0.1 um2 planar capacitor stands upright.
note: Fold planar caps upright via stressed hinges; doubt: nm-registered folding of interconnected arrays is a miracle step.

title: Edinburgh-rock fiber draw: slice prebuilt vertical cell arrays from preforms
idea: Borrow optical-fiber drawing and seaside rock-candy making: assemble a macroscopic preform of doped-Si-core rods clad in gate glass, metal-glass gate sleeves and capacitor shells, co-draw it ~1000x, bundle and redraw to ~40 nm cell pitch, then wafer-slice the boule crosswise so every slice is a ready-made 4F2 vertical-transistor array needing only top and bottom wiring.
note: Pitch set by draw ratio, not litho, is genuinely new; device-grade junctions surviving co-draw at 40 nm needs a miracle.

title: Shingled-recording discipline: overlapping cells written in sequential bands
idea: Adapted from SMR hard drives, which overlap tracks and require sequential zone writes: adjacent storage nodes along a row share partially overlapping electrodes with no isolation, and a band is written in order so each write fixes the trailing cell's charge; reads remain random.
note: Overlapping storage nodes without isolation share charge; random reads would disturb neighbors.

title: Self-stratifying paint: one coat separates into fifty tier layers
idea: Borrowed from self-stratifying industrial coatings that split into primer and topcoat in one application: spin a block-copolymer plus metal-oxide-precursor blend that phase-separates into ~50 parallel lamellae, then UV-ozone convert and anneal it into alternating conductive-oxide and insulating-oxide tiers for a vertical gain-cell stack.

title: Magnify layers to 1000: MLCC-style tape-cast laminated memory
idea: Borrow the multilayer ceramic capacitor industry (tape casting, gravure-printed 2 um electrodes, 1000-layer lamination, co-firing at trillions of parts a year) to build 3D crosspoint dynamic cells: a sub-micron dielectric tape capacitor in series with a co-fired oxide threshold selector.
note: Novel borrowing of MLCC lamination, but per-layer addressing and selector leakage are unsolved; not DRAM-class access.

title: Neural pruning: over-grown random nanowire mesh carved into addressable cells
idea: Brains over-wire and then prune; solution-grow a dense random mesh of ~10 nm oxide-semiconductor nanowires between two orthogonal coarse electrode grids, then use electroforming pulses to burn out shorts and weak paths, characterize the surviving junctions on-die and address them through a learned map stored in a small SRAM table.
note: Addressable bits can't exceed coarse-grid crosspoints; density claim is flawed.

title: Kitchen sponge: gyroid block-copolymer electrode fills each capacitor well
idea: A sponge hides huge internal surface: spin a gyroid-forming block copolymer into each capacitor well, remove one block, and ALD-coat the continuous 3D network with TiN/high-k/TiN so the electrode becomes a triply periodic minimal surface. At a 20-25 nm period the internal area is about 10x that of a plain cylinder.
note: At DRAM pitch the well is only ~1-2 gyroid periods, and TiN/high-k/TiN cannot fit a 20 nm network.

title: Neuroscientist's ion bath: printed ion-gel double-layer storage node
idea: Neurons hold state in ion gradients, not in dielectrics: the storage capacitor is replaced by a printed ion-gel electric-double-layer capacitor (~10 uF/cm2, about 100 fF/um2), so a planar 0.1 um2 node holds ~10 fF, twice a 70:1 pillar, and the charge margin is large enough that leaky, variable printed access transistors still meet retention.
note: EDL charging and self-discharge are microseconds or slower; 10 ns is implausible.

title: Glass-fiber draw tower: thermally drawn nanolayer capacitor fibers
idea: Build a centimeter preform of interleaved conductive and high-k glass/polymer layers, then thermally draw it ~10,000x in a fiber tower so the layers thin to ~10 nm. Chop the fiber and stand the pieces in etched wells as pre-built capacitor cores.
note: Drawn fibers end up ~1 um across, far above cell pitch; placing and contacting billions of chopped cores is unsolved.

title: Vacuum-free tier stacks grown by pulsed-electrodeposition superlattices
idea: Ideal: a 3D memory stack poured from a bath. Closest: pulse-electroplate 100+ periods of Ni or Cu conductor layers alternating with cathodically deposited ZnO semiconductor/dielectric layers (~20-40 nm each, <90 C, aqueous) to replace CVD/PVD tier depositions for 3D gain-cell stacks.
note: Transistor-grade plated ZnO superlattices are speculative.

title: Core-shell nanocrystal barrier-layer film giving colossal-k planar capacitor
idea: Box = {medium: interfacial (Maxwell-Wagner) polarization in a film of 5 nm conducting doped-TiO2 cores with 1 nm Al2O3 shells | access: Si FET | sense: charge share | integration: planar or very-low-AR capacitor | substrate: Si | fab: colloidal dip coat + ALD shell infill}. Each conducting core acts as a floating plate, so the film behaves like hundreds of series-parallel nanocapacitors with effective k of 300-1000, provided core conductance keeps the relaxation frequency above ~100 MHz.
note: At 5 nm cores in ~6 nm film, MW effective k stays ~30, not 300-1000.

title: Array-only DRAM fab plus U.S. mature-node periphery foundry, hybrid-bonded
idea: Substitute the monolithic DRAM die with a two-wafer product: the DRAM fab makes an array-only wafer (cells, bitlines, WL straps, ~40% fewer masks) and an existing U.S. 28-40 nm logic fab makes a periphery-only wafer (sense amps, decoders, I/O) with sub-array-edge pads at ~1 um pitch; the two are hybrid-bonded.
note: Cell-on-periphery hybrid bonding is widely pursued by majors.

title: Wafer bonding fused with monolithic tiers: four wafers of 32
idea: Combine both 3D routes: each wafer carries a 32-tier monolithic memory stack (aspect ratio manageable in one etch), and four such wafers are hybrid-bonded to one periphery wafer, giving 128 tiers without a 128-tier etch.

title: Minify the IDM: pure-play DRAM foundry for fabless designers
idea: Create a DRAM-process foundry that sells array and capacitor modules to fabless memory design houses, separating design innovation (custom HBM base dies, AI-tuned arrays) from $20B capex as TSMC did for logic.
note: PSMC/Winbond already offer DRAM foundry; needs a fab.

title: Eliminate EUV entirely: 4F2 vertical-channel cells at relaxed DUV pitch
idea: Move to a 4F2 vertical-channel-transistor cell but hold F at ~15 nm, which matches the bit area of today's 6F2 at 12 nm and is reachable with immersion DUV plus self-aligned quadruple/octuple patterning. Output is an ordinary DDR5/HBM core die.

title: Inversion: pure-play DRAM foundry with open PDK for fabless designers
idea: TRIZ #13 Inversion: instead of three IDMs designing and fabbing their own DRAM, a pure-play DRAM foundry publishes a cell/array PDK and accepts designs from fabless memory startups, hyperscalers and universities, like TSMC did for logic.
note: Same pure-play DRAM foundry as I-01816.

title: Flip the wafer: build capacitors on the backside
idea: Inverts 'capacitors sit above bitlines on the front'. After front-side transistors and bitlines, bond to a carrier, thin to ~0.5 um and open storage-node contacts from the back directly onto source/drain, building capacitors over the full cell footprint with no bitlines in the way.

title: Ghost kitchen: pure-play DRAM foundry serving fabless memory designers
idea: Random stimulus 'ghost kitchen' -> one kitchen cooks for many brands. A DRAM foundry offers a 1-beta-class cell and capacitor process as a PDK; fabless firms design custom HBM base dies, AI-specific DRAM and niche parts on it, and the foundry aggregates demand to stay full.

title: Pastry chef's croissant lamination: stack-on-stack doubling of tiers
idea: Laminated dough doubles its layers with every fold. Make wafers with 8 monolithic tiers, hybrid-bond two face-to-face, thin and open vias; then bond 16-tier pairs to 16-tier pairs, mirroring orientation so the bitlines align.

title: Two-scale stacking: 32 monolithic tiers per wafer times eight bonded wafers
idea: Combine nm-scale monolithic tiers with um-scale wafer bonding: build 32-tier 3D arrays per wafer, thin each to 5 um, and hybrid-bond eight wafers with one inter-wafer via per mat at 1-um pitch, reaching 256 tiers without any 256-tier etch.

title: Periphery wafer from U.S. legacy fabs bonded onto cell array
idea: Combine image-sensor wafer bonding with DRAM: build sense amps, decoders and I/O on 28-40 nm logic wafers in existing U.S. mature fabs and only the array on the DRAM wafer; the array wafer adds exactly one mask (hybrid-bond pads) and drops its periphery masks.
note: CMOS-bonded-array DRAM is on major vendor roadmaps already.

title: Bond a mature-node periphery wafer under the array
idea: TRIZ #17 Another dimension: move sense amps, decoders and I/O (~49% of the die) to a separately processed 28-40 nm CMOS wafer that is hybrid-bonded beneath the cell array. The array wafer then needs no Hf-based HKMG and fewer metal layers.
note: CMOS-bonded-array DRAM is on major makers' roadmaps.

title: Glass-panel interposers break the silicon-interposer packaging bottleneck
idea: Worsen: make every HBM attach depend on a reticle-stitched silicon interposer from one supplier's line. Flip: build interposers on 510x515 mm glass panels with 2 um semi-additive copper lines and laser through-glass vias, giving ~8x more interposer area per panel than a 300 mm wafer and a lower-loss dielectric.
note: Widely pursued (Intel, Absolics).

title: Onshore HBM stacking hubs using imported known-good DRAM wafers
idea: Worsen: keep all HBM stacking and advanced packaging in one region so one disruption halts AI memory. Flip: fund U.S. packaging hubs that import known-good DRAM wafers and do TSV reveal, hybrid bonding, stacking and test domestically, since a packaging line costs ~$1-3B versus $15B+ for a fab.

title: Cu: hybrid-bond DRAM arrays to periphery from depreciated US fabs
idea: Make only the cell array in the leading-edge DRAM fab and fabricate the periphery (~49% of die) on 28-40 nm logic wafers in existing, depreciated U.S. foundries, joining the two with Cu-Cu hybrid wafer bonding.

title: Hybrid-bond pads double as sense-amp coupling capacitors
idea: In a wafer-on-wafer DRAM (array wafer face-bonded to a CMOS wafer), leave a 2-3 nm oxide in the Cu-Cu bond pads that carry 16:1-muxed local bitlines, so each pad is both the interconnect and the coupling capacitor of a charge-transfer preamp on the logic wafer. The bond needs no DC continuity, and the logic-side sense amp runs at 0.5 V.

title: Refresh cycles fused with page fingerprinting for in-DRAM dedup
idea: Combine the mandatory refresh operation with content hashing: a tiny CRC/hash unit at each subarray's sense amplifiers folds every row into a 32-bit signature as it is refreshed and writes it to a reserved signature row. The controller reads the signature table every 64 ms, verifies candidate matches and merges duplicate pages by remapping, replacing CPU-driven KSM scanning.
note: Pages interleave across chips/banks, so row-level hashes at sense amps map poorly to pages.

title: Refresh-piggybacked mirroring into a bonded non-volatile twin layer
idea: Eliminate the separate backup flush: a ferroelectric or MRAM twin layer bonded under each bank receives a row copy whenever that row is refreshed and its dirty bit is set (the row is already open, so only the vertical transfer is paid); at power loss only rows dirtied since their last refresh are flushed, within the PSU's existing ~10 ms hold-up energy.
note: Piggybacking NV copies on refresh is clever; full-row vertical transfer and NV write energy are costs.

title: Rotate alternate 3D tiers 90 degrees to split staircases
idea: In a lateral 3D DRAM stack, rotate every other tier's cell orientation 90 degrees so odd-tier bitlines run X and even-tier bitlines run Y. Odd tiers stair-step on the east/west edges and even tiers on north/south, so each staircase is half as tall, and vertically adjacent bitlines only cross at points instead of running parallel.
note: Clever staircase split; vertical shared lines must align across rotated, non-square lateral cells.

title: DRAM-bridge: the chiplet bridge die is itself memory
idea: Rearrange the bridge's role: the small embedded silicon bridges (EMIB/LSI-style) that link adjacent GPU chiplets are fabricated as DRAM dies whose top metals carry the die-to-die wires and whose array area is dual-ported to both neighbouring chiplets' edge bumps. Silicon that today only carries wires becomes a shared buffer between neighbours.

title: Local quality: tapered TSV stacks, fewer TSVs in each higher tier
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: in a uniform HBM stack every die carries the full TSV farm, though the top die needs none. One common front-side mask lays out the TSV farm region as spare subarrays, and a cheap i-line backside mask per tier etches only the TSVs that die needs for the dies above it. In upper tiers the unetched subarrays are fused on as extra capacity.

title: Mercury delay-line revival: recirculating photonic loop broadcasts streaming weights
idea: Replace the 1940s mercury tank with a ~2 m low-loss silicon-nitride spiral on the interposer (~10 ns, 64 wavelengths x 50 Gb/s) closed by an SOA regenerator; a weight tile read once from HBM recirculates for N laps and 8-16 compute chiplets tap it each lap via ring drop filters.

title: Woven tiers: alternate bitline direction 90° to dilute row hammer
idea: Inverts 'a row's neighbors are fixed parallel rows.' Rotate line orientation by 90 degrees on alternate tiers so a hammered row's nearest neighbors above and below are orthogonal lines that each share only one cell with it, spreading aggressor coupling over many victims.
note: Alternating line direction conflicts with shared vertical bitlines across tiers.

title: Ant pheromone trails: refresh operations decay per-page hotness counters
idea: Ant trails fade unless re-walked: keep a 3-bit hotness counter per page in spare on-die ECC/metadata bits; accesses increment it and the DRAM's own refresh, which already opens every row, decrements it for free, giving the controller hardware-aged heat maps to drive tiering with zero sampling overhead.
note: Refresh restoring rows could decay counters for free; needs on-die logic changes.

title: Camera pixel: pinned storage-node junction suppresses 125 C generation leakage
idea: Automotive image sensors beat 125 C dark current with a p+ surface pinning layer; the same shallow pinning implant over the storage-node junction surface plus an STI-sidewall passivation liner removes surface-state generation, the dominant hot leakage term.

title: Halve the EUV dose; stochastic misprints become erasures
idea: Po: print the chip blurry. EUV dose on critical DRAM layers is cut 40-50%, raising scanner throughput ~1.5-1.8x, and the resulting rise in stochastic missing or bridged contacts (~0.1-1% of cells) is mapped at test as stuck cells, which as erasures cost about half the redundancy of random errors.

title: Orthogonal-per-tier cells cut by two alternately opened slit families
idea: Worse: point every tier's cells the same way so adjacent bitline columns must sit a full cell length apart. Flip: alternate two sacrificial materials by tier and open X-slits and Y-slits at different times, each selectively recessing one material, so even tiers' cells run along X and odd tiers' along Y and neighboring columns interleave into each tier's vacant quadrants.

title: Latching vertical-thyristor sub-wordline drivers from Kilopass VLT
idea: Failure mined: Kilopass's vertical layered thyristor (VLT) DRAM was abandoned over cell variability and the lack of a fab partner. Fix: use the VLT device where variability is harmless, as the sub-wordline driver. One anode pulse latches it on to drive the 3 V wordline and a cathode pull resets it, so each driver is a single ~4F^2 vertical device with no static decoder hold state.

title: Spin-Hall stochastic writes keep an attention-weighted KV reservoir
idea: When a token's KV arrives, a spin-Hall (beta-W) current pulse tries to switch a low-barrier MTJ, with amplitude set by the token's running attention score. The switching probability equals the keep probability, so the KV buffer becomes a hardware importance-weighted reservoir sample of the context. Only switched tokens are written to the fixed-size KV store; dropped ones are compensated by unbiased reweighting.
note: The KV saving comes from reservoir sampling itself; a spintronic coin flip adds little over a digital PRNG.

title: Pyroelectric film senses heating transients and gates refresh rate
idea: Effect: pyroelectricity. A Sc-doped AlN patch per bank (CMOS-compatible and pyroelectric) outputs current proportional to dT/dt, giving a zero-bias, microsecond heating-event detector; refresh steps up only during and after thermal ramps (for example a GPU power spike), and banks sit at the slow rate while temperature is steady and cool.

title: Convert U.S. silicon-carbide power fabs into refresh-free SiC DRAM lines
idea: C (as SiC): retool 150/200 mm 4H-SiC power-device fabs in NC, NY and TX with existing DUV steppers to build SiC MOS 1T1C cells, whose 3.26 eV gap gave early research SiC DRAM cells orders-of-magnitude longer room-temperature retention than silicon, and sell them as a big-cell, refresh-free working-memory tier behind DRAM on CXL.

title: Basket-weave buried wordlines dive and rise to starve passing-gate leakage
idea: Route each buried wordline over-and-under like basket weave: it runs deep beside one storage node and shallow beside the next. No storage node then sits beside a full-depth passing gate whose toggling pumps electrons into it.

title: Swap ZrO2 for cryogenic quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3 storage dielectric
idea: Operate the array at 20-77 K and use SrTiO3 or KTaO3, whose permittivity climbs toward 10^3-10^4 as quantum fluctuations suppress the ferroelectric transition. A planar or AR<5:1 MIM cap then reaches 5 fF in a 12-nm-class cell footprint, aimed at cryo-cooled AI and quantum-computing racks.

title: Substitute biased well with buried fixed-charge Al2O3 back-gate
idea: Substitute the charge-pumped negative body bias (VBB) with a 3-5 nm ALD Al2O3/SiO2 liner on the back side of each buried or vertical channel. Its built-in negative fixed charge (~-5e12 cm^-2) permanently depletes the body near the storage junction and raises off-state Vt by ~150-250 mV at zero standby power.

title: Substitute hard-switched refresh with LC resonant charge recovery
idea: Substitute CV^2-dissipating drivers with adiabatic resonant drive: an inductor on the package or interposer resonates with wordline and bitline capacitance. Two subarrays refresh in antiphase, so energy swings back and forth between them instead of burning in drivers.
note: Adiabatic LC drive works physically, but refresh is a modest energy share; inductor area and ns ramps limit recovery.

title: Substitute sputtered IGZO with N2-curtain spatial-ALD gallium-tin oxide
idea: Substitute argon/oxygen-sputtered IGZO with amorphous Ga-Sn-O deposited by atmospheric-pressure spatial ALD, in which nitrogen gas curtains rather than argon separate the precursor zones. The result is an indium-free wide-gap channel with angstrom thickness control at high throughput.
note: Spatial ALD oxide channels and GTO TFTs known; combination aimed at supply chain.

title: Substitute amorphous oxides with MBE-grown BaSnO3 perovskite channel
