idea: Substitute amorphous oxide channels with La-doped BaSnO3 grown by MBE on a SrTiO3 buffer on Si (ultra-high vacuum, ozone oxidant, no carrier or sputter gas). It is a 3.1 eV-gap perovskite with film mobility above 100 cm^2/Vs, so on-current and off-leakage stop trading against each other.

title: Substitute VDD/2 idle bitline with trimmed leakage-balance parking voltage
idea: Substitute the fixed VDD/2 standby bitline level with a parking voltage trimmed per subarray by an on-die DAC at test. It is set where channel leakage into the storage node offsets junction and GIDL leakage out of it for the weakest profiled cells.
note: One parking voltage helps one stored polarity and hurts the other.

title: Substitute static cell plate with idle-lowered plate voltage
idea: Substitute the constant cell-plate voltage with one that drops ~0.2-0.3 V while a bank is idle. That couples every floating storage node down and shrinks the storage-to-gate field that drives GIDL on '1' cells; the plate returns before activation, and the negative wordline tracks it to keep '0' cells off.
note: Idle plate lowering cuts GIDL on ones; risks forward bias on zeros and plate settling energy.

title: Analog leaky-capacitor activation integrator replaces row-hammer counter tables
idea: Substitute digital SRAM activation-counter tables with a per-row analog integrator: each activate dumps a fixed charge packet onto a small leaky capacitor in the wordline driver, and when a Schmitt detector trips, the neighbors are refreshed. The leak rate itself sets the time window.
note: Per-row cap in SWD stripe area; PRAC already counts per row.

title: Pulsed back-plate biasing replaces 3 V thick-oxide wordline drivers
idea: Substitute the boosted ~3 V wordline with a buried back plate under each mat that is pulsed during access to lower the access-transistor Vt and held negative during retention. Wordlines then swing only ~1.2 V through thin-oxide drivers.

title: Ferroelectric HZO polarization stores per-amp offset trim
idea: Substitute large matched sense transistors with minimum-size FeFETs whose ALD HZO gate polarization is partially switched at test to null each amp's offset, so the trim is stored as analog polarization. HZO ALD, TiN sputter and RTA are standard nanofab tools.

title: Thin-film AlN piezoelectric transformer replaces wordline charge pumps
idea: Substitute switched-capacitor VPP charge pumps with a released thin-film AlN contour-mode piezoelectric transformer that steps 1.1 V to ~3 V at resonance. AlN sputtering, XeF2 release and e-beam electrodes are university-fab processes.

title: Shadow-evaporated single-electron transistor electrometers sense cryo-DRAM bits
idea: Substitute the CMOS sense amp with an Al/AlOx single-electron transistor (double-angle shadow evaporation, e-beam resist bridge) whose island couples to the bitline, reading sub-attofarad charge for 4 K memory beside quantum processors.

title: NbN nanocryotron sense amplifiers with superconducting niobium bitlines
idea: Substitute both the copper bitline and the CMOS latch with superconductors: zero-resistance Nb bitlines feed an e-beam-patterned NbN nanocryotron (nTron) whose choke switches the channel normal when the bitline current exceeds its threshold.

title: Thin-film Schottky diode-matrix passive row decoder
idea: Substitute transistor NAND decode trees with a 1950s-style diode-matrix decoder made of thin-film Pt/IGZO Schottky diodes at address-line crossings, so only the selected row line stays high. It needs two masks plus sputtering.

title: One-time ReRAM-programmed crossbar decoder routes around defects
idea: Substitute hard-wired decoders with a crossbar of HfOx ReRAM switches programmed once at test to connect each address code to any healthy physical row. Decoding and redundancy repair merge into one reconfigurable layer.

title: Stencil-indexed deposition builds the 3D staircase, replacing trim-etch loops
idea: Substitute the staircase made by dozens of resist-trim + oxide/nitride fluorocarbon etch loops with deposition-defined steps: sputter an oxide-semiconductor/Mo/Al2O3 tier stack through a stepper-indexed stencil whose aperture edges move inward ~0.5 um per tier at each staircase site, so every tier terminates at its own offset; stencils are swapped and stripped in oxalic acid/H2O2.
note: Shadow-mask penumbra at 0.5 um steps is the doubt.

title: Carbon-mandrel, titania-alumina spacers replace fluorocarbon quadruple patterning
idea: Substitute oxide-spacer/fluorocarbon SAQP with an ashable/chlorinable set: amorphous-carbon mandrels (O2 ash), ALD TiO2 first spacers and ALD Al2O3 second spacers etched with Cl2/BCl3 at >20:1 mutual selectivity, printed with a non-fluorinated PAG (sulfonium camphorsulfonate) resist, so ~16 nm pitch uses only O2, Cl2, BCl3 and HBr.

title: Substitute amorphous-carbon molds and ashing for oxide mold HF dip-out
idea: Build the capacitor mold from amorphous carbon etched with O2/COS (no fluorocarbons), form the pillars, then remove the mold by O2/H2 plasma ash instead of a buffered-HF full dip-out followed by rinses and IPA drying.

title: Substitute thermophoretic particle shielding for after-the-fact wafer cleaning
idea: Hold wafers a few kelvin above ambient on heated carriers and stages and add biased electrostatic guard grids, so thermophoretic and electric forces repel sub-100 nm particles before they land, then skip cleans whose only job is particle removal.

title: Substitute tester-based burn-in with on-die BIST and contactless wafer test
idea: Embed a programmable march/retention test engine and near-field RF coupling coils in every die so whole wafers are tested in parallel by a wafer-scale wireless tester without probe cards; weak cells are repaired by on-die eFuses during the same pass.

title: Infrared light through silicon replaces vertical TSV signal lanes
idea: Substitute signal TSVs with bonded 1310 nm micro-LED / Ge photodiode pairs: silicon is transparent above 1.1 um, so each die shines data straight up through thinned neighbours, with Fresnel zone lenses etched in backside oxide to focus; only a few fat TSVs remain for power.
note: BEOL metal in every tier blocks light; needs optical windows per die.

title: Flood-lit optical comb clock replaces per-channel forwarded clocks
idea: Substitute every channel's forwarded clock, DLL and PLL with one mode-locked laser that floods the backside of all chiplets at 1.3 um through the silicon; on-die photodiodes recover a common low-jitter clock so data lanes run source-synchronous with no CDR or link training.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory racks with YBCO superconducting backplanes
idea: Substitute copper backplane traces with YBCO coated-conductor striplines in a 77 K memory enclosure: DRAM leakage collapses at 77 K so refresh nearly vanishes, and lossless lines carry 100 mV low-swing signals for meters without equalization.
note: YBCO lines add little versus cryo overhead.

title: On-package antenna mesh replaces address and command wiring
idea: Substitute command/address wiring to every DRAM die with a ~300 GHz on-chip antenna broadcast network inside the package: the controller transmits each command once, all dies receive it simultaneously, and only data stays wired.
note: 300 GHz on-package antennas for C/A; wireless NoC art exists.

title: Substitute voltage-level sensing with time-to-threshold soft readout
idea: Replace the latch-type sense amp decision with a bitline discharge timer: the time for the bitline to cross a reference is digitized to 3 bits, giving soft reliability info per cell that a soft-decision LDPC decoder uses to fix marginal cells hard-decision ECC cannot.

title: Substitute supercapacitor hold-up with DRAM-process energy capacitors flushing dirty rows
idea: Keep a bounded dirty budget (e.g., 3% of rows) in a write-back policy and pair the DRAM with an on-die MRAM persistence tile; spare high-AR capacitor array area, filled with antiferroelectric ZrO2 energy-storage caps, powers the dirty-row flush on power fail.
note: Niche persistence feature.

title: Substitute UPS spend with NV-memory datacenters selling instant demand response
idea: Business model: datacenters with persistent working memory can drop to zero power within milliseconds and resume exactly, so they sell fast frequency/demand-response capacity to grid operators; the revenue subsidizes the NV memory premium.
note: Grid services revenue small relative to memory premium; UPS savings real but modest.

title: Substitute one stable large MTJ with analog majority of tiny unstable MTJs
idea: Store each bit in 5 sub-15 nm MTJs in parallel, each with low thermal stability (fails ~1e-3/hour alone); reading the summed parallel resistance gives the majority, so the bit fails only if 3 of 5 flip (~1e-8/hour) and periodic scrub restores flips.

title: Substitute single-crystal wafers with crucible-free amorphous carrier substrates
idea: Because <=400 C memory tiers need no crystalline silicon, swap prime CZ wafers for reclaimed test wafers or glass carriers that hold only memory tiers, later bonded to a small periphery die.

title: Separate capacitor wafer hybrid-bonded to transistor wafer at cell pitch
idea: Combine deep-trench decoupling-capacitor manufacturing (mature, DUV-only) with sub-500 nm pitch wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding: one wafer carries only dense trench capacitors, the other carries access transistors and periphery, and each cell's storage node is joined by a Cu-Cu pad. Each wafer is optimized and yield-screened separately, and the capacitor wafer can come from a low-capital U.S. MEMS or passive-component fab.
note: Sub-500 nm bond pitch is ~10x coarser than DRAM cell pitch, so density falls far short.

title: Split-pillar complementary capacitor in one etched hole
idea: Etch a single capacitor hole, then split its bottom electrode lengthwise into two half-shells separated by a dielectric fin, so one hole holds a true and a complement storage node sharing one plate. Complementary charges give a differential 2x signal that cancels plate and coupling noise.
note: Same split-pillar complementary nodes.

title: Gen-10.5 display-glass fabs building IGZO capacitor memory panels
idea: Combine display-panel manufacturing (Gen-10.5 glass, 2-3 um lines, IGZO backplanes already in volume) with 1T1C memory: pattern memory arrays across square meters of glass at roughly a cent per cm2, then cut them into large capacity-tier panels attached by flex to CXL controllers. It trades density for ~1000x cheaper area and zero EUV.

title: High-entropy fluorite oxide dielectric suppressing crystallization leakage paths
idea: Combine the high-entropy-alloy concept with the storage dielectric: an ALD supercycle mixes five cations (Hf, Zr, Ti, Ce, Sn) into one oxide so configurational entropy stabilizes a single fine-grained high-k phase and blocks the grain-boundary leakage paths that cripple pure TiO2 or ZrO2 at k>50. Target: k~50-60 with ZrO2-class leakage.
note: Entropy stabilization in 5 nm ALD films is unproven.

title: Floating negative wordlines replace standby charge pumps
idea: In self-refresh, a single capacitive kick (domino-precharge style) drives all idle wordlines to about -0.6 V, after which they float and their own capacitance holds the bias, topped up rarely by a tiny timer.

title: Sense amp fused with time-to-digital converter as retention canary
idea: Combine every sense-amp stripe with a shared 6-bit time-to-digital converter that timestamps how long each bitline pair takes to cross the latch threshold during ordinary activations; slow-resolving (low-charge) rows are logged in a small per-bank table and refreshed at 64 ms while all others drop to 256-1024 ms. Normal reads become free, continuous retention measurements, which also catches variable-retention cells that offline profiling misses.
note: Sense-time as a retention canary; SA offset may swamp the timing signal.

title: Per-stripe adaptive array voltage regulated by sensed margin
idea: Put a micro-LDO in every SA stripe and close the loop with a replica sense pair on a programmable reference: the regulator lowers that subarray's VARY until measured margin reaches target, so strong subarrays run near 0.7 V while weak ones stay at 1.0 V.

title: Wordline drivers built on the 3D staircase steps
idea: Combine the 3D contact staircase with the X-decoder: deposit thin-film transistors directly on each staircase tread so every tier's wordline driver and pre-decoder sits on its own step, turning dead staircase area into periphery.
note: TFT drive current marginal for fast high-voltage wordlines.

title: Series-stacked array voltage domains recycle bitline charge between tiers
idea: Combine two arrays (bonded tiers) in series between 0 and 2xVARY: the upper array swings VARY-2VARY and its restore current returns through the lower array swinging 0-VARY, recycling charge like stacked-voltage logic, with the scheduler balancing activations.

title: CTE-matched molybdenum TSVs dropped inside the cell array
idea: Fill TSVs with domestic molybdenum, whose ~5 ppm/K expansion nearly matches silicon, so stress keep-out zones shrink from ~10 um to <1 um and TSVs can sit inside the subarray grid (in sense-amp gaps) instead of dedicated TSV channels.

title: HBM die thinning by layer splitting so parent wafers recycle
idea: Combine HBM's mandatory 30-50 um die thinning with porous-silicon layer transfer: build core dies on epi above a buried porous-Si cleave plane, split the 40 um device layer off after carrier bonding instead of grinding ~700 um to slurry, then re-polish and re-epi the parent for 10+ reuses.

title: Molybdenum dioxide electrode replaces ruthenium and templates rutile TiO2
idea: Combine the capacitor bottom electrode with the dielectric's crystal seed: metallic, rutile-type ALD MoO2 plays the templating role RuO2 plays in lab stacks, nucleating rutile TiO2 (k ~80-100) at <=400 C, with an Al-doped TiO2 interface layer to cut leakage.

title: All-carbon capacitor mold etched with oxygen instead of fluorocarbons
idea: Combine mold material and strip chemistry: replace the oxide/nitride capacitor mold with amorphous carbon, etch holes in O2/N2/COS plasma with sulfur sidewall passivation, deposit electrodes, then remove the mold in the same O2 ash rather than an HF wet strip.

title: ALD exhaust cold-trap reclaims precursors for on-site repurification
idea: Combine the ALD foreline trap with a precursor refinery: a staged cryogenic trap captures the >90% of Zr/Hf/Ti metal-organic precursor that passes unreacted during purge pulses, and an on-site fractional distillation unit repurifies it to 6N for re-feed.

title: Deuterated nitride supporter doubles as an interface-passivation reservoir
idea: Combine the capacitor's existing SiN support lattice with trap passivation (zero added masks): deposit it from SiD4/ND3 so it stores ~20 at.% deuterium, which diffuses down during later anneals and passivates access-transistor interface/GIDL traps with stronger Si-D bonds.

title: One block mask lets capacitor ZrO2 double as periphery gate
idea: Combine the cell-capacitor ZrO2 ALD with the periphery high-k gate: periphery moves to a gate-last module whose trenches are opened by the single added mask, so the same ZrO2 run coats capacitor and periphery gates, with La/Al dipoles setting Vt.

title: Silicon-on-nothing voids isolate cells using only silicon and hydrogen
idea: Combine isolation and body insulation via the empty-space-in-silicon effect: the one added mask etches arrays of deep holes under active-area ends, and a high-temperature H2 anneal lets silicon surface-migrate to seal them into buried voids that cut leakage paths beneath the access transistor.

title: Temporary-bond tester wafer probes every die in one touch
idea: Combine temporary direct bonding with wafer probing: a reusable tester wafer carrying BIST controllers and power delivery is bonded face-to-face to the DRAM wafer through the fine-pitch pads later used for stacking. It runs all die tests in parallel and then debonds.

title: Kerfless porous-silicon lift-off reuses each crystal-grown wafer tenfold
idea: Combine solar-industry epitaxial lift-off (porous-Si release layer under 20 um epitaxy) with DRAM. The memory is built in the epi layer, bonded device-side to a carrier or logic wafer, cleaved at the porous layer, and the CZ parent wafer is re-polished and reused 10+ times.

title: Spatial ALD-ALE supercycles sculpt capacitor holes in one tool
idea: Combine spatial (rotary-platen) atomic layer deposition with atomic layer etching on one platen. Alternating sectors deposit a protective liner at the hole top and quasi-isotropically etch the bowed and tapered zones, reshaping each high-aspect-ratio hole into a straight cylinder in one pass.

title: Heat-vanishing polymer capacitor mold eliminates the support lattice
idea: Combine BEOL air-gap sacrificial polymers (thermally decomposable polycarbonate/polynorbornene) with the capacitor mold. Holes are etched in the polymer and low-temperature PEALD electrodes are formed, then the mold is removed by dry burnout rather than an HF wet strip, so no capillary forces topple the pillars.
note: Polymer mold limits electrode thermal budget; HAR polymer etch plausible.

title: Array buried-channel transistor reused as the only periphery transistor
idea: Combine the array's recessed-channel buried-wordline transistor with periphery logic: decoders, sense control and I/O are built only from the same BCAT-style devices (upsized, paralleled, dynamic logic styles), and the separate HKMG planar periphery module is deleted.

title: Delete retention-tail implants and anneals; codes absorb the leakers
idea: Combine the cell recipe with system coding: the halo and compensation implant masks and the extended hydrogen anneal, which exist only to tame the 13 fA leakage tail, are removed. The ~1% of cells that then fall below 64 ms retention are absorbed by scrub plus code.

title: Sort-time error syndromes replace most inline metrology
idea: Combine code-layer syndrome counters with advanced process control: every probed die reports spatial maps of corrected bits, which are decoded into virtual metrology (CD, overlay, etch depth inferred from error signatures). Inline CD-SEM/OCD sampling can then drop ~70%.

title: Lower-grade crystals from recycled-quartz crucibles, leakers absorbed by codes
idea: Combine cheaper crystal growth (crucibles with thin synthetic liners over recycled or non-Spruce-Pine quartz, several pulls per crucible) with error tolerance. Higher oxygen-precipitate and metal densities lengthen the leakage tail, and the extra retention-weak cells are absorbed within the 1% budget.

title: Fiber delay-line carousel circulates weights past pipelined accelerators
idea: Combine 1950s delay-line memory with WDM optics: model weights circulate continuously in a 10-20 km amplified fiber loop at ~25 Tb/s aggregate, and each pipeline-stage accelerator taps the wavelengths carrying its layer exactly when they pass, so weights are stored in flight instead of in DRAM.

title: Sense-amplifier row latch reconfigured as on-die serializer
idea: Combine the bitline sense-amp row (an 8-16 kb latch already holding the opened page) with a SerDes shift register: add a segment-level pass chain so the latched row shifts directly into a local high-speed serializer next to the mat, bypassing column decoders, global I/O lines and the central datapath for streaming reads.

title: Electroplated copper-manganese alloy that grows its own barrier
idea: Combine TSV electroplating with barrier formation: plate Cu-0.5%Mn from a non-aqueous or ionic-liquid bath onto an electroless seed; a 350 C anneal drives Mn to the oxide liner forming a few-nm MnSiO3 barrier and leaves pure Cu, deleting the argon-sputtered Ta/TaN barrier.
note: Cu-Mn self-forming barriers are known BEOL art; plating Mn alloy from non-aqueous bath is the hard, unproven step.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling replaces helium in TSV plasma etch
idea: Combine the electrostatic chuck's backside gas cooling with hydrogen, whose thermal conductivity (~0.18 W/m-K) beats helium's (~0.15), using a low-leak sealed chuck with H2 sensing and interlocks so TSV DRIE and other plasma steps keep wafer temperature control with no helium; H2 is made domestically by electrolysis.

title: Soft-decision sensing plus NAND LDPC to read tiny capacitors
idea: Combine the DRAM sense amp with NAND flash soft-read: the bitline is compared against 3-7 shifted references (a mini flash-ADC sharing one regenerative latch) to give per-bit confidence, and a short-latency LDPC decoder at the bank uses those log-likelihoods. Cells with roughly half today's charge (~2.5 fF, AR ~35) then read at acceptable error rates.

title: Three-tier charge-summing majority vote on a shared vertical bitline
idea: Combine triple modular redundancy with charge sharing: three cheap stacked oxide-TFT/capacitor tiers on one vertical bitline are written together and read by opening all three gates at once, so the bitline sees the analog sum and one fully leaked or shorted cell cannot flip the bit. Buildable in a university nanofab: three sequential low-temperature IGZO/MIM tiers.

title: Test-then-write: maskless e-beam final metal routes around defects
idea: Combine wafer test with maskless lithography: after electrical test of the cell array, a per-die e-beam (or laser direct-write) exposure of the final metal layer is computed so bitline/wordline straps bypass defective cells and segments, giving every die custom wiring. Buildable in a university nanofab: e-beam writer plus probe-station test.

title: UCIe memory die bank: interchangeable known-good DRAM chiplets
idea: Fuse a standard die-to-die interface (UCIe/BoW) with a commodity exchange. Any qualified small maker sells known-good DRAM chiplets with a common footprint, pinout and test spec through a brokerage that warrants interchangeability, the way a grain elevator does.

title: Nanoimprint memory litho with siloxane-brush non-fluorinated release
idea: Fuse Canon-style nanoimprint lithography (already qualified for memory pitches) with a PDMS/siloxane polymer-brush or graphene release layer on the quartz template, replacing the fluorinated FOTS anti-stick monolayer.

title: Solar-cell field-effect passivation shell around the storage junction
idea: Adapt PERC/TOPCon solar passivation: wrap storage-node junction sidewalls in ALD Al2O3 carrying ~-5e12 cm-2 fixed negative charge, and replace the implanted node contact with a 1.2 nm tunnel-oxide/poly-Si passivating contact, removing implant damage and repelling carriers from interface traps.
note: Tail leakage is GIDL/trap-assisted at high field; solar passivation gains may not transfer to 15 nm junctions.

title: Tesla-valve graded barrier that ratchets charge into the node
idea: Borrow the no-moving-parts Tesla fluidic diode: build a compositionally graded oxide barrier (InGaZnO to Ga2O3 to Al2O3) between access channel and storage node so the write-direction barrier collapses under field while the retention-direction barrier stays >1.5 eV.
note: Graded barrier asymmetry; IGZO already gives long retention.

title: MLCC core-shell grain engineering for 5 nm high-k films
idea: Adapt the BaTiO3 core-shell grains MLCC makers use to flatten k versus field: grow nanolaminated rutile TiO2 grain cores with Al/Nb-doped shells via ALD supercycles, so k ~80-100 survives at 5 nm while grain-boundary leakage is blocked.
note: Incremental Cs gain; leakage at 5 nm likely limiting.

title: Canal-lock access: series switches with an equalized middle chamber
idea: Adapted from canal locks, which equalize a chamber before opening a gate: put two access transistors in series and drive their middle node with a minimum-size follower whose gate is the storage node, so the inner transistor always sees ~0 V drain-source. Both gates open together for read/write; in hold, the storage-side device has almost no Vds to drive leakage.

title: Electret-microphone charge sets the access-transistor threshold permanently
idea: Adapted from electret microphones, whose fluoropolymer holds implanted charge for decades: implant a stable sheet of fixed charge into a deep-trap dielectric layer beside the access channel so its threshold is raised permanently, letting the wordline rest at 0 V instead of a negative voltage when off.

title: Pipeline cathodic protection: guard junctions intercept stray carriers
idea: Adapted from cathodic protection, where a sacrificial anode takes corrosion current instead of the pipe: run a shallow, reverse-biased n+ guard stripe between storage-node rows, tied to a collector rail, so minority electrons generated in the bulk or injected by hammered neighbor rows are collected before reaching a storage node.

title: Self-cleaning oven: wordline Joule heating anneals away the leakage tail
idea: Adapted from pyrolytic self-cleaning ovens and Macronix's self-healing NAND: during maintenance windows, drive a controlled current through selected buried wordlines to heat local cells to ~250-400 C for milliseconds, annealing traps and re-passivating interfaces that hot-carrier and hammer stress created over the module's life.
note: Macronix self-healing NAND precedent; heating neighbors and metallization risk.

title: Self-healing concrete capsules: buried hydrogen reservoir re-passivates interfaces
idea: Adapted from self-healing concrete, which embeds capsules that release healing agent into new cracks: deposit a deuterium-rich SiNx reservoir film above the access-device level, capped by a barrier with a controlled leak rate, so D slowly re-supplies the Si/SiO2 interface and re-passivates dangling bonds as they form over a 10-year life.

title: Plumbing unions for 3D stacks: reworkable low-temperature microbump joints
idea: Adapted from plumbing unions that let one pipe section come out without cutting the rest: bond HBM-style stacks with low-melting In or Sn-Bi microbumps at defined 'union' levels, so a die whose retention fails burn-in or ages in the field can be removed near 150 C and replaced without scrapping the stack.

title: Solar PID-recovery box: nightly reverse-bias de-trapping of access devices
idea: Adapted from the PID-recovery boxes that undo potential-induced degradation in solar parks with a night-time counter-voltage: during idle windows the controller applies reverse gate and well bias to blocks of rows for seconds, emptying charge trapped in access-transistor gate dielectrics and spacers by wordline and hammer stress.

title: Resonant gate drive recovers wordline CV-squared energy
idea: Borrowed from resonant gate drivers in MHz power converters: groups of wordline drivers share an LC tank (inductor in the package or interposer), so each wordline charges along a sinusoid and its charge returns to the tank on close instead of being dumped to ground.

title: Noise-cancelling headphone loop on the cell plate
idea: Borrowed from active noise cancellation and ECG driven-right-leg amplifiers: dummy bitlines in each mat pick up common-mode noise (plate bounce, wordline kick, substrate), and a fast amplifier drives the inverse onto the plate and reference lines during sensing.
note: Driving the large plate node at ns speed needs a big amplifier.

title: RFID backscatter turns DRAM output into reflection
idea: Borrowed from passive RFID backscatter: the processor sends a continuous carrier down each data line, and the DRAM die only switches a small termination impedance to modulate the reflection, so it needs no output drivers or their supply current.
note: Resembles POD signaling; carrier separation at multi-Gbps.

title: X-ray flat-panel charge integrators read centimeter-long bitlines
idea: Borrowed from flat-panel X-ray detectors, which read ~1 fC pixel charges down 40 cm data lines: each glass-panel bitline is held at virtual ground by a switched-capacitor charge-integrating amplifier, so the cell's full charge transfers to a small feedback capacitor whatever the line capacitance.

title: Touchscreen mutual-capacitance sensing reads cells nondestructively
idea: Borrowed from projected-capacitive touch controllers: each cell is a coupling capacitor at a wordline-bitline crossing on glass whose value is shifted by a trapped-charge or ferroelectric layer; a TX pulse on the wordline and charge sensing on the bitline read it without discharging any storage node.

title: Ion-exchanged glass waveguides form the panel's global data bus
idea: Borrowed from ion-exchange waveguides used in planar fiber couplers: optical waveguides are written into the glass substrate itself, with microLED emitters at each mat and thin-film photodiodes at the panel edge replacing centimeter-long metal global I/O lines.
note: Assumes glass-panel memory; microLED/TFT photodiode speed and energy.

title: ARM-style IP licensing of thin-film periphery to display fabs
idea: Borrowed from ARM's licensing model: develop a validated library of oxide-TFT sense amps, decoders and pumps (with process recipes) and license it to underused Gen-6/8.5 display fabs for a royalty per square meter, so memory supply grows with existing panel capacity.

title: Event-camera address-event bus for self-requested refresh
idea: Borrowed from neuromorphic event cameras' address-event representation: each row on a glass panel has a sentinel cell with a deliberately weaker capacitor and a thin-film comparator that fires the row address onto an arbitrated event bus when it decays, so only rows that need refresh get it.

title: Hard-disk TDMR: joint bitline sensing cancels neighbor crosstalk
idea: Adapted from two-dimensional magnetic recording, where multiple readers cancel inter-track interference: sense amps resolve neighboring bitline pairs jointly and subtract a calibrated coupling term, letting bitline pitch go below today's coupling limit.
note: Joint detection needs ADC-like sensing per bitline, inflating periphery.

title: Coaxial cable: grounded sleeves around every vertical bitline
idea: Adapted from coax: each vertical bitline in a 3D array is wrapped in a thin grounded metal sleeve over low-k, trading ~20% more self-capacitance for near-zero coupling to neighbor bitlines and plates.

title: Gemstone-style cleaving recovers backside slabs from thinned memory wafers
idea: Stacked and HBM DRAM dies are ground from 775 um down to ~30-50 um, so >90% of the crystal becomes sludge. Adapt gemstone cleaving: after the front side is bonded to a carrier, an IR laser writes a buried damage plane ~60 um deep, and a thermal-stress pulse splits off a ~650 um slab that is repolished into a new wafer.

title: LCD panel fabs build capacitor-free memory on Gen-8 glass
idea: Display fabs pattern oxide TFTs on 2.2 x 2.5 m glass at a tiny fraction of wafer cost per area. Adapt idle Gen-6/8 oxide lines to make capacitor-free gain-cell memory sheets that are diced into tiles and bonded as a capacity tier behind CXL controllers.

title: Data-center 48-volt distribution brought inside the memory stack
idea: Adapted from the 48 V rack transition: the HBM stack is fed at ~12 V through a few TSVs, and integrated switched-capacitor converters on each die step it down. This replaces hundreds of low-voltage power TSVs.
note: 12 V conversion on DRAM-process devices is hard.

title: Power-line communication sends data over HBM power TSVs
idea: Adapted from home power-line networking: modulated high-frequency data is superimposed on the stack's many power/ground TSVs and planes through simple 180 nm couplers, so power vias also carry control, refresh and sideband traffic.

title: Laptop heat pipes etched into silicon spacers cool tall stacks
idea: Adapted from laptop heat pipes: the 1994 Bosch DRIE process etches sealed micro heat-pipe channels with wicking grooves into silicon spacer dies inserted in the memory stack. Filled with water or methanol, they carry heat sideways to the lid passively.
note: Spacer dies add height and TSV length; micro heat pipe capacity at mm scale is small.

title: NAND-style read-reference tracking keyed to time since refresh
idea: Adapted from NAND flash controllers that shift read thresholds as charge drifts: each mat holds a few dummy cells rewritten at every refresh; at read time a small comparator samples their decayed voltage and shifts the sense-amp reference so the decision threshold follows the leakage curve instead of sitting at a fixed VARY/2.
note: Dummy cells track typical decay, not the tail cells that set refresh.

title: Snap-through buckled nanoribbon holds bits as geometry
idea: MINIFY a MEMS bistable beam to a 10 nm x 80 nm pre-stressed SiC or amorphous-carbon ribbon arched up or down; GHz-range resonance allows ~1 ns electrostatic snap-through writes, and position is read through the gap-capacitance change to an under-electrode.
note: aF capacitive read signal and fatigue over ~1e15 cycles at 10 nm scale are doubtful.

title: Solid-electrolyte double-layer nanocapacitor with Helmholtz-scale gap
idea: MAGNIFY areal capacitance ~100x with an electric double layer: a 3-nm solid proton conductor (hydrated ZrO2 or phosphosilicate glass) between blocking electrodes stores charge in a ~0.5-nm Helmholtz layer (~10-20 uF/cm2), so a planar 20x20 nm node reaches ~0.08 fF, enough for a gain-cell read gate with no high-AR etch.
note: 3 nm proton conductor RC ~ns plausible; self-discharge, humidity and BEOL stability are risks.

title: Microsecond-retention parasitic-node bit for streaming activations
idea: MINIFY retention on purpose from 64 ms to ~10 us: store bits only on the ~0.05 fF parasitic node of a capacitor-less vertical transistor and map the tier to AI activations and KV staging data that live < 10 us, so data is consumed before it decays and refresh never runs.
note: 10 us retention is very tight for scheduling.

title: Magnify the gate count: two series wordlines per vertical pillar
idea: Stack two independently driven gate-all-around segments along each vertical access pillar; both turn on for access, but in standby the intermediate node self-biases to give the upper device negative Vgs (stack effect), dropping subthreshold leakage 10-30x.

title: Minify one-size refresh: JEDEC per-module retention negotiation field
idea: Push a JEDEC addition where each module publishes a measured, temperature-indexed retention table in SPD, re-measured by in-field self-test, and the controller negotiates tREFI from it instead of the fixed 64/32 ms rule.
note: VRT makes test-time retention tables unreliable without in-field re-measurement.

title: Magnify restore voltage only on refresh: overdrive write-back
idea: During refresh (not normal access) sense amps restore '1' cells to ~1.4 V from a separate boosted restore rail with a brief overdriven wordline, storing ~40% more charge so cells take longer to decay to the sense threshold; normal accesses keep the low VARY.

title: Minify the flush: dirty-line tracking plus deep-trench energy bank
idea: Each DRAM bank tracks dirty rows in a bitmap and keeps an on-die deep-trench capacitor bank sized only to flush the dirty fraction into a co-integrated MRAM shadow subarray at power loss; clean rows are already mirrored in NV storage.

title: IGZO shadow row buffers magnify open rows eightfold
idea: Stack 2T0C IGZO gain-cell latches (<=350 C; leakage <1e-18 A, so they hold for seconds) above each SA stripe, giving every bank 8 shadow row buffers that keep recently opened rows readable without re-activation.

title: Remanent-polarization offset trim inside each sense latch
idea: Place a tiny AlScN or HZO ferroelectric capacitor (both <=400 C) on each SA latch node and partially polarize it at test so its remanent charge cancels that SA's offset, MINIFYING offset to near zero with no trim SRAM or DAC.

title: N-type-only oxide sense amp using capacitive bootstrapping
idea: MINIFY the device menu to one transistor type: an IGZO-only cross-coupled latch uses bootstrapped capacitive pull-ups (as in display gate drivers) instead of p-FETs, avoiding immature p-type oxides and keeping the periphery tier to ~8 masks at <=350 C.
note: IGZO-only bootstrapped latches enable a low-temperature periphery tier; slow speed.

title: BEOL Schottky diode-matrix decoders minify predecode transistors
idea: Pd/IGZO Schottky diodes (<=300 C) wired as diode-ROM one-hot decoders above the array replace transistor predecoders, MINIFYING decoder transistor count ~10x and moving decode logic off the silicon.

title: Stepwise tank-capacitor charging makes bitline restore nearly adiabatic
idea: MAGNIFY on-die charge storage: bitline restore and equalization proceed in 4 steps through BEOL high-k tank capacitors (<=300 C) instead of one full swing from the supply, so each step dissipates only ~1/4 of the CV2/2 that a direct swing wastes.
note: Stepwise restore adds latency on a small swing.

title: Magnify bitline to 4096 cells using current-read gain cells
idea: In a vertical-bitline 3D array, hang 4096 tiered 3T gain cells on one bitline. They are read non-destructively by current, not by charge sharing, so bitline capacitance no longer limits signal and one sense amp serves 8x more cells than in 1T1C.

title: Minify staircase contacts: in-tier pass-gate decoders
idea: Build log2(N) pass-gate decoder trees from the same lateral access transistors inside each 3D tier, so the staircase needs about log2 of the per-tier wordline contacts instead of one per row. Validate with TCAD, a 4-tier coupon and a patent package, then license.
note: Pass-gate trees from tier transistors reduce staircase contacts; drive strength of lateral devices a doubt.

title: Metallurgical-grade wafer bulk under a five-micron electronic-grade skin
idea: Minify purity to where the electrons live: grow DRAM wafer bulk from 6N upgraded-metallurgical silicon and deposit a 5 um 11N epitaxial layer on top. A buried carbon-rich gettering layer traps bulk metals during every thermal step.

title: Spatial ALD with cold-trap recapture recycles hafnium and zirconium precursors
idea: Magnify precursor utilization from ~5% to ~80%: spatial ALD heads confine TEMAZ/TEMAH to millimetre gaps and exhaust into cold traps, and the condensate is re-distilled on site and returned to the bubbler.

title: Fiber-laser 193 nm sources end the neon dependence
idea: Minify rare-gas use to zero: replace ArF excimer lasers (neon buffer gas, historically ~50% from Ukraine and Russia) with Yb-fiber lasers frequency-converted to 193 nm in nonlinear-crystal cascades for DUV scanners.

title: Germanium-free 3D DRAM tiers using anodized porous-silicon sacrificial layers
idea: Magnify tier count past the SiGe strain limit: grow alternating heavily boron-doped and lightly doped all-silicon epitaxy, then anodize only the p+ layers into porous silicon, which is oxidized or etched out as the sacrificial layer.

title: Silicon-on-nothing cavities under storage nodes cut 125 C leakage
idea: Magnify vacuum as the insulator: anneal patterned trench arrays in hydrogen so silicon surface migration seals empty cavities beneath each storage junction, giving SOI-like isolation on a bulk wafer.

title: Minify the fab: half-inch wafer micro-fabs for distributed DRAM
idea: Minify the wafer to 12.5 mm and the tool to a desk-sized, cleanroom-free unit (Minimal-Fab style sealed shuttle), then run a simple gain-cell DRAM flow in hundreds of $5M micro-fabs placed next to data centers instead of one $15B megafab.

title: Micro-transfer printing 100 um DRAM chiplets onto panels
idea: Minify the die to 100 um chiplets made at a mature node, then magnify deployment by elastomer-stamp transfer printing 100,000 chiplets per stroke onto large panels with printed interconnect.

title: Minify writability: mask-ROM DIMMs for immutable system pages
idea: Minify the writable footprint by moving the kernel text, libc, Python, CUDA libraries and popular container base layers into ultra-dense NOR-style mask-ROM DIMMs mapped read-only at ~50 ns. These are reflashed yearly as 'golden releases'.

title: Minify fragmentation: hardware page meshing at line granularity
idea: Minify allocator fragmentation: the memory controller finds two sparsely filled physical pages whose live 64 B lines do not overlap and merges them into one frame. Both virtual pages keep pointing at it through a line-offset remap, so it works like the Mesh allocator but transparently and for every language.

title: In-package mm-wave broadcast for weight multicast
idea: MAGNIFY fan-out: on-die 140 GHz antennas let one memory chiplet broadcast the same weights to 16 compute chiplets at once, instead of 16 point-to-point copies over the interposer.
note: 140 GHz links give tens of Gb/s, far below interposer bandwidth.

title: Free-space optical memory modules on kinematic mounts
idea: MINIFY contact to none: memory modules drop into a slot with a three-ball kinematic mount, and lenses align free-space optical beams to the host, so there are no connectors to wear and modules swap tool-free.

title: Harvest-and-rebin HBM from retired accelerators
idea: MAGNIFY HBM's useful life: base dies carry standard re-ball pads and a full built-in self-test, so stacks pulled from retired GPUs are retested, graded and rebonded into CXL memory expanders.
note: Debonding underfilled stacks from interposers is the hard part.

title: Swappable PHY adapter chiplet keeps DRAM across generations
idea: MAGNIFY memory lifetime to three compute generations: the DRAM stack talks a fixed simple die-to-die protocol, and only a small reworkable adapter chiplet is swapped to match each new host PHY.
note: Needs reworkable bonding; fixed protocol adds an adapter hop.

title: Magnify row pitch on cheap glass area to starve row hammer
idea: Processed glass area costs ~500-1000x less per cm^2 than DRAM-fab silicon, so space wordlines 3x farther apart with grounded shield lines between them. The insulating substrate also removes the shared bulk path for injected charge.

title: Minify the fab 1000x: shoebox gain-cell micro-fab swarm
idea: Shrink a DRAM line to desk-size tools on half-inch wafers (Minimal-Fab style, sealed wafer shuttles so no cleanroom) running a 90 nm IGZO 2T0C gain-cell process; deploy ~500 such ~$8M lines as regional franchises next to datacenters instead of one $20B megafab.
note: Half-inch wafers make cost per bit poor despite tiny entry ticket.

title: Eliminate the leakage tail: per-cell Vt trim via charge-trap back gate
idea: Give each access transistor a thin back gate with a nitride charge-trap layer; at final test the tester finds the leakiest 0.1-1% of cells and Fowler-Nordheim-programs electrons into their back-gate trap, raising Vt 200-300 mV permanently. The tail cells that set the refresh rate are trimmed to the median.

title: Eliminate ground dumping: resonant LC adiabatic bitline refresh
idea: During refresh, drive bitline restore from an on-package resonant LC tank (thin-film inductors in the interposer) so charge sloshes between banks instead of being dumped to ground; sense amplifiers only steer the resonant swing. Roughly 60-80% of bitline CV^2 is recovered each refresh cycle.

title: Eliminate shared thermal budgets: transfer-printed silicon nanomembrane access transistors
idea: Fabricate access transistors in SOI nanomembranes with full high-temperature processing, release them, and transfer-print them with an elastomer stamp onto a separately built high-k capacitor backplane. Neither part must survive the other's anneal, so junctions stay pristine and the capacitor gets its crystallization anneal.

title: Eliminate the doped storage-node junction: high-barrier PtSi Schottky contact
idea: Replace the n+ storage-node junction with a self-aligned PtSi or IrSi contact on n-type silicon (barrier ~0.85-0.95 eV), forming a gate-modulated Schottky-barrier access device; in hold, the barrier blocks thermionic emission and there is no junction depletion region to host trap-assisted generation. Silicidation runs below 500 C.

title: Eliminate inter-cell dielectric: air-gap isolation against passing-gate leakage
idea: Replace STI oxide between adjacent cells with sealed air-gap trenches (sacrificial poly removed by XeF2, sealed by PECVD), so passing wordlines couple far less into neighbouring storage nodes and no trapped oxide charge sits at the isolation edge.

title: Eliminate metal etch: pillar-first, catalyst-seeded electroless periphery wiring
idea: Photo-pattern an aminosilane SAM with UV-ozone and bind a Pd-ion catalyst only where lines and vias belong. Grow Co (with a Co-B cap) by electroless plating, build vias as plated pillars before the dielectric, spin-coat polysilazane-derived oxide over them, and polish to the pillar tops, so neither lines nor vias are ever etched.

title: Eliminate silicon oxide and nitride etching: chlorine-etchable periphery dielectrics
idea: In the periphery, swap the SiO2 and SiN that practically require fluorocarbon or HF to etch for dielectrics that etch in Cl/Br plasma or mild wet chemistry: Al2O3 and HfO2 (BCl3/Cl2), AlN (Cl2 or hot KOH) and amorphous-carbon hard masks (O2). SiO2 stays only where it is never etched (gap fill, lift-off).

title: Eliminate TSV keep-out: vertical bus runs through scribe lines
idea: Stack whole memory wafers without singulating between dies in a column; place all vertical power and signal vias in the scribe streets that are otherwise wasted, so the active die area has zero TSV keep-out, and dice the finished stack once.

title: Eliminate tungsten wordlines: in-situ doped SiGe wordline tiers
idea: In a Si/SiGe superlattice 3D DRAM, keep the wordline tiers as heavily boron-doped epitaxial SiGe grown in the same epi run, with no replacement-gate metal fill, and use short segmented wordlines with local drivers to tolerate the higher resistance.
note: Doped SiGe resistivity ~100x W forces many local drivers, eating periphery.

title: Eliminate the big monolithic die: fluidically self-assembled mat-lets
idea: Fabricate 0.5-1 mm2 DRAM mat-lets (array plus local SA), test and bin them, then pour them onto a logic wafer where shape-matched recesses and capillary forces seat them before a batch bond.

title: Eliminate the oxide mold and HF dip-out: ashable carbon molds
idea: Form capacitor holes in an amorphous-carbon mold instead of oxide, deposit the electrode, then remove the mold with dry O2/H2 plasma ash, eliminating the HF wet dip-out and the rinse/dry steps where cylinders collapse.

title: Eliminate hafnium, zirconium and ruthenium: rutile TiO2 templated on SnO2 electrodes
idea: Use conductive rutile SnO2 (oxygen-vacancy or F-doped) as the storage-node electrode; its rutile lattice templates ALD TiO2 from TiCl4 and water into the rutile phase at <=300 C, giving k~80-100, with a 0.5 nm Al2O3 interlayer to curb leakage.

title: Eliminate liquid drying and support lattices: vapor-HF release plus supercritical CO2
idea: Remove the capacitor mold oxide with vapor-phase HF and rinse/dry in supercritical CO2, so tall pillars never see a liquid-vapor meniscus and need none of the nitride support lattices added today to stop leaning and stiction.

title: Eliminate burn-in ovens: on-die heaters stress dies during wafer sort
idea: Add a thin metal heater mesh under each die and use internal charge pumps to apply elevated VPP/VARY while heating dies to ~125 C at the prober, screening infant mortality without package burn-in ovens. Shipped parts are standard DDR5/HBM3E; the heaters are left floating.

title: Eliminate probe cards: contactless whole-wafer optical power and RF readout
idea: Each die carries a small photovoltaic cell and a near-field RF backscatter antenna in the scribe; a high-intensity LED array powers every die on the wafer to run internal BIST, results are read wirelessly in parallel, and the test circuitry is cut off at dicing. DDR/HBM pads are never touched and the product interface is unchanged.

title: Eliminate per-product mask sets: one array die personalized late
idea: Design a single core array with interchangeable top-metal and fuse options so the same front-end wafers become DDR5 x4/x8, LPDDR5X or HBM core dies by choosing last-via masks late in the line. Each product still meets its unchanged JEDEC interface.

title: Eliminate backgrinding waste: laser subsurface slicing of HBM core wafers
idea: Before TSV reveal, focus an infrared laser through the wafer back side to write a cleave plane ~40 um below the devices (as laser slicing does for SiC), split the device layer onto its carrier, and repolish the remaining ~700 um slab for reuse as monitor wafers or epitaxial donors. Resulting stacks are standard HBM.
note: Si slicing less mature than SiC KABRA.

title: Series voltage-stacked DRAM dies eliminate most power TSVs
idea: Eliminate low-voltage high-current power delivery: stack 12 dies electrically in series across a ~13 V rail so each die floats in its own ~1.1 V domain and the same current is recycled through all dies; on-die switched-capacitor balancers absorb mismatch and capacitive level shifters carry data between domains.

title: Charge-coupled shift memory streams KV cache without decoders
idea: Eliminate row/column decoders and the address bus for sequential data: store KV-cache pages in CCD-style buried-channel charge-transfer registers that shift packets to one sense node per lane each clock, reviving 1970s CCD memory on modern CMOS-image-sensor lines.
note: CCD density on CIS nodes unlikely to beat DRAM cost/bit.

title: Wireless mm-wave weight broadcast to many chiplets at once
idea: Eliminate per-consumer copies and point-to-point wires for read-shared data: one memory chiplet broadcasts weight tiles over a 200-300 GHz on-package antenna and waveguide cavity, and 16-64 compute chiplets receive the same bits simultaneously.

title: Checkpoint-in-place: non-volatile HBM ends training checkpoint traffic
idea: Eliminate copying model and optimizer state to storage: on NV-cell HBM, a checkpoint is a metadata flip that seals a copy-on-write page epoch inside the stack, so no checkpoint bytes leave the package; recovery remaps to the last sealed epoch.

title: Eliminate separate ECC: lattice-coded multi-level charge across cell groups
idea: Write groups of 8 <=400 C oxide-TFT cells jointly as one point of a dense 8-D (E8) lattice of charge levels, as coded modulation does in modems. Decoding to the nearest lattice point corrects analog drift and noise directly, folding the error code into the multi-level storage.

title: Eliminate the cleanroom building: sealed-pod minimal fabs in warehouses
idea: Eliminate the ballroom cleanroom: adopt the minimal-fab model (half-inch wafers in sealed shuttles, shoebox tools with local mini-environments) to make radiation-hard, automotive and defense DRAM in ordinary industrial buildings.

title: Eliminate process secrecy: open DRAM PDK and periphery IP
idea: Eliminate closed DRAM know-how: fund an open PDK for a 1T1C stacked-capacitor process at a mature US node (40-65nm) plus open sense-amp, decoder and refresh-controller IP so startups and universities can tape out real DRAM.

title: Mechanical access: NEMS relay air gap isolates every cell
idea: Swap electronic isolation for a physical gap: each capacitor reaches its bitline through a nanoscale electrostatic TiN or carbon cantilever relay (5 nm gap) that closes only when the wordline pulls it; open, the leakage is literally zero, and the relay needs no doped silicon so it builds in the BEOL.
note: Zero-leakage access is real, but 1e10-1e12 contact endurance is far below DRAM's ~1e15+.

title: Flip the wafer: backside deep-trench capacitors etched in MEMS fabs
idea: Rearrange front and back: finish access transistors and bitlines on the wafer front in a mature DRAM/logic line, bond to a carrier, thin to ~20-40 um, then use existing 200 mm MEMS-fab DRIE (>=50:1 Bosch etch) to cut deep capacitor trenches from the backside up to each storage node. The capacitor gets the full silicon thickness instead of competing with bitlines for front-side height.

title: Ephemeral-memory cloud instances priced below standard RAM
idea: Reverse the memory guarantee into a product: cloud providers sell VM memory under a published 'touch-within-N-ms' contract (data preserved only if accessed or rewritten within, say, 32 ms) at a discount. These instances run on refresh-relaxed or refresh-off DRAM, including short-retention bins, and suit streaming inference, ETL and video pipelines that rewrite buffers continuously.

title: Roaming sense amp sweeps sixteen bitlines inside their charge-hold window
idea: Reverse the one-amp-per-bitline layout: after charge sharing, a bitline holds its ~100 mV signal for ~1-2 us, so one offset-cancelled sense amp steps through a 16:1 mux, regenerating and restoring each bitline in turn, requested column first. The data waits for the amp instead of each amp waiting for data.

title: Chopped dither comparator reads signals below its own offset
idea: Reverse noise's role: a tiny comparator fires 16 times in ~2 ns with a known dither added and its inputs swapped every other decision; an up/down counter shared per 8 bitlines cancels the offset (it flips sign with the chop) while the dither linearizes, recovering the sign of a signal far smaller than the offset.

title: Victim-margin metering: measure hammered neighbors instead of counting aggressors
idea: Reverse row-hammer defense: on a random 1-in-64 activation, the SA strip re-senses the two neighbor rows with a reference shifted by ~30 mV; only if a bit fails the shifted reference (margin eroded) is that victim refreshed, so no per-row activation counters exist.

title: Stepwise adiabatic restore returns bitline charge to tank rails
idea: Reverse the charge flow on discharge: bitlines are charged and discharged in four steps through intermediate tank-capacitor rails, so charge falling from VDD returns to the tanks instead of ground and restore draws only the top step from the supply; dummy array edges serve as tanks.

title: Voltage-to-time sensing with one TDC shared by 32 bitlines
idea: Convert the signal domain: each bitline drives a current-starved inverter whose delay encodes the ~100 mV signal; edges from 32 bitlines are serialized into one shared time-to-digital converter that also outputs a margin value.
note: Restore still needs per-bitline latch.

title: Array stores its own sense-amp offset trims, refreshed as charge
idea: Reverse who serves whom: at power-up BIST measures each SA's offset and writes 4-bit trims to a reserved row per subarray; at every refresh that row is read into tiny charge-storage trim capacitors at each SA, which bias the latch to cancel offset.
note: Trim cap leakage and trim granularity.

title: Sparsity-biased precharge: assume zero, sense only departures
idea: Reverse the neutral mid-rail reference: for AI tensors where most bits are 0, bitlines precharge to the 0 level and a single-ended detector fires only when a cell pulls the bitline up; rows dominated by 1s are stored inverted with a flag bit.

title: Twist vertical bitline pairs mid-stack for folded-pair noise cancellation
idea: Pair adjacent vertical bitline pillars as true/complement and swap their positions halfway up the stack through a crossover in a middle tier, so each sees equal coupling from every neighbor and the bottom sense amp gets a common-mode-free differential signal, restoring folded-bitline immunity in 3D.

title: One grayscale mask cuts every 3D tier contact
idea: Replace the multi-mask trim-etch staircase with a single grayscale reticle whose resist-thickness steps transfer through a proportional etch, opening contacts to all 64 tiers at graded depths in one exposure: a reversed staircase made of holes instead of terraces.

title: Rotate alternate mats 90 degrees for transposed access
idea: Rotate every second mat 90 degrees in layout (zero added masks), so data written row-major lands column-major there; the controller reads a matrix row from normal mats or its transpose from rotated mats with a single activation.

title: Spall, don't grind: peel HBM dies off reusable parents
idea: Reverse thinning: instead of grinding a 775 um wafer down to 40 um for HBM, deposit a nickel stressor and controlled-spall the 40 um device layer off, then re-epi and reuse the parent wafer as a fresh substrate.

title: Hafnium- and zirconium-free titania capacitors with a corrected leakage tail
idea: Swap ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 for abundant TiO2/Al2O3 nanolaminates (k~40-60) and treat the ~1% of cells with grain-boundary leakage as correctable erasures flagged by a retention-profiling map.

title: Ship the mask defect: unrepaired, pellicle-free reticles
idea: Reverse mask qualification: use EUV/DUV reticles with residual blank defects and no pellicle; every repeating print defect lands at the same cell address in every die, which goes into a single mask-level defect table loaded into each die's remap ECC.

title: Precursor boomerang: recycled lower-purity ALD precursors
idea: Reverse precursor flow: cold-trap the ~90% of unreacted Zr/Hf/Ti amides from ALD exhaust, resynthesize them on site to ~4N instead of 6N, and accept the resulting trace-impurity leaky cells within the 1% BER budget.

title: Build first, define later: antifuse-personalized array
idea: Reverse design-then-build: fabricate a uniform sea of cells plus an antifuse routing lattice with no product-specific decoding, test it, then program the lattice so only good subarrays are wired into the logical address map.

title: Open reticle: a shared public DRAM array mask set
idea: Reverse mask ownership: a government-backed consortium funds and qualifies one open DRAM array mask set and process recipe, licensed cheaply to new fabs, which only pay for their own periphery masks.
note: Mask sets are tied to proprietary process recipes.

title: The mold is the electrode: keep a conductive mold
idea: Reverse mold-then-remove: etch capacitor holes into a conductive mold (doped poly-Si or TiN-rich stack) that stays in place as the outer plate, so you deposit only dielectric and inner electrode and skip mold strip and support-lattice formation.

title: One imprint, three layers: multi-level 3D nanoimprint
idea: Rearrange several flat exposures into one 3D stamp: an e-beam-mastered template with stepped relief imprints the storage-node landing pad, contact and line trench in one stroke, then a dual-damascene-like etch transfers it.

title: 1D-gridded periphery with directed-ion-beam cuts
idea: Reverse free-form layout into one-direction gratings: redesign periphery logic so every layer is a uniform line grating (ArFi plus spacer), and personalize it only with cuts made by a tilted directed ion beam through coarse openings.

title: Free-before-allocate runtimes shrink garbage-collected heap headroom
idea: Reverse GC's allocate-then-find-garbage order: compiler region inference and escape analysis free most objects deterministically at scope exit, and a forwarding table in the memory controller lets the remaining collector compact concurrently, so heaps run at ~1.2x live data instead of 2-3x.

title: Mercury-lamp i-line compression chips tiled on every DIMM
idea: Move memory compression from the CPU to the memory: many slow, wide BDI/LZ compressor lanes are built in 350 nm i-line fabs (mercury arc lamps instead of neon excimer lasers, argon-free fluorine etch with N2 diluent) and tiled on the DIMM or CXL card, each lane handling a slice of bank traffic.

title: One via through the whole stack, etched last
idea: Reverse via-first-per-die: adhesive-bond 4-8 thinned dies that each reserve aligned keep-out windows, then DRIE a single hole through the entire stack, line it with parylene and fill copper once, contacting each die through exposed sidewall metal rings.

title: Optical clock broadcast from above, no clock pins
idea: Reverse forwarded-clock wiring: one modulated LED or laser illuminates the package through a window, and silicon photodiodes on every memory and logic die recover the same clock edge simultaneously, removing clock trees, DLLs and clock bumps from the memory interface.

title: Vertical parity row rebuilds any dead row per subarray
idea: Rearrange ECC from horizontal to vertical: each subarray keeps one parity row equal to the XOR of its ~512 rows, with write deltas accumulated in an SRAM buffer and flushed during refresh, so a broken wordline, hammered row or stuck row is rebuilt as an erasure.
note: Parity updates need old data per write; SRAM delta buffer cost.

title: Voltage-accelerated room-temperature retention test replaces fluid-chilled testers
idea: Reverse the stress axis: instead of heating and chilling test heads with perfluoropolyether heat-transfer fluids, retention screening runs at room temperature with raised cell-node, plate and negative-wordline bias that accelerates junction and GIDL leakage by a calibrated factor equivalent to 85-95 C.

title: Memory outlives compute: debondable HBM stacks
idea: Reverse the lifetime hierarchy: HBM stacks attach to the interposer with low-temperature reversible solder or thermoplastic bonds. When the GPU retires, the stacks are lifted off and remounted on new base packages for inference or CXL use.

title: Raincoat instead of shower: sacrificial caps replace wet cleans
idea: Reverse cleaning into prevention: after each step, a few-nm sacrificial carbon cap is deposited in situ. Particles and contamination land on the cap during transport and queue time, and a dry O2/H2 ash removes it just before the next step.
note: Many cleans remove process residues, not transport contamination; cap/ash adds steps and surface oxidation.

title: Wordline-as-heater in-field anneal rejuvenates aged capacitor dielectrics
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: drive controlled current through spare wordline/plate metal to heat one air-gap-isolated sub-array to ~300-400 C for milliseconds, annealing out trap and oxygen-vacancy build-up in the capacitor dielectric and access-transistor interface after its data are moved to a neighbor mat. The aged storage element heals in place instead of being scrapped.
note: Electrothermal self-heal shown for FETs; 300-400 C local heating risks neighbors and metallization.

title: Overvoltage burn turns flickering VRT cells into deterministic hard faults
idea: TRIZ #16 Partial or excessive action: variable-retention-time cells flicker between leaky and good and escape test. During in-field maintenance, hit any cell flagged even once with a controlled ~2.5-3 V stress pulse that breaks its weak dielectric down to a hard short, so the next scrub always detects it and maps it to a spare.

title: Contactless coupled storage dies lift off for replacement
idea: TRIZ #17 Another dimension + #28 Mechanics substitution: stack storage dies with no TSVs or hybrid bonds; signals cross by inductive/capacitive coupling (~0.1 pJ/bit), power arrives through a few spring micro-contacts, and a reversible clamp holds the stack, so a worn storage die is lifted out and replaced while the logic base die stays.

title: Wordline bootstrap capacitor doubles as an analog hammer counter
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: make an element already present in every row do a second job. Each local wordline driver gets a tiny MIM capacitor that receives a fixed charge packet on every activation (a switched-capacitor integrator) and is cleared on refresh; when it crosses a comparator threshold the driver flags its two neighbours for targeted refresh, giving exact per-row activation counting without SRAM counter tables.

title: Park bitlines at VDD during self-refresh to zero ones' drain bias
idea: TRIZ #9 Preliminary anti-action: remove the harmful driving force before it acts. During long idle and self-refresh, bitlines are parked at VDD instead of VDD/2, so the vulnerable charged '1' cells see zero drain-source voltage and essentially no subthreshold loss, while '0' cells, protected by the negative wordline and far from their sense threshold, absorb the larger bias.
note: Simple standby bias change; zeros see larger Vds, tail could shift rather than shrink.

title: Flip the stack so memory dies, not logic, touch the cold plate
idea: TRIZ #17 Another dimension: use the vertical heat path instead of fighting it in-plane. In HBM and 3D stacks, place the DRAM dies against the cold plate and route the logic base-die heat out through a separate high-conductivity path (thermal TSV bundles plus a backside spreader), so the memory runs ~20-30 C cooler; cell leakage roughly halves every ~10 C.

title: Stainless-steel foil substrate doubles as global back gate and heatsink
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: make the substrate do three jobs. Oxide or 2D thin-film access transistors are built on a dielectric-coated stainless-steel foil; the foil itself is a static global back gate biased negative to push every array transistor into deep off-state, while also spreading heat and shielding the array (periphery lives on a separate die).
note: Global back gate known; foil TFT density far below DRAM.

title: Grow on reusable single-crystal wafers, laser-lift-off the memory film
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: grow single-crystal wide-gap channel layers (GaN, AlGaN or Ga2O3) on sapphire or bulk-oxide growth wafers, bond them to cheap glass panels, and laser-lift-off the film as in micro-LED and flexible-OLED production; the expensive growth wafer is repolished and reused 20-50 times.
note: Substrate is not the main cost; glass-panel lithography cannot reach DRAM density.

title: Built-in negative-charge dielectric replaces negative wordline pumps
idea: TRIZ #8 Anti-weight: counterbalance the depletion-mode tendency of wide-gap oxide TFTs with permanent charge. An AlOx layer on the glass substrate, carrying its native fixed negative charge (~1e12-1e13 cm-2, the effect used for solar-cell field passivation), sits under each channel as a static counterweight that shifts Vt positive by ~1 V, so the off-state is deep at a 0 V wordline.
note: AlOx fixed charge as back counterweight for oxide TFTs; charge stability over life is the doubt.

title: Wide-bandgap memory carve-out funding conversion of U.S. power-device fabs
idea: TRIZ #24 Intermediary: government acts as the intermediary between under-used U.S. SiC/GaN power-electronics lines and hyperscaler demand. A CHIPS-style program co-funds converting 150-200 mm wide-bandgap lines into refresh-free memory pilot lines and backs them with five-year hyperscaler offtake contracts for low-refresh capacity tiers.

title: Local quality: few precision sense amps steered to weak columns
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality replaces uniform sense amps: 7 of every 8 are minimum-size latches and 1 of 8 is a large offset-cancelled precision amp. Wafer test maps columns with weak cells or high-offset latches, and a column steering mux routes only those bitlines to the precision amps.

title: Universality: sense amps chain into shift register, deleting column decoders
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: after a row is latched, each sense amp also acts as one stage of a two-phase shift register (two extra transistors couple neighbours), streaming the page out of one edge port. Column decoders, column-select lines and most local I/O wiring disappear; random columns are reached by pipelined skip-shifting.

title: Skipping: precharge-free rail sensing with auto-zeroed reference sample
idea: TRIZ #21 Skipping: the equalize/precharge phase is skipped; each bitline stays at the rail it was last restored to, a coupling capacitor samples that level, and the sense amp compares the next cell's charge-sharing step against the sample plus a half-signal kick, alternating polarity each cycle.

title: Feedback: time-to-resolve margin meter schedules per-row refresh
idea: TRIZ #23 Feedback: a shared completion detector measures how long each sense amp takes to resolve during refresh; rows whose bits resolve slowly (low remaining charge) are logged in a small per-bank weak-row table and refreshed sooner, while fast-resolving rows stretch their interval to 256 ms or more.

title: Beforehand cushioning: weak-written sentinel rows trigger early mat refresh
idea: TRIZ #11 Beforehand cushioning: each mat reserves two sentinel rows that are written at only ~70% of the array voltage, making them deliberately weaker than any data row; they are read on every refresh pass, and the first sentinel failure raises that mat's refresh rate before real data is at risk.

title: Dual threshold ladders select one tier, deleting the 3D staircase
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: give each tier's lateral access device two series gates whose thresholds are graded in opposite directions through the stack (front-gate Vt rising with tier number, back-gate Vt falling). Driving the shared vertical front and back gates to the level pair for tier k turns on only tier k (tiers <=k AND >=k), so 8-16 tiers share one contact instead of a staircase.

title: LC-resonant wordline planes recycle charge in 3D arrays
idea: TRIZ #18 Mechanical vibration (use resonance): 3D wordline planes are large, regular capacitors, so pair each plane group with an on-package RDL inductor and drive it as an LC tank with adiabatic sinusoidal ramps. Most of the ~3 V wordline charge flows back into the tank instead of being dumped to ground every activation.
note: Adiabatic charge recovery is known; random single activations fit resonant tanks poorly.

title: Bank-switchable floating body: dynamic mode or self-held bipolar latch
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: the same 3D floating-body tiers run in two modes set per bank by source-line bias. At low bias they are dense dynamic cells that need refresh; above the parasitic-BJT latch threshold, impact-ionization feedback holds 1 and 0 statically, so hot banks skip refresh and idle banks drop to near-zero bias.
note: Bistable FB latch known (Z-RAM); per-bank mode switching is the twist.

title: Re-fuse spent crucible cullet into outer walls of new crucibles
idea: TRIZ #33 Homogeneity, rebuilding crucibles from crucibles: crush spent devitrified CZ crucibles, acid-leach the silicon residue, and arc-fuse the cristobalite cullet into the structural outer layer of new crucibles. Only a 2-3 mm inner layer, the part that touches the melt, uses virgin Spruce Pine or synthetic quartz.

title: Laser-sliced HBM wafer bodies reused as bonding carrier wafers
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation through the thickness: instead of grinding away 700 um, focus a sub-bandgap infrared laser ~80 um below the device side to write a modified plane (as KABRA does for SiC), then split the wafer. The ~650 um body is re-polished and reused as the temporary carrier wafer that HBM thinning and TSV reveal already require.

title: Fe/Cr/Fe exchange stack builds cobalt- and ruthenium-free MRAM
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying the original 1988 GMR system: use Fe/Cr/Fe RKKY coupling as the synthetic antiferromagnet in place of Co/Ru/Co, and an Fe(001)/MgO(001)/Fe coherent-tunneling junction with interface perpendicular anisotropy. Mn-N pinning and TiN seed layers replace Ta, W and Pt.

title: Magnesium-zinc-silicon oxide replaces IGZO in gain cells
idea: TRIZ #40 Composite materials, giving each IGZO job to an abundant cation: Zn 4s orbitals provide the conduction path (indium's role), Si binds oxygen strongly to suppress vacancies (gallium's role), and Mg widens the gap to ~4 eV for lower leakage. The amorphous Mg-Zn-Si-O channel is deposited by ALD supercycles.
note: Mg-Zn-Si-O by ALD supercycles is a plausible composite; stability and off-current unproven.

title: Dose-encoded single EUV exposure patterns two layers at once
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging: expose wordline trenches at full dose and contact openings at half dose in one EUV pass on a dual-threshold resist stack; develop and etch the high-dose features first, then trim the resist to uncover the half-dose features for a second etch that is self-aligned by construction.

title: Self-grown landing pads by selective epitaxial overgrowth
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: let exposed silicon active tips grow their own landing pads - after bitline spacers form, selective Si:P epitaxy with faceted lateral overgrowth fills each storage-node contact and mushrooms to pad size, stopping at the spacer walls, so no landing-pad lithography is needed.
note: Epi mushrooms cannot relocate pads to honeycomb capacitor grid; merge shorts risk.

title: Beforehand cushioning: reusable sacrificial test tier for known-good stacks
idea: TRIZ #11 Beforehand cushioning: after each bonding step, attach a reusable probe die with dense test circuits to the top of the partial stack, using micro-spring contacts and a low-temperature debondable adhesive. It tests every tier and TSV so bad partial stacks are reworked or dropped before more good dies go on, then it is lifted off and reused.
note: Reusable probe tier for partial stacks; micro-spring contact at fine pitch is risky.

title: Dynamics: beam-steered free-space optical links between chiplets
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics (make a fixed part adjustable): memory chiplets carry VCSEL arrays and compute chiplets carry photodiode arrays. A lid with a MEMS micromirror or liquid-crystal metasurface re-steers the beams, so any memory chiplet can be pointed at any compute tile for each workload phase.

title: Thin films: chip-on-film display lines make flexible memory ribbons
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells and thin films: reuse display-driver chip-on-film lines (~18 um pitch on polyimide) to make flexible memory ribbons. LPDDR dies on flex tape are bonded to the package edge and folded up around the cold plate, adding capacity in 3D without using board area. (No new fab: only existing trailing-node capacity.)
note: COF reuse for folded LPDDR; signal integrity and thermal routing on flex are the doubts.

title: Sense-amp resolution time as soft-decision reliability information
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way around: instead of waiting for bits to fail, each sense amp's latch time is compared with a delayed strobe; slow-resolving (low-margin) bits are flagged as soft erasures to the ECC decoder and queued for migration.

title: VRT provocation pulses expose flickering cells in minutes
idea: TRIZ #9 Prior counteraction: during wafer test on U.S.-made memory ATE, short high-field gate/junction toggle pulses force variable-retention-time traps to switch states repeatedly, so VRT cells reveal themselves in minutes instead of multi-day retention soaks and are mapped out.
note: Fast VRT screening; effectiveness unproven.

title: Skipping: open shared qualification lab cutting new-entrant DRAM qualification to months
idea: TRIZ #21 Rushing through: a neutral lab runs one public, JEDEC-plus qualification suite (retention, row hammer, burn-in, platform interop) whose results all major CPU/GPU vendors accept, so new suppliers skip 12-18 months of per-customer qualification.

title: Cheap substitute: panel-level DRAM on idle display-glass TFT lines
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap objects: replace costly silicon wafers with 5.5 m^2 Gen-8.5 glass panels from idle display fabs, using the standard oxide-TFT backplane flow plus one added mask for a high-k storage capacitor, to make bulk low-speed capacity-tier DRAM.

title: Tree-resin wound sealing: self-clearing electrodes isolate leaky defects
idea: Trees seal wounds with resin, and metallized-film capacitors 'self-clear' by vaporizing the electrode around a fault. Use an ultrathin 2-3 nm TiN/Al top-electrode skin that oxidizes locally into an insulator when a leakage hotspot's current density spikes during a burn-in pulse. This disconnects only the defective spot and leaves the rest of the capacitor intact.

title: Venus flytrap snap-buckling nanobeam with coincidence-only write
idea: The flytrap leaf is a prestressed shell that snaps between two curvatures. Make each bit a pre-compressed buckled nanobeam (200 nm SiC or AlScN) resting up or down, read by capacitance to a sense electrode. Snap-through needs the row and column electrodes energized together, because either half-voltage alone only bends the beam elastically, which gives crosspoint selection with no transistor.

title: Venus-flytrap analog charge integrator counts row activations
idea: The flytrap counts two touches within ~20 s with a decaying calcium level; give each row group a tiny leaky capacitor in its wordline driver that receives a fixed charge quantum per activation and decays with a ~ms constant, and fire a targeted neighbor refresh when it crosses threshold.

title: Gecko-setae dry transfer of wafer-scale WSe2 access channels
idea: Geckos stick and release with switchable van der Waals adhesion; grow wafer-scale bilayer WSe2 at high temperature on sapphire, pick it up with a gecko-like microfibrillar stamp whose adhesion switches with peel angle, and laminate it onto the BEOL memory layer at room temperature.

title: Octopus-arm local refresh brains in BEOL thin-film logic above mats
idea: Two-thirds of an octopus's neurons sit in its arms; build each mat's refresh controller (row counter, sentinel comparator, hammer integrator) from <=400 C oxide/2D thin-film transistors stacked directly above that mat rather than in the silicon periphery.

title: Glymphatic sleep-flush pulses empty charge traps in oxide access FETs
idea: The brain flushes waste during sleep; low-temperature gate dielectrics trap electrons under bias, shifting Vt and raising off-current over hours, so right after a row is restored during self-refresh the controller hits its wordline with a short deeper-negative pulse (~-1.5 V, ~100 ns) that detraps them, rotating through all rows.

title: Retinal center-surround sense amp referencing six averaged neighbour bitlines
idea: Like retinal horizontal cells that subtract the local mean, each sense amp compares its bitline against the capacitively averaged voltage of six unselected bitlines in the adjacent mat (a passive BEOL coupling-cap network switched in during sensing), so wordline coupling, plate bounce and substrate noise cancel as common mode. Averaging six references cuts reference noise by about 2.4x versus one.

title: Dendritic-tree row decoders in BEOL oxide transistors over the mats
idea: Dendrites compute at branch points, so build the row predecode/decode as a binary tree of 2-input coincidence (AND) gates made from IGZO or poly-Si TFTs in the BEOL directly above the cell mats. Pipelining hides TFT slowness. Only the final high-voltage wordline drivers stay in the silicon strip.

title: Integrate-and-fire latency-code sensing with one shared comparator per 16 bitlines
idea: Like a neuron's latency code, each bitline discharges into a 2-transistor integrate-and-fire node whose firing time encodes stored charge, and 16 bitlines share one arbitrated time-to-digital comparator. A one-transistor restore pull per bitline is driven from the decoded result.

title: Gap-junction wordline charge sharing between closing and opening rows
idea: Neurons joined by gap junctions pass charge directly. When one subarray's wordline (at VPP ~3 V) closes and another's opens, a pass switch first shorts the two, so about half the charge moves from the falling line to the rising one. The VPP pump then supplies only the remainder.

title: Kinetic-proofreading two-threshold sensing that heals marginal cells on access
idea: DNA polymerase rejects errors with an energy-spending delay (kinetic proofreading). The sense path samples each bitline against +delta then -delta references. Cells that resolve consistently restore normally. Cells inside the delta band get a boosted-VPP extended restore, and their address goes to a small weak-row table for faster refresh.

title: Ormia coupled-ear switched-capacitor lever doubling bitline differential
idea: The fly Ormia ochracea links its eardrums with a lever that magnifies tiny interaural differences.
