idea: Box: DRAM dielets with patterned NiFe pads x standard x standard x self-aligned direct bonding x substrate with matching micromagnets x dry vibratory assembly. Dielets scattered on the substrate are pulled into +/-0.5 um registration by magnetic forces and then bonded, with no liquid (unlike capillary or fluidic assembly).

title: Laser-debonded HBM reclaimed from retired accelerators and remounted
idea: Box: used HBM3 stacks x existing x existing x laser debond, laser solder-jet re-bump, remount on new carrier x reclaimed package x dry laser rework. Retired GPU modules have their HBM stacks lifted by IR laser heating, tested, re-balled with jetted solder spheres and reused on inference cards.
note: Damage-free debond and re-bump at microbump pitch is hard.

title: Discharge-slope telemetry from normal reads builds live retention map
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: time-to-digital sense amp | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: EUV]. Each sense amp records the picoseconds the bitline takes to cross a threshold, which encodes the cell's remaining charge; the controller turns these free samples from ordinary reads into a continuously updated per-row retention class and adapts each row's refresh period.

title: Analog leaky integrator capacitor counts hammers per row
idea: Box [medium: per-row MOS integrator capacitor | access: charge-packet injection on each ACT | sense: threshold comparator | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Every activation dumps a fixed charge packet onto a tiny per-row integrator that leaks with a time constant matched to the refresh window; crossing threshold triggers neighbour refresh, giving an exact per-row counter for about one cell's area.

title: Resonant adiabatic wordline drivers recycle charge and soften hammer edges
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: standard | integration: monolithic + in-package LC tank inductor | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Wordlines are swung by a shared resonant LC tank with a ~2 ns sinusoidal ramp, returning most wordline charge to the tank instead of dumping it, and the slower dV/dt cuts capacitive coupling and electron injection into neighbour rows.
note: Wordline energy is a minor part of activation energy; 2 ns LC resonance hard in package.

title: Golden-copy flash backing replaces ECC and refresh for weights
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: low-swing | integration: DRAM + NAND in one package | substrate: bulk | fab: existing]. Immutable inference weights live in a 0.4 V, ECC-less, refresh-relaxed DRAM region with a 16-bit CRC per 256 B; a CRC failure refetches that line from the packaged NAND golden copy and rewrites it.
note: 0.4 V array operation and 10x energy claim are doubtful.

title: Po: the bit is a shrug — sliding van der Waals ferroelectric
idea: Po: the bit is a shrug of the shoulders. Extracted: in bilayer hBN or rhombohedral MoS2 the bit is AB vs BA stacking; a field slides one layer by one bond length without breaking bonds, flipping polarization with almost no fatigue, read as a threshold shift of an underlying 2D channel.
note: Wafer-scale stacking control and small threshold shift are the risks.

title: Po: memory you read by listening — piezo-sensed AlScN ferroelectric bit
idea: Po: memory you read by listening to it. Extracted: store the bit in wurtzite AlScN polarization and read it non-destructively with a small sub-coercive AC drive; the sign of the piezoelectric response (charge or acoustic phase) reveals the polarization without ever switching it.

title: Per-cell threshold trimming via charge-trap layer in access gate
idea: Po: every access transistor is custom-made. Add a thin SiN charge-trap film inside the buried-wordline gate stack; at wafer test, cells in the leakage tail receive a one-time Fowler-Nordheim program pulse that raises their Vt ~150 mV, tightening the Vt distribution until the tail disappears.

title: Pulsed-hold thyristor array refreshed blindly without sense amplifiers
idea: Po: refresh without reading. Use vertical gated thyristor latches (no capacitor) but power their anode lines only in short pulses; between pulses an ON cell's base charge decays slowly, and each pulse re-latches every ON cell in the array at once while OFF cells stay off.

title: Read-restoring gain cell where every read tops up storage node
idea: Po: reading is refreshing. In a 2T capacitorless gain cell, add a diode-connected feedback from the read path so read current through a 1 cell briefly pulls its storage gate back toward full level, while a 0 cell draws no current and stays low; any row read regularly never needs a separate refresh.

title: Po: sense amps take turns — 1:8 charge-parked sensing
idea: Po: a bank with one-eighth of its sense amps. After activation, isolation gates park each bitline's charge-shared signal on the bitline itself; one SA serves 8 bitlines through a mux, sensing and writing back group by group in ~2 ns slots, with the requested column group always sensed first.
note: Parked ~100 mV signals must survive coupling from neighbors swinging full rail.

title: Po: wordlines count themselves — analog hammer integrator cell
idea: Po: a wordline that keeps its own tally. Each sub-wordline driver gets one extra DRAM-style cell coupled to its wordline through a tiny capacitor so every activation deposits a fixed charge quantum; when that integrator crosses a threshold during the row group's refresh, its neighbors are flagged for targeted refresh and the integrator is reset.
note: Analog per-row counter vs JEDEC PRAC; charge-quantum precision over ~1k steps is hard.

title: Po: no reference — read, write midlevel, read again
idea: Po: a sense amp with no reference. Charge-share the cell onto the bitline and hold the result on sample cap A, write VDD/2 into the cell, re-open the wordline and hold the second result on cap B, then compare A vs B; both samples traverse the identical path, so wordline kickback, bitline-pair imbalance and open-bitline layout mismatch cancel.

title: Po: bitlines never precharge — rail-held transition sensing
idea: Po: bitlines that never return to VDD/2. Each bitline stays at the full rail left by the last restore; on the next activation an AC-coupled detector sees either no step (new bit equals held rail) or a full charge-sharing step, and the latch, knowing the held rail, decodes 'same/different' into the new bit.
note: Needs a per-bitline reference tied to held rail; margin similar to single-ended.

title: Po: wordlines latch themselves — vertical Si thyristor drivers
idea: Po: a wordline driver that needs only a nudge. Replace each sub-wordline driver's high-voltage CMOS pair with a vertical p-n-p-n silicon thyristor at wordline pitch: a small decoder pulse triggers it, it regenerates and holds the wordline high through a shared weak bleed, and a common reset pulse turns all off.

title: Po: decoders woven into wiring — a-Si diode matrix
idea: Po: a decoder made of wire crossings. Build the row predecoder as a 1960s-style diode matrix, with hydrogenated amorphous-silicon p-i-n diodes deposited at the crossings of two BEOL aluminum levels above the array, so decoding uses metal-layer space instead of silicon area.

title: Po: gate from underneath — Hf-free back-gated FD-SOI periphery
idea: Po: transistors controlled from underneath. Build the periphery on thin-BOX FD-SOI with SiON front gates and TiN or doped-poly electrodes (no HfO2), using the back gate through the buried oxide for Vt control, and give each SA pair its own back-gate island biased to null its offset.
note: Per-SA FD-SOI back-gate islands for offset nulling; hafnium is not a real chokepoint.

title: Po: periphery made in a TV factory — LTPS glass chiplets
idea: Po: memory periphery from a display fab. Fabricate slow periphery (pumps, test, fuse/repair, ESD, power gating) as laser-crystallized poly-Si TFT circuits on Gen-6 glass panels, dice them into chiplets and bond them beside or under array dies.

title: Bonded nonvolatile shadow tier dumps idle banks before power-off
idea: Po: memory that sleeps with its eyes shut. Pair each DRAM tier with a hybrid-bonded thick-oxide charge-trap shadow tier sharing its vertical bitlines, so an idle bank copies out in parallel in ~10 us and is power-gated; dumps are rate-limited to one per bank per 5 minutes, so 1e6-cycle endurance lasts ~10 years.

title: Photoresist that stays: patternable oxide becomes the device layer
idea: Po: the resist is the product. Use hafnium/zirconium oxo-cluster photoresists that, after exposure and anneal, densify into HfZrO dielectric or hard mask left in place, eliminating the deposit-coat-expose-etch-strip chain for those layers.

title: Memory by the square meter in idle display-panel fabs
idea: Po: RAM is made in TV factories. Idle Gen-6/8.5 LCD/OLED backplane lines already run IGZO transistors; pattern 2T0C oxide gain-cell arrays at ~1-1.5 um rules on glass (a ~5.5 m2 Gen-8.5 panel holds on the order of 20 GB), dice into tiles and bond them to 28 nm controller dies.

title: Laser-written waveguides inside glass interposers link HBM optically
idea: Po: wires are written, not printed. Femtosecond lasers write buried 3D waveguides inside a glass interposer that connect edge-coupled micro-ring transmitters on the HBM base die to the GPU, routing hundreds of WDM channels in 3D with zero lithography.

title: Power fed from the lid into the top of HBM stacks
idea: Po: power falls from the sky. One backside mask adds power landing pads on the top die of each stack; a copper lid with compliant pins injects current into the top of the existing power TSV columns, so power enters from both ends.

title: Stress-metal microsprings for socketed, re-testable HBM
idea: Po: the bumps are springs. A single mask patterns stress-graded MoCr fingers on the DRAM pad field; a release etch lets them curl up into microsprings that press-contact the interposer, so stacks can be tested at speed and swapped before final lock-down.

title: Sacrificial shorting bar removes ESD circuits from bonded links
idea: Po: memory with no protection. One top-metal mask adds a shorting bar that grounds every die-to-die pad during handling and bonding, then is laser-cut after assembly, so the I/O needs no ESD diodes.
note: LCD shorting-bar trick; bar is buried after hybrid bonding, so needs electrical fuse.

title: Self-assembled block-copolymer capacitor holes replace EUV layers
idea: Po: chips grown, not made. Capacitor hole arrays are patterned by directed self-assembly of a cylinder-forming block copolymer guided by a coarse DUV template; DSA's ~0.1-1% missing or merged holes, which kept it out of production, become dead cells that the code treats as erasures.
note: DSA for DRAM holes is known; 0.1-1% erasures need heavy code overhead.

title: Tiny unbalanced sense amps with offsets mapped as erasures
idea: Po: the sense amp is allowed to guess. Sense amplifiers are shrunk to minimum-size devices with no offset cancellation; the ~1% whose static offset exceeds the bitline signal are found at test and their columns treated by the decoder as known-position erasures.
note: Offsets drift with temperature and aging, so a static map is incomplete.

title: Dirty-silicon DRAM grown in non-Spruce-Pine crucibles
idea: Po: memory made from dirty sand. Wafers come from ingots grown in synthetic-silica or lower-purity quartz crucibles, accepting more oxygen and trace metals; the extra generation-recombination centers fatten the junction-leakage tail to ~1% retention failures, which the code tolerates.
note: Synthetic-silica crucible layers already used; leakage-tail cost.

title: Cross-tenant memory exchange points in colocation campuses
idea: Po: memory is a utility traded between strangers. Like an Internet exchange point, a neutral CXL 3.x switch fabric in each colo lets tenants post idle DRAM and others lease it by the GB-hour, with per-lease memory-encryption keys and bandwidth QoS enforced in the switch.

title: Move DRAM burn-in from the factory into the server
idea: Po: never test a chip in the factory. Factory test shrinks to wafer sort plus a fast package screen, and the long retention/burn-in screens run in the customer's server at first boot via on-die MBIST and post-package repair, with anonymized telemetry streamed back to the fab.
note: Customers bear escapes; partial in-field MBIST/PPR already exists.

title: Repurpose LTPS display backplanes as giant 1T1C memory sheets
idea: Worsen: make memory only on 300 mm silicon at ~$10/cm2. Flip: an AMOLED backplane is already a 1T1C array, so re-mask an existing LTPS display line (3 um cells, storage caps, access TFTs) into memory sheets; $1M buys a re-spun driver IC and a 24-month cost-per-bit study for cold bulk-capacity tiers.
note: 3 um cells are ~5000x less dense than DRAM; LTPS leakage high; cost per bit unlikely below DRAM.

title: Decay-clock sensing: reference voltage tracks time since last restore
idea: Worse: assume worst-case decayed charge on every read so the margin is gone early. Flip: keep a coarse per-row refresh-epoch counter and set the sense-amp reference from a replica cell aged the same amount, so a stored '1' can decay to ~30% instead of ~60% before misreading.
note: Reference tracks average decay; fast-decaying tail cells still fail.

title: Aerogel thermal-break trench between accelerator and HBM
idea: Worse: bolt the DRAM onto the hottest chip in the system. Flip: cut a silica-aerogel-filled trench in the interposer between GPU and HBM footprints and give HBM its own top heat-pipe path, holding the stack 20-25 C cooler than the logic die.

title: Built-in electret charge in gate stack replaces negative wordline
idea: Worse: run a negative-wordline charge pump all through standby to hold Vt up. Flip: embed a fixed negative charge layer (Al2O3/SiO2 interface dipole or implanted electret) on the storage-node side of the access gate so the device carries a built-in +Vt shift only where leakage matters.
note: Gate-stack dipole/electret near storage node; similar to dual-WF buried gates.

title: Ultra-thin fully depleted body shrinks thermal generation volume
idea: Worse at 125 C: give the access device a large depleted silicon volume that generates carriers at mid-gap traps. Flip: thin the vertical channel to a 4-5 nm shell on an oxide core so the generating volume is ~50x smaller and quantum confinement widens the effective gap.

title: Reduced-field storage levels when hot: low '1', raised plate
idea: Worse at 125 C: store '1' at full array voltage so field-enhanced generation and GIDL explode with heat. Flip: in hot mode store '1' at ~0.7 V and raise the cell plate to cut junction field, then recover signal with an offset-cancelled sense amp; leakage falls exponentially while charge falls only linearly.

title: Near-miss flagging sense amps drive traffic-based adaptive refresh
idea: Worse: refresh every row at worst-case 64 ms because nobody knows which cells are weak. Flip: add a cheap offset-biased secondary latch per sense-amp group that flags reads whose signal landed near the trip point during normal traffic; flagged rows enter a small refresh-priority table while all other rows run 4-8x longer refresh intervals.

title: Resonant LC tank charges wordlines adiabatically and recycles energy
idea: Worse: slam 3 V wordlines up from ground and dump their charge to ground on every activation. Flip: drive the selected wordline group from a package-level inductor in a resonant loop that ramps it up sinusoidally and swings the charge back into the tank, or into the next wordline, on deactivation.

title: Isolated early-latch sensing with parity-checked deferred restore
idea: Worse: wait for every bitline to fully develop under worst-case corners before latching. Flip: latch at half the usual development time with isolation gates cutting the latch off from the bitlines, ship data out, and write back only after a per-burst parity check passes; on a rare mismatch the still-intact shared bitline charge is re-latched with more time.

title: Per-segment adaptive negative wordline bias tames the leakage tail
idea: Worse: hold every unselected wordline at the same off level so the leakiest 0.01% of cells set refresh for all. Flip: give each wordline segment a test-programmed negative off level (-0.2 to -0.4 V) from a small local bias generator, applying deep negative bias only where the tail lives.
note: Deeper NWL can worsen GIDL, which drives part of the leakage tail.

title: Threshold-coded tier select replaces the staircase
idea: Worse: carve a giant staircase so every tier gets its own contact, with area and trim steps growing linearly with tier count. Flip: dope each tier's built-in select transistor to one of several thresholds during in-situ deposition and drive a few shared vertical select gates with a voltage code that turns on exactly one tier, i.e., a binary decoder embedded in the stack.

title: Memory on the cold side: thermal-break 3D DRAM beneath logic
idea: Worse: stack DRAM directly on a 700 W accelerator so it bakes at 95 C and refreshes 4x more often. Flip: hybrid-bond the DRAM tiers to the logic through a low-thermal-conductivity bonding interlayer that only signal vias cross, and cool the DRAM from its own backside cold plate while logic heat exits the opposite face.
note: Double-sided cooling with thermal break is plausible; vias and thin interlayers leak heat.

title: Floating-plate differential capacitor shared by two stacked cells
idea: Worse: give each cell its own plate electrode, plate contacts and a single-ended half-signal. Flip: place one capacitor dielectric directly between a storage node in tier k and a storage node in tier k+1 so the two access transistors write complementary charge across it, storing one bit differentially with no plate line at all.

title: Ge-fraction-coded superlattice: chemistry, not overlay, cuts every cell part
idea: Worse: align each tier's transistor, gate and capacitor regions with separate masks whose overlay drifts tier by tier. Flip: grow all tiers in one epitaxy run with sublayers of different Ge fraction, then from a single vertical slit run composition-selective lateral etches whose recess depth scales with Ge content, so capacitor cavity, gate recess and spacer of every tier are cut in a few etches, self-aligned by chemistry.

title: Long lateral capacitors storing two bits per cell
idea: Worse: hold to 1 bit/cell because 5 fF barely yields one clean sense level. Flip: exploit the fact that a 3D lateral capacitor's length is set by a cheap timed recess, make ~20 fF capacitors whose 4x signal supports 4-level (2-bit) storage, and read them with a successive-approximation charge-sharing sense amp under the array.

title: Contactless whole-wafer self-test keeps test cost flat at 10x bits
idea: Worse: probe-test 10x more bits per die serially so test time and probe-card capex scale 10x. Flip: power every die on the wafer inductively or through on-die photovoltaic pads, run built-in self-test of all tiers in parallel, read pass/fail maps through an optical or RF backchannel, and program tier and row spares in the same pass.

title: Separable-liner quartz crucibles recycled into new inner layers
idea: Worsen: break and landfill every CZ crucible after one pull. Flip: design crucibles with a separable high-purity inner liner, then crush spent liners, strip the devitrified cristobalite and metal-rich skin by hot chlorination and HF leach, and re-fuse the purified grain into new liners.

title: PCB-free all-silicon memory module as a two-material recycling stream
idea: Worsen: mount DRAM on brominated FR-4 boards full of glass fiber, copper and gold that are costly to separate. Flip: build memory modules on a silicon or glass-core interposer card with only Cu and Al metallization, so the whole module is a two-material recycling stream and the chips can be re-bonded.

title: CVD diamond substrates remove the thermal ceiling on stacking
idea: Worse: stack memory on a substrate that traps heat, so retention collapses and refresh doubles above 85 C. Flip: build tiers on thin polycrystalline CVD diamond plates (~1500 W/mK) that hold stacked arrays near coolant temperature. Leakage roughly halves for each ~10 C of cooling, so stacks of 16-24 tiers stay viable.

title: Hardware page meshing merges half-empty pages
idea: Worsen: let fragmentation leave thousands of pages 10-30% full. Flip: the controller adds a sub-page remap table so two virtual pages whose live objects do not overlap share one physical frame, and a background engine finds mesh candidates from allocation bitmaps without moving objects.
note: Hardware version of Mesh allocator.

title: Reduce-on-the-wire: interposer repeaters sum partial results in flight
idea: Worsen: write every partial sum to memory and read it back at each all-reduce step. Flip: put small adder-repeaters at segment boundaries of long active-bridge wires so gradients and partial dot products accumulate as they travel between chiplets, and only the final sum is written to memory.

title: Display fabs build IGZO gain-cell memory into glass interposers
idea: Worsen: allow only memory fabs with 75:1 capacitor etch to make working memory. Flip: Gen-8.5 display fabs already pattern billions of IGZO TFTs on 2.2x2.5 m glass, so build 3T gain cells (charge held on a read transistor's gate, no capacitor) in the glass interposer's layers, turning the substrate under the chips into seconds-retention memory.

title: Optically bistable microrings buffer packets inside photonic interposers
idea: Worsen: convert every optical packet to electrons and park it in DRAM for microseconds. Flip: use carrier- or thermo-optically bistable silicon microrings, where a holding beam keeps each ring in one of two transmission states, as nanosecond photonic latches that buffer packets in the optical domain.
note: Tiny capacity and holding-beam power limit it to switch buffers.

title: Ephemeral DRAM: refresh-free SKU for data that dies young
idea: Worse: refresh every bit, even KV caches and packet buffers the host rewrites every few ms. Flip: sell a die variant with refresh counters, refresh timing and refresh-based row-hammer logic removed, warranted only for data rewritten within the measured retention window, for activations, network and frame buffers.
note: Retention tail over temperature and dropping row-hammer defenses are risks.

title: Mongolian yurt: dry-peeled single-crystal BaTiO3 membranes, reusable substrate
idea: A herder carries a yurt in pieces and pitches it anywhere, dry. Grow single-crystal BaTiO3 on graphene-coated substrates by remote epitaxy, peel the membrane off mechanically with a dry stamp, and laminate it onto CMOS as the storage layer; the substrate is reused hundreds of times.
note: Membrane lamination cannot coat 3D structures; mainly a water and fatigue improvement.

title: Colorado River water lawyer: liters-per-gigabit permits for memory cells
idea: A water-rights lawyer prices every acre-foot. Make CHIPS-type grants and state water permits conditional on a certified 'liters of UPW per gigabit' figure for the storage-cell module, with a bonus tier for a 10x reduction, so that dry cell technologies win the funding.
note: Water use is fab-level, not cell-level; pull for dry cells is indirect.

title: Child's take-turns sense amp: one latch scans eight bitlines
idea: A child asks why every bitline needs its own teacher. After charge sharing, isolation switches freeze each bitline's signal on its own bitline capacitance (it survives tens of ns), and one offset-cancelled latch visits 8 bitlines in ~1 ns steps, sensing and writing each back to full level in turn.

title: Retina lateral inhibition between neighboring sense amplifiers
idea: Copying the retina's horizontal cells, each sense amp gets weak cross-coupled 'inhibition' transistors to its two neighbors, so a disturbance common to the region (wordline kick, plate bounce, aggressor-bitline coupling) is subtracted before latching while the true local difference survives.

title: Rod-cell cascade: vertical bipolar preamp at every bitline segment
idea: A rod cell turns one photon into a million-fold cascade from a tiny first stage. Build a vertical n-p-n transistor under each short bitline segment, with the segment driving its floating base, so a few-fC cell dump becomes a 10-30x larger collector current onto a global sense line before any MOS latch.

title: 2050 trim: ferroelectric offset memory inside every sense amp
idea: A 2050 engineer would never accept factory-random mismatch. Insert a ~30 nm HZO capacitor at each SA latch node, programmed once at wafer test to a polarization that cancels that SA's measured offset and retained for years.

title: Embargoed engineer's tungsten-free wordline: doped epitaxial gate tiers
idea: Without Chinese tungsten, the embargoed engineer grows the wordline in the same epi run as the channel. A degenerately boron-doped SiGe layer in each tier is the gate, wordlines are segmented every 512 cells and strapped to copper at each segment end.

title: Nose-to-tail butcher saves the silicon ground off HBM wafers
idea: Persona: a nose-to-tail butcher who wastes nothing. HBM core dies are thinned from 775 um to ~40 um, which grinds ~95% of each prime wafer into slurry. Instead, while the wafer sits on its carrier, focus an IR laser 60 um below the devices to make a cleave plane (stealth slicing). Split off the ~700 um back slab and polish it for reuse as a test or prime wafer.
note: Laser slicing Si under live devices; silicon value small vs wafer.

title: Frugal homesteader: implant-free junctionless fab with no furnaces
idea: A homesteader without tractors designs around the missing tool. Make every transistor in the memory tiers junctionless or Schottky-contacted (as-deposited doped oxide or poly channels thinned for off-state, metal-silicide contacts), so no dopant-activation anneal is ever needed and the fab owns no ion implanters, diffusion furnaces or RTP.
note: Sense amps need high-performance CMOS; oxide channels lack good p-type.

title: Bridge engineer's expansion joints: islands-and-meanders segmented interposer
idea: Long bridges need expansion joints: split a large interposer into rigid silicon islands, one per memory stack and logic die, joined by meandering copper-on-glass bridges that flex, so warpage and CTE stress stay small.
note: Flexible meander bridges lose wiring density; CoWoS-L already segments.

title: Alien coder's view: soft-decision LDPC fed by 3-bit sense amps
idea: An alien who sees DRAM only as a noisy channel would never throw away analog information: keep the latch sense amp but add 7 shared flash comparators per 8 columns that grade each bit's margin into log-likelihood ratios, and decode 512-byte pages with an on-die soft-decision LDPC that tolerates a raw BER of ~1e-3.
note: LDPC decode latency on 512 B pages conflicts with DRAM access time.

title: Navigator's dead reckoning: sense reference shifted by time-since-refresh
idea: A navigator estimates position from elapsed time and speed: the controller knows each row's time since last refresh and the temperature, and before sensing it shifts the bitline precharge or reference-cell level by the expected decay, so a sagging '1' still resolves correctly.
note: Reference tracking elapsed decay helps one polarity; tail cells decay unpredictably.

title: Farmer overplants then thins: printed spare columns plus printed WORM map
idea: A farmer sows extra seed and then thins it: gravure- or inkjet-printed oxide-TFT gain-cell arrays on foil carry ~40% spare columns; an in-line probe on the web tests each tile and writes its bad-column map into a printed write-once (electrochemical-fuse) ROM on the same foil, which the attached CMOS controller reads at boot.

title: Soviet scrapyard: transfer-print good tile dielets from defective DRAM wafers
idea: A Soviet engineer under embargo salvages everything: DRAM dies are laid out as mosaics of ~1 mm2 tiles, each with local periphery and scribe lanes; wafers with clustered defects are thinned and diced into tiles, and only known-good tiles are mass transfer-printed with elastomer stamps onto a roll-to-roll-made polyimide interposer with printed redistribution and a small CMOS controller.
note: Yield gain only on defect-clustered lots; transfer-print interconnect cost.

title: Child writes bigger where paper is rough: quality-adaptive bits per cell
idea: A child writes bigger on bumpy paper: the controller reads a per-region print-quality map (device sigma, leakage) for a printed memory foil and configures each region for 2 bits/cell where devices are tight, 1 bit/cell where they are average, and one bit across two ganged cells where they are poor, exposing whatever capacity results.

title: Artist's new canvas: DRAM-class gain cells on display-fab glass
idea: An artist sees the world's underused Gen-8.5 display fabs as huge, cheap canvases. Pattern IGZO 2T0C gain-cell arrays at 1-2 um rules on 2.2 x 2.5 m glass, dice the glass into tiles and stack them as low-cost capacity modules for warm data.
note: Same LCD-fab IGZO gain-cell panels as I-04100.

title: Venus-grade NEMS relay access gives charge node zero off-current
idea: Designed for 460C Venus landers where any junction leaks, the access transistor is replaced by a SiC/TiN nanoelectromechanical contact relay whose open vacuum gap passes literally zero current. The storage node becomes a small MIM or the gate of a read transistor and holds charge for hours to days at room temperature.
note: Relay area and contact endurance toward 1e15 are the limits.

title: Polarization-bound GaN quantum-well charge storage for 200C downhole tools
idea: Oil-well logging tools need memory at 200C; an AlN/GaN/AlN double heterostructure forms a 2DEG well bounded by 6.2 eV AlN barriers and fixed polarization charge, so an injected electron sheet barely emits thermally. The stored sheet modulates an adjacent HEMT channel for non-destructive read, built in existing U.S. 200 mm GaN-on-Si power fabs.

title: Deep-level dopant pocket memory from cryogenic dopant freeze-out
idea: Quantum-computer controllers at 4-40 K watch shallow dopants freeze out and hold their charge state for hours; the room-temperature analog implants, with one mask, a pocket of deep-level dopants (S, Se or Zn in Si, 0.3-0.6 eV) under the access device so captured electrons take milliseconds to minutes to re-emit. Pocket occupancy shifts the device threshold as the stored bit.
note: Few traps per nanoscale device give large threshold variability; emission-time spread is the risk.

title: Silicon-on-nothing vacuum-isolated membrane holds charge at 300C
idea: For hot users such as Venus probes and jet-engine controllers, one trench-array mask followed by a hydrogen anneal migrates silicon to seal an empty cavity under a thin Si membrane (empty-space-in-silicon process); the membrane is the storage body, isolated below by vacuum instead of junctions. Charge in the membrane modulates the overlying channel.
note: Niche high-temperature market; vacuum-isolated membrane body is plausible.

title: Photodiode storage node written by co-packaged laser light
idea: Laser-crosslink satellites receive data as light, so one implant mask turns storage nodes into Si photodiode junctions under a transparent plate; rows are precharged to '1' and a modulated micro-LED/VCSEL array discharges the '0' cells optically in parallel, while reads stay electrical. Write drivers and write bitline swings largely disappear.

title: Leaky-integrator analog counters catch row hammering at activation rate
idea: Design for the extreme user, the attacker: each activation dumps a fixed charge packet onto that row's ~2 fF integrating capacitor in the SWD stripe, which self-leaks with a ~64 ms time constant; a shared comparator checks it on every activation and triggers neighbor refresh past threshold. An analog rate detector replaces SRAM counter tables.

title: Ring-oscillator time-domain sensing at 0.4 V array voltage
idea: Energy-harvesting IoT tags have no voltage headroom, so they sense in time: the bitline voltage starves a tiny ring oscillator per column group, and a counter compares its edge count over a fixed window against a reference column. It works at VARY ~0.4 V, where latch SAs fail.

title: Sense amps chain into a shift register for streaming readout
idea: AI KV-caches read whole rows in order, so in streaming mode the SA latches daisy-chain into a shift register clocked out at the mat edge, bypassing column select lines and the column decoder; random access keeps only a coarse 8-way select.

title: Sample-and-hold capacitors let one sense amp serve eight bitlines
idea: Neural implants and image sensors time-share one converter across many columns; each bitline's post-charge-share voltage is captured on a BEOL MIM sample capacitor above the array, one SA resolves the eight samples in sequence, and a compact per-bitline write-back driver restores each cell.

title: 4 K cryo-DRAM with single-electron-transistor sensing for qubit controllers
idea: Quantum computers need working memory inside the cryostat: at 4 K leakage is zero and single-electron transistors are practical electrometers, so cells store ~20-50 electrons and an SET coupled to each storage node reads them. Lessons on charge-limit sensing feed room-temperature small-island designs.

title: 8K-TV display fabs build slow periphery as IGZO TFTs on glass
idea: With no EUV available, move every non-speed-critical periphery block (fuse banks, repair maps, test logic, refresh counters, power switches) onto an IGZO TFT glass interposer made in depreciated Gen-8.5 display fabs at 1.5-3 um i-line litho, as 8K panels already drive 2 m lines. The silicon die keeps only cells, SAs and fast decoders.

title: Cool instead of shrink: 77 K lets DUV periphery match EUV
idea: Cryogenic computing users show mobility rises ~2x and leakage vanishes at 77 K; a DRAM whose periphery is built on a DUV-only 28 nm-class process and runs in LN2 pods matches the speed and standby power of an EUV-node room-temperature die.

title: Excimer-laser LTPS decoders built monolithically above the cell array
idea: Smartphone OLED backplanes make ~100 cm2/Vs LTPS TFTs by excimer-laser annealing; a laser-crystallized poly-Si layer above the bitlines hosts row decoders and SWD logic at DUV rules, moving them out of the silicon area beside the array.

title: Qubit-control superconducting wordlines shrink sub-wordline driver strips
idea: Control memory for 4 K quantum computers can use NbTiN wordlines with no resistive RC, so one sub-wordline driver can span 8x more cells; at 77 K the same floorplan uses copper or YBCO-strapped wordlines whose resistivity drops 5-7x. Re-floorplan the mats with 4-8x longer wordline segments so the driver strips that tile the array shrink proportionally.

title: HFT dual-port cell: capacitor sandwiched between two vertical transistors
idea: High-frequency traders cannot tolerate refresh stalls; build a vertical cell whose capacitor sits between a bottom access transistor on bitline A, owned by a refresh/scrub engine, and a top access transistor on bitline B, owned by the host. Stacking makes the second port free in footprint, so refresh, row-hammer mitigation and ECC scrub run on port A while port B serves traffic.

title: Spin-qubit plasma-free fab: vapor-HCl carved lateral cells in Si/SiGe
idea: Silicon spin-qubit fabs avoid plasma damage; grow 3D DRAM tiers as an epitaxial Si/SiGe superlattice in H2 carrier, open vertical slits by metal-assisted wet etch, then remove the SiGe selectively with gas-phase HCl to open lateral cavities where gate and capacitor stacks are deposited by ALD. No plasma ever touches the channel.
note: Vapor HCl SiGe removal is standard; plasma damage is a minor share of leakage tail.

title: HBM stacks peel off backside silicon instead of grinding it away
idea: HBM dies are thinned from 775 um to ~30-50 um, which grinds ~95% of every wafer into sludge. A laser-written subsurface damage plane plus polymer-stress cold split, as already used on SiC boules, cleaves off a ~700 um slab that is repolished and reused as monitor, test or epi-base wafers.

title: Tailings-reprocessing mindset: cold-trap and refluorinate escaped WF6
idea: Miners now reprocess old tailings for the metal left in them, and CVD-W tools likewise send most of their WF6 to the exhaust. Put a cryogenic/sorbent trap ahead of abatement to catch WF6 and WOxFy, then refluorinate the captured material with on-site F2 back into WF6 feedstock.

title: Repurpose overbuilt US SiC power fabs for refresh-free SiC DRAM
idea: Extreme user: 200C automotive and downhole electronics. 4H-SiC's 3.2 eV bandgap gives ~10^-20 A off-current, so a small planar capacitor retains for hours; build relaxed-density refresh-free memory for industrial/auto on the 150-200 mm SiC lines now underused as EV demand slowed.

title: Carbon-mold capacitors etched with oxygen and released by dry ashing
idea: Extreme user: a closed-habitat Mars fab where HF and fluorocarbons cannot be scrubbed. Etch capacitor holes in amorphous carbon with O2/N2/COS plasma through an Al2O3 hardmask (BCl3-patterned), fill with TiCl4-based TiN and ZrO2 by ALD, then remove the mold by O2 ashing instead of an HF dip-out.

title: Certified PFAS-free 'clean silicon' DRAM earns EU and defense premiums
idea: Extreme user: EU buyers and 30-year industrial programs facing PFAS restrictions. Create an audited PFAS-free DRAM certification tied to CHIPS-style incentives and procurement preferences, so a fluorine-free U.S. line earns price premiums and guaranteed volume.

title: Rover-hot DRAM: self-expiring banks for data that dies fast
idea: From rover electronics that run hot on tight power: let DRAM run at 95-105 C where retention falls to a few milliseconds, and allocate short-lived data (activations, streaming KV, packet buffers) into refresh-disabled self-expiring banks whose lifetime contract the compiler guarantees; only long-lived state sits in a small refreshed bank.
note: Hot-running dry cooling plus compiler lifetime contracts; ms retention at 105C makes guarantees fragile.

title: EV-pack style series voltage stacking of HBM dies
idea: EV battery packs put cells in series to cut current. Wire the 12-16 dies of a memory stack as four series voltage domains (e.g., 4.4 V across four 1.1 V groups), with on-die switched-capacitor balancers absorbing activity mismatch, so the stack draws a quarter of the current.

title: Aircraft wireless-avionics bus inside the package cavity
idea: Airliners adopt wireless avionics intra-communication to delete harness weight. Give each chiplet a 300 GHz on-die antenna radiating into the metal-lidded package cavity, which acts as a shared multimode waveguide; frequency channels replace interposer traces, so memory chiplets can sit anywhere on a cheap organic substrate.

title: RFID backscatter reads: memory reflects bits instead of driving them
idea: Batteryless RFID tags talk by toggling their antenna load to reflect the reader's carrier. The host drives a continuous carrier onto each read lane; the memory base die returns data by switching a tiny termination impedance between reflect and absorb, and the host's coherent receiver demodulates.

title: Downhole elastic ECC: parity grows as the die heats
idea: Downhole tools at 200 C trade capacity for survival. Tie on-die ECC strength to a junction-temperature sensor: rows step from a (136,128) SEC code to (144,128) DEC to (160,128) as temperature rises. The extra parity comes from a reserved top-of-memory region that the OS gives up through a memory-balloon driver; when the die is cool, that reserve is usable capacity.

title: Miner-style undervolting: per-bank array voltage servoed by live ECC counts
idea: Crypto miners undervolt memory until errors just begin to appear. Give each bank its own array-voltage regulator and a closed loop that lowers VARY in 10 mV steps while that bank's on-die ECC corrected-error rate stays under budget, and backs off immediately on a burst. Banks with strong cells may settle near 0.8 V instead of ~1.05 V.

title: Microring resonance reads capacitor charge nondestructively
idea: Scale shift into photonics: the storage node is a pn junction embedded in a silicon microring; stored charge shifts the ring resonance by plasma dispersion, so a WDM probe beam reads hundreds of bits per waveguide without discharging them.
note: Plasma-dispersion shift from a leaky pn node; ring size kills density.

title: Majority-value bitline parking during long idle
idea: Time shift from ns-scale active behaviour to seconds-long standby: when a subarray idles >1 ms, a per-subarray ones-counter (updated on writes) decides whether most cells hold '1' or '0' and bitlines are parked at VARY or ground instead of VARY/2, so the majority of cells see ~0 V drain-source and stop subthreshold leaking; minority cells get a shorter refresh bin.

title: Compress years of VRT behaviour into minutes at wafer sort
idea: Time shift: accelerate rare variable-retention-time toggling (dwell times of hours at 85 C) with a sort step combining 150 C, cyclic bias-temperature stress on wordlines and a hydrogen-rich ambient, so metastable traps toggle many times within minutes; cells seen toggling are fused out or binned.

title: Solar-cell field-effect passivation transplanted onto storage-node sidewalls
idea: Scale jump from square-metre solar cells to 15 nm cell pillars: line the isolation sidewalls where the storage junction's depletion region meets the surface with ALD Al2O3 carrying ~-5e12 cm^-2 fixed charge (the PERC passivation trick), keeping the p-well surface accumulated so surface SRH generation, a major junction-leakage source, shuts off.
note: PERC Al2O3 negative charge on sidewalls; tail mostly GIDL/TAT, not surface SRH.

title: Silicon-on-nothing: each storage junction floats over a sealed void
idea: Scale shift from MEMS cavities to the single cell: use the silicon-only empty-space-in-silicon process (trench array plus high-temperature H2 anneal so Si surface-migrates into a sealed buried void) to put a vacuum void directly under each storage-node junction, removing bottom junction area and blocking substrate minority-carrier diffusion.
note: SON known (ST); per-cell voids at DRAM pitch challenging.

title: Silicon feedback-FET access switch borrows thyristor latch physics
idea: Scale jump from kilovolt power thyristors to a 15 nm vertical gated p-i-n: charge held in spacer-adjacent potential barriers creates positive feedback so the device turns on at <5 mV/decade, letting a 1 V wordline swing span ~10 decades between on and off current instead of ~6-7.

title: Factory-injected nitride charge trims Vt of only the leakiest cells
idea: Time shift from ns operation to decade-long stored charge: the access transistor's spacer liner includes a SiN trap layer, and at wafer test cells found in the leakage tail receive a one-time high-field injection via their wordline/bitline that permanently stores electrons, raising their Vt ~150-250 mV for the product's 10-year life.

title: Kerf-line test periphery that dies at dicing
idea: Time-scale mismatch exploited: BIST engines, fuse programmers and test muxes are used for hours but occupy die area for years, so build them in the 60-80 um scribe streets, wired across a gapped seal ring at a low metal level, and let dicing destroy them (seal closed by post-dice passivation).
note: Post-package repair and field BIST still need on-die logic; gapped seal ring is a reliability risk.

title: Decay-twin reference cells make sense thresholds age with data
idea: Time-shift the sense reference: each 64-cell segment carries a '1' twin and a '0' twin written at the same moment as the data, and the SA compares data cells against the twins' decayed midpoint, so the threshold follows real leakage and temperature and rows stay readable after ~80% charge loss. The refresh engine is deleted; the mats serve paused-session KV cache and stashed tensors idle 1-60 s.
note: Cell leakage spread is log-normal, so twin cells do not represent their neighbors.

title: Leakier canary cells invalidate rows of a clean DRAM cache
idea: Time-shift retention into a cache lifetime: each row has a deliberately leakier canary cell (narrower storage node, ~5x faster decay), DRAM serves only as a clean cache over flash or NV holding inference weights, and when a read finds the canary drained the row is treated as a miss and refetched, never refreshed.
note: The canary must decay faster than the row's VRT tail cells, or corruption goes undetected.

title: FD-SOI back-biased hold mode for idle mats
idea: Time jump between ns access mode and minute-scale hold mode: access transistors sit on fully depleted SOI, so there is no storage-junction leakage to substrate, and the periphery switches an idle mat's buried back plane to -2 V (a held voltage, no current), suppressing subthreshold leakage ~10^3-10^4 so data idle for minutes survives with no refresh.
note: GIDL and dielectric leakage remain under negative back bias.

title: Stacked SIMOX: multi-energy oxygen implants build tiered crystalline silicon
idea: Use ion range as a depth ruler: implant oxygen at two to four energies with 1990s high-current implanters and anneal, forming multiple buried oxide layers and so several single-crystal silicon tiers inside one bulk wafer with no epitaxy or bonding. Each tier hosts lateral access transistors.
note: Multi-energy SIMOX gives only 2-4 thin tiers with degraded crystal between BOXes.

title: Short-mean-free-path NiAl intermetallic buried wordlines replace tungsten
idea: Scale jump from bulk metal to the 10 nm wire: at buried-wordline widths, resistivity depends on the electron mean free path more than on the bulk value. B2 intermetallics such as NiAl or CoAl (mean free path ~5 nm vs ~16 nm for W) therefore match or beat W. Deposit Ni/Al ALD nanolaminates into the recessed trench, anneal them to the ordered B2 phase, and use a thin AlN liner instead of a TiN barrier.

title: Accept 16 ms retention to delete recessed-channel process steps
idea: Time-shift the refresh interval from 64 ms to 16 ms and let a smart controller absorb the extra refreshes on a capacity-tier product; the looser leakage target lets a shallow-recess planar access transistor replace the buried saddle-fin, deleting the recess etch, halo implants and their masks.
note: Recess exists for short-channel control, not only retention tail.

title: Slow long-bitline capacity die with only two metal layers
idea: Make a second DRAM product with 1024 cells per bitline (vs ~512) and two metal layers, accepting ~50 ns access and using a low-capacitance air-gap bitline to keep sense margin; the higher cell-to-sense-amp ratio halves sense-amp count.

title: Content-addressed CXL switch acting as a rack memory CDN
idea: NICs hash cold 4 KB pages with BLAKE3 and publish them to a CXL switch that keeps a hash-to-physical map in on-switch SRAM. Identical pages from every server in the rack (container layers, libraries, zero pages, model shards, JIT code) collapse into one read-only copy in pooled memory, which every host maps.
note: Cross-host dedup in switch; SRAM map size and latency are the doubts.

title: Predictive-coding memory storing only residuals of a tiny predictor
idea: A small fixed predictor (linear or tiny neural) in the memory controller predicts each 64 B line from its neighbors and a per-page context on every access. DRAM stores only the entropy-coded residuals. This is the brain's and video codecs' predictive coding, run at the nanosecond scale.
note: Predicting from neighbor lines needs extra accesses; gain over BDI/FPC-style compression modest.

title: Ceiling MEMS free-space optics re-wire stranded rack DRAM per job phase
idea: Treat the datacenter ceiling as a memory backplane: MEMS steering mirrors link any compute sled to any memory sled with free-space optical beams, re-pointed in ~10 ms at job-phase boundaries that last seconds to minutes. DRAM stranded behind an idle CPU is lent to the busy GPU one row over.
note: Free-space datacenter optics and memory pooling are both studied.

title: Ship untested wafers: skip hours-long retention test and burn-in
idea: Shift testing from the fab's hours-long retention screens and burn-in ovens to the field's nanosecond decoder: wafers go from light probe straight to bonding, and the base die learns per-row error statistics online.

title: Row-buffer-wide long code computed over the full 8KB page
idea: Scale jump (64-bit word -> 8KB row): activation already latches the whole row into sense amps, so place a polar/LDPC code spanning the entire row and decode it in the row buffer during activation. The 128x overfetch becomes a reliability asset.

title: Reverse-bias healing pulses empty traps during idle periods
idea: Timescale shift (seconds of stress -> milliseconds of recovery): during idle self-refresh windows, drive negative wordline and reverse storage-node bias pulses that detrap charge accumulated at the access-transistor interface, like NBTI recovery in logic.

title: Nanoimprint template defects become one shared repair map
idea: No EUV: nanoimprint lithography copies identical template defects onto every die at the same coordinates. Time/scale shift (one template -> millions of dies over its life): characterize the template once and pre-fuse one universal repair map into every die it prints, adding to the map only when the template degrades.
note: Shared map covers template defects only; per-imprint particle defects remain.

title: Slew-shaped wordline pulses cut hammer coupling
idea: No EUV: drive wordlines with controlled 2-5 ns ramps and an early-close discharge profile instead of sharp sub-ns edges, reducing capacitive coupling and hot-electron injection into victim nodes. Timescale shift: the change is in ps-to-ns edge physics, not geometry.

title: FD-SOI back-gate trims each subarray's leakage over its lifetime
idea: No EUV: build the access array on DUV FD-SOI and give each subarray its own back-gate bias rail. Firmware re-trims back-bias yearly as aging shifts thresholds, keeping each subarray's leakage tail centered.

title: On-site flow-chemistry skids that synthesize ALD precursors at the fab
idea: Scale jump from global chemical plant to bench-scale reactor: modular continuous-flow skids at the fab make Hf, Zr and Ti amide and alkoxide precursors from bulk metal chlorides just in time, so no stockpile is shipped across oceans.

title: All-electrochemical metallization replacing argon sputter PVD
idea: Molecule-by-molecule wiring: ALD seeds, then electroless Co/Ni and electroplated Cu/Ru for contacts, bit lines and the back end, plus reactive pure-N2 deposition for TiN electrodes, so no argon-sputter PVD chamber is needed.

title: Parametron reborn: bits as oscillation phase in pumped nanoresonators
idea: Goto's parametron died because its ferrite-core resonators were big and power-hungry next to transistors. Use GHz AlN nanomechanical resonators parametrically driven by one shared global pump: each holds a 0 or pi oscillation phase indefinitely while the pump runs, is written by a tiny seed pulse and is read by phase comparison.
note: Parametron phase bits shown in NEMS; density and pump power are limits.

title: YMnO3 FeFET retried: improper ferroelectric resists depolarization when hot
idea: Late-1990s YMnO3 FeFETs died from leakage, charge injection and depolarization-limited retention. Use hexagonal YMnO3, whose polarization is improper (slaved to a lattice trimerization, Tc > 1000 K) so depolarization fields barely back-switch it, on a floating-metal MFMIS gate so the semiconductor never sees an injection field.
note: Hexagonal YMnO3 needs high crystallization temperature; depolarization robustness is real.

title: TFET's weak drive is fine for DRAM access duty
idea: Tunnel FETs failed for logic because their band-to-band on-current was too low. A DRAM access device needs only ~1 uA to charge 5 fF in 5 ns. A line-tunneling TFET (gate-overlapped pocket) has no thermionic Boltzmann tail in the off state and only weak temperature dependence. A counter-doped drain pocket suppresses ambipolar leakage.

title: Intel-Opticom polymer ferroelectric becomes a zero-refresh sleep shadow
idea: Intel and Opticom's printed P(VDF-TrFE) polymer memory failed as main memory because of microsecond switching, fatigue and disturb. Print it instead as a per-row shadow layer over an oxide-TFT memory foil. When the foil enters sleep, each row copies itself into its polymer shadow (slow, rare writes), and power and refresh drop to zero. On wake, the rows restore.

title: Rolltronics plastic failure fixed with roll-to-roll flexible glass anneal
idea: Rolltronics' roll-to-roll a-Si TFTs on plastic died on substrate shrinkage and the low process temperatures plastic allows. Build oxide access TFTs on rolls of ~100 um flexible glass, which tolerate 450 C anneals. Those anneals drive out the oxygen vacancies and hydrogen that set the oxide-TFT leakage tail.

title: Kodak spatial-ALD with inkjet inhibitors prints maskless low-leakage channels
idea: Kodak's selective-area spatial ALD for printed electronics was shelved along with its display ambitions. Inkjet a polymer inhibitor pattern onto a moving web, then grow ZnO/IGZO and Al2O3 by ALD only where the inhibitor is absent. Access TFTs are built additively with ALD-grade interfaces instead of solution-processed oxide.

title: Semprius transfer printing puts crystalline access transistors on printed capacitors
idea: Semprius's micro-transfer printing died with concentrated PV, not because the stamps failed. Release arrays of single-crystal SOI access transistors (long channel, thick oxide, low leakage) from a donor wafer and stamp them onto a capacitor foil made roll-to-roll. The donor's handle wafer is reused for many foils.

title: Same-age reference cells let the sense threshold follow leakage decay
idea: Failure mined: resistance drift ate Optane's PCM read window until drift-tracking reads were added. Fix for DRAM: every row carries 4 reference cells written with 1s and 0s in the same activation as the data. At read they are charge-shared onto the reference bitline, so the threshold falls in step as stored 1s leak instead of sitting fixed at VBL/2.

title: PLEDM gain-cell current lets 2048 cells share one sense amp
idea: Failure mined: Hitachi dropped its PLEDM gain cell (a vertical multi-tunnel-barrier transistor on a storage gate) when it exited DRAM. The overlooked strength was a current output that does not depend on bitline capacitance. Fix: hang 2048 PLEDM-style cells on one bitline with a current-integrating, auto-zeroed sense amp, instead of the 256-512 cells per charge-sharing bitline today.

title: Nantero's nanotubes as BEOL periphery transistors, not memory cells
idea: Failure mined: Nantero NRAM stalled on CNT-fabric switching variability. Fix: use aligned CNT films as BEOL CNFETs made below 400 C. A wide device averages over hundreds of tubes, so variability only has to meet logic-level tolerance. Row predecoders, column muxes and secondary sense stages are then built above the capacitor array.

title: Resonant adiabatic wordline drive, reversible computing's missing killer app
idea: Failure mined: adiabatic and reversible logic (MIT, Younis) died because irregular logic needed multi-phase resonant power clocks. DRAM is the opposite case: wordlines and bitlines are large, regular capacitive loads switched on a periodic tRC beat. Fix: drive them from shared LC tanks with inductors in the package substrate, swinging to 3 V and back while recovering the charge.

title: Virtual Channel Memory reborn as BEOL shadow row buffers
idea: Failure mined: NEC's Virtual Channel SDRAM added SRAM channel buffers between the sense amps and I/O but died on area cost and standards politics. Fix: stack 4-8 extra row buffers as BEOL oxide-transistor 2T dynamic latches directly above the SA stripe, at zero silicon area, so each bank keeps several rows open.
note: Multiple open-row buffers as oxide-TFT latches over SA stripe; hit-rate gains are workload dependent.

title: Sun proximity communication revived as solder-free, demountable DRAM stacks
idea: Sun's capacitive proximity communication died on alignment and Oracle's acquisition. Carry die-to-die signals on capacitive pads in a clamped DRAM stack, deliver power through spring pins, and align dies with etched V-groove-and-ball kinematic mounts. With no solder or underfill, a failed die is unclamped and swapped, and dies separate cleanly for reuse at end of life.

title: IBM thermal conduction module rework for serviceable HBM packages
idea: IBM's 1980s thermal conduction modules let individual chips on a ceramic substrate be reworked several times, using spring-loaded pistons for cooling, but lost on cost. Mount HBM stacks on a glass substrate with reworkable solder joints and a spring piston per stack instead of a bonded lid. A depot can then desolder and replace one failed stack without discarding the accelerator.

title: NEMS relay logic failure repurposed: relays isolate dead tiers
idea: Nano-electro-mechanical (NEMS) relay logic has not been adopted because contacts stick after billions of cycles. A spare-tier switch needs only a few dozen actuations, so put NEMS relays on each tier's power and signal rails. A shorted or leaky tier is physically disconnected, with zero leakage, and a spare tier switched in.

title: Directed self-assembly patterning made viable by defect-tolerant repairable arrays
idea: Directed self-assembly (DSA) of block copolymers was dropped from DRAM roadmaps because its defect rates were too high. Use DSA to pattern 4F2 pillar arrays without EUV, and tolerate defect densities around 1e-4 through string sparing and defect maps updated in the field.
note: 1e-4 pillar defect rate means ~1e6 defects per die; sparing overhead may exceed the EUV savings.

title: Z-RAM without SOI wafers: floating bodies over silicon-on-nothing voids
idea: Innovative Silicon's Z-RAM died because it needed SOI wafers (two Cz wafers per substrate via bonding) and lost sense margin on bulk. Form local empty-space voids under the array by hydrogen-anneal surface migration of deep trench lattices (silicon-on-nothing), then partially refill each void with doped poly as a buried back-gate plate so every floating body has a strong back gate to hold stored holes.
note: Floating-body retention and margin issues killed Z-RAM beyond SOI cost; back gate helps but not proven.

title: Kovio's liquid-silicon ink revived as stacked polysilicon memory tiers on glass
idea: Kovio printed cyclopentasilane silicon ink for RFID and died because tiny printed tags could not beat wafer chips on cost per die. Memory is area-dominated: slot-die coat the ink over whole Gen-8 sheets, convert at ~400 C, flash-lamp crystallize to large-grain polysilicon, and stack poly-Si TFT memory tiers without vacuum CVD.

title: MRAM's etch killer bypassed with ion-implant-defined magnetic junctions
idea: Everspin-era MRAM density and cost were throttled by etching magnetic stacks (non-volatile byproducts, sidewall redeposition, slow ion-beam etch). Deposit the MTJ stack blanket and define cells by implanting light ions (He+ or N+) through a hard mask to magnetically deaden the free layer between bits, leaving a planar, etch-free film.

title: Wafer-level burn-in revived as contactless, self-powered on-wafer BIST
idea: Early wafer-level burn-in for DRAM failed on the cost and planarity of full-wafer probe contactors. Build a scribe-line power grid fed by two large pads per wafer; every die runs on-chip BIST and burn-in in a heated cassette, burns results into fuses and reports through an on-die photodiode/LED or near-field link.
note: Power delivery and heat in cassette are the doubts.

title: Mythic analog flash CIM, fixed: only cold MoE experts
idea: Mythic's analog flash compute-in-memory went bankrupt in 2022 on ADC overhead, drift and dense models outgrowing the chip. Narrow it to rarely-activated MoE experts: they live as conductances in NOR flash arrays and compute in place, while hot experts and attention stay digital, and the low duty cycle leaves time for drift recalibration.

title: ThruChip inductive stacking fixed: coils in top metal over cell arrays
idea: Keio's ThruChip Interface (inductive coupling between stacked dies) never shipped because its coils ate die area and power still needed TSVs, so nothing was saved. Draw the transmit/receive coils in the DRAM's top metal directly above the cell arrays, where that level is otherwise lightly used, carry data inductively through all thinned dies, and keep only a few hundred coarse-pitch (50-100 um) power TSVs that are cheap and high-yield.
note: Coil size must scale with stack height; many-die reach is the doubt.

title: Wireless NoC fixed: sealed package cavity broadcasts DRAM commands at 300 GHz
idea: On-chip wireless networks died because tiny antennas radiated poorly into lossy silicon and multipath was unpredictable. Make the package lid and substrate a sealed metal cavity tuned as a 300 GHz waveguide, so on-die antennas on every DRAM die and the controller share a predictable, low-loss broadcast medium for command/address and clock (low-rate, all-to-all), while data stays on wires.

title: Keyssa's contactless connector failed in phones; it fits gold-free memory modules
idea: Keyssa's 60 GHz near-field 'kiss' connectors failed commercially because phone connectors were cheap and good enough. Server memory slots are now the signal-integrity wall at DDR5-8800+ and use gold-plated contacts, so replace the DIMM edge connector with an array of CMOS 60-140 GHz near-field couplers with plain Cu antennas, giving a sealed, wear-free, hot-swappable module interface.

title: Intel FIVR retreated; Sendust inductors in glass give per-channel memory DVFS
idea: Intel pulled its fully integrated voltage regulator after Haswell/Broadwell because air-core package inductors were lossy and hot, and the research magnetic inductors used banned CoZrTa. Embed laminated, sputtered Sendust (Fe-Si-Al) inductors in a glass-core substrate under each memory stack to feed per-channel buck converters in the base die, so each HBM/LPDDR channel scales VDDQ and VDD in 25 mV steps with load.
note: Integrated magnetics plus memory DVFS both known; Sendust thin-film loss at IVR frequency unclear.

title: Piezo-latched snap-through nanobeam holds bits as mechanical buckling
idea: Effect walk: piezoelectricity + Euler buckling. A 200-nm AlN/Si bimorph beam is built pre-compressed so it rests in one of two buckled states (up or down); a +/-1 V piezo pulse snaps it through in ~ns, and a monolayer MoS2 strain gauge at the beam root reads the state non-destructively by piezoresistance.
note: Bistable buckled NEMS known; 4-8F pitch per layer and fatigue limit density.

title: Ferroelectric AlScN barrier toggles GaN 2DEG for gain-read memory
idea: Effect walk: spontaneous and piezoelectric polarization in wurtzite nitrides. A 5-nm ferroelectric AlScN barrier on GaN turns the polarization-induced 2D electron gas on or off depending on its switched polarity, giving a non-destructive gain read with ~10^4 on/off and no capacitor.
note: FeHEMT on AlScN shown in labs; high coercive field and fatigue make DRAM endurance doubtful.

title: Positive fixed-charge nitride spacer relieves storage-junction GIDL field
idea: Effect: field-effect passivation by fixed dielectric charge (the solar-cell passivation trick). A SiNx spacer holding ~+2e12 cm^-2 fixed charge lines only the gate-to-storage-node overlap, accumulating electrons at the n+ surface so band bending under a low wordline is reduced and GIDL falls. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.

title: On-die telegraph-noise detector catches VRT cells in the field
idea: Effect: random telegraph noise from single-trap capture and emission. Inside idle REF windows each bank re-reads sample rows with a deliberately lowered sense reference; cells whose margin toggles (RTN signature) are logged in an on-die CAM and get extra internal refreshes while all other rows get fewer. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.

title: Voltage-stacked subarray pairs halve refresh supply current
idea: Effect: series voltage stacking (charge conservation). Two subarrays refreshed together run in stacked domains, A between VDD and VDD/2 and B between VDD/2 and 0 with plates biased per domain, so the restore current drawn through A's sense amps is reused by B instead of returning to ground. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
note: Shared substrate/plate and sense timing complicate stacking.

title: Spin-Hall nonvolatile shadow latches let periphery power-gate between accesses
idea: Effect: spin Hall effect (spin-orbit torque). Pair each sense amp with a three-terminal SOT-MTJ on a beta-Ta strip (no tungsten) that copies the latched row in ~1 ns; idle banks cut power to SA and periphery stripes and reopen the row from the shadow copy without a new activation.

title: Photoconductive-switch probe card multiplexes thousands of test channels optically
idea: Effect: picosecond photoconductive switching in low-temperature-grown GaAs. Build DRAM wafer probe cards whose fan-out uses LT-GaAs photoconductive switch dies closed by an on-card LED/VCSEL array, so a few tester channels are time-multiplexed across thousands of probe pins with optical control instead of relays.

title: Biased-reference sentinel column detects disturbance before data cells flip
idea: Effect: deliberately offset sense threshold as a disturbance canary. In a small team's memory macro, each row has one sentinel cell whose sense amp uses a shifted reference (~30% of nominal signal), rewritten to 1 at every refresh; it fails before any data cell under leakage or hammer disturbance, so a flipped sentinel triggers immediate refresh of that row and its neighbors.

title: Pyroelectric tile sensors steer per-tile refresh in memory-on-logic stacks
idea: Pyroelectric effect: a thin HZO pyroelectric sheet in each tier's bonding layer outputs charge proportional to dT/dt over ~1 mm2 tiles, driving an analog integrator that sets each tile's refresh interval directly without ADCs or thermal diodes. Cool tiles refresh at 256 ms while only hot tiles above logic hot spots stay at 32-64 ms.
note: Pyro output tracks dT/dt, needing baseline; cheap thermal diodes already enable zoned refresh.

title: Electroformed copper-filament spare vias repair bonded stacks after test
idea: Ion migration (electrochemical metallization): every hybrid-bond interface carries a grid of spare Cu/SiO2 cells. After post-stack test, a forming voltage drives Cu ions into permanent filaments that reroute signals and power around failed bond pads or bad tiers, like antifuses in the third dimension.

title: Workfunction charge-plasma junctions for implant-free stacked lateral transistors
idea: Charge-plasma effect: source and drain regions of the lateral access transistors in each deposited channel tier are induced electrostatically by low- and high-workfunction metal contacts, not by dopant implants. No implant has to pass through upper tiers, and no activation anneal is needed.

title: Johnsen-Rahbek solid-contact chucks remove backside gas entirely
idea: Effect: the Johnsen-Rahbek effect concentrates the clamping field across micro-gaps of a slightly conductive dielectric, giving ~10x the clamp force of a Coulomb chuck. Pair it with a compliant AlN-nanocomposite top layer so heat leaves through >30% real solid contact area instead of gas, and tune temperature uniformity with zoned JR voltages.

title: Non-wetting nitride crucibles exploit molten silicon contact-angle physics
idea: Effect: molten Si wets and dissolves silica but beads up (contact angle >90 deg) on dense reaction-bonded Si3N4 or CVD-SiC. Make crucibles from nitrogen and metallurgical silicon with a renewable nitride release coat; the light nitrogen doping it adds is the same doping already used to strengthen CZ wafers.
note: Si3N4 particles and nitrogen saturation risk dislocations in CZ; reuse claim untested at 300 mm.

title: Size-effect-optimized NiAl intermetallic wordlines replace buried tungsten
idea: Effect: Fuchs-Sondheimer surface and Mayadas-Shatzkes grain-boundary scattering penalize long-mean-free-path metals below 20 nm. B2-ordered NiAl and CuAl2 have ~5 nm electron mean free paths and need no TiN barrier, so at 10-15 nm widths they match or beat W+TiN. Co-sputter or ALD the layers, then order them with a short anneal.

title: LC-resonant adiabatic wordline drive recycles charge energy
idea: Effect: adiabatic charging, where loss is about (RC/T)*CV2. Drive wordlines from a resonant sinusoidal supply through on-interposer inductors so the 3 V swing ramps slowly relative to RC, and return the charge to the LC tank instead of dumping it to ground.
note: Random, sparse activations do not fit a resonant clocked supply; wordline energy is a small share.

title: Ion-irradiation defines spin-Hall MRAM bits magnetically without stack etching
idea: Effect: irradiation-induced interface intermixing plus the spin Hall effect. Deposit a blanket MTJ stack on a W or BiSb spin-Hall write line, then irradiate through a stencil with low-dose He+ or Ar+, which intermixes CoFeB/MgO and kills perpendicular anisotropy everywhere except the bits. Bits switch by spin-orbit torque from the in-plane spin Hall current, with no MTJ etch at all.
note: Continuous barrier/free layer risks lateral shunting and coupling.

title: Buckled AlN micro-beams store compression codebooks with zero leakage
idea: Weight-clustering codebooks and LZ dictionaries (a few hundred KB, rarely updated) are stored as up/down buckled states of AlN-actuated micro-beams next to the decompression engine. A piezo pulse snaps a beam and capacitive sensing reads it. With no charge to leak, 125 C for 10 years is a non-issue, whereas SRAM leaks heavily at that temperature and loses its contents at power-off.

title: Ferroelectric fast checkpoints let exclusive tasks time-share one DRAM
idea: Mutually exclusive vehicle workloads (parking, highway, cabin assistant) each checkpoint their whole state into AlScN FeRAM in milliseconds, using ns polarization switching. The next task is then swapped in, so one small DRAM serves several tasks over time instead of each owning its own. Wurtzite polarization survives 125 C for 10 years.

title: Silicon transparency: infrared optical vias broadcast commands through HBM stacks
idea: Silicon is transparent above 1.1 um, so a 1.3 um VCSEL on the base die shines vertically through 16 thinned DRAM dies, each carrying a small partially absorbing Ge photoconductor window that taps ~5% of the light; command/address and clock are broadcast optically to all dies at once instead of through TSV columns.

title: Electrochromism: zero-holding-power optical shutters reconfigure rack memory-pool topology
idea: WO3/NiO electrochromic shutters placed in front of a fixed fan-out optical mesh open or close specific memory-to-host light paths; they switch in ~100 ms and hold state with no power, letting a rack reassign terabytes of pooled DRAM between servers as workloads shift.

title: Resonant tunneling: InP RTD terahertz transceivers link GPUs and memory towers
idea: Resonant-tunneling-diode oscillators at 300-600 GHz with on-chip slot antennas give 50-100 Gb/s line-of-sight links between a processor and surrounding memory towers in a sealed package or across adjacent boards, avoiding fine-pitch wiring.

title: Phase-gradient metasurfaces: printed reflectarrays steer wireless memory links inside servers
idea: Roll-print copper patch metasurfaces with fixed phase gradients on films lining chassis walls, redirecting 60-140 GHz beams between memory boards and processors so wireless links get high-gain non-line-of-sight paths.

title: Volume holography: printed photopolymer holograms fan one laser to 64 chiplets
idea: Record multiplexed volume holograms in R2R-coated photopolymer film so one input beam diffracts into 64 precisely aimed spots on memory chiplet detectors, distributing broadcast data, clock or optical power across a module with no waveguides.

title: Hot-carrier injection permanently nulls sense-amplifier offset
idea: Effect: hot-carrier injection and oxide charge trapping. At final test each bitline sense amplifier's offset is measured, and controlled high-drain-bias pulses on one transistor of the cross-coupled pair trap charge in its gate oxide, shifting its Vt to cancel the mismatch: a one-time analog trim with no extra transistors that cuts offset sigma from ~15 mV to ~3 mV.
note: HCI-based SA trimming studied for SRAM; charge detrapping over life is a doubt.

title: Kirchhoff current-sum checksum scrubs rows inside the array
idea: Effect: Kirchhoff current summation. During refresh, the restored sense-amp outputs of each column group drive equal unit currents onto a shared analog sum line, so the total current encodes the group's Hamming weight; a comparator checks it against a weight value stored in spare cells at write time. Only rows whose weight changed are shipped to the ECC engine for correction.

title: Capillary fluidic self-assembly aggregates DRAM dielets from many small fabs
idea: Micro-fabs make tiny 0.5-1 mm2 DRAM dielets; a central assembler suspends them in liquid where shape-matched recesses and capillary forces seat thousands per minute onto a wafer-scale interposer. Misses are tested and refilled, so many small producers feed one memory product.

title: Hydrogen-blistered donor wafers reused tenfold, device layers re-transferable
idea: Build the DRAM array in a Smart-Cut layer: implanted hydrogen forms a blistering plane that splits a thin Si film onto a carrier with a laser-release oxide. The donor is CMP-reclaimed ~10x, and at end of life the device layer lifts off so carrier and silicon are reclaimed.

title: On-die microheaters anneal away aging to restore retention for second life
idea: TiN heater meanders under each bank hold the array at 250-300 C for minutes while powered down, re-passivating interface traps with stored hydrogen and relaxing BTI and hot-carrier damage. Retention and Vt margins are restored before resale.

title: Two-part crucible with permanent shell and recyclable synthetic-silica liner
idea: Replace monolithic HPQ crucibles with a reusable graphite/SiC shell and a 2-3 mm synthetic silica liner made by sol-gel or CVD from SiCl4, engineered to devitrify into a stiff cristobalite skin for one pull. Spent liners are crushed and re-fused into new liners.
note: Two-part variant of synthetic-silica crucible in I-00420.

title: Magnetorheological isolation makes relocatable, refurbishable container micro-fabs
idea: Containerized fab modules float tools on magnetorheological-fluid dampers whose viscosity is retuned in ms to cancel floor vibration, so fabs run in ordinary warehouses and can be unbolted, refurbished and redeployed when a product ends.

title: Mg: MgB2 flux-quantum loops for 20 K helium-free memory
idea: Pattern nanoscale MgB2 loops (Tc 39 K, made only of Mg and B) that each trap zero or one flux quantum of persistent current, written by a pulsed bias line and read by a kinetic-inductance sensor, cooled to 20 K by cryocoolers (no liquid helium) beside cryogenic AI accelerators.

title: Si: 20:1 pillars at 1.5 fF accept 1% sense misses
idea: Cut the silicon-supported capacitor to 20:1 (~1.5 fF) and run the sense amp at ~2.3 sigma margin, which misreads ~1% of cells, then protect each 512-bit burst with an on-die LDPC code of ~12% overhead that brings output BER below 1e-15.

title: Si: buried-channel CCD charge loops replace per-bit access transistors
idea: Store bits as charge packets circulating in 64-256-stage buried-channel silicon CCD loops clocked by three-phase gates (the 1970s CCD-memory idea revived at 12 nm), with one injector and one sense node per loop; charge-transfer loss and dark current are allowed to reach ~1% packet errors per circuit, corrected by a per-loop code.
note: 1970s CCD memory revived with ECC; area per bit not clearly below 6F2.

title: Sn: back-end complementary oxide latch from p-SnO and n-ZnO
idea: Stack a cross-coupled four-transistor latch of p-type SnO and n-type ZnO thin-film transistors in the back-end wiring, tens of tiers high; the latch needs no refresh, and SnO's poor hole mobility and variability are allowed to create ~1% weak cells that a row code corrects.
note: 4T latch area and SnO p-channel weakness limit density.

title: Mn: rare-earth-free τ-MnAl nanomagnets run deliberately volatile like DRAM
idea: Build perpendicular MTJ free layers from tau-phase MnAl (Mn and Al only, no Co, Pt or rare earths) sized for thermal stability ~25 instead of ~60, giving seconds-to-minutes retention with ~1% thermal flips between scrubs; write current drops ~2-3x and the cell shrinks.
note: Relaxed-retention STT known; tau-MnAl low TMR and 1% flips between scrubs are heavy costs.

title: Boron arsenide spreader flattens hotspots so refresh tracks average temperature
idea: B: bond a cubic boron arsenide layer (thermal conductivity ~1,300 W/m-K) between the DRAM die and the hot logic or HBM base die, shrinking intra-die temperature gradients from ~10-15 C to ~2 C, so the refresh rate, which is set by the hottest mat, can be specified for the mean temperature.

title: S: sulfide threshold-switch matrix replaces per-wordline decoder transistors
idea: Place a two-terminal sulfide-based Ovonic threshold switch between each local wordline and two crossing global select lines; only the wordline at the driven intersection sees enough voltage to snap its switch on, so N wordlines need only ~2 sqrt(N) drivers.

title: Zr: antiferroelectric zirconia flying capacitors shrink charge pumps
idea: Build charge-pump flying capacitors from antiferroelectric ZrO2, whose field-induced phase change stores ~3-5x the energy density of linear high-k at 2-3 V, operated inside the double-hysteresis window to pump VPP and VBB.

title: Si: silicone block-copolymer self-assembly patterns regular decoder gratings
idea: Redesign decoders and sub-wordline drivers as strictly periodic gratings patterned by PS-b-PDMS directed self-assembly; the silicon-rich PDMS block becomes a SiOx hardmask in an O2/H2 plasma with no argon, and a coarse guide pattern from a non-excimer tool sets registration.

title: N: nitride charge-trap self-trim cancels sense-amp mismatch
idea: Give the SA cross-coupled pair an oxide-nitride-oxide gate stack (Si3N4 from SiH2Cl2 and NH3, N2 carrier); during test a feedback loop injects hot-carrier charge into the stronger device's nitride until the pair balances, permanently trimming offset.

title: Mg: water-dissolved magnesium sacrificial spacer creates air-gap bitlines
idea: Evaporate a thin Mg sacrificial spacer between bitlines, cap it with a porous lid, and dissolve it in dilute carbonated water to leave air gaps, avoiding the XeF2 (xenon) or argon-plasma release normally used for air gaps.

title: N: certified rare-gas-free periphery lines under CHIPS funding
idea: Create a federal certification and cost-share for N2/H2-only periphery lines: solid-state-laser or LED lithography, N2-purged ALD, H2-carrier CVD, electroplating, and H2 or N2 backside wafer cooling instead of helium; DRAM makers buying bonded periphery from such lines earn credits.

title: Magnesium sacrificial layers leave air-gap bitlines between 3D tiers
