idea: Desert dwellers use a ventilated double roof: suspend the DRAM stack over a 5-10 um vacuum gap above the 150 C+ logic die, couple signals across the gap by near-field coupling, and feed power from the board side through separate thermal-choke ribbons.
note: Near-field signaling density across 5-10 um vacuum gap and mechanical support are doubtful.

title: Mars-ISRU gas whitelist as a rare-gas-free DRAM process kit
idea: A Mars fab could only use gases made from CO2, water and nitrogen; define a binding whitelist (N2, H2, O2, CO2, H2O, NH3, NF3, HF, HBr, Cl2, SiH4) and requalify every 3D-array step against it, publishing the recipes as an open process design kit. Make whitelist compliance a condition of federal fab grants so U.S. DRAM lines cannot be stopped by a helium, neon or xenon shock.
note: ArF lasers need neon and sputtering needs argon; binding whitelist is impractical as stated.

title: Phase-change heat-sponge interlayers enable 24-high stacks for burst seconds
idea: Use the thermal timescale (seconds) as a design variable: thin sealed micro-cells of low-melt Bi-In alloy between DRAM dies melt during training bursts and refreeze during communication lulls. Peaks are buffered rather than conducted, so taller stacks stay within temperature limits.
note: Thin alloy layers hold little latent heat; they melt in ms, not over training bursts.

title: Thinfilm polymer FeRAM fixed: proton-transfer organic ferroelectric crystals
idea: Thin Film Electronics' and Intel's PVDF polymer FeRAM died from microsecond switching, half-select disturb and a low Curie point. Grow croconic-acid-type hydrogen-bonded crystals in BEOL vias: they switch by collective proton transfer along H-bond chains (P ~20-30 uC/cm2) and deposit below 150 C, so many tiers can stack.
note: Croconic acid crystals in vias and ns switching unproven.

title: Straintronics unclamped: remanent ferroelastic strain read by MoS2 gauge
idea: Straintronic memories stalled because substrate clamping cut piezo strain to ~1e-4, too little to switch magnets reliably. Drop the magnet: store the bit as a 71/109-degree ferroelastic domain state in a BiFeO3 or PMN-PT island, which holds ~0.1-0.5% remanent strain, and read it through a monolayer MoS2 channel on top whose strain-shifted bandgap changes its current several-fold.
note: Clamped island remanent strain and MoS2 gauge sensitivity likely give small read margin.

title: Printed-electronics bust fixed by toll-printing memory foil on converters
idea: The 2008-2012 printed-electronics boom went bust because startups built their own lines to make low-value labels. Instead, license a memory-foil recipe (printed oxide access devices plus capacitors) to U.S. flexible-packaging converters whose roll-to-roll lines run below capacity, and pay them per m2 of good foil.
note: Printed devices far from DRAM-class density and speed.

title: Kovio printed silicon diode pairs as two-way crosspoint access
idea: Kovio's printed-silicon RFID died because printed tags had to undercut cheap silicon chips. Use its cyclopentasilane ink, crystallized by flash lamp, to print two opposing p-i-n diodes per cell, one to a write-1 line and one to a write-0 line. When idle, the storage node is isolated by two reverse-biased diodes, giving a transistor-free crosspoint 2D1C cell.
note: Two printed diodes replace the access transistor; reverse leakage and micron pitch likely kill retention and density.

title: Plated-wire memory reborn as drawn multimaterial fiber woven into crossbars
idea: Plated-wire memory put the storage film on a beryllium-copper wire substrate and died on per-wire plating cost and coarse pitch. Thermally draw a glass/polymer preform containing conductor, charge-storage sheath and semiconductor layers into kilometers of 20-50 um fiber (multimaterial fiber drawing), then weave orthogonal fibers so each warp-weft crossing is a cell.
note: Fiber crossing pitch of 20-50 um gives ~50 MB/m2, far below the claim; cell physics unspecified.

title: Bell Labs ferroelectric matrix fixed by co-fired ZnO varistor selectors
idea: 1950s Bell Labs barium-titanate matrix memory died on half-select disturb because BaTiO3 has no sharp switching threshold. Co-fire a multilayer ceramic stack on the MLCC process (hundreds of ~0.5 um layers) where each BaTiO3 cell sits in series with a ZnO varistor layer (nonlinearity >30) that blocks half-select voltages.
note: MLCC co-fired FE plus varistor selector is novel; density at printed pitch is orders below DRAM.

title: CCD memory reborn as charge-packet data bus inside DRAM periphery
idea: 1970s CCD memories lost to DRAM because serial shifting made random access slow, yet moving charge packets down a buried channel is extremely cheap per hop. Use a short CCD-style bucket-brigade channel to carry the 128-256 bits fetched from a bank toward the I/O hub as charge packets clocked at ~0.3 V, instead of full-swing global I/O lines, serializing the data naturally as it moves.
note: Buried-channel CCD in DRAM process and transfer loss at GHz rates doubtful.

title: Iron-disilicide LED fizzled; Purcell microcavity makes it a 1.55-um source
idea: Surrey's 1997 beta-FeSi2 light-emitting diode on silicon faded because room-temperature emission was weak. Embed FeSi2 nanocrystals in a silicon photonic-crystal nanocavity (Q ~1e4) to Purcell-enhance the radiative rate 10-50x, couple straight into Si waveguides, and detect with divacancy-implanted silicon waveguide photodiodes, giving an in-package photonic memory link with no InP, GaAs, Ge or Er.
note: Purcell boost of weak FeSi2 emission still far from laser-class efficiency.

title: Spectrum-sliced LED WDM failed in telecom; incandescent silicon sources suit packages
idea: Spectrum-sliced incoherent WDM (one broadband source cut into channels) died in telecom from excess intensity noise and low power per slice over km distances. Over 1-10 mm in-package paths, a microheated SiC/silicon photonic-crystal selective thermal emitter (W-free) can feed SiN waveguides whose silicon microrings slice and modulate dozens of channels, detected by Si photodiodes below 1.1 um, with no laser at all.

title: Prussian-blue electrochromic bit read by light on a photonic bus
idea: Effect walk: electrochromism. Each bit is a 50-nm Prussian-blue (iron hexacyanoferrate, tungsten-free) patch on a silicon-nitride waveguide; inserting ~10^3 K+ or H+ ions from a thin solid electrolyte bleaches or colours it, changing optical absorption, so a passing light pulse reads the bit without electrical bitlines while the coloured state holds for hours.
note: Ion kinetics us-ms and electrochromic endurance far from DRAM duty.

title: Pyroelectric wordline layer auto-cancels hot-die leakage rise
idea: Effect: pyroelectricity. A poled AlScN film in the access gate stack generates bound charge equivalent to a more negative gate bias as temperature rises (~-2 to -4 mV/K), offsetting the access transistor's Vt drop that doubles leakage every ~10 C.

title: Maxwell-Wagner bilayer capacitor back-fills leaked charge from interface reservoir
idea: Effect: interfacial (Maxwell-Wagner-Sillars) polarization, i.e., dielectric absorption. The cell capacitor is a high-k/low-conductivity bilayer engineered so interface charge accumulates over ms after a write and re-emerges as the node droops, like a capacitor's recovery voltage; a reset pulse on writes clears ghost charge from the previous value.
note: Absorbed charge leaks too and causes data-history ghosting.

title: Photon-emission retention mapping fuses per-row internal refresh bins
idea: Effect: junction and hot-carrier electroluminescence. At sort the array is biased to stress leakage paths and a cooled InGaAs camera images the faint NIR emission; leaky row segments glow, so a weak-row map is captured in seconds instead of hours of retention testing and burned into fuses; the die then refreshes strong rows only every 4th REF. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
note: fA leakage yields well under one photon per second per cell; seconds-scale mapping doubtful.

title: Power-up microheater pulses anneal variable-retention-time defects
idea: Effect: thermally activated defect reconfiguration. VRT cells toggle as a metastable defect switches configuration; TiN microheaters in thermally isolated mats deliver ~us pulses at ~250 C during the JEDEC initialization window (before data exists), biased with a gate field that favours the low-leakage configuration, pruning the VRT population each boot. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
note: Boot-time thermal pruning of VRT defects is new; whether anneal favours low-leak state, and on-die thermal isolation, are unproven.

title: NbO2 Mott-switch sense latch replaces cross-coupled sense amplifier
idea: Effect: Mott insulator-to-metal transition. Bias a ~20 nm NbO2 threshold switch just below its transition voltage between the bitline and a reference; the cell's ~60 mV charge-sharing signal tips it across threshold, its resistance collapses ~100x in <1 ns, and one restore FET writes the row back. One BEOL device plus 1-2 FETs replaces the 6-10 transistor latch and equalizer.
note: NbO2 threshold variation far exceeds the ~60 mV signal.

title: Injection-locked oscillator pair turns bitline signal into phase decision
idea: Effect: sub-harmonic injection locking. Each SA stripe hosts a pair of tiny coupled ring oscillators pumped at their second harmonic, so they become phase-bistable (0 or 180 degrees, as in oscillator Ising machines); the bitline differential briefly biases the coupling, the pair locks into one phase, and a phase detector restores full swing. Gain comes from locking dynamics rather than transistor matching.

title: Magnetostrictive-piezo laminate receivers replace TSVs in memory stacks
idea: Magnetostriction: each thinned die carries micro-coils that transmit, and FeGa/AlN magnetoelectric laminate pads that receive. The stray AC field from the die below strains the magnetostrictive layer, and the piezo layer turns that strain into a mV-scale voltage. The laminate's high field-to-voltage gain allows smaller-pitch, higher-bandwidth contactless links than plain inductive coils.

title: Pyroelectric heat-pulse non-destructive read of stacked ferroelectric tiers
idea: Pyroelectric effect: in a 3D-stacked HZO ferroelectric capacitor array, a nanosecond current pulse in a resistive heater line beside each row warms the cells by a few kelvin. Each cell then emits a pyroelectric current whose sign gives its polarization, so the read never switches the cell and the data is non-volatile with no write-back.
note: Pyroelectric charge at DRAM-scale cell area and few-K heating is a handful of electrons; unreadable.

title: Spin-crossover molecular tiers with room-temperature-straddling hysteresis loops
idea: Thermal hysteresis: Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover films whose 30-40 K hysteresis loop is engineered to straddle 20-60 C hold either the high-spin or low-spin state with no power. A heater pulse writes high-spin, a field pulse writes low-spin, and the ~10% dielectric or resistance change is the read. The films can be evaporated at <200 C, so many cheap tiers fit in BEOL.
note: Writing low-spin needs cooling; slow, fatigue-prone, not DRAM-class.

title: Shape-memory NiTi microsprings close warped HBM gaps on heating
idea: Effect: martensitic shape-memory recovery with thermal hysteresis. Sputter NiTi micro-bumps trained as compressed springs; heating above the austenite finish temperature makes each bump extend 1-3 um to meet its pad and absorb die warpage, and the hysteresis keeps them extended at operating temperature. $1M covers the target, university MEMS line time and a 24-month reliability demo.

title: Tunneling-leak gain cells make old KV tokens fade like ALiBi
idea: Store KV entries in gain cells whose tunneling oxide is deliberately thin, so charge decays with a time constant of a few hundred tokens. Each read value is then naturally scaled by exp(-age/tau), which is exactly a recency-bias attention prior. Cells whose signal drops below the sense threshold are reclaimed as free slots, with no refresh or eviction logic.
note: Multiplicative decay is not ALiBi; leakage tail variability makes decay non-uniform.

title: Magnetostriction: magnetoelectric nano-antennas give chiplet memory links without interposer wires
idea: FeGaB/AlN magnetoelectric antennas radiate at their GHz acoustic resonance rather than their electromagnetic wavelength, making them ~100x smaller than patch antennas; arrays on memory and compute chiplets talk wirelessly through mold compound with no interposer routing.
note: Bandwidth and pJ/bit of ME antennas far from link needs.

title: Mott transition: NbO2 steep-threshold receivers enable 80 mV memory I/O swings
idea: Put NbO2 threshold-switch elements at the front end of DRAM I/O receivers; their abrupt insulator-metal transition acts as near-infinite-gain slicing so a 60-100 mV interposer swing switches cleanly, replacing 300-400 mV swings and biased sense amplifiers.

title: Direct tunneling: oxide tunnel-bond hybrid bonding without metal-to-metal contact
idea: Cap both Cu bond pads with 1-1.5 nm of bond dielectric so current crosses by direct tunneling (ohmic-like at mV) plus capacitive coupling for AC; pads no longer need to expand and fuse, so dishing tolerance loosens and anneal drops below 200 C, protecting DRAM retention.

title: Ion migration: electroformed silver filaments grow and repair vias after stacking
idea: Bond dies through a thin chalcogenide solid-electrolyte layer between coarsely aligned pads; a post-bond forming pulse drives Ag+ ions to grow filaments bridging whichever pads face each other, and any open or degraded bond found in field test is re-grown by another pulse.

title: Elastic buckling: roll-printed kirigami interposers pop up into 3D memory cages
idea: Print wiring on a pre-cut kirigami polyimide film; releasing pre-strain buckles it into a 3D cage that surrounds a processor with memory chiplets on all sides instead of along one edge.

title: Ca: mayenite electride cages trap electrons as lattice-site anions
idea: Use a thin crystalline C12A7 (Ca12Al14O33) film, whose sub-nanometre cages host electrons as anions, as the storage layer of a gate stack; a gate pulse loads or empties cages near the interface and the caged electrons shift the read transistor's threshold.
note: Charge-trap memory variant; still needs tunnel oxide, so flash-like wear and no clear DRAM win.

title: LiPON ionic back-gate puts idle subarrays into deep-Vt hibernation
idea: Li: put a thin-film-battery-style LiPON electrolyte plus Li reservoir under each subarray, separated from the silicon by an Al2O3 Li-blocking liner; a ~1 V, ~10 ms pulse builds an ionic double layer that shifts access-transistor Vt up ~0.3-0.5 V for subarrays idle for seconds, and is reversed before reactivation.
note: Lithium in a DRAM fab is a contamination hazard; only helps idle refresh.

title: Post-test oxygen-vacancy trimming raises Vt of leakage-tail cells only
idea: O: use an oxide-semiconductor access FET with an oxygen-exchange TaOx gate liner; at wafer test, locate the ~0.01% leakage-tail cells and apply a per-cell high-field gate pulse that pumps oxygen into the channel near the drain, annihilating donor vacancies and permanently raising that cell's Vt ~0.2 V.

title: Polarization-doped AlGaN access channel eliminates random dopant fluctuation
idea: Al: build the access transistor in a compositionally graded AlGaN layer whose polarization gradient creates fixed 3D charge (polarization doping) instead of impurity atoms, so channel and junction 'doping' is set by a continuous Al-fraction grade identical in every cell.

title: Water-soluble salt release layer for stacking oxide memory tiers
idea: Periodic-table walk, Na+Cl (11,17): evaporate a NaCl film on a reusable carrier, seal it with ALD Al2O3, build an oxide-transistor DRAM tier at <=400 C (below NaCl's 801 C melt), bond it onto the stack, and dissolve the salt in water to release it.
note: Sodium is a mobile-ion poison for oxide transistors; contamination control is the key doubt.

title: Fe: magnetically chained magnetite nanoparticles as wordline etch masks
idea: Spin a monodisperse Fe3O4 nanoparticle ink into coarse DUV guide trenches, apply an in-plane magnetic field so particles chain into parallel lines with spacing set by dipole repulsion, then sinter into an iron-oxide etch mask that strips in dilute acid.
note: Fe contamination is a retention killer.

title: Zn: ZnO piezo transducers send data acoustically through silicon stacks
idea: Sputter ZnO thin-film bulk-acoustic-wave transducers on every die so 1-5 GHz acoustic pulses carry data vertically through the bonded silicon stack (low acoustic loss in crystalline Si), with frequency-division channels per transducer; dies need a bonded acoustic path, not drilled and filled holes.
note: GHz BAW data through Si; low per-channel rate and crosstalk unknowns.

title: O: IGZO-TFT active glass interposer hosts memory buffers and repeaters
idea: Fabricate InGaZnO oxide thin-film transistors (display-fab tooling, 1-10 um rules) directly on a glass interposer to implement repeaters, address buffers, ECC and power gating between logic and many DRAM dies, so the DRAM base die/PHY shrinks and the memory plane can span half a meter.
note: IGZO TFTs at 1-10 um rules cannot drive Gb/s repeaters.

title: Co: CoFeB spin-torque nano-oscillators as in-package memory radios
idea: Use CoFeB/MgO magnetic-tunnel-junction spin-torque nano-oscillators (~100 nm, 5-40 GHz, tuned by bias current) as frequency-agile transmitters and detectors, giving each DRAM die its own wireless channel inside a shielded package so dies can sit without TSVs or bumps.
note: STNO output power is nW-uW with broad linewidth; Gb/s links doubtful.

title: Ge: germanosilicate fiber delay loops hold model weights in flight
idea: Echoing mercury delay-line memory, circulate model weights as WDM light in a Ge-doped silica fiber loop (10 km ~ 50 us at 100 Tb/s ~ 600 MB in flight), re-amplified each lap and tapped at each accelerator exactly when the next layer needs those weights; the wire itself is the storage.
note: Lap amplification noise needs regeneration; 100 Tb/s transceivers cost more than the HBM replaced.

title: Sn: tin-bismuth microbumps self-reflow to heal opened HBM joints
idea: Use low-melting Sn-Bi (~139 C) microbumps with resistive heaters on the base die; when built-in self-test finds an open or high-resistance joint, the controller pulses local heat to re-melt and re-wet it, with spare TSV lanes as fallback.
note: Local re-melt inside underfilled stacks risks neighbor joints; HBM moving to hybrid bonding.

title: One-drop-fill ferroelectric nematic: fluid polar bit that cannot fatigue
idea: Use LCD one-drop-fill manufacturing: dispense a ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (RM734/DIO class: C, H, N, O, F) into sealed nano-cells whose antiparallel polar surface anchoring makes the ~5 uC/cm2 polarization bistable. A low-voltage pulse flips it in ns, and a capacitive charge read senses it.
note: Fluid polarization retention, ns switching and narrow N_F temperature range doubtful.

title: Electrolytic-capacitor 'forming': self-healing anodic Al2O3 kills leakage tail
idea: Copy the forming step of aluminum electrolytic capacitors: each cell has an anodic Al2O3 dielectric under a conductive polymer (PEDOT: C, H, O, S) counter electrode. A periodic forming voltage re-anodizes weak spots, and the polymer over hot spots de-dopes into an insulator, so leaky outlier cells cure themselves instead of setting the refresh rate.
note: Novel, but the refresh tail is mainly junction/GIDL leakage, not dielectric.

title: Thermal-receipt printing: buried metal self-registers the next layer
idea: Like a receipt printer that marks only where heated, flash the wafer with near-IR that buried metal absorbs far more than oxide, so a thermally crosslinking resist hardens only above metal; this registers landing pads to contacts with zero overlay error and no mask, leaving the one allowed new mask for the cut layer.

title: Jacquard-loom woven micro-wire substrate with laser-fused crossings
idea: Weave 10 um insulated copper micro-wires (weft = signals) through glass-fiber warp on a Jacquard loom; a punched-card-style program decides which warp/weft crossings get laser-stripped and welded into vias. The result is a multilayer memory-to-compute substrate made with no lithography.
note: 10 um pitch via weaving with glass warp is implausible; loom-made substrate is a striking but doubtful idea.

title: Damascus-fold edge wiring: film thickness sets 40 nm pitch
idea: Deposit 100 alternating copper/oxide films 20 nm thick, or fold-laminate metal foil like Damascus steel, then slice the stack on edge and polish it. The face shows parallel wires whose pitch is set by deposition thickness, and this becomes a bridge die between memory and logic.

title: Jelly-roll memory: one patterned film rolled into a thousand tiers
idea: IFR: 'a thousand tiers for the price of one.' Backward: pattern one long polyimide ribbon with oxide-TFT memory mats and an edge bus, then wind it like a battery jelly-roll; each turn's exposed edge bus lands on a laser-patterned end-cap whose radius-coded traces act as the vertical interconnect, like battery tabs.
note: Winding adds volume density, not cost relief: the whole ribbon is still patterned.

title: MLCC-line ferroelectric block: one transistor, many plate-selected capacitors
idea: IFR: 'capacitor layers cost what a commodity chip capacitor costs.' Backward: use multilayer-ceramic-capacitor tape casting and screen printing to co-fire a block of thin doped-BaTiO3 layers where each layer is its own plate line, and bond an oxide-TFT glass lid giving one transistor per vertical column, a 1T-nC ferroelectric chain read by pulsing one plate at a time.
note: ~10 Mb/mm2 is ~30x below DRAM; FE endurance and plate disturb unresolved.

title: Self-healing clearing electrodes burn out capacitor weak spots at test
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): the die must look like normal DDR5, so fix the leakage tail inside the cell. Make the capacitor top electrode an ultrathin clearable layer, as in metallized-film capacitors: a wafer-sort overvoltage pulse makes each dielectric weak spot conduct and locally oxidizes or vaporizes the electrode around it, isolating the defect so the dielectric can be thinned ~20%.
note: Clearing needs vented vaporization, which is hard inside high-AR holes; cleared cells lose capacitance.

title: Frequency-division wordline decoding with resonant driver gates
idea: Limit: zero logic gates in the row decoder. Each wordline-driver group is gated by a tiny resonant element (BAW or varactor tank) tuned to a unique frequency pair; the bank broadcasts two tones on one shared line, and only the group resonant at both rectifies enough voltage to fire, so address-to-frequency replaces the NAND decode tree.

title: Molten-salt electro-epitaxy grows wafers without Siemens or Czochralski
idea: Imposed scarcity: no polysilicon reactor and no crystal puller. Electrodeposit 300-700 um of single-crystal silicon from a KF-KCl-K2SiF6 molten salt at ~750 C onto a seed wafer capped with a weak porous-silicon release layer, then peel off the grown wafer and reuse the seed.
note: Electrodeposited Si from fluoride melts is mostly polycrystalline; device-grade single-crystal wafers are a big leap.

title: Idle U.S. silicon-carbide power fabs build hot-proof DRAM transistors
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: 4H-SiC's 3.26 eV bandgap keeps off-state leakage negligible even hot, so build the access transistor (or gain-cell write device) in 200 mm SiC power fabs left underused by the SiC glut, then hybrid-bond a silicon capacitor/periphery wafer on top.

title: Self-assembled tier stack: parallel block-copolymer lamellae + sequential infiltration synthesis [SPECULATIVE]
idea: A lamella-forming BCP (L0 25-40 nm) with preferential wetting on both interfaces orders parallel to the substrate after annealing, giving 25-80 alternating layers in a 1-2 um film. Sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O) converts the PMMA layers into AlOx sheets; the PS layers remain as sacrificial carbon tiers (removed later by oxidation, as in B2-10). A single hole etch then opens all tiers; lateral recess and ALD oxide-channel/gate fills proceed as in B2-09. Tier thickness is set by polymer molecular weight rather than deposition time.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous TiN sponge replaces smooth capacitor electrodes
idea: Substitute the smooth storage-node TiN with a nanoporous one: ALD a TiN/AlN nanolaminate electrode (TiCl4/TMA/NH3), selectively leach the Al phase in dilute NaOH/TMAH to leave a 3D sponge with 5-10 nm ligaments, then conformally coat with ALD ZrO2 and top TiN.
note: 5-10 nm pores leave no room for ZrO2 plus top TiN in a DRAM-pitch pillar; roughness raises leakage.

title: Mo wordline surface sulfurized into its own MoS2 channel
idea: Combine wordline and channel from one element: after each 3D tier's Mo wordline and an ALD HfO2 gate dielectric (Oregon hafnium), a thin Mo film on top is sulfurized below 450 C into 2-3-layer MoS2, giving a self-aligned, atomically thin access channel per tier.

title: NAND-grade LDPC replaces DRAM redundancy, fuses and laser repair
idea: Combine NAND flash's quasi-cyclic LDPC engine with DRAM. A rate-0.85 code in the base/buffer die absorbs a 1% raw cell BER, with a ~10 ns fast path for clean lines, so the DRAM die ships with no spare rows or columns, no fuse bank, no laser-repair pass and no repair-analysis test step.

title: Atmospheric mist-CVD oxide channels for error-tolerant gain cells
idea: Combine atmospheric ultrasonic mist-CVD, as used for Ga2O3 and solar TCOs, with 2T gain cells: the In-Ga-Zn-O-like channel is deposited without vacuum sputtering or ALD, and ~1% of cells with off-current outliers are absorbed by the code layer.

title: Thermochromic-window vanadium dioxide as a Mott-transition latch cell
idea: Smart-window coatings switch VO2 between insulator and metal. Adapt a strain-tuned nanoscale VO2 element in series with an access transistor, using the transition's hysteresis window to hold two stable resistance states, with vanadium recovered from US steel slag and refinery residues.
note: Room-temp transition and hold-bias power.

title: Catalyst regeneration: in-field thermal anneal heals aged DRAM
idea: Adapted from refineries that regenerate fouled catalyst with heat instead of replacing it: DIMMs carry a thin-film PCB heater and thermistor (board-level and trailing-node parts) and, during scheduled windows with data evacuated, bake their dies at ~150-175 C for about an hour to anneal interface traps and restore hydrogen passivation degraded by hot-carrier and hammer stress.
note: 150-175 C bakes give little Si-H re-passivation, but cheap to test on aged DIMMs.

title: Self-assembled BaTiO3 nanocube ink as a spin-coated high-k
idea: MAGNIFY permittivity by printing it: hydrothermally synthesized 10-15 nm single-crystal BaTiO3 nanocubes self-assemble from ink into dense superlattices on the bottom electrode, then an ALD infill densifies the film without high-temperature sintering, targeting k ~100-200.
note: 10-15 nm cubes exceed DRAM dielectric thickness; low-k infill drags k down.

title: Electrohydrodynamic jet printing of maskless periphery wiring
idea: Minify the mask count of interconnect layers to zero: multi-nozzle EHD jets print sub-100 nm silver/copper lines for periphery routing straight from CAD, so every wafer can carry custom wiring or repair routes.

title: Transistor-free crosspoint: printed threshold selector plus capacitor
idea: Minify the cell to 4F2 by printing crossed wordlines and bitlines, with a volatile Ag-filament threshold switch in series with a planar capacitor at each crossing as the access device.

title: Single ink whose function is set by laser dose
idea: Minify materials from six inks to one: print one In-Zn oxide precursor everywhere, then a laser dose map sets each region as conductor, semiconductor or insulator by controlling oxygen-vacancy density.

title: Eliminate deposited tunnel oxides: ligand shells set nanocrystal storage barriers
idea: Eliminate the deposited tunnel oxide: spin-cast monodisperse 4-nm Si or InP nanocrystals as storage nodes whose organic ligand shell (C8 vs C12 alkyl chains) is the tunnel barrier, so barrier width is fixed molecularly to ~0.1 nm and retention from ms to s is chosen by ligand length; writes tunnel in ns at ~1 V, with no vacuum tool or gas.
note: Organic ligands degrade under repeated tunneling; packing defects widen the tail.

title: Eliminate CMP before bonding: in-vacuum atomic diffusion bonding
idea: Stack tiers by sputtering a few nm of Ti or Au-free metal onto both surfaces in the same vacuum and pressing them together at room temperature (atomic diffusion bonding), with no CMP to 0.5 nm roughness and no wet surface activation.
note: Blanket metal films short hybrid interconnects.

title: Eliminate photoresist and PFAS: stamped-inhibitor area-selective deposition
idea: Microcontact-stamp a self-assembled inhibitor monolayer pattern from a reusable master onto the wafer; ALD then grows only on unstamped regions, forming hardmask lines directly with no resist, photoacid generator, developer or immersion topcoat.
note: Microcontact printing defectivity and overlay far from DRAM needs.

title: Electrocyte stack: parallel-store, series-read capacitor quartet
idea: Electric eels get high voltage by firing thousands of thin electrocytes in series. Each cell stores its bit on four small sub-capacitors charged in parallel, and at read three in-cell switches restack them in series so the bitline sees about 4x the voltage. Each sub-capacitor needs only ~1.3 fF at AR ~20, instead of one 5 fF pillar at AR 70.
note: Into a large bitline, series stacking delivers one sub-cap's charge; signal gain mostly vanishes.

title: Hopf-critical oscillator sense amp poised at edge of oscillation
idea: Cochlear outer hair cells sit near a Hopf bifurcation for huge gain on faint sound. A tiny oscillator is biased just below onset, so a few-mV bitline differential tips it into oscillation whose starting phase encodes the bit, captured by a flip-flop in ~2 ns. Proven on an open 130 nm shuttle with on-chip bitline/cell-cap replicas for <$1M in 24 months.

title: Silaffin-peptide biosilica as synthetic crucible-grade quartz
idea: Copy diatoms: silaffin-mimetic polyamine peptides (or cheap long-chain polyamines) precipitate amorphous silica at room temperature and neutral pH from silicic acid made by dissolving ordinary US industrial sand in base and purifying it by ion exchange first. The biosilica is sintered into the inner layer of fused-silica crucibles, so purity comes from solution chemistry instead of rare pegmatite quartz.
note: Base dissolution adds alkali; ppb purity via ion exchange is the doubt.

title: Coral electro-accretion: electrodeposited capacitor dielectric from water
idea: Biorock reefs grow mineral on a cathode straight from seawater. Generate base electrochemically at the TiN storage-node surface in an aqueous zirconyl/titanyl bath, so a conformal ZrO2-TiO2 film precipitates evenly down 70:1 holes and stops itself as it becomes insulating, then densify it with an anneal.

title: Chromatophore-shrink mastering makes nanoimprint templates without e-beam writers
idea: Squid chromatophores expand and contract pigment sacs elastically; write nanoimprint master patterns at 4x size with cheap i-line lithography on a resist atop a biaxially pre-stretched shape-memory polymer, release it so the relief shrinks 4x, then electroform a nickel or replicate a quartz daughter. Shrink distortion is measured once and pre-compensated in the 4x layout.

title: Mussel-foot catechol bonding of chiplets onto glass at room temperature
idea: Mussels stick to wet rock with DOPA catechol-metal coordination bonds. Memory chiplets are attached to a glass panel substrate with a catechol-functionalized adhesive that cures near room temperature, filled with conductive particles only over the pads, which avoids the CTE mismatch and warpage of 250-400 C bonding.

title: Lock-in chopper sense amp doubles cells per bitline
idea: As in a lock-in amplifier, cross-switches chop bitline vs reference at ~4 GHz during signal development; the preamp works in the modulated band and a demodulator feeds the latch, so SA offset and 1/f noise fall outside the signal band. Resolvable signal drops from ~80 mV to ~25 mV.
note: GHz chopping at bitline pitch adds charge-injection offset; offset-cancel SAs already exist.

title: Column-inversion storage cancels bitline coupling, like LCD panels
idea: LCD drivers alternate pixel polarity column by column to cancel crosstalk; store data in alternating true/complement polarity on adjacent bitlines and flip the pattern each row, so neighbour-swing coupling arrives common-mode at each sense amp and cancels, allowing tighter vertical-bitline pitch without shield lines.
note: Data-dependent bitline swings stay random under fixed inversion; coupling does not become common-mode.

title: Delay-line recirculation with decode-and-correct at every string lap
idea: Mercury delay lines regenerated every pulse on each lap; revive that in shift-register 3D strings: as data pass the string-foot regenerator, a short BCH codeword is decoded and rewritten corrected every lap (~1 us), so per-transfer and leakage errors of up to 1% per cell never accumulate.
note: Shifting every bit each ~1 us costs enormous energy at GB scale; ECC-per-lap concept is neat.

title: Apollo restart protection: recompute tensors instead of storing them perfectly
idea: Revive the Apollo guidance computer's restart groups, which recovered from faults by re-running from checkpoints: data in 1%-BER 3D memory carry a light detection code, and on a detected-uncorrectable error the runtime recomputes that tensor tile from its producer kernel instead of relying on heavy ECC.
note: At 1% BER nearly every line has errors, so detection would trigger recompute almost always.

title: Anderson's 1952 crossbar ferroelectric memory revived in hafnium-free AlBN
idea: Revive J.R. Anderson's transistor-less barium-titanate crossbar store using wurtzite aluminum-boron-nitride ferroelectric films (all abundant elements). Anderson's V/3 half-select scheme is combined with pulse shaping that exploits AlBN's very square loop to suppress disturb, and rows are read by switching current and then rewritten.

title: Langmuir-Blodgett colloid monolayers pattern hexagonal capacitor arrays
idea: Revive Deckman's 1982 natural lithography and the 1930s Langmuir-Blodgett trough: transfer a wafer-scale monolayer of 30-40 nm silica spheres, steered into register by coarse imprinted wells over the landing pads, shrink the spheres by wet etch, evaporate a metal mesh and lift off to leave a hexagonal hole mask transferred by metal-assisted chemical etching. DRAM capacitors are already hexagonally packed, so the colloid matches the layout.

title: Rutile TiO2 on MnO2 template replaces Hf/Zr and Ru
idea: Inverts 'high-k capacitors need Hf/Zr oxides on Ru electrodes.' Seed rutile-phase Al-doped TiO2 (k~90-120) on a thin rutile-structured beta-MnO2 template over TiN, so abundant Mn does the templating job RuO2 does today.
note: MnO2 is poorly conducting and thermally unstable; rutile TiO2 leakage is high. Cheap MIM test.

title: Refresh that shifts every row one slot, dissolving neighbors
idea: Inverts 'a row's physical neighbors are fixed': each refresh pass copies row i into row i+1 with in-subarray copy instead of restoring in place, then bumps a per-subarray offset register, so logical rows migrate continuously and no aggressor stays beside the same victim for more than one window.
note: Uniform one-slot shift preserves relative neighbors; aggressor and victim stay adjacent unless mapping is permuted.

title: Sugar cube: croconic-acid proton ferroelectric replaces fluoropolymer PVDF
idea: Stimulus 'sugar cube' (a crystal of small organic molecules) -> vapor-deposit croconic acid, a hydrogen-bonded organic ferroelectric (~20 uC/cm^2, highest among organics) whose polarization flips by proton transfer along H-bonds, as the storage layer of a BEOL cell at <150 C. It replaces PVDF-TrFE, the standard organic ferroelectric, which is a fluoropolymer.
note: Croconic acid is thermally fragile; DRAM-class endurance is unknown.

title: Sand dunes: phase-locked ion-beam ripples as maskless pitch multipliers
idea: Random stimulus 'sand dunes' -> off-normal low-energy ion bombardment self-organizes surface ripples at 15-30 nm wavelength. A coarse 193i grating locks their phase, as graphoepitaxy does, so each DUV period breaks up into 4-6 ordered ripples that serve as a line hardmask, from a blanket exposure.

title: Drum skin: printed relaxor terpolymer capacitors reach k about 50
idea: Random stimulus 'drum skin' -> PVDF films vibrate in speakers. Inkjet/slot-die printed P(VDF-TrFE-CFE) relaxor terpolymer runs in its slim-loop linear regime (no domain switching, so no wear) as a k~50 storage capacitor for printed memory cells.
note: Printed films are thick and relaxor k collapses at ns speeds; charge density claim unlikely.

title: Nanosphere monolayer defines both access pillars and capacitor posts
idea: Box: MIM charge x vertical Si pillar GAA x voltage sense amp x capacitor-over-pillar x Si x Langmuir-Blodgett colloidal monolayer. A close-packed polystyrene sphere layer is O2-plasma shrunk and used to etch hexagonal pillars; after gate ALD and planarization, the exposed pillar tops seed self-aligned capacitor posts, so one self-assembled layer sets the whole lattice with zero overlay.
note: Random colloidal domains cannot register to wordlines, bitlines and periphery.

title: Femtosecond-laser self-organized ripples write maskless wordline gratings
idea: Box: Si charge x lateral access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x laser-induced periodic surface structures. A scanned femtosecond laser on a thin hardmask film self-organizes ripples with period ~lambda/4 to lambda/2 (60-200 nm) through surface-plasmon interference, giving large-area line gratings transferred as wordline or bitline arrays without mask or resist.

title: Modules test and burn themselves in during shipping
idea: Po: the test floor is the delivery truck. Each module gets an on-board BIST controller plus small heater and supercapacitor so burn-in, march tests and retention profiling run in transit and at first boot, reporting back to the vendor; final tester insertions shrink to a quick screen.

title: Anodic electrochemical growth of capacitor dielectric replaces ALD precursors
idea: Worsen: build every capacitor dielectric atom by atom with costly, slow, single-sourced ALD precursors in vacuum tools. Flip: deposit a thin Ti or Ta-Ti electrode liner, then grow a barrier-type anodic TiO2/Ta2O5 dielectric electrochemically at room temperature in a wet cell. Anodic growth is self-limiting and conformal at any aspect ratio, with thickness set by voltage (~2 nm/V).
note: Isolated storage nodes cannot be biased for anodization; anodic films are leakier than ALD.

title: Confectioner's candy-like molecule: croconic acid ferroelectric memory
idea: Persona: a confectioner who knows sugar-acid crystals. Vacuum-sublime croconic acid (C5H2O5) into capacitor wells as the FeRAM dielectric and seal it with ALD Al2O3. This hydrogen-bonded organic ferroelectric switches by collective proton transfer (Ps ~20 uC/cm2) instead of ion displacement.

title: Embargo patterning: i-line stepper plus five spacer doublings
idea: A Soviet engineer denied scanners prints a 350 nm-pitch line grating on a 365 nm i-line stepper, then runs five self-aligned spacer-doubling loops (ALD oxide spacer, mandrel strip, repeat) to reach ~11 nm pitch, cutting lines with one coarse DUV trim mask; each loop needs only an ALD tool and an etcher.

title: Sea sponge chemistry: catalytic room-temperature silica gap fill
idea: Sea sponges build glass spicules at 10 C with silicatein enzymes. Tether biomimetic amine or peptide catalysts to trench walls so they polymerize silica (or titania) bottom-up from aqueous precursors at room temperature, filling isolation and inter-tier gaps without voids, then densify at <=400 C.

title: Fractal H-tree bitlines equalize RC across every tier
idea: Bring the scale-invariant branching of lungs and trees into the array: route bitlines as a 3D H-tree so every cell in a 64-tier subarray is the same wire length from its sense amp. Bitline capacitance per sense amp then grows ~sqrt(N) instead of N.

title: Time-to-threshold sensing on long vertical bitlines
idea: Shift the sense signal from voltage to time: each mat's vertical bitline is precharged and released, and a shared time-to-digital converter measures how many ns it takes to cross a threshold, a delay set by the cell's charge. Integrating over a longer window tolerates 2-3x higher bitline-to-cell capacitance ratios.
note: Passive 1T1C charge sharing gives fixed signal; time conversion adds no information without gain.

title: Crossbar sneak paths decoded as signal via multi-bias network inversion
idea: Selector-less resistive crossbars (HP, Crossbar Inc.) died because sneak currents corrupt reads in large arrays. Fix: read each small tile under K pseudo-random bias patterns and solve the resistor-network inverse problem (belief propagation / least squares) for every cell conductance, treating sneak current as known mixing rather than noise.

title: Low-melt alloy latent-heat pockets in HBM dummy-bump cavities
idea: Effect: latent heat of fusion. Sealed dummy-bump and dummy-TSV cavities are filled with a 60-70 C Bi-In-Sn eutectic that melts during compute bursts, clamping DRAM die temperature below the 85 C refresh-doubling threshold for tens of seconds and refreezing in idle. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
note: Dummy-bump cavity volume stores well under 1 J, buffering milliseconds, not tens of seconds.

title: Deuterium re-passivation anneal shrinks leakage tail of reject dies
idea: Effect: hydrogen-isotope passivation of Si/SiO2 dangling bonds (Pb centers). Bare reject DRAM dies or thinned wafers are annealed in a small tube furnace in 5-10% D2 at ~350-400 C; deuterium re-passivates the traps in junction depletion regions whose SRH generation current dominates the retention tail, and the dies are re-screened before resale.
note: Nitride passivation blocks D2 diffusion; tail is not only Pb centers.

title: Kirkendall-hollowed double-wall nanotube capacitors in each tier
idea: Kirkendall effect: lateral Ni or Cu nanowires are deposited in each tier and coated with an oxidizing or sulfiding shell, then annealed. Unequal diffusion hollows each wire into a tube, and both the inner and outer walls become electrode surface without any deep etch.
note: Kirkendall shells are poor dielectrics and inner-wall electrode access is unclear; ~1.8x area.

title: Croconic acid ferroelectric memory built only from carbon, hydrogen, oxygen
idea: Effect: croconic acid switches polarization (~20 uC/cm2, close to BaTiO3) by collective proton transfer along hydrogen-bonded chains at room temperature. Vacuum-sublime oriented films below 150 C as the last BEOL step and use them as the ferroelectric in FeFET or 1T-1C working memory.

title: Prussian-blue ion-insertion cells electroplated at room temperature
idea: Effect: ion migration and intercalation. K+ moves between a near-zero-strain Fe-hexacyanoferrate open framework and a solid electrolyte, changing the Fe3+/Fe2+ ratio and the conductance of a three-terminal channel. The film is electrodeposited from water at 25 C, and its battery-grade fast ion kinetics allow sub-us switching.

title: Zinc-magnesium-oxide ferroelectric tunnel junctions sputtered at room temperature
idea: Effect: polarization-modulated tunnel electroresistance. Wurtzite Zn(1-x)Mg(x)O (x~0.3) is ferroelectric as-deposited at room temperature; a 3-5 nm layer between asymmetric electrodes (TiN / n-ZnO) makes a tunnel junction whose barrier height follows the polarization, so a small read current senses the state without switching it.
note: High coercive field and limited endurance.

title: Silver-catalyzed wet etching carves damage-free, ultra-high-aspect access trenches
idea: Ag: use metal-assisted chemical etching, in which a DUV- or block-copolymer-patterned Ag film sinks into silicon in HF/H2O2, cutting vertical trenches and pillars at >100:1 aspect ratio with no plasma, ion damage or charging, for buried-wordline recesses and vertical channels.
note: Ag is a fast-diffusing deep-level lifetime killer in Si; contamination likely worsens the leakage tail.

title: Ti: oxidize the TiN electrode into its own rutile dielectric
idea: Instead of ALD-depositing ZrO2 and then a top electrode, convert the outer 4-6 nm of the TiN bottom electrode into rutile TiO2 (k~80-100) with an ozone/radical oxidation that co-incorporates Al from a pre-dosed monolayer to suppress leakage; one conversion step replaces hundreds of ALD cycles and is conformal at any AR.

title: K: KOH crystallographic etch digs ultra-high-aspect capacitor trenches
idea: On (110) silicon, anisotropic KOH/TMAH etching exposes vertical {111} sidewalls with >100:1 rate selectivity, so hardmask-defined trenches reach AR >100 on cheap wet benches instead of cryogenic plasma HAR etchers.
note: KOH {111} walls only give oriented parallelogram trenches; ~20 nm features and roughness doubtful.

title: Yuba-skimmed dielectric: peel atomically thin oxide skins off liquid metal
idea: Copy yuba (tofu-skin) making. A Ga-Hf liquid alloy grows a self-limiting HfO2-rich oxide skin ~1 nm thick, and touching a wafer to the surface prints that skin, pinhole-free, as the capacitor dielectric at near-room temperature.
note: 1 nm HfO2 leaks far too much for DRAM retention and cannot coat 3D structures.

title: Copper anode slime yields selenium-tellurium p-channel access transistors
idea: Copper refineries recover selenium and tellurium from anode slimes, and Utah produces both; evaporate SexTe1-x films below 200 C as p-channel transistors for BEOL-stacked gain cells, raising the bandgap to ~1 eV with selenium to hold leakage down, paired with an n-type zinc oxide device.
note: ~1 eV gap too leaky for long retention.

title: Kagome basket weave: one grating reticle exposed at three angles
idea: Like triaxial kagome basketry, expose the same line/space grating reticle three times at 0, 60 and 120 degrees (wafer rotated in the pre-aligner between passes) into a hardmask stack that opens only where all three space sets overlap, yielding a hexagonal storage-node hole array from one mask.

title: Rubber-stamp inhibitor printing: the one added master is a stamp
idea: Use a hard-PDMS stamp as the only added pattern master to microcontact-print an ALD inhibitor monolayer in the BEOL, then grow the oxide-semiconductor channel and gate dielectric by area-selective ALD only on unstamped areas, so the memory layer needs no resist, exposure or etch.

title: Score-and-snap glass cutting: notch mask guides crack-defined trenches
idea: Use the single added coarse mask only to place notch crack-starters in a tensile SiN film; a thermal shock then propagates straight, few-nm-wide cracks between notches like scoring and snapping glass, and the cracks are transferred as ultra-narrow cut trenches isolating wordlines or active areas.
note: Straight crack control over long runs at few-nm width is unproven at scale.

title: Cotton-candy electrospun nanofiber dielectric for interposer wiring
idea: Electrospin polyimide nanofiber mats, like spinning cotton candy, to form a mostly-air interlayer dielectric with k around 1.4 around interposer memory traces.
note: Fibrous mats cannot support 2 um lithographic wiring or CMP.

title: Engraver's acid: metal-assisted chemical etch revives deep trench capacitors
idea: Plate engravers bite designs with acid. Lift off Ag or Pt catalyst dots by i-line litho; in HF/H2O2 the catalyst sinks straight into silicon, carving holes at AR >100:1 with no plasma. Use this to revive the buried trench-capacitor cell, with catalyst stripping and gettering done before the transistors are built.
note: MACE gives high AR cheaply, but Ag/Pt residue kills retention and pores wander; trench cell scaling died for reasons.

title: Printed magnetoelectric composite written by voltage, not current
idea: IFR: magnetic bits written with zero current. Closest achievable: print magnetostrictive CoFe2O4 nanoparticles in piezoelectric P(VDF-TrFE); a voltage strains the matrix and rotates particle magnetization between two easy axes, read by a printed magnetoresistive sensor line.
note: Printed scale limits density; single-particle readout unrealistic.

title: Dithered sense amps detect signals smaller than their offset
idea: Ideal result: a sense amp immune to its own noise. Inject controlled random dither into the SA reference and fire 8 fast mini-decisions on the shared bitline; majority counting extracts signals well below the static offset (stochastic resonance).

title: Ceria-free planarization using UV-photocatalytic titania polishing pads
idea: Ideal: polishing with light instead of rare earths. Closest: embed anatase TiO2 in the CMP pad and illuminate through a transparent platen; photogenerated holes oxidize and soften Si/SiN/oxide surfaces so a dilute colloidal-silica slurry removes them, replacing CeO2 slurries in STI and ILD steps.
note: SiO2 cannot be further photo-oxidized; ceria's chemical tooth is hard to replace.

title: Thin the die, bias its back: backside retention-bias retrofit
idea: 10-person constraint: post-process purchased dies rather than run a fab. Thin commodity DRAM dies to ~20 um, deposit a backside contact, and add a package bond that applies negative substrate bias in standby. In processes where the array well couples to the substrate, the body effect raises access-transistor Vt and lowers standby leakage.

title: Self-limiting oxidation thins channels until quantum confinement widens bandgap
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: oxidize silicon pillars where stress makes oxidation stop at a ~2 nm core, so quantum confinement lifts the effective bandgap to ~1.6-2 eV; the final channel size is set by chemistry, not lithography.

title: Substitute vapor-deposited dry resist for spin-coat and aqueous develop
idea: Deposit metal-oxo (tin-oxide) photoresist from the vapor phase, expose, and develop it with a halide plasma in the same cluster tool, replacing spin coating, aqueous TMAH development and DI rinse.
note: Metal-oxide dry resist is already commercial.

title: Solderless copper-to-copper bonded stacks immune to intermetallic growth
idea: Minify the bond to 3 um-pitch direct Cu-Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonds in memory stacks, eliminating SnAg microbumps and organic underfill.

title: Lead-free solder playbook: molybdenum oxychloride wordlines end WF6 fluorine damage
idea: Electronics went lead-free in a coordinated material swap that ended up improving reliability. Replace WF6-deposited tungsten buried wordlines with molybdenum from MoO2Cl2 on a TiCl4-based TiN liner, plus a low-workfunction n+ poly cap on the storage-junction side (dual-workfunction gate), so no fluorine diffuses into the gate oxide and storage-side GIDL drops.
note: Mo wordlines and dual-workfunction buried gates are already in industry roadmaps.

title: WWII high-speed-steel swap: molybdenum replaces tungsten in wordlines
idea: During WWII tungsten shortages, toolmakers replaced T-series tungsten high-speed steels with M-series molybdenum steels that cut just as well. Replace W in buried wordlines, bitline contacts and periphery plugs with Mo from fluorine-free MoO2Cl2/MoCl5 precursors, whose shorter electron mean free path beats W below 15 nm; the die keeps its standard DDR5/HBM pinout, timing and JEDEC qualification.
note: Mo replacing W is already being adopted by DRAM makers.

title: Dry-erase resist patterns the array without developer baths
idea: Random stimulus 'dry-erase marker': mark and wipe with no liquid. Pattern the access-device critical layers (active area, buried wordline, storage contact) with vapor-deposited metal-oxide EUV resist that is dry-developed and stripped in plasma, so there is no spin coat, TMAH develop, DI rinse or wet strip.
note: Metal-oxide dry resist already commercialized.

title: Termite mound: ballroom-free fab with clean air only inside tools
idea: Stimulus 'termite mound' (passive ventilation conditions only the nursery chambers) -> seal each process tool in its own HEPA micro-environment, move wafers only in N2-purged pods on enclosed rails, downgrade the open fab to ISO 8 and dump tool heat into earth-coupled loops.
note: Minienvironments and FOUPs already standard; further ballroom downgrade is incremental.

title: Club sandwich: hybrid-bonded SRAM decks swallow activations
idea: Stack more layers in the sandwich: hybrid-bond (<300 C) 2-4 dense SRAM dies onto the accelerator, sized to keep a full transformer block's activations and the hottest KV pages on-package so they never spill to HBM.

title: Angled ion beams stretch features, deleting cut masks
idea: Po: the etcher does the lithography. Add tilted, directional ion-beam pattern-shaping chambers to existing etch bays so one exposure's holes are elongated or trimmed in a chosen direction, merging contacts or cutting lines without a second litho-etch pass.

title: One-brain package: CPU and accelerator share memory, no staging copies
idea: Po: the CPU and the accelerator are the same animal. CPU and accelerator dies co-packaged with Foveros in New Mexico share one coherent pool of U.S.-made DRAM, eliminating duplicate pinned host buffers, dataloader staging copies and host-side mirrors of device tensors.

title: Active mature-node interposer packed with SRAM becomes the L4
idea: Worsen: waste a 2,500 mm^2 silicon interposer as passive copper. Flip: make the interposer an active 28-16 nm die from U.S. mature fabs, filled with SRAM banks under the routing, so the passive area becomes ~1-2 GB of latch-based buffer between HBM and logic.
note: Active base dies with large cache already ship.

title: Imports cost 2x: back-end-first U.S. onshoring ladder
idea: Self-imposed limit: tariffs double the cost of finished imports. Import wafers, and run die sort, stacking, TSV reveal and HBM assembly in the U.S. first. Each step funds the next until the front end follows.
note: Already underway with U.S. HBM packaging plants.

title: Grid-interconnect priority for zero-refresh data centers
idea: Worse: let memory refresh burn scarce grid megawatts. Flip: utilities and regulators grant interconnection-queue priority and lower demand charges to data centers certified to run zero-refresh working memory.
note: Refresh is a tiny share of datacenter power; presupposes refresh-free memory.

title: Substitute one-way STT read currents with disturb-immune state encoding
idea: STT read current can only disturb one state (e.g., P to AP in the read direction); store each word with an inversion flag chosen so most cells sit in the immune state, and keep flags in larger high-barrier MTJs.

title: Local wordline decoders with embedded antifuse tags for repair
idea: Give every local row decoder a tiny antifuse-programmed address-tag comparator, so any spare row in a mat answers for a failed address directly; the central fuse bank, fuse-broadcast bus and redundancy-compare stage are deleted, because the decoder and the repair CAM are now one cell.

title: Landing pad and capacitor bottom electrode become one TiN body
idea: Combine the tungsten landing pad and the bottom electrode (zero added masks, same landing-pad mask): pattern the pads in TiN and grow the electrode cylinder conformally from them, so there is no W/TiN interface and no WF6 fill.

title: Single stitch-metal mask harvests independent quarter-dies at wafer edge
idea: Combine a tiled die with wafer-edge recovery: the die is built as four self-sufficient quadrants, and the one added top-metal stitch mask ties them into a full die in complete fields while edge partial fields are left as independent quarter-capacity dies.

title: Certified Fluorine-Free DRAM label funded by green bonds
idea: Combine an independent PFAS-free fab certification (audited chemical inventory, effluent testing) with green-bond financing and EU and automotive buyers who face the EU universal PFAS restriction and pay a 5-10% premium for certified memory.

title: Panel laser-and-inkjet repair replaces fuse-based redundancy
idea: Borrowed from OLED and LCD line-repair stations: bitlines or wordlines found defective by in-line test are laser-cut and bridged to spare lines with inkjet-printed silver jumpers, so the glass memory needs no fuse banks or redundancy address comparators.
note: Niche to glass-panel memory.

title: Green-building LEED rating applied to memory supply chains
idea: LEED made builders compete on green features; create a 'chokepoint-free memory' rating that scores DRAM by banned-element content (Hf, Ru, Co, W, Ta, In, Ga), helium use and quartz source, and tie federal and hyperscaler purchase preference and accelerated depreciation to higher grades.

title: Print to the edge: sell the wafer rim as high-BER dies
idea: Reverse the edge exclusion: pattern and keep dies out to ~1 mm from the wafer edge, where uniformity is worst, and sell the rim dies with raw BER up to 1% under stronger ECC.

title: Three low-aspect capacitors vote as one via triple-row activation
idea: Reverse one strong cell into three weak ones: with fluorocarbon high-AR oxide etch banned, capacitors are built at ~20:1 in an amorphous-carbon mold patterned by O2 plasma (ZrO2 from amide ALD, TiN from TiCl4); each bit is written to 3 rows and read by activating all 3 at once, so charge sums on the bitline and one failed cell is outvoted.
note: A 3x cell count cannot be offset by cheaper etch.

title: Disposable two-year DRAM tier for checkpointed AI clusters
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap short-living objects: a U.S.-made memory SKU designed for 2-year service in AI training racks with frequent checkpoints skips long burn-in and 10-year aging guardbands, ships with in-field error telemetry, and is swapped and recycled like a consumable.

title: Born hot: bond and stress-trim stacks at their 125 C working point
idea: Thermophiles fold correctly only at their growth temperature; do final hybrid bonding and stress trimming (tuned SiN stressor films) of the 3D DRAM stack with the zero-stress point set at ~125 C, so in service the stack sits near its relaxed state instead of under sustained thermo-mechanical stress.

title: Cofactor plasticity: recipes that swap tungsten, molybdenum or ruthenium
idea: Archaea swap W and Mo into the same enzyme scaffold depending on what the environment offers. Qualify every DRAM metal fill (wordline, contacts, bitline plugs) as a family that can run W, Mo or Ru in the same ALD chamber with a shared barrier and anneal, so a fab can switch metals within weeks as prices or embargoes move.

title: Plasmid-style updatable row-hammer defenses extend old dense DRAM
idea: Bacteria swap plasmids to gain new resistances; the CXL or buffer controller carries an embedded FPGA region whose hammer-tracking logic is updated over the air as new access patterns emerge, so vulnerable modules are patched rather than replaced.

title: Avogadro-sphere isotopic silicon-28 epi cools hot HBM stacks
idea: The kilogram redefinition and spin-qubit research use centrifuge-enriched silicon-28, which carries heat better without isotope scattering. Grow the HBM base-die and core-die device epi from 28SiH4 enriched in repurposed gas centrifuges, improving lateral heat spreading inside the stack while the HBM interface stays standard.

title: Integrated-passive-device fabs supply ready-made trench capacitor wafers
idea: Borrowed from smartphone silicon capacitors (IPD trench caps, ~1 pF/um2) made in old 200 mm fabs: a 10-person team designs a cell-pitch trench-capacitor array, buys the wafers from an IPD foundry, buys transistor wafers from a foundry shuttle and has an OSAT hybrid-bond them; the team owns only design, integration and test.

title: Dekatron token ring scans refresh with no counter or decoder
idea: Dekatron counting tubes moved a glow one cathode per pulse. Thread a one-hot token through a 2-transistor dynamic shift chain built into the sub-wordline driver stripe, like an LCD gate driver. Each refresh pulse fires the token's row and passes the token on, so refresh needs no address counter, no internal address mux and no decoder toggling. Zero masks added.

title: Trench-DRAM revival: HBr/Cl2 deep-trench etch makes fluorine-free TSVs
idea: Repurpose the abandoned IBM/Siemens/Qimonda trench-capacitor deep-silicon etch (HBr/O2/Cl2, AR ~50:1) to etch 5 x 30 um TSVs in thinned DRAM, with SiBrxOy sidewall passivation in place of Bosch fluorocarbon polymer.

title: Early FeRAM imprint fix revived: periodic polarity flips cancel sense-amp aging
idea: Early FeRAMs fought imprint, where a cell held in one state too long comes to prefer it, and periodic inverted rewriting was a classic remedy. DRAM sense-amp latches age asymmetrically (BTI drift) when data sit unchanged for months at high temperature, so every N refresh epochs each row is rewritten inverted under a per-row polarity bit and both latch halves age equally.

title: Kerf-resident test periphery lives in scribe lanes
idea: Test-only circuits (BIST engines, test compression, probe pads) are used once but occupy die forever. Place them in the 60-100 um scribe lanes, wired to each die through traces that are severed at dicing, leaving only a minimal test port on the die.
note: 2-4% area; in-field BIST still needed.

title: Ping-pong sense-enable drivers reverse current for electromigration healing
idea: Black's law makes Cu EM life ~19x shorter at 125 C than 85 C (Ea~0.9 eV), forcing wide SAN/SAP rails. Drive these rails from alternating ends on successive activations so current direction reverses, giving AC-like bidirectional stress with ~10x longer EM life.

title: Automotive-grade MTJ storage holds trims and repair maps
idea: Floating-gate and charge-trap trims lose charge at 125 C, and e-fuses are one-shot. Store sense trims, timing codes and repair addresses in high-barrier MTJs (thermal stability Delta > 80, already qualified for 10 y at 150 C) beside the periphery, rewritable for in-field repair.

title: Laser-CVD wafer repair of interconnect opens, borrowed from displays
idea: First principle: an open in an upper metal line is just ~10^9 missing atoms, which laser-induced chemical vapor deposition can add precisely, as LCD panel lines are repaired today. After wafer probe, locate opens and shorts in the top metal and redistribution layers, then write or cut them at laser-CVD and ablation stations.

title: Hafnium-free periphery transistors with zirconium-silicate gate dielectrics
idea: DRAM periphery needs EOT ~1.2-1.5 nm, not logic's ~0.8 nm, so HfO2's k~25 is overkill: ZrSiOx (k~12-18) or ZrO2/SiON with TiN gates meets the leakage spec. Qualify a Hf-free periphery high-k metal-gate module fed from widely mined zircon (ZrSiO4).

title: Rosetta stone: dual-technology copies with uncorrelated hot failure modes
idea: Critical data (page tables, ECC metadata, kernel) is written in two 'scripts': once in 1T1C DRAM and once in an oxide-channel gain-cell region whose temperature failure mechanism differs, with per-copy ECC arbitrating any mismatch.

title: Scrap-yard LRDIMM: data buffers steer around dead banks
idea: An embargoed engineer rebuilds working machines from rejects. Dies whose only failure is one bank's sense-amp stripe or decoder are paired on an LRDIMM with a spare die; the RCD and data buffers redirect that bank's commands and DQ lanes to the spare, so the host sees a normal DDR5 rank.

title: Billboard painter's giant canvas: idle display fabs print memory panels
idea: A billboard painter works big and coarse. A 10-person team designs oxide-TFT gain-cell arrays for idle Gen-6 display lines. A 1.5 m2 panel at 1.5 um rules holds ~5e10 bits (~6 GB), and it is diced into tiles bonded to logic as a slow bulk tier.
note: $30/GB exceeds DDR5 contract price.

title: Aviation regulator: certify printed memory by error class, not perfection
idea: An aviation certifier grades components by how they fail, not whether they fail: a JEDEC-style qualification ladder for printed and roll-to-roll memory (raw-BER class, fault-geometry class, drift class, required host ECC/redundancy profile), backed by a U.S. test lab funded under CHIPS, lets system makers design in imperfect printed tiers with guaranteed post-correction reliability.

title: Silicon-flux SiO desorption replaces HF-last cleans before epitaxy
idea: Extreme user: space-qualified MBE lines that clean in vacuum without wet chemistry. Remove native oxide by co-dosing a silicon beam/silane at ~750C so Si + SiO2 leaves as volatile SiO, followed in situ by epitaxy, with no hydrofluoric acid at all.

title: $1-IoT repairless DRAM: no fuses, no spares, a bad-row map
idea: Ultra-cheap IoT parts cannot afford repair. Remove laser and e-fuse repair, spare rows and columns, and the repair test insertion from the die. Instead, store the bad-row list measured at test in a tiny OTP block that the host reads at boot, and map around those rows in page tables.
note: Many IoT hosts lack MMUs; yield loss offsets the area saving.

title: Natick-style fail-in-place pods: sealed nitrogen memory sleds, never serviced
idea: Microsoft's sealed undersea datacenter had one-eighth the server failure rate of a land control group and was never touched by technicians. Build sealed, dry-nitrogen DDR5 memory sleds overprovisioned by 15% with rank sparing. The controller retires failing DIMMs in place, and the sled is swapped only at 5-year end of life.

title: Tile-architecture dies that survive wafer-edge truncation
idea: Edge case on the wafer itself: partial reticle shots at the rim are scrapped. Lay out DRAM as independently addressed tiles, each with its own I/O hub tap, so a truncated edge die still works as a half- or quarter-capacity part binned as a lower-density SKU.

title: Container Minimal-Fab for legacy and rad-hard DRAM
idea: Forward bases and space stations want on-site fabrication, and Japan's Minimal Fab runs half-inch wafers in sealed tabletop tools without a cleanroom building. A 10-person team runs a ~40-tool container line making 0.5-1 um trench DRAM for discontinued legacy sockets and rad-hard niches.
note: Half-inch Minimal Fab output is tiny; rad-hard niche only.

title: Hammer-immune coarse-pitch DUV memory sold as secure tier
idea: No EUV: hammer thresholds rise steeply with wordline pitch, so 25-30 nm-class DUV DRAM has thresholds of ~50k+ activations. Scale/time shift (old node reframed as security feature): market it as a premium hammer-immune tier for multi-tenant clouds and confidential computing.

title: Ti: titanium getter ring in hybrid-bond seal absorbs moisture
idea: Pattern a Ti/Zr getter line inside the hybrid-bonding seal ring of each stacked DRAM die so moisture and stray hydrogen entering through dicing edges are chemisorbed before reaching TSV liners and capacitor dielectrics.

title: R744 car-AC playbook: CO2 replaces Fluorinert in chuck chillers
idea: Automakers moved air conditioning from fluorinated refrigerants to transcritical CO2 (R744); do the same for etch and CVD chuck temperature control by running direct-expansion CO2 microchannels inside the chuck base instead of pumping perfluorinated heat-transfer fluid from separate chillers.

title: Pharma flow chemistry: fab-side microreactors brew ALD precursors
idea: Pharma replaced batch kettles with continuous-flow microreactors; synthesize Zr, Hf, Mo and Al ALD precursors beside the fab from Oregon zirconium and hafnium chlorides and Gulf Coast amines in skid-scale flow reactors with inline distillation, delivered by pipe instead of shipped cylinders.

title: Watertight-bulkhead subarrays with current-limit breakers contain metal shorts
idea: Ships survive hull breaches through watertight bulkheads; since argon-free metallisation (N2-reactive or CVD/ALD-only with no Ar PVD) can raise particle and short rates, give each subarray its own power and wordline-pump domain behind a self-resetting current-limit switch, so one short is isolated and the mat is retired instead of sinking the die.

title: Atom-switch rewiring makes decoder redundancy field-reprogrammable
idea: Ideal result: wiring that can be redrawn after shipment. Place Cu-ion bridge (atom) switches in the BEOL between decoder outputs and spare wordline drivers; a field repair command forms or dissolves bridges to remap any row to any spare, repeatedly.
note: NanoBridge exists; field repair is a niche gain.

title: Sand-battery thermal storage time-shifts fab furnaces to cheap solar
idea: Ideal: a fab powered by free sunshine. Closest: charge a resistively heated sand/firebrick thermal store (600-1000 C) with midday solar surplus, use it to preheat furnace, epi and abatement gases and drive absorption chillers overnight, and schedule flexible batch steps (diffusion, anneal, reclaim) into low-price hours.

title: Display-fab DRAM: oxide memory tiles on Gen-8.5 glass panels
idea: Under 400 C, display IGZO lines (all at or below 350 C) pattern stacked oxide 1T1C arrays on 2.2x2.5 m glass at about 1.5 um rules, using thick-film capacitors. Panels are diced into memory tiles that are bonded under logic as capacity tiers.
note: 1.5 um rules give ~1000x lower density; panel area cannot close the cost-per-bit gap.

title: Hot-swap chamber liner cassettes eliminate NF3 in-situ cleans
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero NF3 or fluorinated chamber-clean gas. Build ALD/CVD chamber walls from robot-swappable liner cassettes; after N wafers, swap in a fresh cassette in minutes and strip the dirty one offline in a closed-loop alkaline electrochemical bath that recovers the TiN and ZrO2 deposits.

title: Substitute hydrocarbon dielectric fluids for PFAS heat-transfer fluids
idea: Swap perfluoropolyether and fluoroketone fluids in etch-chamber chillers and burn-in/test handlers for hydrogenated polyalphaolefin or synthetic isoparaffin fluids rated -40 to +150 C, run in nitrogen-blanketed sealed reservoirs to manage flammability.

title: Substitute atomic hydrogen radicals for sulfuric-peroxide resist strips
idea: Strip implant-hardened photoresist with downstream remote-plasma atomic hydrogen followed by a short UV-ozone polish, replacing SPM (piranha) baths and their hot DI rinses.

title: Controller-held repair map replaces on-die fuse banks
idea: Write wafer-test repair results to the module SPD EEPROM; at boot the memory controller loads the bad-row/column map into its own address-translation table and steers accesses to spare rows exposed as ordinary addresses, so the DRAM die drops laser/e-fuse banks and redundancy-compare logic.

title: Gasless copper self-sputtering seeds high-aspect TSVs without argon
idea: Combine HiPIMS with sustained self-sputtering: above a threshold target power density ionized Cu atoms sustain the discharge on their own, so after brief ignition with N2 or H2 the process runs on copper vapor only, and the highly ionized flux is steered by substrate bias deep into 10:1 TSVs for conformal seeds.

title: Soybean transformer oil replaces fluorinated fluids in fab chillers
idea: Adapted from utility transformers, which moved to natural-ester fluids (soy-based, high flash point, biodegradable), and from avionics polyalphaolefin coolants. Use stabilized ester/PAO blends as the heat-transfer fluid in etch-chuck and tool chillers instead of perfluoropolyether (Galden) and hydrofluoroether (Novec) fluids.

title: PCB-etchant electrolytic regeneration recycles persulfate cleaning chemistry on site
idea: PCB shops electrolytically regenerate spent cupric-chloride etchant instead of buying new. Adapt this to wafer cleaning: electrolyze spent sulfuric cleaning streams on boron-doped-diamond anodes to regenerate peroxydisulfuric acid as the oxidant in a closed loop at each wet bench.

title: ACSR power-line composite conductors replace tungsten array lines
idea: Overhead power lines pair conductive aluminum with a strong steel core. Adapt this for a capacitor-free BEOL array: wordlines and bitlines are Al cores with a 1-2 nm Mo or TiN skin that blocks electromigration and diffusion, which works because capacitor-free BEOL cells never exceed ~400 C.

title: Stainless-steel self-passivation: copper-manganese self-forming barriers
idea: Stainless steel protects itself as chromium segregates into a thin oxide; use a Cu-Mn alloy seed so on anneal Mn migrates to the dielectric and forms a ~2 nm MnSixOy barrier, eliminating the TaN/Ta barrier PVD steps in DRAM copper wiring.

title: Aerospace additive manufacturing for domestic fab tool spare parts
idea: Adapted from GE printing jet-engine fuel nozzles: 3D-print fab consumables and spares in U.S. plants, such as binder-jet SiC focus rings, ceramic showerheads, ESC parts and gas manifolds, qualified tool by tool.

title: Parametron revival: bits as phase of MEMS parametric oscillators
idea: MINIFY Goto's 1954 ferrite parametron to ~5-um AlN resonators from a MEMS foundry: a 2f pump makes each resonator oscillate at f with phase 0 or pi (the bit), held while pumped and copied by coupling; majority-vote coupling adds in-memory logic.
note: MEMS parametron bit storage demonstrated 2008; micron size.

title: Magnify old ideas: buy dormant trench-capacitor DRAM IP
idea: Acquire dormant legacy trench-capacitor DRAM patents and design data at distressed prices, then adapt the deep-trench array to a U.S. specialty foundry's existing deep-trench module for a niche legacy-DRAM product.

title: Flash-lamp photonic curing makes ceramic dielectrics on plastic
idea: Minify thermal budget with millisecond xenon flash pulses that heat only the printed film to ~1000 C, sintering dense oxide dielectrics and conductors on a polymer web without damaging it.

title: Minify charged cells with per-burst data-inversion coset flags
idea: Store 1-3 coset bits per 64-byte burst and, at write time, pick the inversion/coset that leaves the fewest cells in the charged, leakage-vulnerable state, accounting for true-cell versus anti-cell layout.

title: Eliminate metal etching: anodization-defined aluminum periphery wiring
idea: Deposit blanket Al, mask the line regions with PAG-free DNQ/novolak i-line resist, and anodize the exposed metal fully into Al2O3 in citric or boric acid. The converted oxide becomes the insulator between lines, giving a planar wiring level with no metal etch, no gap fill and no CMP.

title: Store the bit as a shape: snap-through buckled polysilicon beams
idea: Rearrange storage from charge to geometry: a compressively stressed 2 um polysilicon micro-bridge (1990s surface micromachining) buckles up or down; electrodes above and below snap it between states in ~50-100 ns and a capacitive pickoff reads the gap, with no contact so no stiction or wear.
note: Niche harsh-environment memory at 4 um2/bit.

title: Rotate the wafer, reuse one grating mask for wordlines and bitlines
idea: Rearrange the layout: design wordline and bitline layers as identical line/space gratings, and print both from the same reticle by rotating the wafer 90 degrees between the two exposures.

title: Move decoupling off the DRAM die into the interposer
idea: Rearrange where charge reservoirs live: deposit high-k ALD (HfO2/ZrO2) MIM or deep-trench capacitors in the interposer directly under each memory die's power bumps, so the DRAM die can drop most of its on-die decap.

title: Persistent-current superconducting loops on sapphire for cryogenic racks
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: below Tc a superconducting loop's circulating current never decays, so retention is infinite. Patterned NbN or NbTiN nanowire loops on sapphire store a bit as clockwise or counter-clockwise flux, written and read through nanowire cryotrons (nTrons), giving byte-addressable cryogenic memory for superconducting logic and 4 K quantum-control systems.

title: Electrochemical hydrogen pump recycles EUV scanner hydrogen
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: route each EUV scanner's source and collector hydrogen exhaust (hundreds of slm) through a tin trap and a proton-exchange electrochemical hydrogen pump. The pump compresses and purifies the H2 and returns it to the scanner feed, so the tool supplies most of its own hydrogen.

title: Back-grind swarf from HBM thinning recycled into silicon feedstock
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: grinding HBM core dies from 775 um to ~40 um turns ~95% of each wafer (~120 g) into fine swarf. Collect it in a dedicated closed DI loop, strip the oxide shell with HF, and plasma-melt it into silicon feedstock for CZ recharge or solar.

title: Electrolytically regenerated persulfate replaces sulfuric-peroxide wet strip
idea: TRIZ #38 Strong oxidants: replace single-pass SPM (H2SO4 + H2O2) resist strip and organic clean with an electrolyzed-sulfuric loop. Boron-doped-diamond anodes continuously regenerate peroxodisulfate from the same acid, so it is recirculated instead of drained.

title: Spinel and AlON plasma-facing coatings replace rare-earth yttria
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: coat etch-chamber walls, liners and focus parts with a graded stack: dense MgAl2O4 spinel or AlON at the plasma face, grading to Al2O3 at the substrate. Each layer is placed where its erosion resistance or adhesion is needed, replacing Y2O3 and YF coatings.

title: Murray's-law tapered vascular power grids cut tungsten in tall stacks
idea: Size the vertical and lateral power and wordline-strap trees of a 3D DRAM like blood vessels obeying Murray's law (parent r^3 = sum of child r^3), with thick Cu 'arteries' tapering to thin Mo/Ru 'capillaries' only at cell level, instead of uniform tungsten straps everywhere.

title: Trehalose glass: vitrified nanolaminate dielectrics resist decade-long crystallization
idea: Tardigrades and resurrection plants vitrify trehalose into a glass that will not crystallize when hot; build the tier capacitor and inter-tier insulators from Al2O3/HfO2/La2O3 nanolaminates with sublayers below crystallization thickness so they stay amorphous through 10 yrs at 125 C, with no grain boundaries forming as leakage paths.

title: Acidithiobacillus bioleaching loop for scrapped DIMMs and fab sludge
idea: Run a bioreactor chain: Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans leaches Cu and Ni from shredded modules, cyanogenic Chromobacterium then recovers gold, and engineered tungstate-binding TupA proteins capture W and Mo from CMP and etch sludge.

title: Murray's-law tapered conductors cut metal use in arrays and grids
idea: Blood vessels and leaf veins follow Murray's law (radius cubed conserved at branches), minimizing material for a given flow. Lay out power meshes, wordline straps and bitline tapers with Murray-style branching, thick near drivers and thin at tips, instead of uniform-width lines.

title: Spider-web electret nanofibre ULPA filters without PTFE
idea: Spider webs pull in charged particles electrostatically. Electrospin roll-to-roll cellulose-acetate or polylactide nanofibre mats carrying a permanent electret charge as fab ULPA media, replacing expanded-PTFE membranes.
note: Electret charge decays; ULPA media already largely glass fiber.

title: Hand-warmer phase-change wax keeps HBM below the 85C refresh cliff
