idea: A 2050 engineer builds periphery upward. Grow four monolithic BEOL tiers of MoS2 (n) and WSe2 (p) CMOS above the array; each tier hosts sense amps for one in four bitlines, relaxing SA pitch 4x and freeing the silicon footprint.

title: Biologist's cortical minicolumns: 16-cell bitlines with private sense amps
idea: The cortex scales by repeating short minicolumns. Split the 3D array into 16-32-cell local bitlines; a 4x4 bundle of them is muxed in the array tier onto one hybrid bond to a sense amp in a CMOS wafer below.
note: Sense-amp area cannot fit under so few cells.

title: Skyscraper architect's sky lobbies: periphery tiers every 32 floors
idea: Tall towers use sky lobbies so no elevator runs the full height. Every 32 array tiers, insert a laser-crystallized Si or oxide CMOS 'lobby' tier holding local tier decoders and wordline drivers. Global lines only reach lobbies, and each staircase spans just 32 steps.

title: TV maker's view: DRAM gain-cell tiles on idle Gen-10.5 display lines
idea: A display engineer notes that LCD/OLED fabs already process 9 m2 glass at <=350 C with oxide-TFT tools, and many sit idle. Add panel-scale nanoimprint for ~100 nm features, build 2T0C oxide-semiconductor gain-cell arrays at <=350 C on Gen-10.5 glass, and cut them into memory tiles for CXL far memory, attaching periphery chiplets.

title: Newspaper pressman: roll-to-roll gain-cell memory sheets on steel foil
idea: A pressman prints kilometers of paper per hour. Run planarized stainless or Invar foil through a roll-to-roll line of atmospheric spatial-ALD heads (<=250 C), roll-to-roll UV nanoimprint and web plasma etch to build oxide-semiconductor gain-cell sheets, then cut and laminate the sheets into memory slabs.

title: Alien's question: grow memory tiers on the processor wafer's backside
idea: An alien asks why memory and compute come from different factories. After a GPU wafer finishes its front side and backside power network, deposit 4-16 tiers of <=400 C oxide-semiconductor gain-cell memory straight onto the backside, joined by nano-TSVs and built with the same backside tool set.
note: Hot logic under the memory worsens OS gain-cell retention.

title: Child's floor carpet: TSV-free edge-bonded planar memory tiling
idea: As a child asks 'why stack the blocks when the floor is empty?': tile plain, TSV-free DRAM dies edge-to-edge in a ring around the accelerator on a glass panel and join neighbours by sidewall hybrid bonds at 2 um pitch on the polished die edges, forming a planar 'memory carpet' with die-to-die relay links.
note: Sidewall hybrid bonding at 2 um is unproven; relay hops add energy.

title: Dual-bit cell stores capacitor charge and floating-body charge together
idea: Million-token AI contexts are capacity-starved, so one counter-doping implant mask isolates a floating p-pocket under each access transistor; the cell keeps one bit as capacitor charge and a second as body holes that shift threshold. Reads first sense the body bit by current at an intermediate wordline level, then charge-share the capacitor bit.

title: CCD charge-transfer bitline segments feeding a tiny sense node
idea: Astronomical CCDs move charge packets with 99.9999% efficiency instead of sharing them; each bitline is split into 8-16 clocked transfer gates that shift the cell's packet to a ~0.3 fF floating diffusion at the SA rather than dumping it onto a 50-100 fF bitline. The SA sees roughly 10x the voltage of conventional charge sharing.

title: Vertical CCD charge-shift strings as append-only KV-cache memory
idea: An AI KV-cache is written once in order and read back as a stream, so build a 3D-NAND-like vertical string but run it as a charge-coupled device: 128 stacked gate tiers around one channel pass charge packets along the string by 3-phase clocking to a single sense node at the top. There is no per-cell access transistor, capacitor or contact; a bit is just one gate crossing.
note: Same vertical CCD string, framed for append-only KV cache traffic.

title: Mars-colony do-everything single chamber for regional DRAM minifabs
idea: Extreme user: a Mars colony that can land one tool, not 400. A reconfigurable plasma chamber with swappable gas manifolds and an in-situ ALD head runs etch, deposition, clean and anneal sequentially on one wafer; a minifab of 30 such chambers plus one scanner trades throughput for a 10x smaller tool count.

title: MRI-safe metal-free stack: optical vias through silicon at 1310 nm
idea: MRI-compatible implants must avoid metal paths. Silicon is transparent above 1.1 um, so give each die in a stack aligned micro-emitter and germanium photodiode arrays and pass data vertically through the dies as light; only power needs vias.

title: Venus-lander electronics: SiC access transistors for refresh-free cells
idea: NASA's SiC JFET circuits have run for weeks at 460 C because SiC's intrinsic carrier density is ~10^19 times lower than silicon's. Bond a thin 4H-SiC (or beta-Ga2O3) access-transistor layer onto a silicon periphery wafer, so each cell's off-state leakage is in the attoamps and retention lasts minutes to hours even at 125 C.
note: SiC/Ga2O3 interface quality and layer transfer at DRAM pitch are big unknowns.

title: Heteroepitaxial 3C-SiC access pillar: retention from milliseconds to hours
idea: Time shift through bandgap: grow the vertical access-channel pillars as 3C-SiC (Si and C only, N/Al dopants) on the Si wafer; SiC's intrinsic carrier density (~1e-1 cm^-3 versus 1e10 for Si) suppresses generation and band-to-band leakage by >10 decades, so retention becomes limited by the capacitor dielectric instead of the transistor.
note: 3C-SiC on Si is defect-laden; traps would dominate generation, not ni.

title: Silicon charge racetrack: CCD loops that refresh by moving
idea: Time shift: rather than holding charge still and refreshing it, data circulates as charge packets in short buried-channel CCD loops (e.g., 16 bits per vertical pillar) clocked at ~1-2 GHz with a regenerative re-inject stage per loop, so every bit is restored each ~10 ns loop and random access waits <=8 ns on average; silicon replaces magnetic racetrack's Co/Pt.

title: Gallium-oxide access-transistor arrays bonded onto silicon periphery
idea: Material jump with a time jump to years of retention: 4.8 eV-gap beta-Ga2O3 transistors, grown on native substrates and layer-transferred, form the cell array with off-currents below 10^-21 A, and the slower array is read through time-domain integrating sense amps on a bonded Si CMOS wafer; no refresh circuitry is built.
note: Ga2O3 at DRAM pitch and layer transfer are unproven.

title: One-shot ferroelectric shadow freezes rows before charge leaks
idea: Time-shift between two storage physics: the capacitor stack has a thin HZO layer left untouched during DRAM-speed use, and when a row's age counter passes ~half its retention one pulse copies the charge state into polarization, after which charge may leak freely; the next read senses polarization switching current and returns the row to charge mode.
note: Dual-mode HZO NV-DRAM is known art; copying charge to polarization needs coercive voltage at the cell.

title: Thermally isolated array tier cooled by microfluidics
idea: Scale-shift the thermal stack: the array wafer bonds to the hot periphery/logic wafer through sparse Cu pillars across a vacuum gap and is cooled from its own backside by microfluidic channels on 10 C rack chilled water, holding cells ~75 C below the logic; with leakage halving every ~10 C, worst-case retention goes from 64 ms to ~10 s and refresh is dropped for step- and token-scoped data.
note: Dense Cu pillars conduct heat well; holding a 75 C gap across a bonded interface is doubtful.

title: Vertical bucket brigade: charge hops tier-to-tier down to one sense tier
idea: Take the astronomy CCD and rotate its shift axis to vertical: stacked storage tiers linked by gated vertical channels clock charge packets down plane by plane to a single bottom tier of sense amps, so 64 storage tiers need no periphery of their own. Time split: dense tiers hold charge for ms, and a whole-plane shift takes ns per hop.
note: Charge-transfer efficiency over 64 hops in deposited channels is the doubt.

title: Micro-MLCC: nanolaminate multilayer capacitor inside each lateral 3D cell
idea: Scale the 1000-layer multilayer ceramic capacitor, a mm-size component, down to a 50-nm lateral cell: ALD a blanket nanolaminate of 8 electrode/high-k pairs inside each tier's capacitor cavity, then connect odd and even electrodes at opposite ends by selective recess etch. Eight plates in parallel give ~8x capacitance per footprint.

title: Panel-scale nanoimprinted oxide gain cells on depreciated display lines
idea: Jump from a 0.07 m2 wafer to 5.5 m2 Gen-8.5 display mother-glass: retired LCD/OLED lines run panel-scale nanoimprint at ~50 nm half-pitch to build 8 stacked low-temperature oxide-semiconductor 2T0C gain-cell tiers, which are diced into memory tiles and bonded to silicon periphery chiplets.

title: Fiber delay-line loop memory for strictly periodic weight streams
idea: This revives delay-line memory at datacenter scale. Weights that are read in the same order every decode step circulate in a 40 km dense-WDM fiber spool (100 wavelengths x 400 Gb/s gives about 1 GB in flight on a ~200 us loop), kept alive by optical amplifiers. Accelerators tap the stream as it passes, because sequential lockstep access never needs random addressing.
note: Transceiver and amplifier cost far exceeds fiber cost.

title: Precision-resistor mask enabling charge-domain MAC inside commodity DDR
idea: One added thin-film resistor mask gives commodity DDR dies a calibrated charge-sharing reference, enabling bit-serial analog multiply-accumulate on the bitlines. Bandwidth-hungry decode GEMV runs inside the DDR, so weights can live in cheap DDR instead of HBM. Compute moves from the package scale to the bitline scale.
note: Analog precision and variation on commodity bitlines; requires DRAM-fab adoption.

title: Glass-panel substrate memory: multi-tier oxide TFT cells in package RDL
idea: Jump to display-panel scale: the 600 mm glass package substrate is built on LCD lines with 8 tiers of IGZO thin-film-transistor capacitor cells in its redistribution layers, giving a few GB per package of working memory; the ~1% BER from TFT variation is absorbed by row codes in the logic die.

title: Qimonda trench reborn on a separate bonded capacitor wafer
idea: Qimonda's trench DRAM died because deep trenches competed with the transistor for area and thermal budget below 40 nm. Etch 100:1 trenches with porous-Si sidewalls (5-10x area) in a cheap blank carrier wafer, fill them with ALD high-k MIM, then hybrid-bond the carrier face-to-face onto the access-transistor wafer at cell pitch.
note: Trench capacitor wafer bonded at cell pitch; sub-100 nm bond pitch unproven.

title: Bubble memory's rotating field drives skyrmion loops, no transistors
idea: Magnetic bubble memory died because long serial loops made access slow. Keep its best trick, one global rotating field that moves every bit so no bit needs its own transistor, and fix the latency. Use 64-bit skyrmion loops in thin multilayer rings, each with one sense MTJ, clocked by an on-chip stripline field so that any bit arrives within 64 steps.
note: Global rotating-field drive is a twist on racetrack; not DRAM-class latency.

title: Servo-marked racetracks: hard-disk servo loop fixes domain-wall shift errors
idea: Failure mined: IBM's racetrack memory stalled on pinning-induced over- and under-shifting of domain walls. Fix: interleave a known servo pattern every 32 bits. The read MTJ's sense amp time-stamps each domain-wall arrival, and a per-track controller trims the next current pulse width, like hard-disk servo wedges.

title: Skyrmion bubble memory: globally clocked major/minor loops, TMR detectors
idea: Failure mined: magnetic bubble memory (TI, Intel Magnetics) died on micron-size bubbles, 100 kHz shifting and millivolt permalloy detectors. Fix: keep its best idea, one global drive that clocks every loop at once with no per-bit transistors, but use 25 nm skyrmions in Co/Pt multilayers pushed by a global spin-orbit current sheet. Data is read through block-replicate gates onto a major loop with one 200% TMR detector per 4096 bits.
note: Major/minor loop latency runs to microseconds, not DRAM-class random access; room-temperature skyrmion pinning is unsolved.

title: IBM trench capacitor revived from the wafer backside
idea: Trench DRAM (IBM, Infineon, Qimonda) lost to stacked capacitors because a deep trench competes with the transistor for front-side area. After building 4F2 vertical transistors on the front, thin the wafer and deep-etch (DRIE) trenches from the backside directly under each pillar's source. Trench depth is then limited by the 5-10 um wafer thickness rather than by front-side topology.

title: MAPPER's bankrupt multibeam e-beam reborn as DRAM tile character projection
idea: MAPPER Lithography (13,000 beamlets, bankrupt 2018) died on throughput for random logic. DRAM arrays are ~95% identical cells: give each beamlet a stencil aperture of a full 8x8-cell tile so one flash writes 64 cells, exposing fluorine-free metal-oxide or HSQ resist.
note: Stencil tiles per beamlet add character projection to multibeam; same mechanism as I-04806.

title: NASA's vacuum-channel transistor as a zero-leakage DRAM access switch
idea: NASA's nanoscale vacuum-channel transistor stalled because emitter tips eroded under continuous current. A DRAM access device conducts only nanoseconds per access, a duty cycle near 1e-6: form 50-100 nm sealed vacuum gaps with carbon or Mo tips on glass that connect a storage capacitor to the bitline by field emission only when the wordline gate field passes threshold.
note: Field emission at DRAM voltages needs extreme tip enhancement; tip uniformity across billions of cells doubtful.

title: Canon ELTRAN porous-silicon transfer builds 30-tier single-crystal 3D DRAM
idea: Canon's ELTRAN layer transfer (epitaxy on porous Si, split by water jet) lost to Smart Cut on cost for single SOI layers. For 3D DRAM needing 26+ single-crystal tiers its advantage returns: one donor is re-epitaxied and split repeatedly, each tier bonded below 400 C onto the growing stack with one coarse alignment litho per tier and no hydrogen implant.

title: GE's BEAMOS reborn: microcolumn electron beams address unpatterned MOS film
idea: GE's 1970s beam-addressed MOS memory (BEAMOS) wrote and read charge on a MOS target with an electron beam, but died on bulky vacuum tubes and slow deflection. Wafer-fabricate 10,000 MEMS microcolumns in a chip-scale vacuum package, each deflecting a 10-20 nm spot across a 100 um field of an unpatterned SiO2/Si target and reading bits by beam-induced current.

title: SEL's IGZO DOSRAM built on glass in shuttered LCD fabs
idea: Semiconductor Energy Laboratory's IGZO DOSRAM never found a fab, while Gen-8 to Gen-10 LCD fabs such as Sharp Sakai are closing. Retool one closed line with roll-to-plate nanoimprint at 30 nm, stack 4 layers of IGZO 2T0C gain cells on 2.2x2.5 m glass with wide landing pads that absorb glass distortion, and bond CMOS periphery chiplets along the panel edge.

title: InPhase holography, fixed: optical associative attention over KV keys
idea: InPhase's holographic disc died because tape and disk won archival storage. Use holography where it is unbeatable, parallel correlation: record key vectors as a volume hologram in a photorefractive crystal, shine the query as a beam, read correlation peaks on a camera to get top-k token indices, then fetch only those V vectors from flash.

title: Altermagnet tunnel junction: spin-split readout without net magnetization
idea: Effect walk: altermagnetic spin splitting. Build a tunnel junction whose free electrode is an altermagnet (CrSb or MnTe, avoiding Ru) with momentum-dependent spin-split bands, so the Neel vector produces a TMR-like resistance change; write by spin-orbit or current-induced Neel switching.

title: Charge-order ferroelectric switches by electron hopping, not ion motion
idea: Effect walk: electronic ferroelectricity from charge ordering. Use a mixed-valence oxide (LuFe2O4-type, or a rare-earth-free charge-ordered ferrite or manganite) whose polarization comes from Fe2+/Fe3+ ordering, so switching moves electrons between sites rather than displacing ions, at ~meV per unit cell with no oxygen-vacancy fatigue.
note: LuFe2O4 electronic ferroelectricity is disputed; RT switchable material not established.

title: Resonant-tunneling access diode opens only at wordline-tuned resonance
idea: Effect: double-barrier resonant tunneling. Replace the access transistor with a vertical AlN/GaN/AlN (or SiO2/Si-well/SiO2) stack whose quantized well level aligns with the storage-node Fermi level only when the wordline, acting as a gate on the well, pulls it into resonance; off-resonance transmission is 10^6-10^9 lower and fixed by barrier thickness rather than doping.
note: Room-temperature peak-to-valley ratios far short of DRAM off/on needs.

title: Wordline-gated Coulomb-blockade nanodot valve in storage-node contact
idea: Effect: Coulomb blockade. A ~1 nm Pt or Si nanodot between two tunnel barriers sits in the storage-node plug, capacitively gated by the same wordline: wordline-high moves the dot to its charge-degeneracy point (conducts), wordline-low leaves it deep in blockade with charging energy ~0.6 eV, above the 0.5 V node-to-bitline hold bias, so it blocks transistor leakage in series. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.

title: Lattice-matched GaP storage-node contact blocks band-to-band tunneling
idea: Effect: heterojunction band offset. A few-nm epitaxial GaP layer (0.4% lattice mismatch to Si, Eg 2.26 eV) at the gate-overlapped storage-node contact forces GIDL tunneling across a wider gap (rate ~exp(-Eg^1.5/F)), cutting GIDL by up to ~10^3. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
note: Ga contamination and GaP/Si interface quality.

title: Micro-ring modulators driven directly from sense-amp row skip SerDes
idea: Effect: electro-optic refractive-index modulation (Pockels in thin-film LiNbO3, or carrier plasma dispersion in Si). Put micro-ring modulators at the column-select outputs so each sense-amp group modulates its own WDM wavelength; light carries the page off-die in parallel, eliminating the serializer, DLL and long global data lines.

title: Single-electron-transistor sense amp counts stored electrons directly
idea: Effect: Coulomb blockade. A single-electron transistor with a ~2 nm Si island (charging energy well above kT at room temperature) capacitively coupled to the bitline acts as a sub-electron electrometer; its periodic current oscillation (Coulomb staircase) resolves signals of a few hundred electrons, with reference cells calibrating background-charge drift.

title: Dithered multi-comparator sensing reads four-level cells reliably
idea: Effect: stochastic resonance and dithering. After charge sharing the bitline voltage holds for a few ns; three coarse comparators shared per 8 bitlines sample it several times with injected calibrated dither, and averaging resolves below comparator offset, reading 4 levels (2 bits) from a ~0.8 fF cell before a DAC-driven restore.
note: Four levels from 0.8 fF leave ~20 mV spacing; leakage and kTC noise, not comparator offset, dominate.

title: Na: Prussian-white nanocell stores bit as sodium electrochemical potential
idea: Each cell is a ~20 nm solid-state sodium couple of two Prussian-blue-analogue electrodes (Na, Fe, C, N) across a thin Na+ conductor; a write moves a few hundred Na+ ions, and the bit is the resulting ~0.3 V open-circuit voltage sensed on a read-transistor gate.

title: Diamond inversion-channel access transistor with week-long retention
idea: C: build the access device as an inversion-channel diamond MOSFET (phosphorus-doped n-type diamond with an Al2O3 gate, p-channel inversion) grown as diamond-on-Si; the 5.5 eV gap makes intrinsic carrier density ~10^-27 cm^-3, so off-current is set only by defects and storage nodes could hold charge for days.

title: Lattice-matched GaP storage-node junction moves depletion into wide-gap material
idea: P (as GaP): selectively regrow a thin n+ GaP contact (2.26 eV gap, only 0.4% lattice mismatch to Si) on the silicon access transistor so the junction depletion region, where SRH generation happens, sits in GaP with ~10^7x lower intrinsic carrier density, while the channel stays silicon.

title: Magnetically latched FeCo nanorelay gives true open-circuit access
idea: Fe: replace the access transistor with a vertical FeCo nanocantilever relay with Ru contacts, pulled closed electrostatically by the wordline and biased by a CoPt permanent-magnet film so it latches open or closed; the off state is a vacuum gap with zero subthreshold or junction leakage.

title: MoS2 grown on trench sidewalls: channel geometry set by depth
idea: Mo: etch DUV-pitch trenches and grow monolayer MoS2 conformally by MOCVD on the vertical sidewalls; each sidewall becomes a vertical 2D access channel whose length equals the step height, and an ALD gate fills the trench, giving two cells per DUV feature.
note: Conformal monolayer MoS2 on sidewalls and contacts immature.

title: Mo: grounded molybdenum shield fins screen buried-wordline passing-gate coupling
idea: Insert a thin grounded Mo fin between adjacent buried wordlines, electrostatically screening the passing-gate field that modulates neighbor channels and storage-node junctions; Mo also replaces some tungsten (an 80%-China chokepoint) and is mined in the U.S.
note: No room for a grounded fin between buried wordlines at 6F2 pitch.

title: Williams-tube revival: field-emitter arrays write charge spots on dielectric
idea: The 1940s Williams tube stored bits as charge spots on a CRT face. Its nanoscale successor is a vacuum-sealed array of Spindt field-emission tips, each deflecting its beam over an 8x8 field of spots to write and read electron charge in a trap-rich dielectric film. The bit lives in the film, with no access transistor.
note: Like HP atomic-resolution storage; vacuum packaging, emitter stability and access speed are big unknowns.

title: Lost-wax helical channel packs a 60 nm gate into 12 nm footprint
idea: Deposit a sacrificial carbon helix in the pillar hole by glancing-angle spiral deposition, wrap it with gate dielectric and metal, burn the carbon out (lost-wax casting), then ALD-backfill the helical void with the channel. The result is a gate-all-around helix with L~60 nm in a vertical cell.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembled 3 nm nanowires widen bandgap by confinement
idea: Use block-copolymer self-assembly (no litho) to define 3-4 nm vertical Si nanowire access channels. Quantum confinement raises the effective gap to ~1.6-2 eV, exponentially suppressing BTBT/GIDL and intrinsic generation.

title: Locksmith combination-lock access: resonant-tunneling barrier opens only at key bias
idea: Replace the gated transistor with a double-barrier resonant-tunneling stack (e.g., AlN/GaN wells) between bitline and storage well. Charge passes only when the bitline bias aligns the quantized level, like a key cut to one combination. Off-resonance, thick wide-gap barriers block flow.

title: E-ink microcapsule bit: charged nanoparticle parked top or bottom
idea: Scale e-paper microcapsule manufacturing to a sealed ~10 nm cage holding one charged nanoparticle or ion cluster, held by image-charge adhesion to the top or bottom electrode. It is moved by a field pulse and read by capacitance difference.

title: Perfecting-press wafer: periphery printed on the backside of the array
idea: Like a perfecting press that prints both sides of a sheet in one pass, thin the finished array wafer to ~1 um and build low-temperature periphery transistors (laser-annealed Si or oxide FETs) on its backside. These connect to bitlines and wordlines through sub-um nano-TSVs directly beneath each mat.
note: Low-temperature backside transistors are slow; industry chose bonded cell-on-periphery instead.

title: Duplex-printed pillar: one vertical channel serves front and back cells
idea: Like printing both sides of a sheet, build each vertical pillar with a buried bitline contacting it at mid-height, an upper gate linking it to a front-side capacitor and a lower gate linking it to a backside capacitor formed after bonding and thinning, so one 4F2 footprint stores two bits.

title: Swiss-roll capacitors: strained films self-roll into nano-scrolls
idea: Like a wound film capacitor or a jelly roll, deposit a TiN/dielectric/TiN stack on a strained bilayer over a sacrificial layer; releasing it makes the film curl into a tight multi-turn scroll above each cell, multiplying plate area 10-20x with no deep hole etch.
note: Strained bilayers roll at 100s nm to um radii, far above DRAM cell pitch.

title: Puff-pastry fold-and-bond doubles 3D DRAM tiers each round
idea: Fabricate one complete planar 1T1C tier on thinned donors, then laminate like croissant dough: bond tiers face-to-back in pairs, thin, bond pairs to pairs, so N tiers need only log2(N) sequential bond-thin rounds (5 rounds = 32 tiers) and every tier reuses the proven planar mask set; oversized landing pads absorb ~100 nm bond overlay.
note: log2 bond rounds is neat, but yield compounds and cost/bit barely moves.

title: Fiducial marks: pilot-calibrated two-bit-per-cell DRAM with soft decoding
idea: Pick-and-place machines read fiducial marks to correct for drift. Each DRAM page embeds pilot cells with known values, read through the sense amp at several reference levels to track drift and leakage. That lets each cell hold 2 bits (4 charge levels), and a soft-decision LDPC decoder uses pilot-calibrated likelihoods to turn a ~1% raw symbol error rate into reliable reads for a compressed or cold tier.

title: Lost-foam air gaps between buried wordlines via oxygen ash
idea: Lost-foam casting burns out a foam pattern to leave a cavity; deposit a carbon or polymer spacer between buried wordlines, cap it with porous oxide, then burn it out with an O2 ash (no argon sputter or plasma), leaving vacuum gaps that cut wordline-to-wordline and passing-gate coupling.
note: Buried wordlines are separated by active silicon/STI, leaving little room for gaps.

title: Micro-Williams tube: field-emission beam addresses bare electret film
idea: IFR: no cell has an access device; one beam serves a million bits. Each 30x30 um tile has a gated field-emitter tip and electrostatic deflection plates in a vacuum-sealed MEMS cavity, writing and reading 10-15 nm charge spots on a continuous SiO2/Si3N4 electret film (read by secondary-electron yield, then rewrite).

title: Negative-capacitance bitline dielectric makes the bitline vanish electrically
idea: Ideal result: a bitline with zero capacitance, so every femtofarad of cell charge becomes signal. Closest achievable: line the bitline-to-plate spacer with a thin stabilized HZO negative-capacitance layer in series with the parasitic, so effective Cbl drops 2-3x while staying hysteresis-free in the small-signal range.

title: Microwave dispersive readout senses cells without draining them
idea: Ideal result: a read that costs nothing and leaves the bit untouched. Borrowing qubit readout, make each bitline segment part of a GHz resonator; a storage node gating a tiny varactor shifts the resonance, and a picowatt probe tone reflected from the line reveals the bit with no charge sharing and no restore.

title: Neighbor bitlines form a SAR DAC for two-bit cells
idea: Ideal result: the bitline itself is the analog-to-digital converter. Store 4 charge levels per cell and resolve them by successive approximation, with adjacent precharged bitlines switched in binary-weighted groups acting as the DAC capacitors against the sensed line.
note: Neighbor bitlines are not free DAC caps: every bitline on the row is charge-sharing its own cell during activation.

title: Dual-ended mirror pillar stores two bits per 4F2 footprint
idea: IFR: 'two cells in the space of one.' Backward: build a vertical channel pillar with one capacitor on top (front side) and another at its bottom (after backside thinning), split the gate into independent upper and lower half-gates, and tap the shared bitline at the pillar midpoint.

title: Soft-decision re-sense with shifted bitline references
idea: Ideal: never lose a bit, even when the cell signal is nearly zero. Closest: when the fast decoder fails, the row is re-sensed twice more with the bitline precharge shifted by +/-15 mV, producing per-bit confidence (like NAND read-retry) that feeds a soft-decision decoder able to recover cells with only ~20 mV of signal.
note: DRAM read is destructive: after first sense the restore overwrites charge, so re-sensing needs preserved signal.

title: Altermagnet tunnel junction: magnetoresistance without stray fields
idea: Scarcity rule: no net magnetization allowed, since stray fields set MRAM pitch. Store the bit in the Neel vector of an altermagnet (RuO2, MnTe or Mn5Si3) whose spin-split bands still give tunneling magnetoresistance, and flip it with spin-splitter or spin-orbit torque at THz-class dynamics.

title: Charging-energy wall: Coulomb-blockade island as the leakage stopper
idea: Limit: leakage must be stopped by a quantum effect, not a barrier height. Put a sub-2 nm silicon or metal nanocrystal island in series with the access channel. Its charging energy (>0.5 eV) blocks single-electron transit until the wordline shifts the island level into resonance, and co-tunneling leakage is exponentially suppressed.

title: Spin-orbit voltage readout: nanomagnets drive inverters, no sense amps
idea: Constraint: non-volatile magnetic bits. Instead of current-mode TMR sensing, pass a small supply current through the bit's spin-injection layer into a strong spin-orbit layer (Bi2Se3/Pt), where the inverse Edelstein/spin-Hall effect converts spin to a charge voltage whose sign follows magnetization (MESO-style); that voltage gates a local inverter directly, with no reference or SA.

title: Bond-then-drill: one etch wires a 64-tier wafer stack
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. Fusion-bond 64 DRAM wafers thinned to 5 um each (oxide bonding, <100 nm alignment), then pattern once and etch/fill vertical buses through the whole stack like a 3D-NAND channel hole, so one litho step and one deep etch replace 63 separate TSV and bump steps.
note: 64-tier wafer stacking compounds yield catastrophically; density per footprint, not cost per bit.

title: No silicon: roll-to-roll MoS2 memory grown on copper foil
idea: Forced limit: the channel and substrate must be non-Si. Monolayer MoS2 is grown by CVD on a continuous copper foil web, transferred to glass or polyimide, and patterned into gain-cell access transistors whose wide bandgap gives sub-fA leakage.

title: Deep-level charge bit: QD-Flash physics shrunk toward an atom-placed single-defect cell
idea: Ensemble version (exists): self-assembled GaSb or InGaSb quantum dots in a GaP matrix give ~1 eV hole localisation. A gate bias floods the dots with holes (capture, ns), and a reverse field empties them by field-assisted emission (350 ns measured, ~10 ns predicted). The stored charge sits above a channel whose conductance is read non-destructively. Single-defect version (2040 tools): hydrogen-depassivation lithography or deterministic single-ion implantation places 1-3 deep-level dopants or engineered defects in a crystalline barrier under a 10-15 nm gate. Each trapped charge is a quantised threshold step, so the cell is natively multi-level (bits = number of charges). No amorphous tunnel oxide sits in the write path, so there is no oxide wear.

title: Swap 30,000-electron capacitor for 200-electron node plus single-electron sensor
idea: Shrink the storage node to a ~0.03 fF gate island and read it with a room-temperature silicon single-electron transistor shared by a few cells. The transistor's sub-3-nm dot is formed by a dopant cluster or an oxidised nanowire constriction, and its Coulomb oscillation turns a few-electron change into a large current swing.
note: Room-temperature SET memory known since Yano 1994; offset-charge noise and variability.

title: Swap current-driven magnet for voltage-flipped magnetoelectric BiFeO3 bit
idea: Exchange-couple a CoFe nanomagnet to multiferroic BiFeO3. A 100 mV field flips the BiFeO3 polarization and antiferromagnetic order, which drags the magnet with it, and the state is read through inverse Rashba-Edelstein charge output, as in MESO.
note: MESO-type physics; 100 mV deterministic BFO switching not yet achieved.

title: Swap binary charge for eight-level charge with shared SAR sensing
idea: At relaxed DUV pitch (F ~ 20 nm) the larger cell cap stores eight charge levels (3 bits). They are read by a charge-redistribution SAR sense amplifier shared across four bitlines, protected by a strong symbol ECC, and refreshed at a rate set by the narrowest level margin.
note: Leakage collapses 8-level margins; prior 4-level DRAM efforts stalled.

title: Substitute linear gate dielectric with antiferroelectric ZrO2 steep-switch stack
idea: Substitute the HfO2/SiO2 gate stack with antiferroelectric ZrO2. Its field-induced AFE-to-FE transition gives a transient negative-capacitance boost at turn-on, then relaxes fully to zero polarization at zero field: no remanence and none of the wake-up or fatigue of ferroelectric gates.

title: Capacitor-DAC successive approximation sense for two-bit cells
idea: Substitute the single-threshold latch with a two-step successive-approximation comparison: switched trim capacitors on the reference bitline act as a capacitive DAC that steps the reference to resolve four stored charge levels, so each cell holds 2 bits.

title: Steep-slope tunnel-FET sense amps enable 0.5 V array voltage
idea: Substitute MOSFET sense pairs with heterojunction tunnel FETs (~30 mV/dec) used only in the latch, where low drive current matters less, so the array voltage drops from ~1 V to ~0.5 V while the latch still regenerates.

title: Transferred 2D-crystal tiers replace deposited semiconductor tiers
idea: Substitute epitaxial/deposited tier stacks with wafer-scale dry transfer of MOCVD monolayer MoS2 channels plus hBN gate dielectric grown on reusable sapphire donors, stacked tier by tier with a non-fluorinated polymer handle (PPC); each cell tier including its gate is <10 nm thick.

title: Substitute access transistors with BEOL two-terminal selectors in line-space crosspoints
idea: Build a 1S1C crosspoint: a threshold-switching selector (NbOx or OTS) in series with a planar MIM capacitor at each intersection of two perpendicular line arrays, which need only line/space patterning (SAQP or DSA, no contact holes, no EUV) and stack in BEOL; only the single selected intersection is charged or read.

title: Threshold-switch selector stacked on capacitor for cross-point 3D DRAM
idea: Fuse the ovonic threshold switch selector from 3D XPoint with a MIM capacitor into a two-terminal 1S1C stack at each wordline/bitline crossing, built in 8-16 decks with no transistor. Half-select bias stays below the OTS threshold to isolate the node; a full-select pulse snaps the OTS on to charge or sense it.

title: Porphyrin redox monolayer giving multi-level charge per node
idea: Graft a monolayer of porphyrin or ferrocene molecules with 2-3 discrete oxidation states onto the storage-node electrode, combining molecular electronics with the DRAM capacitor so charge sits in molecular redox states at fixed potentials. Discrete states give quantized charge levels (2 bits/cell), and electrons must cross a molecular tether barrier to escape, stretching retention from 64 ms toward minutes.
note: ZettaCore pursued porphyrin multilevel memory; failed on kinetics, stability and integration.

title: Tunnel-FET gain cell with steep-slope read amplification
idea: Combine a band-to-band tunneling FET (sub-30 mV/decade) as the read device with a small storage node in a 2T gain cell, so every 10 mV of stored voltage moves read current by about an order of magnitude. Storage nodes can be 0.5 fF or less at a 0.4 V swing, and reading never disturbs the node.
note: TFET steep slope rarely holds at useful current; low on-current slows reads.

title: Negative-capacitance HZO layer inside the buried-wordline gate stack
idea: Put a thin ferroelectric HZO film in series with the high-k gate dielectric of the buried-channel access transistor. Its negative capacitance amplifies gate-to-channel coupling and gives a sub-60 mV/dec subthreshold slope.
note: NC-FET steep slope widely pursued; hysteresis and speed remain unresolved.

title: Nanoelectromechanical contact in series with each access transistor
idea: A monolithic BEOL TiN or CNT cantilever relay sits between the access transistor and the storage node. The same wordline field pulls it in, and it springs open during retention to leave an air gap.

title: Tunnel-FET input pair inside a conventional MOSFET latch
idea: Replace only the input pair of the DRAM sense amp with steep-slope tunnel FETs (sub-60 mV/decade) and keep MOSFETs for restore, so the latch begins amplifying at VARY ~0.5 V, where MOSFET-only latches barely turn on.

title: MEMS micromirror process fused with DRAM: nano-relay access switches
idea: Replace the access transistor with an electrostatic nano-cantilever relay built in a back-end sacrificial-gap MEMS flow like TI's Dallas DLP micromirror line; the open contact is a vacuum gap, so off-state leakage is essentially zero, and the relay sits above its capacitor in the same 4F2 footprint.
note: NEMS DRAM was proposed before; 1e15 contact endurance and stiction are unsolved.

title: Two-bit-per-capacitor DRAM made viable by 1% sensing tolerance
idea: Combine NAND's multi-level-cell sensing with the DRAM capacitor: four charge levels per cell are read by a charge-sharing, two-step successive-approximation sense amp. The scheme historically failed on margin but works once the code absorbs ~1% level misreads.

title: NEMS relay access switch: air-gap off-state ends leakage tail
idea: Combine a nanoelectromechanical relay with a storage capacitor: a released TiN or poly-Si seesaw relay replaces the access transistor, so the off-state is an air gap with essentially zero leakage and retention is limited only by the capacitor dielectric. Buildable in a university nanofab: sacrificial oxide released by vapor HF, e-beam defined gaps.

title: LiDAR SPAD avalanche gain reads attofarad storage nodes
idea: Adapt single-photon avalanche diodes: store ~300 electrons on a 50 aF node and read by dumping them into a linear-mode avalanche junction (gain ~100) beside the bitline, so the cell is a 4F2 vertical transistor plus junction with no capacitor.

title: Image-sensor ramp ADCs read sixteen charge levels per cell
idea: Borrowed from CMOS image sensors, whose column-parallel single-slope ADCs digitize thousands of pixels with one shared ramp: each bitline gets a tiny comparator-counter so a cell holds 16 charge levels (4 bits), written by ramp-and-stop and digitally restored on every read.

title: Carbon-fiber furnaces: iron-catalyzed nanotube forests as capacitor cores
idea: Adapt carbon-fiber and nanotube-forest CVD: place Fe catalyst dots on Al2O3 at each storage-node pad, grow vertical multiwall carbon nanotubes 1-2 um tall at ~450-550 C, then ALD-wrap them with TiN/ZrO2/TiN so each tube is the scaffold and conductor of a tall capacitor that is grown rather than etched.

title: LTPS laser crystallization with argon-fluoride light for silicon-only tiers
idea: Borrow the phone-display LTPS line: deposit amorphous Si per tier and melt-crystallize it with a line-beam excimer laser using sequential lateral solidification for cell-sized grains; use ArF instead of the usual XeCl so even the laser gas is abundant, and the heat stays in the top ~50 nm so dozens of tiers stack without disturbing lower ones.
note: Grain-boundary leakage kills DRAM retention; thermal isolation between thin tiers doubtful.

title: Repurpose idle LCD panel fabs for glass-substrate oxide gain cells
idea: Adapted from display makers' Gen-8.5 lines that already deposit IGZO TFTs: retool them to print 2T0C oxide gain-cell arrays on 2.2 x 2.5 m glass panels. Thinned CMOS periphery chiplets are bonded onto the panel afterward.

title: Minify refresh to zero: tunnel-diode trickle latch per cell
idea: Stack a pair of nanoscale Esaki interband-tunnel diodes (Goto pair) on the capacitor top electrode; their N-shaped I-V creates two stable node voltages that continuously replace leaked charge with ~10 fA standby current, so the cell holds itself like SRAM at near-DRAM size.
note: TI's TSRAM did this; fA-scale valley currents with useful peak-to-valley are implausible.

title: Magnify barrier opacity: electron Bragg-mirror superlattice floating node
idea: Surround a charge-storage node with a Si/SiO2 (or ZnO/MgZnO) superlattice engineered so thermal electrons fall in a miniband gap and are reflected, while a ~2 V bias aligns a resonant miniband for ns-scale transport; zero-bias leakage is blocked without Fowler-Nordheim stress.
note: Close to UltraRAM's III-V resonant-tunneling barrier; Si/SiO2 superlattice coherence is poor.

title: Minify the switching volume: hidden-state Mott charge-density-wave bits
idea: Exploit the metastable 'hidden' metallic state of 1T-TaS2 (strain-engineered to stay stable above room temperature): a 10 ns current pulse switches a nanoflake between insulating CDW and metastable metallic order with 10-100x resistance contrast that persists unpowered.
note: 1T-TaS2 hidden state unstable at room temperature.

title: Successive-approximation sense amp magnifies bits per capacitor
idea: MAGNIFY bits per cell to two: after charge sharing, a 3-step successive-approximation sense amp with a capacitive DAC shared among 4 bitlines resolves four charge levels and writes back the quantized level during restore.

title: Dirac-source steep-slope sense transistors at 0.4 V
idea: Low-temperature (<=400 C) MOCVD MoS2 channels with a graphene cold-source contact that filters out high-energy electrons give sub-60 mV/decade switching, letting SAs and the array MINIFY VARY to ~0.4 V.

title: Four charge levels per capacitor double bits per gram
idea: Magnify bits per cell 2x: store four charge levels in each capacitor and read them with a two-step successive-approximation sense amplifier against a reference bitline, with tighter refresh for the top level.
note: 4-level DRAM studied since 1989; modern cell signal margins too small.

title: Direct-tunnel nitride-trap cell: seconds-long retention from silicon, nitrogen, oxygen
idea: Magnify retention from milliseconds to ~100 s at 125 C: store charge in deep silicon-nitride traps behind a 1.5-2 nm tunnel oxide, written by direct tunneling (no hot carriers) and read non-destructively through the transistor's threshold shift.
note: Thin-tunnel SONOS DRAM tried in 2000s; 100 s at 125 C with 2 nm oxide conflicts with direct-tunnel leakage.

title: Ruthenium-free strontium titanate capacitor stays paraelectric through 125 C
idea: Magnify k to ~150: grow SrTiO3 by ALD on TiN over a SrO/TiO2 nanolaminate seed instead of Ru/SrRuO3 electrodes. STO is a quantum paraelectric with no phase transition anywhere near 125 C.
note: STO capacitors long pursued; crystalline high-k STO on TiN without Ru seed is the unsolved part.

title: Multi-level DRAM: two bits per capacitor relax lithography
idea: Magnify bits per cell to 2 using four charge levels and a reference-ladder sense amp with refresh-time calibration, buying a node of density without a shrink.

title: Minify refresh 100x and decode known weak cells as erasures
idea: At final test, map each die's retention-tail cells at a 6.4 s refresh interval and ship the compressed weak-cell list in SPD. The controller refreshes 100x less often and feeds listed cells to an RS/BCH decoder as erasures, which corrects twice as many symbols as unknown errors; leftover VRT failures fall to residual ECC.
note: At 6.4 s many unmapped VRT failures would swamp residual ECC.

title: Minify copies to one: optical broadcast weight streaming
idea: Keep one copy of model weights in a central memory pool and broadcast it over a WDM optical bus to 128 accelerators in lockstep; each holds only a tiny SRAM double-buffer and pipelines layer by layer as weights stream past.

title: Eliminate junction leakage: nano-electromechanical relay seals each storage node
idea: Eliminate the semiconductor access junction: each capacitor connects to the bitline through a 20-nm electrostatic nano-relay (vertical cantilever across a vacuum gap) that touches only during access; when open, the leakage path is a physical gap, so node leakage drops from ~13 fA to effectively zero. Relays switch in ~1-5 ns at this size, with Ru or carbon contacts for high cycle counts.

title: Eliminate dielectric thickness limits: solid-electrolyte double-layer nanocapacitor storage node
idea: Eliminate the conventional capacitor dielectric: the storage node is a nano-electrode against a thin solid ion conductor (protonic phosphosilicate or LiPON) with blocking electrodes, so the sub-nm Helmholtz double layer (~20-40 uF/cm2) supplies the capacitance without any faradaic reaction. That is 2-4x the capacitance per area of ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 at EOT 0.4 nm, so a 5 fF node needs AR ~20-30 instead of 75.
note: Duplicate EDL capacitor.

title: Eliminate stored charge: bistable buckled nanobeam holds the bit mechanically
idea: Eliminate charge as the information carrier: each cell is a pre-compressed 10x60 nm SiC or SiN nanobeam that buckles up or down into two elastic energy minima; a wordline electrostatic pulse snaps it over in ~1 ns (GHz resonance) and capacitive sensing reads its position non-destructively. No leakage can erase a mechanical state, so the capacitor and refresh both vanish.
note: Buckled-beam memories demonstrated at micron scale; ns snapping, stiction and 6-8F2 density are doubts.

title: Eliminate net magnetization: antiferromagnetic Mn3Sn bits read by anomalous Hall
idea: Eliminate the ferromagnet, the fixed layer and the MgO tunnel barrier: store the bit in the octupole order of the noncollinear antiferromagnet Mn3Sn, switched by spin-orbit torque from a heavy-metal underlayer in ~100 ps, and read it from its large anomalous Hall voltage in a simple Hall cross. With no stray field, cells pack at ~10 nm pitch without coupling.
note: Same Mn3Sn SOT bit; uV Hall readout at ns is impractical without per-cell gain.

title: Eliminate atomic motion: hidden charge-density-wave states as purely electronic bits
idea: Eliminate any motion of atoms or ions: a picosecond electrical pulse switches a nano-patch of 1T-TaS2 from its commensurate insulating state into a metastable 'hidden' metallic CDW domain state; the bit is an electronic ordering pattern with 1e2-1e3 resistance contrast, erased by a longer pulse.
note: Hidden CDW state not stable at room temperature; Mihailovic CDW memory precedent.

title: Eliminate full magnetization reversal: single skyrmion presence-absence in nanodots
idea: Eliminate full magnetization reversal: in a 20-nm Co/Pt/Ir multilayer dot with strong DMI, the bit is the presence or absence of one skyrmion, nucleated or annihilated by a voltage-controlled-anisotropy pulse and read through noncollinear magnetoresistance in a vertical tunnel stack.
note: 20 nm room-temperature skyrmion stability doubtful; widely researched.

title: Eliminate the pillar: quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3 reaches giant permittivity at 77 K
idea: Eliminate the 3D capacitor by using temperature: SrTiO3 is a quantum paraelectric whose permittivity climbs from ~300 at room temperature to thousands near 77 K, so an LN2-cooled planar SrTiO3 capacitor grown by MOCVD or hybrid MBE (no argon) stores the ~1-2 fF that 77-K retention requires on a flat ~30 nm pad. The helium ban steers us to the one cryogen that still unlocks this.
note: Same 77 K SrTiO3 planar capacitor.

title: Eliminate electronic charge storage: solid-electrolyte proton-intercalation bit
idea: Store the bit as protons intercalated into a 5 nm WO3 channel, written through a thin inorganic proton conductor (e.g., hydrogenated HfO2) with ~10 ns pulses; at zero bias the ions are immobile, so nothing leaks, and reads measure channel conductance non-destructively. Electrons are not the stored quantity, so they cannot leak away.

title: Eliminate the 3 V wordline: negative-capacitance HZO access gate
idea: Insert an ALD Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 ferroelectric layer, capacitance-matched to an HfO2/SiO2 underlayer, into the access gate so it acts as an internal voltage amplifier with sub-60 mV/dec slope. The same off current is reached with a 1-1.5 V wordline swing, or the same swing gives ~100x lower leakage.

title: Eliminate the wordline wire: light-gated wide-bandgap photoconductive access switch
idea: Replace the electrical wordline with a SiN waveguide row that delivers a nanosecond UV or blue pulse to ZnO or GaN photoconductive switches at each cell; in the dark the wide-gap switch has essentially no carriers and no leakage. The waveguide is passive, so wordline RC delay and 3 V pumps disappear.

title: Eliminate full-row activation with dual-gate cells selected by row AND column
idea: Give each access transistor a second gate tied to a column-segment select line, so a channel conducts only when both its wordline and its 64-bit column segment are high. Only the addressed bits share charge, sense and restore, instead of all 8,192 cells on the row.

title: Eliminate binary storage: three bits per gain cell
idea: Store 8 charge levels on a gain cell's storage node, whose read current maps monotonically to node voltage; read with a column-shared 3-bit SAR ADC and write with a precision DAC plus write-verify.
note: 8 levels on a leaky node: retention margin collapses; refresh and ADC area eat the density gain.

title: Eliminate step-and-repeat: whole-wafer single-shot roll nanoimprint
idea: Roll a flexible replica stamp across the full 300 mm wafer in one pass, patterning every die at once in UV-cured resist; distortion is corrected by thermally actuated zones in the stamp frame, mapped against wafer alignment marks.

title: Eliminate the access transistor: threshold-selector-gated capacitors in BEOL crossbars
idea: Put a two-terminal threshold switch (an ovonic or NbOx selector tuned for femtoamp-class off-current) in series with a MIM capacitor at each wordline/bitline crossing, forming a 1S1C 4F2 cell built entirely in back-end layers and stacked 8+ high.

title: Eliminate litho-perfect decoders: stochastic address decoders calibrated after fab
idea: Pattern dense BEOL crossbar arrays with room-temperature nanoimprint, and build address decoders from randomly doped or randomly gated thin-film lines whose codes are unknown at fab. After fab, a discovery routine probes each line's response and stores a logical-to-physical code table.
note: DeHon stochastic nanowire decoders precedent.

title: Ion-held charge: solid-electrolyte double-layer cell capacitor
idea: Swap the dielectric's role from a polarizing lattice to mobile ions: a 3-5 nm proton- or Li-conducting solid electrolyte between blocking electrodes piles ions into a ~0.5 nm Helmholtz layer at each plate, giving ~10-20 uF/cm2; ions travel <1 nm, so charging is ns-scale.
note: Duplicate EDL capacitor.

title: Series negative-capacitance layer that raises cell capacitance
idea: Reverse the series-capacitor rule: add a thin HZO ferroelectric biased into its negative-capacitance branch in series with the ZrO2/Al2O3 cell dielectric, so 1/C = 1/C_DE - 1/|C_FE| and total capacitance rises 2-3x above the dielectric alone while |C_FE| > C_DE keeps it hysteresis-free.
note: Widely pursued; stable hysteresis-free NC in multidomain films is contested.

title: Negative-capacitance gate stack sharpens the access transistor's off-switch
idea: Reverse the sign of capacitance: add a thin ferroelectric layer tuned for negative-capacitance operation in series with the access transistor's gate oxide, so the internal gate voltage amplifies the wordline swing and subthreshold slope drops below 60 mV/dec. Vt can then be raised ~150 mV for leakage with no loss of on-current and no higher wordline voltage.
note: Steady-state NC remains contested; hysteresis risk; NCFETs widely pursued.

title: Bitline segments become a SAR DAC for two bits per cell
idea: Rearrange the bitline into a capacitive DAC: it is cut into binary-weighted segments switched in successive-approximation steps around the SA, resolving four charge levels per cell in two comparisons, with restore through the same segments.

title: Capacitor that switches itself: Mott-selector-in-capacitor crosspoint
idea: Fold the transistor's role into the capacitor stack: metal / high-k / NbO2 Mott threshold layer / metal, where the Mott layer snaps conductive above ~1 V to charge the cell and returns insulating below, forming a transistor-free 1S1C crosspoint that can be stacked in BEOL.

title: Laser-crystallized polysilicon tiers: grain boundaries accepted for 3D
idea: Rearrange display technology into memory: stack 3D DRAM tiers of excimer- or green-laser-crystallized polysilicon access transistors instead of epitaxial Si/SiGe, accepting ~1% grain-boundary-leaky cells as correctable.
note: Grain-boundary leakage likely affects far more than 1% of cells.

title: Goto-pair tunnel-diode latch turns cell leakage into retention
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise + #13 Other way round: hang each storage node between two back-to-back nanoscale Esaki (band-to-band tunnel) diodes so their negative-differential-resistance curves cross at two stable node voltages. Leakage then pulls the node toward its stored value instead of away from it; the diodes are doped for ~1 pA valley current, and read/write still go through the normal access transistor. Contradiction resolved: tiny capacitor vs. no refresh.

title: Matryoshka coaxial multi-shell capacitor by sequential annular ALD casting
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: inside each pillar footprint grow three concentric electrode shells separated by dielectric, alternately strapped to storage node and plate (interdigitated coax), by repeating ALD electrode/dielectric/sacrificial-carbon fill and recess-etch cycles. Contradiction resolved: more electrode area vs. same footprint and lower aspect ratio.
note: Three shells need ~38 nm of film in sub-40 nm holes; multi-crown capacitors are old art.

title: Porphyrin redox monolayer adds quantized charge states to every capacitor
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging: graft a self-assembled monolayer of multi-state redox molecules (porphyrin/ferrocene dyads) onto the storage electrode so each molecule adds 1-2 electrons at fixed oxidation potentials. Charge density reaches ~10-30 uC/cm2 versus ~5 for high-k at 1 V, and the discrete potentials give native 2-bit cells.

title: Epitaxial all-perovskite SrRuO3/SrTiO3 capacitor without the interface dead layer
idea: TRIZ #33 Homogeneity: make electrodes and dielectric from one perovskite family (SrRuO3/SrTiO3/SrRuO3) grown coherently so no low-k interfacial dead layer forms; thin SrTiO3 then keeps k ~200+ instead of collapsing to ~50 as it does between TiN electrodes.
note: SRO/BST perovskite DRAM caps tried in 1990s; epitaxy on 3D pillars is the miracle.

title: Anti-weight: switched negative capacitance cancels bitline load during sensing
idea: TRIZ #8 Anti-weight counterbalances the dead weight of bitline capacitance: during the charge-sharing window a switched-capacitor negative-impedance converter (or a thin ferroelectric negative-capacitance layer in the bitline shield dielectric) presents about -0.7 CBL, so the cell sees ~30% of the physical bitline load; it is disconnected before restore to stay stable.

title: Goto-pair interband tunneling diodes atop a vertical access transistor
idea: TRIZ #40 Composite materials: grow two series Si/SiGe resonant interband tunneling diodes directly on top of a 4F2 vertical access transistor. Their negative-differential-resistance curves make the midpoint node bistable, a static latch inside the vertical stack held by a tiny supply current.
note: Tunnel-diode SRAM is old art; valley current per cell times billions of cells is prohibitive.

title: Persistent-sodium plateau node: sub-pA tunnel NDR keeps bit static
idea: Some neurons hold a bistable plateau voltage using a persistent sodium current with a negative-slope I-V. Add a vertical broken-gap interband tunnel diode (e.g. black phosphorus/SnSe2) from the storage node to a low rail. Its N-shaped I-V, with a ~pA valley current, creates two stable node voltages, so the cell latches statically like SRAM in a 1T1D footprint.

title: Chlorophyll special-pair redox monolayer as the storage node
idea: Photosynthetic reaction centres store charge as molecular oxidation states. Coat the node electrode with a self-assembled porphyrin or chlorophyll-analog monolayer under a thin solid polymer electrolyte. Each molecule stores 1-2 electrons at discrete potentials, giving pseudocapacitance of ~50-100 uC/cm2, about 10x a high-k MIM, so a low-AR cell holds a full signal.

title: Ball-and-chain nanomechanical plug isolating each storage node
idea: Voltage-gated K+ channels inactivate when a tethered 'ball' plugs the pore. Give each storage node a vertical nanocantilever contact that touches the bitline only while its wordline electrode pulls it in. When released, a vacuum gap gives essentially zero off-current, so leakage is set only by the capacitor dielectric.

title: Cell-membrane double layer: solid ionogel replaces the MIM dielectric
idea: Cell membranes work inside electrolyte double layers. Replace the ZrO2 stack with a 5-10 nm crosslinked ionic-liquid gel so charge sits in two Helmholtz layers at ~20-40 uF/cm2, 3-5x a high-k MIM. At ~10 mS/cm ionic conductivity across a 10 nm gap, the ionic RC time is ~ns, fast enough for DRAM writes.
note: Ionogel version of EDL capacitor; thermal budget is severe.

title: Voltage-sensor-helix cooperative gate for steep-slope access transistors
idea: Sodium channels switch at ~5 mV/decade because ~12 gating charges on the S4 helices move together; mimic this by inserting a thin antiferroelectric ZrO2-rich layer into the access-transistor gate stack, tuned so its field-induced phase transition coincides with threshold and gives internal voltage gain (~30 mV/dec over 3-4 decades).

title: Hemoglobin-cooperative Mott switch in series with access FET
idea: Hemoglobin binds O2 with Hill coefficient ~3, almost all-or-nothing; add a thin NbO2 insulator-metal-transition element in series with the access transistor's bitline contact so the composite stays insulating at retention bias (<VARY/2) and snaps metallic only when the wordline-driven current crosses the IMT threshold.
note: Hyper-FET known; NbO2 off-state leakage far above fA.

title: Stereocilia tip-link NEMS switches as zero-leak access devices
idea: Like hair-cell stereocilia whose tip links open channels only when deflected, make each access device a vertical nano-cantilever that electrostatically bends to touch the storage-node contact only when its wordline plane is energized; the air gap gives truly zero off-state leakage in a 3D vertical array.
note: NEM-DRAM proposed before; ns switching endurance >1e15 and stiction unproven.

title: Capsid proofreading: reversible self-assembly anneals out patterning defects
idea: Virus capsids assemble from weakly bonded subunits that unbind and rebind, so misassembled pieces fall off; pattern cell arrays with block-copolymer or DNA-tile self-assembly using cyclic annealing at temperatures where misplaced domains dissolve and correct ones persist, driving defect density to memory grade without EUV.
note: Annealing is already standard DSA practice; the defect floor remains.

title: Epigenetic-mark 1T charge-trap DRAM produced in NOR flash fabs
idea: Methyl marks change gene expression without changing the gene. A 1-transistor cell with a ~2 nm tunnel oxide and a nitride trap layer stores bits as threshold shifts that last seconds to minutes, written by fast direct tunneling, in NOR and embedded-flash fabs that already run charge-trap modules.

title: Phyllotaxis self-assembly patterns vertical-channel gain cell arrays
idea: Plants pack seeds and leaves in dense spirals through local inhibition. Block-copolymer directed self-assembly forms hexagonal arrays of ~10 nm-pitch vertical channel holes for vertical capacitorless transistors, guided by a sparse coarse pre-pattern.
note: 10 nm-pitch vertical transistors leave no room for a gate stack.

title: Mercury thermometer and electrowetting display: liquid-metal nanomeniscus bit
idea: Seal a gallium-alloy nanodroplet in a 20-nm SiO2 nanochannel with two pockets; electrocapillary actuation (as in electrowetting displays) pushes the meniscus into one pocket, where it bridges or opens a gap between two electrodes, and surface-tension pinning at a constriction holds it with zero power. Read is a resistance check; the liquid reforms perfectly every cycle.
note: Duplicate of electrowetting nanoplug position bit.

title: Photochromic sunglasses: electrically switched diarylethene molecular bit
idea: Diarylethenes flip between open (insulating) and closed (conjugated, ~100x more conductive) isomers; anchor a monolayer in a 10-nm crossbar junction and switch it by field-assisted electrochemical ring closing/opening at ~1-2 V instead of light, reading conductance nondestructively, with thousands of molecules per bit for statistical robustness.
note: Needs ~1e10x fatigue improvement; molecular crossbar memory long pursued.

title: Setting gelatin: glass-transition-locked ions freeze a double-layer bit
idea: Like gelatin that flows warm and sets cold, spin-coat a polymerized ionic liquid (Tg ~60-80 C) as the gate dielectric of a thin channel: a ns local heater pulse lifts it above Tg, the gate voltage forms an electric double layer (~10 uF/cm2), and on cooling the ions freeze in place, holding a doping-like state with no electronic leakage path; read is the channel conductance.

title: Passive-house memory: tunnel-FET latch sensing at 0.35 V
idea: Passive houses skip HVAC by cutting the heat load at the source. Run the array at VARY 0.35 V and sense with a cross-coupled tunnel-FET latch (steep <40 mV/dec slope keeps gain at low voltage), cutting bitline CV2 ~8x so modules stay within air-cooling heat flux and racks need no evaporative cooling for memory power.

title: Noise-cancelling headphones: replica-bitline subtraction enables tiny signals
idea: Like ANC headphones playing anti-noise, give every 8 bitlines a cell-less replica bitline that sees the same wordline kick and neighbour coupling; the sense amp subtracts it in the charge domain, so 30 mV signals become reliable and VARY drops to ~0.4 V.
note: SA offset and leakage, not just coupling, limit VARY; 0.4 V unlikely.

title: MLCC-in-a-hole: interleaved multi-electrode capacitor at low aspect ratio
idea: Borrowed from multilayer ceramic capacitors, which reach uF by stacking hundreds of interleaved electrodes: in a wider, shallower storage hole (AR ~20) ALD 4-6 alternating TiN/ZrO2 shells, then tie odd shells together at the bottom and even shells at the top with selective recess-and-cap, so capacitance multiplies with the number of dielectric layers.

title: Holographic recall: attention keys searched in NV analog CAM
idea: Like holographic associative memories returning the stored image closest to a probe, store KV keys in a FeFET/ReRAM analog content-addressable array that computes query-key similarity in place and returns top-k token addresses; only those k values are read from NV value storage.

title: Esaki tunnel-diode latch reborn as one transistor plus broken-gap diodes
idea: 1960s fast registers used series tunnel-diode pairs (Goto pairs) as bistable stores. Stack two InAs/GaSb broken-gap tunnel diodes (peak ~1 uA, valley ~1 pA through an engineered barrier) on the storage node of one access transistor so negative differential resistance holds two stable voltages without refresh.

title: ZettaCore redox-molecule capacitors multiply charge per 3D node
idea: Revive ZettaCore's abandoned porphyrin memory: graft a monolayer of redox molecules onto each 3D cell's storage electrode so charge is held at discrete oxidation potentials (~10x areal charge versus a dielectric at the same voltage, multi-bit), accepting ~1% molecular-variation errors.
note: ZettaCore abandoned it; molecular variation and speed doubts.

title: Zone-melting recrystallization stacks DRAM tiers without new wafers
idea: Revive MIT Lincoln Lab's 1980s zone-melting recrystallization: deposit amorphous silicon over a finished DRAM tier, melt it with a scanned line laser seeded through vias to form single-crystal islands, and build the next DUV-patterned tier on it, repeating for 8-16 tiers.
note: Seeded laser recrystallization for monolithic 3D known; lower-tier thermal damage and defects are the doubts.

title: Solid-electrolyte double-layer capacitor replaces dielectric polarization
idea: Invert 'capacitance comes from electronic dielectric polarization' -> use an ionic double layer. A 3-5 nm solid proton or Li-ion electrolyte between electrodes forms an electric double layer of ~10-20 uF/cm^2, versus ~2.6 uF/cm^2 effective in today's pillar stacks, so 5 fF needs only an AR ~10-15 cup.
note: Duplicate EDL capacitor.

title: GaN-on-sapphire wide-bandgap charge cell that never needs refresh
idea: Invert 'DRAM charge is volatile and must be refreshed' -> pick a semiconductor whose 3.4 eV bandgap makes thermal generation ~1e-20 of silicon's. An AlGaN/GaN access transistor with a junctionless p-GaN storage node on cheap LED-grade sapphire holds charge for days to years while storage stays pure charge with no material wear.

title: Tunneling-only access switch: no thermal tail, attoamp off-state
idea: Inverts 'the access device is a thermionic MOSFET': replace it with a vertical heterojunction tunnel-FET (e.g., Ge/Si or GaSb/InAs source pocket) whose OFF current is set by band-to-band tunneling through a closed window rather than the Boltzmann tail. Orient it asymmetrically so the tunnel junction sits on the bitline side and the storage node only sees a wide-gap reverse junction.

title: Negative-capacitance gate stack: beat 60 mV/decade to close the leak
idea: Inverts 'the Boltzmann 60 mV/dec limit fixes off-leakage for a given wordline swing': add a thin doped-HfO2 negative-capacitance layer to the access gate (as a voltage amplifier only, not storage) to reach ~40 mV/dec, so the same swing yields 10-100x lower Ioff or the same Ioff at ~2 V wordline.

title: Single-electron grains: revive room-temperature polysilicon percolation memory
idea: Inverts 'a bit needs ~30,000 electrons behind a switch': use an ultrathin (~3 nm) polysilicon strip whose natural grains form a percolation channel, where trapping a few electrons on one grain via Coulomb blockade shifts conduction measurably (Yano-type cell); retention is set by the blockade barrier, not a transistor off-state, and strips can be self-aligned sidewalls without fine litho.

title: Time-to-digital readout turns DRAM cells into two-bit cells
idea: Inverting 'a bit is one voltage compared once': after charge sharing, each bitline discharges through a cell-voltage-controlled current source and a time-to-digital converter shared by 64 columns timestamps the threshold crossing, resolving four stored charge levels per cell.

title: Esaki tunnel-diode Goto pair as a static one-transistor cell
idea: Inverting 'a DRAM cell stores charge': two series interband tunnel diodes form a bistable node via negative differential resistance, gated onto the bitline by one access transistor, and the node already sits at one of two latched levels so the column needs only a simple comparator.
note: TSRAM (TI, 1998) precedent; valley current times 1e10 cells and peak uniformity.

title: Self-rolling nanomembrane capacitors instead of etched 70:1 pillars
idea: Inverts 'tall capacitors must be etched downward.' Deposit a flat strained bilayer carrying electrode/dielectric/electrode, undercut a sacrificial layer and let built-in stress roll it into a multi-turn Swiss-roll capacitor standing over its transistor, giving plate area equal to AR>100 from flat films.

title: Tape-transferred monolayer MoS2 tiers, 20 nm per tier
idea: Inverts 'tiers must be grown on the wafer they live on.' Grow monolayer MoS2 access-transistor films on separate sapphire carriers by MOCVD and dry-transfer each 0.7 nm channel onto the stack, so 100 tiers fit in ~2 um and the ~1.8 eV gap suppresses the leakage tail.

title: Landau-stabilized negative-capacitance boost layer inside storage capacitor
idea: Put a thin ferroelectric layer in series with the ZrO2-based dielectric and match the capacitances so the ferroelectric sits in its hysteresis-free negative-dC/dV Landau region. The series capacitance is then C_eff = C_d*|C_fe|/(|C_fe| - C_d), 3-5x above the dielectric alone.

title: Charge-density-wave metastable state switched by picosecond electrical pulses
idea: Use the collective electron order of thin 1T-TaS2: a ~ps current pulse switches a nanoscale region from the insulating commensurate CDW into a metastable metallic 'hidden' state with 10-100x lower resistance. Confinement and strain engineering stretch its lifetime toward >=1 s at operating temperature.
note: 1T-TaS2 hidden-state memory pursued by Mihailovic group; retention at operating temperature is the gap.

title: Esaki tunnel-diode pair latch giving a static one-transistor cell
idea: Stack two heterojunction interband tunnel diodes in series (a Goto pair) on the storage node. Their N-shaped I-V gives two stable node voltages held only by the valley current; at ~1 A/cm2 valley density a 20 nm diode idles at ~4 pA, behind a single access transistor.

title: Redox-molecule monolayer: quantized one-electron-per-molecule pseudocapacitive storage
idea: Line a shallow 20 nm x 200 nm hole (10:1 AR) with a room-temperature self-assembled monolayer of ferrocene/porphyrin redox molecules on short conjugated linkers (~1e14 per cm2), with a solid polymer electrolyte supplying counter-ions. Each molecule stores exactly one electron at a fixed Nernstian potential, ~12,000 e per cell, sensed as a potential step.

title: Bidirectional tunnel-FET pair sized to the 0.5 uA write budget
idea: Derive what the access device really needs: charging 5 fF by 1 V in 10 ns takes only I = CV/t ~0.5 uA, which a vertical GaSb/InAs or SiGe/Si heterojunction tunnel FET can supply. TFETs conduct in one direction, so stack two opposite-oriented vertical TFETs in one pillar, one for write and one for read. In the off state the band-to-band window is closed, with a sub-60 mV/dec slope.

title: Negative-capacitance HZO buried wordline trades swing for higher Vt
idea: Insert a ~3 nm ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 layer into the buried-wordline gate stack, capacitance-matched to the channel. The internal gate voltage is then amplified (body factor m<1), and swing drops to ~40-45 mV/dec in the operating window. Spend that gain on a higher Vt at the same Ion, not on lower voltage.
note: Steady-state hysteresis-free NC at DRAM speeds remains contested.

title: Self-dissolving silver filament as two-terminal crosspoint access element
idea: A diffusive Ag:SiO2 threshold switch grows a sub-nm Ag bridge above ~0.4 V. When bias drops, surface energy breaks the bridge up within ~100 ns, leaving a 2-5 nm insulating gap (ON/OFF ~1e9-1e10, slope <1 mV/dec). Put one in series with each capacitor in a 4F^2 1S1C crosspoint biased so half-selected cells never cross threshold.

title: Van der Waals resonant-tunneling latch keeps each storage node topped up
idea: Integrate a series pair of graphene/hBN/graphene resonant-tunneling diodes (a Goto pair) in the capacitor top-electrode stack. Each storage node then has two stable voltages, and the RTD peak current continuously replaces what leaks away. The budget from first principles: peak current must exceed the 13 fA tail, and valley current must stay below ~0.7 pA per cell, the average power refresh spends per bit (46 fJ / 64 ms). The target is a peak-to-valley ratio of ~20 at the ~1 pA scale.

title: Column-parallel single-slope ramp sensing reads two bits per cell
idea: Borrow image-sensor column ADCs: one global ramp shared by 8k columns, a tiny comparator plus 3-bit counter per column digitizes the bitline twice (precharge and signal) and subtracts digitally (digital CDS). Offset and kT/C cancel in the subtraction, giving enough resolution to store 4 charge levels per cell.

title: Molybdenum polyoxometalate clusters store two quantized bits per node
idea: A 1 nm Keggin cluster [PMo12O40]3- accepts electrons in discrete redox steps ~0.2-0.4 V apart, so multilevel states are fixed by chemistry rather than by threshold variation. Graft a cluster monolayer as the floating storage node of a vertical gain cell, write levels with gate pulses and refresh like DRAM.

title: Grow capacitor electrodes upward by selective-area growth
idea: First principle: selective deposition happens only where surface chemistry allows, and unlike etch its rate does not depend on aspect ratio. Build the storage node bottom-up: selective-area MOCVD of conductive RuO2 or TiN nanopillars only on exposed storage-node contacts through a thin 100 nm template, braced by a lattice of nitride support rings, then wrap with high-k and a top plate.

title: Corrugated cardboard: charge-density-wave domain pattern as switchable bit
idea: Stimulus 'corrugated cardboard' (a frozen periodic ripple) -> a thin 1T-TaS2 flake whose charge-density wave is driven between an insulating commensurate-like state and a hidden metallic domain state by a ps-ns current pulse; resistance changes ~10x and the hidden state persists. Substrate strain is engineered to keep it metastable at operating temperature.

title: Hula hoop: persistent supercurrent loops at liquid-nitrogen temperature
idea: Stimulus 'hula hoop' (keeps circling once started) -> store a flux quantum in a YBCO nanoloop with a weak link, operated in a 77 K liquid-nitrogen rack memory pool rather than a helium cryostat; current circulates indefinitely and a nearby flux sensor reads its direction.

title: Pogo stick: ferroelectric negative capacitance cancels bitline load
idea: A pogo spring returns energy instead of absorbing it. Put a thin HZO negative-capacitance element in series at each SA input so the bitline-plus-NC network shows a much smaller effective capacitance during charge sharing, raising the signal per unit charge and letting the array run at ~0.4-0.5 V.

title: Swiss roll: self-rolling strained MIM film forms horizontal 3D DRAM capacitors
idea: Random stimulus 'Swiss roll' -> in lateral 3D DRAM tiers, a planar electrode/high-k/electrode stack with a built-in strain gradient is deposited, its sacrificial underlayer is released, and the stack curls into a multi-turn coil filling the tier cavity. Capacitor area grows 5-10x with only planar deposition.

title: Keyboard matrix: selector-free self-rectifying FTJ crosspoint stacks, two masks per layer
idea: Random stimulus 'keyboard matrix' (keys at row/column crossings) -> a ferroelectric tunnel junction (thin HZO with asymmetric electrodes) rectifies by itself, so 4F2 crosspoint decks need only two line masks each. Eight decks are stacked with DUV SAQP, and a DRAM-front cache plus wear-leveling supply effectively unlimited endurance.

title: Room-temperature Coulomb-blockade dot storing five electrons per bit
idea: Box = {medium: 1-10 electrons on a ~2 nm Si dot | access: tunnel barrier to a 5 nm Si nanowire channel | sense: dot charge gates the nanowire (gain read) | integration: stacked vertical nanowires | substrate: Si | fab: self-limiting thermal oxidation sculpts the dot}. The dot's ~0.3-0.5 eV charging energy blocks back-tunneling, so a few electrons hold state for seconds, and the nanowire current amplifies them for sensing.
note: Same few-electron node read by Coulomb-blockade gain.

title: Nanoelectromechanical relay access device with air-gap zero leakage
idea: Box = {medium: charge on a MIM capacitor | access: 4-terminal NEMS relay with a 5 nm air gap | sense: charge-share SA | integration: relay array in BEOL over the capacitors | substrate: Si | fab: sacrificial release + Pt-coated contacts}. When the relay is open, the only leakage path is the capacitor dielectric, so retention moves from 64 ms to hours and the capacitor can shrink to ~1 fF.

title: Redox-molecule monolayer storage node with built-in multi-level voltages
idea: Box = {medium: electrons held in surface-tethered porphyrin/ferrocene molecules with discrete oxidation potentials | access: Si FET | sense: charge read against molecule-defined levels (2 bits per cell) | integration: monolayer grafted inside a short pillar | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: U.S.-synthesized molecules attached from solution, following the North Carolina molecular-memory lineage}. Each oxidation state releases charge at a potential fixed by chemistry, so the multi-level references calibrate themselves, and retention comes from slow electron-transfer kinetics rather than transistor leakage.

title: Nanoelectromechanical relay as zero-leakage DRAM access switch
idea: Box: MIM cap x electrostatic NEMS cantilever relay in a sealed gap x charge-share SA x BEOL monolithic over periphery x Si x sacrificial-layer release with Ru contacts. When open the gap carries essentially zero current, so only capacitor-dielectric leakage remains; ~1-10 ns mechanical closure on a 20 nm gap.

title: Negative-capacitance HZO gate raises access threshold without drive loss
idea: Box: standard pillar cap x recessed-channel access with an HZO negative-capacitance layer over the gate oxide x standard SA x in-array x Si x ALD gate-stack swap. NC voltage amplification gives sub-60 mV/dec swing, so Vt can be raised ~200 mV at the same on-current.
note: Same NC gate idea.

title: Direct-tunneling charge-trap cell with second-scale retention
idea: Box: charge in a SiN/HfO2 trap layer x 1.5-2 nm tunnel oxide written by direct tunneling (not Fowler-Nordheim) x gain-transistor sensing x in-array x Si x ALD gate stack. Direct tunneling at ~1.5 V writes in ~10 ns without the high-field damage that limits flash endurance, while trap depth gives seconds of retention.

title: Coulomb-blockade silicon dot holds bit behind charging energy
idea: Box: few-electron Si quantum dot (<3 nm) storage x wordline-gated tunnel barrier access x single-electron-transistor electrometer sensing x in-array x SOI x oxidation-thinned nanowire. The dot's charging energy (>10 kT at room temperature for sub-3 nm dots) blocks electron escape until the wordline lowers the barrier.
note: Room-temperature single-electron memories (1990s) stalled on variability and slow SET readout.

title: Two-bit-per-cell DRAM with Gray-coded four-level sensing
idea: Box: high-k pillar cap x Si access x 4-level successive-approximation sensing x standard x bulk Si x standard. Each cell stores one of four charge levels read by a 2-step SAR comparator; Gray mapping makes most level errors single-bit, so the ~1% raw error rate fits a rate-0.88 code.

title: Carbon-nanotube forests as capacitor bottom electrodes on each pad
