title: Retrofit fab air-separation units to recover helium and neon
idea: Scale jump from atmosphere to fab: on-site ASUs at large existing fabs process ~4000 t/day of air for nitrogen. A non-condensable-gas column with a cryo-adsorber on the condenser vent captures neon (18 ppm, ~50 kg/day) and helium (5 ppm, ~20 L liquid-equivalent/day).
note: ASU neon recovery is standard at large plants; fab-scale helium yield is small.

title: Warehouse fab: sealed tool pods replace the ballroom cleanroom
idea: Shrink the controlled environment from building scale (ISO 3-5 ballroom with massive HVAC) to the cubic metre around each wafer: every tool sits in a sealed N2 mini-environment linked by enclosed overhead wafer tubes, so the shell is an ordinary warehouse.

title: U.S. hybrid-bond HBM assembly from imported known-good DRAM wafers
idea: Shift the U.S. entry point from the 5-year fab scale to the 18-month packaging scale: tariff-exempt imports of tested DRAM wafers feed U.S.-built hybrid-bonding and stacking lines backed by investment tax credits, producing HBM and DRAM-on-logic domestically; front-end fabs follow once demand is captive.
note: Close to SK hynix Indiana HBM packaging plant already underway.

title: Strategic DRAM Reserve: buy in gluts, release in spikes
idea: Nation-scale, decade time shift modeled on the oil reserve: a government agency buys known-good DRAM die and packaged parts when contract prices sit at the bottom of the cycle, stores them unpowered (data retention is irrelevant and the silicon keeps for decades) in dry vaults, and auctions them during price spikes.

title: U.S. Memories redux: take-or-pay offtake with a price collar
idea: The 1989 U.S. Memories consortium (IBM, DEC, HP, Intel and others) collapsed before raising its ~$1B because DRAM prices fell and members refused binding purchase commitments. Fix exactly that: hyperscalers and OEMs sign 10-year take-or-pay contracts with a price collar (floor for lenders, ceiling for buyers in shortages like 2026) plus a federal buyer-of-last-resort backstop.

title: Continuous Czochralski growth stretches each Spruce Pine quartz crucible
idea: Continuous Czochralski (CCZ) was tried in the 1980s-90s and dropped as batch CZ improved. Feed polysilicon granules continuously into a double crucible so one high-purity quartz crucible grows 5-8 DRAM-grade 300 mm ingots instead of one, with steadier oxygen content for retention uniformity.

title: Tezzaron wafer-stack yield fixed: spare tier plus base-die remap
idea: Tezzaron's wafer-on-wafer DRAM stacks struggled because stack yield is the product of tier yields, with no way to drop a bad tier after bonding. Stack N+1 tiers (e.g., 9 for 8), each tier's TSV bus independently gated by fuse-programmed switches in the base die; post-bond test finds the worst tier and the base die routes around it, and when all tiers are good the extra one is sold as capacity.

title: Elpida's yen-and-cycle death: a cleared DRAM bit futures market
idea: Elpida failed in 2012 with competitive technology, killed by a strong yen and a price cycle it could not hedge. Fix: a cleared futures and options exchange on a standard contract (e.g. 1 Tb of DDR5-equivalent per quarter, cash-settled against a published contract-price index) lets makers sell forward and buyers lock in supply, as airlines hedge jet fuel.

title: Buried piezoresistive stressor trades extra mobility for higher access Vt
idea: Effect: piezoresistance (strain-shifted conduction valleys). Wrap the buried-channel access transistor with a ~1.5 GPa tensile SiN or AlN liner, raising electron mobility 30-50%, then spend that drive on ~90 mV higher Vt, so write speed and VPP stay the same. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.

title: Interface dipole sets access Vt so channel doping can drop
idea: Effect: interfacial dipole at the high-k/SiO2 boundary. An Al2O3 dipole monolayer shifts the buried-wordline gate's effective work function by +0.2-0.3 V, letting channel boron doping fall ~3x; lower doping lowers the peak storage-junction field, and field-enhanced trap-assisted tunneling drops ~10x. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.

title: Epitaxial silicon stack sets access gate length by thickness, not litho
idea: Si: grow an in-situ-doped n+/p/n+ silicon stack by CVD epitaxy so the vertical channel length (80-120 nm) is fixed by the p-layer thickness to +/-1 nm, then etch DUV-immersion SAQP pillars and wrap a gate-all-around wordline, giving a 4F2 cell at DUV-reachable F of ~18-20 nm.

title: Germanium-rich sacrificial layers set lateral gate length by recess depth
idea: Ge: grow an alternating Si/SiGe superlattice, cut deep slits with DUV, then laterally recess the Ge-rich layers with a self-limiting vapor-HCl atomic-layer etch to a programmed depth; the recess depth, not lithography, sets each tier's lateral access-transistor gate length, and the regrown gate wraps the Si nanosheet.

title: Titanium nitride mirror plate pillar serves two cell strings per hole
idea: Lay out 3D DRAM so each vertical TiN plate-line pillar sits between two mirrored lateral cell strings whose capacitors both wrap that same pillar; one deep plate etch and fill serves twice the cells and anchors the alignment of both strings.
note: Mirror-cell shared plate is a common lateral 3D DRAM layout.

title: Unbundle hafnium from nuclear zirconium with a U.S. separation hub
idea: Periodic-table walk, Hf (72): hafnium exists only as a by-product of nuclear-grade Zr purification, so fund a Hf/Zr solvent-extraction plant fed by Florida-Georgia-Virginia heavy-mineral-sand zircon, with chipmaker offtake contracts and a strategic reserve.
note: Known solvent-extraction chemistry; mainly a funding/offtake policy, plant far exceeds $1M.

title: La: LaB6 multi-cathode e-beam writes periphery without mask sets
idea: Use arrays of thousands of LaB6 cathodes in a multi-beam direct-write tool for the irregular periphery and low-volume layers, eliminating mask sets and enabling rapid design spins in a small U.S. fab.

title: Germanium photodetectors: optically pooled rack memory at 0.3 pJ/bit
idea: Ge-on-Si photodetectors and microring modulators in co-packaged optics connect every CPU in a rack to a shared memory pool at ~0.3 pJ/bit link energy over WDM, so servers ship with half their DRAM and borrow the rest from the pool on demand.

title: B: turn idle US borosilicate glass lines into interposer fabs
idea: Retool shuttered or underused US display/solar glass finishing lines to produce 510x515 mm borosilicate glass-core panels with laser-drilled through-glass vias for HBM packaging, using the existing US specialty-glass base instead of building new silicon interposer capacity.

title: Cu: hybrid-bonded 16-high DDR5 3DS stacks in standard packages
idea: Use Cu-Cu/oxide hybrid bonding (no microbumps, no underfill) to stack 16 thinned DDR5 dies within today's 3DS package height, keeping the standard DDR5 3DS ballout and RDIMM interface.
note: Hybrid-bonded 16-high is HBM roadmap; applying to DDR5 3DS is incremental.

title: Ca: CaF2-optic DUV forever-node lines from refurbished scanners
idea: Freeze a DRAM design at an EUV-free 1z-class node with self-aligned quadruple patterning, buy used ArF-immersion scanners on the secondary market and refurbish their CaF2 optics domestically, competing on depreciated capital rather than node.

title: Ar: Industrial-gas cooperative utility for a memory micro-fab park
idea: Cluster 4-8 memory micro-fabs around one cooperatively owned air-separation unit (N2, Ar, O2), shared helium recovery and ultrapure-water plant, each fab paying by metered consumption.

title: Puff-pastry lamination: binary-tree bonding of mature-node DRAM wafers
idea: Laminated dough multiplies layers by folding; hybrid-bond pairs of thinned 2x-nm DRAM wafers face to face, then bond pairs of pairs, so a 16-tier stack needs only 4 serial bond-and-thin steps run in parallel on existing bonding and grinding tools, with relaxed 10 um edge TSVs.
note: Footprint gain only; W2W cannot select good tiers, cost per bit not reduced.

title: Pharma isolator fab: sealed tool tunnels replace ballroom cleanrooms
idea: Aseptic pharma moved from cleanrooms to sealed isolators; connect DRAM tools with nitrogen-purged sealed transport tunnels and mini-environments so only ~5% of fab volume is ISO-class clean and the rest is ordinary industrial air.

title: Melt-pool-style monitoring: test each 3D tier before it is buried
idea: Metal 3D printers watch every layer's melt pool; after each 3D-DRAM tier is patterned, scan it with e-beam voltage-contrast inspection (no xenon plasma FIB or rare-gas plasma) to map opens and shorts, and program that tier's remap into antifuses or a base-die table before the next tier covers it.

title: Kalundborg symbiosis park: fab, data center and grid trade byproducts
idea: Kalundborg's industrial park trades steam, gypsum and water between plants. Co-site a DRAM fab with a hyperscale data center and a power plant. Reclaimed fab water cools the data center, data-center heat drives fab HVAC reheat and UPW preheat, spent acids go to fertilizer, and known-good dies cross the fence straight into servers.

title: Fluorocarbon-free capacitor-hole etch by cryogenic HF/water vapor
idea: Ideal: high-aspect-ratio etch with no PFAS gases. Closest: etch 60-75:1 capacitor holes at -60 to -80 C using HF + H2O/NH4F chemistry where a condensed adsorbed HF layer drives ion-assisted SiO2 removal and frozen reaction products passivate sidewalls, dropping C4F6/C4F8/CH2F2 entirely.
note: Cryogenic HF hole etch already demonstrated by tool vendors for 3D NAND.

title: MeV-implant proximity gettering under the array
idea: Ideal: silicon with no metal impurities near the storage node. Closest: a high-energy (MeV) carbon or silicon implant places a damage layer ~2-3 um below the array that traps iron, nickel and copper during later anneals, removing the deep-level generation centers behind tail cells.

title: Per-mat triple-well back-bias tuned to each mat's leakage mix
idea: Ideal: every mat sits at its own minimum-leakage point. Closest: put each mat in its own 1990s triple-well island with a small local charge pump, and set its substrate bias at test to balance subthreshold leakage (wants deeper bias) against junction and GIDL leakage (wants shallower bias) for that mat's measured tail.
note: Adaptive body bias per block is known.

title: Bottle-bill deposits on DRAM packages to fund reverse logistics
idea: Ideal: memory comes back by itself. Closest achievable: a $3-10 refundable deposit on every device's DRAM, redeemable at e-waste collectors who route memory packages to reprocessors, so the deposit pays for the collection network.

title: Corolla node: freeze one DRAM process for ten years
idea: Ideal: a node whose tools cost nothing. Closest achievable: run a 1y/1z-nm DDR5 process unchanged for a decade on fully depreciated tools and grow volume by moving tool sets from fabs that upgrade, instead of chasing each new node.

title: Die bank: hold wafers before metal, finish to demand in weeks
idea: Ideal: memory made instantly on order. Closest achievable on existing lines: fabs park WIP wafers in nitrogen stockers at the pre-BEOL hold point (~70% done), then metallize, fuse and package into whichever product is short.

title: Tungsten-free periphery: molybdenum contacts and plate-layer routing
idea: Limit: zero tungsten (China ~80% of supply). Replace W contacts and M0 in the periphery with ALD molybdenum or ruthenium, and reuse the capacitor top-plate film (TiN/doped SiGe) as an extra local routing layer for decoder and SA interconnect, deleting one W metal level.
note: Mo replacement of W already pursued by toolmakers.

title: Grounded shield-plate tiers that make row hammer impossible
idea: Limit: no row may have an electrically coupled neighbor. Insert a thin grounded metal plane between every pair of cell tiers, and alternate wordline tiers between different banks. The plane blocks both capacitive crosstalk and carrier migration from aggressor rows.
note: Same grounded shield-plane isolation core.

title: Copper wordlines and bitlines buried beneath the cell array
idea: Under 400 C, an oxide 4F2 vertical-channel array never heats buried wiring past 400 C, so buried word and bitlines can be damascene Cu, normally banned under a DRAM cell flow. Sub-array lines get about 2-3x longer per local driver.

title: Unsawn wafer as memory module: no dicing, packaging or DIMMs
idea: Constraint: zero back-end line. Ship the whole 300 mm DRAM wafer as a ~1.5 TB memory slab: a wafer-level redistribution layer stitches good dies into a mesh, bad dies are fenced off, edge SerDes expose CXL ports and a cold plate bonds to the back.
note: Same unsawn-wafer RDL mesh as I-08981.

title: Implant-free junctions from in-situ doped selective epitaxy
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: replace cell and periphery junction implants with in-situ doped selective epitaxy and conformal plasma doping, eliminating end-of-range implant damage that seeds trap-assisted gate-induced drain leakage at 125 C.

title: Depreciated non-EUV fabs feed forty-tier capacity stacks
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. Source 1x/2x-nm-class DRAM dies from fully depreciated, EUV-free lines (wafer cost ~1/3 of leading edge since depreciation is ~55% of cost) and stack 40 tiers per footprint so tiers, not lithography, deliver bits per mm2 of board.
note: Footprint density is not $/bit; 40-tier stacking cost dominates.

title: No HBM stack scrapped: base-die remap into lower-capacity SKUs
idea: Self-imposed limit: zero stack scrap. Stacks with one or two dead core dies are remapped by base-die logic into 6- or 10-high equivalent SKUs, with channels re-striped, and sold to inference customers who need bandwidth more than capacity.

title: Swap EUV contact holes for block-copolymer cylinder self-assembly
idea: Coat a high-chi block copolymer (PS-b-PDMS or PS-b-P2VP) into relaxed-pitch DUV guide holes, so each guide splits into a cluster of 3-7 cylinders at ~24 nm pitch. The cylinders are then transferred into the hard mask that defines the storage-node holes.

title: Software-switchable twin-cell mode per subarray
idea: Add a switch in each SA stripe so a subarray runs either as 1T1C (full capacity) or as 2T2C differential pairs (half capacity, ~4-8x retention and margin); the OS chooses the mode per subarray by workload and temperature.
note: Essentially CLR-DRAM style capacity/latency reconfiguration.

title: B-grade DRAM tier: buy JEDEC rejects, run them at 4x refresh
idea: Combine die binning with hyperscaler memory tiering: dies failing 64 ms retention but passing 16 ms are sold at a discount on modules whose controller profile sets 4x refresh and stronger ECC, deployed as a capacity tier for caching and inference KV-cache.

title: Wafer-reclaim Smart Cut: reusable donor wafer gives SOI access transistors
idea: Adapted from SOI layer transfer and the wafer-reclaim trade: cleave a thin single-crystal layer for the access transistors off a donor wafer by hydrogen implant, bond it onto oxide on the carrier, then repolish and reuse the donor 10+ times; the buried oxide removes the storage-junction-to-substrate leakage path.

title: Eliminate water rinses: supercritical CO2 cleaning of capacitor holes
idea: Replace post-etch wet cleans and IPA drying of high-AR capacitor holes with supercritical CO2 plus co-solvent cleaning and drying in one chamber, so no liquid-vapour meniscus ever forms inside the structures.
note: Supercritical drying already used for high-AR DRAM pattern collapse.

title: Eliminate the pulse-purge ALD bottleneck: rotary spatial ALD for capacitor dielectrics
idea: Deposit the ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 capacitor stack on a rotating platen that carries wafers through separated precursor and oxidant zones with long dwell for deep holes, instead of time-sequenced pulse-purge chambers. Device and DDR/HBM interface are unchanged.
note: Semi-batch rotary ALD is already used for DRAM high-k.

title: Shape after printing: angled ion beam stretches DUV features
idea: Rearrange litho into litho-plus-sculpt: print one relaxed ArF layer, then use angled reactive ion beams to elongate or merge holes and slots in one direction, replacing the second exposure of double patterning.

title: Area-selective deposition grows features only where needed
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality: use inhibitor monolayers (aminosilanes or small-molecule inhibitors) that block ALD on dielectric but not on metal. Landing-pad caps, contact liners and bitline spacers then self-align by growth instead of by litho + etch, deleting a resist coat, a fluorocarbon etch and a mask for each layer replaced.

title: Thermal expansion: one-mask stressor liner lets legacy fabs hit modern speed bins
idea: TRIZ #37 Thermal expansion: one mask selectively places a high-CTE-mismatch nitride liner over periphery transistors, where cooling locks in strain that lifts drive current ~15-25% so depreciated 1x nm fabs ship faster bins.
note: Stress liners are standard logic practice since 90 nm.

title: HDD glass platters inspire panel glass interposers for HBM
idea: Hard-disk makers moved platters from aluminum to ultra-flat glass. Replace the HBM silicon interposer (cut from 300 mm wafers) with a panel-processed glass interposer from the display/HDD glass supply chain, using laser-drilled through-glass vias and 2 um redistribution lines, while keeping the identical HBM3E/HBM4 PHY, microbump map and protocol.

title: Po: memory is a record player — probe-array ferroelectric domain film
idea: Po: memory is a record player. Extracted: a 10,000-tip MEMS cantilever array scans a blanket LiNbO3 or PZT thin film, writing ~10 nm polarization domains with tip voltage and reading them non-destructively by piezoresponse, so the medium is unpatterned and only the tips need lithography.
note: IBM Millipede/Seagate ferroelectric probe storage precedent; us-ms access is storage, not DRAM.

title: Po: dies talk without touching — inductive-coupled stack I/O
idea: Po: a memory stack with no data TSVs. Replace HBM data TSVs with vertically aligned on-die Cu/Al spiral coil pairs (inductive coupling through thinned dies), keeping only a few large power TSVs for supply.
note: ThruChip Interface (Kuroda, Keio) already demonstrated with DRAM stacks.

title: Po the chip is mostly air: air-gap bitlines shrink capacitors
idea: Po: 'the chip is mostly air.' Extracted: after patterning bitlines, cap them with non-conformal PECVD oxide that pinches off above the spaces, leaving air (k ~1) between neighbors; bitline capacitance falls ~40%, so the same sense signal needs ~40% less storage capacitance.

title: Inductive coil links replace signal TSVs in memory stacks
idea: Worse: drill thousands of signal TSVs through every die and lose area and yield. Flip: put small spiral coils in top metal for near-field inductive data links between thinned stacked dies, keeping only a few large power TSVs.

title: Four-level analog charge storage borrowed from particle-detector pipelines
idea: Collider front-ends store analog samples on capacitors at 40 MHz; applied to DRAM, each cell holds one of four voltage levels, sensed by a two-step successive-approximation sense amplifier, with a per-row reference cell written alongside the data to track leakage drift. Two bits live in one capacitor.
note: MLC DRAM tried since 1990s; margin collapse vs leakage tail is the long-known barrier.

title: Panel-level fan-out packaging retires glass-cloth substrates for DRAM
idea: Scale jump from wafer to 600x600 mm panel: embed thinned DRAM dies in mold-compound panels and build redistribution layers directly on them. This removes BT/ABF laminates reinforced with T-glass cloth (one dominant supplier) and the gold or copper wire bonds.

title: Ion-cut layer splitting turns one donor wafer into many device layers
idea: Scale shift from wafer to micrometer layer: existing SOI wafer plants implant hydrogen ~1 um deep, bond to a cheap carrier and split off a single-crystal layer. The donor is re-polished and reused 10-20 times, and DRAM arrays are built on the transferred layers.
note: Smart Cut; donor reuse limited in practice.

title: Solid-source phosphorus drive-in grades storage junctions to cut peak field
idea: P: instead of implanting the storage-node junction, fill the self-aligned contact hole with phosphosilicate glass and drive phosphorus in by rapid thermal anneal, forming an implant-damage-free, linearly graded junction with ~30-40% lower peak field and no added mask.
note: Doped-poly storage contacts already out-diffuse P to form the junction.

title: Lost-foam casting: sacrificial polymer evaporates into bitline air gaps
idea: Like lost-foam casting, where the foam pattern vaporizes as metal fills the mold, fill between bitlines with a thermally decomposable polynorbornene (late-1990s chemistry) and cap it with porous oxide. A ~425 C bake makes the polymer diffuse out, leaving air gaps.
note: Air-gap bitline spacers already in production DRAM; sacrificial polymer route is old.

title: Stained-glass mosaic interposer from known-good DUV tiles
idea: Make small reticle-size interposer tiles on DUV lines, test them, and join them like stained glass with printed bridge seams playing the lead came, building panels of more than four reticles.
note: CoWoS-L/EMIB bridge tiling already does this.

title: Factory-seconds grade: sell retention-weak dies as inference memory
idea: Like garment 'seconds', create a product grade for dies that fail the 64 ms/85C retention spec or exceed repair, sold with a qualified controller profile (32 ms refresh, page-retirement list, on-module strong ECC) for AI inference and caches where data is rewritten constantly.

title: Spinning-jenny probe cards: MEMS cantilever arrays testing every die at once
idea: The spinning jenny let one worker run dozens of spindles. Fabricate MEMS probe cards in a nanofab: electroplated Ni-Co cantilevers on silicon at ~40 um pitch, so one touchdown contacts every die on the wafer for parallel retention and row-hammer screening.
note: Full-wafer single-touchdown DRAM probe cards already exist.

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal passivates leakage-tail traps
idea: Ideal: an access transistor with zero interface traps. Closest: finish wafers with a high-pressure (5-20 atm) deuterium furnace anneal, a mid-1990s finding, because Si-D bonds resist thermal and hot-carrier breakage far better than Si-H, so trap-assisted junction leakage and VRT cells are passivated more completely and stay passivated.

title: Sacrificial-polymer air-gap bitlines halve bitline capacitance
idea: Under 400 C, fill between bitlines with a polynorbornene-type sacrificial polymer, cap it with porous ALD SiO2, and decompose it through the cap at 350 C to leave air gaps. This works only because no later step needs high temperature.
note: Air-spacer bitlines already in production DRAM.

title: Barrierless molybdenum buried wordline from Colorado ore
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero tungsten (China ~80%). Fill the buried wordline trench by MoO2Cl2/H2 CVD of molybdenum directly on the work-function liner, dropping the TiN barrier because Mo needs no protection from fluorine, and source the precursor from U.S. Climax/Henderson molybdenum.

title: Rotary spatial ALD deposits capacitor dielectrics at 300 wafers per hour
idea: Constraint: one-tenth of today's deposition tool count. Wafers orbit under separated precursor and purge zones near atmospheric pressure, so ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 stacks grow by motion rather than valve cycling; long-dwell and ozone-assisted sectors restore conformality in 70:1 holes.
note: Rotary semi-batch spatial ALD already used for DRAM high-k.

title: Fluorine-free molybdenum wordlines grown barrier-less from chloride precursors
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: deposit Mo from MoO2Cl2 directly on the wordline gate oxide with no TiN barrier and no fluorine, so there is no fluorine to attack the oxide, and the freed barrier volume goes to a thicker, longer-lived gate dielectric.

title: TSV keep-out rings fused with segmented deep-trench storage capacitors
idea: Combine the HBM TSV and the cell capacitor: etch an annular deep trench (AR ~50) in the dead keep-out zone around each TSV, split it into 16-32 sectors with vertical dielectric fins, and use each sector as a storage capacitor read through vertical transistors on the ring rim. One structure is the TSV stress shield, a decoupling cap and bit storage.
note: Novel reuse of TSV keep-out zones, but gain only ~5-8% bits.

title: Magnify usable bits: reclaim on-die ECC parity cells
idea: DDR5 dies carry about 6.25% extra cells for on-die ECC. Partner with a second-tier vendor to expose a test-mode map that releases those cells as user capacity for error-tolerant data such as AI weights and caches, with protection handled by host-side ECC.
note: Parity cells cover weak-cell yield; exposing them needs datapath changes, not a test mode.

title: Transfluxor multi-aperture micro-yokes made in hard-disk head wafer fabs
idea: RCA's 1956 transfluxor used a two-aperture core whose main-leg flux state blocks or unblocks flux around the small aperture, giving non-destructive reads. HDD write-head fabs already plate NiFe/CoFe yokes around Cu coils at 0.1-1 um; build micro-transfluxors there whose minor-aperture coil reads by an AC drive that couples only when the main leg is unblocked.
note: Micron-scale cells; rad-hard niche only.

title: Pool every switch FIFO and retimer buffer into network memory
idea: Worsen: let every switch, retimer and NIC hold its own idle SRAM FIFOs. Flip: expose the tens of MB of SRAM buffering in a rack's switches and CXL retimers as an addressable, latency-tagged pool for in-flight tensors, so data in transit lands in the network instead of DRAM.
note: Switch SRAM is small and needed for packets; little memory reclaimed.

title: Sn: self-healing Sn-In microbumps reflowed by on-die heaters
idea: Replace SnAg microbumps in HBM stacks with Sn-In eutectic (118 C) and add polysilicon microheaters beside bump fields; when base-die link training detects rising error rates or resistance, the stack is reflowed in place during a maintenance window to heal thermo-mechanical cracks.

title: Substitute carborane superacid anions for fluorinated photoacid generators
idea: Make photoacid generators whose anion is a chlorinated closo-carborane (CHB11Cl11-), a weakly coordinating superacid conjugate with no C-F bonds, giving PFAS-class acid strength and low acid diffusion in chemically amplified resists.

title: Induction-heated bumps bond stacks without baking DRAM
idea: Substitute oven or thermocompression heating with RF induction: bumps carry a ferromagnetic nickel core that heats selectively in a 1-10 MHz field, melting solder at the joint while DRAM silicon stays below ~100 C; the tool is a coil, an RF supply and a press.
note: Localized induction soldering has precedent; heating also couples into Cu lines and TSVs.

title: Water-soluble release layer under the interposer
idea: MINIFY end-of-life separation cost: a polymer release layer between interposer and dies dissolves in hot water, so dies, interposer and substrate separate cleanly for reuse or pure-stream recycling.

title: Shape-memory alloy clamps that release chiplets at 80 C
idea: MINIFY disassembly effort: NiTi clamps hold memory chiplets on pressure contacts and spring open when the package is heated to ~80 C in a recycling oven, so dies drop out intact.

title: Eliminate static storage: bistable Duffing MEMS resonators sustained by pump
idea: Each bit is the high- or low-amplitude branch of a nonlinear (Duffing) silicon-nitride nanomechanical resonator; one shared parametric pump tone keeps every resonator on whichever branch it occupies, so state is held by the pump, not by isolated charge. Writes kick a resonator between branches; reads sense amplitude capacitively.

title: Run the fab to the sun: energy-time rearranged WIP
idea: Rearrange the time order of steps: hold larger WIP buffers before energy-hungry steps (EUV exposures, furnaces, anneals) so they batch into curtailed-renewable hours, while low-power steps run around the clock.

title: Manganese oxide abrasive replaces rare-earth ceria in CMP
idea: TRIZ #38 Strong oxidants: use Mn2O3/MnO2 nanoparticles whose Mn3+/Mn4+ redox bonds to and breaks Si-O bonds, supplying the 'chemical tooth' that ceria provides via Ce3+/Ce4+. They replace ceria in STI and ILD planarization.

title: Silica-lined polyethylene replaces fluoropolymer ultrapure-water piping
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells and thin films: build UPW and chemical distribution from high-density polyethylene pipe whose inner wall carries a plasma-deposited SiOx/a-C:H barrier film. The film blocks leaching and particle shedding, the reasons PFA/PVDF (both PFAS) were chosen.

title: Rhodopsin-switch resist: retinal-style photoisomerization, no fluorinated acid
idea: Vision uses retinal's cis-trans photoisomerization to change a protein's shape with no acid catalyst. Build a non-chemically-amplified resist whose side chains carry retinal- or azobenzene-like switches; once isomerized they break a hydrogen-bond network and make exposed areas soluble in aqueous developer, so no perfluoroalkyl sulfonate photoacid generator is needed.

title: Mussel-catechol temporary bonding tape for HBM wafer thinning
idea: Mussels stick underwater with catechol (DOPA) proteins that let go when oxidized. Coat roll-to-roll a dopamine-functional polymer tape that bonds device wafers to carriers for thinning and TSV reveal, then debonds at room temperature in a mild oxidizing or pH-switch rinse.

title: Pine-cone bimorph valves that cool only the dies running hot
idea: On an organic build-up substrate (no silicon interposer), polymer/metal bilayer micro-flaps over coolant ports curl open when the DRAM above them heats, as pine-cone scales open when they dry. Coolant goes to hot stacks automatically, with no sensors, valves or control logic.

title: Taylor-wire woven memory: glass-coated amorphous microwires as bistable bits
idea: Revive the Taylor (1924) and Ulitovsky (1950s) process, which draws glass-coated amorphous Fe-Si-B microwires with near-perfect square hysteresis (a large Barkhausen jump), and weave them with copper word wires like a 1960s core plane. Each crossing segment flips only on coincident currents and gives a sharp sense pulse, and the bit pitch is set by wire diameter and weave rather than lithography.

title: Plated-wire NDRO memory for read-mostly tensors
idea: Revive Apollo-era plated wire: electroplate a 1 um NiFe film with circumferential anisotropy around lithographed copper lines, cross them with word straps, and read non-destructively by sensing the small magnetization tilt a word pulse causes, writing with coincident word and bit currents. Every step is UV litho, sputtering and plating.
note: Plated-wire density is orders below DRAM/NAND; MRAM already covers magnetic NDRO.

title: Full-restore sweep banks maximum charge before long idle periods
idea: Retention is t = dQ/I, and timing-limited activations often leave cells ~5-10% short of full VDD. Before a rank enters relaxed refresh or self-refresh, the controller sweeps every row with 2-3x tRAS/tWR so each cell banks its full charge, and only then lengthens the interval. This is pure controller timing work, prototyped on an FPGA DRAM platform for <$200k.

title: Hot-embossed polymer trenches give 3D capacitors without plasma etch
idea: Emboss 5:1 trenches at 1 um pitch into a COC or polyimide web with a nickel-shim roller, conformally coat metal/AlOx/metal by spatial ALD and fill with printed conductor, giving each cell a folded capacitor.
note: 1 um pitch cells are ~100x less dense than DRAM.

title: Self-unzipping resists recovered as monomer and repolymerized
idea: First principle: lithography needs only a transient chemical contrast, yet resist is burned or dumped. Use low-ceiling-temperature polymers (e.g., polyphthalaldehyde) that depolymerize fully to monomer under exposure or mild heat, capture the evaporated monomer in a cold trap on the track, then purify and repolymerize it.

title: Rice cooker: rice-husk silica replaces rare-earth ceria in CMP
idea: Stimulus 'rice cooker' -> burn rice husks (~20% silica) under controlled conditions into amorphous nanosilica, then surface-dope with Fe, Mn or Ti to mimic ceria's chemical-tooth Si-O-metal bonding; use it as an oxide/nitride-selective STI and ILD CMP abrasive.

title: Vinyl record: electroless nickel-boron contact plugs replace CVD tungsten
idea: Stimulus 'vinyl record' (an electroformed nickel stamper copies every groove) -> fill bit-line and storage-node contacts bottom-up with electroless Ni-B or Ni-P plated from a self-catalyzing seed below 90 C, instead of WF6 CVD tungsten.

title: Rooftop solar: recycled PV silicon cast into dummy and monitor wafers
idea: Stimulus 'rooftop solar panel' -> a 10-person shop recovers silicon from end-of-life PV modules, recasts it by directional solidification and cores/slices 300 mm rounds for dummy, monitor and temporary-carrier wafers that need no prime Cz silicon.

title: Ice hotel: platinum-group-free, tungsten-free MTJ stack from abundant elements
idea: Random stimulus 'ice hotel' (built only from local, abundant material) -> a heavy-metal-free STT stack: MnN exchange-bias pinning instead of IrMn or PtMn, a Cr spacer synthetic antiferromagnet instead of Ru, an Fe-rich FeB/MgO free layer, and Mo caps instead of Ta or W.

title: Parametron revived: AlN nanoresonator phase bits made in U.S. filter fabs
idea: Box = {medium: 0 or pi oscillation phase of a parametrically pumped 2-5 GHz AlN nanoresonator | access: frequency-multiplexed pump rows, no transistor | sense: phase-sensitive mixer per column | integration: resonator arrays released over CMOS | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: the AlN BAW/FBAR filter lines already running in Colorado and Texas}. Goto's 1954 parametron stored bits as subharmonic phase; at Q~1e4 and aJ stored energy the pump dissipates ~0.1 pW per bit, and a write injects a seed tone during pump ramp-up.
note: Resonators are micron-scale, so density is orders below DRAM; continuous pump power.

title: Po: memory made of seawater — track-etched nanofluidic iontronic membrane
idea: Po: memory made of seawater. Extracted: fill ion-track-etched polymer membranes (mass-produced for filtration, ~1e9 conical ~10 nm channels/cm2) with aqueous salt; each asymmetric nanochannel accumulates or depletes ions under a pulse (concentration polarization) and holds a hysteretic conductance state between printed face electrodes.
note: Iontronic memristors exist, but seconds volatility and us-ms speed are not DRAM-class.

title: Execute-in-place code tier: domestic NOR serves read-only program text
idea: Po: there is no NAND fab in America, so use the flash America still makes. Infineon Austin (TX) NOR flash on a CXL card is mapped as byte-addressable read-only memory, and the loader maps code segments, shared libraries and read-only data directly from it (execute-in-place) so they never occupy DRAM.
note: NOR density is low and cost/bit is not below DRAM.

title: Thermoelectric harvester powers key-off self-refresh in hot environments
idea: Worse at 125 C: drain the vehicle battery refreshing DRAM while parked hot. Flip: a Bi2Te3/skutterudite thermoelectric strip between the 125 C module and the chassis harvests 10-50 mW, enough to run self-refresh of the retained partition while the engine bay cools.

title: Inkjet-printed conductive links perform redundancy repair at sort
idea: Worse: burn area on fuse banks, antifuse programming pumps and laser-fuse windows. Flip: at wafer sort an inkjet printer deposits silver or copper nanoparticle links on a top-level link field that sets the spare-address compare bits fuses normally hold, programmed straight from the test map.

title: Printed trimmable reference ladder on package feeds bitline references
idea: Worse: replicate bandgaps, reference generators and trim fuses for VBLP, VREF and VPLATE on every die. Flip: print a ruthenium-oxide or carbon resistor ladder on the package substrate, laser- or inkjet-trimmed at final test, delivering filtered reference voltages to every die in the package.

title: Cooperative-harvester wordlines: one charge-and-float driver serves four mats
idea: Farmers share one combine across fields. A sub-wordline driver charges a wordline to 3 V through a bootstrapped pass gate and then disconnects; the wordline floats high on its own capacitance for the ~30 ns row-open time while the same driver serves wordlines in three other mats.
note: A floating wordline couples to bitline swings; per-wordline pass gates stay.

title: Microbiologist breeds bacteria that mine tungsten from fab scrap
idea: Persona: a biologist who knows organisms concentrate trace metals. Engineer Shewanella or E. coli strains to display tungstate-specific binding proteins (TupA/ModA family) on their surface. Use them to adsorb WO4(2-) from leached spent sputter targets, CMP slurry, WF6 scrubber water and Idaho/Nevada scheelite tailings, then calcine the biomass to WO3 as feed for WF6 resynthesis.

title: Sleep biologist: printed TFT banks rest under reverse bias to undo drift
idea: A biologist knows brains need sleep to clear damage: printed oxide and organic TFTs suffer bias-stress threshold shift, so the controller rotates banks of a printed memory foil into 'sleep' (data migrated out, gates held at reverse bias, optionally lit by a printed OLED backplane) to detrap charge and restore Vth before the bank rejoins.

title: PCB plating-shop logic: electroless nickel-boron plugs replace tungsten contacts
idea: Circuit-board makers fill microvias with electroless metal, with no vacuum and no fluoride gases. Fill bit-line and periphery contacts bottom-up with electroless Ni-B on a NiSi seed that catalyzes deposition without scarce palladium, using suppressor additives for void-free superfill on a university plating bench.

title: Atmospheric spatial-ALD zinc-tin-oxide cells for 200C downhole tools
idea: Extreme user: 200C oil and geothermal downhole tools needing indium-free, wide-bandgap channels. Deposit the ZnSnO channel and Al2O3/HfO2 gate stack with gas-bearing atmospheric spatial-ALD heads (no vacuum chamber, ~100+ wafers/h), giving a vacuum-free BEOL gain-cell module that stacks over any logic wafer.

title: Transient-electronics water-soluble GeO2 sacrificial layers replace HF releases
idea: Extreme user: dissolvable military and medical 'transient' electronics. Use amorphous GeO2 (water-soluble) or ZnO (dilute acetic acid) as the sacrificial film for capacitor support release, air gaps and 3D-DRAM lateral recesses, dissolving it in water instead of HF.

title: Capacitor-on-foil revived: giant-k barium titanate fired on nickel foil
idea: Fired capacitor-on-foil laminates for PCBs stalled on coarse patterning and lamination yield. Make the foil the memory substrate: fire a 300-500 nm BaTiO3 film (k~1,000-2,000) on nickel foil at ~900 C in reducing gas, then build oxide TFTs above it below 350 C, so each cell's capacitor is a flat ~1 um2 pad holding >10 fF (~30 fF/um2).

title: OSP finishes failed after reflows; graphene/h-BN monolayers replace ENEPIG gold
idea: Organic solderability preservatives were the cheap alternative to Ni/Pd/Au (ENEPIG) pad finishes but failed because they degrade after multiple reflows, which multi-die memory packages need. Coat Cu substrate pads with a transferred or low-temperature plasma-grown monolayer of graphene or h-BN that blocks oxidation through repeated 260 C cycles yet is thin enough for Cu-Cu or Zn-Al joints to break through during bonding.

title: Photoconductivity: printed photoconductor pads receive a flood-lit optical reference clock
idea: Flood a whole memory board with a 100-500 MHz modulated light reference from one source through a printed light-guide film; printed photoconductor pads at each memory chip pick it up as a low-jitter reference for local PLLs, removing board clock trees and buffers.

title: Magnetic-seeded sedimentation recovers rare-earth ceria CMP slurry
idea: Ceria abrasive is co-precipitated around superparamagnetic Fe3O4 seeds; spent slurry passes high-gradient magnetic separators that recapture the abrasive, then Stokes-settling classification restores the size distribution for reuse.

title: Piezo acoustic-emission sensors predict solder fatigue before memory fails
idea: An AlN thin-film piezo sensor on the module substrate hears acoustic-emission bursts from solder microcracks and delamination, and a counter in SPD flags the module for re-ball or repair before hard failure.

title: Ceria-free iron-oxide Fenton-assisted CMP slurry with magnetic recovery
idea: Periodic-table walk, Fe (26): swap rare-earth ceria abrasives for Fe3O4 nanoparticles plus in-situ Fenton chemistry (Fe2+/H2O2 hydroxyl radicals) that softens oxide surfaces, and recover the magnetic particles from slurry waste with magnets; post-clean in dilute HCl.

title: Zn: ZnO thin-film varistors move DRAM ESD into the package
idea: Embed ZnO multilayer varistor arrays in the DRAM package substrate under each DQ/CA ball to clamp assembly ESD, letting the die's own ESD diodes and pad structures shrink to CDM minimum while still meeting JEDEC pin capacitance and drive specs.

title: Ga: gallium-tin liquid-metal contacts self-heal intermittent DIMM connectors
idea: An interposer with sealed microcups of Ga-Sn eutectic (In-free; gram quantities despite gallium's China concentration) replaces spring contacts; the liquid metal flows around fretting and oxide, eliminating intermittent connector faults that masquerade as memory errors and trigger DIMM pulls.

title: Fe: Fe/Cr coupled antiferromagnet removes iridium and ruthenium from MRAM
idea: Replace Ru-spacer synthetic antiferromagnets and IrMn/PtMn pinning in MTJ stacks with Fe/Cr interlayer-coupled multilayers and a high-anisotropy Fe-based reference layer.
note: Ru/Ir use per MTJ is tiny; Fe/Cr coupling is weaker than Ru.

title: Line-shaft wordline boost: one resonant tank powers every subarray
idea: Like a mill's line shaft driving every machine through belts, replace dozens of local VPP charge pumps with one package-level LC resonator (off-chip inductor plus on-chip capacitance). Its ~3 V sinusoid is tapped by bootstrap rectifiers at each sub-wordline driver strip, all built in 180 nm.
note: Wordline activation is aperiodic, so resonant energy recovery is weak.

title: Water-developable chitosan photoresist with zero PFAS
idea: Within $1M/24 months: formulate a chitosan- or cellulose-derived resist with non-fluorinated sulfonium photoacid generators that develops in plain water, and characterize resolution and line-edge roughness on a university e-beam writer and 248 nm scanner.

title: Elevator: convert glut-idle 3D NAND lines to stacked DRAM
idea: Random stimulus 'elevator' -> build up, not out. 3D NAND fabs already own high-AR etch and multilayer ALD/CVD stacks; a conversion kit (new capacitor-free vertical gain-cell flow, recipes and a few tools) lets NAND lines idle in a glut build 30-60-tier stacked DRAM.
note: Tool reuse for 3D DRAM is on known roadmaps (NEO X-DRAM, VS-DRAM); vertical gain-cell flow unproven.

title: Convert idle NAND fabs into stacked DRAM-class memory lines
idea: Po: the NAND fab is a DRAM fab. NAND lines already build 200+-layer stacks with zero EUV using high-aspect-ratio etch, staircase contacts and ALD; a stacked-tier DRAM-class cell (horizontal capacitor tiers sharing a vertical bitline) is designed to reuse >80% of that tool set, so NAND overcapacity is converted rather than new fabs built.
note: Tier-stacked 3D DRAM reusing NAND tools would be a density step, but no working 3D cell exists and incumbents already pursue it.

title: Vertical domain-wall racetracks lining deep holes like 3D NAND
idea: Current-induced domain wall motion: Co/Ni multilayer racetracks deposited on the sidewalls of deep vertical holes store 32-64 magnetic domains per hole. A spin-orbit-torque Pt liner shifts the domains to a single read/write MTJ at the hole base.
note: Parkin's original 3D racetrack vision; sidewall domain-wall shifting unproven after 15+ years.

title: Interdigitating nano-comb bond splits one capacitor across two wafers
idea: Substitute one AR-115 capacitor etch with two AR-40 etches: wafer A carries storage-node pillars, wafer B carries matching holes lined with ZrO2 and the plate electrode; face-to-face hybrid bonding with ~10 nm overlay slides pillars into holes, producing a capacitor whose electrode length is the sum of both.
note: Pillar-into-hole with nm gaps needs ~few nm bonding overlay; far beyond current ~50 nm.

title: Eliminate channel charge transport for writes: caged-ion fullerene dipole bits
idea: Eliminate pushing charge through a channel: use endohedral fullerenes (Li+@C60) whose caged ion sits off-center in one of two positions, forming a switchable molecular dipole; a crossbar field flips the ion inside its cage in ~ps, and an underlying 2D-channel transistor senses the dipole.

title: Parametron-pumped refresh: global 2f pump restores charge without sensing
idea: Revive Goto's 1954 parametron, in which a pump at twice the signal frequency amplifies whichever phase is already present: give each cell a tiny MOS varactor coupled to its storage node and drive a global plate-line pump, so stored charge is parametrically amplified toward its own rail and bits are restored in place without row activation or sense amps.
note: Parametric pumping amplifies oscillation phase, not DC charge; restoring level needs a charge path.

title: Wavelength-addressed tiers: light pulses replace wordline voltage swings
idea: Inverts 'wordlines are electrical wires.' Give each tier photoconductive access devices whose band gap is tuned by alloy composition, and select a tier by the wavelength launched into an integrated vertical waveguide grid, so only the absorbing tier opens.
note: Photoconductive access needs >1e12 on/off for retention and light delivery to every cell; miracle-level.

title: Matryoshka doll: lithium ion rattling inside a fullerene cage
idea: Stimulus 'nesting doll' -> Li+@C60 endohedral fullerenes, where the ion sits off-centre in one of several wells inside the cage; a monolayer sits on a FET gate and a field pulse pushes each ion to the 'top' or 'bottom' well, whose dipole shifts the FET threshold. The cage shields the ion from chemistry and moisture.

title: Lighthouse-lit rows: photoconductive wide-gap access channels
idea: Random stimulus 'lighthouse': a beam sweeps, and only what it touches is lit. Each row gets a silicon-nitride waveguide carrying a ~365 nm pulse that photogenerates carriers in GaN access channels beneath it; in the dark a 3.4 eV-gap channel has essentially zero intrinsic carriers, so the bit is isolated with no gate voltage at all.

title: One transistor gates a string of resonance-staggered capacitors
idea: Po: one transistor, many capacitors. Above each vertical access transistor stack 4-8 capacitors, each behind a double-barrier resonant-tunnelling selector with a different resonance voltage set by well width, so the bitline bias chooses which single capacitor conducts: 1T-8C per footprint.
note: RTD valley currents preclude fA-level isolation needed for retention.

title: Child's rattle: off-centre ion bit inside Li@C60 cages
idea: A child shakes a rattle and hears where the bead is. In an endohedral Li@C60 molecule the Li+ ion sits off-centre in one of two stable sites; a field pulse flips it to the other site, giving a ~1 nm molecular dipole bit that is read as a capacitance change on a gate.
note: Li+ rattles thermally in C60 at room temperature; no retention barrier.

title: Firefly's lantern: photovoltaic row gates driven by waveguide light
idea: A firefly signals with light, not wires. Each electrical wordline becomes a SiN waveguide; per 32-cell segment, a series stack of three nanoscale photodiodes turns a femtojoule light pulse into ~1.5 V of local gate drive, and a shunt pull-down discharges it after the pulse.

title: Chameleon's skin: electro-optic non-destructive readout of stored charge
idea: A chameleon displays its state as color. A thin barium titanate electro-optic layer beside each storage node lets the node voltage shift, via the Pockels effect, the resonance of a micro-ring on a row waveguide; reading a row means shining light through and detecting per-cell resonance shifts, with no bitline swing and no charge removed.
note: Micro-rings per cell are microns wide; Pockels shift from a fF node is tiny.

title: Coulomb-blockade quantum-dot islands as the access switch
idea: Spin-qubit fabs already pattern ~5 nm silicon islands; put an array of ~100 parallel sub-3 nm Si dots in series with the storage node so the single-electron charging energy (>10 kT at room temperature at that size) blocks transport unless the wordline aligns the dot levels. Off-current then falls exponentially with charging energy instead of riding the thermionic subthreshold tail.
note: Room-temperature blockade needs very uniform sub-3 nm dots; one leaky dot in 100 dominates.

title: Qubit-style dispersive resonator readout of a varactor storage node
idea: Quantum computers read qubits non-destructively through a tiny shift in resonator frequency; a cell's storage node biases a MOS varactor that loads a shared bitline resonator, and a microwave probe reads the state as a phase shift without discharging the node. Read needs no restore cycle.
note: Per-cell capacitance shift on a bitline resonator is unresolvable at ns and room temperature.

title: Shape-memory twin variants open or close a tunnel gap
idea: Effect walk: ferroelastic martensitic twinning. A 20-nm NiTi nano-pillar has two stable twin variants whose heights differ by ~4% (~0.8 nm); a piezo or thermal pulse selects the variant, opening or closing a ~1-nm h-BN/vacuum tunnel gap above it, which changes tunneling current by up to ~10^6-10^7.
note: Martensitic transformation is suppressed in sub-50 nm NiTi.

title: Spin-Hall-rotated half-metal spin valve as channel-free access gate
idea: Effect: spin Hall torque plus half-metallic spin filtering. Each cell's access element is a Co2MnSi/MgO/Co2MnSi junction; a current pulse in a BiSb topological-insulator wordline strip (no tungsten) exerts spin-orbit torque that rotates the row's free layers parallel (conducting) during access and antiparallel (no minority states at EF, blocking) during hold.
note: Even 0.99 spin polarization gives on/off ~100x versus the ~1e9 a DRAM access switch needs.

title: Magnetostrictive NEMS relay access with vacuum-gap off state
idea: Effect: magnetostriction. A Galfenol (FeGa) nanobeam above each storage contact elongates in the field of a current-carrying wordline and touches a Ru contact pad; with no current a ~5 nm sealed vacuum gap separates node and bitline, giving zero channel leakage; GHz mechanical resonance at 10 nm scale keeps actuation in ns.
note: Magnetostrictive strain ~3e-4 cannot close a 5 nm gap on a 10 nm beam.

title: Phononic wordlines address rows by acoustic resonance frequency
idea: Effect: piezotronic strain from resonant surface acoustic waves. Each row's access junction sits on a phononic resonator tuned to a unique GHz frequency (512 rows over 1-5 GHz at Q~1000); refresh broadcasts a frequency sequence from one interdigitated transducer and only the resonating row gets enough strain to open, replacing decoded wordline drivers.

title: Macrame hopfions: knotted spin textures stacked as beads in one pillar
idea: Borrow knot-tying. Current pulses write 3D knotted magnetic solitons (hopfions) into a thick Co/Pt/Ir multilayer pillar, several stacked vertically like knots on a cord. Each level's presence or absence is a bit, read by depth-resolved magnetoresistance from a segmented pillar.

title: Zeolite autoclave cages: trapped sodium ion hops between two sites
idea: Use hydrothermal autoclave zeolite synthesis to grow sodalite films (Na, Al, Si, O) in the cell, where each cage holds a Na+ ion in a double-well site. A field pulse shifts the caged ions to one side as a bistable dipolar polarization, and the displacement charge is read.

title: Honeycomb-core expansion: staggered-anchor films stretch into capacitor walls
idea: Aerospace honeycomb is made by gluing stacked sheets in staggered stripes and pulling them apart; analogously deposit thin metal/dielectric sheets separated by sacrificial layers with staggered anchor stripes, release them, and let programmed stress expand the stack vertically into a hexagonal wall array that becomes shared capacitor plates.
note: Uniform programmed expansion at 30 nm pitch across a wafer needs a miracle; rolled-up caps exist only at micron scale.

title: Inductive charge sloshing reads and restores bits adiabatically
idea: Ideal result: the cell's charge travels to the sense node and returns with zero loss. A shared BEOL spiral inductor between a cell group and the sense node makes the transfer resonant: full charge moves in half an LC period (instead of lossy charge sharing), is sampled at the peak, and swings back to the cell on the next half-period.
note: fF-scale LC with lossy BEOL inductors and access resistance cannot resonate usefully.

title: Pulse-echo bitline reads a whole column of gain cells at once
idea: Ideal result: one probe reads every cell on a line simultaneously. Treat a long bitline as a transmission line where each non-destructive gain cell loads it with a state-dependent impedance step; a 10 ps edge launched from the end returns a time-encoded echo train decoded by one comparator plus time-to-digital converter.
note: On-chip bitlines are RC lines; resolving 256 sub-ps-spaced echoes needs a miracle.

title: Self-selective optical global refresh through a transparent top plate
idea: Scarcity rule: zero refresh bandwidth. A transparent ITO cell plate lets a chip-wide LED flash generate carriers in a photodiode junction at each storage node, and the node's own voltage steers the photocurrent so '1' nodes recharge toward VARY while '0' nodes drain to ground, refreshing every cell in parallel with no row cycling.

title: Colloidal-sphere inverse-opal electrode gives area without a high-aspect etch
idea: TRIZ #14 Spheroidality + #31 Porous materials: self-assemble 5-8-nm silica nanospheres in each shallow cell well, ALD-coat TiN/ZrO2/TiN through the interstices, then dissolve the spheres to leave a 3D inverse-opal capacitor whose curved shells multiply area ~6-10x per volume at AR <10:1.
note: 1-2 nm interstices of 5-8 nm spheres cannot admit a TiN/ZrO2/TiN stack.

title: Cu: CaCu3Ti4O12 colossal-k barrier-layer dielectric for flat capacitors
idea: Use CCTO, whose internal grain-boundary barrier layers give an apparent k of 1e3-1e4, as the cell dielectric so a planar or 5:1 capacitor reaches 5 fF; its lossy, grain-dependent leakage would doom a standard cell, but a 1% weak-cell budget plus faster refresh of flagged rows absorbs it.
note: CCTO barrier-layer k is a Maxwell-Wagner effect that vanishes at ns timescales and nm films.

title: Borrow power-MOSFET field plate to flatten storage-node field
idea: Substitute the bare gate-drain overlap with a grounded buried field plate, as used in power LDMOS: a thin TiN shield in the isolation next to the storage contact, tied to ground. It spreads the lateral field so the peak field at the overlap drops ~20-30%.

title: Invert strain engineering: heavy-valley transport suppresses source-drain tunneling
idea: Substitute mobility-boosting strain with the opposite: uniaxial compressive stress along a <100> channel fills the Si valleys whose heavy longitudinal mass (0.92 m0) points along transport. Direct source-to-drain tunneling at 6-8 nm gate length then falls exponentially, while on-current drops only ~2x.

title: Substitute sputtered TiN/W wordline with ALD molybdenum nitride gradient
idea: Substitute the argon-sputtered TiN liner and CVD tungsten fill with thermal ALD Mo (MoO2Cl2 + H2, N2 purge). NH3 pulses near the trench top make the MoNx there lower in work function than the deep channel region, keeping Vt high while lowering the gate-drain field at the storage overlap.
note: Dual work-function buried wordlines are known; Mo ALD gradient is the twist.

title: Substitute gas-exposed access modules with rare-gas-free certified process kit
idea: Substitute ad hoc process choices with a U.S. DPA/CHIPS-funded 'noble-gas-free access module': D2 anneal, thermal-ALD Mo gates, imprint/interference patterning and microwave activation, qualified as a drop-in kit any U.S. memory or foundry line can license, with shared reliability data on leakage tails.

title: Arrays on both wafer faces share one sandwiched periphery layer
idea: Substitute the dead silicon bulk with a second array: build the 1T1C array and periphery on the front, bond to carrier, thin to ~1 um, then build a second low-temperature oxide-semiconductor 1T1C array on the backside (backside-power-delivery style) wired through ~100 nm nano-TSVs so both arrays share the same sense amps and decoders.

title: Grounded shield pillars between vertical wordlines trade area for hammer immunity
idea: In vertical-wordline 3D DRAM, substitute every other wordline pillar with a grounded shield pillar etched in the same hole step and tied to the common plate, so no active wordline has an active neighbor; the lost area is bought back with ~30% more tiers, which is cheaper than area in 3D.
note: Trading area for hammer immunity in 3D; gain is removing mitigation overhead.

title: Coaxial grounded sleeve around vertical bitlines replaces bare pillars
idea: In vertical-bitline 3D DRAM, substitute the bare bitline pillar with a coax: ALD grounded TiN sleeve / Al2O3 / inner bitline, the sleeve opened only at each tier's access-transistor window by a self-aligned lateral recess, converting BL-to-BL coupling into fixed ground capacitance.

title: Substitute an electromagnetic cold crucible for the quartz crucible
idea: Grow CZ ingots from silicon held in a segmented copper cold crucible where induction fields form a thin solid skull and push the melt off the walls; deliver the interstitial oxygen DRAM needs for intrinsic gettering by metering SiO/O2 into the argon cover gas instead of dissolving a fused-quartz crucible.

title: Harvest-and-restack business for failed HBM stacks
idea: Substitute scrapping whole 12/16-high stacks that fail final test with a laser lift-off service: stacks are built with a thin absorbing debond layer at each tier, failed dies are released by a laser through the stack edge, and good dies are re-bonded into new stacks.

title: Substitute fixed VDD/2 bitline precharge with time-since-refresh adaptive reference
idea: Lower the bitline precharge/reference voltage step by step as time since a row's last refresh grows, tracking the drooping stored '1' level, so the sense margin stays balanced as charge leaks.
note: Anti-cells and '0' leakage complicate a single drooping reference.

title: Coaxial pillar: storage capacitor core inside vertical transistor shell
idea: Fuse access transistor and capacitor into one vertical pillar: a grounded TiN core plate, a high-k sleeve, and a doped-oxide storage-node shell form the capacitor, and the same shell continues upward as a short vertical channel gated by a wordline ring at the pillar top. The capacitor uses the pillar volume and the transistor uses the pillar skin, so one pillar is one 4F2 cell with no landing pad.
note: Capacitance from pillar core is small; gain bounded at about 1.5x density.

title: Two bonded array wafers share one sense-amp plane
idea: Bond two DRAM array wafers face-to-face with the sense-amplifier layer at the bond plane: each SA's true bitline lies in the upper array and its complement in the lower one, combining open-bitline density with folded-bitline noise cancellation because both halves see the same vertical coupling.
note: Vertical open/folded hybrid; SA sharing already exists laterally in open-bitline, so gain is modest.

title: Backside-illuminated sensor thinning fused with double-sided trench DRAM
idea: Reuse the CMOS-image-sensor flow at a US 300 mm fab (onsemi East Fishkill, the old IBM trench-DRAM site): etch full-depth deep-trench capacitors, thin the wafer to ~3 um as in BSI sensors, and contact capacitor plates and power from the backside while access transistors and bitlines own the front.

title: Grayscale multi-tone EUV exposure defines via and line together
idea: Combine grayscale lithography from micro-optics with a dose-to-depth metal-oxide resist. A three-level attenuated reticle gives contacts full dose and lines half dose, so the resist develops a two-depth relief that transfers via plus trench in one etch.

title: Short-purge high-k ALD triples throughput, thin-bottom leakers tolerated
idea: Combine aggressive ALD cycle compression (3x shorter precursor exposure and purge in the capacitor ZrO2/Al2O3 stack) with error tolerance. The resulting thin or under-dense dielectric at the bottoms of some deep holes creates ~0.5% leaky cells that the code absorbs.

title: Refurbished dry-ArF and KrF fleets run wider-tolerance array layers
idea: Combine the abundant used-tool market (refurbished dry ArF, KrF and older etchers) with cell-level error tolerance. Non-critical and semi-critical layers go to tools with ~2x worse CD uniformity and chamber matching, and the added variability (~0.1-0.5% bit errors) fits the 1% budget.

title: Double-rate capacitor etch accepting rare not-open holes
idea: Combine high-power, high-rate HAR etch recipes with error tolerance: capacitor-hole etch rate is pushed ~2x with higher bias and fewer passivation cycles, and the resulting ~0.5-1% not-open or twisted holes become dead cells logged as erasures at sort.
note: Twisted holes bridge neighbours, not just die.

title: Build the stack top-down on its own SiC heat spreader
idea: Combine the temporary thinning carrier with the final lid: bond the top core-die wafer face-down onto a permanent SiC wafer, thin it, then bond each next wafer face-down onto the previous backside, finishing with the base logic wafer, so the SiC wafer is the carrier for every step and becomes the heat spreader. No temporary bond/debond cycles and no excimer debond lasers (Xe/Kr in neon buffer).
note: Wafer-on-wafer stacking with no known-good die compounds yield loss.

title: Fab-plus-datacenter campus shipping bare dies straight to racks
idea: Fuse a memory fab with an adjacent hyperscale datacenter. They share substation, cooling and water, and bare known-good dies move by internal conveyor to on-site board assembly. That removes packaging, distribution, inventory and channel markup.
note: Packaging still needed for boards; savings overstated.

title: Great Lakes fab siting enabled by zero-PFAS process
idea: Combine a PFAS-free process with siting in strict-PFAS states that have abundant water and power (Minnesota, Michigan, New York). Discharge-permit fights over PFAS currently block fabs there.
note: Depends on an unproven PFAS-free flow.

title: High-voltage cable stress-grading spacer that defuses the GIDL hotspot
idea: Adapted from stress-grading sleeves at HV cable terminations, which use high or field-dependent permittivity to spread equipotentials at the shield cut: form the gate-drain spacer of the buried-wordline device from a graded-k stack (high-k at the gate corner fading to low-k toward the storage node). The field at the overlap corner is spread over a longer distance instead of peaking.
note: Graded-k spacers for GIDL resemble known high-k spacer work; 10x claim optimistic.

title: Southwest Airlines single-fleet logic for a minimal-tool capacitorless fab
idea: Southwest flies a single aircraft type to slash spares, training and maintenance. Adapt this by designing a capacitor-free cell flow (no pillar etch, no ZAZ ALD, no support lattice) that runs on ~6 standardized shallow etch, deposition and litho tool families, sharing spares, chamber kits and gases fab-wide.

title: Army-arsenal GOCO model for a strategic U.S. DRAM fab
idea: Like the Lake City Army Ammunition Plant, the government owns the fab building and tool set and a commercial memory maker operates it under a cost-plus-fee contract, selling output commercially with a guaranteed defense allocation.

title: Skyscraper sky lobbies: express TSV trunks plus local hops
idea: Adapted from tall-building elevator zoning: in a 24-32 high stack, a few wide 'express' TSV bundles run only to sky-lobby dies every 8 tiers. A thin repeater/switch layer there fans out to short local TSVs, so columns no longer pass through every die.

title: Magnify demand signal: federal persistent-memory procurement on legacy U.S. fabs
idea: A CHIPS-style advance market commitment obliges federal datacenters to buy a quota of U.S.-made non-volatile working memory (SiC, AFE, LiNbO3 or MRAM flavors) built on 28-90 nm domestic legacy lines that need no EUV.

title: Crust-only DRAM built from Earth's most abundant elements
idea: Minify the bill of materials to Si, O, N, Al, Ti, C and H: polysilicon wordlines with 4x shorter subarrays, thermal ONO capacitors, aluminum interconnect with Al2O3 liners and TiN only as a barrier. No W, Mo, Hf, Zr, Ru, Co, Ta, In, Ga or Ge.

title: Persistent glass memory backplane with consumable compute
idea: MAGNIFY substrate life: DRAM is embedded in cavities of a long-lived glass-core backplane, and compute chiplets land on top through reversible bumps and are swapped every generation.

title: Minify each 3D cell, magnify copies: three-tier majority bits
idea: Lateral 3D DRAM cells only fit ~1 fF capacitors. Instead of chasing bigger ones, write each bit to the same x-y position on three tiers through a shared vertical bitline and resolve it with a 3-input majority sense amp. Tiers are cheap deposition steps; capacitor aspect ratio is not.
note: Effectively a 3x distributed capacitor; density gain over larger lateral cap is unclear.

title: Minify neighbor coupling with dynamic negative bias on adjacent wordlines
idea: While a row is open, drive its two neighbor wordlines further negative (about -0.3 to -0.6 V) for the open duration. This raises their access transistors' barrier against passing-gate and coupling-induced charge loss.

title: Eliminate tungsten contact plugs with tall raised-epitaxy source/drain posts
idea: Pattern contact holes in an amorphous-carbon template with O2 plasma, then grow in-situ-doped Si:P/SiGe:B selective epitaxy (DCS/HCl/PH3/B2H6) up through them to ~80 nm, so the source/drain posts themselves reach M1. Ash the template and cap each post with NiSi.

title: Eliminate planar sense-amp stripes: tier-flipped checkerboard mats
idea: In a two-or-more-tier stack, place the sense-amp strip of tier N directly above the cell mat of tier N+1 and vice versa in a checkerboard, so no footprint is spent on SA stripes and bitlines stay short.

title: Eliminate the distinct periphery process: array-transistor-only periphery
idea: Build sense amps, decoders and drivers from the same vertical channel devices as the array, in a single homogeneous device process, accepting larger periphery circuits that are tucked under the array.
note: Sense amps from array devices sacrifice matching and PMOS; the water claim really comes from stacking.

title: Eliminate the quartz crucible: cold-crucible skull-melt Czochralski growth
idea: Melt silicon inside a water-cooled, segmented copper crucible heated by induction so a frozen silicon skull is the only surface touching the melt, then pull the crystal from that self-contained melt and add oxygen deliberately by controlled O2/SiO gas doping to keep gettering behaviour.

title: Eliminate the package: wafer-scale DRAM shipped as unsawn memory wafers
idea: Design arrays with spare-tile routing so the whole 300 mm wafer acts as one memory device, then bond it face-to-face to a logic wafer or to a cold plate with edge connectors, skipping dicing, ABF substrates, solder balls, mold compound and per-die handler test.

title: Eliminate up-front tool capex: pay-per-wafer-pass equipment ownership by vendors
idea: Tool vendors own, install and maintain the equipment in a new US DRAM fab and bill per wafer pass with guaranteed uptime; the memory company carries only the building and labor, and vendors refurbish tools for the next node.

title: Eliminate idle EUV capex: national EUV pass utility shared by memory makers
idea: A government-backed consortium owns EUV scanners in one US litho hall beside several fabs and sells exposure passes; FOUPs move by sealed AMHS tunnel between companies, so no DRAM maker buys a full EUV fleet. Products remain standard DDR5/HBM.

title: Eliminate uniform cell strength: significance-graded capacitors within each row
idea: Fabricate rows with two capacitor diameters (a column-mask variant, not an extra layer). About 1/4 of columns get full-size pillars for sign, exponent and high-order bits; 3/4 get thinner, shorter pillars for mantissa LSBs. The data layout packs numeric formats so each bit's significance lands on a matching column.
note: Dual capacitor sizes per row; AI-only and process-heavy.

title: Eliminate the fixed wordline-low rail: deep-negative bias for hammered victims
idea: Give each local wordline driver a selectable off-rail (about -0.2 V normally, -0.6 V as a shield). The controller's activation tracker switches rows next to a heavily activated aggressor to the deeper negative bias until their next refresh. That raises the barrier against hammer-induced electron injection and passing-gate leakage.

title: Eliminate parallel wordline adjacency: rotate alternate 3D tiers 90 degrees
idea: In stacked 3D DRAM, run wordlines in X on odd tiers and in Y on even tiers, so vertically adjacent wordlines cross at points instead of running in parallel. Each in-tier wordline pair is separated by a shield line that doubles as the plate.

title: Eliminate final test: probe each memory tier before depositing the next
idea: In monolithic <=400 C stacking, add an in-line electrical test after each tier, using temporary probe pads on the top surface. Failing regions are logged into a defect map in the base logic die before the next tier buries them.

title: Inverted HBM: logic die on top, DRAM tiers below
idea: Rearrange the stack order: put the hot base/logic die at the top of the stack, directly under the heatsink, and the DRAM tiers beneath it on the interposer, with logic power fed up through a dedicated power-via column in the DRAM dies. DRAM no longer sits in the heat path of the logic die.

title: Pay at write, not at refresh: pre-emphasized writes for weak rows
idea: Reverse when weak cells are compensated: a per-bank retention map fused at test flags the ~0.1-1% weak rows, and whenever such a row is written or restored, the bitline restore level is boosted 150-250 mV for a few ns. The extra charge carries weak cells to the nominal interval instead of refreshing whole banks at the weak-cell rate.

title: Back-gate the array so wordlines swing at logic voltage
idea: Reverse which terminal does the work: a buried, separately biased plate under the access transistors sits negative during retention (raising Vt, cutting leakage) and pulses positive only in the selected subarray, so wordlines need ~1.2 V swing instead of ~3 V and drivers become thin-oxide core devices.

title: 3D DRAM staircase rebuilt as the wordline-driver farm
idea: Rearrange the dead staircase of stacked 3D DRAM: each step landing hosts vertical-channel transistors grown in the same deposition steps as the tiers, acting as tier-select and local wordline drivers, so the contact region becomes active periphery.

title: Sense amps built from the array's own vertical transistors
idea: Reverse the borrowing: instead of the array borrowing logic transistors, SAs and sub-wordline drivers are built from the same vertical-channel 4F2 pillars as the access transistors, in the same steps and pitch-matched under the bitlines, so one U.S. memory fab runs the full flow with no logic module or partner.

title: NEMS relay power gates zero out idle subarray periphery leakage
idea: Reverse electronics to mechanics for slow switches: bank and subarray periphery power gates, toggled only on wake/sleep, are nanoelectromechanical relays from a U.S. MEMS foundry layer bonded above, giving true zero off-current.

title: Measure first, wire last: e-beam personalizes each wafer's periphery
idea: Reverse design-then-build: after array test, a U.S.-built multibeam e-beam writes the final periphery metal per wafer, setting SA reference trims, bitline segmentation and timing taps to that wafer's measured leakage and Cs distribution.
note: E-beam throughput per wafer and modest gain.

title: Flip the wafer: etch storage capacitors from the backside
idea: Build access transistors and bitlines on the front, bond to a carrier, thin the silicon to ~2-3 um, then etch capacitor holes from the backside landing directly on each storage-node junction and fill with MIM. Capacitor height is set by backside film thickness instead of fighting front-side BEOL, and bitline contacts no longer weave between capacitor pillars.
note: Backside cap etch frees front routing; gain ~20-30% area, needs full wafer flow to prove.

title: Backside periphery wiring frees the front for single-exposure DUV
idea: Rearrange wiring sides: move power rails and global sense-amp/decoder routing to backside metal after wafer thinning, which relaxes frontside metal pitch until single ArF immersion exposure works.

title: Backside signal highway on the DRAM die
idea: Reverse backside power delivery: after thinning, put thick low-RC copper on the DRAM die backside for the global data and command buses, connected by nano-TSVs to each bank's local I/O, which frees front-side metal for array wiring and shrinks the periphery's routing channels.

title: Inverted HBM stack puts logic base die beside the lid
idea: Rearrange the stack so the hot base/logic die sits on top against the heat spreader and the DRAM dies sit below next to the interposer, with signals using the same through-stack TSVs; DRAM layers leave the logic die's heat path and run ~8-12 C cooler.

title: Bitlines on the wafer backside for vertical-transistor 4F2 DRAM
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: build vertical transistors and capacitors from the front, then flip, thin and form bitlines from the back so they land directly on pillar bottoms, as backside power delivery does in logic. This replaces the high-resistance buried bitline under the pillars.
note: Backside bitline routing for 4F2 VCT appears in patents; wafer flip adds cost.

title: Inter-tier metal planes double as shared back gates
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: in a stacked thin-Si floating-body array, make the conductive plane between tiers do two jobs: it shields tier from tier and is the negative-biased back gate for both the tier above and the tier below, holding stored holes at the back interface. One deposited film replaces a separate back-gate layer per tier.

title: Skipping: DRAM dies overhang compute edge, bonded face-to-face, no interposer
idea: TRIZ #21 Skipping (rush through the harmful stage): skip the interposer by bonding each DRAM die face-to-face onto a 1.5 mm strip along the compute die edge. The rest of the DRAM die is cantilevered over a mold shelf that carries its power vias.

title: Interference-litho array gratings with 6% spare bitlines
idea: TRIZ separation in space: the perfectly periodic array layers are patterned by mask-free laser interference lithography plus self-aligned multiple patterning on U.S.-built deposition/etch tools, leaving only relaxed-rule periphery for precision writing; stitch and standing-wave defects are absorbed by 6% spare bitlines and an ECC that knows defects arrive as whole columns.

title: Casparian-strip ring seals storage-node sidewall leakage path
idea: Like the suberin Casparian strip that blocks the apoplastic bypass in plant roots and forces flow through gated membranes, selectively recess the STI sidewall where the storage-node junction meets it and fill a thin ring of low-trap, ultra-wide-gap dielectric (crystalline AlN or ALD Al2O3), cutting the interface trap-assisted path so leakage can only go through the gated channel.

title: Dendritic-spine-neck quantum-confined access channel
idea: Spine necks isolate synapses by being long and ultra-thin; make the access channel a 1.5-2 nm-thick Si ribbon segment where quantum confinement widens the effective bandgap from 1.12 eV toward ~1.6-2 eV, while wider source/drain 'heads' stay bulk-like for low resistance.

title: Dsup cloak: grounded coaxial shields wrap each storage node
idea: The tardigrade protein Dsup cloaks DNA against damage; form a grounded TiN sleeve around each vertical storage node with a second conformal ALD liner separated by dielectric, screening neighbour wordlines and sinking carriers injected by repeated activation, which worsen at high temperature.
note: Area cost of extra sleeve in a crowded node; row-hammer gain only.

title: Piano tuning: per-cell charge-trap trimming of leaky access transistor thresholds
idea: A piano tuner adjusts each string individually instead of rebuilding the piano. Add a thin LPCVD silicon-nitride charge-trap layer (dichlorosilane + ammonia, no fluorine) to the access gate stack; at wafer sort, find tail cells and apply hot-carrier program pulses through their own wordline and bitline to inject electrons and raise just their Vt by 150-300 mV.

title: Coaxial cable shielding: grounded TiN sleeve kills passing-wordline leakage
idea: Coax stops signals coupling by wrapping them in a grounded shield. Wrap each buried wordline's passing segment, where it runs beside a neighbor's storage junction, with a thin grounded TiN sleeve deposited from TiCl4/NH3 (fluorine-free), so the passing gate cannot invert or field-stress the neighbor's junction edge.

title: Sky-lobby decoder decks: in-stack tier decoders fed by express vias
idea: Skyscrapers use express elevators to sky lobbies, then local cars; build a 128-tier 3D DRAM as 8 decks of 16 tiers, each deck capped by a thin-film decoder tier that receives a 4-bit tier address over a few express vias and fans out locally to its 16 wordline planes through a short mini-staircase.

title: Back-contact solar layout: bitlines moved to the wafer backside
idea: Interdigitated-back-contact solar cells free the front surface by putting all metal behind; do the same for vertical-channel DRAM: after front-side capacitors are built, bond to a carrier, thin to the channel bottoms and form buried bitlines from the backside, so the front is 100% capacitor landing at true 4F2.

title: Shingled mushroom capacitors: SMR-style overlap of two height tiers
idea: Like shingled magnetic recording overlapping tracks, build capacitors in two interleaved heights: even cells get a short pillar topped by a wide mushroom electrode at level 1, odd cells a taller pillar whose cap sits at level 2, so every cap overhangs its neighbours' footprint.
note: Overhanging caps add little area relative to sidewall; 1.8x area claim looks optimistic.

title: Car platform sharing: one die ships as DDR5, LPDDR5X or HBM
idea: Automakers build many models on one platform. Design one array die with dual pad rings, TSV-ready keep-outs and fuse/metal-option selection so the same wafer becomes standard DDR5, LPDDR5X or HBM core dies at test or stacking time, each meeting its unchanged JEDEC interface.

title: Aircraft-leasing model for EUV and high-NA scanners
