idea: Borrowed from aviation, where lessors like AerCap own about half of airline jets and redeploy them: a scanner lessor owns EUV tools, leases them per wafer pass to memory makers, moves tools between fabs as cycles shift, and funds itself with asset-backed securities on scanner residual value.

title: Prestressed-concrete tendons keep tall capacitor pillars from leaning
idea: Borrowed from prestressed bridges, where tensioned steel keeps concrete in compression: deposit a tensile SiN/TiN liner inside each storage-node cylinder before the mold is removed, so pillars are pre-stressed straight and the multi-level support lattice can be dropped, letting AR reach 100-115 without collapse.

title: Par-baked bread: split DRAM front-end and finishing across fabs
idea: Borrowed from par-baked bread shipped from central bakeries to stores: leading fabs ship wafers with transistors, wordlines and bitlines done; regional U.S. finishing fabs add capacitors, top metals, test and packaging using only 193 nm dry litho, ALD and etch, splitting a ~90-day flow into two ~45-day hops.

title: OLED-demura-style e-beam charge-decay imaging of leaky junctions inline
idea: OLED fabs photograph every panel to build a per-pixel compensation map. Before the capacitor is built, the storage-node contacts would be flood-charged with an e-beam and voltage-contrast imaged twice, seconds apart. Contacts that lose contrast quickly mark leaky junction outliers across the wafer in parallel. Those coordinates feed process learning and are written into die fuse maps.

title: Strategic DRAM Reserve modeled on petroleum stockpiles
idea: Government buys wafers and known-good die in price troughs, stores them nitrogen-purged in bonded warehouses, and releases by auction when a contract-price index exceeds 2x its 5-year median.
note: Generation obsolescence (DDR4 to DDR5) erodes stockpile value.

title: Coincident-current selection: AND-gated access for column-selective refresh
idea: Revive core memory's coincident-current selection: each cell's access path has two series gates, one on the row wordline and one on a column-select line, so only the cell at the intersection opens. Refresh can then target only the few weak columns flagged at test, and reads stop overfetching whole pages.

title: 1952 Bell licensing redux: open-license a low-leakage access cell
idea: Revive Bell Labs' 1952 transistor licensing symposium, which sold patent rights cheaply to any firm and seeded an industry: a national lab or consortium develops a refresh-relaxed access-device module and licenses it, with a process design kit and test structures, to every U.S. fab for a nominal fee.

title: Core inhibit-wire counter-pulse cancels row-hammer disturbance
idea: Core memory's inhibit winding sent an opposing current to cancel unwanted switching. When a row activates, its two neighbor wordlines get a synchronized, shaped negative counter-pulse from the same sub-wordline driver, cross-wired in existing metal with no added mask. The pulse cancels the capacitive kick and electron-injection field that cause hammer flips.

title: Mandatory second-sourcing revived for a no-EUV American DRAM process
idea: Revive the 1960s-80s defense rule that every critical chip has a licensed second source: require CHIPS-funded DRAM designs to be built on an open no-EUV process licensed to at least two US mature-node foundries.

title: SAGE-model university memory production for strategic buyers
idea: Core memory for SAGE was first built at MIT Lincoln Lab before industry took over; repeat that: federal funding lets university nanofabs build first-run specialty memory tiers (CCD weight streamers, back-end ROM, NDRO magnetics) for defense and national-lab systems under guaranteed purchase, then transfer the proven processes to U.S. mature-node fabs.

title: 1950s ferroelectric matrix switches remap failed HBM dies after bonding
idea: Revive Bell Labs' 1952 BaTiO3 ferroelectric matrix as HZO ferroelectric-FET crosspoint switches in the HBM base die that nonvolatilely reroute channels and TSV groups around a dead core die or bad TSV cluster after stacking, holding state with zero power.

title: Von Neumann multiplexed bundles make defect-ridden 3D DRAM tiers usable
idea: Von Neumann's 1956 'probabilistic logics' built reliable organs from bundles of unreliable lines followed by a restoring majority stage. In stacked 3D DRAM, regions mapped as weak write each bit into vertically aligned cells on three different tiers and read them through a 3-input restoring sense stage, so one defective tier per column is harmless; a per-tier quality map keeps healthy regions in one-bit-per-cell mode.

title: Three-head tape deck read-after-write verifies dry-cleaned contact writes
idea: Three-head tape decks read each bit back milliseconds after recording to confirm it. Write drivers add a fast verify: right after a write to a row flagged high-resistance, the sense amp re-senses the restored cells before precharge and extends tWR or rewrites only if the level is short, covering contacts that are 2-3x more resistive.

title: Deliberately non-uniform mats: tall and short capacitors by data lifetime
idea: Inverts 'all cells must be identical': fabricate two retention classes on one die, tall-capacitor long-retention mats (refresh ~1 s) and short-capacitor no-guarantee mats (1-10 ms) that skip the deepest etch, and expose them as separate NUMA tiers so the OS places long-lived pages and transient buffers where each is cheapest.

title: Row decoders built from the array's own vertical transistors
idea: Inverting 'decoders are CMOS logic in the periphery': predecoded NAND-style row selection is made from series vertical-channel transistors fabricated in the same steps as the cell access devices and placed at the mat edge at cell pitch, replacing the per-mat CMOS decoder/driver stripe.
note: Decoders from vertical array transistors; NMOS-only drive needs bootstrapping.

title: Mixed mat: fast floating-body and nonvolatile FeFET share sense amps
idea: Inverting 'one array holds one cell type': alternate rows in a mat are floating-body (fast, volatile) and FeFET (nonvolatile), both read by drain current, and one dual-mode current sense amp switches bias between them so hot data and persistent data live in the same mat.

title: Backside-etched capacitors through thinned wafer free 4F² footprint
idea: Inverts 'the capacitor sits on top of the bitline (COB).' Build vertical-channel transistors and bitlines on the front side, bond to a carrier, thin the wafer to ~1.5 um and etch the capacitors from the back side so they land directly on each transistor's buried drain; capacitor and bitline contact stop competing for the same face.

title: Heterogeneous tier recipes: fat-capacitor base, gain-cell upper tiers
idea: Inverts 'all cells in a stack are identical.' Build the bottom single-crystal tiers as long-retention capacitor cells and the upper, low-thermal-budget tiers as cheap capacitor-free short-retention gain cells used as a hot buffer, with a base-die engine that migrates rows between the two classes over the vertical bitline.

title: In-tier thin-film decoders eliminate the 3D wordline staircase
idea: Inverts 'tiers are selected through an edge staircase of contacts.' Each tier carries its own poly-Si TFT tier/row decoder made in the same step as its access devices, and a few vertical broadcast lines carry the tier address, so no staircase etch or per-tier contact is needed.

title: Cobalt- and platinum-free MTJ using iron shape anisotropy
idea: Inverts 'perpendicular MRAM needs Co, Pt, Ir, Ru and Ta': make tall Fe-B pillar free layers whose perpendicular anisotropy comes from shape (height > diameter) on an Fe/MgO interface, and pin the reference layer with a thick iron-nitride (Fe16N2) hard magnet instead of a Co/Pt synthetic antiferromagnet.
note: Shape-anisotropy MTJs already shown; Fe16N2 hard-magnet thin films remain hard to make reliably.

title: Never dice: wafer-scale DRAM sold as one memory slab
idea: Inverts 'memory is sold as small diced dies'. Stitch reticles across a full 300 mm wafer, route around dead reticle fields with a wafer-level mesh of fuse-configured links, skip dicing, packaging and per-die test, and ship the whole wafer as a rack CXL memory slab (~3 TB) with optical edge I/O.
note: Back-end savings modest; needs stitched DRAM wafers from a fab.

title: DRAM die as the bridge between compute chiplets
idea: Invert 'bridges are just wires': embed a DRAM die as the EMIB-style bridge between two U.S.-fabbed logic dies (Intel Arizona/New Mexico packaging, U.S.-made DRAM), so the die carrying die-to-die wires also stores what they exchange.
note: DRAM BEOL has few metal layers, poor for dense bridge routing.

title: Deliberately short capacitors, rescued by two-level ECC
idea: Inverts 'every cell must meet retention on its own': cut capacitor aspect ratio from ~70:1 to ~45:1 (Cs ~3 fF), halving deep-etch and ALD time, and accept a fat retention tail handled by on-die BCH (t=2 per 256b) plus controller chipkill at a modestly faster refresh.
note: Trading capacitor height for ECC; refresh and soft-error tail grow.

title: Cut the cell plate into strips and bump it on reads
idea: Inverts 'the cell plate is a passive common electrode': one mask cuts the plate into row-group strips; when a row with known weak cells is read, its strip is pulsed +0.2-0.3 V just before sensing so capacitive coupling lifts the storage node and the bitline signal.
note: Plate bump helps '1' but hurts '0'; useful only for known true-cell leakers.

title: Thick dielectric collar at the capacitor's leaky top rim
idea: Inverts 'capacitor dielectric must be uniform': one mask defines a thicker, lower-k oxide collar at the pillar top, where field crowding at electrode corners concentrates leakage and early breakdown.

title: Shipyard-built floating DRAM fab towed to a U.S. port
idea: Inverts 'fabs are built on site over 3-5 years': cleanroom, subfab and utility decks are fabricated in parallel in a shipyard on a ballasted concrete caisson, towed to a deep-water U.S. port and grounded on the seabed for vibration stability, then hooked to grid and desalinated water.

title: Depreciated legacy DRAM lines kept running as a regulated utility
idea: Inverts 'old nodes are scrapped or converted when the next node arrives': a public-private utility buys fully depreciated 1x/2x-nm DRAM lines that vendors plan to convert to HBM and runs them at cash cost for consumer, automotive and industrial DRAM.

title: Standby plate-line swing collapses storage-junction field during self-refresh
idea: Tail leakage is field-enhanced (trap-assisted tunneling ~ exp(gamma*sqrt(F))), so reduce the field instead of the conductance. On self-refresh entry, slowly ramp the shared cell plate down ~0.4 V. This couples every storage node down, so '1' cells sit closer to the p-well potential while '0' cells stay reverse-biased thanks to the negative p-well bias. Ramp the plate back before exit; its large capacitance is swung only twice per idle period.

title: Grounded shield rail kills passing-wordline leakage into storage nodes
idea: In buried-wordline arrays each storage node sits beside a neighboring row's 'passing' wordline. When that line pulses to ~3 V, its fringing field induces leakage and electron injection into the node, the same coupling behind row hammer. Insert a thin grounded conductive rail (doped poly or TiN) in the isolation trench between the passing wordline and the storage node to terminate the field lines.

title: Coincident dual-gate matrix wordline addressing cuts drivers to 2sqrtN
idea: Decoding a row needs only log2(N) bits of information, yet DRAM spends one 3 V driver per row. Use a dual-gate access transistor whose front gate is a row-group line and back gate a sub-row line; it conducts only when both are high, so 1024 rows need 32+32 drivers instead of 1024 (display-style matrix addressing inside the mat).

title: Self-decoding array builds decoders from vertical array transistors
idea: Instead of separate periphery CMOS, implement the row predecoder as a NAND-style ROM matrix made of the same vertical-channel transistors as the array, pitch-matched at array density and fabricated in the same steps.

title: 1310 nm optical links shine vertically through stacked silicon dies
idea: Exploit silicon's transparency beyond 1.1 um: each die carries micro-emitters and Ge photodiodes aligned through the stack, so data passes vertically as light through undrilled silicon, replacing signal TSVs and their keep-out zones.

title: Cold-crucible skull melting grows CZ ingots without any quartz
idea: A crucible's only job is to hold 1414 C silicon without contaminating it, and the purest container for silicon is solid silicon. Use a segmented water-cooled copper crucible with induction heating so a frozen Si skull lines the wall, and pull 300 mm crystals from an electromagnetically confined melt.
note: Cold-crucible Si melting exists for solar casting; 300 mm dislocation-free pulling from a skull melt is unproven.

title: Mirror-polarity cells share every electrode between adjacent tiers
idea: A capacitor plate's field lines can terminate on both faces, yet stacked cells use only one; flip cell polarity on alternate tiers so one TiN/Mo plate serves the cells above and below as a common plate, deleting one metal layer per tier.

title: Defect-tolerant arrays delete half the in-line inspection tools
idea: First principle: yield is exp(-D0*Acrit), so 12% spare rows/columns plus per-subarray remap tables make yield insensitive to random defects up to ~5x today's D0. Spend that margin by skipping ~50% of optical and e-beam inspection and metrology steps (sample 1 wafer per lot) and relaxing some cleanroom zones from ISO 3 to ISO 5.

title: Four bonded DUV array tiers beat one EUV tier on density
idea: First principle: cost per bit = wafer cost / bits. A fully depreciated, DUV-only 16 nm-class 6F2 array wafer gives ~56% of the bits of a 12 nm EUV wafer at roughly half its cost, and face-to-back hybrid bonding of four such array tiers onto one periphery wafer, linked by ~1 um inter-tier vias, gives ~2.2x bits per footprint.

title: Open-standard modular fab tools with swappable chambers
idea: First principle: a process tool is a vacuum chamber plus a few energy and gas sources, and most of its price is integration, not physics. Define an open mechanical, electrical and software chamber standard so U.S. vendors build interchangeable process modules that are repaired, upgraded and redeployed on common transfer platforms over 25-year lives.

title: Slow-edge two-level wordline precharge stops trap charge pumping
idea: One hammer mechanism is charge pumping: each ACT/PRE swing fills and empties interface traps under the aggressor or passing gate, emitting electrons toward the victim. Pumped charge per cycle falls when the falling edge is slower than trap emission time. A two-step precharge with a ramped edge (~ns) keeps trap occupancy near equilibrium.

title: Row-wide product code computed at activation exploits overfetch
idea: Every ACT already senses a full 8 Kb row (128x overfetch), so all bits sit in the sense amps for free. Place a 2D product code (row checksum plus column parity over 64x128 tiles) in the sense-amp stripe and correct multi-bit clusters before the column read.

title: Deliberate BTI stress re-trims outlier read transistors in field
idea: Bias-temperature instability shifts Vt predictably (dVt ~ t^n, partly permanent). When scrub logs show the same gain cell repeatedly misreading because of a low-Vt read transistor, the controller selects only that cell with a wordline+bitline bias and applies millisecond gate stress, which pushes its Vt back toward the population mean.

title: Crucible-free Czochralski: pull 300 mm ingots from an induction cold-skull
idea: A crucible's only job is to contain molten silicon without contaminating it; a water-cooled segmented copper crucible with induction heating freezes a silicon skull that contains the melt in silicon itself. Adapt cold-crucible melting (used for Ti and nuclear glass) with magnetic melt stirring to CZ pulling, eliminating the high-purity quartz crucible.

title: Seesaw cell plate lowers storage-node stress during standby
idea: Random stimulus 'seesaw': push one end down and the other end moves too. In idle mats the shared cell plate drops by ~0.3 V, coupling every storage node down with it; '1' nodes then sit lower against the negative wordline and well, cutting GIDL and junction fields, and the plate rises back just before activation.

title: Lightning-rod p+ electron drains between neighboring active regions
idea: Random stimulus 'lightning rod': give stray charge a better path to ground. Implant a narrow p+ stripe tied to the well under the passing wordline between neighboring active regions; electrons injected by aggressor wordline toggles recombine there before they can drift into the victim's storage node.

title: Limbo bar: back-gate pulse lowers wordline voltage to 1.2 V
idea: Lower the bar instead of jumping higher: give each mat's vertical access transistors a shared back gate held negative in retention (high Vt, low leakage) and pulsed positive only for the accessed mat during activation, so the front wordline needs ~1.2 V instead of ~3 V and can run straight from VDD without charge pumps.

title: Piano keys: staggered-height checkerboard capacitors double each level's pitch
idea: Black keys sit higher than white keys: in a checkerboard, even cells' capacitors start on the landing-pad layer while odd cells' capacitors start one level up on a conductive riser. Each level then holds capacitors at 1.41x the lateral pitch with about 2x the cross-section each.
note: Same two-height interleaved capacitor idea.

title: Hairpin: U-turn vertical channel puts both cell terminals on top
idea: Bend the channel like a hairpin: etch a narrow slot in each 4F2 cell and line it with a U-shaped Si or oxide-semiconductor channel around a core gate, so source and drain both land on top and the bitline and capacitor contacts sit side by side above the cell. The channel is twice the slot depth long, which keeps leakage low, in a 4F2 footprint with no buried bitline.

title: Leaf veins: backside copper grid straps wordlines, halving driver stripes
idea: Leaf veins feed every cell through branching: after thinning, add a low-resistance backside Cu grid that straps each Ru or Mo wordline every 64 cells through nano-vias, so wordlines can be 4x longer at the same RC. The die needs fewer, larger sub-wordline driver stripes, and DDR5 tRCD is unchanged.

title: Stilts: low-temperature wordline drivers built above the array, not beside it
idea: Stilts lift a house over its plot: build the sub-wordline drivers and column-select switches as <400 C oxide-semiconductor or laser-annealed poly-Si transistors in the BEOL directly over the cell array, connected down by vias, while Si sense amps and I/O stay below. Mat-edge driver stripes disappear, and externally it is still a standard DDR5 die.
note: Vias at wordline pitch through capacitor forest are the doubt.

title: Hourglass: pinched-waist vertical channel trims the leakage tail
idea: An hourglass narrows in the middle: shape each vertical access channel with a ~5 nm waist at the gate center (an oxidation-pinch step) and wide ends for low contact resistance, so the gate-drain edge field and the GIDL and trap-assisted leakage tail drop. The die skips most of the controller's REF commands internally while keeping DDR5 timing.

title: Escalator: continuous flow-line DRAM array fab instead of job shop
idea: Random stimulus 'escalator' (constant flow, no waiting) -> an array-only fab is laid out as a process-ordered linear line, with tools sized to takt time and vacuum or overhead transfer straight between steps. Wafers flow like an escalator rather than queueing in a randomized job shop.

title: Two-slot piggy bank: finance NV-memory fabs from memory plus storage budgets
idea: Random stimulus 'piggy bank with two slots' -> because the product is non-volatile, it is sold to hyperscalers as both the DRAM tier and a hot-storage/write-cache tier. Take-or-pay prepurchase agreements from both budgets are pooled into securitized fab financing.

title: Kintsugi spares: repair rows built stronger, doubling as high-retention zone
idea: As gold-filled cracks become the strongest part, spare rows are built at relaxed pitch with ~1.5x Cs; repaired rows become the sturdiest, and unused spares are exposed as a long-retention region for page tables and ECC metadata refreshed 8x less often.

title: Castle moat: storage node on buried insulator removes hot junction leakage
idea: The storage contact lands on a local buried-insulator island (silicon-on-nothing or lateral overgrowth), so the storage node has no p-n junction volume in the substrate and only the access channel can leak.

title: Dairy co-op: mid-size OEMs jointly own a DRAM fab
idea: Random stimulus 'dairy cooperative' -> farmers own the creamery. PC, auto, industrial and telecom OEMs that get squeezed in allocation form a cooperative owning a ~50k wafer/month fab; output goes out pro rata to patronage at cost plus reserve, with dividends paid in bits.

title: Alternate tiers rotate wordline direction 90 degrees against row hammer
idea: [Box: lateral 1T1C | IGZO lateral FET | standard SA | monolithic 3D tiers | Si | ALD] In a stacked array, tier k runs wordlines along x and tier k+1 along y, so no wordline has a parallel aggressor directly above or below, and in-tier neighbors are separated by grounded shield lines from the same metal.
note: Rotation constrains bitline routing per tier; row-hammer-only benefit.

title: Mirror-bond two VCT array wafers at their common blanket plate
idea: [Box: MIM charge | 4F2 VCT | charge-share SA | face-to-face bond at the capacitor plate | Si | blanket TiN-to-TiN bond needing no fine alignment] Finish two VCT arrays with an unpatterned top plate and bond them plate-to-plate; since the shared plate is blanket, overlay can be off by microns, and the upper array's bitlines reach periphery through coarse vias at the array edge.
note: Doubles bits per footprint but nearly doubles wafer cost; cost/bit gain small.

title: Capacitor walls instead of pillars: line gratings segmented by self-aligned cuts
idea: [Box: MIM on both wall faces | VCT | charge-share SA | monolithic | Si | ArF SADP line gratings + cuts self-aligned to wordlines] Form storage electrodes as continuous tall oxide-core walls, far stiffer than isolated pillars so AR 120+ does not lean, coat both faces, then segment each wall into per-cell plates with cuts self-aligned to the wordlines.

title: Solid-state 213 nm laser steppers replace neon-buffered ArF excimers
idea: Box [standard | standard | standard | standard | Si | DUV projection lithography with fifth-harmonic diode-pumped Nd:YAG (213 nm) source]: generate DUV in CLBO/KBBF nonlinear crystals instead of an Ar/F2/Ne gas discharge, and re-coat 193 nm-class optics for 213 nm.
note: 100 W at 213 nm from nonlinear crystals is far beyond demonstrated; optics re-design needed.

title: Minienvironment-only DRAM fab with defect-tolerant wafer-scale sparing
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x self-testing sense with built-in repair x wafer-scale integration x Si x sealed-FOUP and tool-minienvironment fab in an ISO-6 shell. Arrays carry 10-15% spare subarrays and on-die BIST remaps defective rows at power-up, so the higher particle density of a cheap building is absorbed by architecture rather than by an ISO-1 ballroom.

title: Public EUV utility leases scanners per exposed layer to DRAM makers
idea: Box: fab-method axis set to tool ownership. A government-chartered utility owns EUV scanners installed inside participating fabs and bills per exposed wafer-layer at a ~3% cost of capital instead of fab WACC ~10%, with take-or-pay terms moving depreciation risk off DRAM balance sheets during downturns.

title: Fluorine-free mature-node fab builds page-compression co-processors
idea: Box: new hardware × 180 nm-class CMOS × 4 KB page compressor × fab route × i-line DNQ/novolac resist, photo-definable BCB dielectric, Cl2/HBr/BCl3 etch, O2/Cl2 chamber clean, H2-bake oxide removal, hot-phosphoric nitride strip. Vias are defined lithographically in photo-BCB rather than etched in oxide, so no CF4/C4F8/NF3/SF6, HF or PFAS photoacid is used, and the chips act as PCIe zswap accelerators.

title: Bridge-resident row cache absorbs DRAM activations near GPU
idea: Box: 1T1C DRAM x standard access x on-DRAM SA x hybrid-bonded silicon bridge x Si bridge chiplet x 7 nm logic. The EMIB-style bridge between GPU and DRAM carries 64 MB of SRAM that holds whole recently opened 2 KB rows, fed through a 2 um-pitch hybrid bond so a full row moves for ~0.05 pJ/bit; re-hits are served from the bridge and the row is never re-activated.
note: AI streams show limited row reuse; row-buffer caches are known.

title: Backside power mesh halves HBM through-silicon via count
idea: Box: HBM DRAM x standard x standard x front-side signal-only hybrid bonds plus backside nano-TSV power grid x thinned Si x backside-power flow borrowed from logic. Power and ground, about half of HBM's TSVs, move to a backside metal mesh fed by dense 0.5 um nano-TSVs, so only signal TSVs remain in the keep-out zone.

title: Single vacuum cluster: plasma-dice, CO2-snow clean, activate, bond
idea: Box: HBM DRAM x standard x standard x die-to-wafer hybrid bond x Si x integrated vacuum cluster with plasma dicing, CO2-snow particle removal and plasma activation. Wafers enter once and leave as bonded stacks; dies never touch water or room air, so no pre-bond DI clean is needed.

title: Dry-pack foundry business for water-stressed U.S. regions
idea: Box: customer memory dies x any x any x SAB, ACF or inductive stacking x glass or thermoplastic carriers x laser, plasma and dry-film steps only. A U.S. contract packager built with no UPW plant at all, offering memory stacking where wet fabs cannot get water rights, on cheaper land with faster permits.

title: Relaxed DUV array bonded to logic doing per-mat BCH
idea: Box [medium: capacitor at relaxed 18 nm | access: vertical channel | sense: on bonded logic wafer | integration: wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV-only array + advanced logic]. The array wafer skips EUV and accepts ~1e-4 raw BER, while the bonded logic wafer runs a t=8 BCH decoder beside every 512-bit mat word through ~1 um pitch bonds.

title: Containerized hybrid-bond stacking micro-OSATs at data centers
idea: Box[Fab=back-end only x Scale=shipping-container cleanrooms x Integration=custom-height stacks on demand x Owner=data-center operator]: KGD wafers ship to modular back-end pods beside AI campuses that hybrid-bond, test and package memory stacks to each cluster's needs.

title: Bottom-up grown nanowire channels with etch-free sidewalls
idea: Po: chips are grown, not made. Grow single-crystal Si access channels inside the pillar openings by selective epitaxy or tin-catalyzed VLS instead of etching them out of the wafer, so the channel sidewalls carry no plasma-etch damage, the dominant source of trap-assisted leakage in vertical access devices.

title: Po: bitlines live on the wafer's backside
idea: Po: a bitline on the other side of the wafer. After front-side capacitor and buried-wordline formation, bond to a carrier, thin to ~500 nm, and pattern bitlines and the SA strip on the backside, contacting access-transistor drains through nano-vias, so bitlines never run between capacitor pillars or beside wordlines.

title: Po: only one transistor species — array-device periphery
idea: Po: a DRAM with only one kind of transistor. Build sense amps, sub-wordline drivers and local logic from the same buried-channel/vertical access transistor used in the array (plus a wider-footprint variant), deleting the separate HKMG periphery module.

title: Capacitor wafer bonded beneath transistor wafer at cell pitch
idea: Po: the capacitor lives in another factory. Etch ultra-deep trench capacitors (AR 100-150 in single-crystal Si, which does not lean like stacked pillars) on a cheap mature-node 'capacitor wafer', layer-transfer a thin single-crystal Si film on top at <400 C, then build access transistors with laser anneal and self-aligned contacts down to each buried capacitor.

title: Inspection-free fab using on-die sensors and boot-time self-repair
idea: Po: the fab never looks at its wafers. Remove most inline defect inspection and CD metrology; embed ring oscillators, capacitor-leak monitors and array test structures in every die that report process health at sort, and raise defect tolerance with 2x spare rows/columns plus boot-time soft remapping.

title: Cross-company tool-hour exchange routes DRAM steps to idle tools
idea: Po: one fab has two owners. A secure scheduling exchange lets DRAM makers route non-critical steps (implant, CMP, anneal, ALD) to idle, contamination-qualified tools in nearby mature logic fabs via sealed-pod transfer, trading tool-hours like electricity.
note: Contamination, IP and logistics barriers.

title: Interposer that is itself a capacity-tier DRAM
idea: Po: the interposer is the memory. Fabricate the ~2,500 mm2 2.5D silicon interposer, today passive wiring, on a mature trench-capacitor DRAM node so the silicon under and between GPU and HBM becomes a slower but very near capacity tier of several GB, wired to the GPU through the interposer's own dense metal.

title: Undiced DRAM tiles stitched across scribe lanes by one mask
idea: Po: the wafer is never diced. Leave 4x4 groups of DRAM dies attached; one added top-metal mask stitches a wide shared bus across the scribe lanes to a central bond field where a processor chiplet is bonded face-to-face.

title: Buried electron-sink stripe between cells absorbs hammer carriers
idea: Po: rows have no neighbors. A shallow n-type collector stripe implanted between buried-wordline trenches and biased slightly positive captures electrons released by the aggressor's passing gate before they reach the victim storage-node junction.

title: Particle-strike detector strip triggers targeted neighborhood scrubs
idea: Po: memory that feels the bullet. A strip of deliberately charge-sensitive detector cells per bank records the time and position of alpha/neutron strikes; the controller at once scrubs only the rows in that strike's footprint, catching multi-bit clusters before a second hit makes them uncorrectable.

title: Warehouse fab with sealed tool-to-tool nitrogen tunnels instead of cleanroom
idea: Po: the cleanroom is the size of a shoebox. Wafers never meet room air: a sealed N2 overhead tunnel links every tool load-port, so the building is an ordinary industrial warehouse instead of an ISO-class ballroom with massive filtration and HVAC.

title: Regional patterning hub serving several small DRAM fabs
idea: Po: the scanner is a public library. One shared facility runs the ArF immersion critical-layer exposures for 3-5 nearby small fabs; wafers travel in sealed N2 FOUPs on a scheduled shuttle, and each satellite fab owns only cheaper deposition, etch, CMP and KrF tools.
note: Shuttling every critical layer between fabs adds cycle time and contamination risk.

title: Fund U.S. roll-to-roll advanced-packaging lines for memory periphery layers
idea: Worse: leave printed and laminated packaging layers to offshore suppliers so every module ships through Asia. Flip: CHIPS-style grants and offtake guarantees for U.S. roll-to-roll lines making organic interposers, decap laminates and printed repair and configuration layers for domestic memory assembly.
note: Roll-to-roll resolution far from advanced packaging needs.

title: Repurpose OLED inkjet lines to print panel-level memory interposers
idea: Worse: build all new memory packaging capacity from scratch. Flip: convert idle Gen-6/8 OLED inkjet-printing and TFT lines into panel-level printers of interposers, decap sheets and periphery TFT layers for memory packages.

title: Hexagonal vertical bitlines with three cells radiating per tier
idea: Worse: use square grids where each vertical bitline serves cells in only two directions, wasting footprint between capacitors. Flip: place vertical bitlines on a hexagonal lattice with lateral cells radiating at 120 degrees and wordline planes cut into three interleaved phases, so each bitline serves three cells per tier.
note: Three-phase wordline planes complicate isolation; 1.4x per tier is modest.

title: Backside capacitor on a 4F2 vertical-channel cell
idea: Worse: cram capacitor, bitline and wordline onto the same face so they fight over one 4F2 footprint. Flip: build vertical-channel transistors with buried bitlines and the periphery on the front, flip-bond to a carrier, thin from the back, and form the capacitors on the exposed channel bottoms so each capacitor gets the full footprint with no bitline contacts threading between them.
note: Backside capacitor frees the 4F2 front for bitlines; ~1.5x density and thermal decoupling.

title: Smelter-friendly element palette for DRAM back end
idea: Worsen: scatter W, Ru, Co, Ta, Hf, La and Au across every chip so no recycler can recover anything. Flip: adopt design rules that limit the die and package to a minimal palette (Si, O, N, Al, Ti, Cu plus one capacitor metal) chosen to fit copper-smelter flowsheets, so e-scrap DRAM becomes a net-positive feed.

title: Counter-cyclical strategic DRAM reserve keeps fabs fully utilized
idea: Worse: let downturns idle fabs and freeze capex, so the next shortage is deeper. Flip: a government/hyperscaler reserve buys known-good DRAM wafers at a floor price during gluts, stores them in dry nitrogen vaults, and releases them during spikes, like a petroleum reserve for bits.

title: Hydrogen-rich silicon nitride reservoir continuously re-passivates interface traps
idea: Worse: run one forming-gas anneal and let hydrogen leave interface dangling bonds over the product's life, so leakage tails creep up. Flip: deposit a hydrogen-loaded SiN:H / a-Si:H reservoir near the access transistors with a diffusion barrier above, so slow H release keeps re-passivating newly broken Si/SiO2 bonds at operating temperature.

title: Earth-abundant DRAM grade standard with mandatory host ECC
idea: Worse: write qualification standards so strict that only W/Hf/Ru-based processes can pass. Flip: create a JEDEC and U.S. procurement 'EA-grade' spec that allows ~100x higher raw BER and longer retention tails if the module ships with a defined host-side ECC plus adaptive refresh, explicitly so Hf/W/Ru/Co-free cells become buyable.

title: Personality-fused universal die serving DDR, LPDDR or HBM markets
idea: Worse: commit wafers to one interface months before knowing which market will be short. Flip: design one core die carrying DDR5, LPDDR5X and HBM-attach I/O and set its personality by e-fuse at final test, routing finished wafers to whichever market is tightest.

title: Artist's negative space: SRAM-filled grout bridges between chiplets
idea: An artist paints the empty gaps: fill the 100-500 um dead gaps between HBM stacks and the GPU with thin silicon 'grout' bridge strips that hold repeaters plus 2-8 MB of line-buffer SRAM, so the gap becomes a staging cache and a retiming point.

title: Amish barn-raising: warehouse fab with sealed tool minienvironments
idea: Raise a fab the way an Amish community raises a barn. Skip the ballroom cleanroom: each tool sits in a sealed ISO-1 minienvironment linked by sealed overhead FOUP transport inside a cheap warehouse shell that modular crews put up in ~9 months.
note: FOUP minienvironments already standard; full warehouse shell is incremental.

title: Diffusion-barrier monolayer at storage-node contact for 200C retention
idea: Downhole tools at 200C expose tail cells whose mid-gap traps come from contact-metal atoms diffusing into the storage junction; an ALD AlN or hBN monolayer is deposited blanket into the existing storage-node contact holes as a diffusion barrier, and the single added mask only strips it from periphery contacts. The storage junction stays defect-free so its generation current collapses.
note: Assumes contact-metal diffusion drives tail; real tail is mostly intrinsic traps/GIDL.

title: Junctionless access nanowire: predictable decay for cold-boot-proof vaults
idea: Secure-key vaults want memory that decays on a known schedule, which needs a tight leakage distribution. Use a uniformly doped junctionless nanowire access device: with no metallurgical p-n junction there is no junction field peak or dopant-gradient trap zone, so the trap-assisted-tunneling outliers that form the leakage tail largely vanish.
note: Removes junction field peak; secure decaying-memory angle is a niche twist on known junctionless FETs.

title: Printed-electronics nanoimprint access layer with 1% dead cells allowed
idea: Flexible-electronics makers accept defect rates an EUV fab never would. Pattern the access-transistor and buried-wordline layers by step-and-flash nanoimprint (~$1-2M tools vs ~$200M EUV) and treat the ~0.5-1% of defective or leaky access devices from template defects as a known error budget the page code absorbs.

title: Hybrid-bonded GaN HEMT tier for wordline drivers and pumps
idea: GaN, used in space and 200 C power electronics, has ~10x silicon's breakdown field; a thin GaN-on-Si e-mode HEMT tier hybrid-bonded under the array hosts sub-wordline drivers and VPP switches, delivering 3-4 V swings with tiny high-voltage devices instead of thick-oxide silicon.

title: LIGO-style differential cell: true and complement capacitors stacked vertically
idea: Ultra-low-noise instruments sense differentially; store each bit as true and complement charge on two capacitors stacked one above the other in the same 4F2 footprint, a bottom-tier and a top-tier transistor sharing one vertical pillar, read by a reference-free differential amplifier. Signal doubles and reference and offset noise cancel, so each capacitor can be half the size.

title: Row-hammer adversary design: tier-interleaved rows with grounded shield planes
idea: Design for a malicious user who hammers rows: map logically adjacent rows onto different tiers of a 3D array and insert grounded metal shield planes between tiers, so no aggressor shares a tier or electrostatic coupling path with its logical neighbors. The memory controller's address hash enforces the tier interleave.

title: Liberty-ship modular DRAM fabs prefabricated in shipyards
idea: Extreme user: a wartime surge economy. Freeze one standard DRAM fab design, prefabricate cleanroom, sub-fab and utility modules in shipyards/factories, and barge them to sites for bolt-together assembly, replicating the same fab 10x the way Liberty ships were built.

title: Downhole-grade hot memory tiers let racks run waterless dry cooling
idea: From 200 C downhole tools that use SOI SRAM and ROM instead of leaky DRAM: shrink DRAM to a small hot-data cache on one cold plate and put bulk working state in 125-150 C-rated tiers (SOI SRAM, ROM weights, high-temperature NOR), so the rest of the rack runs at 60 C+ coolant and is cooled by dry coolers year-round in any climate.

title: Skyscraper sky-lobbies: express vertical lines to zone decoders every 16 tiers
idea: Copy high-rise elevator design: split a 256-tier stack into 16-tier zones, run a few express vertical lines to a lobby tier in each zone that holds thin-film local decoders, and limit each zone's staircase to 16 steps. Contact area then grows with the log of tier count instead of linearly.

title: Thick-metal coil mask enabling TSV-free stacked dedup engine
idea: One added thick top-metal mask forms inductive-coupling coils on each DRAM die. The dies stack over a logic die with no TSVs, and that logic die runs a stack-wide 64 B content-addressed dedup engine with its hash index in SRAM. Duplicate lines across all 8 dies collapse into one physical copy, so dedup moves to the stack scale.

title: One-metal passive bridge letting four accelerators share HBM stacks
idea: A silicon bridge with a single metal layer (one mask, no active devices) wires each HBM stack to two to four neighboring accelerator dies through an arbiter in the HBM base die. Capacity is statistically multiplexed at the package scale instead of hard-assigned per die.
note: HBM PHY multi-drop signal integrity is the doubt.

title: Broadcast read bus killing per-bank data replication in PIM
idea: Processing-in-memory DIMMs replicate lookup tables and model parameters in every bank, because each PIM unit sees only its own bank. One added metal mask routes a die-wide broadcast read bus, so every PIM unit reads one shared copy at the moment it is fetched. Sharing moves from the bank scale to the die scale.
note: Single shared bus serializes PIM units.

title: Wavelength-as-address: laser comb line selects the DRAM bank group
idea: Move the address decoder from nanometer on-die wiring to the rack-scale photonic spectrum: each bank group has a micro-ring receiver tuned to one comb line, so the host addresses memory by choosing which wavelength carries the request and data. One 64-line comb on a single fiber replaces 64 point-to-point links and the bank-select decode tree.

title: Word-granular remap CAM absorbs directed-self-assembly line defects
idea: No EUV: pattern ~12 nm pitch wordlines with block-copolymer directed self-assembly on DUV guide patterns, accepting the ~0.1-1/cm2 dislocation defects. Scale shift (molecular dislocation -> 64-bit word): each defect is mapped at sort and absorbed by a per-bank content-addressable remap of 64-bit words.

title: Multi-beam e-beam writes per-die personalized repair wiring
idea: No EUV: after wafer sort, a multi-beam e-beam writer exposes one custom upper-metal layer per die that physically reroutes around defective subarrays and bitlines, instead of using fuse banks.

title: Interposer ECC chiplet serves array-only DUV memory dies
idea: No EUV: strip ECC, repair logic and most periphery from the DUV memory die and put them on one mature-node logic chiplet on a silicon interposer that serves 8 array dies. The chiplet can run long codes across all of them.
note: Sense amps and drivers dominate periphery and cannot move off-die.

title: All-solid-state 193 nm fiber-laser light source for DUV scanners
idea: Scale jump from a meter-long gas-discharge chamber to fiber photonics: frequency-convert a high-power Yb fiber laser array (fifth or sixth harmonic in nonlinear crystals) to 193 nm, so scanners need no neon buffer gas and no argon or krypton.
note: High-power 193 nm harmonic generation suffers crystal damage; neon is a niche cost.

title: Allied pro-rata emergency allocation pact for fab output
idea: Treaty-scale time trigger: allied governments and vendors pre-agree that when contract prices rise more than 2x in a quarter, a fixed share of wafer output is allocated pro-rata to members' critical sectors, on the IEA oil-sharing model.
note: IEA-style sharing for wafer output; politically hard, modest supply effect.

title: Orphaned flexible-display pilot lines become a national printed memory foundry
idea: U.S. flexible display programs, such as the Army-funded Flexible Display Center, never found an anchor product. Re-task such roll-to-roll oxide-TFT lines into a federally backed pilot foundry for refresh-free oxide memory foils, with DoD as anchor buyer for low-power ruggedized memory.

title: Early-2010s 4F2 vertical-channel DRAM fixed with backside metal bitlines
idea: Vertical-pillar 4F2 DRAM was shelved in the early 2010s, largely because buried bitlines of doped silicon had high resistance and floating pillar bodies caused hysteresis. After thinning, form low-resistance Cu or Ru bitlines from the backside that contact the pillar bottoms. Add a thin backside body-tie rail along each pillar row to pin the body potential.
note: Backside low-R bitlines and body tie fix VCT's historical problems; backside alignment at 4F2 pitch is hard.

title: PARA revived with sacrificial hammer-canary cells between rows
idea: PARA (probabilistic adjacent-row activation) was never adopted because at ~1k-ACT thresholds its trigger probability must be so high that blind neighbor refreshes eat bandwidth. Fix: place a strip of deliberately hammer-sensitive canary cells (thinner isolation, smaller Cs) along each wordline pair, read through a cheap dedicated sense line, and refresh neighbors only when a canary has physically flipped.

title: The Machine had no fab: tool-condominium ownership inside fabs
idea: HPE's memristor and The Machine stalled because HPE owned no fab and its manufacturing partner put its own roadmap first. Fix: a fab condominium where memory designers and large buyers own specific tools (e.g. one ALD cluster, one etch bay) inside an operator's fab, depreciate them on their own books, and hold guaranteed slots on those tools.

title: Lithium niobate domain-wall cells store write-once KV caches
idea: Each KV entry is written once per token and read many times, so store it in thin-film LiNbO3 domain-wall memory. A voltage pulse creates a conductive head-to-head domain wall between electrodes, and reading the wall current is non-destructive. LiNbO3's 1140 C Curie point keeps walls pinned for 10 years at 125 C, and 1e8+ cycles is plenty for one write per session.
note: Domain-wall LN memory exists in labs; CMOS integration and density unclear.

title: CoZrTa magnetic inductors make refresh adiabatic, recycling bitline charge
idea: Co: integrate thin-film amorphous CoZrTa inductors in the DRAM BEOL, one per bank, so restore swings during refresh are driven as resonant LC ramps instead of abrupt switching, and charge from discharging bitlines is returned to the tank for the next row.

title: Ti: titanium-oxo resist and 213 nm solid-state laser lithography
idea: Pattern periphery layers with a Ti-oxo-cluster photoresist exposed by a fifth-harmonic Nd:YAG 213 nm solid-state laser scanner instead of ArF/KrF excimers, whose gas fills are mostly neon plus argon or krypton; the Ti-O resist doubles as its own hardmask, dropping an argon-sputtered layer.

title: Phosphorus delta-doped epitaxial sheets serve as built-in buried bitlines
idea: In a monolithic Si epi tier stack, grow each horizontal bitline as an in-situ phosphorus-doped (>1e20) epitaxial sheet that the slit etch later segments into short local bitlines, so the bitline is a crystalline conductor formed during growth rather than metal pushed into 100:1 lateral cavities.
note: Doped Si ~100x more resistive than metal; dopant diffusion over stack thermal budget.

title: Francium rows: read-once data read destructively, never restored or refreshed
idea: Francium survives only minutes; the compiler marks tensors read exactly once and dead within milliseconds (pipeline activations, streaming buffers) and places them in francium subarrays with short 128-cell bitlines and 256 B rows, where reads isolate the cell before restore, rows are excluded from refresh, and the slot is freed on read.

title: O: IGZO gain-cell row cache in HBM base die
idea: Add a few MB of IGZO 2T0C gain-cell memory (BEOL, seconds-scale retention, non-destructive read) on the HBM base die that caches recently opened core-die rows; repeat activations to cached rows are served from the base die with standard HBM timings, so core dies are not re-activated.
note: IGZO gain-cell variant of a row cache near the core dies.

title: P: buried phosphorus collector line sweeps hammer-injected electrons away
idea: A deep n+ phosphorus stripe runs between adjacent rows under the passing wordline, biased slightly positive, acting as a drain that collects electrons emitted from traps when aggressor wordlines toggle, before they reach victim storage nodes.

title: Fe: Iron-air multi-day batteries let fabs sit on stranded wind
idea: Pair a memory fab with 100-hour iron-air batteries (reversible rusting of iron pellets) plus a fast flywheel ride-through layer so it can site in curtailed-wind regions with fab-grade power quality.

title: Cu: LME-style physically delivered DRAM futures to finance capacity
idea: Create a standardized, warehouse-receipt DRAM futures contract (16 Gb die-equivalents in bonded vaults) modeled on LME copper and aluminum, so buyers hedge 3-5 years ahead and fabs borrow against forward sales.

title: Mg: Retool HDD read-head fabs as MgO tunnel-junction memory foundries
idea: HDD head fabs already sputter and pattern CoFeB/MgO tunnel junctions below 30 nm; as hard-drive unit volumes fall, convert these lines to STT-MRAM back-end processing on foundry-supplied CMOS wafers.
note: Head fabs run small non-300mm wafers; MRAM adds niche NV capacity, not DRAM-class cost/bit.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembled gates for near-zero-LER sense-amp transistors
idea: Define only the sense-amp input-pair gates with directed self-assembly of a lamellar block copolymer guided by a coarse litho trench; the molecularly set period gives ~1 nm line-edge roughness instead of ~2-3 nm from resist. Both transistors of a pair are cut from the same lamella so they share edge statistics.

title: Die-bank build-to-order: array dies stockpiled, 180 nm interface die added later
idea: Like Dell's build-to-order line, makers stockpile bare array dies (cells and SAs only). A U.S. assembler flip-chips each onto a 180 nm interface/periphery die chosen per customer (DDR, LPDDR, CXL, custom AI) when orders arrive, using 1990s C4 solder bumps and wide, slow buses.

title: Plain-weave bitlines: true and complement swap metal levels every cell
idea: Like warp yarn passing over and under weft, route each bitline pair on two metal levels that cross at every cell pitch through a self-aligned via, so coupling from neighbouring bitlines and wordlines averages out continuously instead of in area-hungry twist regions; open-bitline 4F2 arrays gain folded-array noise immunity.

title: Skull-melting crystal puller: silicon grows its own crucible
idea: Borrowed from titanium and zirconia skull melting: a water-cooled segmented copper cold crucible with RF induction holds the silicon melt inside a frozen silicon skin, so no quartz crucible ever touches the melt; a magnetic cusp field stirs and shapes the melt for 300 mm Czochralski pulls. The crucible is permanent and only electricity is consumed.
note: Cold-crucible melt convection makes dislocation-free 300 mm CZ very hard.

title: Slip-cast synthetic-silica crucibles from polysilicon plant byproduct
idea: Potters slip-cast vessels from liquid clay; hydrolyze SiCl4 byproduct from a Michigan polysilicon plant into colloidal synthetic silica, slip-cast crucible bodies in porous molds, and arc-fuse them with a synthetic inner wall, all within one U.S. chemical park.

title: Float-line continuous fab: capacitor module never leaves vacuum
idea: Replace the job-shop flow (500+ FOUP moves) with a linear vacuum line like a float-glass or coil-coating line for the capacitor module: mold deposition, HAR etch, clean, ALD electrode, high-k, top electrode and anneal stations chained wafer-by-wafer with in-line metrology at one takt time.

title: Multi-head embroidery: write the one added layer maskless per die
idea: Because only one layer is added, write it with a 10,000-beam e-beam direct writer, like a multi-head embroidery machine stitching many garments at once; the mask becomes a data file that changes per product, per lot, or per die to route row and column repair without laser fuses.

title: Sheet-cake cut-anywhere memory sea bonded to logic wafers
idea: Bond whole DRAM wafers made of identical repeating tiles onto logic wafers, then choose product capacity at the dicing saw like cutting sheet cake. Tile-to-tile links are stitched so any rectangle works.

title: Microbrewery packaging lines: containerized U.S. stacking plants
idea: Deploy modular advanced-packaging lines (panel fan-out, hybrid bonding, laser direct imaging) in shipping-container bays across ~20 U.S. sites, at $50-200M each, the way microbreweries spread. They package imported commodity dies into HBM-class stacks.

title: Movable-type sense amplifiers: swappable spare periphery slices
idea: Gutenberg's movable type made every letter replaceable; build the sense-amp, column-decoder and local wordline-driver strips as identical slices behind a small antifuse-configured crossbar, so a failed or slow periphery slice is swapped for a spare instead of scrapping the mat, which row/column redundancy cannot fix.

title: Ladder-stop segmented vertical bitlines tolerate argon-free metal fill voids
idea: A dropped stitch runs the whole knit column unless loops lock; because argon-free fill (CVD/ALD in N2/H2 with no PVD liner) leaves more voids in tall vertical bitlines, split each vertical bitline into 8-tier segments joined by lockable switch transistors, so a void or open loses one segment, which is remapped to a spare.
note: Segmented vertical bitlines with spares; adds switch transistors per segment.

title: AerCap for fab tools: a lessor that redeploys scanners between fabs
idea: Aircraft lessors own planes and re-lease them across airlines. A capitalized lessor owns ArF scanners and deposition/etch fleets with standardized install kits, leases them on 3-5 year terms, and moves them when a fab downsizes. Asset-backed securities secured by the tools fund the fleet.

title: Retool idle U.S. thin-film PV and flexible-display lines as memory fabs
idea: IFR: memory capacity appears without building fabs. Closest achievable: buy or lease idle R2R thin-film PV and flexible OLED lines, add a printed storage-element module, and ship foil memory tiers within 12-18 months.
note: Coarse-rule thin-film lines give low-density, slow foil memory; printed storage element unproven.

title: In-stack binary threshold decoder replaces the 3D staircase
idea: IFR: 'tier selection takes zero area.' Backward: thread 7 vertical select-gate rods through each bitline column and give each tier's series select transistors a binary code of high/low thresholds (set by one coarse i-line implant mask per tier as it is deposited), so a 7-bit voltage pattern on the rods opens only the one tier of 128 whose code matches, an old ROM depletion decoder turned vertical.
note: Resembles layer-selection-by-multilevel-Vt schemes from 3D NAND/RRAM; implant-through-stack Vt spread risk.

title: Array-logic-array sandwich: each sense amp reads both bond faces
idea: IFR: 'periphery is free because every sense amp serves twice.' Backward: hybrid-bond array wafers to both the front and the thinned back of one logic wafer; each sense amp takes its true bitline from the top array and its reference bitline from the mirror cell in the bottom array (an open-bitline pair split across the stack), alternating roles per access.
note: Double-face hybrid bonding of logic wafer; gain ~25% is modest.

title: Freeze one array mask set; multibeam writes all periphery variants
idea: Ideal: masks cost nothing. Closest: freeze a single array reticle set for every product and density, and write the product-specific periphery and option layers with a massively parallel multi-e-beam direct-write tool, so new SKUs, CXL/PIM variants and bug fixes need zero new reticles.
note: Multibeam direct-write throughput on wafers is the doubt; limited to option layers.

title: CFET-stacked two-transistor gain cell from an unmodified logic flow
idea: Ideal: memory that costs zero extra masks in a logic fab. Closest: in a CFET (n-over-p stacked nanosheet) process, the top sheet is a high-Vt write transistor and the bottom sheet a read transistor whose gate is the storage node, giving a capacitorless 2T gain cell in one transistor footprint using only a layout change.

title: All-dry, water-lean flow enabled once capacitor dip-out vanishes
idea: Ideal: a memory fab with no ultrapure water. Closest: with no capacitor mold to wet-strip (the HF dip-out and supercritical drying that dominate DRAM wet work), run the capacitorless cell flow on vapor-HF, remote-plasma and cryogenic-aerosol cleans with gas recycling, keeping UPW only for CMP.
note: Depends on capacitorless cell existing first.

title: Conversion credits that turn idle U.S. logic fab modules into DRAM
idea: Ideal: memory capacity that already exists on U.S. soil. Closest achievable: a 40% tax credit plus a 7-year offtake guarantee for converting existing U.S. 300mm 45-65 nm logic modules to DRAM with ArFi multipatterning and refurbished capacitor tools, with no new shell or permitting.
note: 45-65 nm DRAM is ~10x less dense than 1b nodes; cost per bit uncompetitive.

title: Buried-oxide-isolated storage nodes immune to row hammer coupling
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): controllers keep sending the same RFM and refresh, so the cell itself must stop flipping. Isolate each storage-node junction from the shared substrate with a local buried-oxide pocket (selective SiGe removal and oxidation) and shield it with a grounded buried plate between adjacent wordlines, cutting the electron-injection and trap-assisted paths that aggressor activations exploit.

title: Bias-only toolbox: co-pulse plate and well during idle
idea: Limit: no process change; only array biases may move. In long idle or self-refresh, ramp the cell plate and the array p-well down together by ~0.3-0.5 V. Every storage node then level-shifts down capacitively without forward-biasing its junction, which shrinks both the storage-to-wordline voltage that drives GIDL and the Vds of '1' cells. Both rails return before activation.

title: Cross-shaped four-way cells around every vertical bitline
idea: Limit: vertical bitline holes cannot get denser. Slice each tier around a vertical bitline into four quadrant channels, so one bitline serves four lateral cells per tier instead of two.

title: Scanner-hour exchange: rent idle logic-fab EUV for DRAM layers
idea: Constraint: the DRAM fab may buy zero EUV scanners. A brokered exchange sells logic foundries' EUV utilization dips; DRAM lots travel in sealed FOUPs to a nearby logic fab for 2-3 critical exposures under a standardized resist/track recipe, then return.
note: Cross-fab contamination, queue time and IP control are the real barriers.

title: Wavelength is the address: bank-per-color photonic interposer
idea: Scarcity: no address decode logic on the memory die. A silicon-nitride photonic interposer gives each DRAM bank a fixed WDM wavelength via a tuned microring drop filter; a request is a pulse on that bank's color and the reply returns on the same color, so routing and arbitration happen optically.

title: Own zero EUV: tolling critical layers at a partner scanner
idea: Self-imposed limit: no EUV ownership. A DUV-only DRAM fab ships sealed, nitrogen-purged FOUPs to a partner's EUV cell for only the 1-2 layers where multipatterning is uneconomic, paying per exposure.

title: Swap voltage level for oscillation phase: nanoscale parametron bit
idea: Revive Goto's parametron at the nanoscale. Each cell is a nanomechanical or LC resonator pumped at 2f by a shared clock, the bit is the 0 or pi phase of its subharmonic oscillation (which the pump keeps locked), and the cell is read by phase comparison with a reference.
note: Mechanical parametron memory is shown (NTT); continuous pumping power and poor density.

title: Swap EUV masks for maskless two-beam interference lattice exposure
idea: Memory arrays are periodic, so expose the capacitor and wordline lattices by 193-nm immersion two-beam interference (~40 nm pitch per pass). Double exposure with the grating rotated forms the hole lattice, and a cheap DUV trim mask cuts the array edges.
note: 193i two-beam pitch floor is ~67 nm; still needs multipatterning and overlay to other layers.

title: Substitute fixed sense reference with co-decaying reference cells
idea: Substitute the static VDD/2 bitline reference with reference cells in each row, written to half charge whenever the row is written. They leak through identical access transistors, so the sense threshold sags with the '1' cells instead of staying fixed.
note: Co-decaying reference tracks median, not tail cells; dummy/reference cells known.

title: Substitute plasma etching of access pillars with TMAH crystallographic etch
idea: Substitute argon/helium-diluted plasma etch of fins and pillars with a hard-masked TMAH wet etch that stops on {111} planes. The channel sidewalls come out atomically flat and damage-free, with tightly controlled width.

title: Substitute xenon flash and excimer anneals with microwave activation
idea: Substitute xenon flash-lamp and excimer-laser anneals (both rare-gas tools) with 5.8 GHz microwave annealing below 500 C. The microwaves couple to implant damage and dopants, activating and healing them without diffusing the graded storage-junction profile.

title: Substitute silicon channel with sulfurized MoS2 grown in H2S/N2
idea: Substitute Si with a bilayer MoS2 access channel made by ALD of MoO3 and conversion in H2S/N2 at ~600 C in a resistive furnace (no argon carrier), then encapsulated in thermal-ALD Al2O3. The ~1.3 nm body has no dangling-bond surface generation sites and near-ideal electrostatics.
note: MoS2 access channels widely pursued; sulfurization route known.

title: Substitute oxide isolation with sacrificial-carbon air gaps near passing gates
idea: Substitute the dielectric between passing (neighbor) wordlines and the storage-node junction with an air gap: amorphous carbon is deposited from C2H2/H2 with no argon or helium dilution, then burned out through a porous cap in O2.

title: Liquid-nitrogen DRAM with double-length copper bitlines
idea: Substitute room-temperature operation with 77 K operation: copper resistivity falls ~7x and junction/GIDL leakage effectively disappears, so bitlines can run 1024 cells instead of 512 and refresh is dropped for datacenter racks with LN2 loops.
note: Bitline length is capacitance-limited, not resistance-limited.

title: Randomly coded nanowire decoders mapped after fabrication
idea: Substitute lithographically exact decoders with an e-beam nanowire array whose gate oxide is randomly modulated (random doping or random dielectric patches). After fabrication a tester discovers each wire's address code and stores the map.

title: Nanoimprint-patterned pitch-matched sense and decoder strips
idea: Substitute immersion/EUV exposures of the highly repetitive pitch-matched sense-amp and subword-driver strips with UV nanoimprint from an e-beam-written master. University nanofabs routinely run NIL for such periodic patterns.

title: Epitaxial superlattice edges replace EUV for wordline pitch definition
idea: Substitute EUV/SAQP for the densest line layers with superlattice nanowire pattern transfer: grow a 512-period Si/Si0.7Ge0.3 superlattice (6/6 nm), cleave and polish its edge, recess SiGe with peracetic-acid etchant, evaporate Mo at glancing angle onto the Si ridges, and stamp the 512-wire, 12 nm-pitch array onto the target wafer, one stamp per sub-array mat.

title: Area-selective ALD replaces deposit-then-etch for tier dielectrics
idea: Substitute 'deposit everywhere, then etch' with area-selective ALD: small-molecule inhibitors (acetylacetone, aminosilanes, or alkanethiol monolayers on metal) block nucleation on a tier's metal/semiconductor faces so Al2O3/ZrO2 grows only on dielectric faces (and vice versa for Mo), self-aligning each tier's isolation and capacitor dielectric with no dielectric etch.

title: Peroxide-soluble germanium tiers replace SiGe sacrificial layers
idea: Substitute SiGe sacrificial tiers (normally released with HF/H2O2/acetic or CF4 remote plasma) with Ge-rich tiers (sputtered a-Ge in deposited oxide-semiconductor stacks, thin strained Si0.3Ge0.7 in epi stacks) that dissolve in warm dilute H2O2 as soluble GeO2, selectivity to Si >100:1, opening lateral cavities for capacitors and gate-all-around access devices.

title: Substitute solar-grade handle wafers for prime CZ silicon substrates
idea: Grow a ~10 um prime epitaxial device layer on a porous-silicon release layer atop a reusable donor wafer, bond and split it onto a cheap solar-grade or recycled-silicon handle, then re-polish and reuse the donor 20+ times.
note: ELTRAN-style transfer known; materials saved are a small share of wafer cost, so step change is modest.

title: Substitute supercritical CO2 for ultrapure-water wet cleans
idea: Run post-etch residue and particle cleans in single-wafer supercritical CO2 chambers (100-200 bar, 40-60 C) with 1-5% amine/alcohol chelant co-solvent, recompressing and recycling >95% of the CO2 on-tool; no DI rinse and no spin dry.
note: sCO2 cleaning researched since 2000s; particle removal and throughput limited adoption.

title: Substitute gas-cluster ion beams for slurry chemical-mechanical polishing
idea: Planarize with location-specific gas-cluster ion beams (Ar/NF3 clusters of ~1000 atoms) steered by an in-line thickness map, combined with spin-on planarizing film plus selective plasma etch-back, replacing CMP slurries and post-CMP brush and megasonic cleans.
note: GCIB is too slow for global planarization; useful only for trim.

title: Substitute vapor-phase chelation for SC2 metal-contamination cleans
idea: Remove Fe, Cu and Ni contamination by exposing wafers to formic acid or acetylacetone vapor at 150-250 C, forming volatile metal formate or acac complexes that are pumped away, replacing HCl/H2O2/H2O SC2 baths and rinses.
note: Vapor-phase hfac/formic metal removal studied since 1990s; incomplete removal of some metals.

title: Substitute distillable organic solvent for water in final rinses
idea: Use a low-boiling non-PFAS solvent such as electronic-grade isopropanol or PGME as the rinse fluid in closed single-wafer tools, with on-tool vacuum distillation recovering >99% per cycle and a metal-scavenger resin bed.
note: Solvent rinses do not remove ionic residues like water; IPA drying already common.

title: Copper nanowire velcro: room-temperature interlocking die bonds
idea: Substitute solder microbumps and thermocompression with electroplated copper nanowire forests grown through porous-alumina templates on both mating pads; pressed together at room temperature they interlock and cold-weld at 5 um pitch.
note: Cu nanowire interlocking bonds published; yield at 5 um pitch unproven.

title: Substitute refresh timer with same-process canary cells that flip first
idea: Swap the fixed 64 ms refresh clock for a few deliberately undersized 'canary' capacitors per subarray, built in the same litho/etch steps so they track the local leakage tail and temperature; when a canary flips (checked by a cheap read every few ms), only that subarray is refreshed.

title: Substitute SRAM hammer counters with analog activation-integrating witness cells
idea: Replace per-row digital activation counters with one tiny floating-node 'witness' cell per row pair that gets a fixed charge packet pumped onto it each time a neighbor wordline fires (capacitive coupling pump); crossing a threshold flags a victim refresh, and normal refresh resets it.
note: Same leaky integrator.

title: Four-level DRAM cell using flash-style program-and-verify
idea: Combine NAND flash's incremental-step program-and-verify loop with DRAM charge storage: the write driver applies short pulses and senses the node between pulses until it lands in one of four charge windows, storing 2 bits per cell. A gain read device and a reference ladder resolve the levels, and refresh re-centers each level.
note: Multi-level DRAM proposed since 1989; margin shrinks with leakage.

title: NEMS parametron storing bits as oscillation phase
idea: Revive Goto's 1950s parametron with GHz nanomechanical resonators: each cell is an AlN or SiN nanobeam pumped at twice its resonance, so it oscillates in one of two phases (0 or pi) that encode the bit. A shared pump line drives thousands of resonators, and phase is read by capacitive pickoff against a reference without destroying it.

title: Flash charge-trap layer for per-cell access-transistor Vt trimming
idea: Add a thin nitride charge-trap film to the access-transistor gate stack (SONOS fused with DRAM). At wafer test, retention-profile every cell, then Fowler-Nordheim program electrons into only the leakiest access devices to raise their Vt by 0.2-0.4 V permanently.

title: Adiabatic resonant charging for refresh wordlines and bitline restore
idea: Fuse adiabatic logic with refresh bursts. A stepwise or LC-resonant supply ramps the 3 V wordlines and restore drivers, and charge from the row being closed is recycled into the next row opened.
note: Charge recycling in DRAM arrays studied; refresh share limits system gain.

title: Vertical NPN gain cell with storage on the floating base
idea: A BiCMOS cell puts the storage node on the floating base of a vertical bipolar transistor under the MOS access gate. A read pulses the emitter so collector current amplifies the stored charge by beta, roughly non-destructively.

title: Tunnel-diode latch pair inside a one-transistor cell
idea: Two series resonant or Si/SiGe interband tunnel diodes on the storage node (a Goto pair, after TI's late-1990s TSRAM) create two stable voltages held by picoamp current. Access uses a standard DRAM transistor.
note: TSRAM prior art; ~1 mW/Gb holding power rivals self-refresh.

title: Sense amp with nonvolatile ferroelectric offset trim
idea: Integrate a tiny HZO ferroelectric capacitor in each sense amp and program its polarization at wafer test so it couples a compensating charge onto the weak side of the latch, permanently trimming offset from ~15 mV to ~3 mV with no runtime calibration.

title: Oxide-TFT predecoders and test logic built over the array
idea: Move slow, low-drive periphery (row predecoders, fuse latches, test-mode logic, mode registers) into BEOL IGZO thin-film transistor layers built over the cell array, leaving only the sense amps and fast IO in silicon.

title: Cymer-laser interference lithography plus Multibeam e-beam cuts for arrays
idea: Combine maskless two-beam 193 nm interference lithography (ArF lasers built in San Diego) for the perfectly periodic wordline, bitline and pillar gratings with US multi-column e-beam direct-write (Multibeam, Santa Clara) for the sparse cuts, contacts and periphery, plus one spacer doubling to reach ~20 nm half-pitch.
note: Gratings plus e-beam cuts is known CEBL; dense DRAM contacts overwhelm e-beam throughput.

title: Laser-polymer spalling slices ingots into wafers without kerf
idea: Combine subsurface IR laser modification with polymer stress spalling: a focused 1.3-2 um laser writes a damage plane 775 um deep, and a chilled polymer film bonded on top cracks the wafer off along it, replacing multi-wire sawing that turns ~40% of the ingot into kerf.

title: Two-pass Czochralski purifies upgraded metallurgical silicon, then grows prime
idea: Combine purification and crystal growth (zero masks): a fast sacrificial pull from low-B/P upgraded metallurgical silicon dumps metals into the melt tail by segregation (k ~1e-5 to 1e-8 for Fe, Cu, Ni); the clean section is crushed and repulled as a slow prime ingot.

title: Nanoimprint guide plus block-copolymer multiplication for EUV-free capacitor holes
idea: Combine J-FIL-style nanoimprint, which prints a 4x-relaxed hexagonal guide pattern, with high-chi block-copolymer self-assembly that subdivides each guide cell into a 12 nm-scale honeycomb. The densest DRAM layer, the capacitor holes, then needs no EUV and no SAQP.
note: Both NIL and DSA widely pursued for DRAM holes.

title: Area-selective ALD merges wordline-module patterning and deposition
idea: Combine area-selective ALD (inhibitor monolayers that block growth on SiN/SiO2) with the buried-wordline module. The gate dielectric grows only on exposed trench silicon and the Mo/TiN wordline grows only on that dielectric, so recess, cap and isolation self-align without block masks.
note: ASD widely pursued; selectivity defects remain.

title: NOR flash analog arrays compute FFN layers in place
idea: Combine 40 nm embedded NOR flash cells with analog matrix-vector multiplication: transformer feed-forward weights (~2/3 of parameters) are programmed as cell conductances and compute in place, while attention and KV stay digital in a small DRAM.

title: CXL switch holds a rack-wide page dedup table
idea: Combine the CXL switch's address-routing tables (mature-node switch silicon) with a global content-hash index: identical pages across every host in a rack (OS images, runtimes, model weights) are stored once in pooled memory and mapped read-only into each host, with copy-on-write on modification.

title: Magnetically aligned nanowire underfill replacing microbumps
idea: Combine anisotropic conductive film with magnetic-field assembly: Ni-cored, Au-shelled nanowires dispersed in a curable underfill chain into vertical columns between pads under a field applied during bonding, then cure, giving 2-5 um pitch z-axis interconnect with no microbump plating or Cu CMP.
note: Magnetically aligned ACF published; 2-5 um pitch bridging risk.

title: Final CMP step doubles as bond activation, no plasma
idea: Combine CMP with surface activation: a tailored final-polish slurry (colloidal silica plus OH/amine terminating chemistry) leaves the SiCN or oxide bond face densely silanol-terminated and particle-free, and dies bond in-line within minutes, skipping the argon/N2 plasma activation chamber.

title: Sacrificial-polymer air gaps between wordlines cut hammer coupling
idea: Combine BEOL air-gap interconnect with DRAM wordlines: fill wordline gaps with a thermally decomposable polymer (polynorbornene or polycarbonate), cap with PECVD oxide and bake so the polymer diffuses out, leaving air gaps that cut line-to-line capacitance ~50%. Buildable in a university nanofab: spin-coat, PECVD and bake.

title: Inductive-coupling stacked DRAM eliminating SF6 Bosch TSV etch
idea: Fuse thinned-die stacking with ThruChip-style inductive or capacitive near-field links between layers, plus wire-bonded or edge-plated power delivery. That removes the SF6/C4F8 Bosch TSV etch and the TSV keep-out area.

title: Thermos-style sealed vacuum isolation around each storage node
idea: Borrow vacuum-flask insulation: replace STI oxide next to each storage node with sealed vacuum cavities (sacrificial carbon ashed out, then capped by non-conformal deposition), so no oxide traps or bulk paths remain between adjacent nodes.
note: Air gaps already used in DRAM spacers; tail leakage is mostly junction/GIDL, not via STI.

title: LIDAR time-to-digital converter turns bitline voltage into delay
idea: Borrowed from automotive LIDAR TDCs: the bitline voltage starves a short inverter chain so a 20 mV difference becomes ~30 ps of delay, and a digitally calibrated arbiter flip-flop decides the bit from arrival order. No large matched cross-coupled latch is needed.

title: Laser-trimmed op-amp offset trim for minimum-size sense amps
idea: Borrowed from precision analog trimming: sense-amp transistors are drawn at minimum size (accepting large mismatch), and each SA gets a 3-bit trim capacitor array whose code is measured by power-up BIST and held in a small nonvolatile register per 8 SAs. Matching comes from digital trim instead of area.

title: Differential-GPS reference cells broadcast decay corrections
idea: Borrowed from differential GPS base stations: a few reference cells per mat, written at known levels, are sensed alongside each row to measure how much charge has leaked since refresh at the current temperature, and that correction trims the mat's shared sense reference.
note: Reference cells track average decay, but refresh is set by tail cells.

title: AMOLED threshold-compensation sense amp on glass
idea: Borrowed from AMOLED 7T1C pixel compensation: in each IGZO or LTPS sense amp on a glass panel, the input transistors are first diode-connected so their own threshold is stored on a gate capacitor, then the bitline signal is applied on top, cancelling +/-300 mV thin-film threshold scatter.

title: Downhole-oil-tool SiC electronics make refresh-free hot memory
idea: Borrowed from SiC electronics in oil-well logging tools and EV inverters: cells and CMOS periphery are built on 4H-SiC wafers (bandgap 3.26 eV), whose intrinsic carrier density is ~1e16x lower than silicon's, so junction leakage stays negligible at 150-200 C beside accelerators.
note: SiC DRAM demonstrated at Purdue in 1990s; density and MOS interface limits.

title: LTPS display lasers crystallize silicon for every 3D tier
idea: Borrowed from LTPS phone-display backplanes: each 3D tier receives low-temperature amorphous Si that is melted and recrystallized by line-beam excimer laser pulses too short to heat the tiers below, yielding large-grain lateral transistors tier by tier.

title: Termite-mound chimneys: heat-pipe pillars threaded through the stack
idea: Adapted from termite-mound ventilation shafts: every 64th vertical bitline slot in a DRAM-on-logic stack becomes a Cu/diamond 'chimney' pillar tying all tiers to a top heat spreader, holding every tier within ~5 C of the coolant.

title: HVDC thyristor valves shrunk into a capacitor-free bulk-silicon latch
idea: Grid HVDC valves hold state as latched pnpn thyristors that stay on at minimal holding current. Adapt a vertical pnpn thyristor per bit in plain bulk silicon, gated by the wordline to latch or unlatch, with a sub-uA hold current only on active rows and a slow-decay off state elsewhere.

title: Microwave tunnel-diode latch makes a refresh-free one-transistor SRAM
idea: Microwave oscillators exploited the negative resistance of Esaki tunnel diodes. Adapt two series Si/SiGe interband tunnel diodes as the bistable load on a single access transistor (1T-2TD), forming a static latch at roughly 2x DRAM-cell area with no capacitor.
note: TSRAM concept from 1990s; PVR/valley current.

title: PCB direct metallization replaces tungsten plugs in shallow cells
idea: PCB makers coat through-holes with a graphite colloid and then electroplate copper directly. Adapt this with a conformal CVD amorphous-carbon seed plus electroplated Co or Cu fill for cell contacts, made feasible because a capacitor-free cell has only shallow ~5:1 contacts instead of deep storage-node plugs.

title: Airport baggage CT: inline X-ray laminography for 3D DRAM tiers
idea: Adapt CT and laminography from airport scanners and BGA inspection into an inline compact-source X-ray laminography tool that reconstructs tier-by-tier recess depth, channel thickness and capacitor fill in 100-tier 3D DRAM stacks on every lot without cross-sectioning.
note: X-ray metrology for 3D NAND exists; nm resolution needs flux.

title: Printing-press plates: one copy of model weights serves many hosts
idea: Borrowed from printing, where one plate prints a whole run: a CXL 3.x multi-host shared-memory appliance holds a single read-only copy of popular model weights mapped into 8-32 servers, each of which keeps only KV and activations locally; a hot-row SRAM cache in the switch absorbs repeated reads.
note: CXL bandwidth far below HBM; only host-side staging copies can be shared.

title: Wine-cellar racking: match data lifetime to each row's retention
idea: Borrowed from cellars that put long-aging vintages in the coolest, most stable racks: a boot-time and online profiler bins every row by measured retention (most rows hold 1-10 s, only a tail is near 64 ms), and the OS places each page by its predicted rewrite interval into a row that outlasts it; pages with uncertain lifetimes go to a non-volatile shelf.
note: RAPID/RAIDR prior art; VRT undermines profiling.

title: Cable-TV frequency division: many DRAM dies share one RF line
