idea: Adapted from DOCSIS cable-TV plant: each DRAM die on a stack or interposer gets its own RF carrier (e.g., eight carriers spread over 10-80 GHz) on one shared transmission line, using tiny on-die mixers instead of dedicated wires. Dies tune in and out like set-top boxes on a multi-drop coax-like trace.
note: Echoes UCLA multiband RF-interconnect work; mixer power and area are the doubt.

title: Turbine-blade internal cooling channels inside HBM spacer layers
idea: Adapted from jet-engine blade cooling: serpentine microchannels are etched into thin silicon spacers placed every few dies and carry pumped dielectric coolant through the stack. Heat leaves from the stack interior instead of conducting up through 16 dies.
note: Interlayer microchannel cooling is well studied; TSV routing through channels is the hard part.

title: RFID fluidic self-assembly drops memory dielets into interposer wells
idea: Adapted from 1990s fluidic self-assembly used by RFID tag makers: millions of small DRAM dielets suspended in liquid flow over an interposer with etched, shape-matched wells. The dielets settle into place by gravity and shape and are then bonded by reflow.

title: Supermarket holographic scanners inspire free-space optical memory interconnect
idea: Adapted from the holographic optical elements in 1990s barcode scanners: a single cast hologram plate above the board redirects hundreds of VCSEL beams from memory packages to photodiodes on the processor, replacing board traces.
note: 1990s free-space optical board interconnect revisited; alignment/thermal drift issues.

title: Transit-card inductive coupling powers and talks to glued stacks
idea: Adapted from contactless smart cards: each DRAM die gets on-die spiral coils in 180 nm-era metal, used both for near-field data links and for resonant power transfer like a card reader. The dies are simply glued together, with zero TSVs and zero bumps.
note: Inductive die-to-die data (ThruChip) known; wireless power to DRAM stacks is inefficient.

title: Display-fab DRAM panels: magnify area, minify cost per area
idea: MAGNIFY substrate area ~1000x and MINIFY cost per m2: a 10-person team designs 1T1C arrays of oxide or LTPS TFTs at ~3 um pitch and buys Gen-8.5 glass runs from idle LCD fabs; a 5.5 m2 sheet of ~10 um2 cells holds ~70 GB raw, diced into slabs bonded to logic by panel-level fan-out.
note: Same display-fab panel memory strategy.

title: Magnify refresh duration, minify energy: adiabatic resonant refresh
idea: Refresh whole banks slowly with microsecond ramps driven by an on-package LC resonator that swings wordlines and bitline precharge sinusoidally and recovers charge each cycle, so dissipation scales as (RC/T)*CV^2 instead of CV^2. Refresh has no latency requirement, so stretching it costs nothing.

title: Magnify isolation: storage node floats on buried oxide, no junction
idea: Form the storage-node contact region on a local buried-oxide pocket created by Si/SiGe selective etch-and-fill, so the storage node touches no p-n junction or substrate and the only leakage paths left are the gated channel and the capacitor.

title: Zero-kerf laser slicing: thinner wafers on reusable carriers
idea: Magnify wafers per ingot ~2.5x: split ingots along a laser-modified subsurface plane (zero kerf) into 300 um wafers, temporarily bonded to reusable carriers for processing, instead of wire-sawing 775 um wafers and losing ~150 um of kerf each.

title: Area-selective deposition ends blanket metal plus CMP
idea: Minify metal to only where it stays: self-assembled inhibitor monolayers on dielectric surfaces make Mo/TiN ALD nucleate only in contacts and lines. This eliminates the overburden and the CMP step that today removes 80-95% of the deposited metal.
note: ASD is a heavily pursued research field.

title: Two-beam interference lithography prints the cell grid maskless
idea: Magnify one exposure to the whole periodic array: pattern the perfectly periodic DRAM cell grid with interfering 193 nm beams (standing-wave lithography), and use a cheap DUV trim mask only at array edges.

title: Silicon-on-sapphire DRAM removes substrate leakage at 125 C
idea: Minify the leakage path to zero: grow thin silicon on Kyropoulos sapphire (alumina from bauxite, pulled in molybdenum crucibles) so storage nodes have no junction to a substrate; only the channel can leak.
note: SOS defect density raises leakage; GIDL still dominates.

title: Inductive coupling replaces TSVs in stacked DRAM
idea: Minify die-to-die vias to zero: thin each die to 10 um and pass data through on-chip inductor coils stacked over each other, with power delivered through a single edge-plated rail, removing TSV etch, liner, fill and reveal.

title: High-chi block copolymer multiplies DUV hole density fourfold
idea: Magnify density without new optics: coarse DUV guide posts direct a high-chi block copolymer to self-assemble 4 cylinders per guide at ~12 nm, used for landing pads and storage-node contacts.

title: Rotary spatial ALD at atmospheric pressure
idea: Magnify deposition throughput 10x by spinning wafers under fixed precursor zones separated by gas curtains (spatial ALD) at atmospheric pressure for capacitor high-k and liners, instead of slow pulsed vacuum ALD.

title: Programmable photomask for periphery layers
idea: Minify mask-set cost to zero for non-critical layers by exposing through a 193 nm-compatible spatial light modulator (micromirror array) that reprograms its pattern per layer and per product.

title: Micro-banks: sixteen cells per printed bitline
idea: Minify the bitline to 16 cells and magnify the bank count to millions, each tiny sub-array with its own printed sense amplifier, so printed-wire RC drops about 64x.

title: Minify GC heap headroom with a hardware collector
idea: Minify the 2-3x heap headroom that Java, Go and JS runtimes need for throughput. A memory-side co-processor in the controller does concurrent mark and compaction using read barriers in hardware, so heaps run at 1.1-1.2x live size without GC thrash.

title: Edge-standing die library: DRAM dies stood upright
idea: MAGNIFY dies per footprint by standing 100 thin DRAM dies upright like books, each bonded on one polished edge to the substrate through edge pads, with coolant flowing in the gaps between them.
note: Edge-interconnect cubes known (Irvine Sensors); edge pad bandwidth is limited.

title: Capacitive proximity tiles aligned by micro-magnets
idea: MINIFY the gap to a ~1 um dielectric: memory tiles clamp face-to-face with compute and signal through capacitive coupling pads at 10 um pitch, aligned by patterned micro-magnets; unclamp to replace.

title: Magnify vertical link count: over-provisioned laser-drilled through-glass vias
idea: Stack thin glass memory layers using laser-drilled through-glass vias at ~4x the needed count, with any of four vias able to carry each signal through a switch. Open or high-resistance vias never kill a stack.
note: TSV redundancy schemes are well known; glass stacking adds unknowns.

title: Magnify HBM life: debond retired stacks and remount them
idea: Laser-release and thermally debond HBM stacks from retired AI accelerators, re-bump them, and mount them on fresh low-cost silicon or glass interposers for inference cards binned at lower bandwidth.

title: Minify crucible dependence: kerfless epitaxial wafers peeled from templates
idea: Grow 300 mm device-grade silicon by fast epitaxy on a porous-silicon release layer over a reusable template, peel it off, and reuse the template 50x+ with no Czochralski ingot, quartz crucible or wire saw.

title: Eliminate static states: nanomechanical parametrons store bits as oscillation phase
idea: Eliminate the static bistable well: each cell is a high-Q nanomechanical or LC resonator pumped at 2f by a shared line, which forces it to oscillate at f in one of two phases (0 or pi), reviving Goto's 1950s parametron at GHz. A small injection seeds the phase on write, a mixer reads it, and the pump continuously restores amplitude so the bit cannot decay.

title: Eliminate excimer lithography: block-copolymer cylinders template every storage node
idea: Eliminate ArF and EUV exposure for the cell array, since excimer lasers need neon, argon and krypton and EUV drive lasers use helium: a high-chi block copolymer on a sparse UV-LED-exposed chemical guide self-assembles into a hexagonal 24-nm-pitch cylinder lattice. Sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O, N2 purge) turns the cylinders into AlOx hard masks for the storage nodes.
note: DSA for DRAM holes long pursued; defectivity remains the blocker.

title: Eliminate deposited dielectrics: Bi2O2Se channel with native Bi2SeO5 gate oxide
idea: Grow 2D Bi2O2Se by CVD and partly convert it with UV-ozone or O2 plasma into its native high-k (k~20) Bi2SeO5, forming a Si/SiO2-like clean interface on an atomically thin body; the access device reaches near-60 mV/dec swing with full depletion. All steps are tube-furnace and plasma steps.
note: Bi2O2Se/Bi2SeO5 already demonstrated (Peking U.); access-device use is incremental.

title: Eliminate bulk thickness: 2 nm quantum-confined silicon body widens bandgap
idea: Thin SOI by repeated thermal oxidation and HF strip to a 2-3 nm body, where quantum confinement widens silicon's effective gap by ~0.3-0.5 eV and suppresses intrinsic carrier density 1e3-1e4x; build the access device in this film over a thick buried oxide. Only furnace oxidation and wet etch are needed.

title: Eliminate heat-driven leakage: thin-film Bi2Te3 Peltier cooler under array
idea: Sputter or co-evaporate thin-film Bi2Te3/Sb2Te3 thermoelectric couples into the substrate or interposer beneath the memory array, pumping the cell region 15-25 C below the surrounding logic. Since leakage roughly doubles per ~10 C, cooling only the array extends retention 3-6x.
note: Thin-film TEC heat plus pumping power may cancel savings in hot stacks.

title: Eliminate the solid gate dielectric: air-gap suspended-gate FET
idea: Fabricate a suspended metal gate over the channel on a sacrificial amorphous-Si layer released by XeF2; the gate pulls in electrostatically for access with abrupt switching and springs back to a large air gap in hold, deepening the off state and removing gate-oxide traps. Unlike a contact relay, current still flows through a semiconductor channel.

title: Eliminate per-bitline latches: shared time-to-digital bitline sensing
idea: Remove the cross-coupled latch from every bitline pair. After charge sharing, each bitline gates a single discharge transistor onto a shared ramp, and one time-to-digital converter, time-interleaved over 32 bitlines in about 4 ns, records which bitlines cross threshold first. A global restore bus then rewrites the cells through one-transistor restore switches.

title: Eliminate VDD/2 precharge: plate-pulsed sensing from grounded bitlines
idea: Hold bitlines at ground and delete the equalizer transistors and the VBLP generator. To read, pulse the segmented cell plate of the selected 512-cell sub-array upward (FeRAM-style plate-line drive). A '1' cell pushes more charge onto the floating bitline than a '0', against a half-plate-pulse dummy reference, and a ground-referenced NMOS stage resolves it.

title: Eliminate multi-patterning in sense-amp stripes via block-copolymer self-assembly
idea: SA and column-select transistor arrays are periodic at bitline pitch, so define their gate and active lines by directed self-assembly of PS-b-PMMA guided by coarse KrF chemical prepatterns. Remove the PMMA with UV plus an acetic acid rinse and transfer with HBr/Cl2/O2, eliminating fluorocarbon SADP spacer etches and PAG resists.

title: Eliminate the high-AR capacitor etch: anodic alumina pore templates
idea: Skip plasma-etching capacitor holes; deposit thick aluminium over the transistor array, pre-dent it at each storage node, and anodize so self-ordered pores with aspect ratios above 500:1 grow straight down onto each node; line them with high-k and electrode.
note: AAO nanocapacitors are known; self-ordered pore pitch (~60 nm) and registration to storage nodes are the doubts.

title: Eliminate binary storage: three-level cells paired across adjacent tiers
idea: Store three charge levels per cell and pair cells vertically across two tiers so 9 states encode 3 bits in 2 cells; a shared vertical reference ladder in each pillar tracks temperature and leakage drift.

title: Eliminate etch-fill-polish cycles: flat-by-construction conversion patterning
idea: Define isolation and channels by locally converting silicon rather than removing it: patterned oxygen or nitrogen implant plus anneal (SIMOX-like) turns selected regions into insulator, so the surface stays planar and no gap-fill or CMP is needed.
note: LOCOS/SIMOX-like; volume expansion and implant dose costs.

title: Eliminate implant masks: junctionless in-situ doped access channels
idea: Grow channels in-situ doped during epitaxy or deposition and use junctionless accumulation-mode access transistors, removing source/drain and well implant masks with their resist strips and post-implant wet cleans.
note: Junctionless devices struggle to turn off and add GIDL; oxide channels already junctionless.

title: Eliminate TSVs: through-silicon optical links at 1310 nm
idea: Silicon is transparent at 1310 nm, so stacked thinned dies talk vertically through the bulk with micro-LED or VCSEL emitters and Ge photodiodes aligned in columns, with no drilled or plated vias.

title: Eliminate ceria CMP: flowable oxide plus atomic-layer etch-back planarization
idea: Replace ceria-slurry oxide CMP steps with spin-on polysilazane fill cured to SiO2, then planarize by quasi-atomic-layer etch-back that stops on a SiN etch-stop detected optically, so no slurry or pad is used.

title: Eliminate the wafer fab: oxide gain-cell memory on idle display-glass lines
idea: Build 2T0C oxide-TFT gain-cell arrays on Gen-8.5 glass (~5.5 m2, ~75x a 300 mm wafer) in under-used LCD fabs with 1-1.5 um lithography, then dice tiles for a high-capacity, slower CXL memory tier.

title: Eliminate vacuum pumps: atmospheric spatial ALD for capacitor dielectrics
idea: A gas-bearing spatial ALD head separates precursor zones with N2 curtains at atmospheric pressure while the wafer moves beneath it; pulsed-pressure dwell cycles push precursor down high-AR holes.

title: Eliminate the binary bit: ternary-charge cells give 58% more bits per mask
idea: Store three charge levels per cell (0, half and full VBLH) and read them with a two-reference successive-approximation sense amplifier; pairs of cells hold 9 states and encode 3 bits.

title: Eliminate the capacitor-hole mask: block-copolymer self-assembly guided by landing pads
idea: Coat a cylinder-forming block copolymer over the landing-pad topography so it self-assembles into a hexagonal hole array registered to the pads, and use it directly as the hard-mask template for capacitor holes. The die and its DDR5/HBM interface are unchanged.

title: Eliminate per-die probe touchdowns: scribe-line test bus, one contact per wafer
idea: Wire every die to a shared power and serial test bus routed through the scribe lines to a few large edge pads; one touchdown powers all dies, each runs BIST and reports over the bus, and a fuse isolates shorted dies. Dicing cuts the bus away, leaving standard DDR5/HBM dies.

title: Eliminate duplicate lines with content-addressed main memory in CXL expanders
idea: A CXL memory expander stores 64B lines by hash in a deduplicated store with reference counts; host physical addresses map to hash entries, so identical lines across VMs and containers are stored once.

title: ESD-free hybrid-bond IO for wafer-level-only stacks
idea: Eliminate ESD protection on internal die-to-die pads: hybrid-bonded faces are never touched by humans or probes after bonding, so drop ESD diodes and use a sacrificial wafer-level discharge grid that is severed during bonding, shrinking pad capacitance from ~200 fF to ~10 fF.
note: Same sacrificial ESD grid concept.

title: Photonic phase-change memory read by light without conversion
idea: Eliminate O/E/O conversion at disaggregated memory: store bits in GST or Sb2Se3 patches on silicon-nitride waveguides whose phase state sets transmission, and read them with WDM light pulses arriving directly from compute.

title: Eliminate controller refresh timers: per-row canary cells trigger refresh
idea: Add one deliberately weakened canary cell to each row (smaller capacitor, leakier transistor) and write it to '1' at every restore. A low-power background sense polls the canaries, and only rows whose canary has decayed get refreshed, so refresh tracks actual temperature and leakage.

title: Eliminate helium from the DRAM fab bill of materials
idea: Eliminate helium: replace He backside cooling in etch/CVD electrostatic chucks with H2 or H2/Ar mixes (H2 conducts heat ~1.2x better than He) with chuck seal redesign, and membrane-recapture any residual He at tool exhaust.
note: H2 conducts heat well; seal, safety and chemistry compatibility are the real unknowns.

title: Eliminate one-ingot-per-wafer: reusable donor wafers via porous-silicon transfer
idea: Eliminate consuming a full prime wafer per lot: grow device-grade epitaxial silicon on a porous-silicon release layer over a donor, bond it to lower-grade handle wafers, cleave, and reuse each donor 10-20 times.

title: Leakage as the keeper: Si/SiGe tunnel-diode latched storage node
idea: Reverse leakage from enemy to holder: two series Si/SiGe resonant interband tunnel diodes (1990s low-temperature CVD) on a 180 nm cell's storage node cross their negative-resistance curves at two stable points, so tiny diode currents continuously restore '0' or '1' against junction leakage; one access FET reads and writes (tunneling SRAM).
note: Same tunneling-SRAM latch; Si RITD PVR known.

title: Junctionless storage node removes the leakage-tail junction
idea: Reverse the doping layout: make the access device a uniformly n-doped ultrathin (<=5 nm) junctionless channel that turns off by full depletion under a wraparound gate, so there is no n+/p metallurgical junction at the storage node. Trap-assisted junction leakage and junction-field GIDL, the main sources of the retention tail and variable retention time, lose their high-field region.

title: Thin to widen: quantum-confined 2 nm channel raises effective bandgap
idea: Reverse the scaling instinct of keeping a thick body for less variability: thin the access-transistor body to ~2 nm Si (vertical fin or nanosheet), which raises the effective bandgap ~0.2-0.3 eV by quantum confinement. Band-to-band tunneling and thermal generation currents fall exponentially with the gap, and DRAM's modest on-current need absorbs the mobility loss.

title: Store less charge to keep more: low-field hold during self-refresh
idea: Reverse the instinct to store maximum charge: in self-refresh, restore '1's to ~0.7 V instead of ~1.0 V and set plate and negative wordline so the gate-to-storage-node field is minimal. GIDL and trap-assisted tunneling fall exponentially with field while charge falls only ~30%, so GIDL-limited tail cells hold longer; one full-swing pass restores normal margin on wake.

title: Reference cells that decay alongside their row
idea: Flip the sensing reference from a fixed VARY/2 to a moving one: each row carries a '1' and a '0' reference cell written at the same instant as the data and leaking through identical devices, and their charge-shared average becomes that row's sense threshold. As stored '1's sag, the threshold follows them down instead of waiting for them to cross a fixed midpoint.

title: Resonant wordline tank recycles refresh wordline energy
idea: Reverse the energy flow of refresh: because refresh activates rows in a fixed, known sequence, drive the boosted wordlines from an on-die LC tank (thin-film inductor in top metal) that swings each wordline up and returns its charge to the tank on the way down, instead of dumping pumped VPP charge to ground every row.

title: Resist-free periphery via area-selective deposition, no imported photoresist
idea: Reverse subtractive patterning: periphery contacts and vias are formed by depositing only where wanted, using area-selective deposition with self-assembled inhibitor monolayers from U.S. chemical suppliers and one coarse e-beam template, eliminating several resist-litho-etch loops.

title: Capacitor first, IGZO transistor last, perovskite dielectric
idea: Re-sequence the flow: build the capacitor array first in the silicon wafer and crystallize a SrTiO3 dielectric (k~100+) at 700 C, then build low-temperature (<400 C) IGZO vertical access transistors on top by re-using the existing active/wordline/bitline masks; the only added mask is the via from capacitor top to transistor drain.
note: Capacitor-first with IGZO vertical transistor on top resembles Kioxia OCTRAM; k~100 STO thin-film doubtful.

title: Castellated kerf vias: TSVs moved to die edges
idea: Move vertical interconnect from die interior to edge: one added mask etches via trenches in the dicing streets, and sawing through their centers leaves half-vias on each die's sidewall. After stacking, the aligned sidewall half-vias are connected vertically by plating or printed redistribution.
note: Edge/sidewall die stacking (Irvine Sensors, Vertical Circuits) is known; perimeter limits IO.

title: Move purity from the quartz to a sacrificial inner liner
idea: Rearrange where purity lives: make crucibles from ordinary non-Spruce-Pine fused silica and spray an inner barium-doped devitrifying coat plus CVD Si3N4 liner that crystallizes into a dense cristobalite skin in the first hour, so the melt only ever sees the engineered liner.

title: Waterless fab: supercritical CO2 replaces ultrapure water rinse
idea: Reverse wet to dry: replace most UPW rinse and post-etch clean steps with supercritical CO2 plus co-solvent cleaning in closed recycle loops; this also prevents capillary collapse of high-AR capacitor pillars.

title: Interference-printed array: the light itself is the mask
idea: Reverse the role of mask and light: print the periodic cell array with maskless two- or four-beam 193 nm immersion interference lithography (~40 nm pitch, shrunk by one spacer step), and use only a cheap KrF trim exposure to cut array edges.

title: Chemistry is the mask: area-selective deposition of landing pads
idea: Reverse 'litho decides where material goes': passivate oxide with self-assembled monolayer inhibitors so ALD metal only nucleates on exposed contact plugs, growing storage-node landing pads in place with no lithography.

title: Fluidic self-assembly of shape-keyed memory tiles
idea: Reverse pick-and-place: diced memory tiles with keyed asymmetric outlines tumble in a fluid over a logic wafer etched with matching recesses, and the capillary pull of molten low-temperature solder in each recess drags tiles into ~1 um alignment, assembling thousands in parallel.
note: Fluidic self-assembly known (Alien Technology, Tohoku).

title: Cool from inside: microchannels etched into memory die backsides
idea: Reverse the heat path so memory can sit on top of compute: DRIE ~100 um microchannels into the back of each die, seal them with the next bonded layer, and circulate dielectric coolant through the stack so heat leaves sideways instead of through the hot logic.
note: Interlayer microchannel cooling is a long-studied approach.

title: Microspring sockets for reworkable, upgradable memory dies
idea: Reverse permanent bonding: sputter stress-graded metal fingers that curl up off the interposer into 20 um-pitch microsprings, and clamp memory dies onto them, so dies can be tested, swapped or carried to the next compute generation after assembly.
note: Same reworkable socket mechanism (PARC stressed-metal springs).

title: Silicon ribbon sub-THz waveguides between memory and compute
idea: Reverse 'metal for wires': DRIE-etch high-resistivity silicon ribbons on the interposer as dielectric waveguides for 150-300 GHz carriers, with tapered couplers at each chiplet, giving low-loss 100+ Gb/s channels over several centimetres without copper skin-effect loss.

title: Image-sensor pinned well with source-follower readout replaces the capacitor
idea: TRIZ #3 Local quality + #2 Taking out: borrow the CMOS image sensor 4T pixel and store the bit as ~500-2,000 electrons in a buried n-well under a p+ pinning layer (dark current ~aA, since the surface traps are pinned), transfer it to a floating diffusion through a transfer gate and read it through an in-cell source follower. Gain readout, not charge sharing, senses it, so no tall capacitor is needed; the shrink target is a vertical pinned pillar of ~40 nm.

title: Resonant LC drivers sweep refresh wordlines adiabatically
idea: TRIZ #18 Mechanical vibration / resonance: refresh is perfectly periodic and predictable, so drive it with a resonance. Package-level inductors form an LC tank with a bank's refresh wordline and bitline load, so lines rise and fall as sine half-cycles and their energy is recovered rather than dissipated through the ~3 V VPP pump.

title: Wafer-scale monolayer WSe2 on sapphire: junction-free atomically thin switch
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells and thin films: use a 0.7 nm monolayer channel grown by MOCVD directly on c-plane sapphire and double-gated so the gate controls every atom of the channel; with no bulk, no pn junction and a ~1.6-2 eV gap, junction generation leakage vanishes and short-channel leakage stays suppressed at ~10 nm gate length.
note: Same 2D monolayer access channel.

title: Modulation-doped In2O3/Ga2O3 superlattice channel resolves mobility versus leakage
idea: TRIZ #40 Composite materials: build the channel on glass as an ALD superlattice of ~1 nm In2O3 wells and Ga2O3 barriers, so electrons in the wells give high mobility when the gate fills them, while in the off state the wide-gap Ga2O3 barriers set the leakage floor and trap out oxygen-vacancy donors.

title: Periodic action: resonant LC wordline drive recycles boost energy
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action: wordlines are driven from a resonant tank formed by an interposer inductor and the selected wordline capacitance, so the ~3 V boost arrives as a half-sine and its charge returns to the tank when the wordline falls, bypassing most of the ~30%-efficient VPP charge pump.

title: Zirconium disulfide channel with its own oxide as gate dielectric
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: 2D ZrS2 (bandgap ~1.7 eV) oxidizes easily, which is normally a defect. Here a controlled O2 plasma deliberately converts the top layers into amorphous ZrO2 (k ~20) that serves as a perfect-interface gate dielectric, giving a 2-3 layer ZrS2 write transistor for a 2T0C gain cell.
note: Native high-k oxide on ZrS2/HfSe2 is published; wafer-scale 2D growth remains the barrier.

title: Plasma-deposited organosilicon resist converts to glass under exposure
idea: TRIZ #32 Color changes (exposure switches the film's chemistry): plasma-deposit a solvent-free methylsilane film whose exposed areas photo-oxidize into SiO2-like glass, then dry-develop the unexposed film in a Cl2 plasma.

title: Supercritical CO2 with ozone replaces water rinse-and-dry cycles
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics and hydraulics: clean and dry wafers in pressurized supercritical CO2 carrying dissolved ozone and a little alcohol co-solvent, then recompress and reuse the CO2.

title: Three-beam interference lithography for all dense hexagonal array layers
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: one maskless tool interfering three 193 nm beams at 120 degrees prints the honeycomb lattice for active islands, capacitor holes and landing pads by only changing phase and rotation; spacer doubling brings it to ~40 nm hex pitch and a cheap DUV block mask trims the array edges.

title: 180 nm TCAM dedup engine for constant-time page fingerprint lookup
idea: TRIZ #24 Intermediary: borrow the 1990s router TCAM; a 180 nm ternary CAM holds partial fingerprints of pages, each newly written or newly cold page is looked up in one cycle, and only hits are byte-verified, making dedup a continuous hardware service instead of a CPU scan.
note: 180 nm TCAM cannot hold fingerprints for hundreds of millions of pages; DRAM hash tables suffice.

title: Self-describing paired lines with header-in-slack, no metadata table
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: when two adjacent 64 B lines each compress to 30 B or less, they are packed into one 64 B slot whose first bits describe the encoding, and the freed buddy slot goes to a free list; a decoder simple enough for 180 nm reads the header in-line, so no separate metadata table, metadata cache or extra DRAM access is needed.
note: Similar to LCP/buddy-style compressed layouts.

title: Universality: coaxial TSV acting as signal, decap and heat pipe
idea: TRIZ #6 Universality: build each signal TSV as a coax with a Cu core, a 20 nm high-k ZrO2 liner and a grounded Cu sleeve. The shielded core carries data at tight pitch, the sleeve-to-substrate stack acts as distributed decoupling capacitance, and the extra copper conducts heat up the stack.

title: Microfluidic channels etched in U.S.-made stack base die
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics/hydraulics: coolant microchannels are etched into the domestically fabbed logic base die and capped with a bonded silicon lid, so liquid flows directly under the stack and holds DRAM dies at 60 C or below instead of 85-95 C.

title: Nesting: oxide-TFT memory nested in logic BEOL reusing existing masks
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: a memory layer is nested between two existing logic metal levels, reusing the via mask as the TFT gate contact and metal mask as source/drain, so the only new mask defines the oxide channel island.

title: Physarum oscillation-phase bit: nanomechanical parametron storing 0 or pi
idea: Slime mould encodes information in the phase of its cytoplasmic oscillations. Store each bit as the 0 or pi phase of a parametrically pumped ~1 GHz AlScN nanomechanical resonator: a 2f pump sustains either phase indefinitely, and a weak seed signal chooses which. Read by mixing with a reference phase on a shared line; many resonators share one pump line.
note: Same pumped-resonator phase bit.

title: CaMKII avalanche chain: small trigger magnet flips a stable cluster
idea: CaMKII holoenzyme subunits phosphorylate their neighbours, so one activated subunit switches the whole ring and keeps it switched. Make each bit a chain of 6-12 exchange-coupled nanomagnets. A short SOT pulse switches only the low-barrier 'trigger' magnet at the end, and the reversal runs down the chain as a domain wall; the chain's collective barrier (>60 kT) sets retention.
note: Resembles exchange-coupled composite media; a chain of magnets enlarges cell area.

title: Hippocampal sleep consolidation: in-cell ferroelectric backup at power-fail
idea: The brain stores new memories quickly in the hippocampus and consolidates them into cortex during sleep. Coat each DRAM capacitor's inner electrode with 3-4 nm HZO and run it below the coercive field as a linear DRAM cap. On a power-fail interrupt, energy from a package hold-up capacitor drives all rows to write each cell's charge into polarization within ~10 ms, and the state is restored at power-up.

title: NiFe-hydrogenase proton loading: hydrogen-doped nickelate Mott switch
idea: Hydrogenase enzymes shuttle protons and electrons in and out of a Ni-Fe active site. Gate a thin SmNiO3 or NdNiO3 channel through a solid proton conductor: a write pulse injects hydrogen, which dopes electrons into the nickelate and drives it from metal to insulator (resistance change >10^3). The hydrogen stays put when unpowered and is pulled back out by reverse bias.
note: Known H-doped SmNiO3 work (Ramanathan).

title: Hibernating banks with on-die thermoelectric torpor cooling
idea: Like hibernators that drop body temperature to slash metabolism, place thin-film Bi2Te3 Peltier elements under each bank/HBM die region, pump heat from idle banks into active ones' sinks to hold idle banks 15-25 C cooler, and let the refresh controller stretch tREFI per bank from its temperature sensor.

title: Leaky-integrate-and-fire timestamps let sense references track decay
idea: Neurons integrate with a known membrane time constant; store a 3-4 bit coarse refresh timestamp per row in a sidecar column, and have the sense-amp reference DAC slide with elapsed time to follow the expected droop of '1's and creep of '0's, so a half-decayed cell still resolves.
note: Time-based sliding reference; same decay-tracking reference core.

title: Pneumatized bird-bone air-gap spacers isolate wordlines from storage nodes
idea: Bird bones are hollowed by air sacs; in vertical-channel BEOL DRAM, fill the gaps between adjacent wordlines and storage-node contacts with sacrificial polynorbornene that decomposes at 350-400 C through a porous cap, leaving sealed air gaps (k=1).
note: Same air-gap spacer concept via sacrificial polymer.

title: Plasmodesmata junctionless access channels need no dopant activation
idea: Plant cells connect through continuous plasmodesmata channels that callose closes by squeezing; build the access device as a junctionless, uniformly n-doped 3-5 nm channel (in-situ doped In2O3 or poly-Ge:P deposited at 350 C) that a wrap gate fully depletes to turn off.
note: Same junctionless access concept with low-temp oxide channel.

title: Synaptic-vesicle charge packets shifted by bucket brigade to edge amplifiers
idea: Instead of a sense amp on every bitline pair, the activated row's charges move as discrete packets (like vesicles to a release site) through CCD-style transfer gates under each bitline. They reach a few high-quality correlated amplifiers at the mat edge, which digitize and write back by reverse transfer.

title: Stomatal back-gate planes seal every 3D tier when idle
idea: Give each tier of a lateral-transistor 3D DRAM a buried conductive back-gate plane under its channel layer, driven strongly negative when that tier's banks are idle and relaxed during access, like stomata closing at night, using the plane's large capacitance as a slow low-power control.

title: Hornbeam-leaf fold stacking replaces TSVs in memory stacks
idea: Hornbeam leaves fold along pleats inside the bud and open intact. Mount thinned DRAM dies on a roll-to-roll printed polyimide flex with fine copper wiring and fold it accordion-style so each die connects through the fold edge, giving an 8-16 die stack with no TSVs.
note: Folded-flex die stacking is old packaging art; fold-edge I/O density far below TSV/hybrid bond.

title: Nephron countercurrent coolant loops through stacked DRAM tiers
idea: Microchannels in alternating DRAM tiers carry coolant in opposite directions, like the loop of Henle, so the hot outlet of one layer sits beside the cold inlet of the next and every die sees nearly the same temperature. The whole stack stays below 85 C, the point where DRAM refresh rate doubles.

title: Electric-eel series stack: voltage-stacked HBM tiers
idea: An electric eel sums voltage by stacking thousands of electrocytes in series. Likewise HBM tiers are wired in electrical series: the package supplies ~8-12 V, the same current passes down through each tier at ~1.1 V each, and small on-die push-pull regulators balance the tiers. Supply current, and with it the power TSV count and IR drop, falls about N-fold.

title: Pluripotent wafer bank: hold half-processed wafers to differentiate later
idea: Stem cells stay undifferentiated until signals commit their fate. Fabs run wafers through common front-end steps (isolation, buried wordline, periphery transistors) and bank them, then finish them as DDR5, LPDDR or HBM core dies once demand is clear.
note: Different products differ in floorplan from early masks; only works within a shared die design.

title: DNA-replication templating: nanoimprint masters replace EUV for cell arrays
idea: DNA copies itself by templating from a master strand. Capacitorless cell arrays are laid out on regular gratings that nanoimprint lithography reproduces from e-beam-written masters cloned into daughter templates, removing EUV from the array layers.

title: Goto's parametron revived: bits as oscillation phase in pumped nanoresonators
idea: The 1950s parametron stored a bit as the 0 or pi phase of a parametrically pumped resonator; build rows of ~200-nm GHz NEMS beams (or compact LC tanks) driven at 2f by one shared row pump, so parametric bistability holds the phase while pumped and reading is a nondestructive phase comparison against a reference tone.
note: Same parametron revival.

title: Vacuum-flask isolation: hydrogen-anneal voids float storage junctions above nothing
idea: A thermos keeps heat in by surrounding it with nothing. Etch a dense array of tiny holes with Cl2/HBr plasma beneath each storage-node region and anneal in H2 at ~1100 C so silicon surface migration seals them into a continuous buried void ('empty space in silicon'); the storage junction sits on vacuum, with no HF release etch or fluorinated gas.

title: MEMS bulk-micromachining: TMAH crystallographic etch makes atomically smooth access pillars
idea: MEMS fabs carve mirror-flat silicon walls along slow-etching crystal planes with alkaline TMAH, no plasma. Define vertical access pillars with an amorphous-carbon hard mask opened in O2 plasma, rough-etch with Cl2/HBr, then finish sidewalls in dilute TMAH so channel faces terminate on crystal planes, replacing SF6/fluorocarbon etch and its damage and polymer residue.

title: Vinyl-record pressing: nanoimprint wordline gratings with diamond-like-carbon release, not fluorosilanes
idea: Records are stamped from a master in seconds instead of each being cut. Pattern dense wordline and active-line gratings by UV nanoimprint from a master mold coated with hydrogenated diamond-like carbon as the anti-stick layer, using a PFAS-free acrylate resist, O2 plasma descum and Cl2/HBr transfer etch in place of fluorosilane release layers and PFAS photoacid generators.
note: NIL for memory already pursued; defectivity and overlay limits.

title: Microwave oven annealing: low-temperature regrowth of storage junction damage
idea: Microwave ovens heat what absorbs, not the whole kitchen. Activate storage-node dopants and regrow amorphized silicon by 2.45/5.8 GHz microwave annealing at 400-500 C, where dipole-assisted solid-phase epitaxy avoids the end-of-range loops and diffusion of spike anneals, replacing the fluorine co-implants used to suppress those defects.

title: MicroLED mass transfer of known-good DRAM micro-tiles
idea: Adopt microLED display mass transfer: make DRAM arrays as 200 um micro-tiles on a dense array wafer, test and map them, then stamp-transfer only good tiles, thousands per stroke, onto a periphery/logic wafer with hybrid-bond landing pads, assembling dies from perfect tiles.

title: Sourdough-starter wafers: one CZ seed donates twenty transferred device layers
idea: As a baker keeps one starter alive and bakes off it, grow a 1-2 um epitaxial device layer on a porous-silicon release layer of a premium CZ seed wafer, bond it to a cheap kerfless direct-cast or reclaimed handle wafer, split along the porous layer (ELTRAN-style), re-polish the seed and repeat 10-20 times. Buried wordlines and access transistors live in the transferred epi film.

title: PFAS-free nonstick cookware chemistry for immersion topcoats and resists
idea: Cookware makers replaced PTFE with sol-gel ceramic silica nonstick coatings. Replace fluoropolymer immersion-lithography topcoats with hydrophobic alkyl-silsesquioxane sol-gel topcoats and swap perfluoroalkyl-sulfonate photoacid generators for non-fluorinated sulfonium-carboxylate or metal-oxide resists; process-only, DDR/HBM output unchanged.

title: Solar spatial-ALD conveyor for DRAM capacitor stacks
idea: Borrowed from solar PERC lines, which deposit AlOx by spatial ALD: wafers move under fixed slots of precursor, purge and oxidant at near-atmospheric pressure, so pulses become positions instead of time steps. Adapt a rotary spatial-ALD platen to DRAM ZrO2/Al2O3/TiN capacitor stacks, removing the vacuum purge cycles that dominate cluster-tool time.

title: RFID sweep: in-storage parallel scan replaces DRAM indexes
idea: Like an RFID reader inventorying a whole warehouse in one sweep instead of consulting a ledger, records in NV carry their own tags and computational-storage controllers scan all flash channels in parallel, using per-block Bloom summaries kept in the NV itself, eliminating DRAM-resident indexes.
note: Computational-storage scans with Bloom summaries are known.

title: Phone vapor-chamber layers laminated between HBM dies
idea: Borrow the smartphone vapor chamber. Thin, sealed two-phase micro-chambers (wicked Cu mesh, water) sit between groups of core dies, with TSV bundles passing through sealed pillars. They spread heat sideways to a cold plate at the stack edge.
note: Same in-stack two-phase heat spreader mechanism.

title: Phased-array radar beams to cable-free memory sleds
idea: Borrow phased-array radar beam steering. Each accelerator package and memory sled carries an in-package 140-300 GHz antenna array, forming steerable point-to-point beams across the rack. Any accelerator can attach to any memory sled with no cables or switches.

title: Bookbinding spine: sidewall-plated interconnect replaces TSVs
idea: Stack thinned dies like book pages, with pads routed to and exposed on one edge. Then form a 'spine' of vertical Cu lines on the stack sidewall with a laser-patterned seed and electroless plating plus electroplating below 100 C.

title: MEMS-style post-package trimming of sense-amplifier offsets
idea: MEMS gyros and oscillators are trimmed after packaging to cancel fabrication asymmetry. Each sense-amp pair gets a 3-bit capacitor-DAC trim. Final test sweeps it, and the codes go into a compact on-die OTP array, removing the systematic offset that sets worst-case signal margin.

title: Solar-style layer-transfer wafer reuse to escape quartz crucibles
idea: Borrowing kerfless solar and III-V epitaxial lift-off, grow a thick device-grade epi layer on a porous-silicon release layer over a parent CZ wafer, build the DRAM in the epi, bond to a cheap carrier, and lift off, reusing the parent wafer 10-20 times.

title: Piggyback idle U.S. silicon-carbide EV fabs for wide-bandgap hot DRAM
idea: Borrowing the EV power-electronics supply chain, run SiC MOS-capacitor DRAM cells in underused 200 mm SiC fabs; SiC's 3.3 eV bandgap makes junction leakage ~10 orders of magnitude lower than Si, so retention at 125 C stays seconds-to-hours and the parts are qualified to 10 years at 125 C.

title: Drum memory reborn: stationary disk media scanned by head arrays
idea: Drum memories held bits on a moving magnetic surface under fixed heads. Invert it: existing HDD media sputter lines coat granular CoCrPt on Si, and existing HDD head fabs build 1000-head arrays on a MEMS x-y stage (+-50 um), each head owning a micro-field of media.
note: Millipede-like probe storage; us access, a capacity tier not DRAM.

title: Purdue SiC DRAM revival on U.S. SiC wafers for refresh-free tiers
idea: Revive the 1990s Purdue 6H/4H-SiC DRAM cells, which retained charge for hours at room temperature: build 4H-SiC access transistors and storage capacitors on 200 mm SiC wafers grown in North Carolina and processed in New York SiC fabs, accepting ~90 nm-class geometry for a retention tier that almost never refreshes.

title: Silicon-on-sapphire storage nodes on U.S.-grown sapphire
idea: Revive Autonetics' 1963 silicon-on-sapphire, updated with solid-phase regrowth and laser anneal: build the array on sapphire wafers grown in New Hampshire and Illinois, so storage-node diffusions have no junction to a substrate. The insulating substrate also removes substrate-coupled noise and soft-error charge collection.

title: One base-implant mask revives BiCMOS bipolar sense amps
idea: 1990s BiCMOS DRAMs used bipolar sense amps because Vbe matches to ~1 mV, against ~15 mV of MOS Vt mismatch. Add one p-base implant mask to the periphery flow to form vertical NPNs (the existing n-well as collector, existing n+ as emitter) and place a bipolar differential pre-amp in front of each latch group.
note: Base current drains bitline signal charge, so an MOS input stage is still needed.

title: Setun balanced-ternary charge in 3D cells around the half-VDD plate
idea: Revive the Soviet Setun ternary computer: each 3D cell holds negative, zero or positive charge relative to the existing VDD/2 plate (1.58 bits/cell), read by a two-threshold sense amp; the narrowed margin causes ~1% level confusions, absorbed by a ternary BCH code over GF(3).

title: Widrow memistor revival: electroplated analog weights in solid electrolyte
idea: Revive Bernard Widrow's 1960 memistor, a three-terminal cell that plates copper onto a carbon resistor: use a PFAS-free copper-doped phosphosilicate-glass electrolyte so a separate write terminal plates or strips copper while the read terminal senses resistance. Each cell holds a 6-bit analog weight and multiplies in place.
note: Three-terminal ECRAM is known; write endurance not DRAM-class.

title: Cultured-quartz program revived: fully synthetic silica crucibles from SiCl4
idea: Copy the WWII Signal Corps/Bell Labs move that replaced Brazilian natural quartz with hydrothermally cultured crystal: make the whole Czochralski crucible, not just its inner layer, from flame-hydrolysed synthetic silica soot made from silicon tetrachloride, a by-product of US polysilicon plants.
note: Synthetic silica's lower viscosity at melt temperature risks crucible slumping.

title: Shockley four-layer diode revived as thyristor RAM cell
idea: Revive Shockley's 1956 four-layer diode and the abandoned 2000s T-RAM: a vertical PNPN thyristor with a capacitively coupled gate latches regeneratively and stores a bit without a capacitor, built at 40 nm DUV pitch.
note: T-RAM was commercialized attempt and failed on variability/standby current.

title: Solid-source diffusion and laser melt anneal replace ion implanters
idea: Revive pre-1975 diffusion doping: spin-on or ALD dopant glasses (B, P, As oxides) patterned by the existing masks are driven in by nanosecond green-laser melt anneal, giving abrupt shallow junctions without ion implanters, argon-purged beamlines or xenon flash lamps. Conformal dopant films also dope 3D sidewalls that tilted implants cannot reach.
note: Laser/monolayer doping known; dose control and deep wells limit full implanter replacement.

title: Zuse Z1 mechanical memory reborn as buckled-beam NEMS bits
idea: Revive the Z1's sliding-plate mechanical memory as university-etched buckled Si or SiN nanobeams with two stable positions: reads sense capacitance to a fixed electrode without moving the beam, and electrostatic pulses snap it over on rare writes.

title: Widrow memistor: electroplated analog weights trained in place
idea: Revive Widrow's 1960 memistor, a resistor whose conductance was set by electroplating copper: micro-fabricated three-terminal cells with a solid electrolyte set conductance by gate current, so one analog crossbar both stores and updates weights during training.

title: Cryotron-era cryo pods: LN2-cooled HBM with superconducting YBCO flex links
idea: Revive 1950s-80s cryogenic computing pragmatically: run memory stacks at 77 K in liquid-nitrogen pods (no helium) where DRAM retention rises by orders of magnitude and copper resistance falls ~7x, and connect them to warm compute through YBCO coated-conductor flex cables.

title: Ethernet vampire-tap revival: coupler-tapped multidrop buses restore channel capacity
idea: Like 10BASE5 taps on one coax, hang 4-8 memory modules on a single terminated backplane line through contactless directional couplers instead of stubs, so taps do not reflect and the bus stays clean at high data rates.

title: Analog-computer droop compensation: time-aware sense references for hot memory
idea: Analog computers corrected sample-and-hold capacitors for their known droop by predicting the decay. The controller knows each row's age since restore from the refresh pointer (with a coarse per-subarray flag for recent writes) and reads the die temperature, then lowers the sense reference along the expected decay curve, so a cell that has lost 40% of its charge still reads correctly.
note: Same decay-tracking reference; water claim overreaches.

title: Crowe Cell Revival on SkyWater's U.S. Superconducting Process
idea: Revive J.W. Crowe's 1957 persistent-current cell, a bit stored as a circulating supercurrent in a niobium loop, on the 200 mm niobium superconducting processes already run in U.S. foundries, read by SQUIDs, to build attojoule-access memory banks for cryogenic AI and quantum data centers.

title: Refresh that gives energy back: resonant bitline charge recycling
idea: Inverts 'refresh charge is dumped to ground': during refresh bursts, bitline pairs swing through an on-die LC tank (an integrated inductor shared per bank) so the energy of charging bitlines is stored magnetically and returned on the next row, approximating adiabatic charging; random accesses keep conventional sensing.

title: Chill the memory, not the room: Peltier-pumped DRAM tier
idea: Inverts 'DRAM runs at whatever temperature the package gives it': a thin-film Bi2Te3 thermoelectric layer between the DRAM stack and the logic die pumps heat out of the DRAM dies to hold them ~25 C below the logic; retention roughly doubles per 10 C, so refresh rate drops ~5x.

title: Stepwise adiabatic bitline charging from on-die tank rails
idea: Inverting 'the charge for each bitline swing is thrown away': bitlines are restored in four steps through intermediate rails held by large on-die tank capacitors, which are refilled when bitlines precharge back, so each swing dissipates about 1/N of the usual CV^2/2.

title: Self-timed DRAM bank with replica-bitline completion signals
idea: Inverting 'DRAM runs on worst-case clocked timings': each mat carries a replica bitline that signals when slowest-case sensing has completed, and dual-rail sense outputs drive an asynchronous handshake to the controller, removing the DLL and fixed tRCD/tRP guard bands.

title: Self-restoring floating-body read deletes the write-back path
idea: Inverting 'a read disturbs the cell and needs restore circuitry': floating-body cells are read with drain bias just into impact ionization, so a '1' cell regenerates its own body holes through bipolar gain while a '0' cell stays empty, making every read a self-refresh.

title: Low-barrier volatile MRAM refreshed by stock DRAM periphery
idea: Inverting 'MRAM must be nonvolatile': thin free layers with an energy barrier of ~20-30 kT keep data for ms to seconds and switch with ~10x less current, and the existing DRAM refresh controller periodically re-writes them while TMR sensing reads them.

title: Reusable seed wafer: peel micron DRAM films, skip new ingots
idea: Inverts 'every die consumes a slab of crucible-grown silicon': grow a 5-8 um epitaxial device layer on a porous-silicon release layer on a seed wafer, bond it to a cheap carrier (reclaimed or low-grade wafer), cleave at the porous layer, re-polish the seed and repeat 30-50 times. The DRAM array and periphery only need the top few microns of perfect crystal.

title: Esaki tunnel-diode latch cells in plain silicon
idea: Inverts 'a DRAM bit needs a storage capacitor': pair two degenerately doped silicon tunnel diodes (negative differential resistance) with one access transistor so the storage node sits at one of two stable points held by the NDR valley current, a static cell with no refresh.
note: Tunnel-diode SRAM (TSRAM) published late 1990s; Si peak-valley ratio is weak.

title: Socketed HBM stacks on lithographic microspring arrays
idea: Invert 'memory is soldered permanently next to the GPU': HBM stacks press onto lithographic microspring contact arrays (~40 um pitch) on the interposer under a lid clamp, so stacks are tested in place, swapped on failure and reused in the next accelerator generation.
note: Same reworkable stack socket mechanism via microsprings.

title: In-package mm-wave radio bus replacing interposer wires
idea: Invert 'chiplets must be wired together': each memory and compute chiplet has 200-300 GHz on-chip antennas, the metal lid forms a closed cavity, and links share the medium by frequency division so any memory reaches any compute die without routing.
note: Same lid-cavity 300 GHz antenna mechanism.

title: Mat parity row catches whole-row hammer bursts
idea: Inverts 'each word is corrected independently': every 512-row subarray dedicates one row to the XOR of all its rows, kept current on writes by in-array XOR; a row wiped by a hammer burst or wordline fault is rebuilt from the parity row and its siblings.

title: Analog leaky-bucket capacitor physically caps row activations
idea: Inverts 'hammer defense needs digital counters': each wordline-driver group gets a small capacitor that every activation drains by a fixed packet while a resistor slowly refills it; below threshold the driver triggers neighbor refresh or refuses further ACTs until it recovers.
note: Same leaky charge-bucket counter.

title: Engineered damage sites that getter metals away from cells
idea: Inverts 'defects are always bad': one mask defines implant-damage gettering zones at mat boundaries that pull Fe, Cu and Ni contaminants during later anneals away from storage-node junctions, where they would form generation centers.

title: Crucible-light wafers by reusable porous-silicon layer transfer
idea: Inverts 'every DRAM wafer is a slice of its own crucible-grown ingot': grow 30-50 um device-grade epitaxial silicon on a porous-silicon release layer atop a reusable parent wafer, bond it to a cheap carrier, and reuse the parent 30-50 times.

title: Retention-matched 28 kT magnetic tunnel junction for DRAM duty
idea: Derive the barrier from the job: DRAM data must survive ~1 s, so Delta = ln(1 s / 1 ns) ~ 21 kT plus array/ECC margin ~ 28 kT at 85 C, not the 60 kT used for NVM. Shrink a perpendicular CoFeB/MgO free layer to ~8 nm at Delta ~ 28 kT and add a background read-scrub that rewrites only ECC-flagged flips every ~100 ms.
note: Relaxed-retention STT known; 28 kT gives ~1 s mean life, too many flips for ECC.

title: Strain-switched magnetostrictive nanomagnet driven by sputtered piezo AlScN
idea: A sputtered AlScN piezo layer strains an elliptical FeGa nanomagnet, rotating its easy axis 90 degrees between two states that an MTJ reads. Write energy is the piezo's CV2 at 0.3-0.5 V (~1 aJ), with no current through the magnet and every film deposited at <=350 C.
note: Straintronic switching widely studied; deterministic 180-degree switching remains an issue.

title: Air-spacer drain overlap defuses the GIDL hot spot
idea: GIDL is set by the peak field where the wordline overlaps the storage-node junction, and it scales as exp(-B/F). Replace the gate dielectric in only the last ~5 nm of overlap with a sealed air spacer (k=1). This lowers the overlap field ~3-4x and leaves channel control untouched.

title: Idle-time sense-amp offset self-trim tracks aging in field
idea: Each SA gets a 4-bit current-injection trim; during refresh-idle windows it senses equalized bitlines (zero signal) and binary-searches the trim to null offset, re-running monthly so BTI drift at 125 C is continuously cancelled. Trim codes live in a reserved array row, not fuses.

title: Printed liquid-silane ink laser-crystallized into polysilicon periphery
idea: Print cyclopentasilane ink only for decoder, wordline-driver and sense circuits, convert it to amorphous silicon and excimer-laser crystallize it to ~100 cm^2/Vs polysilicon, while the cell access devices stay wide-gap oxide.

title: Sealed vacuum-gap bitlines let a quarter-sized capacitor suffice
idea: Bitline capacitance is mostly coupling through k~4-7 spacers; vacuum (k=1) gaps made by depositing a sacrificial carbon spacer, sealing it and ashing it out through a porous cap cut CBL ~3-4x, so the same signal needs ~1/4 the cell charge.
note: Air-gap bitline spacers already ship; 3-4x Cb cut and 10x density are overclaims.

title: Exfoliate device layers, reuse the donor wafer fifty times
idea: First principle: a DRAM device needs about 1 um of single-crystal Si, so 99.9% of a 775 um wafer is just a mechanical carrier. Transfer 1 um device layers by hydrogen-implant cleaving or controlled spalling from a premium donor onto handles made of recycled Si, then re-polish and reuse the donor 30-50 times.

title: Shannon-metered inline rANS coding in the memory controller
idea: First principles: a byte of typical server heap carries only ~2-4 bits of Shannon entropy, so storing 8 bits is pure waste. Put a table-driven rANS (asymmetric numeral system) codec in the memory controller, with frequency tables per page class learned online by a sampling engine; 4 KB pages live in variable-size 512 B sub-blocks tracked by a small translation table, and hot lines are cached decompressed.
note: Hardware memory compression well studied; realistic ~1.5x.

title: Vacuum-annulus TSV liners cut via capacitance threefold
idea: TSV capacitance (~30-50 fF) is set by liner permittivity: C ~ 2*pi*eps*L/ln(r2/r1). Deposit a sacrificial carbon liner, fill Cu, then ash the carbon through vent slots to leave a sealed ~200 nm vacuum annulus (k=1) around each via, which also mechanically decouples copper expansion from silicon.

title: Per-row leaky charge-bucket counts activations beside wordline driver
idea: Row hammer is a counting threshold (~1k ACTs). Each ACT dumps a fixed charge packet from the wordline driver onto a tiny per-row floating integrator, which leaks with a time constant equal to the refresh window. When its voltage crosses a comparator level, the neighbor rows are flagged for refresh. The result is an exact per-row analog counter instead of SRAM/CAM tables.
note: Same leaky integrator.

title: Hydrogen backside cooling gives a helium-free fab
idea: Gas-gap conductance in the molecular regime scales roughly with 1/sqrt(molecular mass), and H2's bulk conductivity (0.18 W/m-K) beats helium's (0.15); after accommodation-coefficient correction H2 lands within ~20%. Replace helium in electrostatic-chuck backside cooling and load-lock venting with electrolytic H2 at ~10 Torr in sub-milliliter volumes, diluted below flammability at exhaust.
note: Good gas-gap physics argument; flammability and plasma-chemistry interaction need tool qualification.

title: Molten-salt electrolysis turns sand directly into polysilicon feedstock
idea: The thermodynamic minimum to reduce SiO2 is ~911 kJ/mol, yet carbothermic arc plus Siemens refining spends several times that. Electro-deoxidize SiO2 pellets in molten CaCl2 (FFC-style, ~850 C) to make silicon directly, then zone-refine, using only Si, O, Ca, Cl and C.

title: Light switch: snap-through buckled nanobeam as a bistable bit
idea: Stimulus 'wall light switch' (two detents, no power to hold) -> a 200 nm compressively pre-stressed TiN or SiN beam is buckled up or down over a sense electrode; an electrostatic pulse on the opposite electrode snaps it through, and the up/down position changes cell capacitance ~3x for read. Built-in stress, not charge, holds the state.

title: Pendulum clock: parametron phase bit sustained by one shared pump
idea: Stimulus 'pendulum clock' -> each cell is a GHz nanomechanical or LC resonator pumped parametrically at twice its frequency, so it can only oscillate at phase 0 or pi (Goto's 1950s parametron shrunk to NEMS); one global pump tone sustains every bit at once. Read compares phase with a reference; write injects a small seed signal as the local pump restarts.
note: NTT demonstrated electromechanical parametron memory; density and pump power limit it.

title: Retention passport fused into every die, read by hosts
idea: Random stimulus 'passport': a document that travels with you and gets stamped at each border. Propose a JEDEC field in which each die fuses its per-bank retention class and temperature slope at test; the host reads the passport at boot and sets per-bank refresh, instead of every part inheriting the worst-case 64/32 ms spec.

title: Hibernating-bear wordlines hold their own negative bias, pumps off
idea: Random stimulus 'hibernating bear': store reserves, then shut the metabolism down. On entering deep idle, each wordline is charged to -1 V and its driver disconnects, so the wordline's own capacitance holds the negative bias like a DRAM cell with a slow top-up every few seconds; negative pumps and bias generators power down while access leakage falls ~1000x.

title: Soap-bubble air-gap spacers made by dry polymer decomposition
idea: Random stimulus 'soap bubble': a film that vanishes and leaves only air. Place a sacrificial polynorbornene spacer between the buried-wordline cap and the storage-node contact; after sealing under a porous cap, a 400 C anneal decomposes it to gas, leaving a k=1 air gap with no wet release and no rinse.
note: Same air-gap spacer via polymer decomposition.

title: Ice rink: Josephson comparators sense cryogenic DRAM bitlines
idea: Glide without friction: at 4 K, read DRAM bitlines with Josephson-junction quantum-flux-parametron or SFQ comparators that switch on ~1e-19 J, driving superconducting passive lines to the processor, while the DRAM array runs at ~0.3 V with near-zero leakage and no refresh.

title: Corrugated cardboard: rippled capacitor walls boost electrode area
idea: Corrugation adds surface: during the lateral-capacitor recess in a 3D stack, or the pillar etch in 2D, alternate etch and passivation cycles (Bosch-like scalloping) or a Si/SiGe sub-superlattice with selective recess give the electrode rippled walls before conformal ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN. The cell footprint and the DDR5/HBM interface do not change.
note: Echoes 1990s HSG rugged electrodes; scallops eat space in sub-30 nm holes.

title: Chimney: micro heat-pipe thermal vias let HBM stacks grow taller
idea: A chimney draws heat straight up: etch dummy 10 um vias through the core dies at hotspots, aligned through the stack to the lid, and fill them with sealed two-phase micro heat pipes or a Cu-diamond composite. Bottom dies run 10-15 C cooler, so 16-24-high stacks fit the thermal envelope without changing the HBM interface.

title: Bamboo: NiAl intermetallic bamboo-grain wordlines from abundant metals
idea: Stimulus 'bamboo' (nodes span the full stalk width) -> deposit B2-NiAl into buried-wordline trenches so single grains span the line (bamboo grains), exploiting NiAl's short electron mean free path (~5 nm) so resistivity barely rises at 10 nm widths, and its ~1,640 C melting point to survive the DRAM thermal budget.

title: Pearl: area-selective ALD grows dielectric only inside capacitor holes
idea: Stimulus 'pearl' (nacre grows only around the grit) -> dose a small-molecule inhibitor that blankets top surfaces but cannot diffuse into 60:1 holes, so ZrO2/HfO2 grows only inside; pair with a cold-trap recirculation loop that condenses unreacted metal-amide precursor for reuse.
note: Inhibitor-based area-selective ALD is an active field.

title: Microwave oven: single-wafer microwave annealers replace quartz-tube furnaces
idea: Stimulus 'microwave oven' (heats the food, not the plate) -> a 10-person team builds 2.45/5.8 GHz single-wafer microwave annealers that activate dopants and crystallize dielectrics at 400-500 C by coupling to carriers and dipoles, avoiding batch quartz furnaces.

title: Coral reef: electrolytic bottom-up superfill replaces CVD tungsten wordlines
idea: Random stimulus 'coral' (structures grown by electrochemical accretion from seawater) -> buried wordlines, bitline contacts and landing pads are filled by additive-driven bottom-up electroplating of Ru or Co on a sub-nm seed, the way copper damascene superfill works. This replaces WF6 CVD tungsten fill.

title: Shower head: atmospheric spatial ALD for high-k and electrodes
idea: Random stimulus 'shower head' -> wafers glide under a gas-bearing head with alternating precursor/purge/oxidant slots at atmospheric pressure, so every pass is one ALD cycle with no pump-down. It replaces vacuum batch and single-wafer ALD for the ZrO2/HfO2 capacitor dielectric and TiN electrodes.

title: Zipper: controlled spalling reuses one CZ donor for many device layers
idea: Random stimulus 'zipper' (one crack propagates cleanly) -> a stressed nickel layer is plated on the donor and a crack is propagated at a set depth to peel a few-micron device layer onto a carrier. The donor is re-polished and reused 10-20 times, and the peeled thin layers go straight into HBM stacks without grinding.

title: Sugar cube: water-dissolved sacrificial layer transfers epitaxial perovskite ferroelectric
idea: Random stimulus 'sugar cube' (dissolves in water) -> single-crystal BaTiO3 or PZT-class ferroelectric is grown at high temperature on a reusable SrTiO3 donor over a water-soluble Sr3Al2O6 layer. Dissolving that layer releases the membrane, which is bonded onto finished CMOS at <300 C.

title: Ice-cube tray: compressed lines carry size class inside freed ECC
idea: Each ice-tray slot has a fixed shape: compress every 64 B line into one of four slot classes, and when a line shrinks by at least 4 B write its 2-bit class and slot pointer into the freed bits alongside stronger ECC, so the controller never fetches a separate metadata table; incompressible lines use standard ECC with a flag symbol.
note: Close to COP and Attache compression-ECC co-design.

title: Chameleon skin: lines change encoding instead of location
idea: A chameleon changes colour, not position: rather than migrating cold pages to another device, the controller re-encodes them in place (raw, then light base-delta, then heavy dictionary/entropy) as they cool and returns the slack to a common pool; hot accesses promote them back to raw.
note: Multi-codec compressed tiers like zswap are known.

title: Origami fold: subarray product code repairs whole-row hammer bursts
idea: Fold each subarray into a 2D grid: per-line ECC along rows plus one XOR parity row per 64 rows, kept current on writes via in-DRAM bitwise row operations or buffer-die read-modify-write, so a row riddled with hammer flips is rebuilt from the column parity as an erasure.

title: Nonstick pan: printed barrier coatings let crucibles reuse lower-grade quartz
idea: Random stimulus 'nonstick pan' -> a coating, not the pan, touches the food. Spray/inkjet-printed barium-doped devitrification layers with a Si3N4 inner skin let crucibles made from lower-grade or synthetic quartz survive multiple recharges in continuous CZ.
note: Barium devitrification coatings already known.

title: Snap-through buckled nanobeam: contactless mechanical bistable bit
idea: Box = {medium: up or down buckled shape of a pre-compressed 120 nm SiN/Si nanobeam | access: row/column electrostatic electrodes, no transistor | sense: capacitive gap readout through a shared column amplifier | integration: sealed vacuum-cavity array in BEOL | substrate: Si | fab: sacrificial-oxide release + ALD seal}. Built-in compressive stress pushes the beam past Euler buckling so it has two stable shapes; a 1-2 V pulse snaps it through in ~1 ns (GHz resonance), and it never touches a surface, so there is no stiction or contact wear.
note: Same buckled-beam bit at 120 nm scale; cell larger than DRAM.

title: All-silicon vertical gated thyristor: bistable bit from boron, phosphorus, silicon
idea: Box = {medium: regenerative pnpn latch state | access: the thyristor's own gate | sense: on/off current ~1e5 | integration: vertical 4F2 pillars | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: in-situ doped epitaxy with California boron and U.S. phosphate phosphorus, NiSi contacts from Michigan nickel}. The cell contains only Si, B, P, O, N and Ni, so it needs no capacitor dielectric and no exotic metal.

title: Resonant LC bitline drive recycles refresh energy adiabatically
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x SA swung by a resonant LC tank x in-package spiral inductors per bank x Si x standard. During refresh bursts bitline groups swing through the tank so charge oscillates between groups and inductor instead of being dumped to ground, recovering ~60-80% of CV2.

title: Charge-plasma storage junction: no dopants, no implant damage
idea: Box: cap x access transistor whose storage-side n-region is induced electrostatically by a low-work-function metal contact and a positive fixed-charge dielectric instead of implanted phosphorus x SA x in-array x thin-body Si x ALD. With no metallurgical junction there is no end-of-range damage or dopant cluster to host trap-assisted tunneling.

title: Two-nanometre quantum-confined silicon body widens the access bandgap
idea: Box: cap x <=2.5 nm Si nanosheet access channel x SA x lateral 3D-stackable cell x epitaxial Si/SiGe superlattice x selective SiGe etch. Confinement raises the effective gap ~0.3-0.4 eV, dropping intrinsic carrier density ~100x and band-to-band tunneling sharply, while staying in silicon.

title: Self-aligned dipole layer raises threshold only near storage node
idea: Box: standard cap x buried-channel access with an Al2O3 dipole interlayer added after a partial wordline recess x SA x in-array x Si x recess-deposit-etchback on existing patterns (zero masks). The dipole shifts local Vt ~+0.3 V only in the upper gate segment beside the storage junction, while the lower channel keeps low Vt for drive.
note: Same local Vt shift near storage node via dipole.

title: Triple bitline length to 1536 cells, accept 1% signal failures
idea: Box: standard cap x Si access x standard SA x long-bitline mats x bulk Si x standard. Cut the number of SA stripes ~3x by hanging 1536 cells per bitline; the lower transfer ratio leaves ~1% of weak cells unreadable, and the code absorbs them.
note: A 1% raw BER needs ECC overhead that likely eats the ~10% die saving.

title: Delete redundancy rows, columns and fuse banks; ECC absorbs defects
idea: Box: standard cell x Si access x standard SA x no repair periphery x bulk Si x shorter test flow. Defects and weak cells up to a 1% budget stay in place under the code, so spare rows and columns, redundancy compare logic, laser/e-fuse banks and repair test steps all go.
note: 1% defect budget overwhelms on-die SEC and soft-error margin.

title: Half-volt array: 0.5 V VARY with 1% sensing failures
idea: Box: standard cap x Si access x high-gain SA x low-voltage array domain x bulk Si x standard. Bitline/cell voltage drops from ~1 V to 0.5 V and the wordline from ~3 V to ~2.2 V; the halved signal mis-senses ~1% of bits, which the code repairs.

title: Plate-less floating capacitor between complementary bitlines (2T1C)
idea: [Box: differential floating MIM | two lateral transistors | fully differential SA | lateral 3D tier | Si | ALD] Connect each end of a lateral 3D capacitor through its own access transistor to BL and BLB on opposite sides of the tier, with no common plate; data is the sign of the voltage across the capacitor, so a read gives twice the 1T1C signal from one capacitor and the plate layer disappears from every tier.

title: Two-bit cells in long lateral 3D capacitors via time-to-threshold sensing
idea: [Box: four-level charge | IGZO lateral FET | time-domain SA (bitline crossing timed by per-tier counter) | monolithic 3D | Si | ALD] Lateral capacitors in 3D DRAM can be made long (Cs ~15-20 fF) for little extra cost; spend that charge on four levels and read them by timing when the bitline crosses a single reference.
note: MLC DRAM is old art; leakage erodes four-level margins quickly.

title: CVD diamond interlayers between DRAM tiers to spread heat
idea: [Box: standard cell | any access device | any sensing | wafer stack with 1-2 um polycrystalline diamond bonding layers | Si + diamond | low-temperature diamond growth + through-diamond vias] Insert thin diamond heat spreaders (k ~1000 W/mK) between stacked dies or wafers so hotspots from logic underneath no longer raise local array temperature.
note: Low-temperature polycrystalline diamond has far lower k than bulk; studied for 3D thermal.

title: On-chip MLCC: interleaved deposited electrodes replace deep capacitor etch
idea: [Box: multilayer interdigitated MIM | VCT | charge-share SA | monolithic | Si | blanket ALD/PVD TiN/Ru/ZrO2 multilayer + selective lateral recess] Deposit N alternating TiN and Ru electrode sheets separated by ZrO2, etch one coarse pillar per cell, then selectively recess the Ru from one sidewall and the TiN from the other so storage node and plate interleave like a ceramic MLCC.

title: Area-selective ALD grows landing pads only on contacts
idea: [Box: MIM | VCT | standard SA | monolithic | Si | inhibitor-based area-selective ALD of Ru on TiN, not on SiO2] Replace the overlay-critical landing-pad and storage-contact lithography with bottom-up growth: inhibitor molecules passivate the dielectric, and Ru nucleates only on exposed contacts, self-limiting into mushroom pads.
note: Area-selective Ru ALD is widely pursued; same bottom-up pad core.

title: Porous-silicon lift-off wafers reuse one CZ parent fifty times
idea: Box [standard cell | Si access | voltage SA | thin device film bonded to handle | 30-50 um epi film | anodize + epi + bond + cleave]: anodize a double-porosity release layer on a premium CZ parent, grow device-grade epi from trichlorosilane, bond to a low-grade handle and cleave at the porous layer, then re-anodize the parent and repeat.

title: Indium-free, gallium-free ALD tin-oxide access transistors
idea: Box [stacked MIM cap | 4 nm ALD SnO2 vertical channel TFT | voltage SA | BEOL monolithic 1T1C over CMOS | logic wafer | thermal ALD]: replace IGZO with an ultrathin ALD SnO2 channel whose carrier density is set by oxygen-vacancy control and an O3 post-treatment, giving oxide-class off-current with only tin and oxygen.
note: ALD SnO2 TFTs researched; vacancy control for ultra-low off-current is the open question.

title: Cross-host 64-byte line dedup inside a shared CXL pool
idea: Box: dedup × CXL pool controller × 64 B line × on write × SRAM hash index. The pool controller hashes each incoming line, keeps one physical copy with a refcount, and redirects duplicates through a two-level remap table, so dozens of hosts running the same OS, libraries and model weights share lines across machine boundaries.

title: Charge-sharing pooled reads send sums, not raw bytes
idea: Box: 1T1C x multi-wordline activation x analog charge sharing across N cells digitized by an ADC in the base die x TSV x Si x standard. Activating several cells on one bitline averages their charge into an analog sum the base die digitizes, so pooling, attention accumulation or Bloom-filter reductions ship one value instead of N.

title: Po: the bit is a whirlpool — magnetic vortex-core polarity cells
idea: Po: the bit is a whirlpool. Extracted: in a ~50 nm permalloy disk the magnetization curls into a vortex whose 10 nm core points up or down; a GHz current pulse tuned to that disk's gyrotropic resonance flips only its core, and an MTJ over the core reads it.
note: Resonant vortex-core switching known; frequency-selective shared lines are a mild twist.

title: Po: the bit is one hydrogen away — proton-intercalation conductance cell
idea: Po: the bit is a hydrogen atom that moved next door. Extracted: a 3-terminal cell drives protons from a thin hydrated reservoir (HfO2:H or a solid acid) into a WO3 channel, changing its conductance >100x; the lightest ion moves in ns at ~0.5 V and retention is tuned by the reservoir bias.
note: Protonic ECRAM is widely pursued; hydrogen in CMOS and endurance are risks.

title: Po: memory lives in a freezer — quantum-paraelectric cryogenic capacitor
idea: Po: memory lives in a freezer. Extracted: run memory at 40-77 K, where quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3/KTaO3 films reach permittivity of 1,000+ and access-transistor leakage freezes out; a shallow capacitor then holds more charge than today's 70:1 pillar and retention extends to minutes.

title: Po: memory sold by the kilogram — volumetric electron-trapping crystal
idea: Po: memory sold by the kilogram. Extracted: a cm3 crystal or glass doped with deep electron traps (SrS:Eu,Sm or Ce-doped glass) stores bits as trapped electrons in voxels written by two-photon absorption where beams cross, read by infrared-stimulated luminescence and rewritten to refresh, with zero lithography.
note: Electron-trapping optical memory prior art; storage tier, not byte-addressable DRAM.

title: Decaying reference cells make sense threshold slide with leakage
idea: Po: the reference forgets as fast as the data. Each subarray carries reference cells written to a half level at the same time as the row and sharing its well, so they leak at the same rate; the sense amp compares against this decaying reference instead of a fixed VBL/2, so a decayed 1 still reads correctly long after it crossed the fixed midpoint.

title: Po: the sense amp remembers its offset — AlBN ferroelectric trim
idea: Po: a sense amplifier with memory. One input transistor of each SA gets a thin ferroelectric aluminum boron nitride gate layer; at test the measured offset is cancelled by one program pulse that permanently shifts that transistor's Vt, with no fuses or trim DACs.

title: Po: the row buffer survives power-off — FeB/MgO shadow latches
idea: Po: open rows that survive power-off. Pair each SA with a Co-free FeB/MgO/FeB magnetic tunnel junction shadow latch on Ti/TiN seeds, written as a row closes, so SA and decoder strips can be fully power-gated between bursts and the row buffer restored in nanoseconds on wake.

title: Retention-tail sparing at word granularity in the base die
idea: Po: the weak cells simply don't exist. After stacking, measure every 64-bit word's retention at 95 C over repeated passes, remap the worst ~0.1% (the fA tail plus variable-retention words) to a spare tier through a CAM in the logic base die, so every remaining word retains >10 s and refresh is disabled for shorter-lived data.
note: Known retention-aware sparing; >10 s at 95 C exceeds median retention and VRT undermines it.

title: Po wafers give birth: porous-silicon reusable parent wafer
idea: Po: 'a wafer is a mother that gives birth to daughters.' Extracted: anodize a double-porosity layer on a parent wafer, grow a 20-50 um device-quality epitaxial film on it, build the DRAM, bond to a carrier and split at the weak porous layer; re-polish and reuse the parent 10-20 times.

title: Po tungsten never existed: high-pressure aluminum force-fill plugs
idea: Po: 'tungsten was never discovered.' Extracted: fill all contacts and vias with PVD aluminum forced into the holes at ~700 atm and ~400 C (the mid-1990s force-fill method) over a thin Ti wetting layer, replacing CVD tungsten plugs and the WF6 precursor.
note: Al thermal budget vs later anneals; 20 nm fill.

title: Po one cell holds four voltages: multi-level big-capacitor cells
idea: Po: 'each cell remembers a number, not a bit.' Extracted: use the large storage capacitance practical at 180 nm (30+ fF with trench or HSG capacitors) to store four charge levels (2 bits per cell), read with reference-ladder sense amplifiers and a two-step compare; refresh restores the levels.
note: Multi-level DRAM was tried in the 1990s; margin and retention halve.

title: Maskless interference lithography for perfectly periodic array layers
idea: Po: the pattern needs no mask. Because the cell array is a perfect lattice, expose array layers with multi-beam 193 nm interference that writes line/space or hexagonal hole lattices over a whole field with huge depth of focus, using a conventional scanner only to block out periphery.

title: Edge-face interconnect stacking instead of through-silicon vias
