idea: Use the molecular scale as the lithographer: coat a PS-b-PMMA block copolymer into 180-nm KrF-printed guide trenches and anneal it. It phase-separates into lamellae or cylinders at 12-25 nm pitch, multiplying the guide frequency 8-15x for bitline or hole patterns using only a spin coater, oven and RIE.
note: DSA on guide patterns is widely pursued; 8-15x frequency multiplication and defectivity are the hurdles.

title: Potassium-40 seeds: weights stored as PRNG seeds plus coefficients
idea: K-40's natural decay is randomness for free; each 8x8 weight block is stored as a 16-bit LFSR seed plus four 4-bit coefficients that mix the pseudo-random basis vectors the seed generates, and the accelerator regenerates the basis on the fly with a few gates per lane.

title: Po: memory made of bubble wrap — micro-plasma ferroelectret void bits
idea: Po: memory made of bubble wrap. Extracted: in a roll-to-roll cellular-polymer (ferroelectret) film each closed micro-void is a bit; a field above the Paschen threshold ignites a ns micro-discharge in the void that deposits +/- charge on its walls (an electret dipole lasting years), and the threshold doubles as the crossbar selector.
note: Micro-plasma charging erodes walls; um voids and slow access are not DRAM-class.

title: Ba: barium-titanate acoustic sensors catch stack microcracks early
idea: Bond lead-free BaTiO3 piezo acoustic-emission sensors to HBM/3DS package lids; firmware listens for crack-burst signatures during thermal cycles and pre-emptively migrates data off the affected die and channel before joints open. Off-the-shelf piezo plus a small DSP board.
note: Microbump crack emissions are likely undetectable in noisy servers.

title: LNG terminal cold energy runs fab nitrogen and chillers
idea: Adapted from Japanese LNG import terminals, which use regasification cold (-162 C) to power air separation and cold storage. Site a fab beside a US regas terminal (e.g. Cove Point, Elba Island, Everett) and drive its nitrogen air-separation unit and process chillers from LNG cold through an intermediate loop.

title: Domestic heavy water revived for deuterium-passivated access transistors
idea: Revive the U.S. heavy-water production of the 1950s to supply domestic deuterium for high-pressure D2 anneals of access transistors and buried-wordline interfaces. Si-D bonds resist hot-carrier and wordline-stress depassivation far better than Si-H, so the interface traps behind GIDL and variable retention stay passivated over life.
note: Deuterium is not a chokepoint.

title: Qimonda deep-trench DRAM revived with polysilicon and oxynitride only
idea: Revive the trench-capacitor DRAM abandoned with Qimonda (2009) and IBM eDRAM: deep substrate trenches with doped polysilicon electrodes, an oxide-nitride dielectric and buried-strap access, built on 28-40 nm ArF immersion lines in US foundries.

title: Germanium recovered from Alaskan zinc concentrate and coal fly ash
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ge (32): recover Ge domestically from Red Dog zinc concentrates now shipped abroad and from Ge-rich fly ash via tannin precipitation and solvent extraction, dedicated to SiGe superlattices for 3D DRAM.

title: Molybdenum replaces tungsten in wordline straps and contacts
idea: Substitute tungsten wordline straps and periphery contacts with barrier-thin ALD or sputtered molybdenum, which keeps lower resistivity at narrow widths, so each local wordline driver can serve ~2x more cells.
note: Mo replacement for W is already industry roadmap.

title: Substitute dry coolers and CO2 heat pumps for evaporative towers
idea: Reject fab heat through dry air coolers, and use transcritical CO2 heat pumps to lift low-grade process-cooling heat to 70-90 C for UPW preheat, HVAC reheat and district heating instead of evaporating it in cooling towers.

title: Substitute subtractive-etched aluminum for plated copper damascene layers
idea: Form upper DRAM metal layers by sputtering Al-Cu and patterning with Cl2/BCl3 dry etch, then gap-fill with spin-on low-k, so no electroplating baths, CMP or post-CMP rinses are needed.

title: Substitute hydrogen passivation with deuterium anneal of access transistors
idea: Replace the forming-gas H2 anneal of the array with a high-pressure D2 anneal; Si-D bonds resist hot-carrier and field-driven depassivation, so fewer interface traps are generated over life.
note: Deuterium passivation is long known and used in industry.

title: Steel-mill air separation units retrofitted to capture neon
idea: Ukraine's semiconductor neon came from crude-neon columns on Soviet steel-mill air separation units. Adapt this by bolting crude neon/helium columns onto US integrated-steel and chemical-plant ASUs and purifying the output into excimer laser gas for the DUV ArF/KrF layers that still pattern most of DRAM.

title: Tungsten-free periphery contacts using ALD molybdenum and ruthenium
idea: MINIFY tungsten to zero in SA and decoder contacts and local interconnect by depositing Mo or Ru at <=400 C by ALD/CVD, which also lowers contact resistance at small dimensions.

title: Eliminate copper damascene: subtractive molybdenum array wiring
idea: Pattern bitlines and local interconnect by dry etching a blanket molybdenum film (with self-aligned dry-etched vias) instead of copper electroplating plus CMP, removing plating baths, slurry and post-CMP brush cleans.
note: DRAM bitlines are already subtractive W; subtractive Mo/Ru widely pursued.

title: Mold compound becomes the substrate, deleting ABF and T-glass
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: embed LPDDR/DRAM dies face-down in a reconstituted epoxy-mold wafer and build the redistribution layers directly on it (fan-out wafer-level packaging). Each die nests inside its own package body, so neither organic build-up laminate (Ajinomoto ABF) nor low-CTE T-glass cloth (Nittobo) is needed.

title: Boron-free, low-alpha die stack cuts soft errors at source
idea: Worse: keep borophosphosilicate glass and boron-doped films whose B-10 captures thermal neutrons and fires alpha particles into tiny cells. Flip: build the back-end with B-free dielectrics (P-doped or undoped SiO2, SiOC) and purified low-alpha Al and Si in packaging, so weak small-Cs cells meet soft-error targets without extra ECC.
note: BPSG B-10 soft-error problem identified and removed by industry in the late 1990s.

title: H: deuterium-steam gate oxides quiet sense-amp telegraph noise
idea: Grow SA and decoder gate oxides in D2O steam and anneal in D2 so interface traps are capped by deuterium, which resists hot-carrier depassivation, lowering random telegraph noise and Vt drift that force SA oversizing; no rare gases are used.
note: Deuterium anneals are long-established practice.

title: Self-repairing TSV mesh with spare vias and in-stack switches
idea: Rule: interconnect failures must heal in the field. Stacks include ~10% spare TSVs plus tiny per-die crossbar switches. In-field BIST detects TSVs degrading from electromigration or cracking and reroutes their signals to spares without removing the stack.

title: Room-temperature single-electron electrometers read 300-electron cells
idea: MINIFY the stored charge 100x: sub-2 nm metal or Si-nanocrystal single-electron transistors gate-coupled to short local bitlines sense ~50 aC (about 300 electrons), so the storage capacitor shrinks to ~0.05 fF and the tall pillar disappears.
note: With 300 electrons, fA-level leakage empties the cell within one refresh window; SET uniformity is unproven.

title: Hundred-electron storage nodes read by single-electron electrometers
idea: Box [medium: ~100-electron Si quantum-dot node | access: Si nanowire gate | sense: single-electron transistor electrometer | integration: monolithic | substrate: SOI | fab: e-beam or DSA]. Each bit is ~100 electrons sensed by a capacitively coupled SET that resolves single electrons, stored as 3-way repetition with Poisson-aware soft decoding that treats leakage as counting noise.
note: 100-electron node leaks out in microseconds at fA leakage; room-temperature SET variability and offset charge unsolved since 1990s.

title: 2050 atom engineer: dangling-bond charge pairs on hydrogenated silicon
idea: An engineer in 2050 writes memory with atoms. Hydrogen-desorption lithography creates paired silicon dangling bonds 0.8 nm apart on H:Si(100); one excess electron sits on either the left or the right bond, giving an atomic-scale charge-position bit that a buried charge sensor reads.
note: Atomic density if works; electron in symmetric DB pair hops fast, and wafer-scale STM lithography absent.

title: 16-level DRAM via segmented-bitline capacitive-DAC successive approximation
idea: Failure mined: the 1990s multi-level DRAMs from Toshiba and NEC died because splitting ~150 mV into many levels destroyed margin and their staircase sensing was slow. Fix: split each bitline into binary-weighted segments that double as the capacitor DAC of a 4-step successive-approximation sense, trimmed per subarray against a stored reference charge, with one SAR comparator shared by 4 bitlines.
note: 16 levels means ~10 mV spacing; Cs spread and leakage drift swamp it, and the 10x math assumes a 4F2 cell too.

title: H: hydrogen-lithographed silicon dangling-bond pairs hold single-electron bits
idea: On an H-terminated Si(100) surface, remove single hydrogen atoms to leave paired dangling bonds that share one extra electron on either side; the electron's side is the bit, set by local gates, and ~1% thermally hopped pairs per refresh window are corrected.
note: Same DB-pair mechanism; room-temperature retention and addressing unresolved.

title: Substitute EUV projection optics with X-ray proximity printing from storage rings
idea: A compact electron storage ring feeds 12-16 soft-X-ray (~1 nm) beamlines, each exposing wafers through a 1x membrane mask held 5-10 um away; there are no mirrors to build, and the dense periodic array tolerates 1x masks written by e-beam.

title: Substitute tin-plasma EUV sources with one shared free-electron laser
idea: A single energy-recovery-linac FEL (~10 kW at 13.5 nm) is split to feed 10-20 scanners in a DRAM fab, replacing per-scanner laser-produced tin-plasma sources that waste >99% of their drive-laser power.

title: Array wafers from one US fab, periphery wafers from another, bonded
idea: Split DRAM across domestic fabs: array-only wafers (capacitors, access devices, few metals) at a US DRAM fab, periphery CMOS on depreciated 28-45 nm US logic/analog lines (e.g., TI Lehi, the former 3D XPoint fab), fused by wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding on US soil.

title: Convert idle 3D NAND toolsets into vertical-bitline 3D DRAM lines
idea: Combine the 3D NAND toolset (staircase, channel-hole etch, replacement gate) with a vertical-bitline, horizontal-capacitor 3D DRAM whose steps map one-to-one onto NAND tools: the alternating stack becomes Si/SiGe or oxide-semiconductor layers, the channel hole becomes the bitline hole, and gate replacement becomes capacitor replacement.

title: Magnify cell to 16F2 at F=40nm, magnify tiers to 120
idea: Deliberately enlarge the cell to 16F2 at a 40 nm half-pitch printable with dry ArF (no immersion, no EUV), then make it up in height by stacking 120 deposition-defined lateral-cell tiers, where each tier needs no new critical mask because only the deposition loop repeats. 16F2 at 40 nm is about 25,600 nm2 per tier, so 120 tiers gives roughly 4x the bit density of 6F2 at 12 nm.
note: Relaxed-pitch many-tier lateral DRAM is the mainstream 3D DRAM premise; needs a fab.

title: One sense-amp layer serves every tier via vertical bitlines
idea: Rearrange the scaling direction: in monolithic 3D DRAM grown with U.S.-built deposition and etch tools (no EUV), bitlines run vertically through N tiers to a single SA layer below, chosen by tier-select transistors, so periphery stays constant while bits grow N-fold.

title: One free-electron laser feeds a whole fab of scanners
idea: Inverts 'every scanner carries its own plasma light source'. Build a ~10 kW energy-recovery-linac FEL in the fab basement and split its EUV beam to 8-12 source-less scanners.

title: Convert depreciated 3D NAND lines into stacked-DRAM tier fabs
idea: From a first-principles count of process steps, a 3D DRAM tier stack is mostly deposition, high-aspect-ratio etch and replacement-metal steps, the same tool mix as 3D NAND; retrofit NAND lines idled by oversupply with DRAM-specific modules (capacitor dielectric, anneal) instead of building greenfield fabs.

title: Lending library: used-DUV-only DRAM fab wins density by stacking
idea: Random stimulus 'library' (reuse old books) -> a U.S. fab is built from refurbished ArF immersion scanners and depreciated etch/dep tools at F~18-20 nm using SAQP. The lost density is recovered with a 4F2 vertical-channel cell plus two hybrid-bonded array layers, so the fab needs zero EUV.

title: Lighthouse: one free-electron-laser EUV source shared by many scanners
idea: Random stimulus 'lighthouse' (one beam serves many ships) -> a U.S.-built energy-recovery-linac free-electron laser produces ~10 kW of EUV and splits it among 10-20 scanner bodies, replacing per-scanner tin-plasma sources with their CO2 drive lasers.

title: Single-exposure ArF array, density made up by tier count
idea: [Box: lateral 1T1C | IGZO | standard SA | monolithic 3D | Si | single-exposure ArF immersion only (>=38 nm half-pitch), no multipatterning] Freeze lateral pitch at what one ArF immersion exposure can print and make tier count the only scaling knob, co-designing a wide-pitch cell (longer lateral capacitor, relaxed contacts) so mask count stays almost flat from 32 to 200 tiers.

title: Convert 3D NAND lines into 3D DRAM lines sharing tool sets
idea: [Box: plate-stack 3D DRAM | IGZO or poly-Si | CMOS-under-array | 3D-NAND-style stacking | Si | existing NAND high-AR etch, replacement-gate and staircase tools] Design the 3D DRAM flow around 3D NAND tool recipes and contract NAND makers' underused EUV-free lines, swinging capacity between NAND and DRAM as prices move.
note: Leveraging NAND tooling for 3D DRAM is widely discussed; needs a fab and a working 3D cell.

title: Convert DRAM capacitor-module tool bays into capacitorless 3D tiers
idea: Po: the fab throws away its capacitor tools. In an existing DRAM fab, retire the high-aspect-ratio capacitor etch, high-k and TiN modules and reuse the bays for stacked capacitorless floating-body tiers built from epitaxial Si/SiGe superlattices, leaving the periphery line unchanged.

title: One accelerator-driven EUV light source feeds a dozen scanners
idea: Po: the scanner has no light of its own. A free-electron laser producing ~10 kW at 13.5 nm distributes light by beamlines to 10-20 scanner bodies, replacing a tin-droplet plasma source in every tool.

title: Freeze the lithography roadmap; scale only by vertical tiers
idea: Worse: retire scanners at every node and buy new ones. Flip: commit to a 10-year litho-frozen DRAM roadmap at a fixed F~16-18 nm, with all density gains from deposition/etch tier stacking, so the scanner fleet fully depreciates and serves 3-4 generations.

title: One accelerator, many printers: shared U.S. free-electron-laser EUV
idea: Jump the light source from tool scale to building scale: one U.S.-built energy-recovery free-electron laser (national-lab heritage) feeds multi-kW EUV through beamlines to 10-20 simple exposure stations that print only the periodic array by reflective interference, avoiding imported projection optics.

title: Thulium solid-state laser to drive EUV tin plasma, ending helium
idea: Scale shift from a multi-stage CO2 gas-laser amplifier chain to a compact diode-pumped Tm:YLF slab laser (the big-aperture thulium concept) that drives the tin plasma. CO2 lasers run on a He/N2/CO2 gas mix; the solid-state laser and the hydrogen buffer need no rare gas.
note: LLNL big-aperture thulium concept already pursued; laser dev far beyond $1M.

title: Si: unsawn wafer-scale DRAM bonded to wafer-scale compute
idea: Skip dicing: bond a whole DRAM wafer face-to-face to a whole logic wafer with reticle-stitched routing and a boot-time defect map that routes around bad DRAM dies, so die yield becomes capacity rather than scrap and no packages, interposers or TSVs exist.

title: Free-electron-laser EUV source feeds a whole fab of scanners
idea: Ideal: EUV photons as cheap as DUV. Closest: one energy-recovery-linac free-electron laser produces multi-kW EUV, split by grazing-incidence optics to 10-20 scanners, replacing per-tool tin-droplet plasma sources.

title: Vinyl-record stampers: nanoimprint replicates DRAM array layers without EUV
idea: Record and CD plants electroform nickel mother and stamper replicas from a single master. E-beam write one master per periodic DRAM array layer (honeycomb storage-node holes, bitline/wordline gratings), replicate hundreds of daughter templates, and pattern those layers by jet-and-flash nanoimprint at ~20 nm half-pitch.

title: Thin-tunnel charge-trap 3D NOR DRAM built in idle NAND fabs
idea: Box: nitride-trapped charge behind a 1.5-2 nm tunnel oxide x vertical poly-Si channel in parallel NOR strings x current sensing x 200+ word-plane stack x Si x existing 3D NAND toolset. The thin tunnel oxide trades retention (seconds) for 10-50 ns writes, refreshed like DRAM, while NOR wiring gives random access; staircase, channel-hole and replacement-gate modules are reused unchanged.
note: Essentially Sunrise Memory's 3D NOR quasi-volatile memory.

title: Po chips stamped like coins: nanoimprint for cell-array layers
idea: Po: 'memory is minted like coins.' Extracted: use step-and-repeat nanoimprint with replica templates for the highly regular cell-array layers (bitlines, storage-node contacts) and keep DUV for periphery; the imprint tool uses a small fraction of an EUV scanner's power and no tin or hydrogen plasma.

title: Z-RAM refresh eliminated by buried-well BJT feedback bistable bodies
idea: Z-RAM failed partly because floating-body charge leaked out in milliseconds and needed refresh. Fix: add a buried n-well beneath each floating body so the parasitic vertical BJT continuously replenishes holes by impact ionization when the body is charged and stays off when empty (Zeno-style bistable floating body), latching both states statically.
note: This is essentially Zeno Semiconductor's bi-stable floating body.

title: Resonant-tunneling diode pair makes each storage node self-restoring
idea: Effect: negative differential resistance in resonant tunneling. Each storage node is tied to a series pair of Si/SiGe RTDs stacked above the capacitor (a Goto pair), creating two stable node voltages; leakage only nudges the node and the NDR latch pulls it back, so data holds with no periodic refresh while a sub-pA standby current flows.

title: Wavelength-coded optical row decoding with microring drop filters
idea: Substitute the electrical row decoder tree with wavelength selection: an on-die SiN waveguide carries one of N laser lines, a microring drop filter tuned to each row group routes it to a photodiode, and the photodiode triggers that group's local wordline driver. The address is the wavelength.
note: Wavelength-addressed rows are novel but lasers and ring tuning cost more than decoders save.

title: Piezoelectric liner strains the access channel during retention
idea: Wrap the buried wordline in an AlScN piezoelectric liner on a separate standby bias. While rows retain, the liner compresses the channel and strain raises Vt; strain is released for access.
note: Thin AlScN liner gives small strain; 50-100 mV Vt shift doubtful.

title: Bitline as LC resonator read by frequency-division multiplexing
idea: Make each segmented bitline part of an LC tank (top-metal spiral over the array plus bitline capacitance) with its own resonant frequency; the cell charge shifts a varactor-loaded resonance, and one wideband RF receiver per mat reads 16 bitlines at once by FDM, replacing 16 pitch-matched latch sense amps. This combines RF filter-bank receivers with DRAM sensing.

title: Diversity-pair cell: two capacitors with uncorrelated leakage physics
idea: Combine N-version design diversity with the cell: each bit is held by a silicon-access cell plus an oxide-semiconductor-access cell stacked above it, whose dominant leakage paths (junction GIDL vs. oxide trap-assisted) are uncorrelated; the pair is read as a charge sum, so a tail event in one device rarely coincides with one in the other.
note: Charge-sum read halves signal when one device leaks; doubles cell area.

title: Plasma-display wall-charge memory with global sustain self-refresh
idea: Adapt AC plasma panels, whose cells remember via wall charge: store the bit as charge on a dielectric wall across a 10 nm vacuum nanogap; a chip-wide AC sustain pulse makes only charged cells field-emit and re-deposit their charge, so refresh needs no row activation or sense amps.
note: Plasma-panel global sustain refresh is fresh; nanogap emission reliability doubtful.

title: Nanopore-sequencer molecular tape with rewritable monomer charge
idea: Adapt Oxford Nanopore sequencing: a charged polymer shuttles back and forth through a solid-state nanopore; a write electrode oxidizes or reduces ferrocene side groups as they pass, and the pore current reads them back.

title: Power-MOSFET superjunction pillars inside the vertical access transistor
idea: Adapted from the superjunction in high-voltage power MOSFETs: build the vertical-channel access device with alternating thin p and n columns, charge-balanced so they fully deplete sideways. This flattens the electric-field peak at the drain/storage-node edge where band-to-band tunneling (GIDL) originates.
note: Charge balance impossible with few dopants in ~10 nm pillars.

title: MicroLED mass transfer of GaN-HEMT periphery chiplets onto glass
idea: Borrowed from microLED mass transfer: GaN HEMT sense-amp and driver chiplets (~50 um) are grown on sapphire, laser-lifted off and stamped thousands per second onto IGZO cell arrays on glass, then wired with panel metal.

title: Minify dark carriers: light-gated photoconductive access switches
idea: Use a wide-bandgap photoconductor strip (amorphous GaN or ZnS, dark resistivity >1e14 ohm-cm) as each access switch, turned on by an on-chip waveguide routing 365 nm light to the selected row through micro-ring selectors; in the dark it is an insulator and there is no wordline to charge.
note: Waveguide pitch and photoconductor speed far exceed DRAM cell pitch and ns timing.

title: Goto-pair tunnel-diode latch as two-terminal sense amplifier
idea: Revive the 1959 Goto pair: two ALD MIM resonant-tunneling (negative-differential-resistance) diodes in series form a bistable node; the bitline nudges the midpoint and a clock pulse latches it, MINIFYING the SA to two diodes plus one access TFT, all <=300 C.

title: Minify breakdown damage: self-clearing film capacitors burn off own faults
idea: Borrow the self-healing of metallized-film capacitors: build cell capacitors on a polymer-film or glass substrate with ~20 nm Al electrodes. A local dielectric breakdown vaporizes the electrode around the spot, isolating the short, so the cell loses ~1% of its capacitance instead of shorting its bitline.
note: Film-cap self-healing at 20 nm electrodes in high-aspect pillars is unproven.

title: Eliminate static storage: recirculating magnon delay-line loops hold bits in flight
idea: Eliminate the stationary storage element: bits circulate as spin-wave packets (wavelength ~50-100 nm) in 100-um closed YIG or CoFeB waveguide rings, with one magnetoelectric transducer per ring that regenerates and taps the stream. A ring holds ~1-2 kbit with ~50 ns average latency; storage is travel time, not a held state.
note: Spin-wave damping in CMOS-compatible films and transducer inefficiency; density ~10x below DRAM.

title: Eliminate the switched-capacitor charge pump: on-die piezoelectric AlN transformer
idea: Replace each bank's VPP pump with a solidly mounted Rosen-type AlN piezoelectric transformer (~200 um, ~25 MHz resonance) that steps 1.1 V up to ~3 V at ~80% efficiency into a diode rectifier. AlN is sputtered and etched with Cl2/BCl3, and its Mo electrodes with Cl2/O2, with no release etch.
note: AlN piezo transformer on DRAM die is novel; acoustic isolation and area hard.

title: Eliminate the zero-defect assumption: defect-tolerant arrays allow fewer rinses
idea: Design mats with fine-grained remapping and per-mat ECC so random particle and metal defects cost capacity rather than dies, then run the fab with far fewer UPW rinse cycles and recycled rinse water, trading 1-3% capacity for yield-insensitive processing.

title: Analog pass-through: multilevel NV cells drive PAM4 lanes directly
idea: Eliminate digitization and re-encoding between cell and wire: a 2-bit/cell FeFET array is sensed into four voltage levels that are buffered straight onto a PAM4 lane through an analog mux, and the receiver's slicer performs the only quantization.
note: Noise margins of FeFET levels driven straight onto PAM4 lanes are doubtful.

title: Optical wordlines: photoconductor-gated storage nodes, no access transistor
idea: Reverse the wordline's role from voltage to light: each storage capacitor reaches its bitline through a nanoscale amorphous-selenium/chalcogenide photoconductor (dark resistivity >1e14 ohm-cm), and a row is selected by a ~1 ns light pulse in a SiN waveguide running under it. In the dark the node is isolated by an insulator rather than a leaky transistor.
note: Waveguide pitch per row kills density; photoconductor speed and dark current at nm scale uncertain.

title: Telescoping nanotube bit: storage as superlubric shell position
idea: Rearrange the bit into geometry: the inner shell of a double-wall carbon nanotube slides in or out of its outer shell (a wear-free superlubric van der Waals bearing) between two electrostatic detents; in the out position it tunnels to a contact, so read is current on/off and write is a ns electrostatic pull.
note: Deterministic DWNT placement and detent engineering are unsolved.

title: Reverse-graded threshold tiers replace the 3D staircase
idea: Each tier gets two series n-type select transistors whose thresholds are graded in opposite directions across the stack (set by deposition recipe per tier, no mask). Driving pillar A to Vt_j+d and pillar B to Vt'_j+d leaves only tier j with both transistors conducting: a window decoder. The only added mask is the two select-pillar holes.

title: Shared plate line reads a row's popcount as a checksum
idea: Reverse plate and bitline roles for detection: the plate electrode of each row segment (TiN from TiCl4) is sensed during activation, and its displacement charge is proportional to the number of charged cells, giving an analog popcount compared against a stored count to flag flips without per-word parity bits.
note: Displacement charge signal tiny against large plate parasitics.

title: Peel-and-relaminate van der Waals storage film on a reusable CMOS base
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells + #34 Discarding and recovering: build the bit-storing layer (hBN/MoS2 gain-cell or capacitor film) as a vdW stack held only by van der Waals forces and edge contacts to pads on a finished CMOS periphery wafer. When cells wear out, or a better storage film appears, the stack is peeled with thermal-release tape and a fresh one laminated. Repairable by design: the storage element is the swappable consumable.
note: Peel/relaminate with aligned contacts at nm pitch is doubtful; DRAM cells do not wear out.

title: Lattice-matched GaP pocket on the storage side kills band-to-band tunnelling
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: the access transistor needs a high bandgap only where it leaks, not where it drives. Selectively grow a lattice-matched GaP pocket (Eg 2.26 eV, ~0.4% mismatch to Si) on just the storage-node side of the recessed channel; band-to-band tunnelling falls roughly exponentially with Eg^1.5 while the Si bitline side keeps full drive.

title: Parametron cells: pumped phase-encoded bits that never need refresh
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action: replace static charge with a sustained oscillation. Each cell is a tiny resonator built around a nonlinear (antiferroelectric) varactor, pumped at 2f from a shared plate line; parametric bistability locks it into one of two oscillation phases (0 or pi) that store the bit, and the pump continuously replaces what leakage removes.
note: Nanoscale electrical LC Q is tiny; continuous pump power likely exceeds refresh.

title: Chromatophore stretch-read: MEMS capacitor plate pulled away before sensing
idea: Cephalopod chromatophores change size because muscles stretch a pigment sac. Here the storage capacitor's top plate is a nanomembrane, and just before read an actuation electrode pulls it away from the node. With charge Q fixed, cutting C by 5x raises the node voltage 5x (V=Q/C), so a tiny low-AR capacitor gives a full-size sense signal.
note: Bitline signal is ~Q/Cbl; shrinking Cs at read boosts node voltage but barely raises transferred signal.

title: Tree-ring rolled memory: spiral-wound foil with metallized edge contacts
idea: A tree adds one ring a year. Oxide-TFT memory film is deposited roll-to-roll on stainless-steel or polyimide foil, wound into a cylinder like a film capacitor, and its bus lines end at one edge that is metal-sprayed (Schoop process) to form thousands of axial contacts to a controller cap.
note: A Schoop-sprayed edge shorts the bus lines; R2R density is low.

title: Weather vane rotors: dipolar molecular rotors locked in crystalline cages
idea: Amphidynamic crystals and MOFs hold polar rotors (e.g., difluorophenylene on a rigid axle) that point like weather vanes; engineer a two-fold rotational potential with ~0.8-1.0 eV barrier, grow an oriented 10-nm MOF film as the cell dielectric, and switch rotor orientation with a field pulse so the net polarization shifts a readout capacitance or channel threshold.

title: Woven wordlines zig-zag between tier pairs like weft threads
idea: Treat wordlines as weft threads: each lateral wordline hops between tier k and k+1 every 32 cells through short vias while its partner runs in the opposite phase, so a raised wordline opens a checkerboard row spanning both tiers. Address logic maps it as one logical row, so one staircase contact serves two tiers and systematic tier-thickness variation averages out.
note: Per-32-cell inter-tier vias in lateral stacks add huge process complexity.

title: Seismograph sensor measuring actual substrate disturbance, not activation counts
idea: Seismographs measure real ground motion rather than predicting it. Each subarray gets a well-tap sense resistor and an integrator that measures the minority-carrier/substrate charge actually injected by wordline toggling and long row-open times. When the integrated charge near a region passes a calibrated fraction of Cs*dV, targeted refresh fires.

title: Selectron revival: secondary-emission bistable islands held by a flood beam
idea: RCA's 1948 Selectron kept each bit static because a floating eyelet sat at either cathode or collector potential, self-reinforced by secondary-emission yield above or below 1 under a holding flood. Build a nano-vacuum layer over an array of 30-nm floating metal islands with an on-chip planar flood emitter; islands are bistable at two potentials, written by pulsed X/Y control gates and read capacitively through a buried sense electrode.
note: Nano-vacuum sealing, emitter stability and low-energy secondary yield at 30 nm unproven.

title: Ferreed crosspoint revived: nanomagnet-latched NEMS contact as the bit
idea: Bell's 1960 ferreed latched a reed contact with a remanent magnet. Shrink it to a 100-nm NEMS cantilever with a CoPt hard-magnet tip that latches onto a soft-magnetic pad when the pad is magnetized parallel and springs open when antiparallel; a current-strap pulse flips the pad to write, and contact conduction (on/off >1e8) reads.

title: Twistor-inspired spiral-ribbon channel for a long, compact access transistor
idea: Borrow Bell Labs' twistor, a helical magnetic tape wound on a wire: grow the access-transistor channel as a helical silicon or oxide-semiconductor ribbon spiralling up a dielectric core inside a 4F2 pillar, with the wordline filling the spiral gap as the gate. Two to three turns give an effective channel length 5-8x the pillar height with no extra footprint.
note: Helical ribbon channel multiplies Lg in a 4F2 pillar; fabricating spirals at ~20 nm is the miracle.

title: Acoustic charge transport conveyor for refresh, revived from delay lines
idea: Revive mercury and magnetostrictive delay-line memory, together with 1980s acoustic charge transport: a surface acoustic wave launched across a piezoelectric overlayer carries charge packets from storage wells down a column to one regenerating amplifier and back. Refresh becomes continuous recirculation through one amplifier per column instead of row activations.

title: Ferreed-style latching microswitches for zero-standby bank gating
idea: Bell System's 1960 ferreed crosspoint used remanent magnetization to latch a reed contact, so it held its state with zero power. Build BEOL electrostatic microcontacts clamped closed by HZO remanent polarization, and use them to disconnect idle banks' periphery from the supply and to steer spare rows, with no holding power and no leakage when open.

title: Bonded bit-planes sharing one base-die row decoder, core-stack style
idea: Treat each hybrid-bonded DRAM array die like a core-memory bit plane: dies are thinned to ~5 um and carry sub-micron through-die vias at mat edges so one row decoder/driver on the base logic die drives the same wordline in all 16 planes, while each plane delivers one bit slice of the word. Array dies keep only cells and sense amps.
note: Sub-wordline drivers must stay local; per-wordline through-die vias are infeasible at cell pitch.

title: Selectron-style binary grid stack decodes electrons without transistors
idea: Revive RCA's 1946 Selectron, which steered electrons to one storage eyelet by combinations of voltages on crossed grid bars: stack log2(N) thin perforated electrode sheets over a planar cold cathode so each sheet blocks half the windows and only the coded window passes current to its storage pad. Twenty sheets pick one of ~1M pads with 20 drivers.

title: Bubble-memory rotating field shifts data through stacks without wires
idea: As bubble memory moved every bubble with one rotating in-plane field, wrap a two-phase package coil around a stack of dies carrying permalloy T-bar/chevron domain-propagation tracks, so one resonant global field shifts data from every tier toward a port die at once, crossing tiers by magnetostatic coupling through thin bond layers.
note: Cross-tier magnetostatic coupling and MHz shift rates make bandwidth implausible.

title: Williams-tube revival: electron beams cross a vacuum gap between dies
idea: Revive the CRT storage tube's beam principle with on-chip field-emitter arrays (Spindt or CNT tips) on the memory die firing modulated electron beams across a sealed 5-20 um vacuum gap onto collector pads on the facing logic die, with no metallurgical bond.
note: Chip-scale vacuum sealing and emitter lifetime are speculative.

title: Ferroelastic twin-variant bits read through strain-gated 2D channels
idea: Invert 'a bit is held as electrical or magnetic order' -> hold it as a crystal's shape. A ferroelastic film has two twin variants with orthogonal spontaneous strain; a piezoelectric AlN micro-actuator under each cell toggles the variant, and the strain state is read by the mobility shift of a 2D-semiconductor channel laminated on top.
note: Nanoscale piezo actuation and twin-wall pinning highly speculative.

title: Surface acoustic wave pulses select rows of magnetostrictive bits
idea: Inverting 'rows are selected by wires carrying current': a SAW transducer launches a strain pulse timed to reach the target row of magnetostrictive nanomagnets, lowering their barrier so a weak shared field line writes only that row, while reads use local MTJs.

title: Charge-trap odometer counts each row's activations
idea: Inverts 'activation counting is digital bookkeeping': the single added mask places a trap-rich dielectric under a tiny gate at each wordline end so every activation injects a small charge; during refresh the odometer's threshold shift is sensed to flag hammered rows, then erased.
note: Novel analog per-row odometer; trap charge variability and erase cycling are doubts.

title: Light-addressed foil cells: optical row strobes replace wordline drivers
idea: Give each printed cell an access TFT whose gate is charged by a small printed photodiode, and address rows by flashing a micro-LED line array beneath the transparent foil, so no metal wordline or high-voltage driver exists.
note: Printed photodiodes switching in ~10 ns and optical crosstalk through the foil are the doubts.

title: In-package deuterium reservoir re-passivates retention-tail traps in field
idea: Tail cells trace to single Si dangling-bond traps whose emission is exponential in field, and Si-D bonds resist depassivation ~10x better than Si-H. A Ti/Pd deuteride film in the package releases D2 during a 150 C self-anneal mode, which starts when the ECC-logged weak-cell count passes a threshold.
note: D2 must reach buried interfaces through dense BEOL at 150 C; diffusion doubtful.

title: Chessboard: alternating NMOS and PMOS access rows neutralize row hammer
idea: Black and white squares alternate: alternate n-channel and p-channel access transistors (storing opposite logic polarity) row by row, so an aggressor's wordline swings opposite to its neighbors' turn-on polarity. Its capacitive kick pushes the victims further off, and the electron-injection mechanism behind hammer flips works against p-type neighbors.
note: Alternating n/p wells between rows at DRAM pitch is infeasible in bulk Si.

title: Zipper: sidewall hybrid bonds join DRAM and logic edge-to-edge
idea: Random word 'zipper' forced onto die edges: plasma-diced DRAM and logic dies get interdigitated comb-shaped sidewalls carrying Cu/oxide pads, then they are pushed together laterally and annealed so the teeth hybrid-bond like a zipper. Side-by-side dies then talk through edge bonds less than 100 um long, with no interposer and no silicon bridge.
note: Edge area limits pad count and lateral hybrid-bond alignment is unproven.

title: Lizard tail autotomy: self-clearing electrodes isolate capacitor breakdown spots
idea: A lizard sheds its tail to survive: borrowing metallized-film-capacitor self-healing, the top electrode includes a 2-3 nm resistive, easily oxidized layer that clears locally around a breakdown filament, so the cell loses a sliver of area instead of shorting to the plate.
note: fJ-scale cell energy may not clear a filament; novel transfer from film capacitors.

title: Ferroelastic remanent-strain bit read by piezoresistive silicon nanowire
idea: Box = {medium: one of two remanent strain states from non-180-degree ferroelastic switching in a relaxor-PT film | access: Si FET | sense: piezoresistive Si nanowire under the film (gauge factor ~100+) | integration: BEOL with the nanowire channel below | substrate: Si | fab: sputter + rapid thermal anneal}. The bit is stored as lattice strain, not charge, and the nanowire's resistance differs by several percent between the two states; the read does not disturb the domains.
note: Few-percent piezoresistive signal and ferroelastic fatigue are doubts.

title: In-field wordline self-heating anneal heals variable-retention traps
idea: Box: standard cell x access transistor used as its own heater via ms high-current wordline pulses during idle x SA retention self-test x in-mat x Si x zero masks. Local ~200-300C channel micro-anneals relax metastable trap configurations behind variable retention time, then a self-test confirms the row.
note: Local 200-300C via wordline pulses risks damage; VRT healing uncertain.

title: Electro-optic imaging maps every cell's retention at wafer sort
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: standard | sense: optical, via removable electro-optic polymer film | integration: wafer-level test | substrate: bulk | fab: temporary spin-on film]. At sort a removable Pockels-effect film over the array is imaged with polarized light while cells decay, capturing every cell's leakage curve in seconds; the per-die map is fused on chip to drive repair and per-row refresh classes.
note: Storage nodes sit under BEOL metal; field imaging through stack doubtful.

title: Bistable NEMS beam tier quarantines hammer-hot rows
idea: Box [medium: bistable buckled nanobeam | access: electrostatic actuation | sense: capacitive position | integration: BEOL MEMS above array | substrate: bulk | fab: sacrificial-release MEMS]. A small on-die tier of mechanically latched cells, which hold no disturbable charge and do not leak, receives rows the controller flags as hammered or leaky until they cool.
note: NEMS switching speed and endurance doubtful for a DRAM-rate tier.

title: Po: the wordlines are made of sound — acoustic coincidence-addressed array
idea: Po: the wordlines are made of sound. Extracted: replace row and column drivers with two edge transducers launching surface-acoustic-wave pulses across a piezoelectric-semiconductor film; only where two pulses cross does the summed strain lower a storage node's barrier enough to exchange charge with a blanket electrode, selecting one cell by time of flight.

title: Memory rationing by merit: domestic DRAM goes to efficient workloads
idea: Po: memory is rationed like wartime sugar. Under Defense Production Act priority authority, domestic DRAM output and federal cloud memory go first to workloads certified on a public bytes-per-unit-work benchmark (GB per 1k inferences, per query), with tiers reset yearly.
note: Novel policy lever, but US domestic DRAM output is tiny and politically implausible.

title: Online CVD on hot float-glass ribbon deposits memory blanket layers
idea: Worse: deposit every blanket film in a $5M vacuum chamber, one substrate at a time. Flip: as float glass leaves the tin bath at ~600 C, apply atmospheric online CVD (already used for pyrolytic low-E coatings) to lay down barrier, bottom-electrode and oxide-semiconductor blanket layers at kilometers per day, then cut panels for patterning.
note: Sodium and film purity off a tin bath are far from device-grade.

title: Selector-only memory fills TSV keep-out and PHY back-end areas
idea: Worsen: leave TSV keep-out zones and the space above PHYs as dead silicon. Flip: build stacked layers of chalcogenide selector-only memory (threshold set by write polarity, one two-terminal device per bit) in the BEOL above these regions, adding cross-point bits on area that today stores nothing.
note: Selector-only memory is TRL-2; endurance far below DRAM and keep-out zones exist for stress reasons.

title: Ferroelectric ZnMgO shadow parity protects rows during long refresh gaps
idea: Worse: lean on Hf-based ferroelectrics, or just refresh harder, to guard idle data. Flip: add a small nonvolatile parity array of wurtzite ferroelectric Zn1-xMgxO (all abundant) per bank holding XOR parity of each row group; when relaxed refresh lets a row decay, its data is rebuilt from parity, and parity is rewritten rarely so ferroelectric endurance is enough.

title: Organ builder's tuned pipes: frequency-addressed tier selection
idea: An organ selects a pipe by its pitch. Give each tier a thin-film bulk-acoustic resonator whose frequency is set by that tier's own film thickness. One shared RF tier bus carries a tone, and only the matching tier's resonator rectifies it to turn on its select gates.

title: Venus alien: SiC CMOS base die and memory PHY
idea: For a Venusian 125 C is cold: build the HBM base die and PHY in SiC CMOS (developed for 500 C Venus probes), whose 3.3 eV bandgap keeps leakage negligible at 125 C and whose ~370 W/mK conductivity spreads heat away from the DRAM layers.
note: SiC CMOS is micron-scale and slow; cannot run HBM PHY speeds.

title: Frequency-tuned resonators select mats instead of decoder wiring
idea: Shift the address from space to frequency: each mat's local wordline-driver enable is gated by a micron-scale AlN film-bulk acoustic resonator tuned to a unique GHz tone, and one shared RF line selects a mat by broadcasting its tone; only a short local decoder picks the row inside the mat. Predecoders and the global address bus collapse into one line plus a frequency synthesizer.
note: FBARs are far larger than micron scale; per-mat resonators cost more area than the 3-6% decoder savings.

title: Sense amps that self-trim offset over months via charge trapping
idea: Time jump from nanoseconds to months: each SA input transistor carries a nitride charge-trap spacer, and whenever on-die ECC corrects an error on that SA's column a micro-pulse traps a little charge to null the offset, so offsets anneal toward zero over field life and track aging.

title: Refresh-as-scanner computing row fingerprints for free
idea: This adds zero masks. Every row is already sensed once per 32-64 ms refresh, so a tiny CRC unit at the sense-amp edge folds each refreshed row into a signature table. That gives the OS a continuously updated map of duplicate and zero rows. The DRAM's own refresh rhythm becomes the dedup scan cycle.

title: Williams tube's ghost: vacuum-nanogap access switch for temperature-proof retention
idea: Tube memories died from heaters, size and drift, but vacuum isolates charge perfectly. Gate each storage node with a 10-20 nm vacuum-gap field-emission switch carved in the BEOL and sealed at wafer level: its off-current is Fowler-Nordheim tunneling, essentially temperature-independent, not thermionic or generation leakage, so the femtoamp tail does not grow at 125 C.
note: FN off-current is near zero but on-state needs very high fields; niche high-temperature benefit.

title: ReRAM endurance failure fixed: strippable, re-coatable consumable memory layer
idea: ReRAM and PCM never replaced DRAM partly because the switching film wears out. Put the switching film as the top BEOL layer over a permanent CMOS base die, designed so a depot can plasma-strip and redeposit it. A worn die is then remanufactured instead of scrapped.
note: Depackaging and refab reprocessing likely cost more than new dies.

title: Williams tube on glass: field-emitter arrays read and refresh charge dots
idea: The Williams tube stored bits as charge spots on a CRT face and died on drift, bulk and constant regeneration; Candescent's field-emission display died on vacuum spacers and panel cost. Fuse them: a thin vacuum-sealed glass panel where gated carbon or Mo emitter arrays address an opposing grid of dielectric charge dots, reading by secondary-emission current and regenerating each frame.
note: Field-emission Williams tube on glass is novel; vacuum panel cost and drift are severe.

title: HPE memristor, fixed: stochastic switching as probabilistic optimizer counters
idea: HPE's memristor died because its stochastic, variable switching made it unreliable storage. Turn the flaw into the feature: store Adam moments as Morris-style probabilistic counters in memristor crossbars, where each pulse switches a cell with a known probability, giving unbiased stochastic rounding for free.
note: Signed EMA moments do not fit monotonic counters; 8-bit Adam already cuts state.

title: Core memory's ferrite returns: transformer-coupled power through the stack
idea: Magnetic core memory died of hand-threaded cores, but its ferrites are cheap Earth-abundant flux guides. Spin-spray-plate thin-film MnZn-ferrite cores through ~30 um holes in each thinned DRAM die, with a primary winding in the base die and secondary spirals on each tier, and transfer power magnetically at ~50-100 MHz so power TSVs and their keep-out zones disappear; paired with contactless data links, the stack becomes TSV-free.
note: MnZn ferrite lossy at 50-100 MHz; still needs through-die holes.

title: DX-centre persistent photoconductivity: light writes, lattice barrier holds
idea: Effect walk: photoconductivity with large lattice relaxation. A waveguide photon pulse ionizes DX-type deep donors in a channel (AlGaAs:Si-like centres re-engineered in a wide-gap host with a >=0.9 eV capture barrier) into shallow donors, raising conductance; the configurational barrier keeps electrons free, and a hot-electron gate pulse recaptures them to reset.
note: Needs a new host with room-temperature DX barrier.

title: Acoustic-resonator frequency-division addressing replaces global predecoder buses
idea: Effect: mechanical (BAW/contour-mode) resonance. Give each subarray block an AlScN resonator tuned to a unique frequency (e.g., 64 tones from 1.0-2.6 GHz); the controller sends a tone burst on one shared line, and only the block whose resonator rings up past threshold enables its local wordline drivers. The address travels as a frequency instead of over dozens of routed wires.
note: Needs high-Q AlScN resonators per block and fast ring-up; saves only global wires.

title: Wavelength-addressed photoconductive wordlines through vertical light pipes
idea: Photoconductivity: SiN waveguides thread vertically through the 3D stack, and each tier taps them with a micro-ring drop filter tuned to that tier's wavelength. The dropped light switches photoconductive a-Si/IGZO access channels in place of gate metal. Choosing a wavelength picks the tier, and choosing a waveguide picks the row.
note: Micro-rings per tier kill density; photoconductive oxide channels are slow.

title: Electrochromic tiers with plasmonic readout for read-mostly AI weights
idea: Electrochromism: WO3 nanocells, colored or bleached by proton intercalation, keep their state with no power. Each cell sits on a plasmonic nanoantenna whose resonance shift a bonded photodiode array reads optically, a whole page in parallel. Writes are slow (µs) but reads are fast, which suits model weights that are written rarely.

title: Piezoacoustic recirculating delay loops stream decode weights, skipping DRAM
idea: LLM decode reads every weight in the same fixed order each token, so a bank of GHz LiNbO3 bulk-acoustic delay loops on the interposer holds weight shards as circulating phonon pulses. The pulses are re-amplified each lap and timed to arrive exactly when the systolic array needs them. Piezo transducers convert bits to acoustic packets at ~10 Gb/s per loop, and thousands of loops form a sequential 'weight carousel'.
note: GHz LiNbO3 acoustic loss and transducer energy per lap; kb-scale per loop limits value.

title: Charge sharing rebuilds rows from a base row plus deltas
idea: Store groups of similar rows (neighboring embedding vectors, image tiles) as one full-precision base row plus low-bit delta rows. On read, the subarray opens the base and delta rows together onto shared bitlines with binary-weighted capacitive coupling, so charge redistribution adds them in analog before sensing. Decompression happens inside the mat with no logic.
note: Doubt: analog charge sum of base+delta rows needs multi-level sensing/ADC, not a standard sense amp.

title: Microheater-gated zirconia ionic memory hosts shared read-mostly pages
idea: Store deduplicated read-only pages (shared libraries, model weights, map tiles) in yttria-stabilized zirconia cells. Their oxygen-ion motion is frozen at 125 C but fast at ~400 C, so writes use a local microheater pulse and the hot ambient cannot disturb the data. Reads are fast and resistive.
note: 400 C microheaters in BEOL raise thermal crosstalk and energy; dedup claim is a separate effect.

title: Thermal hysteresis: NiTi shape-memory microcontacts make HBM stacks reworkable
idea: Replace permanent microbumps with NiTi micro-springs that clamp pads at operating temperature and release when the stack is heated through the austenite transition, so one failed DRAM die in a 12-high stack is lifted out and replaced instead of scrapping the stack and its GPU.
note: NiTi springs at ~20 um pitch with stable contact resistance across thousands of TSV-scale joints is doubtful.

title: Electrowetting liquid metal: Galinstan microchannel vias are stress-free and reconfigurable
idea: Fill vertical microchannels with gallium-alloy liquid metal instead of solid Cu, removing CTE stress and keep-out zones; electrowetting electrodes along spare channels move metal plugs to connect or disconnect lanes, giving in-field lane repair.
note: Ga embrittlement and electrowetting reliability in micro-vias are severe unknowns.

title: Acousto-optics: Bragg-cell beam steering time-shares one optical link across memories
idea: A surface-acoustic-wave acousto-optic deflector on a lithium niobate interposer steers a host's free-space beam among 32 memory chiplets in ~100 ns by changing the RF drive frequency, forming a solid-state switched memory fabric with no electrical crossbar.

title: Fe: bacteria-grown greigite magnetosomes self-assemble into magnetic bit arrays
idea: Harvest near-monodisperse 40-80 nm Fe3S4 (greigite) magnetosomes from magnetotactic bacteria and dock them by magnetic self-assembly into a pre-patterned spin-orbit-torque crossbar, one particle per site; the ~1% of sites left empty or doubly filled are mapped out as erasures.
note: Docking accuracy and SOT read speed on 40-80 nm particles make DRAM-class use doubtful.

title: Fe: electroplated permalloy domain-wall counters track row activations
idea: Electroplate Ni-Fe nanowire loops (no argon PVD) as magnetic domain-wall counters, as in multi-turn rotation sensors, per row group; each ACT current pulse advances a wall one notch by spin-transfer, and an anisotropic-magnetoresistance stripe flags when a threshold notch is reached.

title: Vanadium dioxide graded-threshold switches replace the tier staircase
idea: Run one shared vertical select pillar per block through all tiers with a VO2 insulator-metal-transition switch at each tier junction, its thickness graded so switching voltage steps ~0.15 V per tier; ramping this pillar against a counter-pillar opens exactly one tier using two contacts instead of 32.
note: VO2 is metallic above ~68 C and thresholds vary; 0.15 V per-tier discrimination is doubtful.

title: Ge-Sn: group-IV emitters beam data vertically through HBM dies
idea: Grow GeSn light emitters at ~2 um wavelength (where silicon is transparent) and matching GeSn photodiodes on each core die so bit lanes pass optically straight through the thinned stack, dropping signal TSVs; the base die converts to the unchanged HBM interface.
note: Room-temperature GeSn emitters remain inefficient; optical through-silicon links unlikely to beat TSV energy.

title: H: hydride reservoir re-passivates hammer-aged access transistors in field
idea: Deposit a Pd-capped TiHx hydride strip in the BEOL over each bank, above a window in the SiN hydrogen barrier. A controller-scheduled maintenance pulse from on-die poly heaters (~250 C for seconds, bank taken offline) releases atomic hydrogen that diffuses to the recess-gate Si/SiO2 interface and re-caps dangling bonds created by hot-carrier and hammer stress.

title: N: nitride charge-trap sliver as per-row analog hammer dosimeter
idea: A thin SiN charge-trap strip (SONOS-like) under a dummy gate coupled to each wordline receives a small, repeatable charge injection on every activation, so its Vt shift integrates activation count non-volatilely; refresh logic compares it to a threshold, refreshes the neighbors and erases the strip.

title: V: VO2 phase-change thermal integrator flags hammered subarrays
idea: A doped VO2 sliver (insulator-metal transition tuned near 70 C) is thermally coupled to each subarray's local wordline driver; sustained high activation rates heat it through the transition, its resistance drop trips a sense line that forces targeted neighbor refresh, while normal traffic never heats it enough.

title: Crimped weft capacitors: weave 3D DRAM's lateral capacitors over posts
idea: Borrow the crimp of woven cloth. In a stacked 3D DRAM tier, the horizontal capacitor is coated like a yarn (Ru core, HZO/ZrO2 sheath, TiN outer shell) and snakes over and under a comb of sacrificial vertical 'warp' posts that are removed afterward. The crimped path packs 1.3-1.6x more electrode length into the same tier footprint.
note: Novel weave geometry but only ~1.5x Cs and very hard lateral processing.

title: Die-cast gallium droplet bit: liquid metal shuttles between two wells
idea: Borrow metal casting. A ~10 nm Ga-alloy droplet is sealed in a dumbbell-shaped nano-cavity, and electrocapillary pulses move it from one lobe to the other, where surface tension holds it (bistable). A sense electrode reads the position as a capacitance change.
note: Ga oxide skin and 10 nm droplet electrocapillary control are doubtful.

title: Zone-refined access pillars sweep deep-trap metals into a sacrificial cap
idea: Borrow ingot zone refining: scan a nanosecond-laser molten zone up each vertical access-transistor pillar topped with a sacrificial a-Si cap, so Fe/Cu/Ni deep-level impurities (segregation coefficient k<<1) ride the melt front into the cap, which CMP then removes.

title: Parking-garage helicoid tiers via rotating glancing-angle deposition
idea: Thread-rolling and helical-ramp analogy: deposit the tier stack as one continuous helicoid ramp around a central pillar by glancing-angle deposition while rotating and slowly tilting the wafer, so each tier is one turn of a ramp and all tiers are reachable from the ramp edge without a staircase etch.
note: GLAD films are porous; a continuous helicoid does not give electrically isolated tiers.

title: Lost-wax cast aluminum wordlines replace CVD tungsten
idea: Like investment casting: fill buried-wordline trenches with a carbon 'wax' placeholder through all high-temperature steps, burn it out with an oxygen-radical ash, then squeeze-cast molten Al-Si-Sc alloy into the voids at ~600 C and high pressure over the TiN gate liner and planarize.
note: Squeeze-casting molten Al into ~10 nm trenches fights wetting and capillarity at nanoscale.

title: Printed molecular-rotor framework where dipolar guests store the bit
idea: IFR: a crystal of identical, frictionless dipole switches. Closest achievable: print a metal-organic framework film whose pores hold polar rotor molecules that align up or down under a field and stay pinned by tuned ~0.8 eV rotational barriers, read as polarization charge.
note: Polarization charge from rotors likely too small to sense.

title: HBM buyback harvests base dies and good DRAM layers
idea: Ideal result: every die returns to service. Vendors pay a deposit-refund on HBM-equipped modules; returned stacks with reversible bonds are disassembled, dies retested, and good DRAM layers restacked onto new base dies.
note: HBM bonds are not reversible; debonding thinned dies is hard.

title: Two-device sense amp: Esaki tunnel-diode Goto pair latch
idea: Limit: a sense amp may contain only two devices. Use a series pair of Si/SiGe Esaki tunnel diodes (a 1960s Goto pair) whose N-shaped I-V gives the shared node two stable points; a clocked bias ramp drives the node through its unstable point, and the +/-50 mV bitline nudge decides which stable state it falls into within ~50 ps.

title: Pyroelectric read: wordline heat pulse makes polarization announce itself
idea: Constraint: non-volatile, and the read must not flip domains. A ~1 ns current pulse through a resistive wordline strap heats one row of ferroelectric capacitors by ~10 K; each cell emits a pyroelectric current whose sign matches its polarization, and charge integrators on the bitlines read it without ever crossing the coercive field.
note: Pyro charge at 10 K is ~tens of electrons per cell; far below sensing floor.

title: Newspaper memory: reprint embedding-table snapshot daily on microdot film
idea: Constraint (printable/roll-to-roll): each night a maskless electrohydrodynamic-jet printer writes the recommender's long-tail embedding rows as ~2 um microdots on PET sheets, read by lenslet-coupled CMOS image sensors. By day DRAM holds only hot rows plus a delta log of updates since the print, and yesterday's sheet is recycled.
note: Daily printed optical snapshot; read latency and printer throughput are doubts.

title: Printed antifuse golden-page library for hardware dedup
idea: Constraint (printable/roll-to-roll): a cheap printed one-time-programmable antifuse sheet is burned at rack install with the fleet's most common read-only pages (kernel text, glibc, Python runtime, base container layers). Memory controllers map any matching page to the printed copy and keep only a small DRAM/SRAM cache of its hottest lines to hide the slow printed reads.
note: Printed antifuse density is orders too low to hold GBs of golden pages; reads too slow.

title: Million-lane printed scanner sheet filters cold data in place
idea: Constraint (printable/roll-to-roll): the design trades area for speed: a square-meter printed sheet carries a million slow (~1 MHz) oxide-TFT comparators, each scanning its own patch of co-printed cold storage, for ~10^12 comparisons per second in aggregate. Filters and counts over cold datasets run in place, and only matches move into DRAM.
note: Co-printed cold storage cannot hold TB datasets at printed densities; scanning idea sound, substrate not.

title: Roll memory like a film capacitor with sprayed end contacts
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. Transfer DRAM device films onto a 10 um polyimide ribbon whose bus lines all exit at the two ribbon edges, wind it into a tight cylinder like a metallized-film capacitor, and arc-spray (Schoop) metal end caps that tie every turn's edge lines to power and a radial data comb.
note: Footprint density is not cost/bit; transferred thin-film DRAM retention and roll contacts unproven.

title: Latent TSV stubs let retired DDR dies become HBM stacks
idea: Rule: every die must have a higher-value second life. DDR dies are designed with TSV keep-out zones and buried, unrevealed TSV stubs. Retired dies are thinned, revealed and stacked into low-cost HBM-like stacks for second-life inference memory.
note: Burdens all dies; retired DDR I/O unsuitable for HBM.

title: Altermagnetic tunnel-junction RAM: MRAM without stray fields
idea: The free layer is an altermagnet (RuO2, CrSb, MnTe or newer candidates) whose Neel vector sets spin-dependent tunnelling through an MgO-type barrier to a reference electrode. Writing uses spin-splitter or spin-orbit torque from an adjacent line, or the altermagnet's own current-induced torque; reading uses TMR. Zero net moment removes dipolar coupling to neighbours and to external fields, so crosspoint pitch can drop from ~2.5 to ~1.5 diameters, and exchange-enhanced switching could reach ps timescales. Endurance is magnetic, with no wear mechanism.

title: Swap solid dielectric for superionic RbAg4I5 electric-double-layer storage node
idea: Fill the storage node with a room-temperature superionic conductor (RbAg4I5, ~0.3 S/cm) against an ion-blocking electrode. The bit is held as a sub-nm Helmholtz double layer (~10-20 uF/cm2), and the high ionic conductivity keeps the RC charging time near ~10 ns at nanoscale.
note: RbAg4I5 Ag contamination and moisture instability in CMOS.

title: Swap oxide ferroelectric for vapor-deposited molecular ferroelectric croconic acid
idea: Use a proton-tautomerism organic ferroelectric (croconic acid, Pr ~20 uC/cm2, or DIPAB) evaporated onto the cap electrode at <150 C. It switches by proton transfer, not oxygen-vacancy motion, so HZO's vacancy-driven wake-up and fatigue are absent.
note: Croconic acid thin films have lower Pr and thermal stability concerns; still capacitor FeRAM.

title: Swap charge for ferroelastic twin variant read by piezoresistance
idea: Store the bit as which of two ferroelastic twin orientations a nanocrystal adopts (for example tetragonal-twin BiFeO3 or a NiTi martensite nanopillar). A strain pulse from an integrated AlN piezo layer switches it, and the read uses the anisotropic piezoresistance of an underlying channel.
note: AlN piezo strain likely too weak to switch twin variants.

title: Swap tungsten/platinum spin-orbit layer for chiral-molecule spin filter
idea: Write a nanomagnet bit by chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS): a self-assembled monolayer of helical molecules (helicenes or alpha-helix peptides) spin-polarizes the write current, replacing heavy-metal W/Pt/Ta spin-orbit-torque layers.
note: CISS magnitude in solid-state devices remains contested.

title: Replace amorphous oxide liners with epitaxial CaF2 crystalline insulator
idea: Substitute the amorphous SiO2/SiN gate insulator and isolation liner around the access channel with epitaxial CaF2 (0.6% lattice mismatch to Si) grown by MBE on Si {111} facets. A crystalline insulator has orders of magnitude fewer border traps than an amorphous oxide.
note: CaF2 epitaxy needs Si(111) and MBE; conformal growth in DRAM trenches unlikely.

title: Resonant LC energy recovery for bitline precharge and restore
idea: Substitute dissipative CMOS precharge and restore with adiabatic swing: banks of bitlines are switched onto an in-package inductor so their charge rings sinusoidally between two bank groups instead of being dumped to ground and recharged from VDD.
note: In-package inductor timing and switch losses at ns cycles.

title: Dithered minimum-size comparator triplets replace large matched sense pairs
idea: Substitute one large, carefully matched sense pair with three minimum-size comparators per bitline pair, each fed an independent small dither offset, followed by a 3-input majority gate before the restore latch fires. Random offsets average instead of being sized away.
note: At equal area, one larger matched pair beats a majority of three min-size comparators.

title: Self-referenced two-pulse sensing eliminates reference bitlines
idea: Substitute the external reference (dummy cell or VDD/2 twin bitline) with the cell itself: read once, inject a known small charge step into the same cell, read again, and let the sign of the difference give the data. This is the self-reference trick from MRAM applied to DRAM.
note: A linear capacitor gives no data-dependent difference after charge injection, unlike MRAM.

title: Goto-pair Esaki tunnel-diode latch as sense amplifier
idea: Substitute the cross-coupled inverter latch with a Goto pair: two series Esaki tunnel diodes whose negative differential resistance forms a bistable node that the bitline signal tips one way. Degenerately doped Si or uni-MBE InGaAs junctions are within university reach.
note: Si Esaki PVCR and peak-current uniformity; Goto pairs never scaled.

title: Sputtered NbO2 Mott threshold switch as sense comparator
idea: Substitute the transistor comparator with a two-terminal NbO2 insulator-metal-transition device biased just below its threshold: bitline signal above the reference triggers abrupt (~ns) conduction that sets the restore driver. Reactive sputtering and e-beam pillars suffice.

title: Analog-voltage address bus with per-row window comparators
idea: Substitute the binary multi-wire address bus with two analog address lines (row-group and row-within-group voltages); each wordline driver carries a resistor-ladder window comparator that fires only when both voltages land in its window, which is coincidence decoding in the analog domain.
note: Window comparators cannot resolve ~1000 analog levels in the noise.

title: Selective SiGe oxidation converts sacrificial tiers into stacked buried oxides
idea: Substitute etch-and-fill tier isolation with in-place conversion: oxidize a Si/SiGe superlattice from its slit sidewalls at 750-850 C, where SiGe oxidizes 5-20x faster than Si, so each SiGe tier becomes buried insulator and the stack becomes multi-tier SOI; a thin Si:C barrier on each Si tier blocks rejected Ge from the channels.

title: Substitute self-passivating MAX-phase conductor for tungsten bitlines and barriers
idea: Sputter Ti3AlC2/Ti2AlC nanolaminate bitlines and crystallize by laser anneal; aluminum in the lattice self-forms a ~1 nm Al2O3 sidewall skin that acts as liner and diffusion barrier, removing separate TiN barriers and WF6 chemistry.
note: MAX phases need high crystallization temperature; thin-film resistivity unproven at scale.

title: Substitute tin-catalyzed grown nanowires for etched storage pillars
idea: Grow vertical, heavily doped silicon nanowires by vapor-liquid-solid growth from tin catalyst dots (not gold, which kills carrier lifetime) placed on each storage-node contact, then coat with high-k and TiN to form capacitors bottom-up.

title: Substitute manganese-aluminum and oxidized copper for platinum-group MRAM layers
idea: Build spin-orbit-torque memory from a perpendicular tau-MnAl free layer, an oxidized-copper (CuOx) spin-current source and a Mg-Al-O tunnel barrier, eliminating Pt, Ir, Ru, Ta and W from the stack.

title: Substitute NMOS access with PMOS access to blunt hammer charge injection
idea: Swap electron-carrier access transistors for hole-carrier (PMOS) ones in the array; holes have lower trap-assisted injection and weaker GIDL, so both the leakage tail and hammer-induced charge migration may shrink, at some cost in drive current.
note: Hole-transport hammer hypothesis speculative; drive current loss hurts density.

title: Substitute silicon DRAM in edge devices with roll-to-roll foil memory
idea: Swap silicon DRAM in IoT, wearables and appliance controllers for oxide gain-cell memory made on polyimide foil by roll-to-roll sputter/ALD lines at <=300 C, freeing silicon bits for servers.

title: Vacuum nanochannel field-emission valve as cell access device
idea: Fuse vacuum-tube electronics with the DRAM cell: each storage node reaches the bitline through a sealed 10-20 nm vacuum gap between a sharp emitter tip and a collector, gated by a ring electrode. Below the field-emission threshold no carrier exists in the gap, so the node cannot leak; raising the gate field emits electrons for ns-speed write and read.
note: Per-cell emitter uniformity and stability, plus low emission current for ns writes.

title: Idle bitlines parked at the subarray's majority stored level
idea: Write logic keeps a per-row inversion flag so most cells in a subarray hold the same level. In idle, bitlines park at that rail instead of VDD/2, so majority cells see Vds~0 and subthreshold current, proportional to 1-exp(-Vds/kT), collapses.
note: Minority cells see full VDD drain bias, worsening the tail that sets refresh.

title: NEMS relay latch inside the sub-wordline driver
idea: Replace the sub-wordline driver's level shifter and pull-down with a nanoelectromechanical relay whose mechanical hysteresis both latches the wordline state and gives true zero off-leakage; low-voltage decode pulls it in and it switches the 3 V VPP line directly.

title: Polycrystalline diamond bond layer doubles as interlayer heat spreader
idea: Combine bonding dielectric and heat spreader: grow ~1 um CVD diamond (US-built reactors, methane/hydrogen feedstock) on DRAM wafers, polish it, and use it as the bond layer between a hot logic die and DRAM tiers so hotspots spread laterally before reaching the cells.
note: CVD diamond temperatures exceed DRAM capacitor budget; 1 um film spreads little laterally.

title: Area-selective ALD self-aligns storage-node landing pads, deleting masks
idea: Combine area-selective deposition with the landing-pad step: inhibitor molecules adsorb on dielectric but not on contact plugs, so Mo/TiN grows only on plugs and mushrooms into self-aligned landing pads on US ALD tools, removing the landing-pad lithography.
note: Landing pad offsets BC grid to SN hex grid; mushroom growth cannot shift position and shorts at pitch.

title: Molybdenum wordlines double as in-field annealing heaters
idea: Combine the wordline with a micro-heater: during maintenance windows, pulse current through domestic Mo buried wordlines (replacing Chinese tungsten) to Joule-heat a mat to ~250 C for milliseconds to seconds, annealing hydrogen-related interface traps behind variable-retention-time leakage and weak cells.
note: 250 C likely too low to anneal H-related traps; neighbor stress.

title: Self-barrier CuMn bitline merges conductor and diffusion barrier
idea: Combine the bitline conductor and its TiN/WSix barrier into one Cu-0.5%Mn alloy fill; a post-fill anneal drives Mn to the dielectric interface where it forms a ~2 nm MnSiOx barrier in situ, replacing the W/TiN bitline stack (later capacitor anneals capped below ~500 C).
note: Cu in DRAM front-end and the <500 C cap clash with capacitor thermal budget.

title: Replacement buried wordline: sacrificial poly early, aluminum fill late
idea: Combine logic's replacement-metal-gate flow with the buried wordline: a sacrificial poly-Si plug sits in the trench through the hot activation steps, then is removed and the trench filled with Al-Cu by low-temperature CVD, with all later steps (low-temp ALD capacitor) kept <=450 C.

title: Gray-tone mask and dual-tone resist merge two EUV layers
idea: Combine two critical layers in one EUV exposure: a gray-tone mask (partial-transmission absorber) gives two dose levels that a dual-tone resist resolves into two solubility states, developed sequentially (positive, then negative) into two stacked hardmasks; this removes a mask rather than adding one.

title: Reusable silicon-nitride crucible supplies the wafer's nitrogen doping
idea: Combine crucible and dopant source (zero masks): a dense, non-wetting Si3N4 crucible is reused across 10-50 melts, and its slow dissolution supplies the 1e14-1e15 cm-3 nitrogen DRAM wafers already need for void control, with oxygen added by gas.

title: Liquid-metal microchannel interconnects for reworkable memory-on-logic stacks
idea: Combine microfluidic channels with interconnect: a thin glass spacer with fiber-laser-drilled holes filled with gallium-indium eutectic sits between electroless Ni-P/Au barrier pads on memory and logic, so joints form at room temperature without plasma or bonding gases and a memory die can be removed and replaced.
note: Ga alloys with Au/Ni-P over time; pitch and reliability doubtful.

title: Flash-style detrap pulses heal variable-retention-time cells in field
idea: Combine NAND erase-style detrapping with DRAM self-refresh: during idle, access transistors get brief negative-gate and reverse-junction bias pulses that empty the oxide/junction traps behind random-telegraph leakage, pushing VRT cells back into their low-leak state.

title: Wordline doubles as heater for periodic in-situ trap annealing
idea: Combine Joule microheaters with the array wordlines: in maintenance windows, after data is moved to another subarray, current through Mo or TiN wordline segments heats the local array to ~200-300 C for microseconds to milliseconds, annealing hydrogen-related and interface traps that create leakage tails. Buildable in a university nanofab: patterned Mo/TiN lines over IGZO or Si TFT arrays.

title: Photochromic-lens diarylethene switched electrically as the storage molecule
idea: Adapt Transitions-lens photochromics: diarylethene molecules ring-close or ring-open on a redox pulse, changing conductance ~100x; a monolayer between nanogap electrodes stores the bit as molecular conformation.

title: LCD panel laser repair: spot-anneal the retention-tail cells
idea: Adapted from the laser repair stations that fix defective TFT pixels in LCD fabs: after retention test, or at a refurbisher, a nanosecond laser heats ~1 um spots containing weak cells through a thinned backside in forming gas, annealing the traps that cause their leakage.

title: Railway wheel re-profiling: per-cell charge injection retunes leaky transistors
idea: Adapted from underfloor wheel lathes that re-profile train wheels without removing them: for each cell flagged as leaky, a high-field write sequence injects charge into that access transistor's drain-side spacer, relieving its gate-edge field or raising its local threshold until leakage meets spec; it can be repeated in the field.
note: Uncontrolled spacer charge injection may damage oxide and lose charge at 85 C.

title: Telephone-exchange relay logic rebuilt with NEMS relays on glass
idea: Borrowed from relay telephone exchanges, rebuilt with nano-electromechanical relays (metal beam, air gap) made on glass: decoder trees and mat power gates use relays with zero off-current, switched one cycle ahead because addresses arrive early.

title: Display-fab turnkey lines for U.S. memory periphery
idea: Borrowed from the solar and display industries' turnkey-line model: buy standard Gen-6 glass toolsets (flat-panel i-line steppers, PECVD, sputter) and run memory panels with relaxed 1-2 um periphery rules, since glass area costs ~100x less than wafer area, sited in the U.S. within ~18-24 months.
note: 1-2 um periphery rules inflate area far more than glass saves per m2.

title: Charlieplexed wordlines with thin-film bidirectional selectors
idea: Borrowed from LED charlieplexing: wordlines are selected by ordered pairs of N driver lines through back-to-back oxide Schottky-diode selectors on glass, so N drivers address N(N-1) rows (32 drivers select 992 rows).
note: Sneak paths through half-selected rows undermine charlieplexing for wordlines.

title: Aerospace honeycomb: hex-packed cells with three 120-degree line sets
idea: Adapted from honeycomb sandwich cores: vertical-channel cells sit on a hexagonal close-packed lattice addressed by three line families at 120 degrees (wordline, bitline, plate-select), with a cell chosen by coincidence of two of them.

title: Blu-ray layer focus: threshold-window gates select tiers by voltage
idea: Borrowed from multilayer optical discs where focus depth picks the layer: each tier's access transistor has two series gates on two shared vertical lines, with thresholds graded up the stack on one and down on the other, so voltage level k on both turns on only tier k, with no per-tier staircase contact.
note: Resembles layer-selection-by-multilevel in 3D NAND; Vt variation limits tiers per gate pair.

title: Veneer slicing: deposit layers, slice block, get 10 nm lines
idea: Borrowed from wood-veneer slicing and nanoskiving: deposit 500 alternating 10 nm metal/oxide layers as a thick block, slice it perpendicular with a diamond microtome into thin slabs, and lay the slabs flat so the cut face exposes 10 nm lines whose pitch is set by deposition, not litho; cross two slabs for a crosspoint array.

title: Rare-earth-free motor magnet chemistry for platinum-free MRAM
idea: EV-motor makers are replacing NdFeB with iron nitride (Fe16N2) and synthetic tetrataenite (L10-FeNi). Adapt these phases as the perpendicular free and reference layers of a spin-torque cell, removing Pt/Co multilayers, the Ir in the synthetic antiferromagnet and heavy Ta seeds.

title: Planar ferrite inductors revive core memory at micron scale
idea: Power-supply makers now print MnZn/NiZn ferrite planar cores on silicon. Adapt this to bring back magnetic core memory: a 1-2 um ferrite toroid per bit, threaded by BEOL wordline, bitline and sense traces, with coincident-current writes and on-die restore-after-read.
note: Micron ferrite cores give poor density.

title: RF filter aluminum-boron-nitride ferroelectric in an endurance-shielded cell
idea: Phone BAW filters are sputtered aluminum nitride made in vast volume. Adapt boron-doped AlN (a ferroelectric wurtzite needing no Sc or Hf) as a ferroelectric-gated transistor bit on the same sputter tools, and shield its finite endurance with an SRAM write-back buffer that absorbs hot writes so each cell sees <1e9 cycles over its life.
