note: FeFET endurance far below DRAM-class; write buffer cannot fully hide it.

title: Parametron revival using MEMS-timing resonators storing phase bits
idea: MEMS timing chips (silicon resonators that replaced quartz crystals) meet Goto's 1950s parametron. Each bit is stored as the 0 or pi phase of a parametrically pumped nanomechanical resonator; one shared pump tone holds every bit, and reads use phase-sensitive detection.
note: Phase-bit MEMS resonators demonstrated; density, vacuum Q and readout speed far from DRAM-class.

title: Solar-grade silicon plus RAID coding tolerates leaky capacitorless cells
idea: Solar uses cheaper upgraded-metallurgical silicon, and RAID tolerates failing disks. Combine both: build capacitor-free floating-body or gain-cell arrays on 6N-7N wafers and absorb the fatter leakage tail with row-level erasure codes that rebuild expired bits instead of refreshing everything faster.

title: Optical-disc stamper family tree for DRAM array nanoimprint
idea: Adapt CD/DVD/Blu-ray replication: one e-beam-written quartz master is electroformed into nickel 'father', 'mother' and 'son' stampers (each generation multiplies copies ~10x), and the sons serve as UV-nanoimprint working templates for the periodic array layers (capacitor holes, landing pads, bitlines). Each son is retired after a fixed imprint count, as disc plants do, so defects never accumulate; EUV is kept only for the periphery.
note: Nickel stampers are UV-opaque and Si wafers too, so UV-NIL cure fails; overlay at 12 nm.

title: Bear hibernation: migrate idle rows to NVM before retention expires
idea: Borrowed from hibernating animals that drop to near-zero metabolism: the controller timestamps each row's last activation and, when an untouched row nears its retention deadline, moves it once into a dense non-volatile tier and marks it hibernating instead of refreshing it; a later access wakes it back into DRAM.
note: Untouched-for-64ms describes most rows; migration would thrash.

title: Phone-filter piezo transducers send ultrasonic data vertically through stacks
idea: Adapted from AlN bulk-acoustic-wave filters in smartphones: thin piezo transducers on each die launch GHz acoustic pulses through the bonded silicon stack to receivers on other dies. Data TSVs are replaced by frequency- or time-multiplexed acoustic channels.
note: Acoustic channel density and per-channel bandwidth far below TSVs; bond interfaces reflect.

title: Space-solar Miura fold turns one thin DRAM sheet into a stack
idea: Adapted from Miura-ori folding of satellite solar arrays: a strip of DRAM dies is built on an ultra-thin flexible bonded film with continuous copper traces across the fold lines. The strip folds accordion-style into a 16-high stack whose wires wrap around the folds instead of passing through TSVs.

title: Pupin loading coils make long interposer memory lines distortionless
idea: Adapted from the 1900 telephone loading coil: small thick-metal spiral inductors are added periodically along long memory traces to meet the Heaviside condition (L/C = R/G). A wide slow bus can then stretch 5-10 cm without equalizers.

title: Military fuzz-button connectors make solderless, reworkable memory stacks
idea: Adapted from fuzz-button (compressed gold-wire wad) interconnects in avionics: DRAM dies or packages stack in a clamped frame with fuzz-button arrays between them, so any failing die can be swapped after test with no reflow.
note: Fuzz-button pitch ~0.5 mm cannot carry HBM-class I/O.

title: CRT degaussing: trap-reset pulses to tame variable-retention cells
idea: Adapted from degaussing coils that reset magnetized CRT masks with a decaying field: using existing vendor test modes on current dies, the controller periodically applies a short decaying-amplitude negative wordline and plate bias sequence to idle subarrays, trying to drive variable-retention traps into their low-leakage state and hold them there.
note: Whether VRT traps can be biased into low-leak state is unknown.

title: On-chip gigahertz phononic delay loop recirculating bits in flight
idea: MAGNIFY frequency and MINIFY wavelength of 1940s mercury delay-line memory: 20 GHz acoustic pulses travel ~4 km/s in thin-film LiNbO3 or AlScN waveguides, so a 1-mm spiral holds ~5 us x 20 Gb/s = 100 kbit, regenerated by a piezo transducer and comparator at each loop end.

title: Vanadium dioxide hysteresis bit parked inside its transition loop
idea: MINIFY the thermal window: hold a sputtered VO2 cell array at the midpoint of its ~5-10 K metal-insulator hysteresis with a chip thermostat; a forward current pulse through a VO2/Bi2Te3 junction Peltier-heats a 30-nm cell onto the metallic branch, and a reverse pulse Peltier-cools it back onto the insulating branch, read by resistance.

title: Ovonic threshold switch acts as one-device bitline comparator
idea: A room-temperature-sputtered chalcogenide OTS is biased just below threshold; the charge-shared bitline from a '1' pushes it over, and its snap-back delivers a large current pulse (near-infinite gain) captured by a 2-TFT latch, MINIFYING a ~12-transistor SA to ~3 devices.
note: OTS threshold spread (~50 mV) is comparable to the bitline signal; per-device trim needed.

title: Active glass interposer with IGZO switches routes around bad dies
idea: MAGNIFY redundancy from cells to whole dies: a glass interposer carries IGZO TFT switch matrices (<=350 C) that remap channels from a failing HBM die or TSV column to a spare die in the stack, configured at final test.

title: IGZO charge-coupled readout drains rows to few sense nodes
idea: MAGNIFY serialization: like a CCD image sensor, a row's charge packets are shifted bucket-brigade along BEOL IGZO transfer gates (<=350 C) to one floating-diffusion sense node per 64 columns, MINIFYING sense amps 64x for sequential tensor streams.

title: Accumulative ferroelectric FET counts activations per row nonvolatilely
idea: Exploit accumulative partial switching in HZO/AlScN: each ACT applies a sub-coercive pulse to a per-row FeFET (<=400 C), nudging its threshold one step; after N steps it trips a neighbor-refresh flag and is reset, MINIFYING a row-hammer counter to one transistor.
note: Partial-switching fatigue under billions of activations on hot rows.

title: Minify speed to 1 us: 2-bit cells with shared ramp sensing
idea: Build a deliberately slow far-memory tier with 1 us access: cells store 2 bits (4 charge levels), and 64 bitlines share one slow, precise ramp-ADC sense circuit, time-multiplexed.

title: Grain-roughened TiN electrodes let plain alumina replace hafnia capacitors
idea: Magnify electrode area ~2.5x by reviving 1990s hemispherical-grain roughening in TiN form (seeded nanocrystal nucleation inside the hole), so a robust Al2O3/TiO2 laminate (k ~20) stores the same charge as ZrO2/HfO2.
note: HSG roughening needs room inside the hole; sub-30 nm capacitors leave no space for grains.

title: Photo-electrochemical macropore capacitor wafer with thermal oxide-nitride dielectric
idea: Magnify a cheap old process: etch 100:1 macropores into n-type silicon by backside-illuminated HF anodization (no plasma, no EUV), line them with thermally grown ONO, and hybrid-bond this capacitor wafer to the transistor wafer.

title: Printed relaxor polymer dielectric hitting k near 60
idea: Magnify dielectric constant by slot-die coating P(VDF-TrFE-CFE) relaxor terpolymer (k~50-60) biased in its non-switching paraelectric regime as a planar storage capacitor dielectric.

title: Inline print-test-repair loop with capacitive probe rollers
idea: Magnify test throughput by running the web past non-contact capacitive probe rollers that map bad blocks in real time; a downstream laser cuts and a printer reroutes around them before lamination.

title: Print memory directly on package substrate panels
idea: Magnify memory placement onto 510x515 mm organic package panels: inkjet-print oxide gain-cell arrays beside the processor footprint during panel-level packaging, so memory and package are made in one line.

title: Sacrificial backside allows one debond and re-thin cycle
idea: MAGNIFY reuse cycles: HBM dies keep a ~10 um sacrificial backside margin, so a debonded die can be re-thinned, re-polished and hybrid-bonded once more into a new stack.
note: Hybrid-bonded dies cannot be cleanly debonded.

title: Eliminate charge storage: spin-crossover molecules hold bits in spin state
idea: Eliminate charge: a thin film of Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover molecules switches between low-spin and high-spin states, with ~10% volume change and a large permittivity shift, inside a room-temperature hysteresis loop; a strain pulse from a piezoelectric gate flips it and capacitive sensing reads it.
note: Electrical ns switching unproven; volume change fatigue.

title: Eliminate stored charge: 77-K YBCO persistent-current loops as bits
idea: Eliminate charge storage: the bit is the direction of a persistent supercurrent in a ~100-nm YBCO nano-loop broken by a grain-boundary Josephson junction, written by a current pulse and read by an adjacent nano-SQUID. YBCO superconducts at 92 K, so LN2 rather than helium is enough, and it is grown by MOCVD in O2 with no argon sputtering.
note: YBCO grain-boundary junction reproducibility and loop inductance limit density.

title: Eliminate holding energy: van der Waals stiction latches nanocantilever bits
idea: Eliminate any energy source for holding state: a 10-nm graphene or ALD-TiN cantilever is pulled electrostatically onto a pad where van der Waals adhesion keeps it stuck (bit 1) with zero power, and a second pull-off electrode peels it free (bit 0); contact resistance reads the state. The sacrificial ALD oxide is removed by vapor HF, so no rare gases are used.
note: Same stiction-latch mechanism.

title: Eliminate vacuum-deposited ferroelectrics: solution-grown croconic-acid proton-transfer bits
idea: Eliminate inorganic, vacuum-deposited ferroelectrics: grow the room-temperature organic ferroelectric croconic acid (Ps ~20 uC/cm2) from solution inside cell pores, where polarization reverses by collective proton transfer along hydrogen bonds, a light-particle switch that needs small fields and no oxygen-vacancy motion.

title: Eliminate sub-wordline drivers: resonant LC wordlines with energy recovery
idea: Delete the sub-wordline driver stripes by making master wordlines low-resistance Ru lines that a single pass switch per row connects to a bank-wide resonant LC rail. The switch closes at the sinusoid trough and opens at its peak, so the wordline charges adiabatically and most of its energy returns to the tank on discharge.
note: Single pass switch per row and sinusoid timing at ns access.

title: Eliminate probe pads and probe cards: optically powered contactless wafer test
idea: Give each die a 100 um coil and a small photovoltaic cell. Flood illumination powers whole wafers, and test patterns flow over near-field inductive links at ~1 Gb/s, so thousands of dies test in parallel untouched. Probe pads, their drivers and test-lane ESD disappear.
note: Flood-lit PV cells cannot supply DRAM test power per die.

title: Eliminate the sense amplifier via negative-capacitance bitlines
idea: Put a thin ferroelectric HZO layer in series between each bitline and its parasitic shield, biased so its negative capacitance cancels ~60% of bitline capacitance. The charge-share signal rises from ~100 mV to ~300 mV, enough for a plain skewed-inverter pair instead of a matched latch.
note: Same NC bitline-capacitance cancellation.

title: Eliminate the isolation trench: grow periphery isolation by area-selective ALD
idea: Skip the fluorocarbon STI etch and the HF liner and oxide strips. Non-fluorinated alkyl-aminosilane inhibitor SAMs mark the device islands, and repeated inhibitor-refresh cycles of area-selective ALD grow ~80 nm Al2O3 isolation ridges only between them. Selective Si epitaxy (dichlorosilane/HCl) then raises the active areas level.

title: Eliminate transistor sense latches: carbon-released NEMS bistable beams
idea: Each bitline pair drives the two electrodes of a ~2 um buckled TiN nano-beam above it. The charge-share imbalance plus a common pull-in bias snaps the beam to one side, where its contact pulls that bitline to the rail. The cavity is cut by O2-ashing an amorphous-carbon sacrificial layer, which replaces HF-vapor or XeF2 release.
note: Mechanical asymmetry dwarfs mV signals; endurance and stiction.

title: Eliminate address buses: two-wire analog voltage row addressing
idea: Replace the ~13 predecoded address lines per mat with two analog wires (16 coarse and 32 fine levels) and a resistive ladder. Each wordline driver ANDs two 2-transistor window comparators tied to its ladder taps and fires only when both broadcast voltages fall in its window; the wiring is Cl-etched Mo.

title: Eliminate the common plate: pairwise differential plateless capacitors
idea: Remove the shared top-plate electrode and its conformal TiN/poly fill; neighbouring pillar storage nodes face each other through the high-k film so each pair forms one capacitor written with complementary charge (+Q/-Q) and read differentially on a folded bitline pair.
note: Two pillars per bit halves density; pillar-to-pillar crosstalk in hex arrays.

title: Eliminate the 3D staircase: contact tiers at the etched die sidewall
idea: Remove the NAND-style staircase entirely; terminate every tier at a deep-etched trench wall at the mat edge where all tiers are exposed edge-on, then a laser-written or tilted-deposition redistribution layer fans each tier out to the top surface.
note: Resolving ~40 nm tiers on a sidewall with laser writing or tilted deposition is unrealistic.

title: Eliminate the capacitor hole: bottom-up nanowire capacitor electrodes
idea: Instead of etching a mold, grow a conductive nanowire (doped Si or silicide, using a CMOS-safe Al or Sn catalyst) vapour-liquid-solid straight up from each storage node to AR 200:1, then wrap it in ALD high-k and plate.

title: Eliminate sacrificial SiGe: Si/CaF2 epitaxial insulator superlattice
idea: Grow 3D DRAM tiers as an epitaxial superlattice of silicon and lattice-matched CaF2 (~0.6% mismatch), so the inter-tier insulator is grown in its final form and no sacrificial layer needs wet lateral removal and refill.
note: Large CaF2/Si thermal mismatch and poor Si-on-CaF2 regrowth.

title: Eliminate wafers and wet benches: roll-to-roll vacuum web tiers
idea: Deposit oxide-semiconductor capacitor-transistor tiers on a moving stainless or polyimide web inside a vacuum roll coater, patterning with in-line laser ablation and shadow-roll masks, then laminate cut sheets into stacks.
note: R2R pitch (~um) yields bits/area orders below DRAM; cost per bit unlikely to win.

title: Eliminate charge pumps: monolayer MoS2 access transistors driven from 1 V
idea: Replace the buried silicon access device with a gate-all-around monolayer MoS2 channel (U.S. molybdenum, refinery sulfur) whose ~2 eV gap and 0.7 nm body give near-zero off-current at 0 V, so the wordline swings 0-1 V straight from VDD with no VPP pump or negative-wordline supply.
note: MoS2 on-current/contact resistance at 1 V and wafer-scale GAA integration are the doubts.

title: Eliminate access-transistor lithography: grow vertical nanowire channels from catalysts
idea: Place catalyst dots with a block-copolymer lattice (no mask), grow vertical single-crystal Si nanowires by vapor-liquid-solid epitaxy with a CMOS-friendly catalyst (Al or Cu-silicide), then wrap them in ALD gate stacks to form 4F2 vertical access transistors.

title: Eliminate fragmentation slack with transparent hardware object compaction
idea: The memory controller keeps a small redirection table and relocates live small objects in the background into dense pages, updating mappings like a hardware copying collector, so malloc arenas stop wasting free holes.
note: Hardware lacks object boundaries; per-object redirection table would be huge.

title: Inside-out capacitor: block-copolymer pore sponge replaces one tall pillar
idea: Flip the capacitor from a solid pillar into voids: inside each cell footprint a self-assembled block-copolymer template is etched into sacrificial oxide as ~10 nm pores (AR ~20 each), then coated TiN/ZrO2/TiN by ALD, so area comes from many shallow holes instead of one 70:1 pillar.
note: 10 nm pores cannot fit a TiN/ZrO2/TiN stack (~16+ nm); area gain doubtful at DRAM cell pitch.

title: One heavy-metal strip: forward to write, backward to read
idea: Rearrange the spintronic stack around one effect run both ways: a perpendicular nanomagnet on a Pt or Bi2Se3 strip is written by spin-orbit torque (charge to spin) and read by the inverse, a GHz pulse excites precession whose spin pumping yields an inverse-spin-Hall voltage whose sign is the bit; no MgO tunnel barrier.
note: Dropping MgO for uV inverse-spin-Hall read worsens signal; endurance gain unclear.

title: Molecular spin-state bit: hysteretic Fe(II) spin-crossover film
idea: Instead of moving electrons in and out of a node, flip their pairing inside an ion: a thin film of a room-temperature-hysteretic Fe(II) spin-crossover complex toggles between low-spin and high-spin with ~10-20% dielectric-constant change; a field/charge pulse sets the state and a capacitive divider reads it.
note: Solid-film spin-crossover switching is slow, needs temperature bias, and permittivity contrast is small.

title: Write-first read infers old bit from charge the driver supplies
idea: Flip read and write order: a per-column-group write driver forces the opened cell to '1' while a charge integrator measures how much charge it delivered (~0 for a stored 1, ~Cs*VDD for a stored 0); the result is latched and 0s are written back. Latch-type sense amp and separate restore phase merge into one driver/integrator.
note: Integrator also sees large common-mode bitline charge; signal charge is still Cs*VDD, as with charge sharing.

title: High-voltage drivers on glass: TFT periphery on U.S. panels
idea: Reverse the substrate for high-voltage periphery: global wordline drivers, level shifters and pumps, which need 3-5 V rather than density, are built as TFTs on a U.S.-made glass interposer panel and connected to the array die through fine-pitch redistribution.

title: Grow capacitor walls up instead of etching holes down
idea: Reverse subtractive to additive: area-selective ALD grows the capacitor support lattice upward from seeded lines, so the 60-75:1 storage structure forms without a fluorocarbon high-aspect-ratio etch.

title: Helium-off etch: edge dies carry extra parity
idea: Rearrange reliability by location: run etch tools without helium backside gas, accept the resulting radial temperature/CD drift, and assign stronger ECC to edge-zone dies or rows (from a known radial map) so their ~1% raw BER is absorbed.
note: Without backside gas, wafer temperature control fails broadly, not just radially; ECC may not absorb it.

title: Fluorocarbon-free chlorine etch with tapered, error-tolerated pillars
idea: Reverse the anisotropy priority: etch capacitor and contact holes in HBr/Cl2/O2 pulsed plasmas with no fluorocarbons, accept the tapered profiles that leave ~1% weak cells, and correct them with ECC.
note: Cl chemistries etch SiO2 molds poorly; profiles likely far worse than 1% weak cells.

title: Grow pillars, don't dig holes: bottom-up electrode forest
idea: Reverse subtractive to additive: instead of etching high-AR holes in an oxide mold, grow conductive pillars upward from the landing pads by selective epitaxy of degenerately doped Si or SiGe, then coat them conformally with ALD dielectric and top plate.

title: Backside flood exposure through a transparent carrier
idea: Flip the exposure side: build the array on a thin Si layer bonded to fused-silica/sapphire, then flood-expose resist from the backside so already-made opaque wordlines and bitlines act as the photomask for the next self-aligned layer (contacts, spacers).
note: Known in TFT displays; UV absorption in Si and diffraction at sub-20 nm are hard.

title: Atomic steps on miscut wafers guide self-assembly
idea: Reverse the guide: use a deliberately miscut wafer whose annealed atomic step bunches form a natural periodic grating, which aligns block-copolymer self-assembly into cell lines with no litho template.

title: Package lid as a sub-THz broadcast waveguide
idea: Reverse the heat spreader's role: the copper lid and a substrate ground plane form a parallel-plate waveguide, and each chiplet has a slot antenna radiating 100-300 GHz into it, so one memory chiplet can broadcast a read to many compute chiplets at once without routed wires.

title: Data over the power network inside the HBM stack
idea: Rearrange power and signal roles: superimpose low-amplitude, high-frequency data on the many power/ground TSVs (which outnumber signal TSVs) using AC coupling and band separation above the PDN resonance, turning idle PDN capacity into extra channels.

title: Optical vias through solid silicon, no holes drilled
idea: Reverse drill-then-fill: instead of copper TSVs, thinned DRAM dies (silicon is transparent at 1.3-1.55 um) pass data vertically as light from bonded III-V micro-emitters to Ge photodiodes on dies above, with each tier on its own wavelength so beams cross intermediate dies unabsorbed.
note: BEOL metal and intermediate Ge detectors block vertical beams.

title: Wordline Joule pulses anneal retention traps in the field
idea: Reverse aging into healing: during maintenance windows a bank goes offline and high current is driven through segmented wordlines (far end shorted by a switch) to heat the local array to ~250-300 C for milliseconds, annealing the trap states behind variable-retention-time cells.
note: ms-scale 300C local heating destroys neighbour data; Macronix did NAND self-heal.

title: Ionic-liquid nanopore double-layer cell stores charge at angstrom separation
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics/hydraulics (liquid replaces solid): fill a sealed ~20-nm blocking-electrode pore per cell with a high-conductivity ionic liquid whose electric double layer (~0.5-nm Helmholtz gap) gives 10-20 uF/cm2 at under 1 V, versus ~8 uF/cm2 for best solid high-k. Contradiction resolved: more charge vs. lower voltage.
note: Ionic-liquid sealing and self-discharge at 20 nm pores doubtful.

title: Niobium-oxide cell with self-healing solid-electrolyte top plate
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: copy the solid niobium electrolytic capacitor. Anodize a Nb storage electrode to Nb2O5 (k~40) and use a MnO2 or conductive-polymer top plate; at any leakage hot spot the fault current itself converts MnO2 to insulating Mn2O3 (or de-dopes the polymer), sealing the defect, and an in-field 're-forming' pulse regrows thinned oxide by anodization.
note: MnO2/polymer top plate cannot be put conformally into 20 nm holes; gain is ~30%.

title: Ceria oxygen buffer refillable like a catalytic converter's storage
idea: TRIZ #9 Prior anti-action: insert a ~0.5-nm CeO2 interlayer into the ZrO2 stack. As with the oxygen-storage capacity in car catalytic converters, Ce4+/Ce3+ swaps donate oxygen to fill vacancies formed under field stress, and a periodic thermal anneal pulls oxygen back from an RuO2/TiON electrode reservoir to recharge the buffer.

title: Nested charge-trap shadow layer preserves data through heal cycles
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: embed a ~2-nm SiN charge-trap layer inside each capacitor dielectric so that before a repair anneal, detox or module removal the controller programs a nonvolatile shadow copy of every bit with a Fowler-Nordheim burst, then restores it afterwards. Repairs no longer need external data migration, and the shadow is used rarely so its endurance suffices.
note: Trap layer inside the capacitor dielectric degrades leakage and reliability; restore path unclear.

title: Sort-time electrothermal annealing heals leakage-tail cells individually
idea: TRIZ #10 Preliminary action: fix the defect before the part ships. At wafer sort, cells flagged as retention-tail are driven with short high-current pulses through their own and neighbouring access transistors to self-heat the junction region to several hundred C for microseconds, annealing the specific trap responsible, then retested; cells that still fail fall back to row repair.
note: Microsecond self-heating through tiny access FETs risks oxide/EM damage; trap anneal kinetics usually need far longer than microseconds.

title: Atmospheric mist-CVD gallium oxide access transistors on sapphire panels
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics and hydraulics: deposit corundum-phase alpha-Ga2O3 (Eg ~5.3 eV) channels from an ultrasonic aerosol of gallium acetylacetonate solution carried by gas at atmospheric pressure onto sapphire, with no vacuum tools, then pattern access transistors whose thermal generation leakage is effectively nil.
note: Mist-CVD alpha-Ga2O3 known; device quality and sapphire-panel integration with CMOS doubtful.

title: Prior counteraction: data-aware counter-kick cancels bitline coupling before sensing
idea: TRIZ #9 Prior counteraction: a small per-bank row-history cache predicts the neighbouring bitlines' data for the row about to open, and the precharge circuit injects a calibrated counter-charge through dedicated coupling caps so the worst-case bitline-to-bitline coupling during amplification is cancelled in advance.

title: Phase transition: insulator-metal switch replaces the cross-coupled latch
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transition: a single NbO2 or VO2 threshold-switching element biased just below its insulator-to-metal transition sits on the sense node; the few extra millivolts from a stored '1' tip it abruptly into the metallic state, giving full-swing output from one device instead of a 4-6 transistor latch, and a reset pulse returns it to insulating.

title: Hydraulics: electrolyte-gated printed sense transistors on roll-to-roll film
idea: TRIZ #29 Pneumatics and hydraulics: the solid gate dielectric of the sense and decode circuits is replaced by a printed ion-gel electrolyte whose double-layer capacitance (~10 uF/cm2) gives high transconductance below 1 V, so inkjet- or gravure-printed oxide transistors at 5-10 um can still amplify millivolt bitline signals.

title: Read floating-body state through the wordline's capacitance, not current
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: keep the bitlines quiet and sense the cell on the wordline instead. Stored body holes change gate-to-channel capacitance (accumulation vs depletion), so a small probe pulse on the vertical wordline couples a state-dependent charge into a wordline-side charge amplifier.
note: Wordline couples to every cell on it, swamping one cell's signal.

title: Complementary gain cell: p-WSe2 write tier over n-IGZO read tier
idea: TRIZ #4 Asymmetry: make the write transistor p-type (WSe2 or SnO) in one tier and the read transistor n-type IGZO in the tier below, stacked in one footprint. The p-type device passes a full 1 with its wordline at 0 V instead of a ~3 V boost, and its leakage polarity opposes the read device's.
note: WSe2 off-current far above IGZO limits retention; wordline savings overstated.

title: Per-package 180 nm companion die doing wide-slow line compression
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation: instead of one fast advanced-node compression engine, wire-bond a cheap 180 nm companion die beside each DRAM die in the package; each handles only its own chip's x8 slice with a 256-bit-wide internal datapath at 100-200 MHz running BDI/FPC compression, so segmentation makes slow old silicon fast enough.
note: Each x8 die holds a byte slice of every line, which wrecks line compression patterns.

title: Bank-switched DIMM capacity reassigned between hosts by analog muxes
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: like EMS bank switching, a pool box of memory modules sits behind passive analog crossbar switches buildable on old processes; at millisecond-to-minute granularity a controller quiesces a module group and re-routes it from one host's channel to another's, with OS memory hot-plug onlining and offlining it.

title: Merging: data carriers superimposed on power TSVs
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging: about half of HBM TSVs carry only VDD/VSS. Superimpose low-amplitude 10-20 GHz on-off-keyed carriers on them, with on-die LC band-pass taps and notch filters on the decoupling network, so power TSVs also carry data without new holes.
note: Decaps short the carriers; notches weaken decoupling.

title: Equipotentiality: cross-company fab tool-hour exchange for idle litho and etch
idea: TRIZ #12 Equipotentiality: standardize wafer carriers, recipe formats and contamination certificates so idle DUV scanners and etchers in logic and foundry fabs can accept DRAM lots by the hour through a brokered exchange with escrowed IP protection.
note: Cross-fab contamination and requalification make lot-hopping impractical.

title: Magnetosome biomineralization: protein-templated nanomagnet arrays without magnetic etch
idea: Magnetotactic bacteria grow uniform single-domain magnetite crystals using Mms6/MamC proteins. Anchor engineered Mms6 peptides in pre-patterned wells on a tungsten- and platinum-free spin-orbit write line (e.g. BiSb topological insulator), so each well grows one uniform 15-20 nm ferrite particle from aqueous solution. A tunnel-barrier read stack is capped on after growth.
note: 15-20 nm magnetite is near superparamagnetic; tunnel barriers on bio-grown particles are poor.

title: Tardigrade glass lock: ions movable only during a heated write
idea: Tardigrades survive by vitrifying in trehalose glass, which freezes molecular motion. Store the bit as the position of Ag+ or Li+ ions in a 5 nm ion-conducting glass under a gain-transistor gate. A 10-20 ns microheater pulse lifts the glass above its glass transition so the field can move the ions, then quenching freezes them in place.
note: Thermal gating breaks speed-retention tradeoff but costs pJ writes and thermal crosstalk.

title: CAM-photosynthesis refresh banking before predicted traffic bursts
idea: CAM plants fix CO2 at night as malate and keep stomata shut by day; before predicted bandwidth peaks (all-reduce, batch prefill) the controller refreshes rows with a boosted restore level (~1.15-1.2x VARY via extended VPP write), banking extra charge so the bank can skip 2-3 refresh periods during the burst and catch up afterward.

title: Nacre brick-and-mortar nanosheet gate dielectric for BEOL access FETs
idea: Nacre's aragonite tiles in organic mortar stop cracks from running straight through; stack exfoliated perovskite nanosheets (Ca2Nb3O10, k ~200, 1.5 nm) at room temperature by Langmuir-Blodgett, staggered like bricks, with sub-nm Al2O3 'mortar' by ALD at 150 C, so no straight grain-boundary leakage path crosses the gate dielectric.
note: Perovskite nanosheet high-k known (Osada); 1.5 nm films leak and BEOL integration is hard.

title: Axon-hillock NbO2 spiking threshold element replacing large matched sense pairs
idea: Like the axon hillock's all-or-nothing spike, a nanoscale NbO2 Mott threshold switch plus series capacitor at each bitline pair forms a relaxation 'neuron'. It fires only when the differential charge passes a programmable bias threshold, turning a few-mV signal into a large spike that sets a minimal latch. Threshold is trimmed by bias, not by big matched transistors.
note: NbO2 threshold variability far exceeds few-mV signals.

title: Electric-fish lock-in sensing via carrier-modulated cell plate and chopper demodulation
idea: Weakly electric fish detect nanovolt fields by emitting a carrier and demodulating synchronously. During the read window the bitline precharge reference carries a small GHz carrier, and a chopper switch pair at the sense-amp input demodulates it, moving the signal away from 1/f noise and slow offset drift before the latch fires.

title: Magnetosome-chain anisotropic interconnect joining periphery wafer to array wafer
idea: Magnetotactic bacteria align magnetite crystals into chains. Fill a bonding dielectric with Fe3O4/Ni nanoparticles and cure it under a vertical magnetic field, so conductive pillar chains self-assemble at ~300 nm pitch. They join a separately made logic-process periphery wafer to the array wafer without fine-alignment hybrid bonding.
note: A 300 nm pitch is far too coarse for bitline-pitch periphery, and pad alignment is still needed.

title: Gecko-setae dry adhesion: test whole stacks before permanent bonding
idea: Temporarily join stacked DRAM dies with gecko-like nanopillar dry-adhesive arrays plus spring micro-pillar contacts for electrical continuity, run full at-speed stack test, swap any bad die, then convert to a permanent bond with a low-temperature Cu-Cu anneal.

title: Leaf-venation loop-redundant printed interposer for HBM stacks
idea: Leaf veins form closed loops so flow routes around damage. Print panel-level RDL interposers roll-to-roll with fine copper lines arranged as looped meshes instead of single tree routes, so any printed open is bypassed, and use them in place of silicon interposers under HBM.
note: Signal lines cannot be meshed without shorting nets; printed lines miss HBM micron pitch.

title: Cochlear tonotopic wires: passive frequency-split multichannel interposer lines
idea: Each interposer wire carries 4-8 data streams on different RF carriers. At the receiver, a tapered passive resonant 'basilar membrane' transmission line separates the carriers by position, as the cochlea maps pitch to place, so fewer bumps and wires carry the same bandwidth.

title: Gecko-setae dry adhesion for reworkable, repairable memory stacks
idea: Dies in a stack are held by gecko-like micro-pillar dry adhesive with spring-contact or liquid-metal interconnect pads, instead of permanent hybrid bonds and underfill. A stack that fails final test can be peeled apart and only the bad die swapped.

title: Retina-style monolithic IGZO memory layers grown on glass interposer
idea: The retina builds its photoreceptor, bipolar and ganglion layers in one tissue with the wiring on top. Likewise IGZO gain-cell DRAM tiers are deposited directly on the glass-core interposer beside the GPU site at BEOL temperatures (<400 C), so the memory and its wiring are one monolithic structure with no microbumps, TSVs or separate memory dies.
note: Micron-scale TFT cells give low density per interposer.

title: Clotting capsules: liquid-metal microcapsules self-heal cracked HBM bonds
idea: Seed the HBM underfill and bond interface with ~2 um gallium-alloy microcapsules; when thermal cycling cracks a microbump or hybrid-bond pad, the crack ruptures nearby capsules and the liquid metal wicks into the gap and re-closes the circuit like a platelet plug.
note: Ga capsules self-heal shown in flex circuits; Ga attacks Cu/Al at micron scale.

title: Hippocampal CA3 attractors: noisy printed crossbars that self-correct on recall
idea: CA3 recurrent networks recall whole memories from noisy cues; store data as attractors of a dense associative (modern Hopfield) network whose weights sit in a printed resistive crossbar with +-30% variation and dead devices, so iterating recall pulls errors back to the stored pattern and the array itself acts as the decoder.

title: Acidophile biomining of tungsten from U.S. tailings and scrap
idea: Microbes such as Acidithiobacillus already leach metals out of rock. Engineered bioleaching heaps and bioreactors extract tungsten from historic U.S. mine tailings and scrap carbide/e-waste, which is then refined into WF6 precursor for wordlines and contacts.
note: Wolframite/scheelite are not sulfides; bioleaching tungsten is weakly demonstrated.

title: Diatom-grown biosilica as high-purity quartz for crucibles
idea: Diatoms build glass shells from dissolved silica at room temperature. Diatoms grown in photobioreactors on purified silicic acid yield biosilica that is calcined, acid-polished and fused into synthetic high-purity quartz for Czochralski crucibles.
note: If silicic acid is already purified, diatoms add contamination rather than purity.

title: Venus-flytrap snap-through NEMS latches built in idle MEMS fabs
idea: The flytrap stores a state as one of two buckled leaf shapes and snaps between them. Pre-buckled nanobeams with two stable curvatures are switched electrostatically and read through a tunneling gap or a gated FET under the beam, using the release-etch processes U.S. MEMS fabs already run.

title: Refrigerator crisper drawer: thermoelectrically chilled cell array only
idea: Keep only the drawer cold, not the kitchen: integrate a thin-film SiGe or Bi2Te3 thermoelectric layer under the cell-array mats only, holding storage nodes ~25-30 K below the periphery and logic, with heat pumped into the package lid. Junction leakage roughly halves every ~8-10 K.
note: Silicon heat spreading prevents a 25 K gradient between adjacent mats and periphery.

title: TOPCon solar contact: tunnel-oxide passivating junction for the storage node
idea: High-efficiency solar cells reach surface recombination velocities <1 cm/s with a 1.5-nm SiO2 tunnel oxide under doped poly-Si (TOPCon); replace the storage-node contact's implanted n+/p junction with this carrier-selective passivating contact plus solar-style hydrogenation, so the node interface has ~100x fewer generation centers.
note: DRAM node contacts are already poly plugs; tail comes from depletion traps/GIDL, not contact surface.

title: Mood-ring molecules: spin-crossover film switches capacitance bistably
idea: Like a mood ring, Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover complexes switch between low-spin and high-spin states with a 10-30 K hysteresis loop near room temperature and a large dielectric and volume change; thermally evaporate or spin-coat a 10-nm film between Pt electrodes, park the die inside the loop, write with a ns field/Joule pulse, and read the capacitance shift.

title: LCD panel laser repair: hydrogen-ambient spot anneal heals mapped tail cells
idea: Display fabs laser-repair defective pixels after test instead of scrapping panels. After retention mapping at wafer sort, scan a focused infrared laser through the thinned wafer backside in D2/H2 ambient over regions holding tail cells, briefly heating buried interfaces to re-passivate traps; only photons and hydrogen, no fluorine.
note: Wafers are full thickness at sort; local IR heating spreads.

title: Display gate-on-array IGZO wordline drivers stacked above the array
idea: LCD makers moved gate drivers onto the glass as thin-film shift registers (gate-on-array). Do the same: build sub-wordline drivers and local row-decode NAND as IGZO TFT circuits in the BEOL directly over the cell array, leaving only global predecode in silicon.
note: Vias at wordline pitch through the capacitor layer, and NMOS-only IGZO drive, are the doubts.

title: Telescope-mirror peel-off polymer: dry particle capture film
idea: Observatories clean mirrors with a peel-off polymer that cures around dust and lifts it away. Spin a strippable polymer onto periphery wafers after CMP or etch, let it encapsulate particles and residues, then peel it off with an adhesive roller tape in a dry module, leaving the surface clean.

title: Termite-mound thermosiphon chimneys through the DRAM stack
idea: Termite mounds cool themselves with passive convection chimneys; etch a sparse grid of sealed ~20 um chimneys through a 16-24 high bonded DRAM stack, partly filled with a dielectric working fluid that boils near the hot logic tier and condenses at the lid, pumping heat with no pump.

title: Corrugated-board substrate: one array film over V-groove relief
idea: Like corrugated cardboard folding a flat sheet into a high-area core, KOH-etch Si(100) into 54.7-degree V-grooves at ~200 nm pitch and build a thin-film transistor-capacitor array conformally on both groove faces with tilted implants and spacer patterning, packing ~1.7x more planar-processed cells per footprint.
note: 1.7x area at best; litho and implants on sloped faces at DRAM pitch are hard.

title: Copper heap-leach mining: bacteria recover tungsten, hafnium, ruthenium from scrap
idea: Copper miners bioleach low-grade ore with Acidithiobacillus. Run stirred bioreactors where acidophilic and siderophore-producing microbes leach W, Hf, Zr, Ru and Ta from scrapped wafers, spent sputter targets, chamber shields and test boards at ambient temperature, followed by solvent extraction to reagent grade.

title: Nanoporous-gold dealloying grows a sponge-surface storage electrode
idea: Borrowed from catalyst and supercapacitor makers, who leach the less-noble metal out of an alloy to get 10-50x surface area: deposit a Ru-Al alloy bottom electrode, dealloy the Al in mild base to leave porous Ru with 3-5 nm ligaments, then conformally coat dielectric and top electrode.

title: Mercury-thermometer liquid-metal channels in an elastomer interposer
idea: Like mercury in a thermometer, fill micro-channels in a silicone/polyimide interposer with Ga-In liquid metal at room temperature. The result is stretchable, self-healing, reworkable wiring between memory stacks and compute that tolerates warpage.

title: Battery reconditioning pulses that reset variable-retention-time traps
idea: Deep-cycle reconditioning breaks up sulfate crystals in lead-acid batteries. During idle, each row would get a brief reconditioning pulse: a deep negative wordline plus a raised bitline/substrate bias. The pulse empties the metastable gate- and junction-region traps that flip cells into their leaky VRT state. The pulsed rows are then re-profiled.
note: Same pulse-based VRT trap reset.

title: 1960s holographic memory revived on thin-film lithium niobate photonics
idea: RCA and Bell holographic stores wrote whole pages as interference gratings in photorefractive crystals. Put an Fe-doped thin-film LN slab under a SiN optical phased array that steers the reference angle electro-optically in ns, storing ~1000 angle-multiplexed 4-kb pages in a 100x100 um slab read in parallel onto a Ge photodiode row.
note: Photorefractive writes are slow; density below DRAM and retention needs fixing.

title: Ramtron FeRAM revived with non-destructive piezoelectric-sign readout
idea: Early 1T1C PZT FeRAM suffered destructive reads and fatigue. On existing 130-nm FRAM lines that already integrate PZT, read polarization by applying a small AC voltage and sensing the sign of the resulting piezoelectric strain with a capacitive or piezoresistive sense layer over the capacitor, as piezoresponse microscopy does.

title: CRT flyback energy recovery for raster-like refresh sweeps
idea: Revive the television horizontal-deflection flyback circuit, which recycled deflection energy through an LC resonance on every scan line: refresh sweeps rows on a fixed periodic raster, so an on-package resonant LC tank drives the 3 V refresh wordlines and bitline precharge. Most of the CV2 energy returns to the tank at each refresh step instead of being dissipated.

title: Vacuum-tube getter revived inside sealed BEOL cavities
idea: Revive the barium flash getter that kept vacuum tubes clean for decades: deposit a non-evaporable Zr-V-Fe getter film in a sealed cavity over each array mat, activated by the final anneal. It keeps absorbing the hydrogen and moisture that would otherwise migrate to access-transistor interfaces over life, creating trap-assisted leakage and variable retention time.
note: Getter may also strip passivating hydrogen from interfaces, worsening Dit.

title: Neutron transmutation doping at U.S. research reactors for implant-free channels
idea: Revive 1970s neutron transmutation doping, used for power-device silicon: irradiate silicon at U.S. research reactors (for example the University of Missouri reactor) so Si-30 transmutes into uniformly distributed phosphorus. Access-transistor wells then form without implantation, removing the implant-damage clusters that seed trap-assisted leakage.
note: NTD yields only phosphorus (n-type); NMOS access wells are p-type.

title: ESI laser trimming revived to heal weak access transistors
idea: Revive 1970s Portland-made laser trimming of resistors: after a retention test, a U.S.-built infrared picosecond laser fires through backside-thinned silicon to anneal the gate region of the ppm-level worst-leakage cells, healing trap clusters and raising each die's retention floor.
note: IR spot covers many cells at DRAM pitch; trap healing unproven.

title: Quadruplex telegraph bitlines carry two cells per sense event
idea: Copy Edison's 1874 quadruplex telegraph, which sent one message as current polarity and another as amplitude on a single wire. Two cells on paired rows share one bitline event: one dumps charge through its normal access device, and the other is read through a 2x plate-line pulse that injects a doubly weighted, opposite-polarity charge. A 4-level sense (two latches with offset references) decodes both bits.

title: Vibrating-reed electrometer screens leakage-tail cells in milliseconds
idea: The 1940s vibrating-reed electrometer measured femtoamps by modulating a capacitor mechanically. A varactor-modulated test capacitor on each mat's test bus measures each row's integrated leakage directly by lock-in detection in milliseconds, replacing hours-long hot retention tests. Rows are then binned into 2-4 refresh classes stored on the die.
note: Row-integrated leakage hides single tail cells among thousands; VRT also defeats one-shot binning.

title: Vacuum nanogap transistors as oxide-free high-voltage drivers
idea: Revive the vacuum tube at 50 nm. One added cavity mask etches a nanogap between a sharp source tip and the drain under an existing gate, and a non-conformal oxide deposition pinches it shut under vacuum. Field emission across a gap shorter than the electron mean free path switches with no gate-oxide stress and tolerates 3-5 V at minimum size.
note: Emitter degradation and current density at minimum size.

title: Ferrite flux-rod through the stack broadcasts data to all dies
idea: Revive the magnetic core threaded by many wires: one high-permeability ferrite-filled vertical via runs through a 16-die stack and each die's on-chip coil wraps it, so a transmit coil on the base die couples to every die at once like a shared core. Data moves inductively (broadcast writes, time-sliced reads), replacing most HBM data TSVs.
note: Ferrite loss at GHz and single-rod bandwidth cannot replace wide TSV buses.

title: Drum read-retry lets tiny capacitors run at 1% sense errors
idea: Revive the drum and disk habit of re-reading on the next revolution: shrink Cs to ~2 fF so ~1% of reads are noise-limited errors, and on ECC failure re-sense the restored row with a longer bitline development time.
note: Destructive read restores the mis-sensed value, so re-sensing the restored row cannot recover errors; 1% BER too high.

title: Twistor revival: helical-anisotropy Fe-Al nanowire memory, platinum-free
idea: Revive Bell Labs' 1957 twistor: electroplate an Fe-Al (Alfenol) or NiFe shell on copper nanowires while a mismatched coaxial stress layer applies torsion, locking in a helical easy axis. Bits are helical magnetization segments switched by coincident wire current and an orthogonal copper strap, and read inductively along the same wire, so no MTJ stack is needed.
note: Inductive read signal vanishes at nanowire scale.

title: Bubble memory reborn in manganese nitride with on-chip rotating fields
idea: Revive Bobeck's 1970s bubble memory without Gd/Ga garnet substrates: sputter perpendicular ferrimagnetic Mn4N on silicon, pattern permalloy asymmetric-disk propagation tracks, and drive every bubble with a 100 MHz rotating in-plane field from quadrature on-chip striplines. One global drive replaces per-cell transistors, and each minor loop needs just one magnetoresistive detector.

title: GaN-on-silicon power fabs build wide-bandgap 1T1C memory
idea: Revive the 1980s compound-semiconductor dynamic memory experiments (GaAs/AlGaAs charge storage with very long retention) using enhancement-mode p-GaN-gate transistors as access devices: the 3.4 eV gap and heterojunction confinement can push off-current far below silicon's, with MIM capacitors added in a short BEOL. Production uses depreciated 150/200 mm GaN-on-Si power-device lines.
note: HEMT gate/buffer leakage isn't obviously below Si; density 10-30x worse.

title: Zuse relay storage reborn as bistable buckled-nanobeam memory
idea: Revive the relay storage of Konrad Zuse's 1941 Z3, which held its memory in ~1,400 latching relays, as pre-buckled nanobeams with two stable shapes that snap between states under an electrostatic pulse and are read capacitively without ever touching a contact. Beams are released with vapour HF and sealed in vacuum, so the cell's off state is an empty gap.

title: Goto parametron phase memory as attractor-based retrieval store
idea: Revive the 1954 parametron, which stored bits as 0 or pi oscillation phase: a university-fab array of MEMS or LC parametric oscillators, coupled through programmable capacitors that encode stored patterns, relaxes from an injected query to the nearest stored pattern. This gives associative recall of documents or KV clusters without scanning memory.
note: Hopfield-type capacity (~0.14N patterns) cannot replace GB-scale vector stores.

title: Strowger bank switching with university MEMS relays for memory pooling
idea: Revive 8-bit bank switching and Strowger stepping switches: an array of university-fabricated ohmic MEMS relays physically re-points DDR channels between hosts, so a memory module moves to another server in microseconds with no copy, no CXL controller and no protocol latency once connected.
note: Relays on DDR5 channels hurt signal integrity; retraining and hot-plug make microsecond moves unrealistic.

title: Differential-analyzer revival: ship activations between dies as analog charge
idea: Revive analog computing: between a processing-in-memory die and the logic die, send each 6-bit activation as one analog charge sample per wire per transfer, consumed directly by an analog MAC on the far side with no ADC/DAC pair.

title: Core-memory ferrite rings replace TSVs as fluorine-free inductive stack vias
idea: Revive core memory's transformer coupling: each thinned die carries thin-film coils around sputtered NiZn/NiFe ferrite ring segments aligned through the stack, so flux threads 4-8 dies like wires through a core and carries data with no holes etched.
note: Silicon gaps break the ferrite flux path unless cores are etched through.

title: Photophone revival: infrared micro-LEDs signal straight through thinned silicon stacks
idea: Like Bell's 1880 photophone sending speech on light, place 1.3-1.55 um InGaAs micro-LEDs on one die and Ge photodiodes on dies above; silicon is transparent at these wavelengths, so data crosses several thinned dies vertically with no via.

title: Acoustic delay-line revival: AlN gigahertz ultrasound bus through the stack
idea: Revive the delay line's acoustic signaling: sputtered AlN transducers (not PVDF fluoropolymer piezo) launch 5-10 GHz bulk acoustic pulses that travel vertically through bonded silicon tiers to receivers on every die, forming a broadcast command/address and refresh-control bus.

title: Hollerith tabulator revival: spring pins in low-melt cups socket HBM
idea: Revive Hollerith's 1890 tabulator contacts, pins dipping through holes into mercury cups, with Field's-metal (Bi-In-Sn, 62 C melt) micro-cups on the substrate that receive HBM stack pins, making stacks socketed, flux-free and reworkable.
note: Field's metal melts at 62 C, below HBM operating temperature.

title: Bucket-Brigade Analog Storage: 6-Bit Charge Packets Per Cell
idea: Revive the 1969 Philips bucket-brigade device (the analog delay chip in guitar pedals) as multi-level analog charge storage for low-precision AI activations: each capacitor holds one of 64 charge levels, read by a shared successive-approximation ADC per column, built on mature 180-65 nm analog/mixed-signal fabs.

title: CuInP2S6 quadruple-well ferroelectric stores two bits per cell on mica
idea: Invert 'a ferroelectric gives two states' -> use one with four. Layered CuInP2S6 has a quadruple-well potential (low and high polarization of each sign set by Cu displacement), grown by van der Waals epitaxy on cleavable mica and read through the threshold shift of a 2D-semiconductor channel.
note: ~315 K Curie point and Cu migration make it unfit for operating temperatures.

title: Bacteria-grown magnetite nanocrystals as self-made single-domain bits
idea: Invert 'storage elements are fabricated in a fab' -> grow them. Magnetotactic bacteria biomineralize near-perfect 40-50 nm single-domain magnetite crystals at room temperature from iron salts; purified magnetosomes are placed by DNA-origami or field-guided assembly onto glass carrying spin-orbit-torque write lines and Hall read contacts.

title: Self-healing traps: on-die microheaters anneal leakage defects in the field
idea: Inverts 'aging only makes leakage worse': embed a deuterium-loaded SiN reservoir and a TiN microheater per mat; in scheduled idle windows (data migrated to a spare mat) heat the mat for milliseconds so deuterium diffuses to and passivates the dangling-bond traps that cause trap-assisted junction leakage, resetting the retention tail.
note: Millisecond heating too short for D diffusion to traps; local heat disturbs neighbours; on-chip heater self-healing (Macronix) is prior art.

title: Dithered stochastic-resonance voting for weak, leaky cells
idea: Inverting 'noise must be suppressed': during refresh and retry reads a small auxiliary comparator samples the held bitline 8 times with an injected calibrated dither and majority-votes, then forces the main latch, so cells left with only ~1/3 of nominal charge still read correctly.
note: Dither plus voting averages out noise, not comparator offset or lost cell charge.

title: Each cell is its own sense amp: stacked oxide latches
idea: Inverting 'storage and amplification are separate': each bit is a 4-transistor cross-coupled latch of n-IGZO and p-SnO thin-film transistors stacked in 8 BEOL tiers, so the cell itself drives the bitline rail-to-rail and per-bitline sense amps shrink to one shared buffer per 256 columns.

title: Phase-encoded parametron cells read by frequency multiplexing
idea: Inverting 'every bit needs its own wire to a sense amp': bits are the 0 or pi phase of parametrically pumped nanomechanical resonators, each tuned to a distinct frequency, so one shared readout line and one phase-detecting receiver demodulate 32 cells at once.

title: Compressed-sensing reads via random multi-row current sums
idea: Inverting 'each bit is sensed individually': in capacitorless FeFET NOR columns, 16 random-pattern wordline combinations are activated and the summed bitline currents go to a 4-bit ADC, from which sparse 64-cell groups (mostly zeros, as in activations and zero pages) are reconstructed.
note: Relies on FeFET columns lacking DRAM endurance; ADC cost offsets savings.

title: Hexagonal three-axis lattice: select cells by two of three lines
idea: Inverts 'arrays are square grids addressed by row and column.' Pack vertical pillars in a hexagonal lattice crossed by three line directions at 60 degrees and select a cell by coincidence of any two lines, packing ~13% denser and giving a spare addressing path around a broken line.
note: Two-of-three coincidence needs a two-input cell, inconsistent with one-transistor density claims.

title: FeCl3-intercalated graphene buried wordlines replace tungsten
idea: Inverts 'buried wordlines are tungsten.' Grow multilayer graphene in the wordline trench by plasma CVD and intercalate FeCl3 to bring resistivity to a few uOhm-cm, competitive with size-degraded W at 10 nm widths, using only C, Fe and Cl.

title: Wordline-last: aluminum replaces tungsten after all hot steps
idea: Inverts 'buried wordlines are formed early, so they must be refractory tungsten': form a sacrificial poly-Si/SiN buried wordline, finish capacitors and every >450 C anneal, then exhume the sacrificial line through a slot and refill it with high-pressure reflowed aluminum on a thin TiN barrier (replacement-metal-gate logic applied to the DRAM array).

title: Thin-film iron flux rings: core memory reborn at nanoscale
idea: Inverts 'core memory is obsolete': pattern ~60 nm Fe-Si alloy nanorings that hold clockwise or counterclockwise flux-closure states, switch them by current through a central post, and read them by the voltage spike induced in a sense line on switching (destructive read with write-back), as ferrite cores did.

title: Iron spin-crossover molecules as electrically switched bistable bits
idea: Inverts 'memory materials must be inorganic crystals made in vacuum tools': use iron(II) spin-crossover complexes (Fe, N, C, H) with room-temperature hysteresis, switched between high- and low-spin states by field-induced ligand distortion and read by their volume and conductance change in a crossbar.

title: Relax overlay budgets, ship imperfect arrays, remap at boot
idea: Inverts 'memory must leave the fab perfect'. Loosen the storage-node-to-landing-pad overlay spec ~2x so scanners use fewer alignment marks and rework drops; each 512-row subarray carries ~6% spare columns plus a tiny CAM that the controller fills at power-on from a self-test, remapping bad cells at 64-bit granularity like a flash translation layer.
note: Overlay error is systematic across fields, not random; spare columns cannot absorb it.

title: Power-and-signal superposed TSVs carry DC plus data
idea: Invert 'power and signal need separate vias': each supply TSV carries DC current with a small AC data signal superimposed, separated on each die by an on-die bias-tee (MIM capacitor plus active current source), so power TSVs double as data lanes.

title: Cast-mono solar silicon substrates for error-tolerant DRAM wafers
idea: Inverts 'DRAM needs prime CZ wafers from high-purity quartz crucibles': use cast-mono silicon from the solar industry, polished and given gettering layers; the extra leakage-tail cells from metals and dislocations fall within the 1% cell budget.

title: Qualify lower-purity gases and chemicals to break supplier chokepoints
idea: Inverts '9N purity everywhere': qualify 6N-7N process gases, wet chemicals and argon/nitrogen substitutes for helium in non-gate steps; trace contamination adds isolated leaky cells, which the 1% budget absorbs.

title: Order-disorder molecular-rotor ferroelectric printed below 150 C
idea: Print a molecular ferroelectric (diisopropylammonium bromide or imidazolium perchlorate class, Pr 10-20 uC/cm2, Tc >400 K) as the final tier. Polarization comes from whole cationic dipoles rotating in place rather than ions hopping through vacancies, and ~1 V pulses write it.

title: Varactor-state cell read by reactance without removing charge
idea: Store the bit on a MOS capacitor biased so '1' is accumulation (high C) and '0' depletion (low C); read with a small AC probe through the access device and measure the reactance in a bridge, which moves no net charge off the cell. Measuring a reactive parameter costs ~zero dissipated energy in the ideal limit.
note: Reactance read of floating varactor node through access device still exchanges charge; per-cell AC readout costly.

title: Negative-capacitance ferroelectric gate gives sense pair internal gain
idea: Add a thin HZO negative-capacitance layer in the gate stack of the sense amplifier's input pair so the internal channel potential swings more than the bitline (body factor < 1), amplifying a 50 mV signal ~2x before the latch fires.

title: Plywood memory: laminate 100 printed DRAM foils with edge microvias
idea: Test each 25 um printed DRAM foil, laminate 100 known-good foils with B-stage adhesive, then UV-laser drill and silver-paste fill vias through a peripheral via field to a shared bus, with each foil carrying a printed tier-select switch.

title: Spiral-wound memory foil around a silicon logic spindle
idea: Wind a 10 m x 5 cm printed DRAM foil around a 1 cm logic core like a film capacitor, Schoop-spray metal onto the roll's end faces for power and plate, and route signals to pads along the foil's top edge, which land in a spiral pattern mated by an end cap.

title: Superconformal electroplated copper wordline tiers replace tungsten in 3D stacks
idea: Tungsten replacement gates in 3D stacks need ~25-30 nm tiers for acceptable resistance; Cu's resistivity is ~3x lower, so bottom-up electroplating with suppressor/accelerator additives fills ~12 nm tier cavities through the slit, using a ~1 nm self-forming MnSiO3 barrier.
note: Cu size-effect resistivity at 12 nm erodes the advantage; lateral plating fill through slits is unproven.

title: Debondable hybrid-bond layer lets you swap the bad HBM tier
idea: First principle: stack yield falls as y^n because one bad die kills the stack; if the bond is reversible, a failure costs one die instead. Bond Cu pads through a thin indium or Sn-Bi interlayer, with a dielectric that softens near 200 C, so a stack with one failed die is locally reheated, split and rebonded with a known-good die.

title: Liquid-metal microbumps make memory stacks hot-swappable
idea: First principle: solder joints are permanent because they solidify, while gallium-indium-tin eutectic stays liquid above ~11 C and wets only treated pads. Connect DRAM dies to a base die through Galinstan-filled micro-wells sealed by a polymer gasket and held by a mechanical clamp, so dies can be pulled, tested and replaced at room temperature.

title: Roll-to-roll printed ferroelectric polymer read-mostly memory tier
idea: Read-mostly data (embedding tables, checkpoints, search indexes) needs few writes, so 1e7-1e8 cycles of endurance is enough. Gravure-print ferroelectric-diode crossbars from a P(VDF-TrFE):semiconductor blend, which gives a non-destructive resistive read, onto PET film at roll-to-roll speed, and laminate many films into a stack.

title: CCD bucket-brigade memory where moving data is storing it
idea: A CCD keeps charge packets with no contact or transistor per bit and moves them by clock phases, so the cell is only gates (~4F^2) and access is the movement itself. Build circulating CCD loops in depreciated image-sensor fabs with a regenerating sense stage per loop, holding 3-4 bits per packet thanks to few-electron read noise.

title: Vertical nanographite contacts replace tungsten and cobalt plugs
idea: In narrow plugs, metal resistivity is dominated by surface and grain-boundary scattering plus barrier volume, while vertically oriented graphene sheets conduct in-plane along the plug with no barrier. Grow carbon nanowall contacts by catalyst-free ~400 C PECVD inside contact holes and dope them by FeCl3 intercalation (Fe, Cl, C only).

title: Thermos flask: vacuum-isolated node behind a zero-leakage nanorelay
idea: Stimulus 'thermos' (vacuum stops heat leaking) -> replace the access transistor with an electrostatic nanorelay whose contact opens a 5 nm vacuum gap, and wrap the storage node in a sealed vacuum cavity, so the off path has no semiconductor junction or channel to leak through. Stored charge decays only by field emission across the gap, negligible at 1 V.
note: Relay contact endurance is far below DRAM's ~1e15 accesses.

title: Rubik's cube: octahedral-rotation pattern sets polarization, improper ferroelectric
idea: Stimulus 'Rubik's cube' (twist one block, the whole face changes) -> a hybrid improper ferroelectric (Ca3Ti2O7-type) whose polarization is a by-product of two oxygen-octahedra rotation patterns; switching one rotation flips P at low field with domain walls that do not pin. The film is the storage capacitor in a 1T1C or gain-cell read.
note: Ca3Ti2O7 needs epitaxy above BEOL budget; coercive field not clearly lower.

title: Origami scroll: self-rolling nanoscroll capacitor released by plain water
idea: Stimulus 'paper scroll' -> deposit a flat, strain-graded TiN/Al2O3/TiN stack on a water-soluble GeO2 sacrificial layer; dissolving the GeO2 in DI water (instead of HF) lets built-in strain roll the stack into a ~10-turn, ~100 nm diameter nanoscroll over its contact, giving pillar-class electrode area from planar deposition.
note: 100 nm scrolls are far larger than DRAM cell pitch.

title: Photo film: silver-bromide latent-image speck as an atom-scale bit
idea: Stimulus 'silver-halide film' -> a 10 nm AgBr nanocrystal between two electrodes: an electron pulse nucleates a 4-atom Ag cluster (the photographic latent image) at a sensitivity site, making the crystal tunnel-conductive; an oxidizing pulse dissolves it. Bromide chemistry, no fluorine.

title: Sandpaper-free planarization by gas-cluster ion beams
idea: Random stimulus 'sandpaper': smoothing without grit. Planarize the array STI fill, wordline cap and landing-pad layers with gas-cluster ion beam (GCIB) location-specific smoothing driven by in-line topography maps, replacing CMP, its slurry and the post-CMP brush/megasonic cleans.

title: Regenerative brakes: LC-resonant wordline drive returns wordline charge
idea: Like a hybrid car's brakes refilling the battery, connect the selected wordline through its driver to a bank-level spiral inductor so it swings to ~3 V resonantly from a tank capacitor, and on close let the charge ring back into the tank instead of dumping it to ground; the ~30%-efficient charge pump then only tops up losses.
note: Wordline RC kills Q; 0.05 mm2 spiral gives far too little L for ns edges.

title: Tree rings: concentric ALD shells store three bits per hole
idea: Like growth rings in a trunk, fill one wide high-AR hole with alternating storage and plate shells (TiN/ZrO2/TiN/ZrO2/TiN...). Each storage shell surfaces at a different radius on a terraced top and wires to its own access transistor, so one etched hole holds 2-3 coaxial capacitors.
note: Inner shells shrink, terraced contacts hard; net bits per area unclear.

title: Venetian blinds: slanted overlapping plate capacitors cut by angled ion beam
idea: Blind slats overlap one another: angled ion-beam etching at 45-60 degrees cuts slanted trenches so each cell's plate capacitor leans over its neighbors' footprint like overlapping slats. Plate area reaches 3-4x the cell footprint with only a ~20:1 vertical etch.
note: Angled IBE at 20:1 in oxide is immature and the geometric area gain from leaning plates is marginal.

title: Elevator counterweight: two tiers in series voltage domains recycle charge
idea: A counterweight falls as the car rises: run two cell tiers (or two stacked dies) in series voltage domains, the lower array between ground and mid-rail and the upper between mid-rail and supply, so the charge one tier dumps during precharge and restore becomes the supply charge of the other. A small on-die balancing regulator absorbs mismatch, and external rails and the interface stay standard.

title: Pencil lead: intercalated graphite buried wordlines replace tungsten
idea: Stimulus 'pencil lead' -> graphite is the ultimate abundant conductor once doped. Fill the buried-wordline trench with CVD nanographite grown from CH4 on a thin Ni/Cu catalyst, then intercalate FeCl3 or Br2 so in-plane resistivity approaches ~5-10 uOhm-cm with basal planes aligned along the line.

title: Traffic light: three-wavelength resist prints three self-aligned levels per coat
idea: Random stimulus 'traffic light' (three colors, one pole) -> a resist with three photoacid systems is tuned to 365, 248 and 193 nm. One coat is exposed through three masks and developed once into three-level topography, which transfers into a self-aligned contact, bitline and landing pad sequence.

title: Abacus beads: bistable NEMS cells made in DLP-style MEMS fabs
idea: Random stimulus 'abacus' (beads flip between two stable sides) -> each bit is a nanoscale torsion paddle latched in one of two tilted states by electrostatic hold and stiction-free landing tips, the way TI's DLP micromirror is, read capacitively. It is built by sacrificial-release processing in existing U.S. 200 mm MEMS fabs.

title: Watercolor wash: printed analog crossbar on glass computes edge weights
idea: Watercolour is painted at room temperature: solution-process perovskite or organic memristor crossbars (<150 C) on glass, program model weights as conductances and compute matrix-vector products in place for small edge models, so devices ship with no DRAM for weights.

title: Stethoscope: ultrasonic bulk-acoustic links replace TSVs vertically
idea: From the 'stethoscope': ScAlN piezo transducers on each thinned die launch GHz bulk acoustic pulses straight through the stack, and each tier listens with a resonator tuned to its own frequency (acoustic FDM). Vertical signaling then needs no copper via.

title: Magnifying glass: 1310 nm optical vias pass light through silicon
idea: Silicon is transparent at 1310 nm, so stacked dies signal vertically through the bulk with bonded micro-emitters, backside diffractive (Fresnel) lenses that focus the beam like a magnifying glass, and Ge photodiodes on the tier above.

title: Par-baked bread: bank array-complete wafers, finish BEOL to order
idea: Random stimulus 'par-baked bread' -> bake 80%, finish on demand. Wafers are stopped after the capacitor module and banked in N2 stockers; product-defining metal layers, fuses and test decide DDR5, LPDDR5X or HBM core die when orders arrive.
note: DDR5, LPDDR and HBM core dies differ in array and periphery layout, limiting late binding.

title: VO2 bistable inside its thermal hysteresis, erased by piezo-AlN strain
idea: Box = {medium: metallic vs insulating phase of VO2 held inside its hysteresis loop at a 65 C die temperature | access: Si FET | sense: ~100x resistance ratio | integration: VO2 on a piezoelectric AlN underlayer | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: sputtered VO2 from Utah vanadium}. A Joule pulse writes the metallic phase, and a strain pulse from the AlN underlayer shifts the transition temperature above the die temperature so the cell snaps back to insulating; at idle both phases are stable with no power.
note: Narrow film hysteresis cannot tolerate die temperature swings.

title: Ferroelectric domain-wall channel written only during row access
idea: Box: MIM cap x thin-film LiNbO3 where a conducting charged domain wall is nucleated between storage and bitline electrodes x SA x bonded-oxide tier x LNOI wafer x ion-slice bonding. Writing the wall opens a metallic path; erasing it leaves a ~4 eV insulator, so off-state leakage is that of bulk LiNbO3.

title: One shallow p+ pinning implant mask ends storage-node surface leakage
idea: Box: standard cap x standard access x standard SA x in-array x Si x exactly one added implant mask. Borrowing the image-sensor pinned photodiode, a shallow p+ layer over the exposed storage-node diffusion pins the Si/SiO2 interface in hole accumulation so its interface states stop generating current.
note: p+ cap on n+ storage diffusion forms a high-field junction that may raise BTBT leakage.

title: Aerogel thermal break keeps HBM DRAM cores 15C cooler
idea: Box: standard HBM core dies x standard access x standard sense x silica-aerogel or porous-polymer layer between hot logic base die and core stack, with logic heat routed through dedicated copper thermal TSVs to the lid x package x Si x zero masks. Core dies then sit near cold-plate temperature instead of the logic hotspot.

title: Three-transistor single-ended sense amp with 60 mV offset accepted
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x single-ended skewed-inverter sensing x minimum-size SA x bulk Si x standard. The 8-10 transistor cross-coupled, equalized SA becomes a precharged skewed inverter plus a restore transistor that tolerates ~60 mV offset, so ~1% of bits mis-sense and are fixed downstream.
note: 1% mis-sense with destructive restore corrupts cells; heavy ECC overhead.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching carves 150:1 silicon capacitor trenches
idea: Box [MIS trench cap in bulk Si | vertical Si access | voltage SA | revived trench-capacitor 1T1C | CZ Si | NIL-patterned electroless Ag mesh + HF/H2O2 metal-assisted chemical etch]: the Ag catalyst sinks vertically in the HF/H2O2 bath, cutting 30 nm holes at >150:1 aspect ratio with no plasma; the holes are then lined with ALD dielectric and doped poly.
note: MacEtch reaches high AR, but Ag contamination is a retention killer and catalyst wander hurts uniformity.

title: Electroplated NiFe/Cu multilayer nanowires as cobalt-free magnetic RAM
idea: Box [NiFe/Cu/NiFe CPP-GMR pseudo-spin-valve | Si access transistor | resistive sense at ~10-15% GMR | BEOL vias as templates | Si | pulsed single-bath electrodeposition]: alternate the plating potential to stack ferromagnetic and spacer layers inside 20 nm vias and switch the soft layer by spin-transfer torque.
note: Low GMR and STT switching in plated stacks.

title: Atmospheric spatial-ALD tools for capacitor high-k without vacuum chambers
idea: Box: ZrO2/Al2O3/ZrO2 capacitor charge x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x 300 mm Si x spatial ALD. Wafers rotate under gas-bearing heads with separated precursor and oxidant zones at atmospheric pressure, so growth rate is decoupled from purge time; pressure-pulsed dwell zones let precursor diffuse to the bottom of 70:1 holes before the wafer moves on.
note: Step coverage at 70:1 with fast spatial ALD is the key doubt.

title: Inductively coupled stack powered wirelessly: no TSV, no plating
idea: Box: DRAM x standard x on-die coil receivers x inductive data links plus resonant wireless power through 15 um dies x dry-plasma-thinned Si x laminated dry-film adhesive stack. Dies are glued with dry film, data crosses via coil pairs and power via a per-die resonant transformer, so TSV etch, Cu plating, CMP and their rinses disappear.
note: Inductive data links known (ThruChip); wireless power efficiency is the killer.

title: Deliberately weakened sentinel cell per row triggers refresh
idea: Box [medium: capacitor + 60%-size sentinel capacitor | access: planar | sense: sentinel comparator at high reference | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk Si | fab: DUV]. Each row carries one intentionally weak sentinel written '1' at every refresh; every activation and a low-energy idle sweep of only the sentinel column check it, and a decayed sentinel triggers that row's refresh, so each row is refreshed on its own physical clock.
note: Tail cells are random per cell, so one sentinel per row may not track the row's weakest cell.

title: Co-aged reference cells cancel drift in printed ionic memory
idea: Box [medium: proton-intercalation WO3 ionic cell | access: printed organic diode | sense: ratiometric current | integration: 3D printed tiers | substrate: polymer foil | fab: inkjet printing]. Every row write also writes four reference cells to known levels at the same instant so they age identically; reads compare each data cell against interpolated co-aged references, cancelling time and temperature drift.
note: Printed ionic cells far from 10-100 ns.

title: Po: every bit is a battery — electromotive-force readout micro-cells
idea: Po: every bit is a battery. Extracted: each crossbar crossing is a sputtered solid-state sodium micro-cell (iron-phosphate cathode, no cobalt); the bit is its open-circuit voltage (4 levels = 2 bits), read potentiometrically at near-zero current (non-destructive) and written with an nA charge pulse.
note: us-ms writes and finite cycle life put it outside DRAM class.

title: Po: memory grown by bacteria — magnetosome dipole-chain shift registers
idea: Po: memory is grown by bacteria. Extracted: culture magnetotactic bacteria for uniform 40 nm magnetite crystals, deposit them field-aligned in imprinted grooves, and let dipolar coupling plus a global rotating clock field shift bits along each chain (nanomagnet-logic style), with a few MTJ heads per chain.

title: Po: a thermometer stuck halfway — spin-crossover molecular bits
idea: Po: a thermometer stuck halfway. Extracted: hold an iron-triazole spin-crossover film (solution-synthesised by the kg, hysteresis ~345-385 K) at ~365 K inside its loop; a Joule pulse switches a cell to high-spin, a piezo pressure pulse switches it back (low-spin is ~10% smaller), and the conductance/permittivity difference is read.
note: Microsecond-millisecond switching and per-cell piezo reset rule out DRAM class.

title: Resonant charge-recycling refresh through on-package LC tank
idea: Po: refresh pays for itself. During refresh bursts, bitline and wordline charge is swung adiabatically by a resonant inductor-capacitor tank (inductor built into the interposer) instead of being dumped to ground, so energy spent restoring one row is mostly recovered into the next row's precharge.
note: Off-die inductor cannot reach distributed bitline nodes; equalization already recycles half the charge.

title: Po: one device is a sense amp — tunnel-diode Goto latch
idea: Po: a sense amplifier made of one device. Replace the ~10-transistor cross-coupled latch with a series Goto pair of resonant/Esaki tunnel diodes per bitline, biased by a clocked supply so the midpoint snaps to one of its two NDR-stable states as set by the few-mV charge-sharing signal; a single pass transistor writes the snapped state back for restore.

title: Po: sense with the transistor DRAM abandoned — lateral Si BJT
idea: Po: a bipolar memory reader. Place a lateral npn preamp pair (boron/phosphorus-doped silicon only, no high-k, no metal gate) at each SA input; BJT Vbe matching (~0.3 mV sigma vs ~5 mV for small MOSFETs) and higher gm resolve millivolt signals before a cheap MOS latch.
note: Base current drains the fC-scale cell signal; lateral BJT at SA pitch.

title: Po: a sense amp with moving parts — bistable Si nanobeam
idea: Po: a sense amplifier with moving parts. A buckled, bistable single-crystal Si nanobeam (~200 nm long) sits between electrodes tied to the bitline pair; the differential tips it into one well, where it mechanically latches and touches a restore electrode, giving zero leakage and zero standby power.

title: Po: gain from a negative capacitor — ZrO2 NC input pair
idea: Po: a transistor whose gate amplifies before its channel does. Insert a stabilized ferroelectric ZrO2 layer (Zr is abundant; no Hf) in series with the SA input-pair gate oxide, capacitance-matched so negative capacitance gives ~2x internal voltage gain and sub-60 mV/decade turn-on.

title: Roll-to-roll oxide-TFT DRAM sheets laminated into thick stacks
idea: Po: memory is sold by the metre like tape. Sputter and nanoimprint oxide-TFT plus capacitor arrays roll-to-roll on 10 um polished metal foil at <300 C, then laminate 50-200 sheets with anisotropic conductive film and laser-drilled vertical bitline vias, the way multilayer ceramic capacitors stack 1000 layers.
note: Same as I-02020; MLCC-style lamination of TFT sheets; ~100 nm F limits density.

title: Ultra-wide-bandgap gallium-oxide vertical channels through every tier
idea: Po: the transistor is an insulator that occasionally conducts. Use ALD Ga2O3 (Eg ~4.8 eV, no hole conduction so no GIDL path) as a junctionless, fully depleted vertical access channel through each 3D tier; thermal generation scales as exp(-Eg/2kT), pushing off-current orders of magnitude below oxide channels like IGZO.

title: Loadless leakage-ratio latch stacked in oxide TFT tiers
idea: Po: the leak holds the bit instead of stealing it. Stack a 4-transistor loadless latch (n-type oxide drivers, p-type SnO or Te access-loads) in two monolithic tiers sized so p-load off-current exceeds n-driver off-current >10x; leakage itself pulls each node toward its stored state, so the cell is static and needs no refresh.
note: Same leakage-ratio latch in oxide TFTs; weak p-type oxides make the ratio fragile across variation.

title: Po DRAM on dirty silicon: metallurgical substrate plus thick epi
