idea: Po: 'DRAM is built on dirty silicon.' Extracted: use cheap upgraded-metallurgical-grade (~5N) cast silicon as a mechanical substrate, add a heavily doped gettering and diffusion-barrier buried layer, then grow a thick epitaxial device layer from electronic-grade trichlorosilane, so only the top ~10 um needs 11N purity.
note: Metal out-diffusion from UMG substrate would wreck the DRAM retention tail; substrate is a small cost share.

title: Millimetre-wave backscatter antennas on each DRAM die
idea: Po: the memory answers without speaking. One top-metal mask adds a small antenna per die; the GPU floods the package cavity with a 140 GHz carrier and each die returns read data by switching its antenna load with a single transistor, RFID-style.

title: Self-assembling copolymer wires quadruple interposer wiring density
idea: Po: wires draw themselves. One coarse guide mask sets trenches on the interposer, and a block-copolymer film self-assembles inside them into 4x finer lines that become copper wires after pattern transfer and plating.
note: BCP domain sizes are tens of nm, mismatched to micron interposer lines.

title: Printed oxide-TFT glass interposer performs die and bank selection
idea: Worse: repeat chip-select, rank and bank-group muxing logic inside every DRAM die and buffer chip. Flip: build a glass-panel interposer with inkjet-printed oxide TFT switches that set, per page epoch, which of dozens of simple array dies drive each high-speed lane, consolidating selection periphery into one cheap printed layer.

title: Wedge-polished ramp exposes all tiers to one contact mask
idea: Worse: build the staircase with one resist-trim/etch cycle per tier pair so contact cost grows linearly with tiers. Flip: taper a narrow band at the array edge to a ~5 degree ramp with angled CMP or ion-beam polishing, exposing every tier as a ~0.5 um stripe on the slope, then land all tier contacts with a single DUV mask.

title: Copper buried wordlines with self-forming manganese silicate barrier
idea: Worsen: fill every buried wordline, plug and contact with CVD tungsten from Chinese ore via WF6. Flip: fill the buried-channel wordline trench with electroplated Cu-Mn alloy that anneals into a self-forming MnSiOx barrier a few nm thick, capped with graphene against electromigration, so neither W nor a thick TiN liner is needed.

title: On-die microheater anneals heal aging access transistors in field
idea: Worsen: let BTI and hot-carrier damage pile up in access transistors until retention fails and the DIMM is scrapped. Flip: build in polysilicon microheaters, or use wordline Joule heating during scheduled maintenance windows, to anneal a bank locally at ~250-300 C and re-passivate traps, restoring the leakage tail.

title: Blacksmith's temper: martensite variant bit in NiTi nanopillars
idea: A blacksmith keeps memory in the crystal structure of steel. In a NiTi or Cu-Al-Ni nanopillar, a short voltage and heat pulse selects one of two martensite twin variants (ferroelastic switching); the variant is read through piezoresistance or the strain-coupled threshold shift of an attached transistor.
note: Duplicate of martensite-variant storage; electrical variant selection in NiTi is weak.

title: Namib fog beetle: area-selective evaporated molecular ferroelectric dots
idea: The Namib beetle collects water only on the bumps of its back. Patterned nucleation spots make a molecular ferroelectric (diisopropylammonium bromide class: order-disorder cations, Pr ~20 uC/cm2, Tc >420 K) condense from vapor only where cells sit, so the storage layer never needs lithography, etch or clean.

title: Adobe brick builder: GaN polarization 2DEG node, implant-isolated, no etch
idea: An adobe builder makes walls from sun-dried earth with almost no water. Store charge in an AlGaN/GaN polarization-induced 2DEG pocket under a floating gate, and isolate neighbouring cells with a nitrogen implant that kills the 2DEG instead of etching mesas. The planar epi stack then needs no etch, clean or CMP.

title: Electrician's circuit breaker: NbO2 threshold film in the access source
idea: A breaker stays open until demand trips it. A thin NbO2 insulator-metal-transition film sits in series with each access transistor's source contact: it stays insulating, blocking subthreshold leakage, until the low-Vt transistor is driven, then snaps metallic, giving an effectively steep slope so the wordline can swing ~1 V.
note: Hyper-FET known; NbO2 off-resistance far too low for fA retention.

title: Piano tuner's touch: per-cell threshold trim eliminates the wordline pump
idea: A piano tuner adjusts every string. At final test, a thin charge-trap layer in each access transistor's gate stack is programmed by Fowler-Nordheim pulses to center its threshold within +/-15 mV, collapsing the variation margin that forces VPP to ~3 V; the wordline then runs at VDD (1.1 V) directly, with no charge pump.
note: VPP is set by passing full VDD through a high-Vt NMOS, not only Vt spread; trapped charge drifts under wordline cycling.

title: Sculptor's lost-wax casting: inverse-opal sponge capacitor electrodes
idea: Self-assemble 30-50 nm silica spheres into a colloidal crystal as the wax, fill the gaps with TiN or Ru by ALD or electrodeposition, then dissolve the spheres in HF. Coat the interconnected metal sponge with ALD high-k and a top electrode.

title: Shepherd's herding dog: dielectrophoretic placement of nanowire access transistors
idea: A sheepdog drives sheep into pens. Grow doped core-shell Si nanowire transistors in bulk in a tube furnace, suspend them in liquid, and use AC dielectrophoresis on electrode pairs to herd one wire onto each site of a pre-built capacitor array.
note: One-wire-per-site DEP at tens-of-nm pitch with DRAM-grade yield is far beyond demonstrated assembly.

title: Plumber lines copper wordlines with a self-forming manganese barrier
idea: Persona: a plumber who lines ordinary copper pipe instead of buying exotic pipe. Fill buried-wordline trenches with Cu-2%Mn alloy. On anneal, the Mn migrates to the dielectric interface and forms a ~1.5 nm MnSiOx diffusion barrier, so no thick TiN/W stack is needed and copper fills the whole trench.
note: Copper beside the access-transistor gate risks contamination and must survive later thermal steps.

title: Meteorite-collecting alien builds MRAM from cosmic iron-nickel
idea: Persona: an alien who knows meteorites. Use tetrataenite (L1_0-ordered FeNi, Ku ~1 MJ/m3) as the perpendicular free and reference layers of MTJ cells. Make it on-wafer by nitrogen insertion and topotactic extraction (FeNiN to FeNi), forcing the ordering that nature needs millions of years to reach.

title: Child at the beach: sand-memory shadow behind every DRAM cell
idea: Persona: a child who makes a backup of the sandcastle. Pair each 1T1C cell with a tiny silicon-rich SiOx resistive element on its storage-node contact. The element is written only at power-down, copying the charge state into a filament, and read back at power-up, so it needs thousands of cycles, not 1e16.
note: Cell charge cannot form a filament; per-cell write drivers inflate area.

title: Child's Shrinky Dinks: implosion-fabricated nanoimprint master templates
idea: A child shrinks drawings in the oven. Write the template pattern at 10x scale with a cheap laser into an expanded hydrogel, deposit metal or oxide into the written voxels, then dehydrate so the gel shrinks ~10x isotropically to sub-20 nm features, and use the shrunken part as a master for nanoimprint templates.
note: Hydrogel implosion variant of write-large-then-shrink mastering.

title: 2050 atomic inkjet: maskless spatial-ALD print heads write periphery wiring
idea: A 2050 engineer prints atoms like ink. Micro-nozzle spatial-ALD heads confine precursors and a local micro-plasma in a ~10 um gap to deposit oxide and metal only where the head passes, writing periphery wiring and pads (~1-5 um lines) directly at <=250 C with no mask, resist or etch.

title: Biologist's bloodstream: data riding on the stack's power rails
idea: Blood carries oxygen and nutrients in one vessel, so superimpose low-swing, high-frequency data (5-20 GHz OFDM tones) on the HBM power and ground TSVs, which already make up ~50% of TSVs, with on-die LC filters to separate the two.
note: Decoupling capacitance shunts high-frequency data; LC isolation costs area.

title: Alien sees silicon as glass: through-die infrared vertical links
idea: To an alien eye silicon is transparent at 1310 nm. Stack thinned dies with no TSVs and talk vertically with Ge-on-Si micro-photodiodes and tiny modulated emitters or reflectors aimed straight through the silicon bulk, with alignment set by bonding registration.
note: BEOL metal is opaque and silicon lacks efficient emitters; needs optical windows and bonded III-V or external light.

title: Firefighter's bucket brigade: charge-domain CCD data bus on interposer
idea: A bucket brigade passes water hand to hand: move bits across the interposer as packets of charge clocked through CCD-like transfer gates, like a camera readout, instead of charging full wires to rail.
note: Transfer-gate clocking still pays CV^2; transfer inefficiency over cm-scale buses is severe.

title: Nanobattery voltage-mode bit read potentiometrically, signal independent of size
idea: EV battery managers read cell voltage, not charge; likewise each bit is a solid-state micro-battery (LixTiO2/LiPON-like stack) whose open-circuit voltage differs by ~0.3 V between states, sensed by a high-impedance FET gate. A battery's voltage does not shrink with its area, so the read signal survives scaling where capacitor charge does not.
note: Size-independent OCV signal is a nice insight; ion kinetics and cycling remain.

title: VO2 thermal-hysteresis bit held at hot-water-cooled datacenter temperature
idea: Hot-water-cooled racks run silicon at ~60-65C, inside VO2's insulator-metal hysteresis loop; at that bias temperature a nano-island is bistable, set metallic by a short Joule pulse and reset by a field or cooling pulse, and read by its 100-1000x resistance contrast. The extreme cooling regime itself becomes the storage mechanism.
note: Chip-wide temperature holding and thermal crosstalk undermine bistability.

title: MOS-varactor storage node read nondestructively by RF capacitance sensing
idea: KV caches read each bit thousands of times, so one added implant mask converts the storage node into a depletion-type MOS varactor whose capacitance depends on its stored voltage; a small high-frequency probe on the plate senses that capacitance via the bitline without draining charge. Writes stay conventional; reads stop being destructive.

title: Ferroelectric back-gate trim cancels sense-amp offset for 30 years
idea: For 30-year industrial controllers that can never be replaced, each SA transistor pair gets an HZO back-gate whose polarization stores a per-SA threshold trim, programmed at wafer test and re-tuned in the field by a BIST that measures offset. Static mismatch and slow NBTI drift are both nulled.

title: Frequency-multiplexed wordline group select borrowed from MKID astronomy arrays
idea: MKID cameras read thousands of detectors on one feedline by giving each a unique resonance; each wordline group taps a shared global line through a passive high-Q LC notch tuned to its own frequency, and a tone burst on the line selects that group. Global predecoder wiring collapses to one line per bank.

title: Coincident half-pulse wordline select borrowed from Apollo core memory
idea: Core memories selected a bit where two half-currents met; two half-amplitude pulses launched from opposite ends of a bank-wide transmission line meet at a sub-array chosen by their relative delay, and only there does the sum exceed the local access threshold. Local decoders vanish.

title: Chlorine-etchable alumina interlayer stack replaces fluorocarbon oxide etch
idea: Extreme user: 200C downhole tools that need high thermal conductivity. Swap SiO2/SiN interlayer, spacer and support films for Al2O3, AlN and ZrO2 stacks that etch cleanly in BCl3/Cl2 plasma and atomic-layer etch, removing every fluorocarbon oxide-etch step.

title: Reactor-style self-anneal: on-die heaters heal leakage-tail traps
idea: Radiation-damaged detectors and fusion-reactor sensors are recovered by thermal annealing. Embed polysilicon heater lines in the periphery stripes of each bank. During a scheduled window, after the bank's data has been migrated away, the heaters hold the array at ~250 C for minutes to passivate the interface and oxide traps that create GIDL and VRT tail cells. An on-die tail monitor decides when a bank needs annealing.
note: Holding one bank at 250 C while neighbors operate is thermally implausible on a single die.

title: Transferred single-crystal SrTiO3 membrane as cell dielectric
idea: Scale shift across wafers: grow epitaxial SrTiO3 (k~300) on a sacrificial Sr3Al2O6 layer on a donor wafer at 800 C, release and transfer the membrane onto the low-temperature DRAM BEOL, then pattern stacked planar capacitors in it.
note: Transferred membrane is planar only; planar 5 fF at DRAM pitch needs k in thousands.

title: Thermostat-held VO2 phase bits in hysteresis window
idea: Couple chip and datacenter scales: hold the die by liquid cooling at the middle of a W-doped VO2 thermal hysteresis window, where both metal and insulator phases are stable; Joule pulses set metal and Peltier micro-coolers reset insulator.

title: Wordline Joule self-annealing heals the retention tail yearly
idea: Time shift from a one-time fab anneal to in-field anneals every year, and scale shift to a single row: in maintenance windows the controller drives DC current along selected buried wordlines (small potential difference between both ends) to heat the access region locally to ~250-300 C for milliseconds, annealing the metastable defects behind VRT cells found by retention profiling.

title: Copper buried wordline with self-forming manganese silicate barrier
idea: Scale shift of a BEOL interconnect trick (um) into the ~10 nm buried-wordline trench, plus a time shift in row cycle: fill with CuMn alloy and anneal so Mn diffuses to the SiO2 liner and forms a ~1 nm self-aligned MnSiOx barrier, replacing TiN/W fill and avoiding TaN; the lower RC shortens every refresh row activation.
note: Cu next to the access channel is a contamination risk; size-effect resistivity at 10 nm.

title: Millisecond flash anneal grows rutile TiO2 capacitor without ruthenium
idea: Time shift in processing: replace the Ru/RuO2 template normally needed for high-k rutile TiO2 with a ~1 ms flash-lamp or laser anneal that drives as-deposited Al-doped TiO2 on TiN through the anatase-to-rutile transition before the TiN oxidizes, yielding k~80-100.
note: Rutile TiO2 without Ru template hard; small gap raises capacitor leakage.

title: Epitaxial CaF2 gate insulator: a crystal, not a glass
idea: Scale shift from amorphous oxide to an atom-by-atom lattice: grow single-crystal CaF2 (lattice-matched to Si within ~0.6%) as the access-transistor gate dielectric so the interface is nearly trap-free and gate tunnelling at ~1 nm EOT is lower than SiO2; fewer interface traps means fewer trap-assisted GIDL and VRT sites.

title: Guard-driven bitline shields borrowed from femtoamp electrometers
idea: Scale the lab electrometer's driven guard down to the bitline: a 2-transistor follower in the bonded CMOS tier drives a shield trace beside each bitline to the bitline's own voltage during charge sharing, so bitline-to-neighbor and bitline-to-plate capacitance sees almost no voltage and stops soaking up signal.

title: Chopper-swapped multi-decision latch averaging beneath offset
idea: Time-slice one read: the isolated SA latch fires 8 times in ~1.5 ns on the same held bitline signal, swapping its inputs on alternate decisions, and a 3-bit counter takes the majority, so fixed offset cancels and noise averages out.
note: Digital majority with swapped inputs cannot cancel offset larger than signal; only noise averages.

title: Plywood memory: laminate 64 pre-tested thin-film array foils
idea: Scale up to the plywood mill: build thin-film array layers on 4-um polyimide over glass carriers at 180-nm rules and test each foil. Laminate known-good foils face-to-face with anisotropic conductive film, whose ~1-um particles form the inter-foil vias, and stack 64 layers.

title: Bevel-lapped staircase: polish a shallow angle to expose every tier
idea: Use a 1960s bevel-and-stain trick as a scale magnifier: mechanically lap the tier stack's edge at ~0.5 degrees, which stretches each 50-nm tier into a ~6-um stripe on the surface, then contact every tier with a single 180-nm litho step.

title: Package cavity as a 300 GHz waveguide for wireless DRAM broadcast
idea: Shift from wires to a millimeter-scale electromagnetic cavity: the sealed metal package lid forms a waveguide, each DRAM die carries an on-chip 300 GHz antenna, requests are broadcast to all dies and replies use frequency slots. Only power needs physical vertical connections.
note: Shared broadcast channel gives far less than HBM bandwidth.

title: Deliberately weakened honeypot rows give early hammer warning
idea: Scale jump (cell -> datacenter security): each bank includes canary rows with intentionally narrowed isolation that flip after ~200 activations of their known neighbors. The controller scrubs canaries every refresh window, and a flip tells it to migrate victims and alert fleet security long before real rows (~1k) fail.
note: Canaries only see hammering of their own neighbors; coverage of arbitrary aggressors unclear.

title: Widrow's memistor revived: thermally gated oxide-ion bit
idea: Widrow's 1960 memistor, copper plated from a liquid electrolyte, died from slowness and liquids. Use a solid oxide-ion conductor (stabilized zirconia, Ea ~1.0-1.1 eV) between mixed-conducting electrodes, with an integrated nanoheater that takes the 20 nm cell to ~700 C during writes: ions move ~1 nm in ~100 ns when hot, while diffusion at 125 C is roughly ten orders of magnitude slower.
note: 700 C per-cell heating: crosstalk, energy and 100 ns writes too slow for DRAM class.

title: TI TSRAM fixed with atomically exact 2D resonant tunneling diodes
idea: TI's tunneling SRAM added two resonant tunneling diodes to a DRAM storage node to make it static. It died on peak-current spread from monolayer thickness fluctuations in III-V barriers, and on standby current. Use graphene/hBN/graphene RTDs, whose barrier is exactly 2 or 3 atomic layers by construction, with valley current engineered to the pA level.

title: Organic TFT bias-stress killer neutralized by DRAM's tiny duty cycle
idea: Plastic Logic and Polymer Vision died partly because organic TFT thresholds drifted under continuous bias stress. A memory access transistor is on for only nanoseconds per refresh period (duty ~1e-7), and the retention bias can be chosen to anneal any drift back out. Print a wide-gap (~3 eV) small-molecule semiconductor whose tiny intrinsic carrier density gives sub-fA off-current.

title: IBM nanotube logic failure recast as printed foil refresh periphery
idea: IBM's carbon-nanotube transistor program stalled because logic needed perfect tube placement and purity. Printed random networks of semiconducting CNTs make p-type TFTs that tolerate that randomness. Paired with printed n-type oxide TFTs, they form complementary circuits on the foil for per-tile sense amplifiers and refresh/ECC controllers next to the oxide access arrays.

title: Nanotube-source vertical transistor leakage fixed with capped-source access
idea: Carbon-nanotube-source vertical organic transistors (the CN-VFET line of startups) died on high off-current that flowed straight through the porous source. Electrodeposit a 5 nm insulating cap selectively on top of the printed nanotube mesh, so carriers inject only at the mesh edges under gate control. The result is a vertical, printable access device whose channel length is a film thickness (~100 nm).

title: Macronix self-healing flash applied: wordline-heater anneal of DRAM leakage tails
idea: Macronix showed around 2012 that flash cells heal when current through the wordline heats them for milliseconds, but never productized it. In 3D DRAM, pulse current through the metal wordlines during scheduled maintenance to heat cells locally to ~350-400C for microseconds. This anneals the trap sites behind the leakage tail and variable retention time.
note: Same wordline-as-heater mechanism; 350-400 C local pulses risk neighbor damage and data loss.

title: Thinfilm's printed memory minus PFAS: croconic-acid ferroelectric crossbars on plastic
idea: Thin Film Electronics' printed memory used PVDF-TrFE, a PFAS-class fluoropolymer, and died at tens of bits per tag on low density and high-voltage switching. Use croconic acid (C5H2O5), a single-molecule organic ferroelectric with ~20 uC/cm2 room-temperature polarization, vapor-deposited below 150 C on PEN film and imprint-patterned into a crossbar with printed ZnO Schottky selectors.
note: Croconic acid films are hard to process; speed, endurance and crossbar disturb unproven.

title: Thinfilm's printed ferroelectric memory scaled by roll-to-roll nanoimprint
idea: Thin Film Electronics' printed P(VDF-TrFE) memory topped out at ~20-36 bits per label because it was screen-printed at ~100 um. Keep the cheap polymer and the roll-to-roll web but pattern crossbars on metallized PET by roll nanoimprint at 50 nm, then laminate 20 sheets into a block wired at its edge to a CMOS controller.
note: Microsecond switching and 1e6-1e8 endurance fail DRAM class.

title: Acoustic delay lines died; AlN ultrasound carries data through stacked dies
idea: Acoustic delay-line memories died of sequential access, yet they proved GHz acoustic waves travel cleanly through solids. Put thin-film AlN bulk-acoustic transducers with Al/TiN electrodes (no Sc or Mo) on each thinned DRAM die so 5-10 GHz acoustic pulses cross the bonded silicon stack vertically, and phase a transducer array per channel to beam-steer to the target tier, giving a TSV-free, wire-free vertical data path.

title: Adesto CBRAM filament randomness pinned by single-nanopore 2D interlayers
idea: CBRAM (Adesto and others) stayed out of dense memory because metal filaments form at random sites, giving wide resistance spread and high-temperature retention loss. Fix: insert a monolayer hBN barrier with exactly one electron-beam or ion-milled nanopore per cell, so the filament always nucleates in the same ~2 nm spot and its neck is mechanically constrained.
note: Per-cell nanopore milling not manufacturable; CBRAM endurance not DRAM-class.

title: Spin-wave bus reads eight nanomagnets with one multiplexed pulse
idea: Effect walk: magnon phase shift. Eight 30-nm nanomagnet bits sit along a CoFeB or garnet spin-wave waveguide, each coupled to a different resonant mode; one broadband spin-wave pulse picks up a bit-dependent phase at each frequency, and a single inductive detector demultiplexes all eight.

title: Through-silicon infrared beams with retro-modulators replace HBM TSVs
idea: Silicon's infrared transparency: the HBM base die holds InP micro-emitters whose 1.3 µm beams pass straight through thinned silicon dies to Ge photodiodes on each memory die (downlink). For the uplink, each memory die modulates the reflection of a base-die beam with an electro-absorption retro-modulator, so the DRAM dies need no lasers.

title: Thin-film Peltier bonding layer chills DRAM tiers above logic
idea: Peltier effect: a Bi2Te3/Sb2Te3 superlattice thermoelectric layer in the bonding stack between logic and DRAM tiers actively pumps heat downward and doubles as a power-distribution plane. The DRAM tiers stay 20-30 K cooler than the logic.
note: Thin-film TEC COP at 20-30 K with logic heat flux is poor; net gain doubtful.

title: LC-resonant paired wordlines recycle charge between adjacent rows
idea: Electrical resonance: adjacent wordlines are paired through a spiral inductor in the bonding layer, so falling-row charge resonantly transfers to the rising row (adiabatic energy recovery) instead of being dumped to ground at each activate.
note: Per-wordline resonance needs ~sub-uH inductors; on-chip spirals cannot fit per row pair.

title: Deep-trench energy-reserve die flushes stacked DRAM to NV tier
idea: Capacitive energy storage as architecture: each memory stack includes one silicon deep-trench capacitor die holding enough energy (~mJ) to copy every DRAM tier into an on-stack ferroelectric or NAND tier over wide internal buses within ms of power loss. The stack keeps DRAM speed and gains non-volatility.
note: mJ reserve is ~1000x short of energy to flush tens of GB to NAND/FeRAM.

title: Resonant-tunneling Goto-pair latch built from silicon and oxide only
idea: Effect: negative differential resistance in two series Si/SiO2 (or Si/CaF2) double-barrier resonant-tunneling diodes makes a bistable midpoint node (Goto pair) that holds a bit at nA standby with no capacitor. One access transistor completes a ~3-device static cell, with no III-V and no Ge.
note: Si/SiO2 RTDs show weak room-temperature peak-to-valley ratios; cell area 2-3x DRAM.

title: Aluminum-induced layer exchange grows poly-silicon access transistors at 350 C
idea: Effect: amorphous Si dissolves into Al grain boundaries and crystallizes underneath at ~350 C, swapping layer order (layer exchange) to give >10 um grains with no Ni, laser or furnace. Strip the Al, thin and counter-dope the film, and build stacked BEOL access and periphery transistors over the array.

title: HiPIMS-grown VO2 Mott latches hold bits inside hysteresis windows
idea: Effect: the Mott insulator-metal transition has an electrically driven hysteresis window. High-power impulse magnetron sputtering supplies energetic ions so monoclinic VO2 (Cr-doped to move the transition above 85 C operating temperature) crystallizes at <=300 C. A VO2 element biased inside its window latches as a one-resistor static bit switched by ns pulses.
note: Biasing inside hysteresis requires constant standby power and tight window control; density and variability doubtful.

title: Vapor-liquid-solid growth builds vertical access channels upward instead of etching
idea: Effect: eutectic-droplet (VLS) epitaxy. Al or Sn catalyst dots (CMOS-safe, not Au) on buried bitlines grow epitaxial Si nanowires; the liquid droplet confines growth to a 10-15 nm vertical channel already aligned to its bitline, which then gets a gate-all-around wrap for 4F2 vertical-channel DRAM.
note: Perfect catalyst placement and kink-free 10 nm wires at 100% yield are unrealistic.

title: Fourier lens compresses training activation checkpoints at light speed
idea: Activation tiles saved for backprop are loaded onto a spatial light modulator, and a lens computes their 2D Fourier transform in one pass. A thresholding camera keeps only the high-energy coefficients (JPEG-style) for storage. Inverse optics, or a cheap digital IFFT, restores them during the backward pass.
note: SLM I/O rate is far below HBM rates; a digital FFT is cheaper.

title: Fiber speckle random projections shrink recommendation embedding tables
idea: Replace TB-scale embedding tables with compact codes. A thermally stabilized multimode fiber's speckle acts as a fixed, enormous random matrix, so a short per-ID code expands optically into a full embedding (the hashing trick at light speed). Only the codes and a small learned correction table stay in DRAM.
note: A pseudo-random digital matrix does the same; optics adds cost and drift without benefit.

title: Dispersive SAW chirp lines compress radar data before the ADC
idea: Automotive radars buffer the full range-Doppler cube in DRAM. Instead, an AlN-on-sapphire dispersive SAW delay line does analog pulse compression and range transformation on each chirp, so only range bins above the CFAR threshold are digitized and stored. SAW devices are already qualified to AEC-Q200 at 125 C, and the piezo material is stable far beyond that.
note: FMCW dechirp already gives cheap range; CFAR before Doppler integration loses SNR.

title: Piezo: GHz ultrasonic through-silicon acoustic vias replace HBM data TSVs
idea: Pattern thin-film ScAlN bulk-acoustic transducers on each thinned DRAM die; data rides as 5-10 GHz longitudinal ultrasound pulses straight through the bonded silicon stack, each die's transducer tuned to its own frequency band so one acoustic column serves 16 dies. No holes are drilled, so TSV keep-out zones and TSV-induced yield loss disappear.
note: Same GHz acoustic through-Si data path, ScAlN variant.

title: Phonon bandgap: superlattice thermal barrier lets DRAM sit atop hot logic
idea: Insert a 50-100 nm WSe2/MoS2 van der Waals stack or W/Al2O3 nanolaminate with cross-plane thermal conductivity <0.1 W/mK between logic and DRAM, while copper thermal pillars route logic heat sideways; DRAM stays below 85 C despite face-to-face 3D bonding.
note: Thermal isolation traps logic heat; signal vias also conduct heat across the barrier.

title: Magnetic induction: cored micro-coils shrink inductive die-to-die links to 5 um
idea: Add electroplated CoZrTa thin-film magnetic cores to stacked micro-coils so the coupling coefficient rises from ~0.1 to >0.5, allowing ThruChip-style inductive vertical links at 5 um pitch through 32 thinned dies with no TSVs.
note: Magnetic core loss at GHz; coupling range at 5 um pitch cannot span 32 dies.

title: Microphase separation: block copolymer templates print 20 nm wiring on rolls
idea: Coat a block copolymer over a nanoimprinted guide pattern on R2R film; it self-assembles into 20-40 nm lamellae that template electroless metal lines, giving ultra-dense, low-cost local redistribution wiring between memory and processor.
note: 20 nm lines have high resistance over mm lengths; defectivity at area is severe.

title: Orbital Hall torques in titanium make chokepoint-free MRAM a foundry add-on
idea: Light metals like Ti and Cr show a large orbital Hall effect that can switch a magnetic free layer like spin Hall torque does, without beta-W or Pt. The SOT-MRAM stack is sputter-only BEOL, so any U.S. logic foundry can add a refresh-free, ns-class memory tier.
note: Orbital Hall switching still early research; MRAM density far below DRAM.

title: Moire-fringe alignment upgrades refurbished ArF steppers to DRAM overlay
idea: Dual-grating alignment marks produce a Moire beat that magnifies nm misalignment into um fringes read by a retrofit camera, feeding a piezo fine stage. That lets secondhand 2000s-era ArF steppers reach ~2-3 nm overlay for array layers.

title: Fe: iron-triazole spin-crossover nanoparticles store bits as spin state
idea: Fill each cell with a few 10 nm [Fe(Htrz)2(trz)] spin-crossover particles whose low-spin and high-spin states coexist inside a thermal hysteresis loop near chip temperature; a current pulse flips the spin state, changing conductance ~10x, and particle spread causing ~1% misreads is absorbed by majority voting across three cells.

title: Ca: polycrystalline Ca3Ti2O7 hybrid-improper ferroelectric, grain spread tolerated
idea: Sputter Ca3Ti2O7, whose polarization arises from coupled octahedral rotations (low coercive field, no Pb, Hf or Zr), as a polycrystalline capacitor film; random grain orientation widens the Pr spread, and cells with too few aligned grains (~1%) are corrected by the code instead of demanding epitaxy.
note: Ca3Ti2O7 thin films and coercive field unproven; FeRAM destructive read and endurance remain.

title: Tin-catalyzed bottom-up nanowire access transistors grown in place
idea: Sn: place Sn catalyst dots on storage-node landing pads with a relaxed DUV pattern, shrink them to ~10-15 nm by controlled dewetting, then grow vertical Si nanowires by Sn-catalyzed vapor-liquid-solid growth below 400 C, switching in-situ doping to form source, channel and drain, followed by an ALD gate-all-around.
note: Sn-catalyzed VLS below 400 C with positional and doping control unproven at scale.

title: Zn+Sn+Cu: indium-free oxide CMOS tier for row decoders
idea: Build n-type amorphous zinc-tin oxide and p-type Cu2O thin-film transistors in BEOL above the mats to host row decoders and wordline drivers; the wide-bandgap channels block 3 V with sub-fA leakage, and using only Zn, Sn, Cu and O avoids the indium and gallium of IGZO.

title: Ca: calcium-titanate varactor parametrically pumps bitline signal up
idea: Add a CaTiO3 paraelectric varactor to each bitline; after charge sharing, the sense-enable pulse biases it to drop its capacitance 3-4x, so the same signal charge appears as a 3-4x larger voltage before a smaller, less-matched latch fires.
note: CaTiO3 tunability too low for 3-4x capacitance swing.

title: Fe: iron-core inductors resonantly recycle bitline precharge energy
idea: Give each bank an on-die inductor with an electroplated Fe-Ni magnetic core; when sensing finishes, bitline charge is swung through LC resonance into the next bank's precharge instead of being dumped to the half-VDD rail, recovering roughly half of the CV2.
note: Half-VDD precharge already recycles charge; tens-of-nH on-die inductors are large and lossy.

title: Ga+N: gallium-nitride UV-LED maskless lithography for relaxed periphery
idea: Expose non-critical periphery layers (>80 nm pitch) with dense arrays of 365/280 nm GaN/AlGaN micro-LEDs imaged through reduction optics, with no mask, mercury lamp or neon excimer, letting each die's periphery be customized (for example per-bin repair routing) at exposure.
note: 365/280 nm cannot print ~80 nm pitch at any NA; only relaxed layers.

title: Boron nitride monolayers shrink inter-tier spacers to three nanometers
idea: Replace the 20-30 nm SiO2 spacer between 3D-DRAM tiers with 2-3 layers of hexagonal BN (6 eV gap, pinhole-free van der Waals insulator) grown on a sacrificial template and transferred or directly grown by low-temperature plasma CVD, cutting tier pitch from ~60 nm to ~35 nm.
note: Repeated hBN growth/transfer per tier impractical.

title: Carbon wordlines: conformal nanographite replaces tungsten in replacement-gate cavities
idea: After the sacrificial nitride is pulled from each tier, fill the lateral wordline cavities with catalyst-free plasma-grown nanocrystalline graphite (C2H2, ~450 C) and intercalate it with FeCl3 to cut sheet resistance; no WF6, no fluorine attack on the gate oxide and no TiN barrier liner.

title: Bistable buckled aluminum-nitride nanobeam as a leak-free bit
idea: Periodic-table walk, Al+N (13,7): a pre-stressed 100 nm AlN beam buckles into one of two stable states; a piezoelectric kick (ns, since resonance is ~GHz) flips it and capacitive sensing reads it; there is no contact, so wear stays at resonator-class (>1e15 cycles) and nothing leaks.
note: Bistable NEMS memory is known; cell area with anchors and electrodes far exceeds DRAM, stiction and ns switching unproven.

title: Epitaxial nickel-disilicide buried bitlines for vertical-channel cells
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ni (28): cubic NiSi2 is lattice-matched to Si (0.4% mismatch), so form single-crystal NiSi2 at pillar bases by templated Ni diffusion, then overgrow Si to make 4F2 vertical-channel transistors over a metallic buried bitline.

title: Doped single-crystal silicon pillar as a metal-free storage electrode
idea: Periodic-table walk, Br (35): etch degenerately P-doped (>1e20 cm^-3) Si pillars with HBr/Cl2/O2 (bromide-oxide passivation, no fluorine), wrap them in ALD high-k and a TiN plate, so the pillar itself is the bottom electrode with no oxide mold, no TiN bottom electrode and no HF removal.
note: Silicon electrodes grow interfacial SiO2 that kills capacitance; the reason DRAM moved to MIM.

title: Hf: one HfZrO deposition serves gate, capacitor and liner
idea: In a vertical-channel 4F2 cell, deposit a single conformal HfZrO film that wraps the channel (gate dielectric), continues over the storage node (capacitor dielectric) and seals the stack (liner), then tune each region's phase with localized anneal.

title: Ce: ceria oxygen-storage interlayer self-heals capacitor dielectric vacancies
idea: Insert ~1 nm CeO2 between the TiN electrode and ZrO2 dielectric; ceria cycles Ce3+/Ce4+ as in automotive catalytic converters, absorbing oxygen vacancies and releasing oxygen to buffer the vacancy profile that drives leakage drift and breakdown.

title: Springfield Armory standard: public-domain 180 nm periphery masks for U.S. fabs
idea: Like the Springfield Armory's government-owned gauges that made interchangeable parts possible, a federal program funds and publishes an open periphery reference design, bump map and mask set at 180 nm. Any U.S. 200 mm fab can then make certified companion dies that bond to any compliant array die.
note: 180 nm periphery cannot match array bitline pitch, so only control and I/O dies apply.

title: Jelly-roll capacitor: strained bilayer self-rolls into a multi-turn spiral
idea: Borrow battery-cell winding: deposit a flat TiN/high-k/TiN/strained-SiN film beside each access transistor, release a sacrificial underlayer so built-in strain rolls it into a 3-5 turn Swiss roll standing on its anchor, multiplying plate area by the number of turns without any high-aspect-ratio etch.
note: Rolled MIM at micron scale; a 300 nm film is far larger than a DRAM cell footprint.

title: Cotton-candy spun oxide nanofibers as lateral 3D channels
idea: Electrospin aligned In2O3/IGZO precursor nanofibers onto a fast-rotating drum, as in cotton-candy and nonwoven spinning, transfer the aligned mats onto each tier below 400 C and calcine them, giving 10-20 nm lateral channels without epitaxy or Si/SiGe superlattices.

title: Marquetry slab: reconstituted wafer of harvested partial-good banks
idea: Like inlaid marquetry made from offcuts, dice partially failing mature DRAM dies along bank boundaries, inlay the good banks into a pocketed reconstituted wafer on existing fan-out lines, and wire them with one coarse RDL into a wafer-scale memory slab with a routing table.
note: Banks lack own I/O and control; harvesting them is impractical.

title: Cast-iron skillet seasoning: reusable silicon nitride crucibles for CZ
idea: A seasoned cast-iron pan lasts generations; make CZ crucibles from reaction-bonded silicon nitride (U.S. silicon powder nitrided in U.S. air-separated nitrogen) with a self-renewing Si3N4/SiO2 'seasoning' coat reapplied between pulls, so one crucible serves dozens of 300 mm pulls.

title: Volumetric 3D printing: one holographic exposure defines electrode-plus-support lattice
idea: Like volumetric resin printers that cure a whole part at once, expose a 2 um-thick resist with four-beam interference to cure a 3D lattice of vertical posts with horizontal support bridges in one shot, then ALD-replicate it and burn out the resist to leave the capacitor bottom-electrode skeleton with built-in anti-leaning supports.
note: Interference pitch >100 nm at 193 nm, no registration to contacts.

title: Origami accordion fold: one thinned DRAM strip folded into a stack
idea: Leave 8-16 DRAM dies joined in a strip on the thinned wafer, bridged by polyimide hinge RDL across the saw street. Fold the strip like an accordion into a stack, so the hinges carry the shared bus around the edges and no TSVs or microbumps are needed.
note: Hinge bend radius and edge wire count limit bus width; TSV area is not 3x tax.

title: Injection-molded liquid-metal vertical channels for reworkable stacks
idea: Mold the stack's encapsulant with micro-channels, then inject gallium-indium alloy like injection molding to form vertical bus lines between barrier-lined pads. A bad die can be removed by heating and vacuuming out the metal, then replaced.

title: Brewed colloidal quantum-dot photodiodes coated onto memory logic die
idea: Batch-synthesize lead-sulfide or InAs quantum dots in large reactors like brewing, then spin-coat them onto a mature-node memory logic die as SWIR imagers already do. The die gets optical receivers with no III-V bonding.

title: Anodised self-reforming capacitors like aluminium electrolytics
idea: Electrolytic capacitors heal oxide flaws by re-anodising under bias; grow the cell dielectric by wet anodisation of an electroless or N2-purged ALD Ta/Nb/Hf film (no argon sputtering or plasma), leaving a thin ion-supply layer so periodic in-field 'reforming' pulses re-oxidise new leakage spots.
note: Anodization in deep trenches and in-field reforming unlikely.

title: n-i-p-i doping superlattice storing separated electrons and holes
idea: IFR: charge that can never recombine. Closest achievable: a Dohler n-i-p-i superlattice (alternating n and p doping sheets) separates electrons and holes into different layers, stretching recombination lifetimes toward seconds; many periods stack charge vertically in one cell footprint.
note: Room-temperature recombination lifetimes and cell access unresolved.

title: MLCC-style tape-cast 3D capacitor stack for printed DRAM
idea: IFR: 3D DRAM capacitors made the way industry already prints trillions of MLCCs a year. Closest achievable: tape-cast and screen-print 0.5 um BaTiO3 layers (k~2000) with printed Ni electrodes into a 100-layer stack whose per-layer pads are addressed by printed oxide-TFT selectors on the stack edge; 1 um^2 at 0.5 um already gives ~35 fF.

title: Van der Waals adhesion-latched printed nanocantilever bit
idea: IFR: turn stiction, the classic MEMS failure, into the memory. Closest achievable: nanoimprint a cantilever over a printed electrode coated with an anti-wear monolayer; once pulled in, van der Waals adhesion holds it on until a reverse electrostatic or thermal pulse releases it.
note: Adhesion variability and contact wear limit endurance.

title: Ferroelectric polarization kick boosts wordlines without charge pumps
idea: Ideal result: a 3 V wordline from a 1 V supply with no pump. A ferroelectric capacitor at each wordline driver output releases its remanent charge (~20-40 uC/cm^2) on polarization switching, bootstrapping the wordline above the supply locally.
note: Re-poling each cycle needs high voltage; HZO endurance too low for wordlines.

title: Stamped capacitors: nanoimprinted pillar forest on glass panels
idea: IFR: 'capacitors are stamped like coins, not etched.' Backward: UV-nanoimprint a hexagonal forest of 20:1 resin pillars onto a glass panel from a reusable master, ALD-coat them with electrode/high-k/electrode, optionally burn out the resin core for a double-sided shell, and build oxide TFTs above.

title: Vacuum-gap storage capacitors with no dielectric material at all
idea: Ideal: a dielectric that costs nothing and never leaks. Closest: interdigitated vertical fin electrodes (TiN or doped Si) separated by a 4-6 nm sacrificial carbon layer that is ashed out through vent holes, leaving vacuum gaps held open by periodic oxide anchors; many fins in parallel recover capacitance.
note: 4-6 nm vacuum gaps over tall fins face electrostatic pull-in and stiction; needs ~10x area.

title: S-layer protein crystals template ten-nanometer charge-storage dot arrays
idea: Ideal: a nanopattern brewed in a fermenter. Closest: recrystallize bacterial S-layer proteins (2D lattices, 3-30 nm period, cheap fermentation) on a gate dielectric, use their pores to template ALD/electroless Ni or ZnO nanodots as isolated charge sites for a dense floating-dot volatile cell, then burn the protein away.
note: S-layer templating known; protein lattice domains and thermal limits make dense reliable cells unlikely.

title: Aerogel thermal moat between hot logic and memory stack
idea: Ideal: memory stacked on logic yet as cold as if it were far away. Closest achievable: a 20-50 um silica-aerogel or vacuum-gap layer, pierced only by thin copper signal pillars, thermally isolates DRAM tiers from the logic die while a separate cold plate cools the DRAM from its own side.
note: Copper signal pillars short-circuit the aerogel thermally.

title: Latching NEMS relay tiles: bits held by mechanical contact
idea: Ideal: a bit held forever with zero leakage, by geometry instead of charge. Closest achievable: a chiplet of nanoelectromechanical relays with adhesion-latched bistable cantilevers in vacuum-sealed wafer-level cavities, written by a 1-3 V pulse and read by contact resistance in ~10 ns, bonded under the GPU as a static scratchpad.
note: Contact endurance far short of DRAM-class; density poor.

title: Nitrogen-cooled YBCO flux-loop memory with no helium
idea: Scarcity rule: no semiconductor in the cell and no helium (Qatar supply offline). Store the bit as a clockwise or counter-clockwise persistent current in a YBCO nanoloop at 77 K in liquid nitrogen; a current pulse through a phase-slip constriction writes it and a kinetic-inductance or nanoSQUID sensor reads it.

title: Storage node may touch no pn junction: MIS tunnel contact
idea: Limit: the storage node may not have a depletion junction to the substrate. Contact the capacitor through a ~1 nm Al2O3/SiO2 interlayer onto a fully depleted ultrathin-body channel. This metal-insulator-semiconductor contact passes write current by direct tunneling and eliminates the junction depletion volume, where SRH thermal generation and trap-assisted tunneling create the tail.

title: Half the capacitor: negative-capacitance HZO preamp restores sense margin
idea: Limit: storage capacitor cut to 2.5 fF, so the bitline signal falls to ~40 mV. Place a series HZO ferroelectric layer in the gate stack of the sense amp's input pair, tuned to the negative-capacitance regime, so the internal gate swing is stepped up 2-4x before the latch regenerates.

title: Noise as resource: dithered majority-vote sensing with tiny comparators
idea: Limit: comparator offset (sigma ~20 mV) is bigger than the signal (~15 mV). Inject a calibrated random dither on the reference, fire a minimum-size, unmatched, non-loading comparator 7-15 times in ~3 ns, and count: the signal skews the probability of ones (stochastic resonance), so the majority recovers the bit, and only then does the restore driver fire.
note: Dither does not cancel static comparator offset; majority still reports sign(signal minus offset).

title: Read the cell's EMF: electrochemical bits sensed by voltage
idea: Constraint: non-volatile with zero read current. Store bits as ion concentration in a nanoscale electrochemical (ECRAM-like) cell whose open-circuit voltage differs by ~100 mV between states; the SA samples that voltage onto a precharged floating bitline through a high-impedance gate, so the read draws no state-changing current.
note: High-impedance source cannot charge a bitline in ns; ion-write endurance.

title: In-stack voltage-window decoder replaces wordline staircase
idea: Limit: zero staircase area. Each tier is grown with in-situ graded doping so its select device has a distinct threshold. Two series select gates in the same film, one inversion-mode and one junctionless depletion-mode, open a voltage window that turns on exactly one tier. So two vertical gate electrodes address 64+ tiers with no stair contacts.
note: Distinguishing 64 tiers by Vt windows fails under Vt variation; similar to VG-NAND layer-select-by-multilevel.

title: Printed ferroelectric-polymer cold-page tier on flex
idea: Constraint (printable/roll-to-roll): P(VDF-TrFE) ferroelectric capacitors over printed oxide TFTs form a non-volatile, byte-addressable flex tier with microsecond access behind a CXL controller. The OS demotes pages untouched for two minutes or more to this tier, so DRAM holds only the working set.
note: Printed cell pitch implies square meters per GB; $1-3/GB and us access over flex are implausible.

title: Multilevel organic charge-trap buffer for error-tolerant data
idea: Constraint (printable/roll-to-roll): printed organic transistors with a solution-processed charge-trapping dielectric store 4-5 bits per cell as analog threshold shifts. Data tagged as tolerant (image tiles, training-set staging, sensor history) is parked here, and errors are accepted instead of corrected.

title: Elastomeric zebra sheets make tall stacks solderless and rebuildable
idea: Forced: 10x density at the same cost. Stack 32-64 thinned dies interleaved with 30 um anisotropic conductive elastomer sheets (aligned metal filaments in silicone, as in LCD zebra connectors) under a clamped lid; a failed die is swapped by unclamping instead of scrapping the stack.

title: No counter SRAM: weak canary rows detect row hammer physically
idea: Imposed limit: zero bytes of activation-counter SRAM. Each subarray gets a few sentinel rows built with ~30% smaller storage nodes, so they flip after ~300 neighbor activations. They hold a known pattern, and a comparator checks them during normal refresh. A canary flip raises an alert that triggers targeted refresh of the neighbors.
note: Few sentinel rows only sense hammering of their own neighbours, not arbitrary aggressors.

title: No new process step: wordline microheaters anneal leakage traps
idea: Imposed limit: the leakage tail must improve without adding fab steps. Existing wordline and dummy-gate conductors are driven as resistive heaters in maintenance windows (about 1 s pulses heating locally to ~250 C), passivating hydrogen-related interface traps and resetting variable-retention-time defects in the array.

title: No silicon wafer: phone display backplane doubles as standby memory
idea: Forced limit: the memory must ride on an existing non-Si substrate. Low-leakage oxide TFTs already in LTPO phone backplanes get a few hundred MB of gain-cell array in the bezel and backplane, used as frame buffer and standby memory so the LPDDR can sleep.

title: Voltage-clocked skyrmion shift register: magnetic bubble memory revived with gate clocks instead of currents
idea: A chiral multilayer (Pt/Co/MgO type, with perpendicular anisotropy and strong DMI) is patterned into tracks 2F wide. Gates at 2F pitch on 1.5 nm MgO modulate interface anisotropy through VCMA. Two-phase clocks with a built-in ratchet (an asymmetric gate profile) create a moving energy minimum that carries each skyrmion one bit-length per clock, like charge packets in a CCD. A skyrmionic MTJ at the track end reads the bit (20-70% contrast reported), and a VCMA/SOT nucleator writes it. The state is non-volatile between shifts. With no lateral current there is no electromigration or Joule heating, and thousands of tracks share each clock line.

title: Negative-capacitance HZO layer fused onto ZrO2 storage capacitor
idea: Combine a thin ferroelectric HZO film, biased in its non-switching negative-capacitance regime, in series with the paraelectric ZrO2/Al2O3 cell dielectric so the ferroelectric's negative dQ/dV cancels part of the dielectric's inverse capacitance. Thickness-match the layers so the stack stays hysteresis-free while effective k reaches ~70-100 in the same 60:1 pillar.
note: Stabilized NC enhancement contested; MPB ZrO2 already mainstream path.

title: Nanoporous dealloyed metal electrode inside storage capacitor
idea: Borrow dealloyed nanoporous metals from battery and catalyst electrodes: deposit a TiAl alloy in a wider, shallower capacitor hole, selectively etch out the Al to leave a sponge with 10-20 nm pores, then coat ALD dielectric and top electrode throughout. The sponge multiplies internal surface area 3-4x within the same footprint.
note: HSG-silicon precedent; 10-20 nm pores cannot hold dielectric plus electrode.

title: Jewelry lost-wax: sacrificial zinc-oxide layers for lateral 3D cavities
idea: Lost-wax casting relies on a filler that is easy to remove; build the 3D DRAM tier stack with sputtered ZnO sacrificial layers between Si or SiN tiers, then dissolve the ZnO in dilute acetic acid, which leaves Si, SiO2 and SiN untouched, carving micron-deep lateral capacitor cavities from one vertical slit.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina grows the capacitor mold
idea: Reverse etching a mold into growing one: deposit ~2 um of aluminum over the landing pads, use one added mask to imprint pore nucleation dimples aligned to the pads, and anodize so self-ordered pores grow straight down at AR >100; line the pores with TiN/high-k/TiN.

title: Nanosphere monolayer sets the capacitor lattice
idea: Reverse top-down patterning into bottom-up packing: spread a Langmuir-Blodgett monolayer of 40 nm silica spheres that close-pack into a hex lattice, shrink them by plasma, and use them as the etch mask for honeycomb capacitor holes.
note: LB sphere monolayers have domain defects and cannot register to landing pads.

title: Fully silicided titanium wordline grown inward from polysilicon fill
idea: TRIZ #13 The other way round: instead of depositing metal into the buried-wordline trench, fill the trench with doped polysilicon and convert it in place, top-down, into C54 TiSi2 (Ti deposition, Si pre-amorphization, two-step RTA). The conductor is grown from what is already there.
note: C49-to-C54 TiSi2 transformation is suppressed in narrow lines.

title: Holographic binding bundles low-priority tokens into superposed vectors
idea: Peripheral KV pairs are bound by circular convolution (holographic reduced representations, akin to distributed cortical traces) and summed into a few bundle vectors per block; queries unbind to recover approximate values, cleaned up against a small codebook.

title: Keyboard snap-dome: buckled nanomembrane holds bits mechanically
idea: Snap-dome keys and Venus flytraps use buckling bistability: deposit a 20-nm PECVD SiN membrane tuned to ~1 GPa compressive stress over a 300-nm cavity so it rests buckled up or down; electrostatic pulses from top or bottom electrodes snap it within ns (tiny mass, GHz modes), and its position sets a 3-5x capacitance difference read by the sense amp.

title: Traffic-jam phases: charge-density-wave domain states in 1T-TaS2
idea: Traffic flips between free flow and jams; in 1T-TaS2 electrons lock into commensurate or nearly commensurate charge-density-wave states with ~10x resistance contrast, and thin flakes switch between metastable states under short current pulses; build two-terminal cells from exfoliated ~10-nm flakes with e-beam contacts and hBN encapsulation.
note: Flake demo easy; 85 C retention doubtful.

title: Plasmonics nanosphere lithography: floated monolayer masks for capacitor arrays
idea: Borrowed from plasmonics labs, which float colloidal spheres into a close-packed monolayer on water and lift it onto a substrate: float 40 nm monodisperse silica spheres on a Langmuir-Blodgett trough over a wafer with shallow lattice guides, shrink them by plasma, and use them as the etch mask for the hexagonal storage-node array.

title: Shrinky Dinks lithography: pattern large, heat-shrink into imprint masters
idea: Borrowed from the Shrinky Dinks toy, whose pre-stretched polystyrene shrinks ~2.5x when baked: write DRAM array master patterns oversized on pre-stretched shape-memory polymer with cheap optical lithography, shrink thermally, electroform a hard nickel copy as a NIL master, and repeat for a second shrink stage, all in a garage-scale lab.

title: Lehmann photo-electrochemical macropores etch capacitors without plasma
idea: Revive Volker Lehmann's 1990 photo-electrochemical macropore etching (studied by Siemens for trench DRAM): n-type silicon anodized in HF under backside LED illumination grows pores only where photogenerated holes reach the pore tips, giving straight pores of AR >150:1 from shallow seed pits. Dielectric and electrodes go in by nitrogen-purged ALD, so no step uses argon, helium or neon.
note: Macropore pitch tied to space-charge width; sub-100 nm pitch unproven.

title: Williams-tube interlaced raster: rotating row interlace starves row hammer
idea: Williams-tube memories limited the 'read-around ratio' (charge spill from reading neighbouring spots) by interlacing the raster so neighbours were regenerated before spill accumulated. Logical rows map to physical rows through an interlace whose stride and phase rotate every 1/16 of the refresh window, and the migration piggybacks on refresh (each refresh reads a row and writes it into its new slot), so no aggressor keeps the same physical victims long enough to reach ~1k activations.
note: Close to RRS/SRS; a 4 ms phase still allows ~80k ACTs, far above the threshold.

title: Planar sol-gel BST capacitor, flash-lamp crystallized, ends deep etching
idea: Box: paraelectric (Ba,Sr)TiO3 charge (k~300) x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x spin-on sol-gel plus millisecond xenon flash-lamp anneal. The flash crystallizes only the top ~100 nm into perovskite while the substrate stays below 400 C, so a near-planar 1:1 to 3:1 capacitor on Pt or SrRuO3 reaches ~5 fF.
note: k~300 planar cap at DRAM cell area gives well under 1 fF; BST was tried and abandoned.

title: Segmented cell-plate kick boosts read signal before charge sharing
idea: Worse: hold the cell plate at a static VDD/2 so the signal is only what Cs alone delivers. Flip: split the plate into per-mat segments and pulse the selected mat's plate by a few hundred mV during the read to couple extra charge onto the bitline, then return it before restore.
note: Plate kick shifts 0 and 1 equally, so differential signal does not grow.

title: Floating nanosphere monolayers mask capacitor holes without scanners
idea: Scale shift to colloids: U.S.-synthesized 25-30 nm silica nanospheres self-pack as a hexagonal monolayer on a Langmuir trough, transfer onto the wafer, are trimmed by plasma, and serve as the etch or lift-off mask for the capacitor lattice.

title: ZFS dedup's RAM hunger, fixed: flash-resident delta store for fine-tunes
idea: ZFS dedup became notorious for needing ~5 GB of RAM per TB for its dedup table. Serve thousands of fine-tuned model variants by content-defined chunking of weight tensors into flash, with an SRAM cuckoo filter (~1 byte per chunk) to spot duplicate chunks and a flash-resident index, so each variant costs only its unique delta.
note: Full fine-tunes perturb nearly every value, so exact chunk dedup finds little; LoRA already solves deltas.

title: Siloxane soft-stamp nanoimprint copies one e-beam master to every tier
idea: Write a single 4F2-pitch Si master by e-beam, cast hard-PDMS/PDMS stamps from it, and UV-nanoimprint the critical cell layer of every tier on every wafer at ~15 nm resolution, using the master only to replicate stamps and a mask aligner for overlay.
note: Soft PDMS stamps and mask-aligner overlay cannot meet DRAM overlay at 15 nm.

title: Rock-candy croconic acid: proton-hopping organic ferroelectric bit
idea: Like rock candy growing on a seeded string, croconic acid (C5H2O5) crystallizes from vapor onto seed lines between TiN electrodes. It is a room-temperature ferroelectric whose polarization flips by proton transfer along hydrogen bonds, read through a ferroelectric tunnel junction.

title: Ball-bearing packing: colloidal monolayer masks for hex vertical-channel arrays
idea: Like ball bearings settling in a tray, float a Langmuir monolayer of 40-60 nm silica spheres onto wafers, shrink them in plasma to set hole size, and etch a hexagonal vertical-channel array with mature etch tools; periphery uses ordinary litho and colloid grain boundaries are mapped out as spare rows.
note: Nanosphere masks lack registration to underlying layers and semiconductor-grade defectivity.

title: Negative-capacitance superlattice dielectric hitting effective k of 100
idea: IFR: a dielectric with infinite permittivity. Closest achievable: stack 1 nm ferroelectric HZO with 1 nm Al2O3 in a superlattice tuned so the dielectric stabilizes the ferroelectric's negative-capacitance branch, multiplying net capacitance 2-4x without hysteresis.

title: Printed proton-transfer organic ferroelectric with low coercive voltage
idea: IFR: polarization that flips without moving heavy atoms. Closest achievable: solution-print croconic acid or diisopropylammonium bromide films whose polarization reverses by proton hopping along hydrogen bonds (P ~20 uC/cm^2) at low field, used as printed capacitors in a 2T nondestructive-read gain configuration.

title: Printed alpha-indium-selenide ferroelectric semiconductor flake ink
idea: IFR: a channel that remembers by itself with no separate dielectric. Closest achievable: inkjet exfoliated alpha-In2Se3 nanoflakes, a 2D ferroelectric semiconductor whose locked in-plane/out-of-plane polarization modulates its own conductance, so each printed flake is a two-terminal or FET bit.
note: Printed flakes add thickness and orientation variability to the In2Se3 bit.

title: Printed relaxor terpolymer dielectric reaching k of 50
idea: IFR: a printable dielectric with ceramic-class permittivity. Closest achievable: slot-die coat P(VDF-TrFE-CFE) relaxor terpolymer (k ~50 at room temperature, slim hysteresis) as the storage-capacitor dielectric, optionally loaded with BaTiO3 nanocubes to push higher.
note: Polymer k collapses at GHz and nm thickness; BEOL thermal budget incompatible.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous electrode multiplies capacitor area without height
idea: IFR: 'the capacitor has infinite area in a tiny height.' Backward: deposit the bottom electrode as an alloy (e.g., Ni-Al or Cu-Mn), selectively dissolve the sacrificial metal to leave a 3-5 nm ligament nanoporous sponge, then ALD high-k and a conformal top electrode, giving 4-8x the surface of a smooth pillar.

title: No tracking state: keyed rotating row permutation defeats hammering
idea: Imposed limit: no per-row tracking state. Each refresh window, the bank rekeys a lightweight Feistel permutation that maps logical to physical rows within a subarray, migrating a few rows per refresh command. An attacker cannot keep hammering the same physical neighbors long enough to cause a flip.

title: LED constant-lumen drivers: aging-compensated negative wordline trim per mat
idea: Adapted from LED drivers that raise current as LEDs age to hold light output constant: each mat carries a replica access transistor whose leakage is measured monthly, and a small trim DAC deepens that mat's off-wordline voltage step by step to hold replica leakage at its day-one value, logging the trim history for refurbishers.

title: Merge-mask bridges landing pads into double-charge cells
idea: Inverts 'one cell, one capacitor': one added mask bridges pairs of adjacent storage-node landing pads in a designated region so two pillars act as one ~10 fF capacitor driven by two access transistors in parallel.

title: Medieval guild: teaching fab whose apprentices ship real DRAM
idea: On the guild model, a state-chartered 200 mm teaching fab has apprentice technicians run a legacy DDR3/LPDDR2 product for automotive and industrial customers as their coursework, with certification after 18 months. Product revenue covers ~60% of operating cost.

title: Substitute zirconium silicate for hafnium oxide in periphery gates
idea: Replace HfO2 in DRAM periphery high-k metal gates with ALD Zr silicate, using silicon incorporation to suppress ZrO2 crystallization and an Al2O3 dipole layer for threshold tuning.

title: Substitute remote-plasma radicals for hot phosphoric acid nitride removal
idea: Remove sacrificial SiN (and lateral recesses for stacked 3D DRAM) with downstream NF3/O2/N2 radicals tuned for >100:1 SiN:SiO2 selectivity, replacing 160 C phosphoric acid baths that need continuous DI water spiking and heavy rinses.

title: Swap scrapped retention-fail dies for an error-tolerant DRAM grade
idea: Substitute 'scrap' with 'approximate grade'. Dies that fail retention or margin screens are packaged as standard DDR5/LPDDR5 parts rated for a measured bit-error rate, and the OS and ML frameworks place only error-tolerant data on them (activations, media buffers, refetchable caches). DDR/HBM interfaces are unchanged.
note: EDEN-style approximate DRAM; recovers only a few percent.

title: Retention rejects rewired as twin-cell half-density parts
idea: A fuse or metal-option mode pairs each cell with its bitline-pair neighbor storing the complement (2T2C). That doubles the sense signal and extends retention ~10x, so dies that would be scrapped sell at half density.

title: Pair partial-good dies behind a 65nm bank-remap bridge
idea: Instead of scrapping or down-binning dies with dead banks, package two partial-good dies with a small 65 nm bridge chip that presents one standard full-capacity die and routes each bank address to whichever die has it working.

title: Reclaimed monitor wafers reborn under thick device-grade epitaxy
idea: Combine wafer reclaim with epitaxy (zero masks): repolish reclaimed monitor and prime-reject wafers, grow a 3-5 um device-grade epi layer, and add a backside polysilicon gettering layer to replace oxygen-precipitate gettering.

title: Thermoelectric-cooled HBM stacks traded for 4x longer refresh
idea: Combine an in-package Peltier stage between GPU and HBM stack with temperature-indexed refresh: holding the DRAM ~20 C cooler roughly quadruples retention (leakage roughly doubles per ~10 C), so the refresh interval stretches and weak cells pass.
note: Poor Peltier COP dumps extra heat into the package.

title: Piano tuning: periodic field re-trim of sense-amplifier offsets
idea: Adapted from routine piano tuning: each sense amplifier has a small offset-trim capacitor bank whose setting is stored in non-volatile cells, and a maintenance routine re-measures offsets with known test levels every few months and re-tunes them as transistors drift.

title: Charge-pump capacitors move into six BEOL MIM levels
idea: ALD ZrO2/HfO2 MIM capacitors (250-300 C) stacked in six upper metal levels MAGNIFY pump capacitance per footprint ~6x, so pumps run at lower frequency with higher efficiency and their silicon area is freed for cells.

title: Resonant clock grid with electroplated copper inductors
idea: Thick electroplated Cu spiral inductors (<=250 C) in top metal resonate with the periphery clock-grid capacitance, recycling clock energy each cycle instead of dumping it, MINIFYING clock and DLL power.

title: BEOL MTJ repair registers replace laser and eFuse banks
idea: MINIFY redundancy fuse area ~10x by storing repair addresses in BEOL magnetic tunnel junctions (annealed <=400 C) instead of laser fuses or eFuses, and MAGNIFY repair opportunities by reprogramming them in the field after aging or row-hammer damage.

title: Minify waste: bin panel zones into gold, silver, bronze memory grades
idea: Panel uniformity is best at the center and worst near the edges. Test tiles by zone and package them as gold (servers), silver (PCs) and bronze (AI inference with host LDPC) grades instead of scrapping marginal regions.

title: Eliminate the dual gate oxide with drain-extended cascode wordline drivers
idea: Build every 3 V wordline-driver device as a thin-oxide drain-extended or two-high cascode transistor, so one gate oxidation serves the whole die. This removes the thick-oxide mask and its HF strip; pre-gate cleans use SC1/SC2 plus an in-situ H2 bake instead of HF-last.

title: Eliminate deep-trench decoupling capacitors with traveling-wave sense-amp firing
idea: Fire the 8k SAs of a row as a wave crossing the mat over ~2 ns, each SA enabling its neighbor through a delay cell, so the 1-2 A sensing spike becomes a flat ramp. Supply droop falls ~5x, so deep-trench decaps (which need SF6 Bosch etch) and most MOS decaps are deleted; the remaining flow uses Cl-based etches.

title: Eliminate quartz furnace tubes: flash-lamp and microwave anneals
idea: Replace batch diffusion and anneal furnaces (high-purity quartz tubes and boats) with millisecond flash-lamp and volumetric microwave anneals in single-wafer chambers for dopant activation, dielectric crystallization and passivation.

title: Light-latched bits: self-electro-optic effect device memory planes
idea: Reverse light's role from signal to holder: arrays of symmetric SEEDs (GaAs quantum-well p-i-n pairs, 1990s Bell Labs, ~5 um pixels) latch a bit through photocurrent feedback under a uniform bias beam; pages are written and read by light in parallel with no electrical wires.
note: Bell Labs S-SEED known; ~25 um2/bit and hold-beam power make it a niche optical buffer.

title: Test brains live in the probe card, not every die
idea: Reverse where DFT lives: test-mode logic, BIST engines, compression and burn-in controllers are stripped from the DRAM die and implemented once on an ASIC in a U.S.-made probe card, reaching the array through a thin raw-access port.
note: Test logic in probe card; loses package-level BIST and PPR.

title: Abatement fluoride captured as synthetic fluorspar for HF regeneration
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: run fluorine-bearing scrubber effluent through lime crystallizers that precipitate high-purity CaF2 pellets instead of sludge. The pellets go back to an acid plant that regenerates electronic-grade HF with H2SO4, closing the fab's fluorine loop.
note: Same CaF2-capture-to-HF loop as I-09865.

title: Bamboo-node diaphragms segment vertical lines below the Blech length
idea: Bamboo compartmentalizes its culm with periodic nodes; insert thin Ru/Co node diaphragms every ~0.5 um along vertical Cu/Mo bitlines and power pillars of tall stacks so each segment is shorter than the electromigration Blech length and atoms cannot migrate past a node.

title: RV absorption fridge: GPU waste heat chills memory without fluorinated refrigerants
idea: Absorption refrigerators in RVs and hotels run on heat, using water/lithium-bromide or ammonia/water instead of HFC/HFO refrigerants. Drive a rack-level LiBr/water absorption chiller with the 60-90 C accelerator coolant return to make chilled water dedicated to HBM and DIMM cold plates at ~30 C.

title: Sculptor carving: subtractive dry-etched ruthenium/molybdenum periphery wiring
idea: Damascene copper is casting: pour into a mold, then grind and wash (CMP). Carve instead, like a sculptor: blanket-deposit Ru or Mo, pattern, and plasma-etch the periphery's local/intermediate wiring and contacts, then gap-fill with flowable low-k. No barrier, plating, CMP or post-CMP scrub.
note: Subtractive Ru/Mo is already widely pursued; periphery metal is a small share of fab water.

title: Monument laser cleaning: shock-wave particle removal before periphery contacts
idea: Conservators clean cathedral stone with pulsed lasers and no water. A nanosecond laser flash-heats the wafer surface so thermal expansion and the gas-film shock wave lift particles from periphery contact/via openings, and a nitrogen cross-flow sweeps them into an exhaust, replacing megasonic DI-water scrubs.

title: Electric-arc-furnace scrap loop: wire-saw kerf remelted into wafer feedstock
idea: Steel's electric-arc-furnace route makes new steel from scrap. Recover the ~30-40% of each ingot lost as diamond-wire kerf, strip its surface oxide with HF vapor, densify it by induction melting, and purify it by directional solidification plus vacuum refining into feedstock for handle, test and dummy wafers.

title: Kraft-mill recovery cycle regenerates sulfuric acid and peroxide cleans
idea: Pulp mills recover more than 95% of their cooking chemicals in recovery boilers. Treat spent sulfuric-peroxide and SC1/SC2 baths the same way: boron-doped-diamond electrolysis regenerates persulfate and peroxide in-line, and vacuum distillation restores H2SO4 to semiconductor grade for reuse; no change to the DRAM product or DDR/HBM interface.

title: Catalytic-converter-style tungsten recovery from CVD exhaust and targets
idea: Like recovering platinum metals from scrapped catalysts, fab abatement adds cold traps that capture unreacted WF6 and W-bearing chamber deposits, which a regional refiner converts back to WF6 or APT together with spent sputter targets.

title: Auto-parts core-charge loop for ECU memory remanufacturing
idea: Like alternator cores returned for a deposit, every ECU or ADAS board carries a core charge refunded when the scrapped unit returns; Grade-1 memory die are recovered, rescreened at 125 C, and used in spare-part ECUs that would otherwise force last-time buys of EOL DRAM.

title: Spark-plug ceramic suppliers make hermetic LTCC memory substrates
idea: Like spark plugs whose ceramics survive engine heat (made by firms that also make IC packages), use CTE-matched low-temperature co-fired ceramic substrates from U.S. technical-ceramics plants for memory packages and stacks rated for 10 years at 125 C.
note: Memory packages mostly use BT not ABF; LTCC is known art.

title: Direct-view storage tube revived as bistable pixels without framebuffers
idea: Tektronix direct-view storage tubes held the image on the screen with no frame memory; revive it with university-fabricated bistable pixels (ferroelectric or cholesteric liquid crystal on a glass TFT backplane) that latch their state, so phones, laptops and thin clients send only changed regions and keep no scanout framebuffer or panel self-refresh RAM.

title: Chemical autarky: make fab chemistries on site from air, water and salt
idea: Inverts 'chemicals are purchased from concentrated suppliers': on-site electrolyzers make H2, O2 and ozone from water, chlor-alkali cells make HCl and Cl2 from salt, H2O2 comes from electrochemical oxygen reduction and NH3 from a small Haber-Bosch unit, all distilled to electronic grade at point of use.

title: Fusion-bond stacks of sixteen thinned 180 nm array layers
idea: Inverts 'one wafer makes one memory layer'. Build cheap 180 nm array layers on 200 mm SOI, then oxide-fusion-bond and etch back 16 of them (the 1990s BESOI technique), connected by 2 um through-oxide vias at mat edges to a single bottom periphery layer.
note: 16 stacked 180 nm layers still less dense than one modern layer at 16x wafer cost.

title: AI-grade binning: sell failing DRAM dies to fault-tolerant workloads
idea: Inverts 'every die must pass full spec': dies from existing lines that fail retention screens or have clustered bad rows get a per-die bad-row map in a 40 nm controller's fuse table. They are sold as 'AI-grade' modules for weights and KV, where row remapping plus tensor-level checksums hide the defects.

title: BTI-balanced sense latches through epoch-wise data polarity swapping
idea: At 125 C, NBTI/PBTI shifts Vt ~10-30 mV over 10 years, mostly on whichever latch half sees one data value more often, eating a ~50 mV signal. Store every row inverted on alternate refresh epochs (one polarity bit per row) and swap which SA half is 'true', so both halves age equally to within ~1 mV.

title: FD-SOI periphery with PTAT back-bias flattens hot leakage
idea: Build periphery on fully-depleted SOI: buried oxide removes most junction area (generation leakage scales with ni and junction area), and a PTAT back-bias generator raises Vt ~1 mV/K as temperature climbs, holding standby leakage roughly flat from 25 to 125 C.

title: Vt-tracking wordline high voltage relieves hot oxide stress
idea: Access Vt falls ~1 mV/K, so at 125 C the wordline needs ~100 mV less overdrive than at 25 C. Scale VPP down with temperature exactly by the Vt tempco, cutting oxide field when TDDB is most accelerated (~3x lifetime gain).

title: Spider web: dual-end wordline drive tolerates mid-line opens
idea: Each wordline segment is driven from both ends, with a weak keeper at the far end, so a single open (void, CMP break) still leaves both halves driven - a web that holds after one strand snaps; only shorts consume spare rows.

title: Food freshness label: on-die Arrhenius dose integrator for life-aware derating
idea: Like time-temperature indicator labels on food, a tiny on-die structure (a floating node leaking through thermally activated oxide, cross-checked by a BTI ring oscillator) integrates cumulative thermal stress; firmware reads the 'age' and tightens refresh, VNWL and ECC mode as the dose nears 10 years at 125 C equivalent.
note: Silicon odometer sensors are known.

title: Move DFT and BIST logic onto an active probe-card ASIC
idea: Box: any cell x any access x any SA x test logic off-die x bulk Si x probe-card ASIC. Built-in self-test engines, test-mode decoders and compression logic leave each DRAM die and live on a reusable active probe card that drives a minimal raw test port.
note: Active probe cards known; DRAM keeps BIST for in-field repair.

title: Rescue scrapped dies with per-row refresh maps sold as SKU
idea: Po: the trash bin is a warehouse. Dies that fail the 64 ms retention screen because a few hundred rows are weak get a per-row refresh-class map burned into on-die fuses; the module controller refreshes those rows at 16-32 ms and the rest normally, and the parts ship as a mapped-refresh grade.

title: Po: the charge pump lives in the package
idea: Po: a DRAM die with no charge pumps. Generate VPP (~3 V) and the negative wordline bias in a package-level GaN or deep-trench-capacitor integrated-passive converter at ~85% efficiency and deliver them through dedicated bumps or hybrid-bond pads, deleting on-die pumps and their decoupling capacitors.
note: DDR4 already supplies an external VPP pin.

title: Po: the barrier grows itself — CuMn wiring, no Ta/Co/Ru
idea: Po: copper wiring that makes its own diffusion barrier. Use a Cu-0.5%Mn seed; on anneal Mn migrates to the dielectric interface and forms a ~2 nm MnSiOx barrier, replacing PVD Ta/TaN and Co/Ru liners in all periphery metal levels, with plain Al for top global levels.
note: CuMn self-forming barrier is published art.

title: Po the fab never heard of helium: batch-tool gas-free flow
idea: Po: 'the fab has never heard of helium.' Extracted: build the 180 nm DRAM flow around batch vertical furnaces (LPCVD poly, nitride, oxide), wet etches and low-power batch plasma tools whose wafers sit on boats or mechanical clamps needing no backside gas; use hydrogen or argon for any leak checks and purges.

title: Tungsten-free wordlines driven from both ends with mid-line repeaters
idea: Worse: keep buried wordlines dependent on tungsten, ~80% sourced from China. Flip: switch to supply-safe TiN or doped-poly fill and offset its higher resistance by splitting each local wordline into halves driven from both ends plus a mid-array boost repeater in the sub-wordline driver strip.

title: Art restorer's field retouching: relaxed screening plus in-field PPR
idea: A restorer fixes cracks as they appear instead of discarding the painting. Ship dies screened at a looser sense-margin limit, and let the host's existing patrol scrub find weak rows and remap them with DDR5's existing soft and hard post-package repair commands.

title: Fly-by-wire wordlines: per-mat VPP trimmed to the minimum
idea: A fly-by-wire jet trims each control surface on its own. Each mat gets a small LDO that drops its wordline high level from global VPP to the lowest value that passed that mat's test margin, stored in fuses.

title: Librarian's central catalog: base-die NVM holds all repair maps
idea: A librarian keeps one catalog, not a card box on every shelf. Redundancy and trim data for every HBM core die live in nonvolatile memory on the logic base die (embedded RRAM or MTP) and are broadcast up the TSVs at power-up, deleting the fuse banks from each core die.

title: Grandmother saves the drippings: recapture fluorocarbon etch gases
idea: Persona: a grandmother who saves the bacon fat. Instead of burning C4F8, CF4 and NF3 in abatement, pass etch exhaust through a cold trap and fluorocarbon-selective membranes to recover >70%. Re-purify the gas by distillation at a regional plant and send the cylinders back.

title: DIMM PMIC delivers VPP and VBB, deleting on-die charge pumps
