idea: Automotive and industrial boards push high-voltage generation into 180 nm BCD PMICs; DDR5 already moved 12 V to 1.1 V conversion onto the DIMM, so extend it by supplying ~3 V VPP and negative VBB on dedicated balls and deleting on-die pumps (30-40% efficient), keeping only local switches.

title: Data-polarity rotation balances sense-amp aging over 30 years
idea: Thirty-year industrial parts fail from slow asymmetric drift: the controller inverts stored polarity on alternate refresh epochs (tracked by a per-row flag bit), so both transistors of each SA pair see equal NBTI/PBTI stress and offset stays near zero. SAs can be sized for beginning-of-life margin.
note: Cell-flipping for BTI balance known from SRAM.

title: Package-level GaN switched-capacitor rails replace on-die pumps
idea: Scale shift from die to package: VPP (~3 V) and the negative wordline bias come from a GaN switched-capacitor converter embedded in the package substrate through a dense bond/TSV grid, deleting the dozens of on-die charge pumps.

title: Recover backgrinding swarf as feedstock-grade silicon
idea: Scale shift: a stacked DRAM die keeps 30-50 um of a 775 um wafer, so >93% of the silicon becomes sludge. Collect it unmixed from backgrind tools at existing OSATs, then centrifuge, acid-leach and remelt it as solar or carrier-grade feedstock.

title: Shift legacy DRAM orders onto 200 mm mature lines
idea: Market-scale shift: DDR3, LPDDR2 and low-density (<=2 Gb) DRAM for industrial, automotive and IoT still occupy 300 mm leading DRAM lines. Requalifying them on existing 200 mm 40-90 nm DRAM and specialty fabs lets leading lines convert those starts to DDR5/HBM.

title: Phase-change repair registers replace laser-fuse banks and their latches
idea: Effect: thermal hysteresis of the amorphous/crystalline phase change. Store redundancy repair addresses in small GST or Sb2Te3-superlattice cells in BEOL, programmed once at test by an on-die micro-heater pulse and read directly by the decoder compare logic. This eliminates pitch-limited laser-fuse banks and the boot-time fuse broadcast latches.

title: Cobalt-free Fe-B/MgO tunnel junctions crystallized under 350 C
idea: Effect: interfacial perpendicular anisotropy from Fe 3d-O 2p hybridization at the Fe/MgO interface. Drop Co entirely and use Mg or Al boron-sink caps instead of Ta/W, so Fe-B free and reference layers crystallize from the MgO template at <=350 C while keeping TMR >150%.

title: Closed fluorine loop: scrubber fluorspar back to on-site F2
idea: Periodic-table walk, F (9): capture HF and fluorocarbon exhaust in Ca(OH)2 scrubbers as synthetic CaF2, convert it back to HF, and electrolyze KF.2HF on-site to F2 for chamber cleans, replacing NF3.

title: O: downstream atomic-oxygen ash ends sulfuric-peroxide resist strips
idea: Strip implant and patterning resists with a remote O-radical plasma preceded by an H2/N2 radical crust-break step, eliminating hot sulfuric-peroxide (SPM) baths and their rinses.

title: Ti: rutile-TiO2 trench decoupling under the HBM PHY
idea: Line interposer and base-die deep-trench capacitors with rutile TiO2 (k~80-110, templated on RuO2) instead of HfO2/ZrO2 (k~25-40), tripling decap density directly under the HBM PHY and TSV power columns.

title: Dropped-stitch knitting: token-chained subarrays replace fuse-compare redundancy
idea: Like a knitter passing over a dropped stitch, a token threads through every subarray at power-up (the Catt-spiral idea from 1989 Anamartic wafer-scale memory). A subarray that fails its built-in self-test simply passes the token on, so the chain itself builds the address map with no fuse banks or address comparators.
note: Anamartic revival; coarse sparing at legacy nodes.

title: Sprue-and-runner test periphery: built in scribe lanes, sawn off at dicing
idea: Like the sprues and runners trimmed off a molded part, put test-mode logic, compressed-test comparators, extra probe pads and fuse-programming drivers in the 80-100 um scribe lanes at 180 nm rules, linked across the seal ring by sacrificial connections. After wafer sort and repair, the dicing saw removes them.

title: Optical-fiber soot process makes domestic photomask blanks, recycled like cullet
idea: Use New York flame-hydrolysis high-purity fused silica (the soot method behind optical-fiber preforms) as mask substrate, and add a cullet-style reclaim line that strips chrome, repolishes and recoats retired DRAM masks for reuse.

title: Steel minimill for silicon: remelt kerf and scrap wafers domestically
idea: Electric-arc minimills make new steel from scrap; build a U.S. silicon minimill that collects wire-saw kerf, broken and spent test wafers and off-spec ingot tops, acid-cleans and plasma-refines them, and directionally solidifies them into CZ recharge feedstock.

title: Riveted hybrid bonds: redundant pads with nitrogen plasma activation
idea: Shipbuilders put several rivets in every joint so one failure is harmless; activate hybrid-bond surfaces with N2/O2 plasma (no argon) and give each critical vertical signal three parallel bond pads feeding a majority/OR receiver, so voids from the gentler activation never open a circuit.
note: Redundant TSV/pad schemes common.

title: Double-ended sub-wordline drivers survive any single driver failure
idea: Ideal result: a wordline that cannot be cut off. Drive each sub-wordline from both ends with drivers that can be disabled individually; if self-test finds one dead or a mid-line break, the other end drives the line.

title: Reusable donor wafers supply periphery silicon via layer transfer
idea: Ideal result: silicon that is used ten times. Grow periphery device layers on a porous-silicon or SiGe release substrate, transfer the thin layer onto the bonded memory stack, then polish and reuse the donor wafer.

title: Tungsten-free periphery metal designed for selective recovery
idea: Ideal result: periphery made only of materials you can get back. Replace W contacts and wordline straps with Mo and Ru using liner chemistries chosen for selective wet dissolution, so end-of-life dies yield separable Cu, Mo and Ru streams.

title: Load-and-kill instruction frees memory at a value's last use
idea: IFR: memory frees itself the instant data is dead. Closest: a compiler-emitted load-and-kill instruction marks a line or page dead after its final read; the cache drops it without writeback and the OS reclaims fully dead frames immediately.
note: Dead-block hints and invalidate-without-writeback exist; small gains.

title: Eliminate metal electrodes: degenerate epitaxial silicon plates replace TiN and tungsten
idea: Eliminate sputtered TiN and tungsten electrodes: form both capacitor plates and node contacts from in-situ phosphorus-doped (>1e21 cm-3) epitaxial Si or SiGe grown with hydrogen carrier, so there are no metal targets, no argon PVD and no tungsten; at that doping the depletion penalty is under ~5% of capacitance.
note: Poly-Si SIS plates were abandoned for MIM because of depletion.

title: Cryogenic CO2-argon aerosol cleaning replaces wet rinse steps
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transitions: replace selected post-CMP and pre-deposition wet-clean, rinse and dry steps with a cryogenic aerosol of solid CO2/Ar micro-crystals. The crystals knock particles off by momentum transfer and then sublime, leaving no liquid or residue.

title: Paraffin phase-change lid keeps stacks under 85 C
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transitions: a sealed U.S.-made paraffin/fatty-acid phase-change pack bonded to the memory-stack lid melts at ~70 C, absorbing AI burst heat so DRAM never enters the 85 C+ double-refresh range, and refreezes between bursts.

title: Kombucha: bioleaching vats recover metals from scrapped memory modules
idea: Stimulus 'kombucha SCOBY' (a living culture doing chemistry in a jar) -> a 10-person team runs Acidithiobacillus and cyanogenic Chromobacterium bioleaching vats on shredded DIMMs and memory boards, recovering gold, palladium, copper and tantalum at ambient temperature.

title: Ozone-gas and UV dry stripping to cut ultrapure water
idea: Periodic-table walk, O (8): replace sulfuric-peroxide resist strips and organic cleans with UV-activated O3 gas and humidified-ozone single-wafer dry oxidation, keeping wet steps only for metal and particle removal.

title: Cell-pitch hybrid bonding of separate capacitor and transistor wafers
idea: Combine wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding with the 1T1C cell: all capacitors are made on one wafer (free to use high thermal budget and high-k) and all access transistors on another. The wafers are bonded at ~40-60 nm pitch, and ~1% void-killed bonds are accepted as cell errors.
note: 40-60 nm hybrid-bond pitch is ~10x beyond state of the art.

title: Magnify sharing: eight array-only wafers on one periphery wafer
idea: Bond eight array-only wafers (cells, wordlines and bitlines; about 4 masks each, no periphery) onto one CMOS periphery wafer. Nano-TSV global bitline risers and a tier-select transistor let each sense amp serve all eight tiers.

title: Coulomb-blockade island chain as a leak-proof access channel on quartz
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation, taken to the extreme: segment the access channel into a chain of 1-2 nm nanocrystal islands self-assembled on a quartz or sapphire substrate (no silicon wafer). In the off state the single-electron charging energy (>> kT at room temperature for <2 nm islands) blocks transport exponentially with chain length; the wordline gate lifts the blockade for access.

title: Onion-shell 3D access devices: one etch, one clean, many tiers
idea: Random stimulus 'onion': many layers around one core, peeled at once. In a vertical-bitline 3D DRAM the access transistors of all ~32 tiers are concentric gate-all-around shells around one bitline hole, defined by a single hole etch, one dry clean and one conformal channel/gate deposition, with each tier's wordline a lateral plane.

title: Piezoelectronic pressure switch replaces silicon access transistor
idea: Box: MIM cap x piezoelectronic transistor (PMN-PT actuator squeezing a SmSe piezoresistive layer through its insulator-metal transition) x SA x BEOL stack x Si x sputter + anneal. The wordline drives the piezo, pressure drops channel resistance >1e4x; unpowered, the channel is a gapped insulator with no junction to leak.

title: Cell-stamp e-beam: a million shaped beamlets each write one cell
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x standard sensing x 2D x Si x massively parallel e-beam with a programmable aperture plate shaped to the cell motif. Because the array is a lattice, each of ~1e6 beamlets is shaped into the same cell feature (parallel character projection) and the stage scan makes each beamlet write its own sub-array tile, so there are no masks and shot count falls by orders of magnitude vs pixel writing.

title: NAND fab swing lines producing 3D vertical FeRAM
idea: Worse: let NAND fabs idle in every flash glut while DRAM is short. Flip: reuse NAND high-aspect-ratio etch and ALD lines to build 3D vertically stacked HZO ferroelectric capacitor memory, so lines swing between NAND and nonvolatile DRAM-class output with demand.
note: HZO endurance ~1e10-1e12 falls short of DRAM-class; Micron NVDRAM shows feasibility but not swing economics.

title: Gate-triggered Mott-gap channel gives access device without subthreshold tail
idea: Effect: filling-controlled Mott transition. The access channel is a correlated oxide (e.g., electron-doped SmNiO3 or Ca2RuO4) where the wordline field adds ~0.1 carrier per site and collapses the Mott gap abruptly; below critical filling it is a gapped insulator whose leakage scales as exp(-Eg/kT) instead of following a gradual subthreshold slope.
note: 0.1 e/site needs ~1e14 cm^-2 gating, near dielectric limits.

title: Swap thermionic switching for heterojunction tunnel-FET access device
idea: Substitute the MOSFET's thermionic barrier with band-to-band tunneling: a p+ SiGe source on the bitline side, an intrinsic Si channel and a lightly doped n storage side. The device is asymmetric (it tunnels only when the wordline is high) and sub-60 mV/dec, and the lightly doped storage side suppresses ambipolar leakage.
note: TFET DRAM access studied; on-current and ambipolarity remain hard.

title: Substitute periodic refresh with static Esaki tunnel-diode latch per cell
idea: Substitute capacitor decay plus refresh with a bistable hold: two series interband (Esaki) tunnel diodes at the storage node form a negative-differential-resistance latch with two stable voltages. A tiny valley current (target ~pA) holds the state continuously, and the access transistor still reads and writes it.
note: Tunnel-diode SRAM (TSRAM) explored in 1990s; pA valley current at DRAM cell area and PVR unproven.

title: Single-electron transistor sensing attofarad storage nodes
idea: Combine a room-temperature silicon single-electron transistor (sub-3 nm island) as the in-cell sense element with a 10-50 aF storage node, so a few hundred electrons, not ~30,000, encode a bit. The SET's Coulomb oscillations turn each few-electron change into a large current change, read through a gain path that never discharges the node.
note: RT SETs need sub-3 nm islands with huge variability; Yano-type single-electron memory precedent.

title: Hollow TSVs that are also microfluidic coolant channels
idea: Make annular TSVs whose copper shell carries power/signal while the hollow core carries a two-phase dielectric coolant through the whole stack, combining vertical interconnect and cooling in one via field.
note: Microfluidic TSVs studied (Georgia Tech); two-phase flow in micron cores faces large pressure drop.

title: Image-sensor pixel bonding: one sense amp per 64 cells
idea: Borrowed from stacked CMOS image sensors with pixel-level Cu-Cu hybrid bonds and per-pixel ADCs: bond the array wafer face-to-face to a logic wafer at sub-1 um pitch so every 64-cell micro-bitline lands on its own sense amp, eliminating long bitlines entirely.

title: Printing-press nanoimprint drum for continuous wafer streams
idea: Magnify lithography throughput 20x by passing wafers on a conveyor under a rotating nanoimprint drum carrying the array pattern, printing one layer per second like a newspaper press.

title: Minify leakage by decades with SiC-substrate wide-bandgap access transistors
idea: Build the 1T1C access device as a 4H-SiC MOSFET on SiC substrates, with capacitors deposited above. SiC's intrinsic carrier density is ~1e-8 cm^-3 versus ~1e10 in Si, so junction and band-to-band leakage almost disappear.

title: Magnify the substrate 100x: Gen-10.5 display fabs make memory
idea: Repurpose overbuilt Gen-10.5 LCD/OLED backplane lines (2.9 x 3.4 m glass) to deposit 16-32 stacked layers of IGZO 2T0C gain cells at a 0.5-1 um rule, with periphery on small CMOS chiplets bonded along tile edges; panels are diced into memory tiles.
note: Sub-um rules on Gen-10.5 glass and $0.1/GB both look off by several x.

title: Eliminate analog sensing: Coulomb-blockade dots hold quantized electron counts
idea: Eliminate the continuous charge level: store 0, 1, 2 or 3 extra electrons on a ~2-nm silicon or metal nanodot whose charging energy (>150 meV, ~6 kT) quantizes the stored charge, so each cell holds 2 bits as discrete states read by an integrated single-electron-transistor electrometer.

title: Eliminate the semiconductor channel: NEM contact relay access switch
idea: Remove the transistor channel altogether and isolate each storage node with a nanoelectromechanical cantilever relay whose off state is a 5-10 nm air gap. The wordline electrostatically pulls the beam into contact for read/write; once released there is no subthreshold, junction or GIDL path, only gap tunneling (<1e-24 A).

title: Eliminate leakage pathways: Coulomb-blockade-locked silicon nanodot storage node
idea: Store a small charge on a 2-3 nm Si nanodot (LPCVD-grown or e-beam defined) that gates a sense FET and is separated from the bitline by a tunnel barrier; the >100 meV Coulomb charging energy blocks single-electron escape at hold bias, exponentially suppressing leakage. A write gate lowers the barrier.
note: Room-temperature single-electron memory (Hitachi) known; sub-3 nm uniformity unsolved.

title: Eliminate the Boltzmann tax: all-silicon bilayer tunnel-FET periphery at 0.3 V
idea: Build decoders, sense control and datapath from electron-hole bilayer tunnel FETs in silicon (no Ge or III-V indium), whose band-to-band switching allows sub-60 mV/decade slopes and a 0.3 V supply.
note: TFET drive current remains too low for DRAM periphery speed.

title: Infrared through-silicon optical vias replace TSV stacks
idea: Eliminate copper vias: silicon is transparent at 1.3 um, so each thinned die carries Ge photodiodes and micro-emitters in metal-free windows; beams pass straight through intervening dies to receivers on the target die, addressed by position or wavelength.

title: Charge-coupled pillar: vertical shift-register DRAM, no capacitor
idea: Reverse 3D NAND's vertical string: store charge packets under each word-tier gate of an oxide-semiconductor channel pillar and clock them up the pillar CCD-style (three-phase gates) to one sense node at the top, so each pillar is a 64-bit vertical shift register with no per-bit transistor or capacitor.

title: Sense amps on the host: bitline-pitch bonding across dies
idea: Rearrange array and periphery: the DRAM die carries only cell arrays whose bitline segments end in hybrid-bond pads, and sense amplifiers, decoders and I/O live on a logic-process die bonded below at ~1 um pitch. The DRAM process loses its periphery steps, and fast logic transistors sense at lower voltage.
note: Bitline pitch far below bond pitch; bond-pad capacitance hurts sensing.

title: Vacuum-sealed storage node with field-emission nanogap access switch
idea: TRIZ #39 Inert atmosphere (vacuum): suspend each storage node on thin oxide posts inside a sealed nano-vacuum cavity so no junction or dielectric film touches it, and access it through a gated vacuum-channel field-emission diode with a <50-nm gap that conducts only above its turn-on field. Vacuum has no traps or band tails, so hold leakage is set by Fowler-Nordheim at low field (aA-class).

title: Few-electron quantum-dot bit sensed by an adjacent single-electron transistor
idea: TRIZ #1 Segmentation taken to the limit: store each bit as ~5-10 electrons on a <3-nm Si or SnO2 quantum dot whose Coulomb charging energy (>100 meV) blocks leakage, and sense it non-destructively with an adjacent single-electron transistor whose current swings ~10x per electron.
note: Hitachi-era single-electron memory; room-temperature dot uniformity remains the blocker.

title: GaN/AlN tunnel-diode pair self-holds the bit without refresh
idea: TRIZ #25 Self-service: let the cell maintain itself. On GaN-on-sapphire, two room-temperature GaN/AlN resonant tunnelling diodes are stacked in series with the storage node at their midpoint; their negative-differential-resistance curves intersect at two stable points, so the node self-restores against leakage at pA standby current, accessed through one GaN HEMT.
note: Same NDR latch concept with GaN RTDs.

title: Nanomechanical gap switch isolates the gain-cell storage gate
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution, used in reverse (field -> mechanics): replace the write transistor of a 2T0C gain cell with an electrostatically actuated vertical NEMS contact switch built in the tier stack. An open air gap has essentially zero leakage, so the read transistor's gate keeps its charge until gate-dielectric leakage alone drains it.
note: Same as I-00628; 1e15 contact cycles far beyond demonstrated NEMS relay endurance.

title: Antiferromagnetic Mn3Sn bits pack densely with no stray fields
idea: TRIZ #8 Anti-weight (counterweight): each bit's antiparallel magnetic sublattices counterbalance, so cells emit no stray field and can sit edge-to-edge; spin-orbit torque from a heavy-metal line switches the noncollinear antiferromagnet in sub-ns, an antiferromagnetic tunnel junction reads it, and retention needs no power.

title: Synaptic-vesicle quantal storage: Coulomb-staircase multilevel node
idea: Synapses release transmitter in fixed quanta. Make the storage node a sub-3 nm metal island (e.g. an Au cluster in SiO2) whose >100 meV charging energy quantizes stored charge into discrete electron-number plateaus. A single-electron-transistor sense node writes and reads four robust levels per cell, so the levels are set by physics rather than analog trimming.

title: Shaker-channel ball-and-chain NEMS access gate
idea: Copying the K+ channel's N-type inactivation ball that plugs the pore, replace the access FET with a nanoelectromechanical gate: a conductive nanoball on a compliant SiN tether is pulled by the wordline field into a contact cavity bridging bitline and storage node, and the tether spring plus a self-timed 'inactivation' electrode retracts it, leaving a ~3 nm vacuum gap.

title: Coin-counting purse: single-electron box stores countable electron numbers
idea: Count coins instead of weighing gold: couple a 3-5-nm Si or Pt island (e-beam litho plus oxidation thinning, or ALD nanoparticle) through one tunnel junction to a reservoir so Coulomb blockade (>150 meV charging energy) makes occupancy discrete; each cell stores 0-3 extra electrons (2 bits), read by a nearby single-electron transistor electrometer without disturbing the count.

title: SF6 breakers to vacuum interrupters: nano vacuum-gap access switch
idea: The grid is replacing SF6 gas-insulated breakers with vacuum interrupters because vacuum insulates without fluorinated gas. Build a lateral 20-30 nm vacuum-gap field-emission switch, sealed by a PVD cap, whose emitter tip conducts only when the wordline gate thins the barrier; off-state current is Fowler-Nordheim limited and there is no substrate junction.
note: Same vacuum field-emission access device.

title: Light-switch air gap: NEMS relay access device in BEOL tiers
idea: A wall switch draws nothing when off because of its air gap; make each 3D cell's access device a laterally actuated ~10 nm-gap TiN/Ru NEMS relay built at BEOL temperatures, whose near-zero off-current lets the capacitor shrink to ~0.3 fF (signal-limited, not retention-limited) and removes refresh.
note: NEM-relay memory widely studied; ~1e12+ contact endurance and stiction at 10 nm gaps unproven in arrays.

title: Western Electric relay contacts reborn as NEM access relays
idea: Revive the Bell System's palladium-contact telephone relays: each access device is a nanoelectromechanical relay with palladium/platinum contacts from Montana's Stillwater mines, built with the aluminum-hinge micromirror MEMS process already run at high volume in Texas, which shows >1e12 switching cycles. An open contact leaks nothing.
note: NEM-relay memory widely studied; 1e15-cycle contact endurance and nanoscale stiction are the blockers.

title: Field-emitter-array Williams tube writing charge spots on blanket film
idea: Revive the Williams tube and GE's BEAMOS: a CMOS die carrying a Spindt-tip field-emitter array (one tip per 64x64 spot patch, electrostatically deflected) is vacuum-bonded a few microns above an unpatterned MOS/dielectric target, writing bits as ~30 nm charge spots and reading them by beam-induced current. The storage plane has no lithographic cell, capacitor or access transistor.

title: Ferreed-like latching NEMS relays as access devices in 3D tiers
idea: Revive the Bell ferreed crosspoint (a reed latched by remanent magnetism) as each 3D cell's access device: a ruthenium-contact nanoelectromechanical relay with essentially zero off-current, built in BEOL tiers without single-crystal silicon or tungsten. With leakage gone, storage capacitors shrink to ~1-2 fF, sized only for read margin on short local bitlines.
note: Same NEMS relay access device core.

title: Sealed charge-conserving double-island cell with no path to ground
idea: Invert 'the storage node connects to the outside through a leaky path' -> make the bit a sealed, charge-conserving pair. Two metal nano-islands share one tunnel barrier and have no other conductive path; the bit is which island holds the excess electrons (dipole up/down), flipped by a field pulse from adjacent gates and read by capacitive coupling to a sense FET.

title: Squeeze to switch: strain-gated piezoelectronic access device
idea: Inverts 'a switch is gated by a field in its channel': an AlScN or PMN-PT piezo actuator compresses a SmSe-type piezoresistive channel that undergoes a pressure-driven insulator-to-metal transition; uncompressed, the channel is a true gapped insulator with no subthreshold tail, and actuation needs <0.2 V.

title: Per-subarray micro-ring modulators replace global data lines
idea: Inverting 'data leaves the bank on copper': a silicon-nitride waveguide layer in the top BEOL runs over every subarray, each subarray's local sense output drives a micro-ring modulator on its own wavelength, and 32 subarrays share one waveguide by WDM to the package edge.
note: Monolithic DRAM photonics proposed since 2010; ring thermal tuning at DRAM temperatures is costly.

title: Complementary nanotube sense amps built directly over the array
idea: Inverting 'sense amps must sit in the silicon substrate': cross-coupled sense amps are fabricated from complementary carbon-nanotube FETs at <400 C in the BEOL directly above the cell mats, pitch-matched to the bitlines through short vias.

title: Leakage-balanced bistable floating body that needs no refresh controller
idea: Inverting 'leakage is the enemy': floating-body cells are biased so gate-induced drain leakage generation and junction recombination balance at two stable body potentials, so each cell holds its state statically and the refresh counter, scheduler and temperature-based refresh logic are deleted.
note: Close to biristor/T-RAM bistable cells; leakage-balance margins and variability.

title: Through-silicon light: vertical optical links across IR-transparent dies
idea: Invert 'vertical connections need metal TSVs': silicon is transparent at 1310 nm, so each thinned die carries small emitters and Ge photodiodes in metal-free windows and data beams straight up the stack, die to die, with no holes drilled.

title: Sodium-beta-alumina double-layer capacitors give 4x charge per area
idea: An electric double layer is a ~0.4 nm capacitor: ~20 uF/cm2 (~200 fF/um2) versus ~60 fF/um2 for ZrO2 stacks. A 5 nm Na-beta-alumina solid electrolyte (ionic conductor, electronic insulator) gives RC = (t/sigma*A)*C of ~1 ns for a 0.2 fF cell, and non-Faradaic charging causes no chemical wear.

title: Cold-crucible Czochralski: silicon contains itself, no quartz consumed
idea: First principle: the quartz crucible is consumed only because it touches molten Si at 1414 C, but molten Si can sit in a thin frozen skin of its own Si inside a segmented, water-cooled copper crucible heated by induction. Grow DRAM-grade crystals by skull-melting CZ; the copper crucible is repaired and reused indefinitely, and the skull is remelted into the next charge.

title: Infrared light-through-silicon vias replace TSVs in memory stacks
idea: Silicon is transparent beyond 1.1 um, so a thinned DRAM stack is already an optical medium. Bond 1.3 um InGaAs micro-emitters on the base die that shine straight up through windowed metal stacks of 12 thinned dies; each tier has partially-absorbing Ge photodiode taps and electro-absorption shutters for the return path, forming vertical free-space buses with no holes drilled.

title: Coulomb-blockade nanodot node suppresses leakage by charging energy
idea: A ~2 nm Si nanodot has C ~0.2 aF, so the single-electron charging energy e^2/2C ~0.4 eV ~15 kT, and every escape is penalized by ~exp(-15) on top of the tunnel barrier. Store a bit as N vs N+k electrons, sense with an SET-like gain stage, and vote across 3 dots per bit.
note: Single-electron memory (Yano) is old; room-temperature variability is the killer.

title: Radiant floor tiles: sense amps under array enable short, low-voltage bitlines
idea: Lay sense amps under the mats like heating tiles under a floor, on a logic layer joined by 0.3-0.5 um-pitch hybrid bonds (one per bitline), so bitlines shrink from ~512 to ~128 cells; the ~4x lower C_BL triples read signal, and that margin is spent cutting VARY from 1.0 V to ~0.5 V.
note: SA area per 128-cell segment far exceeds the segment footprint.

title: Bunk beds: upper cell tier serves as lower tier's sensing reference
idea: Bunk beds stack two sleepers on one floor plan: layer-transfer a second single-crystal cell tier above the first array's capacitors and drop its bitlines to the same sense amps, so each sense amp compares a lower-tier bitline with the upper-tier bitline directly overhead (vertical folded pairing). Sense amps and periphery are shared, and the part is a standard DDR5/HBM die of twice the capacity.
note: Same as I-04751 (vertical folded pairing); single-crystal layer transfer over capacitors strains thermal budget.

title: Lava lamp: self-assembled multiferroic nanopillars define bits without lithography
idea: Random stimulus 'lava lamp' (blobs separate by themselves) -> co-deposition of BiFeO3 and CoFe2O4 spontaneously phase-separates into vertical magnetic nanopillars about 20 nm apart in a ferroelectric matrix. Each pillar is a non-volatile bit switched by electric-field strain, and a coarse template guides pillar positions.
note: Known BFO-CFO self-assembly; per-pillar addressing and readout unsolved.

title: Hearing aid: logic die reads DRAM bitlines directly through bonds
idea: Like a hearing aid amplifying faint sound: fine-pitch hybrid bonds expose DRAM local bitlines to a logic die stacked face-to-face, and the logic die's sense amplifiers resolve 50-100 mV signals directly. The DRAM-side global datapath, serializers and I/O drivers are deleted.

title: Vacuum-channel field-emission nanotriode gates each storage node
idea: Box: stacked cap x lateral ~10 nm vacuum-gap field-emission triode with a hafnium-carbide emitter x current SA x sealed-cavity BEOL tier x Si x self-aligned cavity seal. Below emission threshold the vacuum channel has no band, no generation and no GIDL; a gate pulse thins the barrier for Fowler-Nordheim emission to read/write.

title: Vertical CCD memory: charge buckets shifted down gate-stacked pillars
idea: [Box: charge packets in channel potential wells | no access transistor, clocked word-plates | floating-diffusion sense at pillar base | 3D-NAND-like plate stack | Si or IGZO channel | blanket plate deposition + one hole etch] Each tier plate is a CCD gate around a vertical channel; three-phase clocking shifts packets down to one sense node at the base and recirculates them to the top, turning each hole into a 64-128-bit rotating shift register.

title: Vertical NEMS relays as zero-leakage DRAM access switches
idea: [Box: MIM charge | electrostatic vertical nanorelay | charge-share SA | BEOL over CMOS | Si | sacrificial release of a ~10 nm air gap] A vertically actuated nanocantilever touches the storage-node contact only while the wordline pulls it in; through an air gap the off-state leakage is essentially zero, so the cell holds charge for hours.
note: Same as NEMS relay access device; contact endurance and stiction at 10 nm gaps.

title: Infrared light crosses thinned silicon instead of TSVs
idea: Box: DRAM x standard x Ge photodiode receivers x 1310 nm micro-emitter arrays shining vertically through the dies x thinned Si (transparent at 1.3 um) x no via etch. Signals cross the stack as light through the silicon bulk while power uses a few large peripheral vias.

title: Negative-capacitance HZO access gate removes the wordline pump
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: negative-capacitance FET with matched HZO gate layer | sense: standard | integration: monolithic | substrate: bulk | fab: ALD]. A capacitance-matched ferroelectric layer gives the access transistor ~40 mV/decade subthreshold swing, so it reaches today's off-leakage at 0 V and today's on-current at ~1.1 V instead of a ~3 V pumped wordline, pushing the leakage tail down by orders of magnitude.

title: Po: the whole bit is one electron — room-temperature silicon dot box
idea: Po: the whole bit is one electron. Extracted: a sub-3 nm Si nanocrystal embedded in an oxide pillar has Coulomb charging energy >10 kT at 300 K; the bit is n vs n+1 electrons, sensed through the gate of a nanowire channel, with retention set by an energy gap rather than by charge volume.

title: Tunnel-FET access transistors in vertical 3D strings
idea: Po: the transistor opens only by quantum tunnelling. Make the vertical access device a heterojunction TFET (p+ SiGe source, intrinsic Si channel, n drain) with no thermionic subthreshold tail, giving aA-level off-current; its low on-current is acceptable because the 3D storage node is only ~1 fF.

title: Coulomb-blockade storage dots stacked in silicon nanowire tiers
idea: Po: the charge is too lonely to leave. Store each bit as a few electrons on a <3 nm Si dot whose charging energy (>10 kT at 300 K) blocks single-electron escape, coupled by direct tunnelling to a nanowire channel in each tier, with tiers formed from Si/SiGe superlattice nanowires.
note: RT Coulomb blockade needs <2 nm dots; few-electron signals and write/retention barrier trade-off are known issues.

title: Books-on-a-shelf: DRAM dies standing edge-on over logic
idea: Po: the stack lies on its side. Stand thinned DRAM dies upright like books, each bonded along one polished edge carrying fine-pitch pads to the logic die beneath, with coolant flowing in the gaps between dies.

title: Vacuum-gap floating node written by field emission
idea: Worsen: store charge behind oxides whose traps leak and wear out. Flip: put the storage node on a nanoscale island isolated by a sealed 3-5 nm vacuum gap; writes use field emission across the gap, and retention relies on vacuum, which has no traps, no stress-induced leakage and no wear.

title: Optically gated wide-gap photoconductive access switches
idea: Worse: keep a gate field on a narrow-gap channel that leaks in the dark. Flip: replace wordline gates with GaN photoconductive switches lit by row-addressed micro-LED stripes; in the dark a wide-gap photoconductor holds essentially zero free carriers, so the off state is near-ideal.

title: Nanoscale vacuum-channel access switch immune to temperature
idea: Worse at 125 C: use any solid channel whose carrier population rises with temperature. Flip: make the access switch a ~20 nm vacuum gap between a sharp field-emission tip and the storage node, gated by the wordline; with a 4.5 eV work function, thermionic current at 125 C is effectively zero.

title: Domain-wall racetrack shift registers in interposer back-end layers
idea: Worsen: give random-access cells to data that is always read in sequence. Flip: deposit magnetic nanowire racetracks in the interposer back-end, where current pulses shift domain walls past one read/write head per track, so weights and activations stream out with no capacitor and no transistor per bit.

title: Potter's wheel: polar vortex chirality in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices
idea: A potter knows that a pot thrown clockwise looks the same as one thrown counter-clockwise until you feel the spiral. In PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices the polarization curls into ~10 nm vortices whose handedness (chirality) a field can switch; it is read optically or through resistance coupled to the piezoresponse.

title: Embargoed Soviet tube engineer: vacuum-nanogap field-emission access switch
idea: Soviet designers kept vacuum tubes in the MiG-25 because they shrugged off radiation. Put the storage node behind a sealed 10-20 nm vacuum cavity facing a sharp metal emitter tip; the wordline gate raises the tip field to switch on field-emission current, and with the gate low the gap has no carriers, no junction and no trap states to leak through.

title: Geologist's squeezed crystal: piezoelectronic access transistor
idea: A geologist knows squeezing certain crystals turns insulators into metals. Each access switch is a piezoelectronic transistor: a thin PMN-PT actuator driven at ~0.15 V compresses a SmSe pressure-driven insulator-metal layer between bitline and storage node, switching it in acoustic-transit time, with a wide-gap blocking layer in series to reach DRAM-grade off-resistance.

title: Coin collector counts every coin: few-electron Coulomb-blockade cells
idea: A coin collector tracks each coin. Each bit is ~50-200 electrons on a 5 nm silicon or metal nanodot, reached through Coulomb-blockade tunnel junctions of a single-electron access transistor; the island charging energy (>10 kT) blocks leakage, and a ~0.3 V gate swing moves the electrons.

title: Piezo-strain switched pressure-sensitive phase bit from deep-sea electronics
idea: Deep-sea designers see pressure shift material phases; on chip, a thin piezoelectric (PMN-PT or AlScN) squeezes a pressure-sensitive layer such as SmSe or a Mott oxide by GPa-equivalent stress, switching its resistance 100-1000x, while a ferroelastic latch in the piezo holds the strain. Writing needs ~100-200 mV because strain, not current, does the work.
note: IBM piezoelectronic transistor (SmSe) precedent; nanoscale strain transfer and latch unproven.

title: Picosecond-switched hidden charge-density-wave state in 1T-TaS2 bits
idea: Cryogenic and ultrafast computing users exploit 1T-TaS2's metastable 'hidden' charge-density-wave state, entered by a ~30 ps electrical pulse and exited by a longer heating pulse, with 10-100x resistance contrast. Strain or doping engineering pushes the hidden state's lifetime from cryogenic toward room temperature for DRAM-like retention.
note: 1T-TaS2 hidden state lifetime is cryogenic; room-T retention needs a miracle.

title: Venus-probe vacuum-gap switches with film-thickness-defined critical dimensions
idea: Extreme user: 460C Venus landers, where only vacuum electronics survive. Make the access switch a field-emission vacuum nano-gap whose 5 nm gap is set by an ALD sacrificial layer removed late, so the critical dimension comes from film thickness, not lithography, and off-current is near zero.

title: Skyrmion racetrack in synthetic antiferromagnet tubes
idea: Scale bits down to 10 nm topological spin whirls: compensated synthetic-antiferromagnet skyrmions have no Hall drift and move at km/s, so a vertical racetrack tube stores 64 bits per access device.
note: Vertical SAF racetrack tubes very hard to fabricate; widely researched.

title: Spin-crossover molecules switch between high and low spin
idea: Scale down to one Fe(II) complex: spin-crossover molecules with wide room-temperature thermal hysteresis toggle high-spin and low-spin by field pulses, changing junction conductance by 10x.
note: Same spin-crossover mechanism at single-molecule scale; molecular crossbars unproven.

title: Room-temperature Coulomb-blockade island isolates the storage node
idea: Scale jump to the few-nanometre quantum dot: insert a sub-2 nm silicon nanocrystal between access channel and storage node so the single-electron charging energy (~200-300 meV) exceeds 8 kT; in hold the bias sits inside the blockade window so leakage is exponentially suppressed, while the wordline shifts the dot level to allow ns sequential tunnelling during access.

title: Nano-vacuum field-emission access: a vacuum tube shrunk to 10 nm
idea: Scale jump from 1940s vacuum tubes to a sealed ~10 nm cavity: a sharpened Si tip on the storage-node side faces a Si/TiN collector across vacuum, encircled by a gate ring; Fowler-Nordheim emission turns on exponentially only above a gate-field threshold, and below it the gap holds no carriers at all.

title: Coulomb-blockade nanocrystal storage islands read by gain FETs
idea: Molecule-scale jump: 5-20 electrons are stored on a ~3 nm Si or metal nanocrystal between thin tunnel barriers, where charging energy >> kT blocks leakage, and read non-destructively through the threshold shift of an adjacent gain FET; writes use low-field direct tunneling that does not wear the oxide, and no refresh is issued.

title: Two-faced wafers: DRAM arrays on front and back
idea: After front-side DRAM is complete, bond to a carrier, thin from the back to ~5 um and build a second array on the backside with U.S. backside-power processing know-how, sharing one periphery through nano-TSVs.

title: Cr2O3 magnetoelectric memory's 34 C Neel point swapped for BiFeO3
idea: Voltage-controlled exchange-bias memories built on Cr2O3 stalled because its Neel temperature (~307 K) is below normal operation, let alone 125 C. Use La-doped BiFeO3 (TN ~640 K, Tc ~1100 K): a 100-200 mV pulse switches its ferroelectric polarization, which rotates the antiferromagnetic axis and, through exchange, a CoFe free layer read by an MTJ.
note: MESO/Heron-style BFO exchange switching; 100-200 mV writes are optimistic.

title: Vacuum tube returns as nanogap field-emission access transistor
idea: Vacuum tubes and Candescent's field-emission displays died on size, heaters and emitter non-uniformity. Use a ~20 nm vacuum-channel transistor in which a sharp source emits by Fowler-Nordheim tunneling only when the gate lowers the barrier. With no semiconductor in the channel, the off state has no thermal generation and no junction leakage, and a gap shorter than the mean free path does not need hard vacuum.

title: Bubble memory's bias-magnet killer removed with zero-field skyrmion loops
idea: Magnetic bubble memory (TI, Intel Magnetics) never needed refresh but died because it required permanent bias magnets and coil drives, making it slow and bulky. Fix: use exchange-biased synthetic-antiferromagnet multilayers that stabilize skyrmions at zero applied field, move them with spin-orbit current around loops, and keep bubble memory's proven major/minor-loop redundancy with an on-chip bad-loop map.

title: Antiferromagnetic memory's weak readout fixed with Mn3Sn tunnel junctions
idea: CuMnAs electrically switched antiferromagnetic memory stalled because its readout signal (anisotropic magnetoresistance ~0.1%) was too weak. Fix: use noncollinear antiferromagnets such as Mn3Sn or Mn3Pt, whose momentum-space spin splitting yields large tunneling magnetoresistance in an all-antiferromagnet tunnel junction, while keeping spin-orbit-torque switching.

title: Single femtosecond pulse toggles ferrimagnet bit: light-written magnetic memory
idea: Effect walk: helicity-independent all-optical switching in ferrimagnets. A 10-nm GdFeCo (or rare-earth-free Mn-based ferrimagnet) free layer of an MTJ sits under a plasmonic nano-antenna fed by a waveguide; each ~100-fs pulse deterministically toggles magnetization through ultrafast sublattice demagnetization, and TMR reads it electrically.
note: Known AOS-MTJ research; on-chip fs light delivery is impractical.

title: Voltage-only magnetoelectric cell read by inverse Rashba-Edelstein voltage
idea: Effect walk: magnetoelectric coupling + spin-to-charge conversion. A 10-nm La-doped BiFeO3 film reorients its canted antiferromagnetic order at ~100 mV, dragging an exchange-coupled CoFe nanomagnet; reading passes a tiny spin current into a Bi/Ag or topological interface whose inverse Rashba-Edelstein effect outputs a voltage whose sign is the bit.
note: Essentially Intel MESO; BFO switching speed and endurance and tiny IREE output are known gaps.

title: Band-to-band tunneling FET sense amplifier enables 0.4 V array voltage
idea: Effect: band-to-band (Zener) tunneling. Build the SA cross-coupled pair from vertical Ge/Si heterojunction TFETs with ~30 mV/dec turn-on, so the latch regenerates with only 0.4 V across it; complementary n/p TFET pairs handle their one-way conduction.
note: TFET on-current too low for fast latches; widely pursued with poor results.

title: Vacuum-channel field-emission nanotriode as stacked access device
idea: Field emission: each tier's access device is a 10 nm sacrificially formed vacuum gap between a sharp emitter tip and a collector. A gate electrode modulates the Fowler-Nordheim emission, and with zero field the vacuum carries no current at all.

title: BiFeO3 exchange-coupled magnetoelectric tiers via layer transfer
idea: Magnetoelectric exchange coupling: about 100 mV across La-doped BiFeO3 rotates its antiferromagnetic order, which flips an exchange-coupled CoFe magnet read by an MTJ. The BFO is grown at high temperature on donor wafers, then layer-transferred into stacked BEOL tiers.
note: Intel MESO/Ramesh lineage; BFO layer transfer and switching speed/reliability unproven.

title: Coulomb-blockade silicon nanodots hold countable electrons in all-silicon cells
idea: Effect: a 5 nm Si nanodot has a charging energy well above kT, so Coulomb blockade adds an escape barrier on top of the SiO2 tunnel barrier. Store ~10-30 electrons by direct tunneling and read them with an adjacent room-temperature single-electron-transistor charge sensor; the cell needs only Si, SiO2 and doped-Si wiring.
note: Room-temperature SE memory known since 1990s; retention vs tunneling speed tradeoff.

title: Strain-driven self-rolling membranes form Swiss-roll capacitors without deep etch
idea: Effect: strain-gradient self-rolling. Put a pre-strained SiNx/TiN/HfO2/TiN stack on a sacrificial Ge strip in each lateral 3D DRAM cell; releasing the strip lets built-in strain roll the stack into a 4-6 turn micro-roll inside the tier cavity, multiplying capacitor area with no vertical etch.

title: Photorefractive hologram recalls top-k keys so values stay offloaded
idea: All keys of a long context are written as superimposed holograms in an Fe:LiNbO3 crystal. Shining the current query beam reconstructs correlation peaks whose brightness equals each query-key dot product, all in parallel, and a camera picks the top-k tokens. Only those k values are fetched from flash or CXL, so the bulk KV never sits in DRAM.

title: Si: Coulomb-blockaded 3 nm silicon dot holds exact electron counts
idea: Shrink the storage node to a ~3 nm silicon dot whose single-electron charging energy (>100 meV, far above kT) blocks tunneling unless the gate is pulsed; the bit is 0 or N electrons, so leakage becomes a rare discrete event instead of a continuous drain, read by an integrated single-electron transistor.

title: C: carbon nanotube sense-amp tier stacked above the array
idea: Print aligned semiconducting carbon nanotube films at <350 C on the bitline-contact level and build complementary CNT-FET latch sense amps and column muxes there, so the SA stripes move vertically over the mats instead of beside them. CNT's high mobility at 0.5-0.7 V keeps latch speed while the array below is untouched.

title: Nanoporous-carbon ionic double-layer storage node
idea: Periodic-table walk, C (6): replace the dielectric capacitor with an electric double layer, a 5 nm-pore CVD carbon electrode filled with a nonvolatile ionic liquid or solid polymer electrolyte; ~10 uF/cm2 times internal pore area gives ~20-50 fF in a 30x30x300 nm volume, and ion transit across 5 nm pores is ~10-30 ns.

title: Bookbinding signatures: capacitors printed on a cheap 200 mm wafer
idea: Bind memory like a book: a U.S. 200 mm foundry prints the capacitor array as a separate 'signature' wafer, using i-line litho and Earth-abundant AAO or Ni/BaTiO3 capacitors, and sells it as a merchant product. It is wafer-to-wafer hybrid-bonded face-to-face onto transistor wafers from a leading-edge fab.
note: Same separate capacitor wafer hybrid-bonded to transistors.

title: Ceramic-glazed wide-gap heterojunction skin on the storage-node junction
idea: Like a glaze fired onto pottery, grow a 2-3 nm lattice-matched wide-gap crystal skin (e.g., GaP or AlP on Si, Eg ~2.3-2.5 eV) only on the storage-node side of the access channel. Band-to-band tunneling and GIDL must then cross a wide gap.

title: Glassblown vacuum-tube nanochannel access switch canned in every cell
idea: Hermetically seal a ~10 nm vacuum gap between a sharpened bitline emitter and a metal storage node, with a surrounding gate electrode, like miniature canned vacuum tubes. Charge moves only by field emission when the gate lowers the barrier.

title: Micrometer-screw tunneling-gap shutter switches without any contact
idea: A nanocantilever, positioned like a precision micrometer screw, moves the bitline electrode from a 0.5 nm tunnel gap (on) to a 3 nm gap (off) above a metal storage node. It never touches, so there is no stiction or contact wear.

title: Kiln-shrunk silicon dots make a Coulomb-blockade multi-junction access chain
idea: Like clay shrinking in a kiln, use self-limiting oxidation to shrink Si islands to ~1.5 nm, forming a chain of 4-6 tunnel junctions between bitline and storage node. The chain's Coulomb blockade is lifted only when the side gate is pulsed.

title: Twenty-electron Coulomb island read by an in-cell single-electron sensor
idea: IFR: storing a bit needs only a few electrons. Closest achievable: hold ~20 electrons on a 3 nm silicon island whose Coulomb charging energy (>kT) blocks leakage, sensed nondestructively by an adjacent single-electron transistor whose current shifts a full period per electron.
note: Same few-electron island plus SET sense.

title: Optically gated access: waveguide wordlines, zero-dark-current channel
idea: IFR: a switch with no electric gate to leak through. Use an ultrawide-gap photoconductive channel (AlN or Ga2O3, negligible dark current) as the access device, and route each wordline as a silicon-nitride waveguide that delivers a ~1 ns UV pulse to open a whole row of channels.

title: Room-temperature Coulomb-blockade box stores bits without a switch
idea: IFR: isolation comes from the electron's own charge. Store each bit as ~20-50 electrons on a sub-2 nm silicon nanocrystal coupled to the bitline by a tunnel junction whose charging energy (>10 kT at 300 K) blocks transport unless a gate pulse aligns the island to a degeneracy point.

title: Transferred micron-thin array films replace thinned TSV dies
idea: Ideal: stacking costs no silicon area at all. Closest achievable: instead of thinning HBM dies to 30-50 um and drilling 5-10 um TSVs with keep-out zones, smart-cut a 1-2 um device film of each DRAM array and bond it sequentially, linking tiers with ~0.5 um nano-vias that need almost no keep-out.

title: 2D interband tunnel-diode Goto pair: static bit with picoamp hold
idea: Scarcity rule: zero hold power and nothing above 1 V. Two series interband tunnel diodes (broken-gap black-phosphorus/SnSe2 vdW junctions with peak-to-valley ratio >100) form a bistable midpoint node held at valley current, and one access transistor reads and writes it like an SRAM half-cell.

title: Swap dielectric charge for porphyrin redox monolayer storing discrete electrons
idea: Graft a tripodal porphyrin or ferrocene self-assembled monolayer onto the storage electrode, with a solid electrolyte. The bit is held as molecular oxidation states (two states give 1.5 bits per cell) at ~10^14 molecules/cm2, or about 16-30 uC/cm2 per state; ZettaCore showed 400 C survivability and 10^12 cycles.

title: Geiger-mode avalanche junction as a digital charge-threshold detector
idea: Substitute the regenerative latch with an implanted silicon p-n junction biased just below avalanche (as in SPAD pixels) with a quench resistor: the bitline signal pushes it over breakdown or not, giving a full-swing digital output in ~100 ps. Implant, anneal and contact are basic nanofab steps.
note: Geiger-mode junctions fire on random carrier arrival, not a deterministic voltage threshold; dark counts.

title: Miura-fold origami: one patterned membrane folded into 16 tiers
idea: Borrowed from origami solar arrays and Miura-fold maps: pattern 16 DRAM array tiles side by side in one planar pass on a 100 nm Si/oxide membrane with thin polymer hinge lines, release it, and fold it accordion-style onto a periphery die, with interconnect running across the hinges.
note: Tiles side by side use the same litho per bit; only footprint shrinks, and hinge wiring is speculative.

title: Read resistance states by listening to their Johnson thermal noise
idea: Effect walk: Johnson-Nyquist noise. A selected high- or low-resistance cell (e.g. 100 kOhm vs 10 MOhm) is connected unbiased to a local low-noise correlator that distinguishes the ~10x noise-voltage difference over a 20-ns window; no current is driven, so the cell is never disturbed.

title: Printed electric double-layer storage capacitors
idea: Magnify areal capacitance about 1000x by printing an ionic-gel film whose electric double layer (~10 uF/cm2) stores the bit's charge in a tiny planar footprint.
note: Ion double layers respond in us-ms and self-discharge; not ns memory.

title: Chain DRAM: series-connected cells eliminate per-cell bitline contacts
idea: TRIZ #26 Copying (from chain FeRAM and NAND strings): place each access transistor in parallel with its capacitor and chain 8-16 cells in series between a block-select device and the bitline. To read cell k, turn off only its transistor; its capacitor voltage then appears in series on the bitline through the conducting neighbors.
note: Fatal: neighbors' on-transistors short linear caps, erasing data; works only for ferroelectric remanence.

title: Sand-mandala monk: dry-sprayed BaTiO3 nanocrystal planar capacitor
idea: A monk builds a mandala grain by grain without water. Aerosol deposition fires sub-micron BaTiO3 particles at the wafer at room temperature, where they fracture and bond into a dense ceramic film (k in the hundreds) with no sintering, solvent or rinse; the film serves as a planar high-k storage capacitor.
note: Aerosol-deposited films are microns thick; a planar DRAM-size cell needs k in the thousands at 5 nm.

title: K: drifting potassium ions in gate oxide as threshold memory
idea: Deliberately dope a 4-6 nm SiO2 gate layer with K+ (the classic mobile-ion contaminant) and drive the ion cloud to the top or bottom interface with +/-3 V pulses; ion position shifts the read FET threshold ~0.3-0.5 V, and heavy ions cannot tunnel away like electrons.

title: Substitute leading-edge EUV nodes with relaxed-pitch DUV DRAM in idle fabs
idea: Re-tool existing U.S. 300 mm mature-logic fabs to make an ~18-20 nm DRAM entirely with ArF immersion SAQP using 2018-era cell layouts, sold as capacity memory where a cost-per-bit premium is tolerable. The shell, utilities and most tools already exist.

title: Nuclear SMR co-located fab: one reactor powers, chills, purifies
idea: Combine an SMR's electricity, its steam and its low-grade heat into the fab's three biggest utilities: power for tools, steam-driven absorption chillers for process cooling, and waste heat for thermal desalination of UPW feedwater from brackish sources.

title: Liberty-ship fab modules: identical U.S. fabs built serially
idea: Time-compress fab construction from 3-5 years to ~15 months by freezing one standard 20k-wafer-per-month module (shell, utilities, layout) and building copies serially from prefabricated U.S.-made subfab skids, as WWII yards cut ship build time 10x through repetition.

title: Revive depreciated 2010s DUV DRAM lines with weak-die-accepting ECC
idea: No EUV: buy or restart fully depreciated 30-40 nm DUV DRAM fabs whose capital cost is already written off, and ship their output with stronger on-module ECC and runtime row retirement so higher defect and retention-fail rates still meet spec. Time shift: a decade-old asset meets 2026 demand.

title: Eight-tier hybrid-bonded SRAM towers as the hot tier
idea: Ideal: a static memory as big as DRAM. Closest achievable: stack 8 thinned SRAM-only dies (no logic) with 1 um hybrid bonds directly over compute, each ~100 mm2 tier holding ~150 MB at 3 nm-class density, giving ~1 GB of refresh-free, sub-5 ns, ~0.1 pJ/bit storage per stack for hot KV pages and activations.

title: Automotive-first entry: new U.S. fab bootstraps on 125 C premium
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: a new entrant builds a small 10-20k wafer/month fab tuned for the 125 C automotive and industrial grade that incumbents underserve, selling at 2-3x commodity prices to profit at low volume, then learns its way into commodity DRAM.

title: No fab below 15 nm: U.S. legacy-DRAM relief line on licensed IP
idea: Self-imposed limit: only mature nodes. License DDR3/DDR4/LPDDR4 designs and process recipes from makers exiting legacy DRAM and run them in a U.S. 2x-nm line for automotive, industrial and networking buyers, so leading makers can move those wafers to HBM and DDR5.
note: Sound but conventional; needs a fab line.

title: Two-deck capacitor reusing one hole mask for AR 120
idea: Reverse 'one tall etch' into 'stack, etch, stack, etch': etch and line deck-1 capacitor holes, deposit a second mold deck, and re-expose the SAME capacitor mask aligned to deck 1 so deck-2 holes land on deck-1 electrodes, forming one continuous electrode. Zero new masks: one existing mask is used twice.
note: Multi-deck capacitor molds already in development at major makers.

title: Refinery fluid-catalytic-cracking reactors become the polysilicon template
idea: Oil refiners run fluidized-bed reactors continuously with particles suspended in gas. Restart and scale U.S. fluidized-bed granular polysilicon (silane decomposed on heated seed granules) to semiconductor purity, giving ~80-90% lower deposition energy than Siemens rods and free-flowing granules that feed continuous-recharge Czochralski pullers.

title: IKEA flat-pack: onshore U.S. assembly of imported known-good DRAM
idea: Flat-pack furniture ships compact and is put together near the buyer. Import thinned, tested DRAM wafers, then do all stacking, ≤300 C hybrid bonding, base-die attach and packaging in U.S. brownfield sites whose tools all run ≤400 C.

title: One block implant makes the access transistor asymmetric
idea: Inverts 'access transistors are symmetric': the single added mask blocks the bitline side so a low-dose counter-doping implant grades only the storage-node junction, lowering the peak field that drives GIDL and trap-assisted tunneling where the leakage tail originates.

title: Wafer-to-wafer bonded HBM shrinks TSV keep-out area
idea: Box[Fab=wafer-on-wafer hybrid bonding with sub-5 um vias x Transform=replace die stacking with W2W then dice x Integration=unchanged HBM3E/HBM4 pinout]: bonding whole core wafers with fine-pitch vias shrinks TSV and keep-out area per die.
note: Hybrid bonding for HBM4/5 widely pursued; W2W compounds stack yield.

title: Artillery-fuze lesson: mold-retained honeycomb braces AR-120 capacitors
idea: Artillery-fuze electronics survive 20,000 g by having no unsupported tall structure; likewise keep the oxide mold in place as a hexagonal honeycomb that braces every storage node, so tall electrodes cannot lean, bend or stick during wet cleans. Electrodes line each honeycomb cup, and the extra height (AR 120 instead of ~65) more than repays the lost outer surface.
note: Supporter lattices and concave in-mold capacitors are established DRAM practice.

title: Deep-trench storage revival from America's eDRAM heritage
idea: Revive the substrate deep-trench capacitor of the IBM/New York eDRAM lineage for standalone DRAM: trenches etched ~10 um into silicon beneath the transistor hold ~20 fF, freeing the surface for an 8F2 cell built on existing U.S. logic-fab trench tooling.

title: Undiced wafer-scale DRAM panel that maps out failing tiles
idea: Rule: defects are routed around, never scrapped. DRAM stays as an undiced wafer of tiles linked by a mesh network. Defective tiles are mapped out at test and in the field, and when enough tiles fail, the panel moves to a lower service tier rather than being discarded.
note: Anamartic wafer-scale DRAM did this in the 1980s.

title: Kerf-resident BIST and test modes sawn off after sort
idea: Place BIST engines, test-mode decoders and probe-only analog monitors in the scribe lanes, wired across the kerf to each die; they run at wafer sort and are physically discarded at dicing, leaving only a lockout fuse on the die.
note: Wires cut at dicing breach seal ring; reliability concern for small area gain.

title: Recirculating acoustic delay-line memory on US BAW filter fabs
idea: Adapt 5G BAW/FBAR filter technology: launch 20 GHz phonon pulse trains into a folded AlScN waveguide loop with an on-loop regenerative amplifier, so bits circulate like mercury delay-line memory and are tapped at a known phase.
note: Low density buffer niche.

title: Thin-film-solar steel foil acts as global plate and ground
idea: Borrowed from roll-to-roll CIGS solar on stainless-steel foil: oxide-TFT memory is built on insulated steel foil, and the foil itself, reached through periodic contacts, serves as cell plate, ground return and heat spreader.

title: Pharmaceutical cyclic-olefin polymers replace fluoropolymer wetted parts
idea: Pharma prefilled syringes use cyclic olefin polymer (COP/COC) because it has extremely low leachables. Adapt COP-lined, PEEK-bodied valves, filters and distribution lines for UPW and non-oxidizing dilute acids in place of PFA/PVDF, keeping fluoropolymer only for ozone, peroxide and solvent service.

title: Zero-waste garment cutting reclaims wafer-edge area with tiny tiles
idea: Zero-waste fashion nests pattern pieces to use the whole bolt of cloth. Lay out capacitor-free memory as 1-2 mm2 self-contained tiles (own sense amps, redundancy and BIST) that fill the partial-die ring at the wafer edge, then sell them as chiplets binned by tile count.

title: Mono-material all-silicon memory package
idea: MINIFY material diversity to one: a silicon interposer, silicon lid and silicon stiffener joined by oxide-oxide and Cu-Cu bonds, with no epoxy mold, gold or solder, so the whole package is one recycling stream.
note: Recyclability niche; costs and reliability of all-silicon package unclear.

title: Minify thermal gradients on AlN ceramic substrates to shrink refresh guardband
idea: Build thin-film memory arrays on planarized AlN or diamond-coated ceramic substrates (170-1000+ W/mK) so the whole array stays within ~1-2C. Refresh is set by the hottest cell, so removing hotspots shrinks the thermal guardband.
note: On-die gradients already small.

title: Eliminate decoder transistors: Schottky diode-matrix row decoding
idea: Build row predecode and decode as a classic diode-AND matrix of NiSi/n-Si Schottky diodes formed by self-aligned silicidation (unreacted Ni stripped in H2SO4/H2O2). Each decode node is dynamically precharged and pulled down by diodes on the complement address lines, so only the final wordline driver remains a transistor.

title: Eliminate plasma fin etch: crystallographic TMAH wet-etched sense-amp transistors
idea: On the bonded periphery wafer, use (110) silicon, where TMAH etches vertical {111} sidewalls at ~100:1 anisotropy, to form SA fins through an Al2O3 hard mask patterned with BCl3. The fins come out with atomically smooth walls and no fluorinated or HBr plasma.

title: Hardmask becomes the wordline: keep the TiN, skip tungsten
idea: Rearrange roles of patterning and function: the TiN hardmask that defines the recessed gate trench is left in place and thickened as the gate metal, with shorter wordline segments driven by more local drivers to compensate RC.

title: Write first, compute on-die parity later in idle
idea: Reverse write ordering for on-die ECC: partial writes land immediately without read-modify-write, affected codewords are marked parity-stale in a small SRAM bitmap, and parity is recomputed at the next activation or idle slot, accepting a microsecond-scale unprotected window.

title: Water-dissolvable transient storage cells for short-service bulk buffer memory
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap short-living objects: fabricate cells from the 'transient electronics' palette (Si nanomembrane transistors, MgO dielectric, Mo/Mg electrodes on a polymer handle) for 2-3-year bulk buffer memory; at end of life the boards dissolve in buffered water, leaving Si and Mo for recovery.

title: Bimorph stress layer self-delaminates the storage tier during recycling bake
idea: TRIZ #37 Thermal expansion: insert a high-CTE metal / low-CTE nitride bimorph between the storage-capacitor tier and the CMOS logic. It is inert below the 450 C back-end budget, but a 550 C recycling bake drives mismatch strain past interface toughness so the capacitor tier (Zr, Ru, Ti) curls off as flakes.

title: Etch passivation engineered to become the contact insulating liner
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: the sidewall passivation that storage-node-contact etch deposits (normally stripped by wet cleans) is tuned with SiCl4/O2 into a dense 2-3 nm SiOx-rich film and kept as the contact-to-bitline insulating liner, skipping the separate liner ALD and spacer etch.

title: Sea-urchin self-sharpening CMP pad saves ceria slurry and diamond
idea: Sea-urchin teeth self-sharpen because layered fibres break away to expose fresh edges. Cast roll-to-roll CMP pads from aligned fibre-polymer laminates whose fibres erode at a set rate, renewing asperities without diamond conditioning and holding abrasive in fibre grooves so less slurry is needed.

title: Mitochondrial fusion merges two half-good modules into one
idea: Damaged mitochondria fuse to complement each other's defects; the controller interleaves the healthy banks of two partially failed modules into one full-capacity logical rank via a per-bank map, so modules with dead banks are combined rather than scrapped.

title: AMI VMOS revival: crystal-etched V-groove access transistors
idea: Revive 1970s VMOS, which American Microsystems used for memories: KOH anisotropic etching produces self-limiting {111} V-grooves whose geometry is set by the crystal, and epitaxial or diffusion depth sets the channel length. A uniform vertical access transistor forms with a U.S.-built 1X stepper and no EUV.

title: Rosen piezoelectric transformer generates wordline voltage acoustically
idea: Revive the 1950s Rosen piezoelectric transformer as an AlN MEMS resonator in the package or interposer (AlN is CMOS-compatible and made in the U.S.). Driven at resonance from 1.1 V, it steps the voltage up acoustically to 3-4 V and replaces on-die Dickson charge pumps for the VPP and negative-wordline rails.

title: Diode-matrix predecoders printed in BEOL above the array
idea: 1950s computers decoded addresses with passive diode matrices. Deposit a thin-film oxide Schottky diode stack (e.g., Pt/IGZO) between upper metals and wire it as a diode-AND predecode matrix directly over the cell array, so the silicon below holds only the final wordline drivers.

title: Transfluxor-style ferroelectric column gate eliminates repair comparators
idea: The 1956 transfluxor used flux stored around a control aperture to block or pass transfer through a second aperture. Put one HZO ferroelectric FET in series with each column-select line. Programmed at wafer test, a bad column's FeFET stays permanently off and its spare's turns on, so column repair needs no fuse-address comparators in the read path.
note: One-time FeFET switch per CSL; adds a series device to the column path to save small comparator area.

title: Slow-light silicon-nitride delay-line memory from depreciated photonics fabs
idea: Revive the mercury delay line as coupled-resonator slow-light silicon-nitride waveguides (group index ~50-100) made in depreciated 200 mm photonics fabs with i-line litho and 1-2 masks: 64 WDM channels at 50 Gbaud recirculate through an on-chip amplifier and retimer, and data is tapped as it passes. It serves bandwidth-hungry, capacity-poor sequential buffers such as activation staging.
note: ~1 Mb/cm2 density; niche bandwidth buffer only.

title: Vacuum-tube mica revival: muscovite sheets as PTFE-free high-speed dielectric
idea: Revive mica, the dielectric of early capacitors and tube spacers: cleave natural muscovite to 10-25 um sheets and laminate it with copper by adhesive-free thermocompression as the high-speed layers for memory-to-logic package traces.
note: Brittle cleaved mica lamination hard to scale; small gain.

title: Fiber-loop delay-line memory holds cold pages in flight
idea: Inverts 'memory is a place in space' into 'memory is time in flight': cold pages circulate in a DWDM fiber spool (10 km, 100 channels x 400 Gb/s, about 250 MB in flight per loop) with optical-electrical regeneration each lap, and a rack controller grabs a page as it passes. Average access is ~25 us, which suits far-memory tiers that today pin DRAM for cold pages.

title: Network of university 200 mm lines making error-tolerant memory chiplets
idea: Inverts 'only elite, ultra-clean fabs can make DRAM': fund ~20 academic and community-college 200 mm lines to run a shared mature-node gain-cell/1T1C flow whose higher defect density is absorbed by 1% tolerance, supplying defense and edge chiplets.

title: Planar thin-film magnetic cores on glass revive core memory
idea: Core memory was byte-addressable, had unlimited endurance and needed no refresh; it lost only on size. Pattern micro-toroids of electroplated permalloy or ferrite with multi-turn copper windings on glass panels using panel-level packaging lithography (~10 um features), select them by coincident-current half-select and sense them inductively at ~100-300 ns.
note: At ~10 um features density is orders of magnitude below DRAM; cost/bit poor.

title: Honeycomb: brick-bond mat tiling shares each sense strip three ways
idea: Bees get the most area per wall with hexagons. Lay mats in a Manhattan-friendly brick-bond pattern that approximates hexagons so each SA strip segment borders three mats, and give each SA 3:1 isolation switches; only one of the three mats is active per strip at a time, versus 2:1 sharing today.
note: Three-way SA sharing via brick tiling; ~7% area at activation-constraint cost.

title: Old TV: recycled LCD glass becomes low-CTE package cores
idea: Stimulus 'old TV' (millions of discarded LCD panels) -> LCD panel glass is already alkali-free aluminoborosilicate with CTE ~3.2 ppm/K; strip, re-melt and re-draw it into glass-core substrates and interposers for DRAM/HBM packages with laser-drilled through-glass vias.

title: Post-it note: back-end oxide-TFT metadata layer stuck atop DRAM
idea: A sticky note added after the book is printed: deposit a <=350 C IGZO thin-film-transistor memory layer on top of finished DRAM or controller wafers to hold compression tags, hotness counters and dedup pointers; because metadata is recomputable it needs only seconds of retention and tolerates bit loss.

title: Sundial: leaky back-end TFT capacitors timestamp page age
idea: A sundial tells time without gears: give each 2 MB region a back-end IGZO TFT 'age capacitor' recharged on access that leaks predictably; the controller reads its voltage to rank regions for compression or demotion, getting LRU age from physics with zero DRAM bits or counter traffic.

title: BTI-recovery pulses scheduled into refresh slots
idea: Worse at 125 C: let bias-temperature instability creep the access-transistor Vt for 10 years until leakage or write speed fails. Flip: use each refresh slot for rows not being restored to apply a short reverse-polarity gate pulse that de-traps the BTI charge, holding Vt drift below ~10 mV over life.

title: Inkjet-printed personality layer turns one die into many SKUs
idea: Worse: tape out separate masks and dies for each width, density bin and speed grade. Flip: leave the final configuration via layer unpatterned and inkjet-print jumpers per wafer to set I/O width, bank grouping, redundancy and timing options, so one mask set serves the whole product line.
note: Fuses and bond options already configure one die across SKUs.

title: Print-on-die carbon-nanotube TFT layer hosts slow control logic
idea: Worse: spend DRAM silicon on mode registers, BIST engines, temperature sensors and power-up sequencers that run at kHz-MHz. Flip: after passivation, inkjet-print a low-temperature carbon-nanotube TFT circuit layer on top of the die to host those slow functions, wired down through pad openings.

title: Printed nanoparticle varistor film takes over ESD protection duty
idea: Worse: guard every I/O pad with large on-die ESD clamps that add capacitance and area. Flip: screen-print a ZnO-nanoparticle varistor film between I/O traces and ground on the package substrate so surges clamp off-die, letting on-die clamps shrink to minimal size.
note: Die-level CDM during assembly still needs on-die clamps.

title: Display-glass fabs make oxide-transistor memory on Gen 8.5 panels
idea: Worsen: insist that every DRAM bit needs a 300 mm single-crystal wafer from a CZ puller with a quartz crucible. Flip: repurpose underused LCD/OLED fabs to build stacked oxide-TFT gain-cell arrays on 2.2x2.5 m glass (~60x the area of a 300 mm wafer) with their existing PVD/ALD and litho tools, and bond the logic periphery from silicon fabs.
note: Display litho ~1.5 um makes cells ~1e4x larger; 60x substrate area cannot compensate.

title: Robot-swappable chamber liners replace NF3 plasma cleans
idea: Worsen: clean deposition chambers by blasting NF3 plasma, a potent greenhouse gas, every few wafers. Flip: let films build up on a cassette of thin swappable aluminum or silicon liners that robots exchange in vacuum. The liners are stripped wet off-line and the recovered Zr/Hf/Ti oxides are refined.

title: Plasma-catalytic PFC conversion returns fluorine as reusable HF
idea: Worsen: burn PFC exhaust in natural-gas abatement and dump the fluoride as CaF2 sludge. Flip: use plasma-catalytic abatement to convert CF4/NF3/SF6 to HF, capture it as clean HF in a wet column, and ship it back to the NF3/HF supplier as feedstock in returnable totes.

title: Microfabricated ferrite-core planes plated onto package substrates
idea: Worsen: make memory require the most advanced lithography. Flip: plate few-micron NiZn-ferrite or permalloy micro-toroids on organic or glass substrate panels, threaded by lithographic X/Y/sense lines, reviving core memory with PCB-class tools: no capacitor, no transistor per bit, unlimited endurance.
note: Tiny density, destructive microsecond reads; persistent niche only.

title: Program-verify writes tolerate higher-resistance NiSi contacts
idea: Worse: replace cobalt and tungsten contacts with nickel silicide and watch write failures rise from higher contact resistance. Flip: give DRAM a NAND-style write-verify loop: after restore, the sense amp re-checks the bit against a tightened reference and re-pulses only failing columns, so marginal-resistance contacts no longer cause silent errors.

title: Memory ESCO financing refresh-free swaps from saved electricity
idea: Worse: make operators pay up front for any memory-efficiency upgrade. Flip: energy-service companies finance replacing DRAM tiers with static or nonvolatile memory and are repaid from metered refresh and cooling savings over 4-5 years.

title: Setun-style ternary global pre-decode cuts address wiring
idea: Soviet engineers built the ternary Setun computer when parts were scarce. Drive global pre-decode lines in balanced ternary (three-level signals with multi-Vt CMOS receivers), so 9 trits replace 14 bits and the pre-decode gate count drops.

title: Farmer's single tractor: one column decoder per bank group
idea: A farmer shares one tractor across fields that are never plowed at the same time. DDR5's tCCD_L already forbids back-to-back column commands within a bank group, so one column decoder and CSL driver set serves all four banks of the group through bank-select gating on shared column-select lines.

title: Horologist's gridiron pendulum: temperature-compensated interconnect delay
idea: A gridiron pendulum pairs brass and steel so their expansion cancels: build skew-critical interposer clock and strobe lines from segments whose delay-temperature coefficients cancel, using a Cu conductor plus a dielectric whose permittivity falls with heat, so skew stays flat from 25 C to 125 C.

title: Geneticist's double helix: complementary bits printed on both foil faces
idea: DNA stores every base twice as complementary strands: each memory cell is printed on the front of the foil and its complement on the back (roll-to-roll double-sided printing with laser through-foil vias), read differentially, and any non-complementary pair is flagged and resolved in favor of the strand with the larger margin from midpoint.

title: Phase-state NEMS parametron for megagray nuclear reactor instrumentation
idea: Reactor instruments absorb megagray doses that wreck oxides and stored charge, so bits are stored as the oscillation phase (0 or pi) of parametrically pumped nanobeams, as in 1950s parametron computers; one release mask lets a vapor etch free beams from an existing BEOL metal layer. A shared pump keeps beams oscillating and reads detect phase capacitively.

title: Reactor neutron-transmutation-doped donor wafers for transferred array tiers
idea: Power-device makers dope silicon in a nuclear reactor, turning Si-30 into phosphorus with near-perfect uniformity; NTD-dope the donor wafers whose thin layers are transferred to form junctionless n-type channel tiers, so channel doping is fixed before transfer. Array implants and their xenon or argon plasma flood guns are skipped.

title: On-chip phononic delay line recirculates acoustic bit packets
idea: Shrink the 1940s mercury delay line to a chip: GHz bulk-acoustic pulses in AlScN/LiNbO3 waveguides travel 100,000x slower than light, so a 1 cm folded path holds micro-seconds of 10 Gb/s data, regenerated at each lap.
note: GHz acoustic loss and microsecond serial latency; ~kbit per cm path, buffer niche.

title: AIST Minimal Fab repurposed as regional memory repair depots
idea: Japan's Minimal Fab (half-inch wafers in desk-sized tools) failed as production because its throughput was low. Repair does not need throughput: equip US regional depots with minimal-fab-style tools to rework stacks, rebond patch tiles, replace dies and re-ball modules.
note: Hybrid-bonded stacks are not reworkable; module-level rework already exists.

title: SrTiO3 DRAM capacitors failed on leakage; decaps tolerate it
idea: Strontium titanate (k ~100-300) was abandoned for DRAM storage capacitors because its leakage was far too high for fA-level retention and it wanted Ru electrodes. Power decoupling tolerates ~1000x more leakage, so deposit STO on TiN electrodes in deep trenches of the interposer or base die for several-uF/mm2 decaps that steady ultra-wide I/O supplies, replacing Ta capacitors and Hf/Zr-oxide MIMs.
note: STO decaps viable but only marginal VDDQ benefit.

title: Pyroelectric HZO film senses per-mat heating for mat-level refresh scaling
idea: Effect: pyroelectricity. Deposit a 10 nm Si-doped HfO2 pyroelectric capacitor (same ALD as HZO) beside each mat; temperature change yields charge dQ = p*A*dT with no bias power, integrated by a shared ADC and periodically re-zeroed against one diode sensor. Refresh rate is then set per mat instead of by the hottest on-die sensor.

title: Silver-ion drift integrators remember page heat across reboots
idea: Every 64 KB region gets a nanoscale Ag/electrolyte integrator. Each access pulse drifts a few silver ions, so conductance becomes a nonvolatile, slowly relaxing log of cumulative accesses. On boot or VM migration, the placement engine reads the map and pre-places hot data in DRAM and cold data in CXL/flash right away, instead of relearning for minutes.

title: Thin-film Peltier strips cool only refresh-dominant hot banks
idea: Effect: Peltier thermoelectric cooling. A Bi2Te3/Sb2Te3 superlattice thin-film cooler in the interposer under the HBM base die pumps heat out of the 2-4 banks sitting over GPU hotspots, dropping them ~10 C; the controller runs it only when the computed refresh-energy saving exceeds the Peltier power.
