note: Peltier power likely exceeds refresh savings.

title: Villari magnetostrictive sensors map TSV stress for zone-specific refresh
idea: Effect: inverse magnetostriction (Villari). FeGa thin-film stripes whose permeability changes with mechanical stress, read inductively, ring the TSV clusters in HBM core dies and report local stress during warpage and thermal cycling; the controller maps stress-induced (piezoresistive) leakage to zone-specific refresh rates instead of a die-wide guard band.

title: Rewritable phase-change repair fuses enable re-repair across multiple lives
idea: Replace one-time e-fuse redundancy maps with small GST phase-change cells (amorphous/crystalline thermal hysteresis), so each new owner reruns full repair and re-maps spare rows as cells age. Part of the spare budget is reserved for second life.

title: Al: AlN acoustic delay loop recirculates bits as phonons
idea: Launch bits as 10 GHz acoustic pulses into a folded AlN/Al2O3 acoustic waveguide where sound travels ~10 km/s, so a 1 mm loop holds ~1,000 bits for 100 ns; a piezo transducer reads and rewrites each bit per pass, and soft-decision regeneration absorbs ~1% raw symbol errors from dispersion and noise.
note: ~1,000 bits/mm loop and 10 GHz acoustic loss give density orders below DRAM.

title: Mg2Si thermoelectric film under the array cools only retention-critical mats
idea: Mg: deposit thin-film Mg2Si/Mg2Sn thermoelectric couples (abundant, non-toxic, no tellurium) in the backside BEOL with i-line patterning and drive them only under mats holding data in long-refresh mode, keeping those mats ~15-20 C below die temperature.
note: Thin-film Mg2Si ZT is low; Peltier power likely exceeds refresh saved.

title: Sn: tin-oxide Schottky diode matrices revive core-memory predecoding
idea: Spray-pyrolyze SnO2 films in air over the decoder region and form Schottky diode AND matrices, the 1950s diode-ROM decoding style, so row predecoding is done by stacked two-terminal devices and only final drivers stay in silicon.

title: Strontium-catalyzed native-oxide desorption replaces the HF-last clean
idea: Periodic-table walk, Sr (38): before epitaxy or gate stacks, deposit ~0.5 monolayer Sr in vacuum and anneal at ~750-800 C; Sr reduces SiO2 to volatile SiO plus SrO and leaves an oxide-free (2x1) surface, borrowing the SrTiO3-on-Si MBE trick.

title: Robot-swapped recyclable aluminum chamber liners instead of NF3 cleans
idea: Periodic-table walk, Al (13): deposition chambers get thin anodized-Al liners that collect film deposits and are swapped through the load lock every N wafers, then remelted (secondary Al takes ~5% of primary energy) with residues separated as dross; sold as liner-as-a-service.

title: Mg: magnesium-silicide thermoelectric micro-coolers spot-cool HBM PHY
idea: Integrate thin-film Mg2Si/Mg3Sb2 Peltier elements (abundant, tellurium-free alternative to Bi2Te3) in the HBM lid over the hottest base-die PHY region, actively pumping 5-10 W/cm2 during bursts so the stack never crosses 85 C; control is local and the interface unchanged.

title: K: KNN piezo chuck actively flattens interposers during HBM bonding
idea: Embed lead-free (K,Na)NbO3 piezo actuator arrays in the bonding chuck that measure and counter-bend large interposers in real time during HBM thermocompression or reflow, holding coplanarity under 5 um across ~100 mm packages.

title: One roving spare sense amp covers any failed column
idea: Ideal result: one spare that is everywhere. A single fast spare SA per mat is time-shared through a column steering bus with per-column sample capacitors; when built-in self-test finds a dead SA, the spare substitutes, and its assignment moves as new faults appear.

title: Tungsten-free buried wordline: fully silicided polysilicon fill
idea: Constraint: zero tungsten. Fill the buried-wordline trench with doped polysilicon over the gate oxide, cap it with thin nickel or cobalt and anneal until the whole fill converts to NiSi/CoSi2 (full silicidation), then recess; no WF6 CVD and no TiN barrier.

title: Sell retention-reject DRAM dies as ephemeral-data memory
idea: Imposed limit: no die leaves the fab as scrap. Dies that fail 64 ms retention but hold data for 1-10 ms are binned into 'ephemeral' modules reserved for short-lived data (activations, packet buffers, single-shot KV) whose lifetime software guarantees to be shorter than the measured retention.

title: Organic-TFT event backplane makes the sensor emit only changes
idea: Constraint (printable/roll-to-roll): a printed organic photodiode array with a printed organic-TFT comparator in each pixel holds the last value on a pixel capacitor and fires only when intensity moves past a threshold. The result is a cheap, large-area event camera whose output stream needs no full-frame buffer.
note: Event cameras exist; surveillance frame buffering is a tiny share of DRAM.

title: Substitute additive printed circuits for etched-and-plated memory module boards
idea: Print DIMM and CXL board traces with copper nanoparticle ink by aerosol jet or laser-induced forward transfer, sinter photonically, and print vias instead of drilling, plating and etching.

title: Fixed-abrasive pad releases its own silica, ending ceria STI polish
idea: Combine pad and slurry: a polyurethane pad loaded with sol-gel silica nodules releases fresh colloidal silica as it is conditioned, while an amino-acid additive in plain water supplies the oxide/nitride selectivity ceria normally provides.

title: ALD hermetic wafer-level seal replaces epoxy mold compound
idea: Minify the package to a 1 um skin: seal finished memory dies at wafer level with ALD Al2O3/SiN multilayers and a metal seal ring, eliminating epoxy mold compound with its antimony and halogen flame retardants and fused-quartz filler.

title: Vertical printed transistors: channel length set by film thickness
idea: Minify channel length to ~100 nm without fine lithography by building vertical printed transistors in which source and drain are stacked layers and the channel is the coated film thickness.

title: Archerfish jet printing of photoresist instead of spin coating
idea: Archerfish shoot shaped water jets that focus on a target. Replace spin coating with a multi-nozzle jet printhead that lays resist, BARC and spin-on carbon only on the wafer at the needed thickness, followed by a brief solvent-vapour reflow to level the film.

title: Spiking-neuron voltage-to-delay time-domain sensing
idea: Like an integrate-and-fire neuron, the developed bitline voltage sets the discharge current of a small node, turning a 30 mV difference into a ~20 ps race; a tiny SR-latch arbiter decides whether bitline or reference fires first, with digital delay trims absorbing mismatch.

title: Harmonic-telegraph frequency-division global data lines
idea: Revive Bell's and Gray's harmonic telegraph. Each subarray's secondary sense output modulates its own on-chip tone (1-8 GHz, from an injection-locked ring oscillator) onto one shared global data line, and the I/O block separates the channels with passive N-path filters. Eight banks' data share one wire instead of eight.
note: Close to RF-interconnect work (Chang, UCLA).

title: MEMS parametrons store bits as oscillation phase, no leakage tail
idea: Revive Eiichi Goto's 1954 parametron with AlN-on-silicon micro-resonators pumped at twice their natural frequency. Each resonator settles into a 0 or pi phase state that persists as long as the shared pump runs, and is read by phase comparison with a reference line.

title: Chewing gum: tree-latex and sugar resists with non-fluorinated acid generators
idea: Stimulus 'chewing gum' (chicle tree latex plus sugar) -> build a chemically amplified resist on bio-derived terpene/sugar polymers (cyclized polyisoprene or trehalose-ester backbones) with a non-fluorinated sulfonium camphorsulfonate photoacid generator and aqueous development.

title: Po oxide is only grown, never etched: fluorine-free LOCOS flow
idea: Po: 'oxide may only be grown, never etched.' Extracted: define isolation and contact windows by local oxidation through nitride masks (LOCOS and poly-buffered LOCOS), etch silicon, poly and aluminum only with chlorine and bromine plasmas, strip nitride in hot phosphoric acid, and drop fluorocarbon oxide etches entirely.

title: Back-gate trimmed tiny sense amps replace large matched pairs
idea: Worse: make sense-amp transistors huge so random mismatch stays below the signal. Flip: shrink sense-amp devices 3-4x and cancel each pair's offset with a per-column back-gate voltage programmed at wafer test from a shared trim DAC row and held as a fuse code.

title: Pool idle switch packet-buffer SRAM as rack staging memory
idea: Worse: leave hundreds of MB of SRAM idle in every switch and DPU. Flip: expose spare switch packet buffers and DPU SRAM as RDMA-addressable regions that the network OS manages as a rack-level static pool for hot tables and staging buffers.

title: N: silicon-nitride nanostring parametron stores bit as oscillation phase
idea: Pump GHz Si3N4/AlN nanomechanical resonators (Q~300) at twice resonance so each settles in ~100 ns into one of two oscillation phases, 0 or pi, as in Goto's 1950s parametron; one frequency comb pumps thousands of resonators, and phase slips up to ~1% per hold interval are corrected by the code.
note: Mechanical parametron bits already shown (NTT); micron resonators and pump power cap density.

title: Titanium and PEEK wetted paths for a fluoropolymer-free fab
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ti (22): once HF is gone from the fab, the main reason for PFA/PTFE plumbing disappears, so distribute UPW and oxidizing acids in electropolished titanium (passive TiO2 film) and use PEEK/high-purity polypropylene for reducing acids, solvents and slurries.

title: Electroless nickel-boron plating fills contacts without WF6
idea: Periodic-table walk, Ni (28): activate silicided contact bottoms and plate Ni-B bottom-up from an aqueous NiSO4 plus dimethylamine-borane bath at 60-80 C with a suppressor additive, then anneal to form NiSi at the interface.

title: Hydroforming wordlines: bootstrapped local boost replaces high-voltage drivers
idea: Like hydroforming, which shapes metal with uniform fluid pressure instead of heavy punches, precharge each local wordline to VDD through a small thin-oxide device, float it, then pressurize it to ~3 V by capacitive coupling from a shared boost line. This revives the 1970s NMOS bootstrap, so no thick-oxide PMOS is needed at every wordline.
note: Thin-oxide devices see the 3 V boosted node.

title: Printed conducting-polymer ion-doping bit read as channel conductance
idea: IFR: a transistor whose channel is itself the memory. Closest achievable: an organic electrochemical transistor (PEDOT:PSS class) where a pulse pushes ions into or out of the printed channel and a barrier layer pins them; read current is nondestructive and multilevel.
note: Ion-doped OECT memory known; slow and low-density, a flexible-electronics niche.

title: Printed coded-aperture masks capture images pre-compressed
idea: Constraint (printable/roll-to-roll): a roll-to-roll printed pseudo-random amplitude mask in front of the sensor performs compressive sensing optically, so the sensor reads 10-25% as many measurements as pixels and the buffer stores only those measurements. Full frames are reconstructed only when a downstream detector flags one.

title: Silver-nanowire mesh reservoir holds recurrent state physically
idea: Constraint (printable/roll-to-roll): a roll-to-roll coated random silver-nanowire network with memristive junctions acts as a physical reservoir computer: time-series inputs drive its electrodes, the decaying junction states hold the recent history, and only a small linear readout is trained. No recurrent state or history window sits in DRAM.

title: Leak-to-archive cells write their own nonvolatile backup
idea: Time-shift the leak into a write: each cell's leakage path runs through a tiny ionic memristive integrator, so the charge draining from a stored '1' over seconds moves ions and leaves a resistance state recording it; after full decay the sense amp reads the memristor instead, and the next write resets it.
note: fA leakage carries far too little charge to move ions in a memristor.

title: Wavelength-division tier select with color-tuned photoconductive access devices
idea: Scale fiber-optic WDM down to a die: each tier's access device is a photoconductor sensitized by quantum dots of a size unique to that tier, so a waveguide carrying wavelength k turns on only tier k. A tunable laser at the package edge picks the tier in ns, with no staircase or per-tier wordline contacts.
note: QD absorbers respond to all shorter wavelengths, so spectral tier selectivity fails; photoconductor dark leakage too.

title: Coulomb-blockade charge packets store 3-bit KV and compute attention
idea: Store each KV element as an integer number of electrons (0-7) on silicon nanodots, where the Coulomb staircase quantizes charge natively. A key column's packets are merged onto a shared island and a single-electron transistor counts the electrons, giving the attention dot product. Physics enforces 3-bit quantization, so no codec is needed.

title: Swap capacitor for single deep-donor atom charge state
idea: Place one deep donor (Se or Te in Si, ~0.3 eV) per cell by deterministic single-ion implantation or hydrogen-resist STM lithography. Its neutral or ionized charge state is the bit, read by a nearby charge sensor.

title: 1T-nC cell: one access transistor, eight plate-addressed capacitors
idea: Inverts 'one transistor serves one capacitor.' Hang n capacitors off a single storage-node transistor, each with its own plate line; pulsing one plate couples only that capacitor's charge onto the node for sensing, as in 1T-nC FeRAM but with linear-dielectric charge.
note: Linear caps on one shared node hold a single state; n independent bits need ferroelectric nonlinearity.

title: Abacus-bead Coulomb-blockade island isolating the storage node
idea: Random stimulus 'abacus bead': beads move one at a time and only when pushed. Place a sub-2 nm silicon nanodot between the access channel and the storage node; its >0.3 eV charging energy blocks single-electron leakage when the wordline is off, and the wordline lowers the blockade to let charge through.

title: Origami memory: fold a low-resolution sheet into 3D density
idea: Worse: chase density by shrinking features with ever costlier lithography. Flip: pattern a large memory sheet on polyimide at relaxed 100+ nm rules with stress-engineered SiN/metal hinge lines, then release it and fold it accordion-style into 50-100 layers. Interconnect runs across the hinges instead of through vias.

title: Neuron's resting potential: nanobattery bit read as open-circuit voltage
idea: A biologist notes that neurons hold state as an ion gradient behind closed channels, not as electrostatic charge. Each cell is a ~10 nm solid-state Li-ion couple (LixCoO2 / LiPON / Si) whose state of charge sets a 0.3 V or 0.6 V open-circuit potential; a ns current pulse through a selector writes it and a high-impedance sense FET reads it.
note: ns ion kinetics and self-discharge in a 10 nm Li cell are implausible.

title: Undersea-fiber draw: thermally drawn preform sliced into vertical memory arrays
idea: Fiber makers draw a macroscopic preform 100,000x into kilometers of perfectly periodic structure; assemble a centimeter preform holding a lattice of silicon cores, glass gate insulator and metal-alloy gate lines, draw it in nitrogen to ~50 nm core pitch, then slice the rod into wafers whose silicon cores become vertical channels finished by ALD. No lithography or rare gas is used for the array.

title: Room-temperature nanocluster single-electron electrometer as sense element
idea: Molecule-scale jump: a sub-2 nm metal-nanocluster single-electron transistor (charging energy >10 kT) at each short bitline segment counts tens of electrons, so a cell needs only ~0.02-0.05 fF (the storage gate itself) and no capacitor.
note: Tens of stored electrons need <1e-18 A leakage, and placing nanoclusters is a miracle step.

title: Van der Waals resonant-tunneling pairs make each node bistable
idea: Atomic-layer scale jump: two stacked graphene/hBN resonant-tunneling diodes on each storage node form a Goto pair, so the node latches statically at either rail with valley current engineered below 1 fA; data never decays, so there is no refresh cycle at all.
note: Revives TI's tunnel-diode SRAM, which needs a peak-to-valley ratio near 1e6; graphene/hBN RTDs reach about 10.

title: Delete the electrical wordline: optically gated photoconductive access switch
idea: Limit: no metal wordline is allowed over the array. Each cell's access device is a wide-gap GaN or ZnO photoconductor bridge between the bitline and the storage node. A row is 'opened' by a light pulse through a SiN waveguide with grating taps, fed by edge micro-LEDs or lasers. In the dark the bridge holds almost no carriers.

title: Gravure-printed redox molecules as storage capacitors
idea: Magnify charge per area by printing a monolayer of porphyrin or ferrocene redox molecules; each molecule stores discrete electrons faradaically, so a planar printed cell stores what a 70:1 pillar does.
note: A monolayer under a ~20 nm footprint holds ~hundreds of electrons, far short of ~15k needed.

title: Mainframe-style page-only DRAM die strips column periphery
idea: Combine IBM's expanded-storage concept (page-addressable-only memory) with a DRAM die redesign: a die accessed only in 4 KB blocks drops fine column decoders, most data-path muxing and per-bank DLL logic, giving much of the ~49% periphery area back to cells on a DUV node; it serves as the tier below byte-addressable DRAM.
note: Column path is a minority of periphery; 1.4-1.7x optimistic; needs a DRAM fab.

title: Eliminate multi-year construction: factory-built containerized fab modules
idea: Build standardized 2,500 wafer-per-month array-line modules, with tools pre-installed in sealed clean containers with integrated utilities, in a shipyard-style factory, and bolt them onto an on-site utility spine one module at a time.

title: CFET-stacked sense amp transistors to halve SA stripe height
idea: Box: pillar cap x vertical-channel access x CFET-stacked latch x pitch-matched under bitline x bulk Si x sequential 3D integration. The NMOS and PMOS halves of each cross-coupled latch are stacked vertically as complementary FETs, so a full SA fits the bitline pitch of a 4F^2 array.

title: DRAM-only 450 mm fab reviving immersion 450 prototypes
idea: Po: the wafer is twice as big. The 450 mm transition stalled partly because EUV never had a 450 mm version; a DUV-only DRAM fab revives the 450 mm immersion scanner and process-tool prototypes from the G450C era and runs DRAM wafers with 2.25x the area per wafer pass.

title: Low-Vt implant mask for bank-edge LUT dequantizers
idea: One added low-Vt implant mask speeds up a strip of periphery transistors next to each bank enough to run a 16-entry LUT dequantizer at internal row speed. Weights and KV are stored at 3-4 bits and expanded to BF16 at the bank edge, so neither capacity nor external bandwidth pays for full precision.
note: Capacity gain comes from quantization itself; adds a DRAM process mask.

title: Tungsten-free 3D NAND with silicided-poly wordlines as KV overflow tier
idea: IFR: unlimited KV overflow with no chokepoint materials. Closest: 3D charge-trap NAND built with TiSi2-clad doped poly-Si wordlines instead of W replacement gates, accepting higher wordline RC through shorter blocks, read in large sequential KV pages behind a small DRAM cache.

title: Substitute solid-state 193 nm lasers for neon excimer lasers
idea: Generate 193 nm light with fiber-amplified 1 um lasers frequency-converted through LBO and CLBO stages, replacing the neon/fluorine gas fills of ArF excimer lasers that drive immersion scanners.
note: Power scaling of CLBO-converted 193 nm to scanner-class watts is the open risk.

title: Substitute periphery photomasks with maskless digital-micromirror lithography
idea: Pattern non-critical periphery layers (thick metal, implant blocks, pads, fuses) with a DMD-based maskless DUV writer, so each layer is a data file rather than a reticle; reticles are reserved for the critical array layers.

title: Substitute tungsten spin-orbit layers with titanium or chromium orbital torque
idea: Replace W/Ta/Pt spin-Hall layers in SOT-MRAM with light 3d metals (Ti, Cr) that produce torque through the orbital Hall effect, converted at a Ni interface; the write current never crosses the MgO barrier.

title: Substitute charge-trap endurance limits with periodic microheater self-annealing
idea: Fast-write charge-trap (SONOS-like) NV cells get buried microheaters per block; when ECC errors climb, a ms-scale ~800 C local anneal empties damaged traps and repairs the tunnel oxide, resetting wear.
note: Self-healing flash via heaters known; still far from unlimited endurance.

title: Substitute declining HDD head fabs for low-temperature memory foundries
idea: Swap the shrinking market for hard-disk read/write heads by converting those thin-film wafer fabs, which already run fine-litho magnetic and oxide processes kept below ~300 C (e.g., in Minnesota), to make BEOL memory tiers.

title: High-temperature superconductor persistent-current loops at 77 K
idea: Combine REBCO high-temperature superconductor films with an LN2 memory rack: each bit is a micro-loop holding a clockwise or counterclockwise persistent supercurrent (one flux quantum), written by a Josephson-junction pulse and read by an adjacent SQUID. Persistent currents do not decay, so refresh energy is zero and write energy is ~1e-19 J.

title: FeRAM-style driven plate line biases cells during retention
idea: Segment the DRAM cell plate per subarray and drive it as FeRAM does. On entering standby, the plate steps so every storage node couples toward the bitline precharge level, which shrinks |Vds| and the junction field, and it steps back before the first ACT.

title: Maskless multi-beam writing for periphery, mask-defined SAQP for array
idea: Combine 260k-beamlet e-beam writers, today used only to make masks, with the DRAM product flow. Irregular, sparse periphery layers that change with every product are direct-written with no reticle, while the regular array uses one shared immersion-SAQP mask set.

title: Post-tensioned capacitor pillars that resist leaning at AR 120
idea: Borrow post-tensioned concrete: deposit a compressive inner liner and a tensile outer TiN in each pillar so residual stresses cancel bending and capillary collapse during wet clean, letting pillars reach AR ~120 without extra support lattices.
note: Stress tuning of capacitor electrodes is existing practice.

title: Aviation line-replaceable units: swappable refresh-and-periphery die
idea: Adapted from aircraft line-replaceable units, built to be swapped on the flight line: split each DRAM into an array die (cells, access devices, sense amps) and a separately mounted periphery die carrying refresh scheduling, temperature sensing, ECC and retention maps, joined by a reworkable fine-pitch interposer, so the refresh brain is upgraded or replaced without discarding the array.

title: Core-memory coincident selection shrinks decoders and overfetch
idea: Borrowed from magnetic core memory's coincident-current addressing: each cell has two series access transistors, one gated by an X line and one by a Y line, so only the intersection is selected. A mat needs 2*sqrt(N) drivers, and one Y line opens just a 64-bit segment.
note: Two series access transistors per cell erase the density gain.

title: Cold-crucible levitation melting adapted from aerospace titanium skull melting
idea: Aerospace titanium is melted in water-cooled segmented copper cold crucibles, where induction fields push the melt off the wall and a thin frozen skull is the only contact. Adapt this to Czochralski growth: hold the silicon melt in an induction cold crucible with a solid-silicon skull and pull the crystal from the free surface.
note: Same cold-crucible CZ as I-10303.

title: Solar kerfless epitaxial wafers grown on reusable porous-silicon seeds
idea: Adapted from the solar industry's kerfless wafer process: epitaxial silicon is grown from trichlorosilane on a porous-silicon release layer atop a reusable template, then detached. Grow 150-300 um, 300 mm DRAM substrate wafers directly from gas and reuse each template 20-50 times.
note: Solar kerfless epi exists; DRAM-grade defect density in thick epi wafers is unproven.

title: Bottling-line linear fab: single-wafer flow without FOUP queues
idea: Borrow the beverage bottling line: arrange process modules along a linear inert-gas track balanced to one takt time, so each wafer flows step to step singly with no FOUP batching, stockers or overhead hoists; slow modules are duplicated in parallel lanes as in line balancing.
note: Minimal-fab style concepts known; hard to prove without a line.

title: Magnify the threshold during storage with a pulsed back-plate
idea: Give vertical-channel access transistors a buried back-gate plate per subarray held at -1.5 V during retention (raising Vt ~0.4 V by body effect) and pulsed to 0 V only in the subarray being activated. Leakage falls ~10^4x in storage while access on-current is untouched.

title: Vacuum-sealed cavities around bitlines minify parasitic capacitance
idea: MAGNIFY the air-spacer idea into a fully sealed vacuum tunnel: bitlines are suspended between storage-node contacts on periodic posts, a sacrificial carbon fill is ashed out, and a pinch-off dielectric seals the cavity, giving k~1 on three sides.
note: Air-spacer bitlines already in production; full vacuum suspension adds mechanical risk.

title: Magnify access gate length 10x using free vertical space
idea: Since 3D arrays have spare height, make the vertical gate-all-around access channel about 300 nm long with a 5 nm thin body, instead of a short planar or recessed channel. This suppresses short-channel and DIBL leakage paths that create the 13 fA tail.
note: Long vertical channels cut DIBL, but the DRAM tail is trap/GIDL-dominated; 10x retention optimistic.

title: Magnify capacitor height with three stacked 40:1 decks
idea: Build the capacitor mold in three decks, each AR about 40 (easy to etch), joined by self-aligned landing plugs, borrowing the multi-deck channel-hole method of 3D NAND. The total effective AR is about 120.
note: Deck-to-deck landing at sub-40 nm pitch is the hard part; 1.6x Cs is incremental.

title: Magnify row spacing: spend 3D density on grounded shield wordlines
idea: In a stacked array where density is abundant, insert a grounded shield wordline between every pair of active wordlines and a shield plane between tiers, so aggressor-victim capacitive and charge-migration coupling falls sharply.
note: Same grounded shield wordline mechanism.

title: Zero-ballroom fab: wafers travel in sealed nitrogen tubes
idea: Minify the cleanroom ~100x: connect tools with sealed N2/vacuum wafer highways and keep ISO-1 air only inside tool mini-environments, so the building is a cheap warehouse instead of a filtered ballroom.

title: Wafer-scale memory slab with no package substrate
idea: Magnify the die to the whole wafer: redundancy-healed DRAM wafers bond directly to a logic wafer and a cold plate, eliminating dicing, ABF build-up substrates, solder balls and mold compound.

title: Molybdenum-disulfide access transistors grown from domestic molybdenum
idea: Minify the channel to three atoms: grow MoS2 monolayers by low-temperature MOCVD from US-mined Mo and sulfur as access transistors. Their 1.8-2 eV gap and lack of junctions keep leakage below 1e-18 A/um at 125 C.

title: Wafer-scale DRAM: no dicing, no packaging
idea: Magnify the die to the whole wafer: one 300 mm wafer becomes one memory module with wafer-level redundancy and a bonded edge connector, skipping dicing, die sort, packaging and module assembly.
note: Anamartic wafer-scale memory precedent.

title: Aircraft-style leasing of fab tools across memory makers
idea: Magnify tool ownership to third-party lessors who buy EUV, etch and deposition tools and lease them, redeploying tools between memory makers as cycles shift, like aircraft leasing.

title: Magnify contract length: 15-year securitized memory bonds
idea: AI buyers sign 15-year take-or-pay capacity contracts for a new U.S. fab; the contracts are securitized into investment-grade 'memory bonds' sold to pension funds, cutting the fab's cost of capital from ~12% to ~5%.
note: 15-year commitments in a cyclical commodity are a hard sell; 5% cost of capital optimistic.

title: Eliminate the storage-node junction: electrostatically induced virtual drain
idea: Delete the n+ storage-node implant: a thin, always-biased spacer gate (polarity gate) induces an electron layer that acts as the drain, so there is no metallurgical junction under the gate edge for band-to-band tunneling. The storage node contacts the induced layer through a silicide.

title: Eliminate interlayer dielectric fill: vacuum-gap array wiring
idea: Leave the space between bitlines, wordlines and tiers as sealed vacuum cavities (pinch-off cap deposition) instead of gap-fill oxide followed by CMP, with nitride posts holding the structure.

title: Eliminate neon excimer gas: all-solid-state 193 nm lithography laser
idea: Generate 193 nm light from high-power Yb fiber lasers via frequency conversion and sum-frequency mixing in CLBO crystals, replacing ArF excimer chambers that consume Ne/Ar/F2 gas fills.
note: Solid-state 193 nm sources exist for inspection; litho power level not reached.

title: Eliminate the tall capacitor: short storage nodes plus offset-cancelling sense amps
idea: Halve capacitor height (AR ~35:1, Cs ~2.5 fF) and recover margin with offset-cancelled, bitline-isolated sense amplifiers and shorter bitlines, absorbing the extra refresh inside the existing DDR5 refresh budget. The die still runs standard DDR5 timings.
note: Offset-cancelling SAs already in production DRAM.

title: Eliminate the storage-node junction: junctionless accumulation-mode access transistors
idea: Replace the n+/p junction at the storage node with a uniformly doped junctionless (accumulation-mode) channel. This removes the high-field depletion region where trap-assisted tunneling and GIDL create the leakage tail.
note: Junctionless devices need high doping, raising BTBT; 10x tail claim doubtful.

title: Eliminate photomasks: multi-beam direct write for low-volume DRAM
idea: Eliminate $10-30M mask sets for small-lot memory: multi-beam e-beam writers expose critical layers directly for specialty DRAM (rad-hard, automotive, custom HBM base dies), allowing per-wafer design changes.
note: Multi-beam direct write (MAPPER etc.) has struggled on throughput.

title: Block-copolymer self-assembly draws sense-amp fins at bitline pitch
idea: Reverse lithography's role: coarse guides from U.S. interference or e-beam litho steer U.S.-made block copolymers to self-assemble the 20-30 nm fins of SA transistors at exactly the bitline pitch, so SAs pitch-match open bitlines without folding.

title: Wafer-scale memory slab: one periphery per quadrant, no packaging
idea: Reverse die and wafer: a whole U.S.-fabbed 300 mm array wafer becomes one memory appliance with stitched global buses, redundant reticle tiles and one shared periphery/I/O tile per quadrant, mounted directly on a U.S.-made cold plate with no dicing or offshore packaging.

title: Silicon holds itself: cold-crucible skull Czochralski growth
idea: Reverse container and content: melt silicon by induction inside a water-cooled segmented copper crucible so a frozen silicon skull forms the only wall the melt touches, then pull 300 mm ingots from the levitated-contact melt with a cusp magnetic field for oxygen-free, quartz-free growth.

title: Solid-state 193 nm light: lithography without neon gas
idea: Reverse the laser medium: replace ArF excimer gas discharge with frequency-converted fiber/solid-state lasers (e.g., sum-frequency mixing to 193 nm) as DUV scanner sources.

title: Periphery on reclaimed wafers with old-node, hafnium-free gates
idea: Rearrange array and periphery onto separate wafers: build the 49% periphery on reclaimed monitor wafers at an older node with poly/SiON gates (no Hf, no EUV), then hybrid-bond it under the cell array.

title: Square panels for HBM stacking and bonding
idea: Rearrange the substrate shape: after front-end, re-tile known-good DRAM dies onto 510x515 mm rectangular panels for hybrid bonding, thinning, TSV reveal and molding instead of round 300 mm reconstituted wafers.

title: Maskless periphery: multi-beam e-beam writes the logic, not masks
idea: Reverse which part gets masks: the regular array uses cheap periodic patterning, while the irregular periphery (~49% of die) is direct-written by massively parallel multi-beam e-beam, so no periphery reticles exist.

title: Stack eight cheap wafers instead of shrinking one
idea: Rearrange density from the XY plane to the Z axis: build 2D DRAM arrays at a relaxed DUV pitch on 8 wafers and stack them wafer-on-wafer with hybrid bonding (no TSV), sharing one periphery wafer at the bottom.

title: Map bf16 mantissa bits onto weaker pitch-walk bitlines
idea: Rearrange data significance onto process asymmetry: fluorine-free spacer patterning (non-PFAS resists, Cl/HBr/O2 etches) enlarges SAQP pitch walk so alternate bitline sets are systematically weaker; the controller maps sign/exponent bits onto strong lines and low mantissa bits onto weak lines without ECC.
note: Same LSB-on-weak-lines mapping.

title: Smart-Cut donor reuse yields twenty single-crystal tiers per wafer
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: hydrogen-implant one premium 300 mm donor, bond and split a ~50 nm crystalline Si film onto the growing 3D stack, re-polish the donor, and repeat ~20 times so every tier has bulk-quality lateral channels. Bonding at <=400 C builds monolithic crystalline stacks without strained Si/SiGe superlattice epitaxy.

title: Air gaps between buried wordlines cut hammer coupling
idea: TRIZ #31 Porous materials: a sacrificial carbon spacer between neighboring buried wordlines is ashed out through a pinch-off cap using U.S.-vendor deposition/etch tools, leaving an air gap (k=1) that weakens capacitive and field coupling from aggressor to victim.

title: Inert atmosphere: sealed-pod minimal-fab makes DRAM inside ordinary warehouses
idea: TRIZ #39 Inert atmosphere: every wafer stays in nitrogen-filled pods docked to sealed tool minienvironments, so a fixed legacy DRAM flow plus at most one new mask runs in a standard warehouse without a ballroom cleanroom.

title: Myelin air-gap sheaths between wordline planes shrink tier pitch
idea: Myelin lets axons be thin yet fast by insulating them; deposit sacrificial carbon layers between the wordline plates of a 3D DRAM stack and ash them out through vent slits after the stack is built, leaving pillar-supported k=1 air gaps between planes.

title: Plasmid process modules dropped into existing logic foundry flows
idea: Bacteria gain new abilities by taking up small self-contained plasmids. DRAM-specific steps (buried wordline, cell module, bitline) are packaged as licensed 'plasmid' modules with qualified recipes and tool kits that a mature logic foundry inserts into its flow, sharing FEOL/BEOL tools with its existing products.
note: Embedded DRAM in logic foundries existed; commodity cost parity doubtful.

title: AMOLED dual-gate TFT trick: breathing back-gate for hold versus access
idea: Display backplanes add a second gate under the TFT to shift its threshold on demand. Give vertical-channel 4F2 access transistors a shared back-gate plate held at about -1 V during retention (raising Vt ~0.3 V, cutting subthreshold leakage ~1000x) and pulsed positive only for the activated mat during access to boost on-current.

title: Hospital plasma sterilization: radical-based pre-gate clean for periphery
idea: Hospitals swapped steam autoclaves for hydrogen-peroxide plasma sterilizers. Replace the RCA wet sequence before the periphery high-k/metal-gate stack with remote hydrogen-radical organic/metal removal plus anhydrous HF/alcohol vapor oxide etch in one vacuum chamber.

title: Solar epitaxial lift-off: periphery layer on a reused donor wafer
idea: High-efficiency III-V solar cells peel their thin active layer off a GaAs substrate that is reused many times. Grow the periphery CMOS device layer on a porous-silicon release layer, bond it to the array wafer, split it off, and re-epi the donor 10+ times instead of consuming a fresh prime wafer for the periphery tier.

title: Thermos flask: sealed vacuum gaps around vertical bitlines
idea: Like a vacuum flask, after the 3D stack is built, selectively remove a sacrificial carbon or SiGe interlayer between vertical bitlines and wordline plates and pinch it shut with a non-conformal cap, replacing k ~4 fill with vacuum.

title: Cubic-zirconia skull melting: quartz-free cold-crucible Czochralski silicon
idea: Cubic zirconia is grown in a water-cooled, segmented copper 'cold crucible': RF induction melts the charge while a frozen skin of the same material forms the container. Apply it to silicon: hold an induction-heated melt in its own frozen silicon skull inside a slotted copper crucible, with electromagnetic confinement shaping the melt surface for Czochralski pulling of 300 mm ingots.

title: Color-addressed banks: the wavelength is the address
idea: In DWDM networks the color routes the call. Here each DRAM bank group owns one wavelength from a host comb laser through its own microring. A request is just lighting that color on a shared bus waveguide, so routing and bank selection happen in optics with no address decode or arbitration.

title: Utility-tunnel backside power delivery for HBM core dies
idea: Cities run utilities in tunnels under the street. Move HBM power delivery to the back of each core die with nano-TSVs and a backside power mesh, leaving every front-side TSV and bump for signals.
note: Backside power is industry roadmap; vertical power TSVs between dies still needed.

title: Soviet cold-crucible skull melting for crucible-free Czochralski silicon
idea: Revive Soviet-era cold-crucible induction melting: hold the silicon melt in a water-cooled, segmented copper crucible where a frozen silicon skull forms the container, then pull Czochralski ingots from it, adding oxygen by gas doping for gettering.

title: Skull-Melting Silicon: Cold-Crucible Czochralski Without Spruce Pine Quartz
idea: Revive the Lebedev Institute's 1970s skull-melting technique (cold-crucible induction melting, used to make cubic zirconia) for silicon crystal growth: a water-cooled segmented copper crucible inductively melts silicon that freezes into its own thin solid-silicon skull, so no high-purity quartz crucible ever touches the melt.

title: Mirror-paired tiers share one bitline and one plate layer
idea: Inverts 'each tier is a complete self-contained layer.' Build tiers as mirror-image pairs flipped about a shared middle bitline film, with each pair's outer plate shared with the next pair, so two tiers need one bitline and one plate film instead of two each.

title: Microfluidic-cooled DRAM tiers keep 32-high stacks at 45 °C
idea: Inverts 'heat must flow down through the stack to one lid.' Etch microchannels into the back side of each thinned DRAM tier and pump dielectric coolant between tiers so retention-critical tiers run ~40 C cooler than in a conventional HBM-style stack.
note: IBM-style interlayer cooling known; refresh savings bounded by refresh share of power.

title: Short wordline segments with bonded local drivers make resistive TiN fine
idea: Inverts 'wordlines need a low-resistivity metal.' Cut every wordline into 32-64-cell segments, each fed by its own driver in the hybrid-bonded logic wafer below, so plain TiN or degenerately doped Si wordlines meet RC targets without W, Co or Ru.

title: Cold-crucible Czochralski: silicon melt levitated, no quartz contact
idea: Inverts 'silicon melt must sit in a high-purity quartz crucible': hold the melt in a water-cooled segmented copper crucible by induction, with a thin frozen silicon skull as the container, and pull the crystal from it; electromagnetic stirring sets interstitial oxygen.

title: Federal offtake guarantees for old-tool tier-stacked DRAM
idea: Inverts 'markets fund only leading-edge memory'. DoD/DOE sign 10-year take-or-pay contracts at a fixed $/GB for DRAM-class memory made on >=180 nm tool lines in the U.S., with the price ratcheting down as tier counts rise.

title: Build ISO 7 ballroom fabs relying only on sealed minienvironments
idea: Inverts 'DRAM needs ultra-clean cleanroom buildings': rely solely on sealed FOUPs and tool-level minienvironments with the building at ISO 7, accepting a higher particle-defect rate whose isolated cell kills fit within 1% and whose line-level kills are remapped.

title: Run array litho on non-ASML scanners with relaxed overlay
idea: Inverts 'array lithography needs the tightest overlay from one supplier': print array layers on Nikon/Canon-class immersion scanners with looser overlay, accepting misalignment-induced contact faults in up to 1% of cells.

title: US DRAM entrant leads with 125 C automotive and defense grade
idea: A new US memory maker first targets Grade-1 (125 C) automotive, industrial and defense DRAM, where self-calibrating periphery is a moat, volumes suit a modest fab and prices are high, then scales to datacenter.
note: The niche-DRAM model is already used by Winbond, ISSI and Etron.

title: Parallel MEMS tips write atom-precise imprint masters
idea: First principle: the resolution limit is one surface atom, which STM hydrogen-depassivation lithography reaches; it is slow, but a master only has to be written once. A 10,000-tip MEMS array writes a DRAM array master on H-terminated Si with ~1 nm edge roughness, selective ALD converts it to a hard template, and it is cloned into thousands of imprint working templates.

title: Igloo: silicon skull crucible eliminates high-purity quartz crucibles
idea: Stimulus 'igloo' (a shelter built from the very material it keeps out) -> melt silicon in a water-cooled segmented copper cold crucible by RF induction so a frozen silicon skin forms the crucible wall; pull Cz-style 300 mm crystals from the skull melt and add controlled oxygen through a gas-phase SiO doser to keep gettering.

title: Chain-cell PZT FeRAM on a Texas line with domestic electrodes
idea: Box = {medium: PZT polarization | access: chain architecture, each FeCap in parallel with its transistor and cells linked in series (4F2-class) | sense: destructive charge read with in-chain restore | integration: 3D trench FeCaps | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: Dallas-style PZT module using Missouri lead, Oregon zirconium, and LaNiO3 conductive-oxide electrodes from California lanthanum and Michigan nickel}. Conductive-oxide electrodes suppress PZT fatigue toward 1e12-1e14 cycles, and a small SRAM cache absorbs hot writes.
note: Chain FeRAM and Dallas PZT exist; PZT scaling below ~130 nm is the unresolved blocker.

title: DUV-only arrays with loose CD control, weak-cell tail coded away
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x soft-decision SA x standard integration x bulk Si x ArF-immersion SAQP without EUV. Critical layers are patterned with DUV multipatterning at wider CD variation, letting ~1% of cells be too weak or leaky; soft sensing plus the code covers them.

title: Open-bitline 4F^2 vertical cells, coupling noise absorbed by code
idea: Box: vertical-channel 4F^2 cell x VCT access x open-bitline SA without dummy mats x tight-pitch array x bulk Si x standard. Accept the higher bitline-to-bitline coupling noise and weaker reference symmetry of open-bitline 4F^2 arrays, and delete edge dummy mats, letting ~1% of reads fail and be corrected.

title: Cold-crucible induction Czochralski growth with no quartz at all
idea: Box [standard 1T1C | Si access | voltage SA | standard | ingot pulled from a segmented water-cooled copper cold crucible with RF-levitated melt skull | magnetic CZ]: the melt touches only its own frozen Si skull, so no silica crucible and near-zero oxygen; nitrogen co-doping at 1e14-1e15 cm-3 replaces oxygen precipitates for intrinsic gettering.

title: Memory dies stand on edge like books on logic
idea: Box: DRAM die x standard x standard x sidewall-metallized edge bond at 20 um pitch x logic die as the shelf x laser-patterned sidewall plating. Thin DRAM dies are diced, edge-metallized and stood vertically in rows on the base logic die, so stack height no longer limits die count and each die's top edge touches the cold plate.

title: Sub-critical stochastic MTJ writes with ECC absorbing misses
idea: Box [medium: perpendicular MTJ | access: spin-orbit-torque line | sense: TMR at 50 mV bias | integration: BEOL over CMOS | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Writes use a short pulse at ~60% of deterministic switching current so ~1e-3 of bits fail to switch; instead of write-verify loops, a BCH code over each 512-bit word absorbs them and background scrubbing rewrites only failed bits.

title: Wafer-scale DRAM tiles sold undiced for rack memory
idea: Box[Integration=whole-wafer memory with on-wafer spare routing x Transform=no dicing or packaging x Owner=startup x Scale=rack appliance]: keep the DRAM wafer intact, route around defective dies via redistribution-layer switches, and mount it as a single ~300+ GB memory plane fed by a wafer-edge controller.

title: Po: every bitline wears a shield — coaxial poly-Si bitlines
idea: Po: a bitline wrapped like a TV cable. Form bitlines inside a grounded conformal doped poly-Si sleeve separated by an SiO2/air liner, so neighbor-bitline coupling and wordline kickback terminate on the shield; Cb rises ~15% but pattern-dependent noise (up to ~30% of sense margin) disappears.

title: Multibeam e-beam direct write replaces masks for irregular layers
idea: Po: masks don't exist. Use a ~250k-beam electron writer (today's mask-writer technology) directly on wafers for the irregular, low-area layers (periphery cuts, fuse/redundancy personalization, product variants) while periodic array layers use cheap patterning.

title: Fab in a tube: continuous vacuum track for capacitor module
idea: Po: the wafer never leaves the tool. Chain all ~40 capacitor-module steps (mold deposition, etch, clean, ALD, anneal) in a linear vacuum-linked track with single-wafer flow: no FOUPs, no queues, no air exposure between steps.
note: Vacuum-linked linear track, a module-scoped version of I-07598.

title: Self-aligned octuple patterning lets old 193i scanners print 1x-nm
idea: Po: the old scanner prints finer than its spec. Add three generations of spacer cascades (SAOP) to a 2x-nm DRAM line's existing 193i scanners so an 80 nm litho pitch becomes 10 nm lines for wordlines/bitlines; only extra ALD and etch chambers go into the existing building.

title: Retention-mode back-gate swing on double-gate vertical transistors
idea: Worse: use one fixed Vt that must stay low for speed. Flip: in 4F2 vertical-channel arrays, make the shared isolation plate a back gate driven to about -1.5 V in self-refresh (Vt +300 mV, subthreshold leakage about 100x lower) and to 0 V when the bank is active.

title: Laser-regrown epitaxial storage contact removes implant-damage leakage
idea: Worse: implant the storage-node junction and leave damage clusters that drive trap-assisted leakage. Flip: form the junction by in-situ-doped selective epitaxy followed by nanosecond laser melt-regrowth, giving a defect-free graded junction with no implant cascades.
note: Selective epi contacts already standard; laser regrowth is the twist.

title: Solid-state 193 nm lasers eliminate neon and fluorine gas
idea: Worsen: make every immersion DUV scanner burn neon sourced from a war zone, plus fluorine-rich gas fills. Flip: replace ArF excimer lasers with fiber-laser-pumped solid-state sources that reach 193 nm by cascaded harmonic generation in CLBO-type borate crystals grown domestically, so no rare gas is needed.

title: Undiced wafer-scale DRAM panels for rack memory pools
idea: Worse: dice, package and test thousands of dies, each losing scribe and edge area. Flip: keep the whole wafer as one memory, with reticle-stitched interconnect and die/row-level redundancy routing. Mount it directly in a rack memory appliance behind a wafer-level CXL fabric.

title: Silicon-on-sapphire cells eliminate substrate junction leakage tail
idea: Worse: keep the storage-node junction in a bulk crystal whose defects create the 13 fA tail. Flip: put thin epitaxial Si on Kyropoulos sapphire, so the node has no substrate junction and leaks only through the channel. Sapphire boules use molybdenum crucibles, not high-purity quartz.

title: Wafer-scale DRAM modules that never dice, test or package dies
idea: Worse: dice every wafer, throw out flawed dies and package survivors one by one. Flip: keep the 300 mm wafer whole as one memory module with defect-tolerant routing and spare-block remapping, bonded directly to a cold-plate carrier board.

title: Submariner's bulkheads: grounded shield tiers isolate hammer coupling
idea: Submarines compartmentalize so one flood does not sink the boat. Interleave a 3 nm grounded conductive bulkhead film between active tiers, and grounded shield fins between adjacent lateral wordlines in 3D DRAM.

title: No-till farmer grows silicon without any quartz crucible
idea: Persona: a no-till farmer skips the plow, so skip the crucible. Run Czochralski growth from a cold, segmented, water-cooled copper crucible. Induction fields push the melt off the walls, so a frozen silicon skull is the only wall the melt touches. Add nitrogen co-doping to make up for the wafer strength normally supplied by oxygen.

title: Stage magician hides magnetism: Mn3Sn antiferromagnetic tunnel junction memory
idea: Persona: a magician whose magnet is invisible. Store bits in the chiral antiferromagnetic order of Mn3Sn and read them with a Mn3Sn/MgO/Mn3Sn all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junction. Write by spin-orbit torque in picoseconds.

title: Homesteader builds upward: memory-layer foundry on legacy logic wafers
idea: Persona: a homesteader who adds a floor instead of buying land. A U.S. business deposits non-volatile BEOL memory layers, such as nitride ferroelectric or MRAM below 400 C, directly on customers' finished logic wafers in existing lines.

title: Prospector without Spruce Pine: reusable crucibles with continuous Czochralski
idea: A prospector cut off from the one quartz mine refuses to scrap a crucible per ingot. Grow DRAM-grade silicon by continuous Czochralski with granular-poly feeding in a long-life crucible: synthetic sol-gel silica made from fumed silica (any sand plus chlorination) inside a reusable silicon-nitride-coated graphite susceptor, pulling 5-10 ingots per crucible.

title: Child asks why break the cookie: wafer-scale DRAM, no dicing
idea: A child asks why you bake one big cookie and then break it into crumbs. Keep the whole 300 mm wafer as one memory: redundant tiles with an on-wafer mesh that maps out bad tiles at test, wafer-level power planes and edge optical I/O, giving a ~1-2 TB rack memory slab per wafer.

title: Commodity trader's forward curve: hyperscaler-funded DRAM capacity options
idea: Grain markets finance planting with forward contracts. Hyperscalers buy tradable 10-year wafer-start options on a new fab, prepaying 30-40% of capex at a strike price and keeping the right to resell on an exchange; builders get capital at near-sovereign cost while demand risk shifts to buyers who can hedge it.

title: Detector-grade crucible-free float-zone wafers for leak-free arrays
idea: Particle detectors use float-zone silicon grown without a quartz crucible, with ~100x less oxygen and few oxygen-vacancy traps. Develop 300 mm float-zone (or crucible-free pedestal-grown) substrates for DRAM array wafers so oxygen-precipitate generation centers near the access junction are gone.
note: 300 mm FZ unproven; loses oxygen-precipitate gettering.

title: Nanoimprint templates pattern decoder and sub-wordline-driver stripes
idea: Patterned-media hard drives and RFID makers imprint sub-20 nm features cheaply; the highly regular decoder and SWD stripes are imprinted from a master template at 15-20 nm half-pitch, while irregular logic stays on DUV at relaxed rules.

title: Deposition-defined vertical decoder transistors replace lithographic gate lengths
idea: Like MEMS and solar fabs that set critical dimensions by film thickness, decoder transistors are vertical channels whose gate length is an ALD film thickness and whose width is a spacer thickness; logic personalization is done with implants at relaxed DUV pitch.

title: Dumb-array DRAM: CXL controller absorbs refresh, ECC, repair, test
idea: Hyperscalers already own smart memory controllers, so strip the DRAM die to cells, SAs, decoders and a narrow I/O; refresh scheduling, row-hammer tracking, ECC, repair remapping, mode registers and BIST move into a CXL controller on a logic node. With no random logic left, the DRAM die needs no EUV.

title: Well-less satellite tiers: oxide-isolated array layers remove STI for 4F2
idea: Satellites dodge single-event upsets by putting transistors on buried oxide with no bulk well; build every DRAM array tier on transferred thin silicon over oxide so there is no substrate junction, no well contact and no shallow-trench isolation between cells. Gate-all-around vertical channels abut at true 4F2 because isolation comes from the oxide below, and the bulk charge-collection volume behind soft errors and junction leakage disappears.
note: SOI DRAM floating-body effects degrade retention; 4F2 via oxide isolation is known.

title: Containerless space-furnace logic: cold-crucible induction Czochralski for 300 mm
idea: Space crystal growers avoid containers altogether. On Earth, a segmented water-cooled copper cold crucible with induction heating makes silicon hold itself inside a frozen Si skull, so the melt never touches quartz. Controlled O2/Ar ambient or SiO dosing restores the oxygen needed for intrinsic gettering, and cusp magnetic fields steady the melt.

title: KV-cache-grade rows: full cells for exponents, cheap cells for mantissas
idea: AI KV-caches and weights survive flipped low mantissa bits but not flipped exponents. Build a 'BF16-graded' region where hard-wired bit-lane routing places sign, exponent and high mantissa bits in standard ~5 fF cells on normal refresh. The 8 low mantissa bits go in half-height (AR ~35, ~2.5 fF) capacitors on a relaxed 256 ms refresh with no retention guarantee.
note: Same graded capacitor mechanism.

title: DRAM futures exchange lets new fabs borrow against forward sales
idea: Airlines, extreme fuel users, hedge on exchanges. A cleared DRAM futures contract (per Gb of DDR5-equivalent, quarterly delivery) lets AI clouds and phone OEMs hedge, and lets new entrants pre-sell output and borrow against hedged revenue.

title: Coaxial capacitor shell wraps the vertical access transistor
idea: Collapse two scales into one pillar: the vertical channel transistor sits in the core and the storage capacitor is a coaxial dielectric/electrode shell wrapped around its upper half, so a 4F2 footprint holds both.
note: Modest 6F2-to-4F2 gain; coaxial shell capacitance small without tall pillar.

title: Bond eight DRAM wafers before dicing: TSV-free wafer-stacked HBM
idea: Replace die-by-die microbump stacking with sequential wafer-on-wafer hybrid bonding of 8-12 DRAM wafers, using fine-pitch bonded vias through 5 um-thinned silicon instead of large TSVs, then dice the finished stack once.
note: Compound wafer yield is the known blocker.

title: One vacuum cluster runs forty capacitor steps without queuing
idea: Collapse the wafer's timescale: a linear vacuum cluster integrates ~40 sequential deposition, etch and clean steps of the capacitor module, so the wafer never leaves vacuum or waits in a FOUP queue; the module goes from ~20 days to ~1 day of cycle time.

title: Domestic multi-column e-beam writes periphery and cut layers maskless
idea: Use thousands of parallel miniature e-beam columns built in the U.S. to direct-write only the sparse, irregular layers (periphery contacts, cut masks, chip IDs), while self-assembly or imprint handles the dense arrays.

title: Nanoimprint-first DRAM fab for repetitive array layers
idea: Molecule-to-wafer replication: a master template stamps the extremely periodic cell-array layers (bit lines, capacitor holes) into resist by UV nanoimprint, with no excimer laser and so no neon, argon or krypton. LED UV cures the resist.
note: Canon NIL already evaluated for memory; defectivity and overlay limit.

title: Quartz-free crystal pulling: cold-crucible Czochralski from failed electromagnetic casting
idea: Electromagnetic casting held molten silicon in a water-cooled segmented copper crucible by induction, with no quartz, but died because it only made multicrystalline solar ingots. Combine that cold crucible with seed pulling and a cusp magnetic field so 300 mm dislocation-free crystals grow with zero quartz contact, and add nitrogen doping for gettering since the crystal is now oxygen-poor.

title: Canon nanoimprint for DRAM: repair maps absorb defects, fluorine-free resist
idea: Nanoimprint stalled on particle-induced defects and template wear. DRAM already repairs defects with spare rows and columns: imprint capacitor-hole and storage-node layers in UV-cure acrylate resist with a non-fluorinated siloxane release layer, map imprint defects by fast inline e-beam inspection, fuse them to redundancy, and replicate cheap daughter templates from one e-beam master.

title: Ball Semiconductor's sealed-flow, cleanroom-free fab applied to flat memory wafers
idea: Ball Semiconductor proposed processing 1 mm silicon spheres in sealed tubes without a cleanroom and failed because lithography on spheres was poor. Keep the part that worked, sealed continuously flowing minienvironments, but carry flat wafers in nitrogen-purged pods through linked single-wafer modules so DRAM's repetitive flow needs no ballroom cleanroom.

title: Air gaps between buried wordlines stop passing-gate leakage
idea: Effect: fringing-field coupling (passing-gate effect). The oxide between neighbouring buried wordlines and the storage-node junction becomes a sealed air gap (k~1), so a neighbour's 3 V swing no longer lowers the barrier of the passing cell, removing the activity-dependent leakage spikes that force conservative refresh. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
note: Air-gap spacers already used in DRAM bitline isolation; modest tail and hammer gain.

title: Cold-crucible induction skull melting gives quartz-free Czochralski silicon
idea: Effect: eddy-current induction heats silicon inside a segmented, water-cooled copper crucible while the Lorentz force pushes the melt off the wall, so molten Si rests on its own frozen Si skull and never touches fused quartz; add a cusp magnetic field to damp convection while pulling 300 mm crystals.

title: Pockels thin-film lithium niobate links make rack memory pooling viable
idea: Use thin-film LiNbO3 Pockels modulators (sub-pJ/bit, no carrier lifetime, ns latency) in CXL optical links so a rack-scale memory pool sits under 100 ns away. Servers keep a small local DRAM and borrow from the pool on demand, which removes per-server overprovisioning.
note: Pool latency dominated by protocol/switching, not modulator; TFLN adds cost.

title: Carbon-nanotube van der Waals memory runs code and weights in place
idea: Use CNT-fabric memory, which switches by van der Waals contact and is projected to retain data over 10 years well above 125 C, as byte-addressable main storage. OS images, maps and model weights then execute in place, removing the duplicate copy that is loaded from flash into DRAM at boot.

title: Heat-annealed self-healing flash becomes a write-tolerant DRAM extension
idea: Use the 125 C ambient plus brief on-die heater pulses to keep annealing trapped charge out of NAND tunnel oxide (the self-healing flash effect), pushing SLC endurance toward 1e8 cycles. Flash can then act as a swap tier for warm pages behind a small DRAM.
note: Macronix showed heater-annealed flash with ~1e8 cycles.

title: Aluminum-doped zinc oxide shield planes stop vertical row-hammer coupling
idea: Insert a 5 nm ALD Al:ZnO conductive plane, grounded through the staircase, between each pair of 3D-DRAM tiers so an aggressor wordline in tier k couples into the shield instead of victim cells in tiers k+1 and k-1.

title: F: fluorine-hardened recess-gate edge resists hot-carrier depassivation
idea: A tilted low-dose fluorine implant aimed only at the gate-to-storage-node overlap corner replaces Si-H with Si-F bonds (~5.7 eV vs ~3.1 eV), so hammer-induced hot carriers and GIDL fields cannot re-create the interface traps behind RTN and variable retention time.

title: U: Uranium-style take-or-pay contracts finance new non-volatile memory fabs
idea: Like utilities buying enrichment a decade ahead, hyperscalers sign 7-10-year take-or-pay contracts for MRAM/FeRAM wafer output at indexed prices, letting startups finance fabs with project debt.

title: MLCC-style multi-plate lateral capacitor for 3D DRAM tiers
idea: Copy multilayer-ceramic-capacitor construction: inside each tier's lateral capacitor recess, ALD 2N alternating TiN/high-k layers, then open one vertical slit where odd plates are recessed on one side and even plates on the other (like MLCC end terminations), so all plates connect in parallel between storage node and plate line.

title: Zoned newspaper editions: consortium base wafers, one personalization mask
idea: Like papers that print a common edition and swap one plate per zone, a consortium fab runs one standardized DRAM base wafer (array, sense amps, generic I/O) at maximum volume, and each buyer personalizes it with exactly one metal/via mask (density cut, interface, I/O width) on its own BEOL line.

title: Sacrificial-anode collector implants absorb hammer-injected electrons
idea: Galvanising protects steel with a zinc anode that corrodes first; add a shallow grounded n+ collector ribbon (or biased deep well) between adjacent active regions in the buried-channel array so electrons emitted by aggressor wordline traps and passing-gate charge pumping are collected before they reach a victim storage node.

title: Sixteen-tier decks hybrid-bonded with stitched vertical bitlines
idea: IFR: 'unlimited tiers without an unlimited etch.' Backward: build 16-tier decks with modest 30:1 etches, thin each deck to ~3 um, and hybrid-bond decks face-to-back at ~200 nm pitch so each vertical bitline continues through bond pads; six bonds give 96 tiers.

title: Crucible-free 300 mm silicon via cold-crucible induction skull melting
idea: Ideal: a crystal grown from a melt that touches nothing. Closest: pull 300 mm Cz crystals from a water-cooled segmented copper cold crucible where induction heats and partly levitates the melt and a frozen silicon skull is the container; interstitial oxygen for gettering is dosed via a controlled O2/Ar ambient instead of dissolving quartz.

title: Kerfless laser-split wafering of DRAM-grade silicon ingots
idea: Ideal: slicing with zero sawdust. Closest: focus an IR picosecond laser inside the ingot to write a sub-surface modified plane (KABRA-style, proven on SiC), then split each wafer off by thermal/ultrasonic stress; kerf drops from ~150 um to ~20 um and lapping shrinks.

title: Laser-crystallized silicon tiers stack refresh-free SRAM toward DRAM density
idea: Ideal: a static, refresh-free cell at DRAM density. Closest: monolithically stack 6-8 tiers of thin single-grain Si, crystallized by pulsed-laser melting of amorphous Si at <450 C wafer temperature, with n and p halves of each SRAM cell on alternate tiers, so bits per footprint multiply with no capacitor and DUV-friendly 28 nm rules.
note: Still 4-8x below DRAM density; CFET-like split known.

title: Wavelength is the address: passive AWG-routed photonic memory pool
idea: Ideal: addressing that costs no logic and no switching energy. Closest achievable: the host tunes a comb line whose wavelength encodes the target bank, a passive arrayed-waveguide grating steers that light to the bank's receiver, and the reply returns on the same wavelength, so bank selection needs no electronic switch or decoder tree.

title: Shaped wordline falling edge and capped row-open time
idea: Ideal: activating a row disturbs nothing. Closest: the wordline driver uses a slow, shaped falling ramp (~5 ns) instead of a sharp edge to cut electron injection and capacitive kick into adjacent rows, and the controller closes rows after <=36 ns to avoid RowPress-style long-open disturbance.
note: RowPress tRAS capping already proposed; edge shaping gain uncertain.

title: SIMOX-isolated access transistors remove junction leakage tail
idea: Ideal: a storage node with no leakage path to the substrate. Closest: build the cell array on 1990s SIMOX silicon-on-insulator so the storage-node junction sits on buried oxide, eliminating the substrate junction area and deep-level-defect generation current that create most retention tail cells.
note: SOI DRAM researched in the 1990s-2000s; cost and capacitor integration issues.

title: Mid-size OEM memory cooperative owning a shared DRAM line
idea: Ideal: memory always available at cost. Closest achievable: auto, industrial, PC and console OEMs jointly fund a line as a cooperative (Airbus-GIE or farm-co-op style) and get allocation in proportion to equity at cost-plus during shortages.

title: Undiced wafer-scale DRAM: RDL-stitched good dies on mature wafers
idea: Ideal: memory with no package, socket or dicing. Closest achievable with no new fab: existing OSAT redistribution-layer lines stitch every good die on a mature 2x-nm DRAM wafer into one wafer-scale slab with spare routing around bad dies; one wafer gives ~2 TB on a cold plate serving a rack over CXL.

title: Multi-beam e-beam writes only cuts, making DRAM variants maskless
idea: Constraint: no new mask set per product. Print array gratings once with cheap periodic litho, then use a ~250k-beam electron writer only on sparse cut and via layers (<5% exposed area) to customize die size, ECC layout and bank count.

title: Substitute area-selective deposition for resist-pattern-etch-strip loops
idea: Grow films only where wanted by first patterning inhibitor monolayers (UV-cleaved aminosilane SAMs or DUV-written carbon), then running ALD that nucleates only on uninhibited regions, deleting resist coat, develop, etch, strip and their cleans.

title: Substitute stochastic filaments with deterministic proton intercalation cells
idea: Swap filamentary ReRAM (random breakdown, high variability) for nanosecond protonic electrochemical cells where a gate pulse shuttles protons through a solid electrolyte (e.g., phosphosilicate glass) into a WO3 channel, giving smooth, repeatable non-volatile conductance states.
note: MIT protonic PSG/WO3 programmable resistors already demonstrated; not DRAM-class endurance.

title: Magnify nanotube count per transistor to average away leakage variance
idea: Build each access transistor from ~20 aligned semiconducting carbon nanotubes on quartz or glass instead of 1-3. Per-device variance falls ~1/sqrt(N), and any metallic tube is burned open by an electrical breakdown pulse at test.

title: Nanomechanical parametron stores the bit as oscillation phase
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action + #15 Dynamics: revive Goto's 1954 parametron at nanoscale. Each cell is a high-Q nanomechanical resonator pumped at 2f by a shared wordline AC drive, ringing at f in one of two phases (0 or 180 degrees); phase is the bit, the pump continuously regenerates it, and a small injected signal picks the phase on write.

title: Spatial ALD carousel boosts dielectric deposition throughput tenfold
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action: replace pulse/purge temporal ALD with wafers rotating under gas-curtain-separated precursor and oxidant zones, so every revolution is one ALD cycle; ZrO2/Al2O3 capacitor dielectrics and liners deposit ~10x faster near atmospheric pressure.
note: Spatial/rotary semi-batch ALD already commercial; HAR conformality limits gain.

title: Zebra stripes: superlattice edge transfer defines 8 nm bitlines without lithography
idea: Random stimulus 'zebra' -> an ALD/epitaxial superlattice of alternating materials (for example Si/SiGe) is cleaved and polished edge-on, selectively etched, metallized and stamped onto the wafer as a line array (superlattice nanowire pattern transfer). Film thickness, controlled to the angstrom, sets pitch and CD instead of optics.
note: Heath group SNAP, 2003.

title: Pacemaker heartbeat: NEMS parametron stores bit as oscillation phase
idea: A biologist sees life keeping information as a rhythm, like the heart's pacemaker. Each cell is a nanomechanical resonator pumped parametrically at 2f by a shared global pump; it settles into one of two phase states (0 or pi) that encode the bit, and it couples to a read line only when selected.

title: MLCC-style strontium titanate nanolaminate stretches pillar capacitors past k=70
idea: MLCC makers ship trillions of titanate capacitors made from abundant Ba, Sr and Ti. Grow ALD SrTiO3/TiO2 nanolaminates (Sr cyclopentadienyl + TTIP, two-step crystallization) inside TiN-lined pillars in a university fab, with Al2O3 interface doping to tame leakage.

title: NEMS parametron: bit as the phase of a vibrating beam
idea: IFR: a bit made of motion, free to keep if lossless. Closest achievable: a high-Q nanomechanical resonator pumped at twice its frequency oscillates in one of two degenerate phases (0 or pi); a small seed signal sets the phase (write) and phase-sensitive detection reads it, reviving Goto's 1950s parametron.

title: Cochlear tonotopic row selection with frequency-addressed wordline groups
idea: Like the basilar membrane, where each position resonates at its own frequency, each local wordline-driver group gets a tiny on-die resonator (BAW/MEMS or LC) tuned to a unique frequency. The bank broadcasts one tone burst on a single shared line, and only the matching group rectifies it into a wordline enable, replacing predecode buses and one decoder level.
note: MEMS/LC resonators dwarf decoder logic area; ring-up latency.

title: Triboelectric generators: contact-electrified charge patches store bits
idea: Triboelectric nanogenerators move a saturating charge between dissimilar surfaces on contact; let an e-beam-defined, electrostatically actuated Ti cantilever tap a PTFE- or Al2O3-coated pad above a sensing transistor, transferring a self-limiting ~50-500 e- charge per contact, and reverse it by tapping with an opposite-polarity material, the patch retaining charge with electret-grade stability.
note: Mechanical tapping per bit is slow and wears; charge per contact is tiny.

title: Diatom biosilicification: room-temperature catalytic silica for gapfill and supports
idea: Diatoms build intricate silica shells at ambient temperature using polyamine/silaffin peptides that catalyze silicic-acid condensation. Use synthetic polyamine-catalyzed silica sols to conformally fill capacitor support lattices and shallow trenches below 100 C with a gentle cure, replacing high-temperature furnace TEOS and polysilazane steam anneals.

title: Acoustic delay-line page buffer frees sense amps instantly
idea: A modern mercury delay line: an AlN surface-acoustic-wave track runs under each bank's I/O edge. A sensed row is launched as acoustic pulses that take ~100 ns to cross, during which the sense amps precharge and open the next row; a transducer at the far end recaptures the bits as they arrive and serves bursts in flight.

title: Marconi coherer revival: link receivers that latch arriving bits nonvolatilely
idea: Like the 1890s coherer whose filings fused under RF, end each die-to-die write lane with a filamentary Ag/Cu nanogap switch that forms a filament when a pulse arrives, so the receiver is itself a nonvolatile staging latch, reset later by a counter-pulse 'tapper'.
note: Filament formation time and endurance make it a niche staging trick at best.

title: Core-weaving revival: robots thread insulated microwire through laser-drilled stacks
idea: Like core-memory weavers threading wires through ferrite rings, laser-ablate aligned 20 um holes through a stack of thinned dies or glass and robotically thread polyester-imide-enamelled (not PTFE) copper microwire through them, then press-contact it to pads on each tier.
note: Robotic threading of 20 um holes is impractical at volume.

title: Twistor Revival on Magnetic-Tape Coating Lines
idea: Revive Bell Labs' 1957 twistor (magnetic tape wrapped helically on a sense wire) as laminated sheets: surviving data-tape coating lines deposit high-coercivity barium-ferrite stripes on PET film over printed copper sense lines, then laminate crossed drive-line films roll-to-roll at km per hour.
note: Twistor bits are mm-scale and microsecond-class; density orders of magnitude below DRAM.

title: Po: banks chosen by pitch — AlN resonator select tones
idea: Po: a decoder that listens for its note. Each bank or subarray group enable is gated by an AlN thin-film acoustic resonator with a unique frequency on one shared RF select line; a single-tone burst wakes only the matching group through a rectifier, replacing trees of global decode wires and repeaters.

title: Sacrificial printed fan-out exposes internal test nodes, then dissolves
idea: Worse: dedicate die area to hundreds of large probe pads and on-die test muxes. Flip: inkjet-print a temporary solvent-soluble polymer-and-silver fan-out over the wafer that connects tiny internal test points to large probe pads, test through it, then strip it before final passivation and bumping.
note: Inkjet resolution far coarser than internal test points.

title: Compressed-sensing reads of sparse tensors with fewer sense ADCs
idea: Borrow compressive sampling from MRI and radio astronomy and shrink it to the column: in non-destructive gain-cell mats holding ReLU-sparse activations, the read currents of 8 columns are summed onto one sense line through pseudo-random +/-1 select patterns, taking 3 measurements per 8 columns, and a small base-die solver reconstructs the (at most 1-of-8 nonzero) data. Dense data falls back to normal column reads.
note: Needs strict 1-of-8 sparsity and analog current summing accuracy; real activations rarely meet that.

title: Core memory rethreaded by lithography: microtoroids around through-glass vias
idea: Magnetic core memory died on hand-threading labor and millimeter cores, not on its materials (iron oxide ferrite and copper). On glass panels, laser-drill via arrays, electroplate copper X, Y and sense lines through them, and form 5-10 um ferrite or NiFe rings around each crossing by room-temperature aerosol deposition, writing by coincident current.
note: Microsecond, ~1 GB/m2 density keeps it niche.

title: Sn: reflowable tin micro-links make field-reprogrammable repair fuses
idea: Replace one-time laser/e-fuses with Sn micro-links in sealed cavities: a Joule pulse melts a link so surface tension beads it open, and a second heater over wetting pads reflows it closed, so repair maps can be rewritten in the field as cells weaken.

title: Electrochromic rewritable optical pages host the LoRA adapter library
idea: Constraint (printable/roll-to-roll): a roll-to-roll coated electrochromic film (WO3/PEDOT) is written electrically through a passive printed electrode grid and read optically in parallel by an image sensor. Serving clusters park thousands of rarely used fine-tune adapters on it and load a whole adapter into HBM with one optical page read when a request arrives.

title: Chill first, etch second: ride on thermal inertia, no helium
idea: Reverse when cooling happens: pre-chill wafers cryogenically in the load lock and run short etch/deposition steps on the wafer's own thermal mass, replacing continuous helium backside gas with a time-budgeted temperature window.

title: UV-transparent lid lets depots erase trapped charge in oxide storage layers
idea: TRIZ #28 Mechanics substitution (optical for electrical): for back-end oxide-semiconductor storage tiers that sit at the top of the stack, package them under a fused-silica window like an EPROM; in a repair depot, deep-UV de-traps charge accumulated in the gate dielectric and channel, restoring threshold voltage and retention without electrical stress.
note: UV often worsens oxide-TFT instability (NBIS); niche repair use.

title: Hair-cell stochastic resonance: dithered mini-latch with majority vote
idea: Cochlear hair cells use stochastic resonance, where added noise helps a threshold detector see sub-threshold input. An isolated mini-comparator hanging off the bitline pair gets a controlled zero-mean dither on its tail node and fires 3-5 times in ~4 ns. A majority vote sets the main latch, which then restores the cell.
note: Dither plus voting reduces noise but not static offset.

title: Xylem-sap capillary wicking fills contacts without tungsten CVD
idea: Plants lift sap up narrow, hydrophilic, slightly tapered xylem vessels by capillarity. Make periphery and BEOL plug holes slightly tapered and plasma-hydrophilic, spin on a Cu-Mn nanoparticle ink that wicks to the bottom, then sinter at ~400 C so the Mn forms its own MnSiOx barrier while the copper densifies.

title: Blind-spot filling-in regenerates lost weight blocks approximately
idea: The visual cortex fills the retina's blind spot from its surroundings; weights are stored with a tiny per-layer predictor so if a recycled chip's bank dies, its weight blocks are regenerated from neighboring blocks plus a stored residual sketch, keeping the model serving until the part is swapped.

title: Electroless nickel-boron electrodes coat 100:1 capacitor holes conformally
idea: Box [MIM cap with Ni-B electrodes | Si | voltage SA | standard | Si | autocatalytic electroless deposition after molecular Sn/Ag activation]: seed the hole walls, grow 3 nm Ni-B autocatalytically (self-limiting by bath depletion), then nitridize its surface with NH3 for a stable interface to the dielectric.

title: Sous-vide chef: memory held isothermal at a constant 125 C
idea: Sous-vide works because the temperature never changes: instead of fighting heat, on-die heaters hold the memory stack at a constant 125 C at all times, so it never thermally cycles, and refresh and link timing are calibrated once for that single point.
note: At 125 C retention collapses and refresh rises sharply.

title: Zinc solders abandoned for corrosion; Zn-Al fluxless joints inside sealed stacks
idea: Sn-Zn and Zn-Al solders were rejected in the 2006 lead-free transition because Zn oxidizes and corrodes in humid, flux-based board assembly. Inside an HBM-style stack the joint is never exposed: deposit Zn-Al eutectic caps on Cu pillars, reflow fluxless in formic-acid vapor and encapsulate immediately in molded underfill, replacing SnAg microbumps and In-based low-temperature solders.
note: 381 C reflow exceeds the DRAM assembly thermal budget.

title: Domestic molybdenum dual-work-function buried wordline replaces tungsten
idea: TRIZ #35 Parameter change: tungsten (China ~80%) is replaced by molybdenum from U.S. mines in the buried wordline; Mo needs no thick TiN barrier, which frees room for a low-work-function lower segment next to the storage-node junction that softens the gate-to-drain field.
