note: Mo wordlines and dual-work-function gates already pursued in industry.

title: Instant-photography dry resist and dry develop for periphery litho
idea: Like Polaroid replacing the wet darkroom, vapor-deposit a metal-oxide photoresist, expose, develop it in a plasma/thermal gas step and strip it dry on every periphery-only mask (implant blocks, contacts, metals), so these layers never touch developer, rinse or wet strip.

title: Vacuum canning: no-air-break integration of periphery gate and contacts
idea: Canned food needs no preservatives because it never meets air. Run the periphery gate stack (interface, high-k, metal, cap) and the contact module (etch, liner, fill) each in one vacuum cluster with in-situ dry cleans, so wafers never grow native oxide or pick up airborne contamination, and queue-time wet re-cleans disappear.

title: Molybdenum buried wordlines exploit shorter electron mean free path
idea: Effect: electron mean-free-path size effect (Fuchs-Sondheimer/Mayadas-Shatzkes). Replace TiN/W buried wordlines with barrierless Mo or Ru (mean free path ~11 and ~7 nm vs ~19 nm for W), cutting 10 nm-line resistance ~30-40% and freeing the barrier's trench volume; faster wordline edges shorten each internal refresh burst. DDR/HBM pins, commands and timings stay unchanged.
note: Mo/Ru replacing W is mainstream industry roadmap.

title: The wire is the memory: electron-position cells that store and route
idea: Erase the line between storage and interconnect: four-dot silicon dangling-bond or molecular cells hold a bit as which diagonal two electrons occupy, and the same cells chained in a line shift the bit to the array edge under a clocked field (quantum-dot cellular automata); no bitlines, no charge sharing.
note: QCA serial memory is old idea; room-temperature margins and atomic-precision fabrication at scale need a miracle.

title: Molecular quantum-dot cellular automata loop memory
idea: Scale bits down to electron positions inside a 2 nm mixed-valence molecule: the bit is which diagonal pair of four redox sites holds two electrons, and a clocked ring of molecules circulates bits like a shift register.
note: Promises 1e14 bits/cm2, but molecular QCA has not been clocked or read at RT in 25 years.

title: Substitute one shared free-electron laser for many tin-plasma EUV sources
idea: Build an energy-recovery-linac free-electron laser producing ~10 kW of 13.5 nm light and split it by grazing-incidence mirrors to 10-20 scanners, replacing per-tool tin-droplet plasma sources from a single supplier.

title: Synchrotron-style shared light source: free-electron laser feeds many scanners
idea: Cities replaced household generators with central power plants. Build one energy-recovery-linac free-electron laser per fab and split its multi-kW EUV beam to 10-20 scanners, replacing per-scanner laser-produced tin-plasma sources; wafers and DDR/HBM products are unchanged.

title: Shared energy-recovery free-electron laser feeds a whole EUV fab
idea: Tin-plasma EUV converts wall power at ~0.02%; an energy-recovery-linac FEL recycles the electron beam's energy and lases at 13.5 nm at ~0.1-1% wall-plug. One 10 kW source split by grazing-incidence optics feeds 10-20 scanners with no tin droplets and no hydrogen debris flow.
note: Shared ERL-FEL EUV already pursued by startups/labs; needs $100M+.

title: Po one lightbulb lights the whole fab: shared FEL EUV source
idea: Po: 'one lightbulb lights every scanner in the fab.' Extracted: drive 10-20 scanners from a single energy-recovery-linac free-electron laser at 13.5 nm, distributed by grazing-incidence beamlines, replacing per-scanner tin-droplet laser-produced-plasma sources.

title: Inkjet-head e-beam writer: 10,000 beamlets pattern without EUV
idea: Inkjet heads fire thousands of nozzles in parallel; build U.S. multi-column electron-beam direct writers with MEMS beam-blanker arrays that write DRAM critical layers straight into resist, replacing EUV exposures with a mask-free step.
note: MAPPER-style multibeam direct write pursued for decades; throughput never met fab needs.

title: Offset-trim implant enabling 2-bit cells only for millisecond-lived data
idea: One added halo/Vt implant mask tightens sense-amp transistor mismatch enough for 4-level sensing. Cells store 2 bits only for data that lives shorter than the shortened MLC retention of ~4-8 ms: in-flight activations and current-step scratch. Before that deadline, the allocator demotes any surviving data to 1-bit mode. Data lifetime is matched to cell retention.
note: Matching data lifetime to MLC retention is clever; 4-level sensing margin is the doubt.

title: Swap litho-patterned storage nodes for area-selective bottom-up growth
idea: Use area-selective ALD/CVD (inhibitor self-assembled monolayers on the dielectric, so growth occurs only on metal landing pads) to grow TiN storage-node pillars upward from each contact. The node layer copies the DUV-made contact pattern with no lithography or etch of its own.
note: ASD selectivity lasts nanometres, not tall pillars; mushrooming expected.

title: Replace semiconductor switch with non-touching tunneling-gap NEMS relay
idea: Substitute the channel with a vacuum-gap nanomechanical beam. When the wordline pulls it in, it stops ~1 nm from the storage electrode on an oxide standoff, so charge moves by electron tunneling and never by metal contact. When released (gap >5 nm), the only off-current is vacuum tunneling, effectively zero.

title: Substitute argon-purged Cz crystal with hydrogen-ambient crucible-free silicon
idea: Substitute argon-purged Czochralski pulling in quartz crucibles with electromagnetic cold-crucible casting in a hydrogen/nitrogen ambient for the substrate. The access transistors live in a 3-5 um low-oxygen epitaxial layer grown by H2-carrier CVD, with nitrogen co-doping for gettering.
note: Cold-crucible cast Si is multicrystalline; epi inherits grain boundaries.

title: Backside-etched capacitors in the thinned bulk replace front-side cylinders
idea: Substitute the front-side capacitor stack with capacitors etched from the wafer backside: after front-end transistors and bitlines, bond face-down, thin to ~3 um and etch capacitor holes from the back into silicon directly beneath each access transistor's storage junction, then line with ALD dielectric/electrode.
note: Backside trench needs 90:1 AR in 3 um and a junction connection; gain modest.

title: Infrared through-silicon optical links replace Bosch-etched copper TSVs
idea: Substitute SF6/C4F8 Bosch-etched Cu TSVs with vertical free-space optics: silicon is transparent at 1310 nm, so beams from bonded InP micro-emitters (Cl2/BCl3-etched) on the base die cross 30 um-thin DRAM dies to Ge-on-Si detectors (GeH4 epi) placed at a unique XY site on each die (position multiplexing).

title: Substitute quartz crucibles with electromagnetic cold-crucible silicon crystal growth
idea: Melt silicon in a water-cooled segmented copper crucible where induction currents push the melt off the walls (skull melting), and pull single crystals from the levitated pool under a cusp magnetic field. No fused-quartz crucible is consumed and oxygen from SiO2 dissolution disappears.

title: Bucket-brigade row buffer replaces column decoder and datalines
idea: Turn the sensed row into a CCD-style charge-transfer shift register: after sensing, bits march out of the stripe edge in parallel lanes at GHz rates straight into the serializer, so the column decoder, column-select lines and global I/O sense amps are gone. This combines CCD readout with the DRAM row buffer.

title: Solution-grown YBCO superconducting interposer lines cooled by liquid nitrogen
idea: Combine coated-conductor chemistry (TFA-MOD chemical solution deposition of YBCO on solution-deposited buffers, no argon ion-beam assist or sputtering) with interposer wiring operated in LN2, so memory-to-processor transmission lines have zero DC resistance and carry low-swing signals over 10-50 cm without repeaters; no helium cryogenics.

title: Laser-trim healing: test, then locally anneal each leaky cell
idea: Combine laser trimming of analog resistors with retention test: after mapping tail cells, a focused laser pulse locally anneals each leaky cell's junction or channel to passivate the defect, or deliberately opens it so it is mapped out. Buildable in a university nanofab: laser writer plus probe-station retention map.
note: Cannot target ~15 nm buried cells through BEOL with a laser.

title: Minimal Fab half-inch wafers plus maskless direct-write lithography
idea: Combine Japan's Minimal Fab (0.5-inch wafers, desk-sized local-cleanroom tools) with multibeam e-beam or laser direct-write. The result is a mask-free micro-fab that makes small lots of radiation-hard or specialty DRAM inside defense or auto plants.

title: Fluoride-free effluent enabling 95% water recycle in arid sites
idea: Combine a fully F-free process (no HF, no fluoride effluent, no CaF2 sludge) with reverse-osmosis plus EDI zero-liquid-discharge loops. With fluoride gone, the hardest RO-fouling and scaling ion is removed, so 95%+ of UPW can be recycled.

title: Carbon credits for avoided NF3, SF6 and CF4 finance fab capex
idea: Fuse a fluorine-free DRAM flow with verified carbon-credit issuance. Avoided F-gases (NF3 GWP about 16,100, SF6 about 23,500, CF4 about 7,400) earn credits over a baseline fab's emissions, which are pre-sold as offtake to fund construction.

title: Scanning-tunneling-microscope gap switch: non-contact NEMS access device
idea: Adapted from the STM, whose current changes ~10x per angstrom of gap: a nano-cantilever tied to the storage node is pulled by the wordline from a 3 nm gap to ~0.8 nm from the bitline contact so electrons tunnel across in the on state. It never touches, so there is no contact wear, and at full gap tunneling current is ~1e-9 of on-current.

title: DWDM wavelength-addressed wordlines through transparent glass
idea: Borrowed from telecom DWDM: each wordline driver on a glass panel is a photo-TFT under a thin-film Fabry-Perot filter tuned to one of 64 wavelengths, and a fast tunable laser beneath the transparent substrate selects a row by color, with 1-of-16 electrical predecode choosing the mat.

title: Foldable-phone flex hinge folds periphery behind the array
idea: Borrowed from foldable phones and flex-PCB folding: array and periphery are built side by side on polyimide, then the periphery strip is folded 180 degrees behind the array through a thin bent interconnect zone, so it takes no footprint and sits ~20 um under its mats.

title: Roof shingles: inclined lateral capacitors overlap neighbor footprints
idea: Like overlapping roof shingles, each lateral capacitor in a 3D stack is built on a slant, climbing one tier over its length, so it extends beneath the next cell's footprint without colliding; the slant comes from an inclined sacrificial ramp cut by tilted ion-beam etch.
note: Tilted etch inside buried lateral cavities is not practical.

title: Multilateral oil wells: six lateral cells branch from one hole
idea: Borrowed from multilateral drilling, where one vertical well feeds many horizontal laterals: each vertical bitline hole in a 3D stack is recessed in six directions per tier by a crystallographic wet etch, forming six lateral cells in a star around one vertical line.

title: Duplex printing: DRAM arrays on both faces of one wafer
idea: Adapted from duplex printing and logic backside power delivery: build the array on the front, bond to a carrier, thin, and build a second array on the backside of the same silicon, sharing periphery through nano-TSVs in the middle.

title: Antifouling-paint copper oxide and varistor zinc oxide form oxide SRAM
idea: Marine antifouling paint consumes Cu2O by the kiloton, and surge arresters use ZnO. Adapt p-type Cu2O and n-type ZnO thin-film transistors into a complementary BEOL latch: a static 4T/6T cell stacked in multiple tiers over logic.

title: PCB laser direct imaging: maskless DUV for low-volume periphery layers
idea: PCB makers dropped phototools for DMD laser direct imaging; apply a 193/248 nm micromirror-array maskless writer to DRAM's relaxed periphery layers (40 nm and up) and HBM base-die redistribution layers, so custom memory variants need no new reticle set.
note: DMDs at 193/248 nm and 40 nm resolution are unproven; mirror damage and throughput.

title: Titanium-industry cold crucibles: quartz-free Czochralski silicon
idea: Titanium and multicrystalline-silicon casting melt the charge inside water-cooled segmented copper 'cold crucibles' where induction fields hold the melt off the wall; adapt a cold-crucible induction Czochralski puller to 300 mm DRAM ingots, metering oxygen through a controlled SiO feed to keep the interstitial oxygen needed for gettering.
note: 300 mm dislocation-free growth from a cold crucible is unproven.

title: Dairy fresh-processing: consume activations in-DRAM before they decay
idea: Borrowed from dairies that process milk within hours rather than store it: activations are written into refresh-free DRAM subarrays and consumed within microseconds by charge-sharing multiply-accumulate in the same subarray (processing-in-memory), so no datum ever has to outlive milliseconds.
note: Analog charge-sharing MAC precision is limited.

title: Self-clearing film-capacitor electrodes for thin high-k DRAM capacitors
idea: Adapted from metallized polymer film capacitors, whose ultra-thin electrode vaporizes around a breakdown spot so the part survives with negligibly less area: use a 2-3 nm top electrode of a low-melting conductive oxide so a local dielectric breakdown burns a sub-10-nm hole in the electrode, isolating the defect instead of shorting the cell.

title: Civil Reserve Air Fleet adapted: retainer-paid U.S. reserve fab fleet
idea: Adapted from CRAF, where airlines get peacetime contracts in exchange for lending aircraft in crises: U.S. logic, NAND and foundry fabs are paid retainers to keep a qualified DRAM-compatible module flow (capacitor and buried-wordline recipes, spare tool kits) that they can activate within 90 days of a declared shortage.

title: NEMS relay wordline drivers with zero off-leakage
idea: Ruthenium-contact nanoelectromechanical relays are built in BEOL at <=350 C with a sacrificial release and used as mat-select and wordline-driver switches: they pass 3 V natively, need no level shifters or stacked high-voltage transistors, and leak nothing when open.

title: SiN photonic H-tree replaces the die's global data wires
idea: PECVD silicon-nitride waveguides (<=350 C), electro-optic polymer ring modulators (cured <=200 C) and sputtered polycrystalline Ge detectors form an optical global bus from banks to I/O, MAGNIFYING bandwidth per wire ~20x.
note: On-die mm-scale links rarely favor optics over wires.

title: Retrofit idle web presses into printed-memory lines
idea: Minify fab capex to ~$20M per line by converting idle US newspaper and packaging web presses into memory lines, adding laminar-flow tunnels around the web path and inline photonic/laser stations.

title: YBCO superconducting interposer lines at 77 K
idea: MINIFY line loss to near zero: pattern YBCO superconducting traces on a sapphire interposer, cool the package with liquid nitrogen, and let memory sit centimeters away with lossless, low-swing transmission.
note: Cryocooler wall-power overhead and driver-dominated link energy erase most of the gain.

title: Minify replacement unit: swappable foil-memory cartridges with wear telemetry
idea: Make oxide-TFT memory roll-to-roll on polyimide or steel foil and package it as cheap hot-swap cartridges. Each reports ECC-correction and retention telemetry and is swapped like an ink cartridge when it crosses a threshold, so cells only need a 2-3 year life.
note: Oxide-TFT foil memory unlikely to meet DRAM-class latency.

title: Eliminate per-column sense amps: charge-coupled shift readout to edge amplifier
idea: Under each row of storage nodes, run a buried-channel CCD register. On read, all cell charges of the row dump into the CCD and are clocked sideways (4-phase, ~1 GHz) to one floating-diffusion amplifier per 1,024 columns, which digitizes them in series. Restore uses reverse clocking.

title: Eliminate CMOS sense latches: resonant-tunneling-diode Goto pairs
idea: Two series resonant tunneling diodes (SiGe/Si or InGaAs, grown on the bonded periphery die) form a MOBILE/Goto-pair bistable whose midpoint ties to the bitline. When the shared clocked bias rises, the pair snaps in ~10 ps to the state set by the bitline imbalance, and the same NDR logic can do column muxing.

title: Eliminate the voltage-mode latch: selective-epitaxy bipolar pre-amp in bitline contact
idea: Form a vertical n-p-n inside each bitline contact by in-situ-doped selective epitaxy (DCS/HCl with PH3/B2H6, avoiding BF2 implants), with the bitline driving the base. The charge-share signal becomes a collector current (beta ~50) into one shared current comparator per 16 bitlines, and a shared write driver restores the cells.
note: Base current drains the femtocoulomb charge-share signal.

title: Eliminate the landing pad: oxide capacitor grown self-aligned on channel
idea: Delete the storage-node contact and landing-pad litho layer; grow a conductive perovskite oxide (e.g. SrRuO3 or LaNiO3) by selective-area epitaxy only on the exposed top of each vertical channel, so the capacitor bottom electrode self-registers to the transistor with zero overlay margin.
note: Selective perovskite epitaxy on Si pillar tops needs buffers and high temperature.

title: Eliminate ingots and wire saws: kerfless seeded direct-solidified wafers
idea: Freeze 300 mm wafers directly from a silicon melt onto a cooled, seeded template that imposes single-crystal orientation, then high-temperature anneal to drive out dislocations; there is no ingot, no wire saw and no kerf.

title: Eliminate refresh and capacitors: complementary oxide-TFT static latch cell
idea: Build a cross-coupled latch from n-type Zn-Sn-O and p-type SnO thin-film transistors stacked in the BEOL; wide-gap off-current near 1e-19 A means the static cell draws almost nothing yet never needs refresh, and reads non-destructively at ~100 mV differential swing.
note: p-type oxide TFT quality poor; latch density far below 1T1C.

title: Memory cartridges: ship non-volatile modules instead of moving bytes
idea: Eliminate the network for bulk model distribution: package NV HBM-class stacks on hot-pluggable carriers written once at a central site and physically installed into inference servers, which execute directly from them as working memory.
note: Needs NV HBM-class memory that does not exist; network rollout not a key bottleneck.

title: Spin-wave buses carry data between MRAM banks without charge
idea: Eliminate charge-carrying wires between NV banks: CoFeB or YIG magnonic waveguides move data as spin-wave phase from one bank's MTJ transducers to others, with interference-based fan-out to many banks at once.

title: Eliminate the quartz crucible: cold-crucible levitation silicon growth
idea: Eliminate the Spruce Pine high-purity-quartz crucible: grow large-diameter ingots in water-cooled segmented copper cold crucibles where induction fields push the melt off the wall so silicon touches only its own frozen skull.

title: Empty the channel: nano-vacuum field-emission access device
idea: Remove the semiconductor from the switch: the storage node faces a sharpened emitter tip across a sealed ~5-10 nm vacuum gap, and the wordline acts as an extraction gate. With the gate low there are no carriers in the gap, so leakage is only direct tunneling through vacuum; with the gate high, Fowler-Nordheim field emission conducts uA currents in picoseconds.

title: Cross-fab sequential build: U.S. logic fab first, memory fab last
idea: Reverse the wafer-flow order: a U.S. logic fab builds periphery FEOL and a Mo-based interconnect, then ships wafers to a U.S. memory fab that grows the array above at <=450 C with laser-recrystallized Si access devices and MIM capacitors, giving monolithic CMOS-under-array across two U.S. companies without bonding.
note: Low-temperature recrystallized Si access devices are unlikely to reach DRAM-grade leakage.

title: Sense amps on the wafer backside via U.S. backside flow
idea: Rearrange the faces: using a U.S.-developed backside-processing flow (the kind built for backside power), the array occupies the front, the wafer is thinned, and SAs and wordline drivers are built on the back, joined to bitline groups by nano-TSVs.

title: Dry fab: skip non-critical cleans, let particles become correctable bits
idea: Rearrange where cleanliness is enforced: delete ~half of post-CMP/post-etch wet cleans on non-critical layers and accept the resulting particle-induced cell defects, held below 1% BER and corrected on-die.
note: Particles cause row/column shorts, not isolated bit errors.

title: Skull-melt crystal growth: silicon is its own crucible
idea: Reverse the container: use cold-crucible induction melting where a water-cooled segmented copper cage keeps a frozen silicon skull that holds the melt, so no high-purity quartz crucible is needed for Czochralski pulling.

title: Laminate a hundred ultrathin glass memory sheets into a 3D block
idea: TRIZ #7 Nesting: instead of growing 26+ tiers monolithically, build one memory tier per 25-50 um flexible-glass sheet roll-to-roll, test every sheet, then nest 50-100 known-good sheets in a laminated stack with edge-plated wordline/bitline risers and a periphery chiplet at the edge.
note: Display-scale TFT litho gives far lower density than DRAM; edge risers limit array pitch.

title: Graphene liner lets copper fill the buried wordline
idea: TRIZ #2 Taking out: grow a 1-2 layer graphene diffusion barrier in the wordline trench by low-temperature plasma CVD, then fill with Cu. A ~0.4 nm barrier replaces ~3 nm of TiN, and Cu, the lowest-resistivity abundant metal, replaces W.
note: Gate work function and Cu diffusion under thermal budget are open.

title: Periodic in-situ microheater anneal heals VRT traps
idea: TRIZ #19 Periodic action: TiN heater strips beside each mat run a few-millisecond 300-400 C local anneal during maintenance windows, with data evacuated to neighbor mats, detrapping the oxide/interface defects behind variable retention time and hammer susceptibility.
note: 300-400 C local anneal risks hydrogen loss and neighbor damage; similar to Macronix self-healing flash.

title: Preliminary anti-action: cold-crucible levitation Czochralski removes quartz crucible dependency
idea: TRIZ #9 Preliminary anti-action: pre-empt the Spruce Pine chokepoint by growing DRAM-grade silicon in water-cooled segmented copper cold crucibles with induction-levitated melt (skull melting), so the melt never touches high-purity quartz.

title: Termite-mound stack-effect cleanroom air handling
idea: Termite mounds ventilate passively with a tall chimney, thermal mass and porous walls. Build the fab with a process-heat chimney that drives make-up and return air by buoyancy, earth-tube preconditioning and phase-change thermal mass, so fans only top up the flow through the ULPA ceiling.
note: Buoyancy gives a few Pa vs >100 Pa ULPA drop and huge recirculation rates.

title: Electrolyte 'blood' power delivery replacing HBM power TSVs
idea: A redox-flow electrolyte circulates through microchannels in each DRAM tier, and on-die flow-cell electrodes convert it to the local supply voltage, so the same fluid cools and powers the die as blood carries both oxygen and heat. The power and ground TSVs, the majority of vias in an HBM stack, are removed.

title: Telomerase anneal: on-die microheaters periodically reset leakage traps
idea: Embed polysilicon micro-heaters under each mat; in maintenance windows the mat's data is moved out and the mat is flash-annealed (~300 C for ~10 ms) to re-passivate the hydrogen-related interface traps and GIDL defects that create variable-retention and hammer-damaged cells, resetting the 'telomere' of the array.

title: Cubic-zirconia skull melting: crucible-free silicon with fewer oxygen-related leakage traps
idea: Synthetic-gem makers melt zirconia inside a crust of its own frozen material in a water-cooled copper 'cold crucible'. Grow DRAM-grade silicon by cold-crucible induction Czochralski, eliminating the Spruce Pine high-purity quartz crucible and its oxygen supply, and engineer gettering with nitrogen/carbon co-doping instead of oxygen precipitates.

title: CCD bucket-brigade shifts row charge to one edge sense node
idea: Like a CCD image sensor, each mat's bitlines become buried-channel charge-transfer registers: an activated row dumps its packets into the channel, and clock phases march them to one high-gain floating-diffusion amplifier at the mat edge, read serially and restored through a write-back register. One sense chain serves 16 columns.
note: 1970s CCD memories precedent; transfer efficiency and serial latency.

title: Core-memory coincident selection with threshold-switch row drivers
idea: Revive magnetic core memory's coincident-current trick: each local wordline driver is gated by a two-terminal ovonic threshold switch fed by one X and one Y predecode line, each at half threshold. Only the row where both are active fires its driver, replacing NAND decode trees.
note: OTS endurance and drift at wordline toggle rates are doubtful.

title: Xerographic dry printing of periphery power and global routing
idea: Xerography means 'dry writing': image the periphery's relaxed-pitch (>=300 nm) global/power metal pattern onto a charged photoconductive transfer drum, pick up copper-nanoparticle 'toner' electrostatically, transfer it to the wafer and laser-sinter in forming gas. No resist, plating bath, CMP or post-CMP clean.

title: Model T periphery: sense amps from the array transistor only
idea: Ford's Model T came in one colour to cut production steps. Design every pitch-matched periphery circuit (SAs, sub-wordline drivers, column switches) from the buried-channel array transistor plus one thick-oxide variant, using bootstrapped gates and NMOS-only latches with capacitive pull-up instead of a separate HKMG CMOS periphery module.
note: NMOS-only bootstrapped periphery from slow array transistor; water claim is the twist.

title: Float-glass analog: silicon ribbon floated on molten metal
idea: Borrowed from Pilkington's float-glass process: pull a thin single-crystal silicon ribbon horizontally from a seed across a denser molten Sn-based bath under a barrier skin, producing 300 mm-wide wafer-thick sheet with no quartz crucible and no wire sawing, then grow a device-grade epi layer on top.

title: Cubic-zirconia skull melting: silicon grown inside its own frozen crust
idea: Borrowed from cubic-zirconia growth, where an RF-heated melt freezes against water-cooled copper fingers into its own container skin: apply cold-crucible induction melting to silicon crystal pulling, so a silicon skull holds the melt and no fused-quartz crucible is used.

title: Spin-echo storage revived: electron-spin ensembles as phase-coded bit trains
idea: In 1955 Anderson and Fernbach proposed computer memories that store data in spin precession phases and recall them with a refocusing pulse. Couple ensembles of donor electron spins in isotopically pure 28Si:P to on-chip microwave resonators so each resonator holds a train of thousands of time-multiplexed, phase-encoded bits recalled as echoes.

title: Crucible-free float-zone wafers: long carrier lifetime, no quartz crucibles
idea: Revive float-zone crystal growth, sidelined for CMOS by Czochralski: grow nitrogen-doped 200-300 mm FZ silicon in U.S. plants, so storage-node junctions sit in oxygen-free, long-lifetime silicon where generation leakage (proportional to 1/lifetime) is lower. No high-purity quartz crucible is consumed.
note: 300 mm FZ unavailable and lacks oxygen gettering; DRAM tail is process defects, not bulk lifetime.

title: Xerographic amorphous-selenium photoconductor as optically gated access switch
idea: Revive xerography's amorphous-selenium photoreceptor (dark resistivity ~1e14-1e15 ohm-cm) and the vidicon target: each cell's access element is a tiny a-Se photoconductor between bitline and capacitor, gated by light from silicon-nitride waveguide wordlines. Selenium is refined in Utah and the waveguides come from U.S. photonics foundries.

title: Smart-pixel free-space optical page readout to processor
idea: Revive 1990s smart-pixel optical interconnect. Each sense-amp group drives a micro-LED or electro-absorption modulator on the memory die's backside, and a microlens array images the whole open page onto a photodetector array on the stacked processor, moving thousands of bits in parallel with no TSVs or serializers.
note: Stacked dies get far cheaper bandwidth from hybrid bonds.

title: Parametron phase bits held by pumped NEMS beams in stacked cavities
idea: Revive Goto's parametron: each cell is a nanomechanical beam parametrically pumped at 2f by a tier-wide electrostatic line, ringing at f with phase 0 or pi and holding that bit as long as the pump runs. Tiers of vacuum-sealed beams stack in BEOL, and reads use phase-sensitive capacitive pickup on the bitline.

title: Thin-film transfluxor cells that compute while reading, ferrite-only materials
idea: Revive RCA's 1956 transfluxor: sputter NiZn-ferrite rings with one large and one small aperture in BEOL. The stored blocked/unblocked flux state of the outer leg decides whether a drive on the small aperture induces an output, giving non-destructive read plus AND/inhibit logic in the same element, so rows can be filtered before any data leaves the array.
note: Nanoscale ferrite rings lose bistable flux and inductive output; density uncompetitive.

title: CRT rejuvenator revival: on-die microheaters anneal away retention traps
idea: 1950s TV-tube rejuvenators briefly overdrove the cathode heater to restore emission. Polysilicon microheaters under each bank let the controller move a bank's data out and pulse it to ~350 C for milliseconds against hydrogen-bearing passivation, re-passivating interface traps and dissolving the metal-related defects that create leaky tail cells, at power-up or in scheduled maintenance.
note: Local 350 C pulses risk neighbors and metallization; dissolving metal defects is doubtful.

title: Core-stack strobe tuning revived: per-mat sense trims absorb CMP-free topography
idea: Core-memory stacks were tuned individually at the factory, with sense-strobe delay and threshold set per stack. At wafer test each DRAM mat is characterized and given its own sense-reference offset, sense-enable delay and wordline boost in a trim table, so a wafer planarized by dry etch-back and spin-on glass instead of CMP (leaving 15-20 nm topography and wider cell variation) still reads with full margin.
note: CMP-free topography breaks litho focus and contacts, not just sense margin.

title: Dynamic row-well back-biasing replaces the 3 V wordline pump
idea: Inverting 'the access transistor needs a 3 V wordline': each row's access transistors sit in an isolated well that is driven with the wordline, strongly reverse-biased when off and forward-biased when selected, so a 1.2 V wordline swing gives the same on-current and off-leakage.

title: Spin-to-charge sign readout instead of measuring resistance
idea: Inverting 'magnetic bits are read by their resistance magnitude': a small supply current through each nanomagnet into a heavy-metal/oxide interface produces an inverse Rashba-Edelstein voltage whose sign follows the magnetization, and that signed voltage directly drives the gate of a single sense transistor.

title: Photovoltaic wordline drivers fed by waveguide light
idea: Inverting 'wordlines are driven by metal and charge pumps': a BEOL waveguide carries light to series photodiode stacks at each floating-body row segment, generating the gate voltage locally when a row's micro-ring is tuned on, so no high-voltage wordline drivers or pumps exist.

title: Panel DRAM: memory arrays built on Gen-6 display glass
idea: Inverts 'memory is built on round single-crystal wafers': use idle LCD/OLED panel lines (1.5x1.8 m glass) with seed-directed excimer-laser-crystallized large-grain silicon access devices and stacked MIM capacitors to build a slower bulk-capacity tier, with small CMOS periphery dies bonded at the panel edge.

title: MgB2 persistent-current loops cooled without helium
idea: Inverts 'superconducting memory needs liquid helium': store bits as persistent currents in MgB2 loops (Tc 39 K; magnesium and boron are abundant) switched by kinetic-inductance gates, cooled to ~20 K by neon- or hydrogen-cycle cryocoolers instead of helium.

title: Crucible-free silicon via cold-crucible induction Czochralski
idea: Inverts 'silicon crystals grow from quartz crucibles'. Melt Si in a segmented water-cooled copper crucible where electromagnetic pressure and a solid Si skull keep the melt off the walls, and pull 300 mm crystals with no high-purity quartz.

title: Fab federation chains depreciated 200 mm fabs into one line
idea: Inverts 'a DRAM line must be one site'. Assign each step block (front end, capacitor, BEOL, test) to one of a dozen fully depreciated U.S. 150/200 mm fabs, move wafers in sealed nitrogen-purged pods on scheduled trucks, and run one shared MES and yield database across them.
note: 150/200 mm tools cannot reach modern DRAM pitches.

title: Half-billion-dollar DRAM line from scavenged 200 mm tools
idea: Inverts 'a memory fab costs $15B'. A consortium buys decommissioned steppers, LPCVD furnaces, RIE and CMP tools at ~3-10% of new price, refurbishes them for a single tier-stacked DRAM flow needing only >=180 nm litho, and replicates the line as identical $0.5B modules.
note: 180 nm cells are ~150x larger; needs implausible tier counts to compete on cost/bit.

title: Post-fab Vt healing of tail access transistors via trap-layer programming
idea: Random dopant and trap fluctuations put a few transistors per billion 4-5 sigma low in Vt, and their subthreshold current dominates the tail. Add a thin SiN charge-trap layer in the buried-wordline liner. At wafer test, find the short-retention cells and inject electrons into only their gate stacks (high wordline voltage, their bitline driven, neighbors inhibited) to raise their Vt ~200 mV.
note: Same test-time trap programming of tail cells; selective injection in buried-WL liner is harder.

title: Nano-vacuum-channel field-emission wordline drivers
idea: Electrons crossing a ~50 nm vacuum gap by field emission have no oxide to break down, no BTI, and no junction leakage; such switches tolerate far beyond 125 C. Use them as high-voltage wordline/plate switches fabricated in BEOL cavities.

title: Solid-state 193 nm light sources remove neon and fluorine
idea: First principle: excimer gas is only a gain medium; 193 nm light can also come from frequency conversion of a ~1 um fiber laser through nonlinear crystals (harmonics plus sum-frequency mixing in CLBO/KBBF). Build a kW-class fiber-laser-pumped solid-state 193 nm source for immersion scanners with no neon/fluorine consumables, no gas-refill downtime and higher wall-plug efficiency.

title: Snow globe: electrophoretic nanoparticle position stores the bit
idea: Random stimulus 'snow globe' forced onto memory: a 5 nm charged oxide nanoparticle is sealed in a 30 nm liquid-filled nanocavity between two plates; a +/-1 V write drives it to the top or bottom by electrophoresis, and a coplanar sense electrode reads its position as a capacitance shift. The bit is where a particle sits, not how much charge remains, so junction leakage cannot erase it.
note: Electrophoretic variant; liquid sealing and transit time unproven.

title: Mousetrap: strain-cocked ferroelastic twin variant holds the bit
idea: Stimulus 'cocked mousetrap' (stored elastic energy, two positions) -> a 20 nm ferroelastic perovskite pillar (e.g., LaCoO3-type) holds one of two twin orientations; a piezoelectric collar applies a ~1 ns shear pulse to flip the twin, and the variants' anisotropic resistivity (~2x) is read nondestructively along the pillar.
note: Same strain-switched ferroelastic twin storage.

title: Pop-up toaster: telescoping nested nanotube held extended or retracted
idea: Stimulus 'pop-up toaster' -> a double-walled carbon nanotube whose inner tube slides out of the outer one; an electrostatic pull extends it to touch a contact pad (bit 1), and the van der Waals retraction force plus a reverse pulse pulls it back (bit 0). Read is contact current; the shell-in-shell sliding is superlubric, so there is no bending fatigue.

title: Jacquard loom: coincident half-select tier addressing, no 3D staircase
idea: A Jacquard loom lifts any thread pattern by crossing hooks and cords. In 3D DRAM, replace the per-tier staircase contacts with a tier-select plate per level and a gate line per vertical pillar, each driven to about half the turn-on voltage, so only the tier-by-pillar intersection conducts, as in coincident-current core memory.
note: With a subthreshold slope, half-selected cells leak; core memory relied on a sharp threshold.

title: Honeycomb: three line families at 120 degrees with active back-gate shields
idea: Forced connection to a honeycomb: put vertical-channel cells on a hex lattice with three line families at 0, 60 and 120 degrees: wordlines, bitlines, and a third family of back-gate 'shield lines'. When a wordline fires, the shield lines that cross its neighbors pulse negative to hold their channels hard off, and hex packing gives about 15% more capacitor footprint than a square grid.

title: Hearing-aid retrofit: compressing buffer chips reflowed onto existing RDIMMs
idea: Retrofit rather than replace: swap the data-buffer/RCD chips on installed DDR5 RDIMMs (rework <260 C) for pin-compatible buffers that compress lines inline and advertise larger capacity through SPD, so existing DIMMs grow ~1.5x without new DRAM dies.
note: Only LRDIMMs have data buffers; fixed advertised capacity vs variable compressibility is unsafe.

title: Beehive geometry: staggered wordlines so no victim has one dominant aggressor
idea: Cells sit on a hexagonal lattice where each storage node's three nearest wordlines are distinct and roughly equidistant, so hammering any single row delivers about a third of today's coupling and a double-sided attack needs three coordinated rows.

title: Nano-DMD torsion latch: Texas micromirror physics shrunk to memory bits
idea: Box = {medium: landed-left or landed-right state of a 100 nm torsion-hinge paddle | access: row/column electrostatic half-select | sense: capacitive tilt sensing | integration: MEMS over CMOS as in DLP | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: the Dallas DLP flow (Al hinges, SAM anti-stiction, spring tips)}. A small hold bias keeps the paddle latched on its landing tip; DLP mirrors already pass 1e12 landings with stiction controlled, and shrinking ~50x raises the resonance to GHz for ns switching.

title: Frequency-multiplexed resonator readout of 64 bitlines per receiver
idea: Box: trench cap x cryo-CMOS access x frequency-division readout x interposer-integrated resonators x sapphire-on-Si x high-Tc superconducting film. At 77 K each bitline ends in a high-Q LC resonator at a unique frequency whose varactor is detuned by the shared cell charge; one broadband LNA plus FFT reads 64 bitlines at once, like kinetic-inductance detector arrays.

title: Boron-arsenide interlayers let HBM stacks grow to 24 dies
idea: Box: HBM die x standard x standard x hybrid bond with 2 um cubic BAs or CVD-diamond interlayers plus thermal vias x Si x low-temperature deposition. Ultra-high-conductivity interlayers spread heat sideways to dedicated thermal through-vias so 24-high stacks stay under 85 C.
note: Low-temperature BAs films do not exist; poly-diamond k low and incompatible with hybrid bonding.

title: Po: memory spins — MEMS magnetic micro-carousel with fixed head arrays
idea: Po: memory spins. Extracted: a mm-scale MEMS rotor coated with perpendicular magnetic media spins at ~100k rpm under 1,000 stationary on-chip MTJ read/write heads, so each head serves one narrow track and the average wait is ~0.3 ms.

title: Self-healing tail cells via localized Joule anneal of junction traps
idea: Po: the leakiest cell sets the refresh, so the leakiest cell must heal itself. On-die BIST finds the worst-retention cells and drives a controlled forward current through their storage-node junction, self-heating it to ~400 C for microseconds so hydrogen/deuterium from a reservoir liner re-passivates the trap that causes the tail.

title: Po wafers have no back: double-sided arrays on one wafer
idea: Po: 'the wafer has no back side.' Extracted: double-side-polish 200 mm wafers, build transistors and capacitors on the front, flip and build a second array on the back with a low-temperature capacitor module last, and connect the faces at die edges for power and I/O.

title: Post-hammer neighbor de-trap pulse cancels injected charge
idea: Po: hammering heals the victim. After each aggressor precharge, the row decoder drives both adjacent wordlines ~0.3 V below the normal negative standby level for ~2 ns, sweeping carriers trapped or injected near the victim storage-node junction back to the substrate before they neutralize stored charge.

title: Unsupported ultra-tall pillars: let 1% lean and short
idea: Po: let the capacitors fall over. Capacitor pillars are etched to AR ~115:1 without nitride support-mesh layers; the ~1% that lean, bridge or collapse become stuck cells mapped as erasures.

title: Laminated van der Waals capacitor stacks instead of deep etching
idea: Worsen: get capacitance only by etching 75:1 holes. Flip: build area by laminating 20-50 alternating graphene/hBN sheets into an interdigitated parallel-plate stack contacted on staircased edges, so capacitance scales with layer count rather than etch depth.

title: Folded U-cell stacks transistor over capacitor inside one tier
idea: Worse: lay the access transistor and capacitor end to end so lateral 3D cells run ~2x longer than the bitline pitch needs. Flip: build each tier as two sublayers where the channel runs out from the bitline in the upper sublayer, turns down through a self-aligned via at the far end, and the capacitor runs back underneath toward the bitline.
note: Self-aligned turn-down via inside each lateral tier is hard; net ~1.4x density per etch depth.

title: MgB2 flux-loop memory banks linked to processors by fiber
idea: Worsen: store bits as charge that leaks at room temperature. Flip: store bits as a persistent single-flux-quantum current in MgB2 superconducting loops at ~20 K, cooled by closed-cycle cryocoolers rather than liquid helium, and link them to room-temperature processors over fiber with cryogenic photodetectors driving the inputs.

title: Oxygen-implanted buried-oxide pockets stop storage-node junction leakage
idea: Worse: sit the storage-node junction on bulk silicon, where defects and depletion volume generate leakage current. Flip: implant oxygen locally under each storage-node contact (SIMOX-like, Si and O only) and anneal it into thin buried-oxide pockets that shrink junction area and remove the bulk generation path.
note: Oxygen implant damage and high-temp anneal at DRAM pitch are serious doubts.

title: Kintsugi artist: in-field electro-thermal anneal heals variable-retention cells
idea: Kintsugi repairs the crack instead of discarding the bowl. When the scrubber finds a variable-retention cell, the controller fires a burst of high-current pulses through that cell's access device to Joule-heat the junction to ~400 C for microseconds, releasing hydrogen from an adjacent hydrogen-rich SiN liner that repassivates the trap.

title: Farmer's alternating furrows: half-pitch-staggered tiers share vertical bitlines
idea: Farmers offset alternate furrows. In a horizontal-cell 3D DRAM, shift every odd tier by half a cell pitch so each vertical bitline pillar zippers between cells on its left and right as it climbs, serving two columns.

title: Card dealer slides boron-nitride sheets to store bits
idea: Persona: a card dealer sliding one card over another. In AB/BA-stacked bilayer hexagonal boron nitride, shifting one atomic sheet by one bond length flips the out-of-plane polarization (sliding ferroelectricity). Grow wafer-scale aligned bilayers by CVD on Cu(111) and use them as a FeFET gate or tunnel barrier.
note: Sliding ferroelectricity is real but tiny polarization and wafer-scale aligned bilayers are unsolved.

title: 2050 engineer's self-healing: wordline Joule-heat anneals retention-tail traps
idea: A 2050 engineer treats defects as maintainable: in scheduled maintenance windows (data first migrated to a sister subarray), drive a controlled current through a subarray's tungsten/silicide wordline segments to Joule-heat it to ~300 C for microseconds, re-passivating the hydrogen-related interface traps that cause variable-retention-time and GIDL tail cells.

title: Pastry chef's lamination: stack only known-good roll-to-roll memory foils
idea: Croissant dough is folded layer upon layer: 3D memory is built by laminating individually tested roll-to-roll memory foils (each a thin tier of printed or nanoimprinted cells), rejecting bad foil segments before lamination and joining tiers with laser-drilled, ink-filled vias, so stack yield no longer compounds as p^N.

title: Switchboard operator: roll-to-roll antifuse crossbar foil reroutes dead bumps
idea: A telephone operator patches calls around a dead line: a thin roll-to-roll-made interposer foil carrying a crossbar of printed antifuses sits between the memory stack's base die and the package; after assembly test, the controller fires antifuses to route signals from failed microbumps or TSV channels to spares.

title: Few-electron storage read by single-electron transistor for smart dust
idea: Millimeter smart-dust nodes cannot afford 30,000-electron capacitors, so a 5-10 nm Si island stores ~50-200 electrons and an adjacent room-temperature single-electron transistor converts each added electron into a large current swing. The storage element shrinks to aF-scale capacitance with no pillar.

title: Resonant LC tank recovers bitline swing energy adiabatically
idea: Pacemakers count every picojoule: bitline restore is driven by a sinusoidal resonant supply from an on-interposer inductor network, so bitlines charge adiabatically and return their energy to the tank at precharge instead of dumping it to ground.

title: Nano vacuum-channel transistors as radiation-proof wordline boost drivers
idea: Nuclear and EMP environments favor vacuum electronics; field-emission vacuum-channel transistors with ~50 nm gaps defined by oxide etch-back rather than lithography switch 3-5 V wordlines with no gate-oxide stress and full immunity to heat and radiation.

title: Defense low-volume rule: one template for every tier, decoded vertically
idea: Defense users need many small memory variants and each imprint template is precious; make every tier identical, printed with one template, and select tiers not with a staircase but with a chain of tier-select transistors in each vertical bitline pillar, driven by a decoder in the bonded logic die. Products differ only in tier count.
note: Per-tier select gates still need individual drive lines, so staircase problem reappears.

title: Cold-crucible induction Czochralski growth eliminates high-purity quartz crucibles
idea: Edge case borrowed from microgravity float-zone growth, where the melt touches nothing. Melt silicon in a segmented water-cooled copper crucible with induction heating so a frozen silicon skull contains the melt, and pull 300 mm ingots without Spruce Pine quartz.

title: HBM-thinned dies host storage capacitors on the wafer backside
idea: Extreme user: HBM stacks whose dies are already thinned to ~30 um. Build access transistors and periphery on the front, then after thinning form the capacitor array on the backside, contacted by nano-vias through ~500 nm of silicon, decoupling the capacitor thermal budget from logic-grade periphery.

title: Quantum-computer SFQ pulse links to a 4 K memory
idea: Quantum computers already run single-flux-quantum logic at 4 K to drive qubits. Build the memory interface and periphery in energy-efficient SFQ, where a bit is one flux quantum (~1e-19 J), paired with a cryogenic DRAM array whose leakage is essentially zero.

title: Altermagnet RuO2 or MnTe bits with picosecond dynamics
idea: Jump to the picosecond timescale: altermagnets have zero net moment like antiferromagnets yet spin-split bands, so the Neel-vector bit is written by spin-orbit torque in ps and read by tunneling magnetoresistance, with no stray-field crosstalk.
note: Altermagnet TMR and SOT switching barely demonstrated.

title: Light-gated access: optical wordlines and dark-off photoconductive switches
idea: Scale jump from fibre optics to the cell: replace the electrically gated access transistor with a wide-bandgap photoconductive bridge (e.g., SiC or diamond-like carbon film) addressed by on-chip waveguide wordlines; in the dark the bridge is an insulator with no thermal carriers across ~3 eV, and a ~100 ps blue/UV pulse along the waveguide row makes it conduct for read or write.

title: Airgap between buried wordlines kills passing-gate leakage
idea: Scale shift from BEOL low-k airgaps down to the buried-wordline level: after wordline recess, ash out a sacrificial carbon liner between adjacent wordline trenches to leave sealed airgaps (k=1), so an active neighbour wordline no longer capacitively lifts the access channel or injects carriers into adjacent storage nodes.
note: Between adjacent wordline trenches is active silicon, not dielectric; coupling path misidentified.

title: Silicon nanocrystal electron-sink layer between wordlines stops hammer migration
idea: Scale jump (single migrating electron -> system security): row hammer is partly driven by electrons injected from the aggressor's passing gate that diffuse to the victim storage node. Embed a deep-trap Si/Ge nanocrystal layer in the inter-wordline isolation to capture and recombine them before they arrive.

title: Area-selective molecular monolayer passivates gate-edge GIDL sites
idea: No EUV: on DUV-defined buried-wordline recesses, a self-assembled monolayer deposited only on exposed Si/oxide edges (area-selective ALD inhibitor chemistry) passivates the gate-edge trap sites that cause the GIDL leakage tail. Molecular-scale chemistry stands in for nanometer patterning.
note: Monolayer unlikely to survive later thermal budget; GIDL is largely field-driven tunneling.

title: Half-inch Minimal Fab lines making legacy DDR3/DDR4 for industrial buyers
idea: Scale jump down from 300 mm wafers to 12.5 mm wafers: desktop tools that each carry their own local clean environment make 40-50 nm-class DRAM for industrial, automotive and defense parts that are being end-of-lifed, with no cleanroom building at all.

title: DX centers rescued: deep-defect bistability in Si-doped AlN
idea: Persistent-photoconductivity DX-center memories in AlGaAs died because the capture barrier (~0.2-0.3 eV) held states only below ~100 K. In AlN:Si or beta-Ga2O3:Si some calculations put the DX configurational barrier near 1 eV, so an ensemble of ~1000 DX centers in a gate layer could be toggled between shallow-donor and negatively charged DX states by hot-electron injection, shifting a transistor threshold that holds at 125 C.
note: Same DX-center bistability storage.

title: Mercury relays shrunk: sealed Galinstan nanodroplet electrocapillary bit
idea: Mercury-wetted relays and mercury delay lines died from toxicity and size. Seal a ~50 nm gallium-alloy droplet in a two-well SiO2 nanochannel and shift it between wells with an electrocapillary pulse, bridging or opening a read electrode pair; liquid metal neither wears nor fatigues and stays liquid and stable from -19 C to above 1000 C.
note: Ga oxide skin and nanoscale wetting hinder 10-100 ns droplet motion.

title: RCA Selectron flood-gun holding rebuilt as optically held printed cells
idea: RCA's Selectron used a continuous flood electron beam to hold every bit (secondary emission made two potentials stable), but the tubes could not be manufactured. Print each cell as a storage node with two organic photoconductors that the node's own voltage gates, giving positive feedback. A uniform low-power LED flood then continuously restores both 1s and 0s, with no row cycling and no sense amps.

title: Rambus royalty lesson: open, interchangeable core-die standard for repairable stacks
idea: Rambus's royalty model and HMC's closed spec both slowed adoption. Define an open, royalty-free mechanical and electrical standard for the DRAM core dies inside a stack, so any vendor's die can replace a failed one. US government and hyperscaler buyers then require serviceable stacks built to this standard.
note: Bonded stacks cannot be repaired by die swap; repairability premise is weak.

title: MRAM minus platinum and cobalt: tau-MnAl junctions with voltage writes
idea: MRAM lost the DRAM-replacement race (toggle MRAM density, STT write current) and its stacks lean on Pt, Ir, Ru, Co and Ta. Build perpendicular junctions from L10 tau-MnAl (high anisotropy, low damping) free and fixed layers around an MgO barrier, written by voltage-controlled-anisotropy pulses instead of current.
note: L10 MnAl films need high anneal; VCMA coefficients too weak for reliable writes today.

title: T-RAM, fixed: replica-tracked thyristor bias for on-die KV window
idea: T-RAM Semiconductor died because thyristor holding current shifts strongly with temperature, ruining margins. Add a per-bank replica thyristor and closed-loop bias generator that tracks temperature and process in real time, and use the dense capacitorless array as an on-die 'hot KV window' for the most recent few thousand tokens.
note: Replica tracks temperature but not cell-to-cell variation and disturb that also killed T-RAM.

title: Z-RAM revived as a bonded cache tile, sense amps in logic below
idea: Innovative Silicon's capacitorless floating-body Z-RAM died because it required SOI logic wafers and its sense margin collapsed under logic-process variation, so AMD dropped it. Build the floating-body array alone on its own SOI chiplet, with no compromise to the CPU process, and hybrid-bond it over a logic die that holds low-offset, auto-zeroed sense amplifiers and refresh logic for every 64 kb tile at 1-2 um bond pitch.

title: CNT vias failed on growth heat; transfer-grow iron-catalyzed CNT TSVs instead
idea: Carbon-nanotube vias (Fujitsu, imec) never reached production because good CNTs need ~700 C growth, incompatible with BEOL, and tip contact resistance was high. Grow dense vertical CNT forests from an Fe/Al2O3 catalyst (no Co) on a sacrificial carrier, transfer them into etched TSV holes with polymer fill, then Cu-plate the exposed tips, so the via is carbon in the barrel and Cu only at the contacts.
note: Transfer-grown CNT bundles; contact resistance and densification remain unsolved.

title: Wavelength-addressed photoconductive switches replace electrical row decoders
idea: Effect: photoconductivity. Run a BEOL SiN waveguide past each sub-wordline driver group, where a ring filter tuned to one of ~64 WDM wavelengths feeds a Ge or a-Si photoconductor that gates the driver; the controller picks a row block by injecting that wavelength, so address decoding happens in the waveguide instead of in CMOS decoder trees.

title: Million-tip field-emitter array writes periphery maskless in proximity mode
idea: Effect: Fowler-Nordheim tunneling. A wafer-scale array of gated Si or CNT tips, each with its own CMOS driver, flies 2-5 um above the resist; each tip writes only its own 50 um patch, so no electron column is needed, and sub-1 kV electrons keep proximity blur low. A digital data path replaces the periphery mask set.

title: Electromagnetic cold-crucible Czochralski eliminates Spruce Pine quartz crucibles
idea: Effect: Lorentz-force melt levitation (cold-crucible induction). Grow 300 mm Si boules from a segmented water-cooled copper crucible in which high-frequency eddy currents hold the melt off the walls, while a cusp magnetic field damps convection. Oxygen for gettering comes from a small consumable silica rod instead of a full crucible.

title: Magnonic interference hashes KV keys to merge near-duplicate tokens
idea: Key vectors are injected as microwave phases into a YIG spin-wave interferometer whose fixed geometry implements a random projection. Output-port intensities give locality-sensitive hash bits in nanoseconds. Tokens that land in the same bucket are merged into one averaged KV entry with a count, so redundant context collapses.
note: Microwave conversion overhead dwarfs aJ spin-wave cost; KV merging works without magnonics.

title: Resonant-tunneling diodes decompress memory lines inline at line rate
idea: Put a multi-valued logic block of InGaAs/AlAs resonant-tunneling diodes (negative differential resistance, 100+ GHz) on the memory channel. Every 64-byte line can then be stored compressed (base-delta or entropy-coded) and expanded within one memory clock. With no latency penalty, the OS has no reason to keep any data uncompressed.
note: Decompression latency is algorithmic, not gate-speed bound; RTD integration unproven.

title: Skyrmion reservoir replaces recurrent weights with magnetic dynamics
idea: Input currents excite a Ta/CoFeB/MgO skyrmion fabric whose nonlinear, fading-memory dynamics act as the state transition of a sequence model. A few MTJs read out the state, so only a small linear readout is stored, not large recurrent or state-space matrices.
note: Skyrmion reservoir computing already in lab literature; niche streaming models.

title: Adiabatic reversible logic makes recomputing activations cheaper than storing
idea: Run on-device adaptation with reversible network layers (RevNet-style) on charge-recovery adiabatic logic. Activations are recomputed backward from outputs at ~10x less switching energy, so they are never stored. Adiabatic switching also cuts self-heating, keeping junctions inside budget at 125 C ambient.
note: Reversible nets already avoid activation storage; adiabatic logic energy gains rarely realized.

title: Spin Hall oscillators: frequency-multiplexed carriers put eight channels per interposer wire
idea: Pt/NiFe spin-Hall nano-oscillators, each <1 um^2 and current-tunable from 5-25 GHz, act as tiny carriers; eight differently tuned oscillators share one interposer line and spin-diode detectors demultiplex them at the memory die.
note: nW oscillator output and phase noise make multi-Gb/s carriers doubtful.

title: Ballistic transport: printed aligned-nanotube repeaters make long flex memory links
idea: Shear-align printed semiconducting carbon-nanotube films on R2R flex to form short-channel transistor repeaters every few mm along memory interconnect, enabling GHz signaling over 10 cm of flex without silicon.

title: Field-steered hydrogen re-passivates traps causing variable retention
idea: Effect: field- and heat-driven ion migration. For a mid-life self-heal, data is evacuated from a mat, built-in heater lines (wordlines driven in a heater mode) raise it to ~200 C for seconds, and a gate bias drifts mobile hydrogen from a SiN:H reservoir back to depassivated Si/SiO2 dangling bonds and GIDL-site traps that create variable-retention cells.
note: Wordline heater mode plus field-driven hydrogen drift; same in-field anneal core.

title: Spin-Hall SOT-MRAM parity layer sits atop the array in BEOL
idea: Effect: spin Hall effect (spin-orbit torque switching). A SOT-MRAM layer built in the BEOL above the cell array holds per-row ECC parity and error-history logs; spin-Hall writes avoid tunnel-barrier stress (high endurance), and parity reads proceed in parallel with the DRAM read.
note: SOT-MRAM cells far larger than DRAM cells; parity layer will not fit over array.

title: Na: sodium-ion glass integrator counts each row's activations
idea: Attach to each row driver a tiny Na+-conducting glass cell encapsulated in SiN; every ACT pulse pushes a fixed quantum of Na+ across it, raising its conductance, and when a comparator crosses threshold the controller refreshes the neighbors and resets the cell with a reverse pulse.

title: MgB2 superconducting flux-loop memory at 20 K, helium-free
idea: Periodic-table walk, Mg (12): build persistent-current flux-quantum cells with MgB2 (Tc 39 K) junctions and kinetic inductors, operated at 20 K by cryocooler or liquid H2 instead of liquid He, as a zero-static-power working memory in cryogenic AI pods.

title: Mg: MgB2 superconducting wiring links 20 K cryogenic memory pods
idea: Run DRAM pods at ~20 K (cryocooler or liquid hydrogen) and wire them to compute with MgB2 superconducting traces (Tc 39 K, made from abundant Mg and B) on flex/interposer, so long lines are lossless and drivers swing millivolts; at 20 K access-transistor leakage collapses and refresh nearly stops.

title: Ca: CaF2 crystalline gate insulator removes RTN traps from access devices
idea: Grow lattice-matched crystalline CaF2 on (111)-faceted recess sidewalls as the access-transistor gate insulator; a crystalline fluoride has far fewer border traps than amorphous SiO2/HfO2, eliminating the single-trap telegraph switching behind variable retention time.

title: Glow-pigment trap bit: persistent-phosphor traps read by stimulated light
idea: Borrow glow-in-the-dark SrAl2O4:Eu,Dy pigment manufacturing. A co-packaged photonic die writes a bit by trapping electrons at Dy traps in phosphor nanodots on plasmonic antennas, and reads it by optically stimulated luminescence into an on-die SPAD. Co-dopant chemistry sets the trap depth and thus the retention.
note: Same trapped-electron stimulated-luminescence store; on-chip optics limit density and speed.

title: Over-center toggle-clamp NEMS relay isolates a junctionless MIM node
idea: The access device is a nano-relay with over-center (toggle-clamp) geometry: it latches open with no hold voltage and leaves a true air gap between bitline and a metal storage capacitor that has no pn junction.

title: Felted random-network decoder, mapped after manufacture
idea: Like felt made by matting random fibers instead of weaving, spray a sparse random network of nanowire switches between a few predecode lines and the wordline ends. Post-fab test discovers which address code reaches which wordline and stores the map in a small table, so no lithographically defined decoder is needed at wordline pitch.

title: Transformer lamination stack with ferrite flux core through dies
idea: Treat thinned dies as transformer laminations: plug a ferrite flux-core post through the stack and wind thick-metal spiral coils on each 65 nm die around it. The core channels magnetic flux so all 16 tiers couple inductively without TSVs.
note: Ferrite post still needs a hole through dies; high-frequency ferrite loss.

title: Dovetail jigsaw chiplets that self-lock edge to edge
idea: Deep-etch puzzle-tab edges on memory and logic chiplets so they interlock side by side to sub-micron accuracy, like dovetail joinery, then plate the sidewalls to form edge-to-edge links. The tiles act as a mosaic with no interposer.

title: Printed vacuum nanogap access device with near-zero leakage
idea: IFR: the ideal insulator is nothing at all. Closest achievable: R2R-print electrodes and open ~10 nm nanogaps by controlled film cracking or sacrificial-layer removal, forming field-emission vacuum switches that conduct only above emission voltage, so a printed capacitor keeps its charge for hours.
note: Same vacuum field-emission access idea, printed variant.

title: Electrophoretic nanoparticle bit shuttling across a printed nanocell
idea: IFR: e-paper bistability at DRAM speed. Closest achievable: confine one charged nanoparticle in a printed ~10 nm fluid cell; a field pulse drives it to either electrode (transit ~10 ns at 10 nm), van der Waals force holds it there, and the bit reads as a capacitance shift.

title: Single-transistor-type periphery built from the array's own vertical channels
idea: Ideal result: periphery that costs zero extra masks. Design sense amps, drivers and decoders entirely from the array's vertical-channel access transistor, with a few gate lengths set by etch depth, dropping the separate high-k metal-gate planar CMOS flow for core periphery.

title: Laser-release bond layers let one bad tier be swapped
idea: Ideal result: a 3D memory whose layers come apart like building blocks. Insert a thin UV-absorbing release layer in each cell-on-periphery tier bond, so laser lift-off separates a failing tier and a known-good tier is re-bonded onto the same periphery.
note: A release layer conflicts with direct dielectric hybrid bonding.

title: IEA-style allied memory-sharing treaty with crisis allocation
idea: Ideal: no country is ever short of memory. Closest achievable: the U.S., Japan, Korea, Taiwan and the EU commit to share a set % of output and reserves on a declared shortage, with coordinated reserve draws and export priority rules.

title: Self-trimming DRAM design multi-sourced across trailing fabs
idea: Ideal: memory that any fab can make. Closest achievable with no new fab: one design with on-die calibration (sense-amp offset trim, adaptive wordline boost, retention-profiled refresh) and wide margins runs from the same GDS at 3-4 mature DRAM and specialty fabs, like 1980s second-sourcing.

title: Coaxial dual-node pillar stores two bits in one capacitor footprint
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): pitch and interface stay, so get more bits per pillar. Build each pillar as three concentric shells (an inner storage electrode, a shared grounded middle plate with dielectric on both faces, and an outer annular storage electrode), each storage electrode tied to its own vertical access transistor, so one footprint holds two independent ~4 fF bits.
note: Three electrodes plus two dielectrics will not fit in sub-40 nm holes.

title: Only 10 nm may change: wide-gap Si:C pocket against GIDL
idea: Limit: the channel stays silicon, and only the 10 nm under the gate-drain overlap may be altered. Selectively grow a carbon-alloyed Si1-yCy or 3C-SiC pocket at the storage-side drain edge. Its wider local bandgap exponentially suppresses band-to-band GIDL tunneling where the negative wordline meets the high storage node.
note: Si:C barely widens gap; 3C-SiC pocket at 10 nm adds heterointerface traps.

title: Zero-leakage idle sensing: pre-biased NEMS cantilever latch
idea: Limit: idle sense amps must leak exactly zero. Each SA is a nano-electromechanical relay biased within ~30 mV of pull-in, so the bitline differential tips the beam toward the BL or BLB electrode; once in contact it latches mechanically, then releases on reset.
note: Biasing within 30 mV of pull-in is unstable under process variation; 1e15 contact cycles unproven.

title: Skull-melt Czochralski: quartz-free silicon in a cold copper crucible
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero quartz crucibles. Melt silicon in a water-cooled, segmented copper crucible where the induction field both heats and pushes the melt off the wall, so a frozen silicon 'skull' is the only contact surface; pull 300 mm ingots from that pool and use nitrogen co-doping to replace the wafer-strengthening role of crucible-derived oxygen.
note: Dislocation-free 300 mm pulls from turbulent cold-crucible melt unproven; energy much higher.

title: Procurement cap on DRAM per inference, with printed-media credits
idea: Constraint (printable/roll-to-roll): federal AI procurement sets a maximum number of DRAM bytes per served token or session and grants credits for verified printed or roll-to-roll media that hold frozen data (weights, shared prefixes, golden pages), creating guaranteed demand for domestic printed offload products.
note: Printed media able to hold weights does not exist; caps may simply raise cost.

title: Socketed DRAM chiplets on a reusable multi-generation interposer
idea: Rule: memory dies must be replaceable without discarding logic. DRAM chiplets attach to an active interposer through anisotropic conductive film or micro-spring contacts instead of permanent bonds, so failed chiplets are swapped and the interposer and accelerator are reused across 2-3 memory generations.

title: Deuterium-passivated cells with depot re-deuteration window
idea: Rule: the retention tail must be restorable at refurbishment. Interfaces are passivated with deuterium instead of hydrogen, using the stronger Si-D bond for slower trap generation. The package includes a gas-permeable window so depots can re-deuterate aged dies in a long, low-temperature D2 soak (~200 C).

title: Each new fab under $1B: replicated fab-in-a-box pods
idea: Self-imposed limit: a capex cap of $1B. Standardize a 5k-wafer-start-per-month DRAM cleanroom pod with a fixed tool set, prefabricated utilities and a copy-exact recipe, then replicate pods side by side as demand grows.

title: Swap charge for molecular spin state in spin-crossover nanocrystals
idea: Store the bit as the low-spin or high-spin state of Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover nanocrystals, which are bistable inside a thermal hysteresis loop centred on the die's operating temperature. A field or current pulse switches the state, and the read senses the ~10^2 change in conductance or permittivity.

title: Swap charge for metastable charge-density-wave hidden state in 1T-TaS2
idea: A ~30 ps electrical pulse of ~fJ switches a nanoscale 1T-TaS2 cell from its insulating commensurate CDW into a metastable metallic hidden state, and a longer pulse resets it. The bit is the electronic order, read as a ~100x resistance ratio.
note: Cryo-only hidden state.

title: Insert NbO2 threshold switch to make access turn-on abrupt
idea: Substitute the plain access FET with a hyper-FET: a 10 nm NbO2 layer in series with the bitline-side source. NbO2's insulator-metal transition is at ~800 C, so it is stable at 85 C operation, and the layer snaps on abruptly once current flows, giving an effective sub-60 mV/dec turn-on. That lets the FET's Vt rise ~200 mV at the same wordline swing.
note: NbO2 off-state leakage far above fA; Hyper-FET is known art.

title: Nanoelectromechanical relay decoders with zero off-state leakage
idea: Substitute CMOS decoder and wordline-isolation transistors with electrostatically actuated TiN or poly-Si NEM relays (sacrificial oxide release, e-beam gaps ~50 nm). Relays have truly zero off-current and abrupt switching.
note: Relay endurance far below decoder switching counts.

title: Catalyst-grown vertical nanowire transistors replace etched 4F² pillars
idea: Substitute etched Si pillars for vertical 4F² access transistors with bottom-up nanowires: Sn or Al catalyst dots placed by block-copolymer templating grow single-crystal Si nanowires (SiH4, Au-free) from bitline seeds, with in-situ B2H6/PH3 switching n+/p/n+ along the growth axis to form source/channel/drain without implants.
note: VLS nanowire placement and uniformity at DRAM pitch remain unsolved.

title: Spin-crossover molecular dielectric with room-temperature hysteresis
idea: Combine iron(II)-triazole spin-crossover complexes, which switch between low-spin and high-spin states with ~10% volume and permittivity change and show 20-40 K wide hysteresis around room temperature, with a capacitor read: a local heating or field pulse flips the molecular layer, and capacitance reports the state. The bistable spin state holds without power.

title: Coolant that is also the power supply: in-stack redox microchannels
idea: Combine interlayer microfluidic cooling with a redox flow battery: a vanadium or organic electrolyte pumped through microchannels between HBM dies passes porous electrodes on each die, generating ~1 V locally while carrying away heat, so most power TSVs and bumps are replaced by fluid.
note: IBM 'electronic blood' prior art; redox power density likely too low.

title: Charge-density-wave domain switching in 1T-TaS2 picosecond bit
idea: MAGNIFY speed and MINIFY energy: a 10-nm 1T-TaS2 film is switched by a ~30 ps electrical pulse into a metastable hidden charge-density-wave domain state (~1000x resistance change) and erased by a longer pulse; run in a ~200 K module where the metastable state lasts seconds to hours, giving refresh-light dynamic memory.
note: Hidden-state TaS2 memory already pursued; retention needs cryogenic operation.

title: Magnify abruptness: NbO2 threshold switch in series (Hyper-FET)
idea: Insert a 10 nm NbO2 Mott threshold-switching layer between access transistor and storage node: below ~0.4 V it is insulating, cutting off-current 100-1000x, and when the wordline drives the cell above threshold it snaps metallic within ns. Its hysteresis window is tuned so stored '1' levels sit in the insulating regime.

title: Driven guard traces hide bitline coupling capacitance
idea: Borrow electrometer active guarding: MAGNIFY the role of shield lines between bitlines by driving each with a unity-gain follower of its neighbor bitline during charge sharing, so bitline-to-neighbor capacitance (~40% of Cbl) sees no voltage change and draws no charge.

title: Silicon-carbide DRAM: refresh-free at 125 C, grown without quartz
idea: Magnify bandgap ~3x: build 1T1C cells in 4H-SiC, whose junction leakage at 125 C is ~10^10 below silicon's, on boules grown by sublimation in graphite crucibles, so no high-purity quartz crucible is needed.
note: SiC DRAM cells shown decades ago; poor MOS interface and wafer cost.

title: CVD diamond heat spreaders keep hot-ambient DRAM twenty degrees cooler
idea: Magnify thermal conductivity ~5x over copper: bond a polycrystalline CVD diamond lid (grown from methane and hydrogen) to the memory die, so a 125 C ambient gives a ~105 C junction.
note: A passive spreader cannot hold junction below ambient; 125 C ambient to 105 C junction claim is unphysical.

title: Page-wide 100,000-nozzle printhead deposits only where needed
idea: Magnify nozzle count to a page-wide MEMS printhead array firing sub-femtoliter drops across the full web, depositing dielectric and electrode only where cells exist instead of blanket coating plus etch.

title: Gallium liquid-metal microbumps in micro-wells
idea: MINIFY the melting point to ~30 C: microbumps are galinstan-filled wells capped by a dielectric frame, so a die lifts off with gentle heat and reseats with the wells reformed.

title: Infrared optical vertical links through bondless stacks
idea: MINIFY metal in the vertical path to zero: 1.3 um infrared emitters and photodiodes send light straight through the silicon dies (silicon is transparent there), so stacked dies need no TSVs and can be separated.

title: Eliminate the VPP charge pump with a shared bootstrap boost plate
idea: Run a common boost plate under all wordlines of a sub-array. The decoder drives the selected wordline to VDD (1.1 V) and floats it, while all unselected wordlines stay actively clamped low. A 1.1 V step on the boost plate then couples only the floating wordline up to ~2.8 V for the restore window, as in a bootstrapped driver.

title: Eliminate transistor leakage: bistable SiC nano-relay memory cells
idea: Each cell is a ~100 nm electrostatically actuated SiC or TiN beam that snaps between two buckled stable states and closes a contact for a zero-leakage read; switching costs aJ of mechanical energy plus wiring.
note: Same bistable buckled-beam mechanism as I-06198, with contact readout.

title: Strain-held Mott latch: VO2 parked inside its hysteresis window
idea: Reverse the bias logic: a static strain from a piezoelectric underlayer holds a W-doped VO2 nanobar at the middle of its metal-insulator hysteresis, and ns current or voltage pulses flip it metallic or insulating; the electronic phase, not stored charge, holds the bit and reads as ~100x resistance contrast.

title: Leakage becomes the latch: tunnel-diode Goto pair on storage node
idea: Reverse leakage from enemy to keeper: stack two nanoscale Esaki (interband tunnel) diodes in series between VDD and ground with the storage node at their midpoint. Their negative differential resistance creates two stable node voltages held by valley-current tunneling, so the node never drifts and the access transistor is only used to read and write.

title: CCD bitline marches charge packets to one edge charge amplifier
idea: Move the charge to the sensor instead of the sensor to the charge: the bitline becomes a buried CCD channel with 3-phase clock gates, cells dump their charge into it, and packets are shifted (image-sensor style) to one low-noise floating-diffusion charge amplifier at the array edge, then shifted back for restore.

title: Lower-purity specialty gases, defects absorbed downstream
idea: Reverse the spec flow: qualify 5N instead of 6N-7N grades of NF3, silane, WF6 and ammonia from a wider supplier base, and let the trace-contaminant cell defects sit inside the 1% BER budget.
note: Trace contaminants hit yield broadly, not just tolerable cell bit errors.

title: VO2 hysteresis latch held bistable by the chip's own waste heat
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise + #36 Phase transition: dope VO2 (W/Ge) so its 5-10 K insulator-metal hysteresis loop sits at the stack's operating temperature, so each nano-VO2 cell stays insulating or metallic indefinitely while warm. Write '1' with a ns Joule pulse, reset with a piezo-strain gate pulse that shifts the loop, and read resistance non-destructively.

title: Pre-implanted cleave plane lets storage substrates be reclaimed repeatedly
idea: TRIZ #10 Prior action: build the storage array in a thin single-crystal layer transferred by hydrogen-implant ion cut onto a handle wafer that carries a second pre-implanted weak plane; at end of life or after test failure, the handle is split there, re-polished and reused 5-10 times.

title: Dynamics: sense amps switch to two-bit multilevel mode when cool
idea: TRIZ #15 Dynamics: each sense amp adds a second time-staggered latch and a mid-reference so a mat can run either 1-bit robust mode or 2-bit-per-cell multilevel mode; the controller enables multilevel on mats whose thermal sensor and retention telemetry show margin (cool, cold data) and migrates data out when temperature rises.

title: Thin films: porous-silicon release layer enables 10x substrate reuse
idea: TRIZ #30 Flexible shells/thin films: one added mask defines anodization windows that form a buried porous-Si cleave plane; after array processing the thin device layer is bonded to a cheap carrier and lifted off, and the CZ wafer is re-polished and reused ~10 times.

title: Statolith shuttle: nanoparticle moves between two ends of a sealed cavity
idea: Plant-root statoliths are dense starch grains that settle inside cells to record orientation. Seal a 10 nm conductive nanoparticle (Ru or a carbon onion) in a 30 nm vacuum nanocavity with an electrode at each end. An electrostatic pulse moves it to one end, where van der Waals adhesion holds it, and the bit is read by capacitance or tunnel current at that end.
note: Bucky-shuttle memory precedent; nanocavity fabrication and stiction reliability uncertain.

title: Proton-relay croconic acid: fluorine-free printed ferroelectric charge booster
idea: Enzymes and bacteriorhodopsin move charge along hydrogen-bonded proton wires. Croconic acid crystals switch polarization by the same proton tautomerism (~20 uC/cm2, no fluorine); inkjet-print them as the cell capacitor and run them in a volatile minor-loop mode that adds displacement charge without full switching, to protect endurance.
note: Same croconic-acid printed ferroelectric as I-08950.
