idea: Ideal result: periphery that resets its own wear. Polysilicon microheaters under SA stripes and drivers heat local transistors to ~250 C for seconds during maintenance windows, recovering BTI and hot-carrier threshold shifts.

title: Off-die replaceable voltage-generation chiplet powers memory periphery
idea: Ideal result: the memory die holds no pumps or regulators that wear out. Move VPP, VBB and VARY generation to a socketed power chiplet on the module that feeds dies through dedicated rails; failing or outdated regulators are swapped, and the chiplet is reused on new modules.

title: Ceria-free shallow-trench planarization by selective dry etch-back
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero rare-earth ceria slurry and no CMP water. Fill isolation trenches with flowable oxide, then planarize with a self-limiting, nitride-stopping remote-plasma etch-back under optical endpoint control instead of ceria-slurry CMP.

title: Titanium-silicide strapped dual-work-function polysilicon wordline
idea: Combine the old poly gate with a self-aligned silicide strap (zero added masks): fill the buried-wordline trench with in-situ doped poly, recess it, then sputter Ti and anneal so TiSi2 forms only on exposed poly, leaving lower n+ poly near the channel and the strap for conduction.

title: PFAS-free DNQ-novolac resist revival for periphery layers
idea: Revive 1980s diazonaphthoquinone-novolac i-line resists, which contain no fluorinated photoacid generators, for every periphery and non-critical layer (about half the die), paired with second-hand i-line steppers.

title: Vacuum-linked cluster runs the whole capacitor module airlessly
idea: Combine the cluster-tool concept with the full capacitor module (mold deposition, HAR etch, dry mold removal, electrode ALD, high-k ALD, top plate) on one vacuum transfer backbone. Wafers never see air, wet cleans or FOUP queues inside the module.

title: Eliminate the ballroom cleanroom: wafers live inside a vacuum backbone
idea: Connect every process tool to a linear vacuum or nitrogen wafer highway so wafers never meet fab air from start to finish; the building becomes an ISO-8 warehouse without raised floors or giant make-up air handlers.

title: Eliminate the arms-length buyer: OEM cooperative co-owns a DRAM fab
idea: Eliminate the pure-buyer role: automotive, industrial and PC OEMs form a cooperative, like farm co-ops or airline fuel consortia, that owns a mid-size legacy-node DRAM fab and allocates output at cost by equity share.

title: Resurrected-scanner fab: build on the industry's retired DUV tools
idea: Reverse the tool lifecycle: buy retired KrF/ArF dry scanners and older etchers on the secondary market, refurbish them, and pair them with a design rule set made only for spacer multiplication and self-alignment.

title: Vacuum-railway fab with no ballroom cleanroom
idea: Inverts 'a fab is a giant cleanroom building'. Link cluster tools with sealed sub-mTorr maglev tube conveyors so wafers never touch air from bare wafer to passivation; the building becomes an ordinary industrial shed with local maintenance enclosures.

title: Cartridge-based fab tools refurbished across node transitions
idea: Worsen: scrap or export whole fab tool sets at every node transition. Flip: build process tools as standard frames with swappable process cartridges and open control interfaces, so older DRAM fabs refurbish chambers for new chemistries (gain cells, 3D) instead of buying new tools.

title: 2050 engineer's cleanroom-less fab: wafers travel only in sealed tubes
idea: A 2050 engineer finds it odd that we filter a stadium of air to protect a 300 mm disc. Link conventional tools with a sealed pod-in-tube network held at vacuum or ultra-dry N2, with load-lock interfaces on every tool, so wafers never meet room air from start to finish and the building becomes a plain ISO-8 warehouse.

title: Wake-shield-inspired all-vacuum DRAM line with no cleanroom
idea: Extreme user: orbital fabs that get free ultra-high vacuum behind a wake shield. Recreate that on Earth by linking deposition, etch, anneal and (already-vacuum) EUV/e-beam tools through a continuous maglev vacuum wafer tunnel so wafers never touch air; the building drops to a gray corridor and native-oxide cleans vanish.

title: Multi-beam e-beam direct-write line accepting slow, maskless cycles
idea: Time-for-capital trade at the tool scale: 250k-beam Schottky-emitter writers in ultra-high vacuum pattern the critical DRAM layers with no masks and no laser gas. Slower throughput is accepted through more writers working longer cycles.
note: MAPPER-style multibeam throughput was the failure mode; only niche secure volumes.

title: LaB6 multi-beam maskless writer prints only the access-gate cut layer
idea: La: deploy a massively parallel e-beam writer (LaB6 source split into ~10^5 beamlets) dedicated to the single cut/contact layer that isolates access transistors and lands storage contacts, while every other layer uses DUV pitch multiplication; no mask set and no EUV scanner are needed.
note: Multibeam cut-layer writers known (MAPPER, Multibeam); building one far exceeds $1M.

title: Convert depreciated planar-NAND lines into DRAM lines
idea: Ideal: an idle fab that already prints 15 nm lines. Closest achievable with no new fab: old planar NAND lines (15-20 nm SAQP on ArFi) left idle by the 3D NAND shift add capacitor-module tools and run 1x-nm DDR4/LPDDR4, because litho, CMP and cleans already match.
note: Planar NAND lines largely already converted.

title: No Si wafer: relocate retired Gen 6 display toolsets stateside
idea: Forced limit: no Si and no new tools. Buy complete Gen 6 backplane tool sets (PECVD, sputter, panel steppers) from retiring Japanese, Korean and Taiwanese LCD fabs and reinstall them in a U.S. brownfield to make oxide-TFT memory panels.
note: Relocation variant of LCD-fab IGZO panels in I-04100.

title: COCOM-embargoed engineer patterns DRAM without EUV using block copolymers
idea: Persona: an Eastern Bloc engineer denied Western lithography, who turns to chemistry. DUV immersion defines guide stripes. PS-b-PMMA, or high-chi PS-b-PDMS, block copolymers then self-assemble into 24 nm-pitch lines and holes that correct and multiply those stripes. This replaces the 5-7 EUV layers of a 1-beta-class DRAM with ArF plus directed self-assembly.

title: Substitute battery ride-through rules with NV-state credits for telecom sites
idea: Policy: let cell sites and critical infrastructure meet backup mandates (e.g., multi-hour battery rules) with fewer battery hours if their compute uses certified non-volatile working memory that resumes state instantly.
note: Logic weak: sites still need power during outages; NV memory does not replace ride-through energy.

title: Wavelength-addressed wordline decoding with silicon microring filters
idea: Broadcast the row address as a WDM optical comb on a waveguide running over each bank; each sub-wordline driver group has a microring tuned to one wavelength plus a photodiode that fires its driver. The predecoder tree and its long, repeated global wires disappear, because a photonic add-drop filter now does the row decoder's job.
note: Microring tuning power per ring outweighs the decoder savings.

title: Radio-frequency tone addressing selects wordline groups via resonators
idea: MINIFY decoder wiring to a single line: the row address is broadcast as a sum of on-die RF tones, and each wordline-driver group has a tuned LC or MEMS resonator filter bank that fires only when its tone combination is present.

title: Sushi-conveyor optical delay-line ring for hot broadcast data
idea: Copy the kaiten-sushi conveyor. A closed, low-loss SiN waveguide loop on the interposer keeps tiny, very hot structures (MoE routing tables, norms, sync flags) circulating as WDM pulse trains. Each compute chiplet 'picks a plate' with a thermally tuned microring drop filter as the block goes by, and an on-loop re-timer re-injects the train every lap.
note: Kilobit loop capacity; self-admitted 5-10% gain.

title: Core-rope weaving: per-die e-beam via layer hardwires repairs
idea: Apollo's core-rope ROM was woven by hand, each wire passing through or around each core. After wafer sort at the via-2 level, a maskless multi-beam e-beam writes one custom via layer per die that hardwires spare rows and columns into place. That layer is the one added 'mask', and no physical mask exists.

title: Goto-pair tunnel-diode CAM as hardware hash-cons index
idea: Revive the 1960s Goto pair, two series tunnel diodes that latch a bit with no transistor, as the storage element of a CAM cell: Esaki diodes made by degenerate spin-on doping in a university fab form a dense CAM that holds content hashes and answers 'is this block already stored?' in one cycle for inline memory dedup.
note: Tunnel-diode latches draw static current and are not dense; the index fits in SRAM/DRAM anyway.

title: Million slow TFT compressors on glass for cold pages
idea: Compressing cold pages is bound by throughput, not latency, so slow transistors suffice if there are enough of them. Tile a glass panel with ~1 million LTPS-TFT LZ/rANS engines at ~1-5 MHz each (aggregate >1e12 symbol operations/s), fed through optical I/O, which compress cold pages in the background and write them back to DRAM compacted.
note: Offloads only zswap CPU cost; feeding a million slow engines over optical I/O impractical.

title: Tree-ring radial tiers: concentric shells in one wide hole
idea: Rotate the stacking axis from vertical to radial: deposit 10 concentric semiconductor/dielectric/conductor shells in a 400-nm hole, each ring the channel and storage node of its own cell. A conical chamfer etched at the hole top exposes each ring for contact, like tree rings on a slanted cut.

title: Optical clock trees failed on alignment; a light shaft through the stack
idea: Free-space optical clock distribution (1980s-2000s research) failed because external optics could not stay aligned to chips. Etch one 20-50 um oxide-lined vertical hole through every die of a memory stack so it acts as a light pipe, put an n-ZnO/p-NiO UV LED in the base die at its bottom, and let a ring photodiode on each die's shaft wall tap the pulse, broadcasting clock and command strobes to all tiers with sub-ps skew.
note: ZnO/NiO UV LED weak; clock TSVs are a tiny share of the tax.

title: Quantum anomalous Hall edge chirality as a dissipationless cryogenic bit
idea: Effect walk: quantum anomalous Hall effect. In a MnBi2Te4 or Cr-doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 micro-Hall cell at 2-10 K, magnetization sets which way the dissipationless edge channel circulates; read senses the Hall-voltage sign at sub-mV, and write uses the topological insulator's own giant spin-orbit torque.
note: Cryogenic niche; very low temperature QAH and write mechanism immature.

title: Pyroelectric film images row heat to steer page tiering
idea: Deposit a thin LiTaO3 pyroelectric layer over each DRAM bank, patterned into per-subarray pixels. Activation bursts heat their rows by millikelvins; each pixel emits charge proportional to dT/dt, and a tiny integrator turns that into a hotness map. The OS keeps only the hottest 20-30% of pages in DRAM and pushes cold pages to compressed CXL or flash, with no SRAM access counters or page-table sampling.
note: Thermal diffusion blurs per-subarray signal; access tracking is already cheap (CXL hotness monitors).

title: AlN resonator spectra read hundreds of ROM bits per wire
idea: Encode tokenizer, embedding and activation lookup tables as the mass-loading of AlN bulk-acoustic resonators, each tuned to a distinct frequency. One RF sweep on a shared line reads hundreds of resonators at once from their spectral peaks, so no row decoders are needed. A reference resonator cancels the ~-25 ppm/C temperature drift, and frozen mass-loads do not change at 125 C.
note: Spectral multiplexing limited by resonator Q and area; niche.

title: Frequency-addressed wordlines replace row decoders with tuned resonators
idea: Ideal result: no decoder at all; the address is broadcast and the right row answers. Each sub-wordline driver gets a tiny BEOL LC or bulk-acoustic resonator tuned to one of 64 frequencies; a global line carries a tone burst and only the matching resonator's rectifier fires its driver, with a 2-level predecode covering 64x64 rows.

title: Two-terminal ovonic threshold switches replace bitline equalize transistors
idea: Substitute the three-transistor precharge/equalize block with sputtered GeSe-class ovonic threshold switches between bitline pairs and the precharge rail, fired by a short overdrive pulse.
note: OTS holding voltage prevents precise equalization; threshold drift.

title: LCD array-tester voltage imaging replaces on-die test periphery
idea: Borrowed from the LCD fab's electro-optic array tester, a modulator plate that images every pixel's voltage without contact: after the array layer on glass is built, a pattern is written and all cell voltages are imaged to find dead or weak-retention cells before periphery and stacking.

title: Eliminate vias in decoder routing: capacitively coupled dynamic signal layers
idea: Decoder and predecoder signals are pulses, so let them cross metal levels through overlap capacitors with 5 nm ALD Al2O3 between the layers instead of vias, with a keeper on each node restoring DC level. Only power rails use vias, placed in a few relaxed landing zones etched with BCl3/Cl2, and the wiring is subtractive Cl-etched Mo.

title: Purity in the code, not the crystal: solar-grade DRAM wafers
idea: Reverse where reliability lives: build DRAM on solar-grade silicon grown in ordinary quartz crucibles, accept that ~1% of cells have contamination-shortened retention, and protect each 4 KB page with an on-die LDPC code (~12% parity) that corrects a 1% raw BER.

title: Skip the deuterium anneal; let ECC cover the trap tail
idea: Reverse the final passivation step: omit the high-pressure deuterium/H2 interface anneal, accept the ~1% of access transistors with extra trap-assisted leakage, and correct them with ECC.
note: Skipping hydrogen passivation raises interface traps broadly, not just 1%; ECC cannot absorb the retention loss.

title: Honeycomb mat tiling sharing each sense-amp hub among three mats
idea: Bees' hexagonal comb shares every wall between neighbors. Mats are tiled hexagonally so each sense-amp hub sits where three mats meet and is time-multiplexed among their bitlines: one active, one as open-bitline reference, one idle. Conventional open bitline shares between only two.
note: Directional SAQP/EUV line patterning cannot run bitlines at 120 degrees.

title: Jet-engine MAX-phase ceramics as tungsten-free buried wordline conductor
idea: Aerospace uses MAX phases (Ti3SiC2, Ti2AlC), layered carbides that conduct like metals yet tolerate heat like ceramics. Deposit nanolaminate Ti2AlC/Ti3SiC2 by ALD supercycles plus a front-end crystallization anneal as buried-wordline and contact fill, exploiting their layered in-plane conduction to dodge the grain-boundary resistivity penalty that hurts tungsten below 10 nm width.

title: Gunn-domain delay line: travelling field domains as a shift register
idea: 1960s engineers proposed Gunn-effect domains as high-speed memories. Launch bits as high-field domains travelling ~1e5 m/s along a long n-GaN or GaAs channel, recirculate them through a regenerating trigger electrode, and tap them with capacitive pickups along the channel.
note: Micron bit spacing and high Gunn power dissipation make density and energy poor.

title: Eccles-Jordan flip-flop rebuilt from nanoscale vacuum-channel triodes
idea: Revive the 1918 vacuum-tube flip-flop at nanometer scale: cross-couple two field-emission vacuum-channel triodes (silicon tips, 50 nm sealed gaps, no gate dielectric) into a static latch. The vacuum gap has no dielectric leakage and no junctions, so the cell holds state without refresh and runs at 250 C.

title: Crowe persistent-current cells in YBCO at 77 K, no helium
idea: Revive the 1957 Crowe cell and Buck's cryotron, where a bit is a supercurrent circulating clockwise or counterclockwise in a superconducting loop, using YBCO films grown by reactive thermal co-evaporation (no argon sputtering, no KrF excimer) and cooled by liquid nitrogen made from air. A persistent current does not decay, so cells never refresh.

title: Halve ultrapure-water rinses in water-scarce fabs, absorbing residue faults
idea: Inverts 'every rinse must be exhaustive': cut UPW rinse time and volume by ~40% on non-gate steps, accepting residue-induced isolated cell faults within the 1% budget.

title: Acoustic delay-line FIFOs buffer pipeline-parallel activations
idea: Pipeline-stage activations and switch packet buffers are strictly first-in-first-out, so they do not need random-access cells. Store them as surface acoustic waves on lithium-niobate or quartz: at ~3.5 km/s a 2 cm line holds ~6 us, and 1,000 parallel 5 GHz channels in recirculating, re-amplified loops hold ~30 Mbit.

title: Banknote press: security-printing intaglio lines print memory module substrates
idea: Random stimulus 'banknote' -> mints already print with micron registration 24/7. National security printers (BEP and allied mints) retool idle intaglio/gravure capacity with conductive and dielectric inks to print DIMM, CXL-module and coarse package-substrate layers as surge capacity.

title: Analog syndrome bitlines compute parity by charge summation in-array
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x multi-level analog-sum sensing x dedicated parity bitline x bulk Si x standard. During activation, cells of a parity group also dump charge onto a shared parity bitline; a small multi-level comparator turns the summed charge into a count whose mod-2 is the syndrome, so only words with a nonzero syndrome go to the full decoder.
note: Multi-level charge-sum parity is fragile; at 1% BER many words have errors anyway.

title: On-site electrolytic hydrogen and nitrogen as the fab's only inerts
idea: Box [supply: PEM electrolyzers on reclaimed water + PSA N2 generators | uses: load-lock venting, carrier gas, PECVD dilution | leak test: 5% H2-in-N2 tracer with Pd-gate sniffers | storage: no rare-gas cylinders on site]: redesign the fab gas plant so N2 and H2 cover every inert role, and send the electrolytic O2 by-product to ozone generators.
note: Argon is hard to replace in PVD and plasma etch, so full rare-gas elimination is doubtful.

title: At-tool electrochemical synthesis of ALD precursors from bulk metal
idea: Worsen: rely on a handful of overseas suppliers for TEMAZ, TDMAT and other organometallic precursors shipped in hazardous cylinders. Flip: put a small electrochemical cell at each ALD tool that anodically dissolves Zr, Ti or Al metal into ligand solution, making precursor on demand at the purity the tool needs.

title: Cleaved mica substrates give atomic flatness without CMP
idea: Worse: add dozens of CMP steps and ceria slurry to flatten each layer. Flip: start on cleaved muscovite mica, atomically flat over cm2. Grow oxide-semiconductor and high-k films by van der Waals epitaxy, and keep later tiers flat by vdW-bonded transfer instead of polishing.

title: Fiber-loop weight carousel stores model weights as light in flight
idea: Worsen: park every weight in a leaky capacitor and drag it across a bus each token. Flip: inference reads all weights in the same order every token, so keep them circulating in a 64-wavelength fiber loop with in-line amplification and periodic electronic regeneration (a 100 km loop holds ~0.8 GB); accelerators tap each layer as it passes.
note: 100 km loop holds 0.8 GB; amps and regenerators cost far more than DRAM.

title: Beekeeper's honeycomb: hexagonal plasma-diced chiplets for more beachfront
idea: Bees tile with hexagons: plasma-dice compute and memory chiplets into hexagons so each compute die shares three or six full edges with memory dies in a honeycomb mesh, instead of a rectangle with only two usable sides.
note: Hexagons have less perimeter per area than squares; beachfront claim doubtful.

title: Potter's kiln: co-fired AlN ceramic memory brick with copper lines
idea: Fired ceramics last millennia: co-fire an aluminium nitride carrier with copper conductors (no tungsten) to form a 'memory brick' that holds 4-8 DRAM dies around a logic die, with a silicon-matched CTE (~4.5 ppm/K) and 170 W/mK conductivity.
note: AlN sinters far above copper's melting point; niche rugged market.

title: Kintsugi artist: liquid-metal microcapsules that heal cracked bonds
idea: Kintsugi fills cracks with gold: embed microcapsules of gallium-indium alloy, with a barrier shell, around microbump fields; when a fatigue crack forms, the capsules break and liquid metal wicks into the gap to restore conduction.

title: Farmer's rain barrel: printed supercapacitor film steadies array voltage
idea: A farmer stores rain for the dry spell: a roll-to-roll-printed thin-film supercapacitor (carbon electrodes with an ion-gel electrolyte, mF/cm2) is laminated under the DRAM package or on the HBM interposer backside, supplying the current spikes of refresh and activate bursts so VARY droop shrinks and the voltage guardband can be cut.

title: Solar-industry kerfless epitaxial wafers: no quartz crucible needed
idea: Solar makers grow wafers directly on porous-silicon templates and lift them off, with no crucible. Use kerfless epitaxial or UMG-seeded substrates with heavy gettering for DRAM array wafers, accepting ~10x shorter carrier lifetime and higher junction generation leakage as errors inside the 1% budget.
note: Shorter carrier lifetime directly raises junction generation leakage, which sets retention; substrate is a small cost share.

title: Micro-LED light selects mats through the silicon backside
idea: Scale jump from datacenter optics to on-die addressing: a micro-LED array on the package lid shines 1.3 um light through thinned silicon onto Ge photodiodes at each mat's driver enable, so mat selection arrives as light and the global decoders and address buses disappear.

title: Depreciated U.S. 200-mm fabs become array-tier foundries
idea: Use the decades-old installed base as capacity: about a dozen U.S. 200-mm fabs at 180-350 nm run array-only tier wafers in the sideways architecture, with no periphery, die-to-wafer bonded to periphery made elsewhere. Contracts are priced per tier, not per die.
note: 180-350 nm arrays are ~100x less dense; cost per bit uncompetitive.

title: S: CaS:Eu,Sm electron-trapping film read by on-chip light
idea: Coat each cell with ~50 nm of CaS:Eu,Sm electron-trapping phosphor; a blue micro-LED or electrical injection pushes electrons into Sm traps (write), and an infrared pulse releases them as Eu emission detected by an under-cell photodiode (destructive read, as in DRAM).
note: Optical write and read per cell is slow and large; not DRAM-class.

title: Zn: zinc-oxide thin-film varistors shrink I/O ESD clamps
idea: Replace bulky diode/SCR ESD clamps at each DQ and CA pad with a Bi/Mn-doped sol-gel ZnO varistor film in the pad stack, whose grain-boundary breakdown gives strongly nonlinear clamping and absorbs surge energy in volume, not die area.
note: Thin-film varistors clamp too high and leak; ESD area gain small.

title: F: fluoropolymer ferroelectric caps hold trimmed reference per mat
idea: Use P(VDF-TrFE) (C, H, F) ferroelectric capacitors as partially polarized analog memories that set each mat's open-bitline reference level; at test the reference is trimmed to that mat's measured signal midpoint and held without DACs or fuses.
note: A P(VDF-TrFE) thermal budget is incompatible with DRAM BEOL.

title: K: potassium-ion oxide electret supplies permanent negative wordline bias
idea: Drift K+ ions into a SiO2 plate under each mat's negative-wordline rail or back gate and lock them with a nitride cap, forming a stable electret (as in MEMS harvesters) that supplies a built-in -0.3 to -0.5 V bias with no VBB/VNWL charge pump.
note: Mobile K+ in oxide is a classic instability; a fixed charge cannot source rail current.

title: C: nanoporous carbon microsupercapacitors buffer activation current bursts
idea: Solution-cast nanoporous carbon electrodes with a gel electrolyte form a microsupercapacitor bank on the interposer or substrate under each DRAM stack, supplying the nC-scale ACT and refresh bursts so on-die decaps and VPP/VARY regulators can be ~3x smaller; processing is in air or N2, no argon sputter.

title: Zn: zinc-oxide acoustic resonator replaces the DLL clock
idea: Fabricate a ZnO film bulk acoustic resonator, with ZnO grown hydrothermally or by O2-only reactive sputtering rather than argon sputtering, on the periphery as a low-jitter GHz reference so the DQ path uses a small injection-locked oscillator instead of a large DLL.
note: A frequency reference does not do a DLL's phase-alignment job.

title: Na: sodium-silicate water glass bonds periphery dies onto arrays
idea: Bond periphery dies face-to-face onto array wafers with a nanometer-thin sodium silicate adhesive cured at ~200 C, with Cu pillars electroplated through it and SiN barriers locking the Na; no argon/N2 plasma activation or argon-sputtered seed is needed.

title: Self-healing microcapsule underfill for hybrid-bonded memory stacks
idea: Self-healing concrete and composites release a healing agent when cracks open; fill HBM/3D-stack gaps with underfill holding microcapsules of low-viscosity resin plus dispersed catalyst that rupture at TSV or micro-bump cracks during thermal cycling and re-bond them, using no rare-gas processing.
note: Hybrid bonds have no underfill gap; capsules too large for microbump gaps.

title: Inkjet nanoparticle repair of interposer and module opens
idea: Display makers repair TFT line opens by direct printing; after test, inkjet silver or copper nanoparticle ink to bridge open RDL/interposer lines or rewire to spare channels, cured by low-temperature chemical (halide) sintering or IR diodes, avoiding xenon flash lamps and argon-carrier laser-CVD repair.
note: Interposer lines are buried and finer than inkjet resolution.

title: Catalyst-regeneration detrap pulses during refresh idle
idea: Refineries burn coke off catalysts to restore activity; because rare-gas-free cell and gate dielectrics (no argon plasma densification) start with more traps, apply periodic negative-bias 'regeneration' pulses on idle wordlines to empty the filled traps behind VRT and gate-induced drain leakage.

title: Printed OECT ionic film stores on-device learned personalization
idea: Constraint (printable/roll-to-roll): printed organic electrochemical transistors (PEDOT:PSS channels) store adapter weights as ionic doping levels that gated training pulses adjust, so a wearable or phone keeps and updates its personal adapter in a laminated film rather than in DRAM or in per-user memory on a server.

title: Downhole-tool silicide: fully silicided titanium buried wordlines without tungsten
idea: 200 C downhole electronics favor refractory silicides that stay stable when hot. Fill the recessed gate trench with doped poly-Si and convert it fully to C54 TiSi2 (or NiSi) by RTA, with the TiN barrier doubling as work-function metal, all with university-fab sputter and RTA tools.

title: IBM X-ray proximity lithography revived for uniform access pillars
idea: Revive IBM's 1990s X-ray lithography program in Vermont with a U.S.-built compact inverse-Compton light source: ~1 nm X-rays expose access-transistor pillars with near-vertical, highly uniform sidewalls and negligible diffraction-driven CD variation, replacing EUV for the critical access layers.

title: Rutile-GeO2 ambipolar BEOL logic performs refresh locally per mat
idea: Ge: use rutile GeO2, an ultrawide-gap (~4.6 eV) oxide predicted to be both n- and p-dopable, to build complementary low-leakage transistors in the BEOL directly above each mat, hosting a tiny local refresh sequencer and restore driver so refresh never toggles global decoders, I/O or long data lines.
note: p-type GeO2 only predicted.

title: Light-driven wordlines turn the decoder into an optical pattern
idea: Ideal result: addressing at light speed with no decoder transistors. A photonic layer above the array carries waveguides with grating taps over each sub-wordline driver; a photoconductive switch fires the driver only when its waveguide-wavelength pair is lit, with decoding done by an off-array laser and arrayed-waveguide router.

title: Pulsed segmented cell plate borrowed from FeRAM boosts signal
idea: Split DRAM's common VDD/2 plate into row-wise segments and pulse the selected row's plate by +0.5 V during charge sharing (the FeRAM plate-line drive), so the stored node is coupled upward and the differential bitline signal grows; the plate returns to VDD/2 before restore.
note: Plate pulse couples both states equally (common-mode); 1-vs-0 differential is unchanged, so the 1.5-2x signal claim is doubtful.

title: Bipolar-input sense amps on bonded SiGe BiCMOS die
idea: Bond array wafers to 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS periphery wafers, where bipolar input pairs (Vbe matching ~1 mV versus ~10-20 mV for small MOSFETs) sense bitlines through an 8:1 column mux, reading groups in rapid sequence.

title: Endohedral ion shuttle in a nanotube, adapted from e-paper
idea: Like E Ink moving charged pigment between two faces, trap a K+@C60 ion-fullerene inside a 3 nm capped carbon-nanotube segment; a field pulse slides it to one end, and its position changes tunneling current through the tube wall to a read electrode.
note: Kwon-Tomanek bucky shuttle proposed 1999; fabrication never achieved.

title: Magnify the value of persistence: kill AI checkpoint memory overhead
idea: Sell non-volatile DRAM-class modules to AI training clusters as checkpoint-free memory: training state persists through power events in place, eliminating host-DRAM staging buffers and periodic checkpoint copies.
note: Depends on a DRAM-class NV memory that does not exist; Optane pitched the same.

title: Magnify heat briefly: in-field bank anneal heals leaky cells
idea: Put thin-film heaters under each bank. In a scheduled maintenance window the controller migrates the bank's data over CXL, heats the bank to ~200C for minutes to anneal hot-carrier/BTI damage and re-passivate interface traps behind leaky and VRT cells, then re-profiles it.

title: Eliminate periphery photomasks: maskless micromirror digital lithography for relaxed layers
idea: Expose the 20-30 relaxed periphery and implant-class layers with a digital-micromirror maskless writer (as used in advanced packaging) pushed to 248/193 nm, so no reticles are bought, stored or requalified per product.

title: All-optical writes to magnetic memory through on-chip waveguides
idea: Eliminate electrical write drivers: deliver femtosecond laser pulses via silicon-nitride waveguides to GdFeCo-based MTJ free layers that toggle by all-optical switching; reads stay electrical via TMR.

title: Eliminate module replacement: embedded microheaters anneal leaky cells in-situ
idea: Put thin resistive heater lines under each bank. In a maintenance window, the bank's data is migrated away and the bank is heated to ~250-300 C for seconds to anneal the interface traps and hot-carrier damage behind VRT and leakage tails, then the data is restored.

title: Negative counter-pulse on neighbor wordlines cancels hammer electrons
idea: TRIZ #8 Anti-weight: after each aggressor precharge, the two adjacent wordlines are driven ~0.3 V more negative for ~2 ns, creating a counter-field that sweeps electrons injected from the aggressor channel back before they reach victim storage nodes.

title: Bamboo-node grow-up pillar capacitors with periodic diaphragms
idea: Bamboo reaches extreme slenderness by growing upward with a nodal diaphragm every few diameters. Grow the storage-node pillars bottom-up by area-selective TiN deposition through a sacrificial oxide stack, and add a thin SiN diaphragm lattice every ~150 nm of height. AR >150 pillars then neither lean nor stick, and nothing has to be etched at that AR.
note: DRAM already uses SiN support meshes; bottom-up ASD growth without holes is unclear.

title: Spindt molybdenum-cone vacuum access switch with zero channel leakage
idea: Revive SRI's 1968 Spindt molybdenum-cone field emitters and the vacuum triode: each cell's access device is a nanoscale vacuum gap with a tip made of Colorado-mined molybdenum and a gate ring. In the off state the vacuum holds no carriers, so leakage is only Fowler-Nordheim tunnelling, negligible at hold fields; build on 130-90 nm U.S. lines with wafer-level vacuum sealing.

title: Sauna recovery: on-die micro-heaters anneal traps after data evacuation
idea: Blocks of the array embed TiN resistive heaters; monthly, a block is evacuated by row copy, heated to ~250 C for seconds to recover BTI and anneal interface traps, then returned to service.

title: Skull: cold-crucible induction Czochralski growth eliminates quartz crucibles
idea: Random stimulus 'skull' -> a frozen shell of the melt holds the melt. A water-cooled segmented copper cold crucible melts silicon by induction inside its own solid silicon skin, feeding continuous 300 mm CZ pulling with no quartz contact.

title: Steep-slope tunnel-FET sense amps for a 0.4 V array
idea: Box: low-voltage cap x Si access x TFET cross-coupled latch x CMOS co-integration x SOI x Ge/III-V source epitaxy. TFETs with 30-40 mV/decade subthreshold slope form a latch that resolves ~15 mV signals at 0.4 V supply, letting the array voltage drop from ~1 V to 0.4 V.

title: Stochastically assembled nanowire decoders with post-fab calibration map
idea: Box: crossbar-pitch storage x nanowire access x conventional SA x self-assembled sub-litho lines x Si x DSA patterning. A few lithographic mesowires address sub-lithographic lines through randomly doped regions, and a built-in calibration pass discovers each line's code and stores it in a lookup, so decoders need no litho pitch matching.
note: DeHon-style stochastic decoders; DRAM wordline pitch already litho-defined, so little gain.

title: Stacked CFET four-transistor loadless latch near DRAM footprint
idea: [Box: bistable latch | complementary stacked FET (nFET over pFET) | differential SA | monolithic CFET | Si | Si/SiGe epitaxy] Build a 4T loadless cell (two pMOS access devices plus two cross-coupled nMOS held by leakage ratio) with CFET vertical stacking so the footprint approaches ~2x a 6F2 DRAM cell, with no capacitor and no refresh.
note: Loadless 4T SRAM is known art; ~2x 6F2 footprint is far below realistic CFET SRAM cell areas.

title: On-die microheater anneals re-passivate leakage traps in the field
idea: Box [medium: capacitor | access: planar | sense: standard | integration: monolithic with polysilicon heater meander under each bank | substrate: bulk | fab: DUV]. Every few months the controller migrates one bank's data to a neighbour, heats the bank to ~250 C for ~100 ms, and lets hydrogen re-passivate the interface traps that create GIDL and variable-retention tails.

title: Po: memory is an old TV tube — field-emitter-addressed charge spots
idea: Po: memory is an old TV tube. Extracted: revive the Williams-Kilburn tube on-chip: a Spindt field-emitter array whose tips are each deflected over a 100x100 field writes, reads (secondary-emission contrast) and refreshes ~20 nm charge spots on an unpatterned dielectric film.

title: Nanoelectromechanical relay access switch with air-gap zero leakage
idea: Po: the access transistor is always perfectly off. Replace the access FET with a vertical NEM relay whose cantilever is pulled onto the storage-node contact by the wordline field and springs back to leave a ~5 nm air gap, so off-state leakage is only gap tunneling (<1e-21 A); a low-adhesion RuO2 contact and pull-in/pull-out hysteresis keep the wordline swing under ~1 V.

title: Face-to-face mirror bonding shares sense amps across two arrays
idea: Po: two chips stare at each other in a mirror. Build identical array wafers with sense-amp stripes on alternate mats, flip one and hybrid-bond face to face so every sense amp senses a bitline from its own array against the mirrored twin bitline across the bond as the reference, the SA stripes interleaving like a zipper.

title: Two bits per cell in trailing fabs with fat capacitors
idea: Po: one cell remembers two things. Old 2x-3x nm DRAM lines have larger capacitors and tighter leakage tails; store four charge levels per cell and read with reference-cell-calibrated time-to-digital sense amps (built in bonded 28 nm periphery), doubling bits on existing lines.
note: Multilevel DRAM studied since 1990s; quartered margin fights leakage tail.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory pods with superconducting YBCO interposer wiring
idea: Po: wires have no resistance. Run memory pods at 77 K and pattern YBCO superconducting lines on the interposer, so links from many DRAM stacks to the processor are lossless over 10-100 mm, while cold DRAM retains data ~1000x longer.

title: On-die micro-heaters anneal leaky access transistors overnight
idea: Po: chips that heal while they sleep. A polysilicon heater grid under each mat pulses the local array to ~250-300 C for milliseconds during maintenance windows (data migrated out first), annealing interface and gate-oxide traps behind variable-retention-time and GIDL tail cells; the mat is re-profiled and returned to service.

title: MRI gradient row selection with window-conducting access devices
idea: MRI picks one slice with a field gradient, not one wire per slice. Use anti-ambipolar access devices (e.g. MoS2/WSe2 heterojunctions) that conduct only inside a narrow gate window; a resistive ladder spreads a voltage gradient across a mat's wordlines, and two DAC-set endpoint voltages place exactly one row in that window.
note: Anti-ambipolar windows (~0.5 V wide) cannot resolve hundreds of rows on a few-volt ladder; hierarchical use only.

title: EMP-hardened NEMS relay access switch with air-gap off-state
idea: Military and nuclear electronics use nanomechanical relays because radiation and EMP do not affect them. Build a vertical NEMS cantilever relay per cell that touches the storage-node contact only when the wordline pulls it in; off, an air gap gives zero subthreshold and junction leakage.

title: Randomly doped mesowire decoder with post-fab code discovery
idea: From molecular-electronics crossbars: wordlines are addressed through mesowires whose doping pattern is set stochastically by a self-assembled mask, not lithography; after fab a BIST sweeps address codes, finds which code selects each wordline and stores the map in fuses.
note: Same stochastic mesowire decoder with post-fab code discovery.

title: Undersea-cable photonics replace global I/O lines via DUV photonic die
idea: Telecom crosses oceans with WDM light: a 45 nm DUV silicon-photonics die hybrid-bonded to the DRAM carries bank data on SiN waveguides, with microring modulators at each bank edge, replacing long global I/O metal lines and pin SERDES.

title: ROADM-style wavelength-addressed DRAM banks
idea: Telecom ROADMs route by color, not by address decode. Give each bank group a microring drop filter tuned to its own wavelength; the host picks the target bank by choosing a comb-laser line, so light itself routes the request and data to the bank and the global electrical decode and data bus disappear.
note: Photonic DRAM routing was studied ~2010; rings on DRAM process need thermal tuning.

title: Self-assembled stochastic nanowire decoders calibrated at wafer test
idea: Molecule-to-wafer jump: block-copolymer self-assembly patterns sub-10 nm address nanowires with random doping codes instead of lithographed decoders, and at wafer test each chip learns once which code reaches which row and stores it in a small address-translation table.

title: Electromagnetic cold-crucible Czochralski eliminates Spruce Pine quartz entirely
idea: Replace the fused-quartz crucible with a segmented, water-cooled copper cold crucible. An RF field heats the silicon and partly levitates it, and the melt freezes a thin silicon skull against the wall, so molten silicon only ever touches silicon. Scale jump from vessel to field: Lorentz force and a self-grown shell do the containing.

title: Ovonic-threshold-switch crosspoint replaces per-row wordline driver selection
idea: Effect: ovonic threshold switching. Select wordlines through a BEOL crosspoint of OTS devices: a group line at +V/2 and an index line at -V/2 exceed the OTS threshold (~1.5 V) only at their intersection, which snaps on and charges that wordline. This is coincident selection, as in core memory, done with threshold switching; N drivers become ~2*sqrt(N).

title: Acousto-optic steered holographic cube as microsecond tier below DRAM
idea: A TeO2 acousto-optic deflector steers a laser to any of ~10^5 page holograms in a photopolymer cube within ~5 us. Each flash reads a 1 Mb page onto a camera chip. Cold but randomly accessed data, such as embedding tables and old KV, lives here instead of DRAM.
note: Holographic storage repeatedly failed; NAND/CXL already fills this tier.

title: Si: CCD bucket-brigade bitlines feeding one floating-diffusion amplifier
idea: Borrow the image-sensor trick: after a row opens, each cell's charge is clocked as a packet along a buried-channel silicon bitline to one ~1 fF floating-diffusion source follower plus comparator shared by 32-64 columns; restore is a reverse shift of a regenerated packet.

title: P: phosphorus-doped Esaki diode Goto pair as sense latch
idea: Use two degenerately doped silicon tunnel diodes (P and B gas-phase doping in H2, no argon-diluted implanter source) in series as a Goto pair on the bitline; the negative-resistance pair has two stable states and resolves a few-mV imbalance in tens of ps at ~0.3 V.

title: Lab-grown-gem diamond storage node: 5.5 eV bandgap kills leakage tail
idea: Borrow CVD gem growth to make single-crystal diamond tiles (carbon only). The storage node is a boron-doped diamond junction capacitor with a hydrogen-terminated diamond access FET, and intrinsic carrier generation is ~1e-36 of silicon's, so retention runs to hours.
note: Same wide-bandgap diamond access idea; single-crystal diamond tiles do not scale.

title: Titanium skull-melting: grow silicon ingots with no quartz crucible
idea: Titanium is melted inside a frozen 'skull' of itself in a water-cooled copper crucible. Adapt cold-crucible induction melting, with a frozen silicon shell as the container, to feed a continuous Czochralski puller so the melt never touches quartz. Dope oxygen in through the gas phase.

title: Stochastically doped nanowire decoders discovered rather than drawn
idea: Ideal result: a decoder that needs no lithographic precision. Grow wordline-select nanowires with random axial doping segments that form random but unique codes against a coarse address mesh; at test, map which code selects which row into a table and accept a few percent unusable rows.

title: Superconducting persistent-current loops behind an optical cryostat window
idea: Ideal: a current that circulates forever with no supply. Closest achievable: store bits as flux quanta in niobium persistent-current loops at 4 K (Josephson memory arrays) driven by on-cryostat SFQ logic, with data entering and leaving through optical fiber links to warm processors.

title: EUV-free decoder: coarse mesowires plus stochastic doping and lookup map
idea: Limit: no EUV or immersion patterning in decoder transistors. Borrowing nanowire-crossbar decoders, a few coarse i-line address wires cross the dense wordline ends, and graded implant or gate-oxide thickness gives each wordline a unique threshold code; a post-fab BIST pass maps logical rows to the physical codes that actually work and stores the map in a few kb.
note: Threshold-coded stochastic decoder with BIST map, same core mechanism.

title: Silicon-free DRAM on glass panels in idled display fabs
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero silicon wafers. Make 1T1C memory with oxide-TFT access transistors and stacked MIM capacitors on Gen-8.5 glass panels in under-used display fabs, stacking 4-8 cell layers to offset the ~1 um design rule, and pair it with a small CMOS controller.

title: Drop-tower silicon spheres skip crucibles, ingots and wire saws
idea: TRIZ #14 Spheroidality: melt granular polysilicon droplets in a drop tube so they solidify without a crucible into 1-2 mm single-crystal spheres (the Ball Semiconductor route). Pattern small memory chiplets on each sphere with conformal maskless lithography, and pack the spheres into 3D memory clusters.

title: Lava lamp: VO2 nanodot parked inside its Mott hysteresis loop
idea: Stimulus 'lava lamp' (a heat-driven state that persists) -> a 20 nm VO2 nanodot, Cr-doped and strained to widen its thermal hysteresis to ~15 K, sits on a bias heater rail holding it mid-loop; a ~5 ns current pulse flips it metallic, a cooling pulse resets it insulating, and the ~100x resistance contrast is read nondestructively.

title: S: tetrathiafulvalene rotaxane monolayer crossbar with defect-mapped molecular switches
idea: Sandwich a monolayer of bistable [2]rotaxanes between nanoimprinted crossbar wires at ~15 nm pitch; oxidizing the sulfur-rich tetrathiafulvalene station shuttles the ring and changes junction conductance, and a defect map plus code tolerates ~1% dead or shorted junctions.
note: Heath/Stoddart rotaxane crossbar memory already demonstrated; slow and fragile.

title: VO2 hysteresis islands held bistable by chip waste heat
idea: Scarcity rule: no electrical hold power; the only free resource is the chip's own heat. W-doped VO2 islands are tuned so the die's ~65 C operating point sits inside their metal-insulator hysteresis loop; a Joule pulse sets an island metallic, a piezo-strain pulse (which shifts the transition temperature) resets it insulating, and read uses the ~100x resistance contrast.

title: Biased deep carrier-sink layer shields arrays from substrate leakage
idea: Scale shift of the analog guard ring (100 um) to every array mat: implant a deep, positively biased phosphorus collector layer under each mat inside a boron array well so thermally generated substrate electrons are collected before they diffuse into storage nodes.
note: Arrays already sit in biased triple-well/deep N-well structures.

title: Meet-in-the-middle capacitor: etch half from front, half from back
idea: Reverse the etch direction for half the hole: etch the storage-node hole to ~35:1 from the front, then after bonding to a carrier and thinning, etch the second 35:1 half from the backside and land it on an etch-stop plug at mid-depth; the two halves join into one 70:1+ electrode.
note: Backside etch would have to pass through the transistor layer beneath the capacitor mold.

title: Piezoelectronic access switch with pressure-driven insulator-metal channel
idea: Effect: pressure-induced insulator-to-metal transition. A thin AlScN piezo actuator driven by the wordline squeezes a ~5 nm SmSe-class valence-change piezoresistor in series with the storage node; at ~1 GPa it turns metallic, and when unpressed it is a ~0.5 eV-gap insulator, so the hold path is a true insulator rather than a subthreshold channel.
note: A 0.5 eV-gap off-state leaks more than silicon at 85 C, so the claimed leakage reduction contradicts physics.

title: Impact-ionization latches sense at a 0.4 V array voltage
idea: Ideal result: CV^2 near zero because the array runs at a fraction of a volt. Build the SA cross-coupled pair from impact-ionization MOS devices whose sub-5 mV/decade switching regenerates full logic levels from a 0.4 V supply, letting VARY drop from ~1 V.
note: I-MOS needs volts of bias for avalanche, which contradicts a 0.4 V array.

title: Liquid-metal capsules self-heal broken vertical interconnects
idea: Ideal result: a broken wire that rejoins itself. Fill spare vias beside TSVs and bitline contacts with encapsulated Ga-In micro-capsules that rupture from the local heat of a forming void and wick into the crack, restoring continuity.
note: Ga-In capsules too large for TSV scale and gallium attacks Al/Cu metallization.

title: Tantalum capacitor powder metallurgy: sintered nanosponge storage electrode
idea: Adapted from solid tantalum capacitor anodes (pressed, sintered powder with enormous internal area): fill each storage-node cavity with a sintered TiN/Ru nanoparticle sponge, then ALD high-k and the plate electrode through its open pores.

title: Tungsten-free TiN wordlines stitched to Cu every 128 cells
idea: Reverse the wordline's job: buried TiN-only lines just gate the cells, while a copper strap above carries the current, connected every 128 cells through one added stitch-contact mask. RC falls ~16x, which covers TiN's ~4x higher resistivity.
note: Wordline strapping is classic; strap metal at buried-WL pitch is hard.

title: Electric-fence gate isolation replaces oxide-filled array STI
idea: Random stimulus 'electric fence': a field keeps the herd apart with no wall. Isolate adjacent access transistors with dedicated always-off isolation-gate lines held at -0.5 V in shallow recesses, in place of deep oxide-filled STI that needs fill, CMP and repeated HF recess dips.
note: Field-shield isolation is 1980s-90s art; passing-gate disturb concerns.

title: Tungsten-free buried wordlines tolerate a slow far-end tail
idea: Po: wordlines with no tungsten. Buried wordlines use a TiN liner with heavily doped polysilicon fill instead of W; the higher RC under-drives far-end cells within the tRCD window, producing a ~1% incomplete-restore tail at mat edges that the code corrects.

title: Silicon-carbide NEMS relays form leak-free CAM for KV prefix matching
idea: Build a content-addressable memory from SiC nano-electromechanical relays (contacts demonstrated at 500 C) that stores prompt-prefix hashes. Each request's prefix hash is matched in one cycle, so shared system-prompt KV is reused instead of recomputed and duplicated. The relays have zero off-state leakage, whereas a CMOS CAM leaks heavily at 125 C.
note: Prefix-hash matching is trivially cheap in software; CAM solves a non-bottleneck.

title: Flip the gate under: substrate-doped buried wordline replaces tungsten
idea: Rearrange the stack so the wordline is below the channel: an epitaxially grown, heavily doped n+ silicon line in the substrate acts as back gate under a thin vertical or planar channel, eliminating the recessed buried-tungsten wordline.
note: Doped-Si wordline RC far worse than W.

title: Brownout-tolerant fab: process excursions become BER bins
idea: Reverse the tie between power quality and yield: run non-critical tools straight on intermittent renewables without full UPS, let power-dip excursions degrade some wafers, and bin those wafers by raw BER up to 1%.

title: Aluminum metal-last wordlines replacing tungsten
idea: Reverse metallization order: form wordlines with a sacrificial nitride, finish all high-temperature steps, then replace it with abundant aluminum by low-temperature CVD; voids and electromigration opens (~1% of cells) are corrected by row-erasure coding.

title: Williams tube rebuilt with Spindt emitters over unpatterned charge target
idea: Revive the Williams/BEAMOS tube in flat form: a university-fabricated Spindt field-emitter array gated by row/column lines addresses spots on an unpatterned SiO2-on-Si charge-storage target a few microns away in vacuum. Bits are written by secondary-emission charging and read as target current, so the storage plane needs no cell lithography and no per-bit transistor.
note: Spot pitch and charge retention give density far below DRAM; vacuum packaging.

title: Frequency-addressed MEMS resonators select mats over one wire
idea: Give each mat's enable a MEMS resonator relay with a unique resonant frequency on a shared bus; driving the bus at f_k rings up only resonator k and closes its mat switch, replacing a mat-select decoder tree with one address wire (orthogonal frequency channels as the address code).

title: Dipolar molecular rotors in nanogaps store dynamic bits for ingestible pills
idea: Ingestible sensor pills need tiny, low-voltage memory; one mask opens nanogaps where a self-assembled monolayer of dipolar molecular rotors aligns up or down under ~0.3 V, and the collective dipole shifts a sense FET threshold. Thermal relaxation over milliseconds makes it a natural refreshed dynamic bit with no bond-breaking wear.
note: Niche pill market; rotor uniformity and readout signal speculative.

title: Ge: germanium strike-detector diodes turn soft errors into cheap erasures
idea: A grid of SiGe particle-strike detector diodes under each mat timestamps and localizes ion strikes; the controller marks the affected symbols as erasures, and because a code corrects twice as many erasures as unknown errors, the same ECC budget covers double the failure density.

title: Liquid-metal droplet position bit in printed microchannels
idea: IFR: a bit held by surface tension at zero power. Closest achievable: a sub-um gallium-alloy droplet rests in one of two pinned pockets of a printed channel; an electrocapillary pulse moves it and the bit is read as the capacitance of the occupied pocket.

title: Resonant LC tank drives wordlines adiabatically, recycling boost energy
idea: Fuse resonant-clock-mesh design with wordline drive: wordlines in a bank charge from a sinusoidal resonant VPP rail set by an on-package inductor, so energy swings between the inductor and the wordline capacitance instead of being dumped to ground at every precharge.

title: CCFL piezoelectric transformer replaces wordline charge pumps
idea: Borrowed from the piezo transformers that drove LCD backlight lamps: an AlN bulk-acoustic resonator (the material of phone RF filters) steps a 1.1 V drive up to 3+ V at resonance, which is rectified into the wordline VPP rail.

title: Eliminate copper and tungsten: oxygen-patterned multilayer graphene periphery lines
idea: Grow 10-20-layer graphene on a Co catalyst at BEOL temperature, intercalation-dope it with FeCl3, and pattern it with O2 plasma, since carbon needs no halogen etch. The lines need no Ta/TaN barrier and resist electromigration.
note: Quality multilayer graphene at BEOL temperature is unsolved.

title: Eliminate oxide CMP: vacuum glass reflow planarization
idea: Return to pre-CMP practice: cap each tier with a low-melting borophosphosilicate glass and reflow it under vacuum so surface tension planarizes it, with a dry etch-back to target thickness.

title: Bat-echolocation TDR to find and remap marginal HBM TSVs
idea: Bats map their world from echo delays. Picosecond time-domain reflectometry through HBM test and boundary-scan paths measures impedance discontinuities in each TSV/microbump lane, flags marginal (resistive or voided) ones before they fail, and remaps them to HBM's existing spare lanes. Instrument plus algorithm work on stack samples, ~$800k in 24 months.

title: Stencil shadow-mask deposition revived: no resist, no etch, no PFAS
idea: Revive 1960s shadow-mask evaporation with MEMS silicon-nitride stencils held close to the wafer, depositing patterned metals and dielectrics directly for BEOL plates, pads and periphery wiring with no resist and no etch.

title: Light as memory: silica fiber recirculating delay loops
idea: Inverts 'memory stores data at rest in matter': store bits as optical pulses circulating in a ~10-20 m silica fiber or silicon-nitride spiral loop with semiconductor-optical-amplifier regeneration, giving 50-100 ns worst-case access to 0.1-1 Mbit per loop at 1-10 Tb/s with WDM, a modern mercury delay line.

title: Po: rust-and-zinc logic above the array — Cu2O/ZnO CMOS
idea: Po: periphery made of rust and zinc. Build complementary BEOL thin-film logic from p-type Cu2O and n-type Al-doped ZnO (no In or Ga) to host refresh counters, mode registers, test and redundancy logic stacked above the cell array.
note: Cu2O p-TFT mobility and on/off ratio are poor.

title: Ni: nickel-silicide Schottky transistors make implant-free periphery logic
idea: Build periphery decoders from dopant-segregated NiSi Schottky-barrier MOSFETs formed by thermal silicidation, skipping ion implanters whose sources use argon dilution and purge; the abrupt metal junction shortens channels and limits short-channel leakage.
note: Dopant segregation itself uses implants; wells and Vt adjust still need implanters.

title: Na: sodium-dosed sentinel capacitors forecast mat failure early
idea: Each mat carries a few SiN-encapsulated sentinel cells whose dielectric holds a controlled Na+ dose, so they leak and age ~10x faster under identical temperature and voltage; refresh logic polls them and tightens refresh or retires the mat as soon as sentinels start failing.

title: Magnetoelectric laminates harvest broadcast field to generate wordline boost voltage
idea: Effect: magnetostriction coupled to piezoelectricity. A package-level planar coil broadcasts a ~10 MHz AC magnetic field; each bank carries a FeGa (magnetostrictive) / AlScN (piezoelectric) laminate whose strain produces several volts locally, which a rectifier stores as VPP. This replaces the area-hungry switched-capacitor charge pumps and long VPP buses.
note: ME laminates deliver uW; VPP needs tens of mW.

title: Swiss roll: strained nanomembranes self-roll into capacitor scrolls
idea: A Swiss roll packs a long sheet into a small volume: deposit a planar TiN/HZO/TiN/HZO multilayer on a strained SiGe/Si bilayer in each lateral 3D cell, then release it with a selective etch so it curls into a 4-5 turn scroll inside the cell recess. Plate area grows with sheet length rather than etch depth.

title: Mg2Si thermoelectric spots cool only the weakest mats
idea: Worse: chill the whole module to rescue a few weak, hot mats. Flip: integrate thin-film Mg2Si / higher-manganese-silicide Peltier elements under the mats that test-time profiling marks as retention-weak, driven only when those mats exceed a temperature, so the weak tail sees ~10 C cooler silicon.
note: Silicon spreads heat; a 10 C mat-local delta with thin-film TE is implausible.
